name: Lauren Merrell
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I offer a range of services to meet your needs, including combined treatment (medication + therapy), medication management, & ADHD evals.
ideal_client: I work with adults who are navigating challenges related to depression, anxiety, ADHD, and life transitions. My ideal clients are individuals who are seeking a deeper understanding of their mental health and are motivated to make meaningful changes in their lives. In our first few sessions, I'll listen to you intently and then we'll determine a path forward. Most of my clients start to feel better within a few months.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I specialize in psychodynamic psychotherapy, which is well-suited to people who want to get to the root of long-term problems and patterns that continually crop up and get in the way of living a fulfilled life. I incorporate this expertise into my medication management appointments, as well as with patients who are seeking therapy. As a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner, sometimes I will recommend medications that I believe will help you to make best use of therapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to care is warm, direct, and attentive. I believe in having honest, thoughtful conversations about your mental health while providing a supportive space to explore what’s working and what’s not. When prescribing medication, my goal is always to find the lowest effective dose.

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: I'm an experienced psychiatric prescriber who focuses their treatment recommendations on the whole person. I'm particularly well-versed in helping clients with depression, anxiety, and ADHD. In addition to my private practice, I teach in the School of Nursing at Oregon Health & Science University (OHSU) which ensures that I'm up-to-date on cutting edge treatments.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I'm a member of of the Oregon Psychoanalytic Center and engage in weekly consultation with an experienced psychodynamic therapist to optimize my therapeutic interventions.

name: Care Nimble
title: Psychiatrist
intro: We are online psychiatric experts, providing you with high quality, convenient, compassionate care. Today. You've got this. We can help.
ideal_client: Our board-certified psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners provide care for a wide range of mental health conditions, including depression, anxiety disorders, adult ADHD, bipolar disorder, trauma and PTSD. We currently provide psychiatric care for independent adults aged 18 and over, including expertise in gender-affirming care.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: At Care Nimble, we make mental health medication simple. Our board-certified psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners provide you with same-day care through an easy-to-use, online platform. No scheduling needed. Get personalized prescription treatment for depression, anxiety, ADHD, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and more. We ask the right questions to understand your unique needs, and get you the right care when you need it - today. Start your journey to better mental health today with effective, affordable mental health medication management that works for you.

approaches.Why We Started this Group Practice: At Care Nimble, we make mental health medication simple. Our board-certified psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners provide you with same-day care through an easy-to-use, online platform. No scheduling needed. Get personalized prescription treatment for depression, anxiety, ADHD, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and more. We ask the right questions to understand your unique needs, and get you the right care when you need it - today. Start your journey to better mental health today with effective, affordable mental health medication management that works for you. Psychiatric care is often frustrating, expensive, and overwhelming, with long waits, inconvenient scheduling, expensive bills, complicated insurance coverage. Care Nimble makes it simple. We provide personalized, affordable, quality psychiatric medication management, on your terms. Right now. Mental health med management made easy.

name: Ryan Brown
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Therapy for human beings in Portland, Oregon.
ideal_client: I work with people navigating the messy challenges of being human—grief, anxiety, identity, life transitions, or feeling stuck or disconnected. Many of my clients are LGBTQ+, creative, or exploring polyamory and nontraditional relationships. If you’re seeking therapy that honors your depth and helps you live with more honesty, clarity, and purpose, I offer a space of warmth, presence, and integrity.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe each of us holds the capacity for growth, healing, and meaningful change. My approach is rooted in Existential-Humanistic therapy, which centers on exploring what it means to live authentically and intentionally. Together, we’ll examine themes like choice, responsibility, meaning, and purpose—so you can better understand yourself and how you want to show up in the world. Often, we suffer when there’s a painful gap between how life is and how we long for it to be. This can leave us feeling stuck, disconnected, or like life is happening to us instead of through us. In our work, I’ll help you slow down, reflect deeply, and reconnect with your sense of agency. My goal is to support you in living with more freedom, clarity, and integrity—aligned with your values and in relationship with what truly matters to you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I’m a queer therapist, Zen practitioner, and former LGBTQ+ rights activist with a deep commitment to authenticity, justice, and meaningful connection. Before becoming a therapist, I spent ten years working in the marriage equality movement—an experience that continues to shape my belief in human dignity and the healing power of relationship. I hold a Master’s in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Goddard College with a focus on Sexual Orientation and specialized training in working with LGBTQ+ clients. I serve on the board of Existential-Humanistic Northwest and am currently pursuing a PhD in Leadership and Change at Antioch University, where I study how to create more ethical, human-centered models of leadership and care. My work is grounded in existential-humanistic values: presence, freedom, integrity, and responsibility. I’m especially passionate about supporting clients navigating depression, anxiety, identity, life transitions, LGBTQ+ experiences, and relationships

name: April Dvorak
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Head Well is a new psychiatric practice. We use an integrative approach to do more than treat symptoms. Our goal is your wellness.
ideal_client: Are you tired of just being okay? Or even faking it most days? Whether you've "tried everything" or are only starting to think about getting treatment, we can help. We are committed to optimizing your function and finding your wellness. April has extensive experience in inpatient and outpatient settings and a wide range of patient populations, including serious mental illness (SMI), corrections, forensic, adolescent, and geriatric psychiatry.

approaches.My Background: April Dvorak, PMHNP-BC, is a Board-Certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner and the founder of Head Well – Integrative Psychiatry, a mental health practice based in Eugene Oregon. She helped found and serves as the President of Projects on Purpose Inc (POPI), a nonprofit serving the seriously mentally ill. A native of Houston, Texas, April started her academic journey at Texas A&M University, graduating in 2009 with a Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Sciences. She continued her education at the University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston, where she studied undergraduate nursing in 2011. She worked as a nurse in the Neonatal ICU and then various psychiatric settings before returning to obtain her Master of Science in Nursing and board certification from the ANCC as a Psychiatric and Mental Health Nurse Practitioner in 2017.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: After years of practicing in the public sector and clunky, bureaucratic institutions, April wanted to build a model based on efficiency and long-term, sustainable solutions. She believes in making sense of things and working through tough problems. April started Head Well – Integrative Psychiatry in hopes of doing both. Her clinical approach is integrative and functionally rooted. She is fascinated by how personality structure and emotional and behavior patterns account for much of how we view and interact with the world. People co-create their realities, and understanding oneself is the key to a cohesive, productive, and meaningful existence. April is passionate about mental health advocacy and maintaining humanity, rationality, and integrity in psychiatry and social services. She loves to learn and recently obtained certificate from Integrative Psychiatric Institute (IPI) as a Ketamine Medical Provider. She was recently awarded Eugene’s top 20 under 40.

name: Lily Packer
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Compassionate counselor specializing in neurodivergent youth and families, creating safe spaces for growth through connection.
ideal_client: I specialize in supporting neurodivergent youth and individuals navigating anxiety, depression, and trauma. My practice welcomes those seeking help with executive functioning, emotional regulation, and sensory processing concerns. Using CBT approaches, I help families develop strategies for managing challenging behaviors and building stronger connections. Whether you're seeking support for childhood anxiety or exploring neurodivergent identities, my toffers a safe space to begin healing.

approaches.How I Can Help You: As a mental health counselor specializing in neurodevelopmental differences, I provide targeted support across age groups. For children, I create playful environments using play therapy to develop self-regulation skills and process emotions safely. With teenagers, I balance respecting autonomy while providing structure to address teen anxiety, depression, and identity exploration. My approach helps teens build emotional resilience while navigating complex social challenges. For young adults, I offer guidance through transitions, supporting them with executive functioning challenges and creating sustainable coping strategies. Families are essential partners in this work. I provide parent coaching to enhance understanding of your child's needs and develop effective behavior management approaches. Through family therapy, we strengthen communication and create environments where everyone thrives.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Choosing the right therapist is deeply personal. My clients often tell me they feel truly seen in our work together—something particularly valuable for neurodivergent youth who may have experienced misunderstanding elsewhere. With specialized training in childhood anxiety, trauma recovery, and neurodevelopmental differences, I bring both expertise and heartfelt compassion to our sessions. Parents appreciate my practical guidance for managing challenging behaviors, while children and teens respond to my authentic, gentle approach to building emotional regulation skills. My background as a behavioral specialist and crisis intervention counselor has shaped my ability to remain calm and present, even during difficult moments. The therapeutic relationship we build becomes the foundation for growth. Through CBT techniques, mindfulness practices, and strength-based approaches, we'll work together to transform struggles into stepping stones for development.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: As an autism specialist, I support neurodivergent children and teens with sensory needs, executive functioning, and emotional regulation. Using neurodiversity-affirming, strengths-based therapy, I help families create routines, visual supports, and sensory-friendly spaces. My approach honors each child’s unique way of thinking, feeling, and communicating—empowering both kids and parents to thrive with confidence.

name: Julie Bloom
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I often work with folks navigating religious or relational trauma, relationship challenges, and grief. Neurodiversity and LGBTQ+ affirming.
ideal_client: Those who are navigating religious trauma, the impact of purity culture, and grief related to faith deconstruction and faith transitions are especially drawn to my work. I am also passionate about working with individuals who have experienced are recovering perfectionists, those navigating career burnout, and neurodivergent folks navigating spaces and systems that aren't designed for them.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use an integrative approach where I attune to my client’s goals, needs, and the greater systems that may be impacting them. My approach is relational, LGBTQ+ affirming, and trauma-informed. I take into account the whole person as well as the relationships, systems of oppression, and barriers that might influence how they show up in the world. So in sessions with clients, we are not simply looking at symptoms, but striving to understand and excavate the deeper places to get the full picture of what’s happening, where it started, and what a path forward could look like. Additionally, I offer EMDR Therapy (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing). I completed my Master of Arts in Mental Health Counseling from Regis University in Denver.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: The therapeutic relationship is a microcosm where an individual will get to experience someone honoring their full humanity—a supportive space to identify and heal relational wounds. And, to enhance ones ability to connect with others simply by having the allocated space of therapy to practice having a sense of safety within the context of the therapeutic relationship. My hope is to highlight client strengths and equip and empower them to move about the world with more ease and a sense of belonging. At its best, therapy is a space where your full identity and humanity is held, honored, and cultivated.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I offer a relational approach which means showing up fully as both a clinician and as a human so that my clients can learn to do the same in the therapy room and outside in all their relationships and connections. Relational therapy centers on the idea that healing happens in relationships—drawing from the psychology of attachment, connection, and co-regulation. You don't have to be perfect or "fully healed" to be deserving of connection and belonging.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I practice EMDR therapy and integrate it into sessions with clients who are seeking relief from distressing or traumatic experiences, and desiring to replace old core beliefs that have been reinforced through relationships or other distressing events. For example, "I'm not good enough," "I'm not safe," or "I can't trust myself." I also offer EMDR intensives to those working with an individual therapist. Note: I'm currently seeking EMDRIA-approved consultation in pursuit of EMDR certification.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I integrate a psychodynamic approach—helping my clients explore how unconscious thoughts and past experiences may be impacting them in the present. Together, we'll explore patterns in thoughts and behaviors, often focusing on early life experiences and relationships to understand and address present concerns or stressors.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is a complex emotional journey—a confrontation of loss in all of it's forms. Although we may tend to associate grief with a death loss, grief is an expansive term for a diverse range of losses—whether it's a transition to a new city, a loss of a friendship, a faith transition, or a late diagnosis of autism or ADHD in adulthood. Every loss deserves to be acknowledged and held with care and support.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I have lived experience healing from religious trauma and the impact of purity culture, the grief of faith deconstruction, and the relational dynamics that go along with a significant faith transition. Additionally, I have sought out additional training to support my work with folks who are interested in navigating religious trauma, the complexity of relationships with family or friends following deconstruction, or who or simply wanting more depth and to explore their evolving beliefs

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I have worked with ADHDers and AuDHers and I am passionate about working with folks who are seeking a neurodiversity-affirming therapist. My goal is to empower my clients to attune to their strengths and to gain tools for areas that feel more challenging—that work with their own way of thinking and being.

name: Michaela Curtis-Joyce
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I believe we all already have exactly what we need. I find it rewarding to team up with clients and find ways to harness their strengths
ideal_client: I work with adult individuals, couples, and broader relationship work. This may mean folks who are struggling with adjustment, managing emotions, or who are concerned for children in their care. I particularly enjoy working with parents/caregivers in unconventional families including queer, trans and polyamorous.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am glad you are here and I genuinely would like to help you find the right support. I believe we all already have exactly what we need. I find it quite rewarding to team up with clients and find ways to harness their strengths. I am relationship based and balance compassion with frank communication.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I understand that finding the right support for unconventional relationships can be challenging. Sometimes the central work is around ethical non-monogamy and sometimes its nice to focus on unrelated challenges with some who "gets it".

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Raising children is the most intense and rewarding experience I have had. No one can do it in a bubble. We all need support sometimes. I find it quite rewarding to offer support for others doing caretaking. It not only supports the adults I'm working with but their children as well.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I work with adults to support the well being of their children. In my professional opinion children benefit most of from smaller and more frequent doses of support. I delight in supporting caregivers to offer this to their children.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Throughout our lifetimes everyone of us experiences anxiety. Whether this is a new concern for you or something you have been managing for a longer time I am confident that we can work together and lessen theintensity.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Throughout the course of our lifetimes everyone of us experiences depression. Whether this is a new concern for you or something you have been managing for a longer time I am confident that we can work together and lessen the intensity.

name: Kir Rian
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: MA, MFA, Licensed Professional Counselor/OR, Licensed Mental Health Counselor/WA, Clinical Supervisor/WA
intro: Trauma-certified therapy in a mindful, collaborative space. Specializing in grief, illness, and stress mgmt. Fully licensed in OR & WA.
ideal_client: Whether recent circumstances are challenging, or aspects of the past need to be reconciled, my clients want to process and cope healthily, moving toward mindful, holistic healing. They want to feel less anxious, own their lives, and feel better. They want clarity, meaning, understanding, and support reaching that place through their challenges, traumas, or grief. They are often dealing with residual and associated anxiety, depression, grief, and stress as they move through their healing process.

approaches.My Background and Approach: These beautiful, unpredictable, messy moments of life shape us, and I've learned that defining who we are through these moments helps us build the life we want. It's hard work. I help people navigate and sift through it all, and I believe in a collaborative, mindfulness-based approach. I am fully licensed in OR and WA, hold a Master’s in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, am trauma certified, EMDR trained, and hold extensive training and experience in grief and trauma counseling. Previously, I worked in community mental health, and led processing groups and classes internationally, and with a variety of nonprofits for over 20 years. I am an advocate for equality and social justice, and an ally for marginalized groups. I utilize an integrated theoretical approach based in person-centered, mindfulness, somatic, ACT, EFT, and CBT. I work with a wide range of individuals and diagnoses including anxiety and codependency, and I specialize in grief, illness, and stress management.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: We hold the capacity to grow and move toward a life of health and happiness. Social, cultural, and family systems influence our perspective, as well as how we communicate with ourselves and within relationships. Sometimes our bodies betray us. Sometimes we need to learn how to carry past traumas or losses. In other words, context matters. The mind, heart, and body are all interconnected, and therapy and mindfulness strategies can significantly affect our stress responses and quality of life. I worked for years with marginalized and trauma-affected individuals through various nonprofits, and that work, combined with chronic illness issues and a sudden death in our immediate family all combined to lead me to do this work. There are tools for coping, and insights to be gleaned from what we've been through. There are connections to be made within ourselves, our community, and even our DNA through things like epigenetics. I help my clients see their light.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: One of my favorite aspects of mindfulness therapy is that the awareness and processing strategies are easily applied in between therapy sessions, and help with a huge range of challenges, from anxiety and depression to PTSD to grief to daily stress management. True healing and coping is integrative, and mindfulness is an important, very well-researched approach to help facilitate ongoing health, growth, and stability. Sometimes this is meditation, but also breath work and other grounding tools.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Learning coping tools to improve functioning, changing underlying thought patterns or perspectives we've held that don't serve us, and re-evaluating our motivations or circumstances, can help us see or understand our challenges in a different way, and respond effectively. Processing thought patterns and responses through a CBT lens have been shown to be hugely effective with anxiety and depression, as well as with trauma and a wide array of mental health issues.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Our bodies hold memories, traumas, and emotions, and a somatic therapy approach recognizes that relationship between the mind and the body. We may think about a stressful or traumatic experience, and feel anxiety or panic in our bodies or have trouble sleeping, for example. Research shows, that an integrated whole-body approach can help provide relief, as well as facilitate processing and help significantly with nervous system management and healing.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Fundamentally, I believe in your worth and your capacity--even if you can't see that in yourself. This premise is the foundation of the humanistic approach and it is paramount to my work. I also believe you are responsible for building your life and knowing and owning who you are. I am here to support, but also to be real with you. The humanistic approach assists people with improving their functioning, their symptoms, their self awareness and self acceptance, personal responsibility, and power

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief can stem from a death close to us, or be lingering and unresolved from our past. Grief can be about things other than death, like loss of the life you pictured, or grief for the impacts of trauma and abuse. It can be all consuming and isolating and nonlinear. If there was a death in the family and we're parents, we're also managing the grief of our kids. Compounding it, most of the time people near us don't know how to support, and that can make things worse. Counseling can help processing

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Managing fears, unknowns, and the healthcare and medical systems is exhausting and can be frustrating. Often, we are also managing the emotions of those around us. We are continuing to work, raise kids, deal with financial implications, and trying to live a "normal" life despite physical or physiological manifestations, and despite a myriad of other factors unique to everyone's specific circumstance. As with grief, it can be isolating and our community often doesn't support in the way we need.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: As a trauma-certified therapist, PTSD, adult survivors of environomental catastrophes, sexual abuse, grief, and medical trauma are a focus of my practice. Trauma affects the nervous system, other aspects of our physiology, as well as our emotional state. At the same time, it can be managed holistically and with a trauma-informed approach. A safe therapeutic healing space conducive to restoration and processing can help with symptom management and overall wellness, somatically and emotionally.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can look like so many things--a steady, constant worry all the way to full-blown panic attacks. It can be restlessness or a tense jaw or neck muscles, poor self care choices, and sleep challenges as your body holds all that stress trying to protect you. Learning tools for anxiety and worry management can help minimize how these symptoms interfere with your life. Often, there are underlying root issues that can be processed through counseling, as well.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: Caregiving--whether in our personal or work life--can take a tremendous toll. It is a constant balancing act to negotiate our own self care and equilibrium along with the emotional expense of managing others' needs. My clients are healthcare professionals, educators, and others, as well as individuals caring for family members. They are responsible for a lot and the exhaustion can be deeply emotional as well as physical. Compassion can be one of our best qualities, but in balance.

name: Rebecca X Casanova
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a seasoned trauma-informed therapist with a down to earth approach who focuses on supporting people to access their own wisdom to heal
ideal_client: I use a variety of compassion-focused techniques to empower adults who have anger, anxiety, depression, trauma and/or experience of marginalization (i.e. Veterans, LGBTQ+ people, BIPOC folks, women) to learn to trust themselves, move forward, and use new tools for personal growth. People who I work with report feeling more accepting of and connected to themselves and others, less troubled by physical and emotional symptoms, and more able to make decisions that reflect their own values.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work with the people who I am privileged to serve is trauma-informed, strengths-based, client-centered, collaborative, and supportive. Many of us have been hurt and have adapted in ways that may keep us safe, but also keep us feeling stuck and disconnected from other people. I emphasize meeting people where they are at and creating a safe environment to grow and try new things. Through our work, you can become more adept at recognizing and responding to difficult emotions (including not feeling anything or nothing but anger or anxiety), and how your past trauma is showing up in your body; building resilience through skills development and practice; and feeling more comfortable in your own skin. It is my hope that everyone I serve as a therapist experiences liberation and/or is able to transcend past difficulties in order to be able to be more fully present in their lives and relationships. I encourage open communication between myself and the people I serve and welcome feedback.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a lifelong commitment to serving people who have experienced many forms of trauma and have specialized training and deep experience in serving LGBTQ+ people and Veterans. I see relationships as the most important element in healing and am also trained in multiple modalities/evidence-based therapy protocols for trauma, anxiety, depression, and related issues. I earned my MSW and MPH from Portland State University in 2013, worked at the Portland VA for nine years, and am a first-generation college graduate. Before graduate school, I was in New York for many years, where I did international and domestic human rights and public health work, including direct action and advocacy. When I’m not working, I ride my bike, hang out in nature, look at art, putter around making art, listen to music, cook, and tease my pets.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I have been certified in Cognitive Processing Therapy for PTSD since 2018 and also have training using other CBT methods.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: I have been certified in Motivational Interviewing since 2019 and have been using this form of therapy for several years.

specialities.name: Anger Management Therapy
specialities.description: I have been serving people who identify anger as a problem in their lives since 2013. I have training in using Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) for Anger and have worked with people on their anger in group and individual therapy settings since 2017. My approach is not to "manage" your anger, but to help you understand where it comes from, what it could be masking, how to move through it without it making your decisions for you, and, most importantly, to live a meaningful life.

specialities.name: Veterans/Military Service
specialities.description: I am not a Veteran myself, but I come from a family with a proud tradition of military service and have worked hard to understand the impact of military service and support Veterans and their families to heal. I was privileged to serve at the Portland VA (including internship) from 2012-2021, where I provided therapy and case management; initiated the LGBTQ+ Veteran Care Coordinator program; and served on the MST Task Force and the Intimate Partner Violence Advisory Board.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have been serving people impacted by trauma for several decades. As a clinician, trauma--and how people adapt to trauma--has been a focus since the beginning of my graduate training. I am certified in three trauma-specific modalities: Cognitive Processing Therapy for PTSD, Strength at Home, and TREM (Trauma Recovery and Empowerment) and am trained in Prolonged Exposure. I also have experience using DBT and ACT to support people with trauma histories to learn skills to be more calm and present.

name: Laura Wozniak
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I use a straight-forward supportive approach, building on diverse strengths to develop internal resources and strengthen relationships.
ideal_client: I enjoy collaborating with other medical professionals. I can support recovery from addictions, recovery from mental illness and have a special interest in creative professionals and systems approaches. I also have a salaried position working with physicians and their families. My practice is part time and so my clients need to be able to maintain themselves safely between visits with relatively low intensity contact.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Though originally trained in family systems with a CBT and Group orientation, I have added from Jungian, self-psychology, internal family systems, and addictions training (including eating disorders and alcohol). I am comfortable working with people who take psychiatric medication or people who have medical conditions. I appreciate collaboration with primary care providers.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am certified in mediation, using the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator, and Gottman couples therapy. I enjoy doing team building with small organizations and have training in DBT/CBT/Mindfulness, PTSD, ADD and critical incident debriefing. My current practice involves handling the special challenges of stress due to the Covid 19 pandemic and social upheavals. I have many years of experience as a clinical supervisor.. I have a limited sliding fee from 50 to 150.00. I can provide a bill for submission to a PPO by the client.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I work to enhance all relationships since they underpin our mental and physical health as well as our ability to learn and adapt in our relationship with our self. I welcome my clients to bring other people in their lives into the therapy setting.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: This style best describes my work after 35 years. I do not want to imply that I have a lack of interest in specific approaches, but it is important to adapt my approach to the personality, strengths and needs of my client. I like to begin with the simplest interventions first and progress through relational and internal dynamics as effective and welcomed by the client. My underlying belief is that human well-being is supported through a sense of internal coherence, meaning and connection.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I started my career working with addictions and codependency using the Johnson Family Institute training. I am qualified to explore diverse addiction issues- and help clients make decisions about further addictions treatment they may need to pursue or I can continue with them on an outpatient basis when weekly therapy is appropriate. I support 12 step programs, but other approaches may fit.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I have worked for 12 years in a medical setting supporting patients who have a wide variety of chronic and acute conditions. I have worked to prepare patients for bariatric surgery, chronic pain, fibromyalgia, transplant and in supporting family members as well. I have skills and experience using guided imagery and relaxation skills which can enhance resiliency.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I love helping people create and maintain happy supportive relationships where they can be at their best. I work with same-gender and male-female relationships as well as parent-child, sibling and work relationships. I have training in Gottman and other approaches such as dialogue. In relationship work, I am directive and support the relationship as my client where possible. I work to enhance couple bonding and bring in some lightness where possible to defuse negative interpretations

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Most people present with a life issue such as career, health or divorce. This issue must be addressed respectfully starting with the clients' concerns. If longer-standing personality, mood or other serious issues are complicating resolution and well-being, trust has been established to address those as well. Many of my clients struggle with historic mood issues as well as current problems.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety and Depression go together. Both can be helped with CBT/DBT/behavioral and supportive interventions. It is important to help the client make life decisions that create a healthy life as the first step and to reduce the suffering due to the symptoms through coping skills including mindfulness and a hopeful perspective. At times, medication may be helpful and I can help monitor this with the prescriber.

name: Maile Sand
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: As an artist and art therapist, I believe wholeheartedly that art therapy is positively life changing and leads to discovery and healing.
ideal_client: Focusing on adults and teens who identify as women, I specialize in managing stress, relationships, anxiety, depression, grief and loss, spiritual abuse, and healing from trauma. If you would like to explore healing in a safe space with a creative approach, please reach out.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic style is empathetic, honest, collaborative, and creative. I use art directives, reflection, affirmation, encouragement, humor, and observation to help you cultivate your awareness, agency, confidence and healing. My practice primarily involves art therapy, for those clients who choose it—I can assure you that no artistic talent is necessary! I aim to create a safe, non-judgmental, compassionate space for you to explore the things that are causing distress or discomfort in your life. Artmaking is a powerful tool that unlocks areas of ourselves we are unable to access verbally. Whether or not you choose to explore art therapy, all my clients benefit from my experience with evidenced-based practices, including CBT, DBT, IFS, MI and Non-Violent Communication. Change, even from something harmful to something healthy, can be scary. This is where trust comes in; trust in yourself, and trust in me. Together we will cultivate, curiosity, discovery, healing, and beauty.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Seeking help is the first step of a courageous journey toward healing and self-discovery. I use the word courageous intentionally because I know that asking for help is hard, sharing your story with someone new is vulnerable, and change can be scary. But I can tell you from experience, my own and so many others, that it is worth the effort. You are worth the effort! Counseling is an investment you make in yourself, in your relationships and in your future. My career has taken a winding road through child rearing, art education, and fine art. I am returning to counseling with a deeper, broader base of knowledge and experience that will enrich my practice and your experience as a client.

name: Sarah Maddox
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Lover of all things beautiful & cozy. Fueled by podcasts & coffee. Walks & yoga are my jam. Midwestern roots, married w/ two kids & a pup.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is eclectic, relational & person-centered. Your values guide our work together. I utilize creativity, training, empathetic listening skills, supported by research to support your healing & growth. I have experience with diverse groups of women in different stages of life. I have a passion for helping women know themselves, their desires & achieve their goals. While I practice with a feminist lens, I’m open to all gender & sexual identities & find this lens offers space for a variety of experiences. Adolescence is a unique period of development that deserves respect & care. I offer a space where teens can process through the big world they’re taking on & utilize talk therapy & other creative means like art, music, & bibliotherapy. I use Attachment Theory with every client, especially couples. Whether it’s sex, communication, finances, parenting, or who’s loading the dishwasher wrong, I offer tools for couples to navigate the issues they’re facing.

My life has afforded me many opportunities to learn about transitions in various relationships, cross-country moves, and parenthood. Whatever transitions you may find yourself in, I am here to support you. I utilize Restoration Therapy as a framework for identifying pain and peace cycles that can be used to empower teens, adults, and couples of all kinds to live in congruence with their values.

name: Naomi Baker, LMFT
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Thoughtful, depth-oriented psychotherapy.
ideal_client: I seek to work with clients who recognize they have untapped potential within themselves but may feel they have lost their way due to trauma, life challenges, or faulty self-perception. These clients understand they have more to offer themselves and others but struggle to navigate the complexities of our current systems. My ideal client is ready to explore their inner world through depth psychotherapy and is committed to personal growth and healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My intention is to create a collaborative, safe and empathic space to explore thoughts, feelings, musings, dreams and behaviors to promote change and healing. I believe that we all have the capacity to repair, grow, and transform our human experiences.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a neurodivergent, wounded healer with a love for writing, stories of all kinds, and walking. I am also a single cat lady and have an interest in web design and coding. I deepen my feminism, antiracism, understanding of the human condition, and insights into the evolution of our species through my work with diverse clients. I am consistently impressed by the strength and intelligence of people from all backgrounds and continually amazed by our resilience and capacity for growth and healing after trauma. In my opinion, post traumatic growth might include the wisdom we need to change the old western stories that have led to the planetary crisis we are currently facing.

name: Lindsay Bong, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Empathetic and experienced therapist specializing in trauma, anxiety, and depression using different modalities like Brainspotting and IFS.
ideal_client: In my practice, I specialize in guiding individuals who are navigating trauma, anxiety, and depression towards healing and resilience. I work best with those who are ready to explore their inner world, seeking to reclaim their narratives and cultivate inner strength. Whether you're facing past traumas or struggling with daily stressors, I provide a supportive and compassionate space for your journey towards holistic well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: For clients experiencing anxiety and depression, my goal is to help uncover areas of strength and employ those strengths to improve quality of life and relationships. Looking for patterns in our thoughts, behavior and our relationships gives us information on what works for us and what doesn’t. Practicing self compassion as we look through these sometimes painful past and current experiences leads to healing and confidence. Achieving a healthy self esteem is foundational in having the kind of relationships we are all craving. Mindfulness is a tool I employ often to help clients make connections with their thoughts and their behaviors and the world around them. I'm also trained in Brainspotting, a powerful tool that helps identify, process, and then release core neurophysiological sources of emotional/body pain, trauma, dissociation and other challenging symptoms. I believe that we all are worthy of healing and enjoying healthy relationships with themselves and others!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received a BA in Psychology at the University of Tulsa in 2002, followed by a Masters in Counseling from Dallas Theological Seminary in 2008. I am currently a licensed therapist with the Oregon Board of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists. Outside of my work, you can find me reading at least three books at the same time, making art and playing with my family and friends. As I encourage my clients to live wholeheartedly, I engage with what I believe in and am always learning more and practicing the arts of self compassion and growth.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: Brainspotting accesses the brain's healing mechanisms by identifying and processing trauma stored in subcortical regions. Its nonverbal approach is accessible to diverse clients, fostering self-awareness and emotional regulation. Clients experience profound shifts, empowering them to navigate life with resilience. As a therapist, Brainspotting enhances my ability to facilitate deep healing and transformation, empowering clients to reclaim agency and thrive.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Practicing knowing ourselves and being present with what we are encountering gives us incredible insight into who we are any why we function the way we do. By becoming mindful of who we are and what we are experiencing, we can gain more understanding of the power we have in our lives.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: IFS is a transformative therapy model empowering clients to explore their inner world with compassion. By understanding and integrating various parts of the self, clients heal trauma and foster resilience. As a therapist, IFS equips me with tools to guide clients through this process so they can better understand themselves and their relationships.

name: Melissa Tomecek
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome! I’m Melissa, and I’m so glad you’re here. I believe therapy should be a space where you feel heard, understood, and empowered.
ideal_client: My ideal client is someone who is curious about themselves, committed to personal growth, and values the therapeutic relationship as a key part of their healing journey. They may come to therapy feeling stuck, overwhelmed, or disconnected, but they have a deep desire to understand their emotions, patterns, and experiences on a deeper level. They are open to exploring both their past and present, recognizing that insight and awareness are powerful tools for change.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have a background in mental health counseling, working with individuals facing severe and persistent mental illness, depression, anxiety, attachment issues, and disordered eating. Over time, my focus has narrowed to complex trauma, helping clients navigate the deep, often unseen wounds that shape their emotions, relationships, and sense of self. I understand that trauma is not just about the events that happened but also about the way those experiences continue to live in the body and mind. My approach to therapy is integrative, relational, and deeply client-centered. I draw from psychodynamic therapy to explore unconscious patterns, humanistic therapy to foster self-acceptance, and Internal Family Systems (IFS) to help clients build a compassionate relationship with all parts of themselves. I also use EMDR to help process traumatic memories in a way that reduces their emotional intensity and promotes healing. Above all, I believe in the power of the therapeutic relationship.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a therapist because I believe in the power of understanding, connection, and healing. From an early age, I was drawn to the complexities of human emotions and the ways our past experiences shape who we are. I saw how unprocessed pain and trauma can impact every aspect of life, and I knew I wanted to help people find clarity, self-compassion, and growth. My passion for this work deepened as I witnessed how transformative the therapeutic process can be—how feeling truly seen and heard can open the door to profound change. I am especially drawn to working with complex trauma because I understand that healing is not just about coping but about reclaiming a sense of self that may have felt lost. Becoming a therapist was never just a career choice for me; it was a calling to create a space where people feel safe enough to explore, process, and ultimately find the strength to move forward.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing) is a psychotherapy that enables people to heal from the symptoms and emotional distress that are the result of disturbing life experiences. Repeated studies show that by using EMDR therapy people can experience the benefits of psychotherapy that once took years to make a difference. It is widely assumed that severe emotional pain requires a long time to heal. (https://www.emdr.com/what-is-emdr/)

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: IFS is a transformative tool that conceives of every human being as a system of protective and wounded inner parts led by a core Self. We believe the mind is naturally multiple and that is a good thing. Just like members of a family, inner parts are forced from their valuable states into extreme roles within us. Self is in everyone. It can’t be damaged. It knows how to heal. (https://ifs-institute.com/)

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Provided for individuals and couples therapy

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Complex-PTSD

name: Amie Christie
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am primarily a cognitive based counselor but I use many other theories and techniques to offer a unique and individualized experience.
ideal_client: I primarily work with adults age 18 years and older. My preferred client is anyone who needs assistance with their mental health or life situations and is ready to start the process of change. I most often assist with anxiety, OCD and thought disorders, depression, past traumas, life changes, emotional regulation, stress disorders and others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use a multimodal approach because everyone is unique and has their own backgrounds, history and experiences. My main methods are CBT, IFS, EFT, mindfulness, sensory based techniques, art therapy and talk therapy. Our first session will be discussing what you are experiencing, possible goals and building a personalized plan on helping you reach your goals. We will work at a pace that is comfortable for you in a safe, supportive, judgement and pressure free space.

name: Robin Carlisle
title: Professional Counselor
intro: Multidisciplinary guidance & support for those ready to recover a deep sense of safety and connection with themselves and others. ​
ideal_client: You are ready to show up as yourself. Through vulnerability & courage you are finally able to meet yourself, whole. To love, validate and accept yourself, not for who you wish to become, but for who you are already are. Complex and complete. Whatever state you may currently be in, you have a right to safety, security & witnessing. You are worthy of your experience. It is important that you are known. It is my honer to be see you and reflect your story back to you in a deep and powerful way.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a result of seeking comes illumination. Both the bright and the shadow parts of your being come clearly into your awareness. But fear not, oh capable one, You will never be alone in this work. It is with my strong intuition, great admiration and total belief in your natural abilities, that you are shepherded with unwavering confidence and impeccable care through this powerful work. It is through kindness, compassion and an open curiosity that we able to heed the call of your heart and respond in a way that is in your highest benefit. It is my belief that you have the answers you need. It is my honor to help you find them!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: 20 plus years in counseling. Certified Consulting Hypnotist, National Hypnotist Guild, 2020. Northwest Hypnosis Institute - Portland Oregon, 2019. MHAP Multidisciplinary Healing Arts Practitioner. Year long Intensive Study under the instruction of Dr. Mindy Nettifee, Doctor of Depth Psychology, with an emphasis in Somatic studies - Individual instruction in the areas of: Eco-Psychology, Somatic Practices, Depth Psychology, Jungian Philosophy, Dream Analysis, Archetypal Studies, Shamanic Rites and Ritual, Extensive exploration in cultivating my personal healing gifts - Heart Medicine, 2018. CBTP, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Practitioner Certification, Institute of Achology, 2016. HMC, HeartMath Facilitator Certification, HeartMath Institute, 2014. Adolescent Treatment Substance Abuse Counselor, 1999-2001. Alcohol, Tobacco, and Other Drug Health Educator, 1997-1999.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: To make meaning is human. Like monkeys are the funny ones and birds are the flyers, we are the storyteller. The stories you tell about yourself and others, about the world around you, create the narrative of your life. So what then if some aspect of your life is not working? You tell a different story. I will help you. And whats better? You will come to believe it!

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Many troubles come from rumination on the past, or our worry about the future-- trying to make sense of the old or prepare for the unknown. We do this all in an attempt to be happy, to enjoy life, to experience freedom, yet where is that joyful life that we seek? It is here, right now, available in the present moment. I can help you access the now and enjoy a state of balance and peace.

specialities.name: Hypnotherapy
specialities.description: Hypnosis gets you beyond stories of stuck-ness and delivers you to an inner space of resource. The subconscious speaks in metaphor and symbols in order shift your perspective and find new approaches to over-coming old problems. The psyche only ever intends to keep you safe and comfortable. Hypnotherapy is direct access to your wisdom and intuition--it is my honor to guide you on this journey!

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Self-esteem is one of the easiest issues to address through hypnosis. Because it is a fundamental and universal imperative that you love yourself, it's required for survival. Self-esteem tends to be at the core of whatever issue you are struggling with. Once we address the core (self-worth), the crust (problematic thoughts and behaviors) tends to fall away.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Everything in our lives has to do with relationships, or, how we relate. Whether it be to ourselves or others this is our primary lens in viewing the world. Our strongest held patterns are shown to us through intimate relationships. When we experience disruption in our relationships we are given profound opportunities to heal our deepest wounds.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a form of habituated negative looping. Hypnosis interrupts the momentum that has been driving the force behind those troubling thoughts and trains the brain to STOP and redirects the thought process towards beneficial patterns of thinking, eventually replacing the old anxiety with new healthy, productive frames of interpretation, resulting in a rich and fulfilling life experience!

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can feel like a slippery slope, and one that is hard to get out of because it attacks your motivation and your will, rendering you in a very low vibration, a bottom state some would say, but if you are here you are capable of elevation, if you are seeking help I am here to assure you there is hope, and hypnotherapy can and has shown effective and immediate felt relief.

name: Alphonso Nunez
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: Oregon Board of Licensed Professional Counselors Approved Supervisor Candidate
intro: I am accepting new clients for telehealth sessions. I am also accepting new supervisees, both LPC and LMFT Associates.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is one that is client-centered and collaborative. While I am versed in many modalities of MFT treatments, I primarily work from a background that leans heavily into Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), as well as Humanistic-Existential Therapy techniques. My perspective is that humans are inherently relational beings and those relationships are ultimately maintained or dissolved by underlying emotional inner-workings. In our time together, we will work to name those emotions and identify what those emotions are attempting to direct us towards. As your therapist, it's my priority to co-create a space with my clients that is affirming, inclusive, safe and supportive.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a strong background in working with issues around intimacy and sexuality both with individuals and couples. I also work with members of oppressed populations to navigate a number of issues they may experience as a result of systemic marginalization. This work is always done with an emphasis on social justice and empowerment in a collaborative manner. I believe that therapy is a delicate contract between myself and my clients and one that takes time and trust to fully realize the potential and power of change. At its fullest potential, therapy can be a celebration of the ways in which we are all different while appreciating how we're all connected.

name: Stacey Vallas
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: MS in Mental Health Counseling; PhD in English and American Literature
intro: I'll meet you where you are with openness, warmth, curiosity, and humor. I look forward to working together with you!
ideal_client: I counsel individuals and couples with diverse backgrounds and experiences seeking support with a range of issues, including life transitions, anxiety, depression, grief and loss, trauma, relationship problems, and generally feeling stuck or lost. I have worked on a crisis line, in a community counseling center, and in a university counseling center. My practice integrates psychodynamic, emotion-focused, and existential therapies, and I tailor my approach to best meet your needs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe each of us is drawn toward fulfilling connections with others and with our most life-affirming self, that inner voice that guides us toward what we truly feel and what most deeply matters to us. Sometimes, though, because of hurtful relationships past or present, self-doubt, loss, trauma, or life transitions, we lose touch with that inner wisdom. We feel lost or empty, or get stuck in anxiety, anger, confusion, or low self-esteem, and need support hearing and trusting that inner voice again. Too often we hide from our pain or try to tough it out alone. That you are here means you are open to trying a different path. I am mindful of how I bring my privileged and marginalized identities into our work together. I value collaborating to create a therapeutic alliance in which clients feel safe and honored exploring all dimensions of their identities. I love the work of therapy--helping others connect with a deeper sense of themselves and create more balanced, joyful lives.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor Intern and a Nationally Certified Counselor. I received my Masters in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Portland State University and also hold a PhD in English and American Literature from Stanford University. Before becoming a counselor, I taught literature and humanities to college students for many years. I’ve always been drawn to the transformative power of stories to illuminate our deepest selves and our links to each other, to history, and to community.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I believe relationships, including one's relationship to oneself, are the foundation of mental health and well being. I will support you in exploring the ways your past relationships have shaped your sense of self and how you relate to others now. I value creating a strong, collaborative relationship that fosters fresh perspectives, exploration, healing, and growth.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotions can illuminate our genuine needs and guide us in fulfilling them. But when our feelings aren't recognized and valued, we learn to respond to life with patterns of emotion that undermine our well being and even mask what we authentically feel. I will support your experiencing and working through of your own emotional patterns to gain clarity about your authentic feelings and needs.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Problems with self-esteem touch many people and are at the root of many mental health problems, such as depression and anxiety. I believe strengthening self-esteem is at the heart of successful therapy. I will get to know you without judgment and help you cultivate a more compassionate relationship with yourself so you are empowered to act on your strengths and make the changes you want in life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have experience working with clients struggling with various kinds of anxiety, such as anxiety concerning self-worth, relationships, socializing, performance, health and aging. I can support you in understanding the roots of your anxiety as well as present triggers and skills to manage and lighten anxiety that is getting in the way of your living more fully and joyfully.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Everyone feels sad or hopeless at times, but when you're depressed it can feel like change and well being are impossible. I am trained in how to diagnose and treat various kinds of depression, some caused by specific events or life changes, others more long-term and deeply rooted. I have experience supporting and empowering clients find new ways of both relieving and managing their depression.

specialities.name: Suicidal Ideation
specialities.description: Thoughts of suicide are common and are usually signposts to a person's unmet needs for connection and meaning. Often these thoughts and feelings come from past hurt or trauma. As a crisis line volunteer and a therapist, l have extensive trauma-informed training and experience in suicide intervention and helping people better understand and heal the suffering at the core of suicidal thoughts.

name: Matthew Geraths
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: "We all have a hungry heart, and one of the things we hunger for is happiness.” - Mary. OliverI

approaches.My Background and Approach: I use a combination of Narrative Therapy, Emotionally Focused Therapy, and a Systems approach. My speciality is sexualities, gender, and relationship therapy

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have worked in the field of gender, sexualities, and identity for the last 12 years. I split my time between teaching at a local university and counseling. As a therapist, I have a strong specialization in sexual intimacy/trauma work, couples/family therapy, as well as grief therapy.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I help individuals and couples explore what relationship dynamics are right for them. Monogamy is never a given and can sometimes be destructive to the well being of those trying to force themselves into it.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I major component of my work is helping male identified folk cultivate a masculinity that does not incorporate toxic elements such as misogyny, violence or isolation

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: My practice is queer inclusive and my therapeutic approach incorporates queer theory/activism.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I work with couples and individuals experiencing a wide range of sexual issues such as mismatched libidos, porn addiction or interest in exploring new sexual communities such as kink/BDSM.

name: Nicole McDonald
title: Professional Counselor
intro: I believe that because you exist, you belong. I help my clients feel held, safe, and spacious to explore.
ideal_client: The world can really make you feel like there’s something wrong with you or that you don't fit in. This can be especially true for anyone that has felt marginalized in some way, whether that's because of your sexuality, gender, class, race, neurodivergence or because you've taken a non-traditional path in life. I love helping people who have felt marginalized find a sense of belonging both inside and outside.

approaches.How I Can Help You: My approach to counseling is relational, client centered and non-judgmental. I can be with you in hard things, offer my presence, and be an active listener and thoughtful questioner. I’m invested in building a trusting relationship with you and helping you to explore.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I was born and raised in Utah and coming out as a queer person surrounded by Mormon culture I often felt repressed and like I didn’t belong. Because of my queerness, introversion, and depression, I felt I could never be accepted as I was. However, through therapy, finding queer community, and the growth and connection that I experienced in school, I found that there was a place I belonged and a place where I could be known. I know the difference it has made in my life to have compassionate and supportive mentors and counselors and I'm honored to have the opportunity to now be in that role for others who need support.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I will help bring awareness to your process so you can become more present and integrated. Together we will work on acknowledging and accepting difficult emotions, thoughts and states of being. I will help you to notice what’s going on in the present moment and in your body so you can feel more whole. I will hold you with care and help you find self compassion.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: One important component of growth can be having an outside witness to help hold your awareness, track your progress, and encourage you along the way. I'm honored to witness my client's growth and be a part of their process. Together we might explore different modalities which can lead to personal growth, such as dreams, meditation, archetypes, enneagram type, and somatic exploration.

name: Jamie Friedman
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I support my clients to find safety, rest, and joy within themselves, often in the midst of very challenging circumstances.
ideal_client: I work with folks healing from trauma – childhood, religious, sexual, and relational traumas – those exploring their authentic identities, and those who want support in life transitions large and small. I believe that you are the expert of your own experience. Together we will create a space where you can explore deeper layers of your experience, to understand, and potentially reframe, strategies that no longer serve you, and to take steps towards a richer connection with yourself and others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I help clients using a variety of approaches rooted in emotion, compassion, and curiosity. Emotion Focused Therapy and Internal Family Systems are two modalities that can help you understand, honor, process your internal experiences. I have also received training in interventions (Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy, Neuroaffective Relational Model) that work in present time to support and repair traumatic experiences, explore identity, and strengthen resiliency. Mindfulness and body awareness may also show up in session to release trauma held there and to ground your experience.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I treat adult individuals and couples with an emphasis on LGBTQ+ experiences, ethical separation, divorce and co-parenting, life transitions, religious exploration, grieving, and discernment, family estrangement, moral injury, reconnecting with your body, racial and racialized experiences, misattributed parentage, as well as depression and anxiety issues. Whether you’ve had many counseling experiences, or this is your very first, I look forward to learning about who you are and where you want to go on your path towards healing.

name: Travis Wright
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Want to find more wonder and joy in life? So do I. Perhaps we can figure this out together.
ideal_client: I have spent a considerable amount of time working with veterans and their families. I have also worked with first responders and those in the helping professions. I have found that folks overcoming some of life’s biggest hurdles just need some time and space to figure it out. I believe that each human being has great potential. Given time and space, most people can explore their past to see how it informs the present. Change is the only real constant we can rely on.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I’m a veteran, and have 20 plus years experience as a therapist with the Department of Veterans Affairs / Vet Center. My work with minority veterans during my time at the Vet Center/VA has given me some small glimpse into the systemic racism of our country and its history. My approach is trauma informed, with extensive training and experience in transpersonal and existential perspectives. Mostly I believe that the awe and wonder of life can be overshadowed with the darkness from our past or the anxiety with our future. Purpose and meaning are a big part of what I am interested in. Particularly through the lens of humor and wonder at our existence. The idea that we could learn to be more comfortable in our own skin underlies much of the work in therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been married for 30 years and have two teenage sons. I have lived in Oregon for the last twenty five years or so and I am in love with the rain and awesome craft beer. I don’t take myself very seriously and find happiness in the small things in life. I am curious about the world and our existence and enjoy reveling in it whenever it presents itself. Nature and relationships are a big deal to me and I’m kind of dork since I read science fiction and fantasy books a lot. I also have too much vinyl and keep telling myself not to go into the record shops.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: My work with trauma survivors has led me to develop and connect with other existential therapists in the community. This perspective addresses some of the deeper questions of purpose and meaning associated with suffering. The intent is not to fix but to learn to become more of yourself within the context of our existential struggles as a human being. To be more in tune with who we are, life can have more profound moments and more freedom.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I believe that each human being has great potential. Given time and space, most people can explore their past to see how it informs the present. Change is a function of time and the more we know about ourselves the larger the role we play to enact change. My goal has always been to come together with people to help them feel less alone and more connected to the world.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: The connections between each other is the way that we define ourselves. There is an old Spanish proverb that says "tell me who you walk with and I'll tell you who you are." To explore and articulate our relationships can have a very profound effect on how we experience this life. People are genuinely happier when they feel deeply connected. This is at the core of therapy and being alive in the world.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: To have some deeper knowledge of our own family system can illuminate much of our habits and behaviors. This then gives us some space to begin to enact change with the people around us. Our own family system is some of the deepest parts of our experience in this life and having some knowledge about it can be liberating. Of course, this kind of work is not so easily explored since much of life's pain comes from our childhood.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I am not sure there are many people nowadays who do not feel some measure of anxiety. In fact, I would like to think that this might be the appropriate response to the world we live in. That being said I think that anxiety can be all consuming and in this respect becomes dysfunctional. The question then becomes how do we mitigate the anxiety of our lives in way that does not avoid necessarily but invigorates us as a call to action.

specialities.name: Veterans/Military Service
specialities.description: My work with veterans spans the last twenty years and I have had the privilege to work with veterans from WWII to the present. I also saw veterans who experienced military sexual trauma. As the director of the Portland Vet Center I facilitated numerous Combat Focus Groups including the African-American Combat Focus Group. I have also worked with family members of sailors and soldiers who were killed on active duty providing bereavement counseling as well.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: Over the last two decades I have worked with combat veterans, veterans who experienced sexual trauma, and family members whose loved ones died in service. Much of this work was in and around trauma and traumatic loss/grief. I have found that most people experience trauma at one point or another in their lives. In fact, people often experience much more trauma than is ever revealed and yet seem to be able to function.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I have worked with men over the years in most of stages of their development. With this work I find exploring cultural and social perspectives along with the pressures of being male very helpful. Exploring male roles and finding deeper connections to who you really are is a core of the work that I focus on. Because of my humanistic and existential perspective exploring "what is a man" can be quite interesting and illuminating as well.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I believe that most of us carry around quite a bit of unexplored grief and loss. Our culture is not very good at allowing these feelings to be present. If you are alive then you will experience grief and loss. By having the time, space, and permission to explore these feelings this then frees us up to the larger experience of being alive.

name: Jess Fox
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I’m excited you’re here! I love supporting both individuals & couples/partners towards their individual, relational, or sexual goals.
ideal_client: I’m experienced working with clients who are queer, gender expansive, kinky, non-monogamous, fat/bigger bodied, and BIPOC. I tend to support those who want to address sexual concerns, improve their relationship(s), explore non-monogamy, process racial trauma & racial identity, and/or work through relational trauma. I want to support you in having space to feel the hard emotions, better understand your needs, and build supportive relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach therapy holistically & aim to help you connect with your body and emotions so that you can feel more at ease. I will highlight your strengths and inner resources that can help you thrive, while also gently challenging you when you’re stuck in unhelpful patterns. I will work to center your needs, capacity, and feedback so that therapy feels supportive to you. My goal in therapy is to help you access a space of authenticity and connection to yourself, your partner(s), and your communities. I work from an ecosystemic and relational lens; this means that I acknowledge the ways we are in connection with each other and the spaces we occupy, knowing our daily life can be impacted by larger systems such as capitalism and white supremacy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I felt inspired to do this work because of my lived experience. I identify as a bi-racial (Mexican American), second generation, Latinx, queer, gender fluid, kinky person who currently exists in a mid-size body. While these identities are a just fraction of who I am, it’s important to me to share them because they have shaped how I navigate the world. As a person with intersectional identities, I have experienced having to hide parts of myself in order to survive. I have also been in spaces with people who embraced me and made me feel cared for, loved, and able to be true to my authentic self. Because of these experiences, I approach therapy as a way to meet people where they are in their lives and work together collaboratively, so people can live as their most authentic selves. Life can bring us uncertainty and challenges; as a therapist, I believe people deserve to express themselves and be heard in an open, curious, and non-judgmental space.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I love working with couples & partnerships! Relationships are such a central part of our lives as humans. When we're experiencing relationship challenges, it can cause so much distress. My hope is to help you & your partner(s) have a more fulfilling & authentic relationship. Whether you want to explore communication challenges, opening up a relationship or navigating non-monogamy, sexual concerns in your relationship, the impacts of trauma, or mixed race relationship dynamics, I'm here for you!

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: Many people struggle with something related to sexuality, but don't have anywhere to get support around these concerns. You deserve a space where talking about your sexuality and sexual concerns is welcome! I'm here to help you with sexual concerns like mismatched desire in your relationship, sexual trauma, low sexual desire, sexual identity exploration, kink exploration, or sexual anxiety. I bring a warm, informed, and sex positive presence to these conversations.

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: As a bi-racial (Mexican American), second generation, & Latinx person, I understand how complex & nuanced racial identity can be. I'd love to support you in exploring your racial identity, processing the impacts of systemic racial oppression, working through inter-generational trauma, or mixed race relationship dynamics.

name: Michelle Shelton
title: Marriage and Family Therapist
intro: I am a licensed Marriage & Family Therapist in the State of Oregon and would welcome the opportunity to work with you.
ideal_client: It is more important than ever to consider your mental health needs. I have over 10 years experience working in mental health as a therapist, leader, advocate, educator, and researcher. I would love the opportunity to partner with you on your mental health and well-being needs. I am passionate about finding ways to work with individuals, families, teens, and adults in order to have their lives be more fulfilling, productive, motivated, and healthy.
