specialities.description: ◦ Attachment repair: Family of origin traumas, reparenting, addiction issues ◦ Gender & sexuality: coming out, Intimacy & sex; mind-body connection; somatic experiences in intimacy ◦ Relationship transformations: Feelings of stuckness or staleness; boredom; liberatory approaches to relationship ◦ Mindful Matrimony: Premarital counseling; wedding worries/family blending; separation & divorce. ◦ Navigations of non-monogamy: opening up; navigating boundaries; kink dynamics; sex work

name: Graham Borgman
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a depth and relationally-oriented psychotherapist in private practice. I am an LPC in Oregon.

approaches.My Background: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor and hold a Master's degree in counseling psychology with an emphasis in depth psychology from Pacifica Graduate Institute. Prior to my current independent practice, I worked as a therapist in a group practice, provided psychotherapy to adults in a community mental health center, and also have professional experience working as a counselor in a semi-residential psychiatric program for adults.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I work well with individuals who are curious about their own minds and emotions. Individuals who can benefit from working with me are those who wish to understand and move through their suffering, as well as to enjoy the vitality that the healing process can bring. Reasons for seeking therapy which I work well with include: Anxiety & stress, depression, grief, relationship issues, existential concerns, difficulty with self-expression, feelings of guilt & shame, self criticism & self-esteem issues, anger issues, life transitions, many more: just ask!

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: Depth therapy refers to an approach to the human psyche that acknowledges the activity of the unconscious in life. 'Unconscious' is simply a scientific term that designates something as unknown. Curiosity about the unknown dynamics and structures upon which our consciousness is based is necessary for the therapist as well as for the patient of depth-oriented therapy.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I include the relational orientation to communicate the fact that as a therapist I participate fully in the therapeutic process. The relationship between therapist and patient is the single most important factor for the effectiveness of psychotherapy.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: A response to the social, political, and religious fragmentation that occurred in Europe in the last century, existential philosophy forms the basis for an existential-oriented therapy. The seemingly meaningless and random nature of existence and the emotional turbulence that accompanies it are collective human issues which, when embraced fully, can yield unexpected joy and vitality.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Personal growth is a term that encompasses something unique for every person. A fundamental assumption of depth psychology is that the psyche tends toward expression and vitality throughout the life-span, and coming to therapy for something along the lines of 'personal growth' may be a good sign that a part of your personality is ready to be lived more fully.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: The rites of passage which have existed in nearly every culture across time and place and function to provide the male-identified person with a coherent understanding of how to organize one's life have all but vanished for many of us. An impoverished mythology of heroic economic achievement has come to fill this void, providing many with a vague emotional undercurrent of longing and frustration.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Our internal and external sources of praise and criticism form complex networks of motivations and self-evaluations. It is a difficult task for many to locate and feel the realistic, innate sources of self-esteem that constitute who you are, buoy your spirits, and provide you with energy for your work and relationships. Self-esteem issues are common and important components of therapy for many.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: The contributing factors to depression are as vast and varied as the individuals who carry it. Whether it is persistent and severe or infrequent and mild, depression is a psychological state that holds many within its grasp. Depression can open us to seeing difficult truths, and can also blind us from seeing others. Navigating depression with another human being, rather than alone, is crucial.

name: Laura Gordon
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I offer a warm and down to earth approach to exploring and navigating the parts of you and your life that feel out of alignment.
ideal_client: I work with children, teens, and adults who are navigating a wide range of experiences including depression, anxiety, life transitions, grief, trauma, identity exploration, and relationship challenges, I value and deeply respect the complexity and unique experiences, identities, and stories each client brings. You might be seeking therapy for the first time or returning to expand your self-understanding- either way I strive to create a safe and supportive space to create a path to healing.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a Clinical Social Work Associate (CSWA) and Licensed School Social Worker in the state or Oregon. I graduated with my MSW from Portland State University. My experience spans a variety of settings, including residential treatment for high-acuity clients, therapeutic and public schools, and specialized case management for unaccompanied minors released through the Office of Refugee Resettlement. My approach to therapy is one of warmth, respect, creativity, and humor when appropriate (life is very long if you cannot laugh at the absurdity of it.) I work from a framework that is client-centered, humanistic, and utilizes Queer and intersectional feminist theories. I believe each individual has their own unique experience of the world that is shaped by the intersection of their identities, their past experiences, and the communities they are a part of. You are the expert on your life, and my intention is to understand your experience so that we can collaborate towards your goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that healing occurs in relationships, therefore, I am not a "blank slate" therapist. This means I will show up authentically- my identities, experience, knowledge, and lack thereof (I am happy to admit I don't know everything!) will also be in the room with us. You are the focus of our sessions together, but in embracing my own human-ness, my goal is to create a safe space for you to do the same.

name: Gemma Baumer
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: Licensed Professional Counselor, M.A. in Counseling
intro: I am passionate about supporting my clients on their journeys--I specialize in complex trauma, attachment wounds, and connection to oneself.
ideal_client: Complex/relational trauma and wounding can be hard to grasp, showing up as anxiety in our bodies, emotions, relationships, expectations for the world and others, and in relationship to ourselves. I specialize in attachment trauma/wounding and sexuality. I also love working with poly folks, queer folks, and really anyone desirous of more freedom, vitality, meaning, connection, communication & those seeking support in defining their own path in relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our earliest experiences formed our nervous systems. We adapted to situations outside of ourselves to meet our inherent need for connection, often before we were even conscious. There is good reason for why we do what we do! Most importantly, we get to continuously reorganize and redefine our experience, and find more connection to ourselves and others. I practice from an Existential-Humanistic framework in which I view building a genuine therapeutic relationship as essential. From this place, I walk beside my clients in their journey of integrating and exploring all aspects of experience--psychological, interpersonal, and emotional. In attuning to our inner experience--needs, boundaries and desires, we are able to connect more to life itself, creating more freedom around how we want to live. Starting therapy with a new therapist can feel vulnerable. I will do my best to honor the inherent bravery it takes to engage in these ways.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I hold a Bachelor's degree in Psychology and a Master's in Mental Health Counseling from Lewis & Clark College. I worked with Philip Zimbardo on curriculum for promoting a Growth Mindset. I completed my internship at the Mindful Experiential Therapy Counseling Center (M.E.T.A.), where I received training in the Hakomi Method and Body-Centered awareness. I currently serve on the board of Existential Humanist NW, where I curate the blog. I became a therapist because I am inspired by the way we humans make meaning of and transform our experiences. I too have benefited from the non-judgmental and embracing space of a good therapeutic relationship in which to explore my own being, and I feel passionate about holding this space for my clients. Because I believe therapy has so much to do with cultivating a genuine connection, and feeling free to show up as oneself, I encourage you to trust your intuition. If you think we might be a good fit, feel free to reach out for a free consultation!

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: Existential Therapy is an orientation to the existential dimensions of life. There are certain givens with this--we all will die, we all will face suffering, and we live with certain limitations. Yet in spite of these limitations, existential therapy holds that we can move beyond despair and anxiety to access the most freedom when we attend to our deepest, core selves, and work to integrate the levels of our experience and find what is most authentic to us.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Humanistic Therapy is person-centered, meaning you are the expert on your experience. It holds the inherent growth potential in each of us, and is influenced by positive psychology, looking not at pathology and what's "wrong" with us, but instead our inherent need for meaning, expansion, and connection. Humanistic therapy emphasizes a strong and connected therapeutic alliance that feels genuine and flexible. Rather than a treatment, humanistic therapy is about a journey.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: As infants and children, we are completely dependent on our caregivers for survival. This need for attachment is innate within us, and forms an intense drive for love and belonging. When these needs are not easily met by caregivers, we make adaptations and accommodations. These show up as different patterns of attachment, which can stick with us into adulthood. Attachment work includes working with these patterns and exploring how we show up in relationship with ourselves and others.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness-based therapy interventions emphasize the here and now. This means acknowledging that we hold onto all of our experiences on a physical and energetic level--they show up in the form of thoughts, assumptions, and physical sensations. Utilizing mindfulness in therapy means taking into account the body, research into the nervous system, and pausing to examine what is showing up right now, and exploring how it connects to whatever we are bringing into the therapy space.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: My approach to couples/relationship counseling is interactive, relational, strength-based and informed by attachment. I work with relationships of all configurations to support a space that is safe for exploration of self and another, historical and current attachment processes. I love working with relationships in need of immediate support, or just desirous of exploration around subjects like trauma, attachment, polyamory/consensual non-monogamy and boundaries.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: PTSD refers to a cluster of symptoms that occur on all levels of experience, and reflect an activated nervous system and a sense of uneasiness and discomfort in our bodies and worlds. We may or may not why this is, but over time, we can begin to access more safety and embodiment. Sometimes this means processing and working through traumatic experiences, and in other cases, it is in learning to care for ourselves in service to releasing patterns of chronic dissociation and alertness.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is our body's way of alerting us that something needs our attention--perhaps we are not living in accordance with our deepest selves, we cannot reconcile our life with what we truly want, or that we hold onto the impact of living with hypervigilence and disconnection. We can address the underlying concerns of anxiety in a therapeutic space that feels warm, safe, and exploratory, and seek to resolve what our anxiety can tell us about our experience of being alive.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: There is no guidebook for being in relationship. We are often confused by the culture we live in which promotes the romanticization of beginnings, and the notion that another could meet our every need. This can be a recipe for disappointment, because relationships take continuous work and tending. Relationships are deeply activating for us as humans because our most formative experiences occurred in our attachment relationships, where we were intrinsically motivated to meet our needs to survive.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: There is no right way to be in relationship. We may be balancing the tension between a desire for freedom, with a craving for novelty. I believe we can feel most empowered and connected to our deepest selves and can define relationship for ourselves, whatever those configurations and boundaries may look like. There is no solution but the one that is best for you. I love working with intimate partners in defining and exploring what relationship means to them and supporting their choices.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I am passionate about working with people with queer identities. I, myself, hold a queer identity as well, and I value being there for others and aim to create a safe space in which to explore all facets of life.

name: Peter Ragen
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I specialize in helping adults and teens heal and grow with evidence-based therapeutic approaches for whatever they may be experiencing.
ideal_client: Are you or a loved one feeling overwhelmed by anxiety, depression, addiction, ADHD, or low self-esteem? As we walk through life, we are bound to struggle in one way or another. Sometimes, when the struggle feels overwhelming, we can look outside of ourselves for a helping hand. Together, we will explore your feelings, build resilience, and develop strategies to improve your well-being. You will build skills and develop a greater level of awareness that will empower you to achieve your goals.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that participating in therapy is collaborating in a safe and accepting space where you can learn practical skills that facilitate meaningful, long-lasting positive change in yourself and your relationships. I believe that it is through a process of self-discovery and practice that we are able to empower ourselves to skillfully make choices that lead us toward our goals. Through a greater awareness of ourselves and how we relate to the world, we can begin to make small but impactful changes that compound over time. I practice from an integrated lens, meaning I pull from multiple therapeutic approaches to best address your particular therapeutic needs. As someone who has grappled with my own mental health struggles, I know that change is possible but not always easy. I also know that when we take responsibility, hold ourselves accountable, and do the good work, we can achieve our goals. If you or a loved one are ready to begin this journey, reach out!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My fiance and I are Oregon natives, and we live in Portland with our two dogs. When I’m not in session, I enjoy spending time with my significant other, exploring the city’s rich foodie culture, walking our dogs, and skiing.

name: Roxanne Ahmadpour
title: Somatic Practitioner
intro: I am a Naturopathic doctor with specialized training in somatics, mindfulness based counseling, and bodywork.
ideal_client: I work with folks who wish to feel more present in their lives, within themselves, and in relationships. My clients desire a deeper connection to their body and their internal world, and wish to grow beyond historical, systemic, cultural, and intergenerational patterns that leave them feeling stuck and unfulfilled. My clients are interested in working mindfully, somatically, and relationally.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a licensed Naturopathic doctor with a Masters degree in Integrative Mental Health and advanced training in somatic therapies. My approach is rooted in Hakomi mindfulness centered somatic psychotherapy, and informed by Attachment theory, 'parts work', yoga therapy, and polyvagal theory. The container of my work is relational, based in the present moment, and embodied. I support folks in building a connection with the present moment, with their bodies, and with the resources that are available in the moment through mindfulness and embodiment practices. Together we slowly work to uncover rigid patterns of thinking and feeling, hidden and disowned parts of the self, and impulses and stories long held in the body. We hold this together with spaciousness and tenderness while offering an opportunity for new information and possibilities to come in and integrate. While this can be deep and powerful work, I aim to bring a sense of lightness, humor, and ease in to sessions.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Healing and growth is in our nature and is our birthright. Our personal healing is integral to collective healing. The ever present forces of colonialism, capitalism, and cis-white-hetero-patriarchy have impacted us all and have resulted in intergenerational trauma patterns that we carry in our bodies and act out unknowingly upon ourselves and others. I value moving beyond examining the personal and including layers of the interpersonal, the systemic, the cultural, and the historical contexts in which our behaviors and beliefs are rooted into my work with people. I deeply value our interconnectedness with nature, the environment, and world around us. I support my clients in connecting with their own nature, as well as the natural world around them, and to this end am excited to begin offering outdoor and 'walk and talk sessions'. My passion for this work is rooted in the promise that as we all heal and grow, so do our relationships, communities, society, and our planet.

name: Lillian Dunham
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
credentials: MA MCFT from Lewis & Clark College
intro: I work with individuals and couples who are struggling with disconnection and burnout. I give you tools to experience healing and growth.
ideal_client: Are struggling with burnout and disconnection in your work and relationships? Maybe you have had a major life change and are having difficulty adjusting. Are you experiencing anxiety and depression and searching for help in making positive sustainable change? I use empathy, humility, and a humor to create the time and space you need to have healing experiences.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work with individuals, couples, and families from the belief that humans are all inherently good and we are all capable of positive change. The joys and struggles of our lives are relational. I came to this work through personal experience as a partner, mother, co-parent, daughter, creator, and employee. My philosophy is grounded in discovering and understanding our context in the systems we participate in, from our most intimate relationships to our locations in greater society. Illuminating unspoken cultural narratives and finding words for the oppressed, forgotten, and shamed can heal ourselves and society. I use empathy, curiosity, and humility and humor in dialogue to help clients imagine and practice authentic and more fulfilling ways of relating to themselves and others. I am trained in Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), which draws from attachment theory. I also use techniques from Internal Family Systems (IFS) to help individuals communicate within themselves.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in supporting our communities with our special strengths. I volunteer at the Dougy Center for Grieving Children and Families. I believe meaningful intimate relationships can take many different forms. I have been active in the polyamory/ethical-non-monogamy and kink communities.

name: Meghan Opbroek, MS
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello and Welcome! My name is Meghan Opbroek (she/her). I am an LCP with the State of Oregon providing telehealth sessions.
ideal_client: I provide counseling and therapy for individuals seeking relief and freedom from problems related to things like trauma, anxiety, depression, and whatever else is getting in the way of you living the life you want.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My practice is inclusive and affirming. I’ve done my own work understanding both my privileged and marginalized identities and I’m dedicated to the continuous work involved in knowing one’s biases and beliefs. I’ve worked with folks from all backgrounds, abilities, and cultures. My practice is not tolerant, it’s affirming. Affirming of all relationship types, sexual orientations, religions, spiritual leanings, body types, kink leaning and lifestyles, races, ethnicity, cultures, gender representations and identities, ages, documentation statuses, socio-economic statuses, educational backgrounds, and more.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received my Master’s Degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Portland State University. If you’re into the technical stuff, my work is rooted in traditional and contemporary psychodynamic theory, specifically Attachment Theory and Object Relations Theory. If you aren’t into the technical stuff, I believe people become who they are in relation to and because of others and their experiences. Understanding who you are as a person, parent, child, friend, partner, or any other identity, is key to happiness and well-being. You’re going to continue to change and move forward in your life. We can work together to help that change be positive.

name: Lauren Hansen
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: MA in Mental Health Counseling, Certified Eating Disorder Specialist
intro: I believe that everyone has the wisdom inside of them to return to who they really are outside of who they were told they “should” be.
ideal_client: I work with individuals who have been trying to "get it together" and live up to impossible expectations. I've been there, and together we will work to let those expectations go. It’s possible to let go of all the expectations you put on yourself to live a full and authentic life. My clients tend to be those struggling with eating disorders/disordered eating/body image issues, are neurodivergent, and/or are a part of the lgbtq+ community. I work with adults and teens ages 16+.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We cannot shame ourselves into behavior change, and that's why I take a compassion-focused approach to everything I do. Self-compassion might be brand new to you, which is totally cool! It's a skill that might not feel natural at first, but eventually can become the default way you respond to yourself (and hopefully others as well). I believe your experience in therapy should be as unique as you are. I integrate many different modalities to fit your personality, goals, and preferences. Everything we do in therapy will be collaborative, as my goal is to reduce the inherent power dynamic that the therapeutic relationship can create. I want you to feel in charge of your healing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received my Masters of Mental Health Counseling from Lewis and Clark College and also work as an Intuitive Eating Coach. I operate from a Health at Every Size framework in my practice and take a strong stance against diet culture. When working with clients, I acknowledge the different systems of oppression that intersect and impact lives in ways that absolutely affect mental (and physical) health. I value showing up authentically, and will always show up as my full human self in session. If you're looking for a more formal therapist, maybe we won't be a good fit, and that's ok! I am a bit of an astrology nerd, and am always hooked on a new hyperfixation hobby! Always feel free to ask me about it.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I believe that everyone has the wisdom in them to recover and to live a full life. Our work together will revolve around guiding you back to the body trust you once had, so you can release any shame you may have around food, your body, and yourself. Together we will get to the root of and process the messages you learned about food and your body, unlearn the diet culture b.s, and create your unique path to healing.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Whether you have a diagnosis or not, living with ADHD or what you think might be ADHD can feel like everyone got the memo for "how to life" except you. As someone with ADHD, I know how hard it can be to navigate a world not set up for you. Without creating systems and tools to set you up for success, it can feel like you're always one, two, or three steps behind. You are not broken, and together we can create those systems so you can thrive.

name: Kristin Fialko
title: Marriage and Family Therapist
intro: Integrating body, spirit & ancestry—Somatic therapy weaving EMDR, spiritual healing & social justice to transform trauma at its roots.
ideal_client: I work with seekers—curious souls who feel the call to reconnect with their bodies and transform their stories. They seek not just relief, but liberation—nervous system regulation, ancestral healing, and a true sense of belonging. Together, we move toward embodied wholeness in a world that often encourages fragmentation. Specializing in chronic illness, neurodivergence, and the tender journeys of fertility and postpartum, I help guide clients toward deeper healing and self-discovery.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We often find ourselves—our bodies, our spirits—navigating the winding path back to health after overwhelming experiences: birth, chronic illness, trauma, grief, or profound loss. Reigniting our inner fire and returning to emotional equilibrium can feel elusive, yet deeply vital. As a somatic psychotherapist, I see my role not as a fixer, but as a sacred collaborator—walking alongside clients as they reconnect with the innate wisdom of their bodies and process the echoes of trauma, anxiety, depression, and grief. My approach weaves together Somatic techniques, EMDR, Parts Work, Transpersonal psychology, mindfulness, and energetic work. Grounded in a trauma-informed, anti-racist, and socially aware framework, I hold space for healing that honors the complex intersections of mind, body, spirit, and lineage. The body is a vessel of profound intelligence—emotional, spiritual, and ancestral—and I am here to help you listen, reclaim, and remember your inherent capacity to heal and thrive.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Rooted in creativity, sensitivity, and a deep reverence for healing, my work as a therapist is shaped by my lived experience as an artist, HSP, mother, chronic illness warrior, and activist. My path—from a childhood in rural PA to studying art in Baltimore, to reclaiming my body and voice in San Francisco—led me to somatic psychotherapy as both a personal and professional calling. I hold a MA in Somatic Psychology from California Institute of Integral Studies and have over a decade of experience working in private practice & community mental health. I move through the world with deep feeling, a vivid imagination, and a relentless curiosity about the human spirit. I am someone who values complexity, who listens closely to the spoken and unspoken, and who is always in process—learning, unlearning, and tending. My work is an extension of who I am: intuitive, grounded, creative, and committed to collective liberation.

name: colby schneider
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I am currently scheduling In Person & Telehealth sessions and look forward to helping those who are looking for positive support.
ideal_client: I help families, couples, and individuals understand the deeper meaning of what might be holding them back and how they can break free and reach their full potential. I work with folks experiences depression, anxiety, PTSD, relationship problems, attachment issues, and just overall trying to get through life the best we can.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer guidance and unconditional positive regard to help people understand themselves using Psychodynamic, Gestalt, Humanistic, and Trauma Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapies. Working together collaboratively but acknowledging that people are the experts of their own life, we will work together to end suffering while building self-growth. The last few years have caused us suffering and loss on a scale we have never experienced before. I am offering help to process these losses and create the tools needed to thrive and live life to its fullest once again. I'd truly appreciate the opportunity to work with you on your journey of healing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe everyone has the right to be happy and feel good about themselves regardless of what they have experienced in their own life. I feel that therapy should be something everyone experiences and uses at some point in their life to get that extra support. My hourly rates are typically $155-$185 for individuals and couples on a sliding scale and am happy to work around your budget and what is affordable and fair for you. I am an advocate for human and animal rights and have been a vegan for over 15 years. I feel that compassion for all living beings is essential and I use that as a guide in my professional and personal life.

name: Jessica Feinsmith MA LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We all have times when we feel buried beneath challenges of life and we need a caring, compassionate hand to help us through it.
ideal_client: I work with young adults who are ready to launch but feel lost, depressed, anxious, hopeless, alone. The world and its demands feel overwhelming. Perhaps social media has left you feeling more disconnected and comparing yourself to who you think you should be. You have dreams and desires but feel a loss of motivation and interest. There's an overall sense of “this is not where I want to be in life" but you don't know how to get moving. Childhood may be in the past but adulthood feels daunting.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We all seek meaning and purpose in life and I have found mine in supporting people on their journey. Whether you are looking for support for healing a specific mental health issue or you feel an overall sense of “this is not where I want to be in life,” I understand. By getting to know you and your history, and finding out what is stopping you from reaching the goals you have, we work together to unravel the past and the issues that are in your way of achieving the life you desire. I combine years worth of personal growth, world travels, graduate school and several prior careers to support and guide clients to achieve goals and live a fulfilling life. I utilize trainings in attachment theory, mindful self-compassion, solution-focused therapy, trauma-informed yoga therapy, and positive psychology in holistic and creative ways. I see clients in Oregon and accept OHP Reach out for a free consultation. I would be honored to meet with you and see if there is a fit.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I work with individuals over the age of 18 and my specialty is working with young adults. Prior to private practice, I was a college counselor. Combining my young energy with my life experience, I feel a deep connection with my clients. From supporting clients with adulting skills and responsibilities to relationship, dating and family issues to substance abuse and disordered eating behaviors. I've also worked extensively with depression and anxiety, especially during and after Covid. I support clients to practice self compassion as a form of self care. To learn to hear one's own voice and desires and define one's path forward. To heal attachment traumas, identify post traumtic growth and experience loving, authentic relationships. To create a trusting relationship together to support you on whatever healing journey you are on. I accept OHP Healthshare Care Oregon insurance and am OON with United Health.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: If it's a relationship issue, depression or anxiety, grief, or another of life’s many challenges, we all face times in our life where we feel overwhelmed and underneath the heaviness of life. Empathetic guidance and support can help us achieve our goals. I work with clients in an authentic and transparent manner, always applying my natural gifts of intuition, compassion and empathy.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I believe that to heal we must feel, and that can be very scary to do alone or with a stranger. If you struggle with insecurity within yourself and relationships, connecting and building a trusting relationship with a therapist will take time. I utilize attachment and bonding interventions to holistically develop a trusted relationship between myself and the client to create a secure attachment.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Combining therapeutic yoga and somatic awareness training, we work together to increase internal awareness, hearing the signals your body is communicating and unlearning patterns related to pain, fear and anxiety.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Whether you are looking for assistance and support for healing a specific mental health issue or trauma or you feel an overall sense of “this is not where I want to be in life,” mindful awareness and somatic-body interventions can be very beneficial. Using stress reducing meditations, increasing present awareness and self compassion and gentle care are all aspects of the work I utilize.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Having experienced depression since I was a teenager, I understand its challenges of shame, heaviness and isolation. Together, we will focus on developing self compassion and resilience, utilizing self awareness and mindfulness to better understand and explore limiting beliefs to decrease your experience of depression and self criticism. Depression is often a sign of anger turned inward. What are you holding in, holding back, needing to speak and process?

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: These are difficult, anxiety provoking times and we can all benefit from stress reduction, self compassion and self care. My approach to decreasing anxiety utilizes practical, everyday techniques to reduce the challenges of living with anxiety, panic and fears of the unknown and uncertain future. We will explore the upside of anxiety and decipher what it is saying to you.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: Growing up in “diet-Culture” can leave us feeling less than loving towards our bodies. I understand. Whether it is disordered eating behaviors, body dysmorphia or shame about yourself, I can offer support. Utilizing therapeutic interventions, increased mind and body awareness and self compassion, we can become allies of our bodies and selves and heal the hatred and shame of being imperfect.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: In life, we will experience some form of loss, whether the passing of a loved one, the end of a relationship or friendship, or the loss of hopes and dreams. I believe that an empathic, resilient, strengths-based approach will eventually result in your ability to discover your silver lining and deeper insight into yourself. Through therapeutic healing, you will develop inner wisdom unique to yourself. I'm also very empathetic of pet loss and grief.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Are you curious about yourself, your patterns, and your relationships? Are you struggling with a mental health issue or addiction that you might need some support in addressing? All humans are faced with problems and challenges in their lives and therapeutic connection and support is helpful for the life you desire.

name: Kristin Tand
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help high achieving women feel less overwhelmed and overworked in order to connect more authentically with themselves and those they love.
ideal_client: Are you awake again at 3 am? Can’t go back to sleep and just WISH you could turn your brain off? You’re thinking about tomorrow’s day full of meetings and also reviewing how yesterday went. Cringing about that off-handed comment you made to your co-worker that you're now second guessing… All this anxiety keeps you on edge, constantly thinking about the future while regretting the past. You just wish you could be more present in your life and enjoy more time with your partner and family.

approaches.How I Can Help You: First of all I SEE YOU. I totally get the stressed-out grind of the day-to-day. The good news is there is a path forward to settle your mind, nervous system and start being more grounded inside of the stress. Sessions with me uncover what's overwhelming you, increase your skills to manage stress and heal from old burdens that keep you stuck. Together, we'll create balance in your life. And we'll always go at your pace, never pushing to a place where you don’t feel ready.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe everyone has unique strengths that when realized, can create healing and lasting change from the inside out. Life is hard and our experiences over time can create burdens that don't always serve us. Through guidance, we all have the capacity to let go of these challenges and feel good about ourselves. I'm a therapist who walks my talk, having done (and continue to do) my own therapy to overcome past challenges and feel less anxious in my day to day life. I also believe dogs are magical creatures that were put on Earth to bring greater joy and happiness, but I am also accepting of cats and will never turn down a good cat video. I believe that all people deserve equal rights and that love is love. I am welcoming and accepting of all and make it a point to better understand my privilege and use my unearned power for good. I also engage in ongoing learning to strive toward dismantling the layers of racial injustice.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Internal Family Systems or IFS is a unique for of therapy that focuses on your internal "world" and how you interact with the different facets of yourself. It can be a helpful model to better understand patterns you find yourself in and how to change your inner landscape. I have completed Level 1 training through the IFS institute as well as participate in ongoing trainings, supervision, continuing education and practice. IFS is a wonderful therapy option to heal from the inside out.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can feel like it sneaks up on you. All of a sudden you're having racing thoughts that you can't quiet, feeling restless, difficulty sleeping and feeling jittery. I've worked with clients struggling with anxiety for over a decade and know many skills to help you manage anxiety and give you day-to-day relief. However, I also go further, helping you to uncover the underlying causes of your anxiety and heal from the issues from your past that may be coming to the surface.

name: karen myers
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi, I'm Karen Myers LCSW. I offer individual therapy and support to help end self sabotaging, patterns, beliefs and behaviors.
ideal_client: How long have you been reading self help books, attending course after course, maybe bouncing between therapists. And how much time/money have you spent with little to show for it. Some of the topics we may explore are: -How to get unstuck from feeling unworthy. -How to stop being held hostage by the past. -How belief creates your perception of reality. -How to let go of family or societal expectations. -True choices vs. ineffective choices. -Problem solving through life vs. thriving in life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Did you know that trauma effects 70% of the population? It's the silence and the shame that keeps us stuck or oscillating in all areas of life, including financially. Your bank account suffers as much as your mind or your body. Because by age 35 your decisions are a memorized set of patterns, beliefs and behaviors. So you keep doing the same thing over and over and over again. Year after year. Maybe a different context but the outcome is the same. It's exhausting. I bring my 35 years of training from EMDR, gestalt, NLP, Self psychology and a little known discovery called the window of consolidation. By incorporating the Window of Consolidation, learning theory and other therapeutic processes so you can finally release the resistance, the fear and the overwhelm. We start by training the brain to find and neutralize unconscious blocks and negative memories. This cutting edge method is validated by neuroscience.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I work with my clients in a fluid and dynamic partnership. We will begin where you are and work with techniques that you find useful to embark on a journey to where you want to be. We will work together to apply techniques that are effective for you. I will provide guidance and resources that can remove stumbling blocks to beneficial changes in your life. All change is a journey from an undesirable to a desired state – your outcome.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I've worked with diverse populations both foreign and domestic. I bring everything I have learned in the past 35 years into my sessions. I am level II EMDR trained (trained by Francine Shapiro PhD) During sessions we may use gestalt, NLP, Cognitive therapy, self psychology (trained by James Hollis PhD), intergenerational trauma and more. I am bilingual in English and Spanish.

name: Arrival Counseling annie dolle LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: If you are ready to heal I am ready to meet you exactly where you are. Together we can get to a place that feels better than OK.
ideal_client: Do you wonder why you can't relax and make peace with yourself and/or others? Do things from the past continue to haunt you and create turmoil in your life? Do you dredge up old stories and replay them over and over wondering what went wrong? Do you fight with yourself and wage inner war~ battling it out without conclusion? Do you question what is blocking you from vitality and playfulness? Do you seek meaning and fulfillment beyond the life that you are living? Lets open to something new.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I would like to know the world in which you live. It is only through careful tracking that we can find our way to what is ailing you. I will join you in this journey. It must be safe, accepting, warm, curious and natural. I am not the expert with the wand (unless doing EMDR;) but rather a fellow human working to find meaning, freedom and truth in this lifetime. I have lived, trained, read, meditated, and contemplated throughout my life/education/career to be a better and more skillful vessel for healing. This is both my interest and passion. Mental health issues are a natural response to trauma and a toxic culture and I understand. It is OK. We will find our way through and you are not alone.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a Peace Corps volunteer decades ago, I found my passion listening and learning from others. I saw first hand that much of what we know and believe comes from our unique families, culture and environment. I then began a career in social services drawn to unfair and painful aspects of our society. My work was very strength-based and problem focused. Always growing my capacity to listen with my heart, I developed greater internal space for truth, pain, and beauty. I shifted my focus from crisis response to curiosity, safety and compassion. Amazingly I found that this led to healing all on its own! I have worked with people of all identities and celebrate diversity. I even had the opportunity to work with a team providing mental health therapy to expats in HCMC Vietnam for five years. I listen with my mind, body, and spirit and know that if I track clients closely, they know what needs to happen. As a student of many modalities I know that I will never stop working to hone my craft.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: From family work (family crisis and adoptions) to the most vulnerable peoples (Emergency Department social work), I know that our attachment templates are primary to the way that we experience ourselves, our relationships, and our world. I keep this awareness close and utilize attachment theory in my work, always.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR trained, Im a believer. Let me offer this intervention to you. Let us soften your trauma response and heal your nervous system.

specialities.name: Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP)
specialities.description: A focus softening the conditioning of our attachment patterning and gently fostering a safe, more secure relational style to foster feeling and dealing in relationship. AEDP level 3.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: As a student of Hakomi and AEDP I am focused on the most gentle, effective, and powerful tools for self awareness and choice. I believe that we can attune to our bodies, minds, emotions, moods, memories, beliefs, and spirit to move towards greater inner peace and joy. Carefully attuned body awareness is an effective tool in driving this process. This background makes me an excellent choice for integration therapy.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Experiential therapy provides an incredible path towards self awareness, empowerment, greater choices, and healing. From there the only thing to do is to grow inward and outward.

specialities.name: Aging Concerns
specialities.description: As a mid-life woman and therapist I am passionate about providing support for others during all phases of life. It is a rich and challenging time! Grief, loss, physical challenges, pain, changing roles, relationships, personal meaning, and certain realization of time; I would like to support you wherever you find yourself. Let us connect and assure that presence and choice are at the forefront of your life.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Make time to explore what ails you. I will follow you wherever you'd like to go, only this time you will be well supported. Lets find our way into the pain so that the path out can be cleared.

specialities.name: Self-Harming
specialities.description: Working in Level 1 Trauma Emergency Dept I have significant experience working to assess and support individuals in acute pain and crisis. I know this serves a purpose and I want to know more. I also use EMDR and experiential therapy to heal the deeper wounds that are managed through any form of self harming behaviors.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have worked with individuals with developmental and acute trauma and use EMDR and trauma informed care to provide somatic and emotional healing from trauma response.

name: Daniel Blumenthal
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Helping adults of all ages, children, and couples address trauma, anxiety, depression, and relationship challenges.
ideal_client: NOTE: I'm accepting new clients. I accept Aetna and Optum insurance. I can also provide "superbills" for clients covered under other insurance providers or paying out of pocket. Please reach out with questions! I work with adult clients experiencing trauma, depression, anxiety, anger, and impulse control/substance use issues; and couples experiencing relationship and communication challenges. I also provide therapy for children and their caregivers.

approaches.How I Can Help You: In my experience, most mental health challenges are complex and can benefit from therapy, use of recommended skills between session, and personal focus on physical health. Each therapeutic relationship begins with an assessment and treatment planning, in which I will gather information. We will then work together to establish goals, and determine which type of therapy will be most helpful based on your symptoms and needs. I use the following strategies with positive outcomes: Psychodynamic therapy is a long-term strategy that acknowledges the complex reasons and causes for emotional suffering, and examines subconscious motivations for our behavior and feelings. Research shows long-term alleviation of symptoms with this therapy. EMDR: A structured evidence-based technique that uses eye-movements and talk therapy to alleviate PTSD symptoms. CBT/DBT: Structured step-by-step therapies that reduce anxious negative thoughts and emotional dysregulation.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I may be a good fit for you if: you are dealing with trauma symptoms, anxiety, depression, or anger challenges; are in a relationship with someone suffering from mental health or personality disorders; are seeking long-term therapy to address complex dynamic challenges and reach a point of self-actualization; want to address trauma using EMDR; are a couple seeking help in improving communication and addressing resentment within the relationship; or are a guardian of a child with mild to moderate mental health or behavioral challenges.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have training in EMDR, CBT, psychodynamic, and client-centered techniques. I have used all these various techniques and seen them successfully address trauma-related symptoms.

name: La Saechao
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi my name is La! I offer a space where you can unpack your experiences, explore, and challenge yourself.
ideal_client: I am passionate about working with adults who might be feeling stuck or stagnant, finding themselves repeating old patterns, and just wanting to do things differently. I support people in finding a deeper understanding of themselves and the world around them. I enjoy working with adults of all identities, backgrounds, and orientations, including individuals from communities of color, adult children of immigrants/refugees, and individuals that identify with multicultural or multiracial.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a woman of color, I have experienced the stressors related to living and navigating the complexity of family expectations, culture, and dominant society. I understand the impact of marginalization and systematic oppression. Most importantly, I understand the benefits of finding a non-judgemental space where you can truly honor who you really are while being seen and heard. I offer a space to sort through demands and stressors of everyday life, relationships, and cultural identity/BIPOC-specific challenges. As a therapist I can offer this space to you. Issues I can help with are life transitions, stress, anxiety, self-esteem, cultural identity, personal growth, relationship issues, and depression. I provide individual therapy to adults through virtual counseling sessions. Unfortunately, I do not have in-person options at this time. Please visit my website to schedule a free consultation at www.growingwithinpnw.com.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe we are all shaped by diverse experiences that influence who we are, how we operate in the world, and the lens through which we view life. Each experience holds profound meaning and value, guiding us as we navigate the world around us. When we take the time to hold space for our experiences, we create opportunities to explore, understand, and nurture them. This process allows for healing, self-discovery, and transformation. As your therapist, my goal is to honor all aspects of your lived experiences. I practice from a social justice, multicultural, and anti-oppressive framework, ensuring that our work together is inclusive, affirming, and compassionate. I strive to create a space where all parts of you are seen, heard, and valued.

name: Courageous Couples Counseling
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I will walk with you to discover the courage to love and recover the courage to be loved.
ideal_client: Everything is easier when you feel confident that your partner is in your corner. Sharing the weight of your struggles and amplifying life's joys in what makes relationships worth all the work. Our greatest wounds in life are relational in nature, which means our deepest healing comes from improving our most important relationships. Schedule your consultation if you're looking for better communication, repairing trust, or throwing out the rulebook and creating your own new paradigm.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Welcome to Courageous Couples Counseling, where I blend the Gottman Method and the Psychobiological Approach to Couples Therapy (PACT) to help you build stronger, more resilient relationships. With the Gottman Method, we focus on enhancing communication, deepening emotional connection, and resolving conflicts effectively. PACT adds a rich understanding of attachment theory, neuroscience, and arousal regulation to address underlying patterns and create lasting change. Together, these approaches provide a comprehensive, compassionate framework for navigating challenges and fostering intimacy. Whether you're facing recurring issues or seeking to enhance your bond, I am here to support you in creating a fulfilling and enduring partnership. I also work well with couples exploring ENM, Polyamory, and Kink dynmaics in thier relationships.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I embrace all identities and relationship structures. As a queer therapist, I love working with other members of the LGBTQIA+ family and provide a broader perspective to my many and varied heteronormative couples. I believe that the human experience is both universal and highly individual. My primary values are kindness and transparency. I play an active role and bring my humanity into my sessions with clients. Most of my clients rarely leave therapy thinking "I wonder what Kevin is thinking". I love personal developlement and I'm a thearpy nerd. You can often find me outside of work reading a new personal development book in the Rose Test Garden or walking my dog Quentin with my partner Spencer. I love checking out the food scene here in Portland or the occational night out dancing.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: Gottman Therapy is a research-based approach developed by Drs. John and Julie Schwartz Gottman. It focuses on improving relationships through seven key components: building love maps, sharing admiration, turning towards each other, maintaining a positive perspective, managing conflict, supporting life dreams, and creating shared meaning. The method also addresses negative patterns like criticism and contempt, aiming to enhance communication, emotional connection, and relationship satisfaction.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: PACT Therapy (Psychobiological Approach to Couple Therapy) integrates attachment theory, neuroscience, and experiential techniques to help couples deepen their connection. Developed by Dr. Stan Tatkin, PACT focuses on understanding attachment styles, enhancing emotional regulation, and improving communication. It aims to strengthen relationships by addressing underlying psychological patterns and fostering secure, supportive bonds between partners.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: The Gottman Method teaches the tangible communication tools that many couples are looking for when they enter therapy. PACT illuminates the often subconscious influences that lead to conflicts or feelings of disconnection in the first place. Blending these two modalities together offers the couples I work with a truly comprehensive approach to relationship therapy.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I love love. I'm a romantic at heart who finds deep meaning in improving relationships. I devoted my life to developing a range of tools, strategies, anthropological insights, and lived wisdom around optimizing romantic partnerships. I can help you repair past emotional injuries, develop more emotional intelligence, improve communication, and enhance your understanding of how your childhood wounds are impacting your current relationship.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I work with my whole community to improve their mental health. Whether you want to focus on a particular element of your queer journey or have a therapist who understands a core part of your identity while you focus on other elements of your mental health, I'm here for you.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have great respect for those that are working to create the relationship of their dreams outside of normative structures. I also have lived experience practicing ENM. I've worked with hundreds of couples and polycules to get the best out of their relationships. Whether you're wanting to focus on the unique challenges that come from ENM or wanting to focus on other parts of your relationship(s) in a non-judgmental space with someone who understands your lifestyle, I'm here to help.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: Sex is really complex. The most erotic organ of the body is the brain. So complications naturally arise between the connection to your head and your body while connecting to your partner who is may be struggling to strike the right balance too. Sex is one of the central ways we express some of the deepest parts of our humanity. I'm here to help you find the most fulfilling sex life you can have for yourself and your partnership. I also feel confident working with Ace folx as well.

specialities.name: Premarital Counseling
specialities.description: Engagements are an exciting and anxious time, yet many couples spend this golden opportunity primarily planning the wedding of their dreams, while failing to plan a marriage to last a lifetime. Why wait to see a skilled counselor until there are serious concerns, when it's much more effective to address relationship pitfalls before they happen? I've supported many couples address a variety of struggles while covering important topics to avoid common relational conflicts.

name: Wendy Micheau
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I offer individual telehealth counseling services to adult women of all identities, backgrounds, & cultures throughout the state of Oregon.
ideal_client: Most people who seek me out are overwhelmed. They may be dealing with life transitions, like separation, divorce, single parenting, empty nesting, or career changes. Sometimes they're doing their best to juggle life's stresses while managing chronic illness or disability—whether that's their own autoimmune condition, their child's autism or ADHD, their partner's sudden stroke, or an aging parent's Alzheimer's. Above all, they want a personal connection to help them move forward.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a counselor, I offer undivided attention and nonjudgement. You’ll find that I’m warm, approachable, and easy to talk to. I will listen with patience and compassion, using curiosity and thoughtful questions to examine your concerns. If you're open to it, we may use creative activities like metaphor, drawing, writing, visualization, or projection to approach problems in new ways. I will also challenge you to take small, frequent action steps to help you meet the goals you've set for yourself. In our work together I will honor your wholeness and recognize your inherent strengths. This means that—while I will attend to the challenges you describe in session—I will also acknowledge your knowledge, skills, attitudes, wisdom, capabilities, community, & resiliency. You are so much more than your current hardship! Rest assured that you will come away from our time together feeling heard and seen.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: All people deserve to be treated with dignity and respect. I advocate for the inclusion and basic rights of all marginalized and oppressed populations--both inside the counseling room and in the larger community; however, I'm especially passionate about serving people with chronic illness and disability. As a single mom with a disability, I understand the experience of adjusting to a diagnosis, learning new ways to accommodate limitations, and dealing with disability stigma and discrimination. Getting through a typical day in our culture can feel exhausting and overwhelming. I would be honored to help you address any barriers keeping you from the vibrant, meaningful life you desire.

name: Luke Allen
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Specializing in anxiety, depression, LGBTQ+ health, body-focused repetitive behaviors & gender care. I provide 100% online therapy.
ideal_client: Sometimes trying too hard to get rid of or control our emotions backfire. Instead of trying to get rid of unwanted thoughts and feelings, I will help you learn to react differently to them so that you can keep your focus on living a meaningful and fulfilling life based on what’s important to you. We will work together to set meaningful goals to address your concerns–whether they relate to life transitions, depression, anxiety, body image, grief, job or academic stress, or gender & sexuality.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I primarily provide individual therapy with late teens and adults. In addition to depression and anxiety, I also specialize in working with transgender and non-binary youth and their families on matters related to gender identity. Transgender clients and family members seeking assessment or counseling services can expect a safe space, and respectful, non-pathologizing, collaborative care. I am a Certified World Professional Association for Transgender Health Care (WPATH) GEI SOC8 Member. I have extensive training, research, and clinical experience working with transgender and gender-diverse youth, adults, and families.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Many forms of anxiety do not respond to traditional talk therapy. Making progress often requires specialized, structured treatments that have been specifically developed for anxiety disorders. I received year-long training and supervision in treating anxiety and anxiety-related disorder with exposure.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I am openly queer/gay. I practice from an Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) approach. This approach focuses on helping you learn to react differently to unwanted thoughts and feelings and live your life based what's important to you even if society pressures you to do otherwise. I have taught, published, and training frequently on working sexual and gender diversity.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: My experience working with transgender individuals includes over 7 years of experience. I received training conducting evaluations within a multidisciplinary transgender health clinic. I am an active member of World Professional Association for Transition Health (WPATH) and a former WPATH board member. I am a WPATH Standards of Care 7 (SOC7) Certified Member and a WPATH SOC7 Certified Mentor and co-author of the Standards of Care 8.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Some depression might go away on its own. This is not always the case and it frequently requires treatment. A major part of treatment will be to learn how to do activities that you care about anyway. Many times, behavior has to change before your mood or feelings will change. We’ll also learn strategies, skills, and for adopting new perspectives in order to relate to unwanted thoughts and feelings that show up for you in the context of your depression.

name: Kimberly Wilcox, Way of River Psychotherapy
full_name: Kimberly Wilcox, Way of River Psychotherapy
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello! Welcome to Way of River Psychotherapy with Kimberly Wilcox, LPC ! I am taking new clients for teletherapy & clinical supervision.
ideal_client: Sometimes along life’s path we can start to feel like we have lost our way. Life can result in feelings of meaninglessness, depression, exhaustion, loss of creativity or emptiness. We may feel a tugging within us that something is wrong, and we are off course. This can often lead us to therapy for relief of difficult experiences, thoughts and feelings. Still other times we may enter therapy with a desire to find meaning and purpose. It is my honor to support you in your healing journey.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Rooted in Depth Psychology, I work with a combination of modalities. Together we will discover the approach that feels best suited for you. By meeting in a confidential, honoring environment we will build a trusting relationship that gives space for the work you want to do together. Our sessions will use a combination of insight, action and integration with skill-based techniques to support you on your healing journey. Together we will work to manage and explore the complex depths of meaning and feelings that come with life and relationships. We will work directly with the core elements of thoughts, feelings and experiences to tap into those lost or unknown parts of self that are key to your healing. This work may not only give symptom relief, but bring individual and relationship growth and meaning that sustains you throughout life’s journey. Over time, clients may report feelings of self-acceptance, transformation, authenticity, renewed energy for life and a sense of purpose.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that we as humans are instinctively drawn toward healing and growth with a desire for meaning and soul. This led me to Depth Psychology which believes that healing comes from a deeper level of processing and introspection. It is interested in healing through awareness of those parts of ourselves that have been cast out or not yet able to be known and their impact on our behavior, thoughts and feelings. As I worked with people, I became deeply interested in the dynamics of a person’s relationship with themselves as shaped by their experiences and perceptions of those relationships. I saw many people cut off from their essence, a sense of disconnectedness from self. I believe that healing comes from allowing what is ousted from our awareness to come forward, explore its significance and integrate it; allowing you to become more fully present to yourself and your life resulting in enhancing your relationship with yourself, others, your community and the world.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have decades of experience working with children, youth and families. In today's world our children are faced with many challenges that can disrupt their development and health as well as the overall family dynamics. During our sessions we will work to alleviate symptoms of distress; we also include efforts to improve their social and emotional resources; increase their use of effective communication skills; and strengthen family, community and peer relationships.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Family therapy will focus on the whole system; concentrating on the relationships between individual family members, their roles and situations, including context, rules, boundaries and communication. Many times parenting information does not address the specific needs of your individual children and your unique family dynamic. Our sessions can help you tailor your parenting to the needs of your individual children and set you and your family on a positive road towards healing and understanding

specialities.name: Schizophrenia
specialities.description: Often times families experiencing the effects of severe mental illness find this experience to be tumultuous, complex, and isolating. Sessions will be designed to help guide families who have a member with schizophrenia or other psychosis diagnosis. This service provides individual, family and system support through extremely difficult times and helps you navigate your feelings, loss and fears as well as the systems that are complex and often do not meet your needs.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have decades of experience working with youth, adults and families who experience trauma. Psychological trauma is an emotional response caused by a severe distressing events that are outside normal human experiences. This may include natural disasters, war, abuse, loss of a loved one, violence, and vehicle collision. Our sessions will address your specific needs and symptoms, offering a compassionate approach to help you heal and move forward with strength.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Issues of self-esteem can be the driver of issues related to relationship with self and others, present as depression or anxiety and come as a result of loss or life transition. We will work directly with the core elements of thoughts, feelings and experiences to tap into those lost or unknown parts of self that are key to your healing. This work can not only give symptom relief, but bring individual and relationship growth and meaning that sustains you throughout life’s journey.

name: Ben Mosebach
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Ben Mosebach, not your usual therapist. No clichés or empty promises here. Just authenticity, rawness, and a desire to effect change
ideal_client: I specialize in helping individuals and couples, regardless of gender, navigate life's challenges. Whether you're dealing with relationship issues, work stress, anxiety, depression, life transitions or simply feeling stuck, I'm here to support you. I'm not here to judge; I'm here to help you find practical solutions and move forward with confidence.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is straightforward and down-to-earth. If theoretical orientation is interesting to you I am rooted in the humanistic perspectives encompassing aspects of existentialism, gestalt and person centered therapy. But I'm not interested in wasting your time with superficial chatter or jargon-filled language. I'm here to roll up my sleeves and get to work with you, tackling whatever challenges you're facing head-on.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: What sets me apart as a therapist is my empathy and compassion complimented with a no-nonsense approach and a genuine desire to see you succeed. I understand that reaching out for help can be tough, and men especially are conditioned to think they need to go it alone. However, embarking on that initial step might just turn out to be the most transformative decision you ever make. During our sessions, you can anticipate genuine and open dialogue. I'll provide constructive challenges when necessary, while also offering unwavering support throughout your journey. Together, we'll tackle any barriers hindering your progress and strive to create a life that inspires you.

name: ELIZABETH PIERCE-GREEN
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Hello! I have immediate openings to help you achieve your best life!
ideal_client: I work with individuals from 5 to 64 years of age who struggle with ADHD, major depression, anxiety, bipolar, autism and a variety of other mental health concerns.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe in treating the mind, body and spirit as a whole person. I am passionate about providing quality, compassionate, and individualized care to patients and families with psychiatric medications and brief psychotherapeutic interventions as well as some alternative therapies in combination with medication management.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: After years of working with people in health care, I realized that many individuals continue to struggle as they do not have that one special person they can pour out their inner most thoughts, doubts, fears, and anxieties to. I believe that to heal we must have a trusting relationship with someone that understands us. Someone that can give us tools to change and grow but not judge our self-perceived inadequacies. It takes time to build a trusting relationship. I want to be that person for you. I am a mother to four amazing adults and a grandmother to four beautiful independent and spicy littles that have made their forever home within an hour drive to my residence. My husband owns and operates a local family business. My home is here. I plan on staying local; therefore, we will have time to build a relationship and work together to device a collaborative plan that meets your needs.

name: Hannah Boyd
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I take an integrative, collaborative approach to therapy, using humor and curiosity to help you explore, heal, and navigate challenges.
ideal_client: I specialize in supporting individuals who have experienced complex trauma, with a focus on sexual abuse, as well as teens and adults navigating life transitions. Additionally, I provide guidance for caregivers to help them manage the unique challenges of their role. I strive to create a space where clients feel heard, validated, and supported as they work toward healing and personal growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: You are multifaceted, and your experiences are unique. Together, we'll take an integrative approach to address the various symptoms and challenges you're facing. While talk therapy can be helpful on its own, I believe in enhancing the process with humor, curiosity, and collaboration to deepen your understanding of your feelings and experiences. Your ideas and creativity are always welcome as we work together. Through empowerment and exploration, you can tap into your internal resources to recognize patterns, solve problems, and cope with life's challenges.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I’m committed to creating an inclusive, affirming space where you can show up as your authentic self, regardless of background or identity. I recognize the significant impact of systemic and cultural factors on mental health and strive to provide therapy that’s not only supportive but also mindful of diversity, equity, and inclusion

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: I began my career at a Children's Advocacy Center, working with children and teens who experienced abuse. This shaped my passion for trauma-informed care. I’ve pursued additional training in treating sexual abuse and am a Certified Clinical Trauma Practitioner, dedicated to helping clients heal and regain a sense of safety and empowerment.

name: Valenca Valenzuela
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I provide a warm, engaging, and authentic space as we work together to find meaning, balance, and healing through life's many transitions.
ideal_client: My ideal clients are navigating the intricate terrain of life's transitions, seeking support for grief and loss, identity exploration, the complexities of death anxiety and existential crises, and those who carry the weight of intergenerational trauma. In our therapeutic journey, we delve into the profound quest for meaning, and explore the depths of existence. My client's cultivate presence, find ways to engage with life authentically, hope to restore balance, and find life's purpose.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is deeply rooted in existential-humanistic principles, providing a safe and collaborative environment for individuals seeking transformation and rebirth. I employ trauma-informed care and view clients' experiences through a grief-informed lens, embracing a holistic perspective that acknowledges the interconnectedness of emotional, physical, and spiritual well-being. Together, we explore somatic awareness and the nervous system, facilitating an intuitive understanding of self. At the core of my therapeutic method is the cultivation of authentic and meaningful relationships. I view my role as that of a mindful companion supporting you on your journey. I will follow your lead, while remaining curious, engaged, and honest in what I notice. Within this relational space, my goal is to guide individuals towards personal transformation and help them discover their unique path to restoring balance and finding meaning in life.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: My path to becoming a therapist was driven by a profound personal journey. My own experiences with grief and loss, intertwined with intergenerational trauma, ignited a passionate desire to support others through their unique life challenges. As a therapist, I find immense fulfillment in helping individuals navigate the intricate tapestry of life's transitions. I view each transition as a profound life cycle in itself, a portal of transformation from one chapter to the next. My background in social work, coupled with my deep-rooted passion for grief and loss, is driven by a vision to transform how society engages with grief, fostering a more compassionate and empathetic approach. My existential approach to therapy serves as a powerful tool to shift feelings of isolation, death anxiety, and existential confusion into a journey of meaning-making, balance, and transformation. I'm here to guide you on your path towards greater understanding, resilience, and a deeper connection to life.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I believe that existential therapy offers a transformative path from feelings of loneliness, death anxiety, and being lost to one of meaning making, balance, and personal transformation. It allows me to guide individuals on their unique journeys, helping them find purpose and understanding in the face of life's transitions and challenges.
