I have a background as a social worker, death doula, and life-cycle educator, which lends itself to helping others navigate existential dread.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: I believe in a holistic approach to therapy. Working with the mind, body, and spirit, can help folks to feel more authentically aligned with oneself. I have a background in understanding body movement, nervous system regulation, and like to combine somatic awareness with other therapeutic interventions. By exploring emotions, body feelings, and existential meaning, I help folks to feel more balanced and whole.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I strongly believe in an authentic and collaborative therapeutic approach. Through using our relationship in the present moment, I help clients to reflect upon themselves, feel validated, and offer a safe and healthy connection while helping clients to work on life's challenges.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: I like to help client's explore the inner beliefs that one holds in order to gain fuller insight and relationship to oneself. As we explore spirituality and consciousness, growth and transformation, meaning and purpose, I hope to provide a deepening of connection to oneself.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I have spent the last 15 years sitting with those living with loss. I am passionate about providing grief-informed care and bring a wealth of experience with me. I am not here to save you from your pain, but to witness and hold space for you to move through your grief. My greatest purpose in life is to help those who are feeling grief after a profound loss.

name: Justice Arledge LPC Associate, MS
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: master's in clinical mental health counseling
intro: **CURRENTLY TAKING NEW CLIENTS** I help people struggling with depression, anxiety, loneliness, isolation, and other life stresses.
ideal_client: I understand no two individuals are the same, and I tailor our sessions together to address challenges unique to you. We will work together to understand the root cause of your struggles and address those issues with long-lasting strategies, helping you get closer to the life you’ve always wanted. If you’re ready to work towards the life you’ve always wanted, I’m ready when you are. Contact me today and let’s get to work.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Life can be a very difficult road to haul, but nobody said you have to do it alone. In the world, we have doctors, teachers, all kinds of people that help us along the way it only makes sense to have somebody to help you process through difficulties in life. Hello, my name is Justice Arledge I have been working in this field since 2009 I also have my Masters degree in mental health counseling. I have more than 10 years of experience helping people work through the many unpleasantries that we find in our everyday life. I have helped people work through trauma, depression, and PTSD. I have worked both with adolescents and adults. My goal as a counselor is to put you back in the driver seat get you to a point in your life where you can make decisions and trust yourself. Help you to make and achieve long-term goals and to walk through life proudly and loving who you are. We all struggle with something, but my goal is to help you find positive voices that can defeat the negative voices.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Seeking help is hard, but it is also one of the best things you can do for your life’s journey and the people that are apart of it. I Think of it this way, if you had a broken leg you would not run a marathon before healing with the help of a doctor. Every day you are running the marathon of your life by trying to get along day today. You could be struggling with anxiety, depression or any other issues with mental health. Seeking a therapist or counselor for your mental health is no different than seeing a doctor if you had that broken leg. My Approach to Counselling and Therapy This is a question that is difficult to answer because there are so many wonderful tools out there. Below are some of the theories that I do lean towards. I consider myself a cognitive-behavioral therapist. I use a lot of elements from other theories, One of my favorite techniques is reality testing and exposure therapy.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: This is the one I lean to the most Person-centered (PC) /Humanistic; client gets to decide what life you want to live. PC reminds client that they are in control of their life and their future. PC believes that the past does not necessarily determine their future. PC asks therapist to consider events from the client’s point of view. Looking at the situation from the client’s point of view can assist the counselor to understand why the decision or particular path was made.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: Existential therapists will ask questions to the client to help them solve their problems like what is it you want to do? What are the feelings you want to feel? What things in your life do you want to accomplish. With the answers the client gives the therapist; the therapist then will simply ask how are we going to solve these goals. Existential therapy is more concerned with the bigger picture. Solving the bigger problems will in turn answer the smaller problems.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT is a behavioral treatment that helps people see the difference between beliefs, thoughts, and feelings, and free them from unhelpful patterns of behavior. CBT is grounded in the belief that it is a person’s perception of events, rather than the events themselves, that determines how he or she will feel and act in response. CBT will help to look at ideas and practices and make adjustments to fit the client’s lifestyle.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness is the idea of paying attention to what is going on this very moment. Mindfulness is the awareness of yourself and your environment and how it affects each other. Mindfulness is not a pass or fail. It is something that you constantly work at to be more aware throughout your life.

specialities.name: Learning Disorder
specialities.description: Living with a learning disability as I do myself, can be challenging. Individuals struggling with learning disabilities can experience anger, frustration, shame, and low self-esteem. Speaking to a therapist about your feelings can be very helpful. A therapist can help individuals understand that although learning disabilities are lifelong and many methods of help including support are available.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is an anxiety disorder caused by severe trauma. This trauma could have been anything from a car accident to experiencing combat. This trauma has rewired your brain to where you are always on the lookout for things to go wrong. Therapy can help the individual suffering from PTSD by helping them through some of their emotions and thoughts.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is the normal healthy fear that we have about everyday things we find in life. Anxiety could also be that paralyzing persistent fear that cripples us and holds us back from achieving our life goals. Therapy helps the client work through some of their thoughts and will help a person be more aware of them self as well as how life affects them.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: People who have struggled with learning differences (learning disabilities) may have been shamed, talked down to, and humiliated. When you were younger, you may have been told that you were lazy, and you may have even been made fun of by some of your friends or peers. These types of events in your life can cause you to have low self-esteem, low self-worth, and create other challenges that follow.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can be so severe even getting out of bed may seem impossible. Depression can be caused by biological issues as well as many other issues including anxiety. Working with the therapist can help you take comfortable easy steps to combat your depression.

name: Lisa Headings
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Expressive arts therapy for deep feelers & misfits ready to ditch stress, self-doubt & people-pleasing. No art skills required.
ideal_client: My clients feel stuck, overwhelmed, or disconnected. Many are midlife women who’ve spent years putting others first and now wonder, “What about me?” If you crave self-expression, clarity, and confidence, expressive arts therapy helps you break old patterns and reconnect with your authentic self.

approaches.How I Can Help You: Words are powerful—but sometimes they’re not enough. Expressive arts therapy weaves together visual art, movement, writing, and creative exploration to help you process emotions, reduce stress, and rediscover joy. No art skills required—just curiosity and a willingness to explore. Therapy with me is deep, playful, and liberating. We quiet the overthinking brain, tap into your inner creativity, and uncover what’s been keeping you stuck. My approach is nonjudgmental and intuitive. Together, we create a safe, non-clinical space where you can show up fully and reconnect with who you truly are.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I know what it’s like to feel like you don’t quite fit in—I’m a lifelong, card-carrying member of the Island of Misfit Toys. That’s why I create space for honest, imperfect expression—where you can show up exactly as you are and feel seen. If talk therapy hasn't quite clicked, expressive arts therapy offers a creative, intuitive path to healing. You don’t need to be “good at art”—just open to exploring. I work best with deep feelers, creatives, and those ready to ditch the script and find themselves again.

specialities.name: Expressive Art Therapy
specialities.description: Sometimes words aren’t enough. Expressive arts therapy weaves together visual art, movement, music, storytelling, and creative play to help you process emotions, release stress, and gain clarity. You don’t need to be an artist—just open to exploring new ways to heal and grow.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: Growth happens when you experience something new, not just talk about it. Experiential therapy helps you break old patterns through hands-on, interactive techniques like art, movement, role-play, and creative expression, allowing for deep emotional shifts.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Feeling overwhelmed? Mindfulness-based therapy helps you reconnect with the present moment, shifting your focus from constant thinking to embodied awareness. Using breathwork, movement, and creative expression, I’ll help you find ways to feel more grounded and at ease.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Your mind won’t stop spinning, your shoulders are tense, and you’re exhausted from overthinking everything. Anxiety can make it feel impossible to relax, but expressive arts therapy helps you shift out of your head and into the present moment. Through movement, art, and creative exploration, I help you process stress in new ways, creating space for more calm and clarity.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Tired of second-guessing yourself? Spent years shrinking, people-pleasing, or trying to be less? I help women break free from self-doubt and reconnect with their authentic selves. Through expressive arts therapy, you’ll rediscover confidence, self-trust, and joy—without the pressure of getting it “right.”

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: You feel a shift happening—you know you’re meant for something more, but you’re unsure how to get there. Expressive arts therapy helps you explore new possibilities, uncover what’s holding you back, and move toward a life that feels more aligned, creative, and true to you.

name: Krispin Mayfield
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I’m Krispin (he/him), a therapist for religious trauma & ADHD. I help people heal from high-control religion & rebuild self-trust.
ideal_client: Many of my clients feel stuck between the life they were taught to live and the one they want to build. They may carry guilt when setting boundaries, question their own instincts, or feel shame about their identity, sexuality or gender expression. I help clients untangle these internalized messages, rebuild self-trust, and create a life that aligns with who they really are.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I specialize in helping people heal from the lasting impact of high-control religious environments. With years of experience supporting clients through religious trauma, I create space to gently explore the beliefs still shaping your nervous system, even if you no longer agree with them. Together, we’ll make sense of the emotions and needs that were once suppressed, so you can build a life where your identity, boundaries, and values take the lead.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: As someone who grew up in a high-control religious environment, I understand how deeply early belief systems can shape our sense of self, even long after we’ve left them behind. For the past several years, I’ve researched and written about the psychological impact of high-control religion — work that continues to inform my approach as a therapist. I’m passionate about helping others recover from religious trauma, rebuild self-trust, and reconnect with their emotions, identity and values.

name: REBECCA ENGLISH
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am very interactive with clients, and help them to navigate issues in practical, as well as in therapeutic ways. (HealthShare/CareOregon)
ideal_client: Each individual is unique, and every couple has its own ecosystem. I bring a broad overview and understanding as well as an ability to navigate that which is unique and particular, in my work with clients. Experience, insight, passion, care and respect inform my work. Clients report feeling truly seen and heard. I am deeply interested in each person, as well as their individual goals and needs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: There is overlap in psychological approaches, because there is overlap in the basic psychology of all individuals. Every client is different, and different modalities will be better for an individual client’s needs. I will likely use one or two primary modalities. However, there are times when using Cognitive Behavioral modalities may move into working with Internal Family Systems. The reverse is also true. I cannot imagine ignoring the wisdom in the tenets of Family Systems Therapy, as an adjunct to any other modality. In all modalities, Motivational Interviewing may play a helpful role at times, with getting un-stuck. Narrative Therapy can be a capstone, as well as an ongoing, and oft-repeated mantra you will hear from me, though I do not use it as a primary modality. A catharsis is sometimes forgotten. A story is not.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: While I have 16 years of formal education in Psychology, Social Sciences, and Counseling, it is my own personal experience which has given me the greatest ability to also understand what my clients are going through. I believe we bring an added dimension into counseling when we augment formal training with those lessons we’ve learned by having to navigate through our own difficult life experiences. I see couples, families, and individuals, and specialize in helping with attachment, anxiety, depression, trauma, and the stress due to life changes. As your counselor, I will be fully engaged in my work with you, helping you to discover answers and solutions.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Our attachment style will color the things we believe about ourselves, do not believe about ourselves, or have no solid conception of, about ourselves. They are such a basic building block, that depending on that attachment style, we will see people and relationships through that lens. Attachment affects all of our relationships, and in particular, those with a significant other. Work on this dynamic is very integral, in individual, as well as in couples counseling.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: For many couples, a limited number of sessions can significantly untangle issues which have come to an impasse. Communication is generally given as the reason things became so convoluted: feeling unheard, misunderstood, discounted. What may seem abundantly clear to the teller may appear to be unintelligible to the hearer. The right tools can significantly change this dynamic. My number one recommendation: come in at that first significant wound, or as soon thereafter as possible.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: I incorporate aspects of coaching into counseling, because so many problems resolve best from a combination of the practical and the psychological. Some problems are purely practical. A new set of eyes can make all the difference. I enjoy the puzzle-solving aspects of tackling difficult decisions and situations. From helping CEO’S design new business models, to incorporating exercise into a client's routine, and everything in between, I enjoy creatively helping clients accomplish their goals.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: I find the use of Gestalt techniques very helpful in using dreams as a way of accessing subconscious material. I employ this with clients who feel stuck, have repetitive dreams, or find it difficult to engage deeply with Internal Family Systems. Clients often report the relaxing and freeing aspect of doing this work. While I do not use this frequently, it is a very helpful adjunct to other modalities.

name: Scott LaForce
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I have danced with the light, the dark, and the spectrum of color. Now I’d like to help you along your journey.
ideal_client: I am currently seeing individual adults and in the context of their relationships (mono, or poly), as well as children, adolescents, and teens, in the context of their families. All clients using insurance will be admitted through New Pattern Counseling: www.newpatterncounseling.com. Please reach out with any questions.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work intersubjectively through a postmodern lens with an emphasis on empowerment. This means that I remain cognizant of all the crucial elements coming into the room, including your unique experience and how my presence interacts with it. Dogma is not a part of my practice. While past theories have insisted on the therapist as expert, I believe that you are the expert of your life and that my job is to assist you in (re)discovering yourself. There are many options. We just need to find the best one for your needs. Social justice is a primary focus for my practice. I will help you to deconstruct the dominant discourses that have been a disservice in your life while helping you to create new narratives that will allow you to build the life you've always wanted... the life you deserve.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a master's degree in Applied Psychology from Antioch University Los Angeles. My focus has been on social justice with an emphasis on LGBTQ+Affirmative therapies. I worked as a rehabilitation practitioner with folks who suffer from severe and persistent mental illness, a therapist for people making strides toward eradicating stigma surrounding HIV, and as an intake counselor at various agencies. I am sex-positive. I am led by synchronicity and the teachings of Carl Jung. I support holistic healing, which means that I will encourage you to seek many other avenues toward betterment. Therapy is only one piece to the puzzle that is you.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: Who makes up the parts of your internal whole?

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Object relations and beyond.. how we orient ourselves to the things outside.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Rewrite the stories that make up your life; identify dominant discourses and author your preferred narrative.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Relationships can be difficult. It's not uncommon to wonder sometimes if they're worth all the work! There are so many variables and possibilities to explore; let's figure out what works and what doesn't. Your intimate life deserves love. We can work toward finding it in as many forms as are available to you.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: Patriarchy has had its day. It is time for the age of the divine feminine, which is not a concept limited to women. All integral beings possess both feminine and masculine traits. intentionally flowing between them is an artform that provides unending benefit. Rejoice in your strengths.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Mind, body, spirit, relationship—to our selves, to one another, to our environments, No good therapy will ever ignore your entirety. We are complex beings that require multiple elements for survival. Neglect in one area often leads to imbalance in others. Reallign with your sense of purpose by honoring your whole self.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a proud member of the LGBTQ+ community, I am dedicated to helping my peers rise from the destructive forces of stigma and oppression. Using strengths-based and person-centered foundations, I believe that you are beautiful and powerful at your core.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: Sexual identity, HIV/AIDS, sexual behavior

name: Melissa Demers
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: As a systemic therapist, I work with couples and families to resolve relational conflict, increase communication, and enhance intimacy.
ideal_client: I welcome folx from all walks of life and who are dealing with various mental health concerns. I can work with you and your partner to learn to speak to each other in a way that strengthens your bond and helps you feel like you are partnered with your best friend. Whether you're dealing with a loss, anxiety, depression, trauma, relational conflict, or coping in ways that don't align with your values, I would be honored to be a witness to your process and meet you right where you are.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: ONLY OFFERING TELEHEALTH (ONLINE) SESSIONS. I want to work alongside you, exploring your strengths and values to help you better cope with life's ups and downs. I use an integrated approach to help you achieve your goals. I am an emotion focused therapist and help couples and families from an attachment framework. I specialized in addictions counseling during my internship at Lewis and Clark College where I saw individuals struggling with addictions and co-occurring disorders for nearly 2 years, as well as helped their family members navigate through that process and be a support to their family member. My passion is working with couples, exploring their strengths and values to help them come together as a team and navigate life's ups and downs. I have an additional year of experience working primarily with couples and families.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that change is constant. I always wanted to find a way to give back and contribute something to society, therefore I became a therapist to help foster positive and sustainable change in people's lives. Due to my own upbringing and family background, I knew that I wanted to help others find ways to come together and create a loving and secure community, something I didn't have much of when I was young. Some random tidbits about myself are that I have a strong affinity for dogs and anything cuddly. You may get the chance to see my dog during our telehealth sessions. She is a Border Collie/Australian Shepard mix. I love my plant babies as well, which will be fully displayed in my home office for your visual enjoyment.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: My passion is working with couples to help them overcome communication breakdown and start talking to each other with more compassion and understanding. My background and education is in marriage, couples, and family therapy and I have worked for nearly 4 years, including the time I spent in my internship during my grad program, with individuals, families, and couples.

name: Erin Fettes
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Attuned Individual Psychotherapy and Support for TTC, Infertility, Assisted Reproductive Technology, Pregnancy Loss, and Reproductive Trauma
ideal_client: You have dreams of adding to your family and along the way, you unexpectedly have to come to terms with an infertility diagnosis. Or you are experiencing the pain of miscarriage, pregnancy loss or termination for medical reasons. You are in the process of utilizing assisted reproductive technologies (ART) like IUI, IVF, or donor assisted reproduction. You are constantly analyzing, questioning, hurting, wondering what now. One thing is for sure - this is not how you thought this was going to go.

approaches.What I Specialize In: As a psychologist specializing in reproductive mental health, with my own experiences of infertility, ART and pregnancy loss, I understand the unique difficulties of this journey. A path marked by cycles of hope and heartache, as the anticipation of new possibilities collides with the anguish of unfulfilled dreams. My mission is to provide a compassionate environment for you to explore feelings, insights, hurts, choices and find resilience, support and care. My areas of focus: 1) Support with Trying to Conceive & Infertility - Psychotherapeutic support for the stressors of trying to conceive and navigating infertility. 2) Assisted Reproductive Technology - Care related to decision making for family building options, emotional support during fertility treatments, and the secondary mental health/relationship stressors that can arise. 3) Pregnancy Loss, Reproductive Trauma & EMDR - Support for addressing failed treatment cycles, pregnancy loss, reproductive trauma, grief and loss.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am a clinical psychologist practicing in Oregon and Colorado. I work with any individual in their experience of the trying to conceive (TTC) process, whether you are the one to carry the pregnancy or a non-gestational partner. The specific focus of my practice is rooted in support for hardships of TTC. I specialize in the needs of this special phase of family building. In addition to emotional support for the challenges of your TTC journey, I also focus on how these difficulties intersect with your treatment of yourself, relationships, prior/concurrent mental health needs, how early-life and formative experiences are impacting how you particularly are navigating these challenges. The present focus on my therapeutic work has personal roots. My therapeutic work has personal roots, with my own path of TTC experiencing many challenges - including queer family building as a fat person, using donor gametes, many rounds of IUI, IVF, failed embryo transfers, and pregnancy loss.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I provide a type of EMDR called Attachment-Focused EMDR (AF-EMDR), developed by the Parnell Institute. If there are painful and disturbing memories, body sensations, or persistent symptoms that you would like to address related to your TTC experiences, this therapy modality is often highly effective at providing relief for traumatic stress and PTSD. Additionally, AF-EMDR focuses on building internal resources like calm, protection, nurturing, wisdom, all resources deeply helpful to those TTC.

specialities.name: Infertility
specialities.description: Infertility carries emotional, physical, and psychological burdens. What sets infertility apart is its profound intersection with identity, relationships, and societal expectations. Infertility often strikes at the core of one’s sense of self, tied deeply to personal and cultural perceptions of parenthood. Experiencing infertility often includes facing a lack of understanding and stigma. The toll of treatments and unpredictable outcomes can make infertility feel particularly relentless.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Pregnancy Loss - whether you have experienced a first time miscarriage, recurrent miscarriages, missed miscarriage, termination for medical reasons, ectopic pregnancy, threatened or inevitable miscarriage, stillbirth, or other loss, you deserve deep support and care. In psychotherapy I can support processing grief, sadness, anger, confusion, guilt, self-blame, creating understanding of events, coping strategies for overwhelming emotions, exploring meaningful ways to honor your losses and cope.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I specialize in treating reproductive trauma (the emotional, physical and cognitive responses to a terrible event(s) or a series of chronically stressful experiences occurring in the context of reproductive efforts and trying to achieve pregnancy). Many of the experiences of TTC, infertility, assisted reproduction, and pregnancy loss can be unexpected, overwhelming and traumatic, and can/may lead to distressing memories, physical sensations, persistent beliefs, and other forms of suffering.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I work particularly well with LGBTQIA+ folks in the process of TTC, for example identifying the right path for you/your family to pursue parenthood, navigating the unique and complex barriers to care, with insurance companies, agencies, medical systems or providers, familial or society related discrimination and bias.

name: Adam Marx
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Warm, caring therapist here to support you with life's challenges. With extensive and varied training, I can flexibly respond to your needs.
ideal_client: I specialize in grief: working with clients who have lost a loved one, or have lost a relationship, a job, a dream--anything that they held dear that is now gone. Closely connected to this loss work, I accompany and support people through life transitions like divorce, retirement, or becoming a parent. I also work with individuals and groups of men on issues of healthy masculinity.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My counseling degree is from a depth-oriented counseling psychology program, and I have been coaching clients for over 25 years. This broad experience gives me a wide ranges of tools and approaches to use with clients, completely dependent on what each client needs. I can empathically listen and support client insight into difficult issues, I can collaboratively explore dreams and memories, and I can help clients achieve specific behavioral goals. Most often, I use multiple approaches with each client, as they move from one aspect of an issue to another, or one stage to the next. I draw from expertise and experience with somatic therapies, NeuroLinguistic Programming (NLP), Gestalt techniques, and parts work.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Two events set me on the path to become a psychotherapist and coach, and they both involve loss. The first was the death of my younger brother, and the second was the death of my son. The combination of these two experiences (25 years apart) and the support I received to deal with those losses set me on the path to counseling. I experienced first-hand how devastating it is to lose a loved one, and how much of a difference a caring and compassionate professional could make as I traveled through my grieving process. I realized that I wanted to help others navigate that grieving process. In addition to grief work, I have benefited from working on healthy masculinity. Involved with men's groups for over ten years (as both a facilitator and a member), I have found them invaluable in working through many of the negative, toxic, and counterproductive beliefs and unconscious training men integrate in our culture.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: My primary specialty is supporting clients through grief and loss. I combine my academic training and counseling experience with my lived experience of grieving the deaths of a brother and of a son.

name: Brad Pankey
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: My heart is filled by helping folks bravely rediscover food freedom, improve how the body is experienced, and realign with their values.
ideal_client: I am honored to work with clients who: (1 ) see their life getting smaller; (2) think about food and/or their body all day; (3) feel stuck in their head in a whirlwind of thoughts; (4) are living a life that lacks personal meaning; (5) who feel trapped by needing to control every aspect of their life; and (6) are experiencing crushing grief and life transitions. They are ready for change, interested in trying something new, and appreciate humor and a therapist who listens with an open heart.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My eating disorder and disordered eating training includes time working at an in-patient clinic and courses on the treatment of eating disorders and trauma. We will also leverage my experience traveling and living all over the world, my MBA degree, and my diverse career and personal background while working with people. With that, we can safely explore topics generally seen as "taboo," such as money, sex, spirituality, and politics, all of which impact our worldview and how we relate to others. In the therapy room, I work with elements of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), RO-DBT, Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) for trauma, and Relational-Cultural Therapy (RCT) through a Person-Centered and Feminist lens. My approach is culturally self-aware and humble, LGBTQ2IA+ aligned, and spiritually connected. I take the position of co-explorer as we navigate the treatment journey together. Wherever treatment takes us, we will always move together.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that we are neither helpless nor capable of being broken and therefore shy away from the idea we need to be fixed. Instead, I see suffering as arising when we become disconnected from our values, when we lose contact with the here and now, and when we get swept up in our thoughts and emotions. Each of us possess the capacity for change. I see my clients as already possessing the attributes that serve as the spark for change and growth. Together, we will discover what is needed to reconnect with one’s values and make the shift from doing to being. In the therapy room, I exist with my clients in shared awareness as we seek understanding rather taking on the role of healer, teacher, or expert. Our relationship is held as sacred and is used as a vehicle for awakening to ourselves. Please feel free to connect if my profile resonates with you. It would be a pleasure to join you in healing your relationship with food, exercise, your body, and yourself.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I work with teens and adult on eating disorders, disordered eating, and body image concerns. I have special interest in working with athletes who are struggling with these issues.

name: Katie Azarow
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am passionate about helping others, and believe firmly that each of us holds the answers to our deepest questions.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am fairly eclectic in my orientation to therapy. I believe strongly in identifying what works for each client and tailoring therapy based upon such. With that being said, my personal goal in session is to ensure my clients are able to identify their progress as it is being made, and to ensure my clients are able to see value in their therapeutic work. I understand the value of my client's time and thus, work to always remain keenly aware of each clients personal time commitment to therapy; tailoring interventions and therapeutic approach to meet these needs.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a licensed clinical social worker in Oregon and Washington. I earned my Master of Social Work degree from University of Nebraska, Omaha, and have been involved in the helping profession since 2007. Over that time, I have worked to build a vast array of experiences ranging from survivors of domestic violence, to those struggling with addiction issues and trauma, to individuals making life transitions, as well as extensively working with adolescents facing anxiety, depression, adjustment issues, self-esteem and issues related to personal identification. I am most passionate about furthering my work with teens and young adults.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I believe firmly that the therapeutic environment serves as a microcosm for the life we live outside of session. Thus, I spend a great deal of time working through relational issues in the context of the therapeutic relationship to help individuals develop and maintain healthy, satisfying relationships throughout their lives.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: As humans living in a technological age, it is easy to become caught up in anxiety-provoking and unhealthy cycles of stress and excessive worry that ultimately lead us to a dead-end. Thus, I rely heavily on mindfulness-based practice in order to help individuals slow down their internal process and find joy and gratitude in moment-to-moment experiences.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I have been trained through my graduate school education and over 50 hours in CEUs on CBT methods for treating anxiety and depression. I believe strongly in the CBT tenant of the connection between thoughts, feelings and behaviors.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have over ten years of experience providing mental health treatment to children and adolescents in Nebraska, Oregon and Washington. I have over 100 hours in ongoing education working with this population and am certified as a child specialist in the state of Washington.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Many mental health issues contain elements of low self-esteem, and many diagnoses can contribute to feelings of low self-esteem. Thus, I investigate and explore issues of self-esteem with every one of my clients. Additionally, working with teenagers has provide hours of work focused solely on exploring self and identifying how individuals interact with the world around them.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: I have worked with many teenagers and young adults who struggle with major life transitions. Honoring the intensity of these experiences and helping clients successfully move forward has been a cornerstone of my work in community mental health.

name: Brad Creel
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Past trauma can cause us to constrict our beliefs about ourselves. Our time together will help guide you on the path of self-discovery.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer a compassionate, non-judgmental, therapeutic environment where my clients can feel welcome and safe. This setting allows clients the opportunity to express themselves deeply, and relate to their authentic self. I utilize an eclectic approach, based on the different needs of my clients. As a trained Depth therapist, I believe that healing can happen through accessing the realm of the unconscious. This process of exploring thoughts and images can be daunting, but also immensely satisfying and life changing. Creativity is an important part of my practice as it is a unique way access material that lies bound up in the psyche. I practice a blend of theories that best serve my clients and help them find their inner voice.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I attended Pacifica Graduate Institute and received a MA in Counseling Psychology with an emphasis in Jungian Psychology. My Master's thesis focused on the process of creativity, inspiration, and overcoming writer' (or artist's) block. I have worked professionally in the arts as an illustrator, woodworker, and performing musician. I also have had past experience owning a small business, and understand the stresses and challenges of running an organization. In my practice, I like to take time to slow down and get to know the parts of yourself that have protected you in the past, but no longer serve you in healthy ways. This journey of self discovery will allow you come into better relationship with your true self and help to create inner wholeness.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: I have a MA in Counseling Psychology with and emphasis on Depth Psychology from Pacifica Graduate Institute in Santa Barbara, CA.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I have had training in Psychodynamic Psychology at my Depth Program at Pacifica Graduate Institute.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I offer a range of therapeutic techniques, tailored to meet the needs of the individual client.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: As the world goes through this dramatic psychic shift, we are asked to reassess our priorities and decisions on how we want to live the second half of our life. I would be honored to act as your guide in this process and also help with the anxiety that comes with change.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I wrote my Master's thesis on the relationship between creativity, imagination, and personal growth. By utilizing a Jungian framework of 'active imagination', I show how personal growth can be obtained through creative expression.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I have a keen interest in men's issues and have facilitated men's process groups groups for 6 years.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: I have both attended and facilitated three separate long-term codependent groups and meetings. I focus on male codependency and it's relationship to addictive behavior.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: A primary focus of mine is working with those who suffer from depression I believe that psychopathology is a revolt of the soul, and depression is a useful tool that tells us we are not living a life that resonates with who we really are.

name: Madeline Ammar
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I'm ready to support you in compassionate, caring and impactful change
ideal_client: As a therapist, I support through a “body first” approach to healing. I merge evidenced based "top down - bottom up" somatic approaches needed to create pathways of new experience. In our sessions, you can expect to go beyond conventional therapy. In our time together, we will engage with your body's wisdom and reimagine personal narratives, turning these insights into practical actions for holistic healing and self-growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My tools include Hakomi Psychotherapy, Somatic Experiencing, Buddhist Psychology, DBT, Play therapy, Motivational Interviewing, Attachment and Narrative Therapy My style is dynamic, collaborative, and validating. These frameworks and my past life experiences provide a lens through which I’ve learned how to offer compassionate, non-judgemental co-resonance. Building our relationship on a basis of shared respect and consent is a huge part of my practice. If you think we’d be a good fit, let's connect!

name: Becca Stock
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help clients heal from trauma, anxiety, and addiction using EMDR and compassionate care to uncover resilience and create lasting change.
ideal_client: I work with people feeling overwhelmed by stress, anxiety, trauma or behaviors like substance use that once helped but now feel like part of the problem. Together, we explore the pain and patterns behind these struggles to create new ways of coping and reconnect with your resilience. Whether it's past trauma, negative experiences, emotions or habits holding you back, my goal is to help you build a life that feels authentic, grounded and manageable.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use EMDR and somatic-based techniques to process trauma and desensitize triggers that fuel substance use. Ego-state therapy helps you connect with and heal different parts of yourself. For anxiety, trauma, mood disorders, and addiction, I use evidence-based approaches to shift patterns and improve coping strategies. Sessions are collaborative, safe, and focused on building resilience and helping you live authentically.

name: Ray Nelson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My approach to therapy is trauma-informed, social justice oriented, inclusive, and grounded in a humanistic framework. I have specialized training as a Holistic Sex Therapist. I help people live connected, authentic, and holistic lives.

approaches: You don’t have to do it alone! Finding a therapist who gets you can be life changing. I work collaboratively with my clients helping them focus on what they're struggling with in a safe, comfortable environment. I encourage my clients to reconnect with feelings and their bodies so they can stop repeating the patterns that are holding them back from who they really are.

I’m a rain loving, urban-dwelling Portlander. Prior to becoming a therapist, I worked in the trades as a DC power engineer and general contractor. In my spare time I enjoy building things, being snobbish about craft beer, B-grade shark movies, and doing outdoorsie things. My goal as a therapist is to provide a safe and compassionate environment that supports my clients in enhancing their awareness, acceptance, and self-expression as they move towards their best self.

name: Shelby Dobrich
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I work with clients (ages 8+) who may be experiencing anxiety, depression, or ADHD.
ideal_client: Raise your hand if you've ever felt personally victimized by your own brain. Let's put 'Regina George' in its place with a med plan that actually has your back. I believe in personalized care that respects the unique chemistry of your mind and your life. With an evidence-based approach, a touch of humor, and an open mind, I'm here to help you find solutions that truly fit you. Mental health care should meet you where you are and that's exactly what I strive to do.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: “My priority is to create a space where you feel safe and heard.” I believe in patient-centered care, where your needs and goals drive the treatment process. My approach is rooted in actively listening to your concerns, so we can collaboratively create a treatment plan that truly fits you. What motivates me most is seeing the positive changes in my clients’ lives. Together, we will work towards your success—helping you live life to the fullest.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a provider dedicated to exceptional care, I take a holistic approach to healing, addressing both the mind and body. This includes a combination of brief therapy and medication management, tailored to support your overall well-being.

name: Hadi Farah
title: Psychiatrist
intro: I'm a psychiatrist focused on psychotherapy, helping you gain deep self-understanding to navigate anxiety, depression, and life challenges.
ideal_client: I work with individuals seeking deeper understanding, whether struggling with anxiety, depression, life transitions, or feeling stuck. People who enjoy working with me are curious about their emotions, and relationships. I help those who feel overwhelmed by the past or worried about the future, guiding them toward clarity and balance. With a psychotherapy-focused approach, I provide a safe space for meaningful exploration and growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is rooted in deep exploration and understanding. I believe that lasting change comes not just from symptom management, but from uncovering the patterns, emotions, and experiences that shape your life. Rather than focusing solely on medication, I prioritize psychotherapy, offering a space for thoughtful conversations that lead to real insight and growth. My goal is to guide you toward clarity, balance, and a greater sense of awareness. Every person’s journey is unique, so I tailor my approach to fit your needs, whether that means exploring past experiences, addressing current challenges, or navigating future goals. All sessions are virtual, allowing you to engage in therapy from the comfort of your own space.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As a therapist, I value the integration of science and compassion in my work, always aiming to take an objective approach to understand your situation. I believe in listening deeply and giving you the time to explore your thoughts and feelings. I enjoy what I do and find meaning in building a collaborative relationship where you feel heard and understood.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a natural part of life—it’s a healthy motivator that helps us progress. A little anxiety can be beneficial, as it drives motivation and growth. However, when anxiety becomes overwhelming, it can become paralyzing, leading to excessive worry, panic attacks, insomnia, or obsessive thoughts. If you're struggling with these symptoms, it's crucial to address the emotions underlying them. With the right approach, many people see improvement within the first few weeks.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Families are fascinating. While they can be our greatest source of support, they can also trigger very intense negative feelings. When conflicts arise, many people try to cut ties, thinking it will resolve the issue. However, this often backfires, leading to even greater challenges in life. Rebuilding relationships on a calm, thoughtful basis is difficult but can bring lasting positive changes and personal growth. Addressing family conflict thoughtfully can improve your overall well-being.

name: April Taylor
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Hi I'm April, a Black therapist based in Portland, Oregon. I'm passionate about creating safe mental health spaces for women of color.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with women of color. Women I work with may find themselves feeling invalidated, isolated, or at a loss with how to move forward from difficult experiences. Maybe work, relationships, or other stressors are increasing feelings of worry or sadness? Do you require support with a difficult transition, desire to create boundaries, or increase positive communication skills?

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic style involves assisting clients in processing and gaining better understanding of emotions, habits, or relationships that may be impacting their life in an undesirable manner. This happens through the creation of a safe space that acknowledges intersecting identities, oppressive systems, and generational trauma often add extra stress and turmoil into the lives of women of color. I also aim to empower clients through normalizing help seeking, education about mental health, and believe no one is without skills, we just need a space to discover them. My hope is clients walk away with increased ability to maintain a level of mental health that feels appropriate for them, and life long tools to cope in the face of stressors.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I was born and raised in Portland Oregon, a city with little diversity. I have encountered much racism, and discrimination in the mental health field and beyond. This lack of diversity, along with narratives of harm I've come across led me to seek out a career in social work, and continue to pursue my MSW. I engage in therapy, particularly with women of color, with the goal of minimizing inequities, and increasing access to anti-racist mental health spaces. I'm hopeful that by being in practice I am increasing diversity in the field, minimizing one less harmful experience, and ensuring that more voices feel validated.

name: Barbara Biedrzycki
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a licensed professional counselor with several years experience treating depression, anxiety, and issues related to low self worth.
ideal_client: Are you ready to process thoughts and feelings that interfere with your desire to live a value driven life? Are you ready to explore the possibility of learning to love and accept yourself while making changes that you yearn for? If this sounds like a project you are interested in, curious about or ready to engage in I am here to help you get started. It is my belief that people have the ability to work through their problems when given the right tools, support and encouragement to do so.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My treatment approach draws from the theoretical framework of ACT (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy). This therapy focuses on pursuing a meaningful life through value driven behaviors and reducing the struggle brought on by problematic thoughts, feelings and behaviors in our lives. It is a highly effective intervention for treating depression, anxiety, chronic pain and other distressing conditions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have an MA from Lewis and Clark college in Counseling Psychology and am Licensed by the Board of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists. I have worked in community mental health since 2000 and have been in private practice mental health counseling since 2013. While I specialize in treating depression, anxiety and low self worth, I am also skilled and experienced in treating other mental health conditions that cause concern: Borderline Personality Disorder, existential issues, major life transitions, grief, loss and shame. I work primarily with populations over the age 17.

name: Brittany England
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: We will use an integrative mind-body-spirit therapy approach to help you move from suffering to more well-being and enjoyment of life.
ideal_client: My ideal clients are open, curious, and interested in approaching their mental health care from a holistic, mind-body-spirit lens. They are committed to self work and have a willingness to go inward, look into the places that may scare them, and have a deep desire for positive change. This isn't always easy, clean, or linear, so trusting the process is important. I will operate as a guide and will be here alongside you on your path.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The integrative Mind-Body-Spirit approach I offer allows us to navigate the subconscious mind in order to help you have a different experience of your past and present so you can create a better future. I aim to assist clients with creating safety in their bodies, utilizing somatic based approaches. Our beliefs about ourselves, our self-worth, whether or not we are lovable and worthy, our relationships with money, success, love, partnership, family, health, body image, self-esteem, etc. are all programmed by a very young age, which means that we are operating from an outdated belief system inside of us. Because of this, it is crucial to gain access to the subconscious programs we carry to bring awareness and transformation to the roots of the challenges we face in one or more areas of our lives. Since roughly 95% of your thoughts and beliefs are dictated by the subconscious mind, it is important to access the information in there that is no longer serving you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My integrative Mind-Body-Spirit approach is influenced by spirituality, EFT (meridian tapping), mindfulness, polyvagal theory, NLP, neuroscience & attachment theory. I have worked with clients in varying capacities in the field of mental health since 1998. I specialize in working with anxiety, depression, stress, sobriety from addictions, codependency, chronic illness & pain, relationship issues, food & body image, sexuality, loss of purpose & fulfillment, life transitions, spiritual awakenings, and women's issues. I practice from a somatic, spiritual, depth-oriented, relational, trauma-informed lens. I have extensive experience working with other therapists, counselors, healers, and practitioners who are also on the journey of growth, transformation, and healing. My intention with folks who have chronic illness, pain, or any recurring patten in one's life, is to facilitate acceptance of one's experience and to explore potential root causes through a mind-body-spirit lens.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: My Mind-Body approach that is rooted in somatic based interventions, meridian tapping techniques (FasterEFT & EFT), NLP, mindfulness and neuroscience. This approach allows us to work with the subconscious mind which is where your internal operating system lives. We will work together to help you tune into your somatic (body/physical) experience to help you gain more awareness of your internal experience. This holistic approach invites in the possibility for deeper healing and transformation.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: I use an integrative Mind-Body approach that is based in somatic embodiment, meridian tapping techniques (FasterEFT & EFT), NLP, hypnosis, mindfulness, polyvagal theory, attachment, and neuroscience. This approach allows us to work with both the subconscious mind which is where your internal operating system lives and the felt sense in the body. We will explore anything from the past or present that may hold you back, so you can create a better, more fulfilling future.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: My Mind-Body approach that is rooted in somatic based interventions, meridian tapping techniques (FasterEFT & EFT), NLP, mindfulness and neuroscience. This approach allows us to work with the subconscious mind which is where your internal operating system lives. We will work together to slow down and bring compassionate awareness and presence to your internal and external experience.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: The integrative Mind-Body approach I use allows us to go into your mind to the root of what is causing you depression. We will notice and examine the thoughts, images, beliefs, physical sensations, etc that all create the feeling of depression in your system, and we will address these using mind-body modalities in order to bring relief to your system.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Mind-Body healing professionals and the field of neuroscience believes that there is no separation of the mind/brain and body. They deeply influence one another. This means that your symptoms likely have an emotional root. I work with clients who have chronic pain /illness who continue to have symptoms despite medical treatment. We work to identify past experiences and traumas that are unresolved that may influence the manifestation of physical illness and pain.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: The integrative Mind-Body approach I use allows us to go into your mind to the root of what is causing you anxiety. We will notice and examine the thoughts, images, beliefs, physical sensations, etc that all create the feeling of anxiety in your system, and we will address these using mind-body modalities in order to bring relief to your system.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Whatever the relationship issue is you are facing, we will work together to address the root causes of the pain. Since our past informs our future and issues with our family of origin often play out in our current relationships, we will identify and explore potential unresolved issues that are preventing you from having the relationship you desire so you can make changes that support your well-being and your ability to create healthy relationships. I work with individuals only, not couples.

name: Abbie Nederhoed
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I love working with individuals and relationship systems. I specialize in non-monogamy, kink, gender, and sex therapy. Sliding scale avail!
ideal_client: Folks I often work with: non-monogamous relationships whether you are exploring opening a relationship or have been practicing non-monogamy for years, Kink and BDSM, relationship conflict and attachment wounding, painful sex, desire discrepancy, sexual trauma, gender and sexual identity. I enjoy working with complex trauma and have a background in mental health crisis work, I approach this work with understanding that the systems we navigate can at times be helpful, but can also cause harm.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Harm reduction is my unifying foundational perspective. I utilize narrative and humanistic frameworks and strive to be authentic and compassion driven, approaching each situation from an anti-oppressive, sex-positive, and intersectional perspective. Approaches I like to currently work with are: attachment, internal family systems, emotionally focused therapy. Shame and judgment are often inherent in the ways we cope, and change can be a difficult process. Mitigating any potential harm in how we cope, while continuing to build on existing skills is often an entry point into the work we can do together. One of my roles is to hold space for you to explore your most authentic self. I will also hold space for the ways you wish to navigate relationships and communities, while honoring that you may have to mask your identities to keep yourself safe within these systems.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As an agender, and queer individual who identifies within the kink and non-monogamous communities, lived experience within these identities helps me to understand that we do not exist on a binary. I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and I have training in sex therapy. Originally a Midwesterner, I moved from Michigan to Oregon in 2015. I have three tuxedo cats and more recently have adopted a 16 y.o grumpy grey boy (cat), I love coffee and cute spooky things.

name: Ryan MacPhee
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I am Ryan MacPhee, a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner who is accepting new clients for medication management and therapy.

name: Liz Ortland
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I believe everyone is capable of growth and healing. Let’s explore your inner world together to remove barriers to being your authentic self
ideal_client: I enjoy working with clients around learning who they are, building self-esteem, understanding neurodivergence, coping with life transitions, healing from past wounding, and creating a sense of belonging or meaning in life. I have experience working with clients from diverse cultural and language backgrounds, and supporting healthy communication in intercultural relationships.

approaches.My Background: In 2017 I graduated from Lewis & Clark College's Marriage Couple and Family Therapy program with a specialization in Sex Therapy. I gained experience working with refugees and low-income individuals, couples, families, and groups at Lutheran Community Services Northwest. I have recently returned from living in rural Japan where I provided teletherapy for English-speaking expats, repatriates, and Japanese citizens living throughout Japan from 2019-2023. Because of my experiences living abroad and working with immigrants both in the US and in Japan, I developed a deep appreciation for the importance of having a sense of belonging and safety in the world. I have a passion for working across cultural and language barriers to help people explore their identities and values, communicate more clearly with others, and to cultivate a life worth living.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I try to form a unique and genuine connection with every client, which means what I do looks a little different with everyone. Together you and I will co-create the healing space that works best for you. You are the expert on your own experiences. I am here to help you in listen more deeply to yourself to discover stuck patterns, shed light on disowned parts of yourself, identify needs you may have a hard time voicing, and unravel struggles with worthiness and barriers to living authentically. We may practice new coping skills, learn about trauma and the body, explore alternative ways to communicate needs / navigate relationships, and face challenging past experiences together through mutual dialogue. We may also bring in art, music, philosophy, spirituality, or whatever else it is that gives meaning to your world. I aim to empower you to take responsibility for your own growth and healing and emerge with more confidence in navigating your life, relationships, and decisions.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: As an existential humanistic therapist, my job is not to give you advice or promise to "fix" you. Instead, I am here to listen deeply to you as you explore your inner world and to act as a guide by shining light on areas in your life that you may be unaware of. My genuine curiosity about your lived experiences can help you to better understand yourself, which will reveal potential for change. I am not an expert, but a fellow traveler through life accompanying you on your journey of discovery.

specialities.name: Immigration/Acculturation
specialities.description: Moving to a new place can turn life upside down! Big shifts in environment can upend our support systems and make our usual ways of coping harder to access. Language and cultural barriers can be a background stress that drastically impacts our overall sense of well-being. As a fellow traveler who has experienced adjusting to a new place, I aim to help you find your footing, develop supports and a sense of belonging, and process difficult experiences in a safe and understanding space.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: As we are understanding more about neurodiversity, many people are recently receiving ADHD diagnoses in adulthood. In recent years I have gained experience helping late-diagnosed adults integrate and understand what ADHD means for them. Together we will explore your challenges and sensitivities as well as your strengths and skills. You will learn to accept your authentic self, to communicate your needs to others in more effective ways, and to create a life where you can thrive. Couples welcome!

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: It is my strong belief that all humans are worthy of love and connection. Low self esteem is a learned behavior that develops through attachment wounding, traumatic experiences, and societal oppression. Through deep listening and unconditional caring, I help clients to explore the origins of their inner critic, unravel struggles with worthiness, and identify their values. I help to untangle appropriate guilt from unhealthy shame and to re-balance self-acceptance with taking responsibility.

name: Kelle DeBruin
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: We are a group practice of diverse clinicians serving individuals, couples, and families with various needs.
ideal_client: Our clients are our priority. We see ourselves as collaborative in our approach to providing wellness to our clients. As a group practice, we are able to diversify our specialties and expertise as we work together with the client to provide the support and services that are needed.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Our practice started with just one clinician in 2018. Fast forward through a pandemic and a couple extra offices here and there - we have a group practice of diverse and talented clinicians dedicated to providing excellent care to our clients. With the original member (Kelle) as practice founder, our love for what we do shows up every day in how we work together and treat each client as the individual that they are. We have grown in numbers and in geography. We hope to have clinicians who are available to serve all parts of the great state of Oregon from bustling P-Town to more quiet out of reach areas in eastern, central, and southern Oregon. Currently we have clinicians who dedicate their services to teletherapy solely, and we have in person opportunities in the Portland metro area.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: With over a dozen clinicians in this practice we have an array of specialties, expertise, life experiences, and individual differences that make us able to fit most of the needs a client may have. Kelle DeBruin Counseling is intentional in our approach of honoring diversity and recognizing the importance of providing inclusive representation in the clinicians that serve our clients.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Society offers us a narrative of how life 'should be' or 'is supposed to be' according to the details of who we are and the life experiences that we have had along the way. Narrative Therapy approaches those spoken and unspoken stories of who we are supposed to be and allows for further understanding of the narrative and how we desire to construct our narrative moving forward.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: Out of the many things that can be understood better through the Gottman Method, two things that the Gottman Method allows us to focus on is our connection with our partner and how we approach communication with each other in our day to day life. I've done advanced trainings in the Gottman Method and commonly utilize the Couples Assessment conducted by the Gottman Method to work through areas of strength and challenge with couples.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive Based Therapy otherwise known as CBT, like all versions of cognitive based approaches, focuses on helping the client to become aware of their thoughts and feelings in order to understand how their thoughts influence their feelings in maladaptive or unhelpful ways. The goal of CBT is to change the patterns of thinking and behavior in order to change the way it makes the person feel.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Life offers us times where we recognize ourselves at the brink of significant life transitions. These transitions are part of life and when addressed well we can live fully in our lives and through these transitions. Interventions in session focus on awareness of movement and change throughout a person's life that allows for the acceptance that our past helps us understand our present and in that discernment can help support behaviors and expectations for our future.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Counseling is an important part of both pre-marital and marriage counseling as it enforces healthy communication patterns and emotional connection with each other. As these understandings becomes more clear for the couple, areas of emotional connection, mutual respect, commitment and desire for each other continue to develop and become meaningful aspects in the relationship.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I approach grief with education, support, and intuition. I find that the most challenging part of grief for people is the unpredictability and the loss of control that is felt as grief tends to take over various areas in people’s lives. To grieve is to acknowledge the loss of something significant in your life while also applying coping mechanisms.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I feel the client’s needs are best met when I am able to engage with the client in a genuine relationship that provides unconditional regard and support while also utilizing cognitive interventions that will aid the client into understanding who they are and changing their behavior in ways that allows them to live more fully into their present reality.

name: Laken Nelson
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi, I'm Laken (she/her) and I specialized in trauma and integrative healing of the mind and body.
ideal_client: Feeling hyperaware of your symptoms, experiences and self in general can be exhausting and often generate feelings of shame, guilt and frustration. You may feel stuck on where to go next once you've learned so much about yourself. Taking a break from your thoughts and dropping into your body can be both challenging and rewarding. You deserve a relationship with yourself that is healing, validating and nourishing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to supporting and helping people on their unique journey of healing is first and foremost collaborative. Therapy is challenging on its own and I strive for each person I work with to feel safe and supported to engage actively in deciding how their treatment goes. I've worked with adults who have experienced complex and chronic trauma that has negatively impacted their relationship with themselves and their ability to experience their emotions. I have experience working with folks who have tried therapy in the past and feel stuck with too much awareness and not enough support to move through and past challenges and problems. I work collectively with each client to identify their current relationship to and with their body when experiencing their emotions and collaborate from there times to weave in breath work, mindfulness, grounding exercises and other somatic interventions to support the relationship between mind and body.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe that everyone is capable and deserving of healing and connection. So many different experiences can impact and influence how we think, feel and function. Another impact on us as people are the various and intersecting identities we possess: partner, sibling, friend, student, parent, child, queer, trans, neurodivergent and that is just to name a few. I take all identities and experiences into consideration when working with folks because I believe that therapy cannot be done without that information. I value folks for all that they are and all that they might wish that they weren't with an aim to healing the relationship amongst all the parts of you through integrative healing with the mind and body. Our mind and bodies cannot exist without one another, yet we often operate as if they do. Reconnecting or plugging back into the body is scary and uncomfortable but it is also rewarding and has the ability to cultivate a healing experience for all your parts and identities.

name: Jenna Steen
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I believe the capacity to build the life you want is already within you. My role as therapist is to help you clear the way. ​
ideal_client: People come to therapy for all sorts of reasons. Perhaps you struggle with unwanted behavior patterns or difficulties in your relationships. Maybe you’re challenged by overwhelming emotions or struggle to know what you’re feeling at all. Or maybe you’re having trouble adjusting to new circumstances or making a big decision. These problems in living and many others may respond well to psychotherapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Studies confirm what I know to be true: the best predictor of therapeutic success is a secure, attuned therapeutic relationship. This means I meet you with compassion and listen without judgment, assumptions, or expectations. I respect your pace and honor the need to feel safe when sharing your story.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: At the foundation of my work is the belief that every human being has an innate ability to thrive. I offer acceptance, empathy, and my own authenticity to enable you towards growth and fulfillment. I believe the capacity to build the life you want is already within you. My role as therapist is to help you clear the way.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: Ever feel like you don't understand or can't explain your own choices or behavior? Depth therapy looks beneath the surface to explore underlying beliefs, feelings, and unmet needs that drive your daily life. We look at how early experiences & relationships shape the ways you show up today. I help you explore how habituated behaviors and thinking patterns that once served you might be holding you back. Depth therapy is a supported process of self-exploration that can lead to real, lasting growth.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: My goal is to help you deepen your relationship with yourself. Therapy offers the opportunity to slow down & explore what’s going on beneath surface-level content. I might ask you to pause and notice what’s happening in your body or mind as we talk, or to describe the feelings that comes to you. Bringing awareness to your here-and-now experience in this way is known to promote stress relief, emotional stability, and increase capacity for connection with others.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is a process, not a pathology. Grievers need a space where they're welcome to feel all their feelings without expectations or judgments. I specialize in helping the bereaved to make sense of the often difficult, sometimes overwhelming feelings and thoughts that arise in the wake of loss. I also work with those who support grievers-- partners, extended family members, friends-- to navigate grief stewardship.

name: Jake Bassen
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Hello there! I look forward to connecting and walking alongside you through some of life's toughest personal and relational roadblocks.
ideal_client: In my practice, I specialize in creating a highly relational therapy process which most often involves working with both you and your partner together to tackle relational challenges both acute and longstanding. No matter if you are dealing with huge life changes, struggles in communicating your needs with your partner, or navigating the fallout of infidelity or grief - I have experience helping couples from all walks of life and ages confront and rebuild the hardest parts of being in love.

approaches.My Background and Approach: It is my goal to help you find hope and empowerment both personally and for the relationships that matter most to you. In our work together, you can expect to find a supportive and safe space to explore and make steps toward changes you would like to see in yourself or in your relationship. I began practicing therapy in 2019 and have primarily focused my practice on working with couples, although I also see adult individuals for a variety of concerns including life transitions, relational challenges, men's issues, depression, and anxiety. I currently see clients at the Couples Clinic of Portland located in NW Portland. As a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT) I am trained in systemic couples and family therapy, Emotionally Focused Couples Therapy, and the Gottman Method.
