intro: Our work will be centered on your freedom, your joy, and your connection to what matters, no matter how long you’ve been away.
ideal_client: Are you are exhausted from the inner battle with your thoughts and feelings? Do you notice that the more you fight with them, the more stuck you feel? I thrive working with adults in high-performance careers (e.g., healthcare, law, athletics, tech) who have learned to achieve, optimize, or "perfect" their way through life's pains, including anxiety, complex trauma, grief, and substance use. You CAN get free from the struggle - it just might not be in the way that you think.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a bisexual/queer therapist, I recognize that aspects of privileged and marginalized identities are both visible and invisible. I aim to create a safe environment for my clients who have experienced oppression, discrimination, and prejudice based on aspects of their identity. The spirit of my therapeutic approach is deeply relational and egalitarian, and informed by social justice and culturally responsive care. I value the context of your life and learning history, including unique aspects of your identity, adaptive coping skills and strengths, and acknowledging the harmful impacts of hostile, oppressive, and/or discriminatory experiences and systems that may have contributed to your suffering. I bring an embodied, relational presence to our sessions. I will empower you to connect to your deeper sense of knowing, learn to flow with your inner experiences, and live a meaningful life, on your terms.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: When I started my graduate training, I hoped that my education would teach transcendence - at the time, I secretly hoped that meant not having to feel anything uncomfortable! As my training progressed, and both past and present life struggles appeared, I employed all of my familiar strategies to fight them. The harder I worked to try and achieve my way out of my own discomfort, I experienced how unworkable that effort became, and transcendence began to take on a new meaning - letting go of the struggle for control, being in compassionate presence with difficult emotions, and allowing for deep vulnerability. As I opened up to the flow of my own experience and full humanity, I made changes I never would have thought possible at the beginning of the long road to becoming a therapist - and I'm here to help you do the same!

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I have years of specialized training in ACT and its "sibling" relational therapy, Functional Analytic Psychotherapy (FAP).

name: Jona Behrer
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Jona (pronounced John-ah)! I specialize in women's issues, trauma and grief. Currently accepting new clients!
ideal_client: We live in a culture which impedes the development of women, systematically hurts women, and tries to silence women’s power. I am here to help! I specialize in women's issues, trauma, and grief. I help clients as they navigate difficulties with anxiety, attachment, depression, grief, loss, low self esteem, pregnancy, postpartum, relationships and trauma.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to counseling is trauma informed, humanistic, feminist and sex positive. I utilize techniques from Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy, Internal Family Systems, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, and Mindfulness. So what does all this mean? I collaborate with clients to build genuine and safe relationship. Using moment to moment awareness, I help clients deepen into and process their emotions. (Yes, you're in therapy to feel your feelings.) I will be there to help you regulate, make it feel less overwhelming, and make sense of it all. Through this process you will increase your self awareness, break out of unhelpful patterns, integrate new insights, learn coping skills and build resilience.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I bring my authentic self to my work with clients. My style is warm, attuned, compassionate, direct and passionate. I truly care about my clients, and this work. I care about your pain, and the injustices you have faced. The therapeutic relationship is one of depth and of great vulnerability. I encourage you to be discerning, and make sure you find someone who is the right fit for you. If you think that could be me, please reach out to schedule a free consultation to help you decide.

specialities.name: Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP)
specialities.description: Together we create a safe and secure therapeutic relationship. My presence in therapy is warm, attuned, & empathic. I help clients break out of patterns of anxiety and defense. Using moment to moment awareness, I support clients as they deepen into & process their feelings. I help clients regulate during emotional release; and to reduce feelings of overwhelm & aloneness. Following this process, I help clients to make sense of their feelings & note insights of change and healing.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: There are a variety experiences unique to women, or being female bodied. These experiences can be beautiful, deeply painful, traumatic and transformative. I help women cope with systemic oppression, rape culture, abuse, cycles of birth and loss, reproductive health, and sexuality. I help women to find their power, have stronger boundaries and a stronger sense of self.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Almost every person experiences some form of trauma in their life. For some, the resulting effect may be Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Symptoms of PTSD can be uncomfortable, and at times scary. Your trauma is something you can gain control over. Through our work together you will learn the coping skills you need to manage the symptoms of PTSD, regain a sense of safety, grieve and reprocess your trauma so that it no longer has a substantial hold on you.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Loss touches us all. In this life we will each have many griefs. You might be mourning a death of a loved one, an end of a relationship or change in health. I know this time is deeply painful. It is often confusing as you figure out life after this loss. I know it's hard right now, but it will get better. It will be easier with support. Grief has been one of the most profound teachers in my life. It would be an honor to help you through.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: Pregnancy and postpartum is a journey! It is a highly emotional time as you adjust to your changing body, relationship, and life. For some birthing persons old traumas may surface. Some might experience a traumatic birth. Everyone will agree that being a parent is hard, and sleep deprivation makes everything worse. It is common to experience mood disturbance after giving birth including worsening depression or anxiety. No matter what your experience is, you deserve support along the way.

name: Jennifer Trupe
title: Student Counselor
intro: Personal challenges and life difficulties can often be more manageable with the right support. You don’t have to face them alone.
ideal_client: I primarily work with individuals who are experiencing career-related stress, processing traumatic experiences, or seeking personal growth. My goal is to empower clients as they navigate their unique journeys toward healing and development. My ideal client is motivated to learn and committed to making meaningful, positive changes. While achieving balance can be challenging, a willingness to explore new perspectives and develop effective coping strategies can lead to rewarding outcomes.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am committed to reducing the stigma surrounding mental health, particularly with clients working in high-stress and high-risk careers. Individuals in high-stress professions often face intense pressure related to job performance, personal relationships, and public safety responsibilities. These demands can lead to anxiety, depression, and strained connections with family members, colleagues, and the broader community. My passion involves supporting clients and their families as they navigate these challenges. I aim to empower clients with effective coping strategies and help them cultivate a strong sense of self-worth. Through a holistic approach that addresses mental, physical, emotional, and spiritual well-being, I guide clients in developing healthy habits and achieving a sustainable life balance that promotes healing and resilience.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am currently serving as an Intern Counselor while actively working toward obtaining my Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) credential. I hold a Bachelor's degree in Interdisciplinary Studies with a focus on Social Sciences from Western Oregon University and am in the process of completing a Master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Grand Canyon University. My background includes several years of experience on a peer support team within the first responder community, where I completed training in motivational interviewing and advanced training in Critical Incident Stress Management (CISM). I believe that with the right support and skills, anyone can make meaningful, positive changes in their life. My goal is to help individuals develop self-acceptance and effective coping strategies—tools that can guide them through life’s most challenging moments and empower them to achieve their personal goals.

name: Darla Harrison
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer a non-judgmental safe space where you can feel accepted and understood. I am here to hold space for you!
ideal_client: I work with adults, primarily cis women and LGBTQIA+ folx. I love when clients are motivated to explore the hard stuff and to work toward positive change. I feel completely honored to support my clients through their journey, whatever that may look like.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Counseling can benefit anyone, but often it can be difficult to find a good counselor. My approach is respectful, non-judgmental and genuine. I support you and build upon your strengths to work toward positive change. I promote skill building and see the counseling relationship as a collaboration. Initiating change requires effort and my role is to support and encourage you in your efforts. I provide individual counseling. My specialties include anxiety, depression, self esteem, relationships, adjustment, trauma, family issues (parenting, divorce, conflict, relationships, etc.), women's issues (relationships, stress, trauma, adjustment, etc.). All of my counseling sessions are provided via teletherapy. Not only is it flexible, but also convenient, professional, and confidential. Call to see if I may be a good fit. I look forward to hearing from you!

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have been in practice for 18 yrs and have extensive training and experience working with symptoms of anxiety

name: Tamara Randall
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: With a strong commitment to helping others, I strive to make a positive impact on the world around me.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In my therapeutic practice, I prioritize creating a safe and non-judgmental space within the client-therapist relationship, recognizing that trust is the foundation for effective therapy. I understand that the journey of therapy can be challenging, and I use my clinical judgment to balance self-exploration with gentle encouragement to step outside of one's comfort zone. I firmly believe in the potential for every individual to be empowered to self-actualize and overcome limitations. My approach is deeply rooted in a commitment to social justice and equity, ensuring that all clients feel valued and respected as they work towards personal growth and healing.

name: Laura Marie Separa MA LPC MFT
full_name: Laura Marie Separa MA LPC MFT
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Establishing a sense of wholeness and direction in our lives is often revealed once obstacles are known and cleared This process of self discovery is far more potent and transformational when working with a therapist who can help navigate these unfamiliar places.

approaches: As a depth-oriented psychotherapist, I blend traditional talk therapy with the creative process and invite a deepening into the unfolding story of your life. With the exploration of symbolism, imagery, and self expression, opportunities for healing can arise which open new pathways, both internally and externally. I incorporate a model of treatment that includes cognitive modalities, emotional regulation, stress management, coping skills, behavior modification, and ways to address the unconscious processes and how they express themselves.Through this work, a deep level of integration emerges which serves to unleash unlimited potential for optimum growth.

I received my Masters degree from Pacifica Graduate Institute with an emphasis in Depth Psychology. I have also received additional training in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Motivational Interviewing, Cognitive Behavioral Skills, Mindfulness Training, and Marriage and Family Therapy. While these theoretical models provide a substantial framework for my practice, my work is largely informed by the personal experience of profound grief. Journeying through these difficult waters allows me to uniquely empathize and assist my clients through life struggles and losses.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: Depth Therapy is the theoretical framework of my graduate program, therefore, I feel knowledgeable and skilled in this area. My training included ways to integrate the unconscious material in our psyche, which is intrinsic to personal healing.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness-based psychotherapy is a process that engages the powerful and transformational tool of being aware of the present moment. It allows us to see clearly what is happening in our mind and heart, offering the opportunity for greater choice and the ability to create positive change. As the breath regulates the nervous system, attention toward stillness creates space for deep healing.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Personal growth often requires an exploration of our value system and step by step planning. A meaningful life can begin at any time and a simple willingness is all that is really needed to get started. We can work on your vision and what is necessary to create a life with intention and purpose.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: A hollow emptiness often characterizes the inner world of grief. This direct experience of mourning is the balancing act of a lifetime. My approach to understanding grief is to turn toward this empty space and to seek meaning within the loss. While this is a profound undertaking, it can often be the challenge that serves our greater purpose.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety often results from feeling overwhelmed and unprepared. While some anxiety is our bodys natural way of warning us of a possible threat, it can often feel like our lives are spinning out of control. Through mindfulness practices and centering techniques, we can begin to feel more empowered and less controlled by our emotional responses.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Feelings of depression are often taboo in our culture yet are often a natural result to loss and change. I believe there is wisdom beneath the dark times and holding ourselves with compassion serves to bring forth a deeper truth that can be transforming. Seeking to understand and allow the meaning of suffering to unfold takes courage and my personal experience of grief may act as a guide.

name: Kat Aguilar
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I provide a warm, compassionate, and non-judgemental space to facilitate growth and healing.
ideal_client: You find yourself numb, feeling as though life is passing you by and you're just going through the motions. You have this idea of how your life is supposed to be, but you feel stuck and not in control over your free will. You may feel shame, guilt, heaviness, and overwhelm. I hope to create a safe space for you to explore those hardwired thoughts and beliefs. You deserve to experience life in a new light, to reduce suffering, and freedom to find peace in your well-being.

approaches.How I Can Help You: There are many ways to experience life, and everyone's journey is different. I hope to grow our therapeutic relationship from a place of openness, trust, gentleness, and compassion. I take a collaborative approach towards counseling, blending techniques to best serve each person and welcoming feedback to increase trust and collaboration. I integrate several orientations to achieve a well-rounded perspective to address and explore the stressors that life has brought onto you. I am happy to meet with you for a free consultation to discuss your goals and determine if I am a good fit for your needs.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Each of my clients deserve my undivided attention. I can best be reached by email for inquiries and consultation scheduling.

name: Kori Kramer
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I have immediate availability. I provide compassionate, supportive therapy services via telehealth.
ideal_client: I work with adults with all kinds of issues, including depression, anxiety, ADHD, trauma, relationship stress, parenting stress, grief and loss, life transitions, etc. I also have specific experience and enjoy working with folks who struggle with substance use and/or eating disorders. I am passionate about social justice and incorporate this lens with all of my patients. I strive to be gender and LGBTQ affirming and have sought out specific coursework to support this effort.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I see my job as a counselor as being a supporter of your work to know, grow, and use your own wisdom and strength to move toward your goals. My approach is a combination of multiple methods. I tend to think about cases through the lens of biopsychosocial, existential, attachment, and person-centered theories. In terms of skills, I lean toward dialectical behavioral therapy (DBT), cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT). More importantly, I like to see what works for you as an individual and adjust the ideas and skills I bring into our sessions to fit your needs. I am also aware of how power, privilege, and oppression can affect our work together. I invite discussion around this and seek to lessen the impact of any imbalance. My goal is to empower you as the client to have choice and autonomy in our work together.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Being a therapist is one of the greatest honors of my life. I am continually humbled by the opportunity to witness and support my clients in their courageous efforts to understand, heal, and grow beyond the difficulties they experience. After all of the hard things they have been through, my clients still take the risk to trust me, to open up, to try to do the thing they are not sure they can actually do. I feel fortunate to get to be a part of such incredible work every day.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I have worked with adolescents and adults with eating disorders in both residential and outpatient settings.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I have my CADC-I and extensive experience working with men and women in early recovery from substance use disorders.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: I have my CADC-I and extensive experience working with men and women in early recovery from substance use disorders.

name: Katrina Severin
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: My style is authentic and assertive, while maintaining trust in your innate ability to heal. I work with couples and individual adults.
ideal_client: I have experience working with Trauma, depression, anxiety, chronic pain, disability, relationship issues, boundaries, attachment, codependency, identity development, and much more. I enjoy working with neurodivergent and LGBTQIA+ folks, as well as couples who are working to liberate themselves from patriarchal roles and relationship patterns. I am committed to ongoing anti-racism and anti-oppression work, and bring a complex understanding of my own intersections of privilege and oppression.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Prior to becoming a therapist, I completed a BA in Global Anthropology from University of the Pacific in 2014. My studies encompassed various aspects of culture and the human experience, which continues to inform my worldview and my understanding of human nature. In 2022, I completed a MS in Clinical Rehabilitation Counseling, which focused on the disability experience from a biopsychosocial perspective. I use an integrated multicultural, anti-oppression, feminist, trauma-informed, and person-centered approach that draws from Gestalt therapy, Jungian psychology, Internal Family Systems, Polyvagal theory, somatics, and mindfulness. I also draw personally from various sources of wisdom and creativity, including astrology, Quantum theory, art and poetry, ancestry, breath and movement, plant medicine, and the Chakra system.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: We will all die someday - and yet, we often forget to live while we are alive. We are all born into circumstances beyond our control, and many of us do not get what we need in the crucial years of development. We find beautifully creative ways to adapt in service of our survival, only to become unconsciously stuck in rigid postures and patterns that keep us defended, reactive, and deeply unsatisfied as we move through the ever-changing conditions of our lives. In our work together, I can help you to increase your awareness of these patterns, review the scripts you've been given, and increase your capacity for agency and choice as you learn to listen more deeply to your own voice. In our work together, I will help you to honor your body as a historical record keeper, a deep source of wisdom, and a vessel for transcendence. I look forward to supporting you in living a life of meaning.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I hold a Master's degree in Clinical Rehabilitation Counseling, which focuses on the disability experience from a social justice perspective. I have familiarity with conditions such as fibromyalgia and other types of chronic pain.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have experience working with trauma using somatic approaches, guided meditation and visualization, and Internal Family Systems.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I can help you understand the ways in which you show up in relationships from an Attachment lens, while building skills for self-soothing and regulation of your nervous system. I will work with you in defining, establishing, and maintaining healthy boundaries in all types of relationships. My work with couples is grounded in the Gestalt model of relating.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I identify as queer, and can offer safety and understanding around sexual and gender identity issues.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: I completed my internship at a clinic focused primarily on supporting immigrants and refugees, as well as various other system-impacted populations. My personal identities as a queer, neurodivergent woman from an impoverished and religious background also inform my understanding of power and privilege. I am committed to ongoing personal and professional work around anti-racism and anti-oppression.

name: Mahina Therapy PLLC
title: Student Counselor
intro: Mahina Therapy PLLC envisions a world in which all underrepresented people have access to quality mental health services that honors them.
ideal_client: Do you feel disconnected or alone? Misunderstood or unheard in your relationships? Struggling to process through relationship or family trauma? Oftentimes, we hold deep feelings of shame, sadness, anger that manifest as irritability, depression, and anxiety that are impacted not only by our life experiences, but also by the world and communities we exist within. I see reconnection (to self, others, community, nature) as the best coping mechanism to many of the problems we experience. I hope to h

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Mahina Therapy PLLC has a mission to provide outpatient mental health services, ADHD + Autism Evaluations, and Gender-Affirming Care to marginalized communities who have been systematically under-served within the mental health field. The clinicians at Mahina Therapy are trained to help you wherever you - and your relationships - are needing additional support in life. Our mission is to provide outpatient mental health services, ADHD + Autism Evaluations, and Gender-Affirming Care to marginalized communities who have be systematically under-served within the mental health field. Clients can expect conversations around macro-systems and to be challenged when they show up in the room with any clinician with us.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Mahina Therapy PLLC believes that therapy is inherently political, thus our stance within the mental health community and with our clients reflects that. We stand with the LGBTQQIP2SA community, Palestinian and Congolese people experiencing systemic genocide, and the Black Lives Matter Movement. We dedicate ourselves to continuous education to be anti-racist, trans-affirming, the Fat liberation (HAES) movement, and kink/sex affirming. Mahina Therapy is QTBIPOC-owned, thus our politics reflect this dedication to systemically marginalized communities. Mahina Therapy PLLC holds a firm stance against racism, xenophobia, queer phobia, transphobia, misogyny, ableism, fatphobia, classism, and any systems of oppression which discriminate against folx with marginalized identities. Clients can expect conversations around these systems and to be challenged when they show up in the room with any clinician or student intern employed at Mahina Therapy.

name: Family Ties Counseling Center
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: also LCSW, PsyD, LPC, Associate, and Intern clinicians
intro: We are a group therapy practice committed to providing compassionate, affirming care.
ideal_client: We are invested in hiring a diverse staff to provide anti-oppressive and inclusive therapy, supporting those in the QTBIPOC (Queer, Trans, Black, Indigenous, People of Color) communities. We believe it is our ethical responsibility as therapists and members of our community to provide affirming care to empower our clients.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: Here at FTCC, we believe in the strength of healing through relationships. We hold an expanded and limitless view of what family can be; we empower each of our clients to define for themselves what and who family is for them. When you’re a client at FTCC, you’re supported by a team of therapists who are dedicated to enriching the lives of you and your loved ones. As a collaborative group practice, we ensure that your whole family gets the care and resources they need. We provide child and family therapy, intimate relationship counseling, individual therapy, teen therapy, group counseling, art therapy, and ecotherapy.

approaches.Why We are a Good Fit for You: Our diverse staff addresses myriad concerns, including: relationship struggles, anxiety and depression, parenting, ADHD and neurodiversity, identity, sexual health, school concerns, life transitions, trauma, cultural and systemic oppression, and eco/climate anxiety, among others. Our clinicians offer a wide range of therapeutic modalities to fit you and your family's needs, always from a trauma-informed, anti-racist, gender-affirming perspective, including (but not limited to): attachment-based therapies, art therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), ecotherapy, dialectical behavioral therapy (DBT), intergenerational, internal family systems (IFS), play therapy, and EMDR.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: We are here to support all forms of intimate relationships, working with folx to help them achieve the connected relationships they envision.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: We our a group practice comprised of systemic therapists who believe in the power of healing through relationships. Our unique model allows for clinician collaboration to treat your whole family.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: We believe in "good enough parenting" - there is no such thing as being a perfect parent. Our compassionate therapists offer services to enrich the relationships between children and their caregivers.

name: Fiona Chen
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am passionate in enhancing clients self care, self esteem, and self motivation, by using a compassionate and non-judgmental approach.
ideal_client: I have expertise in emotional disturbance, stress, anxiety, self esteem, relationship issues, adjustment issues (relocation, life stage transition, fertility and new parenthood, etc.), identity and cultural issues, family of origin, and trauma history.

approaches.How I Can Help You: * telehealth service only *Individual Therapy (no couples therapy) *Oregon & age 18-64 *Office Hours: Tue & Thur 9am-3pm, Fri 9am-2pm

name: Robin Magdahlen
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I believe strongly in the human potential for growth and change especially during times of difficulty and personal crisis.
ideal_client: Our wounds and past experiences can get in the way of our ability to connect deeply and be open to love, forgiveness and change. I work with individuals and couples who are wanting to enrich and transform their ways of being and relating. Some come into therapy spurred by a crisis, others are seeking deeper self-awareness. I work best with clients who are collaborative and open to listening to themselves. I believe strongly in the human capacity to heal and thrive.

approaches.How I Can Help You: Each person, couple and family are unique. I include a blend of conventional and alternative approaches, drawing upon a variety of styles and techniques to incorporate what would be most helpful for you. With sensitivity and compassion, I enable you to build upon your strengths and to identify and achieve your life goals. Some of these modalities include but are not exclusive to EFT Couples, Attachment Theory, EMDR, Interpersonal Nuerobiology.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have had a background in working with marginalized populations including incarcerated women, crisis intervention, abused and neglected animals, elders and special needs children. I believe strongly in Equity. My intention is to be an agent of healing and change one person, one couple, one family at a time, so that we move closer to being part of a greater human family. My Specialties Include: Telehealth - Tele-Therapy, Couples Counseling, Divorce Coaching, Families — Adoption/Divorce/Blended Families, Adult Adoptee/Birth Parent Reunification, Pre — Marital Counseling, Depression, Anxiety, Grief/Loss, EMDR, Crisis Intervention and Stabilization, Mediation, Substance Abuse, Animal Bereavment, Positive Aging, Senior Life Transitions, Mediation, Individual and Group Drama Therapy.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing, is a late-stage, trauma resolution method. Developed in the late 1980's, EMDR currently has more scientific research as a treatment for trauma than any other non-pharmaceutical intervention. Based on empirical evidence as well as thousands of client and clinician testimonials, EMDR has proven an efficacious and rapid method of reprocessing traumatic m

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: In therapy, we will be co-creating a safe place, where there is room for any and all vulnerable feelings, beliefs, and thoughts to emerge. I work in a no-shame no-blame zone of ongoing support and warm curiosity. Together we will learn about patterns, triggers, negative thoughts and cycles, feelings, past and present attachment injuries, and how they affect the relationship.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotionally focused therapy proposes that emotions themselves have an innately adaptive potential that, if activated, can help clients change problematic emotional states or unwanted self-experiences. Emotions themselves do not inhibit the therapeutic process, however learning better coping strategies enables clients to move through old behaviors and patterns into a state of increased well being.

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: The decision to end a significant relationship can be a difficult and challenging process that leaves everyone depleted, confused and anxious about the future and how to move forward. Therapy can assist in working through those feelings, make sense of the end of ones relationship, and obtain a new perspective and healing.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I bring compassionate, practical tools and a common sense approach that enables you and your partner to improve your communication, deepen intimacy, build trust and resolve long-standing issues, in an environment that is safe and non-judgmental. I work collaboratively to provide tools and results that feel durable and long lasting.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is a highly personal experience and is often not a linear process. There is no right or wrong way to grieve, only your way. However, to undergo the process alone can feel very isolating. Counseling can assist in this process, so that you can effectively grieve in a way that allows for the building of new coping strategies and ultimately allow you to move forward.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: The recent outbreak of Covid-19 can be stressful time that can produce increased feelings of overwhelm and cause strong emotions. I hav many years experience working with crisis intervention, anxiety and PTSD and through a variety of interventions can provide tools and support for you during this time. I am currently offering on-line support.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I include a blend of conventional and alternative approaches, drawing upon a variety of styles and techniques and the latest in neuroscience research to incorporate what would be most helpful for you. With sensitivity and compassion, I assist you to in healing in a way that fits your pace and learning style.

name: Dr. Reece Henrichs-Beck
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I believe all of us inherently have what we need to heal, change, and grow when provided the right conditions.
ideal_client: I have over 13 years of experience working with people from all backgrounds in a wide array of settings. I specialize in trauma treatment, particularly complex, developmental, and family trauma. Some of my other specialty areas include the LGBTQ+ community, relationship issues, identity, men’s issues, codependency, living in recovery, and family concerns, including adult children of alcoholic/dysfunctional families.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Being asked and invited to be with someone in the process of healing and change is a true privilege and deeply meaningful to me. As a therapist, I seek to provide a secure and open space in which clients experience being seen, heard, and known. Clients describe me as warm, caring, honest, and authentic. My therapy style is relational, process-focused, and experiential. This means that I will guide us in using the relationship between you and I as a space to support your growth and change. It also means that both the content of therapy (what we are talking about) and the process of therapy (what is happening as we are talking and interacting) are both important for us to engage with. Lastly, it means that I will offer activities ("exploring by doing") that will help you learn more about yourself, develop new choices, and have new experiences in support of your therapy goals.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I specialize in attachment-based EMDR.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Particularly complex, developmental, and family trauma.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I provide therapy to support relationships of all kinds. I am poly and ENM-affirming.

name: Marina Nelson, MC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: The foundation of my practice is a deep respect for your healing capacity and the ability to teach you how to access it experientially.
ideal_client: If you are tired of saying "I know it, but I don't feel it", you may be looking for experiential therapy. Many methods of counseling work issues from the "top-down" (i.e. moving from our thinking experience "down" to our feelings). When that method hasn't entirely worked for you, you may benefit from a "bottom-up" approach, where we re-organize our feeling experience and then focus on our thinking, rather than focusing on thinking first. In trauma work, the felt experience guides healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I strive to make the process as experiential and whole person integrative as possible to make change and healing as easy as possible. Customization and collaboration are important since you are the expert on you. When people have experienced traumas, EMDR and Sensorimotor Psychotherapy (developed from Hakomi) are effective and gentle ways to process and resolve those experiences. Even if talking about the events is difficult, they can be dealt with using mind-body integration. I am also Certified in Trauma-Informed Stabilization Therapy (an Internal Family systems {IFS} based method that incorporates mindfulness & somatic awareness, too). If you've been afraid to address the past or feel like you're just managing symptoms instead of living life fully, this work may be for you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I use many modalities to support my clients' self-healing in a gentle, self-paced manner. My training includes: * EMDR Certified Therapist * Trauma-Informed Stabilization Therapy Certified Therapist (an IFS-based modality that incorporates mindfulness, somatic awareness, etc) * IFS (Level 1) in on-going consultation towards certification * IFS-Informed EMDR Level 3 in on-going consultation towards certification * Sensorimotor Psychotherapy Levels 1 & 2 (somatic AKA mind-body integration), * Hypnotherapy (Level 3) * Mindfulness ***For the time being, all services are offered in an online format only***

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am certified in EMDR through EMDRIA and in ongoing consultation. I am Level 3 trained in IFS-Informed EMDR through the Syzygy Institute and in on-gong consultation towards certification in that modality as well.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I am Level 1 trained and in ongoing consultation towards certification.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I have numerous trainings in mindfulness based modalities including DBT, MBSR, and Sensorimotor Psychotherapy. Additionally, have practiced meditation for over 30 years.

specialities.name: Sensorimotor
specialities.description: I have completed certificates for Levels 1 (trauma & emotional regulation) & 2 (relationship and attachment issues). Sensorimotor Psychotherapy (originated by Pat Ogden), has its roots in Hakomi and incorporates neuroscience.

specialities.name: Hypnotherapy
specialities.description: I have advanced training from the American Society of Clinical Hypnosis and some affiliates in acute pain, surgery preparation and supporting medical recoveries. Most services will require a consultation with your medical provider.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I have training in Trauma-Informed Stabilization Therapy (TIST), hypnotherapy and Sensorimotor psychotherapy for addressing pain management issues.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I specialize in trauma-informed services and have studied and implemented these practices even before completing graduate school. EMDR, TIST, and Sensorimotor Psychotherapy (somatic mindfulness) were designed for this purpose and work well for the mental and physical release of trauma in a gentle, effective manner.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: I believe trauma-informed services are especially relevant to compassion fatigue as the cost of caring has a cumulative effect. Also, professional and non-professional caregivers are often disinclined to acknowledge let alone care for their own needs. EMDR and IFS are both very useful for identifying and "upgrading" core beliefs that keep people habitually over-giving to others and under nurturing themselves.

name: Kelly Rees
title: Clinical Sexologist
intro: I am organizing groups for perimenopausal and menopausal support now!
ideal_client: My clients are varied. They are queer, straight, monogamous, poly, or questioning. They may have been married for a really long time or never at all. They may be single. They may feel sex is very important or they may feel differently. They are intelligent and curious, willing to work to make a more fulfilling life for themselves and each other. They may be wanting to build relationship skills or to develop more confidence. They may be in love or in longing or grieving. They are complex.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I focus on intimate relationships, sexual expression, disparate desire, shifting intimacy, alternative relating styles, polyamory. This often includes performance issues, the impact of aging and menopause, dealing with grief and jealousy. I have experience working with differing abilities and my clients range in age from mid-twenties to mid-nineties. I aim to engage the mind and heart while centering on the body. Pleasure is important and a great way to learn!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been an Intimacy and Sexuality coach since 2008, and completed my PhD in Human Sexuality in 2018. I am a board certified Sexologist with a background in neo-Tantra. I have been guiding people into clarity around their sexuality since 2003. I also work with those in recovery from drug/alcohol addiction and their specific issues around sex and relationships.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Consensual non-monogamous relationships can be very complex! I have extensive personal experience navigating them and can offer guidance on decision-making to preserve health and sanity. Finding the right type of relating can make the difference between chaos and richness. We will consider which boundaries serve you best and how you can maintain them.

specialities.name: Aging Concerns
specialities.description: As we advance in years our sexual relationships may change. Bodies change, interests change. Our culture is at a loss for what healthy, vibrant sexuality looks like in older people. There is no age at which sex becomes inappropriate! It is possible to manage aging in a realistic way around sex. Sexuality may awaken and flourish after you've given up on it, and it may take on different dimensions.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I have worked at a drug and alcohol recovery center since 2016. I provide support for those dealing with addiction in the areas of sexual health, true consent, setting and maintaining boundaries, addressing past trauma, harm reduction, and reclaiming healthy sexual pleasure.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: Sexual types of problems might be the most difficult to talk about due to rampant shame and guilt in which we are immersed as a culture. Sexual problems are almost always related to relationship issues, which give glimpses into our deepest selves. I have extensive experience guiding people through their sexual problems and into ease.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Unprocessed grief can hold us back from living. If you have suffered a terrible loss, we can work together to bring light and air in the wounded places, thereby releasing you to live more fully. Often sexuality is deeply impacted by grief because so many feelings are accessible through sex.

name: Kerry Powers, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We all have uniquely rich and complex stories that shape who we are or aspire to be. I believe we all are evolving and deepening in our individual and interpersonal work. I offer an environment that invites clients to access their deepest, most true selves & a partnership that supports the process.

approaches: I provide a safe, encouraging and non-judgmental therapeutic environment. My style is warm, collaborative and direct. Compassion and humor are vital ingredients for growth and wellness. My approach is integrative; drawing from strengths based, trauma-informed, relational, social justice and anti-oppression perspectives. I place great value on being able to deeply witness, understand and hold space for you in your moments of pain and uncertainty. Some life challenges have the capacity to derail, uproot, and halt us from harnessing our power to live the lives we desire. As a counselor, I place strong emphasis on developing insight & empathy to address and resolve problems, change patterns, improve relationships, heal trauma & navigate hardships. I hope to offer a transformative therapeutic experience that will enable you to realize your goals. Together we will cultivate the skills, insight and draw on your inner strength to benefit you years beyond our time together.

In 2007 I received my M.A. in Counseling Psychology from Lewis and Clark College. I have 22 years of social service and counseling experience serving adolescents, adults and families. My background is in trauma recovery, grief and loss and medical and health psychology. I have served older adults and families through adjustment, chronic illness, end of life issues and caregiving. My community counseling work encompassed a wide range of issues with an emphasis on navigating transitions, relationships and mood disorders. I value existential work, helping clients navigate transitions and deepen in their own process of identity development and self-actualization. I place great value on cultural competency, advocating for social justice and the eradiction of all forms inequality and oppression. I endeavor to deepen in my own personal & professional evolution striving to be congruent with the principles I impart.

specialities.name: Coronavirus/COVID-19
specialities.description: This is a time trauma, uncertainly and profound grief and hardship for our community, our country and the world. If you are fearful and navigating stabilty and economic hardship concerns, health concerns, fear, stress or anxiety for you or a loved one, you are not alone. I would love to support you. Presently I am offering telehealth therapy sessions.

specialities.name: Family Caregiving
specialities.description: Caring for a loved one is tremendous act of love an can be a highly stressful and complicated experience. It's important to know that your own self-care is paramount to being an effective caregiver. I am experienced in working with caregivers and their loved ones who are coping with a chronic medical and or psychological impairment. Having access to resources, education and support is essential.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Having a healthy sense of self is vital to feeling worthy and capable of manifesting the life you long for. We all experience wounds and hardships that serve to invalidate or diminish our sense of value. It is important that you understand the unique qualties that you possess and learn to move through the world holding your power, this is a process that can be reclaimed in our work together.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief exists in many forms from a loss of a dream or opportunity, personal power, a loved one, a health diagnosis or impairment. It is vital that you have a safe and supportive place to process feelings of anguish or sorrow and in time arrive at healing. Much of my clinical work has centered around loss and navigating transitions with a commitment to honor your experience with compassion.

name: Elizabeth (Liz) Ash
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello! My name is Liz Ash and I am a Professional Counselor Associate. I’d love to hear your story and how I can play a part in it.
ideal_client: Do you have difficulty with feeling overly sensitive, not knowing what helps you in times of trouble, or focusing on what’s important to you? Maybe you desire structure, consistency, or the ability to stand up for yourself or others you care about? If your dreams and hopes for confidence, community, and creativity aren't developing strong roots in your life, please get in contact with me as a strong action towards cultivating that growth. Most experienced with LGBTQ+ and trauma survivors.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I like to start with a building a trusting relationship/therapeutic alliance where your voice and opinions on problems and care are equally important in the room. My approach is person-centered, meaning we focus on you as an individual. Other ways we pursue understanding is to explore with intersectional feminist theory, which considers how different aspects of your identity (like gender, race, and class) affect your experiences and nature-based techniques (using the healing power of nature). Other conversations we might have would involve Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) which encourages accepting your thoughts and feelings, Motivational Interviewing which helps you find the motivation to change, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) which helps change negative thought patterns. I highly encourage bibliotherapy which involves reading/listening to materials to supplement the changes being made.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Before I became a therapist, I know when I needed help that I needed someone to sit through the storm of it with me, to accept me a human being (flaws and all), and to listen to me carefully. My hope to is to hold this understanding with you and continue exploring the infinite realm that is the human experience. My values now are to facilitate the space for you to establish your understanding of your whole self and to see what creative paths it will take to create the life you desire.

name: Stephanie Caballero
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I value and believe that compassion for others and oneself is a sign of strength. With compassion and patience, we can overcome challenges.
ideal_client: My work extends from providing therapy to clients with Autism Spectrum Disorder to adults needing support with understanding a family member with ASD. I enjoy working with parents needing a space to vent about the challenges in navigating multiple roles. I work with Latinx adults seeking support regarding identity concerns due to acculturation or upbringing. I help clients work on developing self confidence and learning ways to set boundaries due to various issues.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I allow the therapeutic relationship to build naturally in a relaxed space where the client leads the session. We jointly set your goals and subsequently analyze how your past, present and future are causing negative emotions. We dive into your life narrative to help you find self acceptance and new meaning for your future. During this time I integrate various challenges to help you find answers that support self analyses as well as understanding of others. Sessions may include relaxation skills, such as breathing, visualization or meditation. I often utilize metaphors to increase self awareness and increase confidence in attempting interventions discussed in sessions. I find that therapeutic relationships that are rooted in genuine kindness and a welcoming presence strengthens the progress of therapy because it shows our humanity as therapists.

approaches.Why We Started this Group Practice: Mind Body Soul Mental Health was started by my husband, Dr. David Ixtlahuac PsyD, LMFT, and me. It is a long time dream to open up our practice that focused on our specialties and serves various populations in the city of Portland, including Latinx individuals. Through our experiences and training we’ve found success in treating the whole person: Mind, Body and Soul. We focus on body concerns or responses, neurodiverisity, development, cultural upbringing, identity concerns and welcome discussions about spirituality. I am a first generation Latina with parents born in El Salvador and Peru. I lived in Peru during my childhood and saw first hand the disparities between class differences in a third world country. Coupled with my education in Multicultural Studies, I learned that countries of origin, immigration waves and financial standing contributes to various diasporas in the United States which affect the children of Latino immigrants, faced with challenges growing up here.

specialities.name: Sensorimotor
specialities.description: I am trained and certified in DIR/Floortime.

name: Congruent Therapy: Alexandra Scott
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: New Religious Trauma Group. Alexandra work with individuals, diads, and poly systems. Come as you are.
ideal_client: I'm Alexandra, and I'm more than just a therapist—I'm a compassionate guide on your journey toward self-discovery and authentic connections. Growing up in a religious environment, I know firsthand the challenges of reconciling personal beliefs with societal norms, especially when it comes to matters of identity and relationships. My own experiences have led me to embrace inclusivity and openness in my practice.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Whether you're an individual navigating your own path, a couple facing challenges, or part of a poly system exploring the depths of connection, I'm here to support you every step of the way. I understand that each person's journey is unique, which is why I take an individualized approach to therapy. Together, we'll explore your identity, life choices, and any societal norms that may be holding you back from living authentically. At the core of my practice are values like boundary-setting, communication, and collaborative problem-solving. I don't just talk the talk—I walk alongside you, modeling healthy behaviors and providing you with the tools you need to build fulfilling relationships and lead a genuine life. I'm all about tailoring therapy to fit you like a glove. Whether you're a couple, an individual, or part of a poly system, I recognize that your experiences and needs are as unique as you are. In my toolkit, you'll find a diverse range of evidence-based modalities.

approaches.More About the People We Treat: From Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) to Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (TF-CBT) to Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), `Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), yoga, mindfullness, and more, I've got you covered. But it's not just about having a bunch of fancy techniques up my sleeve—it's about knowing when and how to use them to best serve you. That's where my expertise comes in. By integrating these modalities, I can effectively address a wide variety of concerns, from navigating tricky emotions to overcoming past traumas and everything in between. So, whether you're looking to untangle the knots in your relationship, conquer those inner demons, or simply find more joy and fulfillment in life, I'm here to help you.

name: Antonia Vee
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide a safe, non-judgmental space that opens and supports all possibilities for healing mind, body, heart and spirit.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is mindfulness-based, trauma-informed and derives from the perspective that the body, mind and spirit are deeply interconnected. I believe that we all have the innate capacity to experience vitality, joy and wholeness. My work involves guiding individuals to tap into this potential, and fully realize their own inner-strength, truth, beauty and wisdom. I place an importance on therapist-client collaboration, and I provide a safe, inclusive and non-judgmental space. I am LGBTQ2SIA+ affirming. My demeanor is both gentle and compassionate, as well as direct and honest. I utilize mindfulness and somatic-based psychotherapies such as Somatic Experiencing and Hakomi as well as positive psychology, psychodynamic and cognitive-behavioral therapies that promote self-awareness, healing, integration and self-compassion.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a Master of Arts in Art Therapy/Counseling from Marylhurst University as well as a Bachelor of Science in Psychology and a Post-Baccalaureate in Women’s Studies from Portland State University. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC). I have specialized training and experience in working with issues pertaining to intimate partner violence, spirituality, addiction, mood disorders, anxiety, attachment and trauma recovery. And, I take part in ongoing post masters education around evidenced-based therapeutic practices, mindfulness, somatic mind/body modalities. I am also a professional member of the American Counseling Association and EMDR International Association.

name: Sarah Dykes
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I invite you to join me, with courage and self-compassion, to access your wise self.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Whether you are new to counseling or have experience in therapy, I provide a safe, judgment-free space to explore your inner experience and truth. I use experiential therapeutic tools to sift through the layers. My approach is integrative, humanistic, and strengths-based.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In 2017, I finished my Master’s Degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Portland State University. My experience included a yearlong internship at William Temple House working with diverse individuals in transition. As a Registered LPC Intern in the State of Oregon, I am under the supervision of Karen Hixson, PhD, LPC. I finished training as a massage therapist at the Oregon School of Massage in 2003, and practiced for seven years. This experience continues to inform my understanding of how we carry our lived experience in our bodies. I completed a B.A. in Human Services from the University of Oregon in 1993, and for the next twenty-five years worked with children, youth, families and adults in community based organizations, workforce development, and higher education in Portland, Oregon.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: We all have basic needs for compassion and connection in our lives. We deserve to be treated with respect in our human experience.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I believe we all seek meaning in understanding our truth.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: My style is integrative and includes mindfulness and body awareness.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I use an integrative bio, psycho, social approach to working with clients experiencing depression and anxiety. I draw from LifeSpan Integration, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Narrative Therapy, Internal Family Systems and somatic strategies.

name: Dani Dierking
title: Licensed Art Therapist
intro: I am currently full but building a short waitlist for adult art therapy clients.
ideal_client: I offer individual art therapy to adults and specialize in the treatment of developmental trauma, neurodivergence and chronic pain/illness. I support folks in working through the pain points of life through art and reconnect with themselves along the way.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I firmly believe that all people are unique and all people are worthy of care. I feel honored everyday to create a space for others to move through the tender process of therapy. My aim is to help folks build new relationships with pain and suffering, at the same time that they invite in presence, connection, meaning, and creativity. Through the blend of art therapy and talk therapy, my practice might offer you the missing puzzle piece you need to access this important work for yourself. Read on and reach out if this feels right to you

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Within a couple of sessions, you will probably learn how open and engaged I am with what you are bringing into the room. I truly believe that you are the expert on how our work unfolds, even if you don’t feel that’s true. I will often offer choices like “Do we want to follow this thread around your work frustrations?” or “Do we want to return to this recent art in progress exploring your relationship with your partner?” When we start getting into the weeds of processing, I have favorite approaches to bring into the mix alongside art therapy, especially Gestalt therapy, Internal Family Systems (IFS), and Compassion Focused therapy. I love offering the nerdy science behind mental health, often pulling nuggets from Interpersonal Neurobiology, Attachment Theory, and Polyvagal Theory. I am continuously assessing, exploring, and re-adjusting to fine-tune your therapy experience so you leave each session feeling safe, seen, and supported.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: I am a licensed art therapist with the State of Oregon and I am a registered art therapist with the American Art Therapy Credentials Board. I have been practicing art therapy since 2013.

name: MEGAN WYCKOFF
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: "Hi, I'm Megan! I work with individuals and couples, including trans and polyamorous folks, in person or remotely. Let’s make change happen!
ideal_client: Are you looking create or transform your relationship - both to yourself and to your significant other? Have you tried couples counselling before but left feeling that the main issues in your relationship remained unresolved? Are you in a committed relationship that exists out of the common categories? Are you polyamorous, a sex worker, kinky, in group relationship, or have a similar uncommon setup that makes it hard to find the support you can trust? I can help - with all of the above.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My main belief is that relationships are how we heal, and that the best growth is seen when we feel safe and curious to do the real work of healing trauma. Healing can only happen against a backdrop of trust. I use talk therapy, but also somatic interventions such as EMDR and other modalities such as NET (Narrative Exposure Therapy) and EFT (Emotionally Focused Therapy) to resolve longstanding issues and break harmful and maladaptive patterns keeping individuals and couples from authentic relating. As a therapist, I seek to create collaborative, authentic relationships with my clients. I am direct, caring, and not interested in hiding behind fancy terminology or concepts. My most important skill is my ability to see you and affirm you: where you are, where you came from, and where you are going. I'll develop a roadmap for your work and I'll help keep you on the right track.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a queer, non-binary cis-passing white person with chronic illness, I find that I have a lot in common with many of my clients, and I seek to create common ground so we can do our best healing work together as a team. My pronouns are she/her, they/them, and my commitment to supporting trans, non-binary and gender expansive folks is longstanding. I support movements advocating for HAES, and I am aligned with non-traditional relationship styles and sex-positivity movements, and an advocate for the rights of sex workers, women, immigrants, and other minorities. While I am white, I actively work to create an anti-racist practice and space of healing for BIPOC clients, and am happy to speak with you explicitly about my own racial justice experience. I work out of a practice located on unceded land of the Cascades, Stl’pulmsh (Cowlitz), Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians, Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde, Cayuse, Umatilla and Walla Walla.

name: Kitty Carter
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi! I'm Kitty Carter, a Licensed Clinical Social Worker specializing in working with children, youth and families.
ideal_client: Is your child struggling and you find yourself worrying about them? Are you having trouble connecting with your child? Parenting is an adventure that can be both rewarding and challenging. With so many competing pressures and distractions, it can be hard to find time to build the kinds of relationships we want. I help parents and children build new skills and stronger connections so kids have a secure foundation to develop into their full potential.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I received my PhD in Social Work and Social Research with an emphasis on children's mental health and caregivers work-life balance in 2007 at Portland State University. I completed my MSW in 2004. I have been working in the field of Children's Mental Health for over 25 years in a variety of settings including residential treatment for youth, as a Child and Family Therapist, Clinical Supervisor, Outpatient Clinical Manager, Division Director, Adjunct Professor, and mental health researcher. I have been licensed in the State of Oregon for 15 years and have worked with all kinds of kids and families with various strengths and challenges. My approach to therapy is eclectic and flexible to best meet your needs. My work is shaped by attachment theory, trauma informed practices, cognitive behavioral approaches, neurobiology, child development, the family life cycle, family systems and mindfulness practices. I attend regular training to stay abreast of the latest advancements in the field.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Native Portlandian, wife, mother of one human and two fur babies. In my free time, I enjoy getting out in the beautiful Pacific Northwest, connecting with friends and family and enjoying this amazing food scene we have here. I have spent my entire adult life dedicated to children's mental health and working with kids and families. I love it! Mental health matters! As a Social Worker, I believe in the dignity and worth of all persons. I believe in keeping families together. I believe recovery is possible. I have been on an Equity Advisory Council, participated in Equity Leadership Training, and have specialized training in culturally responsive practice and equity and inclusion. I believe in trauma informed care and have specialized training and experience in organizational models of trauma informed care and trauma specific treatments.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have specialized training in early childhood (child parent psychotherapy, Parent Child Interaction Therapy, play therapy), childhood development from early childhood to teens, and neurobiology-- which is a fancy way of saying brain development. I also integrate trauma informed approaches and specific treatments (trauma focused CBT, Attachment, Self-Regulation and Competency Model) in my work with children, as well as family systems approaches to help build stable systems and connections.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have extensive training in treating child abuse and trauma. I have worked with adult survivors of childhood abuse and trauma, as well as children and teens. I use Trauma Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (TF-CBT), the Attachment, Self-Regulation and Competency (ARC) model and Child- Parent Psychotherapy (CPP). I am currently working on additional modalities to treat trauma and PTSD.

name: Debra Schnack
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I believe that change can happen. I believe in the resilience of the individual and their ability to push through and overcome obstacles.
ideal_client: I realize that no two people are the same and as such tailor my therapy to meet the specific needs of my clients. Whether you are struggling with anxiety, depression or any other issue, I will help you recognize underlying problems, fully realize your strengths and adjust certain behaviors and thoughts to see things a different, healthier way.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I take a holistic approach to therapy, concerned with the overall long-term well-being of the individual and their family. I work with clients on partner relational issues, family of origin conflict, anxiety, depression, low self-esteem, and other issues in a safe, supportive, and non-judgmental environment. I practice EMDR, Brainspotting, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), each depending upon the issues we are addressing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Realizing you have a problem that you can't solve on your own is a brave first step for any person. Seeking out help and support is one of the toughest decisions to make. And as your therapist, I want you to know that I will be here to support you and work with you to help you become the person you want to be.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: Many trauma experts believe that when we are overwhelmed by something traumatic, the emotional “charge” or memory from that event becomes trapped in our body. We’re often unaware this has even occurred, but our brain is altered as a result. It can cause emotional, mental, and physical problems. Brainspotting is designed to discover, dislodge, and ultimately release that trapped energy so it no longer causes problems in our life.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: There’s no denying that life often presents us with our fair share of challenges, usually in the form of sudden change. These life transitions, even the positive ones, can throw us into a tailspin and leave us feeling stressed, confused, and vulnerable. But with the right tools and mindset, you have the power to not only overcome any adversity, but also transform into a more authentic and confident version of yourself.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: There are two specific techniques that are consistently gaining research-based evidence of their effectiveness in successfully treating PTSD. Brainspotting – This modality taps into the body’s​ innate ability to heal in order to reduce and eliminate the impact of unresolved trauma, negative beliefs, and emotional distress. EMDR – This technique uses bilateral sensory input such as side-to-side eye movements to stimulate the brain to process difficult thoughts, memories, and emotions.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: When it comes to treating anxiety disorders, research shows that therapy is usually the most effective option. That’s because therapy for anxiety — as opposed to taking anxiety medication — treats more than just symptoms to the problem. Therapy can help to uncover the underlying causes of your worries and fears, learn how to relax, look at situations in a new, less frightening way, and develop better coping mechanisms and problem-solving skills.

name: Julia Bennion
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I help teens, adults and couples with trauma, depression/anxiety, intimacy issues, and ADHD using techniques such as EMDR and Gottman Method
ideal_client: Everyone has the power to create growth and change in their own lives. Sometimes, you just need a little help learning the right tools to create that change. Whether it be relationship and intimacy challenges, affair recovery, depression, anxiety, ADHD and more, I’d love to join you on your path to growth and change, helping you find the right tools to use on your way.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I specialize in couples therapy and individual therapy with teens and adults for challenges such as trauma, depression/anxiety, intimacy issues, affair recovery, and ADHD. I utilize techniques like EMDR, the Gottman Method, Mindfulness, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Attachment Theory and Restoration Therapy to help you meet your goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Portland native and in our free time, my husband and our family enjoy travelling, going to shows & playing board games.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: When something traumatic happens our feelings and thoughts get mixed up, like jumbled pages torn from a book. We carry those mixed up thoughts, images, sounds, feelings, and emotions with us, stuffed away. When something reminds us of those memories it’s as though it is happening again right now. EMDR helps the brain file away those mixed up images, sounds, feelings, thoughts, and emotions in a calm form, as a memory from the past without all the emotional distress.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: In working with couples, I utilize the Gottman Method, a well-researched approach to relationship counseling. This method is rooted in decades of empirical research, identifying specific behaviors and communication patterns that contribute to relationship success. This therapy offers practical tools and interventions to enhance communication, build intimacy, and manage conflicts effectively.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Building a trusting and empathetic relationship with my teenage clients is at the core of my approach. I believe in creating a safe space where teens feel comfortable expressing their thoughts and emotions without judgment. Understanding the complexities of adolescence, I tailor my therapeutic techniques to address issues such as identity exploration, peer relationships, academic stress, and emotional regulation.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I approach each client with empathy and a deep understanding of the debilitating impact that anxiety and panic can have on one's life. Through evidence-based therapeutic modalities, I work collaboratively with my clients to explore the roots of their anxiety, develop coping strategies, and foster resilience.

name: Dani Maier
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I provide psychiatric evaluations and ongoing medication management via telehealth to individuals 16 years old and older.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a board certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) specializing in diagnosis and treatment of anxiety disorders, including OCD. I also treat mood disorders, ADHD, and eating disorders. I provide psychiatric evaluations, medication management, and limited therapy for patients living in Oregon and New Mexico. I believe strongly in translating evidence/science-based mental health care and collaboration to create treatment plans. I also know that people are more than their mental illness and strive to understand how each person exists within their environment and relationships. I have been in practice since 2013 and worked in rural, frontier, and urban settings. I have a Master’s in Nursing from OHSU and Doctor of Nursing Practice from New Mexico State University. I obtained my undergraduate degree from Stanford University, where I majored in Human Biology and minored in Feminist Studies.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Each of us is a collection of stories that come from our past, our experiences, and our loved ones—at times, without our permission. Ultimately, we are the story we tell ourselves and I hope to work with people as they find the story that helps them achieve well-being and meaning. Please go to www.danimaierpmhnp.com to request an appointment

name: Pacific Psychology & Comprehensive Health Pacific University
full_name: Pacific Psychology & Comprehensive Health Pacific University
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
credentials: QMHP, Mental Health Intern, PsyD, PA-C
intro: We provide outpatient assessment, therapy, and medication management for a wide range of mental health concerns.
ideal_client: We offer therapy and medication management for depression, anxiety, child/family issues, trauma, ADD, and a wide range of other concerns. We can bill most OHP plans in the metro area for therapy and medication management services.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our therapists operate from an evidence-based treatment philosophy. That is, we have a professional and ethical responsibility to provide our clients with the best possible treatment to match their needs. We are able to work with patients interested in CBT, DBT, Mindfulness - based, Psychodynamic, PCIT and a variety of other therapy orientations.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Our providers include experienced licensed clinicians as well as advanced level graduate students working under the supervision of licensed clinical psychologists. We are able to bill most OHP plans in the Portland metro area (Care Oregon, Health Share Oregon, Columbia Pacific, Trillium Health) for mental health evaluation and therapy services.

name: Aurora Counseling (Group Practice)
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Black-owned group practice offering culturally responsive and compassionate trauma therapy. LGBTQ+ & neurodiversity-affirming.
ideal_client: You might be questioning whether what you’ve been through qualifies as trauma, exactly. Sure, you’ve faced some challenges, but hasn’t everyone? There's always someone who seems to have had it worse. Yet, those painful memories keep resurfacing, no matter how often you tell yourself to move on. On the outside you seem like you have it all together, but inside, you feel like everything is falling apart. Whether you call it trauma or not, your experiences deserve to be heard.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: At Aurora Counseling, our BIPOC clinicians meet you from a place of shared experience and understanding. We offer targeted trauma therapy, including EMDR, and Somatic Experiencing, to unpack childhood, relationship, and racial trauma, and help you show up in the life that you have now as a more grounded, self-assured version of yourself. You'll learn to feel more present, confident, and alive. We already believe that you deserve better, and we'll help you believe it too.

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: Our therapists treat a wide range of issues including racial trauma, CPTSD, PTSD, childhood trauma, ADHD, anxiety, depression, relationship stress, multiracial identity development, intergenerational trauma, and religious trauma.
