Our clients identify as Black/African-American, Asian, Caucasian, Multiracial, BIPOC, Middle Eastern, Hispanic/Latino. We are LGBTQ+ and Neurodiverse affirming and have several bilingual spanish speaking clinicians.

name: Rachel Baker
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Aiming to provide a warm, safe and calming space for individual adults searching for more balance, purpose and ease in their lives.
ideal_client: While I work with a wide range of individuals, my focus is life transitions, anxiety, grief/complex grief and trauma. Many of my clients may be yearning for more trust and confidence within themselves through the peaks and valleys of uncertainty and emotional pain. Sometimes my clients are questioning their relationships (social, familial & romantic) and are craving a stronger connection to their mind and body.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: When working together, I view problems from a structuralism framework. In other words, I believe we are deeply impacted by the society we participate in and by our relationships. Therapy is important, and finding the right fit as a client is even more important. I approach therapy from a highly relational, process-oriented framework.. My first and foremost goal , however, is to prioritize and cultivate a strong and authentic therapeutic alliance between myself and you. It is crucial to me that I approach my clients from a forever curious lens. I believe that, no matter how many hours we log together, I will always strive to better understand you than I did our previous session. It is essential to me that I fully believe your story and experience, while holding it with the utmost gentleness and respect.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe that we are deeply impacted by our relationships. In our individualist culture, it is so easy for us to blame ourselves for where we are today and, to forget, that we are companion-oriented species. This ethos is at the center of my work with clients. Studies show that the number one variable responsible for positive change within a client is the therapeutic relationship. This makes so much sense to me because I believe strong therapy has to include authenticity coming from myself. Clients connect with me because they are drawn to my presence and balanced nature. When we are in session, you will feel that I am with you through the laughs, tears, unanswered questions, and discomfort.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: From the beginning of my clinical career, I have utilized mindfulness in sessions with adults and children. I have extra training in Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) and also have acquired my 200 hour yoga teacher training certification. I invite you to schedule a complimentary consultation call to learn more about how I can integrate mindfulness into our work together.

name: Renee Barnett
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My approach blends mindfulness, solution-focused counseling, and lifestyle design to support mental clarity and emotional balance.
ideal_client: You’re here because you are ready to explore ways in which you can achieve your health/mental health goals and you have some curiosity about the mind-body connection.

name: Emily Padilla
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I specialize in working with youth and families, most commonly treating trauma disorders, anxiety and depression.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I seek to create a safe space where children feel accepted and heard. I utilize wholistic and evidence based practices to support and guide clients and families through the therapeutic process. I encourage and empower my clients to honor their voice and embrace their uniqueness. I have been working in education and social services for 10 years.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in the power of nurturing relationships and modeling positive habits and coping skills.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) is a structured program of psychotherapy with a strong educational component designed to provide skills for managing intense emotions and negotiating social relationships. Originally developed to curb the self-destructive impulses of chronic suicidal patients, it is also the treatment of choice for borderline personality disorder, emotion dysregulation, and a growing array of psychiatric conditions. Emily has been trained and is certified in DBT Therapy.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) is an action-oriented approach to psychotherapy that stems from traditional behavior therapy and cognitive behavioral therapy. Clients learn to stop avoiding, denying, and struggling with their inner emotions and, instead, accept that these deeper feelings are appropriate responses to certain situations that should not prevent them from moving forward in their lives. Emily has been trained and is certified in ACT Therapy.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Emily has been certified in Play Therapy and enjoys working with children and adolescents presenting with a number of behavioral health issues. This approach utilizes toys and other expressive activities as forms of communication and as an intervention method for problem solving and promoting well-being.

specialities.name: Sand Tray
specialities.description: Emily has received training and is certified in Sand Tray therapy. Sand Tray therapy is a creative counseling technique where a person expresses their understanding of themselves, their world, and aspects of their reality through figurines or miniatures.

name: Ashley Vande Slunt
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: LMFT, CIMHP, OBLPC & AAMFT Supervisor Candidate
intro: Hello, I'm Ashley, an Integrative and Somatic Therapist specalized in treating trauma, women's issues, and anxiety.
ideal_client: I work best with women navigating trauma, anxiety, burnout, or life transitions. My ideal client is ready to explore mind & body-based healing, deepen self-awareness, and reconnect with their inner strength. I specialize in somatic therapy, EMDR, and mindfulness for those feeling stuck, overwhelmed, or disconnected. Whether you’re healing from past wounds or seeking more balance, I offer a safe, supportive space to help you move forward with clarity, confidence, and lasting change.

approaches.How I Can Help You: You don’t have to navigate healing alone. I offer a grounded, supportive space where you can slow down, reconnect with yourself, and move through what’s been holding you back. Using an integrative, somatic approach—including EMDR, SSP (Safe and Sound Protocol), RRP (Rest and Restore Protocol), mindfulness, and trauma-informed care—I help women work through anxiety, past trauma, life transitions, and burnout. Therapy with me is about real, lasting change rooted in self-awareness, body connection, and nervous system healing. You’re the expert of your experience; my role is to walk alongside you, offering tools, perspective, and presence as you move toward greater clarity, resilience, and ease. Whether you’re feeling overwhelmed, stuck, or simply ready for a deeper kind of support, I’m here to help you reconnect with your inner strength and create meaningful change from the inside out.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe healing happens in safe, attuned, and non-judgmental spaces. As a somatic and trauma-informed therapist, I value deep listening, curiosity, and collaboration. I believe our body caries both resilience and wisdom. I center consent, cultural awareness, and nervous system safety in all of our work together. Therapy with me is about slowing down, reconnecting with your body, and building the internal resources you need to thrive. I honor your pace and your truth. My role isn’t to fix—it’s to offer support and inviting there to be a trusting relationship with oneself. Healing is possible, and I’ll meet you with compassion every step of the way.

name: Danielle McWilliams LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Engaging & Relational Therapeutic Support for Navigating Modern Life: Help to understand who you are, who you want to be & how to get there!
ideal_client: I help clients gain confidence, guide their own ship, identify strengths & create empowered ideas about themselves; supporting them on their path to cultivating awareness, understanding, agency & possibility. In our work, clients’ access to self-expression, personal values & The Self are encouraged & developed; opportunities to let go of old habits & fears & clear the path for growth & healing are brought into focus to be explored & experienced, allowing new, satisfying ways of being to emerge!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a counselor I work from a general theory base of Existential Humanistic and Systems Theory; focusing on the dynamics of creativity, mindfulness, and self-awareness within the context of a person’s worldview. My approach is collaborative & strengths-based, utilizing internal family systems, cognitive, experiential, somatic, creative & relational therapies to encourage clients’ abilities to problem solve, navigate modern life, self-comfort & develop their identity. In sessions clients find a unique space to notice their experiences & observe their place in the world around them. Through this process of individualized, relevant, positive & engaging therapy, clients’ self-expression, awareness & empowerment are cultivated & opportunities for growth & healing can be explored & experienced.

I've been a Nationally Certified Counselor since 2011 & have been providing direct services to youth & families since 2003. I hold a Master’s Degree in Counseling Psychology with a specialty in Children & Adolescent Treatment from Lewis & Clark College, as well as a Bachelor’s Degree in Sociology. My training in both fields helps me see both the individual & the bigger systems (family, culture, world, etc.) they exist within, allowing me to offer my clients a wider perspective & larger framework from which to examine problems & their impact, a particularly useful balance in supporting people of all ages to feel seen & understood around systemic injustices. I’ve worked with children, adolescents, teens, adults & families from a variety of diverse backgrounds, communities, & belief systems; I have experience with issues that span the spectrum of struggles people may face. My work has been done in private practice, elementary, middle & high schools & the juvenile court system.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: What task is greater than personal growth while in the adolescent & young adult phases of life? It emerges quite naturally as a focus during all my work with young people. Identity exploration, awareness of values and needs, and imagination are all cultivated as therapeutic pathways towards becoming more oneself!

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: My truest focus as a therapist is working with young people, & whatever issues or struggles they may be facing, with a developmentally & culturally relevant approach. All theoretical or practical training has been filtered through this lens, leading to a specialized style of building strong therapeutic relationships, supporting & facilitating young clients' ability to navigate their way through...

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Messages about being & loving yourself abound these days, but to feel a sense of authentic self-worth these messages must be supported with deeper meaning! In my practice we focus on gently cultivating a greater awareness & acceptance of what makes you YOU, while exploring how to put those qualities, ideas, & concepts into self-caring practice that nurtures empowerment, compassion & integration!

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Loss, grief, & bereavement take many forms & can have a lasting impact on who we are & how we see & be in our world. Whether our loved one is human or a special animal relationship, processing & healing after loss is essential. Through rituals, expressive work & myriad ways to remember & honor the connection shared, a new place to hold our love safe & secure can be created, treasured & maintained.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is such a shapeshifter, and seems to be a nearly unavoidable companion of the modern era. Learning to recognize & diminish signs & symptoms, as well as transform how we relate to anxiety can facilitate movement, new experience, and a sense of relief from dominating impact.

name: Gabriel Boyer
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Holistic & Relational Therapy

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Meaningful change occurs through connecting to deeper emotions and relational themes. Together we can slow down, explore your experience holistically and connect your history to the present. This expands awareness, softens somatic rigidity and often allows something fresh to emerge. To do this, we cultivate a genuinely safe, supportive therapeutic relationship--tailored to you as a unique person--so you feel more comfortable to explore more deeply and untangle knots keeping you stuck.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I mix attachment theory with relational gestalt, somatic, and contemporary psychoanalytic approaches. These approaches converge on the importance of relationships, both past and current. These practices center on building a safe therapeutic relationship, unique to each person. This provides a foundation to explore more deeply, uproot core issues and create new ways to live and flourish.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: I have 3 years training in Relational Gestalt Therapy, a holistic and more attuned thread of Gestalt. I focus on your experience, your way of making meaning, and our unique way of connecting. I attend to subtleties in your process, not just what you share but how: pacing, body expressions, breath, etc. This is woven together in a genuine, open hearted explorative way. Relational Gestalt has an optimistic spirit, nurturing greater awareness and spontaneity.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: As we work together, I invite moments to slow down and drop deeper into emotion. While we talk, I track your body expression, invite body and emotion into our conversation with attention to express diminished affect and impulse. My background is eclectic in somatic therapy: primarily contemporary Reichian. I also use slower speeds and presence from Hakomi, trauma informed tools from Somatic Experiencing, and personal experience from Yoga and Buddhist practice.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: Relational Psychoanalysis incorporates attachment theory, feminist and queer theory. Coalescing with Stephen Mitchell (ancestor to Esther Perel), healing is through a mutually collaborative exploration of the interplay between your inner process and the world around you. This includes your attachment history, relationship patterns, and leveraging our relationship towards your growth.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: I have a master's in depth psychotherapy for individuals, couples and families. Depth therapy is a matter of engaged listening and holding aspects of life with sacredness. Opposed to pathologizing treads in therapy, we seek the unique support needed to courageously move towards deeper feelings in order to loosen the old knots keeping you stuck.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationship therapy for 2+ or people I use a process orientated approach focused on attachment and differentiation (balanced connection at the boundary of you and I). I also use Stan Tatkin's PACT model, which I think of as "relational somatic." It is embodied attachment-based approach that attunes to patterns of dysregulation: how those patterns disrupt connection and how patterns can shift towards greater connection. I am sex positive, kink friendly and work with open relationships.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: The way we love, touch and fuck--the way we're drawn to others is, in my view, the most important part of our lives. In a culture that harms people for their natural erotic movements, there are times for sanctuary. Weather you want a queer pos space to talk about other issues or or desire more direct untangling of homophobia, we can build towards your goals to continue a life of resilience, connection and love.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I know open relationships work. I bring both personal experience and professional training. Whether you're beginning to explore or further on your way, I support people in many different configurations to thrive in relationships. I also support queer folk and am kink friendly.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: My approach with trauma values consent, respect, and follows your own embodied pace. This involves moving towards and building resilience in a safe, supportive relationship. "The wound is the place where the Light enters." -Rumi

name: Jordan Hubchik
title: Licensed Art Therapist
intro: I'm not a blank slate therapist—I show up as a real person, and invite you to do the same.
ideal_client: I serve teens and adults across Oregon via remote tele-therapy sessions. I specialize in working with individuals navigating anxiety, depression, complex trauma, PTSD, attachment wounds, and eating disorder recovery. I’m especially passionate about supporting neurodiverse and LGBTQIA+ clients in an inclusive and affirming space where all parts of you are welcome. Together, we’ll explore what healing looks like for you, in a space that’s inviting, imaginative, and grounded in genuine connection.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach blends art therapy, parts work, and trauma-informed modalities—offering a deeply creative and integrative healing experience. I help clients zoom out to understand the larger cultural, social, and relational systems they live within. I can support you in reclaiming a deeper sense of agency, self-understanding, and wholeness. As a licensed and certified art therapist, I offer a supportive space where you can explore and express your inner thoughts and emotions through spontaneous or guided art-making and creative interventions. Using art as a therapeutic tool creates a helpful distance from overwhelming feelings, allowing you to observe, reflect, and better understand your inner world. We can incorporate art into our sessions as much or as little as you feel comfortable—no artistic skill or experience is necessary to benefit.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a white, able-bodied, cis-femme, queer therapist. I’m a Cancer through and through—empathetic, creative, and a big believer in the power of feeling things deeply. In my free time, you’ll often find me lost in a romantasy novel, rewatching a favorite show or movie, making art, or exploring the beauty of Oregon with friends and family. In my personal life and in my work as a therapist, I’ve seen how powerful creative expression can be. It’s not about producing something “good” or “right”—it’s about engaging with your inner world in a way that feels safe, meaningful, and alive. Sharing the healing potential of art with my clients feels like passing along something sacred: a way of tuning into yourself, finding your voice, and making space for growth, insight, and connection. If something in my approach resonates with you, I’d be honored to connect. You're welcome to reach out with questions or to schedule a consultation—I'm here when you're ready.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Traumatic experiences are often stored in the body and mind as vivid images and physical sensations. Art therapy offers a unique way to access these inner experiences from a safe, contained distance, making it a highly effective tool for trauma healing. Through a combination of creative expression and narrative processing, I help clients find healing, integration, and a deeper connection to self.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I’ve supported clients in eating disorder recovery across PHP, IOP, and outpatient care. I understand these complex conditions affect physical, emotional, social, and occupational well-being. I see recovery as reclaiming what’s been lost, helping clients live fuller, more balanced lives. I embrace body-trust, body-diversity, and Health-at-Every-Size approaches in therapy.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: LGBTQIA+ individuals often face stigma, discrimination, and rejection, impacting their mental and physical well-being. Drawing on both personal and professional experience, I support trans and non-binary clients through transition and gender-affirming care. I provide affirming, non-judgmental support and advocacy, always grounded in a social justice framework.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: Everyone experiences body image struggles at times. When difficult days outweigh the good, extra support can help. I use a Health-at-Every-Size, body-diversity, and body-trust approach, focusing on understanding and challenging body biases rather than changing the body. True self-acceptance comes from uncovering where these beliefs come from and gently dismantling unhelpful views.

name: Ashley Adler
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: Master of Arts in Marriage, Couples, and Family Therapy
intro: Welcome! Let’s connect—reach out for a free consultation to see if we’re a good fit. I offer support for relationships and individuals.
ideal_client: I am passionate about working with relational dynamics—including both monogamous and non-monogamous relationships—LGBTQ+ individuals, and those seeking to better understand themselves and their patterns. I believe we exist within the context of our relationships, communities, and lived experiences, and that healing happens when all parts of us—including the ones we’ve been taught to feel ashamed of—are welcomed with curiosity and compassion.

approaches.What I Specialize In: When I work with relationships, I take the time to really understand your dynamic—how you interact, where you get stuck, and how your past experiences might be shaping the present. The way we love and communicate is often influenced by what we learned growing up, the relationships we’ve been in, and the unspoken stories we carry. I also bring a focus on equity, exploring how each person’s experiences, identities, and histories show up in your relationship. When I work with individuals, I focus on creating a space of safety, curiosity, and deep listening. I use body-based awareness to help you reconnect with yourself in ways that go beyond words. While I will gently challenge you to step into growth, I trust that you are the expert in your own experience, and my role is to guide and support—not to push.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a white, Jewish, queer cis woman, and my identities shape not only how I move through the world but also how I show up as a therapist. I am committed to providing culturally attuned therapy that honors each person’s unique lived experience. I know that healing doesn’t happen in a vacuum—our identities, histories, and environments all shape us. That’s why I approach my work with a deep respect for the complexities of each person’s lived experience, creating a space where all parts of who you are can be seen, held, and honored.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory explores how our early relationships—particularly with caregivers—shape the ways we connect with others and ourselves throughout life. What was modeled to us in terms of emotional connection, responsiveness, and safety can deeply influence how we navigate relationships as adults. Therapy offers a unique opportunity to experience safe, supportive attachment—one where you are met with empathy, understanding, and care.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Somatic therapy focuses on the deep connection between your body and mind, recognizing that emotions and past experiences are often held within the body. Physical sensations—like tension, discomfort, or pain—can offer important clues to unresolved emotions or trauma. In somatic therapy, we explore these sensations to help you understand and release what’s been stored.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Therapy through a queer and feminist lens acknowledges the impact of systemic oppression, gender norms, and heteronormativity on mental health and relationships. It creates space to unlearn limiting narratives, embrace identity, and explore relationships, power, and pleasure on your own terms. This approach values self-determination, centers your lived experience, and challenges the idea that healing happens in isolation—recognizing that identity, culture, and community all shape personal growth

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Conflict is a part of every relationship, but it doesn’t have to define yours. Maybe you and your partner(s) keep having the same arguments, feeling unheard, disconnected, or unsure of how to move forward. You love each other, but something feels stuck. You want to break free from old patterns and build a relationship that feels more connected, fulfilling, and secure.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a queer therapist, I understand the unique experiences and challenges that come with being LGBTQ+. Whether you're unpacking the impact of societal pressures, exploring your queer identity, or seeking support for relationship dynamics, my approach is grounded in empathy, respect, and a deep understanding of the diverse ways that queerness shapes our lives.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Working with polyamorous clients involves understanding the unique dynamics and complexities that come with consensual non-monogamy. Together, we can explore the values and agreements that shape your relationships, while recognizing the importance of emotional safety, consent, and respect for everyone involved.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: You’re ready to understand yourself on a deeper level—the patterns that shape your relationships, the wounds that still linger, and the ways you’ve learned to protect yourself. Maybe you’re looking for a space where you can be supported in breaking old cycles and stepping into the change you’re craving. Whether you’re untangling childhood wounds, navigating the impact past relationships, or rewriting the stories you’ve carried about yourself, you don’t have to do it alone.

name: Osleidy Soria-Pons
title: Student Counselor
intro: Bilingual therapist offering culturally responsive care in Spanish & English, holding space for diverse identities & lived experiences.
ideal_client: I offer a nurturing and affirming space for clients of diverse backgrounds to explore their concerns. I believe therapy can be used as a tool to navigate life’s challenges. We all have an inner capacity to heal. It is not easy but it is possible. Your healing is worth the effort because you deserve peace and joy. I’m here to support you through your healing process. Together, we will embark on a journey of self-discovery, embracing both the triumphs and challenges that arise.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Building a strong therapeutic relationship based on authenticity, trust, respect, and genuine connection is essential to my approach. Through our work together, we will attend to your body and your mind – the whole you. We are a sum of all our parts and our healing should seek to integrate us and make us feel more whole. I use mindfulness, person-centered practices and other evidence-based approaches to offer support for a wide range of issues, including anxiety, grief, systemic racism, identity exploration, and intergenerational trauma. I hope to guide you as you unlock and magnify the resilience and wisdom within you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I became a therapist to create a space where Black and Brown individuals can find liberation and healing. Growing up as an Afro-Latina immigrant, I witnessed the deep impact of systemic racism, discrimination, and oppression on marginalized communities. These experiences shaped my desire to provide culturally-responsive therapy that honors and validates the unique struggles and resilience of BIPOC individuals. I believe in the power of therapy not just to cope but to dismantle oppressive narratives and systems. My practice is rooted in social justice, equity, and the belief that everyone deserves to be seen, valued, and supported in their healing journey.

name: Riisa Humphrey
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am a person-centered, trauma-focused therapist with lived and professional experience.
ideal_client: We learn to "live" with it and "cope" with trauma, and some of us may feel helpless and hopeless due to the damaging effects trauma has on our minds and bodies. When we experience trauma, we try to manage the effects of our feelings, emotions, and thoughts. Sometimes, we use substances or alcohol to cope with the stressors and triggers of trauma. When our life has become unmanageable, we tend to numb the pain or freeze and these are common trauma responses, but they don't have to be.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I provide the tools necessary to cope with and heal from the everyday effects of trauma. I have worked with individuals who have experienced extensive trauma history for over 10 years. My approach is person-centered and trauma-informed using empathy and active listening skills to support clients with their mental health needs. I am trained in Brainspotting, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT).

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: At the core of my practice, confidentiality, empathy, respect, cultural sensitivity and evidence-based practice are values I constantly strive for.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: I have provided support for many different victims of abuse including adolescents and adults including domestic violence, sexual, verbal, physical, and emotional abuse. ,

name: Iris Torres Garcia
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Waitlist opens Winter 2026
ideal_client: We offer therapy for individuals, 18 years of age or older, who have experienced ​domestic violence, sexual assault, and intergenerational trauma. Our approach is grounded in the understanding that no single therapeutic method can encompass the full spectrum of human experience. As a Chicana therapist and daughter of immigrants, my personal journey informs the way I connect with clients. This integrative approach considers cultural, historical, and individual contexts to provide healing and emp

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Over the past 10 years, I’ve had the privilege of serving parents, youth, and families in the Portland Metro area through my work in juvenile justice, education, and supporting survivors of domestic violence. My approach draws from a diverse set of therapeutic methods, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), narrative therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), strength-based and trauma-informed practices, and culturally responsive frameworks. I believe in an integrative perspective, as no single theory can fully capture the vast complexity of human experience.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: As a Chicanx clinician, I specialize in mental health counseling for Q/BIPOC, who may have experienced sexual assault, domestic- violence, and intergenerational trauma. Maíz y Sol Counseling Services is an offering dedicated to family, community, and the ancestors. It’s an act of love committed to decolonizing mental health services where we believe that Black Lives Matter, We are pro- immigration, and Love is love.

name: Molly Nearman
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I offer a warm and compassionate space to support individuals struggling with anxiety, depression, trauma, emotional pain, and grief/loss.
ideal_client: I provide individual therapy services for adults and adolescents (14+) struggling with anxiety, depression, trauma and/or emotional pain, life transitions, and grief/loss. Generally, my clients are interested in healing from past wounds, exploring themselves and their challenges more deeply, reflecting on interpersonal patterns, and gaining insight into the ways in which these patterns can help or hinder them. I offer a nonjudgmental, and grounded space for clients to do this meaningful work.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach counseling from an inclusive, strength-based, trauma-informed, and client-centered perspective. I believe that all individuals naturally strive toward growth and wholeness, guided by a nurturing inner wisdom or real self. My counseling practice is rooted in attachment-based psychodynamic theory, meaning that our early life experiences impact the way we view ourselves, relate to others, and understand the world around us. Sometimes these experiences can impair our inner wisdom and prevent us from living as our authentic selves. I also view individuals systemically, meaning that each of us is shaped and impacted by the interpersonal patterns and dynamics of our families and relationships. I integrate these theoretical lenses with Eye Movement Desensitization & Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy to help clients process trauma and move beyond their negative experiences to realize their full potential.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My connection and commitment to this work is deeply personal. Having grown up in a Midwestern culture that discouraged seeking help or even talking about painful feelings or challenges, moving to the more open-minded Pacific Northwest was a revelation in many ways. After experiencing my own transformative growth in counseling, I knew I wanted to help others to process and make sense of the past, gain insight, achieve personal growth, and reach their potential. I hold a Master’s degree in Marriage, Couple and Family Counseling from Portland State University. Before joining Eastside Counseling, I worked in community mental health and outpatient clinic settings with teens and adults. In my free time, I enjoy spending time hiking, running, and swimming in the breathtaking landscapes the Pacific Northwest has to offer. I also recharge indoors by reading, spending time with family and close friends, and engaging in creative projects like painting, baking, and sewing.

name: Steve Manthe
title: Student Counselor
intro: Hello! I am a Graduate Intern working with individuals, couples, families, and groups.
ideal_client: I partner best with adults, adolescents, pre-teens, and couples seeking profound and lasting change to their emotional well-being. My ideal clients are those who recognize the courage it takes to seek help and are committed to their own personal growth in a therapeutic relationship built on trust and respect. They value a person-centered, positive, and goal-oriented approach to therapy and are open to exploring their thoughts, feelings, and behaviors to achieve a more fulfilling life.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I offer In-Person sessions on Wednesdays and Fridays and Telehealth sessions on Tuesdays and Thursdays. "The universe is change; our life is what our thoughts make it." This quote from Marcus Aurelius is over 1800 years old but it's still true today. Your thoughts are making your life and change is guaranteed. If you need someone to help you explore your thoughts, navigate through change, and emerge stronger on the other side, I've a career's worth of experience doing just that. I specialize in anxiety & stress reduction, depression, relationships, marriage, careers, chronic & autoimmune disease, men's issues, and death & dying. I bring an integrative, goal-oriented approach to help you achieve the life you envision.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a student at New York University, completing an M.A. in Counseling for Mental Health and Wellness. Prior to NYU, I enjoyed a 25-year career in various leadership roles where I discovered an aptitude for aiding individuals and groups improve themselves and their relationships. During that time, I also earned an MBA from Auburn University and an executive coaching certification through UC Berkeley's Executive Coaching Institute. I believe the therapeutic journey toward a life well lived starts and ends with trust, empathy, and a shared commitment to your well-being and future success. Now as a counselor, I am passionate about helping individuals, couples, and families navigate anxiety, depression, relationship challenges, grief and loss. I'm also a 22-year husband, a 20-year Dad of 2, and a lifelong runner. Please reach out for a free consultation to see if I’m the right fit. I look forward to hearing from you!

name: Eight Matallana
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I support individuals and couples with anxiety, identity shifts, and relational issues through mindfulness-based and holistic therapy.
ideal_client: I specialize in supporting individuals and couples, including creatives, LGBTQIA2S+ clients, and those navigating anxiety, life transitions, attachment wounds, and relationship issues. I also help clients integrating after psychedelic assisted therapy. Using a trauma-informed, holistic approach, I focus on nervous system regulation, mindfulness, and shifting patterns. I provide a gender-affirming, inclusive space for clients from diverse racial and ethnic backgrounds and immigrant communities.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I combine mindfulness, somatic techniques, and parts work to help you regulate emotions, build confidence, feel more embodied, and shift long-standing patterns. I use IFS-Informed therapy, trauma-informed care, Restoration Therapy, Brainspotting, and the Gottman Method to support emotional healing and relationship growth. I also assist clients in processing psychedelic-assisted therapy experiences and navigating life transitions in a thoughtful, holistic way.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: In our work together, I help you navigate anxiety, ruminating thoughts, personal changes, relationship conflicts, and creative blocks in a non-judgmental and supportive way. I maintain a trauma-informed lens that integrates mind-body-spirit connection in order to help clients build self-trust, confidence and emotional resilience. My approach is collaborative: in the first few sessions, we’ll assess if we’re a good fit, and together, we’ll create a treatment plan tailored to your unique goals, supporting lasting personal growth and emotional well-being. Feel free to book a free 20-minute consultation with me.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I work with individuals and couples to understand and improve relationships. This is done by working with you to gain insight into your emotional pain, as well as the fight or flight responses that can occur in those moments, in order to empower you to choose a different path that aligns with your values. These patterns are then practiced and reinforced each session in order to help you gain new mastery over your mental health and solidify behavioral change.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: I have been trained in Brainspotting, an approach that supports trauma.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety amplifies things- especially the unknown. Mindfulness can help slow the process down and help us make wiser decisions about how to move forward. I work with many clients in both individual and relational therapy to address anxiety using the latest developments in mindfulness.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I help individuals and couples identify the source of their reactivity or explore patterns, and then assist them in building new habits. This includes accessing vulnerability, nurturing one another's sense of self, staying connected and valuing themselves in order to have enough to give to the relationship.

name: Hanna Abaata
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Helping Children, Teens, and Adults Feel Safe, Seen, and Understood
ideal_client: You may be here because something doesn’t feel right. Maybe your child is behaving in ways you don’t fully understand, or withdrawing in ways that concern you. Maybe your teen is struggling with anxiety, school pressure, or emotions that feel too heavy for their age. Or maybe you’re an adult trying to make sense of everything you’ve been through while figuring out where you’re headed. If any of that sounds familiar, it’s okay to ask for support, and you don’t have to figure it out on your own.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: When I meet with someone in therapy, I want them to feel safe, heard, and never judged. I draw from trauma-focused approaches like TF-CBT (Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy), Lifespan Integration, and parts work, such as Internal Family Systems. These tools help you or your child reconnect with parts of yourself that have been hurt, silenced, or misunderstood—and create space for healing. In session, we might talk about what’s going on at school, work, or home, but we’ll also explore what’s happening beneath the surface. Whether it’s fear, sadness, anger, or self-doubt, we’ll make space for those feelings. We’ll talk about them in ways that feel manageable. And together, we’ll explore how to make sense of your emotions, heal from what’s been painful, and grow in ways that feel right for you.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Like many people, I faced challenges during adolescence and young adulthood that shaped the person I’ve become. My own healing journey led me to become a therapist. Over the years, I’ve studied psychology and Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACEs), and I’ve come to deeply believe that therapy can be a turning point. It’s a space to pause, reflect, and rewrite the stories that may have shaped us, but don’t have to define us.

name: Katherina Alexandre
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I'll listen, understand your strengths & empower you to discover ways to lessen the struggle w/stress, relationships, anxiety, & depression.
ideal_client: We work together to identify the source of what brought you into therapy, identify your goals, and explore the best possible solutions that will help you feel successful. In addition, I creatively integrate a relational model, neuroscience information, meditation, stretches that help with symptoms of stress, and cognitive behavior techniques. These techniques will allow clients to learn tools, gain insight to make positive life changes and reduce symptoms.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In the past 20 years, my practice has focused on helping my clients with grief, depression, anxiety, work-related stress, parenting relationships, and violence. My approach involves creating a safe space to feel comfortable with me; I use an integrated relational, cognitive behavioral model and evidence-based techniques. We will work with clients to identify goals and find the best ways to achieve them. As a Compassion Fatigue Professional and Marriage and Family Therapist, I offer treatment for symptoms of compassion fatigue (secondary trauma and burnout) for first responders and anyone in the healthcare, addiction, and mental health fields. I offer workshops throughout the year.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: As healthcare and mental health professionals, we speak about the importance of self-care to others but often fail to follow our own advice. It’s time to gather in a supportive, interactive, and relaxed environment to begin the conversation about the demands of our work and the negative effects on our well-being.

name: Rachel McEwen, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Over a decade of experience helping people to be more authentic with themselves and others and with overcoming life's biggest challenges.
ideal_client: Challenges my clients might be facing include: Trauma (early childhood abuse/neglect, trauma in relationships, specific traumatic event), Life Transitions (starting/ending a relationship, having a child, career change), Self-Esteem and Self Worth (confidence, core value system, your place in the world), Perinatal Mental Health (infertility, issues during pregnancy, postpartum anxiety/depression), among other struggles. Reach out for a consultation to see if I could be a good fit for you.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I am a relational therapist at heart, which means I strive to build a meaningful therapeutic relationship with you so that healing and growth can occur. Therapy to me is a collaborative experience, and we will work together to find what motivates and energizes you. During therapy, you will be able to process through your struggles and learn practical skills and new ways of being that will help you feel more balanced in life. I will also help you challenge any negative self-talk you might have going on in your mind, that voice inside your head telling you that you're not good enough. I will help you find the voice inside you that tells you that you are enough, just the way you are, and together, we will make that voice louder. As your therapist, I will meet you where you are. I will work side-by-side with you through this challenging time.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have over a decade of experience working with people who struggle with issues such as anxiety, depression, relationship issues, trauma, and self-esteem, just to name a few. My approach is trauma-informed and integrative. I do my best to be aware and sensitive to your life experience and will adapt my therapeutic approach to best fit your needs. I always strive to provide a safe space where you can be yourself without judgement. As your therapist, I promise to be open-minded and genuine with you. I am committed to being present with you every step of the way.

name: Jireh Miller
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I bring my continuing growth into connection with your desired growth. Together, we will continue the journey of transformation and healing.
ideal_client: Have you diligently worked to create a life that thrives, but still feel stuck by childhood or continuing harm? Often the coping strategies we form survive past their "effectiveness date," creating an invisible force that holds us back from thriving on this journey we call life. In session, we will create a space for you to explore your past, your present, and your hopes for the future. We will hold both harm and healing, as we create a map for the journey towards freedom and thriving.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Perhaps you've heard that understanding comes from walking a mile in that person's shoes. I've come to believe that true understanding comes from walking 'a mile' WITH them. Your journey has been filled with a variety of difficult events (and likely many moments of joy), leading you to the place you now find yourself. As we journey together, I bring an understanding and appreciation for your strengths, enabling a kind and caring discussion of where course correction may free you to thrive. I utilize elements from DBT, ACT, and Psychodynamic psychology mixed with beautiful influences from Narrative, multicultural, and person-centered modalities. I maintain an awareness for where systemic influences are asserting pressure, especially within the therapeutic alliance. Additionally, I offer Lifespan Integration.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Instigated by personal experiences of childhood, intimate partner, and spiritual abuse, I decided to embark on a journey of healing. It's been a wild ride, and one that I don't anticipate ending anytime soon. However, the skills and understanding that I've gained from life-experience, support groups, and professional training have instilled an invaluable sense of how to proceed in life.... at least, I have that sense more often than I did in the past. What I'm saying is this - being able to read the terrain has gotten much easier, allowing me to implement my skills more effectively and a little more quickly. I look forward to helping you learn and grow into similar emotional dexterity. Additionally, I've not yet had a client from whom I didn't learn as much as they did from me. I look forward to our partnership on this therapeutic journey.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: A concentration in Trauma and Abuse as part of my masters program combined with personal experience with emotional and spiritual abuse allows real life understanding of the shame a victim of abuse may carry, and creativity for forging a path forward.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Ongoing supervision and continuing education in DBT skills contribute to my work with Anxiety.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: My masters program emphasis of influences that contribute to experiencing symptoms of depression assist in discovering the underlying cause of the depression and work toward repair of those emotional injuries.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: My masters program emphasis of influences that contribute to emotional upheaval assist in discovering the underlying cause of adjustment difficulties. Work toward repair of those earlier emotional injuries results in repair of current upheaval.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: My masters program and concentration in Trauma and Abuse emphasized the impact of loss, and the important, but painstaking process that is grief.

name: Peter Addy
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Portland psychedelic-affirming therapy helping chronic pain patients find relief. Ketamine therapy, fibromyalgia experience, compassion.
ideal_client: I work best with thoughtful, growth-oriented adults who are managing chronic pain or health conditions while exploring psychedelic therapy options. My clients often seek innovative healing approaches while navigating complex healthcare systems. Whether preparing for Oregon Psilocybin Services or considering ketamine therapy, they're ready to examine their relationship with pain and health in new ways. I particularly connect with professionals whose careers are impacted by chronic conditions.

approaches.My Background and Approach: With a PhD in Clinical Psychology and over 15 years of experience of research and clinical work, I bring both academic expertise and personal insight to my work with chronic pain and health challenges. I'm a licensed counselor in OR and WA, with specialized training in ketamine-assisted psychotherapy and psilocybin facilitation. Living with fibromyalgia has given me a deep awareness of how chronic illness can affect every aspect of life. This informs my integrated approach, which combines evidence-informed practices with innovative healing modalities. I am dedicated to helping clients find new ways to live meaningfully. My practice is explicitly psychedelic-affirming, offering preparation and integration support for legal experiences through Oregon Psilocybin Services and ketamine therapy. I create safe spaces for transformation where clients can explore their relationship with pain, connect with their inner wisdom, and develop practical tools for living fully.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I approach healthcare through a class-based analysis, recognizing that psychological distress and healthcare access are fundamentally shaped by capitalism and economic exploitation. As someone living with chronic illness, I understand how profit-driven healthcare creates and perpetuates suffering while limiting access to healing resources. My practice explicitly affirms all gender identities, sexual orientations, relationship structures, and body sizes. I work to create welcoming spaces that honor diverse experiences and challenge traditional medical models that have historically marginalized many communities. While maintaining cultural humility as a White, cisgender, educated practitioner, I recognize that effective anti-racist, feminist, and disability justice work must address the material conditions and class relations that underpin systemic oppression. I work toward collective liberation by combining direct support for clients with advocacy for revolutionary changes.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: My training in transpersonal psychology informs an approach that honors experiences beyond ordinary states of consciousness, including psychedelic journeys, spiritual emergencies, and profound healing experiences. I help clients integrate these experiences into their daily lives while better understanding consciousness and human potential. This orientation particularly supports work with non-ordinary states and meaning-making.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Understanding that trauma and chronic pain are held in the body, I incorporate body-centered approaches to support healing and transformation. This includes developing a greater awareness of physical sensations, exploring the relationship between emotions and bodily experiences, and working with the body's wisdom. My approach integrates somatic practices with psychedelic preparation and integration work.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I integrate mindfulness practices to help clients develop a greater awareness of the mind-body connection and more effective ways of relating to pain and challenging experiences. Through cultivating present-moment awareness and compassionate acceptance, clients learn to navigate health challenges with greater ease and resilience. These skills particularly support the preparation for and integration of psychedelic experiences.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I help clients explore questions about meaning, purpose, and identity that often arise when living with chronic health conditions. Drawing from existential philosophy and psychedelic research, I support clients in navigating uncertainty, finding meaning despite suffering, and developing authentic ways of being in the world. This orientation particularly informs my work with clients preparing for psychedelic experiences.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: My practice centers on creating warm, authentic therapeutic relationships that honor each client's inherent wisdom and capacity for growth. I combine deep empathy with practical tools for navigating health challenges, emphasizing client autonomy and self-determination. This approach supports clients in discovering their own paths to healing while developing greater self-understanding and acceptance.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Drawing from both professional expertise and personal experience with fibromyalgia, I help clients understand chronic pain within broader systems of capitalism and labor exploitation. My approach integrates practical pain management strategies with analyzing how profit-driven healthcare impacts treatment access and options. I focus on helping clients develop new relationships with their bodies while building solidarity and mutual support networks to challenge systemic barriers to care.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I support clients in exploring deeper questions of meaning, purpose, and identity, particularly as they navigate health challenges and life transitions. Through integrating insights from non-ordinary states of consciousness, mindfulness practices, and somatic awareness, I help clients develop greater self-understanding and emotional resilience. My approach honors both the challenges and opportunities for growth that arise through working with chronic pain and illness.

specialities.name: Political Climate
specialities.description: Understanding that personal health exists within capitalism's broader social relations, I help clients navigate the alienation and exploitation inherent in our current healthcare system. I explicitly acknowledge how profit motives shape access to care while supporting client advocacy and mutual aid organizing. My practice incorporates class consciousness and collective solidarity while working toward the revolutionary transformation of healthcare from a commodity to a human right.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: My background in transpersonal psychology and psychedelic research informs a holistic approach that honors the spiritual dimensions of healing and transformation. I support clients in exploring questions of meaning, purpose, and connection through traditional and non-ordinary states of consciousness. While maintaining respect for diverse belief systems, I help clients integrate profound experiences into their understanding of themselves and their place in the world.

name: Firefly Institute
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We are dedicated to improving the well-being for all individuals and families in our communities through holistic care practices.
ideal_client: We envision a holistic practice of wellness incorporating a mind-body connection to treatment which becomes the client’s internal working model for regulation, achieving life-long health. This is what we envision to become the model for our communities, our nation and world. We are an organization that recognizes mental health as an essential part of overall well being. We understand that trauma and mental illness, like physical illness, is a medically treatable condition.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We offer a variety of services including treatment options that are highly specialized such as play therapy, animal assisted therapy, therapeutic art, yoga and EMDR. These services are provided by skilled clinicians who have certification in the treatment program they are offering. This is what sets us apart from other clinics or practitioners. Training for specialized care is rigorous and requires significant commitment to education post-graduation. Firefly clinicians are certified to do the work, receive ongoing supervision and consultation and are accredited by training programs or institutions. Areas of specialty include: relationships, grief/loss, chronic illness, abuse/trauma, PTSD, mood imbalances, child therapy, attachment issues, behavioral issues, anxiety, adoption/foster care, divorce and difficult life transitions or change.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: The Firefly Institute clinicians are multi-disciplinary and collaborative. Clinicians are skilled at supporting individuals and family systems through life transitions, anxiety, depression and chronic illness. They carry expertise and credentials in trauma, play therapy, expressive arts and animal assisted human health. We understand that trauma and mental illness, like physical illness, is a medically treatable condition. We understand that trauma and mental illness can occur in any life and those who experience trauma or mental illness can return to good health. As a result, there is no room for stigma in our society. Our clinic’s model for mental well-being is the direct result of a robust collection of research and treatment options which includes: movement and expressive therapies, education services to clients and the professional community and research to support practice. This portfolio of services continuously evolves to meet the changing needs and priorities of all people.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR is a research-supported, integrative therapeutic approach designed to treat symptoms of trauma and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). EMDR also has effectiveness in treating anxiety, depression and other mental health conditions. Firefly clinicians can approach EMDR from a traditional or attachment-focused approach.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory is a theory of affect regulation and interpersonal relationships. Adult attachment anxiety is conceptualized as the fear of interpersonal rejection and abandonment, negative view of the self or feelings of increased anxiety or depression within relationships. Children can experience insecurity within their relationships and the behaviors we see are a result of that anxiety.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Play therapy involves using toys, sand, art, games, and other materials to help children express themselves. Play offers the child an environment of safety. If children are able to say what they think or how they feel through toys and art with someone who can translate their behavior and facilitate the process, they will respond positively and are able to successfully work through their problems.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Narrative therapy is a form of psychotherapy that seeks to help patients identify their strengths and value and use those strengths the skills associated with them. It externalizes the problem, providing space for the client to examine their past, present, and future with knowledge of their ability to live their values so they can effectively confront problems.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Family therapy brings all the members together for problem solving, relational repair, conflict resolution or building skills for communication and interaction. We provide family counseling with children, adolescents and for couples support.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Children frequently have difficulty talking about what is bothering them or talking about events that have occurred in their lives. Our approach to counseling children and adolescents is to use a prescriptive method of play or expressive arts therapy (using the best fitting evidenced based practice that meets the needs of your child, integrated into hands-on work that brings counseling to life).

specialities.name: Self-Harming
specialities.description: Whether a person has recently started hurting his or herself or has been doing it for a while, there is an opportunity to improve health and find a new path for managing complex emotions or life experiences. Firefly provides individual, family and group counseling to address self-harming behaviors. We also offer an intensive outpatient program for those who need increased care and support.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma can be a single event or a series of adverse experiences that occur over time, these may include relational and interpersonal violence. Firefly believes in integrated trauma treatment approach, meaning there is no one-size-fits-all approach to trauma. This work is individualized and collaborative with the client and family integrating treatment practices for trauma recovery.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a common condition in which the person excessively worries about a variety of different topics or a specific topic or experience. This worry is excessive and uncontrollable and associated with additional symptoms of anxiety. Firefly clinicians are available to provide support from a relational and cognitive behavioral approach to reduce stress and worry and engage in life.

name: Kasha Woods
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome. I offer compassionate counseling that honors and celebrates your whole being: mind, body, & spirit. www.kashawoods.com/contact
ideal_client: I love supporting adults who long for more balance and ease in life. I assist clients in shifting well-worn relationship patterns by reconnecting with authentic needs, clarifying boundaries, and learning to communicate with care. Many of my clients identify as highly sensitive, empathic, intuitive, introverted, or neurodivergent, and seek relief from overwhelm, anxiety, or attachment wounding. I offer space for grief tending, spiritual exploration, and reflection on life’s mysteries.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I combine somatic (body-focused), mindfulness-based, and depth (psychodynamic) approaches to explore messages that arise through body symptoms, beliefs, patterns, and/or dreams. I work experientially, which means we include your present moment, felt-sense experience to discover direct insight and avenues for change. I have found that these approaches lead to compassionate self-understanding and positive, lasting change. My somatic therapy training includes 7+ years of study in the Hakomi method of mindfulness-based somatic psychotherapy training, including focus in parts work, neurobiology, attachment, character strategies, and trauma-informed practices. My psychodynamic training includes an M.A. in counseling psychology with emphasis in Jungian depth psychology from Pacifica Graduate Institute.

name: Courtney Boyd
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I work with teens (14+), adults, couples and families to address anxiety, depression, conflict, chronic illness, gender identity, and more!
ideal_client: With experience in anxiety, depression, chronic illness, gender identity, and more, I offer tailored counseling to meet your unique needs. My approach fosters a safe, supportive space where you can explore your thoughts and feelings without judgment. Together, we can tap into your inner strength and develop strategies for a more fulfilling life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am excited and prepared to work with clients from a wide array of backgrounds. As a member of the queer community, I have a deep understanding of the unique experiences and challenges faced by LGBTQIA2S+ individuals and am committed to creating a safe and affirming therapeutic space for all. With a background as a registered nurse, I bring a unique perspective and skill set to address the interplay between physical and mental health. Whether you're managing a chronic condition, navigating life transitions, or seeking to enhance your overall quality of life, I believe therapy can be a valuable tool.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I was drawn to the field of therapy by a deep admiration for the human spirit's resilience. Witnessing people overcome challenges inspired me to support others on their healing journeys. I believe everyone possesses the capacity for growth and a fulfilling life, and consider it an honor to accompany individuals on this path.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Through a personal passion, I have been drawn to feminist theory as it challenges the gender roles and cultural stereotypes that can often contribute to personal distress. By focusing on empowerment and social change, feminist therapy aims to help clients develop a strong sense of self, challenge oppressive systems, and advocate for themselves and others.

name: Leif Moa-Anderson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: There is no such thing as a part f yourself that has no purpose and should be gotten rid of, integration works better.
ideal_client: I used to say that I had no agenda except that of my clients, however, I’m finding that is not entirely true, I want freedom and agency for everyone. It turns out that some people don’t want agency and freedom, and I can understand why. Agency and freedom mean that you have to take responsibility for your actions and that is a big burden to shoulder. But for those of you who are willing to take on that burden, I can help you with the stress that comes with it.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am only a mirror from which you can see your own mind. I will not tell you what to do, I have no answers, I have no judgements. I am here to reflects the inner world that you show me. I will reflect your light to illuminate your shadows. I will change the angle of reflection at times to show you new perspectives. I will ask you questions to help you see the shadows on the cave wall as shadows they are. I will help you see that you hold the chains that bind you and show you how to let them go. What you do with this from there is up to you. Sometimes you may learn that you like what you see and don't want to change it after all. Some things you may discover you can't change, and I will help you accept those. What you can and want to change will take time, practice, and patience, but it can be done. You're going to change anyway, you might as well be intentional about it.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a person of strong opinions, loosely held.-Unknown: Your resistance to what is, is the cause of your suffering.-Morihei Ueshiba: The only true wisdom is knowing you know nothing. -Socrates: I cannot teach anyone anything, I can only make them think.-Socrates: Take what works, leave the rest.-Bruce Lee: If you see failure as weakness, you will become weaker. If you see failure as opportunity, it can make you stronger. Nothing can't hurt you, for it is nothing, and an empty bucket gives the opportunity to fill it. Therefore, don't be afraid of feeling empty, for there is freedom in it. My answer to the great epistemological question, how do you know that you know what you know, is that you don't; accepting this is very freeing. I am not a nihilist, however, I believe that the scientific method is as close to real knowledge as humans will ever get; and, there is morality, it’s just that morality is a continually unfolding process that we are part of, not something set in stone.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I studied philosophy before I studied psychology and do believe that the existential conundrums of the human condition are at the root of all our struggle. However, I know that I know nothing. So, I will not tell you what to do, for I have no answers, however, I also have no judgments. I will only help you see through the haze of feelings, thoughts, beliefs, and constructs, and accept was is.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: When I took a certificate program in CBT, I realized that this it is how I automatically and already approached therapy. This is very useful for changing behaviors, which is part of what therapy is about, and I find it useful because sometimes he have to work out the old habits, even once our mind has already changed.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: DBT was born out of CBT and mindfulness, both of which I have studied separately. Getting certified in DBT, thus, seemed natural. I don't do the strict protocols of DBT, which is a group therapy, but I use a lot of the principles frequently.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a natural part of existence, in fact, you need it! However, not all anxiety is useful and too much can be a really big problem. However, we can learn to manage anxiety and help keep it to a functional level. I have helped many clients with OCD, social anxiety, hoarding, and PTSD driven phobias. I use mindfulness based CBT to address the behaviors, a systems perspective to address the thoughts, and a Existential/Humanist approach to address the deeper anxieties we all share.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: There is a theory that all psychologic issues stem from attachment wounds and that everyone one has attachment wounds. Now, I'm not sure if that is really true, but no ones parents were prefect. I have helped with deep attachment issues such as, Reactive Attachment Disorder, Borderline Personality Disorder, and chronic codependence. Your attachment wounds may not be that severe, but they are may still be negatively affecting your relationships in ways you don't realize.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Whether you are a part of a couple (or poly) or just come in by yourself, or maybe it's about platonic or work relationships, this has been the main focus my academic studies. My Masters degree is actually in Systems Psychology, which is basically the perspective that an individual's psychology is driven, at least in part, by all of the systems with which they are connected or even have been connected. I have helped many clients improve their relationships with themselves and others.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I have participated in several men's groups and was elected leader of the men's group at my graduate school my second year. I have spent many years working through my own issues with masculinity and have found comfortable place with it, but I know from personal experience that the journey is not easy. Cultural ideas about masculinity are changing and much of what used to be taught about being a man is now seen as negative, but it is still possible to be a good man and I can help with that.

specialities.name: Personality Disorders
specialities.description: If you have been diagnosed with a personality disorder and have received enough treatment for individual outpatient therapy to be appropriate, I may be able to help you. I have experience helping people with Borderline Personality Disorder, Dissociative Identity Disorder, Narcissistic Personality Disorder, and Obsessive Compulsive Personality. I highly recommend at least one full round through a Dialectic Behavior Therapy (DBT) group course, which takes six months, before individual therapy.

name: Dawn Forrester
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: In-person availability! Together, let's explore your path to growth, healing, and positive change.
ideal_client: Now accepting in-person appointments! Life transitions touch us all—whether it’s divorce, an empty nest, menopause, career dissatisfaction, or retirement. Are you feeling stuck or uncertain about your next step? Change can feel overwhelming and even frightening, leaving you questioning your ability to navigate it successfully. You may feel helpless, sad, or even angry—but there is hope. You are resilient, and together, we can unlock your inner strength to create meaningful, positive change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In 2000, I earned my master’s degree in counseling with a heartfelt mission to help people create positive change and transformation in their lives. I believe we all hold the power within us to shape our future and live authentically. My goal is to help you identify and build on your strengths, guiding you toward a life filled with purpose and meaning. Together, we’ll work to uncover your power, navigate challenges, and move forward with hope, clarity, and support. Using a blend of positive and cognitive theoretical frameworks, I help clients embrace change and overcome obstacles to living a fulfilling life. I listen with compassion and understanding, fostering a strong therapeutic connection to empower you to take action and create the life you deserve.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: My goal is to support you in uncovering what may be holding you back while highlighting and harnessing your unique strengths. Together, we'll nurture your inner potential, guiding you toward a life that feels authentic, purposeful, and fulfilling. With hope, clarity, and meaningful support, we’ll chart a path forward that empowers you to thrive.

name: April Slabosheski
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: You're not too much, and you're not alone. I offer an affirming space for you to explore identity, ease stress, and build self-trust.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Therapy is a place where you get to be yourself. I draw on various counseling theories as well as my personal experiences, identities, and values of anti-racism and intersectional feminism to support you as you work toward your goals. While we can be wounded and traumatized in relationships that don’t meet our needs, the counseling relationship offers a unique connection that can be a source of strength, consistency, and security. Over time, therapy can help us strengthen other relationships in our lives and help us find, or create, the communities we need, even if we’re not born into them.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: No matter what you’re going through, you don’t have to do it alone. I work in person and via telehealth with individuals ages 15+ who are exploring trauma, relationships, attachment patterns, ADHD and other neurodivergence, self-esteem, anxiety, depression, and more. People seek therapy for all kinds of reasons: maybe you’re feeling stuck, not sure who you are anymore, or disconnected from those you care about the most. Perhaps you find yourself not doing the things you really want because of shame or fear. It could be that something big has changed, or maybe you just wish life made more sense than it does right now.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory suggests that our experiences with childhood caregivers continue to shape our lives as we grow older. In therapy, we'll explore the connections between your earliest relationships, the ways you see yourself, and what you expect from others. I believe that consistent and trustworthy connections like the one we can form in therapy can support you feeling a deeper sense of belonging in yourself and the world.

specialities.name: Nonviolent Communication
specialities.description: Often, pain and distress comes from needs that have not been met, but sometimes we don’t even know what those needs are. Nonviolent Communication is a tool we can use in therapy to help you understand your feelings, identify the needs they reveal, and make changes that align with your best interests. We can also draw on Nonviolent Communication to support you in expressing yourself to others, which can help foster more genuine, connective, and satisfying relationships.

specialities.name: Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy
specialities.description: Anxiety, panic, and OCD can drain our energy, make it difficult to show up in daily life, and keep us from trying new things. I’m trained in Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP), a framework we can use in therapy to help you gradually tolerate anxiety, fear, and discomfort, helping you feel more present and engaged in your life.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Sometimes, our relationships get stuck in patterns we don't understand. I draw on Emotionally Focused Therapy to support you in exploring your feelings and needs in relationships, including your relationship with yourself. Together, we’ll slow things down to understand the patterns that make you feel stuck, and gently build ways of connecting that feel safer and more satisfying.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Our experiences, feelings, and struggles exist within important social contexts.
