As a feminist counselor, I make space for us to explore the power dynamics, identities, and social roles that shape your life, including dynamics within the therapy relationship, to support you in deepening your sense of agency, self compassion, personal choice, and well-being.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can make it difficult to focus, rest, and feel like yourself. I bring an attachment lens to working with anxiety to support you in recognizing anxiety triggers, identifying anxious thoughts and feelings, and investigating the ways anxieties may connect to earlier life experiences. Together, we can help you calm your nervous system, tolerate distress, and address patterns that keep you stuck.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Neurodivergence is a natural part of human diversity, yet many of us who are neurodivergent have felt as if we’re “too sensitive” or “too much.” My goal as a neuro-affirming therapist is to create a space where you feel accepted and empowered to explore your identity and strengths without the pressure to mask. I also love collaborating to find ways to honor your day-to-day needs and support your goals while navigating a neurotypical-dominant and ableist culture.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma can shape the ways we relate to others and understand ourselves, making it difficult to trust other people, ask for help, make decisions, and create boundaries. In therapy, we’ll work to build a safe feeling "container" for you to explore all the parts of yourself. I'll show up with warmth, honesty, and care, and together we'll help you strengthen the supports in your life, set boundaries that reflect your feelings and values, and give yourself the care you need.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I am a queer therapist and love working with queer and trans folks to find ways to nurture your sense of self, create meaningful connections with others, and embrace the fullness of your identities. I bring a perspective that recognizes the complexities of power, identity, and the unique strengths that come with living authentically.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can grow from pain, trauma, or feeling cut off from ourselves or others, leaving us feeling stuck, isolated, and unsure of our place in the world. In therapy, I'll create a space for you to explore all the layers of your experience, helping you reconnect with your strength and reclaim your sense of belonging.

name: Susan Rosenthall
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My goal is working together to identify patterns in your life that may no longer be useful/ productive, then developing options for change

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Depending on your needs and goals, I offer brief problem-solving therapy and/or longer-term psychodynamic psychotherapy. By design, I have maintained a broad-based practice, welcoming clients with many presenting concerns. However, some of my areas of special expertise include: Adoption (including adoption consultation & work with all members of adoption triad) Anxiety including AlphaStim Assertiveness Attachment and attachment issues Communication Considering parenthood (for single people, same sex couples, older parents) Couples therapy Depression Divorce/separation FASD Family of origin issues Fertility and infertility Gender identity Giftedness Grief and loss Jewish identity Life transitions LGBTQ+ identified Parenting concerns (including one's own issues playing out in parenting) Reactive attachment disorder Relationship concerns Religious and cultural legacies Self-esteem Single parenting Substance abuse Trans-cultural and trans-racial issues Trauma/PTSD Women's issues

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I graduated from Reed College with a BA in English, in retrospect a wonderful foundation for listening to and coming to understand my clients' life stories. Following my BA, I received an MAT (Master of Arts in Teaching), also from Reed. Some years later, I returned to Portland State University and earned a Master's degree in Social Work. I was a social worker in the heart of London before returning to Portland to begin my private practice. (more coming......................)

name: Bree Koenig
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide a kind, thoughtful approach to exploring what is impacting your wellbeing and will support your processes of healing and change.
ideal_client: I provide therapy for young to middle-aged adults from various backgrounds of ethnicity, sexual orientation, gender identity, and socioeconomic status. My focus is to work with adult individuals struggling with perfectionism, high sensitivity (HSPs), anxiety, depression, and developmental trauma. *Note: I am only seeing clients via Telehealth at this time.*

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy involves person-centered, psychodynamic, and relational modalities that enable us to explore lifelong, underlying patterns of thinking and behavior in a safe and connected environment. My therapeutic style allows me to hold sensitivity towards your emotional and cognitive state while empowering us to access insights into what experiences and beliefs have impacted your wellbeing. With these insights we will explore the most effective forms of coping and change that will be most beneficial to your personal needs.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe that everyone deserves an opportunity to foster an understanding of their own mental health and create insight into what is needed in order to build healthy, personalized approaches to self-care, coping, and communication. Building this type of self-awareness and reaching the point of implementing these skills is often daunting, so connecting with a therapist to support you in processing through these experiences will help lead to feeling genuine change.

name: Terra Marzano
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Healing is possible.
ideal_client: When we are hurting -- whether it be from a break-up, trauma, physical illness, life transitions, or the protracted stress from the pandemic -- we can feel so alone. The world is not always easy on us and being human is hard! When it gets to be too much, having a dedicated space where we feel safe, accepted, and well-nurtured can bring immense relief.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Attachment-oriented, I draw from training in contemporary psychoanalysis to promote resilience, adaptation and emotional freedom. My work is not centered on symptom-reduction, but is focused more on getting to the roots of your turmoil and transforming your relationship to yourself in order to find relief. I bring mindfulness and body-based awareness into nearly every session, trusting and honoring your inherent somatic wisdom. I am trained in EMDR with advanced training in Flash Technique, both of which are effective via video visits, always within the context of well-established psychotherapy relationship.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I am diligent in my efforts to be trauma-responsive, radically gender and identity-affirming, and anti-racist. I interrogate my own biases and participate monthly in individual and group consultation to ensure my work is consistent with the values I hold as a person and as a professional social worker. I strive for the day where all of us can celebrate seeking care for our whole selves, body, mind and spirit.

name: Joby Mahto
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Please send me a message if you are interested in being on my waitlist. Openings anticipated in late May/early June.
ideal_client: I have found that the "best fit" client for me is someone who appreciates humor, values honesty and is motivated to engage in the therapeutic process. I have extensive experience working with people who have difficulty managing overwhelming emotions due to complex PTSD, identify as "Highly Sensitive" and who may struggle with anxiety and/or depression. I have recently completed Level 1 training for Internal Family Systems and I am eager to work with clients who are interested in doing IFS.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I specialize in working from a relational foundation informed by attachment theory while incorporating Internal Family Systems, Mindfulness, Narrative Therapy, and Polyvagal theory. I believe my clients would describe me as animated, engaged, direct, curious, humorous, and down-to-earth in session. I value collaboration and anti-oppressive practices in my approach to therapy.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Prior to getting my graduate degree in Social Work, I worked in a variety of social service settings including in Juvenile Justice, a Women’s Shelter, and an Arts focused nonprofit working with youth in foster care and those experiencing houselessness in New York City and in Los Angeles, CA. I then moved to Oregon and completed my MSW degree at Portland State University in 2013 and have since worked in many different levels of care- from inpatient hospitalization, day treatment, integrated behavioral health, and now- outpatient therapy.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Level 1 Trained through the IFS Institute

name: Amanda Holden, LPC, CADC-I
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help individuals & couples move from overwhelm, self-doubt, & dissatisfying relationships to living with joy, connection, & confidence.
ideal_client: Most of my clients experienced emotional neglect or other forms of developmental trauma as children. Many were raised with well-intentioned, yet emotionally-immature parents & now struggle with heightened anxiety & hypervigilance, feeling shut down or highly anxious in relationships, or feeling as though they are "too much" or "not enough". All come to me with the hope of healing & building healthier relationships, but don't know where to start or haven't been able to do it on their own.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I'm a trauma-informed therapist trained in Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Emotionally-Focused Therapy (EFT) & the Gottman Method. I specialize in working with couples who are struggling to feel connected, have communication issues, or are having the same arguments on repeat. I also specialize in working with individuals who are struggling with anxiety, anger or irritability, setting healthy boundaries or saying 'no', or dealing with difficult relationships. I use my training & expertise to help you heal childhood wounds, gain practical tools to more effectively cope with anxiety & overwhelm, set better boundaries, and improve communication & intimacy with your partner(s). Some, but not all of my clients are also raising children & struggling to be the parents they want to be. All of my work is done through a feminist, anti-hate, anti-racist, decolonized, LGBTQIA2S+ affirming lens. I don't always get it right, but I'm sure as hell going to keep showing up to do the work.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I'm a therapist because I love people. I know I'm going to like you. I always do. If you are coming in for couples' therapy, I'm going to like your partner, too. I'll see the best in you and how damn hard you've already tried before you ever reached out for therapy. I see so much hurting around me & I want to be a healing force in this world. I want to help hurting partners communicate in ways that build trust, increase safety in the relationship, and make people feel like they've got the best, most supportive ally in this often scary and difficult world. I want to help individuals see their innate goodness, to help them feel seen and heard, and to help them cope with the overwhelm, anger, and anxiety they feel too much too often.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: I firmly believe that although you may need support or guidance to reach your therapeutic goals, you are the expert on your own life and you are not your problems. Since my extensive research into Narrative Therapy during my graduate studies, I have utilized this form of psychotherapy to help clients re-author their own lives.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Nurturing a spirit of mindfulness (practicing active, non-judgmental, curious, neutral attention to our moment-to-moment experience) is the foundation of the work I do with clients.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I utilize cognitive-behavioral therapy methods with almost all of my clients. I have discovered that profound therapeutic change often occurs for those who not only accept and make peace with their internal experience but also create practical solutions in their daily lives through behavioral and cognitive change.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: For lasting impact, I have found the foundation of personal growth must be the fostering of a deep sense of worthiness exactly as one is. Although a commonly-held belief, self-judgment and self-criticism do not motivate us to do better; they keep us stuck in the very patterns we seek to avoid. Only when we learn to let go of unhelpful narratives about who we are can we realize our full potential.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I’m a Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor (CADC) and enjoy working with those struggling with patterns of substance use. Whether your teen is using meth, you’re a successful professional concerned about your use of opiates, or you’re worried about your partner, I’m here to help. I have no interest in stereotypes or labels and am here to provide the support you need to reach your goals.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: I’m a Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor (CADC) and enjoy working with those struggling with patterns of substance use. Whether you suspect your teen is drinking too much, you’re a successful professional concerned about your own use alcohol, or you’re worried about your partner's drinking, I’m here to help. I have no interest in stereotypes or labels and am here to provide the support you need.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: To help clients address self-esteem concerns, I use a combination of mindfulness skills, cognitive strategies, and the development of supportive narratives. With these tools, I assist clients in integrating shame resiliency skills into their daily lives.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: In helping you find effective relief from anxiety, I utilize a mindfulness-based approach coupled with cognitive-behavioral skills and strategies.

name: Becca Schwartz
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I offer a safe and warm therapeutic space where all parts of you can show up and be explored with respect and curiosity.
ideal_client: I strive to support clients in identifying and living into their values, understanding and regulating their nervous system, building self-compassion, deepening their mind-body connections, and cultivating relationships with themselves and others in their lives. I offer virtual/online sessions only. I take OHP/Health share/CareOregon, PacificSource, and my out of pocket rate is $185 a session. Sliding scale fees are available so please email to discuss your needs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is relationship based, client centered, trauma informed, and at times playful. I utilize several different therapeutic modalities including EMDR, IFS, Mindfulness and somatic practices, Compassion Focused Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Narrative therapy, and Anti-oppressive frameworks. My therapeutic work is informed by past experience working in community mental health organizations, addiction treatment, and college counseling. Each of which has guided my understanding of the diverse and complex struggles we face as humans.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I identify as a sex positive, pleasure centered, queer and gender affirming therapist. Social justice is the foundation of my practice and I will collaborate with you on dismantling and resisting systems of oppression that impact your life.

name: Carol-Joy Brendlinger
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I work with individual adults, young adults, and couples dealing with depression, relationship issues, and a variety of other topics.
ideal_client: I desire to create a safe space for you if you are in a place of transition, going through loss and grief, or, struggling in your relationships. I am passionate about creating a welcoming and safe space for people to have the courage to face their fears, heal, and live into the deepest expression of themselves.

approaches.My Background: I specialize in both group and individual work. As a certified Spiritual Director, I have held contemplative and mindfulness-based spaces for individuals to slow down and connect with their wisdom and truth. My training has grounded me in the awareness that it is our bodies that give us our answers and when we stop to breathe and listen we can find the answers we have been seeking.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I am in the field of Counseling because I believe that more mental health support is needed in our world, due to the many challenges and traumatic experiences that individuals face. I think that people are resilient and capable of healing and positive change. My life has been focused on peacemaking, social justice, eco-justice, and equality for all people. It is important for me to continue to listen to and learn from marginalized populations and be active in finding ways to provide resources and care to those who do not have access to many resources.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I am trained in Restoration Therapy which is based on Attachment Theory.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: I have 20 years of experience working with clients as a spiritual director and bringing contemplative practices and mindfulness into sessions. Gestalt therapy is an effective theory that I work with to help clients come into the present moment and connect with movement and their bodies.

specialities.name: Nonviolent Communication
specialities.description: Over the past years, I have worked with non-violent communication to help clients build skills in understanding and owning their feelings and knowing how to best communicate with others in times of conflict.

name: Nani Waddoups
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Navigating toward existential meaning, and consideration of conditions at play are the roots of my counseling philosophy and style.
ideal_client: I am committed to a life of self-study and to supporting others in their desire for self-understanding. I love the collaborative effort of unlocking the puzzle of why we do what we do, why we are impacted by specific words or experiences. I believe that it is this self-knowledge and awareness that supports us in our efforts to both be creative in our visions for our lives, and in the strategic navigation of the way there.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a professional listener. My work is to attune with my clients, and to strive for understanding. I believe that we all want to be understood, and to understand ourselves. My natural curiosity, my training and my work with clients continue to hone my skills for asking the right questions, sharing my perspective, and checking in to confirm we are still on the right course.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a Masters in Counseling from Lewis & Clark Graduate School in Portland, and my private practice includes work with individuals, couples, families and groups. I have also worked as a group facilitator at the Dougy Center for Grieving Children and their Families, and for the Washington County Counseling Center working primarily with inmates in the county residential treatment dorm. Counseling is a second career for me. The messiness of life has been my best teacher. I am 60 years old, and have navigated these years in ways that have helped me appreciate the richness and complexity of what it is to be human, and to celebrate the potential for self-determination.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment Theory is an extraordinarily helpful tool to understand how we developed our baseline relational styles. By studying our earliest emotional attachments to our primary caregiver(s), we can understand how we developed our sense of trust, security, and self-assuredness in relationship to others. Knowing your attachment style can become a navigational compass in relationships.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: My approach is influenced by the Buddhist concept of 'dependent arising,' which means that whatever arises in us is the result of multiple conditions. Part of therapy is exploring the conditions of the moment to see how they may be influencing what is currently arising in one's attention or through one's behavioral inclinations.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: My therapeutic philosophy is rooted in the existential belief that we want meaning and purpose for our lives, and that we have the strengths to make our lives how we want them to be. My job is to creatively engage in the process of clarifying that vision and supporting the efforts to navigate the way there.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: There are innumerable conditions affecting our moods at all times. Sometimes we are aware of them -- a loss, a joy, anticipation. Other times these conditions are outside of our consciousness -- the pain in the world touching our hearts, a lingering dream. Therapy helps to characterize the quality of an emotional state, and then explores our ability to affect the conditions at play.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Part of the Existential philosophy that guides my practice is the acceptance that Anxiety is a part of being human. Awareness that our time is limited, and ultimately we alone are responsible with what we do with our lives, creates a natural anxiety. When this anxiety rises to a distressing level, therapy helps to recalibrate, and transform that energy into fuel for a self-directed life.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Though it may seem like therapy cliche, exploration of our attachment style in our family of origin is critical in the illumination of adult relational patterns. How secure we are in the world of relationships is influenced by our earliest attachments. Are we trusting? Or are we in anticipation of a betrayal? Can we be authentic and transparent? Or do we fear abandonment and rejection?

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is a deeply personal experience, and everyone processes thier grief in their own unique way. There is no right way to grieve, no timeline on which we can mark when grieving 'should be over,' no roadmap of what to expect after a loss. My work with clients experiencing loss is to validate all of their responses as right for them, and as a necessary part of the transformational process.

specialities.name: Coronavirus/COVID-19
specialities.description: The global pandemic of COVID-19 has introduced a myriad of new conditions that impact both our logistical and internal worlds. The effort to navigate all that is arising in us can be exhausting, and the unpredictability of the future is mirrored by the fickleness of our emotional responses. My work is to support healthy coping and emergence from this time changed in ways of your own choosing.

name: Karen Albert
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Hi, I’m Karen Albert (she/her), a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner offering thoughtful, collaborative medication support.
ideal_client: You might be feeling anxious, down, emotionally drained, or unsure about what’s next—but you know you want support that feels respectful and thoughtful. Maybe you’re considering medication for the first time, or maybe past experiences left you feeling rushed or unheard. If that sounds familiar, I’m here to offer something different. I work with adults who want to feel more grounded, more balanced, and more like themselves again.

approaches.What I Specialize In: Whether you're navigating stress, depression, trauma, or mood shifts that feel confusing or intense, we’ll take things at your pace. My goal is to help you feel understood—not just as a list of symptoms, but as a whole person with a story that matters. I specialize in providing medication support for anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, trauma-related concerns, and other mental health challenges. I also have experience working with clients who are managing multiple stressors or going through big life changes. If you’re not sure what’s going on—only that something feels off—we’ll explore that together with care and curiosity. My approach is gentle, collaborative, and focused on finding what works best for you, whether that includes medication, therapy, or both.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: If what you need is a provider who listens fully, explains clearly, and collaborates with you every step of the way, that’s exactly how I approach care. I don’t believe in one-size-fits-all care. Instead, I take time to understand what’s been hard, what matters to you, and what kind of support actually feels helpful. Clients often tell me they appreciate my calm presence, my openness to questions, and the way I explain things clearly without judgment. If you’ve had providers in the past who didn’t make space for your voice, I want this to feel different. We’ll work together—at your pace, on your terms—toward care that supports your well-being. As a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner, I specialize in medication management, but our work together will always be about more than just prescriptions. I believe in integrative care that considers your whole self. Medication can be a valuable part of healing, and when combined with therapy, it often leads to even greater progress.

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: Medication can be an important part of mental health care—but it should never feel like the only option. My approach to medication management is collaborative, thoughtful, and grounded in trust. I take time to explain your options clearly, answer your questions honestly, and listen to your concerns without judgment. You’ll always be an active participant in your care. I prescribe and monitor meds for anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, PTSD, and related concerns.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I often incorporate principles of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) into our work together, especially when exploring how your thoughts, emotions, and behaviors are connected. During appointments, we might identify unhelpful thought patterns, discuss coping strategies, or explore how your mindset influences how you're feeling day to day. These conversations can enhance the impact of medication and offer additional tools for managing anxiety, depression, trauma, and mood-related concerns.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I often weave mindfulness-based strategies into our appointments—whether that means slowing down to notice how stress shows up in your body, exploring grounding techniques, or helping you reconnect with the present moment. These approaches can be especially helpful for managing anxiety, trauma, and mood shifts. Mindfulness isn’t about “clearing your mind”—it’s about building awareness and learning to respond to your thoughts and emotions with more compassion and clarity.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: My approach to care is holistic, which means I see you as a whole person—not just a diagnosis or a set of symptoms. I take into account your mental, emotional, physical, and social well-being when we talk about treatment. That might include discussing sleep, nutrition, stress, relationships, or lifestyle alongside medication options. Healing isn’t just about one solution—it’s about understanding the bigger picture and finding what truly supports your overall well-being.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: I use motivational interviewing to support you in exploring your goals, values, and what change might look like for you—without pressure or judgment. This approach is rooted in curiosity and respect. I’ll ask thoughtful questions to help you reflect on what matters most to you and what feels realistic. Whether you're feeling unsure about starting medication or navigating other life changes, we’ll move at your pace and make decisions together, with your voice leading the way.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: When anxiety hits, your mind may race, sleep disappears, and tension keeps you on edge. In our sessions we’ll unpack how anxiety shows up for you, explain what’s happening in your brain and body, and choose care that fits your life. Medication can help, and we’ll consider it together—no pressure, at your pace. I often pair meds with therapy and will coordinate with your therapist or connect you to someone on our team. Let’s help you feel steady, present, and more like yourself again.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Life changes—like a breakup, move, job loss, or health issue—can leave you feeling overwhelmed, stuck, or unlike yourself. If you’ve been struggling to adjust, it’s okay to ask for support. Together, we’ll explore how this transition is affecting you and what might help you feel more grounded. I’ll offer education, coping tools, and, if appropriate, we’ll discuss whether medication might ease symptoms like anxiety, irritability, or sadness. Support is available and healing is possible.

specialities.name: Bipolar
specialities.description: Living with bipolar disorder can feel like riding emotional waves—periods of high energy, impulsivity, or restlessness, followed by stretches of deep fatigue or disconnection. These shifts can be confusing, exhausting, and disruptive to your daily life. In our work together, we’ll explore what you’ve been experiencing and discuss treatment options that support stability and well-being. I offer thoughtful, collaborative medication management and coordinate care with therapists when helpful.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can make everything feel heavier—getting through the day, connecting with others, or even recognizing yourself. You might feel numb, irritable, exhausted, or weighed down by self-doubt. If that’s been your experience, we’ll take time to understand what’s going on beneath the surface. I offer compassionate, personalized medication management to ease symptoms and support your overall well-being. We’ll move at your pace and discuss treatment options together.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: PTSD can show up in so many ways—flashbacks, sleep issues, feeling on edge, or shutting down when something reminds you of what happened. In our work together, we’ll talk about how trauma is affecting your daily life and explore care options that support your healing. I offer medication management to help with symptoms like anxiety, mood changes, and sleep disruption, always with space for your questions and input.

name: Niko Delgado-McGee
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I focus on building a caring, respectful relationship to help you reconnect to your Self.
ideal_client: Maybe you feel lost, isolated or a prisoner in your own head. Maybe you feel like an outsider. You have dug yourself into a habit or addiction that you can't seem to pull yourself out of. A part of you may feel hopeless for real change while another part of you wonders about what healing would feel like. I believe that many of our wounds are relational and thus can be healed through on.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I provide culturally-informed trauma and addiction services to adults and teens (15+) in Oregon and Washington. I offer IFS informed EMDR, psychedelic integration, and somatic focused mindfulness to help you calm your mind and reconnect to your body. I also specialize in addiction counseling so we can address coping mechanisms that no longer serve you as we get to know each other.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am one of the few mixed race pacific island counselors and am passionate about helping marginalized communities and allies. I have years of experience working with veterans, mental health clinicians, teens in crisis, and families who have been affected by addiction. I value the importance of connecting with nature and am happy to meet you at a local park for our sessions.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am EMDRIA approved EMDR level I trained. I have experience working with individuals who have suffered from child physical, emotional and sexual abuse, child incest survivors and veterans. Drawing from years of experience working as a supervisor at a crisis line, I also work well with first responders who have experienced substantial vicarious trauma.

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: "What are you?" was a question I quickly became accustomed to growing up in the Pacific Northwest. With roots in Chamoru, Irish and Armenian heritage, there is no clean box for me to check. This question has been a lifelong journey in understanding who I am in the context of others, and more importantly how I define myself. I hope to work with others who are embarking on their own cultural journey and are seeking deeper answers to questions about themselves.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: My graduate degree is specialized in addiction studies and I am currently in the process of applying for my CADC. I use motivational interviewing to help insight change and work from a harm reduction model to help you create compassionate goals for yourself. I have experience working with individuals and family members who have suffered from porn, internet, alcohol, cocaine, and cannabis addiction/abuse/dependence.

name: Heather Ackles
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Going through a Break-Up? Separation? Divorce? Therapy to Identify and Align with YOUR Values - Empowering Growth.
ideal_client: 'Was that too much?' 'What does that mean?' You re-read text threads and have lost faith in your ability to make decisions, fearing the repeat of past mistakes. Doubtful of your value and desirability, you prioritize the needs of others - and lose yourself in the process. You wonder if things will ever change and ask, "Are these even my choices? What am I protecting? Who am I trying to be in these relationships? What do I want?"

approaches.What I Specialize In: Relationships (breakups, separation, dating, divorce) bring up anxiety, regret, fear, depression and self-judgment - effecting the relationship we have with ourselves. Resentments, anger, and guilt - toward others and within ourselves - make us feel disconnected and alone. Our therapy sessions help you define what’s missing, unpack who you are, and figure out what you want. As a therapist, my aim is to help you reconnect with yourself. Everyone is different. Our expectations and ideals are influenced by family history, cultural expectations, and unique experiences. My therapeutic 'approach' helps you develop tools to define the relationships you want - and work through anxiety, past regrets, self doubt, negative self-image, and slowly dispose of the negative loud inner-monologue (which comes up, frequently, when trying to navigate the road ahead.)

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I’ve been on all sides of relationships. I am grateful to help people strengthen connection, grow confidence, and develop the foundation of who they are and want to be. Defining our core values is challenging - and yet, needed for empowering growth. As a therapist (and human being), I value barre, spin, dance, art, and music. I value therapy as a source of connection. All humans are interesting, complex, and different - similar to my love for music: Vivaldi (Four Seasons), Otis Redding, and HAIM. I am licensed in Oregon and Washington State. Interested in reaching out? Check out my webpage - or give me a call 503-498-6879.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: What Parts take center-stage? Does your Manager Part guilt-trip as your FireFighter Part advocates for escape via non-stop media scrolling, a Netflix binge, or gaming? Our sessions use Internal Family Systems (IFS) to connect with Protector Parts and Exiled Parts - which may connect with trauma, family history, broken relationships, fears of failure, and being alone. My website has articles on IFS Parts (ADHD and relationships.)

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: What values do you stand by? How have your values changed over time? Where are you now- and where do you want to go from here? Do depression/anxiety blocks get in the way? Acceptance Commitment Therapy (ACT) is a foundation therapy to outline roads and direction for ‘forward’ movement. Even bigger: ACT helps you define what ‘forward’ means to YOU. Our sessions use ACT to help you identify your values - delve into the core of who YOU are - and practice forward movement.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I work with individuals going through relationship life transitions (dating, marriage, and divorce) and openly talk about what comes up within relationship(s.) I have completed Gottman Level One and Level Two training - and provide Gottman tools for relationships within individual sessions (in addition to other methods which include Internal Family Systems (IFS) couples therapy tools.)

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: When you have ADHD various 'barriers' can stand in the way of work, due dates, and relationships. Our sessions allow you to open up, navigate limitations, recognize your strengths and creativity - developing growth. I have many tools for ADHD. My aim is to help you truly define what YOUR goals are, identify your sparks of motivation with specific tools that work for your ADHD. Want to connect? Reach out - I am a ADHD-Certified Clinical Services Provider (ADHD-CCSP).

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: In the midst of relationship upheaval? Whether you are going through divorce, dating, in the midst of a break-up, separation, or in the process of defining co-parenting needs - no relationship is the same. Our sessions help you discover how these challenges can be the foundation for opening your ability to define and practice your values - inspiring ideas, newfound strength, and doing what matters when it comes to relationships and your SELF.

specialities.name: Insomnia
specialities.description: I am trained with CBT-I for insomnia and was the Facilitator/Creator of ReScript Nightmare Group - a closed group for those experiencing recurrent traumatic nightmares. I have experience/training with Exposure, Relaxation, & Rescripting Therapy (ERRT). I have many 'tools' in the toolbox to help people experiencing sleep difficulty and recurrent nightmares.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have experience working with Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) survivors. I created/facilitated the THINK B.I.G. Brain Injury Group weekly Acceptance Commitment Therapy (ACT) group for Brain Injury Survivors - and was board member of Brain Injury Connections NorthWest. I collaborate with Center for Brain Injury Research and Training (CBIRT) & provide Brain Injury education. I am familiar with ways trauma integrates within our lives - and the therapeutic tools to broaden perspective.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: I have experience working with professionals who are amidst "compassion fatigue." (Very connected with 'burn-out') I facilitated the weekly Metropolitan Public Defender Engagement Group for lawyers/legal support staff - which specifically addressed compassion fatigue, a variety of difficulties within the work, as well as work/life balance (AKA: the lack of/guilt connected with work/life 'balance').

name: Lisa Sacker
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Counseling Designed to Meet Your Individual Needs / EMDR
ideal_client: As a mental health professional, I bring nearly a decade of experience to benefit clients from a broad range of backgrounds. My professional style is holistic, high-energy, compassionate, organized, and solution-focused with motivation to assist clients in meeting their needs and develop skills through therapeutic treatment to achieve their optimal level of emotional health. I am available to all individuals at various stages of their mental health journey.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Similarly to my choice of approach, the ultimate objective of our time together will differ between individuals, and we can work together to identify your personal goals. I have experience in providing counseling, assessments, and crisis intervention to individuals struggling with mental health, trauma, and addiction issues. I am well versed in the area of trauma and I bring an understanding of the effects of trauma into my work for the therapeutic benefit of my clients. Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing (EMDR) is just one healing modality I can utilize with clients.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My professional experiences have given me a deep understanding of mental health, trauma, addiction issues and their impact on clients. The attitude I bring to my work conveys both dignity and respect and I hold the belief that people can change. My goal is to create a safe space in which clients can explore their life narrative and navigate moving forward.

name: Jim Seger
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: Clinical Mental Health Master's of Arts (Ph.d., Depth Pyschology -- non-clinical)
intro: Whatever you are experiencing is welcomed! I offer an accepting & collaborative style to help you find a greater sense of belonging & peace.
ideal_client: I offer support to people from across social, political, and identity spectrums. Most of us desire to be at peace with ourselves, connected to others, and effective in achieving what we want in the world. But substantial distress, conflict, emotional turmoil and even physical pain result when we encounter difficulties that frustrate those desires and intentions. Often these difficulties manifest as anxiety, depression, and various types of trauma responses.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Working together, we will discuss the challenges you face and consider the therapeutic approaches that seem most likely to benefit you. In some cases, you might decide to focus on how your family of origin or trauma history gets in the way of more fully being your better, healthier self. In other cases, you might want to work through challenging choices or situations in the present.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As important as self understanding is, therapy is much more than just figuring out the what and why of our ways of being in the world. If understanding alone were enough to heal ourselves and our relationships, life would be much easier. But, for many of us, even after we develop some understanding, we still struggle. As understanding is developed we need to use that understanding to cultivate change. I use the term "cultivate" purposefully. We do not simply use our conscious understanding to impose internal change. Rather, like a farmer, we need to establish generative conditions that allow internal growth and shifts to occur. In some cases, therapy provides an opportunity to practice altering how we act in response to certain situations. In other cases, therapy may be more about figuring out how to create conditions in our lives and routines that allow difficult to fathom healing powers to change us in healthful ways.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I use an integrative approach incorporating Restoration Therapy (empowering mindful choices and changing destructive patterns), Dialectical Behavior Therapy skills (a variation on cognitive behavior therapy), and Motivational Interviewing, along with concepts from Solution-Focused Therapy, Movement Therapy, Family Constellations, Internal Family Systems.

name: Ira Winograd
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am passionate about coming into the Here and Now with clients and believe in the healing power of being witnessed with presence and care.
ideal_client: I specialize in LGBTQ issues, grief counseling, anxiety and depressive disorders, and psychedelic integration.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Using mindfulness based practices I focus on supporting clients in addressing issues of depression, anxiety, and identity issues. In session I emphasize bringing the client’s attention out of thoughts/stories and into their present moment bodily experience with the understanding that more immediate change can occur this way. I enjoy experiencing the client and counselor relationship as a microcosm of the client’s greater relational life, and an opportunity to do deep healing. My approach is strongly influenced by Zen Buddhist Philosophy and practice, Somatic Experiencing, Rogerian Therapy, Logotherapy, Transpersonal Psychology, Psychedelic Integration, Ecopsychology and Non-violent communication. My approach is trauma informed and centers on a social justice, and multi-cultural orientation, acknowledging the complexity of identity.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am an active member of the LGBTQ community and believe in the importance of servicing this community, specifically trans/non binary folks. I am also passionate about plant medicine and am in the process of being certified to offer psychedelic therapy, though currently am only offering psychedelic integration.

name: Jake Cavanah
title: Marriage and Family Therapist
intro: A broken home, falling in love, and more taught me how powerful and influential relationships are. They also led me to this profession.
ideal_client: Empowering preteens, adolescents, families, and young couples to deepen their connections drove me to pursue therapy. New circumstances, unresolved tension, and more can cause loved ones to clash. Addressing these challenges and achieving resolution can strengthen these relationships, ultimately leading to more fulfillment and satisfaction. My clients include youth and adults from broken families, engaged couples, and newly married couples.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Making room for everyone’s uniqueness is essential to creating more harmonious relationships. Every individual deserves space to be themselves and express themselves. This promotes more understanding, ultimately leading to more honest and fulfilling relationships. Growth like this drives real change and strengthens connection. My approach includes examining the influence of a client's family of origin. This includes but is not limited to how their family of origin shaped their beliefs and created their understanding of relationships. I also help the client explore their emotions deeper and their associated experiences. Gaining this level of clarity gives a client insight into themselves and reveals what will be the most effective coping strategies.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Where we come from, how we’re raised, societal norms, and more help shape us. But we also possess a unique superpower that deserves a voice: individuality. This can create challenges in relationships, but it can also make those relationships more fulfilling and meaningful. I believe finding an optimal balance between one's individuality and their relationships is integral to a quality well-being. Learning how to be one's true self and how to accept someone else's true self is how we experience and maintain the deepest connection possible.

name: Lesley Lacny
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: With over 25 years of experience in the field of counseling, I am passionate about supporting my clients through life's challenges.
ideal_client: Are you feeling stuck and aren’t quite sure how to move forward? Are your reactions and behaviors no longer serving you? Are your symptoms keeping you from feeling at ease and making it difficult for you to enjoy the simple day to day moments? I strive to create an environment for you to feel supported and understood while encouraging you to go deeper into exploring what truly lies beneath your actions and reactions, creating opportunity for shifts and transformation.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I can help you develop a greater awareness of yourself and your actions. Together, we will explore ways to move forward using tools to help you turn off your “auto-pilot” and to deepen your understanding of what is underneath your reactions so you can begin living freely and within your control. We will explore the root of behaviors, thoughts, and emotional responses that pull you into “reactive mode”. We will explore the physiological impact this creates in your body and ways to move into an aware state that lends to calm, presence, and a sense of self-control. We will explore alternative ways to manage overwhelming feelings and cope with experiences including: anxiety, depression, stress, trauma, relationship struggles, separation and divorce, addiction, anger, parenting, and life transitions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: For the past 25 years, I have been invited to sit with others during some of their most vulnerable moments. The intimacy held in the relationship between myself and my clients has lent itself to a fulfilling career that touches me well beyond my time spent in sessions. Education and training are essential to developing into a skilled therapist; however, for me, it is also what I have leaned in my sessions with clients that has taught me what it means to endure pain, to put our guards down, and to sit with raw emotion. Seeing people work through difficult things and come out feeling more fulfilled and at peace is what encourages me to continue to show up in my own life with curiosity, compassion, and lightheartedness. As I support my clients to find balance and fulfillment, I too strive to live my life in a way that fulfills me. When I am not sitting with clients, I can be found chasing my boys down mountain bike trails, rock climbing, and finding quiet moments in meditation.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I have been trained in Internal Family Systems (IFS), a compassionate, structured approach that helps us understand and care for the parts of us that carry pain or try to protect us. Together we will create space from thoughts and reactions that no longer serve you and explore the beliefs and emotions beneath- so you can respond with more clarity, curiosity, and calm.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: I trained in Hakomi therapy through the Hakomi Institute of Calgary, Canada, completing a 3-year intensive program. This training immersed me not only in learning the model, but also in experiencing it's transformative impact firsthand. Of all the psychotherapy approaches I have studied, Hakomi therapy has been the most powerful- it fundamentally changed how I practice and deepened the way I support meaningful change in others.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I incorporate mindfulness-based practices to help you slow down, notice your thoughts, emotions, and body sensations with curiosity- even if just for a few moments. This creates space between you and your reactions, allowing you to respond with intention rather than habit. In session, it shifts the focus from simply talking about your experience to actually feeling and noticing it so we can work on a deeper, more integrated level.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I use a "neurobiological" approach for treating anxiety, recognizing that anxiety is deeply connected to both our thought patterns, our emotions, and our physiological (body) responses. By understanding how the brain and the body interact under stress, I will help you develop tools to regulate your nervous system, reframe anxious thoughts, explore the roots of the anxiety, and build lasting resilience.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I work with women navigating a wide range of issues including self-esteem, identity, life transitions, relationships, trauma, parenting, and the ongoing pressure of balancing multiple roles. We will work together to explore your full experience, including your thoughts, emotions, any physiological responses to uncover patterns and to help you feel more grounded, connected, and aligned with yourself.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I support personal growth by addressing your full experience- thoughts, emotions, and physiological responses that may be holding you back. Through a blend of insight-oriented work, nervous system regulation, and practical strategies, I will help you to cultivate clarity, break through internal barriers, and support meaningful and sustainable change.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I work with men to address a wide range of issues including self-esteem, identity, life transitions, relationships, trauma, parenting, emotional expression, and societal expectations. Through direct, honest conversations and practical tools for emotional regulation, I support men in cutting through the noise, confronting what is not working and developing a more solid, present, and intentional way of being.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma can leave a lasting imprint on the brain and the nervous system, often showing up as ongoing fear, shame, or disconnection. In a supportive and protective space, we will work together to gently explore your experience, using tools for regulation, grounding practices and strategies to help your brain process and integrate what it has been holding. The goal is to move out of survival mode and toward a greater sense of safety, stability, and connection with yourself and the world around you.

name: Becky Kuhn
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hello, I'm Becky, a clinical social worker in Oregon and Washington. I specialize in anxiety, relationships and trauma
ideal_client: Are you someone who has identified areas in your life you'd like to work on? Maybe it's improving communication in relationships, address stress and burn out, managing depression and anxiety, or working through trauma. Well, I'm here to walk along side of your in your journey of growth and recovery!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have always had a passion for supporting people in their journey with self discovery and personal growth. As a social worker, I like to work from people from the whole person perspective. I like to examine how our personal beliefs and identity, family and social systems and the environment we grew up and live in, impact our daily lives. I feel for therapy to be effective, you have to believe in the work we are doing together. Therefore, I take a collaborative approach to identifying areas you’d like work on, creating therapy goals, and reevaluating how things are going.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe that our life is a journey and sometimes we encounter things along the way that we may need extra support navigating. This is your growth journey, and I'm here to help you navigate it, and give you some tools along the way. Together, we will identify areas of strength in your life, areas you'd like to improve and work together to achieve those goals. In order to begin this work, I feel that building a strong therapeutic relationship with you is essential. Once that foundation is built, we can being to address the root causes of the concerns you're wanting to work on! I work in suicide prevention for the Portland VA. When I'm not working with others, I am spending time with family and friends, gardening and going on walks with m I am a strong advocate for the LGBTQ community, BIPOC communities, and Veterans, service members and their families.

name: Derek Crain
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Derek Crain cofounded Mindful Therapy Group, a group of over 1,700 independent mental health providers serving Oregon & more, in 2011.
ideal_client: Mindful Therapy Group is a diverse group of over 1,700 independent mental health practitioners serving Washington, Oregon, Arizona, Colorado, & Nevada. Our mission is to create access to high quality mental health care for our communities. As a client, you can expect the highest quality administrative services, warm and professional offices, and a seamless Telehealth experience while receiving care from your provider.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Derek has a Masters in Social Work from the University of Washington as well as a Bachelors in Sociology and Criminology from Cal State Northridge. After practicing and helping clients for nearly a decade, Derek founded Mindful Therapy Group with his wife, Jessica Crain. Derek thinks big picture, always pushing himself and his staff to think more critically, and throws around the phrase “self-compassion,” every chance he gets. Derek is an auditory learner and works in words. He hears the details and will use them to pivot and teach anyone who will listen how to be a better communicator.

approaches.Our Values as Mental Health Practitioner: In today’s fast-paced world, mental health and the need for accessible support is more vital than ever. Making resources readily available not only fosters individual well-being but also strengthens communities and workplaces. Mindful Therapy Group began with one goal: Uniting mental health care providers to make it easier to serve and grow the well being of the communities we live in. By giving as many people as possible access to compassionate, experienced, and forward thinking providers we are doing our part to create a more caring and compassionate world today.

name: Lacey Hawkins
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I am a Marriage and Family Therapist Intern who is passionate about seeing marriages and families restored and thriving.
ideal_client: Having a healthy marriage takes work. Many people invest in their retirement, friends, career, church, etc. but neglect to invest in their marriage and themselves. You have a lot on your plate. If you are what you eat, (or what you invest in), how are your relationships? I can help you work to bring your marriage back into balance and help you go from pain to peace. If your marriage and/or family is "okay" but you'd like it to be stellar, let's talk.

approaches.How I Can Help You: Are you in the middle of a divorce or are divorced and want to find healing and health? Has there been an infidelity in your marriage? Are there issues in your family you need a little extra help with? Are you a blended family looking for help blending? Do you need help walking through marital or family trauma? Are you dealing with the death of a loved one? Are you experiencing infertility? Pregnancy or postpartum issues? Are you a Pastor on the verge of burnout? There is hope! Let's get connected.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: After years of helping youth and families, I realized there were so many times that I wished I knew more so I could be better equipped to help those I served to walk through what they were facing. I decided to attend George Fox University and it was there I confirmed that Marriage and Family Therapy was where I was supposed to be. I am Restoration Therapy focused which means I help individuals, couples, and families to identify the pain cycles in their lives, move those to peace, and help to restore love and trust. My husband and I are Marriage and Family Pastors at our church and we are on a mission to help couples have the best marriage they can. We discovered the "secret" for us is open communication, regular check-ins, date nights, marriage retreats, dreaming together, forgiveness, and laughing a ton together. We have 3 children all under the age of 6 who keep us on our toes and who are the light of our life.

name: James Thatcher
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Do you suspect that you or your child may be on the Autism spectrum, have a learning disorder, have ADHD, or other mental health issue?
ideal_client: We can provide accurate, impactful, and life changing evaluations to give you and your family the answers you need and a clear direction forward. We provide assessments that examine Autism, ADHD, learning disorders, schizophrenia, and complex mental health issues by using cutting edge assessment tools. We look at all overlapping factors to give you a clear picture on your mental health along with tailored recommendations so you can get the help you need and deserve.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In regard to my experience, I have administered, performed, and consulted on over two thousand Autism, neurodevelopmental, cognitive, ADHD, learning disorder, and psychological evaluations on children from 18-months through adulthood using state-of-the-art assessment tools and evidence-based measurements to diagnose even the most complex cases. Furthermore, due to my experience, I am able to test individuals within one day. I write a full report within one week of your in-person visit. This way, you and your family get the answers you need immediately and do not have to wait months for the report, or keep returning for further testing sessions.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Imagine confidently managing daily tasks and improving your social interactions. With over 10 years of experience specializing in neurodivergence, I offer evaluations to help you see your neurodivergence as a gift and a strength in all areas of your life. Ready to embrace your abilities and thrive? Please click on the link to our website above and schedule a free 15-minute consultation today.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I have provided well over two thousand Autism evaluations in my career. I use gold-standard tools, evidence-based measurements, and collateral information to come to a clear and concise diagnosis so you can get the answers you need quickly, along giving tailored recommendations to provide a direction forward and help you and your family.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Is your child or teen having emotional issues, trouble socializing, body image issues, behavioral concerns, or issues with bullying? Working with children/teens through their struggles, using empathy, and providing clear strategies to help is a passion of mine.

name: Cassie Liu
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer a space of safety, trust, and equity to support individuals and families with growth and well-being.
ideal_client: As a second-generation Asian immigrant, I intimately understand the experience of being marginalized and “othered.” It’s from this deeply personal place that my passion for supporting individuals with marginalized and intersecting identities has emerged. I am committed to supporting clients with processing and healing, strengthening a sense of identity, and fostering deep self-compassion and self-assurance.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach can be described as warm, transparent, and insightful, and I strive to bring genuine care and humor to our interactions. Our work together will be collaborative and focused on your feelings of safety and trust in our relationship. Creating a safe space for you to authentically be yourself is at the heart of my practice. We’ll navigate things together at a pace that feels right for you, one step at a time.

name: Mindful Oregon Clinic
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Your journey toward wellness deserves to be as distinctive as your story. We offer personalized and unique healing for every individual.
ideal_client: We stand out by providing personalized treatment plans tailored to each client’s unique needs. Many people reach out to Mindful Oregon Clinic for help with the following challenges: Depression • Mood disorders • Anger Management • Anxiety/Panic Disorder • Eating Disorders • Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) • Loss and Grief • Divorce counseling & Co-Parenting • Brief Strategic Family Therapy • Collaborative Problem Solving • Read more @ https://oregon.clinic/mental-health-therapy-specialties

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Your journey toward wellness deserves to be as distinctive as your story. We believe that healing is deeply personal and unique to every individual; That’s why we craft a therapeutic path tailored to your needs, goals, and experiences. ••• At Mindful Oregon Clinic, we specialize in treating a range of mental health challenges, including anxiety, depression, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), and ADHD, while also addressing many other concerns that impact emotional and psychological well-being. ••• We understand that seeking help can feel overwhelming. Whether you're facing anxiety, trauma, relationship struggles, or navigating life's challenges, we've created a supportive and healing environment to support you. ••• Our team of experienced professionals is committed to creating a safe and supportive environment where you can explore your thoughts and feelings, develop coping strategies, and work toward achieving your personal goals. ••• Read more at https://oregon.clinic/

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: At the heart of my work as a counselor is the belief that everyone has the capacity for growth and change at any stage in their life. I strongly believe that mental health challenges often stem from learned behaviors and patterns that no longer serve us. ••• With the right tools and support, we can unlearn these behaviors and replace them with healthier, more empowering ones. My own journey with anxiety and panic attacks taught me the value of resilience and the transformative power of therapy. Today, I’m passionate about helping others find the same freedom and peace I’ve experienced. ••• I strive to make a positive impact through fostering meaningful connections, supporting personal growth, and advocating for mental wellness. I believe in creating a judgment-free, supportive space where individuals from all walks of life can feel safe, understood, and empowered to take control of their mental health journey. ••• Dr. Shirin Yekekar • CEO/Clinical Director, Mindful Oregon Clinic

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) is a highly effective therapy for treating trauma and other mental health issues. It helps individuals process distressing memories by using guided eye movements, reducing the emotional intensity of those experiences. Its benefits include: • Reducing symptoms of PTSD, anxiety, and depression • Improving emotional regulation and resilience • Boosting self-awareness and fostering a sense of empowerment. It’s a proven method for lasting recovery.

name: Erin Axelrod, MA
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Deep listening, attuned to you, in service of change.
ideal_client: It takes tremendous courage to see ourselves fully, as we are. I love working with individuals who are ready to take steps towards that clarity, who desire a fuller, more authentic, more healthful relationship with themselves and others. I specialize in supporting people who are helpers or caregivers of some sort themselves, as well as individuals navigating anxiety, grief, life transitions, burnout, and relationship challenges.

approaches.How I Can Help You: Sometimes we need someone who can skillfully and empathically mirror back who we are, and where we'd like to be, in order to better understand ourselves and know how to move forward. It is an honor to be this mirror for others. I am certified in Somatic Attachment Therapy from the Embody Lab, and find utilizing this framework to be particularly effective in supporting stuck emotions and attachment wounds. Please reach out to me if you are interested - I currently have some reduced rate spots reserved for this work.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a Master of Arts in mental health counseling from Lewis & Clark Graduate School. Before becoming a counselor, I worked in diverse settings as an environmental educator, studied international systems, and navigated my own mental health challenges. I truly believe in your body and mind's innate wisdom and ability to heal.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Honoring emotion is a continuous thread throughout our work together. As recent research demonstrates: we are not thinking beings who sometimes feel, but rather feeling beings who sometimes think. I will invite your emotional self in a gentle way that always leaves space for your boundaries, process, and where you are at in this moment.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: Tuning into your experience of the present moment is a powerful way to connect with insight and direction. I am trained in experiential therapies that support you in checking in with your present experience in a safe and profound way.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I will support your connection to awareness and choice in each moment of your experience.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Certified in Somatic Attachment Therapy, I am trained to effectively and compassionately facilitate connection with your bodily experience, in order to support you in processing deep emotions and building a more secure attachment with yourself and others

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is such an uncomfortable, distressing experience. At the same time, I find that it holds so much power for transformation when we are supported with the right resources. Working with individuals experiencing anxiety is incredibly meaningful for me. I will meet you exactly where you are, while helping guide you toward calm and grounding.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: If loss is present for you, I am here to be with you in a meaningful way, holding the stance that we grieve because we have loved. It is both a uniquely personal, and universal experience - however grief exists for you, know that you don't have to be alone with it.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: I am passionate about caring for those who spend their energy caring for others. Whether you are a parent, a health care provider, or any other role that requires setting aside your own needs in order to support others, let's create some space for you.

name: Justine Elstad
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: We’re a warm, thoughtful team of therapists here to support you with care, curiosity, and tools that truly help. You’re not alone.
ideal_client: Life can feel incredibly hard sometimes—overwhelming, stuck, disconnected, or just not how you hoped it would be. We are a team of compassionate, reflective therapists who offer a warm and relational space for clients to deepen self-understanding, heal from pain, and grow into more empowered versions of themselves. Whether you’re navigating anxiety, trauma, relationships, grief, life transitions, or simply seeking to know yourself more fully, we’re here to walk with you.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: Our clinicians offer psychodynamic, relational, trauma-informed, somatic, and evidence-based approaches to support meaningful and lasting change. We help clients explore root patterns that shape their current struggles while also offering practical skills to navigate daily challenges. Drawing from cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), we support clients in identifying and challenging unhelpful thoughts and beliefs. Through dialectical behavior therapy (DBT), we build emotion regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness skills. We also incorporate acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT) to help clients reconnect with their core values and take action aligned with what matters most to them. Somatic tools—such as grounding, breathwork, and nervous system education—support clients in feeling more regulated, safe, and resourced. Together, these tools deepen insight and promote greater self-awareness, while offering a clear path toward resilience, connection, and intentional

approaches.Our Values as Mental Health Practitioner: We believe that mental health care is a vital aspect of social justice. We are deeply committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and affirming space for all individuals, particularly those who identify as LGBTQIA+. We are proud to have a team with diverse perspectives, including multiple clinicians who identify as queer, allowing us to offer a deeply affirming and inclusive environment for all clients. We recognize that everyone’s journey is different, and that’s why we offer a variety of therapeutic styles and specialties to best support our clients. Whether you’re looking for psychodynamic therapy, cognitive-behavioral therapy, DBT skills, or somatic approaches, we have a clinician who can help. We’re a bunch of therapy-obsessed, self-proclaimed therapy nerds who are constantly diving into our own work and love learning new techniques and approaches,— because we believe in practicing what we preach and that the best therapists are always learning and growing.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Several clinicians on our team are trained in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), a powerful approach that focuses on helping individuals accept their thoughts and feelings rather than struggle against them. ACT encourages clients to clarify their values and commit to actions that align with those values, even in the presence of discomfort or difficult emotions. By fostering psychological flexibility, ACT helps individuals create a life that is meaningful and in line with their priorities.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Several clinicians on our team are also trained in Somatic Experiencing (SE), a body-focused therapeutic approach that helps individuals process trauma and stress by bringing awareness to physical sensations. SE works by helping clients tune into their bodily experiences, allowing them to release tension and emotional blockages that may be stored in the body.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: Some of our clinicians are trained in Brainspotting, a cutting-edge therapy that helps individuals process and release deep-seated trauma and emotional blockages. By identifying "brain spots" — specific points in the visual field — clients are able to access and release unresolved emotions stored in the brain and body. This method allows for profound healing, as it taps into the brain’s natural ability to process trauma at a deep, unconscious level.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Several clinicians on our team are trained in Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), a structured approach designed to help individuals manage intense emotions, improve relationships, and develop coping skills for dealing with distress. DBT combines mindfulness practices with skills training in areas such as emotional regulation, interpersonal effectiveness, distress tolerance, and acceptance.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: All clinicians have several skills and strategies for anxiety management including: somatic skills, distress tolerance tools, and mindfulness strategies to feel more comfortable and grounded in your skin; cognitive reframing to build awareness around and question patterns of thought that increase anxiety and fear; as well as self acceptance and value work to foster a deeper connection to who you truly are.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Strategies for managing depression include becoming aware of patterns of thought and finding reframes that align more with personal values, behavioral techniques to help break the cycle of inactivity and increase engagement in meaningful activities, as well as self-acceptance and self-compassion strategies to foster a kinder relationship with oneself. Additionally, incorporating mindfulness practices and grounding techniques can help cultivate presence and reduce rumination.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: Clinicians are trained in exposure and response prevention (ERP), the gold standard treatment for OCD, and we approach this process with care and patience. We provide psychoeducation and work through progressive exposures at the client’s pace, empowering them to build confidence in facing their fears. While the process can be challenging, nothing builds confidence like overcoming the patterns of OCD or phobias — each step forward brings a sense of accomplishment and greater confidence.

specialities.name: Social Phobia
specialities.description: The team employs a variety of strategies for managing social anxiety, including identifying and gaining awareness of thought and behavior patterns that trigger anxiety, reframing those thoughts, and exploring personal values. We integrate mindfulness and somatic techniques to help clients feel more grounded and comfortable in their own skin. Additionally, we support clients in gradually increasing their tolerance for social situations, guiding them through the process of building confidence.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Our team uses a combination of behavioral strategies and mindfulness techniques to support individuals with ADHD, helping them develop practical tools for managing time, staying organized, and improving focus. We also emphasize the importance of self-acceptance and self-compassion, encouraging clients to embrace their unique neurodivergent traits without judgment.

name: Haku Mease
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Haku is a trans nonbinary, disabled, and hard-of-hearing Japanese person with Hawaiian, Japanese, and White families.
ideal_client: Haku has experience and strength in working with 2SLGBTQIA+, BIPOC, Chronically sick, Disabled, Neurodiverse, Youth, Individuals, Families, and Communities with a focus on cultural experiences, queer and trans experiences, life transitions, and trauma recovery. Topics within Haku’s scope of practice include: 2SLGBTQIA+, Adjustment, Adolescents, Black, Indigenous, People of Color, Chronic illness, Depression, Disabilities, Grief, Life Transitions, Neurodivergence, and Religious Trauma.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Haku’s therapeutic approach is rooted in a relational worldview that centers storytelling as a means to reclaim personal power and honor people’s unique experiences.
