He does this through narrative therapy, internal family systems, somatic inquiry, and solutions-focused therapy. It can be hard to find the words and language to understand and explain our experiences which is why they enjoy exploring world-building through sand tray, play, and art therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Haku believes in the radical possibilities of change and transformation that exist when we have the safety, trust, and established therapeutic relationship to build towards the new experiences we want and need for ourselves. He views therapy as a practice of collaboration, in trusting people as the experts of their own lives, and of building towards the self-identified skills and experiences that folks would like to explore together, on their own, and in their communities.

name: Sam Trillo
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I'm ready to listen. I am here to facilitate a space that is uniquely yours and cater to what you need.
ideal_client: I work with your needs. I create space to explore your past and current selves. My ideal client is willing to reflect on the past and how it relates to the present and is ready to feel their emotions, even if some of them may be difficult or haven't been fully felt in a long time. You are willing to work on yourself in and out of session. Our therapeutic relationship is collaborative. My work with couples involves learning compassionate and non-judgemental listening techniques.

approaches.My Background and Approach: The most important tools I possess are my listening ability and empathy. The main therapeutic effect then becomes the real relationship you and I create. Through my work as a counselor, I provide a space for you to explore and work through feelings you've never put a name to. I believe Western society has left us detached from our emotions. I can help you learn to trust your emotions. By letting you be yourself and say whatever comes to mind, you can access unknown parts of yourself that deserve to be heard. Talking is just one of the tools we can utilize to find those parts of you that may be hidden; through art, music, and movement, we can communicate with the whole of you. My approach is integrative, meaning I pull from different techniques catered to you. Using humanistic, person-centered, and psychodynamic techniques, we can build a trusting relationship where you feel safe to explore. I believe everyone possesses an unconscious that is ready to be listened to.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I am invested in helping people find their self that has been covered over by capitalism and societal expectations. I believe social media has exacerbated the loss of community and intimate relationships that neoliberal policies helped erode over the last five decades. I believe in community activism and solidarity. Through my counseling work, I hope to help LGBTQ2SIA+ communities, People of Color, BIPOC individuals and organizations, and low-income individuals. I am deeply concerned by the effects of climate change. I'm willing and able to explore the feelings of grief that may be associated with climate change. I have worked with many people who have experienced unexplainable or paranormal events. I am non-judgemental and open-minded to all types of spiritual and metaphysical beliefs.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Our culture is obsessed with productivity. ADHD doesn't mean you haven't tried hard enough to implement the best "organizational hacks." You are unique with your own story to tell. Cutting through the societal stigmas and personal shame about this diagnosis is often the first step to self-understanding.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Modern society has stripped away spirituality and sold it back to us in wellness trends and self-help fads. I believe human spirituality can't be fully narrowed down or defined, but I do think it is reflective of how a person understands themselves through community. Capitalism and neoliberalism have eroded our sense of community and I want to help restore it by starting with you.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Men often hold unconscious beliefs that they must hold in their emotions lest they be perceived as "weak." Or that the only acceptable emotions to express are anger and aggression. I believe vulnerability is a sign of strength. I have worked with men to uncover repressed emotions and put a name to them, allowing them new ways of being.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have worked with couples to come to a mutual understanding about needs that are difficult to express or put words to. I have no preconceived notions about how a relationship should function or look. I help implement listening techniques that will give each person time to be fully heard by others.

name: Nancy Pearson, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Welcome to FAMILIES THRIVE. I am here to help with play therapy, teen and young adult counseling, parenting consultations, and mediation.
ideal_client: Do you want the very best for your child and your family? Are you concerned that your child is not getting the emotional/psychological support they need to thrive? Do you feel that your very best efforts have not stemmed the conflict, depression, anxiety, or behavioral outbursts in your family? Your concern and passion have brought you to the right place and will help you find greater peace and satisfaction in family life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Through active listening, individualized problem solving, and experiential activities, your family will receive the best support for stabilization in transition (school, divorce, relocation, new family member, health crisis), emotional self-regulation for all family members, and skill building to reach maximum potential. I work individually with children and with parents and then work together with the family at large. We build action plans based on your wishes for the outcomes you desire. All families are welcome, regardless of size, composition, race, orientation, or belief systems. My goal is for parents to fall in love again with their children and for children to live joyously and harmoniously within their families. I also offer family mediation for custody and parenting time issues. I am collaborative and focused and can help you find solutions that you are not able to reach on your own. Having done more than 1000 meetings of these kinds, I can offer your experienced support.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been in practice for more than 30 years, working in client homes, offices, clinics, and schools. I sometimes practice with my Labradoodle, Sophie, who lends lightheartedness and joy to the work. I practice from my home office space which is warm and inviting, not coldly clinical. I work for you and with you, not on you. That means that I honor your goals, priorities, and values and work together to achieve your desired ends. Working with Nancy Pearson, "Families Thrive!"

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: There is no dispute that attachment, bonding, and attuned interpersonal relationship forms the foundation for thriving children. When that is achieved the child and the family move together as a working unit. When it is disrupted, all manner of chaos can pursue. Let me help you identify practices to help you strengthen your connections and improve the working ability of your family.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Play is the medium for children to express themselves and to gain mastery over challenges in their environment. It is their 'language' and their course of meaningful action. I have trained and practiced in support of children gaining full expression of themselves. It is also a way for me to learn about a child so that I can assist the parent(s) to find harmony with their child.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: Coaching is another way of describing problem solving. It is generally delivered by someone who has experienced the very thing they are assisting with. The coach has mastered both information and technique and can use the experience thus gained to help others do their best in the field of endeavor. Let me be a source of experience for you to draw on as you work to make your family uniquely yours!

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: The postpartum period is one of the most sensitive periods in a family's life. Major shifts in life experience mingle with the joy of bringing new life into the world and are unsettling for mothers, fathers, and siblings. I have trained to assist you with both the practical and the emotional and can help you smooth out this very important period of transition.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Parenting is one of the biggest challenges and biggest sources of satisfaction that some of us will ever take on. We have such big expectations for ourselves and our children and we struggle to live up to who we want to be. It can be helpful to get perspective and assistance from a trained professional who has also walked this walk. Together we can explore, problem solve, and actualize success!

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: Having experienced the trauma of divorce first hand, I had to find ways to protect my children from the deleterious effects it can have. So I studied, and I practiced, and I took risks both professionally and personally until I could co-parent harmoniously and coach others in how to achieve that outcome. The result is a satisfying co-parenting family life where children flourish!

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Family is the organizing principle that allows each of its members to grow and prosper. When family is going well, each individual is stronger for the experience; when it is not going well, all members suffer. I have helped thousands of families as they struggle with barriers and find solutions to harmonious living that supports the individuality of each of its members.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: There are so many kinds of loss and grief . . . divorce, death, illness, failure, and poignant missed opportunity. They are a part of the life cycle and can not be avoided or overlooked. Instead, they become markers of change that can help inform us and inspire us to meaningful ways of living. I can work with you and your family to integrate grief and loss into your bigger life story.

name: Cameron Kemper
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: With 30 years of practice in mental health and mindfulness, I have the knowledge and life experience to help you with anxiety and depression
ideal_client: I am currently only accepting clients with Oregon Health Plan coverage due to a contract agreement with Medicaid. I am also in network for Blue Cross plans and should be able to start seeing Blue Cross clients again in a few months. I also can provide a superbill for out-of-network clients to make therapy affordable. Additionally I see some clients who pay out of pocket and offer reduced rates for low income clients.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: When you come to therapy, you seek answers to difficult life challenges. Perhaps you lack a sense of purpose, are in a relationship or job that is no longer satisfying or are experiencing overwhelming depression or anxiety. I ground my work in respect and compassion for you because this contributes to the foundation of trust, self-acceptance and courage necessary for you to successfully overcome your difficulties and create the life you want to live. Through the cultivation of mindful awareness and the implementation of proven stress management and emotion regulation skills, I will teach you how to calm anxiety, cope with distressing feelings, access your intuitive wisdom, and review your behaviors and beliefs so that you can commit to those which align with your values. This will help you realize your personal, professional and relationship goals and ultimately experience what all of us want in this life - a greater sense of peace, vitality and happiness.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have provided mental health and substance abuse counseling in private practice, hospital behavioral health and community mental health settings for the past 30 years. I graduated from Stanford University and received my Masters degree in Clinical Psychology from CIIS, a program which integrates Eastern and Western views on psychology. I have received extensive supervision and have expertise utilizing several evidence-based therapeutic modalities as well as mindfulness-based stress reduction which helps me work effectively with anxiety and mood disorders as well as existential and relationship issues. My mindfulness orientation is informed by over 30 years of meditative practice including residency in a Buddhist monastery. I also have extensive experience working with geriatric clients while employed with Providence Behavioral Health.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I have received specialized training in mindfulness-based stress reduction, practiced in a Buddhist monastery, and have integrated mindfulness into my life and professional practice for 30 years. This transformative practice teaches you to identify less with your limiting thoughts and more with pure awareness. By developing more objectivity about the stories you tell yourself about who you are and what is possible, you can experience greater happiness and create the life you choose to live.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I was supervised for two years by Dr. Matthew McKay, well-known author of multiple CBT texts used in psychology, counseling and social work graduate programs around the world. I have incorporated a CBT orientation in private practice and hospital behavioral health settings for the past 25 years.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have extensive training and experience working with relationship issues for individuals and understand the most effective ways to teach you how to reframe problem issues in your relationship and develop the communication skills necessary for you to create a healthy relationship. I was supervised for two years by Dr. Matt McKay who is a respected expert in couples counseling who has written Couples Skills.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have utilized CBT and mindfulness-based approaches to manage anxiety for over 25 years in different treatment facilities and in private practice. I have received specialized training in mindfulness-based stress reduction, practiced meditation in a Buddhist monastery, and have used mindfulness meditation in my own life for 35 years. I received two years of supervision from Dr. Matt McKay who has written The Relaxation and Stress Reduction Workbook and The CBT Anxiety Solution Workbook.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: My expertise utilizing CBT and mindfulness approaches has also been effective with my clients experiencing mood disorders. I have used these orientations in multiple settings along with relational approaches that focus more on your family history and need to connect more personally with me as a real person with whom you have a trusting relationship and not just as a therapist. I also have two years of supervision with Dr. Matt McKay who has written Mind and Emotion and Thoughts and Feelings.

name: Gabby Hancher
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I’m a white, trans nonbinary, and queer therapist who has lived experience with chronic illness.
ideal_client: I work best with: *Collaborative individuals *Folks who are curious about mindfulness *Folks who are creative and/or highly sensitive *Folks who identify as care-givers *Activists looking to process and integrate their experiences *Adult parentified children *Perfectionists *Queer folks who want to explore their identity more deeply *Neurodivergent individuals *Folks who feel they've gotten what they can from talk therapy and need something else *Folks who want to feel more embodied

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In a typical session, we will slow down and listen to the wisdom of your body. Together, we can discover what it is that you need to process in order to experience more integration in your life. We may work to support your own innate resilience by developing a felt sense of safety based on your own true sense of that or use the therapeutic relationship as a container to explore attachment wounding patterns through our present moment relationship. All of these experiences can offer fundamental shifts in your overall mood, the way you show up in the world, or even in your relationships. Whether you are experiencing difficulty with grief, relationships, anxiety or any number of concerns, together we can help you orient towards your inner knowing and personal agency.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I approach all of my work through a social justice lens and believe deeply that when we transform on an interpersonal level, social change ripples outwards. Accessibility, embodied experience, and trauma-informed care are important pillars of my practice. Persons of all races & ethnicities, genders, sexual orientations, and abilities are welcome. I am also affirming of kink, non-traditional relationship structures such as polyamory and non-monogamy, and sex work. Some of my identities hold varying levels of privilege which I always invite conversation around in session.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: I utilize a variety of somatic and attachment based techniques with Hakomi, or mindfulness based experiential therapy, as my main modality. During a Hakomi session, you may have your eyes closed while we develop your ability to be mindfully aware of yourself. This helps us to listen to the wisdom of your body and reprocess underlying core beliefs on a neurological level.

name: DeLyn Griffin
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: MA in Marriage, Couples, and Family Counseling
intro: My specialties are kiddos (play therapy/parenting support), teens (expressive arts/sandtray), couple/family relationship issues, and EMDR.
ideal_client: I welcome individuals, couples, and families dealing with relationship conflicts, parenting, behavioral challenges, depression, anxiety, developing sexual health, life stress & balance, or personal identity. I was a teacher for many years and welcome children ages 3 and up for play therapy to help them communicate their inner experiences as they learn new skills and practice new ways of coping. I recognize the impact of trauma (big and small) and provide EMDR as a treatment option for all ages.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The most important aspect of counseling is for you to experience a therapeutic environment that is warm, accepting, empathetic, encouraging, and patient. In that environment, you are empowered to know your inherent value and worth, and find ways to access the inner wisdom to guide you toward your goals. I believe people are relational beings with physical, emotional, social, and spiritual needs. Increasing awareness of and integrating these needs can lead to a richer, more meaningful life. While I believe psychological insight is important, it is also essential to be action oriented. I help clients acquire new tools and experiment with new behaviors and ways of thinking to create the desired changes in their lives and relationships. I have additional training to work with children & teens (play therapy, sandtray, & expressive arts) couples (Gottman, Emotionally Focused, & RelateStrong) & trauma (EMDR with infants, children, adolescents & adults).

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My favorite things are spending time with my husband, our four children and their partners, and snuggling our 2 grandkiddos. In my free time I love all sorts of books, quilting, knitting, and gardening.

name: Josephine Jardine
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Reach out with any questions you might have! I provide a free consultation so you can make sure your therapist is the right fit.
ideal_client: I have worked with a wide range of issues, and a wide range of folks. This space is safe, and this space is for everyone. I believe we are the cartographers of our own internal world, and my role is to guide you in this process of self-discovery.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Using a range of adaptive therapeutic modalities, I offer a collaborative and safe space where all aspects of your experience—whether spontaneous, curious, brave, or vulnerable—are welcome. With gentle challenging, perspective shifting, humor, kindness, and deep respect, I support you in exploring, understanding, and integrating all parts of yourself, helping you feel seen, held, and empowered.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My therapy-style is rooted in the belief that individuals shouldn't bear the sole responsibility for creating a quality of life without the support of reciprocal communal care, advocacy, ad accountability. As your therapist, I play an active, and involved part of your larger circle of care. I work closely with multiple supervisors, and clinical consultation groups, so that my practice maintains the ethical and updated standards of our field.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: With over ten years of somatic therapy experience, the integration of the body, and nervous system is a supportive way to integrate sustainable mental health care, and accelerate any goals a client has in therapy.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: With a certification in nature-based therapy, I utilize these evidence based interventions in sessions if a client is interested in them.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: If you are interested in brief therapy, powerful work can be done in just a few short sessions, setting you up for long term success.

specialities.name: Career Counseling
specialities.description: Figuring out the next steps of your career impacts so many other areas of your life.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: The stories we tell, the language we weave, shapes the reality in which we interact with, and exist in.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Transitions in life are where we need some of the most consistent support. Adjusting to change is what makes us human.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Exploring our concept of self, our sense of identity, our purpose, our goals, are all things that can feel expansive, and exciting, if we are supported through this process.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety manifests itself in a diverse range of ways. Getting to know the way your anxiety expresses itself, and learning how to support this expression, is something I have years of experience working with as a therapist.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Your therapist can help you lighten the load that is depression.

name: Teresa Stroup
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Compassionate therapist helping individuals and couples navigate trauma, relationships, and life transitions with evidence-based care.
ideal_client: I connect deeply with those carrying the weight of trauma, relationship struggles, or feeling misunderstood in a neurotypical world. Whether you're a couple seeking to rebuild trust, an adult processing painful experiences, a parent needing guidance, or someone navigating faith alongside life's challenges—I offer a safe place for understanding. My practice welcomes teens, adults, and elders from all backgrounds who seek not just symptom relief but real change through compassionate care.

approaches.My Background: As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) with 15+ years of experience, I offer specialized trauma therapy, PTSD treatment, and relationship counseling in Portland. My background includes leadership at Good Samaritan Ministries, providing Christian counseling while honoring diverse beliefs. I'm certified in anger management, couples therapy, and evidence-based parenting programs. My approach blends Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and Solution-Focused Therapy to address immediate concerns and deeper patterns. I specialize in life transitions, neurodiversity challenges, and family conflict. With a Master's from Portland State and experience as a clinical supervisor, I uphold the highest practice standards. My background in hospice social work and crisis intervention equips me for complex emotional needs, creating a safe space where healing flourishes through trauma-informed care and authentic connection.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: My clients find our work together transformative because I blend professional expertise with genuine compassion. As your therapist, I create a uniquely safe environment where trauma healing and personal growth naturally unfold. My integrated approach combines evidence-based therapy with heartfelt understanding of your unique journey. If you're seeking couples counseling to rebuild connection, PTSD treatment to reclaim your peace, or Christian counseling that honors your faith while addressing real-world challenges, my practice offers specialized support. For those navigating neurodiversity, family therapy needs, or anger management, I provide both practical tools and deeper emotional understanding. My background in crisis intervention and hospice care has refined my ability to meet you exactly where you are—whether in acute distress or subtle dissatisfaction. Through CBT techniques, DBT skills, and solution-focused methods, we'll address both symptoms and underlying patterns.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: As a trauma-informed therapist with specialized training in PTSD treatment, I help clients process painful memories and reclaim their lives. My approach combines evidence-based trauma therapies including CBT for trauma, and somatic experiencing to address both psychological and physical manifestations of trauma. I create a safe therapeutic environment where trauma survivors can heal at their own pace, developing resilience skills and emotional regulation for lasting post-traumatic growth.

name: Nicole Kennelly
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am passionate about helping you to create a meaningful and fulfilling life, as you learn to move from cycles of pain to cycles of peace.
ideal_client: Are you struggling to adjust to life circumstances? Do you need clarification about your future? Are you worn down and depressed? If so, I can offer you a safe, nonjudgemental space to process, share and grow. I am passionate about supporting individuals as they seek meaning and fulfillment in their lives. With creativity and choice, you can move from pain to peace, discover your strengths, learn to manage anxiety and extend compassion to yourself and others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I view our human experience through an existential lens where you are encouraged to engage with your own "becoming" as you create a life worth living. I welcome all ways that bring awareness and change, including restoration therapy and solution-focused therapy. I take an individualized approach to each client, offering techniques of self-compassion, mindfulness, art exercises, spiritual integration, and somatic regulation. With curiosity and compassion, I am eager to get to know you and create a space where you can find hope for this moment.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I believe in the effectiveness of therapy. In therapy, I have felt less alone. I have gained new insights and perspectives. I have found compassion for myself and others. I have explored challenges and learned to manage anxiety. I have dug myself out of the hole of depression and apathy. I have gained clarity and regained a sense of self. I have experienced the gift of being heard, seen, and invited to share more of my yucky thoughts - which is a profound and sacred experience. I am passionate about the therapeutic relationship, and I love being with people in the fullness of their lived experiences.

name: Laura Birchard
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Trauma-informed therapy for teens and adults—guided by dreams, emotions, and symptoms—to foster healing, self-awareness, and growth.
ideal_client: My clients are ready to uncover what feels authentic and whole—they can no longer put off “the only way out is through.” I help them make meaning of their inner world and expand their capacity to access it as a guide in their relationship with self and others. Using imaginal, relational, and depth-oriented practices, I support clients in building resilience and navigating overwhelming experiences with greater self-awareness and inner strength.

approaches.My Background: Laura Birchard, LPC is a depth-oriented psychotherapist in private practice, serving individuals in Portland, Oregon. She specializes in therapy for teens and adults, offering an insight-driven and transformative process. Depth psychotherapy creates space to engage with the living mystery—the edge between what is known and unknown. Through dreams, images, creative expression, and relationship dynamics, Laura helps clients reconnect with their inner depths and move toward greater self-integration. Laura has extensive clinical experience in outpatient, residential, and emergency psychiatric settings, working with individuals and families. She has specialized training in depth-oriented, psychodynamic, Sandplay, and experiential therapy. Her work is guided by the language of the unconscious—symptoms, symbols, and creative processes—inviting clients into a deeper dialogue with themselves.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: One of the paradoxes of therapy is that it is both deeply personal and highly professional. My practice is grounded in depth and analytical psychology (Jungian), trauma-informed care—including somatic therapies—feminist theory, and psychodynamic approaches. I also have additional training in assessment and DBT. I am committed to being an ally and anti-racist. Jungian analyst Marion Woodman wrote, “mystery is the depth of the sacred.” The sacred is not bound to any specific religion—it is woven into the very fabric of our being, connecting us to the earth, the stars, and one another. At times, this connection may feel fractured or lost, leaving us unmoored. Therapy offers a space to rediscover hope and deepen self-awareness. Beyond my practice, I find inspiration wandering forest trails, volunteering in my community, and immersing myself in yoga, meditation, and creative practices. Reading and creative expression are integral to my own ongoing inner work.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: I provide trauma informed therapy that welcomes dreams, images, emotions, experiences, symptoms guide our work and shape a treatment only for you, making changes at a deeper level. With training in psychodynamic and analytic (Jungian) psychotherapeutic practices, I am highly skilled at making the focus of our work contacting and amplifying your unique process of embodied psyche (soul making) ; supporting meaning making in relationship to self and others (and the Self). Let's talk today.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: Experiential therapy is an active, process-oriented approach that goes beyond talk therapy. It uses creative, somatic, and interactive techniques—such as Sandplay, role-play, art, and guided imagery—to access deeper emotions and unconscious patterns. This approach is especially effective for treating burnout, helping clients release stress, reconnect with themselves, and restore a sense of vitality and balance.

specialities.name: Addiction Therapy
specialities.description: Addiction often reflects deeper emotional, psychological, or spiritual wounds. From a depth psychotherapy perspective, healing involves exploring unconscious patterns and causes. Integrating Internal Family Systems (IFS), we work with parts of the self to heal the fragmentation behind addictive behaviors. Through dreams, symbols, and the emotional body, we can reconnect with your true self and build healthier, more meaningful ways of coping.

specialities.name: Sand Tray
specialities.description: Adults and teens can benefit from Sandplay therapy as it provides a nonverbal, embodied, creative way to access and process unconscious material. Like dreaming, Sandplay allows emotions, traumas, and experiences to emerge through the symbolic language of sand and figures. It creates a safe space to explore inner conflicts, heal unresolved wounds, overcome shame, and foster self-discovery, integration, and transformation.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: Psychodynamic psychotherapy explores how unconscious patterns and early relationships shape our emotions and interactions. We move through life with many internal layers, influenced by early attachments and unconscious dynamics. This work isn’t stuffy—it’s highly relational. By integrating object relations theory, we help you experience something new in therapy—a different way of relating and being. Come try on the authentic you as we address challenges, heal wounds, and foster growth.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: "The privilege of a lifetime is to become who you truly are." – Joseph Campbell. Individuation—the process of unfolding into your true, unique self—is at the heart of my practice, informed by specialized training in depth psychology. This journey of personal growth can be overwhelming and isolating, yet it also holds moments of profound meaning and sacredness. You don’t have to navigate this deeply personal process alone; I’m here to support you throughout your journey.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is rarely just one thing—it feels like everything. It may start with racing thoughts or physical symptoms like a pounding heart or a tight chest. Anxiety can be profoundly unraveling, striking at the core and spiraling through layers of biology and spirit. Though deeply disruptive, it can also serve as a compass, pointing toward what needs attention and care. Reach out today for a free consultation.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is not meant to be carried alone. I am here to walk alongside you on your journey through loss. As a Dougy Center volunteer, I gained firsthand experience with the multidimensional nature of grief, deepening my understanding of this process. Since then, I’ve received additional training in supporting individuals through grief with a depth psychological lens. Grief takes many forms— death, miscarriage, divorce, loss of identity, job loss.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is more than the absence of joy—it can feel like being cut off from the inner source of life and spark. It may show up as heaviness, numbness, or disconnection from yourself and the world. From a depth psychological perspective, depression is not just a symptom to eliminate but a summons from the soul. By working with dreams, symbols, and the unconscious, we can explore the deeper meaning beneath the suffering, fostering renewal and a more authentic connection with yourself.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma leaves an imprint on both body and soul, often fragmenting our sense of self. To survive, we develop coping strategies that can later become traumatic themselves. From a depth psychological perspective, healing is not just about symptom relief—it’s about reclaiming lost parts of yourself. Through dreams, symbols, and nonverbal interventions like Sandplay, somatic work, and creative expression, we engage the unconscious as a guide, fostering integration, resilience, and renewed wholeness.

name: Mikki Jordan
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I specialize in working with adults and teens (16+) who struggle with food, body image, and/or anxiety concerns.
ideal_client: My clients have a strong sense of wanting to be more, to do more, but can’t stop getting in their own way. They have high expectations of themselves, but often feel like they’re falling short. They possess a deep desire to grow beyond personal challenges because they desperately want to feel more connected to themself and the world around them. Many of them are navigating life transitions that cause them to question their identity and/or their place in the world.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My approach is rooted in a relational, humanistic framework, which means I view therapy as a collaboration. I challenge the conventional, medical model which views therapists as experts and clients as patients with a disorder that needs to be “treated." I take a more holistic view because I want to understand you as a whole person. As an integrative practitioner I often incorporate expressive arts, yoga, mindfulness, and meditation as I believe that creativity, movement, breath, and focused attention have the potential to deepen our capacity for self-healing.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I came into this work after recovering from my own eating disorder almost 20 years ago. Once I found myself on the other side, I realized I wanted to help others find their own path to freedom. I know first hand how difficult this process can be. If you're struggling, please know you're not alone. I'd love to support you in any way I can.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I believe full recovery is possible, but there isn’t one approach that works for everyone. My goal is to help you find your own unique path to healing. I enjoy getting creative and figuring out a framework that best serves you in your recovery process.

name: Ryan Leiderman
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a trauma-informed, solution-focused, mindfulness-oriented therapist. I take OHP, Care Oregon, Pacific Source, & First Health insurance.
ideal_client: Are you ready to take a step toward personal growth and healing? My clients are individuals—adolescent-aged or older—who are seeking not only relief from suffering but also greater insight into their psychological histories and subconscious patterns.

approaches.My Background: Credentials I hold a MA in Counseling and am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) as well as a Registered Clinical Counselor (RCC). Since 2014, I have been dedicated to supporting individuals on their journey toward mental and emotional well-being. Experience With a decade of experience, I have had the privilege of working with a diverse range of clients in various settings, including private practice, EAPs, and community health centers. Specialties I specialize in helping individuals navigate the challenges of anxiety, trauma, and addictions. These areas of focus are close to my heart, and I am committed to providing collaborative, evidence-based therapies that meet your unique needs.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I’m an advocate for animal rights and deeply committed to environmental conservation. My love for animals extends into my vegan lifestyle, where I am passionate about plant-based cooking and nutrition.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I use a collaborative, solution-focused and psychodynamic approach, along with mindfulness and CBT.

specialities.name: Coronavirus/COVID-19
specialities.description: I have lived experience as someone still navigating the realities of the pandemic.

specialities.name: Obesity
specialities.description: I work with clients on their psychological issues around eating, as well as practical plant-based nutrition tips for better health.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: I use a collaborative, solution-focused and psychodynamic approach, along with mindfulness and CBT.

name: Gary Conachan III
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Based in Portland, I'm a Professional Counselor Associate specializing in sex therapy, relationship issues, and religious trauma.
ideal_client: We might be a good fit if you need queer-affirming care, sex-positive care, support in your relationships, or want to explore faith, spirituality, and religious trauma. From exploring new parts of your identity or seeking healing from religious trauma, to opening up your relationship or learning how to set boundaries with others, there is room for all of you in our work together. Rather than settling for quick-fixes and simple answers, you dive into the grey areas and messiness of life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I tell every client that the most important part of effective therapy is the fit between therapist and client. As proven by research, the therapeutic relationship is one of the biggest contributors to meaningful and lasting change. I want our work together to be focused on what you want and need. Because the therapeutic relationship is so important, I offer time and space for regular feedback. I name my identities and parts and invite clients to do the same, especially where power and privilege might be impacting with our work. Yes, I am the therapist with education and clinical experience - and, clients are the ultimate experts on their own lives. I view us as fellow travelers, bringing all our parts, identities, and humanity into our work together.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a therapist because I grew up queer in an evangelical church and home. I've experienced first-hand what it's like to deny who you are for your faith and community. In my undergraduate studies, everything I'd known was challenged and deconstructed. Incidentally, it was through my studies that I became affirming of LGBTQIA+ people, which eventually led to accepting myself. I decided to pursue counseling because I want to help those with similar backgrounds. Faith and spirituality have caused tremendous harm and trauma, and healing from those things is possible. Whether you want to reconstruct your faith, create or find a spirituality suited to you and your values, or leave it all behind, you know what's best and I'm here to support you. Additionally, a lack of sex education from my church and upbringing sparked a passion to help people thrive in their sexuality. Together, we can determine your sexual ethics, explore your identities, and increase pleasure in your relationships.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I have read several books and pursued my own learning about the Internal Family Systems approach. I've used it with clients and seen them find healing from acute trauma backgrounds. Conceptually, the IFS approach aligns with my values and beliefs around how we can change and heal.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory can be helpful in understanding both ourselves and selves-in-relationship: with friends, family, significant others, and our planet. The therapeutic relationship can be incredibly healing when it becomes a secure attachment and model for other relationships in our lives.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: In sex therapy, CBT is often used to address sexual problems and dysfunctions. Sometimes we get in our own way and need to change our thinking, receive education (especially where there's been none), and learn better communication skills to help our sexual relationships.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: For me, my orientation as a feminist therapist looks like naming my identities and biases, the reasons behind treatment approaches, and always asking for consent in treatment. In other words, I work to equalize the power imbalance as much as possible, always working collaboratively with my clients.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Humanistic therapy places the client at the center of their treatment. While the therapist brings expertise from their field, the client is in charge of their goals for treatment and empowered to share what is working and what needs improvement. Both therapist and client show up in their full humanity.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: From working through sexual dysfunctions to exploring your sexuality, sexual concerns can take a toll on us individually and relationally. When our concerns impact those around us, they can become especially distressing. One of my top specialties is sex therapy, which means I am regularly researching, consulting, and seeking further training in these areas.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As an LGBTQ person, I have lived experience and knowledge around coming out, navigating non-affirming family relationships and faith communities, exploring sexuality, and more. I actively pursue my own learning about topics involving gender and sexuality to expand my own knowledge and fill in the gaps where my lived and professional experiences fall short. Additionally, I provide pro-bono evaluations and care letters for those needing them for gender-affirming care.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: From courses in relationship and family therapy to my own personal work and studies, I have knowledge and experience around navigating difficult relationships. I can help you implement boundaries, increase communication skills, and clarify your personal values.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: As an ex-evangelical queer person, I've experienced first-hand what it's like to deny who you are for your faith and community. While my experiences and knowledge are rooted in the Christian faith, folks of other faiths have had similar experiences and I recognize the need in our field to help clients work through issues of faith and spirituality.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: As a cisgender, gay, queer person, I've had my own experiences around navigating gender identity. I'm passionate about helping folx find supportive, gender-affirming care; as such, I'm currently offering care letter evaluations pro-bono. Recognizing the limits of my experience and knowledge, I seek to learn what I don't know and stay up-to-date on the latest research regarding trans-affirming care.

name: Katherine Chiba, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I believe we are all good people, doing the best we can, and it is my privilege to welcome a few splendid souls into my office.
ideal_client: I suppose my ideal client is the person who contacts me and wants to work! In twenty six years as a full-time therapist I have had the privilege of working with hundreds of different people, and I can honestly say that I have been glad to know all of them. Although I am trained in a variety of evidence based practices that seek to address specific diagnoses, I feel passionately that the treatment has to fit the individual, and not the reverse.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy is pretty simple: two or more people get together in a room and talk. It's not a magic bullet, and it's not pain free. Sometimes, for a while, people in therapy feel worse because they are opening up hurts and traumas that haven't been addressed. Sometimes its painful because we have to face up to things about ourselves or our situations that we would rather ignore. It's worth it because we have the chance to look at things from a different perspective, to ask different questions, to challenge ourselves and, ultimately, get more of what we want out of life. Understanding where we've been and how we got here is important, but in order to feel better, we often have to do something different. In therapy we can learn to identify what the options are, evaluate the risks and benefits of different options, and make the best choice for ourselves. We also have to learn to live with the fact that some choices are not, sadly, on the table.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I lived in Japan for 17 years, during which time I taught in a community college and did graduate studies in clinical psychology. After the death of my husband I brought our two children back to the US and started my graduate studies over again, this time pursuing a master's in social work at Portland State University. I have been in practice since 1999, first in community mental health, then for 20 years at the VA, where I was hired to help start a Dialectical Behavior Therapy program. I started my private practice in 2017 and went full time in 2023. Since then I have focused on general psychotherapy for clients with a wide variety of diagnosis, including PTSD, depression, and anxiety disorders. I have also trained in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia, and have utilized this modality in individual and group treatment.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: The only two certainties for human beings are life and death. What we do between those two goalposts is up to us. How do we live with joy and excitement knowing that life is temporary? How do we live with joy and excitement when it seems our lives have dragged on for too long? Acknowledging and accepting the realities of human existence frees us up to engage fully and create lives worth living.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I have been a DBT therapist for over 20 years. The approach informs all of my work with clients and I integrate skills training into both individual and couples therapy.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: How we think about things affects our behaviors. How we behave affects how we think and what we believe. Too often our beliefs about ourselves or other people do what they do are distorted or incomplete. Challenging those beliefs opens up new ways of behaving and interacting with ourselves and the world.

specialities.name: Veterans/Military Service
specialities.description: I have had the enormous privilege of working with veterans and their families for 15 years. Although I am not a vet myself, I have learned a great deal about military culture and the ongoing impact of military service. As veterans have expanding choices for receiving treatment in the public sector, I hope to provide another resource for the support and treatment they have earned.

specialities.name: Aging Concerns
specialities.description: Sexuality, parenting adult children, estrangements from family members, living with chronic illness and chronic pain, retirement, choices about where and how to live, and end of life issues are just some of the topics I have enjoyed addressing with my clients of mature years. Being a not-so-young person myself, I have a particular interest in helping my peers live full and interesting lives.

specialities.name: Insomnia
specialities.description: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (cbt-i) is an evidence based, six- to eight-session treatment that quite simply helps people achieve more satisfactory sleep. I have been extensively trained in this modality, and also help patients with CPAP machines increase their tolerance and improve adherence to treatment plans. You can learn the tools to sleep well without medications!

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have been working with veterans for fifteen years, and a majority of my clients suffer from PTSD related to combat trauma, childhood trauma, or sexual trauma, or, far too often, a combination of these. I won't lie to you: people who suffer from this kind of catastrophic pain are never going to be the same as if it hadn't happened. The good news: you can have a life worth living. Therapy helps.

name: Heart Thyself, LLC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Heart Thyself, LLC is a counseling service dedicated to helping people recover from Narcissistic Abuse. Rogerian. Polyvagal informed.
ideal_client: People who have experienced Narcissistic Abuse have been exploited, rejected and devalued. Often this begins with family of origin and in adulthood tends to carry over into romantic relationships and friendships. Kids who grow up with Narcissistic Abuse become adults with unresolved identity trauma and confusion. This is often displayed as self-hatred, harm and abandonment. Boundary formation becomes impossible, leading to interpersonal struggles and difficulty forming secure attachments.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Narcissistic Abuse Recovery is deeply intense personal work that will transform your life. It involves breaking the cycle of generations of abuse and dysfunction. Recovery work is a pro-active process of establishing a treatment plan focused on your identity and relationship goals. Most clients see significant changes after 4-6 months of dedicated weekly therapy. Change is painful, but not nearly as painful as spending an unfulfilled life in a narcissistic family system or relationship. Heart Thyself is dedicated to helping you through this pain into the life you would choose to live. You can do it!

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Narcissistic Abuse Recovery

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Divorce and family court support. Relationship conflict help.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Spiritual abuse recovery, cult recovery and exiting support, faith building and exploration.

name: Alexandra Moskovich
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help clients figure out what joy and authenticity mean to them, and then help them identify and remove obstacles to gettin' there.
ideal_client: I work best with curious and motivated adults who are interested in deepening their understanding of themselves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With a largely existential focus, incorporating depth-work, attachment work, and somatic work, I take an integrative and holistic approach, believing that true healing occurs when clients are able to confront the core issues that are holding them back. By exploring each client’s unique intersections and circumstances, and delving into the underlying emotions and beliefs that drive our behavior, I help clients gain a deeper understanding of themselves and their place in the world. My approach is relational and grounded in the belief that, even with our unique circumstances, we all have the power of choice. By recognizing our inherent freedom, we can create more meaningful and fulfilling lives.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold certificates in Sex Therapy through CIIS, as well as Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy through IPI.

name: Dr. Katie Statman-Weil
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I work with parents of children impacted by foster care, adoption, navigating neurodivergence (PDA/Autism, ADHD), and with big behaviors.
ideal_client: I know parenting can often feel isolating and overwhelming. f you feel anxious, overwhelmed or just plain exhausted, that makes perfect sense. It can be tough to manage the daily challenges of parenting, especially when you're child is facing unique emotional or developmental hurdles. I can help you reduce your feelings of loneliness, fear, and overwhelm and grow your skills. I specialize in compassionate, tailored support for any parent wanting to explore their experiences as a parent.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am passionate about Parenting and supporting children's healthy development; I wholeheartedly believe that your relationship with your child is the foundation for health and healing. I am both a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and I hold a doctorate in education focused on supporting students' behavior and mental health in the classroom. I support families and schools caring for children with trauma histories, family conflict, attachment issues, depression, anxiety, ADHD, PDA, and behavioral challenges. I am a foster, adoptive, and biological parent and bring this lived experience into my work. I understand the impact trauma can have on relationships and attachment firsthand, and I know healing is possible. Parenting can be hard and lonely, especially when your child's emotions or behaviors feel bigger than those of their peers. I am here to help you find a way out of the loneliness. I am a collaborator and help you problem solve ways to create more joy and ease in your lives.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe children, and parents, do well when they can. Sometimes it takes some work to figure out exactly what it is that children need to feel better. I work from an attachment and relationship focused lens to support parents raising children with emotional, behavioral, and learning differences. I work with families who could describe their children as: challenging, explosive, difficult, neurodiverse, gifted, different, struggling in school, or having experienced trauma.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: I often work with parents who are wanting direct feedback and ideas about ways to improve their parenting experience. Is dinner time not going well? Are you wondering how to help your child get out the door in the mornings? Does it feel like your child is getting upset about everything? I've got ideas!

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I use the latest research in relational neuroscience to help you create a shift in the ways that you think about your child. My approach is strength-based, relationship focused, and integrates the complexity of the human experience in all interactions. I work with you to figure out what it is your child is communicating through their behavior so we can use those clues to figure out what they need to feel more regulated and calm.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Play is the work of childhood. When working with parents and children we often use play as a way to build attachment, create joy and closeness, and build and maintain boundaries. Often children love coming to therapy because we have a lot of fun!

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: As a therapist working with families of children who have experienced trauma, including foster and adoptive families, family therapy allows me to engage all family members in the healing process, addressing dynamics that influence a child's sense of self and behavior. By fostering open communication, we create a safe space for everyone to express their feelings and perspectives. This not only strengthens relationships but also empowers families to develop effective strategies together.

specialities.name: Adoption Issues
specialities.description: I work with foster and adoptive parents who want to explore the complexities of parenting after trauma/loss. I use an attachment based framework to support you in building a homelife where your child feels fully seen and valued. As a former foster parent and now adoptive parent, I understand the experience of building attachment with a child/children from the ground up.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: If you look around and see a bunch of fairly happy parents that seem to think parenting isn't that hard while you feel like you're drowning in your child's endless needs and a pool sized pile of laundry, I can help. You may have a few small issues you want to discuss or maybe you have tried every last trick in the book and nothing works. I can help you reclaim yourself while allowing you to be the skilled, confident, and nurturing role model you are meant to be.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I work with parents figuring out how to best support their PDA kids. Learning to parent a child with a sensitive nervous system can sometimes feel like we are diffusing bombs more than enjoying life- but this does not have to be the case. I can support you in finding the joy in your unique parenting journey.

specialities.name: ODD
specialities.description: Does your child have big unexplainable behaviors? I work with families who feel like they've tried every specialist and no one is understanding their child. I use a brain-based, relationship focused lens that allows us to dig deep and figure out what it is your child is needing to thrive.

name: Grace Forrester
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am a Trauma-informed psychotherapist. If you are dealing with Complex-Trauma, neurodiversity and/or identity concerns, please see me.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach stems from an Existential-BIPOC-Humanistic lens. Thus, finding and valuing your authentic narrative is essential in my practice. So, if find, you have goals, dreams, and aspirations, but you are uncertain whether you will ever make everything in your mind work out the way you planned. Here’s to meeting your goals!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a Trauma-informed Therapist, I work from an empathetic, strength-based lens. I strive to create a generous, welcoming, judgment-free, and secure space. Along with you (the client), the aim is to form an equitable collaboration for however long it is needed. My work as a social justice therapist understands how various institutionalized parameters may impact a healthy-wellbeing: such as Anti-Blackness, Gender-Based Oppression, Anti-Climate change, and other forms of systemic injustice. Therefore, my therapeutic praxis is inculcated from an anti-oppressive, gender-affirming, and Mindful-radical acceptance perspective. Additionally, my work has highlighted but is not limited to: Anxiety, Trauma, LGBTQ+, non-monogamy, sex workers, depression, relational conflict, addiction and dependence, Somatic theory, and geropsychology

name: Jeffery Wise
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I offer compassionate counseling and psychiatric care. I am client centered, identifying goals and offering concrete solutions.
ideal_client: Turn self-criticism into self-love. See anger as a tool that is pointing you to healing and growth. View your relationships as reflections of your own vulnerability, self acceptance and projection. Understand addiction as a coping mechanism. Honor yourself in all ways. Recognize and release beliefs and inherited thought structures that are not yours. Release that which is not longer serving you. Open to your unlimited capacity and potential.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My clients typically describe me as approachable, compassionate, caring, intelligent and non-judgemental. I address immediate concerns but also tend to go deeper to address underlying thoughts, beliefs, structures and patterns that may be limiting and that prevent your true potential to come forth. I work with meditation, journaling, breath work, medication, visualization, cognitive behavioral therapy approaches, and deep listening. I have many years of meditative experience and am interested in a deeper energetic approach to blocks or resistances that could be impeding the fulfillment of goals and dreams. Sometimes our bodies may need extra support with medication. I see medication as a tool, not as an end. Together we identify those blocks that are preventing you from expansion. We address the fears that exist, for whatever reason, and gently address then, opening the way for freedom, authenticity, and robust joy to emerge.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My space is open and welcome for all types of people. I especially enjoy helping to turn difficult circumstances, past or present, into opportunities for growth. Whether that means a history of low self-esteem, religious dogmatism, sexual or gender identity, I am there to help. My clients who are open to addressing fears or resistance to moving into emotional spaces that are more conducive to who they really are tend to experience great joy and satisfaction with me. What is it that is not allowing you to be truly you? Identifying the root of dissatisfaction, apathy, and limited beliefs opens the way to spaciousness, increased self love, improved self esteem, more energy, motivation to make the changes that you know will result in joy and well-being. Courageously allowing yourself the focus and awareness to exist in the space is the greatest you can give to yourself.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: We work together to identify the causes of depression and how to have greater control over one's mental outlook and emotional response. I work with anxiety in the same way. Often, compulsive tendencies and addiction can be ways to help manage underlying emotions. We find ways to get those needs met in a healthier way.

name: ariel reiner
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am so glad you are here. Whether you are new to therapy or have not achieved your goals in regular talk therapy, somatic therapy can help.
ideal_client: In therapy, I provide a warm and accepting space where we work together, respectfully exploring what nourishes you and what your needs, values, and aspirations are. We’ll explore what holds you back, where you’d like to see change, and what may support you in expressing your whole authentic self. We’ll gently and slowly uncover what experiences your body may be holding as they arise in the present moment and how to interpret your body's innate guidance and knowledge.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work is informed by bioenergetics, spiritual psychology, and a relational, solutions-oriented approach. In my work with couples, I lean into the Hakomi principles of mindfulness, organicity, non-violence, body/mind holism, and unity. I am passionate about supporting people in becoming more fully embodied.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Many of us want the same things: to feel safe, to love and be loved, to be seen, heard and supported, and to be at home in our bodies. However, being a human is complicated, and when presented with more than is manageable, our bodies' innate intelligence takes over and holds onto tough experiences for us. This is where somatic psychotherapy can help.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I practice relationally meaning I am a human in the room with you - I may cry and laugh with you and use self-disclosure. We are equals in the therapy room.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: While I love working with individuals around empowerment and embodiment, I am particularly passionate about working with couples. Couples therapy works best when both parties are in individual counseling.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Our past pains and trauma don't live in our mind, the residual of our experiences is held in the tissues and fascia of our bodies. This is why a bottom-up approach is helpful in therapy. When we lean into our body's intelligence and learn to listen to and honor the voice of our body, that's where healing happens.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: As a society, we don't collectively have a proper container for marriages and partnerships, and so I seek to provide a solid ground and container where we work together to improve communication and deepen intimacy.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Trauma and abuse have been passed down from generation to generation. And, so has resilience. I hold a transgenerational lense in our approach to moving forward.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: For many of us in the West spirituality is missing from our lives. Let's work together to uncover what fills your cup.

name: Doug Chapman
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: You may not know it but you are already whole. Together we will collaborate to rediscover your authentic self.
ideal_client: My clients typically are mid-life or older. They may be struggling with mild/moderate anxiety and working through a difficult transition. I love working with clients who have experienced religious harm or who want to work on personal or spiritual growth. I no longer work with clients who are primarily working through childhood trauma issues or clients who have severe and complex problems. (For example severe depression with suicidal actions or thoughts, self-harm, drug/alcohol problems.)

approaches.My Background and Approach: I studied Transpersonal Psychology in graduate school and have a credential as a Spiritually Integrated Therapist. I am licensed as a professional counselor in both Oregon and Washington. I am a Master Addictions Counselor. I hold national and state credentials as an Approved Clinical Supervisor and has supervised and mentored many younger clinicians. I am a past secretary of the Oregon Mental Health Counselors Association. In 2009, I won an Award “for substantial contribution to the counseling profession." Regarding my own lived experience, I grew up in a fundamentalist sect. I was a minister in the sect in my 20s and 30s. I left the sect and experienced the power of healing via therapy. At this time in my life I identify as having multiple spiritual identities including Buddhist, Christian, Pagan, and Hindu. I enjoy helping clients who have experienced religious harm and also with clients who want to explore their spirituality.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I have extensive training to provide services for the needs of African Americans, Hispanics, Older Adults and Sexual Minorities. I enjoy working with clients in life transitions including loss & grief, midlife crises, retirement, and other life changes. If you are feeling stuck in your life, experiencing a difficult life transition, or would simply like to experience more joy, fulfillment, and wholeness I invite you to email me about openings. Together we will help you to build a life truly worth living. Finally, if you are a registered therapist associate in Oregon or Washington I invite you to contact about my supervision services. Registered interns may be able to see clients remotely in Oregon AND Washington. Ask for details. Ind. $120. Group $60. 25+ years experience providing clinical supervision. Approved Clinical Supervisor in Oregon and a ACS through NBCC. Licensed in Oregon and Washington and have a CADC3 in Oregon. Contact me for a Supervisor Disclosure Statement.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: I have a graduate degree in Transpersonal Psychology. I am certified in Spiritually Integrated Psychotherapy. I utilize the Enneagram in my work with clients.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I have had a personal meditation practice for over 30 years and am trained in a variety of mindfulness and practices for use in counseling. I have studied Buddhist Psychology extensively.

specialities.name: Contemplative
specialities.description: I have experience with contemplative approaches to inner work from Christian, Buddhist, and Secular perspectives.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I have a master's degree in Transpersonal Psychology. I am certified as a Spiritually Integrated Psychotherapist. I often utilize the Enneagram in my work with clients. I enjoy working with clients who have experienced religious harm. I also enjoy working with clients who want to use spiritual resources to further personal growth.

name: Lisa Gascho
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi, I'm Lisa. I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and I specialize in working with trauma and stress related issues and concerns.
ideal_client: I commonly work with people who have had trauma and losses in early life, sexual trauma, and those who struggle with codependent dynamics in relationships in which healthy boundaries are not maintained. I treat adults across the lifespan, but most often work with young adults, women, and those in the helping professions such as teachers and social workers.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize various therapeutic modalities depending on the person’s needs and goals for treatment, which can include EMDR, Narrative Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, and others. My goal is to help people work through whatever pain they’re experiencing so that they can live in a manner that better supports their well-being and aligns with their values. This can look like helping a person process difficult life experiences in a more effective way in order to reduce the impact to them, teaching skills to grow the person’s ability to soothe and center themselves when feeling emotionally dysregulated or disconnected, and empathically challenging negative beliefs about themselves that do not reflect the full reality of who they are and their worth.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I’ve learned that whatever a person’s life experiences have been, they can be experienced as a crisis or a traumatic event when it exceeds the person’s capacity to cope. It is there where I like to come alongside and help the person sort out what is needed in order to heal and move forward in their life. As a therapist, I take a strengths-based approach with clients by not only working to address the issues they are seeking treatment for, but also helping them to recognize and access their own resilience, abilities, and resources; using these to address present-day challenges that they face.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am trained in and provide EMDR along with other therapies that are known to help resolve issues related to trauma. This extends beyond coping skills into work focused on resolving the root of trauma and its physiological impacts.

name: Allison Strausberg
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Welcome! I work with individuals and couples and specialize in EMDR, parts work, , and Emotionally Focused Therapy.
ideal_client: I work with adults individually and with couples who feel stuck in thoughts, emotions, or relationship patterns that just aren’t working. I also work with those struggling with a sudden stressor or those who want to work through past events. This includes things like trauma, depression, a challenging transition or loss, and low self-esteem. Or maybe you and your partner feel stuck in cycles of conflict and disconnection. You might feel lonely, unsatisfied, worn out, or hopeless.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My collaborative approach integrates evidence-based therapy methods with compassion, humor, and attuned listening. My practice is Internal Family Systems informed and incorporates mindfulness-based somatic work, interpersonal effectiveness skill building such as mutually respectful boundary setting, Emotionally Focused Therapy, and Somatic and Attachment Focused EMDR. I am proactive, provide structure, and welcome long silences, fast-paced intensity, and everything in between. I find that most people who come to see me are ultimately longing for a sense of inner peace, personal agency, and meaningful connections. My focus is on creating a safe and authentic space where you (or you and your partner) can heal your nervous system, expand your emotional capacity, learn to relate more effectively, and begin to build a life that resonates deeply with your dreams and values.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received my Bachelor of Arts from Juniata College with a double major in International Relations and Theater. I have worked as a process facilitator of restorative justice in Maine and a housing access case manager in rural Colorado. I practiced applied arts and theater for social change across many settings including rural Ecuador and Portland, ME before receiving my Master of Social Work with a certificate in Applied Arts and Social Justice from the University of New England in 2016. As a clinician, I worked in residential treatment programs with adults struggling with co-occurring mental illnesses and houselessness and residential treatment programs with neurodivergent teens and teens struggling with complex trauma, before transitioning to outpatient therapy settings in 2019. I am originally from the east coast and relocated to Oregon in 2020. My life outside of work is guided by a love of adventure, play, and connection.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I provide Somatic and Attachment Focused EMDR. SAFE EMDR harnesses the brain and nervous system’s natural healing process to make sense of the past and the present, release old negative beliefs, and to alleviate symptoms. EMDR is unique in that is does not require discussing details of distressing events in order to be effective. SAFE EMDR is effective for a wide range of challenges including trauma, anxiety, depression, and complex grief.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I am an IFS-informed therapist and integrate the principles of IFS throughout each therapy session. IFS understands each of us as comprised of protective and wounded parts, with a centered Self at our core. Through relating to protective and wounded parts from Self, rather than pathologizing them, IFS offers tools for healing and transforming the way you relate to yourself and others.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I help my clients build skills in the four pillars of DBT: distress tolerance, mindfulness, emotion regulation, and interpersonal effectiveness.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: ACT is a mindfulness-based approach that emphasizes understanding and acceptance of difficult thoughts and emotions while cultivating psychological flexibility and encouraging you to commit to new actions that align with your values.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) is an experiential approach that draws primarily from attachment science to facilitate relational healing and foster secure connections with self and others. With EFT, I will help you and your partner identify the patterns and cycles that create distress and transform them into opportunities for deeper understanding and connection, resulting in a more joyful and satisfying relationship.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am trained in Somatic and Attachment Focused EMDR. This approach integrates the evidence-based models of EMDR, somatic therapies, mindfulness, neurobiological regulation models, and attachment theory.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: I utilize a variety of modalities, especially Internal Family Systems and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, to help folks better understand and address the underlying causes of low-self esteem. I also support folks to build skills in identifying and expressing needs and boundaries across relationships and settings.

specialities.name: Anxiety
