specialities.description: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy is about finding a new way to relate to difficult thoughts and feelings instead of getting stuck in them or letting them dominate your life. It helps build a focus on what really matters to you and take small steps toward that—even when things feel difficult or messy.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Internal Family Systems sees the human mind as made of “parts”—like a worrier, a critic, or a people-pleaser—each trying to help in its own way. IFS helps you connect with your own calm and courageous inner voice to understand and heal these parts with compassion. What makes it unique is that it sees all parts as valuable, and trusts your inner self—not just the therapist—as the key to lasting healing and balance.

name: Ron Fox
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: My approach to therapy is supportive & empathic, affirming the diversity & uniqueness of individuals, relationship, & families.
ideal_client: I work with a wide range of persons, and my interests and expertise include: self-expression and creativity; anxiety and depression; self-reflection and mindfulness for stress reduction, personal growth and self-discovery; intimacy and sexuality in relationships; LGBTQ+, multicultural, and alternative relationship and family concerns; and ACA, co-dependency, abuse, substance, and other recovery and family of origin related issues.

approaches.My Background: I am a Portland based therapist with an MA counseling psychology and a PhD in clinical psychology. I have over 30 years of experience working with individuals, relationships, and families. I have worked as a therapist and supervisor in community mental health, and I have also taught graduate counseling and psychology courses for students on the path to becoming professional therapists.

name: Christa Cummins
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Do you feel stuck, anxious or depressed? I support people through life changes & difficult relationships in a non-judgmental space.
ideal_client: Are you unsatisfied with your relationships or work? Are you looking for support with chosen or unchosen transitions? Are you having trouble making changes in your life? I help people explore their needs and values, and to feel empowered to set healthy boundaries with significant others, family members, managers and colleagues. I love helping others clarify their values and find direction, and I'm here to support you at a pace that feels right for you.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I took a nontraditional path to become a therapist; after over 20 years in corporate positions, I found myself more passionate about helping my colleagues work through challenges in their personal and work lives. I’d volunteered for trauma- and grief-focused agencies for years, so it felt natural to get an MA in Mental Health Counseling from Lewis & Clark's graduate school. My focus draws upon 3 approaches: Relational-cultural constructivism, which suggests that our challenges are influenced by our sociocultural environments, and that recognizing our authentic selves is important to create change; Attachment Theory, in which our experiences, relationships, and interpretations from the past might be reflected in how we relate to the world now; and Cognitive Behavioral Theory, which emphasizes using these understandings of our constructions and ourselves to practice new ways of thinking, feeling, and behaving.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I help people get in touch with their authentic needs and values, and feel empowered to set healthy boundaries in relationships with significant others, family, and in the workplace. We may take a look at ways of coping that no longer serve you, and identify changes you want to try in your life. I’m here to help you practice change in a place where you feel heard and supported, and your intuition is valued without judgment. I especially love the opportunity to support people at transition points in their lives: career and workplace difficulties, life changes, and the anxiety, depression and 'stuckness' those can bring about. I am queer-affirming and welcome a diversity of clients.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Empowering women--and men--to understand their experiences to the extent that cultural influences have played a role is an element of my practice. We'll explore the ways in which your life might be changed by living in a way that is true to yourself by tapping your strengths.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: I help clients see how their strengths can be applied to make changes in their lives. We'll explore not only what has worked well in the past, but what may have worked well at one time but is no longer serving you, and work toward change.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: We'll examine the way you view yourself, others, your relationships, and the conventions in our culture. By taking small, measured steps to new behaviors in a supportive environment, you can practice awareness and positive change in a safe space.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can be one of the clues we use to know we need to make adjustments in our lives. When you feel like anxiety is getting in the way of your goals and quality of life, I can help you understand the source of those feelings, find tools to work with anxious feelings, and to work with this emotion.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Women face unique barriers, often due to cultural expectations. Family, work, burnout, self-esteem, transitions from motherhood to empty-nesting, the choice to forego marriage or not to have children, challenges of retirement: these all look different for women, and we'll explore what they look like for you as the individual person you are, in the context of what you would like from your life.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: My professional expertise in office settings and holistic view of workplaces as unique systems lends me a unique perspective. I combine my experience in the workforce with my approach to therapy to support you as an individual, focusing on the goals and challenges that keep you true to yourself.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Life transitions and change, whether chosen or otherwise, can bring feelings of anxiety, depression, and feeling trapped. I'm here to support you as we explore potentially difficult choices and actions to find confident ways of being true to yourself.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I support clients with depression by providing a safe place to bring your vulnerability, meeting you where you are and moving forward at the pace you need. I find that setting small, attainable goals that we work through nonjudgmentally helps many of my clients with depression. Throughout the process, I help you to feel understood and seen.

name: Taryn Holm
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I enjoy working with teens and young adults on issues such as trauma, anxiety, body image, gender expressions and sexual identities
ideal_client: I specialize in working with teens and young adults. I strive to be queer/LGBTQIA+ affirming, as I am part of the community as well!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I chose to pursue a career in counseling to hold a space for individuals to feel safe in their mind and body. My passions within the therapy world are working through trauma, anxiety, body image, and exploring gender expressions and sexual identities. I integrate internal family systems therapy, interpersonal neurobiology, and somatic/mindfulness practices. I believe that all parts of us are good and deserve to be heard, seen, and loved.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe that reconnecting and healing the relationship with oneself is the most beautiful aspect of therapy. In my experience, therapy is a mixture of cultivating inner love, deconstructing shame, and allowing all emotions to exist without judgment. Laughter and tears are welcome too! I would love to get to know you. Reach out with any questions! :)

name: Alina Khodadian
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am deeply committed to supporting people of all identities towards greater healing and empowerment.
ideal_client: As much as we may wish we could get rid of difficult and painful emotions, human suffering is unavoidable. I offer gentle exploration towards what it can feel like to begin to develop new relationships with unwanted feelings. My ideal client is someone who is looking to gain insight and find a new path forward.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I will spend a considerable amount of time learning more about you and what your values are. I have an extensive background in mindfulness and offer clients a variety of mindfulness tools (that aren't too precious). My aim is to explore tools that actually work for you. Self compassion will be at the heart of our work. I believe that the most healing aspect of therapy is the connection between the therapist and the client. I feel honored and privileged to get to work with clients and it feels especially sweet when people begin to feel comfortable opening up. I provide warmth, patience, mediocre metaphors, and occasional humor.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that everyone has the ability to grow and change at any point in their life. We all get stuck in some form or another and therapy can offer a safe enough space where we can gain new insights and develop tools to support us in our well being. I am always amazed by the bravery it takes clients to begin opening up to a stranger (aka me) and to seek out change. Regardless of whether you choose to reach out to me for a consultation call to see if we are a fit, I am on the sidelines cheering for you on this journey. In my free time I like to swim, be outside with friends, meditate, read, stare at my two cats and think about how cute they are, and enjoy occasionally performing bad improv.

name: Justin Little
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I work with adults, couples, families and teens with a wide range of issues including anxiety, trauma, autoimmunity and hard relationships.
ideal_client: Are you struggling with worry and stress that feels overwhelming? Have you had traumatic or abusive experiences that are still affecting your life? Do you have physical symptoms that are triggered by too much stress? Do you want to work through a difficult relationship or experience in order to restore trust and joy? I work with many clients dealing with these and many other issues, and I believe I can help you, too.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I take 3-6 sessions assessing individual or family clients to get an in-depth understanding of what you are experiencing. If we together decide to continue working together, I then help clients begin to gain both insight and skills regarding their mental health and behaviors, in order to empower you to understand yourself and your relationships more clearly and then take concrete steps to control what you can and improve your wellbeing with a lot of support along the way!

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I have benefited so deeply from my own therapy, as well as becoming more aware and educated about mental health and the ways my own feelings, thoughts and actions impact myself and others. Because I have found great meaning and have benefited from therapy, I am passionate about working with clients like you to help you carve your own path towards healing and thriving in your mind, body and relationships. I also believe that quality mental health care is a human right, and I am passionate about making therapy affordable and accessible to all.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: I work with individuals, couples and families to understand and improve relationships. This can be with an adult client's family of origin as they work through anxiety or depression, a couple wanting to improve their communication, a teenager and their caregiver struggling to find common ground, a parent seeking to work through their own traumatic experiences in order to improve their relationships, and many more!

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I practice Restoration Therapy, which is a newer theory that combines mindfulness, attachment, experiential interventions and behavior change. Restoration Therapy is also highly influenced by Narrative, Internal Family Systems, EMDR and Contextual Family Therapy.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety speeds us up! Mindfulness can help slow the process down and help us make wiser decisions about how to move forward. I work with many clients in both individual, family and group therapy to address anxiety using the latest developments in mindfulness.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have greatly benefited from couples and family therapy, and have been trained extensively in the Restoration Model, which assists couples (and all clients!) to identify the source of their fight/flight responses, and then empower themselves to act in more loving and trustworthy ways towards those they care about (including ourselves!).

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: As someone who lives with an autoimmune disorder, I have spent the last 4 years educating myself on the connection between our mental health (anxiety, depression, brain fog, lack of motivation, etc) and our physical health and gut health. I often work with clients in partnership with medical professionals to address the mental health side of chronic illness: learning to control what you can, reduce stress, improve nutrition and prioritize a regulated nervous system to increase wellbeing.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: The effects of trauma can reverberate down the generations. Additionally, secondary trauma can have similar effects as first-hand trauma or chronic stress. As the son of a combat veteran, I am passionate about helping clients identify ways in which their own traumatic experiences (or those of their loved ones) are impacting their mental health. As we learn to heal from trauma, our relationships and personal wellbeing will be positively impacted as well.

name: Kathryn (Jasmine) Green
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: As a dedicated Licensed Therapist (OR/TX), I am passionate about guiding individuals toward emotional, spiritual, and psychological healing.
ideal_client: My ideal client (YOU) is someone who is ready to engage in the therapeutic process with openness and curiosity. You don’t need to have all the answers—just a willingness to explore your thoughts and feelings in a safe and nonjudgmental space. Together, we can uncover your strengths, identify patterns that may be holding you back, and create a path forward that aligns with your goals and values. If you’re looking for a counselor who will meet you where you are-you have her!

approaches.How I Can Help You: *Serving clients in Oregon and Texas.* Why Choose Me? Expertise: Extensive training in evidence-based therapies combined with Spiritual integration. Compassion: A warm and empathetic approach that prioritizes your unique journey. Faith-Based Care: Holistic support for those seeking to incorporate their spiritual beliefs into the counseling process. Whether you are seeking professional guidance or support that honors your values and beliefs, I am here to walk alongside you on your journey toward healing and growth. Together, we can work to create a brighter future built on hope, resilience, and purpose.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I specialize in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Person-Centered Therapy, and Solution-Focused Therapy. My approach is tailored to meet each client’s unique needs while integrating Spiritual principles for those seeking faith-based support. Whether you are navigating life’s challenges or seeking personal growth, I offer a safe and nonjudgmental space to explore your concerns and discover meaningful solutions. I believe in the transformative power of empathy, active listening, and collaboration. My goal is to empower clients to overcome obstacles, find clarity, and achieve lasting change while nurturing their spiritual growth. As someone committed to creating a supportive environment, I strive to help individuals align their lives with their values and faith. *Serving clients in Oregon and Texas.*

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Treating anxiety in counseling includes identifying triggers, challenging negative thoughts with CBT, and teaching coping strategies like mindfulness or relaxation. Solution-Focused Therapy aids in setting achievable goals, while exposure therapy helps reduce fears. For clients seeking faith-based support, integrating practices like prayer and scripture can provide additional strength and resilience.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Treating depression in counseling involves identifying negative thought patterns, improving coping skills, and fostering positive behaviors. Techniques like CBT help reframe negative thinking, while Person-Centered Therapy provides a supportive space for growth. Encouraging healthy routines and exploring life goals build motivation. For those seeking faith-based support, integrating prayer and scripture offers hope and spiritual encouragement.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: With training in grief support, I help clients navigate loss by providing a safe space to process emotions and memories. Counseling focuses on understanding the stages of grief, finding ways to honor the lost relationship, and building coping skills for life adjustments. Techniques like journaling, mindfulness, and creating rituals aid healing. For clients seeking faith-based support, prayer and scripture offer additional comfort and hope.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I help partners address relationship challenges by improving communication, resolving conflicts, and rebuilding trust. Using evidence-based approaches like Gottman methods and Solution-Focused Therapy, I guide couples to strengthen connection and teamwork. For those seeking faith-based support, I integrate Christian principles, encouraging grace, forgiveness, and shared spiritual growth to enhance their relationship.

name: Sabrina Walters
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I am a Gottman Certified Therapist who specializes in couples therapy, family therapy, and working with adults and young adults.
ideal_client: I work with couples who are seeking a better relationship, healing from affairs, or are struggling with a phase of life that is unfamiliar. I use Gottman Couples therapy and am also trained in EMDR as well as Equine Assisted Therapy. I look forward to helping couples manage conflict and deal with differences in their relationship. If I am not able to get you scheduled with me, I manage a group of great therapists who can probably see you sooner than I can. We are here to serve you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a Certified Gottman Therapist, I focus on the research-based approach to helping couples heal. We have you do an in-depth assessment and use the Core Values Index to understand you at your innate, unchanging core level.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been licensed since 2006 and have been practicing the Gottman Method for the past several years, and became fully certified as a Gottman Certified Therapist in 2017. I am also a Gottman Trainer as well. My husband and I have been doing couples conferences since 2003 and he also offers relationship coaching and co-therapy if that is something you would like to do. I became certified in the EAGALA method of Equine Assisted Therapy in 2014. I use a combination of EFT, EMDR, Intersubjectivity, Gottman, Equine, and Strategic/Structural therapy to serve my clients best. I believe clients need to feel safe and secure in my presence, so that is my greatest strength: the ability to make you feel safe enough to explore your strengths and struggles and secure enough to try something new.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: At Core Values Counseling, we specialize in The Gottman Method of Couples therapy. We also provide couples conferences to add in your growth as a couple.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am trained in S.A.F.E. EMDR which is based in somatic and attachment theory. This mode of therapy is well documented and researched as the gold standard for dealing with trauma of all kinds.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Helping relationships heal and prosper is my passion. So often couples struggle and have no one to help them connect. That is what we do best. Give you tools through our training as a Gottman Certified therapist and relationship coach. We will cultivate hope through practicing compassion and forgiveness and bring you to a better place~

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: I have worked with youth and their families for over 30 years (as a youth mentor for 20 and in the schools for seven as a school counselor). I love helping young adults find a path to their future and help parents become the best consultants they can!

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: So often when we are going through a transition in life, we hit some bumps along the way. It is normal, and I hope to help smooth the way to a new place in your life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Everyone has some sort of anxiety, some of us are debilitated by anxiety. I work with you to find ways to cope with and overcome anxiety, or at least make more manageable to handle.

name: Iphilosophy Psychotherapy
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: PhD, MA, LPC, LCAT, NCC, Art Therapist
intro: We are a group of therapists from diverse backgrounds and life experiences.
ideal_client: We are a group of therapists from diverse backgrounds and life experiences, aiming to serve our communities through compassionate, affirming, and holistic care. We are invested in our responsibility to provide multi lingual inclusive, culturally specific therapy to BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and People of Color) communities. We would be honored to support your journey towards wellness and fulfillment. We offer services in multiple languages, including English, Arabic, Spanish, French, and Bangla.

approaches.Our Background: We are a diverse, multicultural group of providers with extensive experience in serving individuals and families from various cultural and ethnic backgrounds. Our team is dedicated to delivering culturally responsive care, understanding the unique needs of each community we support. We prioritize inclusivity, ensuring that language and cultural differences are respected and integrated into our approach to care.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: We have extensive experience in trauma-informed care, culturally responsive services, and working with diverse populations, including refugees and immigrants. Our team specializes in integrating mental health services with a whole-person approach, ensuring comprehensive support for individuals with complex needs.

name: The DBT Clinic
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: DBT (Dialectical Behavioral Therapy) focuses on skills to manage emotional and interpersonal challenges, especially depression and anxiety.
ideal_client: Life can be messy and feel overwhelming, and sometimes we can feel ill-equipped to handle it effectively. We might find ourselves having a difficult time controlling our emotions and reacting in ways that we later regret. Perhaps we blow up at others, pushing those closest to us away; or we might turn on ourselves with self-criticism, self-harming behaviors and/or thoughts of death. We can find ourselves trapped in troubled relationships, or stuck in worry and despair.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: Simply put, DBT teaches people how to live well. It doesn’t matter the diagnosis, or even if there is no diagnosis. If one has a model of strategies and skills to deal effectively with the inevitable stress that is part and parcel to the human experience, one is better equipped to manage their life more effectively. One can learn to create “a life worth living”. There are four skills sets: 1) Core Mindfulness; 2) Distress Tolerance; 3) Emotion Regulation and 4) Interpersonal Effectiveness.

approaches.Social Justice Issues We Care About: We, The DBT Clinic of Portland, stand in solidarity with the fight for racial equality. We continually scrutinize our company’s policies, procedures, and hiring practices. We engage in ongoing conversations around our Mission Statement and Inclusivity Statement that act as our guide to serving our community. And in full support of our statements we also have a multi-point plan of action that guides continuing therapist training and company practices, ensuring that our practice acknowledges the intersectionality of every experience and interaction, decolonizing our therapy and research. We are constantly growing and maturing to better show up for our community and those most underserved.

name: Living Well Counseling Center
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Living Well Counseling Center is centered on helping you build skills to love and live well.
ideal_client: We work with couples, families and individuals. Looking to strengthen your relationships, build confidence, feel empowered, and learn new skills to cope with life and relationships? This is the place for you!

approaches.Our Background and Approach: Our founder, Emily Brems is a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist who supervises a team of caring and compassionate interns at Living Well. We specialize in supporting couples, families, adolescents, and children, as well as assisting clients dealing with depression, anxiety, self-esteem, sexual abuse, and developing healthy sexuality. We are passionate about helping people restore peace in their relationships by building upon the foundations of love and trustworthiness.

approaches.Why We Started this Group Practice: We are centered on helping you build skills to love and live well. Living Well Counseling Center provides personalized care for each individual, couple, and family. Our work is focused on empowering you to achieve a high level of emotional regulation and mindfulness to produce meaningful and lasting change in your life and relationships.

name: Elizabeth Knutsen
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Reconnect with your body. Reconnect with you.
ideal_client: I work with individuals who are interested in building a deeper level of understanding of limiting beliefs held about themselves and the world that keep them from living the fully expansive lives they deserve. My clients are sex workers, those with eating disorders/disordered eating, non-monogamous, kinky and queer populations and those who are involved in community organizing. Please note I only provide telehealth sessions; I no longer live in OR. Please inquire about sliding scale rates.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Mind and body connection is one of the main portals to gaining a deeper understanding of ourselves. I utilize Somatic Experiencing and Mindfulness to help support my clients build safety and connection to their bodies to support their healing and growth process. I am deeply committed to obtaining consent and feedback from clients to ensure they are getting their needs met in our time together. It takes courage to show up as one's authentic self and to be vulnerable. I will validate the hell out of you and also provide reality checks when needed. Your feelings are real and they need space AND we can explore new ways of being in the world. Have you ever had feelings of being too much? I promise you, you're not.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: We'll be a good fit for one another if you appreciate direct feedback that has a softness to it. If you are ready to consistently show up and feel. I actively strive to dismantle beliefs that have been socialized in me that are harmful to others and myself. This is an ongoing task as, globally, we continue under late stage capitalism. I will often "punch up" at systems of oppression that hurt us all. We all live in a world that doesn't always support expansion and safety. Explore building safety in ourselves and our world and look at some of the ways your beliefs and actions may not be aligning with your values so we can come back home to those values. I take identity into consideration in my work with clients and will support you in separating your identities from the identity politics; a tool of the ruling class used to keep us separated.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: Many sex workers often burn out from the level of emotional engagement their job requires. Holding boundaries for yourself and with clients takes so much energy -- especially when you safety is at risk. It makes sense you're feeling burnt out. Let's build some skills around taking care of you and allow for space for burnout without normalizing it as a "right of passage" under capitalism.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Personal growth is a wild ride. I know in my lived experience that I was never told how painful and lonely it can be. Often personal growth involves grief and letting go of what our lives used to look like and radically accepting where we're currently at in our journey while still dreaming of what we want our future to be like. It's a lot to hold! I'd love to help support you in opening up space for the most authentic version of you.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: If you struggle with your relationship to food and movement -- I can help. Many of us struggle with internalized fatphobia and I can provide you resources and tools to dismantle this belief that was socialized into you. We've come to learn through living under capitalism, that it can feel safer to live in a particular kind of body; the kind of body that capitalism deems "acceptable." This simply isn't a reality. Work with me to dismantle unrealistic expectations we hold for our body.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Are you in a non-monogamous relationship or are curious about what those relationship structures can look like for you? Get some support around building, maintaining and growing your most intimate connections all while building awareness around power dynamics, communication and wants and needs in your interpersonal relationships.

name: Claudia Brown
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I help out of the box folks embrace liberation, authenticity, and healing through a collaborative, values-driven approach
ideal_client: If you’ve ever felt like you don’t fit into society’s expectations—whether you’re queer, nonmonogamous, kinky, an artist, or just someone charting their own path—I understand. My practice is a space where you can show up exactly as you are, without judgment, and explore what it means to live your truth. Whether you’re navigating relationships, your identity, or any aspect of self-discovery, I’m here to support you in creating a life that feels liberating and fulfilling.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: While I may have training in mental health, you are the expert in your own life. For me, it is crucial to stay present and curious about my client's experiences. I start all of my relationships by getting to know you deeply. Your history, perspective, point of view, and your feelings. Relationship building and trust is crucial, and some clients start to see transformation in their lives just from feeling fully seen and heard. If and when you become ready to go deeper into real lasting behavioral change, I employ frameworks such as Dialectice Behavior Therapy (DBT) and Mindfulness. I also use Internal Family Systems (IFS), inner child work and somatic work. As a queer person that lives with CPTSD and ADHD myself, I have done a lot of my own healing in therapy and bring many of my skills to you.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Human liberation is central to my practice, and I strive to create a space where you can challenge oppressive systems and embrace your true self. While the world around us may not always reflect the understanding or support we need, we can work toward a place of inner peace and resilience. My goal is to help you navigate these complexities, offering both compassion and empowerment as we work together to create meaningful change in your life. I am a proud member of the LGBTQ+ community, and have served LGBTQ+ youth in the school system. I also have a background in activism, within the Black Lives Matter movement as well as within immigration reform. As an immigrant child myself I resonate deeply with the feeling of displacement and survival that many of us experience. I am a Soviet Jewish cisgender woman, a mother, a dancer, and an artist

name: Tristan Kaczmarek
title: Student Counselor
intro: Scrolling through countless profiles can feel overwhelming—you're not alone in that.
ideal_client: I am looking to help anybody that is suffering and needs to feel supported. No matter your story, I want to be there for you and work collaboratively with you towards your goals.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from a couple different therapeutic approaches where I emphasize person-centeredness. I believe therapy is about empowering the client to find healing and growth in their own life and I want to assist you in that journey. I also work from an Emotional Focused Therapy (EFT) lens when working with couples and families highlighting family dynamics and cycles. I strive to build authenticity and trust into our relationship. With me, you’ll find a safe and supportive environment where your story matters. My goal is to help you explore your experiences, work toward your personal goals, and create a life that feels more aligned and fulfilling. If you’re feeling unsure or hesitant about reaching out, I invite you to take that first small but powerful step—send me an email or reach out through the contact page below. Whether we work together or I help you find someone else who’s the right fit, I’m here to support you on your journey toward healing and self-discovery.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Some of the reasons I became a therapist stem from my own personal traumas. I have seen a world of hurt and I want to make a difference in people's lives. I have always wanted to help people, it just took me a couple years to figure out the modality of helping others was through therapy.

name: Paige Medina
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Immediate Openings! My approach is collaborative, nonjudgmental, and focused on finding the best medication or treatment for you.
ideal_client: My clients are individuals seeking psychiatric care. They may be struggling with mental health issues, addiction, or both. My clients are ready to take steps towards healing and improving their quality of life. They value a collaborative approach to care, and are open to treatment plans that may include medication and therapy. My clients are committed to their well-being, and are looking for a supportive and understanding provider to guide them on their journey.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With almost a decade of nursing experience and behavioral health, I possess a deep understanding of the complexities of psychiatric care. My journey to become a Nurse Practitioner was driven by a desire to do more for my patients and their families. My approach to healing is patient-centered and holistic. I believe in empowering individuals to take an active role in their mental health journey. I provide compassionate care, education, and tailored treatment plans with medication management. I strive to create a safe space for patients to explore their concerns and work towards wellness. Through compassion, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence, I strive to make a positive impact on the lives of those I serve.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in the importance of mental health and wellness. I'm passionate about empowering individuals to reach their full potential. I believe everyone has the strength within them to overcome challenges and achieve their goals with the right support and tools. In my free time, I enjoy outdoor activities such as hiking and gardening. I also prioritize self-care through mindfulness and meditation. I'm always looking to learn and grow both personally and professionally. With my expertise in thorough testing, tailored evaluations, and individualized medication guidance, I can create focused treatment plans.

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: I empower you with personalized mental health medication management, education, and tailored plans. Together, we'll address anxiety, depression, ADHD, and more. My compassionate approach fosters a safe space for your journey to wellness. Let's navigate your path to recovery as a team.

specialities.name: Psychological Testing and Evaluation
specialities.description: As a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP), I believe in the power of connection and understanding to foster healing. My approach to psychiatric evaluations is centered around creating a safe, non-judgmental space where you feel seen, heard, and empowered. I take the time to truly listen to your story, not just your symptoms, because I know that your experiences and perspectives are unique. Through open dialogue and collaboration, we'll work together to identify areas of concern a

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Through my personal and professional journey, I've gained a profound understanding of the experiences of those with ADHD. I've witnessed the distinct challenges and remarkable strengths that accompany this diagnosis. My approach is to provide empathetic, tailored medication management, equipping individuals with the tools to navigate their symptoms and unlock their full potential. I'm dedicated to education, collaboration, and building a strong support network for those with ADHD.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have extensive experience working with individuals struggling with anxiety. I understand the impact it can have on daily life and well-being. My approach is to provide a safe and non-judgmental space for patients to explore their concerns. I offer tailored treatment plans with medication management. I empower patients with the tools and strategies they need to manage their anxiety and improve their quality of life.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I have a strong passion for working with women and addressing their unique mental health needs. I provide compassionate and empowering care, creating a safe space for women to explore concerns and work towards wellness. I offer tailored treatment plans in medication management and believe in the strength and resilience of women.

name: Dr. Udo Chukwuocha
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I offer holistic, integrative, patient-centered mental health care, helping individuals manage anxiety, depression, ADHD, and more.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with nurses, professionals, college students and individuals from BIPOC and immigrant communities, navigating anxiety, depression, ADHD, and life transitions. My ideal client seeks compassionate, culturally responsive, and integrative care that goes beyond medication. Whether you're feeling overwhelmed, struggling with focus, or searching for a provider who understands your experience, I offer personalized support to help you regain balance, confidence, and well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I take an integrative, patient-centered approach to mental health, blending evidence-based psychiatric care with holistic and lifestyle-based strategies. As a dual board-certified psychiatric mental health and family nurse practitioner, I provide comprehensive care that considers the whole person. With over a decade of experience in diverse healthcare settings, my goal is to empower you with a treatment plan that aligns with your values. My approach includes medication management when appropriate, therapeutic techniques, lifestyle coaching, nutritional guidance, and culturally responsive care tailored to each individual's unique needs. I believe in collaborative healing—working together to help you gain clarity, confidence, and balance. Whether you’ve struggled with finding the right provider or feel like past treatment didn’t fully address your needs, I strive to create a supportive space where you feel seen, heard, and empowered on your journey to mental wellness.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I am deeply committed to providing compassionate, inclusive, and culturally responsive mental health care for individuals who have felt unseen or unheard in traditional treatment spaces. My approach is rooted in understanding the complexities of identity, culture, and lived experiences, ensuring that every client feels valued and supported. As a provider with a background in both psychiatric and family medicine, I focus on integrative care that goes beyond symptom management to address the root causes of distress. I am particularly passionate about working with individuals navigating anxiety, ADHD, depression, stress, and I strive to create a safe space where healing, self-discovery, and growth can thrive. My practice embraces a holistic perspective, incorporating medication, lifestyle modifications, mindfulness, and evidence-based treatments to foster resilience and overall well-being. No matter where you are in your journey, I am here to support and empower you.

name: Jeri Parks
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Support that honors your intuitive resilience and infinite creative intelligence. Sliding scale inquiries welcome.
ideal_client: I offer services for individuals, couples, and adolescents. I am particularly passionate about serving late-diagnosed and self-diagnosed high-masking/camouflaging, internalizing autistics and neurodivergents.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Intentional change includes acceptance, respect, and gratitude for adaptive psychological and behavioral patterns. Resistance to resistance only multiplies tension. I will accompany you in cultivating clarity and choice about the ways you meet needs for survival, safety, belonging, and love, through presence and compassion.

My holistic power-with approach to therapy is founded upon my background and training in Hakomi mindful somatic therapy, Mindful Compassionate Dialogue, and Vipassana meditation. Access and re-inform the implicit material that shapes present experiences and relationships, and find liberation from chronic patterns. Develop a vocabulary for integrating experiences and self-responsible expression. Gain competence with concrete relational skills like life-serving boundaries, self-empathy, and working with reactivity. Understand interpersonal systems and patterns, and develop the fundamental framework and skills necessary for effective, satisfying communication.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: Misconceptions and stereotypes about autism have resulted in many high-masking, camouflaging, internalizing autistics being misdiagnosed or undiagnosed-- particularly those of us AFAB. Studies now acknowledge a “lost generation” of autistic adults, as well as the harm caused by certain approaches to treatment. As a late-discovered autistic myself, I am passionate about offering gentle, empathetic support attuned to your individual experiences, strengths, adaptations, and resilience.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Awareness is expanding about the vastness of the spectrum of neurodiverse presentations and experiences. As a result, a new era of self-discovery is blossoming for many previously-overlooked women, femme, and AFAB neurodivergents. Further, historically treated as mutually exclusive, new research shows that most people with autism also have ADHD. As someone with this lived experience, I will support you on your journey toward understanding, authenticity, and integration.

name: Cory Anton
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Cory! I'm enthusiastic about challenging anxiety and helping you thrive!
ideal_client: Anxiety sucks, let's face it. If you're sick of using coping skills that only seem to scratch the surface and you're ready to experience healing and relief, together we will help you get your life back and put anxiety back in its place! Learning to understand the mechanisms that keep the anxiety cycle maintained and breaking them by facing fears can be scary, but you have more courage than you may even know.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use humor, compassion, and a soft but direct approach to helping my clients find freedom and heal from anxiety disorders, depression, and life transitions. I use effective treatment methods (CBT, ERP) that help you get back to living your life faster and spend less time on my couch! I understand how scary and overwhelming living with anxiety can be. Often, the things that we are worried about are things that have happened before (like a panic attack or social judgement) and are strong in our memories. Challenging these fears can seem daunting, to say the least, and it can feel like a losing battle. Together, we will raise your hopefulness and get you back to living life in control.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been working in mental health for over 10 years, starting out in psychiatric residential treatment and inpatient programs. I received my Masters in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis and Clark and am licensed in both Oregon and Washington. I love working with adolescents and families as well as emerging adults. As a therapist, I have worked in residential treatment, the school setting, outpatient and private practice. I have expertise in treating OCD and anxiety disorders and have trained with the BTTI (Behavioral Therapy Training Institute) through the IOCDF.

specialities.name: Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy
specialities.description: Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) is considered the gold standard treatment for OCD. While seemingly straight forward, the ideas behind how to utilize this method are nuanced and talking back to OCD can be tricky. We get creative together! ERP helps you learn to face your fear while preventing you from engaging in the compulsions (or responses) that maintain the fear. Consent is of utmost importance and you have the final say in readiness and motivation to face your fear head on.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy can help you identify the connection between your thoughts, feelings and behaviors to help you better challenge negative thought patterns and create healthier thoughts and actions to combat anxiety and depression.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Acceptance of the unknown can be daunting and overwhelming, but ultimately leads to freedom and relief. ACT is often a very helpful adjunct to ERP and CBT when treating OCD and anxiety.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Dialectical Behavior Therapy can be very effective at helping you manage overwhelming feelings, irritability, depression and anxiety. If you are struggling with chronic suicidal ideation or self-harm behavior, I can help you learn the DBT skills to weather these emotional storms safely.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I believe in meeting clients where they are at and helping each and every person succeed in therapy. Sometimes that means using different approaches, such as CPS (Collaborative Problem Solving), solution focused, motivational interviewing or a narrative style.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: I am BTTI (Behavior Therapy Training Institute) certified to treat OCD. This includes a combination of using Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) therapy, which is the gold standard treatment for OCD. ERP helps you to build tolerance to the feelings of anxiety and panic that can occur.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is one of the most commonly experienced human emotions. However, if you are feeling worried more often than not, if reassurance and checking is no longer helping reduce anxiety, or you find yourself avoiding things that might cause anxiety, you may be experiencing symptoms of an anxiety disorder. Therapy can help you regain control of your life and put your anxiety back in it's place.

specialities.name: Panic
specialities.description: If you have experienced panic attacks and are constantly worried about having another one or avoiding places or situations in which you've had a panic attack before, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy can help. I can help you regain your life and control your symptoms. Together, we will work to increase your ability to tolerate these really uncomfortable feelings and help you get back to living fully!

specialities.name: Social Phobia
specialities.description: Second guessing yourself, worried about people judging you, difficulty ordering for yourself or speaking in public? You may be experiencing social anxiety (social phobia). Social anxiety can take many forms and you may be experiencing it even if you consider yourself extroverted or have many close friends. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy can help you work through these worries and build resilience.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Sometimes life can feel like too much. You lose motivation and things you used to enjoy become hard to do or tiresome. I can help you find your hopefulness and get your energy back.

name: Annie McConnell
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Therapy is a collaborative process and I hope to foster a safe environment that allows for movement into positive change. Please reach out.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with people of all different ages, abilities, identities, sexual orientations, and backgrounds. I incorporate equity and justice within my work. I especially enjoy working with people as they move through different life cycle stages and the ways that this might impact functioning or sense of identity. I have experience working with people living with anxiety, depression, experienced trauma, and navigating challenges within a complicated family system or relationship.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is psychodynamic, person-centered, and trauma-informed. I believe that human beings thrive off the connections we make and are shaped into our unique selves based off of the feedback we receive from people, communities, and society. Therapy can be an enriching and transformative experience that often requires vulnerability and hard work. My approach is warm, safe, and assertive. My therapeutic work is informed by Narrative Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Internal Family Systems (IFS) as I support clients in unpacking the many parts of themselves and their story.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist and received my Master's degree in Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy from Lewis & Clark College. I received a Bachelor's degree in Family & Human Services from University of Oregon. Through experience gained in working within the social work field at various non-profits, I realized my passion for working with people on their relationships by providing direct therapeutic support. I am a white, able-bodied, cisgender woman who strives to improve upon ways to listen and learn from others that identify differently than me. I hold my own unique experience of what it is like to move through the world, just as you hold your own experience. I strive to support you and to advocate for greater equity within society. Your lived experience is important and considered within your therapeutic work and also vital towards positive growth.

name: Aletha Eastwood
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: MA, Certified Hakomi Therapist, Level 2 AEDP therapist
intro: I offer a safe space for us to explore and heal hurtful patterns and to help you uncover and move in alignment with your authentic self.
ideal_client: I work with individuals and couples who are looking for relief from distress or searching for clarity amidst confusion. This distress and confusion may be in relationship with yourself, with others, or with the world you find yourself in. I endeavor to meet you where you are to create a healing relationship with you. Together we will make a safe space for you to have new experiences of trust, ease, belonging, and authentic connection.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have been a Certified Hakomi Practitioner since 2013. I invite you into a place of curiosity and nonjudgment about your experience. Using mindfulness and experiential approaches drawn from attachment theory, Hakomi, AEDP, EFT, and interpersonal neurobiology, we can identify and untangle old patterns of behavior and process unhelpful beliefs and old or ongoing wounding or trauma. These old patterns and beliefs are based in our experiences of the world, often from our earliest experiences in childhood or through trauma. Over time, they continue to function and can create a barrier to living a more satisfying life. In our work together, I offer a safe space to explore and heal patterns that are no longer working for you and to help you uncover and move in alignment with your authentic self. Our relationship becomes a foundation for exploration, acceptance, and growth from which you learn new ways to create greater fulfillment and connection with yourself, others, and your world.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I see therapy as a relational process. Hakomi is a practice of active, deep listening that invites you, as the client, to experience your own inherent wisdom. With my presence and guidance, I help you to anchor into this wisdom. Holding an attachment-based lens and recognizing how trauma disrupts our natural attachment system, I adjust and attune when difficult feelings, thoughts, and experiences arise. I help you to find your deeper connection to yourself once again. From Hakomi and my Buddhist meditation practice and studies, I believe that even the parts of ourselves we would rather get rid of have wisdom. No part of our experience is without wisdom. It is in the listening that we discover what is needing to be heard. In my work with couples, I draw on Nonviolent Communication and Emotion Focused Therapy to strengthen communication skills and uncover rutted patterns that have become barriers to intimacy and connection.

specialities.name: Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP)
specialities.description: AEDP recognizes that relational traumas occur when we are isolated in our experience in the face of overwhelming emotions. We become contracted around this traumatic experience, unable to move forward. Healing occurs in undoing the aloneness, giving space to gently re-orient the contraction toward our natural curiosity and creativity. In working together, we can rebuild your capacity to be with your emotions, out of survival mode, and into your natural state of flourishing.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is complex, and each person has their own unique experience. Sometimes we collect our losses and do not recognize our deep need to grieve. Sometimes our loss is unrecognized by others. The dominant American culture often does not allow much space or permission to grieve. A sudden or unexpected loss can lead to traumatic grief, kicking in our body's survival mechanisms. Wherever you find yourself in the process, I can help you navigate to a place that feels workable and connected.

name: Portland Therapy Project
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We are a queer owned, somatic based agency committed to serving marginalized populations on OHP. We serve individuals, couples and families.
ideal_client: Our clinicians serve queer, trans, BIPOC clients who may experience anxiety, depression, and trauma. We understands that many of us may experience trauma or other symptoms due to race, size, class, sexual orientation, socio-economic status or family culture. We also work with couples and families and welcome non-traditional relationships. Our clinic is a great place for those interested in body-centered (somatic) approaches within a warm and caring relationship with a therapist.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Our counselors are a passionate group of graduate therapy students invested in providing personable, caring and empathetic therapy. Traumas, our history, the socio economic and cultural realities we face can make it difficult to connect to ourselves and others. We provide a space where clients can connect with their body and emotions with clinicians dedicated to care and connection. Please check out our website for more info about our counselors: www.portlandtherapyproject.com.

approaches.More About the People We Treat: To get started, fill out our intake online: https://www.portlandtherapyproject.com/#new-client-intake We will contact you as soon as we have an opening that matches your availability!

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: All clinician and supervisors work through the lens of somatic therapy. We believe understanding our whole self starts with holding space for all the emotions and experience of the body.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: We create a supportive, caring place for all community members.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Understanding trauma and creating a place where one can explore the effects of trauma is our main priority.

name: Benita Munson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Are you feeling stuck in your life or in your current relationship? I am here to help explore and build healthier communication patterns.
ideal_client: I am experienced and happy to work with heterosexual, LGBTQ relationships, support around dating, parenting teen issues, chronic illness, and substance abuse disorders. In individual sessions, I will teach you ways to set boundaries, show up compassionately for self and others, how to use grounding techniques to soothe yourself when you are activated, and identify areas in life where you are struggling.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have post graduate training in EFT Couples Therapy, which has allowed me to help couples create healthier, more satisfying relationships with themselves and others. EFT Couples Therapy is evidence based to be highIy effective in relationship satisfaction. I believe that quieting the inner critic, and increasing self compassion changes the way we see ourselves and the world, and I incorporate Kristen Neff's work around self compassion into my practice. I am experienced working with chronic illness and disability, and use EMDR in my practice to treat negative beliefs as well as previous trauma. I am passionate about helping clients recognize and set boundaries, and learn compassionate yet assertive communication tools. We will work collaboratively to identify areas in your life that are problematic, and work on necessary changes. For more information about me and my practice you can go to www.maplecounselingpdx.com

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I grew up in Canada and have been working in a helping capacity since my early 20's. I have a Bachelor's Degree in Criminology/Psychology and a Masters of Science in Rehabilitation Counseling. I am a Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor, and have previously worked in inpatient drug and alcohol treatment. I am also a Certified Rehabilitation Counselor, which means I specifically support people with chronic illness and disability to achieve their maximum potential. I completed an externship in EFT Couples Counseling and continue to pursue training in Gottman, Terry Real and self compassion. I am passionate about my children, travel, animals, and equality for all people. In my spare time I enjoy connecting with friends, family and pets, finding new restaurants in PDX, nature walks, and playing pickleball. I enjoy helping clients make sense of their past, in order to appreciate the present, and look forward to the future. I truly love what I do.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I am passionate about working with couples and work from an attachment lens. I am consistently seeing parties make micro changes in the way that they communicate and learn about each other in our sessions. This enhances their relationships immensely. I am PACT Level 1 trained, which is neurobiology for couples, as well as EFT couples therapy trained, weaving in John Gottman's research, Terry Real, Esther Perel and evidence based practices for each.

specialities.name: Addiction Therapy
specialities.description: Motivational Interviewing is a tool used in addiction therapy which helps to address ambivalence in a person's quest to reduce substance use. There is a part of you that knows you need to cut down usage...yet you also need that substance as a security blanket or a coping strategy. Motivational interviewing helps us to address this. I am comfortable working with clients with both abstinence and moderation management/harm reduction models.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I am trained in Emotionally Focused Therapy for Couples through Edwards Psychotherapy in Portland. In EFT I will teach you how to access your primary emotions (IE sadness, fear) that are underlying secondary defensive reactions (resentment, jealousy). Once a person can communicate their primary emotion to a partner, it helps to increase connection and attachment. We will also do enactments in session which heighten emotion and also build connection and attachment.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am Level 1 EMDR trained and regularly incorporate EMDR into my work with clients. EMDR is eye movement desensitization reprocessing therapy, and is evidence based to reduce symptoms of anxiety, trauma, and negative beliefs that clients hold about themselves. The therapist uses either a wand/pen or hand that the client follows with their eyes, the bilateral movement reprocesses the way we hold trauma in the brain. I am happy to discuss this with your further.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: During our sessions we will review what is working and what is not working. We will identify your negative interaction cycle in the relationship, taking steps to break it down and improve it. I have completed an EFT couples training as well as participate in an EFT couples consultation group. I weave in Gottman strategies, as well as Terry Real to build support. I believe humor can be an important part of therapy as well.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Are you co-dependent in your relationship? I can help you to identify the warning signs of a one-sided, emotionally destructive and/or abusive relationship. Together we can rebuild your identity and self worth, weaving in self compassion and exploration of your family of origin, as well as necessary boundary work.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I have worked with numerous LGBTQ clients with varying issues over the course of my career, and am extremely comfortable with appropriate language, and offering a climate of total support without judgement. All parts of you are welcome here. I have worked with many LGBTQ+ relationships and continue to pursue training in this area.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: I have extensive experience working with alcohol abuse/dependence and drug addiction after working in an inpatient program for years. If you are struggling with either of these issues, I can help you recognize triggers, deal with relapse, and provide support for your recovery.

name: Emily Palmgren
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Welcome! Please reach out to schedule a free 20-minute video consultation to see if we're a fit for working together & to join my waitlist.
ideal_client: My clients are interested in exploring their early experiences with intimacy and love to foster more presence, awareness, and honesty in their relationships today. Whether you are wanting to work on your relationship with yourself or your partner(s), I offer you space to get real. My clients are willing to engage in mindfulness in session and occasionally practice activities outside of session to support them towards achieving their therapeutic goals.

approaches.My Background: I hold a Master’s of Arts in Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy with a specialization in Sex Therapy from Lewis & Clark Graduate School of Education and Counseling. I have clinical training in sexual and relational concerns like sexual difficulties, trauma, desire/arousal differences within partnerships, gender and sexuality expression, nonmonogamous and polyamorous relationships, and pain during sex. I completed a year-long internship with M.E.T.A. Counseling Clinic where I received extensive supervision, training in mindfulness, the treatment of trauma, anti-racism in counseling, supporting activists, and early childhood attachment. I worked with individuals and partnerships around a variety of concerns including anxiety, depression, communication skills, sex concerns, and trauma processing. At M.E.T.A., I co-facilitated a support group called PolyCurious focused on affirming and exploring the emotional attachment responses nonmonogamy can spur.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Working from a stance that promotes social justice is integral to my practice. In my mission to be a trauma-conscious provider, I prioritize client consent and safety. I am a kink/BDSM, polyam-, LGBTQIA+ affirming, body-positive, and continually learning anti-racist care provider. I am a white, Queer/Poly human working in Portland, OR (occupied land of the Clackamas and Cowlitz). My experiences in queer and multi-partnered relationships have been both challenging and profoundly healing. I am passionate about working with my community, and celebrate the full spectrum of relationships - from monogamy to relationship anarchy. I help people find resonant relationship practices for their lives centered in equity, consent, and compassion. I currently live in Corvallis (occupied land of the Kalapuya). When I’m not in session, I enjoy connecting with my loved ones, dancing, eating good food, and being in nature.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I have completed the Emotionally Focused Therapy for Couples (EFCT) Externship through ICEEFT.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: I am currently completing the Hakomi Professional Skills I training through the Hakomi Institute.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Our intimate relationships directly impact our wellbeing. It’s tough to feel centered when we’re feeling disconnected from our loved ones. In my work with partnerships, I emphasize mutuality, equity, and care. I want to ensure all partners are feeling heard - that you're really talking, and really listening. Whether you are seeking deeper intimacy or wanting clarity about where to go next in the relationship, I can support you towards meeting your relational desires.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Whatever the shape of your Consensual Nonmonogamy (CNM), chances are you’ve experienced edges arise as you practice this way of being in relationship. I celebrate radical relationship structures, and understand how complex these ways of loving can be to our attachment systems. CNM calls us into deeper work around our relationship to uncertainty, trust, change, and vulnerability. I can help you through navigating this process with care.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Perhaps the feeling of disconnection, loneliness, and self-doubt are familiar to you. Maybe feeling your emotions makes you want to run away or hide. Maybe there's a nagging feeling that you're not enough... Maybe it's just confusing inside. Through exploring and processing your lived experiences in your body, relationships & culture, I can support you towards growing more self-trust, self-compassion, and felt security that can fundamentally change your relationship with yourself and others.

name: Steven Balshem
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hello, my name is Steven and I am here to offer you a space for healing, growth and change, and to offer support through challenging times.
ideal_client: Are you a teen or young adult experiencing changes in your mood, or feel that your emotions and negative thoughts are becoming too difficult to manage? Do these changes impact every day life? If they do, maybe they were brought on by a significant life event, a traumatic experience, feeling oppressed, and may even be linked to underlying anxiety, depression, ADHD, or past trauma. Whatever it may be, your willingness to be vulnerable and commit to growth and change is the first step.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My collaborative approach to helping begins with establishing a therapeutic relationship rooted in trust, non-judgment, empathy, and validation. I recognize the challenges around sharing your thoughts, feelings, and life experiences with a complete stranger, so I am a big advocate of meeting you where you're at as we begin our work together. As our therapeutic relationship strengthens, we will begin to unpack the connection between your thoughts, feelings, and behavior (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy) to assist us in identify areas of growth that you feel will be most beneficial to you. Along with setting concrete therapeutic goals, we will also identify skills to assist you in increasing distress tolerance, emotional regulation, strengthening interpersonal effectiveness skills, and practicing staying in the present moment (Dialectical Behavioral Therapy). Lastly, we will often engage in effective problem solving (Collaborative Problem Solving) to address ongoing concerns in your life.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I am a Korean American, adopted, cisgendered individual who has worked in mental health since 2013. I've worked at varying levels of care after receiving my Bachelors Degree in Psychology at Oregon State University in 2012, and while completing graduate school at Portland State University, where I received my Masters in Social Work in 2017. Through my personal, educational, and professional experiences, I have completed trainings in Diversity Equity and Inclusion, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Collaborative Problem Solving, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, along with running a social justice group for high schoolers and implementing a suicide prevention curriculum at a local high school. As an Asian American growing up and living in the Portland Metro area the majority of my life, I value addressing the impact of oppression and oppressive systems that often intersect with many aspects of identity and identity development for teens and young adults.

name: Yi-Hsin (Cindy) Hung
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Therapy rooted in clarity, courage, and connection—where all parts of you are welcome, and none of them have to do it alone.
ideal_client: Hi, I’m Dr. Cindy Yi-Hsin Hung, a licensed marriage and family therapist, educator, and clinical supervisor. I work with individuals, couples, and families to help them reconnect with themselves, with each other, and with what really matters. I specialize in working with people who feel stuck in familiar pain patterns they see but can’t seem to shift. I support navigating both the loud arguments and the quiet disconnects, helping them explore the deeper dynamics beneath the surface.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I integrate Internal Family Systems (IFS), Relational Life Therapy (RLT), and EMDR to help clients move toward healing with clarity, accountability, and compassion. IFS helps us slow down and build respectful relationships with the different parts of you that have helped you survive. RLT brings direct, honest work into your relational dynamics so you can speak truth without shame. EMDR allows us to process trauma and painful memories that are stored in the body, even when your mind knows you're safe. My approach is structured yet flexible, always rooted in attunement and respect for your pace.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe therapy should be a space where you don’t have to shrink any part of yourself to stay connected. Healing doesn’t mean being regulated all the time—it means feeling safe enough to stay present, even when things get hard. I draw from both Eastern traditions like Buddhism and Taoism, and Western clinical models, blending mindfulness, nervous system awareness, and relational truth-telling. I grew up in Miaoli, Taiwan, and now call the Pacific Northwest home. Outside of therapy, I love creating mental health content in English and Mandarin, playing tennis, and spending time with my fur babies. I’m passionate about making therapy more real and more human.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I’m EMDR-trained and specialize in helping clients process trauma, anxiety, and overwhelming experiences that often live in the body, not just the mind. My clinical experience and research focus on trauma, cultural identity, and relational healing. EMDR is never a one-size-fits-all approach—I use it thoughtfully and collaboratively, honoring your pace, your consent, and your nervous system’s readiness to heal.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I’m Level 1 trained in Internal Family Systems (IFS), and it’s one of the core frameworks I use in therapy. IFS helps you build a respectful relationship with parts of you that feel reactive, numb, ashamed, or overburdened. These parts are not flaws. They’re protectors. Through this lens, we slow down and listen, allowing those parts to soften and unburden, so your Self, calm, clear, and grounded, can lead with greater ease and confidence.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I’m currently completing the certified track training in Relational Life Therapy (RLT), a bold and compassionate approach developed by Terry Real. One of his core teachings is that “we are not born knowing how to love well—loving is a skill.” I use RLT to help clients navigate power struggles, break reactive cycles, and build relational integrity. Whether with partners or family, I support honest, connected conversations that create real change.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I’m also Level 2 trained in the Gottman Method, a research-based approach to strengthening relationships. I draw on Gottman tools to help clients improve communication, rebuild trust, and de-escalate conflict. Combined with RLT and IFS, this framework allows me to support couples and families in both practical and emotionally grounded ways, so you can feel more connected, understood, and supported in your relationships.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: When working with relationship issues, I use RLT to name the power dynamics, defenses, and patterns that keep you stuck, whether loud or quiet. IFS helps you understand the parts of you that shut down, explode, or over-function in connection. EMDR supports healing past relational wounds that still live in the body. You get to show up more fully in relationships, without losing yourself in the process.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: When working with anxiety, I use IFS to help you connect with the parts of you that feel stuck in worry or pressure. RLT helps uncover relational patterns, like people-pleasing or conflict avoidance, that keep anxiety alive. EMDR supports the body in releasing stored fear from past experiences. You don’t need to fight your anxiety. You just don’t have to let it run the show.

specialities.name: Immigration/Acculturation
specialities.description: When it comes to immigration stress, I’m not speaking from theory—I’m living it too. As someone currently navigating the U.S. immigration system, I deeply understand the uncertainty, emotional weight, and identity shifts that come with it. I use IFS to help you hold all the parts of you—grief, pressure, hope. Through a relational lens, we’ll make space for your full story, not just survival. You’re not alone in this—I truly get it.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I’ve been through my own dark place—the kind where you’re functioning on the outside but barely holding on inside. For a long time, I thought I had to push through, stay strong, and hide the heaviness. What helped me begin to shift wasn’t “fixing” myself—it was learning to meet the parts of me that were hurting with compassion instead of shame. That’s why I now work through the lens of IFS, RLT, and EMDR—to help others find their way out.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I get how ADHD can feel—like your mind is always on, yet nothing gets finished. The overwhelm, the forgetfulness, the frustration of trying so hard and still feeling behind. I use IFS to help you understand the parts of you that overwork, procrastinate, or shut down. Through RLT, we explore the impact of ADHD on your relationships and self-worth. My role isn’t to fix you, but to support you in building systems, self-compassion, and a life that works with your brain, not against it.

name: Sawyer Salameh
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: What a wild confusing world we can live in sometimes. Let's try to figure it out together!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy can extend beyond the mind by incorporating the body and our experiences. This approach provides us with a more comprehensive understanding, enabling us to make more grounded and intentional choices. It helps us clarify how we want to show up and live the life we’re in.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a white, queer, nonbinary therapist, I recognize that my identity has uniquely shaped my experiences and influences how others perceive and treat me. I understand that privilege extends beyond financial stability; being part of the queer community allows me to create connections and offer support. As a nonbinary individual, I have the privilege of understanding the complexities of both masculinity and femininity.
