Examining the intersectionality of one's life, culture, and experiences is crucial for me to fully understand you and your place in the world. My whiteness has afforded me significant financial and safety privileges, and I am mindful of the disparities created by Western colonialism that have impacted others.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I use attachment theory as a foundation to support both individuals and couples. This approach helps us understand how you interact with others and with yourself, offering insight into the patterns and dynamics that influence your relationships. By exploring your attachment style, we can identify and address these patterns, which are often shaped by early interactions with family members and guide how you relate to the world.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: I focus on what’s happening in the room to help you better understand yourself and gain more control over your choices and life. Our experience encompasses everything occurring in the room, including our thoughts, feelings, and bodily sensations. By paying attention to these elements, you can explore how they influence your behaviors and decisions, leading to a deeper understanding and more empowered approach to life.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Internal Family Systems (IFS) helps us explore the roles we adopted as children and how these roles might influence our current relationships. This approach fosters compassion and understanding for our inner child, allowing us to address and heal past wounds. By integrating this understanding, we can improve our present relationships and create healthier, more fulfilling connections.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: Since beginning my career, I have specialized in working with PTSD and historical trauma. My focus has been on helping individuals move past their trauma and prevent it from dominating their present experiences. By addressing and processing these painful histories, we can reclaim control over our lives and mitigate the impact of past events. This process allows us to heal and build a more empowered and resilient future.

specialities.name: Sexual Abuse
specialities.description: I have extensive experience working with adults who have experienced both childhood sexual abuse and recent trauma. My background includes specialized trauma education and training in EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing) therapy. This training equips me with effective tools to help clients process and heal from their traumatic experiences, supporting them in finding relief and reclaiming their lives.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I focus on addressing systemic struggles that encompass cultural influences, family dynamics, and interpersonal relationships. I view a couple as comprising three components: the two individuals and the relationship itself. My goal is to help you gain insight into your relationship, identify what is important to you, and determine what changes are needed. I work with each person to articulate their needs and desires, both for yourself and the partnership, facilitating clearer communication.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can make it difficult to connect with ourselves and other. Almost every client I've worked with has faced some form of anxiety, which highlights its pervasive role in our lives. In our sessions, I aim to build a supportive and understanding space where we can explore how anxiety affects your relationships and work together to find strategies listen to it so that you can learn to take care of yourself in it.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Many of us experience some form of depression, but when it starts to interfere with your ability to live fully and do the things you want, it becomes a serious concern. My goal is to support you in finding effective ways to take care of it and work with your depression, helping you to coexist with it and regain a sense of control and purpose in your life.

name: Ellen Eberhardt
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) and a therapist for 17 years. I provide a non-judgement and safe place to heal and grow.
ideal_client: Ages I treat are 8 years old to seniors. I provide therapy to individuals, couples, and families. Therapies I provide are: CBT (Cognitive Behavioural Therapy), DBT (Dialectical Behavioural Therapy, ACT (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy), SFT (Solution Focused Therapy, and SP (Strengths Perceptive).

approaches.My Background: Education and Years In Practice: In Practice for 17 years Attended Hawaii Pacific University, Masters in Social Work, Graduated 2008 Additional Credentials Licensed by State of Oregon / L6646 License: License Clinical Social Worker L6646 / 2015 Degree/Diploma from Hawaii Pacific University Masters in Social Work / 2008

approaches.More About the People We Treat: Types of Therapy I Provide: Acceptance and Commitment (ACT) Cognitive Behavioral (CBT) Dialectical Behavior (DBT) EMDR Family / Marital Family Systems Feminist Person-Centered Solution Focused Brief (SFBT) Strength-Based Trauma Focused

name: Eric Hertz
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: BA Stanford University, MA University of Cumberlands, MFA Boston University
intro: I offer psychodynamic psychotherapy to adults and adolescents, with an emphasis on mindfulness, somatic awareness, and creative compassion.
ideal_client: Do you find yourself in a small world constructed from repetitive habits and limiting beliefs, out of touch with the vibrant joy of life, and your inherent curiosity and creativity? Are you spending your human life shaming and criticizing yourself? Have you glimpsed a way of living your unique flavor of love and grace, but find yourself far away from this full expression? I work well those interested in spirituality and art, and those looking to find deeper meaning and inner guidance.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Human beings are incredibly creative creatures. With our thoughts, words, and actions, we are able to create lives of beauty, joy, generosity, and freedom. However, often we find ourselves out of touch with this inherent creative potential, and we instead end up following repetitive patterns of mind and action that are not born out of well-being and wisdom, but out of reactivity and ignorance. I can help you explore and unravel these habits of mind--anxiety, depression, shame--and reconnect with the inherent, vital creativity that is our essential nature. The primary virtue that guides my work is Curiosity. The answers we're looking for want to reveal themselves to us--they are just waiting for us to let go of resistance and shame and be genuinely open. However, it can be quite challenging to touch our most painful habits, beliefs, and traumas. At some point in our journey, all of us need a skilled friend, teacher, or therapist to help us refine our investigation and expression.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Meditation and Mindfulnesss: Having spent two years training full time at a Zen monastery, and over a year total in silent Buddhist meditation retreats, my approach is based on present-moment experience, grounded in this breathing body. Care of the Soul: I like the ancient Greek translation of psycho-therapy as "Care of the Soul." Symptoms are not problems to be fixed, but invitations to deeper understanding and fuller spectrum of self-expression. I use dreamwork, myth, and active imagination. Parts Work: I've completed a year long training in Voice Dialogue, a parts-work modality, as well as study of IFS. Creativity: As a writer, and musician who has taught Creative Writing at the University level, my style is creative and invites your creativity. Inquiry: As an ongoing student of the Diamond Approach method of spiritual inquiry, I trust that Reality reveals itself to attentive curiosity. Practical: Shifting and playing with our outer material conditions is important too.

name: Lauren Stines
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Set up a free 20-minute consultation to feel out whether we are a good fit
ideal_client: My ideal client is open to trying new ways to get in touch with themselves; like mindfulness, breathing exercises, gentle movement, or philosophical discussion. You want to interrupt unhelpful patterns and find more meaningful was to relate and cope.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The practice of observing and feeling one's feelings can build a sense of aliveness, decisiveness, clarity, compassion, and confidence in tending to the emotions that inform our thoughts, behaviors, wants, and needs. In session, you will be invited to tap into the emotional content that comes up as we discuss the topics of your life. You will be invited to use your imagination and creativity as you explore who you are and what you feel. I find that this provides opportunity for emotional processing, increased insight, developed intuition, developed decision-making skills, overall emotional awareness and wellbeing. It becomes easier to connect with others, when we build a practice of connecting to ourselves.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I practice from a trauma-informed perspective which enacts physical and emotional safety, choice, and transparency. You are always allowed to say “no”/”not right now” to a check-in or question I ask, though depending on the topic I may ask for clarification on what informs your “no”. So many of us have been taught that our feelings are something to push down, avoid, to apologize for, or hide from others. Feeling Space Oregon Therapy rebels against that belief and practice by creating a space where clients' feelings are valued and cherished as vital information to our lived experience as humans.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: When we have a sense of security and belonging, we feel much more confident to explore the world. We can explore your attachment style, how it impacts how you relate to the world, and tap into your ability to change it and find a sense of security in your life and relationships.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: Our experiences make up who we are. As an experiential therapist, I will invite you to explore how you are experiencing the content of your life within the 'here and now'. I do so by engaging my clients with mindfulness exercises that explore their present emotional responses to the content they bring to therapy.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Our bodies hold wisdom and insight into our wants, needs, and boundaries. Our bodies allow us to experience parts of life like pleasure, play, and joy. They are also vessels that hold our pain. Through somatic therapy, we can reconnect to the feeling body, deepen into pleasure and joy, and identify where trauma/anxiety/depression is held in order to tend to it. I will invite you to check in with how your body responds to content expressed in session with compassion and curiosity.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: So, you live in a body on a rock rotating around a big ball of gas in a limitless universe...yikes...now what? Well, whatever you want I suppose. I will compassionately support you through crises of isolation/belonging, death/life, freedom/responsibility, and the general run-of-the-mill sense of meaninglessness. I will invite you to create meaning for your experiences and touch base with how you experience them in the present moment.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: In a society that profits off of our insecurities, it's no wonder so many of us have a hard time loving and accepting ourselves. In addition to cultural influence, our experiences of relational harm and traumas can breed shame and isolation. I believe you are valuable and deserving of care, even if you can't accept that right now. I will hold compassion for you while challenging you to engage in self-acceptance and compassion. It's so hard to hate ourselves into someone that we love.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: You are more than your trauma. In working with me, you will never be expected to disclose the fine details of your greatest hurts. Instead, we will gently cradle the emotional residue of those experiences, hold curiosity for those hurts as well as compassion for the ways that you continue to survive. That compassion will pave a path toward letting go of the survival strategies that are no longer serving you. We will slowly reintroduce you to your feeling body and invite you back into your life.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: As someone who identifies as neurodivergent, I have big empathy for the magic and challenges that come from our unique experiences in this world. I warmly welcome allistic, autistic, ADHD, and AuAdhd clients alike. My approach to the neurodiverse client is one that encourages self-compassion, reframing mindfulness toward accessibility, and overall creating a space where you can be you. Where you can take the mask off and be fully yourself, even if you aren't entirely sure what that means.

name: Simeon Roane
title: Student Counselor
intro: Hello, my name is Simeon. I am glad that you are here and I look forward to the opportunity to work with you.
ideal_client: If you are wanting to heal from grief and loss, trauma, addiction, self-esteem issues, or the overwhelming stress and anxiety that can accompany life’s transitions, you have come to the right place. As a practicing clinician with a lifetime of experience (and many hours of graduate course work) I am trained to offer guidance and support to those who seek change within themselves, their lives, and their relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Together, in a safe and supportive environment we will access the many therapeutic benefits found within Talk Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Restoration Therapy, and Mindfulness Based practices. So – regardless of your age, gender identity, sexuality, or spiritual affiliation – you are welcome here. And I look forward to working with you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Many times, people can handle life’s problems on their own but some problems, regardless of their perceived size, require a little help or even a ton of it. Asking for that help isn’t always easy. However, I can assure you that it is the first and perhaps most important step on your path to healing and recovery. As a practicing clinician with a lifetime of experience–some good, some bad and some ugly–I am trained to offer guidance and support to those who have come to a crossroads; those who are either willing or forced to make changes within themselves, within their lives, and within their relationships.

name: Hannah Oliver
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: It is an honor to support folks in their healing journey. Together, we’ll navigate your needs in a warm, non-judgmental space.
ideal_client: I typically see adults facing challenges related to attachment, relational, loss, and/or complex trauma. Trauma recovery can present in a number of ways including depression, anxiety, disordered substance use or eating, mood instability, unfulfilling relationships, or numbed emotions. I thrive in creating a supportive, empathetic space where we can explore these issues together at your own pace.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I graduated from Syracuse University with a Master of Social Work (MSW). I bring valuable experience volunteering on a suicide hotline and interning as a counselor for individuals facing financial and housing insecurity. My specialized training focuses on trauma recovery, suicidal ideation, and LGBTQ+ issues, allowing me to support a diverse range of clients. In therapy, I take an integrative approach, utilizing various modalities such as narrative therapy, art therapy, somatic (body connection) techniques, behavioral strategies, and talk therapy. This flexibility allows me to tailor sessions to each your unique needs and preferences. I create a supportive and honest environment where you can explore their thoughts and feelings, build resilience and coping skills, and work toward healing and personal growth. Together, we can navigate challenges and foster a deeper understanding of your challenges, strengths, and self.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am dedicated to social justice and anti-oppressive values in my therapy practice. I believe everyone deserves equal access to mental health care and a safe space to share their identities. I focus primarily on LGBTQ+ issues and the unique challenges this community faces in acceptance and visibility. In my free time, I enjoy playing table top RPGs, board games and video games with my friends. I love trying out new restaurants and food trucks. Last but certainly not least, I love spending time at home with my family and pets!

name: Madison Carter
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I help couples, families & individuals navigate life's challenges. Creating a warm, safe space where you can grow, heal, and feel understood
ideal_client: In our work together, you'll find a nonjudgmental space where you can safely explore challenges and work toward your goals. Whether you're a couple seeking to strengthen your bond, a family working through communication issues, or a child processing complex emotions, I'll meet you where you are with warmth, expertise, and genuine dedication to your growth. Our sessions will balance practical skill-building with deeper emotional work. I believe in creating a collaborative therapeutic relationship

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that healing and growth happen within safe, nurturing relationships. As a Marriage and Family Therapist Associate, I create a therapeutic environment where clients can explore their challenges, understand their patterns, and develop stronger connections - both with themselves and others. My approach combines evidence-based practices with deep compassion, ensuring that each person's unique background and experiences are honored and respected.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I create a safe, nurturing environment where you can explore your challenges and work toward meaningful change. Whether you're a couple looking to rebuild connection, a family navigating communication difficulties, or an individual, I'm here to help. What sets my practice apart is my dedication to meeting you exactly where you are. I don't believe in one-size-fits-all solutions – instead, I tailor my approach to your unique needs and experiences. Together, we'll work at your pace to strengthen relationships, improve communication patterns, and help you feel more connected to yourself and others

name: Erika Tarjan
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I help clients uncover their authentic selves through compassionate support and self-discovery.
ideal_client: I work with people navigating life transitions, parenting challenges and relationship struggles, helping them implement health boundaries, find relief from anxiety, depression, grief and trauma, and create a more meaningful life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a compassionate and collaborative mental health therapist, I create a safe, non-judgmental space where trust can flourish. I specialize in supporting individuals and couples who feel overwhelmed by life’s challenges, whether navigating anxiety, depression, trauma, or significant life transitions. Together, we will explore your unique strengths, challenges, and goals, working to develop practical coping skills that empower you to feel more in control of your life. My goal is to support your journey toward healing, resilience, and a future filled with confidence and meaningful growth. Drawing from evidence-based interventions, including strength-based approaches, EMDR, Internal Family Systems (IFS), and mindfulness practices, I help create a personalized map to help you facilitate meaningful change.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I deeply value compassion, authenticity, cultural humility, and collaboration. My goal is to create a safe, supportive space where clients feel truly seen, heard, and empowered to heal and grow. I approach therapy with a systems perspective, recognizing the influence of family dynamics, societal structures, and systems of oppression on our lives and well-being. I also emphasize acknowledging power imbalances, being aware of societal and systemic inequalities, and working toward equitable relationships and practices

name: Gregory Kaplan
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: You can: grow after abuse or neglect, temper anger, navigate conflict, grieve loss, create effortlessly, and communicate effectively
ideal_client: My clients have experienced childhood or transgenerational trauma, abuse, neglect, and/or systemic oppression; cannot control anger or verbalize feelings; suffer shame; experience religious/spiritual/political change or conflict; and explore creative expression. I connect with students, activists, writers, teachers, techies, and entrepreneurs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We will go beyond relieving symptoms to unpack the sources of your life's pain and purpose. I listen attentively, with curiosity and no judgment, allowing your experience to unfold so we can sense into its uniqueness. I help you revise outdated patterns and repair old wounds that break through coping mechanisms and defenses into symptoms such as anxiety, depression, uncontrollable anger, toxic shame, unresolved grief, mood swings, and insecure attachments. You can adjust behaviors, feelings, and thoughts that were once adaptive and are no longer. You will rediscover flexibility and adaptability, resilience and grace—appreciating how to track and shift emotional states, what to say to a loved one, why to connect more deeply with or cut someone off (e.g., an abusive relationship), etc. I help adults, adolescents, families, and groups. By dismantling oppression together, we can hear ancestral voices and unpack intergenerational trauma that resonates in us all collectively.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My orientation to counseling is psychodynamic, feminist, multicultural, anti-oppression, neuroscience-aware, and trauma-informed. Before counseling, I had careers in academia and book publishing that prepared me to nurture people's growth in an adaptive way. My academic focus on philosophy of religion encouraged me to explore how people have made very different senses of their lives in the world. I experience my own privilege as a White upper-middle-class assigned-male-at-birth. I identify as a member of non-Zionist Jewish ethnicity and the LGBTQIA+ community. I am educated in psychodynamic psychotherapy and trained in EMDR, somatic therapy, group work, trauma recovery, anger management, White anti-racism, and Internal Family Systems. I earned a PhD in Comparative Religious Studies from Stanford University and a MA in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from the Family Institute at Northwestern University. I serve as adjunct faculty at Lewis & Clark.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: My education at Northwestern University was centered on psychodynamic psychotherapy. It was incorporated into multiple skills courses. In addition, I have trained extensively in psychodynamic group therapy. My practice centers around insight-based therapy, which means we are trying to uncover the roots of feelings, behaviors, and beliefs that are fed by unconscious sources, not exclusively memories but also fantasies and, most of all, unmet or over-met needs.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma is an over-adaption to an overwhelming event (e.g. assault, abuse). PTSD disrupts our capacity to regulate thoughts, feelings, and behaviors, and puts us into survival mode. It can leave our relationships and nervous systems in need of repair. Symptoms include intrusive thoughts of harm and distressing memories, being. Yet with adaptation and resilience, most of us are able to grow stronger from the most grievous wounds. I am a Level I Trained EMDR therapist.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Religion & spirituality are potentially helpful or harmful, sources of distress or sustenance. They can restrict us or foster resilience. Broad and open, religion/spirituality can nurture value and connection to other beings and a greater power; narrow and rigid, it can induce anxiety and shame. Interventions will develop internal and external support systems, explore beliefs that induce suffering, enhance joyful feeling, or strengthen social connection. I am versed in Psychedelic Integration.

name: Julian Montanez
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Hablo español. No Waitlist! Immediate Availability! I partner with clients for medication management for mental health concerns.
ideal_client: I frequently work with adults managing anxiety, depression, ADHD, and bipolar disorder who want collaborative care. I take time to understand how symptoms impact your daily life, carefully considering factors like work demands, sleep patterns, and overall wellness goals. By combining my medical expertise with a holistic understanding of your life, we develop medication strategies that align with your needs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I'm committed to patient education and shared decision-making. I explain medications thoroughly, discussing potential benefits and side effects, and ensuring you feel confident in your treatment plan. My background in nursing brings a unique perspective to psychiatric care, allowing me to address both biological and personal aspects of mental health.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: If you're considering medication management or looking to optimize your current treatment plan, I welcome you to reach out. I offer both in-person and telehealth appointments, providing flexible options for ongoing care. Together, we can work toward finding the right medication approach to support your mental health goals.

specialities.name: Psychological Testing and Evaluation
specialities.description: I provide comprehensive psychiatric evaluations and testing services to help clarify diagnoses and guide treatment planning. Using standardized assessment tools, I offer ADHD testing for adults, depression and anxiety screening, and diagnostic clarification for complex presentations. My evaluation process typically includes detailed clinical interviews, standardized rating scales, and evidence-based assessment measures.

name: Andrew Friede
title: Psychiatrist
credentials: MD, MPH -- Board Certified in Prevention, Addiction; Certified in Obesity Medcine
intro: The key is establishing a relationship based on trust & caring. Schedule a free 10 min phone call at Bluestone-Clinic.com.
ideal_client: I see adults 16+ from every background, faith, and work experience. I have worked in university hospitals, in shelters for the unhoused, and overseas, and with persons with every kind of sexual orientation.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use structured counseling and the latest medications (including Suboxone). Together we will find practical ways to enhance mindfulness, sound sleep, nutrition, and exercise. If you already have a counselor, I can offer medication-management in collaboration with them. I only see patients in-person (no video or phone calls), ages 16+. Please find more details at Bluestone-Clinic.com.

I treat the whole person because psychological pain has its origins in the complex interactions of personal and cultural history, physical health, individual neurochemistry, and life struggles. Together we will help you find meaning and peace in the context of complex family issues, your own history, and work and school challenges. Not everyone needs medication, but if you do, we identify medications for anxiety, depression, bipolar disorder, ADHD, personality disorders, PTSD, addictions, and weight management. You may have found that psychiatric medications either do not help or have bothersome side effects. However, these issues can be caused by drug or alcohol use, sleep deprivation, or untreated medical conditions. I will help you sort this out. Sleep, exercise, nutrition, and mindfulness have a profound impact on mood, productivity, addictions, and relationships. We will help you find ways to sleep and eat better, and learn relaxation techniques, including meditation.

name: Michelle Robertson
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I specialize in working with teens, adults, relationships/partners, military personnel/families and trauma.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with teens, relationships/partnerships (including relationships with parents or other relationship challenges, both current and past), adults, and those that are dealing with trauma. It’s great when clients come ready to do the hard work. However, I understand a client may not be ready for that yet and that we may need to take it slower. I recognize coming into counseling is the first step and am glad that you are taking it. I am ready to go at the pace that best works for you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Life can be challenging. At times it can be filled with obstacles that seem insurmountable. Anxiety, depression, stress, relationships, work, low self-esteem and trauma can make one’s life even more difficult to navigate. Learning skills to help you through these challenges can be key to helping you overcome them. I would like to come alongside you on your journey to help you find peace and freedom. I will bring compassion, genuineness, empathy, directness, and humor into our sessions. I will also bring my understanding of how trauma can affect every aspect of your life, including your body. One of my main goals is to create an environment of safety and a place to explore to gain an insight.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In my spare time, I love to cook and laugh with my family and friends. My other hobbies include gardening, reading, cooking, and sewing. The longer I work on my self-care practices, the more I see them intersect with my hobbies and I love this.

name: Arwen Huffman
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hello! I'm Arwen & I'm glad you are here. My focus is to help you heal, self-empower, and become aware of your inner strengths. Let's talk.
ideal_client: We all have times when daily life is harder than we expected. Are you dealing with natural life transitions, the upward struggles of aging, grief/loss, lack of support, feeling sad, or just need general coping skills? I have helped folks just like you return to a more supportive and stable path in their lives, and I'm here to help you as well. I work with individuals aged 16 and up.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have a Master of Social Work degree and am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker in both Oregon & Washington. I am a Certified Anxiety and Trauma Treatment Provider & LGBTQ+ Affirming: I Specialize in Women's Mental health, focused on perinatal/postpartum, infertility, infant/pregnancy loss (including abortion), menopause; as well as life transitions, divorce, PTSD, life challenges, grief/loss of a loved one & pets. My focus is to partner with you to help identify what issues are interfering with your daily life. I provide a safe, neutral space, while listening to your concerns, focusing on how together we can best work to meet your therapeutic goals and customizing a treatment plan using multiple treatment modalities which are tailored to you and your current needs. I utilize a variety of techniques derived from CPT, CBT, DBT, Solution Focused, ACT, Evidence Based, Mindfulness, Interpersonal and Person-Centered therapies.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in equality for all folks (it's not pie). I believe we all deserve love, respect and support. I believe that no human is illegal and no one human is better than another. I believe that most people are good and decent, trying to do the best they can. I believe that learning is life-long, and reading is fundamental. I believe that you deserve to feel happy. About me... I am a twice divorced mother of 6 grown children, have 3 amazing rescue pups, love reading and enjoy visiting the Oregon coast, watching movies and playing video games. I grew up in Eugene and have been in the Portland area since 2011.

name: Krysta Snyder
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Immediate Openings! I am open, nonjudgmental, and I work collaboratively with my patients to find the best medications or treatment.
ideal_client: My clients are individuals seeking psychiatric care. They may be struggling with mental health issues, addiction, or both. My clients are ready to take steps towards healing and improving their quality of life. They value a collaborative approach to care, and are open to treatment plans that may include medication and therapy. My clients are committed to their well-being, and are looking for a supportive and understanding provider to guide them on their journey.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With over 15 years of nursing experience, 13 of those in behavioral health, I possess a deep understanding of the complexities of psychiatric care. My journey to become a Nurse Practitioner was driven by a desire to do more for my patients and their families. I am dedicated to providing holistic, individualized care that addresses the unique needs and circumstances of each client. My approach integrates medication management with psychotherapy, empowering individuals to achieve their personal goals and enhance their well-being. I take great joy in educating my patients, believing that knowledge is power in the path towards healing and self-improvement. Through compassion, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence, I strive to make a positive impact on the lives of those I serve.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: My strong suit is providing personalized, holistic Psychiatric care. With my expertise in thorough testing, tailored evaluations, and individualized medication guidance, I can create focused treatment plans. My supportive therapy style and commitment to understanding each patient's unique circumstances position me as a great match for those seeking a psychologist who will partner with them to address challenges and improve well-being.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I possess extensive experience in the diagnosis and treatment of ADHD. My knowledge of this complex condition enables me to create personalized treatment plans that address the unique needs of each individual. I understand the impact of ADHD on daily life and relationships, and am skilled in medication management and behavioral therapies to improve focus, impulse control, and overall functioning.

specialities.name: Aging Concerns
specialities.description: I hold a special interest in providing psychiatric care to the aging population, particularly those affected by Alzheimer's disease and other dementias. My experience has equipped me with the knowledge to address the complex mental health needs that often accompany aging and neurocognitive disorders. I am dedicated to creating individualized treatment plans that alleviate symptoms, improve quality of life, and support both patients and their caregivers through this challenging journey.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I specialize in providing compassionate psychiatric care to individuals with ASD. My personal experience, combined with extensive professional training, gives me a unique understanding of the complex needs of this population. I am dedicated to creating individualized treatment plans that address co-occurring mental health conditions, while considering the distinct challenges and strengths of those with ASD.

name: Bea Hurston
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: M.A. in Professional Mental Health Counseling
intro: Focus: Complex & Relational Trauma, Queer/Trans Issues, Sex & Pleasure, Shame, Religious Trauma, Relationships, Psychedelic Integration
ideal_client: Many of us didn't get the love, support, or connection that we deserved from our families or communities growing up. Because we're resilient, we developed creative strategies for getting our needs met (ex. people-pleasing, perfectionism, numbing-out, withdrawing, overanalyzing, rebelling, lying, etc.). And these strategies worked for a while! They helped us get through complicated childhoods. But as we get older, many of us begin to notice a toll on our minds, our bodies, and our relationships.

approaches.My Background and Approach: As a queer kid who grew up in a fundamentalist community in Mississippi, my journey has been long and hard. But it's also given me the ability to connect deeply with others, both in their pain and in their longing for healing, pleasure, and joy. Using a blend of parts work, self-compassion, and the collective knowledge I’ve gained from the many healers who have helped me, I will help you learn to see yourself more clearly and to navigate your life more peacefully. It's my honor to help my clients find their way to the life of freedom, joy, and intimacy that we all crave.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe we all have the capacity to not only weather the storms our lives bring us, but also to create deeper meaning and connection in our lives because of our unique storms. I see the work I do with my clients as being intimately connected to social and global justice because I believe that in healing our relationships with ourselves, we begin to heal the world.

name: Christopher Creaturo
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Powerful tools for healing trauma, building connection, and meeting your best self.
ideal_client: Now accepting new clients without wait list. Do you feel stuck in the past, weighed down by shame, struggling to be fully seen in your relationships, or just searching for deep meaning in life? Reach out to explore if embarking on a therapy relationship together can help you, and if sought after tools like EMDR, Internal Family Systems, and Mentalization Based Therapy (among others) will jumpstart a process of becoming your best and most free self.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I specialize in techniques of EMDR for trauma, Internal Family Systems for meeting and healing our exiled parts, Mentalization Based Therapy for Borderline Personality Disorder, Jungian techniques such as dreamwork, and Attachment-informed strategies to improve relationships. These techniques and perspectives compliment a therapy relationship built on deep trust, which can be inherently healing to the patterns of our life and our deep sense of being valid and whole in the world.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: When someone sees the best in us it's easier to see that for ourselves. Therapy at it's best can hold up a healing mirror to ourselves and our lives. In therapy, I work hard to honor the best possibilities of you and support you on a road of healing. Reach out by email with a short description of what you're seeking, and I'll get back to you promptly!

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Trained by the EMDR Institute for trauma treatment (including over telehealth). A very powerful and evidence-based treatment for resolving traumas big and small.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: IFS is a lens to view therapy where one's internal conflicts are made explicit as sub-personalities and engaged with from a place of love and fairness (titled Self, in the theory). This approach can make sense of longstanding patterns of behavior, resolve feeling "stuck" in various places in life, and let one heal and move forward with a new sense of wholeness.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Mentalization Based Therapy derived from Attachment Theory. Person-Centered work to establish model of the secure relationship in therapy and allow for Attachment style repair.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: EMDR-trained in interventions for trauma treatment by the EMDR Institute.

specialities.name: Personality Disorders
specialities.description: Supervision in Mentalization Based Treatment for Borderline Personality Disorder.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Supervision in techniques for anxiety abatement, exposure therapy, particularly for Phobias.

specialities.name: Panic
specialities.description: Supervision in techniques for anxiety abatement, exposure therapy, particularly for Phobias.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Supervision in issues related to healthy spiritual relationship and exploration therein.

name: Gabriella Losada
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Collaborating to find meaningful ways to strengthen the mind/body connection and move through grief.
ideal_client: My clients are interested in navigating uncomfortable emotions and connecting with their bodies in the process. Their concerns fall into three (often overlapping) categories: 1) a lack of mind/body connection due to dissociation in the form of depersonalization or derealization (DPDR) 2) grieving a death, a romantic or platonic breakup, or a loss of self 3) sex and pleasure (or lack thereof) and looking for new ways to connect with themselves and others

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Your process is important and I don’t believe in changing or taking away coping mechanisms that have allowed you to survive until this point. Instead, the idea is to give you new or different options to sift through complicated situations or feelings and help you evaluate what you feel is no longer serving you. Talking can be a great way to process but sometimes words aren't enough. During sessions, I use a mix of talk therapy, experiential and somatic techniques. Experientially, we might do some writing, make art, use music, or create a tangible coping tool you can use. Somatically, this might look like doing body scans, grounding exercises, small physical movement, guided visualizations, or just pausing and noticing what your body is doing and how it’s feeling. All of my work is rooted in trauma-informed care and intersectional feminist theory to create a collaborative environment where your "no" is honored and where we acknowledge the ways oppressive systems hinder healing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Above all else, I believe in liberation for all marginalized groups. I believe in active mutual aid, radical collective care, and harm reduction. The personal and political are impossible to disentangle and what is happening globally, nationally, and locally often shows up in the therapy room. I hope to create an environment that embodies intersectionality, sex positivity, gender-affirming care, disability justice, and anti-racism. However, I fully acknowledge that this is an ongoing, imperfect process that I have to actively work on. I hold a lot of privileged identities (white, cisgender, thin, formally educated, US citizen) and some largely invisible marginalized identities (Latina, woman, living with chronic illness/pain, queer, neurodivergent). It’s important to me that I understand the impact my privilege has and how that shows up in and out of the therapy room. I always welcome conversations about how our differing or similar identities impact your process.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: Experiential therapy involves bringing creative elements or activities into session that take us beyond just staring at each other and talking. Sometimes this means writing, making art, using music, or creating a tangible coping tool to process things in a different way. Creativity can be helpful in moving through grief, trauma, and dissociation, especially when verbal processing feels difficult.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Our bodies hold so much information that we aren't always (or can't be) attuned to. In session somatic work might look like doing body scans, grounding exercises, small physical movement, guided visualizations, or just pausing and noticing what your body is doing and how it’s feeling. Sometimes with neurodivergence, chronic pain, or trauma our bodies aren’t always a comfortable or accessible place to be and if that is a concern, we can collaborate to find a component that works for you.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: The word feminist can be loaded depending on your identities. To me, feminist therapy is intersectional and includes looking at layers of privilege and oppression. Feminist theory as a therapeutic lens involves collaboration, balancing power dynamics in the traditional client/therapist relationship, and talking about identities and systems and how they impact your well-being.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: My personal experience with grief and loss led me to volunteer at the Dougy Center where I spent time with teens whose parents or siblings died. After two years of helping facilitate grief groups there, I began seeing clients one-on-one who came in with various concerns but each of them had experience with grief or loss that impacted them deeply.

specialities.name: Dissociative Disorder (DD)
specialities.description: Please note that I specifically work with depersonalization and/or derealization (DPDR) and that I do NOT have experience working with Dissociative Identity Disorder (formerly, Multiple Personality Disorder). My knowledge of dissociative disorders includes personal experience, direct client work with people experiencing dissociation, and trainings such as "Treating Trauma" with Bessel van der Kolk and Pat Ogden

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: Burnout and compassion fatigue go hand-in-hand and I love collaborating with clients who are experiencing burnout from caregiving or being in a helping profession. We can work toward restoring (or creating from scratch) a more balanced approach to being present in all aspects of your life.

name: Saren Craig
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm a queer and transgender identified counselor and social justice advocate based in Portland Oregon. See my website for full details.
ideal_client: I am passionate about social justice advocacy and prioritize the experiences of LGBTQ+ and BIPOC communities when addressing mental health. I provide letters of support for gender-affirming surgeries and strive to make scheduling a consultation simple—just send a Google Meet invite using the calendar on my website. The most rewarding part of my work is helping people discover their own happiness and watching them grow more confident in who they are.

approaches.My Background and Approach: With experience in diverse settings such as inpatient psychiatric hospitals, community mental health, case management, and supported housing, I have gained valuable skills and resources. I understand that external systems often contribute to internal struggles and aim to empower clients by acknowledging the power dynamics in the counseling relationship. I focus on the parts of ourselves that may not have received the affirmation needed along our journey. By offering these younger parts compassion and understanding, healing can occur. I am deeply committed to social justice and continually seek ways to engage in advocacy. I believe that reducing oppression through systemic change and increased awareness fosters healthier, more inclusive communities.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I'm involved in advocacy and activism for the LGBTQ+ Community and support Black Lives Matter. I believe in treating each person with warmth, dignity and respect, while upholding the professional boundaries of the counseling relationship. I work from a broad theoretical background and approach care with a systemic lens. I aim to empower clients, and I understand that each individual has their own pace and path in the growth process. The Portland Metro area rests on traditional village sites of the Multnomah, Wasco, Cowlitz, Kathlamet, Clackamas, Bands of Chinook, Tualatin, Kalapuya, Molalla, and many other tribes who made their homes along the Columbia River. I also acknowledge the systemic policies of genocide, relocation, and assimilation that still impact many Indigenous/Native American families today. I respect the work of Indigenous leaders and families, and pledge to make ongoing efforts recognize their knowledge, creativity, and resilience.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: As an LGBTQ+ affirming provider, I believe everyone deserves the autonomy to make choices about their body and how they experience the world. I provide a safe, supportive space where your gender identity is respected and valued. For those seeking gender-affirming care, I write letters of support to help you access the medical care you need. My goal is to empower you in your journey and ensure you feel seen, heard, and affirmed.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Whether you're coming out to family, navigating relationships, or seeking clarity in your identity, I'm here to support you every step of the way. Coming out can be a challenging and emotional experience, but with the right guidance and encouragement, you can feel empowered and accepted for who you truly are. I provide a safe, affirming space to explore LGBTQ+ issues, helping you build confidence and strengthen your relationships as you embrace your authentic self.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Everyone experiences anxiety, but at times it can feel overwhelming. I provide a supportive space and offer practical coping strategies like breathing exercises, progressive muscle relaxation, and other personalized approaches to help manage anxiety in the moment. My goal is to equip you with tools that reduce anxiety’s impact and help you regain control. You don’t have to face it alone—support is here when you need it most.

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: I offer compassionate support for individuals navigating the complexities of divorce. This life transition can be incredibly challenging, often involving the rupture of relationships, triggering anxiety, and stirring up intense emotions about one's identity and future. In some cases, both parties may agree that divorce is the best path forward and separate amicably. Whether the process is contentious or peaceful, divorce remains a stressful and emotionally charged experience. My goal is to help

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I am here to support and encourage your personal growth as you pursue your goals and dreams. Together, we will clarify your objectives and create a plan to achieve what you truly want. I provide both emotional support and practical resources to help you overcome challenges and stay on track. Throughout this journey, we’ll celebrate your successes, no matter how big or small, as you continue to grow and reach your full potential.

name: Megan Campbell
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I center my work collaboratively with individuals, partners, and other forms of relationships navigating the human journey.
ideal_client: In our work together, I view YOU as the expert of your own life, experience, and self. I believe we all hold "the answer(s)" we need most, but we aren't always taught how to get there or how to tune into ourselves. I view our time together and the nature of therapy as an opportunity to explore and "be with" yourself in deeper and new ways. I believe the exploration of self is inextricably interwoven with the unfolding of our life. Are you ready to explore yourself deeper?

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe healing and growth can happen in an infinite amount of ways, and I believe therapy can look and feel different for everyone. There is no one size fits all for healing, growth and exploration, and this can feel both daunting and liberating. We are often born into a world that defines us before we define ourselves, which can create a sense of disconnection from who we are. Therapy can offer a space where you are given an opportunity to explore and "be with" yourself in new ways as you navigate your human journey in this world and in relationship to others. Exploring ourselves and our journey(s) in life takes courage, bravery, and openness, as we learn how to surrender deeper into our unique being-ness. If we begin by looking within, we may observe our external world shifting as a result, creating more harmony and ease in our lives, as well as in our relationship to ourselves and others.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I utilize a holistic lens in my work, meaning I acknowledge the complexity of what it means to be human as a mind, body, soul, and spirit. In growth, healing, and exploration, I believe it is necessary to tap into all of the layers that encompass who we are, as well as assess our relationship to the world around us. I pull from a variety of perspectives including both Eastern and Western philosophy, earth-based wisdom, experiential and existential-humanistic practices, somatic and mindfulness techniques, systemic and relational frameworks, and everyday life experience as a human being in this world alongside you.

name: Elyse Conterno
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: You can't stop the waves but you can learn to surf. -Jon Kabat-Zinn
ideal_client: At Portland Behavioral Therapy (PBT) I provide therapy for individual adults and children ages 10 and older. My specialty is treating anxiety disorders, and obsessive compulsive disorder. I can also help people dealing with situational stressors and life transitions. As a client of PBT, we will work together to help you feel empowered as you increasingly engage in the things that matter to you! Please check out my website linked under "Contact."

approaches.My Approach to Helping: When it comes to engaging in therapy, it is important to know what type of treatment your therapist uses and determine if it is the best fit for you. I utilize concepts and approaches of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT). These behavioral therapies have robust research designating them as “evidence-based treatments,” for anxiety and depressive disorders. Using these theoretical frameworks and related interventions, like mindfulness and Exposure Response Prevention (ERP), I help my clients learn new skills to more effectively overcome mental health challenges and situational stressors. My goal is to support my clients as they re-shape their thinking and behaviors so that they can more consistently engage with life in ways that reflect their values. Therapy will include evaluating problematic avoidances, making plans to challenge unhelpful thinking, and practice new behavioral patterns, and exploring personal values.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As I have settled into my clinical and professional identity, I continue to strive to provide compassionate, culturally responsive evidence-based behavioral therapy. I seek out up-to-date research and training in my commitment to the ethics and principles as a licensed clinical psychologist. This includes additional training and supervision to uphold values of social justice in my personal and professional life. In treatment, I use a trauma-informed approach to consider how systems of inequity and oppression impact those in marginalized groups including BIPOC and LGBTQ+ persons. I seek to create a space where personal and cultural identities are thoughtfully and deliberately brought into the room as an essential consideration in treatment.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: My specialty is treating anxiety disorders including social anxiety disorder, obsessive compulsive disorder, specific phobias, and panic disorder. Treatment includes concepts and approaches of CBT and ACT. I generally utilize Exposure Response Prevention (ERP) as an effective evidenced-based intervention to help my clients increase their tolerance for discomfort as they work towards decreasing their avoidance so they can engage in the things that matter most.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: I am trained in Exposure Response Prevention (ERP), which is considered the gold standard for treating OCD. I integrate the theories of ACT to help clients make the tough and brave choice to challenge their fears and expand their world.

name: Jessica Butler
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: *currently accepting individuals* I am passionate about supporting your sex and relationship needs.
ideal_client: You may be feeling disconnected, misunderstood and unsatisfied. You really want to make things work, but you’re feeling stuck and confused. You want to better understand your partner, and you want your partner to better understand you. You’re ready to do the work, you just need some extra support.

approaches.What I Specialize In: When I work with couples and relationships, it is important to me that we create a space where you can show up fully and authentically. I want to support you both in having healthy conflict, feeling like your partner really gets you, working through a break in trust or jealousy, and in having a fulfilling sex life. When I work with individuals, I am passionate about supporting you in navigating the often chaotic world of dating, understanding and advocating for your needs, and cultivating an empowering relationship with your sexuality. I believe that everyone has the right to live their happiest life, and it is my goal to assist you on this journey.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that every person has a unique story, and because of this, unique needs. There is not one correct way to be, and I strive to create a space where you feel safe to be your most authentic self. Whether you are monogamous or poly, kinky or vanilla, straight or queer, I am affirming and celebratory of your story. I look forward to discovering with you, your strength, your resilience, and your capacity to heal and grow.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: The goal of attachment theory is having kindness and compassion for yourself and others, with the acknowledgment that every interaction is a new chance to build connection or repair a hurt one. Part of how we do this is learning to communicate and advocate for our emotional needs to be met in a safe way.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Relational therapy acknowledges that it's not only the things within ourselves causing frustrations, but the presence of others in our lives (friends, family, romantic partner etc.) create an impact as well. Part of how we can work on your relationships is setting/maintaining boundaries and speaking to your needs within relationships.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: Sex can be confusing and society hasn't given us the tools to talk about it. You deserve to have a sex life that feels fulfilling and empowering. You may need support in asking for what you need or guidance in finding pleasure again.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: You're both really motivated to make your relationship stronger and healthier. You need support in handling conflict and understanding one another. Many of us don't have good examples of how we'd like to relate to our partner and, with help, it's possible to build the relationship you deserve.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: You want to be your best self and feel confident in who you are. You are ready to prioritize yourself by setting/maintaining boundaries and communicating your needs to others. One of the ways we can do this is through identifying and embracing emotions, which can create lasting change.

name: Jessica Wynant
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Jess (she/her) and I am so glad that you are here. In my work as a therapist, I aim to provide a safe and inclusive space for all.
ideal_client: I utilize narrative therapy to assist clients in discovering how past and present experiences have shaped the story of their lives. I am a HAES-aligned practitioner with years of experience in working with individuals struggling with eating disorders. In my practice, I also work with couples wanting to strengthen and work on their relationship. I am also a member of the LGBTQ+ community and strongly believe in being an ally and advocate for this community and with these clients.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I have years of experience in working with folks struggling with disordered eating. Whether you are in recovery for an eating disorder or want to improve your relationship with food and your body, I am here to walk alongside you in this journey. I practice from a Health At Every Size (HAES) approach and believe that we are all deserving of food and body freedom. I help clients identify and break down harmful patterns with food and exercise that lead to undue stress, chronic dieting, and disordered eating. I also have experience working with couples and families. Our relationships are often the most rich and at times challenging aspects of our lives. All couples and families experience times of friction and disconnection and I am here to help. Whether you need guidance in navigating a difficult decision, need help reconnecting, or are simply wanting to strengthen your communication, we can work together to achieve your goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In my work as a therapist, I aim to provide a safe and inclusive space for all and I believe deeply that we are wildly capable of healing. As someone who experienced the transformative work of therapy in my college years, I instantly became fascinated with mental health and helping others achieve healing in their own lives. I am constantly in awe of the resiliency of the human spirit and feel deeply grateful for the work I get to do. When I'm not in the office, I love cooking and spending time with my wife and our pup. I also love exploring the beauty of the Pacific Northwest and watching lots of women's soccer.

name: Ashleigh Zoerb
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a licensed therapist providing compassionate and effective therapy to clients in the states of Washington and Oregon.
ideal_client: Do you find yourself constantly overwhelmed, anxious, depressed, and/or numb? Do you feel stuck and unable to create the changes you desire in your life? Maybe you feel disconnected from your relationships and completely alone. I know how scary and hopeless this can feel; I am here to help you navigate these feelings and find another way, a way which gives you greater peace in your life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from an attachment and somatic based perspective meaning I look at the relational experiences you've had over your life and how these have translated into survival strategies which your body continues to hold onto today. Together we will untangle these, learn to tune into the wisdom of your body, and begin to learn new ways of living which allow you to thrive instead of simply survive. I will help you to re-gain a sense of safety and security within yourself and in your relationships giving you the ability to be more resilient.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Life is difficult to say the least, and often gives us experiences which leave us hurting. I believe we are all doing our very best in any given moment and that change is possible even when it seems impossible. I believe every person matters and every aspect of what makes each person who they are, matters. Having safe, healthy, and supportive relationships in our lives, makes navigating the greatest challenges, more bearable. And I believe dogs to be some of the greatest healers here on Earth.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I use evidence-based practices to treat PTSD including Lifespan Integration and Somatic Experiencing.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I use several evidence-based practices to treat Anxiety including ACT, Lifespan Integration, Somatic Experiencing, and mindfulness based therapy.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I work with couples using Gottman's method, EFT, and attachment-based therapy.

name: Joaquin Lopez
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Evaluating our symptoms is a bridge to healing. Symptoms direct us toward the source of our suffering in order to find solace.
ideal_client: Human beings adapt to life. Humans beings adopt behaviors to avoid conflict, to fight stressors, or to suppress difficult emotions. Over time, the behaviors cause disease or distress. Behavioral adaptations modify the personality. Behavior tells the story the body holds. The client explores their story in counseling, restoring a soulful well-being. I work with clients who are ready to delve into what lies beneath the surface to externalize what longs to be seen.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our bodies have an inherent ability to heal themselves. Our minds do, too. All clients can tap into their own healing, and with counsel, cultivate their strengths and personhood. Counseling provides a time to understand our state of mind, affect, or mood. Counseling offers a time to be seen and listened to with undivided attention, I offer compassion and listen to understand. I bring my whole being and imagination into the work to offer an authentic connection to create a working relationship based on trust, openness, and possibility. I incorporate tools garnered from psychodynamic approaches, humanistic/existential psychology, motivational interviewing, and CBT. I believe reflecting on life’s past and present relationships offer insight to help us navigate our current and future relationships, experiences, and self. Together we can help you achieve your goals, make new choices to create new experiences that ultimately forge a new understanding and a more satisfying, fulfilling life.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Pain, stress, and trauma can cause restlessness, sleepless nights, loss of pleasure, difficulty concentrating, low self-esteem, and the sense of not being fully present. The body expresses these symptoms accompanied by feelings of anger, guilt, anxiety, and shame. These feelings separate us from ourselves and from the people we love. These feelings prevent us from forming loving relationships and hinder our ability to enjoy life. In counseling, the client and the counselor enter a mindful and healing professional relationship. This connection is cultivated through the exploration of the client's presenting concerns, feelings, and mental disposition. The counselor listens with a clinical understanding while offering insight, therapeutic awareness, and tools for personal growth. The client works with honesty, vulnerability, and openness. A desire to change, self-awareness, and regular reflection by the client generate an environment for personal healing and growth.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: A Jungian orientation offers a warm, creative, and inviting space for the exploration of personal stories, dreams, and myths. The counselor and the client observe aspects of personality, patterns of behavior, the use of language, and creative imagination. A soulful approach allows the client to feel and explore their inner world. The client gains emotional insight and develops an understanding of the experience called life. The client identifies their values and forges a new identity.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Using the insight garnered from our personal work, CBT offers the tools to restructure our thought patterns, modify our emotional responses, and create practical solutions to adapt new healthy behaviors and patterns that lead to successful mental health outcomes.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is a debilitating and paralyzing experience of the soul and spirit. Depression lives differently in everyone. I utilize a multifaceted approach that includes soulful explorations, mindfulness, CBT, and unconditional positive regard to work with a client's whole being and life experience.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a symptom of uncertainty, experiencing the unknown, and the inability to quiet the 'noise' that permeates our being. I believe in approaching anxiety with mindfulness, stream of consciousness to reveal what lies beneath the surface, and behavior modification.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: Systems of oppression permeate every moment of our lives. Racism, sexism, and classism are few of the many systems of oppression that have been part of our story whether we are aware of it or not. Understanding how oppression has affected my personal being, I am able to work with clients to create a safe authentic space to honor their whole experience, and see them for who they are.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a Latino gay male in his 40s, my compassion is informed by my survival as an out teenager during the late 80s and 90s during the time of AIDS. LGBTQ issues include self-esteem, code switching, family attachments, feeling safe, forging your own identity, and being seen. I create a loving and safe environment that embraces every aspect of the LBGTQ client.

specialities.name: Immigration/Acculturation
specialities.description: Drawing from my experience and identity as a Mexican American person, I understand the nuanced experience of code switching and managing family and social dynamics that come with being bicultural and bilingual (Spanish/English) in a mainstream dominant culture. Immigration issues create additional barriers that affect familial and social interactions.

name: Gillian Callahan
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm a licensed therapist specializing in PTSD, LGBTQIA+, Psychedelic Integration and Reproductive Trauma.
ideal_client: My clients are people who have decided that they want to feel different, that the way their lives are currently operating isn't how they want it to be. This might be due to unhealed trauma, shame, anxiety, depression or anything that makes us not feel okay. The way we cope with difficult things as we grow up works, for a given value of "work"; but eventually the costs of those coping strategies begin to outweigh the benefits and they stop working. That's when folks come to therapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work is largely influenced by our constantly evolving understanding of neurobiology and central nervous system functioning. I'm also currently working toward certifications in psychedelic assisted therapy modalities. Trauma triggers, anxiety and anger are elevated physical responses that can be met and addressed in the body, where they're happening, so that we can find other ways to think and act on those difficult emotions. Language is a vital way in which we make sense of our experience, but when language is inaccessible ("I don't know how to talk about this") or played out ("I've talked about my trauma a million times but it never seems to get better"), the body gives us information and wisdom about what we need to heal. I utilize curiosity, empathy, humor and compassion to help people feel comfortable and safe, and then we listen to what the body has to tell us.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a proud member of the queer community. I am passionate about racial justice and understand that my privilege and blind spots as a white cis woman require constant checking, learning and humility. I believe that patriarchy is harmful to all genders and that healing the wounds of toxic masculinity is a path to true connection and happiness for all genders. I often bring my dogs to work with me to help people relax and regulate when they're struggling in session, and also because dogs are awesome. I'm an avid learner of history and often find myself bringing the lessons of the past into my work. I'm also a big giant sci-fi and fantasy nerd and have been known to use allegories from early 80's young adult fantasy movies, Tolkien, Dr. Who and Star Trek, among other things, as teaching tools.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: As a survivor myself, I've spent a lifetime studying the effects of trauma on the body and the brain. I specialize in helping people understand the ways trauma impacts their lives, their relationships and their futures. Using somatic mindfulness, psychoeducation and empathetic support I teach people how to work with, rather than against, their trauma affected brains and find true safety and happiness.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Our sexuality and gender can be the source of our greatest joy and our greatest pain. I want to help people accept themselves, find connection with supportive community and celebrate the magic of queerness in all its gorgeous forms.

specialities.name: Infertility
specialities.description: Infertility and pregnancy loss are just two of many reproductive experiences that don’t follow the socially supported narrative. For folks not represented in that narrative the pain is isolating and demoralizing. The het/cis-normative imperative that says our bodies don’t matter unless we reproduce, in biologically prescribed gender-role-confirming ways, reduces our value to lines on a pregnancy test. I work to provide the help I needed and couldn't find when I was going through it myself.

name: Cheryl Lane
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I specialize in helping individuals whose lives are negatively impacted by chronic pain, anxiety, depression, and other life challenges.
ideal_client: Are you struggling with chronic pain and feeling hopeless or afraid that it will never go away, that this is how your life will always be, so you’ll just have to learn to live with it? Is your chronic pain, anxiety, or distress keeping you from doing things you once loved, or from living your life to the fullest? Have you seen countless doctors and tried every treatment recommended, yet you’re still not getting better? If this sounds like you, I’m confident I can help you get your life back!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I’m certified in Pain Reprocessing Therapy (PRT). It’s designed to treat chronic psychophysiologic pain, and has been found to be very effective for a wide range of common chronic pain syndromes and other chronic ailments (e.g., dizziness, IBS, and migraines). Most chronic pain is due to the brain’s faulty interpretation of signals from the body. We call this “mindbody” or “neuroplastic” pain. That doesn’t mean your pain isn’t real – ALL pain is real! I combine PRT and EAET (Emotional Awareness and Expression Therapy), along with other therapeutic approaches to help you learn a new way of responding to pain signals. You and I will work together to help you “retrain your brain” in a way that can significantly reduce your symptoms, and in many cases, completely eliminate them. It’s not uncommon for individuals with chronic pain to also struggle with anxiety, depression, obsessive / compulsive tendencies, and / or unresolved trauma. I can help you with those as well!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that everyone has the capacity for positive change, and that whatever challenges or concerns have brought you to therapy do not define you. I strive to create a therapeutic space that feels both emotionally and psychologically safe for every client I see, and treat each individual with unconditional positive regard - accepting you for who you are without judgement. These are necessary elements for healing to take place. My approach to therapy is based on establishing a relationship of mutual trust, authenticity, and respect with each client. I believe each individual embodies a unique combination of life experiences, beliefs, values, challenges, and personality traits. With this in mind, I don’t believe in a one-size-fits-all approach to therapy; rather, I will tailor my work with you based on your individual needs and treatment goals.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: As mentioned previously, I specialize in treating chronic pain and other chronic ailments. Some of the most common chronic pain issues we see in our practice include chronic back pain, migraines, fibromyalgia, chronic dizziness (PPPD), CRPS (chronic regional pain syndrome), TMJ, repetitive strain injury, and chronic tendonitis, to name just a few. If an injury has healed but is still causing pain, or the issue isn't responding to treatment as expected, it may be a mindbody issue.

name: Anjulie Semenchuk
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a LCSW who specializes in Anxiety and Depression. I believe that with support and trying new things you can heal.
ideal_client: Anxiety and Depression make individuals feel isolated, misunderstood, or hopeless. As a clinician, I focus on creating a safe, nonjudgmental space where clients feel heard and validated in their experiences. I also focus on giving you the skills you need to live a more fulfilling life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe we are all moving through life learning new things and that from time to time we are faced with challenges that may require extra assistance. I am happy to partner with you to find the tools you need to deal with these challenges effectively. To learn more about me visit my website alpiniacounseling.com I have a uniquely logical and practical method toward treatment that allows me the capacity to connect with individuals who process information more cerebrally. I believe this balance of being able to meet clients in both an emotional and cognitive space has specifically attuned me to working with populations who are more analytically minded.

name: Taunya Gesner
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: If you are looking for someone who is compassionate, adventurous, intelligent and creative, I might be the right therapist for you.
ideal_client: I work well with a wide variety of clients, especially those who are struggling with social connections (AuADHD). I tend to focus on looking at how your past experiences influence and shape your emotions and behaviors today, and exploring techniques and understanding to shift to a direction you prefer. I particularly enjoy working with LGBTQ+ and am a sex and body positive practioner. If you are a spiritual person, I enjoy incorporating those values into your treatment.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I worked in the corporate world for many years in a wide variety of positions that give me a lot of insight into the challenges of being in that environment. Additionally - I have adventured and explored the world living and visiting, through military service and sailing the ocean.
