I shifted careers into counseling and finally feel like I found the right career for me, because I love connecting with people and understanding your stories. I am very respectful of your needs (you are the expert on your life), while also pointing out perspectives and patterns you may not have previously noticed. My life has been an adventure and I've had to overcome many hardships. I have a wide variety of experiences, (including physical and mental health challenges) that often give me unique insight and understanding. I'm also very much a nerd at heart - being into gaming, story crafting, art, cooking, homesteading and family.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I'm good at asking questions, looking for and noticing patterns that you might not have seen. I'm a very good listener, giving you the space to say what you need. I'm very patient and understanding and compassionate. But the truth is - these skills are probably true of most counselors - and I often find myself wondering what makes me different from anyone else? I dunno - I'm a strange combination of nerdy awkard, intelligent, warm, compassionate, helpful, intellectual - always striving to improve my own life and help you find ways to improve yours. I've studied a variety of techniques that I know can be helpful in the right moment. How much time you want to spend utilizing those skills versus talk therapy, is up to you, as I also believe in client led sessions. Also - I'm knowledgable in a wide variety of cultures because of my extensive travels, studies and work with exchange students. If all this sounds appealing/interesting, we are probably a good fit!

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I have taken trainings 1 and 2 and am working on certification. My experience with EMDR has been overwhelmingly positive and I have been able to utilize this technique in a variety of ways to reach clients who had been at a high level of distress prior to our work together.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I am formally trained in IFS through their program. Let's heal your wounded inner parts.

specialities.name: Anger Management Therapy
specialities.description: I did training through Allies in Change who has a program on anger management and domestic violence treatment. I combine this education with my EMDR/trauma focused background to combine a therapy which helps relieve emotional triggers as well as teach better communication and collaboration skills.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I have studied and incorporated DBT into my practice as it can be extremely helpful to have definite behavioral changes to help improve areas where skills may be lacking. DBT focuses on four fundamental skill areas which are Mindfulness, Interpersonal Effectiveness, Emotional Regulation and Distress Tolerance. I am currently running a skills training group and am happy to incorporate these skills there and/or in individual counseling sessions.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: I have trained in working with offenders of domestic violence, so I have a better understanding of what abuse looks like, how it's expressed and what causes it. This enables me to better understand how you might be experiencing abuse and to clear up confusion you may be experiencing. This understanding combined with trauma relief offers effective treatment.

specialities.name: Anger Management
specialities.description: Anger management is a combination of emotional reactivity which can be reduced with trauma processing, combined with psychoeducation on controlling and abusive behaviors. It's a matter of changing from a competitive to a collaborative perspective.

specialities.name: Panic
specialities.description: Panic is an extreme expression of anxiety - and while you may find your heart racing and limbs tingling and numb, it is your body's response to feeling extremely threatened. By processing the memories that bring you to this state, we are able to bring your body to a place where it no longer feels threatened.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety comes when your body is not feeling safe, which is usually due to an accumulation of unprocessed memories. By identifying the emotions surrounding your anxiety and then processing them until they are no longer triggering - relief of anxiety is the automatic side effect.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression comes from feeling stuck and tired and angry at where you are in life. Being able to relieve the emotions around what brought you to this state, will help you to find your joy in living once again. I can do this with EMDR - it's an awesome technique that helps remove the emotional angst from your memories.

name: Wyatt Okeefe
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm a queer & transmasc with 20yrs experience specializing in working with depression, anxiety, trauma & queer and gender identity issues
ideal_client: .My clients are often navigating significant life changes and transitions that prompt big questions about their identity and purpose. They may be adjusting to singlehood after a breakup, changing careers, graduating from student to professional life, planning for retirement, undergoing gender transition, relocating, or coming out. On top of these major life events, they may also be grappling with mental health challenges like depression, anxiety, or unresolved trauma. I'm here to support you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As an experienced therapist my primary goal is to empower my clients to live their most authentic and fulfilling lives. I employ an existential approach, emphasizing the importance of finding meaning in one's daily activities and relationships as essential to thriving. Through our collaborative work, I guide my clients in exploring their identities, values, and beliefs about themselves and others, and how these factors shape their interactions and satisfaction with life. My role is to provide the tools and support my clients need to assert themselves with confidence and self-awareness. By delving into these core aspects of their personal experience, my clients are able to develop a stronger sense of self-understanding and agency, ultimately enabling them to live more purposeful and enriching lives.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I understand the impact of transphobia, homophobia and misogyny on our mental health and the challenges we face as a community. I know the anxiety and fear we face is real and I also know we can persevere and still experience the joy of living authentically in spite of it. I strive to create a safe, validating space where clients can explore their thoughts, feelings, and personal journeys with authenticity. Through an integrative, client-centered approach, I collaboratively develop tailored strategies for managing concerns like depression, anxiety, and trauma. This may involve evidence-based therapies combined with holistic, identity-affirming practices. Underlying my work is a commitment to empowering LGBTQIA+ clients to live their most authentic, fulfilling lives. I believe self-acceptance and a strong sense of identity are essential to thriving, and I help guide clients in cultivating these qualities. Reach out, I'm here to support you.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: My goal for therapy is to assist clients to explore themselves, their experiences and their responses, their purpose in life and how to move toward their goals. I encourage my clients to exercise their free will to live a courageously authentic life. An Existential approach can help with anxiety,, depression and feeling stuck by helping clients deeply explore their deepest selves with love and compassion.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Exploration of attachment styles can help couples find creative ways to better meet their needs and those of their partner(s) Understanding one's attachment style can help alleviate unhealthy relational habits that destroy relationships. romantic and non-romantic interpersonal issues can be explored and addressed to alleviate anxiety and distress.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Using this modality can help address how ones thoughts effect one's emotions. I help clients explore and reshape their thoughts to reduce emotional distress. CBT offers tools one can use to to create behavioral change.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Somatic therapy explores how the body expresses deeply painful experiences, applying mind-body healing to aid with trauma recovery. I believe our bodies inform us in many ways and help clients explore what the body knows to better understand and heal from trauma.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I am transmasc, non-binary and go by he/they pronouns. I provide ongoing psychotherapy and write letters of support for gender affirming care.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I use a variety of approaches to address anxiety including Rational Emotive Behavioral Therapy (REBT) CBT, existentialism and Internal parts work or IFS to assist in addressing anxiety.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I use a variety of approaches to address depression including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) aspects of Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT) and talk therapy.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I am a lifelong member of the LGBTQIA+ community and have been a therapist working within the community for over 20 years.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma and PTSD are common issues faced by the queer community. I have over 20 years experience working with trauma, PTSD, Dissociation and helping clients make sense of their experiences and heal from them to live their most empowered healthy lives. .

name: DENNIS LAURENTS
title: Clinical Psychologist
credentials: Ph.D. Clinical Psychologist, Licensed Oregon, California
intro: Please see my profile at: Dennis Laurents, Ph.D. on line

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: I have successfully assisted many individuals who seeking relationships who are experiencing difficulty, couples who are currently experiencing difficulties in their current relationship, including couples, parent-child, sibling relationships and people dealing with recent and past traumas and traumatic relationships I am aware that Self-esteem is an Inside job, and that we learn is a developmental milestone progression and at a very important time, is ultimately an inside job, as in SELF-esteem

name: Genevieve Payne, LMFT
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Hi! I'm Genevieve. I promote a deep level of healing through relational and psychodynamic therapy, IFS, and EMDR including EMDR intensives.
ideal_client: I'm a therapist with a real passion for working with women during difficult transitions such as going to college, experiencing heartbreak, becoming pregnant, learning how to be a parent, perimenopause, separation, divorce. During these times we discover reserves of inner strength that we never knew we had.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I will work with you in a safe and collaborative way to determine your goals for therapy. I'll also invite you to slow down and turn your attention inward, so you can notice thoughts and feelings that emerge and ultimately learn how to make more choices in the moment rather than simply reacting. I'll help you explore patterns of relating to others, without judgment, so you can decide which parts of your identity feel right and which no longer serve you. You will develop new skills that allow you to feel more at peace, safer in your body, and more conscious of your internal thoughts and feelings. With 13 years of EMDR experience, I am now offering 1-3 day EMDR intensives to help you find pathways to healing in a condensed amount of time without the need to commit to weekly or biweekly therapy. Limited space available for weekend intensives, so please inquire about eligibility and scheduling. Let's get started!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been practicing since 2009 and hold a license in Marriage and Family Therapy. I specialize in working with anxiety, depression, major life transitions, trauma, and pregnancy, postpartum and parenting issues. I treat a variety of traumas including acute trauma, childhood or attachment trauma, sexual trauma, and medical trauma.

name: Brave Hope Counseling
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Brave Hope Counseling is Mental Health collective striving to create a safe space full of understanding, pride, and strength for our clients
ideal_client: We are dedicated to working with folx who: Experience less access to care due to their race, sexual orientation or language abilities. Immigrants and Refugees looking for culturally humble and affirming care. Individuals who are looking for representation options within their providers choices. Youth who need experienced and compassionate therapists. Families and Couples looking to find a guide to their healing. ​ Our work together will be an ongoing conversation and collaboration.

approaches.Our Background: Brave Hope Counseling’s mission is to provide accessible mental health care that is representative, affirming and collaborative. We are dedicated to working with folx who experience less access to care due to their race, gender, sexual identity, language, or socio-economic status. We believe that counseling should never be one size fits all and intentionally operate from an anti-oppressive platform. One of our unique strategies is to support social services professionals by providing quality, culturally informative supervision, and a supportive work environment. This strategy ensures counseling services are comprehensive, ethical and appropriate. We’re committed to partnering with our clients and workforce to accomplish our mission by offering unconditional positive regard, honesty and empowering them on their unique journeys. Driving Values Representation Accountability Compassion Honesty Anti-Oppressive Collaboration Advocacy Access to Care Empowerment

name: Andrea Love
title: Somatic Practitioner
intro: I teach you how to heal, overcome generational trauma, and consciously create a relationship with yourself that you love.
ideal_client: I work with women in their mid-40s to early 60s who are financially established and have raised families. Many feel unfulfilled in their relationships, whether divorced, widowed, or in unequal partnerships. Having lived half their lives in pain, they’ve reached a breaking point and crave transformation. These women are ready to embrace their soul’s purpose and live their remaining years with meaning and alignment, stepping into a new paradigm of fulfillment and authenticity.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I’d describe my approach to healing as passionately guiding clients through various life transitions, facilitating personal development, and offering support in processing experiences of anxiety, depression, and trauma. I value being compassionate, direct and having client-centered approach which I believe empowers individuals to overcome challenges and find healing on their path towards mental well-being. When I say I understand your sadness, grief, shame, pain and anger, I do. When I say that I understand how your trauma and experiences have affected your choices and all the relationships in your life, I do. I also know how to find the courage to overcome the unthinkable. My goal is to empower you to feel incredible and live a life you love. I will meet you where you are on your path and help guide you toward authenticity, freedom, and joy. Together, we will gain breakthroughs and clarity in your relationships, career, and health that you can carry with you each day of your life

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I know what it’s like to have your pain be so great, you’ll try anything to make it stop. Growing up, I experienced physical, emotional, and sexual abuse. I am a survivor of rape. I had an abortion at 19 and became a single mother at age 23. I have two DUIs and have also spent time in jail. I’ve navigated anorexia nervosa, addiction, chronic depression, a suicide attempt, and Graves Disease. And that’s just part of my highlight reel… I have lifetime experience with Cluster B Personality Group, and High Conflict Personality Disorder (HCP’s) deriving from my family of origin. I also have extensive professional experience with mental health disorders, as well as how your attachment style impacts your adult relationships. I only share these intimate details with you so you know where I come from and how far I’ve come in this lifetime. This is how I hold the lantern for you—with compassion, humility, honesty, grace and a deep understanding and awareness.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: I come from a background of several types of abuse: physical, emotional, sexual, religious, intellectual, and financial. My lived experience allows me to come from a place of empathy, compassion, understanding and inclusion.

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: In 2021, I filed for divorce, enduring a three-year process that included a three-day trial with 10 witnesses and cost over $300,000 collectively. After the ruling, my ex-husband filed a supersedeas and an appeal with The Appellate Court. Now a year into the process, and with extensions from his second appellate attorney, we've received the opening brief. This appeal will take another three years, potentially overturning the decision and setting a legal precedent that could change the law.

specialities.name: Personality Disorders
specialities.description: I have lifetime experience with Cluster B Personality Group, and High Conflict Personality Disorder (HCP’s) deriving from my family of origin.

name: Izy Leighton
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Compassionate trauma-informed therapy for individuals, relationships, and sexual wellness.
ideal_client: As a therapist, I enjoy working with a wide breadth of the human experience. I love supporting adult individuals and partners with a broad range of concerns, including depression and anxiety, sex and relationship challenges, trauma and attachment wounding, identity exploration, and grief & loss. As a queer and intersex woman, I particularly enjoy working with other members of the LGBTQIA+ community and have intimate understanding of some challenges this community faces.

approaches.My Background: Prior to becoming a therapist, I worked for many years in an inpatient treatment setting for kids and teens struggling with their safety, supporting them with emotion regulation, trauma recovery, and family dynamics issues. I left this position to complete my Master's degree in Marriage, Couples, and Family Therapy at Lewis & Clark Graduate School of Education and Counseling, where I earned an additional specialization in Sex Therapy. Since then I have worked with diverse populations in an array of settings - including a community counseling center, a family medical clinic, and a group practice specializing in couples and sex therapy - before starting my own practice, where I provide compassionate trauma-informed therapy for individuals and relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Though I have valuable experience and knowledge to share with my clients, I pointedly do not identify as an expert and do not claim to have all the answers. I recognize my clients' innate wisdom and seek to honor their agency and intuition throughout the therapeutic process. I approach therapy as an active collaborator, a curious explorer, and a loving witness. I believe it's critical to "zoom out" and consider the contexts in which my clients' concerns occur, exploring the impacts of trauma, attachment, culture, and oppression. My therapeutic style is authentic and warm, though I gently challenge my clients to approach their growing edges and take risks that support their healing. I believe a strong therapeutic relationship is a cornerstone of truly transformative therapy and a key change agent in itself; I continually invest in this relationship to provide my clients with reparative emotional experiences and support them in moving toward secure attachment with themselves and others.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have specialized training and experience working with intimate partnerships of all kinds. I approach relational work primarily through a culturally-responsive application of Emotionally Focused Therapy, which helps partners turn toward one another with vulnerability and authenticity and deepen their emotional bond. I welcome integration of sex therapy within relational work, recognizing sex as an important part of many relationships that can become loaded with complication and challenge.

name: Michelle Perez
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with children, teens, adults and families. Disfruto trabajar con niños, adolescentes, adultos y familias.
ideal_client: My goal is to offer you a safe space where you can find healing and self-discovery. My expertise is working with individuals with issues of depression, anxiety, anger, trauma, parenting, sexuality, and those who are neurodivergent. I am fluent in Spanish and identify as bicultural. I also have trained in several modalities of Play Therapy such as Gestalt, and Sand tray.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Change can be difficult and scary, and I want to support you in finding the tools to bring needed change into your life. I believe in our capacity to transform wounds into wisdom and to cultivate self-awareness. I use a holistic approach that recognizes all aspects of a person. I enjoy working with children, teens, adults and with families. I integrate techniques from Psychoanalytic, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, and mind-body interventions such as mindfulness and breathing work. When working with children I utilize techniques from Play Therapy and Attachment Theory.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: During my free time I enjoy spending time with my family and friends, dancing, traveling and the outdoors.

name: Sarah Fawcett
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I work with adults on issues often related to their childhood and I support adolescents on their complex journey to adulthood.
ideal_client: Sometimes, we just need a little help to touch ground long enough to hear the sound of our own voice, gain insight, and remember what it is that makes us feel truly alive. Therapy can be that grounding help, offering a mirror to see ourselves from a new angle, uncovering unconscious patterns, and seeing all of our parts from a new and accepting perspective. Therapy can uncover the “why” behind our actions or choices that don’t seem to be working for us anymore and help us change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach, drawing from depth psychology and attachment theory, centers around first creating a safe and compassionate space for clients to consider their inner world and uncover unconscious patterns and beliefs. I believe therapy (at its best) is a safe place to repair how we interact with the outer world, i.e., relationship patterns and intimacy issues, as well as a safe place to uncover and repair our relationship with our inner world, i.e., negative self-image, addiction, etc. Therapy is your time; I am here to help guide and reflect and offer you about 50 minutes to touch ground, feel heard, and perhaps, spin a little less. My work with children and adolescents is similar in approach, with the addition of art and play-based therapy, family systems, and developmental theories. As a designer and artist, I love to work with other creatives and incorporate creativity and art-making into sessions with kids as well as adults.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I have always been drawn to understanding what makes people tick. Psychological or otherwise, symptoms are cues for where to look but aren’t the true problem to be solved. Our symptoms (anxiety, depression, etc.) are the outward manifestations of our inner wounds and where the “work” begins. I love helping people uncover their own personal blocks to their path toward happiness and help them feel like the truest version of themselves.

name: Mary Roberts
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Licensed counselor & educator with deep clinical training. Collaborative, integrative, and active—real work, real change, together.
ideal_client: I work with adults, couples, and teens navigating relational trauma, neurodivergence, and identity-related stress. Many of my clients are unique, deep thinkers who feel stuck or overwhelmed and want a collaborative, active space to explore change and transformation. As a supervisor, I specialize in supporting early-career professionals, caregivers, and those managing complex family dynamics. If you're seeking real insight and real tools—with warmth and clarity—I’d be honored to work with you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My clinical approach is collaborative, integrative, and grounded in relational neuroscience, justice, and posttraumatic growth. I draw from psychodynamic, feminist, and systems-informed models, tailoring the work to your unique needs and goals. Sessions are active and insight-driven, with a focus on connection, clarity, and sustainable change. I work best with clients ready to explore patterns, deepen self-trust, and engage in meaningful, values-based transformation.

approaches.Our Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that effective clinical care is rooted in humility, responsiveness, and a deep respect for each client’s lived experience. I value multicultural awareness, acknowledge systemic harm, and approach every person with curiosity rather than assumptions. My work is guided by a commitment to justice, integrity, and relational accountability. I strive to create a space where complexity is welcomed and where healing is tied to both personal and collective liberation. As a supervisor, I'm also very concerned with the state of the profession and take an active role in advocating for issues that affect both our clients and communities, and also the field of Professional Counseling.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: I use Narrative Exposure Therapy (NET) to process chronic trauma or complex trauma. NET is an evidence based, formal approach to integrating and reprocessing trauma that integrates brain science with interpersonal and cultural factors.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: I have extensive training and education experience in the field of abuse recovery. Though I am not personally a survivor of abuse, it runs in my family intergenerationally. In addition, I've served in DV/SA clinical settings, participated on nonprofit boards, and participated in multicontextual legislation for improved recovery.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Neurodivergence runs through my family, and I've witnessed first hand the challenges of trying to fit a square peg in a round hole. Let's work toward multicontextual solutions for these challenges at all levels.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: As a clinical supervisor, issues like burnout, compassion fatigue, and vicarious trauma run pervasive in the lives of clinicians I serve. Often, the solutions to these challenges are systemic. Let's collaborate on a path toward reengagement, connection, and resilience together.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: Issues related to cultural and systemic oppression inform all aspects of my work as a clinician, supervisor, and counselor educator. For me, it's impossible to talk about what's going on for an individual without exploring what's occurring in their systems. Anti-oppression action toward justice is usually multicontextual, and I approach these issues as a learner, collaborator, and advocate.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I provide immersive, exploratory guidance to people in relationships from a judgment-free, compassionate, and hopeful lens.

name: Matthew Boylan
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: Gottman Couples Method, Emotion Focused Therapy, Psychodynamic Intersubjectivity, Equine Assisted Psychotherapy for Trauma
intro: My goal is to help you create positive and thriving relationships with yourself and those important to you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that the most important part of counseling is the relationship. I work from an Intersubjective perspective and integrate Gottman Method, Emotionally Focused Therapy, and Equine Assisted Therapy to create safe and accepting relationships which foster growth and healing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a masters degree in Marriage Couple and Family Counseling from George Fox University. My focus in graduate school was on Couples Therapy, Family Therapy, and Child-Centered Play Therapy. I have specialty in the Gottman Method for Couples Therapy, the Core Values Index for relationships and individual potential, and EAGALA to work with horses in counseling individuals, families, and groups.

name: Lindsey Lundin
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I support clients as they process their experiences and increase their understanding of their emotions, reactions, and relationships.
ideal_client: My work with clients often involves processing harmful experiences throughout life. It can also look like emotional exploration, examining patterns and learning new ways to communicate and exist in relationship to others and to yourself. Clients have shared that through our work together they feel an increased sense of self-awareness as well as feeling empowered to advocate for themselves, communicate their needs, and navigate all relationships in healthier ways.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is very relational as I believe that long-term growth and healing happens within trusting, healthy relationships. My relational lens also means that I see the therapeutic relationship as the catalyst for shifting inner narratives and working towards lasting change. That said, we live in a world where varying systems impact our lives every day depending on our identities and working within a structure that we can't quickly change can be challenging. That is why I believe it is important to acknowledge these systems and how my client's daily lives are impacted by them. It can be difficult to find spaces where we feel safe enough to be vulnerable and examine all our parts with compassion which is the kind of space I work to cultivate. I use an attachment and systems lens, elements of Internal Family Systems, skill development, and interpersonal awareness. If looking for Mentalization-Based Narrative Exposure Therapy (MBNET) for trauma processing, reach out to discuss options.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I'm passionate about helping people feel less stuck as they navigate their journey through healing and growth. In acknowledging my varying identities, I work to examine and discuss how my privileged identities impact and intersect with my client's identities and how we navigate building trust. I deeply value the relationships I build with my clients, knowing that an honest, reflective therapeutic connection can foster lasting growth and change.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I have been trained in and use a systems lens throughout my work which includes social and familial systems as well as larger oppressive systems. Most of our experiences and traumas happen interpersonally which is why I believe that understanding how my clients experience their relationships and inner life is key in building a deep and insightful understanding of what they need on their journey of growth and healing.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Supporting my clients as they build a deeper awareness of themselves & their relational patterns can be an important part of getting past feeling stuck in our lives and relationships.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can take hold of our lives so quickly which is why I work with clients to gain tools for anxiety management as well as exploring the experiences at the origin of their anxieties.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I am passionate about supporting clients in my community as they explore themselves, their experiences and work towards healing.

name: Laura Raynor
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Helping kids, families & couples heal, connect & grow—through play, curiosity, and a trauma-informed, attachment-focused lens.
ideal_client: I love working with kids, families, and couples who are looking for more connection, understanding, and healing. Whether it's a child working through big feelings in the playroom, a couple feeling stuck, or an individual carrying old wounds, I offer a warm, supportive space to explore and grow. Together, we’ll make sense of the hard stuff—with curiosity, compassion, and just the right amount of play.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe healing begins in safe, trusting relationships—with others, and just as importantly, with ourselves. My approach is rooted in a trauma-informed, attachment-focused lens, and includes somatic work to help clients reconnect with the wisdom of their bodies. So much of what we carry lives beyond words, and I gently guide clients to notice what’s happening inside—physically, emotionally, and relationally. For children, the playroom becomes a space where play is their language and healing happens through creativity, movement, and connection. For adults and couples, we explore patterns shaped by past experiences, and how those live on in the body and in relationships. Healing with me is a collaborative, compassionate process. We'll move at a pace that feels right for you, creating a space where you feel safe, supported, and deeply understood—so that real connection and meaningful change can unfold naturally.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe we are all doing the very best we can to find peace, joy, and meaningful connection. Our past experiences can shape us in ways we don’t always see or understand, and healing begins when we feel safe—in our bodies, in our environments, and in our relationships. Each person, each child, has a unique path toward healing. My role is to walk alongside them with compassion, curiosity, and respect for their individual journey. I believe in the power of play as the natural language of children—a way for them to tell their stories, explore emotions, connect with their bodies, and discover their own sense of self and worth. As a mother of three, I deeply understand the beauty and complexity of parenting. I believe we come to know ourselves through our relationships, and the most important of these is the one we have with ourselves. Learning to treat ourselves with kindness and gentleness is one of the most grounding and healing things we can do.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: With 16 years of experience working with children and adolescents, I’m passionate about helping kids feel seen, heard, and understood. In my cozy playroom, children are invited to explore their feelings, express themselves freely, and build resilience through play therapy, somatic tools, and evidence-based approaches like CBT and DBT. I also support adolescents as they navigate the unique challenges of being a teen—helping them find their voice and develop healthy coping skills. I partner closel

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I help children, teens, and adults manage anxiety using a blend of play therapy, DBT, CBT, and somatic techniques. With trauma-informed training, I support clients in understanding how anxiety affects their thoughts, emotions, and bodies. Together, we build practical, personalized tools to foster calm, resilience, and confidence—helping anxiety feel more manageable and less overwhelming.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: I help families move through conflict with greater understanding, compassion, and connection. Using a trauma-informed, attachment-focused approach, I support each family member in feeling heard and valued while working together to shift stuck patterns. Whether it’s parent-child tension, sibling dynamics, or broader communication struggles, I guide families in building healthier relationships rooted in trust, empathy, and shared growth.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: As a mom of three, I know firsthand how beautifully challenging parenting can be. I bring both professional expertise and real-life experience to my work with parents—offering support that’s grounded, non-judgmental, and truly gets how hard (and rewarding) this job can be. Whether you're navigating tantrums, big emotions, or feeling stuck in power struggles, I’m here to help you understand what’s underneath the behavior and build a more connected, peaceful relationship with your child.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships can be both deeply fulfilling and incredibly challenging. I support couples who are feeling disconnected, stuck in painful patterns, or struggling to communicate. With a trauma-informed and attachment-based approach, I help partners better understand themselves and each other, rebuild trust, and create stronger, more compassionate connections. Whether you're navigating conflict, life transitions, or just feeling distant, I offer a safe space to grow together.

name: Kendra Smith
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I use a relational, client-led approach to support grief, anxiety, trauma, life transitions, and relationship concerns.
ideal_client: Do you feel "blocked up" inside or stuck when trying to connect to your emotions? Is it difficult to connect to yourself or others at times? It can be so difficult to work toward embracing our full range of emotional expression or our true experience. I believe in your ability to gain trust in yourself as you learn to integrate your most authentic self into your present day experience.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am trained in Gestalt therapy with a focus on Attachment theory. This means that I use curiosity to approach how you have evolved to survive in and respond to your past and current environments, including your relationships with others. Sometimes, we find that the strategies that were effective in navigating the world in the past don't meet our needs in our present day. I am here to walk alongside you as a support as you experiment with ways to respond more authentically to yourself and others as you go through your life. While my primary position is to let clients lead their own journey, I will from time to time drop in a gentle challenge or question if I see an opportunity for growth. This sounds like a serious task, and it is, but there are lots of moments for humor and levity in the counseling process.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a white, cis woman who is currently able-bodied. I am from the Pacific Northwest. I obtained my graduate degree in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis and Clark's Graduate School in Education and Counseling. I have received training in Gestalt Therapy with an Attachment focus from the Gestalt Therapy Training Center Northwest. These two training backgrounds have given me a place to explore how oppression can show up at various social levels most of us interact with, and attending to those factors is a prominent part of my client work. I strive to be anti-racist, am LGBTQIA+ affirming, neurodiverse affirming, sex positive, and engage in continued training to support my ability to work with people with different identities from my own. I welcome all clients to my practice regardless of their backgrounds, what will determine if we can work together is a goodness of personality fit, and if my training supports your needs.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: I am naturally a curious person who likes to observe the world around me. Gestalt Therapy is a counseling approach that looks at the way people interact with their environment, which includes relationships with others. People creatively adjust to survive, and as we develop, not all strategies are effective for us. It promotes curiosity and gives clients room to experiment with ways they might shift their responses to the world around them to better represent themselves and get their needs met.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: The way we were taught to relate to the primary people who provided us care when we were babies and children can shape how we act in relationships as adults. Establishing an understanding of how we connect with others in different contexts can help improve communication skills and expression of intention, which can improve the quality of relationships. I use individual family of origin history to help guide clients as they work on understanding their participation in relationships.

specialities.name: Psychological Testing and Evaluation
specialities.description: I am trained in Level One Autism Assessment for Adults. The ongoing training I am participating in is neurodiverse affirming, and takes into account intersectionality of identities. This type of assessment is appropriate for people over 18 who are looking for language for their experience, as well as referrals and resources for ways to help their environment be more supportive of them.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Loss of someone in our lives can have a ripple effect of change and bring up a variety of emotions. I believe that grief and loss can extend to changes that life transitions can bring. I have several years of experience facilitating bereavement support groups, as well as personal experiences with loss. I have learned that grief is complex, and the processing of it is not linear. Tears and laughter can coexist in the grief processing space. I am honored to hold both, and everything in between.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can be viewed from an evolutionary lens as response that warns us of danger. In present day, sometimes anxiety is giving us accurate cues, and other times it is overstating the level of concern. Learning to assess the appropriate level of concern can be complex. I use an approach that highlights the awareness we experience when we have contact with our environment. Through curiosity, we can work together to establish a way of interacting with the world that feels more manageable.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: We all have experiences we carry with us that shape the way we interact with the world around us. Sometimes, those experiences weigh heavier and impact us more deeply. Using trauma-informed care, I view all clients as people impacted by their individual history, as well as social-cultural and intergenerational histories. I incorporate that awareness into my work with clients as they examine how past strategies for staying safe and getting needs met either are or are not currently serving them.

name: Teresa Zahariades, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Come home to yourself, awaken within to move your life in congruence with what matters to you.
ideal_client: The time to begin is now. You are already in the transformation process as you are searching for the right fit for yourself, determining what is working for you in your life and what needs changing. Together in therapy we examine patterns you would like to address, build compassion for your history of how these originated, explore new practices to return back to your Inner Resourced Self to grow more resilient. I specialize in support for those experiencing anxiety, trauma and transition.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My approach is rooted in acknowledging the acceptance and change process. Learning to be still and pause within our patterns supports the change process. Many people consider therapy after months or years of enduring emotional pain or wondering why things are as they are. Many have wished that sadness, grief or life stress would ‘just go away’ but don’t know how to transform pain into growth. Often people seek therapy when they feel they have worn out their natural supports such as family or friends. As a Psychotherapist and human I meet you without judgment. I work to challenge you while also helping you to support yourself differently to become less stuck. I specialize in working with people experiencing transition, whether relational, career, life or existential. If you are reading this, there is likely a part of you that wishes to be seen and to make important changes to grow and be more comfortable as you are. I hope to be a part of that change process with you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: -I've had extensive training in Buddhist Psychology, Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP), Acceptance and Commitment therapy, Dialectical Behavior Therapy and presence-oriented clinical work. -I have practiced meditation on a daily basis since 1999 and believe it to be a pivotal factor in wellbeing, balance and change. -I have taught meditation since 2005, I had previously taught yoga from 2005-7 and see the importance of how we move trauma and emotions through the body which I incorporate into my therapy practice. -I personally heal through nature, being in the woods, exploring creative process via arts/ceramics/painting. My outlook is rooted in realistic understanding of the human experience. I specialize in trauma support, depression, anxiety and transforming losses/ transitions into growth/resilience.

specialities.name: Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP)
specialities.description: "Become stronger at the broken places" is the tagline for AEDP and it is the core of my approach to therapy. Very much rooted in neurobiology, presence-focused therapies, AEDP is designed to work on attachment and trauma issues from a deep, resonant place.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I have trained with Steven Hayes, Ph.D, the co-creator of ACT, attended ACT bootcamps and continue self-study daily with ACT principles.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have over 20 years experience and expertise guiding others to live differently and more skillfully with anxiety and panic. I understand anxiety from first-hand experience and can attest to evidence-based practices that work, including body-mind integration, nervous system repatterning, Cognitive Behavior Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy.

name: Maddie Cameron
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am committed to helping individuals and couples find more ease & magic in their lives.
ideal_client: If you feel called to connect to something bigger, a deep inner knowing that there is something “off” or missing in your life, but you just don’t know what that thing is, I aim to cultivate the space to support you in making happen what you have been invited toward.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have no theory to prove or agenda to push, I do not work toward “fixing” people or relationships and aim to steer clear of our one-dimensional focus on behavioral health change. Instead, I hope to walk with you as we explore how to live with more alignment, authenticity, and depth, whatever that may mean or look like for you. When we turn our attention toward this, health and wellness follow.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I am currently working with individuals and couples through grief, life transition, identity development, and women’s issues. I act as a guide and support in this work of returning to the spirit of self. “For a seed to achieve its greatest expression, it must come completely undone. The shell cracks, its insides come out and everything changes. To someone who doesn't understand growth, it would look like complete destruction,” Cynthia Occelli.

name: Paula Emerick
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Hey y'all! Yup..that's me, a horse and 2 goats. I invite you to reach out if you'd like to do this therapy thing together. You are fabulous.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: At your most vulnerable time, you need someone who will hold a safe space for you to approach your edges - the parts of us we tend to avoid or neglect. Addressing our 'issues' is intensely brave and can also be terrifying! So I commend you for embarking on this journey and invite you to call me if my words resonate with your needs.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have worked with folx in intimate relationships (poly/open and monog) and all kinds of friend/family combinations for over 15 years. I believe in co-creating safe therapeutic space to unravel and challenge deep rooted beliefs/dynamics/meanings/identities to foster new ways of understanding and connection. My specialties include attachment, relationship dynamics (couples, poly, open, kink), lgbtq identity, sex work, family of origin, mental health, recovery and addiction, and healing from trauma.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: It's not as fluffy as it sounds. I believe in it. It works. But it goes deep. In a nutshell - integrating emotional understanding with intellectual meaning and attending to the body while creating a trusting relationship with me working from the foundation of attachment. Wow. That's quite a sentence, Paula! Or just google it. ;)

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Oh snap. Welcome to the world of possibility and also crazy emotions! But for real....I like to start with what needs to be unlearned and what might be holding you back individually before jumping into the realm of expectations/boundaries/etc. Again - I do not claim to be an expert...and I am also VERY willing to navigate areas that promote honesty, connection, authenticity, and trust.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I am a Certified Drug and Alcohol Counselor and I was a Family Therapist at 2 treatment facilities in the Portland area for 3 years. Currently I am an Addictions Specialist at a Mental Health Agency downtown and I also practice the CRAFT Model (Community Reinforcement & Family Training), working with families who have a loved one using substances.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Personally, I identify as a 'faggy dyke' and I've been a loud and proud member of queer communities in Detroit, Ann Arbor, San Francisco, and Portland since the 90s. Clinically, I have worked with queer, poly, and kink folks for six years. I don't claim to be an expert, but I feel at home outside of the box.

name: Casey Black
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: If you can be curious about it, you can change it. Online therapy in WA & OR. In person in Vancouver.
ideal_client: Some of my clients know exactly why they need therapy. They have names for it, like childhood trauma, cPTSD, depression, or people-pleasing. Many don't have words yet. They just know they're suffering—something just feels off. Maybe there's a sense of numbness, of being shut down, or anxious. Or there's a lack of purpose; a persistent feeling that something is wrong, or something's missing They come to therapy first to find a name for their suffering, then to find a way of coming back to life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to helping is to let whatever is happening in the present moment lead us deeper into your self. If you arrive with a strange feeling, we sit with it. If you arrive with a thought, we unpack it. If you arrive with a numbness, we’ll be with that too. The more we can just be with a thing, the more we’ll understand your suffering. Curiosity and compassion will guide us. Meaning, if we’re curious about your pain and kind to yourself while tending to it, change will happen. Being with yourself in this way may not feel natural at first. That’s okay. We'll work with an eclectic approach that works for you: This may include somatic mindfulness, Internal Family Systems, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, or psychodynamic therapy. Non-clinically speaking, it just means we're going to use whatever we need to to help you feel better. My experience: Before opening a private practice three years ago, I worked for three years as a therapist at the Portland VA.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: A humanistic approach means that you’re going to experience me as being extremely curious about what it’s like to be you in this world right now, and that as you explore yourself in deeper and deeper ways I’m going to be right there with you, helping you process those findings. The humanistic approach also means that you’re going to get a real live person in the room, rather than a therapist with a blank face behind a notepad.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Being a humanistic therapist informed by mindfulness means that as difficult experiences arise in session, I may invite you to do something other than 'talk' about them. For example, we may pause to get really curious about what's going on in the body. While I believe that mindfulness can be life-changing when practiced intentionally, we won't necessarily practice it in every session (unless you'd like to). Rather, the therapy session in and of itself will act as a kind of mindful dialogue.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: Therapy through a psychodynamic lens recognizes that 1 - painful patterns and experiences in the present likely have roots in past experiences. 2 - These past events inform our present selves outside of our awareness. 3 - It can be healing to bring these past events into awareness.

name: Douglas Johns
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I'm a relationship specialist; I only see couples. Utilizing 90 minute sessions, I teach skills anchored in Collaborative Couple Therapy.
ideal_client: Sessions are a full 90 minutes in length; this helps couples more easily transition into each session and explore their needs. I also offer "Last Chance" couple therapy: One session, three hours in length, to understand what changes your relationship needs for both of you to be happy together. I have over 30 years experience as a family therapist & have been a relationship specialist, who only sees couples, since 2014. I help couples turn arguments into opportunities for intimacy & connection.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Collaborative Couple Therapy (CCT), my primary orientation, structures and models intimate conversations that enable couples to maintain emotional connection during painful interactions. These skills are foundational to healthy relationships. I also incorporate "differentiation" (as described by David Schnarch, Ph.D.): the ability to 'self-soothe' when painful interactions tempt you to angrily blame your partner and/or surrender your innate strength and resiliency. My foundational task as a CCT therapist is in helping you and your partner have intimate conversations about your problems through relating with each other as allies and confidants. In a collaborative conversation I help you and your partner talk with each other as if observing the problem from a platform, suspended high above the fray, looking down at the situation and people with compassionate curiosity, awareness, and reflection. Your experiences and practice in session transfers to your lives outside of my office.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a relationship specialist I devote my entire practice and professional life to understanding what skills make relationships strong and joyful. My primary orientation is called Collaborative Couple Therapy (CCT). I have over sixty hours of training in CCT through direct mentorship with Dan Wile, Ph.D., its originator. I believe so strongly in CCT that, prior to his death in 2020, I invested six years of regular travel down to Oakland, California to train with Dan. I'll bring that same level of commitment to my work with you. John Gottman, Ph.D., arguably the foremost research psychologist on what factors build good relationships, has written that Dan Wile is a “genius” and that CCT comports with his research findings for effective couple therapy. I am also informed by David Schnarch’s description of ‘differentiation’, by depth training in Existential Psychotherapy, by many years of training in and practice of Brief-Solution Focused Therapy, and by Buddhist Psychology.

specialities.name: Collaborative Couple Therapy
specialities.description: Collaborative Couple Therapy (CCT) starts from a belief that problems in relationship are also opportunities for increasing intimacy. Through understanding & communicating the deeper truth of your feelings (beneath anger, defensiveness, & avoidance), you can change adversarial dynamics into intimate connection. As your therapist my repeated role is to help you & your partner have intimate conversations about your dilemmas. I have 60+ hours of training in CCT with its originator Dan Wile, Ph.D.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: John Gottman has described Collaborative Couple Therapy, my speciality, as completely consistent with his research findings for cultivating loving relationships and named its originator, Dan Wile, "the greatest living marital therapist." I have 36+ hours of training with the Gottman Institute and, in particular, utilize Gottman Institute Research to inform my practice methodology.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I have been a dedicated student of Zen Buddhism since 2002. My daily meditation practice has only changed my life for the better. I am also a student of Jon Kabat-Zinn, having participated in his week long training in Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction in 2008. Mindfulness is a potent way to soothe our own vulnerable feelings and reduce our suffering.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I'm a relationship specialist: Collaborative Couple Therapy (CCT) is the sole focus of my practice; that's important because couple therapy is inherently different from other types of therapy. Effective couple therapy keeps the focus on the client-couple’s relationship patterns which takes skill to consistently follow, maintain, & interpret. I have 60+ hours of direct mentorship with the originator of CCT, Dan Wile, Ph.D. I provide a mature perspective refined through only working with couples.

name: Rani Gupta
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Limited weekly individual therapy openings for sensitive millennial professionals who are feeling lonely and misunderstood
ideal_client: I work with sensitive millennial professionals who are feeling lonely and misunderstood at work, with family and friends, or even with their partners. If you’re drawn to working with me, you’re likely someone who’s in touch with your emotions, a high achiever (looking at you, my fellow “pleasure to have in class” people!), and ready to commit to self-exploration.

approaches.What I Specialize In: My clients are sensitive millennial professionals who often describe the following to me: 1) Even though they're making a great salary, they notice their anxiety increasing. They see their bosses or co-workers treat every minuscule task like it's a fire to be put out, and they dread starting their work day, 2) They swore they wouldn't become workaholics, because that was never aligned with their values, but here they are...and it's been months since they've hung out with friends, been on a date, or had a relaxing day to themselves, OR 3) They feel disconnected from their family, not just because they haven't seen them in a while, but because they have a gut feeling something intense or traumatic happened to their parents, grandparents, or somewhere else in their lineage *Are you ready for a change? I also offer a 10-week accelerated 1:1 therapy experience. Visit my website for more information about my practice and to schedule your free 15-minute video meet-and-greet!*

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: My training in EMDR, Flash Technique, and somatic parts work means I have the expertise you need and deserve when processing work stress, generational wounds, and healing your relationships. But at the end of the day, you want to know you’re working with someone who gets what it means to be an ambitious, sensitive-hearted young professional struggling with "doing it all", right? I get it because I’ve lived it myself. I know that sometimes you wonder, “Who am I outside of this job?” I know you grapple with trying to have hobbies again. So when we work together, you won’t just get a trained therapist. You’ll get someone who truly understands what you’re going through.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR is a powerful type of therapy that allows people to process intense things they’ve experienced, whether it’s stress, trauma, anxiety, or a variety of other experiences. EMDR helps the body and the mind move from a state of fight, flight, freeze, or fawn to a state of more grounded presence within oneself. I guide clients through addressing the negative beliefs they have about themselves to feeling deeper connection with their inner calm, compassion, and confidence.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I work with numerous men who care deeply about the world around them, their loved ones, and their community. They tend to work in fields where their sensitivity and empathy aren't valued. They often end every work day wondering, "Ugh, what am I actually doing this job for, aside from the paycheck?" When we work together, you build greater awareness and gain skills to move from dissatisfaction, disconnection, or frustration to compassion, knowledge, and understanding of the body’s wisdom.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Because you’re a sensitive soul who’s had to suppress certain emotions, we take our time building trust and rapport so we can get to the heavy stuff. I often hear, “Reaching out to you and seeking therapy were big steps for me.” I help clients not only identify what triggers their work stress, but also notice their body’s responses. I guide you through the process of getting in touch with your inner world and listening to what it has to tell you.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: You’ve had a sinking feeling for a long time that something happened somewhere in your lineage - whether it was your parents, your grandparents, or beyond - that has become a repetitive pattern. Maybe you’re typically a flexible or adaptable person, but you notice you feel sudden fear when you have to go somewhere that, for most other people, would be an “everyday” place to go. Maybe you’re typically a patient person who notices that you suddenly turn impatient and irritated with certain tasks.

name: Carolyn Peterson
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I help adults struggling with trauma, grief, and life transitions by navigating intense emotions and finding peace and connection.
ideal_client: Are you caught in an unending cycle of feeling insufficient, regardless of your achievements or efforts? As you navigate various roles in your life – partner, friend, caregiver, parent/child, coworker, or manager – do you constantly feel like you're falling short, despite your best efforts? Whether you experience anxiety, stress, depression, or simply feel stuck in a state of "fine" or "meh," know that you're not alone.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I’m passionate about helping thoughtful, driven adults who feel overwhelmed and insecure find comfort in who they are and build deeper connections with the people and things that matter. I recognize the weight of unrealistic expectations, both self-imposed and external, that leave you perpetually unfulfilled. Whether stemming from past trauma, intricate learning histories, or the pressures of daily life, these challenges may make you feel like you're merely existing rather than truly living. My approach is grounded in scientific principles, tailored to help you break free from this cycle. Together, we navigate the complexities of your background with compassion and understanding, uncovering the roots of your feelings to cultivate a deeper sense of fulfillment and authenticity in your life. If you're ready to move beyond survival mode and embrace a life that aligns with your true self, I'm here to support you every step of the way.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am multiracial, bilingual in Thai and English, and the proud daughter of a Veteran. My experience of growing up abroad and coming to the United States as an adult allows me to bring a unique perspective to therapy. I am deeply committed to exploring the intersectionality of identities. I strive to create a space that honors and embraces the complexity of our individual background, identities, and experiences. I understand societal context plays a significant role in shaping our perspectives and challenges we face. Throughout my training and professional journey, I've had the privilege of supporting individuals from diverse backgrounds in a range of settings, including university counseling centers, child and family centers, community mental health organizations, and Veteran Affairs Hospitals. You will frequently catch me experimenting with new recipes, watching football, hitting the trails with my furry friend, and giving rock climbing my best shot.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am trained in Cognitive Processing Therapy, Prolonged Exposure, and ACT for Trauma. I have experience working with both men and women for a variety of traumas to also include Moral Injury. Additionally, I am familiar with the co-occurring nature of substance use with trauma.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I work with men to empower them to overcome barriers to seeking help, cultivate self-compassion, and develop healthier emotional expression, ultimately leading to greater fulfillment and connection in their lives. My approach focuses on helping recognize and challenge unhelpful narratives that contribute to feelings of shame and disconnection. I'm familiar with the presentation of cooccurring disorders in men and how this may present differently than in women.

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: I specialize in racial identity development, particularly multiracial backgrounds. My dissertation delved into the complexities of navigating multiracial identity, including challenges and opportunities inherent in this journey. Having grown up in a multiracial family myself, I intimately understand the cultural and intergenerational dynamics at play. I am sensitive to the nuanced demands and expectations that individuals from multiracial backgrounds often encounter.

name: Sophia Jarvis
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Hi there! I'm passionate about working with couples and adult relationships to find your way back to feeling connected and on the same team.
ideal_client: Relationships can be joyful, messy, stuck, and full of meaning—all at once. I work with couples and intimate partners who want to understand their patterns, feel more connected, and communicate with more ease. Many of my clients are queer, kinky, nonmonogamous, neurodivergent, or part of nontraditional communities. Life is so much more colorful when you paint from your own palette!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use Emotionally Focused Therapy to support couples in building real understanding and repair. For deeper wounds, I also offer EMDR and Flash Technique when talking alone isn’t enough. My style is laid-back and conversational, with a steady focus on what’s happening beneath the surface. We’ll explore the cycles between you, how each of you makes sense of them, and what it would take to feel more seen, safe, and connected. I work collaboratively—I’m not here to fix you, but to help you understand yourselves and each other in deeper, more honest ways so you can create the relationship that's right for you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I come to this work with the understanding that we all live within systems that shape how we relate to ourselves and each other, with some carrying more weight than others. For me, relational healing is inseparable from social justice—it’s about dignity, care, boundaries, repair, self-expression, and the ongoing practice of humanizing ourselves and each other. This work requires deep reflection on both how we’re harmed and how we perpetuate harm, and a commitment to creating space for healing through connection and authenticity.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR and Flash Technique. I seek consultation with Dr. Lynn Fontana, PhD, LMFT.

name: Alex Harrison
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi, I'm Alex. I'm a relational, trauma-informed therapist blending Jungian psychology, somatic psychotherapy, and creative expression.
ideal_client: Are you feeling lost and disoriented in a transitional time of your life? Frustrated with repeating the same patterns and losing touch with the magic of who you are? Maybe you have encountered adversity in your life that has left you feeling emotionally dysregulated and disconnected from yourself, others, and the world. Or maybe you are looking for support in finding meaning and purpose, reclaiming your inspiration and passion, and rewriting your story as one of empowerment and expansion.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is to help you explore the unconscious forces contributing to pattern repetition, emotional distress, and disconnection from self and others. I strongly believe we all possess an inner healing intelligence that speaks to us in a variety of ways, and my intention is to facilitate this process by listening deeply and providing space for you to express those parts of you that have been suppressed or discouraged out of fear or out of necessity. I am also trained in EMDR and somatic therapy and often incorporate techniques like meditation, art, and parts work to help access and integrate difficult life experiences, amplify your intuitive capacity, and remove the blocks keeping you from sharing the gift of your authentic self with the world.

name: Kristine Zappa
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I take a heartfelt, compassionate, and non-judgmental approach to counseling with an emphasis on somatic (body-based) approaches.
ideal_client: Overall, my goal as a trauma-informed and person-centered therapist is to help you move through life in ways that feel more aligned with your deepest sense of self. I enjoy collaborating with folks on issues like processing life transitions, anxiety, feelings of low self-worth, body image, perfectionism, relationship dynamics, and patterns of shame. My clients also tend to have a history of complex or developmental trauma and want to find relief from years of reliving old, painful patterns.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to counseling starts with a belief that healing happens within a safe, compassionate, non-judgmental relationship. I hope to create a space to process overwhelming experiences in order to help you gain more clarity and move forward with new skills and a sense of empowerment in your life. From a somatic perspective, I believe the body and the mind are intimately linked and I safely incorporate body-centered trauma processing tools as a path towards finding stability in your life. I also believe that systems play an important role in our experience and should be taken into account when treating mental health; these systems can include culture, institutions, community, family, intimate relationships and more. Lastly, and importantly, my approach to counseling is not one of being an "expert", but my goal is to help you discover your own inherent wisdom.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I believe in the power of relationships and know firsthand how supportive a trusting, safe therapeutic relationship can be. I became a therapist because of my own journey of self-growth and healing through therapy and I wholeheartedly believe people are so much more than their struggles. I am dedicated to helping folks see and feel their innate goodness, beyond their past experiences, and lean into the potential for a life of ease and wholeness. I also became a therapist because I believe that healing as an individual can ripple out and help heal the collective in which we are all apart of, and which we all play a role.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am trained in Deep Brain Reorienting (DBR) - which is a clinically-proven approach to help folks recover from trauma. I also incorporate Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, a holistic and gentle approach to working with trauma using body-based processing.

name: Natalie Mickola
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I’m a Licensed Professional Counselor providing virtual individual therapy to adolescents and adults in Oregon.
ideal_client: To me, therapy is about having a place where you can come, be yourself, and use the space to explore the thoughts/feelings that you may not feel comfortable expressing outside of therapy. Whether your goals are about healing or changing, therapy can be that extra tool to help you figure out how to get there. Many of the clients I have worked have goals related to body image dissatisfaction, trauma, emotional stability, disorder eating and eating disorders, self-harm, depression, and anxiety.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My first 6+ years of therapy experience was with adolescents with eating disorders. When people think of eating disorders, they often imagine a stereotypical version, which doesn’t represent the majority of people who experience eating disorders and disordered eating. This is something that can happen to anyone, for many reasons. I view it as a way of coping, similar but different to addiction, that is aimed to help someone but has too many negative consequences. Whether you are looking to change your behaviors and/or mindset, I am here to help you better understand why you’re engaging in your behaviors and to decrease your need to rely on this specific way of coping. My biggest goal is always to help you find better ways to take care of yourself. I use an eclectic mix of therapeutic modalities, based on what seems to best match with my client’s needs. I view therapy as a place to build trust so you can do your most vulnerable and deep exploration to meet your therapeutic goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I value being that person to hold space for you and your emotions. It’s hard enough managing our life stressors day-to-day sometimes, but as you add up the other challenges that are often out of our control (past trauma, systems of oppression, diet culture, social media, societal messaging, imbalances in the brain, etc.), moving forward and making change can feel impossible. I think everyone could benefit from having that extra support, and I’m proud to be that person. I work from a Heath at Every Size (HAES) approach, meaning an anti-weight bias and anti-fatphobic view of people and bodies. I support clients of all backgrounds and identities.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Relational Cultural Therapy (RTC) uses a feminist, multicultural lens to focus on the growth that comes from connection. I highly value RTC's emphasis on building a strong therapeutic relationship to help support your deeper growth. This theory also notes the importance of identifying the overlaps in people's identities and how this influences the experiences they have in their lives. The goal is empowering people against systemic oppression and building relationships based on authenticity.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: To summarize, ACT focuses on accepting what you can't control and committing to what is important to you. I have used many components of ACT with clients, but my favorite is exploring someone's values and how life feels when they do/don't honor those values. While it can feel like a simple concept, this can often be key in creating a life that feels more authentic and fulfilling.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I have used CBT for many years while supporting clients with eating disorders, mood dysregulation, and trauma. I appreciate the structure CBT offers in addressing the relationship between our thoughts, feelings, and actions. When you boil things down to the basics like this, it can help increase self-awareness in a way that serves the deeper work in therapy too. There is a specific form of CBT I use to address trauma called Cognitive Processing Therapy. If you have questions about it, just ask!

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: DBT is often used to build skills in therapy, such as self-acceptance, tolerating and regulating distressing emotions, communicating your needs, and changing harmful behaviors. Another part of DBT is shifting how we perceive what is going on in our lives in new ways that may influence our emotional experience. I often utilize parts of DBT when supporting clients with emotional regulation or replacing maladaptive behaviors.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: Motivational interviewing is a modality used to help people build motivation towards change. It is a person-centered, evidence-based approach that helps you reflect on your life and behaviors in a way that is especially helpful when you're feeling ambivalent or resistant to change. My use of motivational interviewing techniques often depends on how "stuck" or unmotivated a client is feeling in therapy.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: Eating disorders rarely follow the stereotypes we see in media. Overall I view eating disorders as a disordered relationship with food, self, and usually body, where ED behaviors are often used to cope with one's internal experience. The way I support clients in addressing their eating disorders in therapy really depends on what their goals are, how the ED is impacting their life, and the underlying reasons beneath the behaviors.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: Anyone can have body image issues. We are taught so many different things, even from a young age, about what bodies "should" look like and how we "should" be treating our bodies.
