intro: Currently accepting new clients. I bring a warm, accepting, and straightforward approach. I would be honored to work with you!
ideal_client: You’re stressed, overwhelmed, and finding it difficult to find enjoyment in most activities. You are struggling, and you don't know what to do. You are starting to worry about your health, your relationships, and you wonder if anything will ever feel right again. You’ve spent countless hours searching for answers on the internet – but you are left feeling lost and alone, and you desperately want help. I can help you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I will help you process your emotions and experiences and help you evolve your strategies for coping with life events and transitions. We will work together to help you build a secure relationship with yourself, to build your self awareness and confidence so you can lead your life authentically, courageously, and compassionately. I bring warmth, acceptance, humor and compassion when working with you. I will combine my own lived experiences, my genuine love for helping people, and my training to best serve you. I believe every person has the ability to change and evolve, I am honored and excited to walk beside you in this journey.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: This is my second career - my first was as a team leader in the corporate world where my ability to see people's potential and to help people grow/develop were put to good use...but there was always a nagging feeling that I was not fulfilling my life purpose and that I needed to serve people in a different way. It was the guidance of a very astute career counselor who helped me reflect on my interests, talents, passions, and life priorities. It was the realization that without the help of our amazing couples counselor, my wife and I would have likely divorced just a few years after the birth of our beautiful son (we are pushing +27 years now – but who’s counting!). It was so many things that came together and led me to this incredible profession where I am humbled and honored to hear people’s stories, to walk alongside them, to challenge them when necessary, and to support them in navigating life’s challenges.

name: Eden Baron-Williams
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
credentials: MA, Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I assist clients in unlocking their inner wisdom and dismantling barriers in their life, deepening their relationships and sense belonging.
ideal_client: You came here because you have a desire to deepen your relationship with yourself and others, you feel stuck in patterns you hope to change, are processing trauma, or are looking to reclaim lost parts of yourself. You have come to the right place. Working with adults with childhood trauma/complex trauma, couples/relational systems, chronic pain/illness, and queer/trans/non-binary individuals and relationships, I work collaboratively with clients to create spaces for care, depth, and connection.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I am a registered Marriage and Family Therapist Associate with a specialization in sexualities. I hold certifications and special training in Somatic Attachment Therapy, EFT, and am a Certified Sexual Assault Survivor Advocate. I have a background in the creative arts, which has allowed me to think creatively with clients and explore artistic mediums in our work together. Being a person who is invisibly physically disabled and neurodivergent, I have a passion for working with folx struggling with chronic pain/chronic illness. I have both experience and specialization in working with, advocating for, and supporting queer individuals and relationships, trans and non-binary individuals and relationships, kink/BDSM, folks suffering from systemic marginalization, and PTSD/complex trauma. I have a special passion for supporting individuals navigating the medical system, be that people needing treatment for chronic pain/illness to folx seeking gender affirming care and surgery.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I think about mental health through a systemic lens - the understanding that we are all impacted by one another, the sociopolitical systems in which we live, and our social locations. Our bodies are also a system as is the Earth, plants, and animals we live among. The way we communicate within our own system, is a reflection of the way we communicate with other systems and vice versa. Through this lens, I center those impacted by systemic marginalization and emphasize social justice in my practice. I believe therapy can be a building block not only for you and your relationships, but for community change and liberation. I am invisibly physically disabled and neurodivergent, which fuels me toward naming and dismantling ableism on the systemic level. I am an active advocate for the LGBTQ+ community and have served as an advocate and educator teaching students and community members about topics such as systemic racism, the importance of sex-positive education, and trans rights.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Everyone has strategies to get their needs met. Often times these once essential strategies become patterns in our life that keep us from connecting and turning toward one another. Attachment and emotion-focused therapy invites us to understand and build compassion for our old patterns, while building new, healthier strategies for connection by identifying our emotions and giving voice to our needs.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: We are made up of many parts that guide us, protect us, and walk along side us throughout our lives and relationships. Sometimes, these parts are loud while other important parts remain hidden, yet to be given an invitation to come out of the shadows and join us in our life journey. By engaging in inner child work, exploration of our parts, and promoting the Self, we can come closer to who we are, what we need, and how we access belonging in the intricacies of our internal and external world.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Everything in life is a physical, mental, social, and spiritual experience. Yet, many of us are disconnected from our bodies. I believe that our bodies are vessels of wisdom from which we hold our experiences of pain, joy, belonging, intuition, and information. Through the process of slowing down and noticing, we can uncover a well of resources you already have within you, as well as heal from a foundational level. I am a Certified Somatic Attachment Therapist

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have specialized training in working with couples and relational systems. I particularly enjoy working with queer relationships. I have additional training in Emotionally-Focused Couples Therapy, sexualities, kink/BDSM, polyamory, open relationships, and couples in transition. As a trauma specialist, I feel passionate about supporting couples who have complex trauma/PTSD, assisting them in building safety and security with one another.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I work primarily with adults with childhood trauma, individuals and couples with complex trauma, and those who were rejected from their families and communities due to their sexual orientation and/or gender identities.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I personally deal with chronic pain/chronic illness and am invisibly physically disabled. Working with those who are impacted by ableist systems and helping them navigate the world in a way that promotes their wellbeing and helps them receive necessary, validating, informed care, is a special passion of mine.

name: Robin Perez
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: As a mental healthcare provider I believe everyone deserves to be happy, healthy, and thriving and I love to help people grow and heal.
ideal_client: Although I am not accepting new patients at this time, my team is. We have providers who are able to see new patients with in a week or two.

approaches.My Background: I have worked as an outpatient Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner since 2001. During my carrier as a registered nurse (RN) I worked at inpatient psychiatric units for adults and children as well as other areas of medicine throughout the hospital. The last several years of my RN career I worked as an ICU nurse.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I had always wondered what made people "tick" and why some were happy while others sad. In my efforts to understand and learn to help others, I pursued a degree psychology in college but became a nurse at the same time. This dual approach to how the mind and brain/body work only enhanced my understanding and passion to help others. I truly love my work and enjoy working with a very diverse population of people from all genders, backgrounds, races, religions, and lifestyles, etc. I feel that connecting as partners in healthcare has made it easy to understand the uniqueness of each person needs and plan to help them grow and heal.

name: Kelly Reams MSW, BCD Psychoanalyst
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Talk therapy in a trusted, collaborative relationship for making enduring change-more joy, emotional aliveness, intimacy, and satisfaction.
ideal_client: I see children, teens and adults with a wide range of issues that include anxiety, depression, "feeling stuck," identity, sexuality, relationships, and self growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a psychotherapist and contemporary psychoanalyst, I work with both situational, short-term issues or the more chronic concerns depending on your goals for therapy. I have found that establishing consistent meeting times at a particular frequency (once a week or more often) helps create a sense of safety and trust that supports you in making more fundamental changes on the inside and in daily life. We will jointly explore your inner world of feelings, hopes, dreams, fantasies, thoughts, anxieties, fears, secrets and memories to help you understand these profound influences that continue to impact us in the present in ways that we haven't known, before. I will deeply respect your unique self and self-direction based on confidence that with help, you will be able to experience new ways of being and understanding yourself that are liberating and transformative.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Over the past thirty years, I've actively sought out teachers, mentors, supervisors, play therapists, psychotherapists and psychoanalysts to help me develop the skills and knowledge needed to offer a range of treatment options that differ in depth and intensity depending on one's goals for treatment. After completing a M.S.W. (1980), I've worked as a psychotherapist with children, teens, adults and families in residential treatment, the Child & Adolescent Clinic at O.H.S.U. and have had a private practice for over 30 years which has included individual therapy, play therapy, couples and family therapy, consultation/ supervision and now, psychoanalysis. I finished a 6 year psychoanalytic training program (OPC) in 2004, am a certified analyst and a Training-Supervising Psychoanalyst. I also am a faculty member at OPC and continue to learn through study groups, continuing education, consultation, and as a consultant to mental health therapists.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I've been practicing psychodynamic psychotherapy from a contemporary relational orientation for over 30 years. I selected my graduate program due to a strong emphasis of understanding both the conscious and unconscious factors that influence who we are. I both seek and provide mental health consultation within the rich variety of analytic perspectives

specialities.name: Psychoanalytic
specialities.description: I completed a six year psychoanalytic training program at the Oregon Psychoanalytic Institute in 2004 and see adults in psychotherapy and psychoanalysis. I also use this analytic understanding to inform individual psychotherapy, play therapy, couples counseling, consultation.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: I began learning play therapy 1978 in graduate school with analytic supervision using play technique to understand child's emotional and behavioral issues. Studied with the Child Therapy Study Group for over 10 years meeting as a group and weekly individual supervision. Also did 1 year child analytic training, Seattle, worked 8 years Child Psychiatry OHSU, 3 years residential treatment children.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have over thirty years of psychotherapy experience with children and adolescents dealing with a wide range of emotional and behavioral issues in several settings. As a member of the Child Therapy Study Group for over ten years, I received individual consultation on my child therapy cases with psychoanalytically trained professionals and met with colleagues for ongoing clinical discussions.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Training in developmental theory and contemporary psychoanalytic theories provide a solid base of information and experience working with the complexities around vulnerabilities of self-esteem. There are different ways these problems manifest and having a broad understanding and flexible therapeutic style helps me meet the patient where they are to strengthen self esteem from the inside out.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have extensive experience working with couples and/or individuals dealing with relationship and marital issues. My analytic training with both attachment and relational theories provide the theoretical and technical skills that enable me to tailor a treatment approach that matches the individual or couple's needs. I am currently seeking consultation to expand my knowledge and skill level.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: A large percentage of the children and adults I see are seeking help with grief reactions or loss experiences, either contemporary or a past history of early loss. Trained as a psychoanalyst, I'm able to help patients access unprocessed grief that has been hidden away or not accessible for other reasons. I receive referrals from the Dougy Center for children and families with loss through suicide

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I am trained as a contemporary psychoanalyst with successful experience treating depressive symptoms in both adults and children/teenagers with intensive treatment. I also work collaboratively with physicians or nurse practitioners who may prescribe medications concurrently.

name: Alli Swift
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I believe that engaging in therapy allows us to connect and nurture all parts of ourselves. It is a gift to know yourself.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to counseling rests on my belief that the therapeutic relationship is central to client growth and change. Creating a space of safety, trust and unconditional positive regard for the client guides all my interactions and interventions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a Masters degree in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis & Clark in Portland, OR, and have spent most of my clinical hours working with adolescents around issues of anxiety, self image, relational difficulties and life transitions. I believe in social justice for all, and creating an environment that welcomes anyone and everyone.

name: Anchi Howitz
title: Student Counselor
intro: Creating a compassionate space where individuals and couples can deepen connection to themselves and each other, and achieve healing
ideal_client: I love working with individuals, couples, and families who prioritize and want deeper connection to themselves and others, even when that work can be vulnerable and challenging. I enjoy clients who are open to reflection and change, and are engaged in the therapeutic process. I support and encourage clients in embracing the multitudes of their authentic self.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My mission is to create a collaborative environment, grounded in warmth, authenticity, and compassion, nurturing your innate abilities to heal and grow. Throughout life’s journey, unhelpful patterns, cultural messages, and oppressive systems may have promoted disconnection within yourself, in your relationships, with community, and to the Earth. I believe that through reflection, insight, and deepening connections both internally and externally, we can achieve healing, liberation, and expanded possibilities. I am currently finishing my Master's Degree in the Marriage, Family, and Couple Therapy program at Lewis & Clark Graduate School. In addition, I am completing a specialty certification in Ecopsychology. I primarily draw from Narrative Therapy, Emotionally Focused Therapy, and Ecotherapy. Attending therapy is a vulnerable and courageous act, and I feel honored to be able to hold space for you as we embark on this journey.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a biracial Asian-American woman, I have observed how my intersecting identities have shaped relational power dynamics. I bring a systemic perspective, which takes into consideration issues of equity and justice. I value and look forward to working with individuals and families of all identities and configurations, including the LGBTQIA+ and BIPOC communities. I graduated from Cornell University's school of Hospitality Administration, and my first career was in luxury spa management. Quickly I realized that I wanted to step away from the management side and have a more intimate role in people's healing. I spent ten years after this working as a Licensed Massage Therapist. In this time, I also co-founded a farmed animal sanctuary. Currently as a therapist, I see that I have always been drawn to work that is about healing, empathy, and connection. I am honored to do this work.

name: Jamee Puccio
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I work with teens (14+), adults, and couples dealing with anxiety, parenting, spiritual trauma and LGBTQIA+ mental health support, and more.
ideal_client: I am especially passionate about helping folks explore, shift, and understand identities. I love working with queer folks, new parents or soon-to-be parents, teenagers, and young adults, and people struggling with faith transitions and spiritual trauma. I love being curious alongside my clients as we explore "Who's in there?" and "How do I want to live?" and "What's been in my way?"

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I deeply believe that we all thrive best when we are taking care of one another. However, most of us these days live in cultures that de-prioritize that community care and expect us to suck it up and take care of ourselves, by ourselves, even in the murkiest times. I don't know about you, but I don't feel very successful when I try to move through life without support. I became a therapist because I love being a part of people's support networks, and I think that therapy is a unique and beautiful way to do that. I love helping folks navigate shifting identities, uncover and care for old wounds, and move into the person they know they really are. I am passionate about exploring the role of systemic oppression and collective trauma in my clients’ stories. As a member of the LGBTQIA+ community I am especially drawn to helping fellow queer folks. I also love helping support parents!

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: I practice Restoration Therapy, an approach that combines the best of Attachment Theory, Behavior Change, Emotional Regulation and Family Systems. Restoration Therapy is designed to efficiently and compassionately empower my clients to practice mindfulness on a daily basis, in order to increase loving and trustworthy behaviors towards themselves and those they are connected to.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a member of the queer community, I am passionate about supporting others in the LGBTQIA+ community through insightful, compassionate and systemic counseling.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Parenting is an amazing, and often difficult, journey. I work with parents (or soon-to-be) parents on identifying ways to reduce stress, increase mindfulness and nurture connection with their children, themselves and their community of support.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I work with teens and adults dealing with depression to identify ways in which their symptoms get in the way of thriving, as well as how to foster self-compassion and mindfulness in order to increase mood and motivation.

name: Midori Ferris Wayne
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Feeling anxiety or disconnection? You're not alone, and things really can get better. I do therapy differently, and I'm here to help.
ideal_client: I work with individuals and couples/partners who feel anxious or disconnected and who are often seeking help navigating the impact of previous trauma on current relationship concerns, particularly around identity, sexuality, intimacy, marginalization, and nontraditional partnerships. I support clients in increasing connection and shifting imbalances in their relationships with compassion and accountability rather than blame.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I do therapy differently than most, because I trust that you already have all the inner resources to deal with stuck patterns in your life. I also won't minimize you. I know the struggle is real and is compounded by systemic oppression that isn’t going away soon enough for any of us. But you have so much more coping potential than you realize. Rather than approaching therapy as treatment for mental illness, I can help you see yourself as fundamentally healthy and whole. This isn't woo woo stuff, it's brain-science and evidence-based, and you'll see the difference. I've been trained in trauma-informed, body and sex positive/kink/polyam/neuroqueer approaches for individual and relational therapy with a specialization in intimacy/sex therapy. I've also worked with neurodiverse families for almost two decades. I integrate Internal Family Systems, narrative therapy, and interpersonal neurobiology with a focus on equity by balancing independence and compassion for self and others.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My identity as a person and as a therapist is based in a neuroqueer framework, which is really more of a verb than a noun. Let's neuroqueer this therapy process! Neuroqueering honors a diversity of minds as well as bodies and recognizes that rigid expectations around ability, gender, sexuality, etc. are simply age-old products of societal oppression. This world is not designed for anyone who doesn't fit neatly into societal norms for experiencing the world or expressing themselves, and it's harder than we think to unlearn inherited beliefs about what is "normal". I'm passionate about tracking the impacts of normative ideology directly in sessions and hold myself accountable to untangling these relational patterns for each of us. It's an exciting process which has also become a life practice for me, as I become more aware of vulnerabilities and show up in my relationships more courageously. We can collaborate to create safety for this transformative work in your life as well.

name: Forage Wellness Collective
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: We are a group practice located in Tigard and Sisters, Oregon. We work with many insurance plans and hold an OHA Certificate of Approval.

approaches.Our Background and Approach: At Forage Wellness, our treatment team has hundreds of combined training hours in the Restoration Therapy approach. Our Clinical Supervisor, Justin Little, LMFT (RT Certified Level II), is heavily involved in every aspect of your care. Student interns and pre-licensed clinicians receive top-notch attention, training and supervision in order to provide you with the best treatment possible. Justin will often participate in therapy sessions in addition to supervising and training in real-time.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Restoration Therapy (also known as “RT”) uses the latest developments in Attachment Theory, Emotional Regulation and Mindfulness in an understandable and effective approach that empowers clients to clearly identify and name fight/flight reactions in order to facilitate growth. All of our therapists receive extensive training and supervision in RT in order to maximize positive clinical outcomes for you.

name: Elise Helms
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hello! I provide a warm, engaging, and accepting space for you to be your authentic self as you explore and step toward growth and healing.
ideal_client: Perhaps you are stuck in your personal process or relationship(s), feeling anxious, depressed, unworthy, overwhelmed, or unsure of what to do next or how. Sometimes when lost or disconnected we need support to process emotions, interpersonal issues, or painful life events, to once again feel whole, centered, and connected to self and others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach is genuine and warm, highly relational, integrative, and grounded in attachment, humanistic, holistic, and existential theories. I honor the connection of mind, body, heart, and spirit, and I incorporate mindfulness and somatic-based interventions to bring greater awareness to one’s whole being. I aim to provide a safe and supportive environment where you will know and feel that you are accepted just as you are. I view my role as that of a mindful companion supporting you on your journey. I will follow your lead, while remaining curious, engaged, and honest in what I notice. I invite you to stay open to new directions, yet grounded in the present moment, as you access your own wisdom and gain new insight and awareness. I will meet you with an open heart and mind, with understanding, patience, encouragement, and compassion as we uncover and explore the underpinnings of your life experiences to facilitate the growth, healing, and change that you desire.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in your wholeness and inherent worth and wisdom. I also believe that you are meant to be truly heard, seen, and witnessed by another. As a client, I have experienced the healing and growth that is possible when one is met with the genuine presence, support, and compassion of an attuned therapist. It is my honor to collaborate with and hold space for others as they reclaim their strength, repair their relationships, and remember their true self. As a therapist, I am committed to my own personal, political, and spiritual evolution, grounded in the belief that compassionate counseling requires a commitment to personal growth, cultural humility, and always striving to genuinely understand the myriad lived experiences of diverse populations. I view humans through a multicultural and relational lens with the understanding that our well-being is impacted by our identities, the social and cultural systems we inhabit, and the state and health of our relationships.

name: Megan McDavid
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I'm a queer therapist passionate about helping people improve their mental health. I specialize in sexuality, gender, and fertility.
ideal_client: People often find my practice looking for a therapy space where they don’t need to explain themselves or educate their therapist on their identities or experiences. They want a therapist who is going to gently challenge them to look deeply at themselves while being valued, seen, and supported. My practice provides specialized treatment of sexuality concerns, and support for LGBTQIA+ communities and people experiencing fertility challenges.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is not one-size-fits-all and is tailored to your specific goals and needs from therapy. I strive to help you feel comfortable and at-ease discussing topics that can sometimes be very sensitive. I strive to create a space free from judgement that can support you on your own individual journey.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am an AASECT Certified Sex Therapist. I received my Master’s Degree in Social Work at the Silberman School of Social Work at Hunter College in New York City and a Master’s Degree in Education with a specialization in Human Sexuality and Sex Therapy from Widener University in Pennsylvania.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Using a warm, positive approach, I help clients develop a stronger sense of themselves and harness the strengths already inside of us.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: Motivational interviewing is a powerful technique that helps people clarify what they want and how to make changes in their lives.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT is an evidence-based technique that shows amazing results in helping manage depression, anxiety, and other issues that often bring people to therapy.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Whether you are looking to come to therapy to explore an aspect of gender or sexuality, or you just want to work with a therapist who you don't need to educate about who you are, working with a therapist experienced in LGBTQIA+ identities can help you feel safe and accepted on your therapy journey. I have extensive experience working with LGBTQ people and those living with HIV, and can provide supportive and culturally competent therapy around these issues.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can leave us feeling overwhelmed and unable to sleep, focus, and be present for our lives. I provide evidence-based, action-oriented treatment for anxiety disorders. Together we will work to identify the source of the anxiety and develop a treatment plan that will retrain your body and mind to better be able to cope with stress.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can be situational or it can be a lifelong struggle. I will work with you to find hope, build energy, and reconnect with your life. My approach to depression treatment is tailored to each individual.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I am an AASECT-certified sex therapist and have specialized training is addressing sexual concerns such as low desire, difficulty with arousal or orgasm, compulsive sexual behaviors, and unwanted desires. I strive to make discussing sensitive issues comfortable and help work with you to create a plan for therapy that works towards your goals.

specialities.name: Infertility
specialities.description: Experiencing fertility challenges can be an incredibly painful and isolating experience. Working with a therapist that "gets it" can help you feel supported through medical appointments, painful conversations with family and friends, and all the ups and downs on your journey to parenthood. I completed training through the American Society for Reproductive Medicine and am a Certified Sex Therapist. I provide kind, supportive care for those struggling with fertility challenges.

name: Kathleen Converse
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi! I’m Kathleen Converse, LCSW (she/her). I specialize in working with anxiety, trauma, and relationship issues.
ideal_client: I love working with a wide range of clients, but we may be an especially good fit if you are struggling with anxiety, relationship issues or past trauma. I love helping people better connect to the wisdom of their bodies and the wise voice inside them that already knows how to heal. I also love working with highly sensitive clients and helping them to regulate their nervous systems and be able to see their sensitivity as a strength.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I'm an anti-oppressive relational therapist and bring that lens into all of my work with clients. I take a personalized, collaborative approach to healing work. I prioritize creating a strong relationship with clients with safety and trust. I am trained in EMDR and Internal Family Systems Theory informed, and draw on somatic mind- body techniques in my work with clients. I use attachment theory to explore relational wounds and use a strengths based approach to build on your existing coping strategies. I am a former sexual assault advocate, and university Director for the Center for Gender Equity. I have 10 years of experience working with survivors of trauma, and draw on this background to help you have healthier relationships with yourself and others.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I have a background in community organizing and am passionate about social justice. My practice strives to be anti-oppressive, queer and trans affirming, neuro-affirming, and trauma- informed. I'm a queer therapist and passionate about supporting the LGBTQ+ community, . I believe that individual healing creates ripples in the world, and that a more equitable and just world is possible starting by healing ourselves.

name: Jessica Franco
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Hi! I'm Jessica. I provide online therapy to clients in Oregon. I have immediate availability with openings Monday - Thursday until 8 p.m.
ideal_client: I work with adolescents and adults navigating trauma, anxiety, depression, life transitions, and behavioral challenges. I also specialize in supporting neurodiverse individuals and those facing significant mental health challenges. My approach is collaborative and empowering, providing tailored tools to help you uncover strengths, foster resilience, and create meaningful progress. If you're ready to explore your experiences and work toward growth, I’m here to support you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to healing focuses on creating a collaborative, empowering, and supportive space where you feel safe to explore your emotions, experiences, and goals. I draw from evidence-based practices, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Dialectical Behavior Therapy, and Motivational Interviewing, tailoring each session to your unique needs. Together, we’ll identify challenges, set meaningful goals, and develop strategies that resonate with you. I believe healing happens through understanding, connection, and growth, so I emphasize building a strong therapeutic relationship grounded in empathy, trust, and mutual respect. Whether we’re working through past trauma, managing anxiety or depression, or navigating life’s transitions, I aim to provide tools that not only address immediate concerns but also support long-term resilience. With a person-centered and strength-based approach, I’m here to help you uncover your inner resources and embrace your strengths.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe that therapy should be a collaborative and supportive process tailored to your unique needs and goals. With experience working with adolescents and adults facing challenges such as trauma, anxiety, depression, and life transitions, I understand the importance of creating a compassionate and inclusive space where you feel safe to explore and grow. Drawing on evidence-based approaches like CBT, DBT, and strength-based methods, I provide practical tools and insights to help you navigate your challenges and uncover your inner resilience. My experience working with diverse populations, including individuals navigating neurodiversity and significant mental health concerns, allows me to adapt my approach to meet you where you are. If you’re looking for someone who will listen with empathy, collaborate with you, and empower you to create meaningful progress, I’m confident we can work together to build a path toward the life you envision for yourself.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is a powerful approach that invites you to embrace your thoughts and emotions, rather than struggle against them. In our work together, you'll learn how to create space for your feelings while focusing on what truly matters to you. ACT encourages you to live in alignment with your values, even when challenges arise. Whether you're navigating anxiety, depression, or life transitions, we’ll work together to build a fulfilling life guided by your goals.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: If you’re struggling with thought patterns or behaviors that no longer serve you, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) might be the key to finding a new path forward. I specialize in CBT, a well-researched approach that focuses on identifying and changing unhelpful thoughts and behaviors. Whether you’re dealing with anxiety, depression, or other challenges, CBT can help you build a more balanced and productive mindset. Let's explore how CBT can support your journey toward meaningful change.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness-based therapy helps you cultivate awareness of your present experience, allowing you to observe your thoughts and emotions without judgment. In our sessions, we'll focus on building your ability to stay grounded in the moment, so you can approach challenges with greater clarity and intention. This practice can be helpful in managing stress, anxiety, and emotional struggles. Together, we’ll explore how mindfulness can support you in creating a more centered and purposeful life.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: Motivational Interviewing (MI) is a collaborative, goal-oriented approach that taps into your inner motivation for change. If you're feeling uncertain or ambivalent about making decisions in your life, MI can help you clarify your goals and align your actions with your values. In our sessions, we'll explore your personal reasons for change, helping you move forward with confidence and clarity. Together, we'll work to uncover the motivation that's already within you to create meaningful progress.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT) offers practical tools to help you manage intense emotions and build more balanced relationships. Whether you're dealing with emotional ups and downs, difficulty navigating conflict, or feeling disconnected, DBT can support you in finding stability. In our sessions, you'll learn skills for mindfulness, emotional regulation, and communication, empowering you to respond to life's challenges with more intention and ease. Let’s explore how DBT can help you.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Struggling with anxiety can feel overwhelming, but you don’t have to face it alone. My expertise lies in helping you manage anxiety through proven methods like Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and mindfulness. Together, we will explore the factors contributing to your anxiety, develop practical coping strategies, and build skills to regain control and find calm. Let’s work together to create a personalized plan that brings you lasting relief and renewed inner strength.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Are you experiencing sadness or a lack of motivation? Depression can make everyday tasks feel challenging and leave you feeling stuck. My specialty in treating depression involves using evidence-based approaches like Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy. Together, we will uncover the underlying causes of your depression, create effective strategies for managing concerns, and design a plan for meaningful change. Let’s foster a path toward a more fulfilling and engaged life.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have specialized training in trauma-informed care and approaches like CBT, DBT, and Collaborative Problem Solving to support clients navigating PTSD. My experience includes working with individuals processing trauma and creating safe, collaborative spaces to explore their experiences. Together, we’ll build strategies to help you manage symptoms, reconnect with your strengths, and regain a sense of control and safety in your life.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I help clients foster personal growth by creating a supportive space to explore their unique strengths, challenges, and aspirations. Drawing from mindfulness practices, creative therapies, and solution-focused techniques, I work with you to navigate life’s transitions, overcome obstacles, and uncover opportunities for meaningful change and self-discovery. Together, we’ll focus on building confidence and clarity as you move toward your goals.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: I support clients in building self-esteem by helping them recognize their strengths, challenge limiting beliefs, and develop a more compassionate relationship with themselves. Through mindfulness, collaborative problem-solving, and strengths-based approaches, we’ll work together to explore the factors impacting your self-esteem and create strategies to foster greater self-acceptance and confidence in your daily life.

name: Liam Woods
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I support individuals and couples in exploring what growth, healing, and trauma mean to their story and to the changes they want to make
ideal_client: My ideal clients are individuals who are curious about themselves, their lives, and what they need to release in order to feel free. They seek support in understanding and letting go of the ways in which our culture and upbringing have shaped their responses, perspectives, and their ability to feel safe and truly enjoy life. Whether through somatic work, relationship conflict resolution, parts work, or psychedelics, I love working with people who are ready to embrace change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work through a somatic and transpersonal lens, focusing on the relationship between the mind and body. I specialize in attachment, somatic awareness, processing and bringing meaning to trauma, ecotherapy, and integrating experiences of psychedelic and expanded states of consciousness. My practice is tailored to the needs of each individual, offering a warm and understanding space to share and attend to the parts of our experience that need attention and care. The offerings in my practice are for individuals and couples of all identities. They are not specific to a particular demographic but are oriented toward people who want a holistic approach that brings together attuned connection and the innate wisdom of the body. Our bodies have an inherent healing intelligence, and by letting that guide our work, we can move toward and through difficulties at a pace that is safe for you.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: A part of my practice is supporting clients in deepening their own perspective about where our culture is failing them. This perspective can be an antidote and a counterbalance to what many of us do, which is to take the failures and the toxic messaging of our culture inward and to make it mean that we are in some way damaged, different, unworthy, or simply not trying hard enough. This story we are being told is based in capitalism, patriarchy, and colonialism. In therapy we can create a space to challenge these stories of unworthiness and disconnection. When we share them and the way they impact us in a safe and intimate setting we begin to unravel them and to break their power over us. We as humans are meant to be in connection, to share, and to be seen in both our joys and our wounding. It is my privilege to provide the connection and presence to that allows people to be seen in their wounding and to begin to believe that they are not not damaged, different, or unworthy.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I specialize in helping individuals and couples understand their attachment patterns and take concrete steps toward developing secure attachment. Attachment plays a central role in most romantic relationships, as well as in many family and close friendship dynamics. While much of the existing literature on attachment focuses on identifying these patterns, it often falls short in providing practical tools and strategies to work through attachment issues and foster earned secure relationships.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: One of my areas of passion is couples therapy and relational conflict. With the right support and container, conflict can be an incredible path to deeper intimacy. I specialize in helping couples move through blame and criticism and into greater trust and understanding. I often support clients experiencing triggers and reactivity, sexual issues, attachment conflict, and difficulty communicating.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: IFS (Internal Family Systems) is an incredible modality that helps us better understand our many parts and discover what they are trying to protect us from. "Parts Work" allows us to navigate and understand our conflicting needs and impulses. I love using IFS as a framework to foster understanding and non-judgment toward these parts. In a culture where self-criticism and self-hatred are so prevalent, IFS offers a powerful counterbalance— a way to gently facilitate change rather than force it.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: Hakomi somatic therapy helps us connect with the sensations, emotions, and intuitions within our bodies. Deepening and exploring these connections can be transformative in many ways— from gaining a clearer understanding of our emotions, so we can care for or communicate them in real time, to accessing deep intuition about our needs, what our bodies truly want, and what we might need to heal. Stepping out of our thoughts and into our bodies is often a powerful catalyst for change and growth.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: I find great fulfillment in supporting clients as they explore or deepen their connection to the mystery of life, whether through spirituality, psychedelics, or ceremonial practices. I believe that connecting to something greater than ourselves can be profoundly transformative and should always be approached with care, respect, and a sense of wonder.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is the embodiment of fear—a signal from our body that we are experiencing a lack of safety. Working with anxiety in the body provides a deeper, more nuanced understanding of what needs to be addressed, whether it’s nervous system healing, trauma, relationship conflict, or the impact of excessive technology. For me, anxiety has been a generational inheritance and a lifelong practice of discerning where to make changes in my life and where to work through fear in order to recognize safety.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: One of my areas of passion is couples therapy and relational conflict. With the right support and container, conflict can be an incredible path to deeper intimacy. I specialize in helping couples move through blame and criticism and into greater trust and understanding. I often support clients experiencing triggers and reactivity, sexual issues, attachment conflict, and difficulty communicating.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is a pathway to a deeper understanding of ourselves and what we truly care about. I encourage anyone who has not yet had the opportunity to sit with their grief—whether in therapy or, even better, in a grief ceremony—to do so. In these spaces, you can grieve, release, and be held in community. Grief can be a gift that brings connection, wisdom, and growth. It is a powerful force that our culture does not teach us the has value.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in helping men redefine what masculinity can be. As men we can work to strip away the conditioning that keeps us isolated and that makes us feel that the empowerment of other men, women, and different cultures is a threat to us. In the retreats, workshops, and individual sessions that I lead for men, we work to understand what this conditioning has stolen from us and how to rediscover healthy masculinity and the healing it can bring to ourselves, our families, and everyone around us

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Spirituality, psychedelics, and ceremonial work have been foundational in my own healing and awakening process. Through these experiences, I’ve learned the importance of having a guide or support as we explore our relationship with ourselves, spirituality, and our core beliefs. I love supporting clients who are eager to explore or deepen their connection with the mystery—whether through prayer, psychedelics, breathwork, or religious community.

name: Jordan Ashford
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi! :) I am a person-centered therapist, I aim to create a supportive, nonjudgmental space where clients feel seen and supported!
ideal_client: In my practice, I welcome individuals who are open to exploring their thoughts and behaviors in a supportive, nonjudgmental environment. These clients are seeking understanding and empathy while also being willing to collaborate on identifying and challenging negative patterns. Together, we focus on building resilience, developing coping skills, and fostering positive change in their lives. I especially enjoy working with an older population and teens!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Being a counselor for me means being that safe space for somebody who is struggling with the way they view themselves and the world around them. I want someone to walk away from sitting with me and feel like they were truly seen and celebrated. I want them to feel empowered and like they are capable of getting through the things they're struggling with.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I always knew I would end up in a helping profession but as I got older I realized I loved talking to people about feelings and why they thought about things the way they did. I loved hearing about people relationships and where they felt like they really flourished and where they felt like their growth edges were. I loved hearing about peoples fears and what scares them, and then what gives them life and fills their cup. Every aspect of our lives is valuable and important and the conversations held in the therapy room are the types of conversations I love having with people. Its an honor to be trusted with these things and to feel that in a place of invisibility, you are seen.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Abuse & domestic violence

name: Noha Mostafa
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome! Areas of Focus: anxiety, grief, loss, PTSD, chronic stress, transitions, relational difficulties.
ideal_client: If you experience anxiety, grief, transitions or trauma and you value working with a therapist who co-explores origins of current difficulties and help you move towards durable outcomes without pathologizing your experience, you are welcome to reach out. I use a whole person and culturally responsive approach to help adults who work, study and / or live in highly demanding or stressful environments access more aliveness, presence and connection to what/who they care about.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Using a well rounded approach to wellbeing, I co-craft with each client every counseling session as a "1 hour retreat" from daily stressful cycles and an opportunity to experience meaningful presence and real aliveness. I hope that when strengths and inner resources are more intentionally accessed; and when patterns of relating to self and others as well as identity related aspects are compassionately and honestly confronted, sustainable therapeutic outcomes can be facilitated. I see humans as parts of larger structures and systems that constantly impact their health. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor Associate (LPC) with the Oregon Board of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists, a National Certified Counselor (NCC) and registered in the EMDR International Association as an emdria certified therapist who also offers consultation hours to EMDR trained clinicians working towards their certification and to clinicians completing their EMDR basic training requirements.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I enjoy working with people who hope to optimize their health and increase the capacity to be present for what they care about. Prior to becoming a therapist, my work as a "master certified" health coach focused on educating and coaching professionals and caregivers on sustainable nutrition, movement, lifestyle and mindset habits for optimal health. As a certified teacher of mindfulness based somatic practice since 2010, my work with clients navigating chronic imbalances has been focused on actualizing their hopes to expand their potential and feel free from unhelpful patterns related to undetected past memories and environmental stressors. While each therapeutic journey is meant to patiently meet clients' minds, bodies and hearts where they are at, the majority of the clients I work with can refine the regulation skills and wellness practices learnt during sessions and conclude their therapeutic experience feeling confident in their capacity to sustain their therapeutic gains.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy is a psychotherapy method that uses a technique called bilateral stimulation to repeatedly activate opposite sides of the brain to facilitate healing. The form of bilateral stimulation used in EMDR therapy is determined based on each person's capacities and can take place using tactile or auditory stimulation instead of eye movement. EMDR has been useful for a variety of conditions including PTSD, anxiety and relational difficulties.

specialities.name: Panic
specialities.description: Does it feel as if anxiety and panic can ambush your body anytime no matter how hard you try to stop them? Nervousness, restlessness, panic or dread, rapid breathing or hyperventilation, increased or heavy sweating, trembling or muscle twitching, difficulty focusing or thinking can be symptoms of anxiety. You are invited to request an initial consult, learn about individual and group therapy and hear your symptoms as invitations for new healing experiences and true aliveness.

name: Xan Scott
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Xan is an avid lover of the arts and outdoors and is passionate about working with individuals ready to make a change.
ideal_client: Therapy can be a revitalizing experience where, together, we can unpack our worries, listen to our bodies, and practice tools for calming and centering when difficult issues arise. I have years of experience working with families in crisis and transitions and am confident in my abilities to listen and find ways to heal that work individually with your needs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Xan has multiple degrees in Theatre Arts and yoga and has decades of experience working in home caregiving. Working with various populations like incarcerated women, domestic violence, and vulnerable youth Xan has life experience that you cannot go to school for. Through studying the arts Xan knows the power firsthand of sharing your story. Therapy sessions with the right fit of client to counselor can be full of fun and emotional exploration. Sharing stories of deep-seated secrets frees our internal pressure of "doing things right" and we can start showing up for ourselves including regulating our bodies and nervous systems. Xan herself experienced wanting to be seen as "normal," whatever "normal" is since she can remember. Everyone is unique and deserves to be listened to deeply in a judgment-free space.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I became a counselor after years of fellow students and clients generously sharing all of their grief and heartache on the stage. Looking around the room at my fellow teachers and performers I thought to myself, "Who is in charge here?" How does the healing continue after they leave the stage, workshop, and classroom? I am a firm believer in arts in education and the power of play! In a world with building pressure and high expectations, we need more time to slow down and connect with ourselves and others. It is easy to become isolated and stuck in an anxiety/depression cycle and realize that we are not living but merely surviving and watching time go by. I truly love helping people learn to find what they love to do that involves community. Learning to love yourself and find more compassion and curiosity is the recipe for success. Xan lives with her adopted shelter cat Merlin who teaches her daily the power of love can heal the most traumatic circumstances.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: Xan believes in a holistic, mindful, body-centered approach to counseling. Learning the language of our bodies and being aware of when we are dysregulated is paramount to learning to love ourselves and access the support we need from within. Through various exercises with the body, we can explore what works uniquely for you.

name: Clara Villalobos Andino
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Supporting you as you explore, adapt, and grow in your relationship to yourself and loved ones. I work with teens and adults. Bilingual.
ideal_client: As a therapist, I am a firm believer that all people have the ability to learn, adapt and grow through their relationship to themselves, and others, in compassionate and productive ways. I believe that each client knows their lived experience best and that there is inherent value in understanding larger societal forces that affect our interactions, relationships and lives. As a multilingual and multicultural person, I provide culturally relevant therapy and facilitate a sustainable, non-judgment

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I focus on trauma work, supporting new parents, addressing women’s issues, and providing couples and family therapy. I work with a diverse community of clients, always focusing on creating a safe, inclusive, and supportive space for healing and growth. I am direct and compassionate in my approach—I won’t provide the answers, but I will help you discover them. Whether working with individuals, couples, or families, I believe in the power of collaboration, empathy, and respect for each client’s unique lived experience. I approach therapy from a narrative and emotionally focused lens, guiding clients to explore and reframe their life stories while deepening their emotional connections and understanding of their experiences. I also offer walk-and-talk therapy, integrating the environment as a natural part of our sessions. In addition, I use Mentalization-Based Narrative Exposure Therapy (MBNET), a powerful method for processing trauma.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Originally from Argentina, I migrated to California as a teenager and have a rich background in agriculture, both as an educator and a small-scale farm owner. My experiences in farming deepened my appreciation for the interconnectedness of our humanity with the environments we inhabit and how these relationships shape us throughout our lives. This perspective informs my therapeutic practice and enriches the work I do with clients. I have a Masters in family, couples, and marriage therapy with a focus on ecopsychology.

name: Michael Morales
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Greetings! I’m Michael. I’m a couples counselor, a first-generation Filipino-American, and a purveyor of hope.
ideal_client: You’re looking for a counselor because you’re stuck and need help now. Relationship issues are my specialty and we can work on them in individual or couple counseling. Topics like intimacy, unmet needs, trust, safety, and the inability to resolve past conflicts. What you need is a safe space to share and work through these concerns–some of which you’ll share for the very first time. And you’ll do it because you’re motivated to work for the betterment of yourself, your partner, and your family.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: People often ask me–after sharing about their situation–if I have any hope for them. The answer is: I always have hope! But it’s not unfounded. It comes from years of experience and the success I’ve seen using research-based treatment methods. I prefer to use the Gottman Method, Emotion-Focused Therapy, and Interpersonal Neurobiology as our foundation. As we do the work together, we may find that additional tools, techniques, or outside professional support are needed. I expect to work with couples for an average of 3-4 months (10-15 weekly sessions). As you put in the effort, you will begin to see shifts in your relationship within the first two months (8 sessions) of treatment. This is when the "average couple" begins to make and maintain meaningful changes. As a result, their hope for sustaining change and their confidence in getting "unstuck" from past and future problems grows. And just like that–we’re talking about how we want to continue or conclude our work together.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Every couple is different, and we’ve all got our unique preferences and communication styles, so I can’t promise I’ll be the best fit for you. Just like shopping for a car, you can do all kinds of research, but you never know which one is right until you take it for a test drive. That’s why I offer free 15-minute consultations, so you can get a feel for what therapy will be like with me. There are a few things I can promise if you choose to work with me: to remain neutral and create space for you and your partner to talk through your issues. I commit to doing my best work in every session and to be honest when I have not. I will support you in the work of exercising productive communication skills in the moments that matter. Flexibility and responsiveness to your unique needs will be the hallmarks of the work I do with you. We’ll definitely get along if you also hail from California, are a covert coffee snob, shed tears for bygone pets, and wish Ted Lasso was a real person.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I have found this method blends a great mixture of scientific research on relationship as well as the therapists lived experience and ability to ply their craft. It gives structure to treatment to those couples that benefit from structure (think topics to talk about in session and homework afterwards) as well as the flexibility to address immediate themes that arise during the week leading up to the therapy session. I typical use this method for about 80% of the couples that I see.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: For many of us, our first years of life can influence how we interact with our chosen intimate partners and family members today. In counseling, we will explore how those early experiences have created a kind of relational framework that informs how you relate to yourself (think self-esteem issues) and others (think conflict resolution styles). We will also explore how you learned to resolve conflict and get your needs met (think safety, connection, or feeling empowered).

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: There are times where you have a sense that something is off but cannot quite put a finger on it. You are not alone! In treatment we may explore underlying issues or the "roots" that continue to support habits, behaviors, or ways of thinking you have been wanting to change. Throughout our work together we will highlight how these past unconscious thoughts, beliefs, or principals continue to shape how you make meaning and move about in your world.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Using this framework, we will help you understanding how your perceptions, thoughts, feelings, and actions interconnect and impact your understanding and ability to address the concerns you hope to address in your life. This type of treatment typically includes assigning "homework" to promote treatment progress.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Working with couples, especially in moments when everything is hitting the fan, is when I most come alive in this work. It allows me to bring all of my previous professional experience to the forefront. Working with youth in crisis (foster care, in-home, and community-based mental health), individuals in group homes (mental health and developmental needs), and a variety of agencies has prepared me for the range of challenges that surface in the couple relationship. It’s where I do my best work.

name: Sophie Blauer
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hello! I am glad you are here and considering me as your therapist. I will respond to all therapy inquires within 24 hours.
ideal_client: Compassion, support, and empowerment are at the center of my practice. I work from a holistic, client-centered perspective and through a collaborative process. Using an eclectic approach helps me apply techniques that best apply to your personal history and goals set in therapy. I am passionate about teaching effective coping skills, providing psychoeducation, guiding the adjustment of unstable thoughts and behaviors, working through trauma, and meeting goals to live a higher quality of life.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I work with teens, adults, and couples, and specialize in anxiety, ADHD, and relationship issues. I practice from a mindful, strengths-based approach, and I provide a safe, warm environment that is conducive toward you achieving your goals.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Our mental health can impact all aspects of life. I look forward to starting this mental health journey together, and working collaboratively with you to increase your overall well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: People usually come to therapy because life isn’t working, they feel stuck, or because they want something to shift. Having a non-judgmental, supportive space to think through what feels wrong can be helpful. We are able to make new meaning when someone listens, helps us focus in on what is important, understands our challenges, and grasps who we really are. We begin to understand our own stories and become able to shed new light on older, outdated narratives. We untangle from the repetitive pain we impose on our selves, family, partners, friends, and begin to take charge of our lives. I help people to understand and change long standing behaviors, recover hope and self-confidence, become more self reflective, work through difficult feelings, come to terms with past losses and traumas, find new independence, and improve relationships with their selves and others.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I work with each of my patients as individually as possible because our culture, race, personal history and unique attributes shape who we are. Every person is different. A successful therapy works best when designed to fit you and your needs. Prior to starting my private practice I worked with a wide diversity of people in a variety of mental health settings including high schools, a suicide hotline, a mobile crisis team, adolescent foster care, a prison facility, and in medical clinics. I also have experience in residential construction/home restoration, as a musician, and a lifelong athlete. These different experiences all inform my approach as a therapist.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: I have years of experience utilizing depth therapy to help people address complex and longstanding problems to make positive changes. Depth therapy is a non-pathologizing way to focus our attention, curiosity and active imagination to make meaning of themes, dreams, and in-the-moment associations we have to early life experiences as fundamental aspects influencing us here and now.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I will remain present and actively available to help my clients develop an understanding of themselves so that they are better able to experience psychological well being through growth fostering relationships.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: My three years of post-graduate training in psychodynamic oriented psychotherapy (The Psychotherapy Institute, Berkeley) helped me to develop my attention to support my clients to work through unconscious content and make real and lasting changes.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Masculinity, emotional vulnerability, anger, self-respect, intimacy, courage, and reason. I offer a space to examine what that might mean in your life.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I have a lot of experience helping people with grief and past trauma. There is no grief like the grief that does not speak. -Henry Wordsworth

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have a lot of experience helping people to successfully cope with mild to severe anxiety. People with anxiety often experience: Restlessness or feeling on edge, difficulty falling or staying asleep, intrusive thoughts, fear and panic, indecisiveness, difficulty concentrating, muscle tension, irritability

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can feel both painful and overwhelming. Someone suffering with depression may also feel their experience is misunderstood (or unseen) by others around them. If you feel stuck in your depression it is important for you to seek help.

name: Kate Reece
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I believe psychotherapy is designed to set a person free. I offer expertise and a warm, conversational style to support you and your goals.
ideal_client: ​I specialize in working with adolescents and adults struggling with anxiety and depression, and families engaged in patterns of unhealthy relationships and interactions. Through my work in group homes, schools, a psychiatric hospital, community mental health center, in-home, and private practice, I learned to effectively treat those struggling with symptoms related to trauma, relational difficulties, emotional and behavioral challenges, and family conflict.​

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My style is down to earth, warm, and supportive. I believe my clients should control as much of their treatment as possible. I honor an individual's vision of their journey and act as a guide to help them meet their goals. I also offer challenges and strategies to help clients achieve emotional and mental wellness in ways they had not considered before. My background is in attachment and family structural therapy. I believe individuals are deeply affected by their first attachment relationships, and the relationships they form later in life play a part in both their successes and difficulties. I utilize cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) techniques, mindfulness techniques, dialectal behavioral therapy (DBT), and motivational interviewing to promote change and healing. Therapy is a process of growth. I provide a judgment-free environment that encourages self-expression, cognitive and emotional transformation, and self-awareness.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Helping others discover peace, connection, and confidence in the face of turmoil has long been a passion of mine. I believe everyone is capable of growth and healing if they are provided sufficient encouragement, support, and effective strategies. I encourage clients to identify and communicate their unique needs and concerns in order to improve interpersonal relationships, manage bothersome emotions or behaviors, and develop healthier family connections. My background is in Family Structural Therapy, which places value on and examines an individual’s relationships, both past and present. This approach assesses the ways in which relationships shape people’s self-worth, how they interact with others, how they manage difficult experiences, and their emotional and mental health. My family is mixed race, and I work with a diverse array of clients. I am committed to serving as a support to those exploring their race, gender, and sexual identity.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have specialized in anxiety disorders for the duration of my career. I utilize some CBT skills, but include acceptance commitment therapy and motivational interviewing to increase a client's competency, control, and sense of peace.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Issues pertaining to self-esteem flood into all parts of a person's life, often negatively-effecting their relationships, jobs, and sense of competency. I have worked my entire career with young adults, adolescents, and adults to increase their understanding of their strengths, abilities, and realistic goals to improve their sense of themselves.

name: Ryja (Rylan Jay) Testa
title: Clinical Psychologist
credentials: PhD; Psychologist Licensed in OR and CA
intro: Psychologist, Spiritual Counselor, Buddhist Practitioner, Nature & Forest Therapy Guide, and Trans Man
ideal_client: Are you going through a time of major transformation or healing? This could mean a shift in gender or sexual identity, spiritual perspective, health status, career, relationship, or a recent loss. When we are thrust into the unknown, finding a new way forward can feel confusing, overwhelming, scary, or overwhelming. You might be unsure of what to do next or worry you have lost your way, or find it hard to trust you will be okay. I specialize in working with people navigating major change.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My combined personal and professional paths uniquely prepare me to guide others through times of unknown. I offer counseling based on: - over a decade professional experience as a clinical psychologist - over two years of full-time residential training at a Zen monastery - certification as a Nature and Forest Therapy Guide (anft.earth) - certification in ministry and Depth Hypnosis (developed by Isa Gucciardi, PhD.; sacredstream.org) - personal experience healing my own nervous system from burnout, mold toxicity, and dysautonomia, through neural reprogramming, guided imagery, dreamwork, and creative practices - countless hours listening to the teachings of the more-than-human world - lived experience as a transgender man I walk alongside you as fellow human, having gone through my own transformations of gender, health, and spirituality. I offer you all the gifts that have been gathered through my own evolution and healing. Please see my full CV on my website, including publications.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I personalize treatment for you, using a combination of insight oriented work, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, guided meditation, dream work, forest therapy, hypnotherapy, art, movement, and music therapies. I help you connect with your deepest intentions and inner wisdom, and heal from any trauma or stuck patterns that block you from moving forward. You don't have to do the unknown alone. I walk alongside you in the mystery until you find your way to the other shore. I have particular specialized expertise the areas of gender and sexuality, spirituality, and health. If you are experiencing distress related to any of these areas, please don't hesitate to reach out for a free consultation! I would love to hear more about your journey and see how I might be of support.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: I am certified in Depth Hypnosis through Foundation of the Sacred Stream, under the guidance of Isa Gucciardi, PhD. This training is thorough and integrates transpersonal psychology, shamanism, and Buddhist philosophy. This is the primary orientation I practice in, allowing change to occur at the subconscious level and thus be integrated and influence thoughts, feelings, and behaviors across contexts. This work empowers the client and is powerful and transformative.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Over the years I have received formal training in ACT through my initial doctoral internship and followed this with additional trainings in my post-doctoral years and beyond. I have consistently used ACT integrated into my therapeutic work since 2012 and consider it to be one of my primary treatment approaches.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: I am certified as a Nature and Forest Therapy Guide, through ANFT.EARTH. This training is extensive and further requires completion of an immersion program for lifelong certification, which I did complete in 2021. I offer free forest therapy events for medical and mental health providers regularly, in effort to honor their work and prevent burnout.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: -Former Assistant Professor whose research and teaching focused on Gender Minority Stress and Resilience. -Published over 15 peer-reviewed research articles on this topic. -Author of The Gender Quest Workbook (2015) -Completed Post-Doctoral Fellowship: Sexual and Gender Identities Clinic and Center for LGBT Evidence-Based Applied Research, Palo Alto University -Prior Program Manager of the Gender Identities Program; Palo Alto University, Palo Alto, CA -Former Volunteer for The Trevor Project

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: -2 and 1/2 years living and training full-time at a Zen Buddhist monastery -Certification in Depth Hypnosis (a healing methodology that combines transpersonal psychology, shamanism, and Buddhist philosophy -Certification as a Nature and Forest Therapy Guide (therapeutic practice that explores relationship with self, others, and the more than human world, incorporating Zen Buddhist philosophy)

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: - Experience healing from and working with people healing from chronic diseases and poorly understood conditions such as chronic fatigue, multiple chemical sensitivity, mold toxicity, nervous system dysregulation/imbalance, dysautonomia, Lyme, and chronic pain - Experience working with clients with terminal illnesses - Doctoral Internship rotations in behavioral medicine - Experience providing group therapy for veterans with chronic pain and insomnia

name: Isaiah Bartlett
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a queer and trans therapist that provides attachment focused psychotherapy through an anti-oppressive lens.
ideal_client: I work primary with queer and trans communities as well as those who have experienced marginalization in any other way. I have a particular interest in working with young adults roughly ages 16-30 as this is often a time of identity development and exploration.
