I have experience working with people struggling with issues related to depression, anxiety, life transitions, gender identity, queer issues, and relationship & family challenges. ***OHP for surgery assessments not ongoing therapy***

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I draw upon interventions from psychoanalytic psychotherapy, attachment focused therapy, emotionally focused therapy, radical acceptance, and health at every size. As an attachment focused therapist, my therapeutic work with clients centers around helping people better understand how attachment wounds and early experiences of caregiving impact relationships later in life, both with ourselves and with others. I have extensive training and personal experience in psychoanalytic psychotherapy and I believe strongly in the use of transference in the therapeutic relationship. Through my own personal and professional work, I have learned that some of the most transformative and healing work can be accomplished simply by exploring our connection as therapist and client.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received my Masters in Social Work from New York University, a program known for its clinical and psychoanalytic focus. My graduate coursework allowed me to explore the intersections between psychoanalysis, queer theory, critical race theory, and their implications on clinical work. I have over ten years of experience providing therapy in community mental health agencies as a child and family therapist and have been in private practice since 2015. Outside of my work, I am a dedicated adventurer and spend as much time as I can bicycle touring, skiing, and surfing. I enjoy bringing this same enthusiasm, energy, and love of exploration into my clinical work.

name: Aaron Miller
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: As a compassionate psychologist, I help individuals, couples, and families through challenges. Specialized in trauma and abuse recovery.
ideal_client: As a compassionate clinical psychologist, I understand that life's journey can be challenging. The weight of daily struggles and the echoes of past events can sometimes become overwhelming, leaving you feeling adrift in a sea of confusion, stress, and exhaustion. It's okay to acknowledge these feelings – they're a natural part of being human. However, it's also important to know that you don't have to face them alone.

approaches.How I Can Help You: In times of uncertainty and turmoil, psychotherapy offers a path towards clarity, freedom, and relief. It's not just a tool for navigating difficulties; it's a gateway to self-discovery and growth during life's transitions. With nearly two decades of experience, I've had the privilege of walking alongside individuals, couples, and families as they navigate relationship challenges, work-related worries, personal losses, and the twists and turns of life's journey. One of my areas of expertise lies in guiding individuals through the aftermath of trauma and abuse. I've undergone extensive advanced training to provide the specialized care needed to heal and rebuild after such experiences. Your pain is valid, and together, we can work towards finding strength, healing, and renewal.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We humans have an innate drive towards growth and health and expansion. Over time and throughout life, this natural drive is often hampered through difficult experiences and problematic "lessons" we learn from others. When this occurs, we become cut-off from our experiences, cut off from our hopes, cut-off and cut-off from ourselves. Over the past 20 years in the mental health field, I have worked broadly with children, adolescents, adults, and families. This has included work in psychiatric day treatment programs, community mental health from our needs, cut-off from ourselves, and cut-off from others. Unfortunately, this process is often less-than-conscious and occurs outside of our awareness, leaving us bored, dissatisfied, isolated, stuck, anxious, and depressed. As a therapist, I work hard to co-create an ongoing dialogue with my clients in which they can safely become aware of their experiences, hopes, needs, and desires without fear of judgement.

name: Robert Field
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I specialize in diagnostic evaluations of children, adolescents and adults and individual therapy for adolescents and adults.
ideal_client: Those who are experiencing learning struggles, emotional and social difficulties and need the proper diagnosis to identify problems and develop appropriate interventions. Concerns whether ADHD, autism, learning disabilities or anxiety are answered through the evaluation. Clients and family attend an initial session to review history and talk about perceptions of the problem. Based on concerns, Dr. Field will guide the family to provide a thorough history and develop the assessment tests.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Before one can receive effective treatment, a better idea of what are the basis of the problems and how to best help need to be established. If there are school related issues, Dr. Field will assist to develop interventions with school staff. Dealing with emotional issues, specific recommendations are made for the best therapeutic approach and if social issues exist, specific approaches will be recommended to fit the issues at hand. After more than 40 years of providing services and developing innovative therapeutic approaches (www.questcamps.com), Dr Field is best suited to provide a correct assessment.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My motivation to become a psychologist was based on my desire to "heal the world". Tikun Olam is the hebrew phrase of putting a priority of helping others and fixing injustices and help reduce pain. I have worked with thousands of families while in practice in Danville, CA and continue to be motivate to continue.

specialities.name: Psychological Testing and Evaluation
specialities.description: With diagnostic background in a variety of cognitive, academic, learning disability diagnostic, emotional and social assessments, I can provide a thorough understanding of the nature of the problems and best interventions. A comprehensive report with specific treatment recommendations, school interventions and accommodations for school is provided.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Providing an accurate differential diagnosis of ADHD is more complicated than sending out rating forms to parents and teachers. It requires direct observation of an individual on a cognitive test to assure the proper diagnosis. Many symptoms of anxiety are very similar to ADHD and providing the wrong treatment can be harmful to the individual.

name: Jaxon Shaffer
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Hi, I'm Jaxon; I respect that you are here. My practice focuses on support and healing for LGBTQ+ people and other underrepresented groups.
ideal_client: Are you looking to process trauma? Gender? Figure out what flavor of neurodivergent you are and the best ways to cope? Maybe you are in a relationship with complex identity intersectionalities that needs support. I specialize in working with gender-diverse youth and adults, queer couples, those with insecure attachment, introverts, and neurodivergent folks. I support clients grappling with minority stress, facing unique challenges and societal pressures that exacerbate mental health struggles.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I consider the therapist/client relationship sacred and personal. I believe that the relationship and dynamics in the therapy room are of the most essential mediums for change. With this, I bring immediacy to my engagement with clients. Using immediacy means that clients can expect for me, at times, to reveal how I am feeling in response to them. This approach focuses attention on the here-and-now relationship of therapist and client with intentional timing to challenge defensiveness and/or heighten awareness of patterns of relating to others outside the therapy room. If you are looking to process trauma, I am trained in and use a modality called Narrative Exposure Therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a non-binary trans-masculine clinician, I am dedicated to helping clients who are transgender, non-binary, agender, gender expansive, or clients who are questioning their gender identity. Understanding that so many of us have been harmed by the medical system (including therapists), I first and foremost strive to create a therapeutic relationship that feels safe and welcoming. Secondly, I am passionate about guiding my clients through their journey with gender: establishing a strong sense of self, coming out, dealing with challenging family responses and dynamics, considering or maintaining physical interventions to treat dysphoria, navigating educational and medical systems or/or workplaces, learning to cope with and exist within a cis and heteronormative society. Thirdly, it is essential that my clients feel as though their gender IS NOT a problem to be solved and is not the sole focus of therapy.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: My training at Lewis and Clark Graduate School was grounded in family therapy through a social justice lens. I work with couples, families and individuals from a relational framework, this means seeing a person as a culmination of the relationships and social systems that they are and have been a part of. I consider family of origin, dysfunctional cycles, self in the context of a family unit, attachment development, intersecting identities, diagnosis (if desired), and much more.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I work with couples of all genders and sexual orientations to overcome barriers to healthy connection through a blend of Emotionally Focused Couples Therapy, Queer Theory, and the Gottman Method. "EFT focuses on emotions and emotional communication in relationships and their influence on patterns of interaction. It also recognizes emotion as a powerful agent of change rather than simply part of the relationship problem."

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: My approach to healing is rooted in an ecosystemic, social justice framework. This means that when working with individuals, couples, or families, I am considering how each individual person’s context, culture and relationship dynamics impact their thoughts, perspectives, emotions, behaviors, and symptoms. To find healthier ways of processing, CBT focuses on identifying and changing negative thought patterns and behaviors.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: MI is a counseling approach designed to help people explore and resolve ambivalence about behavior change. It's particularly effective in addressing addictive behaviors, but it's also used to address a variety of "stuck" and/or problematic ongoing behaviors. In MI, we focus on exploring your values, goals, and concerns.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I specialize in working with PTSD, using Narrative Exposure Therapy (NET) to help clients process and integrate traumatic experiences. NET is an evidence-based approach that supports individuals in making sense of their life story, reducing distress, and fostering resilience. With extensive training in NET, I guide clients in structuring their narratives to reprocess trauma, regain agency, and move toward healing.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: Gender identity and gender exploration is the main focus of my work. I have experience working with children, teens and adults who are questioning their gender, going through gender transitioning, or just needing a safe space to discuss life as a gender non-conforming person. I have received academic training on working with gender non-conforming folks as well as my personal life experience.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: As a Marriage and Family Therapist Associate, my training and practice are heavily rooted in relationship dynamics of all kinds, from family of origin, to romantic relationships, to friendships, to relationship with ourselves. I enjoy working with couples and families as well as individuals who are struggling with, or are looking to strengthen their relationships. The modalities I use are rooted in attachment and are emotionally focused.

specialities.name: Social Phobia
specialities.description: Social anxiety or social phobia is a primary focus of my work, particularly in teenagers, helping them navigate fears of judgment, embarrassment, and exposure. Social anxiety is often rooted in self-esteem challenges, and I use evidence-based approaches to build confidence, develop coping strategies, and foster meaningful connections.

name: Sarah Curts
title: Student Counselor
intro: I am a counseling intern with 15 years of experience in Somatic Re-Education Therapy, Mindfulness, and Internal Martial Arts.
ideal_client: Trauma has an impact not just on the mind but on somatic experiences in the body. I offer a holistic approach that accounts for how thoughts, emotions, and physical sensations interact and feed off each other. By addressing the entire system, I am able to help individuals, couples, and families unwind from the trauma that has limited their well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In Somatic Re-Education Therapy, injury is treated as an incomplete action. The body and mind hold tension patterns out of an effort to "do" something. This approach helps the system complete the action it has been stuck in and thus release the pain that has been held onto. By offering awareness, acceptance, and guiding support, I help clients recognize the unmet needs of their pain, and how to address them so long-held problems release.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a deep spiritual background that informs my practice. Through the study of internal martial arts and mindfulness meditation, I have come to understand how our thoughts and beliefs shape our lives and how by working on the subtle level, big changes can occur.

name: Katya Stark
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer an engaged, dynamic approach to help clients break patterns and build fulfilling lives and relationships.
ideal_client: I work with individuals and couples—both monogamous and polyamorous—who are navigating relationships, emotional processing, and life transitions. My clients appreciate an active, engaged approach to therapy and are open to being challenged in a supportive environment. My clients seek self-awareness, meaningful growth, and deeper connections. They are ready to explore entrenched patterns, develop emotional resilience, and shift unhelpful relational dynamics.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a deeply engaged, intuitive, and experiential therapist who thrives on curiosity, emotional depth, and meaningful transformation. My work is dynamic and immersive, fostering deep self-exploration and real-world application. My immersive and interactive approach guides clients toward deep insight and meaningful, lasting change. My clients appreciate an approach that is both structured and fluid—offering the safety of guidance while encouraging self-directed discovery. They seek therapy that is engaging, thought-provoking, and capable of initiating true change. I balance warmth with directness, creating a space where clients can confront deep-seated patterns, reframe limiting beliefs, and cultivate more fulfilling ways of thinking, feeling, and connecting. My therapeutic style is active and experiential. I incorporate somatic awareness, relational dynamics, and emotional processing to help clients recognize patterns and make lasting shifts.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in transformation that arises from deep self-reflection, self-compassion, and the willingness to challenge internalized narratives and external limitations. My values are rooted in equity, autonomy, and emotional integrity, guiding me to create a space where clients feel seen, heard, and empowered. I am committed to anti-racist, anti-oppressive work and strive to dismantle systemic barriers that restrict self-expression and relational healing. I hold a deep respect for human complexity and the power of connection in fostering growth. I value intellectual curiosity, authenticity, and the courage to explore life beyond conventional norms. As a queer immigrant, I have experienced reinvention and resilience, shaping my ability to support those navigating identity, belonging, and personal evolution. My approach encourages exploration, challenges limiting beliefs, and fosters a life aligned with one’s deepest truths and aspirations.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I help couples break recurring patterns, improve communication, and foster intimacy. My approach integrates Gestalt therapy, the Developmental Model of Couples Relationships, and Imago Relationship Therapy. Through experiential techniques, structured dialogue, and deep exploration of relational dynamics, I help partners understand each other beyond surface conflicts. I support couples in unpacking past influences, including attachment styles and family-of-origin patterns.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a queer-affirming counselor, I understand the extra pressures and challenges LGBTQIA+ folks face. I focus on processing religious trauma, fear of rejection, minority stress, and the negative impact of heteronormativity, cisnormativity, internalized homophobia, and minority stress on mental health. As a polyamory-affirmative counselor, I am dedicated to expanding my knowledge and counseling skills to work with people in polyamorous relationship structures.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: As a queer therapist, I help partners navigate relational challenges, deepen trust, and foster meaningful connections. Committed to ongoing education, I actively expand my expertise in working with non-traditional relationship structures. Currently training at the Queer Relationship Institute, I specialize in supporting queer, non-traditional partnerships and complex relational dynamics, ensuring my approach is informed, inclusive, and affirming.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: My approach integrates somatic awareness and relational dynamics, allowing clients to recognize how anxiety manifests in their bodies and relationships. Using Gestalt techniques and mindfulness-based interventions, I guide clients in shifting from overthinking to embodied presence, fostering a sense of grounding and control. I challenge unhelpful thought patterns while providing practical tools for emotional regulation, helping clients regain confidence in their ability to navigate uncertainty.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I provide affirming space to explore sexuality and gender identity and to process how that may be implicated in relationships with family, friends, intimate partner violence, and sexual trauma. I enjoy working with genderqueer, non-binary, gender-fluid, and gender-nonconforming folks and provide letters to support gender-affirming related care access.

name: Stephanie Avery
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Ready to move toward growth, healing, and wellbeing? Let's go!
ideal_client: I am a holistic therapist who loves working with those who are interested in moving deeper into their healing process and exploring their inner landscapes. I find in person therapy is be very powerful, and it is my favorite to provide, but I am happy to offer telehealth as well. Through promoting curiosity and values-driven action, experiencing safe and supportive connection, and practicing wellness techniques, we can work, together, toward building you a more meaningful life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My practice, Coastal Trails Holistic Counseling, provides integrative therapy to support you on your journey toward growth and wellbeing. To view treatment holistically is to take into account physical, emotional, mental, social, cultural, and spiritual dimensions. I use a combination of Internal Family Systems (IFS), Narrative Therapy, Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT), and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) to assist in exploration and integration of thoughts, body sensations, and emotions while also helping you move toward positive change. To learn more about these approaches, see the Techniques and Specialties section below.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in the restorative power of therapy, nature, spirituality, and creativity. I have lived experience with chronic health issues, grief and loss, and intercultural experiences and relationships which lends me a unique perspective as well as deep compassion and understanding toward the myriad life challenges that each of us face. My personal joys and interests include reading, writing, painting, cooking, and exploring our beautiful, natural world. I also have a sweet tuxedo cat that makes occasional appearances during telehealth sessions. I'd love to get to know you and speak with you further about your personal goals for therapy. Are you interested in navigating big life transitions or current challenges? Exploring new aspects of your identity? Discovering and committing to passions and pursuits? Healing childhood wounds, or changing current relationship dynamics for the better? Feel free to get in touch to schedule a free 20 minute consultation.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Person-Centered/Humanistic Therapy is how I show up to our sessions, always bringing unconditional positive regard, empathy, and personal authenticity.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy focuses on reducing feelings of distress through mindfulness techniques, acceptance of what is both in our control and out of our control, and refocusing on the things that are most important to us so that we can live more fulfilling value-driven lives.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotionally Focused Therapy is based on research related to attachment and bonding, focusing on the healing power of meaningful connection, safety in relationship, and vulnerability. Coming from an attachment perspective, I may address what is emotionally happening between the two of us, including tough feelings like disappointment, rejection, or anger. This can help clients practice authenticity and gain insight into relationship dynamics that are occurring outside of the therapy space.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Parts Work (Internal Family Systems) includes the stance that there is an inherently good, wise, and health-seeking core Self to each person. It says that we are also made up of multiple other parts (inner critic, inner parent, inner perfectionist, etc.) and that these parts get trapped in behaviors and thought patterns from the past that no longer serve us. The goal in Parts Work is to help those parts “take a break” and instead be led by our core wise Self.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Narrative Therapy examines the myriad stories we carry with us that influence our present day lives. Some of our stories are known, some of them are hidden, and some are waiting for an opportunity to be brought to life. Through Narrative Therapy, I help clients experience their life stories in new ways that are both meaningful and fulfilling.When we are able to bear witness to our stories and discover their complexity through exploration, that is when we have a true opportunity to grow.

name: Nadya Mirza
title: Student Counselor
intro: I work with children ages three and up, teens, adults and couples dealing with traumatic experiences, loss, depression or anxiety, shame.
ideal_client: I welcome individuals of all ages, couples, and families seeking to overcome life's challenges and live wholesome lives. My primary focus is to help clients navigate through everyday stresses and developmental milestones as they deal with difficult decisions, emotional dysregulation, depression, anxiety, relationship difficulties, and challenges in parenting. I am bilingual and offer services in both English and Russian.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Every client has a unique and valuable story that offers a glimpse into their journey through life. It is a privilege for me to listen to and to try to understand these experiences, whatever they may be – stress, anxiety, depression, struggle with finding one's identity, trauma, shame, or difficulty with relationships. As you make important decisions in navigating those challenges, I would be honored to support you in exploring your inner strengths and finding additional resources that foster hope, resilience, and a sense of purpose, including but not limited to family bonds, community, meaningful activities, past accomplishments, and spirituality.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Life is full right now, but I love every minute of it. I enjoy spending time with my family and pets, traveling, camping, playing board games, listening to audiobooks, and cross-stitching in my free time.

name: Leanne Bergman
title: Student Counselor
intro: I support children, individuals, couples, and families navigating anxiety, trauma, and parenting.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with children through play therapy and supporting individuals, couples, and families dealing with anxiety, trauma, and parenting challenges. My approach is person-centered and trauma-informed, drawing from attachment theory. I incorporate trauma-informed techniques that support nervous system regulation, resourcing and healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe healing happens within safe and supportive relationships. Whether supporting a child in play therapy or helping parents strengthen their connection with their child, I offer a space where clients feel seen, valued, and understood. My approach is warm, nonjudgmental, and rooted in connection, helping clients build resilience and deeper self-awareness.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: The foundation of my work is the belief that every person (child or adult) deserves to feel understood, accepted, and supported. I bring warmth, curiosity, and deep respect for each individual’s experience, creating a space where healing and growth can unfold. Check out our website to schedule a 15 minute consultation to see if we're the right fit.

name: L Pearson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: "I am because we are.”—Ubuntu.
ideal_client: I believe in the utmost importance of relationship with self, friends, family, partners, lovers, community, and the spaces we occupy. Each of these connections influence and inform our well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My intention is to create an authentic, non-judgmental, safe environment in which I can join you on your journey of self-compassion, exploration, restoration, and growth. I have specialized training and experience in a number of therapeutic modalities and techniques such as: mindfulness, psychodynamic theory, DBT, attachment theory, motivational interviewing, and trauma-informed care. However, there is no one approach that fits all. You and I will work together to develop a therapeutic relationship that provides you with the support you need to actualize your goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am passionate about living in a world that is safe for all. I strive in my practice to be sensitive to concerns regarding intersectionality, marginalization, and oppression which may include but not limited to: race, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, migration status, acculturation, ability, body size, age, social class, and alternative relationship structures. I affirm relationships of all configurations, gender identities, and sexual orientations. My work is informed by an anti-oppressive, relational-cultural, sex-positive feminist lens. I believe to understand another person one must include the context of culture. Therapy works best when one feels seen, connected, respected, and heard.

name: Congruent Therapy: Italia Hensley
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Hi, my name is Italia (she/her), and I work with individuals dealing with many different struggles and meet them where they are at.
ideal_client: I work with individuals dealing with trauma, C-PTSD, PTSD, boundaries, self-esteem, sexuality, identity, shame, anxiety, panic, negative self-talk, relational issues, family trauma, and polyamorous/CNM exploration from a systemic perspective. My work is eclectic, reflecting the diverse backgrounds, experiences, personalities, and issues of my clients. My goal is to help you find acceptance and happiness within yourself, your relationships, and your environment.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I have experience with various modalities and work with people from all walks of life. I primarily use Narrative Therapy, Humanistic approaches, Internal Family Systems, and Emotionally Focused Therapy. I also have specialized training in EFT, EFIT, IFIO, supporting LGBTQIA+, polyamorous/CNM relationships, couples, trauma survivors, and neurodivergent humans. A good fit would be someone who has the openness to take on the slow burn that therapy requires. If you’re seeking someone who is both supportive and challenging, that’s me. I'll be a secure attachment in your life that also kicks you in the butt. I work with couples, poly systems, individuals, queer and neurodivergent, using an affirmative approach with empathy, curiosity, and compassion. I am Consensual Non-Monogamy certified through The Sexual Health Alliance. I employ Emotionally Focused Couple Therapy, Narrative Therapy, IFS, and Gottman, and integrate other modalities as needed to meet clients where they are.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe that you are the expert of your life, but while I can give you insight and many tools, you're the most important factor to change and success. I’m a cis neurodivergent individual with fibromyalgia, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, and ADHD. I’m a self-made business owner, supervisor, and PhD student, as well as a cat mom, partner, and a direct and sassy person. Some of the reasons I became a therapist include childhood trauma, poverty, abuse, and feeling unsafe in my body.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I'm enrolled at The Modern Sex Therapy Institutes working on my PhD in Sexology to become a sex therapist. My goal is to expand my knowledge to help clients address sexual issues by addressing sexual desire discrepancies with their partner(s), sexual pain, challenge patriarchal views of sex, exploration of sexual identity, processing sexual trauma, find pleasure, and challenge shame narratives around sexuality. *Disclaimer, I am not a certified sex therapist, but I am being supervised for this.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I am Consensual Non-Monogamous Certified through The Sexual Health Alliance. My work with poly and consensual non-monogamous clients is centered around supporting you and your partners to create fulfilling, rewarding, safe, consensual relationships. I can help you on your journey if you are just starting to question monogamy to seasoned individuals, couples, and systems that need extra support and guidance.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: I love working with individuals around self-esteem. Self-esteem work is vital to a healthy and happy life as an individual, in a relationship, and in the workforce. Let me help you melt away societal, familial, and relational constraints getting in the way of living your most authentic and congruent life.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Supporting you in fostering healthy and happy relationships, be that individually, couple, ethically non-monogamous, or polyamory, is my bread and butter. I believe in dependency and individualism in relationships. Many people do not like the word dependent, defined as "a person who relies on another." But what is a relationship? It is "the way in which people are connected." Connection and trust are the cornerstone of this. You must have both and it is my pleasure to help you find them.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I work with many LGBTQIA2S+ around a variety of concerns. My approach is affirming and I create a safe place for you to be or learn who your authentic self is in a nonjudgmental environment. Our work is always going to be centered around empathy and safety, but also be challenging and rewarding.

name: Katelyn Bessette
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with people who are exploring their relationships and sexuality, whether monogamous or non-monogamous. I am kink friendly and sex+.
ideal_client: I have experience working with depression, anxiety, substance use disorders and borderline personality disorder. I think that the mind-body connection is essential, both in expressing desire and maintain lifelong health. I am excited to work with people who want to explore relationships, sexuality and deeper meaning. Your journey is unique and I am grateful to anyone who is willing to grow and share in that journey with me. I am open to provide supervision to LPC interns as well.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: People show up to therapy in various stages of change, and the only way to facilitate that is through meeting client's where they are at. The importance of mind-body connection is so often forgotten, and my passion is awakening this essential element of life to help people reconnect with themselves and their community. I believe sensuality and exploration of desire is essential to the full expression of who we are as human beings. I received my Master's of Counseling Psychology from Lewis and Clark College. I am a licensed professional counselor (LPC), Certified Sex Therapist (CST) and a certified alcohol and drug counselor (CADCIII). I am also formally trained in DBT and have extensive training in substance use disorders. I am also accepting LPC interns for supervision

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I began this journey wanting to provide sex therapy and start a sexuality resource center. My path diverged from this into addictions, where I have seen all the same challenges and questions arise in terms of our physical and emotional wellbeing. I have seen how sexual trauma shows up in many different areas of life, how negative coping skills can destroy our hopes and how people have endless capacity to heal. I am excited to rejoin the path to provide therapy to those seeking a deeper understanding of their relationships, their sexuality and their desires. This may include addressing past trauma, relationship difficulties and negative sense self. Whatever it is that is creating barriers for you, I am ready to start that journey with you! I know that there is a huge gap in understanding when it comes to kink and non-monogamy and because of that I am particularly passionate about providing a safe space for people to process without having to educate or feel judged.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I work closely with couples and beyond to help support them in navigating conflict resolution, infidelity, communication issues, intimacy and sexuality difficulties and more. I am a trained sex therapist.

specialities.name: Nonviolent Communication
specialities.description: I believe deeply in the power of communication and use Nonviolent Communication as the base of much of the couples work that I do.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Awareness in the present moment is key for movement toward change. Mindfulness has been the single most important concept I have learned and given to others throughout my time as a therapist and a yoga instructor.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I am trained at Level 1 in Gottman techniques.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I am formally trained in DBT and worked in a DBT intensive program.

name: Leonie Fischer-Laycock
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Now taking new clients! I work with burnout, co-dependency, anxiety, decision-making, and prolonged grief.
ideal_client: My ideal client is someone who is ready to embrace their journey toward self-discovery and healing. Whether you're navigating the challenges of burnout, depression, self-esteem, anxiety, or working to set boundaries, I'm here to support you. I am especially passionate about working with those who identify as adult children of emotionally immature parents and those that burnout through caregiving. I am LGBTQ+ affirming and body positive.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work has roots in person-centered counseling, as well as Internal Family Systems (IFS) therapy. This perspective centers each client and their experiences, perspectives, and interconnected parts in sessions. My goal is to support clients in developing a deeper understanding of their experiences and identities, and to build a stronger internal relationship with parts of themselves that they may not yet be familiar or comfortable with. I utilize Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) to help folks with decision-making and shifting how they relate with anxiety. I operate from a multicultural feminist lens, providing LGBTQ+ affirming and anti-racist care. Clients of all identities are welcome, and our time together will always include space to explore your unique lived experiences and culture.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am well versed in trauma-informed care and prioritize a fat-positive, anti-racist, and queer-affirming approach with all clients. I am grounded in social justice and advocacy, and seek to understand clients individually and within the systems they are in.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Internal Family Systems (IFS) therapy offers a compassionate and transformative approach to healing from PTSD. In IFS, we explore the different "parts" of ourselves—those that hold pain, fear, or anger as a result of trauma, and those that protect us from re-experiencing that pain. By gently guiding you to connect with and understand these parts, IFS helps to unburden the wounded parts of your psyche, allowing you to heal from past traumas.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is a mindfulness-based approach that helps individuals develop psychological flexibility. Instead of avoiding or fighting uncomfortable thoughts and feelings, ACT encourages acceptance and teaches skills to respond to these experiences in ways that align with personal values.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I use Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and Internal Family Systems (IFS) to support individuals navigating grief. With ACT, I help you make space for difficult emotions, honor your loss, and reconnect with what matters most. Using IFS, we explore the different parts of you that may feel overwhelmed, stuck, or in conflict after a loss, fostering compassion and healing within yourself.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: In treating anxiety, I use Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) to help you reclaim your life. ACT teaches you to accept anxious thoughts and feelings without letting them control your actions. This approach will help you manage anxiety effectively, allowing you to live more fully in line with your values.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: In my work with clients experiencing depression, I focus on a strengths-based approach that emphasizes your inherent resilience and capabilities. Rather than only addressing the symptoms of depression, we explore and build upon the strengths you already possess, helping you reconnect with what gives your life meaning and purpose. By identifying and nurturing these strengths, we work together to create positive changes, boost self-esteem, and foster a greater sense of hope.

name: Sean Callahan
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I've always had a tender heart and a deep curiosity about others, and I'm passionate about helping people feel more at home in themselves.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with those in helping roles, including other therapists, healers, and massage therapists, as well as artists and creatives. Those wanting to build trust in their intuition and knowing. Those wanting to incorporate somatic and/or spiritual components into therapy. People of all genders wanting a safe place to explore and work on their relationships with men and their own experiences of gender and sexuality. Those struggling to prioritize their own needs in relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am passionate about helping people feel at home in themselves. I integrate Somatic IFS and Gestalt therapies to support others in staying radically present with their experience, going beyond the stories that keep us stuck in our heads and disconnected from ourselves and each other. The intention of this work is to deepen your relationship and trust in yourself, which leads to more authentic, meaningful, and vibrant relationships with others and the world around you. Showing up as your self can be terrifying, but I believe that a meaningful life requires being valued for who you truly are. My approach is: Relational, because we come to understand ourselves through our relationships with others. Somatic, because our bodies are capable of processing information and experiences that we can’t access through thinking. Spiritually engaging, because when we don't include the human spirit, we ignore important aspects of who we are. Grounded in IFS, because it is both powerful and respectful.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: While completing a master’s degree in forest ecology, I felt overwhelmed by the disconnect between the research I was doing and the change that I hoped to see in how we care for our planet, our non-human relatives, and one another. I felt strongly that we already had enough information to know that we need to make changes, and yet everywhere I looked I saw how trapped we were in our systems and ways of being that rely on exploitation and extraction, and how many of us seemed to be struggling in those same systems. So my focus shifted towards understanding people, and what became clear is that when we experience trauma and do not have the opportunity to heal and make sense of what we’ve gone through, we pass that trauma on to others and to the world around us even as we continue to suffer ourselves. This is how I understand the way we’ve arrived where we are today, and it is why I decided that the most meaningful thing I could do is find a way to heal and help others do the same.

name: Kristi Cash White
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help people navigate anxiety and changing life stages as they reimagine their personal stories and goals for the future.
ideal_client: I help teens, adults, and the elderly who are dealing with relationship struggles, identity development, chronic pain & medical issues, anxiety, trauma, and self-harm. I endeavor to help you find your footing, so that you can face your future with greater confidence and peace of mind.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have extensive training and experience in various forms of theory and practice, which include treating each individual in a holistic manner, recognizing the importance of family and social systems in a person's growth, building on one's strengths, and seeing people as creative and social beings who need encouragement to thrive. We'll work together on establishing goals for your treatment, and we'll address what is happening in your brain and your body when you are experiencing anxiety and stress in order for you to learn how to calm your systems.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in the healing power of connection, vulnerability, and relationship. It is my desire for everyone to have access to evidence-based, excellent mental health services with a counselor who fits their particular needs. I am passionate about growing diversity within the field, researching and advocating for greater representation of minority populations in counseling and counselor education. As a lifelong Oregonian, I, like the forest mushrooms, thrive in the cool and moist climate of the Northwest. My family embraces the outdoor life of hiking, campfires, and owning more than one Subaru. I am married and actively working to launch my three children into adulthood (we don't talk enough about how difficult this process can be!). Our family practices social justice, participating in marches and community actions that support our Black neighbors, women's rights, and the LGBTQ community. I am an avid fan of the Timbers and Trail Blazers, no matter how often my heart is broken.

name: Katie Eichner
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I am a queer psychologist passionate about helping folks to improve their relationships with themselves, others, and their mental health.
ideal_client: Clients often tell me that our work has helped them to sort through their thoughts and feelings to gain clarity, to grow, to learn about themselves, to develop confidence, and to heal wounds from the past. If you are feeling stuck, wanting to grow or learn about yourself, noticing the effects of trauma, struggling with depression or anxiety, or wanting support in a warm and collaborative environment, I can help you to heal and reach your goals.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Some healing can only happen in the context of a trusting and supportive relationship, and it is crucial to find the right therapist for you. I may be the right therapist for you if you are looking for someone who is warm, transparent, friendly, genuine, and active. I am collaborative and work to tailor our work to your needs, values, and goals. It is important to me that we actively discuss and minimize power dynamics in our relationship so that we can genuinely connect. Do you struggle with self-judgment, self-criticism, or self-blame? We live in a culture that promotes these as paths to self-improvement; instead, they are paths to depression, dissatisfaction, and feeling stuck. I can help you to develop a more compassionate, supportive, accepting, and loving relationship with yourself. Healing and caring for your own wounds and trauma can help you to improve all aspects of your life and your relationships with others.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: People do not have problems outside of context; we are all struggling to exist in a neoliberal capitalist system that is not designed to support our mental health or wellness. Helping my clients to understand how systems of oppression impact their functioning is critically important to shifting from self-blame to healing and action in support of a more just world for all. I have an anti-racist, intersectional feminist lens in my work, and social justice is deeply important to me. I work with a wide range of clients struggling with many different issues, but have a particular focus on working with trans and gender diverse clients, other members of the LGBTQ community, kinky folks, college and graduate students, and people in polyamorous relationship structures. I am also passionate about working with fellow therapists and therapists in training!

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a member of the queer community, I am passionate about helping folks explore their identities, navigate systems of oppression, and grow and heal from trauma. I specialize in helping folks to explore their gender identities, which can include supporting them through transitions. I also provide letters in support of gender affirming care (e.g., WPATH letters).

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma can keep us stuck and frozen reliving the most painful times in our lives. I work with many different types of trauma, including long-term and attachment-related trauma, as well as trauma related to a single event. I tailor treatment to particular individuals and incorporate person-centered, relational, narrative, and internal family systems (IFS) into my work with trauma, as well as offering Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT).

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Humans need each other, and can also cause one another immense amounts of pain. We may use the therapeutic relationship as a place to explore relational patterns, practice new ways of being, and strengthen the capacity for intimacy and ability to navigate conflict. We may also explore how past relationships, starting in childhood, can affect current patterns and how to heal attachment wounds to promote deeper and more joyful connections with others.

name: BBH Psychiatric Services
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Now providing psychiatric services across Oregon and Washington via telemedicine! Most major insurance plans accepted!
ideal_client: **To get started, click SCHEDULE NOW above and complete a brief intake form.** We see clients ages 13-65 years for psychiatric medication management and supportive psychotherapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: **We are psychiatric providers. We incorporate elements of psychotherapy into my sessions when appropriate, but we do not conduct therapy-only sessions.** Are you struggling with irritability, anxiety, low mood, poor focus, substance use, or lack of motivation that is impairing your relationships, your career, or your overall quality of life? Have you perhaps tried therapy, but found that your problems persisted? Have you tried medications, but found that psychiatric appointments were too impersonal or that your concerns about possible side effects or worsening symptoms were met with indifference?

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: **We are a psychiatric providers. I incorporate elements of psychotherapy into my sessions when appropriate, but we do not conduct therapy-only sessions.** We believe primarily in a listening-oriented approach to care, as well as incorporating your preferences into our treatment plan as much as possible. We provide evidence-based mental health treatments, which may include medications, nutritional supplements, sleep pattern modifications, referral to talk therapists or treatment centers, and more.

name: Lolo Halman
title: Professional Counselor
intro: Empathetic and practical counseling for couples and individuals using a mix of embodied approaches and communication skill-building methods
ideal_client: I'm deeply committed to supporting individuals, couples, and families on their journey towards growth and healing using embodied and experiential techniques. I work with clients from diverse backgrounds, including those navigating relationship challenges, exploring non-monogamous dynamics, and seeking to deepen their self-awareness. My approach is client-centered, collaborative, and tailored to meet the unique needs of each individual, partnership, or family.

approaches.How I Can Help You: For individuals, I use embodied techniques to help you explore and uncover deep insights into your personal challenges. If you value active engagement and a balance of compassion and critique in counseling, my approach could be right for you. I'm also committed to social justice and skilled in navigating the dynamics of polyamory/ENM, inviting a safer space for exploring diverse identities and relationships. For couples and families, I help you manage recurring conflicts through a mix of clear interventions, conflict resolution tools, and work to do outside of sessions to foster progress and instill a sense of hope. If you're considering polyamory or ethical non-monogamy, I offer guidance to help determine if this path aligns with your relationship goals, supporting healthy and informed decisions.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Becoming a counselor was an unexpected journey for me. Initially drawn to the Process Work Institute by my passion for innovative conflict resolution, I yearned to discover methods to transform conflicts from sources of division into opportunities for growth and insight. Throughout my training, especially as I began working more regularly with individuals and couples, I discovered a profound enjoyment and effectiveness in this work that genuinely surprised me. As my practice has evolved, I’ve shifted my focus more towards facilitating relationship conflict. I find relationship counseling particularly fulfilling because it challenges us to confront the intense emotional challenges and pain that can appear most powerfully in intimate relationships. In navigating the intricate dynamics of human connection, I believe my work becomes truly transformative, offering both my clients and myself rich opportunities for insight and growth.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I work with couples who are deeply invested in their relationship but find themselves caught in seemingly intractable conflict cycles. I support these couples to reconnect to their relationship purpose, build awareness of their triggers and how to de-escalate in moments of activation, interrupt unhelpful patterns, and realign towards a greater sense of unity as a couple.

specialities.name: Nonviolent Communication
specialities.description: I use nonviolent communication (NVC) as a tool for helping those who are new to awareness-based communication methods, sharing their emotions and needs, or as a first step in beginning to build one's capacity for more authentic communication. I see NVC as a stepping stone for many looking to deepen their communication with partners, friends, and others.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I am trained in Process Work, which uses somatic awareness practices to work with body symptoms, nighttime dreams, relational difficulties, vision for the world, and more. Through embodiment of that which attracts or disturbs us, we can often gain insights that can bring new ways of being and living our lives more fully. Embodiment can allow for a more rapid integration of these learnings.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I specialize in supporting individuals and couples exploring polyamory, non-monogamy, and relationship anarchy, as well as those considering these relationship structures. Together, we deepen awareness, communication, and autonomy, fostering intentional decision-making and deeper relatedness. As someone from these identities, I offer unique insight and understanding to navigate the challenges along the way

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: With over a decade of experience in social movement work, I specialize in transformative justice and healing within relationships. As someone from privileged identities, I've undergone significant personal growth to understand and dismantle how these identities shape my perspective and further social injustice, and I'm dedicated to supporting others in building this awareness too.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I work with couples who are deeply invested in their relationship but find themselves caught in seemingly intractable conflict cycles. I support these couples to reconnect to their relationship purpose, build awareness of their triggers and how to de-escalate in moments of activation, interrupt unhelpful patterns, and realign towards a greater sense of unity as a couple.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Stepping into personal growth work initially through men's work, I specialize in supporting men on their journey of self-discovery, emotional exploration, and nurturing healthy relationships. With a perspective rooted in advocating for gender equality and understanding the diverse experiences of all genders, I offer compassionate guidance to men seeking personal growth and authentic connections.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: I specialize in working with families facing conflict, aiming to build resilience and transform challenges into opportunities for growth. With an unbiased perspective, I guide families in navigating conflict, fostering unity, and recognizing when temporary separation may be necessary for intentional healing and transformation.

name: Michael Wilson, MA
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with couples to help them achieve deep connection and a fulfilling relationship.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: You may have lost the ability to hope that your relationship can improve, but a better life awaits you. I work with couples in distress, and it is a privilege and an honor. I help my clients reconnect with parts of themselves they feel too afraid to acknowledge and certainly don’t feel comfortable sharing with others. I then work to help you and your partner better understand one another, to truly hear one another and meet one another’s deepest needs. My hope and my belief is that when you can communicate your deepest fears and needs with each other, you can begin to understand one another and love one another in a new, more fulfilling way.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Since becoming a counselor I’ve developed a passion to help couples regain connection and a deep sense of contentment and fulfillment with one another. I’ve often been told by couples that I work with that I have a way about me that helps them feel comfortable and capable to be open and deal with the real problems in the relationships. I have extensive experience helping clients with identity formation, largely because I think it is vital to being in a relationship to understand oneself before you can reach out to another. I also have experience working with depression, anxiety, and self-criticism.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I view my therapy through an attachment lens. Attachment lays the groundwork for how we will interpret and process the world around us. Utilizing EFT I examine my clients attachment style, identify mismanaged emotions, and develop healthier strategies of coping with negative emotional experiences.

specialities.name: Interpersonal
specialities.description: As with EFT, interpersonal therapy utilizies an attachment base. Once we understand your attachment style we can then examine the unique ways in which you engage in relationships to meet your needs. We will identify unhealthy interpersonal patterns and work to develop more adaptive techniques to engage in relationships.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Nothing saps the joy from life more than relationship conflict. I love having the opportunity to help couples hear each other, to see the relationship from each other's perspective and recognize the need to work together.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: In working with individuals suffering from anxiety I have found that it is an inability to properly identify and manage the body's emotional experience that leads to the distress. I utilize emotion focused therapy to identify the negative emotional experience and together with the client develop healthier coping strategies to deal with that emotion.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I have received training in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) as well as Interpersonal Therapy (IPT), both of which have been shown to be effective in the treatment of depression. By addressing both maladaptive thought patterns and unhealthy interpersonal patterns, we can work to address the unmet attachment needs driving the depression.

name: Katelin Harrington
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Hello! I am passionate about helping people find emotional healing and freedom in a world that is full of hurt, pain, challenges and trauma.
ideal_client: It is a deep honor to have the opportunity to walk beside my clients as they seek healing and wholeness for their heart and soul. Therapy can feel scary and hard and my ideal client is one who is courageous enough to step into this unknown space in order to have a life marked by healing. If you are walking through grief, loss, a traumatic event, a painful relationship, struggle with anxiety, depression, or feel stuck, I would love to offer a safe and connective space to help facilitate healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer a collaborative, person-centered approach while using attachment-based therapy, polyvagal theory and Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) when working with my clients. My client is the expert in the room and has everything within them to create a life of healing and wholeness amidst the feelings of defeat, frustration, overwhelm or confusion. My role is to come beside my clients and help create a safe environment for healing to occur and empower them to believe in the strength within themselves. Through various tools and strategies, self-awareness and attachment, a new life can be forged and your heart can come back to life from its dormant, painful, or empty state to one full of life, vigor and transformation.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe people are wired for connection and therefore we are most often hurt within the context of relationship or lack thereof. This also means we can find healing through positive, safe and empathetic connection. During the hardest seasons of life, when more support is needed to navigate the trenches, the times that take us off guard and we feel unequipped to handle life, people need safe connection, empathy, tenderness and care. These are the sacred spaces that I have the privilege and honor to step into and be a support when it feels like you are walking alone. I have a deep and unique passion for supporting mommas, couples or families who've lost a baby or child. It is one of the most painful and devastating experiences you can walk through as a parent. As a mother who has had to say goodbye to my own baby boy, and as a therapist, I bring a unique perspective. It would be an honor to support you and be a safe space to process the grief and trauma you have had to live through.

name: Kate Sturges, MA, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I believe transition is a process unique to every individual, occurring throughout our lifetime.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Believing in our drive to connect through relationships, I work from a space of collaboration. It is my desire to accompany you, to be a witness for you and offer a safe nonjudgmental space for you to look inward and find the answers that lie within you. I strive to provide a space for individuals and couples to be able to find clarity during times of chaos. I seek to create a space that can open up dialogue for people to explore the places they feel unbalanced whether it be in work, relationships, or other forms of transition.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a Master’s Degree in Counseling Psychology from Lewis and Clark College, Graduate School of Education and Counseling. As a Nationally Certified Counselor and a Licensed Professional Counselor with the State of Oregon and Washington, I offer a broad base of knowledge with over 13 years’ of experience spanning the spectrum of the mental health field. Prior to entering into private practice I worked in community mental health and group practice clinics. As a counselor over the years I broadened my experience by working with a wide range of clients experiencing depression, anxiety, relationship issues, transitions and grief in a clinical setting.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I specialize in utilizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to help us understand how our thoughts, feelings, and behavior impact each other and work towards changing thought patterns. My training also includes utilizing behavioral interventions including Exposure and Response Prevention treatment primarily to help those experiencing Anxiety and/or OCD.

specialities.name: Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy
specialities.description: I have specialized training for the last 9 years utilizing Exposure and Response Prevention treatment primarily to help those experiencing Anxiety and/or OCD.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Humans strive for connectedness, to themselves, and others. At the heart of my therapeutic philosophy is my belief in the ability of every individual to create positive relationships. By creating a safe space to explore relationship patterns, I provide clients with the opportunity to create new ways of engaging and how to create fulfilling connections.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: I specialize in treating OCD utilizing CBT, including Exposure and Response Prevention. I completed the BTTI (Behavioral Training Therapy Institute) Certification and have been providing specialized OCD/anxiety treatment for the last 9 years.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I specialize in treating Anxiety Disorders utilizing CBT. Anxiety is a challenging part of life that affects most people at some point. In my experience, anxious thoughts can multiply and start a downward spiral that affects self esteem, confidence, and self worth. Becoming aware of these thoughts and finding where you can stop the spiral can greatly impact the power anxiety has over your life.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a queer identified woman, it is my goal to create a safe space for people who identify as LGBTQ.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Often times depression feels overwhelming and too much to manage. I believe that it is important to become mindful of negative self-talk and seek tools that will allow clients to address depression one step at a time. Depression requires planning and setting down a map of what tools to use in those moments that feel overwhelming.

name: Becca Flatt
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I'm Becca; I'm an interracial, mixed-race adoptee who provides adoptee-competent therapy for transracial and interracial adoptees 15+.
ideal_client: I am only accepting cash-pay clients who are interracial, transracial, Domestic adoptees who are Black, African Indigouness, Latino/Latine, Asian, or multi-racial. The sliding scale fee range is ($137-$190).

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am an eclectic therapist who practices from a foundation of attachment theory. The most important part of therapy is developing a solid therapeutic relationship with clients. My goal is to help you understand yourself in a safe space free of harmful judgment and full of compassion and kindness. I hold space for all emotions and hope you bring all of them in with you even the ones that might feel not okay to have.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a licensed clinical social worker. I have worked with people from every stage of life. My favorite populations to work with are adolescents 15+, young adults, adults, and older adults. My focus of practice includes adoption-related complex trauma, racial identity development, grief, secondary rejection, search & reunion, estrangement, and parenting as an adoptee. I am an adoptee-competent therapist and specialize in working with adoptees and transracial adoptees 15+. As both an adult adoptee and adoptive parent, I have the understanding clinically and through lived experience of the complexities, difficulties, and mixed emotions that punctuate adoption. I specialize in working with marginalized communities with complex identities, specifically: people of the global majority and queer women/fems, identity, racialized trauma, and the deconstruction of internalized racism and homophobia.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory is a major part of how I conceptualize how I work with clients. I personally feel attachment plays such an important role in human experience because it's how we relate to the people around us. In therapy, the relationship between the therapist and the client is significant as trust and vulnerability are a major part of the client's process through treatment.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Relational therapy, also known as Relational Cultural Therapy (RCT) posits that human beings thrive on mutually satisfying relationships. RTC utilizes the therapeutic relationship as an example of a healthy relationship and helps clients understand how past relationships, culture, class, gender, and other social factors affect relationships and create power struggles in the life of the client.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy is an intervention that puts the focus of treatment on acceptance of thoughts, feelings, and emotions. It also focuses on values guided action which means actions that are based on the things that bring value and meaning to our lives. The way I often conceptualize ACT is the Serenity Prayer in action.

specialities.name: Adoption Issues
specialities.description: I work from the Adoptee's standpoint. As both an adult adoptee and an adoptive parent, I not only understand adoption from a clinical perspective, but I have the lived experience of approaching adoptees with a fundamental understanding and empathy. I Only provide therapeutic services for adoptees.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma takes place as a singular event or many events that overwhelm a person's ability to cope. I use an integrative approach for working with complex trauma and trauma-related to single events. I offer EMDR and am EMDR trained working towards EMDR certification.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief and loss are two of the most unifying issues humans face. I've taken specialized training in grief and loss issues. Disenfranchised grief is an area that I have a great deal of knowledge in. Disenfranchised grief often feels like you have to qualify why your loss is painful. I provide a safe space to work through issues of grief and loss no matter how trivial it may seem. Your pain matters.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: I have researched a wide verity of resources pertaining to the oppression faced by Black, African American, Latino, and Chicano communities. My clinical conceptualization of the oppression facing these communities comes from a Black feminist/ Chicana feminist lens. It can help significantly to have someone who has walked a mile in the same type of shoes.

name: MindRx Group
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: We offer compassionate, integrative mental health care that empowers you to achieve true well-being. Mind & body wellness starts here.
ideal_client: At MindRx, we support individuals navigating anxiety, depression, trauma, life transitions, and perinatal mental health. We understand that mental health isn’t one-size-fits-all, so we take a personalized, mind-body approach to care. Our ideal client is someone seeking compassionate, science-backed treatment and is open to exploring new ways to heal and grow. Whether you need short-term support or long-term care, we’re here to help you thrive.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: At MindRx, we understand that mental health is deeply personal, and no two journeys are the same. That’s why we take an integrative, whole-person approach that goes beyond just symptom management. Our team of board-certified psychiatric and mental health practitioners blends neuroscience, functional medicine, and innovative therapeutic techniques to address the root causes of emotional and mental health challenges. Whether you’re struggling with anxiety, depression, trauma, perinatal mental health concerns, or simply feeling stuck, we work with you to develop a personalized plan that supports healing, resilience, and overall well-being. Our goal is to empower you with the tools, insight, and support needed to regain balance and live a fulfilling life.

approaches.Our Values as Mental Health Practitioner: At MindRx, we are more than just a mental health practice—we are a community dedicated to breaking barriers in mental health care. Our foundation is built on curiosity, compassion, and accountability, ensuring that every patient feels seen, heard, and supported. We welcome individuals from all backgrounds and are committed to creating an inclusive, affirming space for LGBTQ+ individuals, BIPOC communities, parents, professionals, and anyone seeking meaningful change. Our practitioners are passionate about reducing stigma, embracing innovation, and continuously learning to provide the best possible care. Whether you’re looking for a fresh perspective, long-term support, or guidance through life’s challenges, we are here to walk this path with you.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR is a powerful therapy designed to help people process and heal from past trauma. Using guided eye movements, EMDR helps the brain reprocess distressing memories, reducing their emotional impact and making them easier to manage. It’s especially effective for PTSD, anxiety, and other trauma-related conditions.

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: Finding the right medication for your mental health can be a process, and we’re here to help. Our providers take the time to understand your symptoms, medical history, and goals to create a personalized treatment plan. We’ll work with you to adjust dosages, address side effects, and ensure your medication supports your overall well-being.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT is a structured, goal-oriented therapy that helps you recognize and change unhelpful thought patterns and behaviors. It’s great for managing anxiety, depression, stress, and more by giving you practical tools to shift your mindset and improve your daily life.

name: Mara Sobesky
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
credentials: Master of Arts in Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy
intro: An invitation to slow down, put words to your story, & expand your sense of possibility for living in a way that is meaningful to you.
ideal_client: Often, a sense of disconnection brings clients to therapy, seeking more agency, choice, and belonging in their lives and relationships. Conflicting messages about how we “should” be from family, community, and culture can cause distress and create barriers to our ability to live in alignment with our own integrity. I work with individuals, romantic or platonic partners, and adult families who want to deepen their sense of connection to life, to their relationships, and to themselves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Many people experience a tension in desiring both stability & change, surrender & control, freedom & its’ limitations. The distress behind these mutual and conflicting needs is part of what clients want to explore when they choose to work with me. Mapping themes such as identity development, life transitions & grief, can illuminate patterns that support and block your sense of presence. Together, we can build mutual trust and explore historic, cultural and social contexts to make sense of your experience, as we contemplate the question “how are you willing to live?” My approach is relational, collaborative & centered in Existential-Humanism. I also have specialized training in treating disordered eating and body image concerns.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I love working with clients who are LGBTQ+, identify as neurodivergent, or are in mixed-neurotype relationships, communities in which I am a part.

name: Mary Knoblock
title: Hypnotherapist
intro: Haven Wellness was founded in 2013 in order to provide comprehensive holistic healthcare services via Hypnosis (RTT) and more.
ideal_client: Are you suffereing from past trauma loops and anxiety or mental health issues that just don't seem to go away? I understand how frustrating this can be and have helped tons of humans just like you who after doing integrative holistic hypnosis sessions were able to break free from the trauma and experience a new level of freedom and wellness in their life. I'm here to help you find your joy and peace again in your life!

approaches.What I Specialize In: My Qualifications are as follows: 1. Licensed Clinical Rapid Transformation Therapy Practitioner 2. Emotion Code Practitioner 3. Duke Trained Integrative Holistic Health Coach 4. Reiki Master 5. Spiritual Counseling (ordained minister) 6. Homeopath Student of two years with Dr. Faulkner, MD

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I have had the wonderful opportunity to work with clients from all religions, and genders, and am an advocate supporter of the LGBTQIA+ healthcare community after many LGBTQIA members found my sessions so welcoming and helpful. I have many clients who have worked with me who felt comfortable reaching out to a non biased, welcoming holistic hypnotist. I also support families from very diverse cultures and advocate for equality and inclusion and fair treatment in client care.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I work with a lot of woment who are experiencing start of career anxiety and mid life anxiety. We work together to find a comprehensive hyponosis focus and work to resolve your issues together through a hypnosis session.

name: Rachel Spooner
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi, I'm Rachel, and I'm passionate about creating an empathic, judgement free and empowering space for you to conquer your fears.
ideal_client: I am very passionate about working with those experiencing anxiety related challenges, including but not limited to: general anxiety, social anxiety, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, Panic and adjusting to life’s transitions and changes. I love to support those I'm working with in taking power back over their lives from their fears.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My first priority in approaching our work together is to build a therapeutic relationship that feels safe for you to express your full self, feelings and experiences. This relationship is the foundation of our work together in exploring and reaching your goals. Wherever you are at, I will strive to meet you there and support you in building connection with yourself and others on your path to emotional wellbeing. When you are ready, we will work together to explore your thoughts, feelings, challenges, and goals. My therapeutic approach includes a combination of cognitive-behavioral therapy techniques, narrative therapy techniques and motivational interviewing.
