Together, we’ll explore practical solutions that align with your goals, helping you move through life’s transitions with greater ease and confidence.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe the world is a better place when we can fully be ourselves, and therapy is a powerful way to support that process. As a client-centered therapist, I bring a compassionate, down-to-earth, and strategic approach to my work, creating a non-judgmental and strengths-based space. With a social justice perspective, I help clients recognize the impact of oppression and related traumas on their well-being while guiding them toward healing and self-discovery. My journey of learning—through relationships, parenting, and embracing my strengths and vulnerabilities—deepens my understanding of this work. Outside work, I find joy in gardening, discovering new restaurants, and exploring nature. These passions help me stay grounded and continually inspired, much like the work I do in helping others find fulfillment and growth in their lives.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: My degree included specialized training in art therapy. No art skill is necessary to try out art therapy. In our sessions, I might use some art therapy if it seems appropriate or suggest some homework. Examples include: making a vision board, drawing your feelings, creating a object that celebrates the loss of a loved one.

specialities.name: Expressive Art Therapy
specialities.description: I have immersive, graduate-level training in expressive art therapies from Lesley University. In expressive art therapies art, music, movement, and drama therapy are used as tools to understand the client's experience from different perspectives and to create healing. No experience is needed. Examples include: writing a letter to your younger self, using imagery and movement to calm anxiety, creating a "character" for one of your parts, and dialoging with it.

specialities.name: Nonviolent Communication
specialities.description: Non-violent communication is an excellent tool for improving communication skills, de-escalating people who are activated, and parenting. I have used and taught non-violent communication for 10-plus years. NVC teaches us to get to the underlying issues behind difficult communication in a respectful and connected way.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Much of my experience is related to the empowerment of women. I am particularly interested in women's health transitions such as birth and perimenopause/menopause. I've provided counseling as part of the Sexual Information Center in college and volunteered for Planned Parenthood. I've also worked closely with women professionals and women arts in the areas of career and leadership development providing mentoring, coaching, and therapy for women growing their power and role at work.

specialities.name: Alzheimers
specialities.description: An Alzheimer's or dementia diagnosis for an individual or for people in their lives can be devastating. Together we can navigate these challenges. Areas we may address include: coping with the initial diagnosis (What does this mean for me?), identifying how to get the most out of your next years (What matters most to me?), planning for changes and end of life considerations (What needs to be in place as the disease progresses to ease the journey?).

name: Kate McNulty
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My practice is devoted to helping people improve their relationships and intimate lives through research-based expertise.
ideal_client: Most of my clients are resourceful and bright people who have run out of their own ideas and are looking for a fresh point of view. Many want to develop new interpersonal skills beyond those they already possess. A lot of the people I see are psychologically curious, but not everyone is; I also enjoy more practical-minded people who are interested in solving a problem they face and getting back to their lives, better equipped to handle their challenges.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My orientation in working with clients is strengths-based and collaborative. Most people find the type of therapy I offer is informative and engaging. I enjoy helping people learn new ways of looking at themselves. Counseling is often referred to as "hard work." Indeed, our discussions may bring up emotions that are quite intense and difficult . However there is also a lot of room for humor, pleasure and the delight of the unexpected in any counseling session. I seek out those moments and call them to your attention. I see counseling as a place to try out new behaviors, receive honest feedback and increase your emotional intelligence. My approach is pragmatic; I provide people with plenty of handouts, information, tools and resources. You will find the way I work with you is tailored to your particular situation and needs. Although I am trained in many methods of counseling, the very best method is always based on your immediate circumstances and concerns.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have extensive training and experience working with relationship issues and sexual concerns. I am certified as a Gottman Relationship Therapist by the Gottman Institute of Seattle, a research institute that has spent 40+ years studying couple and family relationships with true scientific rigor. I also hold certification as a Sex Therapist through AASECT, the American Association of Sex Educators, Counselors and Therapists. Both of these credentials required comprehensive study, direct demonstration of clinical skills and endorsement by other therapists who could attest to my competence. I am proud of my association with these organizations because of their dedication to protecting clients' well-being and to ongoing, engaged critical thinking about the field of mental health. Prior to opening my private practice my professional experience was in local agencies with children, teens and families. I also worked in a hospital ER for 15 years.

specialities.name: Collaborative Couple Therapy
specialities.description: Collaborative Couples Therapy helps couples learn to attend to one another's natural emotional reactions with empathy and compassion, rather than becoming adversarial with each other. I have studied intensively with Dan WIle, who developed this method and who john Gottman, a renowned researcher in this field, has called 'our greatest living marital therapist.'

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I am certified as a Gottman Relationship Therapist by the Gottman Institute of Seattle, where a team has spent over 40 years looking into all the ways happy and healthy couples function together. This method helps couples improve their patterns of communicating based on using their existing strengths and adding new tools and awareness.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: My orientation is pragmatic and my interest in therapy is helping you get access to the tools and information you need. Typically people come in for a series of sessions and then return whenever they feel the need for a check-in or when they hit another bump in the road. We are always collaborating when it comes to deciding how long it makes sense for us to work together.

specialities.name: Sexual Addiction
specialities.description: Although the concept of sexual “addiction” is widely-recognized by the general public, it remains a controversial topic in the sex therapy field. If your sexual thoughts or behaviors are upsetting to you or your partner, I provide a level headed and well-researched perspective. I have helped many people with this and would love to hear from you.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I am certified as a Sex Therapist by AASECT, the preeminent organization credentialing specialists in this field. I help with a wide range of concerns such as lack of desire, difficulties with orgasm and sexual pain, and sexual conflict or confusion. See www.sexpositivetherapist.com

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: My professional career has been devoted to the mystery of what it takes to have great relationships. After all, what is more important in life? I have trained intensively with John Gottman and Dan Wile, widely recognized experts in this field, and can help you quickly switch from ineffective to effective habits and behaviors, to bring you the loving relationship you deserve.

name: Tristan Smith
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: My intention to is to cultivate a space that honors their current reality while also collaborating with them to cultivate fulfilling skills.
ideal_client: If you’re facing uncertainties in your life and are ready to embrace the journey, consider how sitting with tough times can lead to growth. This is a part of life! Developing introspection and critically examining your choices and environment can clarify your path forward. We will work together to create the best path for you moving forward. Through holistic and reflective listening, we will make foundational changes that your future self will be grateful for. Consistency a tremendous power.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have a passion for supporting individuals on their journey toward healing, growth, and self-understanding. Born and raised in Portland, I have always been deeply curious about the world and how we can transform it, both individually and collectively. My experiences working with at-risk youth and individuals struggling with addiction have reinforced my belief in the power of human connection, empathy, and resilience. I earned my Master of Social Work (MSW) from Portland State University, where I was trained in a wide range of therapeutic approaches, but I have always been drawn to holistic methods that address the mind, body, and spirit. I believe that true healing requires more than just symptom management; it involves understanding the underlying emotional, psychological, and physical factors that contribute to one’s struggles. My approach to therapy is integrative and client-centered, focusing on creating a safe, nonjudgmental space where individuals can explore themselves.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I was born and raised in Portland, and for as long as I can remember, I have always possessed a deep curiosity about the world. Why is it the way it is? How can we change it? The love I have received from my family throughout my life has taught me that the human bond is the greatest power we, as humans, have to offer this world. Therefore, it is truly a privilege for me to be of service to you. The education I received in both undergraduate and graduate school has awakened a sensitive and critical-thinking lens within me, allowing me to believe that people who seek to understand both the world around them and the world within them are bound by nothing. My priority as a therapist is to be the best resource I can be for you, and to work together to build a healthier future while striving for more internal and external validation.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: As someone who has personally navigated addiction and its challenges, I bring a deep, empathetic understanding to my work. My experience is further enriched by my education, where I studied the systemic factors and trauma that often underpin addiction. I approach addiction with a holistic, trauma-informed lens, recognizing that healing involves addressing not just behaviors, but the underlying emotional and environmental factors that contribute to substance use.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Life is full of adjustments in one way or another. Having worked with at-risk youth and in addiction services, I have seen that how we handle adjustments throughout our lives is a reflection of the direction we are heading. I aim to assist clients in identifying unhealthy coping mechanisms and developing effective strategies for emotional regulation, problem-solving, and resilience. Stronger strategies allow for greater balance when challenging incidents arise in one's life.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Abuse deeply impacts our way of thinking and feeling about the world. Through my vocational experience, I have observed that any form of abuse shapes our behavior and coping mechanisms. Many people turn to various endeavors to avoid confronting the trauma, perpetuating a cycle of pain and stunted growth. Developing introspection, understanding our external environment, and building internal validation are key foundational steps in reducing the impact that abuse can have on us.

name: LAUREN MULLINS
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi! I'm Lauren. I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker. I provide compassionate counseling to folks looking for support along their journey.
ideal_client: I primarily work with individual adults who have experienced depression and anxiety related to interpersonal, social and occupational stressors. I aim to create a safe, collaborative relationship as we navigate your healing. The focus may be placed on utilizing personal strengths, increasing safe coping skills and improving feelings of empowerment through evidence based interventions.

approaches.My Background: I have over 10 years in working with people who are recovering from relational abuse. I have worked with various domestic and sexual violence agencies providing individual and group counseling services. I have experience in suicide prevention and crisis intervention. I received my EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing) certification in 2019 and enjoy providing EMDR therapy to clients looking to heal from past traumatic experiences and relationships. In my free time I like to garden, kayak, camp and go for walks with my Boston Terrier, Baked Beans.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a graduate from Portland State University, the majority of my training is centered in trauma-informed, strength-based, anti-oppressive and collaborative perspectives. I utilize a multi-dimensional assessment with individuals, giving special attention to cultural responsiveness and power dynamics.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: What is EMDR therapy? According to the EMDR international association, Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy is a psychotherapy method to help people recover from trauma and other distressing life experiences including PTSD, anxiety, depression, and panic disorders. For more information visit: https://www.emdria.org/about-emdr-therapy/

name: Karla Wolf, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: Certified Internal Family Systems (IFS) Therapist. Providing evidence based, trauma informed therapy (with a social justice lens) to individual adults & couples
intro: Experienced clinician of 20+ years. Licensed in OR & WA. I bring compassion, authenticity, warmth & humor to the counseling relationship.
ideal_client: "Sometimes I wrestle with my demons, sometimes we just snuggle" -It can be hard to get rid of the demons inside of us, perhaps because they were holding us when nobody else did. What if, instead of getting rid of them, we can learn to love them. -Whether you need help in navigating your relationship with yourself or other's in your life, or a LOSS-we will find a way together.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a Certified IFS therapist, I believe that our wholeness is not achieved by cutting off a portion of ourself but by inviting in ALL parts of ourself, which all want to play a positive role in who we are. To help you reach this goal of wholeness I work primarily from the Internal Family Systems (IFS) model (parts work). This model utilizes both the client’s & therapist’s inner capacities for curiosity, compassion & courage to support your journey. I use Non Violent Communication (NVC) & IFS (IFIO model) to assist you & your partner in developing the skills to problem solve well together. As Marshall Rosenburg (NVC) said, “Every criticism, judgment, blame & expression of anger is the tragic expression of an unmet need.” We will work together so that unmet needs can be expressed & met. I will also invite you to notice the ways you are already supported. I find that gratitude can be a wonderful antidote to resentments.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am drawn to counseling because I love working with people. I think each person has their own abilities & wisdom to find their way, develop the tools they need to be an anchor for themselves & their loved ones. I bring a social justice perspective to my work & will support you in recognizing the ways oppression & related traumas have affected your sense of self & well-being. In my own life, I continue to learn about myself, & my vulnerabilities & strengths, through partnerships & parenting, & through embracing the demons in myself & finding healing. I love being with friends & family, being outdoors, finding solace in nature & playing with my 3 cats. My counseling style is compassionate, down to earth, casual, full of humor & warmth. I love working with people & I learn from you every day. “Compassion is not a relationship between the healer & the wounded. It’s a relationship between equals. Only when we know our own darkness can we be present with the darkness of others." P.Chodron

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: IFS believes that each of us is comprised of many psychological "parts", each with valuable qualities to help us thrive & protect us from pain. Each of us also has a core Self that can provide these "parts" with compassionate guidance which heals us & elevates our self esteem. As a Certified IFS therapist I use this evidence based model to support you on this journey. I also use IFS personally for my own growth & healing to insure that I can bring my whole Self to the therapy sessions with you.

specialities.name: Nonviolent Communication
specialities.description: Nonviolent Communication (NVC) teaches us how to use compassion to access our own feelings & needs & how to communicate with others in an effective way so that everyone's needs can get met. It is a perfect model for those looking to improve their relationships with themselves & others. I trained with NVC's founder, Marshall Rosenburg, & I have over 20 years practicing & utilizing NVC with couples & individuals. I continue to deepen my NVC practice & learning by attending an NVC group for myself.

name: Anne Horgan
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am an EMDR therapist who focuses on trauma resolution and healthy mind-body connection to facilitate healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is eclectic and person-centered. I utilize EMDR for trauma healing and incorporate elements of Cognitive Behavior Therapy, art and narrative therapy, Dialectical Behavior Therapy, mindfulness and imagery/meditation, discovery of mind-body connection, solutions-focused, and strengths-based approaches. My ultimate goal to create and provide a safe space for connection, empowerment, comfort, trust and engagement. I work to provide a down to earth and non-judgmental environment with a natural and genuine approach to supporting individuals in all walks of life!

name: Melissa Yeary
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Compassionate somatic therapist guiding you to shift perspectives, transform behaviors, and grow with creativity, care, and insight.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe everyone has an innate capacity to grow and thrive. Therapy offers a safe space to explore the depth of your inner life and identify what may be holding you back from becoming the person you want to be. Together, we’ll work to understand your unique emotions, thoughts, body, and history as the process of healing unfolds. By gaining clarity about yourself—individually and in relationships—you can make thoughtful, meaningful choices. Exploring long-held thought patterns can free you from emotional limitations, opening the door to greater engagement, passion, and purpose. I also believe in the power of creativity to enhance growth and self-expression. Integrating creative practices into therapy can deepen insight and healing. I enjoy supporting clients who wish to explore their creative process in any form. Additionally, I facilitate SoulCollage®, an experiential art practice that brings profound meaning and insight, helping you connect with your inner wisdom.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have extensive experience working with adults of all ages, specializing in anxiety, depression, self-awareness, resolving childhood trauma, and nervous system regulation. As a certified Hakomi therapist, I support clients in achieving meaningful transformation by exploring their thoughts, emotions, body sensations, and memories. My approach is guided by a diverse background as a parent, artist, coach, and former software designer and manager. This blend of experiences allows me to offer a unique combination of creativity, intuition, and practical insight. I believe creativity plays a vital role in nurturing the spirit and often encourage clients to explore their creative interests as a pathway to self-renewal and emotional balance. In sessions, I frequently incorporate parts-of-self work, which helps clients connect with and understand the many layers of their inner world, fostering deeper self-awareness and lasting healing.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: I am a Certified Hakomi Therapist. Hakomi is an orientation that uses mindfulness to illuminate how you organize your experience and supports profound change to the core beliefs that limit your happiness. I have practiced mindfulness meditation for many years and believe that by strengthening our awareness of the present moment, we greatly enhance our capacity to enjoy the gifts of being human.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: The client-therapist relationship offers a unique opportunity to practice how we relate to others in a caring, honest environment. I am trained in interpersonal and relational therapy methods to support exploration of what goes on with you in a relationship. Working relationally in therapy offers powerful benefits to your success in intimate, work, and friend relationships in your life.

specialities.name: Expressive Art Therapy
specialities.description: My training in Expressive Art Therapy supports your exploration of challenges and dreams with images, music, poetry, or movement. As a SoulCollage® facilitator, I offer groups and workshops at PCC and in private sessions. You are welcome to bring in your creative interests, and we will integrate creative expression into your process of self-exploration and change.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Loss, disappointment, and grief are inevitable parts of being human. My experience and training in navigating these difficult times will support you to emerge with renewed hope. Working through the stuck places you encounter along your journey to healing will bring you insight and wisdom you'll be able to apply to all aspects of your life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: It's important to explore the underlying thoughts, feelings, and related experiences associated with anxiety as well as the body's response to stress. My training in working with anxiety includes ways to calm the physical stress response and reshape the body's response to trigger events, as well as a variety of options for exploring and changing the accompanying thoughts and feelings.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: It is natural to feel sad at times, but experiencing ongoing hopelessness, despair, and a reduced interest in life may indicate depression. I'm experienced in working with depression and offer compassion, insight, and effective tools. Together we can explore options and if appropriate, collaborate in changing the underlying beliefs, habits, and behavior that fuel depression.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: The major events in a woman's life can be challenging. Relationship growth or difficulty, becoming a mother or deciding not to have children, managing work and family, coming into your own as a woman. These transitions are rich times to take stock of who you are, claim your power, and choose to live your life with heart and creativity. I've been there. I can help you find your way.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Feelings of self-worth depend on the meaning we’ve given our life experiences. Exploring what we've come to believe about ourselves can be an exciting and rewarding journey. I bring a wealth of tools and strategies useful to creating the strong sense of self that underlies positive self-esteem, including creative strategies like journaling and collaging and body-centered tools like mindfulness.

name: David Hanna
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I specialize in helping people build meaningful, fun relationships. Contact me to move together towards a more connected & integrated life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: When seeking a therapist you want someone who'll be able to recognize who you are and what you're needing. No one wants to waste their time or have the setback of meeting with someone and leaving the experience more discouraged than before you came in. You're looking for someone to see you clearly and support you with whatever you're struggling with, wherever you're stuck, however much (or little) pain or confusion you're in - whether you're single, married, struggling as a step-parent, dealing with the loss of someone close, feeling lonely or dissatisfied. If you've ever felt like you're "too much" for those around you or if you're depressed, anxious and not getting what you want out of your relationships, work, or dating life, then counseling may be for you. I understand these challenges and together we can help you find a better way forward. We all need to be seen and no one's been seen enough. Let's build a therapeutic relationship that encourages your growth & health.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I’ve been working as a therapist since 2006. I received my master’s degree in applied behavioral science with a focus on systems counseling from The Leadership Institute of Seattle at Bastyr University. I hold a bachelor’s degree in electronic communication arts from San Francisco State University. I'm a Licensed Mental Health Counselor in WA and a Licensed Professional Counselor in OR. I come from a blended family, with full, half and stepsiblings. I have lost a parent and come through a challenging divorce stronger and more able to connect to others with similar challenges. I am empathic to the complex emotions and binds of being a sensitive person in relationships with friends, colleagues and family members who don’t always value those traits. As Hemingway said, "The world breaks everyone, and afterward, some are strong at the broken places.”

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: In my work as a couples therapist, I use insights from my family systems counseling training, and my additional studies of Gottman, Hendricks, Richo and Real's writings to guide my work with couples. I'm passionate about helping couples navigate the complexity of relationships and dealing with the often unsupported and rough waters of partnerships both new and established.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: We all have a family and that family can be the source of great joy... and great frustration. Understanding how to build successful family relationships is a struggle for most of us. My training is specifically in family systems counseling from Bastyr University and my ongoing training and professional growth is always related to better understanding family systems.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: With the current state of the world, sometimes results need to be immediate. We don't always have time to explore the roots of our challenges. Coaching can be a great way to tackle a problem at face value and get it taken care of and behind you.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Being a man in this culture is not easy. There's a myriad of mixed messages about how we are supposed to act, think, feel, not-feel and behave. Our roles seem to be increasingly narrowed, as advertisers and media outlets continue to target our insecurities, therefore our sense of personal power can begin to diminish. I work with men to help them identify and understand their authentic selves.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: So many of our challenges are rooted in our relationships with our romantic partners. Our romantic relationships are often our most precious, triggering, rewarding and conflict-laden relationships. Many of our conflicts in these relationships will never be resolved. We must learn to support our partners toward their greatest selves and vice-versa.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I care deeply about the rights, struggles and needs of gay, lesbian and transgender people. It is important to me to provide a place that is safe, supportive and attuned to the needs of all who experience and express their gender and sexuality in any way that they are most comfortable.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: I have years of experience working successfully with the complex challenges, feelings and binds that arise inside families for children, parents, grandparents, and siblings. I am able to support multiple family members through conflicts. I provide perspective and support at those times when the family is most angry and at odds with one another.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have many years of experience treating anxiety and stress successfully inter and intra-personally. I use both mindfulness practices as well as coaching interventions to tackle stress and anxiety in relationships to other people.

name: Day Adams
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: "To learn which questions are unanswerable, and not to answer them: this skill is most needful in times of stress and darkness." - Le Guin
ideal_client: People I work with may be: - struggling to engage meaningfully in their lives and relationships - seeking individual therapy to support couples therapy - wanting to understand and change after having an affair - having difficulty communicating and connecting in a partnership - wanting to feel closer as adults in a family together (siblings, parent/child, extended/chosen family) - wanting to explore ideas and experiences around masculinity - navigating feelings about being new dads

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I practice narrative therapy in a warm, conversational, and practical way, often incorporating writing of some kind. I believe therapy is a collaborative process in pursuit of preferred ways of living, facilitating different kinds of attention, perspective, and relationship. I'll accompany you in your search for understanding and welcome your curiosity, feelings, and reflections into our conversations. I'm here to help you articulate and foreground what you value and cherish most and to tell the meaningful stories of your life, painful, joyful, and in-between. I know you walk your own path, and where you head is up to you - it’s my honor to help you uncover and recover the skills and knowledges most needed to move in that direction with all possible resilience, flexibility, and a sense of connection with others.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I chose to pursue the work of relational therapy under the spell of a great curiosity and love for the diverse lives and relationships of this world. Partly this love and curiosity emerged from my own learning about how to navigate life and relationships as a man, in a society that has a wide variance of ideas about what that means. Partly it came about through my own experiences, both nourishing and difficult or confusing, in relationships of all kinds, with family, friends, and partners. Through personal relationships, education and clinical training, my own therapeutic experiences, and the many conversations with people I work with, I’m centering the idea that meaningful connection is the crucial element to living the lives we want to live.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Narrative therapy is a collaborative, non-pathologizing therapeutic approach. Two central ideas of this approach are that people are separate from problems and that we make meaning, act, and relate based on the stories that we know about our lives and the world. I first met narrative therapy in my graduate program and have since done extended graduate-level narrative therapy development through the Evanston Family Therapy Center.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: To me, a feminist approach to therapy involves being aware and critical of power differences and the way that narrow and culturally-influenced ideas about our identities can negatively impact our wellbeing. I try to center often-marginalized voices and question what might seem like "common sense". I work hard to practice therapy as horizontally as possible, leaning on collaboration around direction, self-disclosure, and not pretending to have the best answers.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I was educated and trained at Lewis & Clark to practice therapy in a relational way. To me that means always recognizing that we are not just individuals cut off from the world and acting in a vacuum. We are fundamentally in connection with others, from before birth until long after death, and that, more than anything else, is what gives our lives shape and meaning. I do my best to always honor and center that connectedness in the therapeutic relationship.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Conflict exists in all relationships, but it can get disconnecting and distressing. Habits, expectations, and values all impact how we collaborate with the people we love. Through talk about how we experience these things with our partners, we open doors to being able to relate in preferred ways and reconnect. I also work individually with people who have engaged in affairs and want to understand and change those behaviors, as well as individuals concurrently in couples/relational therapy.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Men face a particular array of challenges these days and we are prone to feeling isolated and burdened with expectations and uncertainty. It can be helpful to have a space to talk with another man and consider what we're up against and what might be done to live in preferred ways. It's my honor to hold space for men to share what's really on their hearts and minds and talk it through together.

specialities.name: Political Climate
specialities.description: This historical moment is a scary one for many people. I believe we take care of us and that therapy can play an influential role in how we orient and respond to what is happening. As a leftist and someone who has been involved in a variety of leftist organizing and political projects, I feel strongly about how personal and political struggles are interwoven and how acting collectively with others has a powerful influence on our own sense of agency and hope for a better future.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Families bear all kinds of histories, as well as habits of living, communicating, and connecting. Not only this, but they must also grow and change together over time, as everyone involved is always in the process of "growing up". This can cause all manner of stuck or sore spots. Let's take the time to slow down, explore what has influenced the relationship to be the way it is and determine ways of being together through life's changes that feel more connective.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Everybody grows and changes throughout their lives, sometimes in preferred ways and often in unexpected ways. There is a kind of power in exploring and learning how to make the kind of commitment and direct the kind of energy necessary to develop those areas of life that seem most vital.

name: Derrick Radford
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Accepting OHP - PacificSource. Are you struggling from childhood wounds, relationship issues, or overwhelm? I am here to help.
ideal_client: My practice focuses on individuals, couples, and Native American/Indigenous peoples through culturally responsible practices. I specialize in helping others overcome depression, PTSD, childhood wounds, relationship issues, and navigating the complexities of life. I'm here to guide you through the depths of your past, helping you to mend old wounds and navigate the intricacies of relationships. If you're feeling overwhelmed by all of life's challenges, I am here for you

approaches.My Background and Approach: As a psychotherapist, my approach is deeply rooted in depth psychological and integrative perspectives, reflecting a blend of relational, psychoanalytic, emotionally focused, and trauma-informed methods. Grounded in empathy, understanding, and safety, I help clients navigate the complexities of life by promoting the freedom of selfhood, inner strength, curiosity, and communal relations. Additionally, I incorporate a psychospiritual and holistic perspective, acknowledging that wellbeing encompasses the totality of ones being which includes the mind, the body, and the soul. My background and approach offer a therapeutic experience that honors the complexity of each individual's story while fostering profound growth and transformation. As a tribal member of a sovereign Indigenous nation, my life path is rooted in Indigenous culture and knowledge. My practice is ideal for Indigenous peoples or those seeking to reclaim their relationship with their Indigenous roots.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I am passionate about helping others reach their fullest potential in life through fostering empowerment and resilience. In particular, I am fond of helping others rewrite their stories so they may live the life they have always wanted to live. It was through rewriting my own story that allowed me the privilege to guide others in doing the same. I would not be where I am today if it were not for those around me who deeply care about my life. I believe that if it weren’t for others in our lives, our potential would diminish. A loving hand is vitality casting itself through generations. I truly believe that growth can come from places we least expect it and through even the darkest of challenges, transformation can be found.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: Depth psychotherapy delves into the underlying, often unconscious, aspects of the psyche to address issues at their roots. Unlike more surface-level approaches, it explores the depths of one's experiences, emotions, and patterns, aiming for profound and lasting transformation. By uncovering hidden motivations, unresolved conflicts, and unconscious beliefs, individuals can gain insight into their behaviors and find healing from within. This is my primary method and the root of my masters degree.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Relationship counseling, within the context of depth psychotherapy, goes beyond surface-level conflicts to explore the deeper dynamics that shape relationships. It delves into unconscious patterns, childhood experiences, and attachment styles that influence how individuals relate to one another. As an expert in this field, I draw from modalities including emotionally focused therapy and psychoanalytic insights to deepen understanding, emotional intimacy, and relational healing.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: Holistic psychotherapy is an integrative approach that considers the interconnectedness of mind, body, and spirit in the healing process. As a holistic psychotherapist, I draw upon a diverse range of modalities, including mindfulness, somatic experiencing, and the depths of imagination, to address the entirety of one's humanity. Ultimately, considering that mental well-being includes the body, brain, environment, and the mythic realms of the mind.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I provide comprehensive treatment for PTSD using evidence-based techniques grounded in depth psychology and integrative psychotherapy. Through a trauma-informed approach, I collaborate with clients to address the roots of their PTSD symptoms. Combining relational therapy, psychoanalytic insights, and trauma-focused interventions, I empower clients to navigate their trauma with resilience and self-awareness. Ultimately, rebuilding and strengthening the core of selfhood.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I specialize in navigating depression with a nuanced understanding of the challenges individuals face in a world that can often feel painful and isolating. I offer empathetic support to help clients explore the roots of their depression and develop strategies for healing. I believe in the transformative power of community and incorporate the importance of connection and belonging into my approach, recognizing that healing often flourishes within a supportive network of relationships.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in relationship counseling, offering a comprehensive and compassionate approach to couples or two individuals seeking support in their relationship. I work collaboratively with clients to explore relational dynamics and develop personalized strategies for growth and healing. Through a blend of relational therapy, emotionally focused techniques, and psychoanalytic insights, I empower couples to navigate challenges, deepen connection, and foster mutual understanding.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I focus on fostering personal growth and development, offering a holistic approach to support individuals on their journey towards self-discovery and fulfillment. I work with clients to explore their unique paths, uncover their robust and influential history, and challenge core beliefs that may be holding them back. Through a combination of relational therapy, psychoanalysis, and life coaching, I help clients to overcome obstacles, cultivate resilience, and realize their abundant potential.

name: Emma Jewell
title: Somatic Practitioner
credentials: Radical Aliveness Practitioner, Family Constellations Facilitator & LMT
intro: (Re)claim your energy. Build capacity to stay in the face of challenging realities. Navigate sticky interactions with more ease.
ideal_client: People who feel mad/sad with the world and struggle with what to do about it. Want to build capacity for challenging relationships. Are not where you want to be in your life. Feel the pain of the world, and long to not be alone in it. Want to be kind. Willing to feel deeply and take risks to be in your truth. Believe in building bridges in connection across complexity of cultures, religion, systems, race, social economics and beyond.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I bring a powerful empathetic presence with focused support for your personal journey. I help you weave a way back to connection through movement exercises, sound, and expansive wisdom. Whether it's heart break, anger, terror, insecurity, anxiety and so much more, sessions will help you show up in your life with more agility and ease. Meeting everyday challenges with more capacity and space rather than reaction. I am always continuing on my path of learning and unlearning. Unwinding the oppressions passed to me and my ancestors and the people around me and of the land: Indigenous people. I bring forth this work for the liberation of the people and the whole world.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: The body holds memory, healing the mind and the body is interconnected. As a body worker for over 10 years, and training in body-centered emotional work, I integrate movements, sensations and sounds into each session. So much is possible through the body that words cannot achieve

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Therapeutic relationship has the power to rewire your nervous system. Through relationship we see, we belong, we connect, we uncover the truth. My therapeutic relational approach unravels and rebuilds capacity for more connection, more pleasure, more curiosity and understanding. To build bridges in every aspect of your life.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in working with moon/menstruation cycles, mood regulation and awareness for this powerful natural cycle. I work with your Menstrual origin story, and social and systemic impacts on your body, to integrate and build understanding to prepare and navigate this ongoing natural process.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: I approach all personal healing through the lens and awareness of the cultural and systemic impact of someone's experience. I integrate awareness of these systems through research and personal study to meet each individual with more depth and specificity.

name: Kaia Stamiris
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer a compassionate, collaborative space to explore what matters to you, and to facilitate the development of your unique strengths.
ideal_client: I work with adult individuals experiencing anxiety, depression, LGBTQ+ concerns, relational problems, truama, and childhood trauma. I enjoy supporting neurodivergent clients and am neurodivergent-affirming, but I do not offer assessment services for ADHD or autistic clients at this time. Sliding scale is available upon request.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My work blends Person-Centered Therapy, Internal Family Systems (IFS), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), and mindfulness techniques to help clients increase awareness of patterns and inner dynamics that may be holding them back, and increase motivation to intervene in those patterns to create new outcomes. Relational boundaries, self-compassion, and cognitive flexibility are topics that frequently arise in my sessions. I hold a Master of Arts in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis and Clark College (2020), and a BA in Psychology from the University of Oregon (2003). I have done extra study and training in ACT and mindfulness skills, and I have completed the official Level 1 training in IFS.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I’m grateful to live in a time where work is being done to de-stigmatize mental health conditions, as they have long been a natural part of the human condition. Shame, self-judgement, and comparative thinking regarding inevitable inner experiences like anxiety and negative mood states are habits of mind that can be unlearned. I am aware of the privileges afforded by my white, able body and am committed to furthering my awareness of systematic oppression.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I have completed the official Level 1 training program for this model of therapy. I have also completed several continuing education courses, done extensive readings, and done IFS-specific consultation. This model appeals to me for its non-pathologizing stance and built-in supports for client autonomy.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I have taken 2 training courses in the ACT model (in 2021 and 2023), and have benefited from ACT concepts on a personal level as well! I apply the model flexibly and especially enjoy guiding clients through exercises to facilitate defusion from thoughts (i.e. stepping back into the "observing self").

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I've done extensive study of the Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) model and yoga and meditation are a part of my personal self-care routine. I employ a trauma-informed, individualized approach when offering mindfulness exercises in session. This allows clients to engage with a "dosage" and style of mindfulness that works well in the moment, and to feel comfortable interrupting the exercise at any point.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I work with anxiety using both top-down and bottom-up methods. Concepts from Acceptance and Commitment Theory and other forms of Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy are helpful in providing a "mental map" for action and can be used as "leverage" when feeling stuck in negative or anxious thoughts. Bottom-up methods include exercises like meditation, grounding in the 5 senses, and mindful movement. These exercises facilitate awareness, and increase your ability to stay with these challenging feelings.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: As a therapist, I've been extensively trained in reflective listening skills. The idea of reflective listening may be relatively simple, but it's application is nuanced, and it is a powerful means of cultivating the skill of self-awareness required for personal growth. I also frequently use concepts I've learned in my study of the Internal Family Systems model to help clients make sense of and resolve internal conflicts that may arise from simultaneously holding multiple perspectives.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I practice neurodivergent-affirming care. In a nutshell, this means our work will emphasize strengths over differences, and affirm your lived experiences. I understand the challenges of living in a society that is not set up to understand neurodivergent perspectives. I place great importance on both autonomy and authenticity, and I give clients lots of space to provide feedback on what is and is not working for them in therapy. I have a naturally slow pace in session and many find this helpful.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: My work in this area leans on both both academic training and lived experiences. As a non-binary human who has long worked to overturn gender roles, I am deeply supportive of both trans and nonbinary clients. I've worked with a wide variety of individuals, and have helped to address concerns ranging from dysphoria and coming out, to the invisibility of passing post-transition. I'm here to support you in becoming authentically you, and at home in your body.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: I have done professional training and study in this area and am Health at Every-Size informed, and aware of the presence of toxic cultural influences around dieting and fatphobia. I am accepting of clients as they are and believe that the work of unplugging from biased sources and de-programming cultural myths around our bodies is both valuable and necessary.

name: Léah Ferreira
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I’m Léah Ferreira. As a Queer therapist, my practice is a safe place for all people. No matter how you identify, you are welcome.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with adults coping with complex or childhood trauma, OCD, and relationship challenges like infidelity and communication breakdowns. I support LGBTQIA+ individuals and couples, including those exploring gender identity, non-monogamy, kink, and BDSM. My approach is trauma-informed and affirming. You don’t have to fit a label to feel welcome—my practice is open to all.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Anxiety can feel overwhelming, and depression can weigh heavily—sometimes even physically. To cope, we may adopt habits that feel helpful but aren’t always healing. Trauma can be isolating and exhausting. As a Queer, LGBTQIA+ therapist, I offer a holistic, eclectic approach tailored to your needs. I believe you are the expert of your own life. My role is to support you with compassion and collaboration as you move toward healing and growth.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Start your path toward growth and healing with a personalized approach that honors your unique mind and spirit. Together, we'll uncover what’s holding you back, tap into your strengths, and reshape patterns for lasting change. Nothing changes if nothing changes. My goal is to help you see that you are not your struggles. You have the power to overcome them, and it’s an honor to be along for the ride. With humor, mindfulness, empathy, and active listening, I validate your experiences and celebrate your strengths.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Narrative therapy helps individuals separate their identity from problems like anxiety or trauma, empowering them to rewrite limiting life stories. It centers on how personal, social, and cultural narratives shape identity, encouraging clients to re-author their stories in ways that reflect their strengths, values, and goals. This approach fosters agency, reduces shame, and supports more fulfilling relationships and personal growth.

name: Kaley Carpenter
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I help children & teens 3-18 with anxiety, depression, ADHD, trauma and more, utilizing play therapy and EMDR.
ideal_client: I work with children ages 3-12, adolescents ages 13-18. If your child is struggling with anxiety, depression, ADHD, trauma reaction, or if they are having a difficult time coping with family changes or transition; therapy could be a wonderful tool to help them move towards health and mental wellbeing!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I specialize in play therapy and EMDR. Past experiences, attachment, and familial relationships are important to therapy work, though my main focus in the therapy room is a strengths-based and present-focused approach. While in the counseling room, I will focus on mindfulness, attuning to both myself and my client and keeping our work focused on the here-and-now and bring awareness to the client’s emotional state. I will utilize different play therapy techniques, along with EMDR. Overall, my approach is integrative and I enjoy tailoring my therapeutic work to the specific needs and development of my client. Overall, my approach is integrative and I enjoy tailoring my therapeutic work to the needs and development of my client.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I was born and raised in Portland and am a big Portland Timbers and Thorns soccer fan! In my free time I also love reading, going on walks, and enjoying coffee with friends and family.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: If your child is struggling with anxiety, depression, ADHD, trauma reaction, or if they are having a difficult time coping with family changes or transition; therapy could be a wonderful tool to help them move towards health and mental wellbeing!

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I specialize in play therapy and EMDR. Past experiences, attachment, and familial relationships are important to therapy work, though my main focus in the therapy room is a strengths-based and present-focused approach. While in the counseling room, I will focus on mindfulness, attuning to both myself and my client and keeping our work focused on the here-and-now and bring awareness to the client’s emotional state.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I wholeheartedly believe all people have the capacity for growth, healing, and wellness. Reaching out for help is a powerful first step, and I would be honored to work with you as you navigate understanding ADHD and how it may impact you.

name: Jason Schaefer
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Helping adults explore autism, ADHD, or heal from trauma using a psychodynamic approach in teletherapy. OHP-CareOregon. Immediate openings.
ideal_client: My clients often feel like outsiders and seek validation for their unique perspectives. They may have a strong sense of justice and struggle with self-acceptance. My clients sometimes navigate internal contradictions, like being frequently forgetful yet able to recall obscure details, or being highly sensitive while struggling to identify emotions. Many have faced trauma, resulting in anxiety, emotional dysregulation, or relationship issues. Together, we build self-confidence and foster growth.

approaches.How I Can Help You: As a psychodynamic and depth psychology-oriented therapist, I specialize in supporting adults exploring their own possible autism or ADHD, or who are healing from trauma through teletherapy. Drawing from my personal experience as a late-diagnosed neurodivergent adult, I understand the unique challenges you face. Together, we work to validate your unique perspectives, navigate internal contradictions, and address trauma-related issues like anxiety and emotional dysregulation. My approach emphasizes self-acceptance, building self-confidence, and fostering personal growth. By creating a safe and accepting space, I help you move from seeking external validation to trusting your own insights and decisions. I have immediate openings and offer a tiered, honor-based sliding scale cash fee arrangement. I'm here to support your journey toward a more confident and authentic self.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: My path to becoming a therapist was shaped by my own journey to understand and accept my identity as a late-diagnosed neurodivergent person. Therapy was pivotal in embracing my differences and aligning my career with my core values of honesty, social justice, and acceptance. I am deeply committed to truly understanding how you feel, ensuring that you are always heard and understood. As an empathetic listener who asks clarifying questions, I create a safe and supportive environment where you can freely share your experiences. My personal and professional background allows me to recognize and honor your unique challenges, fostering a relationship built on trust and respect. With specialized training in Jungian psychodynamic and depth psychology, complemented by humanistic and parts work techniques inspired by Carl Rogers and Voice Dialogue, I offer a versatile and compassionate approach. Additionally, I integrate mindfulness and body-centered practices to support your overall well-being.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: My master's education was in a Depth-oriented program where I wrote a thesis dealing with the importance of the individual subjective experience. I believe the unconscious has a profound effect on how we interact with the world. I work to bring troublesome unconscious patterns into the open where you can make conscious decisions about them and move forward with your life.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Being in the grip of depression may mean you feel numb. Any emotion that passes through you feels like it is out of reach or dampened by a thick cotton pad. It also may show up as a distinct lack of energy and motivation to go about the activities of your daily life. Depression shows up in very individual ways. Therapy can help you regain full access to your emotions and unlock the energy and will to move forward again.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Do you have a persistent feeling of unease, worry, or fear about perceived threats or some future event? Anxiety can be mild to severe and can show up in multiple ways, such as rapid breathing, increased heart rate, restlessness, sleeplessness, or difficulty concentrating. Therapy can help you address the voice inside that is constantly worried about everything. I can help you find the source of this voice and turn down the volume, so you can focus on moving forward with confidence.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Has your relationship become dissatisfying? Are you wondering if this is all there is? Do you want your relationship to be a sanctuary, but don’t feel the necessary trust? Relationships are the yoga of the soul. No two relationships are alike and each one is packed with the specific emotional and soul work needed from the two participants in the relationship. Relationship therapy can help you unpack that work and help you learn how to relate from your authentic self.

name: Dr. Tee Mayfield
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Dr. Tee is a (LPC) licensed professional counselor in the state of Oregon and holds a PhD in Marriage Family Therapy.
ideal_client: Dr. Tee is an essential therapist who helps with FMLA, Medication Management, CPS, Foster Care, DHS cases and is savvy with utilizing different resources to assist in day to day obstacles. She enjoys meeting clients where they are at in their treatment and in their crisis. Her schedule is very flexible and will work with clients based on their availability and finances.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: She has been practicing mental health treatment in a variety of settings such as Inpatient, PHP, IOP and private practice. She has Bachelor's degree in Psychology and a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Texas Woman's University and is currently a Doctoral Candidate in Marriage and Family Therapy from NCU. She is skilled in different modalities such as DBT, CBT, EMDR as well as Existential therapy. Tee is also resourceful and helpful with navigating through minor to major crisis in life.

name: Anthony Boyd
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I align closely with Jungian theory and primarily use Psychodynamic Therapy as a healing modality.
ideal_client: I work with adults and teens of varying cultural backgrounds struggling with issues including, but not limited to, LGBTQ+ issues, gender identity issues, body image, self-esteem issues, depression, anxiety, grief, sexuality, PTSD, and personality disorder.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Working from a multicultural perspective that employs a Person-centered approach, I am able to gain a holistic perspective of you. Throughout your therapy, we will collaborate as we tend to your inner life; both the light and shadow. I will listen to you closely with care and curiosity, and without judgment. I align closely with Jungian theory and primarily use Psychodynamic Therapy. By helping you find and recognize patterns in your emotions, thoughts, and beliefs, you can gain insight into yourself. I find this approach fosters individuation and integration, allowing for wholeness and becoming the highest version of yourself. I have a deep interest in utilizing expressive arts as a tool within therapy to aid in self-discovery. I work with adults and teens of varying cultural backgrounds struggling with issues including, but not limited to, LGBTQ+ issues, gender identity issues, body image, self-esteem issues, depression, anxiety, grief, sexuality, PTSD, and personality disorder.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a therapist because I felt like I was wasting my innate gifts by continuing down the 20 year long path of a graphic designer in a corporate world. Throughout school as a child, I was severely bullied for being different. It took many years to understand myself, and to understand that people really did love and care about me. As a member of the LGBTQ+ community, I work to help all that struggle with not only their sexuality, but also their gender. I believe in and support equality for all, and human rights for all. I support Black Lives Matter and am an ally for all BIPOC peoples. I work hard to identify my bias, understand my intersectionality, and do my best to use my position and privilege to benefit those without it. That said, I am also willing to be called out by someone when a micro-aggression occurs in the course of therapy. They happen, and to pretend they don't means I am part of the problem. I'd much rather be part of the solution and help you thrive.

name: Patrick Petrie
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Depth-oriented and Relational Psychodynamic Therapy
ideal_client: Do you feel free to live out your values, your wants, your deepest heartfelt desires? Do you struggle to reconcile your identity, your status, or lack of opportunities with the life you actually dream of living? Are you grieving something that is difficult to name, touch, or even look at? I admire your openness and commitment to taking the next step. What arises in you will always be worthy of love, presence, and curiosity during our work together.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe therapy is a radical process that hinges entirely on the trust we establish and voluntarily commit to. When else do we get to slow down for an hour and have the opportunity to practice being vulnerable with ourself, let alone a stranger? Despite the sufferings and stressors plaguing our lives, I believe your inner world holds a beautiful hearth that longs to center you and call you home. Over the course of therapy, I believe we will cultivate a practice of trusting this to be true, and a place that can be accessed more readily throughout your day to day life. I trust that what brought you here matters, I trust that change is possible, and I trust that we will make great strides in this work together. My frame of reference is driven by the importance of relationship while also utilizing the wisdom of the body, mind, and spirit to inform us of our best approach to holistic wellbeing.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: The particularity of our stories matter. I strongly affirm the interconnectedness of all living beings, that our struggles are both personal and collective. I welcome your lived experience, your personal beliefs, and your identities without judgment. As a White, able-bodied, and male practitioner, I recognize my areas of privilege and inherent differences in lived experiences. I strive to practice with an open mindset that is culturally sensitive and anti-oppressive. I strive to be a provider who uses my position to empower others, advocate when systems do not serve us, and continuously learn/unlearn for the betterment of our collective liberation and growth.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: As a Relational Psychodynamic therapist, I bring a depth of training that honors the beautiful complexities of the human psyche, as well as the belief that what arises in the therapy session is always worth being curious enough to sit with. More often than not, we'll stumble upon unconscious patterns, long held beliefs, past attachment wounds, and an internal wisdom that will likely arrive have transformative ripple effects on your life.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Eye Movement Desensitization & Reprocessing is an evidence-based method of treatment. I enjoy utilizing the structure and container of EMDR through a uniquely tailored approach to your specific struggles. EMDR works well for letting go of long-held beliefs, stuck patterns, and especially for lingering traumatic or stressful memories. EMDR is quite different from regular talk therapy and can possibly bring about distressing emotions during the session.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I employ a comfortability in sitting with themes that are often difficult to name, explain, touch, or even look at. Sometimes therapy can be most effective and healing by just providing enough space to speak something aloud for the first time, and to then digest, process, and determine what meaning it has for us moving forward. Human beings are incredibly resilient in the face of suffering, so long as they have a grasp on their innermost values and meaning they hold in this life.

name: Dr. Tee Mayfield
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Dr. Tee is a (LPC) licensed professional counselor skilled in different modalities such as DBT, CBT, EMDR as well as Existential therapy.
ideal_client: Our team of providers are experienced in all areas of mental health. We believe in a holistic approach to health care, treating each individual with dedication and compassion. We pride ourselves on getting to know each one of our clients and tailor treatment plans to fit each individual. We understand the complexity and depth of mental health and well-being. We believe developing a strong therapeutic relationship is pivotal to helping you unlock your full potential.

approaches.My Background: Dr. Tee is a (LPC) licensed professional counselor in the state of Texas, Arizona and Oregon. She has been practicing mental health treatment in a variety of settings such as Inpatient, PHP, IOP and private practice. She has Bachelor's degree in Psychology and a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Texas Woman's University and is currently a Doctoral Candidate in Marriage and Family Therapy from NCU. She is skilled in different modalities such as DBT, CBT, EMDR as well as Existential therapy. Tee is also resourceful and helpful with navigating through minor to major crisis in life. Tee is an essential therapist who helps with FMLA, Medication Management, CPS cases and is savvy with utilizing different resources to assist in day to day obstacles. She enjoys meeting clients where they are at in their treatment and in their crisis. Her schedule is very flexible and will work with clients based on their availability and finances.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Here at Center of Cultivating is dedicated to the mission of partnering with patients to improve their quality of life. We promise to be there for you every step of your journey. Our goal is to create a healthy and reliable patient and professional partnership in which is the heart of our organization. We are committed to providing high quality care. Let’s us work together to get you feeling your best!

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: With an emphasis on confidential, personalized support, our Domestic Violence Survivor Program offers: Counseling: Experienced, master’s level counselors specializing in domestic violence recovery provide four individual counseling sessions. Support groups: Our groups cover a variety of topics, with a focus on helping survivors heal from the impact of their trauma. Crisis intervention: Our experts lead crisis intervention and support groups

specialities.name: Adoption Issues
specialities.description: If you know of anyone caring for a child with a traumatic history, don’t hesitate to recommend Center of Cultivating Parents services today. We welcome the opportunity to provide caregivers with mental health professionals and resources equipped to help children or teens heal. This is a fight no foster child or parent should weather alone.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Our broad range of support programs, many of which are offered via Zoom, and video chat, provide services to children from pre-school through late adolescence as well as their parents. All programs are guided by agency experts in youth development, education, literacy and learning, parenting, mental health, and trauma. Through collaborations with community partners, COCP addresses the challenges faced by many families in under-resourced communities in Dallas.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression, fear, and anxiety are some of the most common and uncomfortable emotions that we can experience at some point in our lives. Through therapy and treatment, we are able to help you recover motivation, perspective, and joy that you once had in your life.

name: Sarah Moyer
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I'm passionate about helping parents, children, teens, and adults feel more confident and connected in their everyday lives.
ideal_client: I work with parents, kids, teens, and adults navigating anxiety, ADHD, stress, emotional regulation, and life transitions. Many feel overwhelmed, stuck, or unsure of their next steps. I’m passionate about helping parents reconnect with their strengths, supporting kids and teens in building confidence, and guiding adults to explore their patterns and find clarity in order to move forward.

approaches.My Background: My path into therapy began as a personal trainer and basketball coach, where I discovered my love for motivation, mindset work, and helping others reach their potential. I later worked as a professional school counselor in both elementary and middle schools, where I supported students with emotional and behavioral challenges and collaborated closely with educators and families. In addition to my school-based experience, I gained valuable clinical experience working in private practice supporting children with ADHD, anxiety, and emotional regulation, as well as partnering with parents to strengthen the parent-child relationship. As a parent of three myself, I understand firsthand how rewarding—and at times overwhelming—family life can be. That personal experience continues to shape my compassionate, down-to-earth approach to supporting others through the ups and downs of parenting and daily life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My style is warm, collaborative, and grounded in both emotional insight and practical tools. I use a strengths-based, coaching-informed approach that blends reflection, skill-building, and support for meaningful change. Whether you're navigating the day-to-day or diving into deeper patterns, I’ll walk alongside you—helping you slow down, gain clarity, and take steady, empowering steps forward.

name: Mary Bruce-Owenby
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I offer a supportive, interactive approach to help you and your partner move from disconnection to the joy and intimacy of a secure bond.
ideal_client: I work with all types of couples at every stage of their relationship. From current, arising, emergent issues to longstanding ones, I am here to help and support you on your journey. I bring more than fifteen years of specialized training to couples work, and and I enjoy taking the two of you through a dynamic process where you build the skills, understandings, and experiences that grow and strengthen your bond toward secure functioning and relationship longevity.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have a BA from Wellesley College, an MA in clinical psychology from Antioch University, couples certifications from the Developmental Couples Institute and the PACT Institute, and a deep interest in helping couples thrive. Together, through a flexible but structured process, we identify pain points in the relationship and work through them using focused experiments and experiences that are similar to the difficulties you are experiencing. Throughout the process, we are strengthening emotional safety and the couple bond.

My approach is experiential. I am well versed in attachment, developmental, phenomenological, and psychoanalytic theory, and I believe that each person's earliest relational dynamics with their first caregiver makes a deep, formative impression on them that shows up in their relationships later in life. Buddhist Psychology, Gestalt Psychotherapy, and the psychobiological model (PACT) inform my somatic approach, which focuses couples on an awareness of their thoughts, behaviors, and emotions, without judgement.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Gaining a deeper understanding of yourself and your partner, learning how to co-regulate, practicing how to listen differently and respond more effectively, collaborating, cooperating, and relating through experiments that mirror your struggles and challenge your patterns--are just some of what you will actively work on.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: This approach explores the impacts that early relational patterns with first caregivers have on later life, when they show up in the couple. I have completed five years of specific training in psychoanalytic/psychodynamic theoretical frameworks (Object Relations) under the supervision of contemporary psychoanalysts and psychologists.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: I have trained in Gestalt therapy, a strengths-based, non-pathologizing approach, for the past eight years with the Gestalt Therapy Training Center Northwest (GTTCNW). Gestalt's emphasis on the importance of being aware of and accepting your current emotions without judgement and paying attention to here-and-now experience lays the groundwork for co-regulation and interactive regulation, a process we focus on in couples work that helps partners stay attuned and connected.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: An important part of our work together is somatic (relating to the body) in its focus, and we explore what happens when big emotions, like anger, frustration, or sadness come up. During these moments, it can be extremely difficult to regulate feelings, pay attention, and stay connected to each other. We often act out of our survival instincts, with automatic, lightning-fast reactions, which make it hard to stay present, understand, or empathize.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I use the PACT (Psychobiological Approach to Couples Therapy), a model that incorporates attachment theory as it relates to couples. Attachment theory focuses on our human need to form close, emotional bonds, and the impact of our first experiences of closeness with our caregiver on future relationships. There are attachment styles that emerge from this early experience that show up in our later relationships, and understanding them is key for becoming even more knowledgeable about your partner.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I help with understanding and navigating conflict, learning how to reconnect after disconnection, betrayals and repairs, issues coming up around commitment, and resolving historical anger, among many other issues.

specialities.name: Premarital Counseling
specialities.description: I help couples work through and resolve struggles coming up that they want to resolve before deepening their commitment.

name: Rebecca Brown Schroeder
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Nature-based and animal-assisted experiential therapy for children and adults on a 60-acre farm just outside Portland.
ideal_client: "Love recognizes no barriers. It jumps hurdles, leaps fences, penetrates walls to arrive at its destination full of hope." (Maya Angelou) Children & families encounter stressors in life that can be overwhelming - grief, loss, medical & environmental traumas. Children (even infants) are very sensitive to these stressors but they can recover with the support of parents/caregivers. I support children and families who have been through challenging experiences to grow together, heal and thrive.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to helping is holistic, compassion-focused, nature-based and experiential, including animal-assisted therapeutic activities. I have specialized training in Child Parent Psychotherapy - compassionately addressing complex issues impacting young children and their caregivers.
