I also specialize in treating youth and adults experiencing grief, loss, trauma, chronic and acute illness/pain, mood disorders and neurodivergence. My life experience with parenthood, grief/loss and caregiving for aging parents inform my practice and my connection with clients. I continuously cultivate a special interest in supporting grievers including those experiencing traumatic grief, end of life, and eco-grief. I have experience in supporting young grievers and their caregivers through my work at The Dougy Center for Grieving Children and Families, a place with so much heart and deep understanding.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I understand that play is a window into the internal world of the child and that holistic healing occurs across the lifespan in emotionally attuned relationships. I am passionate about the power of nature to awaken us to the present moment and spark the mind-body's innate capacity to heal. I believe that experiential and animal-assisted therapies are especially effective at deepening each client's awareness and understanding of themselves, their relationships and their environment. I have worked previously as a licensed special education teacher, a parent support coach, and an education policy advocate. I hold a B.S. in Human Development and Social Policy from Northwestern University and advanced degrees in Public Policy, Special Education, and Professional Mental Health Counseling. I am honored to walk alongside my clients in open-hearted connection as they grow toward healing, wholeness and vitality. I look forward to meeting you.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: I see clients at The Center at Heron Hill, a unique outpatient mental health practice located on a 60-acre farm just outside of Portland in Canby, Oregon. Our agency offers an Ecotherapy experience that utilizes nature and animals as well as a wide variety of experiential activities such as mindfulness, gardening activities, embodiment, movement and yoga-based activities, art activities, archery, slack line, sand tray, fire building, and opportunities to experience equine-assisted therapy.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Play is a window into the internal world of the child. Through play children are able to communicate their needs and feelings. Helping parents and other caregivers understand the unique emotional, social and developmental needs of their children is at the heart of my practice. I utilize a nature-based, child-centered approach to play therapy, often incorporating animal-assisted experiences. My approach is grounded in evidence-based practices, attachment theory, and interpersonal neurobiology.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I continuously cultivate a special interest in supporting grievers, including bereaved infants, toddlers and preschoolers. I have specialized training in supporting these youngest grievers and their caregivers using the evidence-based approaches of Child Parent Psychotherapy and EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing) Therapy. I offer grief counseling to people of all ages, including those experiencing traumatic grief, end of life, and eco-grief.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have specialized training in helping young children and their families/caregivers navigate stressful life events including trauma, medical issues, loss of a parent/caregiver, divorce, violence, and systemic oppression/marginalization. Utilizing the evidence-based Child Parent Psychotherapy approach, I help parents and caregivers support the child(ren) in their life to address behavioral concerns, to recover and to thrive.

name: Elizabeth Sokolowski, PhD
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Hi! I'm Soko, a queer psychologist with experience helping clients heal trauma, regulate emotions, and improve their trust in themselves.
ideal_client: I provide therapy for adults (18+) who may be struggling with anxiety, depression, PTSD, trauma, grief, chronic illness, or identity. I may be a good fit for you if you want to explore your lived experiences, learn more about your mental health symptoms, reinforce and adapt strengths to your advantage, and try out new coping skills, like self-compassionate alternative perspectives or mindfulness. I can work with you to collaboratively develop a treatment plan that empowers your needs.

approaches.My Background: I am licensed as a Psychologist in the State of Oregon (#3490) by the Oregon Board of Psychology. My interest in mental health started in undergrad during a philosophy class exploring the mind and early psychology. Due to experiences with chronic illness, I learned the importance of caring for both mind and body. I graduated with a PhD in Psychology from Colorado State University. I was trained as a generalist clinician to treat a wide variety of presenting concerns. I often saw clients for anxiety, depression, PTSD, trauma, grief, loss, and other life stressors. I focused my dissertation to benefit the LGBTQ+ graduate student population by identifying climate concerns (e.g., microaggressions, harassment, mental health impacts, efforts to cope) and generating a list of recommendations to improve campus climate. I became a psychologist because I wanted to provide the same safety, validation, understanding, and support for others, just like my first therapist provided for me.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from trauma-informed, humanistic, and cognitive-behavioral lenses, which together recognize the influence that past and present traumatic experiences can have upon our mental health, our relationship with ourselves, and our relationships with others. I believe that change can occur for you through exploring your stories, learning about yourself, building skills, challenging your doubts, and recognizing your strength and resiliency. I recognize that our personal and cultural identities often influence our mental health and social interactions, leading to both strengths and traumatic experiences within our lives. I identify as white, genderfluid, queer, a dog mom, an aunt, and living with chronic health conditions. I invite you to discuss how your identities and lived experiences have influenced your mental health. I approach therapy with warmth, empathy, openness, and light-hearted humor to foster spaces for these conversations and identities to grow.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: From a humanistic lens, I believe that people are fundamentally good and doing the best they can to live happy and healthy lives. Reducing distress often includes building awareness about yourself, your identity, and who you want to be. It is important to restore your trust in yourself, your wisdom, and your ability to heal from within.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I use CBT to help clients understand the relationships between their thoughts, emotions, and actions. This work begins with an intake to gain clarity of symptoms, diagnosis, impairments, and treatment goals. CBT helps to create change by treating the unhelpful maintenance factors (e.g., low motivation) through alternative thoughts or behaviors. When change is unhelpful, I help clients find balance through acceptance skills (e.g., mindfulness) and processing stressors.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I treat PTSD through a three-phased approach: 1) building coping skills to reduce severity of current symptoms, 2) processing traumas through narrative methods, and 3) re-establishing thriving (e.g., setting and achieving goals, connecting interpersonally).

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Utilizing CBT, I help clients explore unhelpful belief systems and treat the psychological maintenance factors of depression, such as low motivation, poor sleep, ongoing stressors, or past trauma.

specialities.name: Social Phobia
specialities.description: I help clients reduce the intensity of their social anxiety and gain confidence through CBT, mindfulness skills and exposure activities. Sessions may focus upon identifying unhelpful belief systems, exploring originating traumas, learning mindfulness skills, and developing alternative thoughts to try-out during the week as homework.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I am a genderfluid and queer identified psychologist with lived experiences of being queer within multiple climates within the United States. I completed the WPATH Global Education Institute's Foundations Course training online in 2021. I have experience providing assessments and letters of support for gender-affirming medical care.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I have experience learning about the cognitive components of ADHD while I provided neuropsychological assessments for three years, with one year focused solely upon assessing ADHD. Please note: I do not currently provide neuropsychological assessment or diagnosis for ADHD. However, in individual therapy, I help clients differentiate their attention and working memory difficulties from their mental health symptoms. I also help clients build skills and fine tune routines.

name: Joe Cross-Sarvis
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: ACCEPTING NEW CLIENTS!!! The fastest way to start services is to visit our website at WWW.SYNCHRONOUSMENTALHEALTH.COM

name: Bryce Taylor
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help people heal from trauma, grief, and life changes by offering support, understanding, and tools to manage overwhelming emotions.
ideal_client: In this space, I work best with adults navigating trauma, grief, anxiety, or life transitions. I support those healing from childhood abuse, loss, or relational wounds, and individuals who feel overwhelmed, isolated, or misunderstood. I especially welcome neurodivergent clients and those seeking a deeper understanding of themselves. My approach is compassionate, trauma-informed, and rooted in EMDR, Internal Family Systems, and Attachment Theory. Together, we create a path toward healing, resilie

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work with people navigating trauma, grief, anxiety, and major life changes. You might be feeling overwhelmed, isolated, or unsure how to move forward, especially if you're healing from something like childhood abuse, a traumatic loss, or the impact of neurodivergence. I offer a compassionate, nonjudgmental space where we can explore your experiences together. My approach draws on EMDR, Internal Family Systems, and Attachment Theory to help you process what you’ve been through and build meaningful coping tools. Healing is possible, and you don’t have to do it alone. I'm here to walk with you through it.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I'm a trauma-informed therapist who believes that healing happens in safe, supportive relationships. My work is rooted in social justice, and I welcome clients of all identities, including LGBTQ+ and neurodivergent individuals. I believe in showing up with compassion, authenticity, and curiosity. I’m trained in EMDR, Internal Family Systems, and Attachment Theory, and I'm passionate about helping people make sense of painful experiences and reconnect with their inner strength. Outside of therapy, I care deeply about mental health access in rural and coastal communities and believe everyone deserves to be seen, heard, and supported.

name: Kirsten Kelly Chambers
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Serving teens, adults, couples and families. Accepting new clients for in-person sessions.
ideal_client: Are you constantly feeling like you're not good enough, that you don't measure up? Are your relationships suffering? Are you feeling hopeless, irritable, exhausted and chronically stressed and uncertain why? I can help you uncover the answers that will strengthen your relationships with yourself and others, and enable you to find joy again. When you are ready to start, I will be here with a safe, supportive and open heart, and hold space for you to process, heal and grow.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I will help you identify the source of your symptoms and help you find acceptance and self-compassion while discovering healthier ways to heal, connect and eventually thrive. I use authenticity, humor, directness, warmth and a strengths-based approach to help you build resiliency and self-confidence. Treatment is an individualized process, which means I meet you where you are and create a plan to support your individual needs and goals. Through my work as a therapist, I strive to integrate social justice and equity, and thus my goal is to make counseling more accessible and less stigmatized. I offer a select number of sliding scale spots for those experiencing financial hardship.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor registered with the State of Oregon license number C7531. I earned my masters in professional mental health counseling with a specialization in addictions from Lewis & Clark College and my bachelors in communications and psychology from Syracuse University in New York. Prior to joining the counseling field, I spent 15 years as a public relations specialist working in both the corporate and nonprofit sectors. As a therapist, I have 10 years of experience providing individual, group and family therapy to youth, adults and families in residential, outpatient, school-based and community mental health settings. I am a mom to identical twin post-college age daughters, a native Portlander, an active ally to BIPOC and LGBTQ communities and graduate of Portland Public Schools.

name: Daniel Hofmann
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide counseling for adults experiencing depression, anxiety, trauma, relationship troubles, or just struggling with life in general.
ideal_client: I enjoy getting to know clients human-to-human and understanding their unique histories and contexts. My most rewarding work is in helping people uproot problematic ways of coping that they've internalized from their families and society at large. We'll work well together if you're looking to change relationship patterns, free yourself from feelings of sadness and fear, and work through old traumas. I have experience with folks across spectrums of gender, sexuality, ethnicity, SES, age, & faith.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have a Masters degree in Couples and Family Counseling from Portland State University and experience working with children, teens, couples, families, and individuals in community mental health and private practice settings. My approach to counseling is trauma-informed and integrative, drawing on my knowledge of a variety of therapeutic models while being rooted in humanistic, psychodynamic, and emotionally-focused psychotherapies. I believe that we all naturally have many facets, or parts, of ourselves that help us navigate our complicated world. When these parts are balanced, we feel good and function well in relationships. Stress and trauma push our innate mechanisms for healing and coping into extremes. Many mental health symptoms can be viewed as counterproductive attempts at restoring our natural equilibrium. I will create a space in which we can safely explore the origins of your difficulties and help you find a new sense of balance in the present.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I work from a non-pathologizing and non-judgmental stance. I believe that all people have a core of good and wellness within them; even those who have it buried very deep down. When you view things from a systems perspective, concepts of fault and blame start to lose their meaning. I have yet to encounter a person whose feelings and actions didn't make sense after taking a holistic view of them. I will strive to understand and build your own awareness of who you are. I will be compassionate when challenging you to try something new. I will find and amplify the good in you, even when all you can feel is bad.

name: Nathan Becker
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Feeling scattered, stuck, or spun out? Let's slow it down, sort it out, and find what works. For your brain and your life.
ideal_client: I work best with adults who feel overwhelmed, scattered, or stuck— whether you're navigating Anxiety, ADHD, OCD, BFRBs (Skin Picking & Hair Pulling), Insomnia, or all of the above. My clients are often deep thinkers with busy minds, big feelings, and a desire for change that feels doable and real. We focus on building practical tools, self-understanding, and a relationship with your brain that’s rooted in compassion, not criticism.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am committed to creating a collaborative space in which you and I can work together to cultivate change. My approach is informed by my values and qualities of empathy, authenticity, openness, and social justice. I believe in gently challenging, pushing you outside of your comfort zone while focusing on and acknowledging your sources of strength and resiliency. I incorporate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) into much of my work, where we will focus on changing maladaptive behaviors and disengaging from negative thought patterns.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I became a therapist because I know what it’s like to feel overwhelmed, misunderstood, and unsure how to move forward. As someone who identifies as neurodiverse, I bring not only clinical training, but lived experience to the work I do. My practice is rooted in authenticity, compassion, and a belief in the power of small, meaningful change. I specialize in working with adults navigating ADHD, Anxiety, OCD, Insomnia, BFRBs, and the heavy self-criticism that often comes with them. I use evidence-based therapies like CBT, ACT, and ERP, and I balance those tools with warmth, curiosity, and respect for your unique experience. I care deeply about creating a space where all parts of you are welcome—including the messy, scared, or uncertain ones. Whether you're seeking clarity, healing, or simply space to breathe, I'm here to walk with you, not ahead of you.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: With Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, we learn to accept the experience of our thoughts and feelings, rather than attempting to avoid or control them. We also set out on a path of self-discovery, uncovering our values and what truly matters to us. ACT teaches us to let that awareness guide us, so we can pursue a life filled with meaning and fulfillment.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy is the gold standard approach for treating anxiety, depression, and insomnia. If any of these concerns are interfering with your peace during the day or keeping you up at night, I hope it gives you hope to know there’s a path forward and that change is possible.

specialities.name: Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy
specialities.description: Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) is an evidence-based therapy for anxiety disorders like OCD, social anxiety, panic, and phobias. Anxiety can be so intense that we start to believe the story it’s telling us—or avoid the very things we care about most. ERP helps us interrupt those patterns and gently face our fears, so life can start expanding again.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: At the forefront of my work, I am human. While I’m passionate about behavioral techniques, they come second to our shared humanity. My goal is to create a space where you can come exactly as you are: your thoughts, your emotions, your story. I’ve been told I bring warmth and compassion into the room, and I do my best to lead with those qualities every time we meet.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: Motivational Interviewing is a collaborative approach that helps you explore your own reasons for change, without pressure or judgment. I’ll hold space for ambivalence, honoring the part of you that wants something different and the part that’s still unsure. Together, we’ll clarify what matters to you and gently move toward action that feels aligned and doable.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Life with ADHD can feel like a constant game of catch-up: racing thoughts, lost keys, piles of laundry, unfinished tasks, and that endless inner voice saying, “Why can’t I just...?” I work with adults navigating the overwhelm, shame, and unique strengths that come with neurodivergence. Together, we’ll build understanding, structure, and self-compassion, without trying to “fix” who you are.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: When your mind won’t slow down, when worry runs the show, when you’re exhausted from overthinking everything, you’re not alone. Anxiety can feel all-consuming, but it doesn’t have to control your life. We’ll work together to help you reconnect with the present, loosen anxiety’s grip, and build a life that feels spacious, steady, and aligned with what matters to you.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: OCD can be a lonely, exhausting loop; obsessions you don’t want, compulsions you feel you can’t resist, and a cycle that steals your time, energy, and confidence. You may wonder if anyone really gets it. I do. Together, we’ll use Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) to help you face the fear, break the patterns, and reclaim your freedom.

specialities.name: Insomnia
specialities.description: If falling asleep feels like a battle and staying asleep feels impossible, you know how much poor rest takes from you, emotionally, mentally, physically. Insomnia isn’t just about sleep; it’s about reclaiming your peace. With evidence-based tools like CBT-I, we’ll quiet the spiral, rebuild trust with your body, and help you find rest again, without relying on quick fixes.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Therapy isn’t just for crises, it’s also for those moments when something deeper is calling you forward. You may not be falling apart, but you want more: more clarity, more peace, more purpose. I’ll help you explore your identity, values, and the stories you carry, so you can move through the world with more intention, direction, and trust in yourself.

name: Dr. Michelle Pliske
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I work with individuals and families across the lifespan both in person and via telehealth formats.
ideal_client: My specialty areas include child development, trauma, anxiety, grief & loss and chronic medial issues. I have a play therapy room designed for expressive therapies and family systems work. I am certified in trauma, EMDR for children and adults and am faculty at the institute teaching in trauma informed care, play therapy, clinical supervision and animal assisted human health. I provide clinical supervision for professionals seeking licensing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Creating an environment of safety means having a focus on relationships. It is impossible to think creatively, problem solve or think through some of the most profound or difficult experiences in life if there isn't a feeling of trust. Relationships matter and I believe it is important to invest in building that trust and safety in therapy. Children find trust and safety through an environment in which they can be authentic. Play therapy offers a child an environment of safety. If children are able to say what they think or how they feel through toys/art/sand/media with someone who can translate their behavior and facilitate the process, they will respond positively and can successfully work through their presenting issues.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a doctoral degree in clinical social work and social policy with a trauma specialization. This includes not only how we support individuals but communities as a whole. I have post-graduate certifications in play therapy, adoption and foster care, trauma informed care, children's yoga and animal assisted human health. I work in partnership with my therapy dog Mercury. I am dual board certified as a supervisor in social work/counseling and play therapy practices.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Relational-cultural therapy examines the complexity of human relationships, exploring concepts of connection and disconnection as a primary source of stress, as well as recognizing and exploring the social implications of theory and mental health. Culture brings into focus the influence of larger dominate voices and policies and how power differentials impact the quality of daily living, adversity, trauma, and the nature of relationships.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Play therapy involves using toys, sand, art, games, and other materials to help children express themselves. Play offers the child an environment of safety. If children are able to say what they think or how they feel through toys and art with someone who can translate their behavior and facilitate the process, they will respond positively and are able to successfully work through their problems.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: Family therapy includes every member of the family. My role is to find opportunities through creativity for every member to have a voice and to feel included regardless of age. Each family member holds a different role and perspective and should be a part of the therapy process.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Adverse experiences in early childhood and throughout adulthood contribute to a variety of health issues. I provide clinical mental health care and collaborate with allied healthcare professionals to support children, adolescents, and adults impacted by abuse and trauma.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Children frequently have difficulty talking about what is bothering them or talking about events that have occurred in their lives. My approach to counseling children and adolescents is to use a prescriptive method of play or expressive arts therapy (using the best fitting evidenced based practice that meets the needs of your child, integrated into hands-on work that brings counseling to life).

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a common condition in which the person excessively worries about a variety of different topics or a specific topic or experience. This worry is excessive and uncontrollable and associated with additional symptoms of anxiety. I provide support from a relational and cognitive behavioral approach to reduce stress and worry and engage in life.

name: Cedar Hills Outpatient Services
title: Social Worker
intro: We offer Intensive Outpatient and Partial Hospitalization group therapy programs to help you back on the road to health, hope, and healing.
ideal_client: Group therapy can instill a renewed sense of hope, remind us that we are not alone in our struggles, and give us a safe place for empathy, vulnerability, and learning. Our clinicians facilitate a structured group environment where you can learn and practice new skills for positive change in your everyday life. Your treatment is driven by you, the client, while heavily supported and guided by our clinical and administrative team. You are not alone, and you are worth investing in yourself!

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: We are not all in the same boat, but we are all in the same stormy ocean. Here, we recognize a need for versatility in treatment. We offer Intensive Outpatient (IOP) and Partial Hospitalization (PHP, aka, Day Treatment) levels of care. We have in-person and virtual options, as well as morning, afternoon, or evening groups. Programs are typically 6-8 weeks long. While enrolled, you will have access to the program's psychiatric provider for medication management. Group program options vary and currently include mental health focus co-occurring mental health and substance use disorders, health and wellness, DBT skills based, and women's group treatments. Our group therapists utilize skills in crisis intervention, safety planning, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, Motivational Interviewing, Narrative Therapy, Internal Family Systems, Acceptance & Commitment Therapy, and more. We specialize in treating depression, anxiety, bipolar, trauma, addictions, and more.

approaches.Our Personal Beliefs and Interests: All of our therapists have at least one thing in common: We are all human. We appreciate authenticity and accept you as you are right now. We believe in compassion, kindness, and strengths. We also believe that life is really hard sometimes, and we can support you through it! Our group program therapists have a wide range of professional backgrounds and experiences ranging from work in youth programs, shelters, crisis hotlines, psychiatric hospitals, domestic violence, addiction and recovery, medical social work, child welfare, individual therapy, schools, donation centers, the Peace Corps, and more. We also have a lot of fun and different interests. We're all a bit different, and we love it that way.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Our program therapists provide psychoeducation on depression, symptoms, treatment options, and coping skills. Group therapy provides the space for processing, interpersonal learning, empathy and vulnerability, and learning and practicing new coping skills to manage depressive symptoms.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Our program therapists provide psychoeducation on anxiety and panic disorders, symptoms, treatment options, and coping skills. Group therapy provides the space for processing, interpersonal learning, empathy and vulnerability, and learning and practicing new coping skills to manage anxious symptoms. Group therapy is also a safe space to venture out to when struggling with agoraphobia or social anxiety.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Our program therapists provide psychoeducation on substance abuse and risks for relapse, treatment options, and coping skills. Group therapy provides the space for processing, interpersonal learning, empathy and vulnerability, and learning and practicing new coping skills to achieve and/or maintain sobriety.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Cedar Hills Outpatient offers a Women's Group that is a safe, supportive, and empowering space for women to focus on their mental health and / or substance recovery while balancing the pressures of womanhood and / or historical trauma. This program therapist is female and is certified in trauma treatment (CCTP).

name: Nancy Walker
title: Professional Counselor
intro: Practicing IFS, I serve clients to know & lead from their true Self by exploring conflicting parts of themselves w/curiosity & compassion

name: Emalie Coplan
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Trauma-informed therapy for queer adults in OR. Client-led, somatic, and IFS-rooted. Heal past wounds & reconnect with your authentic self.
ideal_client: ​​I’m passionate about working with folks who want to process past trauma and relearn how to feel safe in the present. I frequently work with people who grew up in dysfunctional families, and have experienced neglect and abuse in close relationships. These experiences often lead to secondary challenges such as depression, anxiety, and relational concerns. I work with clients who are eager to reconnect to their authentic selves & feel ready to dive into this process with dedication and courage.

approaches.My Background and Approach: In our therapeutic relationship, we will collaboratively create a safe space for exploration, delving into your past and navigating the path between where you currently stand and where you aspire to be. I tailor interventions for each client, drawing on IFS and experiential techniques like EMDR, Brainspotting, and psychedelics (psilocybin and ketamine). My approach is relational, client-led, collaborative, and social justice-oriented. As a white therapist, I am deeply committed to actively learning from those who hold marginalized identities, applying an intersectional lens, and practicing from a place of cultural humility and anti-racism. Additionally, this means I am sex, kink, and fat-positive, and aim to provide neurodivergent and polyamory/non-monogamy affirming care. Our lives are political, and our mental health and well-being is always tied to the systems and structures we live within. As a queer person, I am especially committed to working with queer and trans communities.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: As someone who overcame a difficult childhood, I’m not too different from you. I come from my own traumas throughout childhood and into adult life. I experienced and survived a dysfunctional childhood, I’m a 10/10 on the Adverse Childhood Experiences (ACES). Despite seeming to “have it together”, I felt detached from my emotions and my sense of self. I had numerous relationships but lacked true intimacy, not realizing this was a common experience for trauma survivors—feeling a painful internal split and deep self-estrangement. When I began my own healing, it became a transformative process for me. It helped me integrate my childhood trauma and reclaim lost parts of myself. With the right support, I stopped avoiding my feelings and started feeling a sense of belonging, finding the courage and safety to reconnect with myself. Therapy profoundly transformed my life and mended my heart. Inspired by my own journey, I am dedicated to offering others the same support and encouragement.

name: Michael Running
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor offering relationally-oriented counseling for individuals, relationships, and groups.
ideal_client: I work with different kinds of people who are often looking for relief from distress or seeking clarity from confusion. I have a particular focus on supporting men who struggle in their relationships with themselves, and quite often in their relationships with other men. I endeavor to form a healing relationship with you where the acceptance and presence I offer provide a safe space for you to move into new experiences of contentment, a sense of belonging, and the experience of fulfillment.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Counseling is relational: your relationship with yourself in your world, my own relationship to my self, and the relationship we form together. My person-centered and existential orientation to counseling sprouts from the rich soil of Gestalt Therapy, which brings curiosity, exploration, and present-process into the healing you wish to see. From this ground, I also utilize mindful somatic psychotherapy in understanding the wisdom your body and felt experience hold. To help transform painful emotions or traumatic experiences, I also use Emotion-Focused Therapy to access emotions that promote well-being which often lie underneath more painful ones. Bringing mindfulness into our relationship can also be an effective support to access and understand your experience. Curiosity and acceptance are the two pillars my counseling approach rests upon. Most of all, I trust in and rely upon your holistic experience and organic wish for well-being.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor and a Nationally Certified Counselor in private practice. Much of what I bring to therapy is informed by the near-decade I spent as a Buddhist monk both in the U.S. and overseas in Taiwan. This transformative and dedicated experience continues to unfold in meaning and purpose today. I was born here in the Willamette Valley of Oregon, falling in deep connection with the lands and waters that make this home so special. Before and after my time in the monastery, I worked for a decade with land conservation nonprofits throughout the state. I graduated from Portland State University in 2020 with a master’s degree in counseling for relationships and individuals. Concurrent with the accredited counseling program at PSU, I also received extensive training in Gestalt therapy, somatic psychotherapy (Hakomi), Emotion-Focused therapy, and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy. I also serve on the board of the Oregon Counseling Association.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: I have been in Gestalt Therapy training groups since 2018, including the integration of Buddhist Psychology and Gestalt Therapy, and find Gestalt to be a natural theoretical home for me. Gestalt therapy values the exploration of your present experience and curiosity around what gets in the way of engaging fully with the world.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness is at the core of both how I am with clients as well as the type of work we do together. I have over 20 years of experience in meditation and mindfulness, and much of my training (from somatic psychotherapy to ACT to Gestalt therapies) utilizes mindfulness (non-judgmental awareness of what is presently happening) to increase your well-being and capacity for choice in your life.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I have completed both individual and couples Emotion-Focused Therapy training programs from Edwards Psychotherapy here in Portland. EFT, Relational Gestalt, and mindfulness-based approaches are naturally complementary and offer a powerful fit for many clients.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I enjoy working one-on-one and in groups with men, whether they struggle with emotional awareness or regulation, relationship issues, life purpose, complex PTSD symptoms, or the like. I offer a safe, curious, and caring relational space to explore what it is like to be you and what might be holding you back from the life you wish for.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Relying upon the trifecta of Emotion-Focused, relationally-oriented, and body-centered methods, the approach I bring to the therapeutic relationship supports you in expanding your understanding of, and shifting your relationship with, emotional states (like anxiety and depression) that cause you distress.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Relying upon the trifecta of Emotion-Focused, relationally-oriented, and body-centered methods, the approach I bring to the therapeutic relationship supports you in expanding your understanding of, and shifting your relationship with, emotional states (like anxiety and depression) that cause you distress.

name: Matt Newey
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Reaching out for help can be difficult, but once the decision has been made, most people find the outcome to be extremely rewarding.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My style is interactive and goal-driven. Clients describe me as professional, personable, engaging, humorous and helpful. Most are able to quickly feel at ease around me and trust my expertise. My goal is to provide a safe and supportive environment where people can confront deeply personal matters even if those matters are difficult to talk about. Sometimes I am the first person my client has risked talking to about an issue; other times a client may have talked to many people but needs expert guidance to determine what to do.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Over 30 years of professional experience on top of two masters degrees in the field I have worked with a wide variety of people and issues. In addition I am certified in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, and am a certified anxiety and trauma treatment professional.

specialities.name: Addiction Therapy
specialities.description: Specialized training and experience with TCU Node Mapping substance use treatment

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Over 30 hours of training and supervision in IFS

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Earned certification in advance use of CBT for depression and anxiety.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Trained in the theory, interventions and skills of DBT through nearly 20 hours of continuing education.

specialities.name: Anger Management Therapy
specialities.description: Completed SAMSHA evidenced based training in Anger Management.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Earned a certificate in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for the treatment of depression.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Certified Clinical Anxiety Treatment Professional by the Institute of Certified Anxiety Treatment Professionals

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Certified Clinical Trauma Professional by the International Association of Trauma Professionals

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Supervisor/Provider for Substance Use Treatment programs for 6 years including residential, outpatient and drug court.

specialities.name: Anger Management
specialities.description: Trained in SAHMSA evidenced based anger management for those with mental health and or substance use disorders

name: Jessica Baker, M.A. LMFT
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: B.S. Health Psychology, M.A. Counseling, LMFT
intro: Together we will navigate life’s complexities to help you find healing, balance and happiness.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with individuals who consider themselves to be complex. Being human is a messy, complicated endeavor and my joyous work is to be with each one of my clients as they navigate their self discovery. From complicate relationships, to multifaceted health issues, to complex trauma, I will be there along side my clients as we peel back the layers to create health and freedom.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have a eclectic approach which is based upon the needs of my client at that time. I believe that the person, or people, that I am working with hold the wisdom to find happiness and healing. My role is to facilitate their goals through use of in depth exploration of the psyche, reflection and behavioral modification within the context of a safe space. I have a strong medical background and believe that people need to be treated as a whole system. This includes mind, body, spirit and relationships.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a background in developmental psychology, nutrition, eastern, western and natural medicine, as well as midwifery. I received my B.S. in Health Psychology from Bastyr University and my M.A. in Counseling with and emphasis in Depth Psychology from Pacifica Graduate Institute. I have clinical experience working with individuals, couples, children and families.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I often find that a person's attachment style is one of the strongest factors in how they related to the world and other people. When working with children I always hold their early experiences in mind and take them into account when working toward goals. The issues that couples face can often be traced to their attachment pattern. My role is to help translate each person's needs to their partner.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I really enjoy working with couples of all backgrounds to help them communicate more effectively and flourish as partners in life, as well as individuals. I often use Non-violent communication, Emotionally focused couples therapy and Gottman method techniques. LBGTQ friendly.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: While I am experienced in, and often use a wide range of therapeutic approaches, I am heart and soul a depth psychotherapist. I was trained at one of the only depth psychology schools in the country, Pacifica Graduate Institute. For those unfamiliar with depth psychology, I describe it as an approach that takes a person's unconscious into account just as much as the presenting issues.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: As a women, mother, wife and human being, I hold women's issues very close to my heart. Specifically, I work with pregnancy and birth experience, grief, health issues and identity. My published Master's thesis is on the topic of child birth as a rite of passage.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Parenting can be a very fulfilling and life changing journey; yet it is also challenging and can push a parent or couple to their limits. I offer a space to explore the new identity of being a parent, parenting consulting/ advice and way to cope with the challenges that arise from the blessings that are our children. I strongly identify with attachment theory and practices.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Sometimes families are in conflict because they are unable to hear what another is saying or understand where they are coming from. I work with families to effectively communicate and compromise, so everyone can feel heard and valued within the family unit.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I love working with people to help them find ways to live well together. I am open to seeing couples of all orientations and backgrounds. Some of the issues I specialize in are parenting, sexual issues, health, finances, infidelity and effective communication.

name: Sam Wilson
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: If you feel stuck, alone, overwhelmed or confused, talk therapy can offer a way forward. Now accepting new clients for teletherapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is always client centered and solution-focused. I employ narrative, cognitive, behavioral, and strengths-based approaches to helping you identify paths to achieving emotional wellness and satisfying relationships. I strive to create a space that is collaborative and non-judgmental for every client. I favor self-reflective interventions because I believe that most of the positive change that occurs through counseling comes from self-learning. I am happy to meet with you for a free consultation to discuss your goals and determine if I am a good fit for your needs.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I welcome adults, teenagers, and couples to my practice. My work with individuals often focuses on the following issues: -ADHD -Anxiety -Workplace stress -Addiction and Dual Diagnosis -Gaming, electronic, and other behavioral addictions -LGBTA adjustment issues -Bipolar Disorder -Depression (including Treatment Resistant Depression) -Coping with a loved one's mental illness I have worked in a variety of settings including homeless shelters, a foster care facility, a domestic violence treatment center, two outpatient mental health clinics, and two career centers.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Are you ready to commit to being the person you want to be? Are you ready to leave your reservations behind on your path to becoming your authentic self? Using ACT, I can help you chart that path, combining existential techniques with proven lessons from cognitive and behavioral research.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: Solution focused therapy is one of the fundamental techniques underlying the social work worldview. Therapy is often at it's most effective and efficient when it is built around goal-setting, identifying your strengths, and breaking down a problem into manageable steps. Once you start checking items off your list, you will realize that you have the strength to overcome the seemingly overwhelming.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: While the current vogue is to combine cognitive and behavioral therapies into one school of thought, I see them as two fundamentally different techniques that work powerfully together. Cognitive therapy helps us modify our reactions by reexamining our fundamental assumptions. And behavioral modification is a way of tracking and rebuilding the activities that make up our lives.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: 'Men's issues' is a broad umbrella. Men often face overlapping issues such as chronic anger, role strain, dysfunctional stress-management strategies, sexual performance issues, social isolation, and difficulty finding healthy and satisfying outlets. I have experience sorting out these issues and connecting you with your power and intention.

specialities.name: Internet Addiction
specialities.description: Gaming, internet, and media addictions of all kind are becoming a defining feature of the challenges of modern living for people of all ages and levels of functioning. I understand these challenges and I can help you develop a behavioral plan to change the way you use technologies to better suit your long-term goals in life.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Attention Deficit Disorder can strike at any time of life, and often compensation techniques that worked well earlier in life can break down when the challenges of career and family place ever increasing demands on your time, energy, and focus. Society often labels people with attention issues as 'lazy' or 'unreliable', making it feel even harder to feel valued and capable. I understand your needs

specialities.name: Bipolar
specialities.description: Bipolar disorder is often a lifelong challenge, but it can be managed successfully, and it does not have to be a barrier to happiness or success. Outside of medication management there is a great deal that the individual can do to institute a healthy routine, monitor symptoms, and compensate for temporary impairments. I can help.

specialities.name: Dissociative Disorder (DD)
specialities.description: Dissociation is generally a reaction to trauma and overwhelm and in my experience it always has some protective features. But what's adaptive in one situation can be harmful or unmanageable in another. Dissociation can rob us of the full experience of ourselves, our emotions, our sensations, even our intuitions. I use mindfulness techniques including wave meditation to practice reconnection in a safe way.

name: Michaela Christopher
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I’d be honored to support you in exploring past relational patterns and help you discover new experiences of authenticity and intimacy.
ideal_client: My clients include a variety of cultures, sexualities, genders, and abilities. Much of my work is with adults in varying relational structures and I hold a keen interest in working with those who are exploring sex and intimacy within their relationships. I support individuals who are on their own journeys of healing past wounding, trauma, illness, and grief/loss. I am honored to accompany clients first stepping into the therapeutic space and those who are reconnecting with past work.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I was privileged to grow up in a culture of sex positivity, which has supported me in forming a secure relationship with exploring sex and sexuality. I view sexuality as something that is uniquely ours to define and honor the dynamic, fluid nature of our sexual identities and experiences. I strongly believe in the importance of a consent based approach, amplifying sexual autonomy, and encouraging curiosity and open mindedness in sexual exploration. I utilize models such as Sensate Focus and the Good Enough Sex, to support individuals and partners in creating unique and fulfilling connections with their sexual identities and in their sexual relationships. I especially enjoy working with partners who are new to parenthood or are experiencing chronic illness, and are looking to reconnect and rediscover sex and intimacy in their relationships.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: At my core, I believe that we are all emotional beings who are influenced by our connections to the people and world around us. My own upbringing was shaped by valuing social justice, understanding the importance of my personal relationships, and creating meaningful connections to my community. Not only as a therapist but as a human being, I enjoy connecting to others through the power of storytelling. Whether our stories are similar or different, I believe sharing them furthers human connection and understanding. It is through the fabric of our relationships that we are able to make larger impacts on our communities and world.

name: Alex Perez
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I provide therapy in both English and Spanish. My years of experience in the mental health field is over 11 years.
ideal_client: Ages I treat is 12 years old to seniors and provide therapy to individuals and couples. The therapies I provide are: Acceptance and Commitment (ACT), Attachment-based, Cognitive Behavioral (CBT), Culturally Sensitive, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT), Eclectic, Family Systems, Humanistic, Interpersonal, Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy, Motivational Interviewing (MI), Solution Focused, Somatic, Strengths Perspective, and Trauma Focused.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide care with a holistic approach that focuses on healing all aspects impacting an individual's well-being (physical, emotional, mental, social, and spiritual). My specialties are: Mental Health, ADD/ADHD, Anger Management, Anxiety/Phobic Disorders, Bereavement/Grief, Co-dependency, Central Cultural Ethnic Issues, Child Abuse/Neglect, Chronic Illness, Depression, Divorce, Domestic Abuse, Family Conflict, Geriatric Seniors, Infidelity/Affairs, Internet Addiction, LGBTQIA2S+, Life Coach, Life Transitions, Marital and Premarital, Medical, Mood Disorders, Relationships Issues, Parenting, Peer Relationships, Pregnancy, Prenatal, Postpartum, PTSD, Sleep and Insomnia, Self Esteem, Stress, Teen Violence, Thinking Disorders, Transgender, Trauma, Women's Issues, and Work Stress.

name: Daniella Kramer, Keshet Counseling LLC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: The relationship between client and therapist is the most important part of your healing, so let's see if I am the right therapist for you.
ideal_client: I founded Keshet Counseling to help those who are not feeling seen in traditional therapy spaces. This includes people navigating the difficulties of chronic illness, specifically Lyme Disease, Mold Toxicity, MCAS & invisible disabilities, those dealing with antisemitism, or discrimination for not participating in political expectations at their job or schools. I also specialize in teen issues, narcissistic abuse, multicultural issues, codependency, love addiction, grief, and trauma.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: At this time I am additionally extending services and support to Israeli's and Jewish teens, couples, and adults experiencing horrific levels of hate and antisemitism in their communities, jobs, schools, and day to day lives. I practice holistic and integral psychology, taking the whole body, mind, and spirit into consideration, bringing a somatic, depth, and mindfulness approach to our work. Using mindfulness we will often pay attention to “where” and “how” feelings and experiences are held within your body, work to understand the unconscious stories we tell ourselves, and explore the deeper meanings in your life, as well as the deeper reasons behind your challenges and difficulties. I don't subscribe to the belief that there is something wrong with you, rather "what happened to you".

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a humanistic perspective, meaning that I believe you are whole, deserving, and perfect at your core. I trust that your inherent intelligence and ability to connect to yourself can be revealed and encouraged through the therapeutic relationship that we will create together, which is why I will often turn to you for answers, as I respect that you are the ultimate authority on your life and experience. I am much more of an engaged and directive therapist than a passive listener, and I will assume you are coming to therapy to make changes. Congrats on taking the first step of reaching out for the help you deserve.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: In addition to many other specialties, I have particular experience with navigating the trauma and difficulty of chronic illness and chronic pain, especially Lyme Disease and Mold Illness.

name: Matthew Beeble
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I enjoy assisting people who desire to be more relaxed, increase their confidence, get unstuck and are looking for purpose in their lives.
ideal_client: I like working with clients who have difficulty with boundaries and assertiveness. These people sometimes identify as "people pleasers." I like working with people who feel stuck or are lacking direction in their life. One of my favorite exercises is working with "value cards" to help clients connect with what is truly important to them and to identify a concrete plan for living more according to these values. I like working with people who want to improve communication in their relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I operate on the belief that you already have what you need within yourself to experience fulfillment in your life. Unfortunately, there are a lot of things that can get in the way and leave you feeling like you are falling short of who you should be and what you should be doing. This can lead to a sense of being out of sync and other symptoms that are causing you to seek therapy. I believe that the most important task set before you is to make meaning of your life and to remain steadfast in this task. This is done by increasing awareness of your experience and letting a new understanding come forth, one that clarifies your identity, results in a shift in the way you experience yourself and your relationships and a feeling of peace and presence in everyday life. My passion is to help you see your struggles as an opportunity for growth and aiding your search for understanding. I find it rewarding and I'm humbled by the opportunity to witness bravery on a daily basis.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a licensed mental health counselor who has been providing therapy for Clark County residents since 2008. I grew up in Portland and got my training in Seattle. I graduated from Seattle University's Master of Arts in Clinical Psychology in 2005. Before settling in the Portland/Vancouver area, I spent 2 years in London and I worked as volunteer counselor for individuals without insurance.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: Whether meaning and purpose are things you think about a lot or not, they are core factors in what drives you from day to day. You may be seeking therapy because the things going on in your life have caused you to revisit the questions, 'Who am I?' and 'What do I want from life?' The existential approach believes that answering these questions are essential to health and well-being.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: You may be seeking therapy because you are struggling with the way you are feeling or acting. These patterns are often influenced by inaccurate or negative ways you are thinking about yourself or interpreting situations with others. I use CBT to illuminate these patterns and help you change them.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: The theoretical orientation I was trained in focused heavily on the causes and treatment of anxiety. In addition to my undergraduate and graduate training, I have had over 9 years experience diagnosing and treating individuals with various types of anxiety diagnoses.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: I enjoy helping individuals increase their self-esteem. It is one of the tasks that I feel the most confident will end with success. Low self-esteem is often about negative self-talk based on faulty beliefs about oneself due to past experience. These beliefs are often powerful and convincing. Therapy is about unmasking these beliefs, stealing their power and creating a new sense of self.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: The theoretical orientation I was trained in focused heavily on the causes and treatment of depression. In addition to my undergraduate and graduate training, I have had over 9 years experience diagnosing and treating individuals with various types of mood-related diagnoses.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Everyone needs others in their life, yet everyone is unique. This can contribute to conflict and other difficulties. These difficulties can be most pronounced in romantic relationships and it's easy for bad habits of communication to lead to deep hurt. I want to help you understand your role in these dynamics in order to increase your ability to have successful and resilient bonds with others.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Adjustment Disorder is an experience that many people have. It is often what brings someone back into therapy or causes someone to seek therapy for the first time. Many of the clients I have been working with over the years begin therapy when their life is thrown off by a major life event. Much of the work I have done has involved processing and adjusting to significant life changes.

name: Alicia Banister
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My role is to help you access and tend to your emotional landscape and by doing so, discover a deep, inherent sense of wholeness in yourself

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I draw on the mindfulness-based, body-centered psychotherapy of Hakomi. I hold a particular focus on the nervous system, neuropsychology, and the relationship between trauma and the body. My approach involves both holding oneself with radical acceptance and inclusion, while also holding the possibility of change. Claiming Self and cultivating a sense of embodied wholeness informs all of the work that I do. I hold a deep respect for the wounds and scars we each carry and a profound gratitude for the brilliance inherent in each person that helps them to navigate the world with these wounds.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my Masters in Counseling Psychology at Lewis & Clark College in 2018. Prior to that, I completed a year-long internship and extensive study at Mindful Experiential Therapeutic Approaches (M.E.T.A) in Portland, OR, focusing on Hakomi and mindfulness-based body-centered psychotherapy, as well as the Re-Creation of the Self, and Primary Attachment Psychotherapy. I have a broad background in somatic-oriented therapies, including massage therapy, Biodynamic Craniosacral Therapy, and therapeutic yoga. Prior to counseling I ran an Integrative Bodywork practice for 10 years, focusing on mind-body integration and trauma. I have studied extensively the work of Stephen Porges and Peter Levine and find that their work informs much of my approach to counseling.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: I have studied Hakomi with META (Mindful Experiential Therapeutic Approaches) here in Portland, OR, including a year-long internship during which I was immersed in study of Hakomi, Primary Attachment Psychotherapy, and the Re-Creation of the Self.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: My background is in somatic-oriented therapies, including Craniosacral therapy, massage, and therapeutic yoga. Much of my practice involves integrating the body into your lived experience, through movement, experience, and nervous system regulation.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: I have completed trainings in Birth Trauma and Postpartum Mental Health.

name: Ursina Teuscher
title: Professional Counselor
credentials: PhD in Applied Psychology, Career Counseling License from the University of Freiburg, Switzerland
intro: As a decision coach, I help with major as well daily choices: e.g. career counseling, executive coaching, ADHD skills coaching, habit change
ideal_client: Do you feel stuck or overwhelmed with an important decision, such as a career choice? Or do you struggle with your daily decisions, such as time management, personal productivity, or creating and maintaining healthy habits?

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer decision coaching to help you solve problems and achieve your goals. Issues I can help you with include: improving your time management, setting priorities, getting more work done, and establishing healthier habits. For your big decisions, we will use a structured process to clarify your core values and evaluate your options. This process will give you the necessary confidence in your decision and peace of mind, so that you can commit to taking action. Throughout our work together, I use decision-aiding tools that were developed on a scientific background and designed to enhance our ability to think systematically as well as creatively. I employ coaching methods that are evidence-based and have been shown to be effective for supporting decisions, improving performance and achieving goals. (Examples: mindfulness-based, cognitive behavioral, value focused, paradoxical, creative thinking and problem-solving techniques.)

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: After my training as a Career Counselor (professional license and MS in Psychology in 2000), I gained my doctoral degree (PhD) in Applied Psychology in 2004 from the University of Freiburg, Switzerland. I have co-authored the textbook, “Heart and Mind: Mastering the Art of Decision Making,” and have published peer-reviewed research articles in the fields of cognitive psychology, neuroscience, decision-making, and coaching techniques. I have been teaching Psychology and Decision-Making classes at high-school and university levels since 2001 (currently at PSU). My ongoing research and teaching complements and informs my work in private practice. It continues to give me insights into disciplines that are fast-changing and rich with new findings about the way people think, feel and behave. Those insights continue to inform my approach and methods. I’m deeply committed to bringing you well-researched, highly relevant techniques and practices.

specialities.name: Career Counseling
specialities.description: Career counseling: In my approach to career counseling, we will assess your interests, values, strengths and skills, but also your potential and resources to acquire new skills. From there, we explore options and develop strategies to take your career into the right direction. I will help you plan and realize practical steps to get you moving on that track.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Whether you have ADHD or not, coaching can give you the skills to cope better with distractions or improve your time management. More generally, coaching can help your executive functioning - which is your ability to self-regulate your emotions, thoughts and actions. With or executive functioning or ADHD coaching, I will help you figure out your own best practices. I will support your individual needs along the way, as you move towards your personal best performance.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Decision counseling for personal growth: Decisions are a particular challenge these days because there is so much uncertainty. I will be excited to help you think through your big and small decisions and get in charge of the parts of your life that you CAN control.

name: Chynna Springer
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide individual counseling services and have been in practice for 16 years.
ideal_client: Do you want to improve your quality of life? Are symptoms of stress, anxiety or depression getting in your way? Do you feel trapped in an unhealthy or abusive relationship? Are you overwhelmed, burnt out, or juggling multiple roles? Counseling can support you through these challenges!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I will create a safe therapeutic environment where you can be heard, feel understood, and work towards positive growth. You will learn practical tools to reach your goals based on your individual needs. I approach counseling from a client-driven and strengths-based perspective. I infuse and encourage the use of humor in therapy and believe it can be a beneficial part of the process and positive coping mechanism. ALLIED COMMUNITIES: Body Positivity, LGBTQIA+ Allied, Open Relationships Non-Monogamy Allied, Racial Justice Allied, Sex Worker Allied, Women's Rights Allied

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I'm skilled in treating the different varieties of anxiety and I really enjoy being a part of people's healing process. I'm experienced in working with people struggling with multiple symptoms since conditions such as ADHD/ADD, trauma, grief, panic, depression etc. can often accompany other issues. I provide guidance through life transitions, balancing multiple roles, and life stressors. I'm also passionate about empowering survivors of abusive relationships. I'm a Licensed Professional Counselor in Oregon, a Licensed Mental Health Counselor in Washington, and a Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor in Oregon. With 16 years of experience, I've worked in crisis centers, outreach programs, residential treatment facilities, domestic abuse programs, etc.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is a therapeutic approach with the emphasis of psychotherapy on how things are currently impacting you and focuses on practicing skills to change unhealthy thinking and behaviors. Exploring and processing where these emotions, thoughts, and behaviors stem from is also integrated. I practice Trauma Informed Care by understanding the impact of your traumatic experiences, providing psychological safety, and helping you rebuild a sense of control and trust.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness and Acceptance based approaches to counseling can also be very effective. I infuse these elements into my practice, including relaxation training, breathing exercises, visualization, and accepting or acknowledging the difficult aspects of our lives without judgement. With Mindfulness you can learn to pay attention to thoughts and feelings with acceptance and non-judgement.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: I meet you where you are at in your healing journey! I help you to build insight and gentile, positive motivation for change.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I really enjoy working with and empowering women. Women face many unique challenges in a patriarchal society and our experiences in this world are colored by our culture and our roles. Whether dealing with general life stressors, discrimination, women's rights, balancing work/home life, parenting, divorce/uncoupling, navigating relationships, etc. A feminist and equality lens I believe is beneficial for everyone.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Whether due to stressors, life changes, or feeling overwhelmed by everyday life, anxiety can crop up in our lives in many ways and for some it can become debilitating. CBT is very effective for the many different manifestations of anxiety. I'm also trained and experienced in exposure therapy which is one of the primary evidence based treatments for certain types of anxiety disorders. I especially enjoy working with individuals who experience Social Phobia and Generalized Anxiety.

specialities.name: Domestic Abuse
specialities.description: Working with survivors of abusive relationships, domestic violence and coercive control including verbal, emotional, and psychological abuse is one of my specialties. I am experienced in supporting individuals whose partners are exhibiting manipulative, controlling and coercive behaviors.

name: Bonnie Davey
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Play Therapy for ages 3-7. Whatever life is handing you and your child at the moment – growth is possible!
ideal_client: If you've been concerned about your child and are hoping for a play-based child specialist to point you in the right direction and provide a safe space for growth and healing, you've come to the right person. I work exclusively with: Children ages 3-10 Emotional Regulation Trauma Developmental or Behavioral Challenges Family Conflict Sexual Abuse ADHD Aggression

approaches.What I Specialize In: My work as a child therapist is grounded in person-centered therapy and interpersonal neurobiology, with a particular focus on the use of child-centered play therapy, expressive arts, and incorporating nature in the therapeutic process. I've engaged in extensive trainings in nature-based child centered play therapy as well as in child therapy, and have a fully furnished, inviting, and child-centered therapy playroom and outdoor space for nature-based work. I specialize in working with very young children, specifically ages 3-7 years old.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: We are all growing together. We all experience beauty, as well as thorns. I hope to provide a place for you where thriving once again feels possible.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Play Therapy is an evidence-based counseling service provided by trained therapists. Masters of Arts in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from George Fox University Bachelors of Arts in Social Work from Concordia University 59 hours of professional continuing education in Play Therapy through the NW Center for Play Therapy Studies. 134 hours of masters-level play therapy training through George Fox University 62 hours of professional continuing education in Interpersonal Neurobiology

name: Brigid Bello
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: accessible, liberation-centered virtual counseling based in portland, oregon
ideal_client: I might be a good fit for you if you’re looking for support with any of the following: Disordered Eating / Body Image | Neurodivergence | Queer Fertility / Perinatal Mental Health | Racial Identity | Queer Identity | Cultural Alienation / Isolation | Relationships | Burnout. That said, I enjoy working with individuals from all walks of life and have experience supporting folks navigating a broad spectrum of experiences.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In my work as a therapist, I believe in centering you as the expert of your own experience. I value reciprocal feedback and I make an effort to approach the therapy process as a learner and collaborator. I strive to provide trauma-informed, anti-oppressive care that acknowledges how systems like capitalism, fatphobia, and white supremacy impact our well-being. Prior to my journey as a mental health practitioner, I completed my undergraduate degree in Theatre Arts which cultivated an appreciation for storytelling, empathy, and the power of personal narratives. I also spent many years working in the tech sector as a people manager and customer success coach. Navigating the corporate and start-up worlds gave me a deep understanding of the challenges faced by individuals seeking to find their authentic selves and overcome barriers to personal growth and fulfillment.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I am committed to Disability Justice, take daily Covid safety measures, and prioritize maintaining an accessible, anti-ableist therapy practice. As a Black, mixed-race, queer, cisgender woman, and as someone who grew up with most of my material needs met, figuring out how to leverage my various privileged identities while holding space for my marginalized, racialized existence is something that I am always exploring. I very much believe Maya Angelou’s assertion that no one of us can be free until everybody is free, and I approach this work doing what I can to help shift us towards that collective goal.

name: Mimosa Constans
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: My therapeutic approach examines how family of origin, cultural upbringing, socioeconomic inequality and attachment style impact your life.
ideal_client: My clients are cycle breakers..... "A cycle breaker is someone who grew up without an example of the life they wanted or needed, and they fought like hell to build that life anyway." -Nate Postlethwait- To be a cycle breaker is a burden and a gift. To create a path forward in life on your own requires vision, determination, and a natural tendency towards hyper-independence. That's the part that can become the burden. It can be rewarding, but equally lonely, and exhausting.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My role as your therapist is to provide you space and support with attunement, compassion, and empathy so that you can put burdens down, and rest your weary heart. My goal is for you to feel safe to express your needs and vulnerabilities that you've buried for so long. In the process of uncovering the foundation you were built on, we can identify the spaces of your mind and heart that need healing. Highlighting your natural strengths and drawing from your inner compass to help us navigate our therapeutic journey together.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I'm a fully inclusive therapist and support all communities. I know how it feels to not quite “fit in”. I've lived in a world of many cultural influences and learned that we are all longing for love, acceptance, meaningful connection, and autonomy no matter where started or how we got here. Outside of therapy I am a wife, mother, and self proclaimed foodie. I love quality time with my husband, four amazing daughters and our pack of (4) dogs.

name: Nova (Stephenie) Knutson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: LPC, Certified Hakomi Practitioner, AEDP level 2
intro: Therapy is a place where we can be accepted in our entirety-understood in our struggles & reflected in our innate capacity, worth & dignity.
ideal_client: Many of the people I work with have experienced childhood, sexual, cultural or attachment trauma. Many come reporting difficulty in the arenas of connection, community and belonging; struggling with anxiety, isolation, self-doubt or the sense that something is holding them back from living as their fullest self. My clients report that our work together leads to decreased physical and mental symptoms of trauma & stress and increased satisfaction in relationships, work & creativity.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work uses mindfulness and a body oriented approach to foster palpable positive changes in the quality of the experiences you are having day to day. As your experience of life changes for the better, behavior, feelings and actions naturally change with it. My clients say that I am kind, warm and gentle but also willing to be direct. Therapy with me is effective and deep and also frequently joyful and filled with laughter.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a certified Hakomi Therapist and Teacher, I have more than a decade of experience and the skills to promote lasting change.
