Sometimes it’s most helpful to pay close attention to the bricks and mortar of our minds – through mindfulness, problem-solving, journaling, and other activities – to begin to change embedded patterns.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Living as a man in our society comes with unique limits and opportunities. We develop and strengthen parts of ourselves to survive struggle and meet expectations of masculinity. While these parts can be incredibly effective, they can also lead to frustration, relationship issues, and unhelpful coping strategies. Specializing in Men's Issues means creating a space that's to comfortably explore these issues, while becoming better at addressing feelings, meeting needs, and connecting with others.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: How do we feel like we are enough? It’s a simple idea that’s complex in the real world. I have experience helping clients navigate these murky waters to the source of low self-esteem and begin the healing process. Together we can discover, accept, and celebrate your authentic self while learning how to work with shame, self-criticism, and low confidence.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Junctures in life can affect our mood, our beliefs, and even our core identity. Events like moving to a new town, a break up, the onset of a disability, or a change in job can spin us out. However, these events can also lead to growth and greater life satisfaction. Working towards this goal involves tolerating discomfort, building self-determination, and finding the meaning in our struggle.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: A feeling that is meant to protect us and keep us safe can take on a life of its own and become overwhelming. The energy spent on anxiety, nervousness, fear, and dread can come out in a variety of ways but is always exhausting and restricting. Together we can develop awareness of your symptoms and triggers and then develop coping strategies to help you reclaim ownership of your life.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is more than just feeling sad. Depression comes with hopelessness, entrenchment, and a lack of interest in the things that once brought joy. Building relief involves both findings ways to alleviate symptoms in order get a handhold back on life as well as addressing root causes, be they biological, psychological, behavioral, or systemic. Together we can do these things.

name: Katherine Lindsay
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: MSW, MPH, CADCI
ideal_client: Since 2014, I have been dedicated to supporting individuals across all age groups as they navigate a variety of mental health challenges. Whether you're dealing with anxiety, depression, trauma, or substance use, I provide a safe, affirming space to help you make sense of these experiences and foster positive, lasting change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic style is rooted in warmth, creativity, and directness. I blend affirmation with clear guidance, helping you build new, healthy dynamics in your relationships and daily life. Therapy is not just about addressing difficulties—it's about creating a space where you can grow, heal, and discover a stronger version of yourself. I believe deeply in the power of therapy to transform lives, and my approach reflects that belief. Together, we will work to help you understand your past, navigate your present, and build the future you deserve.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have worked in the behavioral health field since 2014. I have a Master of Social Work from Portland State University and a Master of Global Public Health from New York University. I also hold a Certified Drug and Alcohol Counselor in Oregon. I am a mother of four, wife, and co-parent. I love cooking, travel, dancing, and raising guide-dogs. I am often accomponied by a guide-dog-puppy in training. I am currently raising a Golden Retriever named Clara and a yellow lab named Vada.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I work with adolescents (16+) facing substance use, mental health challenges, trauma, and homelessness through a non-judgmental, harm reduction, and strengths-based approach. My practice is focused on fostering resilience, self-determination, and emotional regulation. I prioritize building trust and safety, meeting youth where they are, and tailoring interventions to their unique needs, whether through motivational interviewing, DBT-informed strategies, or community-based advocacy.

name: Mary Diorio
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Psychotherapy Individuals and Couples
ideal_client: My ideal client is motivated to see change. I can take it from there! Couples and Individual Therapy Anxiety Depression Difficult Life Transitions Emotional Eating Binge Eating

approaches.My Background and Approach: I take a creative and collaborative approach in my practice, researching new techniques and information to help you make the changes you desire. My clinical focus areas include: relationships, anxiety, depression, eating disorders, life transitions, and stress management. I work with adolescent and adult clients. I use cognitive behavioral therapy, psychodynamic theory, and emotionally focused therapy as my main theoretical lenses.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have completed multiple years of training in Emotionally Focused Couples Therapy in Seattle, New York, and Portland. Emotionally focused Therapy developed by Dr. Leslie Greenberg, PhD, helps couples seeking greater intimacy, facilitates healing after an affair, and changes negative relational communication problems/cycles. With this approach, couples communicate their emotions effectively, create an intimate secure bond with each other, and heal from past attachment injuries. I have also studied under Dr. Susan Johnson's, PhD, Emotionally Focused Therapy Center in Seattle, Washington. I have many years of experience and training working with people struggling with eating problems and weight management. I have worked in outpatient, partial day treatment, and a hospitilazation level of care adressing complexities of eating disorders. I also work with clients who are just trying to develop healthier eating patterns and ways to cope with stress more effectively.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have attended training in Emotionally Focused Therapy in Seattle, NYC, and Portland. I have attended trainings by both Dr. Les Greenberg and Dr. Susan Johnson, author of Hold Me Tight, I am also familiar with the Gottman model.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I have many years working experience with eating disorders, disordered eating, body image, weight management and exercise balance.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Many of my clients struggle with either underlying issues of anxiety and/or depression. I have worked in individual, couples and group settings addressing both anxiety and depression.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Many of my clients struggle with either underlying issues of anxiety and/or depression. I have worked in both individual, couples and group setting addressing both anxiety and depression.

name: Sarah Sumner
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
credentials: LCSW in OR & LMSW in NY, MSW, C-YT, IFS Level 1 & IFS Level 2
intro: Hi, I'm Sarah! I offer individual, couples, and sex therapy. I’m here to help you live a fulfilling, empowered, and pleasure-filled life.
ideal_client: I’m so glad you’re here- it takes courage to ask for help, and I’m honored to be considered. I enjoy working with a range of clients and specialize in assisting individuals and couples who are neurodivergent, LGBTQ+, and/or adult survivors of complex trauma and their partners navigate anxiety, depression, communication issues, and cultivate healthy sexuality. I am also kink/BDSM affirming and poly/ethical non-monogamy affirming.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that people already have exactly what they need to heal. Rather than focusing on what is lacking, I collaborate with clients to remove external constraints that block access to that power, harmonize your inner system, and build a relationship to your core self. As a result, behavior, emotions, and thoughts tend to change naturally. I strive to facilitate healing that includes both interpersonal challenges and how systems of power and privilege are affecting your livelihood. I previously provided individual and group counseling at DVRC and somatic therapy at Harlem Hospital and on interdisciplinary therapy teams. I received a Master’s degree in Clinical Social Work from Columbia University and completed IFS Level 1 from the IFS Institute. In addition to providing evidence-based practices, I’m also a trained Yoga Therapist and enjoy offering somatic and psycho-spiritual approaches bolster holistic healing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I became a therapist because even in the face of the most challenging circumstances, I believe everyone deserves the right to feel fulfilled, safe, and empowered. As a Pleasure Activist, I love to help people move from shame-based to a pleasure-centered relationship to their sexuality and see this work as integral to collective liberation. Accompanying people on their own journey of self-discovery whether that’s solo or in partnership, fills me with an immense amount of meaning and joy. I am an active ally; I’m a queer neurodivergent femme-presenting and white-bodied person who is aware of my privilege and continuously humbling myself. I look forward to bearing witness to your growth!

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I don’t know about you, but I didn’t grow up in a sex-positive household, nor did my family of origin equip me with the tools I needed to build a relationship with myself that was expansive enough to outweigh the messages of shame I inherited from society about my sexual identity. . As a Pleasure Activist, I love to help people move from shame-based to a pleasure-centered relationship to their sexuality and see this work as integral to collective liberation.

specialities.name: Sexual Abuse
specialities.description: I’m passionate about supporting survivors of sexual abuse (and their partners in a couples therapy context). My goal is to help you heal, find a sense of relief from the way trauma impacts you, build up compassion and confidence in yourself, find pleasurable ways to connect with your body & sexuality, and integrate your trauma into a fulfilling and empowered life.

name: Margaret King
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I strive to support & hold space for marginalized folks who are experiencing the traumatic effects of oppression.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with Highly Sensitive People (HSPs)/empaths, sex workers, LGBTQIA+ folks, BIPOC clients, and people who have survived religious trauma. I work with people who have experienced a range of traumatic experiences throughout their lives and want to explore ancestral-based healing work. As a person who has healed from severe Panic Disorder, I have a unique perspective on ways to move through the overpowering feelings of anxiety and enjoy support folks through this.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My willingness to stay open to my clients' unique experiences in the space we create together allows me to facilitate safety for my clients. My approach operates in the "here-and-now" from a place of both intuition & professional training. I work with clients using a trauma-informed lens to deepen self-knowing, meaning making, support shifts in perspective, as well as emotional and behavioral support. *I believe the therapeutic relationship created between client and therapist in the present moment is the most essential tool for learning, growth, and deepening.* I use a variety of creative interventions to assist the process: -Internal Family Systems (IFS) -Brainspotting -role play -mindfulness/guided meditation -dream assessments -sand tray

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I moved to Portland from New Orleans, LA about 8 years ago in search of new opportunities and a deeper connection with the natural world. I have a background in embodiment practices, comedy/theater, energy work, creativity, and personal struggles that make me the unique healer I am today. Providing mental health services to the community has been a part of my life for the past 10 years. I received by BS in Psychology from Tulane University and my MA in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis & Clark College. I interned for 9 months on the Post Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) specialty team at the Portland VA Hospital where I served Veterans with PTSD and a variety of other mental health issues. I worked for 1.5 years with children ages 8-17 in crisis on a children's inpatient psychiatric unit in New Orleans, LA.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Parts work is extremely powerful and allows a deeper inner healing experience than many other modalities I have worked with. I incorporate the body & spirit into my work with clients. I am a believer that the there is no separation between mind and body when it comes to mental healthcare. Check out the IFS website more more: https://ifs-institute.com/about-us

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: I offer Brainspotting therapy to a variety of clients and continue to see incredible results. To learn more, visit the website: www.brainspotting.com

specialities.name: Sand Tray
specialities.description: Sand Tray is offered in-person only (Mondays and Wednesdays) and can be very helpful for processing dreams, feelings, family issues, pre-verbal memories, and more.

name: Aly Davis
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Hi, I'm Aly, a dedicated mental health therapist on a mission to help you navigate life's challenges and rediscover your strength.
ideal_client: My specialties include depression, anxiety, trauma, substance use, OCD, ADHD/Neurodivergence, LGBTQIA+ concerns. I believe in unconditional positive regard, gentle reframing, and customized treatment tailored to your needs and values. Together, we'll engage in meaningful work, fostering self-love and empowerment.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With a counseling philosophy rooted in CBT, narrative therapy, solution-focused therapy, and other therapeutic approaches, I firmly believe in your ability to heal in a safe space. Passionate about overcoming trauma, I offer a straightforward approach to help you reach your goals rapidly while allowing space for exploration, emotions, and healing.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I've experienced firsthand the transformative power of therapy and mental health care, reinforcing my belief that everyone can heal and lead a fulfilled life. I have a passion for helping clients overcome trauma and distressing pasts, employing a straightforward approach, and building trust and honesty in our therapeutic relationship. I stand out as a friendly and warm individual, known for my ability to see all sides in every situation, understanding perspectives deeply.

name: Kristen Seghete
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Compassionate women's mental health care, including postpartum depression and anxiety, trauma, and parenting stress . In-person or virtual.
ideal_client: Are you looking for therapy or a psychological assessment tailored for women? Do you feel sad or anxious after having a baby? Do you feel stressed or overwhelmed as a parent? Does past trauma affect your life? You are not alone. It starts to feel scary when overwhelm takes over. You deserve emotional support from someone who is ready to listen with compassion and without judgement.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have 20 years of experience working in women's and infants' mental health, and I am certified in perinatal mental health. My expertise includes postpartum depression and anxiety, trauma, and parenting. In our work together, you will learn how to make space for sadness, anxiety, and fear. We'll work on pushing pause on the endless loop of worry, guilt, and judgment that plays in your mind. Once again, you will learn how to have compassion for yourself, nurture yourself, and ask for what you need. We will figure out how you can become less isolated. My approach includes understanding how feelings and emotions are related to each other and how we can change our behaviors (cognitive behavioral therapy). I also focus on mindfulness-based interventions, meaning using non-judgmental, present-moment awareness as a guiding principle to make space for your inner experiences and emotions.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe in compassionate and collaborative care based in an authentic and non-judgmental relationship. I care about your story, the experiences that have shaped you, and any pain you carry with you. Trauma is something that shapes us, gets passed down, and physically affects us. I am particularly passionate about understanding how women's experiences of trauma affect how the world interacts with them and how they can interact with the world. Therapy takes work. Hard work. And I will honor and respect your unique journey. I am here to meet you where you are at right now and recognize you are doing the best you can at any given moment.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Traditional CBT. I also engage in Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) for PTSD.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT)

specialities.name: Psychological Testing and Evaluation
specialities.description: Neuropsychological and diagnostic testing for adult and adolescent ADHD, autism, mental health disorders, head injury, and other medical conditions.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: Therapy for pregnant individuals experiencing depression, anxiety, intrusive thoughts, PTSD, high-risk pregnancies, infertility, loss, and abortion. Preventive therapy for individuals who are concerned about developing depression and anxiety is also available.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: I provide services for most postpartum mental health concerns and symptoms - including depression, anxiety, intrusive thoughts, birth trauma, and NICU experiences.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: I provide parent coaching for parents of infants, toddlers, and preschoolers. Parent coaching collaboratively supports strategies that support infants, toddlers, and preschoolers based on child cognitive and emotional development. I also with you to reduce parenting stress.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Providing evidence-based therapy, including cognitive processing therapy (CPT), for women with a history of birth trauma, childhood trauma, and interpersonal violence.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Assessment of adults and adolescents for ADHD, autism, learning disorders and mental health diagnoses. Specializing in gender-informed assessment to better understand diagnoses in the context of overlapping neurodivergence, medical conditions, and/or mental health disorders.

name: Judith McIntosh
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: MS Counseling - Marriage and Family Therapy 2002
intro: Hello! Thank you for reviewing my profile. Still have questions? Please send me a message and I'll do my best to address your concerns.
ideal_client: I work primarily with adults who struggle with depression and anxiety related to relationships, life transitions, trauma, workplace conflicts, serious illness, grief, and loss. Most of my clients are not mentally ill but having a very human emotional response to challenging life circumstances. As your therapist, my role is to help you sort through these difficulties to increase your self-awareness and understanding within the context of your life, family, workplace, and community.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My role as a therapist is to foster psychological health by assisting my clients to identify and utilize their existing strengths. My approach is collaborative and supportive. Symptoms of depression - sadness, loneliness, meaninglessness, hopelessness - can be excruciating. However, each symptom holds the potential for greater self-awareness, the key to moving beyond it. By sharing your story with me, I can help you dig down to the root of the issue and uncover its hidden value. My therapeutic approach combines the practicality of cognitive behavioral therapies with the creativity of depth psychology and mythology by tapping into the realm of the imagination and utilizing a variety of tools that may include storytelling, art, writing, literature, film, and dreams.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In addition to my private practice, I have had the good fortune to work in a variety of mental health settings including a community counseling clinic, an employee assistance program, a non-profit support community for cancer patients and caregivers, county mental health services and a crisis line. I have taught counseling and communication skills courses at California State University Northridge, as well as provide clinical supervision to MFT graduate students. Although I value all of these experiences, I am thrilled that at this point in my life I have to freedom to focus exclusively on my private practice. While my previous experience has provided me with a solid clinical foundation, my passion lies in helping clients tap into the unconscious realm through humanities-based expressive arts. I love how working this way brings an element of creativity and fun to the therapeutic process with less focus on diagnosis and more attention to each person's inherent movement toward health.

name: Eric Goodwin
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: If you're experiencing anxiety or shame and self-criticism, I'm a Queer therapist here to help you heal and grow self-compassion.
ideal_client: You’re feeling stuck in familiar patterns of shame and self-criticism, and it’s hard to tap into your strengths when you need them most. Whether it's the weight of anxiety or the impact of prejudice and discrimination, especially toward the LGBTQ+ community, it feels overwhelming and you feel vulnerable and out-of-touch with your own voice. You are ready for help and deserve support as you take steps toward healing and growth—you don’t have to go through this alone.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Clients often describe me as warm, patient, and curious—qualities I bring into every session. My approach centers on creating a safe, grounding space where you can explore your thoughts and feelings with mindful awareness and self-compassion. These tools help relieve anxiety, heal from past trauma, and gradually replace self-criticism with self-kindness. Life may be full of challenges, but your therapy and healing don’t have to be rigid and harsh. Together, we’ll work at a pace that feels right for you and collaborate on goals that help you develop resilience and a deeper connection with yourself. With over a decade of experience, including work in clinic and college settings, I’ve learned to be creative, flexible, and direct as we navigate your path forward. We may even share a laugh from time to time, because growth doesn’t have to always be serious. I’ll meet you where you are, walking alongside you each step of the way.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: When it comes to healing, I believe in the power of challenging the stories we’ve been told about who we’re “supposed” to be - stories shaped by prejudice, shaming, and expectations that don’t reflect our true selves. For many, these beliefs come from bigoted words or actions, especially toward the LGBTQ+ community. How often do you treat yourself with judgment, in ways you’d never treat a loved one? Together, we can explore where that inner critic came from and whether it’s time for a change. I also believe in the profound healing that comes from mindfulness and self-compassion. Beneath the layers of anxiety, shame, and pain is a clear, wise voice - your authentic self. In therapy, we can increase your connection to that voice, helping you develop a deeper sense of self-compassion for the everyday struggles you encounter. I’m passionate about supporting LGBTQ+ rights from an intersectional lens and advocating for mental health, especially when it comes to destigmatizing seeking help.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: With advanced training in mindfulness-based approaches and over 25 years of personal practice, I help clients cultivate present-moment awareness, a key to relieving anxiety, self-criticism, and healing from trauma. I guide clients in developing a non-judgmental awareness of their experiences, empowering them to respond with self-compassion. This approach is helpful for the LGBTQ+ community, but anyone seeking deeper self-understanding can benefit.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: This approach helps you explore and heal the different parts of yourself that may feel anxious, critical, or overwhelmed. I’ve had advanced training in Internal Family Systems (IFS), I am not yet Level 1 certified so I focus on parts work with clients. By understanding and caring for these parts, you can experience healing from anxiety, self-criticism, and trauma. My work is rooted in creating a safe space for this inner exploration, allowing you to feel more whole and at peace.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Homophobia and related trauma can create deep feelings of shame, isolation, and a sense of not being safe, even in spaces meant to be inclusive. It’s hard to open up about experiences with anti-LGBTQ+ violence or abuse when trust feels risky. As a Queer therapist, I understand these challenges and am here to offer a space where you can heal and grow. Together, we’ll navigate your story, working through the pain of past traumas so you can move forward with greater self-compassion and strength.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can feel overwhelming, like you're losing control, with racing thoughts and physical symptoms that make it hard to feel grounded. When your mind is constantly fixated on worries, it can feel isolating. But you don’t have to face it alone—there is hope. I’ve helped many people break free from the grip of anxiety, gaining the tools to manage and change their relationship with it. Together, we can work toward a calmer, more balanced life where anxiety no longer holds you back.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: In my practice, I integrate self-compassion and mindfulness to support your personal growth. Through self-compassion, you’ll learn to replace self-criticism with kindness, recognizing your worth even in moments of struggle. Mindfulness helps you stay present, observing your thoughts and feelings without judgment. Together, these approaches create space for healing and growth, empowering you to navigate challenges with greater resilience, clarity, and self-acceptance.

name: Alyssa Gursky
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm passionate about creativity, psychedelic healing & supporting clients to find healthy relationships, starting with their own bodies.
ideal_client: My clients may identify as sensitive, managing depression, anger, anxiety, or loneliness. They may feel disconnected from their creative power or want to embody their creative self more. Or, they may desire re-connecting to their creative power. They crave a space to look within and befriend their inner world. They want their relationship with sex and/or drugs to be taken seriously. They want new tools outside of traditional talk therapy.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My academic training provides me with an abundance of tools for teaching emotional and nervous system regulation, mindfulness practices, and creative processes for healing and insight. No artistic experience is necessary to participate in art therapy. My extracurricular training in psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy has cultivated passion and expertise around the preparation and integration of non-ordinary state experiences. I also offer Ketamine Assisted Psychotherapy in my practice. My approach is collaborative and non-directive. Curiosity is critical in the healing relationship.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a queer person, I'm passionate about working with individuals who are on the LGBTQIA+ spectrum. With eight years of working in the field of psychedelic therapy and psychedelic research, I am devoted to helping my clients explore their relationship with all substances in a judgment-free zone. This is known as Harm Reduction Therapy. Creativity manifests in many ways and is a powerful force of healing. l I feel a deep resonance in working with artists. When creativity can come into the therapy space, it can offer a profound mirror to witness oneself and their inner multitudes. However, this is not a requirement. In art therapy, we do not look at art for it's aesthetic value. I'm kink informed, BDSM friendly, and am educated on non-traditional relationship structures.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: Benefits of art therapy may include the development of non-verbal forms of self-expression, trauma resolution, increased self-esteem, and nervous system regulation/stress management. Art materials can be used in the session, or, prompts can be given to complete outside of the therapy space. I hold the belief that art is like a dream, or a snapshot of some facet of the psyche, latent with imagery, waiting to be de-coded and integrated into one’s daily life.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: Transpersonal psychology is a therapeutic discipline that focuses on the importance of experiences that are considered to be outside of one's habitual waking consciousness. This may include topics such as spirituality, ritual, mindfulness, and non-ordinary states of consciousness. I enjoy discussing and supporting clients in finding relationships with each of these topics, through personal history and clinical training.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: A relational therapeutic approach entails looking at how past relational experiences play out in our current relationships. The therapeutic relationship itself becomes an opportunity for healing and insight. Through mindfulness and radical self-reflection, These patterns can be identified. The therapy space becomes a space to take risks and try new ways of relating. Certain traits such as embodied empathy and curious listening can be reparative experiences for clients.

name: Kalpana Krishnamurthy
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Working with API & BIPOC folks to support healing and joy. I work in person and am accepting clients on Tue afternoon in NE & Wed in SW PDX.
ideal_client: Many clients I work with are dealing with anxiety or depression, grief and loss, parenting, exploring or navigating racial and cultural identities, exploring gender identity or preparing for gender affirming surgery, or working on their romantic relationship. Some clients aren't "working" on anything, but looking to create time each week to process, slow down, and have a regular space to check in with themselves. Where ever you are starting, I bring my curiosity and humor.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I start by listening to build a strong relationship and making sure that the goals and direction in therapy are where you want to go. I focus on learning about you - strengths, growth areas, hopes, family, and fears - to understand the patterns in your life right now. As we get deeper, I use a mix of tools in session - from mindfulness to somatic work to creating maps to exploring thoughts and feelings. For South Asian, API, and other BIPOC clients, exploring your thoughts, beliefs, emotions, and personal story in therapy can be a risk. May be it goes against your cultural or family norms, or may be you’ve had bad experiences with white therapists. As a South Asian therapist, I bring my lived experience to our work together. While I may not share your specific racial or ethnic identities, I will respect and affirm your experiences while holding space for you to explore.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: When I first started therapy, I could label 3 of my feelings: angry, sad, and hungry. And I wasn't even sure that hungry was a feeling? Little did I realize--most people can't name more than three feelings. Therapy helped me slow down and find my own experience of my feelings. That was a gamechanger. After 25 years as a community organizer working primarily with BIPOC and LGBTQ+ communities, I decided to change directions and become a therapist. You’ll always get some organizing flavor in my therapy because I believe that much of the suffering we face is because the systems around us (like schools, housing, or workplaces) weren’t built for us. Therapy can’t solve that–but our work can be a place of individual healing, connection, and radical understanding of your experience(s). Some identities that matter to me—and that might matter to you as you look for a therapist—include being South Asian, a cisgender woman, straight, and a parent.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: ACT helps individuals build psychological flexibility which can be really helpful in our day to day lives. ACT also focuses on helping take action toward living a life aligned with your values. I have utilize ACT tools and approaches, have attended ACT trainings, and participate in an ACT consultation group.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: The focus of my course work was in Marriage, Couples and Family Counseling at PSU. I work with individuals in the relationship on skills (learning to listen to one another or developing new ways to navigate conflict) and also having hard conversations from finances to intimacy challenges or mismatched desire to changes within the relationship or its structure.

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: I grew up in Portland, as the child of immigrants from India. Which means I went to mostly white schools where folks couldn’t say or didn’t bother learning how to say my name. I am deeply familiar with being the “only one”—whether it’s because of your race, ethnicity, immigrant family, or other cultural identities. While I may not share your specific racial or ethnic identities, I will respect and affirm your experiences while holding space for you to explore.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I support LGBTQ+ clients in their journey around sexual and gender identity, internalized homophobia or transphobia, and living in a system that regularly causes harm and can lead to grief, anger, depression and a host of other symptoms. Support includes: exploration around gender identity, navigating sexual expression and joy, preparation for gender affirming surgery, and post-operative integration and connection.

name: Kendall Herr
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello everyone! I am currently accepting new clients of any age. I look forward to being part of your story!
ideal_client: Life is hard but you don't have to do it alone! Do you find yourself struggling to keep yourself composed because you feel like your world is crashing down around you? Do you feel like you have become a burden to your family or friends because you keep talking about the same struggles that are on your mind and heart all the time? Are the things going on in your life getting in the way of you being your best self? If you could answer yes to any of these, I am here and ready to help!

approaches.My Background and Approach: I started my career working in the school system as a support to students in elementary school and went on to become a school counselor in a rural high school for the last 3 years. I have experience working with children and teens navigating the challenges of school and life outside of school. As much as I loved being a school counselor, I have transitioned into mental health counseling because I wanted to be able to help on a deeper level. I take time to really get to know my clients to help determine the best course of action to help. I use a variety of interventions ranging from CBT to Person Centered and also work with kids using art and play therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that change is possible with the right support, tools, and the determination to put in the hard work to make it happen. I believe that creating a strong connection with my clients is vital because healing and growth happens when you feel safe and heard. Suicide prevention/intervention have been a big part of my career. I have created prevention programs in schools and train staff on interventions. I became a counselor because I have had a few different counselors help me along my journey and I would not be where I am without them. I hope to be that for you! I have a passion for helping people and it is truly an honor to have people let me in their world and hear their stories.

name: Michael Junkins
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Hello! I am a Marriage and Family Therapist who approaches care with patience, curiosity and a sense of humor when working towards change.

approaches.My Background: I have a background in working with children and family from a wide diversity of life circumstances and needs including families experiencing houselessness, and families with children requiring both inpatient and outpatient mental health care.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that change and healing can be found through the bonds we share in our closest relationships. As a therapist, my role is to work with you to find new ways of being with your loved ones as well as new insights and possibilities for yourself. Whatever challenges you are facing, know that you are not alone and that things can get better. All of us inherently have the capacity to grow in order to achieve our goals. I approach therapy from an attachment-based, humanistic, and emotion-focused perspective, and I hope we can work together to bring forth the internal wisdom you already possess. My work with children and families has taught me the value of patience, humor, and creativity when working with others, and I seek to create a safe environment where you can feel free to be your authentic self. I am passionate about working with all configurations of families trying to navigate the complexities of life’s changes.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have extensive experience in working with child and adolescent issues ranging from family outpatient to acute psychiatric residential care.

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: I have worked with many families at many different stages of the divorce, separation and restructuring process and am familiar with the unique challenges than building and maintaining a complex, blended family can bring.

specialities.name: Anger Management
specialities.description: I have experience with with adults who are working on building a better relationship or sense of control over how they experience, process and express anger to better the relationships that matter to them.

name: Natalie Seibel
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: LPC in Oregon, LMHC in Washington and Certified Reiki Master
intro: I help guide you back home to yourself, building trust within so you can make aligned decisions that lead to love, joy and fulfillment.
ideal_client: I'm here for the individual, at any point in their life, who is on a path of self-reclamation and ready to embody their fullest, most authentic expression. They're remembering who they truly are. They're learning to love and honor the wounds of their past and present, even as they boldly step forward into what's next. They're called to do the deep work of knowing themselves fully and embracing all parts (especially the shadowed, hidden ones) with compassion.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I integrate evidence-based modalities like ACT, DBT, and IFS, along with energy work and spiritual guidance. As a Reiki Master and Spiritual Death Doula, I weave in energetic healing and intuitive insight where it’s desired and aligned. My deepest passion (and most cherished modality) is inner child healing, where some of the most profound shifts occur. Clients I work with often walk away with a deeper sense of self-trust and inner safety; greater clarity and confidence in life decisions; stronger boundaries and more authentic relationships; emotional resilience and the ability to hold discomfort without abandoning themselves; reconnection to their intuition, body, and spiritual path; integration of inner child and shadow parts, leading to wholeness and empowerment. If this speaks to you, I’d be honored to join you on your journey. You don’t have to do this alone.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe we all carry the wisdom to navigate life’s challenges. We already hold the keys to thrive but have likely been made to forget. Systemic & cultural conditioning, rooted in fear and shame, may have led you to disconnect from your truth. It can be hard to imagine another way; I’m here to help you remember. Our wounds aren’t barriers, they’re messengers. Even though you may have been taught to silence or suppress them, they hold deep insight. Shame, in particular, is often the deepest wound. It can whisper that you’re not enough and never will be, keeping you locked in patterns of avoidance. But when you make space for pain, as an inevitable and sacred part of life, you also create space for clarity, healing, and transformation. My practice is rooted in compassion, acceptance, and trust in your inner knowing. I help you build safety within yourself so you can return to your most empowered and authentic expression. I believe this is the heart of reclaiming your personal power.

name: Congruent Therapy: Madison Paskett
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hey there! I’m Madison, your millennial therapist who brings a splash of whimsy and a hearty dose of humor to the therapy room.
ideal_client: I have had years of experience working with couples, individuals, families, and systems, all of whom bring their own unique lived experiences, including LGBTQIA+, first responders, trauma survivors, and those who experience emotional intensity. She aims to help individuals/families/couples/systems build skills and find their path to the life they are wanting to live. This means together, we will work to identify and utilize strategies to best handle whatever life throws your way.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a queer individual who experiences ADHD, I understand firsthand how life’s quirks can shape our experiences. I’d describe myself as someone who feels deeply, loves hard, and shows up with an open heart and approachability. I’m all about curating an inclusive therapy space where laughter and lightness are welcome, proving that personal growth doesn’t have to be scary or even that serious. I firmly believe that you are the expert in your own life and the journey you find yourself on is your’s. My role is to walk alongside you in your process, ensuring that you are the one in the driver’s seat and I am with you. I believe the therapeutic relationship is rooted in transparency, respect, trust, and unconditional positive regard. I'm an eclectic clinician who leans into trauma informed, strength-based, and skill building interventions. My work often includes DBT, CBT, motivational interviewing, Parts work, Ecosystemic Structural Family Therapy, Emotionally Focused Therapy, and many more!

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am most passionate about supporting individuals with intense emotions and dysregulation, helping them navigate these experiences with compassion and resilience. My focus includes young adults, LGBTQIA+ individuals, and those who are neurodivergent. I also specialize in working with couples, polyamorous relationships, kink, and sexuality, recognizing the unique dynamics and challenges they present. Using evidence-based interventions and a holistic approach, I collaborate with individuals and their support systems on a journey of self-discovery. My goal is to help you view your emotions as valuable insights and create a therapeutic space where you feel heard, understood, and validated, equipping you with the skills to build the life you want. I work to cultivate a safe therapy space that meets you where you are at and invites collaboration, compassion, and connection.

name: Janel Ruehl
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I love working with individual adults and teens struggling with anxiety, depression, neurodivergence, and trauma, as well as couples.
ideal_client: I believe every individual can be empowered to define their own idea of wellness and discover ways to feel peace, joy, and hope in their lives. I focus first on building safe and nurturing relationships with my clients. From this foundation, we will work together to understand your current coping styles and identify opportunities to shift painful patterns of reaction. I also incorporate mindfulness and body-based techniques to increase somatic self-awareness and strong emotional regulation.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a Level I Certified Restoration Therapist and have studied with Dr. T. Hargrave, the founder of the Restoration Therapy Model. I hold a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Oregon State University- Cascades, and a bachelor’s degree in English from the University of Oregon. Prior to transitioning into the Mental Health field, I worked for five years in education, and more than a decade in the non-profit and local government sectors.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I'm a human too! After years of struggling to understand my own anxiety and depression, I began to develop healthy coping skills through my relationships with skilled counselors and therapists. This impacted every aspect of my life, including my career in community development. Although I enjoyed working toward positive change at the community level, I realized I can make an even bigger impact by working with individuals and couples one-on-one. Now, I love to combine my belief in the power of community with my work as a counselor, helping my clients find healing connections all around them. In addition to counseling, I also continue to support a variety of non-profit organizations through grant writing, organizational development, and facilitation services. In my free time, I volunteer with several organizations focused on food security, LGBTQ+ community building, and animal welfare. I also enjoy gardening, cooking, hiking, and skiing and find deep peacefulness in nature.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I specialize in Restoration Therapy, a blend of attachment, family systems, and mindfulness-based theories.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I frequently utilize Internal Family Systems (IFS) style parts work to increase understanding of current patterns of coping and areas of internal conflict or tension.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I have studied mindfulness and somatic awareness for more than a decade through the lens of Buddhism as well as Somatic Therapy.

name: Guillaume Counseling Services
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: We are a team of Clinicians who specializes in maternal and paternal mental health, and provide culturally specific services.
ideal_client: Our clients comes from all walks of life, with various ethnic and religious/spiritual background. Some our clients identify as black/African American/Haitian/Afro-Caribbean/African, others identity as Hispanics/Latino, Asians, Mixed race or multi-ethnic, and Caucasian. We do specialize in providing couples counseling so interracial couples. Some of our clients identify as Christian, spiritual or other faiths. We work with teens and adults, individuals, families, and couples.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our primarily lens is family system as we provide family therapy and couples therapy. We utilize Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Brief Solutions Focused Therapy, to name a few. Some of our Clinicians also have background in trauma informed care and also incorporate DBT. We have an eclectic approach to treatment, meaning that we first assess and then pull from treatment approaches to help our clients based on their present needs in the moment. We are very client-centered and tailor the service to individual needs. Most of our clients who are getting couples therapy are also receiving individual therapy. Our approach in working with couples is to focus on each person's mental health, which include individual and family (couples) sessions) with the same therapist. Most of our clients utilize their insurance to pay for services. We have a small percentage of clients who just want couples' counseling, focusing on the relationship only and not their mental health.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Clinical Supervisor and Clinician, Nahomie Guillaume is a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in the state of California (#48571), Oregon (# T1492) and Texas (#202775). She has 18 years of experienced in the field and has been licensed 14 years. She has a master's in Counseling Psychology, a Master of Business Administration, and a bachelor's in Psychology (emphasis in Christian Behavioral Science) and Communication arts (emphasis in Theater Arts). She also has a certification in life coaching and prayer therapy. She went to California Baptist University for both her undergraduate and graduate studies in psychology. Nahomie understand firsthand the challenges of being a mother, wife, with 4 little ones under the age of 12, juggling a career, and home life. Nahomie understand the challenges of losing a child through miscarriage and stillbirth. She understand the daily struggles of managing a relationship, striving to maintain love and respect, and growing as one. She is compassionate

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: Nahomie Guillaume is a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist and provide mental health services within a family relationship context, even if only one person present, attending individual therapy. All Clinicians who work under Nahomie's supervision and licensure are also trained to have a family system lens when working with clients. We specialize in improving family relationships.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: We primarily utilize Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to help individuals and couples address their presenting problems. CBT is designed to help the client gain awareness of their own thoughts/feelings/behaviors as well as greater understanding of the thoughts/feelings/actions of others around them. CBT is designed to help client gain awareness to make concrete behavior and cognitive changes.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: Many of our clients are dealing with solvable and situational stress, related to daily life functioning. We utilize Solution Focused Brief Therapy to help our clients problem solve, get unstack, and have tangible hope, based on real life solutions. This approach is used with individuals and couples.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: We utilize psychodynamic therapy to address past pain and hurt, exploring the unconscious, and past familial relations in how the shape the present. We also address defense mechanism learned from the past to protect the self. We utilize this approach to help client gain deeper insight of the self and the forces that shape the present self.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: We specialize in relationships and work with couples who just want to improve their relationships, pre-pared for a committed relationship, or who are struggling and needs healing. We utilize Gottman Method, Prepared and Enrich, as well as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to help our couples. We specialize in working with interracial/multiethnic/intercultural/interfaith couples.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: We specialize in maternal mental health and paternal mental health, where we work with both mom and dad, dealing postpartum depression and anxiety. We provide individual therapy, family therapy, and couples therapy.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: We specialize in maternal mental health and paternal mental health, where we work with both mom and dad, dealing with pregnancy related stress, anxiety, and depression. We provide individual therapy, family therapy, and couples therapy.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: We specialize in relationship counseling, offering pre-marital and marital counseling, individual therapy/family addressing mental health and relationship issues, as well as couples therapy focusing on just the relationship. We work with clients dealing with infidelity issues, in-law issues, cultural differences, as well as general relationship problems.

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: We provide culturally specific services to those who identify as black/African-American/Black descents struggling with racisms/prejudice related issues, as well as work with interracial/intercultural/multiethnic/Interfaith couples dealing with cultural differences stress.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: We work with clients struggling with mental health issues such as depression, anxiety, bipolar, trauma and PTSD.

name: Patrick Hyland
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Wherever you are now, I have been there. I am a retired attorney and military pilot, so I have significant experience to help.
ideal_client: Before becoming a counselor, I continued to do the same things over and over again in my life, making mistakes and bad choices, hoping for better results. My combat PTSD contributed to that continuing circle of frustration and anger. I have learned the lessons that help me begin each new day with an open and eager anticipation of exciting things to come. Now, I have the tools to help others achieve their hopes and dreams and to become ready, empowered, and on a positive path to change.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I specialize in childhood trauma, including abuse, latch-key, abandonment, and parental rejection. I also am experienced in other traumas, such as combat, workforce, or other significant trauma, having PTSD myself from Vietnam and multiple divorces. I empower adults, both men and women, to become the person they truly want to be, their individual and "True Self."

approaches.Why We Started this Group Practice: I started the group practice named Oregon Directions, to find, keep, and teach all counselors the importance of agency support, group recognition for all counselors and therapists, and the value of personally interacting with all other counselors, regardless of their present or future employers, in ways that exemplifies and raises each of us to higher standards of care and capabilities for the benefit of all clients. The Vision and Mission Statements provide clear guidance to all counselors that our clients deserve only the best and our daily work and on-going intentions are to work together to achieve that goal.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Neurofeedback is offered in Lane County.

name: Michael Ianello
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with adults seeking relief from anxiety, depression, loneliness, harsh self-criticism, and/or interpersonal conflict.
ideal_client: I work well with clients who are experiencing anxiety-based disorders (generalized anxiety, social phobias, relational issues). I have knowledge and experience working with mood disorders, ADHD, intimate relationship issues, sudden life change (loss of job, big move, end of relationship). I am happy to work with people who are new to therapy as well as those who have "tried it all".

approaches.My Background and Approach: I help clients reduce their anxiety and develop strategies to reduce suffering. I am direct, with a light touch, to ensure both comfort and authentic connection are achieved in every session. Through the development of renewed vitality, curiosity, and joy, my clients rediscover core life values; learn and develop concrete skills to find relief from sticky or painful thoughts; cultivate empathy; connect compassionately, and deeply, with their own true heart. I have worked in the developmental and mental health fields as an educator, researcher, and counselor for over 15 years. I have a bachelor's degree in Psychology and a Master's degree in Professional Mental Health Counseling. I have received professional training in DBT, ACT, and mindfulness based behavioral interventions as well as depth focused, process oriented modalities.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: The core values of my practice are: safety, honesty, and curiosity. A feeling of safety and confidentiality is paramount to the profound work of self-discovery that occurs in a therapeutic practice. I seek to model honesty, directness, and vulnerability with clients so that they can experience the unique freedoms that arise from honest and open dialogue. Cultivating curiosity can provide relief from rote ways of thinking or perceiving. A simple practice of reframing an issue, might provide tremendous relief from unnecessary suffering. I value diversity and strive to treat all clients with dignity and respect, no matter their beliefs or background. I also commit my time away from work to health care reform and community mental health outreach with the hopes that quality mental health care is no longer out of anyone's reach due to social, cultural, or financial position

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: ACT has two basic principles for therapist and client to follow. One, accept that we have unwelcome thoughts sometimes and that these thoughts are out of our control. Two, commit to a life which is focused on core values defined by you. In other words, "Embrace your imperfections and learn how to trust that you know what's best." ACT is a research and evidence based approach which has been shown to assist with the following: Anxiety, Depression, Social Insecurity, Perfectionism, ADHD and more.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I have a background in existential philosophy and psychology. Discovering deeper meaning by confronting the difficult questions that arise from the unique nature of the human condition. What does it mean to be alive? How do my choices define me? How can I live a life committed to action and purpose? How can I embrace my failures and celebrate my success?

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: Many fields in psychology today draw on the rich history and research that psychodynamic modalities have been developing for the better part of the last 100 years. Studying this broad and rich tradition inspires me to maintain curiosity around: awareness of self; relationships with others; relationship with society; relationship with nature. Seeing one's self as part of a vast, ever changing system can provide deep insight into who we are as individuals.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I specialize in working with people who are experiencing anxiety-based disorders (generalized anxiety, social anxiety, panic attacks, phobias). I assist clients in developing a deeper sense of meaning through the investigation of patterns of suffering. Stop feeling paralyzed in your thinking and your life, break free from constantly second guessing yourself and learn what it takes to trust others as well as yourself.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Who decides how your life is going to develop? Taking back ownership over the direction of our growth can be a vital and powerful tool in becoming who we've always wanted to be. Take stock of your life and learn what it takes to become who you truly are.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: How do you experience your depression? What impact does it have on your life? Everyone gets down sometimes but what do we do when we feel like our melancholy is bottomless? What if your depression had a place to emerge, had a place to be seen without judgement? Would the way you experience it change? How might you change if it did? I will work with you to answer these questions and help you deepen your own understanding of how you can cultivate and sustain renewed vitality.

name: Elizabeth Nelson
title: Art Therapist
intro: I am a queer art therapist and counselor conducting virtual art therapy in Oregon for ages 11-24 to address anxiety and depression.
ideal_client: My passion is working with ages 11-24 suffering from anxiety and depression. Clients typically have an affinity for art as a way that they process. Art therapy interventions I utilize are drawing, environmental art, poetry/spoken word, mask making, printmaking, altered books, fiber arts and a few other surprises....

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist, I seek to foster healing in action, play, imagination, wholeness, meaning making, connection, courage, authenticity, a sense of belonging, transformation, agency and resilience in the lives of the individuals I work with. My work is grounded in attachment, trauma informed, and experiential theoretical orientations. Art therapy is a powerful, experiential, expressive arts therapy that helps address that which is difficult to put words to. It focuses not necessarily on the art product, but rather using art in the process of therapy as a lens to access parts of the brain, body and psyche that talk therapy may not fully reach. Humanity has turned to various types of art for millennia to heal, long before therapists in the modern sense existed, and this type of therapy engages in this phenomenon.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I strive to make space in therapy to examine the impact of my and my clients' social locations and the impact of the systems we are all apart of, knowing this brings a broader and more complete picture in regards to how we all show up in the world.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: I completed a masters degree in Art Therapy Counseling from Marylhurst University in 2006 and have obtained board certification as an art therapist with the national Art Therapy Credentials Board.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have worked with children and adolescents for 25 yrs. in both educational and therapeutic settings (hospitals, schools, community mental health agencies and day treatment facilities). My passion is working with teenagers and my practice is uniquely designed to treat the developmental and mental health concerns of this population.

name: Caitlin "Caity" Lynch
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: You, your relationship, & your family deserve to thrive and be accepted as you are. Experience LGBTQ+ and Neurodivergence-affirming therapy!
ideal_client: If you found me, you're likely outside of "the norm." I enthusiastically affirm fat, disabled, gender and sexual minority, polyam, and Black, Indigenous, other People of Color in our therapy sessions. I work to help us create a space to explore trauma healing, understand emotional patterns in your romantic relationships, identify family of origin/attachment concerns, hold boundaries, explore your sexual and gender identity, & support you with grief and loss, ADHD, Autism, anxiety, or depression.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapy style is collaborative, integrating wisdom from your experiences and from counseling theories rooted in empowerment and equity. I consider your family influences and how systemic "isms" impact you & your relationships. *NOTE: I do not provide ADHD or Autism Assessments. Please seek this through your PCP or a psychologist.* I am a sex-positive therapist and welcome all relationships, whether you're seeking pre-marital therapy, are a poly, kink, BDSM, or LGBTQIA+ relationship. I use Emotion-Focused Therapy to help you get curious about how your attachment styles (the way you relate to significant people) impact your relationships. Together we'll note relational patterns aren't working and strengthen the ones that are. With Narrative Therapy, I'll encourage you to consider your strengths and creative solutions. We'll use Internal Family Systems to help you reconnect to your core, authentic self and parts you may have ignored or been afraid to look at.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Therapy has been an important part of my healing work in both relationships and self-discovery. I've also encountered therapists who were unhelpful -- even harmful. I want to be a supportive, healing, decolonized space for individuals, families, and couples/relationships to explore uncomfortable, interesting, difficult, freeing, healing patterns and ideas. My healing journey includes formal therapy, body awareness practices, meditation, spiritual exploration, relational boundary setting, self-education, and lots of trial and error. I expect many of my clients will come to therapy with a similarly rich, complex, and varied healing path. I welcome you to bring your whole selves to therapy sessions. I became a therapist so I could meet you where you are, bring your strengths to light, and send you on your way into this brave, beautiful, scary, strange, and transformative world.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I use Emotionally-Focused Couples Therapy (EFCT) based on the work of Dr. Susan Johnson. We'll work collaboratively to decide on common goals for your relationship, discern unhelpful relationship patterns, work to understand why those made sense and helped you previously, and how to move forward with empathy for each other, meeting individual needs, and creating sustainable, healthier relational habits.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Dealing with intrusive thoughts and ongoing stressors can make life very difficult. Often clients express feeling stuck in their head, struggling to make decisions, and experiencing flashbacks to traumatic moments. I use Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapy from a trauma-informed and neurodivergence-informed perspective to help people struggling with trauma, depression, and anxiety to find a compassionate and brave way forward.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: When we know that all of our parts are welcome, we can let the Self -- our core part -- lead. We all know what it's like to feel torn about a decision, we feel two or three ways about something and aren't sure which part to listen to. IFS helps you to slow down and hear what each of your parts wants for you, and how to honor each one as part of your internal "family." Many clients find IFS helps them feel more empowered and in the driver's seat of their own life in a new way.

specialities.name: Aspergers
specialities.description: If you're Autistic or questioning if you're on the spectrum, welcome. If you're entering into therapy as an individual or in couples/relationship therapy, you probably want someone who will listen to you, understand you, and treat you as the valuable, creative, and capable person you are. Unfortunately, many Autistic people feel the need to hide or "mask" traits that are not the norm (neurotypical), even in therapy! I provide a space that is accepting, mask-free, and neurodivergence-affirming.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: We'll work collaboratively to decide on common goals for your relationship, discern unhelpful relationship patterns, work to understand why those made sense and helped you previously, and how to move forward with empathy for each other, meeting individual needs, and healthier relational habits. I use Emotionally-Focused Couples Therapy (EFCT) based on Dr. Sue Johnson's experience and research to guide our relational work.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a queer and genderqueer clinician, I bring personal and professional experience into my therapy work with the LGBTQ2SIA+ community. I offer WPATH gender-affirming care assessments and support letters as part of your care. If you're exploring parts of your identity: welcome! I know that path personally, and I am very happy to be with folks on that journey. If you want to talk about anything BUT your LGBTQ+ identity, I get that, too. Bring your whole self, and let me know your goals.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Many people grow up in situations where having needs and expressing them in a healthy way is a challenge. Sometimes families and romantic partners fall into unhealthy habits that they swore they would not repeat. I'll approach your healing from codependency with compassion for how it served you previously, and a hopeful lens for practical steps you can take to regain healthy relational boundaries.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: Healing from past abuse and individual traumatic situations can feel like an uphill battle and I want to be able to support you on that journey. I use EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing), Internal Family Systems (IFS), and Somatic Experiencing therapy modalities to help people move from feeling stuck in traumatic pasts to leaning into a hopeful and more adaptive future.

name: Elyse Beckman
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I embrace a solution-focused, client-centered perspective to help facilitate the process of change. YOU matter in this process!
ideal_client: I help clients examine all the relationships in their lives—whether with the self, others or even their vices. I specialize in helping clients by both validating and understanding their experience and in the same space being curious about how to navigate change. I believe in direct communication and that the relationship between therapist and client can foster growth. I work with clients working on substance use, grief, loss, relationships, personality traits and emotional disregulation.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am trained in dialectical behavior therapy with a focus on regulation emotions. If you ever feel like your emotions are in control and not you - we can work together to help problem solve how to regain a sense of control. I focus on person centered, solution focused relational therapy. For us to grow and change as people, its often in relation to others and we can use our time in therapy to foster growth and change within yourself. I have a deep respect for the bravery and courage it takes to reach out for help and I want to honor that you have started that journey! My role is to help clients examine all the relationships in their lives—whether with the self, others or even their vices. I embrace a solution-focused, client-centered perspective to help facilitate the process of change. I want to make your strengths shine.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that all of us have the power to change, we often just need help to get started. Growing up in the pacific northwest, I am intimately familiar with the culture of the region and how isolating we can feel in the world around us at times. I am hear to offer that support, encouragement and skills that can help you through a stressful time in your life.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: Recovery from a substance, vice or behavior can be a hard and impactful process that is often done best with additional support through therapy. As a licensed substance use counselor in Oregon and Washington I have provided therapy to many throughout the years who are starting or continuing along their own process of recovery.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships are defining in many ways for our lives, whether we have challenges, positives or not enough relationships and I help clients explore how relationships impact their thoughts and emotions. By using DBT therapy we can examine how to regulate emotions in the face of challenges in our relationships with others and ourselves

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Personal growth is a life long learning process. I am trained in different alternative treatments exploring psychedelic therapies or somatic therapies to practice growing and changing our lives.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I worked for many years as a bereavement therapist in the community helping others through individual and group therapy to process and incorporate losses of all kinds. I often think of loss as a coin and on the flip side of the same coin is love.

name: Daniel Maher, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Compassionate. Effective. Transformative. As a seasoned, trauma-informed therapist, I help individuals and couples move towards healing.
ideal_client: Many people come to therapy seeking relief from painful symptoms, relationship issues and self-defeating patterns. They may feel alone and isolated in their suffering. I work to create a safe, respectful and supportive environment that alleviates aloneness and facilitates positive change.

approaches.My Background: I have over 17 years of diverse clinical experience, including psychotherapy, medical social work in emergency rooms, ICUs, psychiatric emergency services, addiction services, and working with military veterans and their families. I specialize in treating depression/anxiety, PTSD/trauma, complicated grief, relationship issues, and the impact of physical illness and addictions. I am also sensitive to the particular needs of LGBTQIA people. My training and experience blend psychodynamic, attachment neuroscience, DBT and Mindfulness-based, experiential methods to help you feel better, heal, and be more connected.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: My style is warm, active, forthright and supportive. I consider it a privilege to accompany clients towards healing and greater fulfillment in their lives. My approach is highly informed by Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy. AEDP aims at healing attachment wounds and other kinds of trauma, and is also effective in treating depression, anxiety, addictive behaviors, relationship difficulties, and many other issues. Often session work includes a combination of us attending to present-moment emotional experience and learning skills to regulate feelings, reduce anxiety, and facilitate connection with self and others. I also enlist tools from Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) when helpful.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can be a primary problem from genetic and biological vulnerabilities, or a secondary condition from past, unprocessed trauma, loss and adversity. In any event, symptoms of depression can be debilitating and serious. I use a variety of modalities and supports to help cope with and relieve symptoms to help you feel like yourself again.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can be a primary condition or a symptom — or both. I can help you better understand the nature of your anxiety — it's origins and triggers — and learn skills to decrease it. Using a combination of cognitive and behavioral skills (including mindfulness) to soothe, you can access deeper emotional processing and experience that anxiety blocks us from feeling.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Whether it be to heal with the impact of discrete traumatic events or complex interpersonal trauma, I use a combination of attachment theory, DBT and a relational-psychodynamic therapy to help you build safety and seIf worth. I teach emotion regulation skills and we use the therapeutic relationship itself so that you can feel more grounded and secure in connection with yourself and others.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a gay cis male therapist, I bring empathy and lived experience to my work with people in the LGBTQIA community. Creating safety, affirmation, and attunement, providing support and undoing aloneness are central to my work with LGBTQIA people impacted by oppression, isolation, homophobia and transphobia. I am also aware of and sensitive to issues that are unique to same-sex and mixed-gendered couples.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Everyone experiences loss of all kinds -- people, pets, relationships, jobs, physical ability, material items, roles, identity, etc. I work to create a respectful and supportive space in which we can help you move through the very normal but painful process of grief and bereavement, as well as help identify and attend to areas where you may be stuck.

name: Angelie Karabatsos
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My practice is about courage, strength, and trust. I help people build the life and relationships they desire.
ideal_client: Does life feel like a Merry-Go-Round? Spinning around and around with no way off. I help people build the life and relationships they desire! I work with Individuals, Couples, and Families experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, relationship concerns, marital unrest, or infidelity. Courage, trust, and strength are the pillars we all possess but rarely see in ourselves. It takes courage to embrace hopes and fears. Trust to explore hidden passions and find forgotten dreams. S

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is based on 3 C's: compassion, collaboration, and creativity. Individualized treatment is provided based on each person or couples' need. Interventions include recognizing unhealthy thinking patterns, reframing self-limiting talk, developing behavioral and emotional coping cards, utilizing principles of mindfulness and guided imagery exercises to reduce anxious feelings. Empowering my clients to see new opportunities or directions is the goal in every session.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became interested in human behavior after taking several psychology courses my senior year of high school. My undergraduate and graduate degrees focused on organizational development and marketing, which allowed me to explore behavior from a holistic and analytical perspective. My business career spans 23 years and encompasses relationship, marketing, and project management. I have worked in the Banking, E-commerce and Advertising industries.
