I have seen the impact of mergers and layoffs. Watched couples’ struggle balancing careers, family, and relationships.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Women today face many difficult choices and must deal with numerous life challenges., which can cause emotional conflicts. One such conflict, for professional women is choosing between a promotion or marriage. Other conflicts revolve around childhood trauma or intimate partner violence. I build a caring and compassionate alliance to help you confront deep wounds and plot a new course.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: An opportunity to develop a professional identity. Whether you are just beginning or changing careers, figuring out which career is right for you can be difficult. I utilize various card sorts and skill/interest assessments to assist individuals in finding their passion not a job.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Creating a couple's identity without losing your own identity is tough. Each partner has their own communication style, interests, and dreams. I work with couples with communication concerns, affair recovery, co-parenting issues, and balancing career with family life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Life can sometimes feel overwhelming, confusing, or challenging. When you find your mind is racing, your palms are sweating, and your stomach hurts, its difficult to make sound decisions. I use guided imagery and mindfulness techniques to calm the internal system and allow you to time to think through your unique situation.

name: Mark Pechovnik
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: As both a psychotherapist and a Zen priest, I work closely with individual and couples to help normalize their experiences while also helping them to move beyond barriers behind which they feel stuck, creating a more spacious, confident and authentic life.

approaches: The emphasis on therapy is always on what is happening now, here in session. Even when thoughts of the past arise, they are being metabolized in the present. We work to acknowledge and allow our reality to fully express itself and then make choices about what is the most skillful way to move forward. Whereas we often think we are broken, we are always less broken than uncomfortable with our own complexity. We all have darkness inside of us. Therapeutic work helps us to familiarize ourselves with the rich landscape of our life experiences. In the end, we build a set of tools to help us navigate our lives well and with integrity. In so doing, build our self-confidence and self esteem.

I am both a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and a Rinzai Zen Priest. I am committed in both fields to help others find freedom in their lives. I have extensive experience in various cognitive, emotional and somatic modalities as they relate to relationships, trauma, mood disorders and addiction. I have worked in youth facilities, addiction treatment centers, community mental health, mindfulness clinics, and most recently in private practice. Currently, about a third of my case load is couples.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: There is an emphasis on clear, empathic communication (NVC); sexuality and differentiation (Schnarch's Work); relationship building tools (Gottman and others); sexuality; acceptance; attachment; and emotional attunement (Emotion Focused Therapy).

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Fundamental to our work together is the fact that there are two people in a room discussing very personal and intimate information. The reality of the relationship we develop is both acknowledged and worked with not only as natural outcome of the work we do but as a tool to help increase tolerance for intimacy, authenticity and self-confidence.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness arises in the session naturally as we spend an hour looking deeply at what is happening here and now (even if it's thoughts and feelings about the past). In addition to cultivating mindfulness in session, we can also develop meditation skills (though meditation is helpful, it is not required).

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: In the end, all therapy focuses on personal growth. Very often our complaints stem from some fundamental unwillingness to grow. Childhood wounding leaves us hoping for a parental figure (or lover) to fill a void in our lives. The maturity that comes from looking at and facing our lives and the disappointments in our lives and taking responsibility for moving forward is a life-long process.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Spirituality is often the component most often neglected in our modern lives. Though it can have many expressions , its absence of expression can often be the root of our own disquiet and dissatisfaction. Spiritual work is hard work, and we will often avoid to engage in more immediately gratifying activities. Therapy can help create your own spiritual identify and clear away blocks to practice.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: Weekly therapy can be a great addition to personal recovery work. I have great respect for and advocate for 12-Step programs. Outside of community support, individual therapy is a boon to working through the inevitable mental health issues that helped cause and were created by addictive behaviors.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationship problems often stem from unrealistic expectations about what our partners are meant to do for us. Therapy helps transform expectation into appreciation. In the end, our romantic relationships can be wonderful and deeply intimate friendships of mutual support and care.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma are experiences that either actively and vividly haunt us or go underground and reveal themselves only through behaviors that limit our full engagement in life. I utilize various techniques (including EMDR) to help uncover and work with the trauma so that it becomes less a defining factor and more an historical artifact.

name: Emaline Friedman
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: My desire for you is what you desire for you. I work to honor and develop your unique existence through speaking and listening.
ideal_client: Do you ever find yourself at odds with yourself? I work best with people who feel internally conflicted about one or many aspects of life, whether in self esteem, relationships and love, artistic and professional achievements, or inexplicable habits and compulsions. If you are afraid of yourself, or what you might be holding on to internally, I offer a starkly nonjudgmental space to say *anything* that comes to mind. I accept parts of you that you may not.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My education is in humanistic, existential, and psychoanalytic approaches to personality maturation. My PhD research focused on Internet Addiction and the way that digital life changes our experiences of ourselves, relationships, and ways we express ourselves. Some notable symptoms of digital culture - that psychotherapy addresses - are alienation, loneliness, increased social comparison, impulsivity, a sense of meaninglessness, and lowered tolerance for frustration and disappointment. As a therapist, I offer a protected space for working through fantasies, dreams, intense affects, and relational and emotional difficulties. Therapy is an opportunity to develop a relationship that supports construction of your individual history and thinking about personal and relationship issues that get pushed to the margins of awareness.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am constantly in awe of the tenderness, and tenacity, of the human spirit - especially under difficult social and environmental conditions. While therapy addresses self- and relationally-generated obstacles to living fully, external obstacles are ever-present in the clinic. This is why I practice therapy in addition to more overt activism and political participation around universal basic goods, digital and privacy rights, climate justice, and resisting the encroachment of financialization and digital capitalism. I also train and facilitate non-violent communication, in support of our right to education about how to stand for ourselves. I am also a lover of music, dogs, pickleball, and crossword puzzles.

specialities.name: Internet Addiction
specialities.description: Internet Addiction encompasses the compulsive use of games, pornography, shopping, and media, and also the difficulties of living in hybrid/virtual environments that over-expose our lives in ways we cannot control. Integrating what you do and who you are online is part of my therapeutic technique.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I work with clients exploring their gender identities and working on questions about their self-image and embodiment. I believe gender is not secondary to personality, but pervades how we think, act, love, and operate in the social order.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Our greatest vulnerabilities lie with our major relationships. My psychoanalytic approach to therapy is extremely well-suited to working with relationship, marriage, and family issues. I support clients in understanding relationship issues at the root and problem-solving in the present.

name: Caroline McGrath LPC, NCC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: Certified Master Jungian Life Coach, Certified Trauma-Informed Breathwork Facilitator, Certified TRE® Provider, Certified Yoga Calm® Youth Instructor, Holistic Health Practitioner
intro: Integrating Therapy, Breathwork, & Coaching, I support you through life's challenges. Fostering self-discovery, healing, & personal growth.
ideal_client: Through Therapy, Trauma-Informed Breathwork, & Somatic Coaching, my collaborative approach supports you -or your child- in navigating life's challenges. Specializing in self-discovery, healing, & personal growth, I offer a safe space to break free from patterns, nurture inner healing, & unlock new possibilities. Whether you're struggling with school or career stress, navigating relationships, family dynamics, divorce, or simply seeking personal growth, I'm here to empower you along your journey.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I support clients in their personal journey to discover tools that resonate with them, explore their sense of self, uncover personal coping strategies, and develop new, healthy ways to express their emotions. As a Trauma-Informed Breathwork Facilitator & Somatic-Based Coach, I incorporate a blend of integrative techniques, which encompass Coaching, Breathwork, Shadow Work, TRE, & Social Neuroscience. I hold a Master's Degree in Counseling Psychology from Lewis & Clark Graduate School. I specialize in working with children, adolescents, and adults, employing a variety of individual and group counseling modalities. My extensive experience includes helping clients who have navigated challenges such as divorce, trauma, grief/loss, anxiety, depression, life transitions, self-esteem, and self-worth issues. Additionally, I have a background in assisting children and teens in shelter and residential treatment facilities who were facing serious to severe emotional and behavioral difficulties.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am deeply committed to destigmatizing mental health issues, especially among children, teens, and young adults. Many young individuals in our communities grapple with the overwhelming stressors and high expectations tied to school, peer relationships, parental pressures, college, sports, and future planning. These pressures can culminate in anxiety, depression, as well as strained relationships with family and peers. My passion lies in helping children, teens, and young adults navigate these challenges and emerge with a strong sense of self-worth, equipped with the coping skills to journey through life's ups and downs. On a more personal note, I cherish spontaneous adventures with my family and friends, and I make it a point to take mental health days to rejuvenate from life's daily demands. Being a mom to my boys is a source of immense joy and fulfillment as we journey through life together.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: Areas and Specialties in my Coaching Practice as a Certified Master Jungian Life Coach & Trauma-Informed Breathwork Facilitator: Coaching for Adults & Parents; Life & Career Transitions; Burnout; Feeling Stuck and Resistant; Shadow Work; Reconnecting With Your Intuition & Spiritual Growth; Strengthening Self Worth & Self Confidence; Family/Parent/Work/Relationship/Life Balance; Ready to Level Up in Business; Entrepreneurship; Stress Management/Anxiety/Overwhelm

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: As a Therapist, a Master Jungian Life Coach, and a Breathwork Facilitator, I work with younger clients to help reduce anxiety, stress, anger, & overwhelm as they build resiliency with tools to redirect when life doesn't go as planned. I work with Parents & Adults to reduce overwhelm, stress, anger, and to release negative thought patterns and limiting beliefs that keep them from moving forward. I also work side by side with clients who are ready to shift from burnout to bliss in their business.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I support teens, college students, and young adults who are struggling with the stressors and anxieties of post-pandemic struggles, school, friends, families, life, and self. Many teens and young adults may also be experiencing other emotional or behavioral responses to the challenges they are enduring, as well as past traumas. Add in a pandemic and todays youth’s lives have been flipped upside down. Together we work collaboratively as we navigate through the up's and downs.

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: I support children and adolescents whose parents are going through, or have gone through, a divorce or separation. Children experience familial divorce differently at every age. The grief, loss, fear of the unknown, as well as whether or not the divorce is amicable, holds many factors and many emotions for children and teens. I also work with parents, helping them support their children through the divorce process and years after. I also support adults throughout their divorce process.

name: Emily Rose
title: Hypnotherapist
intro: I help you heal and clear ancestral patterns and karmic cycles ~ so you can live from your truth, not your trauma.
ideal_client: You’ve carried too much for too long. On the outside, you hold it together; but inside, it’s tangled. You’re done shrinking. Done pretending you’re fine. You want real connection, nervous system safety, and a life that actually fits. You’re not here to fix yourself, you’re here to remember who you are. Fully. Deeply. And on your own terms.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to healing is rooted in the knowing that you are already whole. This work isn’t about fixing you, it’s about creating space for what’s already within you to come forward: your clarity, your strength, your truth. What makes this work different is the depth. We don’t stop at surface-level coping. We go to the root; into the unconscious layers where real transformation happens. Where other approaches may focus on managing symptoms, this work helps you shift the patterns, beliefs, and internal narratives that have shaped your life. We’re not just talking about change; we’re rewiring it. Each session is designed specifically for you. I pull from a wide range of tools: hypnosis, somatic healing, parts integration, energy work, and NLP to meet you exactly where you are and guide you toward what’s next.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Choosing someone to walk with you on your healing path is personal. You’re not just looking for credentials, you’re looking for someone who sees you clearly, honors where you’ve been, and knows how to hold space for where you’re going. I don’t take that lightly. You think you need something new—but what you really need is to remember something within you that was never lost, just buried. You’re not broken. You’ve been carrying too much for too long, and somewhere along the way, you disconnected from a part of yourself that’s still here… and ready to return. Healing begins when we create space for that remembering. If you’ve felt unseen or misunderstood in other healing spaces, know this: that won’t happen here. I work with the patterns underneath; ancestral wounds, relational trauma, and the unconscious beliefs shaping your life. Together, we meet what’s been waiting. And we begin again, with you at the center.

specialities.name: Hypnotherapy
specialities.description: If you’ve tried mindset work, talk therapy, or pushing through, and still feel stuck; hypnotherapy goes where most methods can’t: the root. This work dives below the surface, into the unconscious patterns and beliefs quietly running the show. Together, we’ll access those deeper layers and start to rewire the thoughts, stories, and emotional blocks keeping you in cycles you’re ready to break.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: You’re self-aware. You’ve done the journaling, the workshops, the books; but something still isn’t shifting. That’s where this work comes in. My coaching approach combines grounded, honest support with powerful tools like NLP to help you uncover what’s really driving your choices—the unconscious beliefs and patterns that keep pulling you off track. Once we find the root, we shift it.

specialities.name: Past Life Regression
specialities.description: When emotional patterns, fears, or blocks keep showing up and nothing in this life fully explains them; it’s often because the root is older. Past life regression helps you access the deeper layers of your soul’s story. In session, we follow what’s alive in your system and trace it back, sometimes into other lifetimes so you can release what’s still lingering and reconnect with the wisdom you’ve carried all along.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Talk alone can’t reach the places where trauma lives. That’s why somatic therapy works through the body—because healing isn’t just mental, it’s physical, emotional, and energetic. Using sound, breathwork, and body-based awareness, we’ll access the tension, emotion, and survival responses your system has been holding onto. These practices help you move out of freeze, out of overwhelm, and back into presence.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can feel like a constant hum in the background; keeping you on edge, disconnected from your body, and bracing for what’s next. Together, we’ll get to the root of it. We’ll look at the patterns, beliefs, and lived experiences that have kept your system stuck in survival.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Codependency can make it hard to tell where you end and others begin. You get so used to managing everyone else’s needs that your own voice goes quiet. Over time, you start to feel invisible; even to yourself. In our work together, we’ll uncover the patterns and beliefs that keep you stuck in cycles of overgiving and self-sacrifice. You’ll begin to reconnect with your own needs, rebuild trust with yourself, and reclaim your boundaries, your voice, and your worth.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: Ancestral and historical trauma doesn’t just live in the past; it lives in your body, your relationships, your patterns. It can shape how you show up, what you tolerate, and what you believe you’re allowed to want. In our work together, we’ll unravel what’s been passed down: unspoken grief, survival strategies, inherited fears, so you can stop carrying what was never yours to hold.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Your spiritual path is your own: complex, evolving, and often full of questions that don’t have easy answers. You might be feeling disconnected, searching for clarity, or sensing that something deeper is calling you forward. Wherever you are, I’m here to walk with you.

name: Celine Redfield
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: MA, LMFT, Certified Havening Practitioner, EFT Master, Practitioner
intro: I am a queer/NB/ND art therapist who wants to help you reconnect with your higher self and show up for you with compassion and attention.
ideal_client: Do you want to feel more connected and less triggered? Would you like to better understand your choices, emotions, and reactions? I help people feel grounded, enabling them to respond thoughtfully rather than impulsively. By reconnecting with themselves, individuals can become aware of their patterns and triggers. I educate people about the nervous system and its impact on mood, sleep, and interactions, guiding them to explore their internal world and the aspects that influence them.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Working from a holistic approach that brings together body, mind, and spirit. I mix scientific and woo-woo perspectives to facilitate personal healing through mindfulness and acceptance-based approaches, creative arts therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), somatic-based psychology, EFT tapping, hypnosis, EMDR, Havening, and acupressure. I enjoy educating clients about their nervous systems as a foundation for understanding their mental health symptoms. Then, with art, metaphor, and somatic therapy, clients can use the right side of their brain to find new ways of expression and understanding to attend to themselves more and build a better relationship with themselves. My goal in therapy is to help individuals become their guide to understanding themselves in a deeper and more meaningful way, so that they can feel the freedom of connecting with their authentic selves.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Everyone deserves to practice listening to and healing parts of themselves that may be hidden from them. I have navigated this personally and have often been the odd one in my family. I came out late as queer and did not identify as Trans/Non-Binary until about three years ago. I work well with individuals who struggle with their identity, are in transition, and need to build greater awareness, compassion, and clarity within themselves. I am part of both the sober community and the LGBTQ community. I am trained in six different trauma modalities: Art Therapy, EMDR, EFT, Hypnosis, Havening, and Self-Acupressure. I became an art therapist because I genuinely enjoy helping others learn to listen to themselves, understand their needs, and embrace their shadows, welcoming all parts of themselves, including the vulnerable and needy ones, as well as the mean and aggressive ones. I have a therapy dog, Remy, that works with me Monday through Thursday and he is just the sweetest.

specialities.name: Energy Psychology
specialities.description: I use energy psychology to help my clients to transform thought patterns and energy that are no longer serving them.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Trained by Kristen Neff and Christopher Germer in Mindfulness Based self compassion. I help clients to learn how to use mindfulness to be more compassionate with themselves and the world.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: I use art therapy to help clients to externalize their problems so that they can have different perspective on them and to use the right side of the brain instead of the left. Through use of the art clients gai insights into their bodies and the unconscious process that occurs within them.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: If you have historical trauma that continues to haunt you and you would like to work through it. Art therapy, EMDR, hypnosis, and energy medicine can be beneficial in addressing and releasing historical trauma. I work with my clients to create a safe space and give them tools to address old traumas in a kind and gentle way that respects their body, mind, and spirit.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: If you are having difficulty with addiction, I have helped many clients to work on having and maintaining sobriety. I can help you to address underlying issues that may be causing relapse and abuse. If you are willing to take a look at harm reduction and eventually sobriety, then I can help you with your process.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I wrote my thesis on integrating sexual and cultural identities for Latina Lesbians. I was trained at the LA LGBTQ Center. I am also queer, so I understand the challenges of being LGTBQ. Whether you are struggling with coming out, dealing with internalized heterosexism, needing support for your transition, or just needing support, I can help you.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: If you have difficulty with control issues, wanting things to be a certain way, and needing to be perfect, you may struggle with codependency. I have worked with and helped many clients find freedom from this pattern. I helped them feel more fulfilled in their lives by learning to focus on themselves instead of others.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I love to help individuals who are having difficulty resolving anxiety and trauma. I help clients to reinhabit their bodies and help clients to change thought patterns and move energy that is stuck.

name: Zachary Cope
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I work with adults, couples, and teens struggling with an array of issues, including depression, anxiety, trauma, abuse, and grief.
ideal_client: I work with adults, couples, and teens struggling with an array of issues, including depression, anxiety, trauma, abuse, grief, relationship challenges, vocational decisions, and other major life transitions. Helping parents who have gone through divorce and those with blended families is work that is especially close to my heart. I know firsthand the difficulties of these experiences and the immense reward of working through the interpersonal challenges associated with them.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a current graduate student at George Fox University and my primary approach to working with clients is Restoration Therapy. This model uses mindfulness, attachment theory and emotional regulation for a holistic approach to bettering mental health and relationships. I also believe in the importance of the mind-body connection and working with the nervous system. I like to use TRE (tension, stress, and trauma releasing exercises) for those it can benefit. I value work with people of all genders but love to help males create a new lens for viewing the world. Society does not teach the value of vulnerability and emotionality to boys. Men often put on a mask, being competitive, aggressive, rational, tough, and not viewing interpersonal relationships as a true measure of success. Working with individuals with ADHD through a strengths-based approach is also a passion of mine.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I have always been inclined towards helping people. I worked at summer camps with kids suffering from life threatening illnesses and coached sports when I was younger. I am a small business owner and have found joy over the years in mentoring young entrepreneurs. I’ve worked to develop community-oriented projects and have traveled internationally for volunteer projects. My views of culture, values and beliefs were in part shaped by these experiences. Most of my background is in the business world but I always had the underlying thought inside of me about having a career helping others work through personal and interpersonal issues.

name: Rosemary Elliott
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am a compassionate therapist who is committed to helping others heal from trauma, feelings of social isolation, and anxiety.
ideal_client: Are you overwhelmed by troubling thoughts about the future or the past? Do you struggle to make meaningful connections with others? Do you find it difficult to relax in social settings? I am passionate about working with clients who are grappling with these difficulties in an increasingly isolating world. I believe that a life full of satisfying relationships and a deeply held sense of meaning is possible.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy with me isn’t one-size-fits-all. I start by working with you to engage in mindfulness to better understand the intricacies of your internal experience and identify your core values. Then, I help you explore the different parts of yourself with compassion in order to create a sense of an integrated whole. I offer a holistic frame that understands you as an individual and also within the context of your family, your community, and the systems you interact with. I believe in the healing experience of being seen in all of our complexity. I primarily utilize Acceptance and Commitment Therapy in concert with techniques from Internal Family Systems tradition to work with individual adults and couples struggling with anxiety, trauma, depression, and OCD. Together, we will learn about your own unique way of engaging in the world, and practice breaking free from the deeply engrained patterns that inhibit you from achieving your goals.

name: Karen Corona
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: As a psychotherapist with an office in Portland & Beaverton, I help women heal from emotional wounds & trauma to a restore well-being.
ideal_client: Are old emotional patterns and limiting beliefs holding you back from a joyful, free, and abundant life? I specialize in helping women to heal emotional trauma and loss through the expressive arts, guiding you to connect with your Authentic Higher Self. Together, we will address the protective strategies – like people-pleasing, anxiety, perfectionism, low mood states, and overwhelm – that keep you stuck. If you’re seeking transformative healing, I’m here to guide and support you to flourish

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to healing trauma involves beginning to work with the parts of yourself that surfaced to protect the more vulnerable, wounded parts. This often shows up as distressing symptoms and emotions along with 'survival skills'. While these emerged to help you survive, these strategies are often what are keeping you stuck and blocked from creating the life you long for. The strategies are no longer serving you. We work to understand these protective parts and their roles in order to release the aspects that are creating problems for you in your life today. The outcome of this is more harmony in your inner system and space for emotional well-being and a newfound freedom to flourish. In this process I often integrate expressive arts therapy as a way to externalize the feelings and gain increased self-awareness as a catalyst for making these desired changes.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: The combination of my own healing & recovery journey along with my clinical training equips me to effectively work with women to heal childhood trauma and restore emotional well-being. This is my passionate purpose and I'm honored to do this work with clients. In my approach to healing family-of-origin issues, I integrate Internal Family Systems (IFS) and Expressive Arts Therapy (EXA) for a unique and yet evidenced-based treatment for trauma healing. Additionally, the 12 Step program of ACA (Adult Children of Alcoholics & Dysfunctional Families) can be a powerful adjunct to healing trauma (especially the Loving Parent Guidebook which is a resource for Re-Parenting work of the wounded Inner Child). I know suffering up close and recognize that the darkness can block out the light of hope, but claiming a newfound freedom and awakening to a sense of wholeness is possible as you embark on a healing journey.

name: Geraldine Kuphal
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Welcome! Starting therapy is a big step. With my collaborative, strength-based approach, I can help feel safe to start your journey.
ideal_client: I have 15+ years of experience helping adults, teens and families overcome a wode range of issues such as anxiety, OCD, depression, anger, grief/loss, trauma, stress, immigration issues, etc. I specialize in women's issues such as Postpartum Depression and Anxiety Disorders, issues adjusting to being a new mom/parent. I work with adolescents and young adults deal with issue related to becoming, romantic relationships, life transitions, social anxiety, etc.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have a background in family therapy, cognitive-behavioral therapy and a strength based-approach. I have worked with families in various settings such as shelters, crisis lines, preschools, mental health clinics and other outpatient settings. Depending on your personal style and goals, I use a variety of tools such as narrative, solution-focused, mindfulness-based, art therapy, family-based interventions. Therapy can be short-term or long-term depending on your personal style and goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Whether you realize it or not, there are unique aspects of who you are today that work in your favor: your life experience, your skills, your belief system, perhaps even your ethnicity or family history. We will identify these and use them as resources to help you heal. I also believe that therapy is a two-way-street. We will meet each other halfway, each of us actively participating in the process, to reach our shared goal of overcoming your challenges, whatever they may be. A cognitive behavioral approach is one that takes into account how your thoughts affect the way you feel about yourself, other and the world. And how these affect your behavior. Together, we will create a treatment plan that best fits your needs, goals and personal style.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Together, we create a treatment plan that best fits your needs and goals. I use a collaborative, strength approach that include a family-systems, cognitive behavioral framework. I use a wide range of interventions depending on your personal style, age and interests.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: Postpartum Depression and Anxiety Disorders

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: obsesive compulsive disoorders

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: Pregnancy issues, family planning

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: past or present traumatic experiences

specialities.name: Panic
specialities.description: panic attacks and acute anxiety

name: Dr. Wilson, DNP
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Dr. Wilson, DNP is dedicated to building long-lasting relationships with her clients. She believes you are more than a diagnosis or label.
ideal_client: Are you questioning life in general? Having difficulty concentrating? Feeling unmotivated? Moody, stressed, or anxious? Questioning identity? Have you tried everything? Therapy, mindfulness, lifestyle changes, and still struggling? Entering treatment can be an intimidating process & making that first appointment can be one of our biggest hurdles. Relief Mental Health primarily offers medication management. We also offer assessments and some elements of psychotherapy into sessions.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Your treatment will encompass your holistic health to improve your overall well-being and support the path to healing. Medication management services consider your symptoms, treatment goals, and physical health, as well as developmental considerations for children and teens. We know that finding the right medication or combination of medications and dosage can be a challenge. But with over a decade of experience and clinical expertise in complex patients with multiple diagnoses, we can help you discover the most effective and well-tolerated treatment.

name: Megan Sapp
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Appointments available in 1-2 weeks. I'm a Psych Nurse Practitioner who helps you live your best life through medication & therapy services
ideal_client: As a Psych NP, I want to support you through life's challenges. I support nearly every mental health concern, including anxiety, depression, bipolar, sleep, & PTSD. I have special interest in serving clients who are pregnant, postpartum, experiencing loss or fertility issues, or affected by hormonal changes/HRT. I bring a comprehensive understanding of reproductive and physical health to assist you in weighing options for care and creating a plan that is consistent with your goals and values.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I integrate education, transparency, shared decision-making, and humor when meeting with clients. While I offer med management, I believe that meds are only one of the available tools, as behavioral and lifestyle changes are important for sustainable well-being. I offer med management with or without brief therapy but cannot offer stand-alone weekly therapy.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: I am also a certified and practicing Nurse Midwife

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I am a certified Family Nurse Practitioner.

name: Meaghan Frost
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer a safe, non-judgmental space for you to be your true self, with gentle guidance and tailored approaches to help achieve your goals.
ideal_client: My work focuses on empowering individuals to create safe spaces within themselves to process their experiences and overcome obstacles. I specialize in supporting those with histories of trauma, including intimate partner violence and childhood abuse, as well as those dealing with social anxiety, self/other expectations, and the LGBTQIA communities.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker in the states of Washington and Oregon and hold a Master’s degree from Portland State University. I have experience working with a wide range of clinical issues and specialize in anxiety, complex traumas, and navigating stressful life events. I use an eclectic approach, integrating modalities such as EMDR, attachment theory, parts work, and somatic therapy. I believe in the transformative power of human relationships to reveal our best selves, understand our desired changes, and choose paths to healing and growth.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I primarily work with adult women and college students, addressing issues related to trauma, anxiety related to a wide range of topics, and life stress. I also support clients navigating major life transitions and other challenges. Starting therapy can feel daunting, but I'm here to help make the process as smooth as possible. Feel free to reach out with any questions to see if we might be a good fit. I aim to respond promptly to phone calls and emails. Please contact me via email or phone to schedule a free 15-minute consultation. I look forward to meeting you!

name: Stuart Malkin
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Supporting you with compassionate, mindfulness-based therapy, I help you heal, grow and thrive!
ideal_client: Some issues I can help with include developmental trauma, anxiety, co-dependency, career, men's issues, neurodiversity issues (ADHD and Autism), climate grief and anxiety, and creating better communication and more intimacy in your relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am now seeing clients in person! One of the most important factors that predicts successful therapy is the relationship between us. Our working alliance must allow you to trust, feel safe, and feel open. I strive to attune and collaborate with you to help build a safe, authentic connection that will serve your healing and growth. I incorporate somatic and 'bottom-up' based approaches of Hakomi, Lifespan Integration, Recreation of Self (RC-S), attachment work, trauma resourcing. In couple's work, I use a combination of PACT (Psychobiological Approach to Couples Therapy), Gottman, experiential and mindfulness, and compassionate communication/NVC.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I've been in practice since 2015 and have been specializing in mindfulness-based depth work , trauma resourcing, and attachment. Most recently I completed Level 2 of Lifespan Integration, which is helpful in processing childhood wounding. I completed a Masters Degree in Counseling in Clinical Mental Health at Portland State University. In addition, I completed a year-long internship practicing mindfulness-based, somatic therapy approaches with the M.E.T.A Counseling Clinic. Previous to my internship, I had completed the two-year M.E.T.A. Comprehensive Training program. I also assisted in teaching the M.E.T.A Comprehensive year one program in 2015 to deepen my training.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: I incorporate mindfulness-based methods of Hakomi, Recreation of Self (RC-S), attachment work, and trauma resourcing. I have extensive training learning these modalities through my internship experience and training with Mindful Experiential Therapy Approaches (M.E.T.A.).

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Drawing on mindfulness-based, somatic training in Hakomi, Recreation of Self (RC-S), I use the body as a way to access emotions, sensations, imagery, memories that may related to a way a client experiences their body and their therapeutic goals. Lifespan Integration, as the name suggests, helps integrate unprocessed wounded states from past and teaches your mind and body that these events are over.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I incorporate mindfulness-based methods of Hakomi, Recreation of Self (RC-S), attachment work, and trauma resourcing. I have extensive training learning these modalities through on-going practice, supervision, and previous internship experience and training with Mindful Experiential Therapy Approaches (M.E.T.A.).

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: I help clients heal from adverse past emotional, physical, and sexual experiences using lifespan integration, trauma resourcing and mindfulness-based, somatic counseling. Working slowly to create collaboration, safety, and resiliency, past traumatic events are processed in mindfulness, reworking the past experience in safety.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I help men build better relationships, build skills and confidence in fully expressing themselves, and feel more holistically empowered with their masculinity. In the past, I have facilitated a men's process group exploring all of these issues and more.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I help partners identify undesired ways of relating, communicate in healthier and more connecting ways, and make different choices in relating. I use experiential, mindfulness, and attachment based approaches to help couples experience better understanding, empathy, and skills in connecting with each other.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: I work with clients to help them see how they contribute to co-dependent relationships, where they learned it, and support them to help break the cycle.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I provide compassionate, mindfulness-based counseling to process what may be causing depression, help access resources in the self for more resiliency, and help you find more contentment in life.

name: Ryan Grassmann, M.A., LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello, I appreciate the effort that this process takes. You can do this. Don't give up. Things can get better.
ideal_client: My clients occupy a broad demographic space. I treat people on an individual, group, and relationship basis here in my office and via telehealth. I work best with those that desire to build a safe and reliable working relationship. My clients are invited to view me as a helper; a life agent. I treat people that identify anywhere on the gender, racial, and sexual spectrum. I treat people who sense that it's time to take action, who are ready to collaborate with a therapist that they can trust.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: While my therapeutic approach is grounded in the cognitive-behavioral practices, I integrate numerous other useful modalities, like Animal Assisted Psychotherapy, Existential-Humanistic Psychotherapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Emotion Focused Therapy, Gottman Method (relationship therapy), Relational Life Therapy (relationship therapy), and more. My relatable style allows for our work to progress along a seamless path that's curated for each individual. No two clients are the same, and no two courses of therapy are the same. The process evolves along with us.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Like many in the helping professions, my motivation to pursue this work arose from my lived experience. Like so many of us, I've endured pain and suffering. As a result, I noticed an innate response to help; people, animals, even the environment. I use my entire life experience in harmony with my education and training. I don't know of any other way that would be more congruent with my core personal and professional values. A bit about my journey into the art and science of my training- I earned a Master’s Degree in Counseling Psychology from Pacific University School of Professional Psychology where I learned the ethical practice of evidence-based integrative healthcare. I also completed a concentration in organizational behavior or "work psychology." I earned a Bachelor’s of Science in Psychology from Portland State University with a strong focus on neuroscience, cognition, and philosophy of medicine. Earlier, in my pursuit of justice, I earned a Paralegal Science degree from PCC.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Professionally, I find that the Gottman Method, Relational Life Therapy, and Emotion-Focused Couples Therapy all have proven to be effective in defining, treating, and resolving relationship conflicts. With helpful companion books and weekly therapy sessions, change can occur quickly. Those in relationships often find that loving support and trust lie just underneath the fear and hurt. I teach people how to repair ruptures, identify and transform shame, and confront concerns with skill.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy assists the client in helping to change unhelpful thoughts into thoughts that are more beneficial, and often more accurate! CBT addresses those troublesome core beliefs about yourself, others, and the world around you. Often clients find that re-framing these thoughts by challenging them results in more rational thinking and doing.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: In conjunction with the numerous forms to cognitive-behavioral therapies I use in session, I also take much pleasure in introducing clients to the benefits of doing our work as two humans. I'm a person; you're a person. This cannot be avoided, nor should it. My job is to hold the space for your experience, your thoughts and emotions. I take this role seriously but I never abandon the fact that we are two people sharing time and space with each other. This is the human condition.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: As men, we're being asked to change, and we are. With effort and focused commitment, we can achieve a much more enriched way of life; a life that's free of emotional restriction. This work is best done individually with a therapist AND in a supportive group of other men. I facilitate a quarterly 10 week men's support group called Modern Man. 6-7 men work together for 10 weeks. We process and resolve issues involved contemporary masculine life. Please see my website for more information.

specialities.name: Bipolar
specialities.description: I have a particular interest Bipolar disorders due much in part to it's presence in so many people I have known in my personal life. This intrinsic motivation has drawn me to study and train in the most up to date treatments available. Due to my graduate level training's foundation in multidisciplinary studies, I am particularly skilled in working in conjunction with mental health prescribers. Achieving a state of remission is possible with courage and commitment.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I believe loss and grief is the great leveler. Nobody, regardless of their privilege, can escape the inevitability of loss. As a culture, we suffer from a lack of pathways to effective and meaningful grieving. I help people learn to identify the opportunities for meaning-making that follow loss. If you're experiencing acute loss, I recommend reading the work of David Kessler, particularly, "Making Meaning," released in late 2019. Professional support can help tremendously too.

name: Veronica Melo
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Veronica is a bilingual bicultural associate clinical social worker with multiple years of experience working with adolescents and families
ideal_client: Accepting Spanish Speaking Clients. Veronica is a bilingual bicultural associate clinical social worker with multiple years of experience working with adolescents and families in residential and school settings. Veronica’s methods often include client-centered, strengths-based, and trauma informed care as well as motivational interviewing. Veronica has experience supporting clients through depression, anxiety, trauma, and immigrant related stressors.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Veronica specializes in work with tweens and teens and is able to clearly support families in need. She is knowledgeable in the barriers the Latinx population face and is allied with LGBTQIA+ communities and other intersectionality. Please contact her today to get started! It is hard to reach out for help but the benefits can be very rewarding.

name: Mary Hanel
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I help adolescents and their parents navigate this challenging time in development. I help young people launching for the first time.
ideal_client: I truly appreciate the amazing brilliance of adolescents and young adults. Their energy, passion and introspection is a gift that I value. I am grateful when families/parents allow me to partner with them as they navigate times that may be filled with trepidation and grief. I feel privileged to be allowed to help adults navigate challenging times as we search for the self compassion that we should all have for ourselves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: After over 30 years working with a wide variety of adolescents, families and adults; I have wisdom to share. I will partner with clients to reach their mental health and social connection goals. We will look at the challenges through a Poly Vagal lens and move forward to Safety and Connection.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I am a woman, a mother and a Social Worker; I believe in the goodness of all people and acknowledge that fear keeps many from establishing and keeping safe and healthy connections with others. I am an Oregonian, daughter of a Forest Service Worker, wife of a carpenter and was a Portland Public Schools employee for over 20 years. I became a therapist/Social Worker because people are amazing and I want to help folks realize their own gifts and how they can use these strengths to improve their lives and the lives of others. I want to help diminish the hopelessness that often leads to behaviors that can be hurtful.

name: Skylar Windham
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi! I'm Skylar. If we were to have sessions together and the therapy were working, how would you know? What would be different in your life?
ideal_client: My ideal client is anyone that is ready to feel better. I don't have a magic wand, nor can I read minds, but with time, perspective and teamwork we can tackle anything together, including but not limited to: anxiety, trauma, depression, life changes, stress, grief, identity, sexuality, substance misuse and more.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am not one who finds utility in elaborate hypotheses filled with flowery psychobabble. I work primarily within frameworks of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, as well as Existential Therapy, and I consider psychodynamics to be a crucial component of the therapeutic process.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I'm Skylar first, therapist second. This means that while I take professionalism and the American Counseling Association's Code of Ethics very seriously, I bring my authentic self to each session. The relationships I form with clients are real, and necessarily so, because it is through genuine human connection that clients find their way. I am LGBTQ+ affirming and welcome clients from all walks of life, experiences and identities. I grew up on the southern Oregon coast and I am a member of an indigenous community, the Tolowa Dee-Ni Nation. I have taught in Oregon public schools, traveled throughout various countries as an ESL teacher, worked in port administration as well as local politics. I enjoy spending time in nature, dancing Argentine tango, sailing and frolicking with my corgi Scuttle.

name: Sofia Jasani
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome! I'm glad you're here. I provide affirming, empowering care to children and adults in Oregon.
ideal_client: We might be a good fit if you are Asian, Black, Indigenous, Latinx, first generation, queer, or gender expansive. I help people find relief from the pain and stress of grief, anxiety, depression, parenting, intergenerational trauma, chronic illness, and systemic oppression. If you are the parent of a child ages 3-10 adjusting to loss and change in the family, struggling in school, experiencing anxiety, depression, chronic illness, disability, and racial stress-- I'm here for you.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I believe each client has the capacity for healing and self-actualization. I bring genuine empathy, acceptance, curiosity, and hope into my relationship with clients so they may feel understood, valued, and empowered to move towards growth at every point in the lifespan. I celebrate my clients’ unique culture, wisdom, strengths, and identities. I collaborate with clients to explore how systems of power and oppression impact their well-being. I support clients in making meaning in their lives and relationships. I provide individual counseling, play therapy, and child-parent relationship therapy. I also provide group therapy for women of color. My approach is informed by Existential-Humanism, feminism, and multiculturalism. I hold a master’s degree in Clinical Rehabilitation Counseling from Portland State University with a focus in chronic illness and disability.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a passionate advocate and community leader. I currently hold a Governor-appointed, Senate-confirmed position on the Oregon Board of Psychology. I am the Past President of the Oregon Association for Multicultural Counseling and Development, served as the Secretary of the Oregon Counseling Association, and served on the American Counseling Association Anti-Racism Taskforce in 2020. I am the proud daughter of Muslim immigrants and am a first-generation college student. I have been teaching in PSU's Counselor Education Department since 2020. I am currently offering both in-person therapy and secure telehealth video sessions for clients in Oregon during the COVID-19 pandemic. Schedule a free 20-minute video consultation so we can get to know one another and find out if we are a good fit! I am currently accepting new private pay clients and do not accept insurance at this time. I have a waitlist for sliding-scale clients.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Play is the language of childhood. Young children respond to stress and change differently than adults do, and they communicate differently, too. As a play therapist, I provide a safe environment where children can express their emotions, learn coping skills, develop self-control, and build self-esteem in a way that comes naturally to them. I love working with children, and would be honored to help support your family!

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: Wellness naturally arises when we experience empathy, acceptance, curiosity, and hope in relationships. I aim to bring these qualities to our therapeutic relationship, and support you in creating this kind of relationship with the important people in your life. I believe each client has the capacity for healing and self-actualization. I bring my full authentic self into my relationship with clients so they may feel understood, valued, and empowered to move towards growth.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: In the playroom, children can express their emotions, develop coping skills, improve social skills, strengthen their family relationships, and improve behavior in a way that comes naturally to them. I provide in-person play therapy for children ages 3-10 adjusting to loss and change in the family, struggling in school, experiencing anxiety, depression, chronic illness, disability, and racial stress.

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: If you are Black, Indigenous, a person of color, queer, trans, gender expansive, or live with a disability, you may be tired of being strong. You may notice certain spaces and people where you don’t feel comfortable being your full self. ​In therapy you can feel understood, valued, and empowered to heal and grow. In therapy you can explore and celebrate your culture, your wisdom, your strengths, and your identities.

name: Katherine Noonan
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I am passionate about helping you achieve your health and wellness goals.
ideal_client: I specialize in helping people with anxiety, depression, adjustment to life transitions, adjustment to disability, insomnia, and other sleep disorders. I use a mindfulness-based approach as well as CBT approaches, and I have advanced training in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBT-I), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Chronic Pain (CBT-CP), Hypnosis, and Mindfulness.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Growth and empowerment occur when we feel seen and heard, and this is what I strive to foster in my work as a psychologist. I use an evidence based, integrative approach, and my goal is to identify your unique needs and aspirations. You’ll find I am warm , empathetic, kind and accepting, and that in our work together, I create a space where you can feel comfortable and free to share all parts of yourself.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: When I am not at Aspire Psychology, you’ll find me on a bleacher at a high school ball game or walking the golf course. I enjoy reading, traveling and most importantly, spending as much time as I can with family and friends.

specialities.name: Insomnia
specialities.description: I provide CBT-i

name: Alexandria Moore
title: Marriage and Family Therapist
intro: Welcome. My name is Alexandria (she/her). I help people repair relationships, connect back to the body, and nurture a love of self.
ideal_client: We will work to understand how your family of origin and cultural influences shape you, freeing you to choose how you show up in the world. My couples work takes this a step further; you and your partner or partners will learn to see the architecture of your own emotional influences and needs. With time and compassion, we will work to open stuck doors. The goal is for you and your partner(s) to turn towards one another instead of away when things get hard.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is intuitive, grounded, and warm. I will guide you through ways to physically calm your system, to be attuned to what signals the body is sending, and ultimately feel more connected to your self. If this work sounds right, let’s begin. It’s a long road, and there’s no knowing where we’ll be swept off to!

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: My approach is intuitive, grounded, and warm, inviting moments that challenge assumptions with true care and respect. I allow the spoken and unspoken cues in the room to guide the process. From years of teaching yoga, I have a deep regard for the connection between mind and body. I will often ask you to consider, can you be curious and nonjudgmental towards your body to create a healing mindset? This will support our larger work, as we practice awareness that every thought and emotion has a physical, embodied component.

name: Alex Lazar
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Level 2 Gottman trained couples and individual therapist.
ideal_client: My clients often come to therapy looking for a way to experience this thing we call life differently. I work with teens, couples, parents and adults. I also work with folks struggling with active addiction and/or in recovery. I am level 2 Gottman trained for couples therapy.

approaches.How I Can Help You: What you and I identify as your goals for therapy will guide me in how I approach therapy with you. I am a person centered therapist at heart who also uses motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral therapy, narrative therapy, and existential therapy. Learning what works for you and what doesn't is very important to me in your treatment. If you have tried previous therapies you did not find helpful, I am not going to force that back onto you. Healing does not look the same for everyone. Some folks want to be able to get out of bed in the morning and make it to work on time without forgetting their lunch. Other folks want to be able to go to a grocery store without having a panic attack. And some people just want to live to see tomorrow. How you heal and what that process it looks like will not look the same for everyone.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Couples Therapy: I help couples strengthen their connection using the evidence-based Gottman Method, with a focus on improving communication, deepening emotional intimacy, and fostering greater hope, acceptance, and appreciation for one another. I believe couples come to therapy because they long for something to shift—and that meaningful change is absolutely possible. My approach is collaborative, warm, supportive and direct, creating a grounded space where both partners can feel valued and understood. I provide gentle yet direct challenges when appropriate and aligned with your established goals. I offer structure, focus, and direction throughout the couples therapy experience, helping you stay grounded and purposeful in your growth together. I aim to help you build and strengthen your relationship awareness—like a muscle that grows with intention, reflection, and practice. I believe in the power of relationships to heal, grow, and transform. It would be a privilege to support you.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I help couples strengthen their connection using the evidence-based Gottman Method, with a focus on improving communication, deepening emotional intimacy, and fostering greater hope, acceptance, and appreciation for one another. I believe couples come to therapy because they long for something to shift—and that meaningful change is absolutely possible. I am level 2 Gottman trained.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Using a client-centered approach, I treat depression by fostering a supportive, empathetic space. I integrate CBT to challenge negative thoughts, narrative therapy to help clients reshape their personal stories, and existential therapy to explore meaning and values. This holistic blend empowers clients to find resilience, purpose, and lasting change.

name: Colin Wolf
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Experienced therapist with heart-based wisdom plus a foundation of 15 years of evolving therapeutic knowledge and skills.
ideal_client: You long for more ease, clarity, and feeling understood and supported. Instead you often feel overwhelmed, confused, misunderstood and/or alone, despite your best efforts. You're hard on yourself and frustrated with a chaotic world. I specialize in outcasts, nerds and bleeding hearts, including LGBTQ+, poly/ENM, kink and/or neurodivergence, so you'll find no judgement here. Let’s create space to acknowledge and deal with your pain, discover and expand your strengths, and build a path forward.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My Master's degree in Integral Counseling Psychology is enhanced by training in Brainspotting, Narrative Exposure Therapy, Pain Reprocessing Therapy and polyvagal approaches. My clinical approach is trauma-informed and integrates psychodynamic, existential-humanistic, CBT/ACT and mindfulness-based perspectives and strategies that are customized to your preferences and needs. My therapeutic style is fundamentally relational. I'm your confidante and ally. We'll explore your thoughts and emotions, and how you relate with yourself and others, to increase your awareness of the patterns and stories of your life and transform limitations into resources. Discover new perspectives, life strategies and ways to move through anxiety, depression or numbness to feel more connected and grounded, with increased ability to flexibly respond to life stressors. I'll help you know (and love!) yourself more, experience deeper connections in your relationships, and feel more ease and joy.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: My training in Integral Counseling Psychology at the California Institute of Integral Studies blended Eastern and Western perspectives on human psychology and development. I incorporate mindfulness as the gateway to authentic presence and connection to the body, mind and heart.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: My approach is deeply humanistic, with a focus on increasing access to your intuition and heart through a collaborative, curious and compassionate therapeutic relationship.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Over 15 years of experience working with LGBTQ+ clients on a variety of issues and concerns, including developing authentic identity, strength through vulnerability, life beyond trauma and resilient, loving relationships, as well as queer family planning.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: Over 15 years of experience working with trans and non-binary clients, supporting authentic identity exploration, transition related care (for those pursuing transition), and overall support beyond identity.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Over 15 years of experience working with clients in polyamorous and open relationships, supporting individuals and relationship partners in developing more intimacy through expanding curiosity, improving communication and collaboration skills, reducing reactivity and increasing authentic connection.

name: Jenna LeJeune
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: Licensed psychologist with 25+ years experience. I use evidence-based approaches to help people get unstuck & move toward what matters most.
ideal_client: I work with adults who feel stuck in patterns that no longer serve them. Whether you're finding it hard to move forward, find meaningful, authentic connection, or live aligned with your values, my approach can help. I'm particularly skilled at helping those struggling with self-criticism and shame, body image concerns, or intimacy and sexuality. My evidence-based, time-limited approach is designed to help you identify unworkable patterns and develop concrete tools for lasting change.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My work is guided by what science has shown to be most effective. I specialize in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and incorporate elements of Emotion Focused Therapy (EFT), evidence-based approaches that help people navigate life's challenges with greater flexibility. Therapy is a significant investment. To help you make the most of your investment, I work in a focused, time-limited model of up to 12 sessions centered on a particular struggle or theme. This approach allows us to dive deeply into making important changes in your life with clear direction and purpose. We can work together to identify unworkable patterns and develop concrete tools for lasting change. I also have extensive specialized training in psychedelic assisted therapy. I provide harm reduction and integration services for those exploring psychedelic journeys. I'm also a research therapist at Portland Psychotherapy, where I work on clinical trials investigating the therapeutic uses of MDMA and psychedelics.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: A fundamental belief in my practice: You are not broken. You are stuck. We all struggle, at times deeply struggle. And it's often during those times when it's most difficult to stay connected with what matters most. But often, it's finding a way to stay connected with our values and what truly matters, that enables us to navigate life's inevitable challenges with greater flexibility and purpose. As for what is most important to me and how I choose to be in this world, I seek to walk through this world open-heartedly. I bring this value of open-heartedness into every area of my life, including my work where I have deep care for the clients I serve. I also find value in the simplicity I find with being in nature, including going on long walks with my dog. I find that adding a bit of whimsy to everyday moments brings me joy. Finally, I love being curious and exploring other cultures and perspectives, especially through food and travel.

name: Danielle Meyer
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: IFS and Jungian therapy for mood, women's concerns, and trauma
ideal_client: My clients are searching for authenticity, their inner truth, and a feeling of direction and purpose in life. They are soul-searchers who have experienced a dark night of soul, and are looking to restore their inner light. My clients are interested in self awareness and connecting to their inner wisdom. My clients are also looking for a relational and dynamic therapist that offers tools for coping, skills to practice, as well as a depth of insight into their symptoms.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I specialize in the treatment of women's issues, mood disorders, trauma, grief and loss, eating disorder recovery, and life transitions. Many of my clients are neurodiverse and empathic. I aim to help individuals manage difficult emotions and recover a lost sense of self and meaning. We do this through the Jungian lens of approaching and integrating the unconscious through dreams, symbols, the imagination, and archetypes. By using internal family systems I help clients form new attitudes towards their inner parts, and cultivate a center of self. A lot of this work is based around self-compassion and attachment theory. By using re-parenting tools with ourselves and our parts, we can feel more whole and less conflicted by difficult emotions in the body. I also work with trauma and stress and find art therapy, internal family systems, and a mixture of dreamwork or imaginative work can be helpful for creating meaning and resilience.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a Jungian psychotherapist I believe that there is a collective unconscious that we are all connected to. I believe in a holistic appraoch to understanding symptoms as messengers from the unconscious that offer helpful information. I believe all of our inner parts possess an innate wisdom that is unique to each person and that by connecting to and healing these split off parts, one can connect to a deep sense of personal meaning. This meaning can also be found through art-making, dreamwork, imaginative/visualization exercises, and journaling prompts. I also believe that archetypal astrology can be a helpful tool in psychotherapy, which can help connect daily life experiences to deeper underlying patterns that inform our lives.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I was trained in IFS in 2012 and have used it since. I love working with inner parts and a big part of my approach is cultivating inner wisdom and connection to self. Parts include managers, firefighters, and exiles. The self is framed as the center of personality that is compassionate and curious that encompasses all the parts, but is also something greater that is partly unknown and to be discovered.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: I provide art therapy via telehealth and like to make art in session or provide clients with prompts to explore creatively in and outside of session. I encourage clients to keep a journal of some kind for writing, art, dreams, or notes in session.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: I am a Jungian oriented psychotherapist and integrate dreamwork, active imagination, and archetypal ways of knowing into our session. I am a certified archetypal astrologer. I offer astrological counseling as a way to access the archetypal map of an individual's life.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: Constructing meaning is important as we weave the narrative of our lives. I believe it is helpful to consider what the universe, self, God, soul, the unconscious, etc. is putting in front of us. At times we observe what is occurring outside of us as having a larger meaning for our lives. It is helpful to observe things symbolically to help tap into the what the unconscious is bringing forth to be integrated.

name: Brandy Halprin
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I have 20+ years experience helping clients adjust to life's changes and thrive in difficult circumstances.
ideal_client: My clients are ready to learn new skills to manage what life has put in their path. Have you lost someone? Had a change in your health, career, or relationships? Feeling down, anxious, or disconnected from yourself or others? I can support you on a journey of healing that focuses on your strengths, your goals for a life-well-lived, and accepting reality as a path to change toward the person you want to be.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My background includes work with children, older adults, those with life-limiting illness, and people struggling with grief, loss, and adjustment to life transitions. My approach is collaborative, conversational, and warm. I incorporate mindfulness and parts work to help you learn to manage every day struggles. I will continually work with you to set and re-evaluate your therapy goals, then tailor your sessions to work toward those goals.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe that the central task of therapy is finding the balance between acceptance and change - acceptance of what is and change to enable what can be. I believe that, like plants which put on new leaves every year of their existence, we all have the capacity to grow at every stage of our lives.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a common symptom - most people will struggle with some level of anxiety at some point in their lives. I can teach you useful coping skills to help manage your anxiety in the short-term, as well as guide you through deeper work to heal the source of your anxious feelings.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: We all experience grief and loss - whether it is the loss of a pet, a friendship, a job, or an opportunity. At some point in our lives, we will experience a major loss - that of a close loved one, a serious change to our own health or ability, or the ultimate loss that comes with our own mortality. I can help you face this loss with tools to manage the deep grief and exploration toward integrating the loss into your newly meaningful life.

name: Miki Darby
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I offer individual counseling and social communication skills training + performance enhancement support for youths 12+ and adults.
ideal_client: Do you feel overwhelmed by racing thoughts, restless energy, or social anxiety? Living with ADHD, Autism Spectrum, anxiety, or social challenges can be exhausting and isolating. You don’t have to struggle alone. My practice focuses on providing counseling support for people experiencing depression, anxiety, social skills, and/or cultural adjustments. In therapy, we will collaborate to focus on symptom relief and skill-building for long-term growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from a neurodiversity-affirming, trauma-aware framework. That means I don’t pathologize what are often natural human responses to overwhelming environments. Instead, I aim to understand the context - social, cultural, sensory, historical - that shapes your inner and outer world. This might involve exploring how masking, burnout, or chronic invalidation have impacted your sense of self. It might mean unpacking the quiet grief of not having been supported earlier in life, or the relief (and uncertainty) that can come with newly and/or late-diagnosed autism or ADHD. It often involves helping people feel less alone with their experiences. You may have felt that your sensitivity, intensity, or way of processing the world is “too much.” I see those qualities as deeply human—and often deeply valuable. Therapy with me is a space where those parts of you are welcome.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe everyone deserves to be understood on their own terms, not just through a clinical lens. I’m committed to maintaining spaces where people can be and accept their true selves, and exist without needing to justify their way of being. I value authenticity, quiet resilience, and the deep intelligence that comes from lived experience. Culturally sensitive care matters deeply to me. That means respecting how identity, history, and context shape our stories and how trust is earned, not assumed. I work to acknowledge power, hold nuance, and meet each person with humility. I love exploring identity, creativity, and the things we were told were “too much” but are often our greatest strengths. Outside of work, I’m drawn to music, visual storytelling, and finding beauty in small, ordinary things.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I use a psychodynamic approach to explore how past experiences, unconscious patterns, and inner conflicts influence present behavior. I believe that understanding the deeper roots of emotional struggles can lead to lasting change. My work is collaborative, focusing on building insight, fostering self-awareness, and strengthening emotional resilience.
