I believe this approach helps clients understand themselves better and create healthier ways of relating to others and the world.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I take an eclectic approach to therapy, tailoring techniques to fit each individual's needs. Drawing from a variety of therapeutic modalities - such as cognitive behavioral therapy, psychodynamic, and humanistic practices - I create a flexible, personalized treatment plan. This allows me to work with you in the way that resonates most, whether that’s through exploring past experiences, building new coping skills, or enhancing self-awareness and personal growth.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: I believe in treating the whole person - mind, body, and spirit. My holistic approach integrates emotional, physical, and environmental factors to help you achieve balance and wellbeing. I draw from diverse techniques like mindfulness, somatic awareness, and stress-reduction practices, focusing on the interconnectedness of your thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. My goal is to support you in nurturing your overall health and fostering sustainable, meaningful change.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I support youth and adults living with depression, whether it feels like exhaustion, numbness, irritability, or quiet disconnection. I offer a space where there’s no need to perform or explain away your pain. My approach is gentle, relational, and grounded in honoring what your mind and body have been carrying. Together, we work toward relief, reconnection, and a life that feels more possible.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I help youth and adults navigate anxiety with compassion and curiosity, not pressure. Whether it shows up as overthinking, people-pleasing, shutdowns, or physical overwhelm, I offer support that’s paced, nonjudgmental, and tailored to how you experience it. I focus on nervous system awareness, practical tools, and the deeper work of understanding what your anxiety has been trying to protect.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I support ADHDers in navigating overwhelm, burnout, and systems that weren’t designed for how their brains work. My approach is strengths-based and shame-free, recognizing the emotional toll of masking, RSD, and chronic self-doubt. I integrate practical support with validation and work with both diagnosed and self-identified clients.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I work with autistic youth and adults—especially those who are late-identified, self-diagnosed, or exploring their identity. My approach is neurodiversity-affirming and trauma-aware, honoring sensory needs, communication differences, and the impact of being misunderstood. I support self-discovery, self-trust, and creating lives that feel safe, authentic, and sustainable.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I support youth and adults in their journey of personal growth, helping them build confidence, resilience, and authentic self-expression. With specialized training in the UCLA PEERS program, I work with individuals to develop strong social skills, improve relationships, and navigate challenging transitions. My approach is grounded in self-compassion, practical tools, and empowering clients to align with their true values and potential.

name: Monika Sammon
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I am currently accepting new clients both in person and via telehealth.
ideal_client: I work with individuals—including adults, adolescents, and children ages 5 and up—as well as couples and families. Together, we will explore your experiences, uncover patterns, and cultivate healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that healing begins in a safe and supportive environment where you feel seen, heard, and valued. My approach to therapy is collaborative, client-centered, and grounded in a systemic lens, honoring your unique story and strengths. I integrate Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) with an attachment theory focus, Internal Family Systems (IFS), Narrative Therapy, and Child-Centered Play Therapy to best fit your therapeutic goals.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My experience as a therapist has been shaped by my work in community-based mental health, where I have supported individuals, children, adolescents, couples, and families through a variety of challenges. Working with diverse populations, including marginalized communities and those affected by trauma, has deepened my appreciation for the unique stories each client brings into therapy and reinforced my commitment to providing trauma-informed, culturally responsive care through a systemic lens. I believe in meeting clients where they are at without judgment, offering a compassionate and collaborative space for healing, self-discovery, and growth. My approach is grounded in empathy, respect, and an understanding of the complex systems that impact mental health, with a dedication to supporting clients in building meaningful relationships, embracing their strengths, and achieving their personal and therapeutic goals.

name: Erin Webb
title: Licensed Art Therapist
intro: Specializing in therapy for youth and families, women who experienced childhood trauma, and highly sensitive people.
ideal_client: Is your teen experiencing increased stress, anxiety or depression during these challenging times? Or have they been struggling for a while? Youth often lack the skills, not the will, to meet the demands of daily life. Together we will identify underlying causes and strategies to support your teen and family. We will build on what you're already doing well. Imagine your teen feeling better and gaining confidence and independence. All changes start with a vision and the time is now!

approaches.How I Can Help You: I provide individual and family therapy for youth (age 12 and up). I offer a free video consultation, so we can discuss how I can help. During sessions your teen will learn and practice calming skills and mindful self-compassion to increase feelings of connection, happiness and relaxation. We will also work on effective communication, exploring values and finding meaning in life to improve motivation. I love supporting and guiding youth as they learn to manage emotions and stress better and become more comfortable being themselves. I will listen closely to your teen and offer support, validation and humor. I will also encourage them to consider other perspectives, take responsibility, set goals and envision their future. Please visit my website for more information about my private practice. After-school and evening appointments are available.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I also specialize in individual therapy for highly sensitive people and women who have experienced childhood loss, abandonment and trauma. I have found that combining the following approaches supports healing and change on a much deeper level: Polyvagal Theory, Internal Family Systems, Art Therapy, EFT tapping, Mindfulness and Emotion Code. However, services are individualized to fit your needs.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: The Collaborative Problem Solving approach, that I use when working with families, is an evidence-based method for decreasing stressful family interactions by teaching youth the skills needed to meet expectations. Engaging your teen in Collaborative Problem Solving discussions will help them open up, consider the perspective of others and increase their problem solving and thinking skills.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: Making art reduces stress and helps many teens engage more in therapy. Art therapy helps youth process difficult experiences and communicate feelings, thoughts and memories that are hard to express in words. Art therapy is also used during family therapy to support positive interactions and the sharing and revising of family stories. Artistic talent is not necessary and stick figures are welcome!

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Is your teen experiencing anxiety due to increased stress, isolation, unknowns and changes? Therapy helps youth express and externalize their fears and worries and learn calming skills. Learning how to lower stress and manage anxiety leads to increased confidence and connection with others.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Many teens and young adults are feeling more depressed during these challenging times. They are facing a future of unknowns and spending more time on screens than ever. Therapy helps youth maintain healthy, productive and safe behaviors. I have found that both talk therapy and Art Therapy help youth express and externalize difficult feelings and thoughts that are contributing to depression.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I have more than 20 years experience providing treatment services to youth diagnosed with ADHD. I also taught art to students with ADHD and learning differences at a small private middle school for 5 years. It's common for youth with ADHD to struggle with managing school, emotional regulation, anxiety, depression and underlying feelings of shame. Therapy helps youth strengthen lagging skills and increase self-compassion and confidence.

specialities.name: Adoption Issues
specialities.description: I have a passion for helping adopted and foster youth with healing, setting healthy boundaries, developing healthy coping skills and accessing self-compassion. For many years, I have supported families through crises and with understanding and addressing the effects of developmental trauma.

name: Maxfield Koontz
title: Student Counselor
intro: Through existential and experiential approaches I support client's own innate process of growth, healing, and transformation.
ideal_client: We all grapple with the extraordinary difficulties of ordinary life. I believe life’s struggles, however difficult they may be, are sustenance for personal and collective growth, healing, and transformation. I view our time together in therapy as an opportunity to walk alongside you on your journey, however that may look. Whatever brings you in for therapy, I am honored to meet you there.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is rooted in experiential modalities that bring awareness to all aspects of the human experience from a non-judgemental, compassionate, and curious place. I believe that when we allow ourselves to sit with our present felt experience, to be with discomfort and pain, possibilities of change come into reach. It is also through vulnerable connection with others that we heal both individually and relationally. Often, our inability to be with ourselves is what inhibits us from the relationships we crave. Connection to others is what makes life’s pain bearable, and is a means to find joy in times of hardship. I view our time together as a collaborative space to explore the complexities of your human journey. I work with individuals, those in relationships, and families.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a cisgender gay man I have lived experience in the queer community and am committed to practicing from an intersectional, anti-oppressive, trauma-informed lens. I strive to hold an inclusive and affirming space that honors the experiences of all marginalized identities. Whatever your background may be, I invite you to bring your authentic self into the room.

name: G. Ravyn (Ravyn) Stanfield
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
credentials: M.A.in Counseling, EMDR trained, Licensed Acupuncturist
intro: When life or relationships seem overwhelming or impossible, I help people make necessary changes and find solid ground again.
ideal_client: I combine supportive cheerleading with truthful reflection to help people transform their lives. I help folks dealing with anxiety, depression/suicidal ideation, complicated grief, trauma, chronic pain, and systemic oppression. I serve adults, teenagers, couples, families, and folks in biological or chosen family and other kinds of relationship dynamics. I love helping couples who have communication challenges.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I believe we need empathy, acceptance, support, and accountability in order to heal our old pain and create positive changes. I know a lot of tricks and tools that can help change stories, habits, perspectives, patterns, relationships, and eventually, lives. Often, we come to therapy to change a behavior that was originally developed as a survival strategy. As we learn and grow, we evolve past our own strategic defenses. Too bad our habits and patterns don’t always get the memo! We can learn to shift stubborn patterns of protection, in order to find joy and connection. Sometimes, we make change one breath at a time. Other times, there are body based exercises we can use to release stress and tension. And still other times, we need to challenge systems and narratives that don’t support our values. Clients generally experience improvement in the first month, and find growth in goal areas throughout the course of therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that all people are worthy of dignity and respect, no matter what their circumstances. In the past, I have worked as a social worker, an advocate for accessibility, an environmental activist, a theatre artist, and a writer. I currently work as a therapist, an acupuncturist and a Trauma Informed Care trainer. I play multiple hand drums, including djembe, tar, doumbek, and am learning to play the Irish bodhran. Much of my stress relief comes from hanging out with the natural world, including playing with my dogs, and hikes in the PNW. I'm a world traveler, and have been to Nepal, Israel, Palestine, Bali, Germany, Iceland, Scotland, Greece, Australia, and Italy, to name a few. I have family in Eastern Europe and plan to travel to Poland and Russia at some point.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: When memories or experiences from the past continue to negatively influence the present, EMDR can often help. I use a trauma-informed and attachment based EMDR to help heal old wounds and decrease emotional triggers.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I work with people in all kinds of relationships who want to communicate better, solve problems, rekindle their spark, fight smarter, or move past obstacles.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: When we don’t understand our own behavior and feel frustrated that we can’t immediately change, IFS is often helpful. By understanding the parts of ourselves that try to manage and protect us, we can often find more ease, self-empathy, and motivation to change our lives.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: After over 20 years as an acupuncturist, I’m convinced that many of our emotional challenges like anger, anxiety, depression, and grief live in the body. Somatic therapy can help uncover and shift uncomfortable feelings and chronic issues that we haven’t been able to talk our way out of.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: It is possible to rewrite old tired stories that we and others keep telling about ourselves. When we shift the narrative, we often get a whole new perspective on problems that have plagued us.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I work with all kinds of relationships and relationship styles/configurations including monogamous couples, blended families, chosen family, and folks practicing ethical non-monogamy.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I support folks through chronic pain challenges including exhaustion, hopelessness, frustration with the medical system, changes in function, and ways to cope.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am a trauma specialist, and have worked with trauma for over 20 years, including survivors of assault, combat veterans, survivors of disaster, family trauma, adult children of addicts, oppression trauma, and complicated or sudden loss and grief.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Whether expected or sudden, loss and grief can turn our lives upside down. I help people navigate grief, even when it’s complicated, and find meaning and solid ground.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: It can be even more isolating to work through challenges when people don’t understand or accept your relationship style. I work with relationships in all kinds of configurations. LGBTQIA+ and all gender identities are welcome. I believe people can practice ethical non-monogamy and polyamory with honesty, integrity, and satisfaction. I also work with folks who have differences in attachment styles.

name: Susan Gulka
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help women and couples, along with adults with ADHD, who are motivated to pursue growth and change in order to have the life they desire.
ideal_client: If you are someone who wants to learn and grow, understand more about yourself and your partner, including exploring how your past affects who you are, I would love to help. I believe change and growth is possible for every individual, and sometimes having the courage to ask for help is what can bring us the most positive momentum moving forward. Learning skills, gaining insight, and having support are just some of the things that counseling can help you with.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a Marriage and Family counselor, I provide professional mental health services to individuals and couples. I approach counseling as a joint endeavor in which you, as the client, and I work together to understand your goals, uncover and approach difficulties, and move towards your healthy functioning and personal fulfillment. I believe that inside each of us is a unique human being that has the resources for positive growth. Often our families of origin have influenced us in numerous ways the have created various ways of coping, some healthy and some not so healthy. Therefore, it is my goal with each client, couple, or family to tap into those inner resources of each individual and discover their unique feelings and perspective in order to create healthier and more effective ways of living, loving, and communicating in their lives. I use emotionally focused approaches including developmental models, along with Internal Family Systems approaches to therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a Masters of Arts in Marriage, Couple, and Family Counseling from George Fox University. I am a member of the Oregon Counseling Association. I have worked as a Life Coach, and have a background in accounting and finance. Please check out my website to learn more about me and my approach.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Sorting out who you are, life transitions, support and listening, motherhood, identity in relationships

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Identity, compassion, strengths, finding SELF, being heard, discovering values, (re)discovering who you are, women, understanding past trauma

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Gottman method, communication patterns, conflict resolution, restoring closeness and partnership, adapting to children, intimacy

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Get help in managing your own ADHD and/or understanding how to best help your partner or family member with ADHD.

name: Hannah Brassell
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I knew my calling was to become a psychologist since middle school.Today I am grateful to know I was able to make my dream a reality.
ideal_client: As a former all-state ski racer and competitive soccer player, I understand the unique challenges that can come with transitioning out of sport as well as the identity shifts that can follow. This experience feeds my passion for supporting individuals navigating performance anxiety as well as complexities of life transitions, especially individuals stepping away from competitive sports.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist, I take a holistic and individualized approach to understanding each person's unique challenges, drawing on evidence-based modalities like CBT, ACT, and solution-focused therapy. I also value the mind-body connection and incorporate this exploration into our work when it aligns with an individual’s needs and goals. I believe that a strong, collaborative, therapeutic relationship is essential for meaningful change. My approach centers on creating a safe, supportive space where you feel heard, understood, and empowered, with your goals guiding our work together. My aim is to help you build resilience and foster personal growth, and I am here every step of the way!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Outside of my work at Aspire, I love spending time cooking, gardening, paddleboarding, reading crime novels, and exploring the outdoors with my husband and our two dogs Virgil and Sophie.

name: Lisa Sloan Strom
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm your ally on the road to wellbeing. I'm committed to deepening your long term recovery, and supporting your transformation.
ideal_client: You are experiencing a major change in your life, and feel anxiety, depression, triggered, overwhelm. Although family and friends are helpful, you seek someone you can talk to, someone to witness your needs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from a hybrid model, meaning I offer counseling sessions either in person, in the comfort of my well appointed SW Portland office (with plenty of free parking), or through the convenience of telehealth, through a secure video platform. In person or by telehealth. Your choice. My style is integrative, meaning that I utilize techniques tailored to fit your individual needs. My counseling approach utilizes cognitive behavioral, attachment, poly vagal theory, narrative, person centered, psycho-dynamic, mindfulness, neuroscience, and depth techniques, which include exploring dreams, metaphor and movement.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I've been around the block and have walked the walk. I have extensive training and the tools and skills for supporting your deep and long-lasting, sustained recovery and personal growth. My office is set up to meet you safely, with HIPAA compliant online counseling services. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor and Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor. My Masters Degree in Counseling Psychology is from Pacifica Graduate Institute, with an emphasis in Depth Psychology. Give me a call, and let's chat to see if we're a good fit.

name: Rebecca Garetz
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: "I held my fear by the hand, honored its existence, and thanked it for teaching me that happiness exists beyond the boundaries it creates"
ideal_client: Therapy offers a safe, nonjudgmental space where you can explore your thoughts and emotions, develop practical coping strategies, and regain a sense of control in your life. Whether you are seeking tools to manage intrusive thoughts and compulsions, relief from persistent worry, support in navigating profound loss, or guidance in coping with chronic pain, I am here to support you on your journey to healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is rooted in evidence-based practices, including Exposure Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), and Somatic Therapy. Together, we will gently and effectively work through challenges, helping you build resilience and confidence. Exposure Therapy can support you in confronting fears in a safe and structured way, ACT encourages embracing life’s uncertainties with openness and values-driven action, and Somatic Therapy connects the mind and body for deeper healing. Throughout our work, I bring a spirit of gentle compassion and humor, recognizing that healing takes a lot of courage and vulnerability.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I became a counselor because of my interest in how we can feel safe in a world that has a lot of uncertainty.Growth and healing often require stepping into the unknown, facing discomfort, and embracing change with courage. The brain has an incredible ability to adapt and rewire itself—a phenomenon known as neuroplasticity. Exposure Therapy is a powerful tool in this process, helping retrain the brain to experience safety in situations that once felt threatening. When we avoid feared situations, our brain receives the message that they are dangerous, reinforcing anxiety, and pain. Over time, avoidance strengthens the belief that we are not capable of facing our fears. Through gradual, guided exposure, we work together to challenge these patterns, allowing your brain to recognize that you can tolerate discomfort and that many fears are not as threatening as they seem. This process helps break the cycle of avoidance and fosters a sense of empowerment, resilience, and confidence.

specialities.name: Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy
specialities.description: I use ERP to treat anxiety disorders and OCD. ERP is a type of CBT, that works on changing behaviors and managing unpleasant thoughts and feelings. We take the time to expose yourself to the anxiety without engaging in safety behaviors and/or compulsions. Through exposure we are training the brain to face fears despite anxiety being present, and when we prevent compulsions we train the brain that the feared stimulus isn't worth the extra time and energy. Let's be brave together.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I use ACT to practice bringing distance to our thoughts so that we can implement compassion and acceptance practices that align with our values in our daily lives.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I am a trauma informed certified yoga teacher and therapist (500 hours). Yoga is a great addition to talk therapy. The body holds emotions and trauma that sometimes our brains haven't even processed or consciously aware of. Working with the body can calm the nervous system and teach us about safety, boundaries, and connection. Polyvagual Theory and mindfulness has greatly informed my practice

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: The art of storytelling informs how we see ourselves and interact with the world. Who is the writer of your story? It can be very empowering to use the spoken and written word, or art/music to own our stories.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: OCD is my main speciality that I am very passionate about treating! I use CBT (Exposure Therapy) and ACT to treat general anxiety, performance anxiety, perfectionism, over-control, anxiety, OCD, and social anxiety. I have OCD myself and have also done training through IOCDF, The Knowledge Tree, and CBT School.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I use CBT (Exposure Therapy) and ACT to treat general anxiety, performance anxiety, perfectionism, over-control, anxiety, OCD, and social anxiety.Anxiety can also get in the way of maintaining healthy relationships which is why I also help clients communicate needs and set appropriate boundaries.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Chronic pain is well.. a pain in your... Needless to say, it's not a friend we like to bring with use to activities or outings, but I hope with compassion, gentleness and humor we can learn to befriend our pain. I use CBT, ACT, and pain reprocessing therapy to work with chronic pain.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Loss and Grief can show up when there has been a death, but can also show up when there has been a loss of self or others through injury, illness, life transitions, or even just aging. I use the witnessing and compassion of holding space for the grief process to happen organically. I also use ACT and experiential approaches through, art, music, writing and rituals.

name: Leslie Rosenfield
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am a highly relational person and I believe that all clients should feel safe, seen, held, and deeply listened to in the counseling space.
ideal_client: Moving through any life stage can have its ups and downs, I am here to support, listen, and help facilitate personal, emotional, and spiritual growth through your counseling journey. Whether you are approaching adulthood, have just moved to a new city, working through relationship difficulties, or are in a transitional place I am here to support all of your goals. I primarily work with adults and adolescents.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I am grounded in a trauma informed person centered model. I believe each client is the expert in their own lives and are the drivers of the therapeutic process. Healing can be held and processed through a strong, trusting relationship, empathy, self-compassion, and unconditional positive regard for each client. I integrate internal family systems, expressive arts therapy, somatic therapy, and mindfulness based techniques into my practice. I believe that integrating breath-work into the counseling practice is a key component to regulating the nervous system. I support many clients that are moving through anxiety, depression, relational stress, grief, life transitions and also teachers! I am a former teacher so I now how taxing the education space can be for many.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I decided to become a therapist while I was a middle school teacher. I had so many of my students coming to me with their struggles related to anxiety, family life, social issues, relationship issues and everyday life. I felt a strong pull to be able to support and help my students. However, my training was limited to teaching, I knew I wanted to do more. From there I earned a masters in science in counseling so I could learn how to best support those in need of mental health support.

name: Ivy Ross
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: LMFT, Registered Play Therapy Supervisor, Clinical Supervisor Oregon
intro: My name is Ivy Ross and I work in the Beaverton area. I incorporate sandtray, art and play into therapy.
ideal_client: I believe all individuals have strengths and the capacity to meet their full potential. My main approach is to provide a safe and secure environment for clients to process feelings and learn to manage emotions and behaviors. I incorporate play, art, sandtray, and symbolism to aid in the therapeutic process. My therapy dog, Daisy, is present one day a week and is used for animal assisted therapy.

approaches.My Background: I have a Bachelors degree from Western Oregon University and aMasters degree from George Fox University in Marriage and Family Therapy. I have been practicing as a counselor for almost 20 years. I am also a Registered Play Therapist Supervisor and Clinical Supervisor. I hold a certification in Animal Assisted Human Health and Play Therapy.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I see children, teens, and adults in my practice. Social justice and LGBTQ issues are important to me and I am a strong ally. I am also a fierce advocate for children and teens.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I treat anxiety and OCD using a variety of therapies tailored to each client.

name: Andrea Woodward
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Andrea specializes in helping individuals address anxiety, depression, life transitions, health, family and relationship challenges.
ideal_client: As a culturally sensitive Marriage and Family Therapy Associate, she aligns with challenges faced by LGBTQ+, polyamorous, sex workers and Latinx communities. In addition, she excels in working with adolescents and their families. Bilingual in Spanish, Andrea enjoys working with Spanish-speaking clients. With over 12 years’ experience as a sex coach, Andrea helps women, men and couples to resolve obstacles to communication and intimacy.

approaches.My Background: To support clients’ transformation, Andrea employs Compassionate Communication, Solution-Focused Brief Therapy and the Gottman approach for couples. In addition, she applies a collaborative problem solving process (CPS) developed while working with Fortune 500 company innovators. Most recently, she has used CPS to help at-risk youth and families learn to communicate more effectively.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Andrea adores her adult kids and her ancient, 10-pound dog. A resident of Bend, Oregon, Andrea enjoys hot springs, mountain bike riding, standup paddling and snowboarding.

name: Jonah Ross
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: -Now accepting new clients, Telehealth- I employ Psychodynamic and Humanistic approaches to help you reach your goals, and full potential.
ideal_client: I specialize in Anxiety, Depression, and Trauma (PTSD and C-PTSD), as well as life transitions, feeling stuck, wanting to learn more about yourself, and improving your quality of life in work, relationships, family, friendship, and/or community. I have worked with a wide range of demographics: genders, sexualities, races, ethnicities, religions, neurodivergences, and socio-economic backgrounds.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I try to create a space where discovery can happen. We will work towards your goals, emotional growth, and full potential. I hope to provide the trust and safety necessary for these acts of courage, and, ultimately... love. Something that distinguishes me from most therapists is that I have a PhD from UC Berkeley in Humanities, in addition to an MA in Psychotherapy. Both programs included Psychodynamic, Psychoanalytic, Humanistic, and Existential theories, but Berkeley also offered Cultural Studies, Gender Theory, and Media Studies, which enrich my approach to therapy. I offer a free 15 minute initial call. I look forward to meeting you!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a Licensed Professional Counselor Associate, I am under Supervision, of two Supervisors: Dr. Sarah A. Baird, Psy.D. and Kelly Hirstein, LPC 3C5026.

name: Daniel McClure
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi! My name is Daniel McClure and I am a Mental Health Therapist working in Portland Oregon!
ideal_client: Are you feeling weighed down by depression, struggling to find hope or motivation? Whether you're new to counseling or considering re-engaging in this meaningful work, I'm here to offer you support. My approach is centered on authenticity, empathy, and creating a space of unconditional acceptance. I understand the challenges of navigating depression, and I'm dedicated to providing a holistic approach that meets you where you are. Together, we'll work at a pace that feels comfortable for you, foc

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I aim to deeply understand your experience and tailor tools and treatment techniques to your specific needs. My experiences in education, mentorship, client interaction, as well as my own personal mental health journey have equipped me with a diverse array of resources to offer you

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: The human experience is a profound journey filled with both joys and significant challenges. If you're here, it may be because you've sensed an inner calling that something in your life needs attention. Whatever unique challenges you face, we can collaborate to foster change, gain new insights, and make meaningful progress toward your therapeutic goals. I deeply honor the vulnerability of my clients and hold immense respect for the transformative work that occurs in therapeutic spaces. I've been fortunate to learn from exceptional mentors, supervisors, clients, and my own therapists. Together, we can embark on a journey toward renewed beginnings and the pursuit of a more meaningful and healthy life.

name: Sasha Swerdloff
title: Student Counselor
intro: I will be accepting new clients in August. Reach out today to schedule a free 20 minute consultation.
ideal_client: Are you longing to feel seen, heard, and understood? I get it. We've all been there. The truth is, no relationship is perfect and we all need a little help sometimes. If you are: Feeling disconnected and distant, arguing more, having a hard time making decisions collaboratively, taking longer to kiss and make up, or feeling discouraged and scared, you are not alone. I provide counseling for couples and families looking to connect more deeply, communicate more authentically, and grow together.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I can help you explore and understand where you get stuck in unhelpful patterns of interaction, uncover the emotions and needs that lead you to react in habitual ways, practice communicating and listening vulnerably, increase mutual respect and understanding, foster deeper connection, and learn to resolve conflict by leaning in instead of leaning out. I am a marriage and family student therapist at Lewis and Clark College in Portland, OR. As part of my degree, I completed 12 months of clinical training at Oregon Pediatrics in Clackamas, OR and the Lewis and Clark Community Counseling Center. I have completed advanced training in Emotionally Focused Couples Therapy and Emotionally Focused Family Therapy through the International Center for Excellence in Emotionally Focused Therapy (ICEEFT).

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist, I believe that change is always possible and that healing happens through new emotional experiences. My style is caring genuine, playful (and a little irreverent), hopeful, and direct, helping to create a space where you feel safe, understood, empowered, and challenged. I use the evidence based approach of emotionally focused therapy (EFT) paired with parts work and socio-emotional relationship therapy (SERT), to guide you as you explore attachment wounds, uncover core emotional experiences that shape your relationship dance, learn to accept your whole self, and foster mutual respect and understanding. As a person-centered therapist, I know you are doing your best with the tools you have and recognize the impact of context, power, and oppression on your mental and physical well-being. I also know that together we can transform suffering into more secure and resilient relationships. I welcome clients from diverse backgrounds and social locations.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) is an evidence-based approach grounded in attachment theory that supports the (re)creation of secure connections with self and others. Based on the belief that humans are wired for belonging and growth, EFT helps identify patterns of disconnection, core emotions, and unmet attachment needs—guiding people toward new ways of relating that foster emotional safety and lasting connection.

name: Sarah Hardin
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Relational and emotionally-focused therapy for individuals, couples, and families to help you access your internal ability to heal.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Above all else, I believe in the healing power of relationship. During therapy, we co-create a space that provides you with the safety to explore your feelings, challenge old assumptions and stories, and do the brave work of transformation. My work involves us noticing and responding together to whatever unfolds, and using the therapeutic relationship to unearth compassion and create change. I believe we all have the innate capacity to do this, but sometimes we need a little boost from an ally to remember what we're capable of. Come as you are. Expect both laughter and tears.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I'm a marriage and family therapist with a strong training background in family systems -- thinking about ourselves in relationship to others, rather than as isolated individuals. I am trained in Art Therapy. I have extensive experience treating trauma survivors, LGBTQ folks, non-traditional and blended families, and teens. My work tends to be emotionally-focused with a strong emphasis on relationship. My master's degree is from Antioch University Seattle and I hold a bachelor's degree from Harvard University in Visual Art.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: It is a fundamental belief of mine that we are both hurt and healed in relationship to others. My approach fosters safety, predictability, and trust within the therapy relationship to offer you corrective experiences of yourself in relation to others. Together we will collaborate to explore and dismantle unhealthy beliefs you may have developed about yourself and your capacity to love.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: What feelings underlie your behaviors and your ways of relating to others? This approach helps you identify your core emotional needs and learn ways to express those to others. EFT works wonderfully with individuals, couples, and families alike to deepen connection and fine-tune communication skills. I excel at helping folks uncover the feelings that are often difficult to name.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: Sometimes, words don't suffice. Or we tell ourselves the same stories over and over again, not allowing us to get unstuck from these old narratives. The power of image and of creative expression to get at the heart of a feeling or a problem is immense. If you think visually or are curious about new ways of approaching old problems, art therapy may be very effective for you.

specialities.name: Sexual Abuse
specialities.description: Being a survivor is immensely complicated. I have extensive experience working with sexual abuse survivors and their families, and will witness and support your healing work with care and compassion. I use a family systems perspective to work in a relationship-based manner to address the complexities of abuse in individuals and families.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Families are messy, glorious business, and every single one is different. Coming from a strong systemic perspective, I hold space for multiple perspectives, and will assist your family in identifying and meeting common goals, working through crisis and conflict, and finding reconnection and new intimacy. We will work to improve communication and closeness in a really compassionate, hands-on way.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: You are the expert on your own identity. I provide identity-affirming therapy to support your process and struggles with being yourself in this world.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma re-wires our brains and can make it difficult to feel safe or in control of our own emotions and actions. Working from a trauma-informed perspective, I will help you re-experience safety and control in your own life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is our brain's way of trying to 'do something' to change a hard situation, but it often results in us simply treading water (or barely even staying afloat), and it can be debilitating. Together we will brave the waters and calm that impulse to help you actually be able to find your center and go with the flow.

name: Will Fairchild
title: Social Worker
intro: As a therapist, I strive to help folks feel empowered, heal, and grow.
ideal_client: Whether you're navigating major life transitions, processing trauma, or exploring gender and sexual identity, I am here to provide a safe, empathetic, and judgment-free space—with just a touch of humor. Together, we’ll identify meaningful strategies to help you build the skills and confidence to move forward in ways that align with your values and goals.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work is grounded in the belief of the inherent strength of each person, and I am dedicated to helping clients build resilience, self-compassion, and agency in their lives. My goal is to provide compassionate, trauma-informed care that empowers you to create meaningful change. Whether you're seeking CBT for anxiety, trauma therapy, or support navigating gender identity, I offer a collaborative, affirming, and client-centered approach to help you move forward.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: When I’m not working, you’ll likely find me running around the city or Forest Park training for the next half-marathon, at the coast or a hiking with my two wiener dogs, and most importantly spending time with my friends and loved ones.

name: Recreate Pathways
title: Occupational Therapist
intro: We support Autistic, AuDHD, and neurodivergent folx navigating cPTSD, anxiety, burnout, and the challenges of daily life.
ideal_client: You’re doing your best to keep up, but the world feels unforgiving and overwhelming. Tasks pile up, routines fall apart, and even simple things take too much energy. You wonder why it feels so hard when you’re trying so hard. We work with self & late-identified neurodivergent adults (and teens) navigating burnout, sensory overload, executive functioning challenges, life transitions, and the everyday demands of just getting through the day..

approaches.Our Background and Approach: At Recreate Pathways, we specialize in occupational therapy for neurodivergent adults, with expertise in sensory processing, emotional regulation, and executive functioning. Our clinical approach integrates polyvagal theory, interpersonal neurobiology, and core occupational therapy principles to support nervous system regulation, build sustainable routines, and improve quality of life across environments. We know that traditional systems often overlook or pathologize the lived experiences of neurodivergent people. Our work is grounded in the belief that your lived experience matters. We trust your insights about your body, brain, and history—and our role is to support and expand on what you already know. We recognize and affirm self-identification, and we’re here to help you better understand and embrace your neurodivergence in a way that makes sense for you. Whether you’re navigating sensory overload, burnout, workplace challenges, or just seeking support in daily life.

approaches.Our Personal Beliefs and Interests: We take a collaborative, strengths-based, and client-led approach to care. We intentionally create a space that is open, safe, and affirming—where you are never expected to mask, downplay, or justify your needs. You are the expert on your experience, and we’re here to walk alongside you as you build something that actually works. We are also invested in dismantling systemic barriers that keep neurodivergent people from sustainable employment, healthcare access, and education. Much of our work focuses on helping clients navigate those spaces while preserving their energy, safety, and sense of self. This work is personal for us—because we also live it. As neurodivergent practitioners, parents, and people, we understand how hard it can be to access care that truly fits. We’re not separate from the systems we’re trying to change, and that lived connection is part of what drives our commitment to this work every day.

name: Jess Firestone
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I delight in supporting families with kids age 8+, teens, and adults who have overlapping and different identities and experiences from me.
ideal_client: I love working with members of the queer community and parents supporting kids who are exploring their identities. I support clients who want to be gentler with themselves and deepen their connection with themselves and the people in their lives. I work with families who want to be more attuned to what family members need and find ways to communicate and express care with each other. I help people befriend anxiety and grow more able to tolerate distress.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that growth and healing happen when you are seen, supported, and cared for no matter how you feel or what is happening in your life. I love listening to you and helping you hear your own wisdom about the challenges you’re facing. Sometimes it’s helpful to hear me reframe the way you’re thinking that may come from being too hard on yourself. I can help you develop confidence in your ability to ride the waves of emotion that can be overwhelming. It is beautiful and painful to be a human and I want you to know you’re not alone. I use a strength-based approach, helping you re-write stories about yourself and your relationships. While we work together, we can do art, go for walks outside, or play with toys. That goes for kids and adults!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Before becoming a therapist, I worked in schools for almost 20 years. All that time in school communities prepared me to help you navigate issues you may be having as a current student, as an educator, or as an adult processing things that happened when you were younger. I am deeply familiar with the ways school systems can cause harm or fail to offer the support you need, especially for BIPOC, queer, and neurodiverse students. I am passionate about helping clients identify and advocate for what they need.

name: Anthony Marchant
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: The core of my practice is helping people create authentic relationship - with their self and with others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The perspective I have on health and healing is deeply rooted in my training in Transpersonal/Buddhist Psychology. I use Gestalt, Systems, and Experiential therapy to help clients move deeply into their experience in the here-and-now to live life more fully. I use Somatic Experiencing (TM) to work with all trauma related issues. I use Nonviolent Communication to help clients explore their feelings and needs, improving their connection to their self and to others. I also use meditation and mindfulness practices to increase a client's awareness, helping clients to feel grounded in their self and in the world. I work with people’s strengths and challenges to help them find the unique tools that are just right for them in their journeys towards health and happiness. The path towards greater fulfillment in life begins the moment one feels this longing for something more and answering the call to one’s personal quest is one of the most rewarding gifts a person can give their self.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a masters degree in Transpersonal Psychology from Naropa University and did my undergraduate work at the University of Oregon in psychology. In my early twenties I began to get involved in mentoring youth-at-risk and learning and practicing Nonviolent Communication. I also spent two years living abroad as a volunteer in the Peace Corps. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor in Oregon and have extensive experience working with couples, families, and adolescents. I also have experience working in a school setting and with domestic violence issues. Some of the areas I specialize in are: co-dependency issues, adolescent and parenting issues, communication problems, anger, mood and anxiety problems, men's work, spiritual/personal transitions, and trauma related issues. I have been practicing in Oregon since 2009.

specialities.name: Nonviolent Communication
specialities.description: I have over 20 years of experience teaching and practicing NVC and hundreds of hours of training. NVC is s core component of my approach and practice.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: I have a degree in Transpersonal Psychology from Naropa University.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I have training and experience in: Gestalt, Family Systems, Marriage and Family therapy, Solution Focused and Strategic Therapy, Mindfulness and Mediation, Client-Centered Therapy, Buddhist Psychology and Somatic Experiencing (TM).

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Extensive training and experience with parenting issues and family issues.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Extensive experience and training in family therapy .

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Extensive training and experience working with the problems associated with adolescence.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Extensive experience and training in relationship issues and tools related to improving relationship.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Extensive experience working with relationship dynamics and training in communication skills.

name: Joy Oelfke
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Trouble Sleeping? Sleep challenges getting in the way of living your life? I support individuals with sleep disturbances and insomnia.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I enjoy supporting individuals with sleep disturbances and insomnia, primarily drawing from CBT for Insomnia, Interpersonal Neurobiology and DBT. My experience also includes working with trauma, anxiety and depression, in cross-cultural and community systems. I strive to be LGBTQ+ affirming and intentional about cultivating a perspective of cultural/racial humility and curiosity. I am a member of the Society for Behavioral Sleep Medicine. I have completed EMDRIA approved EMDR basic training Levels 1-3 through the Parnell Institute.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT for Insomnia is a short-term, evidenced-based treatment option. CBT for Insomnia works to address difficulty initiating and/or maintaining sleep and/or nonrestorative sleep that results in difficulty functioning in daily life. It may be helpful for sleep disturbance as a result of Stress, Trauma, Anxiety, or Depression. It can be a supplemental treatment option for sleep disturbance related to Chronic Pain, TBI, Circadian Rhythm Disorder and Obstructive Sleep Apnea.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) is a skills-based approach that teaches four different sets of skills. The core DBT skills are Mindfulness, Distress Tolerance, Emotional Regulation and Interpersonal Effectiveness. I offer DBT skills support in group settings or individual DBT skills planning sessions (5-10 sessions) to manage a specific target behavior or symptom. Clients are usually established with a primary therapist while participating in either DBT group or DBT skills planning.

specialities.name: Insomnia
specialities.description: Insomnia and sleep disturbance, including difficulties falling asleep, staying asleep, waking early and non-restorative sleep can be both distressing and get in the way of life. Sleep challenges can also exacerbate stress, trauma, anxiety, and depression, as well as be related to chronic pain, TBI, circadian rhythm disorders, movement-related sleep disorders (i.e. 'restless leg') and sleep apnea.

name: Selin Strait
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a somatic therapist. I support people in attending to their embodied experience to guide foundational healing and change.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with people who want to build awareness and connection with their bodies, context, emotions and nervous systems to cultivate awareness, discernment, and connection to truth, wisdom and greater choice. I am experienced working with trauma and attachment related wounding with in a social and cultural context.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Life can be hard in so many ways. We live in oppressive systems giving or denying power, access and affirmation based on racial, gendered, class, sexual, ablist constructions of humanity. Our experiences, generational, familial, interpersonal, societal, cultural impact our everyday reality as well as teach us about who we are. They are held in our brains and bodies in unconscious and subconscious patterns throughout multiple systems. When we mindfully bring our attention and acceptance to our experience in the moment, these patterns can open and reveal themselves and allow for awareness, connection to self and truth and support greater choice.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a 52 year old, white, queer, gender fluid human with invisible disabilities. I understand webs of trauma result from colonialism and settler colonialism, capitalism, cis-hetero patriarchy, from generations of stolen land and chattel slavery; i know that ongoing genocide and violent anti-Blackness constantly retraumatize and reharm ...as a white therapist, I recognize that I embody white violence and can/may/do perpetuate it. I am practiced at identifying, uncovering and confronting white supremacy in myself and the world around me. I work to understand and see clients and their unique experiences within context, including the generational violence of settler colonialism, capitalism, cis-heteropatriarchy and white supremacy and value their knowledge of their experience, acts of resistance, survival and resilience.

name: Nuria Gomez
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Counseling for Healing Bodies
ideal_client: Are you worn down from trying so hard? Physical pain, exhaustion, and chronic health conditions take a toll on your physical and mental wellbeing. You may feel alone in navigating it all. But you deserve support, and you don't have to go it alone.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: MY PRACTICE AND WAITLIST ARE CURRENTLY FULL. We'll work together to look at how your life and environment contribute to your mental and physical well-being, build on your strengths, and incorporate new tools. I've worked with people in some of their hardest moments to find their way through with balance, peace and resilience.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I’ve spent the last fifteen years getting to know bodies by trying on various professional and personal lenses including public health service, massage therapy, functional nutrition treatment, organic farming, outdoor education, myofascial release, meditation and mindfulness techniques, and body-oriented trauma treatment. I work with individual adults and adolescents as a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in Portland, Oregon. I completed a Master’s in Counseling Psychology with a specialization in Somatic Psychology from California Institute of Integral Studies in 2012. I came home to the Pacific Northwest so that I could do the work I love, providing counseling to people with healing bodies.

name: Rainer Rivenburgh
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: MAAT, ATR-BC, ATCS, LAT, LPC, SEP
intro: Providing relational, trauma-informed clinical supervision for supervisees with lived experience.
ideal_client: Folks who seek me out for supervision are most likely to be queer and trans, people of color, who have lived experience of mental health challenges, disability, burnout, and neurodivergence. They routinely serve low income, queer/trans, sex workers, neurodivergent clients across the lifespan in community mental health, group practice, IOP, and private practice settings. They are likely to take OHP and I find it gratifying to support them becoming versed in OHP documentation.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I supervise with an integrated developmental, feminist, and trauma-informed model. My approach to supervision is to acknowledge and dismantle (to whatever extent possible) power differentials in the supervision relationship. This power issue is, again, mirrored in the client-counselor relationship. I prioritize psychological and physical safety for clients and for my supervisees. I help support supervisees in how to create a felt sense of safety in sessions. I help clients recognize when trauma response patterns are showing up in session--in themselves and in clients--and how to respond in ways that do not cause re-traumatization, and foster resolution of the trauma. I also help supervisees attend to vicarious trauma they are experiencing, repairing interpersonal/childhood shildhood survival patterns, so as to steward this trauma toward growth and autonomy rather than moral injury and shutdown.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: As a clinician, I hold LGBTQ+ community competences with a special focus on the needs of transgender/gender diverse people, including gender issues for children and youth, and WPATH Standards of Care. I have training in art therapy, Narrative Therapy, Relational-Cultural & Feminist Therapy, Internal Family Systems, and Somatic Experiencing© Therapy. I have training in mindfulness approaches. I work from a systemic, trauma-informed perspective, using a client-centered approach. I have worked in a broad range of settings including inpatient psychiatric, assisted living, day treatment, and outpatient settings. I am a Board-Certified Art Therapist, Art Therapy Credentialed Supervisor (ATCS, with the Art Therapy Credentials Board), a Licensed Art Therapist (LAT), Licensed Professional Counselor, and Approved Clinical Supervisor (including Disciplinary Supervision) for LPC and LMFT-track associates with the Oregon Board of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists.

name: Modi Soondarotok
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I’m Modi, a non-binary, trans, queer, femme person of color with multiracial, multicultural identities. Accepting clients with CareOregon.
ideal_client: My ideal clients are individuals seeking a compassionate, relational, inclusive, and collaborative therapeutic space to navigate life's complexities. Most of the clients I work with are from BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and People of Color) communities, LGBTQIA2S+ identities, neurodivergent experiences, creative fields, and those living with disabilities. I feel honored to support those who face unique challenges and intersecting identities while working toward personal healing and growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work best with community members experiencing trauma symptoms such as PTSD, anxiety, depression, ADHD, or grappling with the overlapping challenges of oppression and climate change distress. I also provide support for personal growth, career transitions, and navigating complex relationship dynamics, including those in monogamous and ethical non-monogamous partnerships. I am inspired to journey with teens, young adults, adults, and couples who value anti-oppressive frameworks and seek healing through lenses of social justice, intersectionality, and cultural humility. My practice integrates existential psychodynamic frameworks, Liberation Psychology, Queer Theory, Indigenous Theory, System Theory, Buddhist Psychology, and Interpersonal Neurobiology to co-create a path forward tailored to each individual's needs.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As someone deeply committed to equity, climate justice, and collective liberation, I strive to cultivate a therapeutic space that uplifts and honors each client’s unique lived experience. I offer gender-affirming care for LGBTQIA2S+ individuals and cultivate an inclusive, safe environment for BIPOC clients. Together, we will reimagine and decolonize the therapeutic process, nurturing growth and adaptability in ways that align with your values, identities, and aspirations. If you share a commitment to transformation, collective care, and healing that challenges oppressive systems, I welcome you to connect with me. Let’s envision and create what’s possible—together. Now accepting few new clients. Prioritizing BIPOC & Trans/Queer community members with OHP CareOregon/HealthShare. Affirming space for healing.

name: Zachary Ash
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Hi there! My name is Zach and I specialize in treating depression, anxiety, and trauma in adults, children, and adolescents.
ideal_client: Do you struggle with anxiety, depression, and/or a general uncertainty on where to go in life? Have the changes of the last year made you feel isolated and struggling to cope with life pressures? Are past traumas interfering your daily life to the point to where you're ready to take steps to gain relief? Do you feel like you would benefit from having someone in your corner to listen, strategize, and guide you through these difficult times?

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I've worked in the field of mental health for over 10 years, serving clients at every level from inpatient psychiatric care, to community mental health, and now outpatient mental health services. I've been fortunate to have the opportunity to help people from all backgrounds manage and resolve struggles around depression, anxiety, and trauma. During my time in practice, I have treated clients suffering from issues such as post-traumatic stress disorder, anxiety, ADD & ADHD, and depression.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: One of the biggest and hardest step that one can take in their mental health journey is that first phone call or email to reach out for professional health. My practice is based around a relational approach, building a strong partnership to process, strategize, and lift the weight of unresolved trauma and self doubt that many of us carry everyday. My practice is also based on a racial justice and equality framework and follow the NASW (National Organization of Social Workers) Code of Ethics. I believe that mental health care is a human right, which is why I am currently accepting OHP insurance as a way to ensure that there is no cost to you when seeking treatment.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have treated many clients who have met the clinical definition for post-traumatic stress disorder and traumatic stress disorder unspecified. These cases have ranged from individual discrete traumas to historical and multi-generational traumas utilizing evidence based treatments such as Narrative Therapy and Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Over the years I have treated many clients suffering from depression using a variety of approaches suited to the individual person. I believe in a humanistic and client centered approach that takes into account external and societal factors in addition to internal cognitions.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Many of the children clients I've treated have met the diagnosis for ADHD and suffered from behavioral problems in home, daycare, and school settings. I've had a lot of success helping kiddos to manage their emotions, learn to "stop and think" before acting impulsively, and learn to self soothe when upset so that they can better participate in group settings.

name: Colette Cottrill MA LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: "Life is short. Don't dilly dally" -Dorothy Dinneen

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Moving Through Uncertainty To Rediscover Peace: Hi, I'm Colette. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor in Portland, Oregon. I specialize in grief/loss and anxiety, and also help people with depression, addictive behaviors and individuals who experience an unhealthy relationship with food. I know firsthand the emotional and mental toll that the death of a loved one can take, and the many ways in which anxiety can leave one feeling stuck and isolated. My practice is all about helping my clients rediscover their place of peace. By creating a safe space to talk and move through uncertainty, I can help you find your new joy. I can help you explore a major loss of a loved one or friend, as well as the ‘little deaths’ that accompany us through life—work transitions, changes in relationships, and more. I believe that not all change needs to be life-altering. Sometimes it’s the smallest shifts that have the deepest impact.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my Bachelor's degree from Portland State University in Community Health Education, and my Master's degree in Clinical Mental Health from George Fox University. Some of the modalities and strategies I use include: Mindfulness, person centered, mind/body connection, narrative therapy, motivational interviewing and cognitive behavioral techniques. My work to date has been done in private practice as well as working as a Mental Health Counselor for both men and women in the State Prison system and the Washington County Jail. My current office location is not ADA compliant, however I am available to meet at alternative locations which are ADA compliant. **Feel free to email or call with any questions. To schedule a consultation online locate the website button below which will take you to my calendar.

name: Shelby Tuthill
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: Hi, I'm Shelby! I offer a supportive, collaborative, integrative, and evidence-based approach to mental health care. I'm excited to connect!
ideal_client: I love working with motivated adults - if you feel ready to make a change but are unsure where to start or feel like you don't quite have the tools to begin, I would love to be your guide! Primary areas of focus include (but are not limited to) life transitions, LGBTQ+ identity, creativity, depression, anxiety, trauma, interpersonal patterns, and building community.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My PhD background gives me a strong foundation in research-supported forms of treatment, which I integrate with collaborative, client-centered care that is tailored to your specific needs. I use an integrative approach, drawing from evidence-based orientations such as Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Interpersonal Process Therapy. Underlying all my work is the belief that individuals are best understood in context: the relationships, institutions, and broader sociopolitical systems in which they exist. Thus, my approach also centers a framework that openly and explicitly acknowledges power, oppression, and privilege. All of these factors are woven together in therapy to create a treatment plan and approach that works for you - your specific goals, needs, preferences, identities, and material realities.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I am especially interested in working with members of the LGBTQ+ community, a community with which I identify. I have been out for almost ten years and strongly value supporting other community members in their journey. The focus of my doctoral dissertation, an area of passion for me, was on contributors and barriers to connection and sense of community among LGBTQ+ young adults. Another aspect of my work is psychodiagnostic assessment. This is a process by which clients seek clarity about their mental health concerns. These evaluations may focus more on clarifying the nature of mood-related or interpersonal concerns, or may involve more specific testing for diagnoses such as ADHD. I offer in-person services on Wednesdays in Lake Oswego or telehealth services on other days of the week.

name: Natalya Imboden
title: Registered Somatic Movement Therapist
credentials: BA Dance Movement Therapy, BMC, LMT, Somatic Trauma Coach
intro: I offer body-centered inquiry and experiential practices, resources, somatic mindfulness, bodywork, and Trauma Integration Protocol.
ideal_client: Are you tired of talk therapy? Do you feel disconnected from your body and aliveness? Do you want to shift your biology and your nervous system? Do you suffer from anxiety, fear, irritation, depression, or loneliness? Are you not the same since an accident, surgery, chronic illness, or acute trauma? Are you wanting to create new outcomes and solutions to behaviors in your relationships? Do you want the ability to set boundaries while staying calm, powerful, and relaxed?

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach the body as a completely intelligent, conscious, and energetically attuned system. Your body knows exactly what it needs to heal and give you the feedback for innate health. I define body as Mind, Spirit, and Physiology. Each person is unique in their pace, nourishment needs, style of connection, and change pathways. We clarify your needs through simple body centered practices with sensation, breathing, perception, and orientation being our guides. We understand change comes through repetition through various neurological pathways so we create guided and self-directed resources of: breathwork, audio sound meditations, dance prompts, cognitive reframing, and nourishment styles. I also do hands on work with your energy system and your blocks that may need your attention. Once we feel your are resourced and their is relational safety and trust I offer a somatic session of selective inhibition with Medicine or non-medicine to access deeper biological charges.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a survivor of Complex Childhood PTSD and this gives me a nuanced lens through which I view the process of healing and transformation. I began my recovery from dissociative states and invisibility through the study of dance ethnology and dance movement therapy in the 90's. I lacked a sense of belonging and power which led me to studying with other cultures rituals and spirituality. Experiencing firsthand the power of shamanism, primal movements, emotional release, and the power of a witness I learned a non-colonial approach to healing. I found that most healing happens not by talking about it but by the nuance of experience, emotions, felt sense of attunement, rhythm (repetition), and human connection. I also was blessed to meet my Spiritual Guru at a young age who offered me a calm resting with clarity that was not conditional on outer phenomenon. These two orientations create a creative and open atmosphere of my coaching practice.

name: Chris Gorski
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I provide a safe, warm, nurturing space for my client to experience change. Let me help you transform yourself from the comfort of your home
ideal_client: Are you overwhelmed with life? Feel like you can't get ahead no matter how hard you try? I will help you take charge of your life by equipping you with tools to transform yourself. I will help you navigate your everyday challenges that seem to obstruct your path to creating a life worth living that you are excited about. I also help people explore their spirituality. Were you raised in a rigid religion or have left one that dominated your life? Let's together create meaning in your new life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I practice from a Person-Centered approach. I believe in the human Spirit’s potential for growth, change, and renewal to bring about transformation that creates a life worth living that you can be excited and passionate about. I utilize the Science of Yoga and Meditation and Mindfulness practices such as the power of the Present Moment and other Mindfulness practices that bring compassion and unconditional acceptance of self to help my clients achieve their treatment goals that we agree upon together. I use Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT) to help clients in working through and resolving personal relationship issues that they struggle with at their job, at home as well as with their children and spouses. Changing is hard I encourage you to have compassion for yourself during this process. I have been a Yoga and Meditation Teacher for 7 years and have practiced and been a recipient of the transforming power of the Science of Yoga and Meditation for around 20 years.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe the most important component in Counseling is first and foremost the Therapeutic Relationship. This will determine how effective and successful therapy will be for you. Do you feel heard? Do I see you for the unique individual that you are? Do you feel understood, do you feel safe? All research confirms the relationship between therapist and client needs to be supportive, nurturing and intact for you to feel safe enough to change and achieve your goals that we set together as a team. I have served in diverse types of nonprofit agencies over the years. Such as an emergency services counselor at a homeless shelter to battered women and children at a runaway youth shelter to working at a juvenile detention facility with felony convicted juveniles. I have also worked with elementary, junior, and senior high school students with different personal and academic issues with which they were struggling. I have worked with the elderly. I worked with impoverished kids from Mexico.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I was trained in Dialectical Behavior Therapy at the DBT Clinic in Portland by Larry Smith the owner. I have used DBT for years as one of my primary modalities in my work with my clients.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I have been a Mindfulness based practitioner for around 15 years and have used it in my work with clients for years.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I have worked for years helping couples establish more harmony in their relationship or marriage.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have many years of experience helping people cope with anxiety issues.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I have years of experience treating adults with ADHD using Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) and the Science of Mindfulness.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I have many years of experience working with people who are exploring their spirituality especially if you were raised in a strict organized religion that stifled your personal growth.

name: Jae Douglas
title: Social Worker
intro: Jae Douglas is a social worker in Portland OR. She works with adults of all ages, especially those experiencing major life transition.
ideal_client: I am particularly passionate about working with people experiencing or contemplating major life changes due to health, relationship or professional challenges. Many of my clients come to me feeling disoriented, overwhelmed by uncertainty, fear, and sorrow, and facing decisions in the context of the loss of the familiar. For people facing a life-threatening illness themselves or in a significant other, my focus will be on preparing for and navigating the process and meaning of dying and death.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I utilize cognitive-behavioral and strengths-based therapies to explore the experience and meaning, as well as the challenges and opportunities, present in major the changes that they are experiencing. In session, we focus on grounding tools to develop and utilize strategies to calm and ground yourself in the present, and to imagine and realize a future when you will feel stable, healed and whole.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I strive to create a warm, welcoming atmosphere that is thoughtful, active and engaging. I believe it important to create a safe space for clients to explore their history and life story with openness and curiosity. I focus on supporting and guiding clients in exploring how their life experience, skills, strengths and insights can be brought to bear on their current situation so as to find and move authentically and positively forward.

name: Emily Smith
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
