intro: I love supporting individuals and couples through the many peaks and valleys of the human experience.
ideal_client: My clients tend to be creative, thoughtful people experiencing life transitions, feeling stuck, or seeking to explore their inner world. I support individuals and couples in cultivating self-trust and trust within their relationships, breaking out of negative communication patterns and conflict cycles, and deepening their connection and understanding of themselves and one another. I am also passionate about grief and loss work, helping you find meaningful ways to continue bonds after a loss.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that how we exist in the world is shaped by our present and past experiences, triumphs and sorrows, relationships, and the stories we tell ourselves about it all. My path to becoming a therapist was born out of my own experience with therapy during a challenging season of life, and is grounded in the growth I have experienced myself. I strive to offer clients guidance towards true connection with themselves and to foster trust in the inner wisdom we each have. With deep respect and curiosity for each person’s unique experience, I am committed to meeting you exactly where you are. I incorporate Attachment & Emotionally Focused Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, IFS, and mindfulness and storytelling techniques in my approach. I’ve been described as calm, warm, thoughtful, relatable, and compassionate. At my core, I deeply believe in the human capacity for growth, change, and healing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am dedicated to creating a welcoming and affirming space for people of all expressions and identities, providing culturally-sensitive, trauma-informed care, and supporting you in embracing and living your most authentic self. I believe every individual encounters struggles in life’s journey and deserves to feel respected, heard, and supported in their healing. I view the human experience as deeply connected to the natural world, often finding inspiration in the shifting seasons and natural life cycles as mirrors for personal growth and transformation. I have specific experience navigating relapse and recovery in couples relationships, and have served as both a leader and member within a community grief group of 21-45 year olds who have experienced significant loss.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory underpins all of the work that I do, as I believe we are all wired for connection with one another. Attachment styles are characterized by different ways of interacting and behaving in relationships, and are influenced by both present-day relationships as well as our earliest relationships with our caregivers. I will work with you to explore and heal attachment wounds and move towards a greater sense of safety and connection in relationship with others.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: As a MFT associate, I have specific training and experience with working from an Emotionally-Focused Therapy perspective with couples. I will work with you to become aware of the emotional patterns and dynamics of your relationship, help you process reactivity, wounds, and emotional triggers, and guide you in practicing new ways of communicating and relating with your partner.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Narrative therapy focuses on the way we tell stories and relate to problems, and I will bring insight and awareness into what happens for you when you tell a story in the therapy room. I notice language and will be curious about certain phrases or words that you use in order to help you make sense of your experiences and how you relate to them.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I incorporate mindfulness practices into all of my work, including slowing down and focusing on present moment awareness, sensations, and emotions, meditation, and breathing exercises. This helps ground clients in the here and now and can help decrease overwhelm. Mindfulness is also a helpful skill for you to carry over into your everyday life.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: When our sense of communication and connection is “off” in our relationships, we can really suffer. I work from an Emotionally-Focused Therapy perspective with couples, and I help partners become aware of their relational patterns, provide space and guidance for processing conflict and emotional wounds, and help you lean into mutual vulnerability in order to strengthen attachment, love, and support within your relationship.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: My approach to grief and loss work is grounded in the idea that "We don't "move on" from grief, we move forward with it" (Nora McInerny). Loss can be so isolating and can manifest in many different, unexpected, confusing ways. I work with clients on exploring the impact of new and old losses, anticipated loss, sudden loss, and/or disenfranchised grief. I can help you find ways to continue bonds and meaningfully integrate the memory of your loved one as you move forward.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I enjoy working with individuals and couples who are curious - those who might feel lost or stuck, but are also open to exploring existential themes around identity, meaning-making, purpose, spirituality, and how to have more connected, meaningful relationships with others.

name: Bjanikka Ben
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My name is Bjanikka Ben, and I believe in the power of curiosity, non-judgment, and openness with ourselves as essential components of the h
ideal_client: I work with individuals navigating various forms of trauma, relationship challenges, abandonment issues, anxiety, and depression. Many of my clients are on a journey of self-discovery, seeking a supportive space for authenticity, growth, and vulnerability.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I graduated from Lewis & Clark College with a degree in Professional Mental Health Counseling, and I approach my work through a social justice framework and a trauma-informed lens. I believe in challenging and transforming old narratives that may no longer serve you in your daily life. My goal is to help you identify and heal wounded parts of yourself, fostering resilience and growth. Additionally, I deeply value the bond between humans and animals, recognizing its healing potential. I have a golden retriever puppy named Wednesday who is a trained service animal and you may see her in our sessions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: A Beginner's Mind Counseling approaches healing through curiosity, non-judgment, growth, and learning. It invites individuals on a journey of self-discovery, where all parts of themselves can be fully felt, seen, and heard. I believe it is essential to cultivate a capacity for change, which allows us to shift unhealthy narratives and better understand the root causes of maladaptive behaviors. By doing so, we can actively engage in the healing process—because time alone doesn’t heal; it only creates distance.

name: Diana Russo
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Diana uses a warm empathetic person-centered style using a strengths-based approach to works with adults, teens and children.
ideal_client: Diana supports children and adults through life transitions, grief and loss, anxiety, attachment, depression, parenting challenges, learning disabilities, and divorce.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I strive to provide a calm, safe and warm space for clients to show-up as their athentic self where they feel heard. I believe counseling is a collaboration between the client and counselor. My holistic approach combines Person-Centered Humanistic Therapy and Solution-Focused Components to foster growth and fulfillment. I firmly believe that unconditional positive regard and empathetic understanding are crucial in nurturing a person's desire for personal development. With a respectful, non-judgmental, multicultural perspective, I see supporting the client's goals as a partnership. Together, I aim to facilitate and develope a deeper understanding and self-knowledge and acceptance as well as your potiential for change and growth.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: After working in schools both in the United States and abroad Diana brings this unique perspective to the therapy setting where she focuses on life transitions, belonging and multicultural counseling to enrich and infor her lens for attachment, belonging and wellness.

name: Emma Bridges
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am an individual therapist and approach counseling with exceptional compassion, curiosity, and thoughtfulness. I am EMDR Certified.
ideal_client: Perhaps you struggle with anxiety, have been through difficult life events, or even trauma, and seek to break free from the impact of these experiences. Maybe you feel low and struggle to understand why. You may struggle with attachment or relationships, or feel creatively blocked or uninspired. Perhaps you experience ADHD or neurodiversity and struggle to navigate the world at times. You could be in a life transition, or looking to deepen your connection and security in your relationship.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and I help those who seek to heal from trauma as a Certified Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) therapist. EMDR is a highly researched technique that is uniquely effective at freeing people from traumatic experiences. I also delight in supporting those with ADHD. I enjoy acting, filmmaking, and comedy in my spare time. Seeking counseling is an act of bravery--I am here to travel alongside you and offer support. My goal is to put you at ease and offer exceptional support as you find your most grounded and healing path forward.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe Black lives matter and social justice is of core importance to therapy. I welcome and empower LGBTQIA+ clients. I inspire growth in my clients with gentle encouragement, evidenced based practices, and humor. I offer support to people with relational, career, creative, and personal challenges through a trauma-informed lens. I use CBT and mindfulness to help clients overcome anxiety, depression, or attachment challenges in order to help make life dreams come true. I see Oregon and California residents. My goal is to put you at ease and offer exceptional support as you find your most grounded and healing path forward. Email hello@emmabridgeslcsw.com for a free 20-minute consultation.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am an EMDR trained therapist and clients often seek me out in order to process past trauma. EMDR is a highly effective treatment modality.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I believe that if we can change the way we think about situations, we can change our experience of anxiety and depression.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I enjoy supporting couples as a level one trained Gottman clinician.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I believe that attachment is the core of how we relate to others.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I offer EMDR extended sessions. Learn more here: https://www.emmabridgeslcsw.com/emdr-intensives

name: Christina Sheehan
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Radical Counseling for Highly Sensitive People. I specialize in helping highly sensitive people integrate their trauma and thrive.
ideal_client: Highly Sensitive People (HSP) make up a 15-20% of the population. It's not a disorder or a weakness. In fact it is estimated that 50% of all people in therapy possess this trait, so there is a 50/50 chance right off the bat that you might be an HSP! As an HSP you are meant to do great things. Your trait is here for a reason and your superpowers make you very valuable. Therapy provides the roadmap to understanding yourself and designing your life in order to take advantage of your gifts.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I know that you are exhausted and feel there is nothing to be done about it. Too many responsibilities and people depending on you. You want to let go, but fear disaster if you are not in control. I know you feel pressure from friends/family/society to be ok, think happy thoughts, just do yoga, try this diet, stop being so sensitive, meditate 3 hours a day—and Oh the real reason I called you, can you do me a favor? I know that it feels like putting yourself first is selfish. I know that the over thinking, replaying conversations and worrying about making someone upset is exhausting, and I know there is more in life for you then to-do lists, and fulfilling others priorities.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Counter-Culture. Rebellious. Empowered. Radical Counseling is about acknowledging that we do not grow up in a world free from influence and agendas and that social justice ills affect us all. We look critically at what society is offering- like the limited definitions of success, patriarchy, gender roles, developmental expectations, and we consider whether those things add value to our lives or not. We tune into our own guidance & sensitivity system- instead of only referencing the outer world-and use this wisdom to create the life that supports our inner wisdom.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: Depth Therapy is based on the psychology of Carl Jung and believes you have a conscious and an unconscious life. The unconscious can be running the show without your knowledge. In this type of therapy I guide you through a process to help you access self awareness and inner wisdom as we gently uncover the parts of you that need conscious healing. We work from the inside out & we always uncover without shame or blame. This is how we start becoming more of who we are & less of who we are not.

specialities.name: Aging Concerns
specialities.description: Mid Life Crisis! Feeling stuck, disillusioned and purposeless when you are supposed to feel only gratitude sucks. You have no energy, you're crabby all the time, and nothing really matters. It's not just anxiety or depression, it's your life/soul calling you to grow. Midlife gives you the challenge of realigning to a new purpose. The problem is we can't see the new purpose and meaning while the old is still hanging around. I help support and guide this process.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: In everyday life anxiety can be a helpful feeling. It can encourage you to finish the work or school assignment, push you to get the oil changed in your car, or help you notice when something important has been forgotten. When anxiety is happening more often then not, is not attached to a specific thing or floats from one thing to another and is causing you distress, it might be time to get some help. Constant anxiety is not a fun way to live and change is possible.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Your Soul is Calling. Soul work is all about empowerment. It’s about deciding to move in a direction that honors what you truly want for yourself, not what your family or society believe is best for you. Our culture has worked hard to have a powerful hold on us and it takes courage to take a look at ourselves and our lives to see if we are leading it, or if others are doing it for us.

name: Joshua Bradshaw
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Welcome. I look forward to starting work together on your sexual and relationship needs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The relationship we build as teammates through the process of therapy can establish trust and understanding that translates towards positive outcomes in your lived experience. I work to enhance that relationship through compassionate listening, validation, and encouragement through exploring the person within. As your therapist, I will create a space that feels safe, which will allow the journey of understanding your relationships and sexuality to feel protected. Our work together will allow you to be confronted with the difficult questions and experiences life has presented while navigating these with a therapist who looks to create wholeness with their client. Throughout our time together, you will feel accepted, appreciated, challenged, and validated. This journey will enhance your understanding of yourself, your relationships, and the intersectionality of who you are. I look forward to working with you.

name: Sarah Tedrick
title: Licensed Art Therapist
intro: Reaching out is the first step, but also the hardest and most important. I look forward to meeting you; I wish you well in the meantime.
ideal_client: Hi, My name is Sarah I am a Licensed Professional Counselor, a Board-Certified Art Therapist, studio artist, public speaker, and LPC supervisor. I bring my lifelong art background and skills, training in Art Therapy, counseling, drug and alcohol counseling, psychology, years of experience working with adolescence and their families, many years of motherhood, and 18 yrs of sobriety into my role as a helper. I enjoy working with adolescents, young adults, and adults, with varying levels of needs.

approaches.How I Can Help You: There are many modalities that I am trained in, but it is my commitment and priority to collaborate to find a best fit approach, ensuring we develop a cohesive relational space in which to work together toward your goals. I believe relationship has the power to create positive change and I welcome the opportunity to walk alongside you in that endeavor. Reaching out for support can be challenging, but I encourage you to take that first step. I look forward to working together to achieve the outcomes you desire for yourself. You got this, and I believe in you. In the meantime, take care of yourself and those around you; take a moment to notice the spark inside you leading you forward. Until then, -Sarah-

name: Kayla Davidson
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am a Professional Counselor Associate striving to serve others who desire to heal.
ideal_client: I deeply enjoy working with individuals who have an innate desire to better understand themselves, forgive their past selves, and grow into their potential. I have worked with those struggling with anxiety, depression, PTSD/trauma, relationship, communication and attachment issues, and spiritual/religious exploration. I connect with those who care to heal their hearts and seek a more meaningful and fulfilling life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that each individual deserves the right to tell their story. To feel seen, heard, and deeply understood. At the core, most of us desire the same things in life; to experience love, joy, health, connection and longevity. But we live in a world full of constant distractions keeping us from looking within. My approach is centered around deep holistic healing. I may use spirituality to connect deeper to those with similar views. I view each individual as a complete being that has shifted, changed and evolved during their unique experience on Earth. While I choose to view each client as who they are today, I believe much of the healing work happens when we reflect and look at the past with fresh, new eyes. I focus on acknowledging and healing trauma, and prioritize the idea of building the strongest relationship with yourself.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Being the youngest of four with a long family history of drug addiction (specifically alcohol), I was extremely conditioned and had a lot to unlearn. I have spent majority of my 20's on a deep healing journey. I removed alcohol from my life, began seeing a therapist, and build my own self-care toolbox that has helped me learn who I am at the deepest level. I have found that answers come when you stop looking for them. Mediation, journaling, yoga/intuitive movement, and simply being present has allowed my heart to heal. I deeply enjoy connecting with other vulnerable souls and shining a light on their magic, the way all of my healers have helped me.

name: Karenna Bozicevich
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Licensed Professional Counselor practicing since 2018. Graduate of Portland State University.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with ADHD, trauma, anxiety, relationship struggles, and identity issues. I identify as queer and particularly enjoy working with the LGBTQ+ population.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use an eclectic approach to counseling, integrating elements of narrative therapy, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment therapy, and existential therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I work from a client-centered and strengths-based perspective, which views counseling as a collaborative process and the client as the expert in their own life. I work with each client to foster self-exploration, strengthen their relationships with themselves and others, and to find meaning and purpose in their lives.

name: Tatum Santacasa
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Tatum is biracial queer woman whose personal and professional identity is deeply rooted in anti-oppressive healing and the pursuit of equity
ideal_client: For over seven years, Tatum has been working with adolescents, adults, couples, and families across all levels of care—including Outpatient, IOP, PHP, Residential, and Inpatient programs. She specifically loves working with couples, young adults apart of LGBTQ+ population in areas of: Life and vocational direction, Relational difficulties, Fertility struggles, Disordered eating tendencies, Diagnosed eating disorders, Trauma, Abuse, Depression, General longing for a sense of belonging.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Her individual and couples therapy centers on helping clients process emotions to reach core affective experiences, allowing for deeper integration and growth. In family work, she helps de-escalate conflict cycles that reinforce insecurity, guiding parents and caregivers to be emotionally engaged, responsive, and present. She partners with families to rebuild secure connections marked by trust, communication, and mutual support.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Tatum’s goal is to foster safety, deepen insight, and create transformative spaces where clients can move toward wholeness, connection, and lasting change.

name: Drew Smith
title: Licensed Art Therapist
intro: I provide art therapy and creative approaches in professional counseling to help you find clarity & meaning while relieving pain & stress.
ideal_client: Are you looking for new ways to gain perspective and examine your life, access the healthiest version of yourself, and get in touch with your sources of inspiration and meaning? Do you find yourself struggling to connect with your health, happiness, and motivation? Together, we'll work together using arts and creative process to identify and address areas for growth while nourishing your strengths, so that you feel clear, calm, and empowered.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Incorporating art and creativity in the context of therapy is not about creating a masterpiece or finished product, but about engaging in the process as a tool for insight, self-awareness, and catharsis. Worrying about how "good" the work looks can actually be counterproductive to the goals of therapy. Most of our lives are not perfect. The art doesn't have to be either. Sometimes, talking about painful topics can be overwhelming and disorienting, but externalizing thoughts and feelings through a creative medium allows you to process challenges with the cognitive, emotional, and sensorimotor areas of your brain, all at the same time. In short, things often seem more clear, connected, and contained. My work is firmly rooted in the understanding that individual health is deeply influenced by systems of power, oppression, culture, and heritage, which demand our active attention in all spaces, and especially in the context of therapy.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: You don't need to be an artist or identify as creative for us to work well together, although creative process does allow for us to jointly examine aspects of your life in a new way. If you haven't felt that talking about things has been the most helpful, then working with creative elements may provide a fresh and inspiring perspective. If you have a creative hobby, profession, or identity (in any art form or medium) you may also feel that my approach feels especially supportive and helpful relative to traditional talk therapy approaches. If you are steeped in creative ways of thinking, that can make approaching your own emotions, challenges, and areas of growth with this lens extremely powerful. If you are struggling professionally with burnout or other challenges, then reconnecting with your creativity can help you access personal and professional clarity, calm, and meaning in your life.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: I'm a Licensed Certified Art Therapist with five years of experience providing individual and group therapy to children, teens, and adults. Prior to completing my Master's Degree in Art Therapy I worked in community arts centers, museums, and classrooms facilitating arts programming in numerous settings and for people of all ages.

name: Sabrina Arnold
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I’m Sabrina Arnold, a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) and Autism Spectrum Disorder Clinical Specialist (ASDCS) in Portland, Oregon.
ideal_client: I work with all sorts of people, though the niche I've found myself is working with those who have experienced trauma and who are neurodivergent and/or LGBTQIA+. One of the most important parts of therapy is the relationship between the client and the therapist. This is why I offer a free fifteen minute consultations so you can get an idea of whether I would be a good fit for you. We can still work together, even if you might not be part of the niche I described above.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide a safe space to talk about anything you want to. I use a mix of CBT, EMDR, and IFS, with little bits of other therapy approaches, depending on what works best for each person. I find that EMDR and IFS works great for trauma.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As for who I am outside of being a therapist: I love tabletop roleplaying games, like Dungeons and Dragons and Ten Candles. I enjoy reading, karaoke, video games, and watching low budget sci-fi movies.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT is one of the styles of therapy I started out with. I still use it in a lot of my work, and it pairs very well with EMDR and IFS. I generally use CBT to explore unhelpful beliefs, where they come from, and shift them to more adaptive beliefs.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I was certified in EMDR and trained through EMDR Consulting. I use it to help people process trauma and it works great with CBT and IFS. It can be a bit intense for people, so it's important to me to create some trust with clients before we start EMDR.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I use IFS to help people explore the different parts of themself. I appreciate how IFS helps people grow compassion for themself, and, like I said above, it goes well with CBT and EMDR.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I use a mixture of CBT, EMDR, and IFS to explore and process past and/or current trauma. I help people not only shift their unhelpful beliefs stemming from trauma, but also their relationship with the part of themselves that hold trauma.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I've worked with autistic, ADHD, and AuDHD people throughout my time as a therapist (and even before then in other jobs). I help people explore how neurodivergence affects their life, identify what supports could be helpful, and create a space where it's okay for someone to be themself.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: Similar to what I said above, I've worked with people who are gender nonconforming throughout my career. In a world where there is outright hate for those who are gender nonconforming, I want to make a space where it's safe to be oneself and have the support they deserve.

name: Gina DeLeo
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I work with individuals, couples, and families who are hoping to heal past trauma, improve communication and find new possibilities.
ideal_client: I work closely with clients who wish to reduce feelings of distress, improve their relationships, and feel empowered to problem solve. I see people as part of their ‘systems’; their history, family, culture, beliefs, current relationships and jobs…it’s an ecology, so any changes can improve the whole. I enjoy working with couples and families to increase communication and feelings of safety and acceptance through an attachment based, emotionally focused lens.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that therapy is a relational process where we work toward helping you find self-compassion, growth, and healing. I am trained in a systems approach, meaning that I look at the individuals, couples, and families I work with as being part of a meaningful web of connection with others in their lives. I believe that our histories are important to our emotional work in the here and now, and that it is empowering to explore what we value to help create a roadmap to a more purposeful and wholehearted life. I work mainly from an attachment lens, using emotion-focused and experiential approaches. My style is warm, non-judgmental, and engaged. I may bring in mindfulness practices in our work together to learn feelings of safety, process feelings and events, and ease the impact that stress and trauma has on the body.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I take a holistic perspective, considering the multiple facets of each person and their experiences, and view each of my clients as social and political beings whose health is impacted daily by the systems in which they live and interact. I recognize that systems of oppression affect us each differently and in specific ways. I also realize that they create privilege for some while making healthcare that much harder to access for others. I welcome people of all cultures, races, sizes, abilities, religions, sexual orientations, and gender identities in my counseling practice, and I seek to create a safe space that is tailored to my clients’ individual needs.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: As a Marriage, Couple and Family Therapist, I believe relationships are central to our experience of the world. We take into consideration the effects on each person's life of differences in power or equality as well as the impact of social issues such as class, race, gender, and culture. Relational therapy is collaborative and supportive.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I work collaboratively with partners, families and individuals who want to foster connection and form deeper, more loving relationships. I also work with parents to identify their struggles with parenting (be it a one time issue or an on going parenting struggle) and develop a plan to support the entire family system.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Working with moment-to-moment awareness helps us to gain insight and emotional healing. I am a certified 300 hour yoga instructor and have clinical training in mindfulness, experiential and somatic based therapies.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I have worked closely with women across the lifespan, especially around big life transitions, family/relational issues and inter-generational trauma.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: In my experience, anxiety is almost always a symptom of another issue, one that perhaps remains beneath consciousness. Anxiety is often accompanied by feelings of shame or not being good enough. We will work together to expand awareness, track patterns that may be constricting you, and gently help you find healthy and compassionate ways to relate to yourself and those you love.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: As a marriage, couple, and family therapist, I believe relationships are central to our experience of the world. I also believe that we often aren't given the relational tools we need in order to thrive in all relationships. Relationship counseling can be a transformative experience that provides new ways of connecting to yourself and to your partner(s). I typically utilize emotionally focused therapy and experiential therapy when working with couples and relationships.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: I believe in meeting caregivers where they are at, and working together to create a plan for mental and emotional wellness for the whole family. I help families learn ways to increase emotional closeness and change patterns. I have experience helping families support children who are exploring their gender identity and expression.

name: Jeremy Whiston
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I'm a down-to-earth licensed professional counselor associate, working with adults. My office is a non-judgemental space for my clients.
ideal_client: I work with folks of all genders and backgrounds, people who are suffering from all types of difficulties. You and your reasons for seeking help are unique, and the work we do together will also be unique. Historically, my clients have needed help with anxiety, depression, body image / eating, inability to focus, or difficulties with their loved-ones. Whatever brings you here, I'm interested in getting to know you, and helping you make that change you desire.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My strength as a therapist is that I'm a regular person, and I don't pretend to have any fancy magic powers. What I do have is a high capacity for understanding, for listening, as well as a few techniques that can help folks understand themselves better, and get some relief. The approach I take is based on the needs of my client on that particular day. Sometimes we just need to be heard, sometimes we need someone to tell us that we're not crazy, sometimes we need tangible tools to help overcome an obstacle or unhelpful behavior. I work with my client to create a plan that they feel good about.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I know from personal experience how difficult it is to find a therapist that you connect with (and who is available), and I will do everything I can to help. I believe we can make meaningful changes to ourselves and our lives if we really want to. I believe the most important thing I can do as a therapist is create a safe, non-judgemental space. My clients can share anything with me without fear that it will make me think differently about them.

name: Tiffany Del Pozo
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I’m a compassionate, dedicated, person centered therapist, who will meet you exactly where you are and help you get to where you want to be.
ideal_client: I absolutely love what I do and being able to connect with people in a humanistic, compassionate, and empathetic way is something I never take for granted. I want my clients to be themselves whenever they come into my office. This is your time to be vulnerable, validated and to never feel judged.

approaches.What I Specialize In: My specialities include working with clients who are experiencing anxiety, Obsessive compulsive disorder, panic, depression and or trauma. I’m also very skilled in helping clients navigate changes they want to make in their lives whether that’s a career, relocating, leaving a relationship and or divorce, etc.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I’ve worked with clients around anxiety disorders throughout my career. Challenging our anxious thoughts and finding appropriate coping strategies makes all the difference in helping us feel more in control of our lives.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Sometimes life is unpredictable and we feel lost and out of touch with what we truly want. Let me help you navigate these changes so that you feel comfortable and develop the confidence you need to move forward.

name: Pam Wood
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I use creativity and mindfulness with a trauma-informed, intersectional and strengths-based approach.
ideal_client: I have supported clients through grief and loss, PTSD, anxiety, depression, ADHD, parenting challenges, learning disabilities, abuse/neglect, foster and adoptive placement, parental substance abuse, divorce and racial trauma, and have years of experience working with LGBTQiA+, immigrants, and refugees.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I see kids, teens and adults, and lead two groups for women: Women's Art Therapy, and Trauma-Sensitive Yoga. I have 30 years of experience working in schools, day treatment centers and community mental health clinics. I am a dedicated student in the neurobiology of stress and trauma, and enjoy supporting adoptive kids and parents. I integrate art therapy, EMDR, Lifespan Integration, mindfulness, attachment theory, and DBT into my work with clients.

name: Annette Smith
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I work with adults of all ages who seek to forge their own path of authenticity through the practice of discovering meaning in their life.
ideal_client: Feeling disillusioned by life, desiring a change, but feeling stuck is common. If you're overwhelmed, stressed, anxious, depleted, or depressed about the many complex issues in your life and want to feel some relief, I help you to process and manage the problems of your life while seeking meaning for yourself. Existential crises are increasingly effecting individuals and you're not alone in these feelings. I specialize in helping individuals (re)create and regain a sense of purpose and wellness.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have been working with children and families in various capacities for over 20 years and one of the greatest things I have learned is that human connection is a conduit of healing. When there is a lack of connection, humans can feel despair, helplessness, fear, hopelessness, anxiety, and depression. Attachment disruptions, trauma, and lack of emotional attunement can create wounds that are felt for a lifetime. When those wounds go left untreated they can create problems and distress in our lives in the here and now. Healing those wounds become part of the process of gaining wellness, repairing relationships, and becoming fulfilled versions of ourselves. I work individually with adults 18+. I specialize in Attachment and trauma work using an Existential lens of discovering meaning in life. I work well with individuals who are experiencing existential crises that range from discovering one's authentic self to creating and accepting the meaning their life and experiences have.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I became a counselor to co-facilitate others' healing journeys. I believe that every individual has the ability to heal themselves and to find the peace and fulfillment they desire. I believe that my role as a counselor is to guide others on their journey. As a member of the BIPOC community, I am committed to serving those who also identify as BIPOC as well as other communities who have been marginalized in the mental health field. My position as a counselor also places me in the role of a social justice advocate seeking to support individuals in their empowerment. Within a collaborative environment, I work with clients in practical ways that give them real-world tools to navigate challenging experiences. I also work with clients to deepen their own understanding and meaning-making of their life and the world around them.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I have used Attachment Theory in the decades of work I have done with children and families. It is a lens through which I use to understand the needs of individuals and to explain the behaviors we see in both children and adults.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: I have been using coaching as a way of supporting individuals in their life and career goals as well as with parenting. It is a useful and complementary tool with use in counseling to help individuals apply practical skills to their lives. Where counseling is a great venue for processing, coaching supports tangible action steps a person can take.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I believe in the individual's ability to find their own healing path and to make choices that support that healing. I take the stance that an individual is an expert in their own life, and do what I can to provide the space for them to grow and experience wellness.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: One of my greatest joys is to see individuals grow in the many different ways that help them feel fulfilled and to live with purpose. I help support individuals in making small steps towards change as well as supporting them through major life transitions. Support for personal growth includes processing grief, change, and transitions. We also dive into discovering where we have been as a way of understanding ourselves now and charting a new future.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: I have been working with parents for several years on skill building, creating and securing an Attachment, and learning attunement with their children. I work with parents individually and within groups. I am also a firm believer that how we are parented greatly impacts our lives. I work with adults who are looking to heal their wounds around how they were parented, helping them to re-parent themselves in healthy ways.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Much of my work focuses on the loss and grief individuals experience throughout their lives. Life transitions, both positive and negative, carry with them some level of loss and grief and I help individuals process those and work toward creating balance in their lives as they experience these losses.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: How we are within relationships can greatly affect our quality of life. I work with individuals to support their relationships to include open/non-monogamous relationships.

name: Hollywood Mental Health
title: Psychiatrist
intro: Hollywood Mental Health is a clinic comprised of several therapists, psychiatrists and psychiatric nurse practitioners.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We believe in treating the whole person, and see people of every socioeconomic and ethnic background. We support individuals who identify with the LGBTQ community. We believe in helping our clients find a healthy balance and meaning in their lives. In regards to medications, we believe in a careful informed consent process. This involves sharing potential risks and benefits in some detail without jargon. We believe in evidence-based medicine.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a group, we have the ability to provide therapy and medication management for most issues. We work with all ages and provide support related to anxiety, depression, life transitions, relationship issues, bipolar, family systems, adoption and foster care, perinatal mental health, issues related to transgender and queer identity and ADHD to name a few. We use some of the following modalities: CBT, DBT, EMDR, Narrative Therapy, Humanistic and Family Systems work and Art Therapy. Learn more about our team at https://www.hmhpdx.com/providersandstaff/ If you are interested in making an appointment please complete a new client inquiry form at: https://www.hmhpdx.com/new-client-inquiries-1/

name: Kathryn Woicicki
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: I empower you to break free from isolation using compassionate, evidence‐based care that helps you reconnect with life.
ideal_client: I work with adolescents (14+) and adults experiencing depression, anxiety, trauma, and postpartum challenges, as well as parents facing modern-day stresses. If you feel overwhelmed, isolated, or misunderstood—trapped in painful emotions that keep you from living fully—my practice is a safe space for exploring new, compassionate ways to reconnect with yourself and those around you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I partner with you to dismantle the grip of painful thoughts and deep-seated disconnection. Using Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) as our core approach, we’ll clarify your personal values and develop concrete, practical skills to move toward what truly matters—despite the noise of overwhelming emotions. I also draw from Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) to offer evidence-based tools that help you manage intense feelings and reduce self-criticism. Together, we’ll work step-by-step to create space for joy, genuine connection, and self-compassion, helping you discover that healing isn’t about “fixing” something broken, but about reclaiming the parts of you that already work.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I treat individuals and families who feel overwhelmed by depression, anxiety, trauma—including postpartum challenges—and the everyday stresses of parenting. Many of my clients come to therapy feeling isolated, burdened by self-criticism, or trapped in patterns that rob them of joy and connection. Drawing on my personal experience as a parent who has navigated postpartum depression, I offer a uniquely empathetic perspective alongside my professional expertise. I’m dedicated to providing an anti‐oppressive, LGBTQIA+ affirming, and decolonized approach that respects your lived experiences and values, paving the way for lasting, meaningful change.

name: Caitlynn Hill
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello! I'm glad you came by! I identify as a queer, client-centered therapist and I think seeking help radical!
ideal_client: My goal is to provide a space for folks to feel accepted and to be held in nonjudgmental understanding. If you are struggling with depression, anxiety, pondering gender and sexuality, wanting to bring your spirituality into sessions, or needing a space for deep listening, I may be a good fit for you!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach therapy from a Cognitive Behavioral and Humanistic perspective. Sessions with me are relational, focused on deep understanding, and recognize that you are the expert of your own life! As your therapist, I see myself as walking along the path with you. You lead the way but I am there to help clear the weeds and find the best path forward.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I consider my personal and professional values to be one in the same. They include: - To accountably dismantle racism and other oppressions in myself and the mental health profession. - The inherent worth and dignity of every being, community, and relationship. - The right to free and responsible search for truth and meaning for every being and community. - Respect for every being and community as my liberation is tied to theirs.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I approach treatment from a client centered orientation. That means I strive to assist you in working towards the goals that are important to you because you are the expert of your own life.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I bring to my work a lived queer experience. I enjoy working with folks at any point on their sexuality and gender journey!

name: Teamworks Non Profit
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Teamworks integrative health clinic is an LGBTQ+ specialized clinic committed to providing care to underserved Oregonians.
ideal_client: The behavioral health team will be a comprehensive, social justice oriented program that will include therapists and peer support specialists. Peers will provide services based on the intentional peer support model. This program will provide outpatient mental health services, such as individual and group therapy, case management and peer support, with a focus on providing specialized care to the LGBTQ+ community.

name: Monica Metzler
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I help transform pain into connection with creative, evidence‐based therapy—empowering you to reclaim a meaningful, vibrant life.
ideal_client: I work with adolescents (9+) and adults, couples, and families facing depression, anxiety, trauma, and relationship challenges. My ideal clients are those who feel isolated by painful emotions or overwhelmed by life’s pressures, and who are ready to reconnect with themselves and others. I especially welcome individuals from diverse backgrounds, including LGBTQI+ and culturally marginalized communities, seeking a compassionate, non-judgmental space for healing.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I earned my Masters in Counseling from Lewis & Clark in 2018 and have been practicing since then, offering a strength-based, evidence-informed approach to therapy. My work integrates modalities such as Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and the Gottman & Gottman Methods, along with elements of Bowenism, Expressive Arts, and Narrative therapy. Drawing on my background as an artist and musician, I often incorporate creative, non-verbal interventions to help articulate and transform difficult emotions. I tailor my work to each client’s unique family history, cultural context, and personal values—empowering you to break free from unhelpful patterns and build genuine, lasting connections.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe every individual carries unique gifts and the capacity for resilience—even amidst pain and trauma. As a queer, biracial person living with a chronic illness, I know firsthand how our identities and experiences shape our struggles and strengths. I am deeply committed to anti-oppressive, inclusive practices and strive to support BIPOC, LGBTQI+, and disabled communities. My passion for creative expression, rooted in my experiences as an artist and musician, informs my belief that art can open new pathways to healing when words aren’t enough. I continuously work to challenge my own biases, ensuring a truly collaborative, empathetic space where you can thrive.

name: Jane Ward, PhD
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: My treatment supports personal growth, mindful choices, and healthier relationships.
ideal_client: Do you have a history of sexual trauma? Or some sexual interest or behavior that is troubling to you? Are you concerned that you may have a sex or pornography addiction? I can support you as you navigate these issues and re-establish equilibrium in your life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe in the importance of personal accountability, integrity, and building on individual strengths. My treatment enables people to understand themselves more wholly, think more clearly, better manage their emotions, and make more mindful choices about their behavior. My goal is to help each of my clients live a good life with greater meaning and purpose.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a licensed psychologist. My doctorate is from Seattle Pacific University. I have been working in the field of sexual adjustment since 2007. I am certified as a sex offender treatment provider in the state of Oregon and have advanced training in the area of sexual addiction.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: In 25 years of experience both before and after earning my doctorate, I have been exposed to and trained in a wide variety of treatment approaches that I am able to use as needed.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT helps individuals identify and change errors in their thinking and consequently their behavior.

specialities.name: Sexual Abuse
specialities.description: I am a certified Sex Offender Treatment Provider, which authorizes me to work with perpetrators of sexual abuse in the state of Oregon. I am able to work with people who are court-mandated or self-referred. I also provide therapy to victims of sexual abuse and sexual trauma.

specialities.name: Sexual Addiction
specialities.description: I have training and experience in sexual addiction issues. My work includes helping people whose marriage, career, or professional license may be in jeopardy because of their untreated addiction.

specialities.name: Internet Addiction
specialities.description: I have advanced training and experience treatment sexual addiction. My work includes helping people whose marriage, career, or professional license may be in jeopardy because of their untreated addiction.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I provide treatment for people who are experiencing distress about their sexual identity or sexual attraction. I have never provided 'conversion therapy' and never will, just to be clear.

name: Jams Markovics
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My life experience as a transgender person and my knowledge of neurobiology inform how I assist clients to improve their mental health.
ideal_client: I best serve clients who are motivated to do both top-down and bottom-up regulation of their nervous system. The typical clients that I serve may be neurodivergent, gender diverse and questioning, have a history of trauma (including societal trauma due to discrimination and bigotry), and often experience anxiety and/or depression. I am particularly eager to work with transgender and/or neurodivergent clients as they explore their identities and how they navigate their environment and society.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe mental illness or mental health challenges are due to both intrinsic and extrinsic factors, or nature AND nurture. The intrinsic factors are related to genetics and the function of the nervous system, while the extrinsic factors are related to the impact of environment (including family-of-origin and society at large). Therefore, I believe that treating mental health challenges requires treating both of these factors. Since everything we do affects the brain, there are many different ways to treat the brain, including top-down processes such as talk therapy using aspects of narrative, feminist, and acceptance and commitment therapy [ACT], mindfulness and/or spiritual practices, physical exercise, and positive social interactions, as well as bottom-up processes such as self-calming strategies including self-havening, tapping/EFT, and breathing exercises, as well as mindful eating of a personalized diet, typically anti-inflammatory.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: Since I can remember, but particularly since middle school, I have wanted to fight for the underdog. I fought to bring awareness to climate change back in the 1990s which has now become a climate emergency; I remember playing John Lennon's Imagine in a piano recital in 1991 when Bush senior decided to invade Kuwait in project Desert Storm (or the first Iraq war). Later in high school I came out as a lesbian, (and now more recently I have transitioned to become a trans-masculine, non-binary individual), and, ever since, I have been very active in the LGBTQIA+ community and activism. In more recent years, I was involved in the "No on 8" campaign in California, then I was active in the federal push for marriage equality and I have also participated in Black Lives Matter and anti-ICE protests. I carry these values into my work as a counselor, as well. I believe that societal discrimination based on who you are or what you believe is inherently traumatizing.

specialities.name: Biofeedback
specialities.description: I use EEG biofeedback as an intervention of neurocounseling, which is a relatively new theoretical framework of psychotherapy that uses neuroscience and brain health to conceptualize and form treatment plans for mental health challenges. EEG biofeedback (or neurofeedback) is a brain-based intervention where the client's brain learns to self-regulate better through receiving information about its own activity in real-time. This process helps the client regulate their nervous system better.

name: Chelsea Casey
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: MA in Marriage and Family Therapy
intro: Using connection as a tool for self-compassion, healing, growth for young adults, parents/prospective parents, and teens.
ideal_client: My clients are mostly teens & young adults, folks on their journey in Eating Disorder recovery, parents and prospective parents around the experiences of infertility, pregnancy, parenthood, and loss; as well as families. I work with folks to start recognizing patterns in your ways of being, feeling, and relating. I help clients navigate the challenges around decision making, healthy relationships, identity and value formation, boundaries, and general well-being.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I've spent a good portion of my career working in Eating Disorder treatment higher levels of care and came to private practice in 2019 where I continue to support clients through recovery, difficult patterns in relationships with food or exercise, and long standing body image concerns. I'm also certified in Perinatal Mental Health, and have found so much. meaning in working with prospective and current parents through all it means to bring a child into a family. I can offer support through journeys of infertility, loss and miscarriage, family planning decisions, navigating pregnancy, choosing life without children, or the entrance into parenthood. A good portion of my clients are also folks between 16 & 35 looking to better understand themselves, their histories, and cultivating a life congruent with their values. I often work with people in the LGBTQIA+ communities, and offer gender affirming support for teens and adults.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I see therapy as a healing relationship, not a quick fix. Because of this, I focus on trust and connection as a tool for helping you make practical changes, at your pace, and in a way that feels right to you. With me, therapy is a co-created, safe space. I offer warm, direct, and compassionate dialogue. I can offer support in areas of anxiety, depression, grief, family and relationship challenges, identity formation, sexuality, gender identity, and personal growth. I take a Client-Centered approach to therapy, while drawing upon insights from Narrative Therapy, Internal Family Systems, Attachment Theory, broader Family Systems, and Mindfulness. I aim to create an environment supportive to people with all body sizes/shapes, abilities, genders, sexual orientations, relationship statuses, races and ethnicities, and religious affiliations. I am committed to anti-racist work in my life and the therapy room. I'm also learning how to continuously do better here, and I'm open to your feedback!

name: Kelly Sestero
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Individual therapy focused on building mindfulness to be the best version of yourself in this moment.
ideal_client: Do you feel like you are constantly worrying about what will happen next? Do you get lost in thoughts about the past and future and feel out of control of your emotions and lost in your own body? Give me a call, I may be able to help. I come from a Buddhist Psychology perspective, focusing on building mindfulness to be in the ever-changing now. I can help you learn skills to build spaciousness around your thoughts and emotions, so you can choose a purposeful path forward.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I graduated with B.A. in Psychology from Gonzaga University and an M.A. in Counseling from University of San Diego. I was originally trained in the CBT model, focusing on reducing suffering by understanding how our emotions, thoughts and behaviors work together. In recent years I have found my passion in mindfulness-based therapy using Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Mindfulness Integrated Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (MiCBT) and Intuitive Eating. I work from a Buddhist Psychology orientation, integrating meditation, mindfulness and compassion to reduce distress from anxiety, depression, and chronic pain. I am a trained provider in MiCBT, an intensive 10-week program based on the work of S.N. Goenka and Insight Meditation retreats. This is a program that takes dedication and effort, but the outcome of peace and equanimity are well worth it. Invest in yourself!

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I am trained in ACT to help build cognitive flexibility and the ability to commit to values-focused behaviors. It is effective in treating depression and anxiety.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I am certified in Mindfulness-integrated CBT, which is a structured mindfulness program with daily meditations and behavioral skills to practice that builds equanimity and space to live as the person you want to be.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I primarily work with individuals with generalized anxiety and panic. Mindfulness techniques can help promote present-moment awareness, reduce rumination, and improved emotion regulation.

name: Erin Carney Moline
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I welcome people who are looking to heal their hearts and souls while relating to the larger context in which we live our lives.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I meet my clients where they are, and connect with what is important to them, in order to elicit the best possible experience both in and out of session. We all have stories we need to tell, skills we need to learn, and feelings we need to feel. My mission as a therapist is to help my clients to heal and be in deeper connection with themselves, their gifts, and our shared world.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been studying meditation and spirituality my entire adult life, and these experiences and my feelings around the importance of love and connection in life deeply inform my practice as a therapist. Formally, I received my MA in Counseling Psychology from Lewis & Clark in 2007, and my LPC license in 2009.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: Having studied yoga and nutrition (formally and informally) for many years, I believe that mental health is not separate from our entire health, and encourage all my clients to seek ways to round out their overall well-being through these practices. Our session together are a grounding point for your transformation, but that transformation occurs in your life.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: You are the most important person in the therapy room. This is your life, your therapy, and within you is a spark of light and intelligence that will grow if given the chance. For me, the greatest gift of being a therapist is watching that spark come to life.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: We live in each moment, grappling with who we are, experiencing joy, resolving pain. I use our time in session to bring you into this moment, to experience yourself as you are now. I have trained extensively in the art of therapy in the here and now.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: True Self-esteem comes from facing ourselves and realizing that we are deeply connected to the world around us. We are all here to walk the earth, and finding and discovering your particular way of walking is a life-changing experience.

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: I began my own antiracism journey several years ago and it is continually deepening and informing my therapy practice.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I believe that the experience of anxiety is one of disconnection; we have lost our connection to the ability to calm and make sense of life in all its glory and difficulty. I work with yoga, mindfulness, meditation, relaxation, and the processing of difficult experiences and emotions to mitigate the effects of anxiety.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: I enjoy working with clients to find healthy boundaries and a sense of self that is loving and connected. Healing codependency brings us home to ourselves, and gives us the gift of healthy community and relationships. My approach to codependency is informed by my antiracism work and understanding of white supremacy culture and its violence, both internally and externally.

name: Myles Rizvi
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I am a clinical psychologist specializing in evidence-based treatment for anxiety and OCD-related disorders in youth and adults.
ideal_client: My clients are individuals who struggle with anxiety and/or obsessive-compulsive-related disorders, the latter of which include obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD), hoarding disorder, hair-pulling disorder, skin-picking disorder, and body dysmorphic disorder. The anxiety and distress they experience has gotten in the way of how they want to live their lives. My clients want to take back what anxiety took from them and learn how to manage their anxiety independently.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have dedicated myself to the treatment of anxiety and OCD-spectrum disorders. Passionate about providing early intervention for anxiety, I obtained my Psy.D. at Pacific University, where I focused my training in the Child and Adolescent Track. I completed a postdoctoral fellowship at Texas Children’s Hospital’s Obsessive-Compulsive and Anxiety Disorders Program to become proficient in treating a variety of anxiety and OCD-spectrum disorders. I have treated anxiety and OCD-spectrum disorders across the lifespan as a licensed clinical psychologist since 2019. My treatment approach is strongly informed by cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) and exposure and response prevention (ERP). I also incorporate treatment principles and interventions from acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), dialectical behavior therapy (DBT), and metacognitive therapy (MCT). I provide individual and family-based treatment, the latter of which is often the best practice for treating pediatric anxiety.

approaches.Why We are a Good Fit for You: Treating OCD and anxiety requires a collaborative, supportive, and team-based approach. You and I will work together to treat your symptoms by learning how to change the way you think and (perhaps most importantly) change how you behave in response to fear, anxiety, and panic. I will help you learn that you are stronger and more capable than your anxiety may suggest. It is difficult to move towards what scares us, and you will always have the choice of pace in your therapy journey. Each individual always chooses how hard they are willing to push themselves in order to face challenges and create change. My clients usually struggle with at least one of the following: Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Panic Disorder, Social Anxiety Disorder, Specific Phobias, Agoraphobia, Separation Anxiety Disorder, Hoarding Disorder, Body Dysmorphic Disorder, Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder, hair-pulling disorder (trichotillomania), and skin-picking disorder (excoriation disorder).

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive behavioral therapy was the primary treatment orientation I was trained in throughout my graduate and postgraduate training. I have completed a several specialized cognitive behavioral therapy trainings, including the Behavior Therapy Training Institute (BTTI) course sponsored by the International OCD Foundation (IOCDF), and Supportive Parenting for Anxious Childhood Emotions (SPACE) Training workshop. I have also provided supervision in CBT for doctoral students.

specialities.name: Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy
specialities.description: I have received extensive training in ERP throughout my graduate and postgraduate training. I completed a specialized training in ERP for OCD through the Behavior Therapy Training Institute (BTTI) course sponsored by the International OCD Foundation (IOCDF), and I have given professional presentations on ERP at the IOCDF and the Anxiety and Depression Association of America (ADAA). I have also provided supervision in ERP for doctoral students.

specialities.name: Psychological Testing and Evaluation
specialities.description: I provide psychological testing services to evaluate attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and specific learning disorders in individuals aged 11 and older. I provided such assessments throughout my graduate and internship training for youth and adults.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have completed clinical rotations at anxiety-specific treatment centers throughout my graduate training, including OHSU's Fear and Anxiety Disorders Treatment Clinic and Texas Children's Hospital's Obsessive-Compulsive and Anxiety Disorders Program, and I have four years of experience treating anxiety disorders as a licensed clinical psychologist. I have given presentations on anxiety-related topics at professional conferences, and I recently published an article on dating anxiety.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: I completed a postdoctoral fellowship at the Texas Children's Hospital's Obsessive-Compulsive and Anxiety Disorders Program, and I have four years of experience treating OCD as a licensed clinical psychologist. I completed the Behavior Therapy Training Institute (BTTI) course in OCD treatment cosponsored by the International OCD Foundation (IOCDF). I have given several presentations on OCD-related topics at the IOCDF, and I published an article on pediatric OCD.

specialities.name: Panic
specialities.description: Panic attacks and panic-like symptoms are common experiences in anxiety and OCD-related disorders, concerns that I have had considerable experience treating throughout my graduate and postgraduate training, and my career as a licensed clinical psychologist.

specialities.name: Social Phobia
specialities.description: Social phobia, or social anxiety disorder, was my first clinical and research interest and inspired me to dedicate myself to specializing in anxiety treatment. I have had considerable experience treating this disorder throughout my training and professional career.

name: Nancy Pounds
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I have many years of experience working with individuals to address all sorts of issues that inevitably arise in life. I’d love to help!
ideal_client: Your past is invading your present. Your emotions overwhelm you at times. Many of your relationships are unfulfilling - or outright painful. Your self-esteem is low to nonexistent, and you often feel you aren’t good enough. Celebrating your successes is hard for you because you feel like you don’t deserve them. Your inner critic is your constant companion. And the worst part is: overcoming these obstacles seems like a huge mountain to climb. I’d love to help you find peace and happiness!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Imagine feeling confident, empowered and more in touch with your Authentic Self. Picture yourself free from the struggles of your past. Together we can bring about change in your life by tailoring your therapy sessions to meet your unique needs. Along with talk therapy, I offer EMDR and Hypnotherapy, which can aid in (and often hasten) the healing process. Take back control of your life. Become your best self. Therapy can help. Contact me for a free 20-minute phone consultation where we can discuss what’s happening and what you’re wanting to change about your life. I would be honored to walk with yiu o your healing journey.

I use a psychodynamic approach to therapy, which means I believe our past directly affects our present. However, I don’t believe in spending a lot of time digging up the past, but instead, examining it to see what type of clues we can find to help you heal from present issues.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I naturally lean toward this orientation, and have studied it for many, many years. It’s based on past affecting the present, personality traits, and subconscious influences.

name: Sara Vetiver
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Through mindful and embodied counseling, I support clients in reclaiming agency in their personal healing and in their relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that every person holds the map to their own healing. Within the therapeutic relationship, I support my clients in re-connecting with their inherent wisdom and the tools needed to further liberate it. To do this work, I like to move slowly to build trust and forge a relationship that feels solid yet flexible. This relationship building occurs through curiosity, patience, and embodiment. In this space, it is then possible to foster comfort in vulnerable exploration and to cultivate mindfulness of one's patterns and constrictions, one's desires for growth, and all the various parts of the self that are waiting to be seen and loved again. Using this mindfulness practice as an anchor, we can begin to explore trauma and process it gradually and intentionally over time. I use this approach with both individuals and couples, co-creating an environment in which we can see our cycles, and from this perspective, feel the agency to make new choices.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My path has been by shaped by somatics, yoga, and wilderness immersion; my writing practice and transformation through arts’ communities; the cohort and coursework of California Institute of Integral Studies; community organizing; deep dives into psychedelic healing; my journey of understanding how trauma has shaped me— the losses and the fortifications; and, most significantly, the relationships that bless my life with ongoing opportunities for mutual evolution. I am a queer, femme, she/they, white, Pacific Islander, first-generation college student, an oldest sibling, temporarily able-bodied, a settler on Indigenous lands, and a lifelong learner. I am a lover of poetry, philosophy, astrology, backpacking, swimming, and pups.

name: Kyong Yi
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Connection is vital to life. Through our connection with others we find safety, meaning, strength and inspiration.
ideal_client: It’s little wonder that when life brings us challenges, our relationships suffer. Whether relationship issues are the cause or consequence of your struggles, the pain of disconnection and isolation can be detrimental to your well-being. Through our work together, I can help you better connect to your feelings and find strength in vulnerability. We can address past trauma(s) to lessen their hold on your life. These are the foundations for healthy relationships and meaningful living.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Cultivating intimacy in relationships can be scary. It requires understanding your emotions and needs and a willingness to take risks, be vulnerable, and show your authentic self. So many times, our fears and thoughts that we are not enough, we will be rejected, and that we are invisible trap us in internal suffering. It can feel like we are watching life happen around us from behind a glass window, longing to join but with no way of breaking through. Using evidence-based treatments such as Emotion-Focused Therapy and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, I will partner with you to open to your feelings, let go of suffering and understand and express your needs. We will explore what and who is most valuable in your life, and I will support you in making the small and large changes you desire. Together, we will tackle barriers as they arise and develop skills and resilience.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In addition to my regular therapy practice, I also offer therapy services to individuals considering or having participated in psychedelic experiences. If you are considering engaging in a psychedelic experience, I can help you think through the potential harms and explore your hopes and intentions. (Please note that I do not provide or help individuals acquire psychedelic substances). If you have had a psychedelic experience, I can help you work to integrate your experiences to support lasting and meaningful change. I have specialized training in multiple forms of psychedelic assisted therapy including MDMA and psilocybin. I am also a research therapist on Portland Psychotherapy’s clinical trial of MDMA for Social Anxiety Disorder.

name: Cornelia Taubmann
title: Hypnotherapist
intro: My holistic approach incorporates a variety of techniques, including hypnosis, Somatic Experiencing (SE™), Parts work, and CBT.
ideal_client: Life can be scary. Sometimes we get overwhelmed and let our fears dictate what we can and cannot do. In my practice, I see many clients who want their life back. One key to conquering our irrational fears is to avoid avoidance. Together we will find out what that means in your specific case and what your goals are. With hypnosis, it is possible to speed up the process of responding more appropriately to previously dreaded situations. We will help you experience yourself in control and confident.

approaches.My Background: As a hypnotherapist with over 600 hours of training and Somatic Experiencing ® Practitioner (SEP), I understand the importance of a multimodal approach to treatment. While traditional talk therapy can be helpful, I believe that true and lasting change often requires engaging the body and subconscious mind.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe unhelpful patterns are a result of a survival/adaptive response that has become obsolete. Reconnecting with our body and small gradual changes steps are the keys to changing our nervous system's response.

specialities.name: Hypnotherapy
specialities.description: Hypnotherapy is a recommended treatment for IBS, particularly when brain-body communication contributes to symptoms. It can also be highly effective for other physical ailments, such as chronic lower back pain and fibromyalgia, which often share similar underlying mechanisms of stress, tension, and nervous system dysregulation. By addressing the mind-body connection, hypnotherapy helps reduce hypervigilance, anxiety, and physical symptoms, promotes relaxation, and enhances overall well-being.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Somatic Experiencing (SE) is a body-focused therapeutic approach designed to help individuals process and release trauma stored in the nervous system. By gently guiding awareness to physical sensations, SE supports the completion of natural survival responses that may have been interrupted during traumatic events. This process helps restore balance, reduce symptoms of trauma, and build resilience, fostering a sense of safety and connection in both body and mind.

specialities.name: Insomnia
