specialities.description: Sleep difficulties can manifest in various forms, including difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up too early. It’s crucial to rule out sleep apnea as a potential cause. Often sleep problems do arise when we are stuck in high energy levels of fight or flight. As a result, our ability to transition into resting states is blocked. Through hypnosis, mindfulness, and Somatic Experiencing, you can learn to navigate the natural waves of activation your body goes through.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Are anxiety and its symptoms holding you back? Anxiety can show up as constant worry, tension, or physical issues like IBS, and it’s often linked to fears or phobias that feel hard to overcome. You don’t have to manage it alone. Through hypnotherapy and gentle, proven techniques, I can help you calm your mind, ease your body, and break the cycle of anxiety. Together, we’ll address the root causes, reduce symptoms, and help you feel more in control, confident, and at ease in your daily life.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Living with chronic pain or illness can be exhausting, especially when health concerns and unhelpful beliefs heighten your awareness of discomfort. These patterns can create a cycle that feels hard to escape. Through hypnotherapy, I can help you gently shift these beliefs, reduce tension, and reframe your relationship with your body. Together, we’ll work to ease your symptoms, calm your mind, and help you feel more at ease and in control of your well-being.

name: myra bazell
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Re-discover your natural strength and deep rooted source of power.
ideal_client: Myra has been in practice for twenty years, working with diverse populations in areas of anxiety, depression, body image, loneliness, procrastination, relationships, LGBTQIA+, the social and internal dynamics of aging, teen challenges, illness, PTSD and Trauma. Myra teaches mindfulness and meditation when desired and collaborates on finding motivation for change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Myra Bazell is a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and received her Masters in Social Work from the Bryn Mawr Graduate School of Social Work & Social Research. Myra comes with an extensive background in dance that has provided her with an understanding of how our histories live in our bodies and provide a great resource for understanding our lived experience. Myra is passionate about escorting clients on a journey of rediscovery; the revealing of one’s natural strength and deep-rooted source of power is for her a road to managing stress and embracing daily challenges.

Myra employes a wealth of client centered therapeutic modalities including; Cognitive Behavioral Therapies ( CBT), Narrative Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Attachment-Based Therapy, Mindfulness, Breath work, Compassion-Focused Therapy (CFT), and when appropriate Trauma Informed Authentic Movement. Give yourself permission to do you. Overcome stress and enjoy your daily challenges. Explore early attachment and its impact on your current self-view. Improve your relationships. Rewrite self-script. Plan your next move while learning to be in the moment. Discover reasons to be holistic. Transform negative energy into creative ability. Align with your true self.

name: Heather Lokteff
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Helping you take care of your mental health, personal growth, and relationships. I use a collaborative, skilled, & empathic approach.
ideal_client: As my client I would work with you on better managing anxiety, work through traumas and/or major life transitions, and strive for you to feel more engaged and connected to your values. I see a wide range of clients - some are in the midst of an urgent situation while others are wanting to be preventative and focus on self-care. I feel honored to witness my clients’ vulnerability and be a part of their willingness to examine their lives and make changes that make sense for them.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I finished my Masters in Counseling Psychology in 2006 and I have 16+ years experience providing therapy to a variety of clients. Prior to starting my own practice in 2011 I worked at various non-profit agencies providing in-home and intensive community-based treatment for children and families in crisis and/or DHS involvement. I helped create safety and stabilization in families and worked with children and teens providing intensive mental health services. I continue to carry my knowledge and experience with children into my work with teen and adult clients and feel it gives me a unique perspective on people’s pasts, family of origin, and struggles that started in childhood. I’ve expanded my practice to work with couples as well as continuing with teens and adults. I utilize evidence-based therapies including Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT), Acceptance & Commitment Therapy (ACT), and am a Level 1 trained clinician in Internal Family Systems and the Gottman Method.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I value a practical, collaborative and personalized approach to your therapy experience. I provide insight, encouragement, and a safe and non-judgmental space. I value honesty, humility, and self-compassion. I value my clients and their self-advocacy and resiliency. I value humor, engaging in life with a sense of adventure and gratitude, and being holistically healthy. I believe in identifying and building on personal strengths, and equipping you with practical life skills to get you to where you want to be. I believe in the transformative power of a safe, supportive, collaborative and confidential relationship that therapy provides. I value creating a compassionate, non-judgmental space to be heard and listened to. I value being a neutral support person and a knowledgeable sounding board. It’s important to have a therapist you feel safe with and encouraged by. This is how I aspire to operate in my practice.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Our therapeutic relationship is the most important predictor of success in therapy. My main focus is creating a collaborative environment where you feel heard, validated, and have a safe space to express your thoughts, emotions, and experiences. You are the expert of you! Together we can move towards having more connection, vulnerability and authenticity in your relationships and inner peace.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Acceptance & Commitment Therapy aims to become more cognitively flexible, more engaged in the present, take committed action steps towards change, and become more connected to your personal values. It centers around finding ways to live more intentionally in the moment and act in ways that are more helpful to yourself.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotion Focused Therapy is an attachment-based therapy that can be used for couples as well as individuals. EFT focuses on becoming more aware of emotions and learning to label, allow, experience, transform, and regulate emotions. For couples, EFT helps to create a more secure bond between partners and shifts interactions and dynamics in a more positive, affirming direction.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: In Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy, we take a look at how your thoughts, emotions and behaviors interact and effect one another. It helps identify unhealthy ways of thinking and replace them with more beneficial thoughts that are in our own best interest. You’ll learn tools to practice outside of session in a practical, helpful way.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I am a Level 1 trained IFS therapist. IFS conceptualizes individuals as having a system of "parts" within themselves. You might have an "inner critic" part of yourself, for example, that has held onto extreme beliefs that try to manage you. IFS is an experiential therapy that is designed to have your "Self" identify different parts of you that may be holding onto burdens and hurts from the past and build relationships with these parts to lead to healing and self-understanding.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Focusing on your own personal growth can be an exciting and insightful time. If you're wanting to pause and reflect, be more intentional with your time, and focus on personal goals, now is the time to make changes and therapy can help! It’s some of my favorite kind of work with clients.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Adjusting to a major life change? I work with clients who have recently moved to the Portland area, are going through a relationship break-up or divorce, experiencing career changes, becoming a new parent or empty-nester, or graduating college.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Most of us have some degree of anxiety, so you’re not alone! For some it can be debilitating or take control of your mind. I work with my clients on processing situations both past and present that create anxiety and identify skills to shift mindsets, be more relaxed, and be more connected to the present instead of feeling highjacked by anxiety.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I work with couples who are wanting to increase their sense of vulnerability, partnership and security with one another. I also work with couples who are blending families and navigating being previously divorced. I use Emotion-Focused Therapy and the Gottman Method as well as my personal experiences to inform my practice.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: I have experience working with individuals who have left abusive situations or have experienced childhood abuse. I am Level 1 Internal Family Systems (IFS) trained. I work with individuals who are processing past hurts and reconnecting with a sense of safety and a calmer nervous system. Early in my career I worked with children in foster care and the DHS system as a play therapist. I feel my work with children informs me daily in my work with adults who have experienced abuse as a child.

name: Megan Koehler
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I am a mental health therapist who believes all change is possible with the right supports.
ideal_client: My ideal client is motivated to create change in their life, even if they are unsure where to start. They've often had to become resilient-perhaps out of necessity rather than choice-and are now ready to transform that survival into growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use evidence-based practices—including Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), and strengths-based approaches—to address a range of concerns such as PTSD, anxiety, depression, traumatic stress, and complex grief.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I understand how vulnerable it can feel to reach out for support, and I don’t take that lightly. I strive to create a space where you feel safe, seen, and genuinely supported—where your story is met with compassion, not judgment. I bring honesty, authenticity, and a belief in your capacity to grow—even in the face of challenge. I believe all people are capable of creating the change they want to see in their lives given the right tools. I have seen first hand the impacts of how traumatic experiences can change everything.

name: Lisa Winestock
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I'm a therapist with lived experience eager to destigmatize mental health.
ideal_client: Whether you're just getting started and opening up to the idea of exploring therapy, or you are ready to dive deep into past trauma and explore issues you've identified, I am here to provide you with a safe space to process your thoughts, feelings, experiences, and meet you where you are.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist, my goal is to provide you with the appropriate tools to help you navigate your healing journey. It is important to me that we work collaboratively because YOU are your own expert.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I support and am a part of the LGBTQIA2S+ community. I believe that Black Lives Matter. Nobody is illegal on stolen land. Equity over "Equality".

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: I have over three years of experience in crisis mental health where solution focused therapy was primarily utilized to help clients process and navigate their crises as well as de-escalation.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: I have experience working with individuals experiencing loss, particularly aging older adults, where storytelling and reflection helped to reframe life experiences and create empowering narratives to restore peace and find acceptance.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I provide unconditional positive regard, when appropriate, to support clients on their journey to develop self-acceptance

specialities.name: Suicidal Ideation
specialities.description: I have over three years of experience in crisis mental health. I also completed the Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training (ASIST).

specialities.name: Aging Concerns
specialities.description: I have experience in long-term care settings working with older adults who had a variety of aging concerns including loss of physical functioning and cognitive decline.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I have experiencing working with individuals living with chronic illness and helping them process their grief, as well as helping them navigate healthcare systems.

name: Justin Panneck
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) with a PhD in Health Psychology and an MS in Counseling
ideal_client: My ideal client is someone who is either successful and looking to achieve peak performance and flow states, or someone looking to become personally and professionally successful and feeling stuck or held back by anxiety or poor self-esteem/self-image issues. I like working with folks who are familiar with the more existential, philosophical, and spiritual domains of life and seeking greater life attunement or growth--spiritually, personally, professionally, etc.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I specialize in life coaching, spiritual development, personal growth, getting unstuck, life transitions, career success, self-esteem and self-image, confidence, men’s issues, post-divorce for men. One of my most passionate interests and endeavors is utilizing a unique balance of humor, creativity, and psychological-cultural science. Over the last decade, I have combined my nature-based, psychedelic, and clinical experience toward a focus on optimal living and radical flexibility and achievement, employing peak performance components, which includes such concepts as flow states, “bullet-proof mind” modalities, authenticity, motivational or transformational coaching and behavioral health support (nutrition, movement, etc.).

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: When we get hit by a major life disruption, we often freeze with indecision and fear. The life transition is how we get out unfrozen and move into a period of reinvention and renewal. These transitions may involve confronting our emotions and turning to rituals to put our past behind us; unveiling our new selves and updating our personal stories and mythologies; shedding certain habits, whether mindsets, routines, delusions, or dreams; creating new things, such as new attitudes, aptitudes, skills, talents. These transitional periods can give us superpowers or bog us down. Sometimes the best ideas come from the worst times in our lives. I have spent the last 10 years researching and in some cases facilitating plant medicines and have witnessed some of the most powerful and remarkable healing transformations

name: Fox Convey
title: Professional Counselor
credentials: Masters of Arts in Clincial Psychology (MA), Registered Associate
intro: I am a warm, supportive, and loving presence. I can help support you in creating a life that feels delicious, meaningful, and truly yours.
ideal_client: My ideal client wants to grow, learn, and expand their vision, heart, and community. They are willing to engage in a sincere, humble, and wholehearted investigation of self, others, and their world. They are willing to sit with, confront, and challenge structures and beliefs that are causing harm to both themselves and others. They are looking to create a life that is meaningful and life-giving to both themselves and their communities. They are willing to do the work, in and out of session.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I customize therapy to suit each client's unique presentation, needs, and goals. That being said, the primary therapeutic tool is the relationship we will create together. While I am interested in working with diverse clientele, I am particularly interested in working with gender identity and sexuality exploration, career/community role expansion, emotional literacy, boundaries, self-esteem, identity development, and folx experiencing intersectional marginalization. I have a background in social justice, anti-racism, herbalism, yoga, expressive arts, children and families, and the service industry. I have taught yoga for 10 years, so yogic concepts and body healing certainly have a place in the services I offer. I am invested in my client's overall well-being - the physical, mental, emotional, spiritual, relational, and metaphysical aspects of being-ness intertwined.

approaches.Social Justice Issues We Care About: I care about how systems of oppression have harmed and continue to harm certain groups especially, including but not limited to People of Color & BIPOC, women/womxn, LGBTQQIP2SAA+, low-income individuals, prisoners, the disabled, and senior citizens. No one is free until we all are free. I am an active member of the queer community and the Black Lives Matter community. I volunteer for The Council for Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (CEDI), an activist group I cofounded to help fight racism in higher education. To learn more about our work, check out our website: www.thecedicircle.com. In the past, I volunteered through community herbalism with Herbs for Activists.

name: Amber Liechty
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: If you're a teen (in high school) or parent of an adolescent, teens are the heart of my work at Deep Space.
ideal_client: Teen life can be overwhelming, confusing, and exciting all at once. Their internal and external climate is chock-full of newness, opportunities for growth, as well as potential pitfalls. They want guidance from a trusted adult outside of their circles who sees them accurately, speaks their language, and takes them on a journey of self-discovery to arm them for the real world. My rough-around-the-edges, direct approach facilitates that journey in a compassionate, secure and humorous way.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I offer group therapy for teens in high school. Since group therapy out-performs individual therapy in research, I prioritize my schedule for teen therapy groups (some individual therapy on a case by case basis). For my fellow colleagues: I hold a masters in dual-diagnosis (mood/addiction/eating disorders) from Lewis & Clark College. I have since worked in co-occurring addiction and mental health social services treating eating disorders and addiction at the following institutions: Oregon Youth Authority, Community Services NW, Sound Mental Health, and Harborview Trauma Hospital in Seattle, WA. In addition to continuing education in ACT and Harm Reduction, I received extensive specialty training in Radically Open DBT from Abri RODBT (clinic in Portland, OR).

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: If you are looking for a therapist that is a little rough around the edges in terms of demeanor and language while having high-level knowledge of the issues you struggle with, I'd be your therapist. I can be validating but am also one to challenge my clients with difficult questions - humor/sarcasm also plays a big role in my therapeutic approach. Check out my website for more info!

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: I have extensive training in body image and eating disorders, with primary experience in disorders of over control - namely anorexia and body dysmorphia.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: Body confidence goes hand in hand with sexual confidence. I lean in an Esther Perel direction (Google her, she's amazing) and have enjoyed her trainings. I've found that many of my clients benefit from having both body image and sexual empowerment folded into their treatment.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I personally struggle with ADHD, was diagnosed my first year of college and have gone most of my life unmedicated. I have learned and been educated in organizational systems (both mentally and hands-on) that lead to a successful and happy life. Do yourself a favor and get a "time timer."

name: Karin Pfeiffer-Robinson
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Accessible and culturally respectful mental health counseling for adults and teens over 16. In-person, outdoors, or through telehealth.
ideal_client: I honor who you are. I'm committed to providing a safe space where you can be understood and supported as you explore your experiences and change in helpful ways. I am especially passionate about working with clients who are in their late teens and early 20's, a time of life that brings a lot of challenges as well as a chance for a great deal of discovery and growth. That said, I enjoy working with clients who are going through significant changes in their lives, at any age.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I graduated with an M.A. in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis & Clark College. Prior to becoming a mental health counselor, I worked with Latina women and their children as a case manager in a transitional housing program as well as with Latinx farmers, both in Paraguay and in the Portland Metro area. My approach is guided by relational cultural theory, attachment theory, and ecotherapy. These philosophies recognize that each person is part of larger social, cultural, and environmental contexts that influence and impact them greatly. I utilize somatic therapy, parts work, EMDR, and mindful self-compassion in my work with clients. More important than a specific theory or approach, for counseling to be effective it is essential that you feel respected, safe, and understood by your therapist. I offer free 20-minute initial consultations for anyone interested in becoming a client, to see if this would be a good fit.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe that you know yourself better than anyone else does. Sometimes that inner wisdom can feel obscured. Painful life experiences and systemic oppression can lead to mental health challenges. Therapy is one avenue for reconnecting with yourself, with your values, and with others. I recognize that the field of mental health counseling has its roots in serving the dominant, white culture in the U.S. Access to nature has also traditionally been much more available for middle to upper-middle class, able-bodied white people than for anyone else. I started my private practice, Fern Path Counseling, to be one small part of changing mental health care to better align with social justice values and the rights of all people to access mental health care that they deserve.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Our bodies hold so much wisdom. And yet, many of us have learned how to disconnect from them as a way to avoid feeling pain and other intense emotions. It is possible to rebuild your connection, gradually and safely, with the feelings your body holds. I often weave together somatic therapy with parts work, informed by Internal Family Systems therapy, and find that this helps clients access their internal experience in deep, meaningful ways.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing) therapy through the EMDR Institute. An evidence-based treatment for addressing trauma, depression, anxiety, and a variety of other concerns, I have found EMDR therapy to be a powerful and helpful approach that can lead to lasting change.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Technology and the pace of our modern world often brings us out of ourselves and out of the present moment. The practice of being mindful and approaching ourselves with an open, compassionate curiosity has the ability to dramatically shift our relationships, both with ourselves and with others. Scientific research also shows that mindfulness leads to lasting, positive changes in the brain.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: In my work with clients, and in my own life, I have observed that it is very common to feel overwhelmed and confused by our emotions and to judge them negatively. Developing the ability to recognize, accept, and address our emotions can be the basis of a more grounded and meaningful life.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: I completed courses in Ecopsychology and Ecotherapy at Lewis & Clark College while in the professional mental health counseling M.A. program. During my graduate internship, I worked with individual clients of all ages at a nature-based therapy agency. I bring this expertise to my work with clients whether sessions take place outdoors, indoors, or through telehealth, if it is something that is important to you.

name: Roger Tunks
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I'm a Board Certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
ideal_client: Roger sees patients from school-aged to 64, specializing in people struggling with focus, inattention, depressive thoughts, anxiety, and mood irregularities. He has 8 years of nursing experience working in emergency departments and ICUs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: He has 8 years of nursing experience working in emergency departments and ICUs. It was in those environments that he witnessed first-hand the effects of people struggling with mental illness who were unable to get the support before it became a crisis. Realizing the need for mental health services, he continued his education as a PMHNP. His hope is to help people understand what is causing their struggles and how to achieve a higher level of mental health before it comes a crisis. Roger sees psychiatry as a collaboration where the patient brings the knowledge of their lived experiences and unique symptoms while he brings his knowledge of mental health diagnoses and treatments. Together they are able to collaborate to create an individualized treatment plan.

name: Anat LeBlanc
title: Professional Counselor
credentials: MA Transpersonal Psychology, CBC Grief Practitioner, Hakomi
intro: Hi, I'm Anat — grief therapist, death and dying guide and soul midwife
ideal_client: Have you been uprooted by a life-limiting diagnosis or significant life event? Are you revisiting an ancient wound or tending to a fresh loss? Are you facing death, your own or a loved one’s? I support folks who are grieving, facing a new diagnosis, or confronting their mortality.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With deep compassion, a courageous heart and a warm and calming presence, I companion individuals and families through grief and loss, personal transformation, chronic illness and the mysteries of death and dying. Combining years as an interfaith hospital chaplain with potent personal experience, a deeply empathic heart and skills from neuroscience, mindfulness and meditative practice, I honor the holistic and somatic impact of loss, and the challenges of personal growth. Together we will hold space for your deeper story to unfold.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I graduated with a Master's degree from Sofia University in Transpersonal Psychology in 2010 and in 2013 completed a residency year of post-graduate training at Emanuel Medical Center (Clinical Pastoral Education) where I served on staff several years as an interfaith chaplain before joining OHSU's Bridges Pediatric Palliative Care team in 2017. I have deepened my practice with the M.E.T.A. Institute, studying Hakomi, a somatic and mindfulness based therapeutic modality and is a certified Compassionate Bereavement Care provider through the MISS Foundation. Working at a level 1 trauma center has given me extensive experience in companioning families and individuals through traumatic events, acute crisis and sudden loss, providing a warm and calming and presence for those facing significant life changes.

name: Catherine Blanchard
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi. Welcome to my PTC page.

name: Scott Dupuis
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I work with kids and adolescents over come the challenges and difficulties they are having.
ideal_client: I work with kids and adolescents, helping them understand their emotions and needs while laying the foundation for a brighter future. I draw on person-centered therapy and a variety of counseling techniques, including play therapy and cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), to best support each individual’s journey. https://forms.gle/FFqXLMMwxtpbrwYG7

approaches.My Background: Scott earned a Master’s degree of Counseling Psychology from St. Thomas University in 2014. His previous experience includes: • Mental health therapist in a school setting working with kids age 5-11 in Minneapolis, MN • Mental health therapist working with adolescents in high school in Minneapolis, MN • Outpatient mental health therapist working with adults in Minneapolis, MN

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Scott was born and raised in Aurora, IL and has also lived in Minnesota before moving to Oregon. His interest are: • Bread making (Sourdough fanatic) • Cooking • Soccer • Reading • Gardening

name: Kelsey Huber
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I provide specialized treatment designed to heal and help you live life to your fullest potential
ideal_client: Through our work together we can help release stuck patterns and increase understanding. I specialize in complex trauma treatment, behavior change, maladaptive coping strategies, anxiety, and depression. I believe in looking at the whole self through a lens of kindness and self-compassion. We will examine and break down the roots of why you're not feeling fully satisfied with your life and we'll partner together to move towards healing and strength in both a comfortable and challenging manner.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach incorporates being your advocate while working to challenge you to bring about change and growth. I endorse acceptance of the self by digging into the why's of behavior. I am trained in EMDR and have done extensive research regarding somatic and behavioral therapies. I conduct trauma informed care and social justice oriented care in order to bring about regulation to the body. I bring in aspects of motivational interviewing, somatic therapy, person-centered, relational, psychodynamic theory, narrative therapy, and existential therapy to customize a therapeutic approach that would be most beneficial to you as an individual. I am always open to feedback from my clients in order to shift what might not be working for them so we can make this the most effective use of your time.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Working with clients in their healing journey is the highest honor. It's my personal belief that we all have the strength to change, grow, and heal. We will work together to design and implement a plan to heal and help you live life to your fullest potential. I would love for you to send a message sharing a bit about what you want support in as well as times that work to connect. Looking forward to meeting and working with you! I spend my off time as Treasurer and board member of The Equi Institute, a nonprofit working to enrich the health of the Trans, Queer, Gender Diverse and Intersex communities through trauma-informed and culturally affirming care and social justice advocacy. I am originally from LA, but have found my home in the Pacific Northwest. I love baseball, all things horror, painting, traveling, weightlifting, and listening to the rain while enveloped in a good book.

name: Laurie Kress
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I provide individual counseling for adults living in Oregon and Washington as well as clinical supervision to MSW CSWA's in Oregon.
ideal_client: I work with adult individuals seeking support for issues including life transitions and adjustments, loss and grief, anxiety, and depression. I'm seeing clients primarily on Mondays both in-person and via Telehealth.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I’ve had the privilege of working with individuals, couples, families, and groups in my over 25 years of experience as an LCSW in the mental health field. I’ve worked in a wide range of practice settings including outpatient mental health clinics, community mental health, bereavement program, crisis intervention, and at-risk youth services. I draw from an eclectic mix of therapeutic frameworks and techniques including Acceptance Commitment Therapy, Dialectical Behavior Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, and Interpersonal Neurobiology, among others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My style is warm, collaborative, client-centered and trauma-informed. I strive to create a safe, respectful and supportive environment, honoring the intrinsic wisdom and strength of all my clients.

name: Alicia Turgesen
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: My goal is to empower you! If you're ready to find your voice and regain your confidence then let's work together to get you there!
ideal_client: Do you want to feel confident in who you are? If you answered "yes", then perhaps it's time we talk! As a therapist, one of my main goals is to help you feel confident and empowered in who you are. We'll do this through talk, art, and exploring all the ways you're unique. It's natural that our confidence ebs and flows (becoming a parent, starting a new job, or being in a new relationship) but if you're reading this you're probably ready to bring that confidence back! Let's chat!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I've found every client to be different in what they need to heal. Some need to talk and feel heard while others just want to feel validated in who they are. With that, my approach to you will be just as unique as you are. We will collaborate to find what works for you! My work is influenced by many different models but is deeply rooted in the workings of Internal Family Systems, Expressive Arts Therapy (including SoulCollage®), Emotionally Focused Therapy, and Experiential Therapy. With these perspectives in mind, I create a space for you to explore you inner and outer world, to create meaning through art, and to find your voice in a space the is validating, affirming, and empowering.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: If you're ready to feel confident, to find your voice, to explore and understand more about who you are, then I may be the right fit for you! My passion for therapy is driven by the people I call my clients. They each have a story to tell, and when I'm lucky enough to witness their healing and transformation, there's truly nothing more gratifying. I am committed to supporting each and every client - when a client walks in, ready to heal, there's no limit to what they'll do and how they'll grow! I'm a cis-woman, mother, partner, friend, sister, therapist. I've gone through challenges, much as we all have, and through my own experience in therapy and healing, rediscovered who I am. To have felt disempowered, to then regain that power for myself, is what fuels my work with people. I earned a Masters of Arts in Marriage and Family Therapy and a Certificate in Ecopsychology from Lewis & Clark College. Recently, I earned my credential in SoulCollage®.

name: Kara Kazemba
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi there, I'm Kara. As a therapist, I'm here to support you with my blunt approach and healthy amount of swearing.
ideal_client: I tend to work with folks who say they had a "messed up childhood" but are "totally over it". Or, maybe they don't recognize their childhood stuff until they are swapping stories with someone, only to discover their formative years weren't "typical", so to speak. What we tend to see in day-to-day life is people pleasing, struggles with boundaries, relationship fears, and/or chronic overachievers.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I'm a former CPS social worker, which lends me to really appreciate how early childhood experiences tend to shape how we show up in the world today. With that understanding, I use a variety of modalities including attachment, DBT, EMDR, and somatic experiencing- tailoring your therapy to fit you and how your brain operates. After the free consultation, we would do a "life story" session, where I come to understand the circumstances bringing you to therapy. At the end of that appointment we discuss your hopes and goals- AKA how will you know if you get to "fire" me? Then we come up with a "treatment plan" together- talking about how we will get there in our sessions together. As I mentioned before, I am blunt. My approach does include taking a look at how you contribute to patterns and situations. Then, the plan is to provide you with tools and supports to break those cycles.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I became a social worker because of the person-in-environment perspective that the profession takes. As a counselor, I need to appreciate that you can't heal in the same environment that made you sick. That means being mindful of not only direct interpersonal trauma, but trauma at the macro level as well. I try as hard as possible to be anti-racist and LGBTQ+ affirming, and where I falter or fall short I will 100 percent own that. I am active in the LGBTQ+ community and sit on my local chamber's diversity council.

name: Megan Lammers
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
credentials: LCSW licensed in Oregon and Washington
intro: As a Mental Health Therapist I truly believe that we all inherently have the capacity for deep healing within ourselves.
ideal_client: Are you searching to deepen your connection with yourself? To heal past wounds so you can life more fully in the now? Do you struggle with cycles of shame or feeling disconnected to yourself or your body? I work with clients to help deeply heal old patterns that are no longer serving them. We work together to identify patterns of shame, "stuckness" and then to gently and slowly rework these patterns into most sustainable ways of being that center truly loving one self as you are, right now.

approaches.My Background and Approach: As a Mental Health Therapist, a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) in Oregon and Washington my practice is rooted in culturally affirming, intuitive and trauma-informed mind-body healing, using somatic noticing, mindfulness and narrative, or story. I believe in the value of cultural and ethnic diversity, and it is my personal and professional mission to end discrimination, oppression, poverty, and other forms of social injustice for all people. My approach to health and wellness is to support every clients’ intuitive body awareness. This is only reached through liberation from diet culture and through somatic embodiment. I will never support diet culture and will not engage in any interactions with clients that promote body shame. I am a Certified Brainspotting Clinician. Brainspotting offers us a deeply healing experience and is something I love sharing with my clients.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I see my role in my clients healing process as helping to elicit and support a deep connection between one's mind, body and spirit. I do not believe humans are in need of 'fixing'. Rather, I believe that we all have within us what we need and that we all benefit from having compassionate support to find and embrace our own strengths. All humans have stories to tell. Each story we carry is rooted in our ancestors. I believe therapists must honor intergenerational trauma and provide space to allow for and elicit whole self healing. I enjoy getting out into our beautiful NW forests, rivers and oceans to hike, play and relax. I am an avid fan of soccer and most other sports. I believe it's vitally important to enjoy good food, to spend time with the people we love and for each of us to find our own unique ways to be present in our lives.

name: Katie Clark, LMHC, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I honor your values, views, experiences, and goals, and I will make every effort to develop a true understanding of you.
ideal_client: My clients are often highly motivated to make changes in their lives. Not content to keep sitting in the swirl of anxiety or depression, they want tools and support in making progress in areas of life most meaningful to them.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a solution-focused, cognitive-behavioral therapist, my goal is to help you uncover your true potential and lead a life worth celebrating. While you can't change difficult situations of the past, we can work together to better understand and resolve the challenges in your life. By applying complementary therapy approaches and techniques, we will unearth long-standing behavior patterns or negative perceptions that may be holding you back from experiencing a more fulfilling, balanced, and meaningful life. I will work to build an individualized treatment plan in collaboration with you, so you can get the most from our time together.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Nationally Certified Counselor (NCC), Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), and Licensed Mental Health Counselor (LMHC) registered with the states of Oregon and Washington. I conduct myself and my services in accordance with the ethics and guidelines set forth from the Washington and Oregon Boards of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists, as well as the ACA Ethical Code of the Oregon Counseling Association and the American Counseling Association. I am also a member of the ACA. I have a Master’s degree in Counseling Psychology from Pacific University and a Bachelor’s degree in Psychology with an emphasis in Business Administration from UCLA. In addition to my education and clinical training, I have significant and varied professional and life experiences to draw on in service of the needs of my clients.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive-behavioral therapy is considered among the most rapid in terms of results obtained. What enables CBT to be briefer is its highly instructive nature and the fact that it makes use of homework assignments. CBT is time-limited in that we help clients understand at the very beginning of the therapy process that there will be a point when the formal therapy will end.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: ACT is a mindfulness based method of treating anxiety and other disorders and challenges. It's empirically supported and proven to be effective.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: If you are struggling with a specific issue, SFBT is effective in finding an effective way to address it.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Methods of treatment used are evidence-based, supported by research, and by the American Psychological Association (APA). Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, and Exposure and Response Prevention are the most scientifically supported methods of treating anxiety, so are the main methods I use in working with clients.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: Methods of treatment used are evidence-based, supported by research, and by the American Psychological Association (APA). Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, and Exposure and Response Prevention are the most scientifically supported methods of treating OCD, so are the main methods I use in working with clients.

specialities.name: Social Phobia
specialities.description: Methods of treatment used are evidence-based, supported by research, and by the American Psychological Association (APA). Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, and Exposure and Response Prevention are the most scientifically supported methods of treating social anxiety, so are the main methods I use in working with clients.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Methods of treatment used are evidence-based, supported by research, and by the American Psychological Association (APA). Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy are highly effective in helping shift relationship issues, so are the main methods I use in working with clients.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Methods of treatment used are evidence-based, supported by research, and by the American Psychological Association (APA). Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy are highly effective in living with pain and illness, so are the main methods I use in working with clients.

name: Michaela Rushing
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I work to help people make meaningful change in their lives.
ideal_client: As you navigate life you may find that your current habits and coping skills are no longer helping. Sometimes when you build skills to help you survive a difficult situation you later realize those skills are no longer serving you. It is important to remember that you have the ability to change if you want to. I work with individuals (adults) who want to overcome symptoms of anxiety, depression, and trauma and create real change in their life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize a person-centered, compassion-focused approach to help you learn how to support yourself and make the positive changes you want to make in your life.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a therapist after going through therapy as a teenager for an anxiety disorder, and realizing how important finding the right therapist is for the therapy process. I also genuinely enjoying hearing peoples stories and helping them process their emotions.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I focused my studies on working with adult who experienced childhood trauma or neglect. I am able to help adults navigate the difficult task of sorting through their past and discovering new ways to move forward.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have worked with many people struggling in their current relationship or the end of their relationship.

name: Anna Belle Marin, Ph.D., LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: You deserve support from someone who believes you can succeed. I offer therapy where you feel safe, heard and accepted. I collaborate with you in discovering and using resources so you effectively change your life. This is your life and path. I serve as your guide to take steps to being your best.

approaches: I provide therapy that is tailored to your unique situation, whether you experience depression, anxiety, unresolved trauma, relationship problems, or any other issues that keep you from being your best. You need good nervous system regulation to cope with life’s challenges. I use an eclectic, holistic approach with body-centered, mindful therapies so you can increase your capacity to manage life’s difficulties. Therapies I offer include: Somatic Experiencing: body-centered therapy for nervous system integration; EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing): for trauma healing so you can move beyond past triggers; Depth Psychology and Dream work to uncover your unconscious strengths so you can navigate life with purpose and joy; and the Prepare-Enrich on-line inventory: a tool to help couples at any relationship stage including marriage preparation. My goal in therapy is to empower you to identify and use effective skills to enhance your daily life.

I am a life-long learner and infuse therapy sessions with curiosity and fresh approaches to help you identify, initiate and complete steps on your unique life path. I have developed my love and curiosity for people traveling the world from a very young age. So, I draw on a wealth of life experience, my passionate curiosity and diverse education to serve you. My experience and skills include: Licensed Professional Counselor, LPC, OR Board of Licensed Prof. Counselors & Therapists, #C3008; National Certified Counselor, #290484, M.A in Counseling Psychology from Pacifica Graduate Institute, Carpinteria, CA with a focus on marriage and family therapy and depth psychology, Ph.D. in Food Science with a minor in Psychology from Cornell U., Ithaca, NY.

name: Kyan Osher
title: Professional Counselor
intro: I’m a warm and genuine therapist My goal is to help people accept their whole being so that they can cultivate a life with joy and purpose

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My foundation to counseling is a Humanistic or “person-centered” approach. I believe that all humans have an innate wisdom and that it’s my role to help my clients discover their own path. I have great respect for each person’s individual process and employ multiple techniques to facilitate that discovery, including mindfulness, cognitive behavioral therapy, family systems therapy, internal family systems therapy and interpersonal therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a Masters of Arts (MA) degree in Counseling from Pacific University in Oregon. I received a Bachelor's degree in Nutrition and Pre-Medicine from California Polytechnic University. In addition to my eduction and clinical training, I have some varied life experiences to help me counsel my clients.

name: Mike Grant
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I specialize in assisting folks w/ performance & life goals, including sports/career/creative goals as well as trauma and addiction support.
ideal_client: If you struggle with intrusive thoughts and challenging emotions that get in the way of your goals then I may be able to assist with this. Also if you have unprocessed trauma or difficulty in abstaining from substances/behaviors than we should talk.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I have training in trauma therapies including EMDR and Brainspotting which can be used to assist in processing trauma in a safe, effective way. I also teach HeartMath which can assist with managing stress and developing resiliency. I’m also an athlete and coach and understand the specific challenges that impede performance goals and work with a range of folks who want to be present so they can have peak performance.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe that therapy doesn’t always need to be so serious, laughter and joy are important to overall wellbeing. Let’s do some hard work but also enjoy the process some. I also believe that there needs to be more customer service in therapy, with flexibility and understanding. I try to meet you where you are and if mistakes happen, let’s chat and figure out the best solutions.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I’m a certified alcohol and drug counselor with 8 years in the field.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I specialize in peak performance for athletes, creatives, and business leaders. Our own thinking prevents us from reaching goals that are attainable, I can help.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I assist trauma processing with EMDR and Brainspotting.

name: Korina Jochim
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Through self-compassion and empathy, all things are possible.
ideal_client: Are you healing from an abusive relationship or other systems of control? Do you find yourself googling "narcissistic abuse" "coercive control?" or "high-control groups"? Are you struggling with a narcissistic parent, partner, boss, or exploitative spiritual group? Have you felt powerless, unable to move forward? If you're trying to create wellness and balance, we can work together to help you create safe boundaries and move into healthier relationships...first with yourself.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach with my clients is one of collaboration and strong teamwork. I favor a directive, psychoeducational way of working with my clients and believe in empowering them with knowledge and tools. As a therapist I join each of my client's in their subjective world, endeavoring to understand them deeply and support their process, whatever their healing or life goals may be. Because we are all different, I don't work the same way with everyone, and adapt my approach to the needs of my clients. What therapy is to each person is a unique experience. Some need to resolve a crisis or grapple with a life transition or loss. Others want to focus on perceived blocks to moving forward into a state of greater mental wellness. Still others need to re-work their difficult attachments to early caregivers and require a longer therapeutic relationship. After a therapeutic relationship has been established, I make myself available to my clients for booster sessions when the need arises.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Prior to my psychotherapy career I was a journalist and professional writer. People's stories have always been what compelled me and drove me to understand and connect on a deeper level. In graduate school I focused on equity and inclusion, addictions and trauma, and my earlier career experience was in residential and outpatient treatment. Gradually I began to focus on intersectional approaches to mental health and have experience in treating mood disorders, abuse recovery, addictions, grief and loss, and negative relationship patterns. As a Marriage and Family therapist I view individuals as inextricably linked to the systems and groups of which they are a part. I am trained in trauma-informed care and mindfulness modalities such as third-wave CBT. In my free time I blog about intimate partner violence and other systems of control and advocate for abuse survivors.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I utilize a technique and approach known as Mentalizing, which was developed in the UK to treat complex trauma, and is still largely unknown in the U.S. Mentalizing is an imaginative process in which we are able to understand ourselves, and how our minds interact and conceptualize the minds of others. Our ability to Mentalize well allows us to accurately understand the intentions of others, as well as how to better understand how we are viewed by others. It is essential for healthy relationships

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Trained by Francine Shapiro (EMDR founder)'s organization EMDRIA in Levels I and II EMDR, I utilize this method with my clients who are addressing specific traumatic memories that continue to trouble them. EMDR is best utilized when clients have some relative stability and are not undergoing a current depressive episode or active substance abuse. It is a helpful tool in moving traumatic events to the background as a "footnote" in one's story and not the foreground of your life.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I practice third-wave CBT, which is a more modern, mindfulness-based form of CBT. In CBT we address long-standing automatic negative thoughts that stem from core beliefs we may need to re-tool. It is based on the theory that changing your thinking changes your feelings, which in turn adjusts behavior. It involves task and homework and is an excellent tool for reducing anxiety and depression.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: Also known as solution-focused, coaching is a more directive approach that helps to achieve specific, measurable goals that are defined by the client. We work on identifying goals aligned with your values, resources available, barriers to past achievement of goals, "chunking" tasks, creating timelines and accountability. Some common problems that benefit from coaching are career and education goals, wellness, leaving difficult relationships, and cultivating healthy relationships and behaviors.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: Theoretically I favor an object relations approach as popularized by psychotherapists Melanie Klein, Anna Freud, Calr Jung, Donald Winicott, and Heinz Kohut. I've also been highly influenced by existentialist psychiatrists Irvin Yalom and Viktor Frankl. Psychedelic integration work is also an area in which I have experience and enthusiasm, especially for trauma and depression. I will work with you on the integration/understanding of psychedelic experiences.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: If you have noticed a pattern of codependency in your relationships (family, work, intimate partners) and/or have experienced harm from relationships with people who suffer from addictions or personality disorders, I can help you empower yourself to make more self-caring choices and develop your own emotional life, goals, and community.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: I offer safety and empowerment counseling to survivors of intimate partner violence (IPV), interfamilial abuse, psychological, spiritual (high-control groups) and narcissistic abuse. Please note that I do not treat offenders.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Whether you suffer from major depression or trauma-driven depression, you need a plan, support, and education to help get through depression episodes successfully. I also offer CBT for thought re-framing related to depression recovery.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Issues pertaining specifically to women and femme persons including trauma, codependency, abuse, systemic oppression, and empowerment.

name: DeShawn Williams
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Welcome! I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker who believes in joining with clients as they embark upon new discoveries of themselves and those around them. My goal is to assist with raising hope and new perspectives in the clients I serve. I am here to serve the worried well and worried heart.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My philosophy is there are no two individuals alike nor are two families alike. Therefore, my practice is more integrated utilizing multiple treatment orientation depending on the need of the client. I primarily work through a CBT, psychodynamic lens however; I do like to use other orientation ex. mindfulness, narrative therapy, motivational interviewing, etc. I believe that everyone can benefit from support and that is exactly what I provide. I am a proponent of counseling not because this is the work that I do, but those who attend counseling as a preventative save themselves time and money in the long-run. Simply put, counseling is for us all no matter what stage of life we reside. I employ the idea of us working together and taking a journey that may appear to be rough in the beginning, but the rough places will soon be made straight. As we journey together in agreement there lies hopeful, fulfilled, enlightened road ahead.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Portland, Oregon native. I have been working in this field with young people and families for 15 years. I obtain my Master Degree in Social Work, and my undergraduate in Administrative Justice. I am board certified Clinical Social Worker. I have experience in treating Anxiety Disorders, Depression, working with families and clients who have experienced their first episode of psychosis. I have worked extensively with multi-cultured, multi ethnic and disenfranchised families. I have spent many years working with families in the Salem area as an Intensive Services Therapist and in Multnomah County Schools offering individual and family therapy, group work, culturally specific services, trainings and consultations. I am trainer of ASIST (Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training) Youth Mental Health First Aid, and I am certified to do SIPS (Structured Instrument for Prodromal Syndrome) screening. I enjoy seeing families and individuals find hope in the midst of chaos.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: For individuals or families needing to talk about the challenges they are faced with which can be more crisis oriented or time limited will benefit from a more solution focused or problem-solving approach. I work to focus on the challenges at hand rather the past. In addition I work to assist with getting families to their desired goals in their desired time frame.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I often integrate psychodynamic approach into my sessions to assist with bringing awareness to clients who are often stuck. I believe many things are revealed during a session which is unconscious to the client but is very telling to the therapist. Through careful examination the recognition of these unconscious acts can be very liberating and bring enlightment to client and or family.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT is one of the most common practiced and evidenced-based therapies among psychotherapies. Following my master's level training in social work I underwent another two years of supervision utilizing this treatment. This therapy is scientific and teaches skills that can be generalized across life situations. This therapy is very powerful to bring desired change in one’s life.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Families inherently have multiple systems and sub-systems. I work with families to help them understand their unique family system, the roles each member plays, and how these roles are interdependent. I like to have families explore and discover their roles and how they are contributors to the overall system and functionality.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: I believe that self-esteem plays a huge role in who we are as individuals and how we see ourselves in this world. Individuals struggling with concerns of their self-esteem will journey together with me to uncover where a self-esteem injury occurred, and evaluate how to move past the injury. Through self inventories and discovery a new you will emerge.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: This disorder is gaining more recognized and identified in many individuals who have experienced a traumatic event. I have treated many individuals in my years of practice who are in great pain as a result of trauma. I utilize a very empathetic, attentive, and structured approach that creates an environment for healing and recovery for those who knowingly need it and those who are unaware.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is almost inevitable, especially is this fast-paced world that we live in. As a therapist who successfully treats anxiety, I work along side you to bring you to a place of calm, by identifying the source, slowing down the thinking and utilizing grounding techniques. CBT approach is great for allowing your to re-gain control often lost by anxiety.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: The bulk of my experience has been working with youth and families who are struggling with depression. Depression for young people often looks different in adults. Youth who are acting out at home or school, and is often irritable or angry may be in conflict with feelings of depression. I work with youth and families to identify sources of these complicated feelings and utilize CBT a to treat them

name: Deborah Nichols LPC, NCC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help anxious mamas stop the unrelenting cycle of guilt, shame, and controlling behavior.
ideal_client: As a mom, you experience the seemingly never-ending roller coaster of ups and downs and it’s A LOT, sometimes too much. You may be fed up with feeling utterly lost from the person you used to be before you became a mom, feeling disconnected from your partner and your friendships or conflicted, and filled with anxiety. You might not even remember a time when things didn’t feel this way. But one thing is for sure: you’re ready for some relief. You’re ready to discover yourself again.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Clients come to me looking for a therapist who is in it, because therapy should be a place where you feel seen and understood. Sessions with me don't always look the same. We tailor each session to your needs so that together, we nurture and empower you to move towards being the mom you have always known you could be.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a certified anxiety treatment professional and mother of two, I believe that your anxiety is telling you something. Your body is telling you something. Something must change. You don’t have to continue to suffer with the constant worry, and you don’t have to do it alone. Contact me today for a free 30-minute consultation. I can’t wait to hear from you.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I work from a cognitive behavioral model to challenge unhelpful patterns and create new ways of coping with the challenges you are facing.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Trained in part one and part two ACT training to work with our thoughts, how we respond to the situations and elements of our lives that we may not be able to change.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: By helping clients develop a mindfulness practice, I assist in creating sustainable and lasting change grounded in awareness.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: In working with clients that have experienced trauma that is impacting their lives, I will utilize EMDR as an intervention to allow reprocessing. I have completed Part I & II EMDRIA EMDR trainings.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: My approach to therapy with expecting and new moms comes from a place of compassion and understanding: knowing that you don’t have to lose yourself when you become a mother; you can move through motherhood with confidence meeting the challenges as they come.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Mom-ing is hard. That’s the truth. It’s the anxious spiraling thoughts, the heart pounding deep pit in your stomach and the constant need to control all the things that are constantly taking from you. Working with a therapist can really help you to identify the areas that are creating your anxiety, and give you tools and strategies to manage it effectively.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety doesn't have to be what drives you to get sh*t done. You will learn what really matters to you and put your energy into the places where it counts. We’ll find the areas that bring healthy motivation for you and identify the patterns and fuel that are not serving you.

name: Audrianna J. Gurr
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: LPC License and CADCI certificate, CDWF certificate
intro: I am a CBT, DBT, Gottman trained counselor and a Certified Daring Way ™ Facilitator (Brené Brown) in Portland, Oregon.
ideal_client: My treatment approach is to provide support with insight and feedback to help clients address current challenges and long-standing issues. I specialize in maternal mental health challenges (miscarriage, infant loss, new parenting, difficult births), menopause processing, grief and loss, trauma, shame resilience, anxiety, depression, assertiveness training and addictions work (both substances and behaviors). I do shame resilience based curriculum as a Certified Daring Way Facilitator.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is described as active and supportive. I work with clients to address current issues and long-standing challenges. Applying sensitivity, empathy and compassion, I help individuals bring resolution to a wide range of life challenges and clinical psychological issues. I work with each client to find the appropriate match for your needs regarding the challenges you are facing. Our work will be active, I ask a lot of questions and we will discuss your answers to help you best help yourself. From time to time I use handouts, online resources and to supplement our work. I utilize an approach of applied empathy to help you feel safe and in time, confident to discuss your concerns. I'm trained in shame resilience, do a lot of assertiveness, cognitive reframing work as well as unpacking life experiences around maternal and menopause journeys as well as grief and loss along the life span, not just losing people, but lives changes and those effects on you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I specialize in maternal mental health challenges (miscarriage, infant loss, new parenting, difficult births), grief and loss, trauma, shame resilience, assertiveness training and addictions (both substances and behaviors) as well as perimenopause work. With an integration various methods, drawing from a selection of styles and techniques to apply what is most helpful for each individual. Together with each client I work to build on strengths and achieve life goals.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: My longstanding practice involves exploring how our thoughts, feelings, actions and behaviors effect each other every day. In our work we identify thinking errors that can harm us in our work to resolve conflicts in our relations and within self esteem challenges. I am also certified in Brene' Brown's work which involves exploring our thought processes and how they can hinder us.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I am Gottman level one trained clinician. This work can be done individually or in couples work. The content is also applicable to new families with new or additional children in helping the parents communicate in a healthy and effect ways during this time of change and transition in their lives. This can also be applied in grief and loss work.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: Our work can be centered on identifying and working towards resolution on a current or persistent issue that is interfering with your current life healthy balance. Sometimes this may lead to deeper unpacking of issues but, initially it is about problem solving and stability.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I work with women at all stages in their lives. I have particular training and background with perinatal mental health challenges including infertility, infant loss, new parents, new identities and mom and parenting challenges as well as those in the perimenopause arch. I have been working with the Baby Blues Connection and Brief Encounters organization for over 10 years and work with clients individually, a couples and in groups.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Self Esteem encompasses so many areas of our lives...communication, relating, making plans/goals in our close relationships and in our communities of work, family and play. I am certified in Brene' Brown's curriculum of Shame Resilience to help us sort out the details and live our fuller and happier life.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: We all experience loss in our lives whether it is the loss of an influential person, job or experience. We even experience loss and grief with 'good' things happen, we move, have the birth or adoption of a child, get a new job, etc. We often need help and compassion to sort through the various feelings and process the steps to help us move into places of acceptance of our new situations.

name: Rebecca Lundberg
title: Student Counselor
intro: I strive to bring deep empathy, humor, warmth, and an open heart into every session.
ideal_client: I warmly welcome individuals, couples, families, children, and teens seeking support. My clients come to me with a wide array of concerns, including anxiety, depression, grief and loss, relationship issues, religious trauma, and the challenges associated with chronic illness or disability. I also work with those navigating ADHD, gender and sexuality, trauma, identity, and career development.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach is integrative and collaborative, emphasizing connection and compassion. I draw from various modalities, including: *Attachment Theory: examining how interpersonal relationships affect emotional well-being. *Mindfulness: focusing on present-moment awareness. *Relational-Cultural Theory: highlighting the significance of connection in relationships. *Internal Family Systems: aiding individuals in understanding and harmonizing different aspects of themselves. *Art and Play Therapies: fostering expression and healing through creativity. I view counseling as a way to explore the complex ways our bodies and minds adapt to this wild world. Together, we will tune into your experiences and support you as we delve into the core beliefs, values, and narratives that shape your life. Recognizing that there is no one-size-fits-all approach, I am committed to tailoring our process to meet your individual needs and goals on your path to exploration, growth, and healing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My career journey has taken me through diverse experiences, including landscape design, working with at-risk youth, adults facing memory loss, and individuals undergoing physical rehabilitation. Additionally, my background arts education has shaped my perspective on healing and connection. As a native Oregonian, I have come to accept the beauty of soggy hikes and windy beach walks—because who needs sunshine when you have character, right? I deeply believe in the inherent value of our relationships—with ourselves, our loved ones, and our communities. My intention is to create an authentic, affirming space where you feel seen and valued, looking at how various elements of context and culture have shaped your life. Whether you are facing challenges or seeking personal growth, I am here to walk alongside you.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: I have degrees in fine arts and dance, and have worked as an art teacher and certified movement therapist. By encouraging self-expression through various artistic forms, I aim to create a safe and supportive environment where clients can explore their emotions, build confidence, and develop coping skills. This holistic method not only promotes personal growth but also enhances physical awareness and emotional resilience, allowing individuals to connect more deeply with themselves and others.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I have completed extensive training in Attachment Theory, which I apply in my counseling work with individuals and couples. This theory explores how early relationships shape our emotional well-being and influence our interactions throughout life. By helping clients identify their attachment styles—secure, anxious, avoidant, and disorganized—I facilitate awareness of relationship patterns and emotional triggers to foster healthier communication and connection.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I have completed training in IFS therapy, an approach that allows people to identify and engage with different aspects of themselves, fostering self-compassion and healing. By facilitating dialogue between the core "Self" and various internal parts, IFS promotes integration and emotional balance. This model has been effective in addressing issues like trauma, anxiety, and self-esteem, enhancing personal growth and relationships.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I have completed training in Relational Life Therapy with Terry Real, focusing on enhancing emotional intimacy and communication within relationships. Additionally, I trained in Integrative Sex and Couples Counseling with Tammy Nelson, which addresses the interplay between emotional and physical intimacy. I also utilize principles from Emotionally Focused Couples Counseling (EFT) to help couples reformulate their emotional interactions, along with strategies from Imago Therapy.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: In previous work as a certified movement therapist, I provided personalized physical therapy to individuals suffering from chronic pain, injuries, and degenerative conditions. As a counselor, I integrate in somatic approaches, helping individuals tune into their bodies, encouraging them to explore and process deeply held emotions that may be contributing to their distress. This holistic approach also enables individuals to reclaim their physical presence and live more fully in their bodies.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I collaborate with my clients to find the approach that works for them. I may incorporate Relational Cultural Theory to explore the role of relationships in emotional well-being, and Attachment Theory to address patterns formed in early relationships. Additionally, I use Art and Expressive Arts Therapy to facilitate emotional expression and self-discovery. Finally, Internal Family Systems (IFS) helps clients understand and harmonize their inner parts, promoting healing and emotional resilience.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I integrate Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), movement therapy, breathwork, and Internal Family Systems (IFS) to create a comprehensive framework for addressing chronic pain. This approach provides clients with the tools they need to empower themselves and improve their quality of life. I draw on my background in movement and physical therapy, as well as my own experiences of chronic conditions.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: For children, I use play therapy, fostering expression and understanding in a safe environment, and layer in age appropriate skill building and parent education. With adults, I incorporate mindfulness-based stress reduction, ADHD life coaching, and somatic interventions. In addition to present-focused techniques, I emphasize the importance of exploring historical and contextual factors that may intersect with their ADHD experience, as well as trauma, attachment styles, and anxiety.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I help individuals and partners navigate relational issues, including communication, attachment, and sexuality.
