I work with clients from diverse relational orientations including monogamy, ethical non-monogamy, polyamory, and polyfidelity. I focus on enhancing communication skills, emotional intimacy, and an understanding of relational dynamics, empowering clients to build healthier, more fulfilling relationships based on trust and respect.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I counsel clients with diverse religious and spiritual beliefs, guiding them through their identity, values, and sense of belonging. My support extends to individuals firmly rooted in their faith, as well as those who are questioning or dealing with religious or spiritual trauma. I aim to create a safe space for exploration and healing, ensuring that each person's unique journey is respected and valued.

name: Harini Sukumaran
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: My holistic approach to mental health care treats the person as a whole, by integrating the healing of mind and Body using Mindfulness.
ideal_client: Are you worried too much that an anxiety is around the corner? Have you been overwhelmed lately and unable to cope? Maybe you're a parent, feeling lost with your child/teen's behaviors at home? Your child's anxiety & depression may have increased with isolation from friends, adjustment to online schooling, and disruption in schedule. My holistic practices can help reduce your anxiety tremendously. I primarily work with women, children and families using mindfulness as a foundational approach.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I strongly believe in a collaborative, holistic, strength based approach to therapy. I draw out an individual’s unique inner strength and foster optimum physical, emotional and mental health. I listen and respond to each person in a non -judgmental, compassionate way, so that each person feels safe, develops trust and be heard. With children, i routinely uses child centered play therapy, where a child’s play is used as a natural medium for expression of feelings, learn social skills, and learn effective problem solving skills to cope with their difficulties. With children i enhance the play therapy, by weaving in Body Awareness ( Yoga), Mindfulness Meditation , Art Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral therapy and PCIT. With Women & Families, I implement different psychotherapeutic treatment modalities including but not limited to Mindfulness based stress reduction, CBT, Attachment therapy, Internal Family systems, Acceptance Therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My unique qualification in Counseling, Yoga, Ayurveda and Energy healing medicine helps me to treat clients holistically, addressing the physical, emotional and spiritual needs. I have over 10+ years of experience treating women and children in both inpatient and outpatient settings; my specialization includes, treatment of children with behavioral/emotional struggles, women suffering from trauma, depression, anxiety and Pregnancy/Postpartum mood disorders.

name: Edward Quedado
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Where pain can be thought and spoken about, I believe possibility, creativity and change can emerge
ideal_client: I believe psychotherapy is a project between two people where the goal is to make contact with conscious and unconscious sources of emotional pain. Psychotherapy circumscribes a space where what has been denied, unimagined, forgotten, or unspeakable can become imagined, spoken and felt. The process generates a reading of the self that is vastly more dynamic than what our lives often permit, leading to the easing of suffering and the creation of new possibilities.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Psychotherapy is fundamentally an open space, an invitation. There is a freedom to it that takes courage and tolerance. It can involve a deconstructive or constructive momentum where you may not necessarily be told what to do or how to feel. I provide a space that is confidential, patient and curious to allow us to experience what comes to mind and indeed, what does not.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My personal belief is that all people should have access to long-term, deep psychotherapy. The origins of the field at one point lived up to this promise, and I believe that we should continue to honor this history by treating the psychotherapeutic relationship as a place where political, cultural and psychological strains can all converge and mix. Please feel free to get in touch about sliding scale options; it is something I am open to discussing.

name: Eileen Summit
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I work with women who are facing life transitions, health issues and loss. I believe each woman has the inner strength needed to heal.
ideal_client: Life is full of challenges. Some are exciting, while others are difficult. Everyone needs support when experiencing stress, pain, sadness, or fear. I specialize in working with women, 21-101 yrs, who are experiencing anxiety or depression, struggling to overcome negative thought patterns and interactions, or facing serious health issues, caregiving issues or loss of a loved one I believe each woman has the inner strength needed to take meaningful steps toward life-giving goals.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker(LCSW) with over 30yrs of experience. I worked as an elementary school counselor for 7 yrs, then as a Hospice and Palliative Care Social Worker since 2004. I started my private practice, Mountain Sage counseling, in 2020. I have had the opportunity to work with youngsters and their parents, and patients, family members and caregivers. I understand the health care systems benefits and problems, and am familiar with supporting elders and their families, as they consider transitioning to higher levels of care. I have an empathetic, client-centered approach, focused on helping you recognize and enhance your strengths, improve your coping skills, alter you negative thought patterns, and find meaning and joy in life, by living from your values. I use an insight-oriented approach and draw from many therapeutic models, including cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT) and internal family systems(IFS).

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I was raised in the Judeo-Christian tradition. I had opportunities to work as a volunteer at a 'soup kitchen' and with children with disabilities, from the age of 13. In HS, I was drawn to service activities, and to 'helping those less fortunate'. In college, I learned about racism, feminism, 'the military industrial complex', and the dangers of nuclear energy. I developed a justice lense, asking, "who gains by this action or policy?" and developing a 'preferential option for the poor' stance. I had the meaningful opportunity to be a 'Jesuit Volunteer', after college, working with emotionally abused children, and then moving to the NorthWest to be a supervisor for volunteers working in rural cities and on 'Indian Reservations'. I learned to love the NorthWest, and continued working with low income families until I went to graduate school. I have been fortunate to have a degree that allowed me to do the work I care about, while raising 2 daughters!

specialities.name: Aging Concerns
specialities.description: I have worked as a Hospice and Palliative Care Social Worker for over 15 yrs. In this role, I have supported patients and their loved ones, including addressing emotional and practical issues as one ages, declines and faces end of life. I have experience in caregiving and placement, Advanced Directives and POLSTS, and anticipatory grief and bereavement.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have supported many women dealing with anxiety. I am supportive of a multifocal appoach, including 'talk' therapy, CBT, developing coping skills, and medical interventions, as needed.

name: Amanda Best
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Currently accepting clients for sex, couples, and relational therapy. Specialties include non-monogamy, kink, and c-ptsd.
ideal_client: Are you having the same fight with your partner in a slightly different context each time? Do you feel stuck even though you love your partner? Do you feel like you're consistently enacting behaviors in your relationship that you're not proud of? Whether you're looking for couples, poly, or individual therapy, we start with validating the barriers such as systems of oppression or poor modeling of intimacy that can prevent us from leading with emotional maturity or our best selves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a systemic and relational therapist, I offer a challenging yet nurturing presence to help guide you to your therapeutic goals. Whether it be sexual concerns, resolving trauma, managing anxiety, or changing your relationship structure from monogamy to non-monogamy, I aim to offer support and insight throughout your process. Sex and couples therapy is approached from a queer and feminist framework while issues are contextualized through the systems of patriarchy. As a pleasure activist, I will work with you to deconstruct the impact of patriarchy and individualism to re-route you to your ideal life. Staying pleasure-centered is a value in my therapy, which means there will be fun and hard work. I specialize in the treatment of erotically marginalized folx, queer, trans, non-monogamous, and kink. Modalities for couples and relational therapy are Emotionally Focused Therapy, Relational Life Therapy, and Gottman.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Originally hailing from the east coast, I was raised in both New York and New Jersey. I have resided in Portland for the past 5 years. I am a first-generation college student and was privileged enough to attend Lewis and Clark College where I completed my Masters in Marriage, Couples, and Family Therapy. As someone of Greek and Jewish descent, I have spent much of my free time understanding my own culture and others through travel. I find myself the most comfortable in queer and diverse spaces. I have been a social justice activist since I was 19 where you could find me hopping from one Occupy Wall St. camp to another. As a white, cisgender, hetero-passing, able-bodied woman, I have been able to traverse many spaces with ample privilege. Utilizing that privilege to continuously advocate for my community and my clients is how I remain accountable to them. When I’m not doing therapy, I’m usually spending time with my friends, dancing, hiking, and doing colorful makeup!

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: If you feel stuck in a negative conflict cycle and as if you cannot break this pattern with your partner, EFT could be for you. We will focus on attachment, emotional safety, and greater emotional intimacy while working from an EFT lens. We will aim to deepen the emotional bond while also catering to your specific relationship structure. I use a socio-culturally attuned approach with using EFT which allows me to translate the theory to queer couples.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Whether your looking to re-author the story of your life, align with a new narrative, or deconstruct dominant narratives, working with narrative therapy is a great way for us to co-author your story. My skills as a narrative therapist are focused on facilitating the process of narrative exploration and reconstruction, helping clients gain a fresh perspective on their lives, and empowering them to make meaningful changes in the stories they tell about themselves and their relationship.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: With extensive experience in the Gottman Approach, I have catered this empirically backed theory to clients of all backgrounds. I tailor Gottman to your unique needs and concerns while utilizing its structured approach. Gottman is specifically great for couples or individuals looking to enhance communication skills, conflict resolution, and emotional connection.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: When it comes to understanding your own unique trauma, triggers, and inner child, there is no theory like IFS! Once we building a trusting therapeutic connection, we can utilize IFS to empower you to access the compassionate, centered and wise being that you are. Once we work together to guide you to trust your inner parts, we will watch the triggers melt away.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I am well-versed in addressing issues related to sexuality, helping you explore and enhance your sexual well-being, and fostering healthy, fulfilling connections. Whether you're dealing with sexual discrepancies, sexual abuse trauma, ED, or orgasm inequity, we will work together to get to the root of the sexual issue. Exploring sexual health and well being is my top priority in all sexually fluid, asexual, or kink contexts. I use a non-judgemental and affirming stance with all sexual concerns.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in identifying and helping couples break free from repetitive, unproductive patterns of conflict. Together, we'll explore the underlying issues and develop healthier ways to communicate and resolve disagreements. We'll develop conflict resolution skills tailored to your unique dynamics. You'll learn how to manage disagreements constructively, leading to greater harmony and intimacy in your relationship. My goal is not just to resolve the current conflict but to help you both grow.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have extensive experience working with individuals in various non-monogamous relationship structures and that personal issues are not inherently tied to your relationship style. We can focus on improving communication skills, setting healthy boundaries, and fostering trust and intimacy within your relationship(s).

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I offer expertise in supporting transgender and non-binary individuals in their journey, including discussions around gender identity, transitioning, and sexual health. I specialize in working with LGBTQI+ couples and families, helping you navigate the complexities of relationships, communication, and intimacy within a supportive and affirming context. I understand the diverse experiences within the LGBTQI+ community and provide a safe, inclusive, and nonjudgmental space.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I provide guidance on navigating issues related to body image, consent, and self-acceptance. I provide a safe, nonjudgmental, and confidential environment where you can openly explore your feelings and thoughts related to your femininity. We can challenge societal stereotypes and expectations about femininity, allowing you to define it on your terms and break free from any limitations that may have been imposed on you.

name: Kendyl Watts
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi, I'm Kendyl (she/her) and I am passionate about supporting people who are struggling and want to feel better.
ideal_client: I especially enjoy working with folks who are motivated to identify and release old patterns that are no longer serving them well. Changing unhelpful behaviors can be hard, but it is so rewarding. Together, we will leverage insight and self-compassion to find healthier, more sustainable ways to reach your goals. It can be hard to set aside time and resources for self-care, but you are worth it! Whenever you are ready to reach out, I would love to meet you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I strive for a balance of therapeutic connection, support, reflection, and skill-building, but the amount of each is flexible depending on client needs and preferences. I draw heavily from a cognitive-behavioral framework with other evidence-based techniques woven in as appropriate. My approach is warm, responsive, and compassionate. I am a Certified Clinical Trauma Professional. My highest priority is helping you to reach the things that matter most to you, whatever they may be. For some, that may be a tangible goal or completed task; for others it's increased feelings of safety, clarity, or empowerment. I pride myself on being flexible and responsive to meet my client's unique needs.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I completed my Master of Social Work degree in 2004 with a concentration in Sexual Health Promotion and Advocacy. I obtained my clinical license in 2007 and continued the work I was already doing with a highly diverse client base in St. Louis, Missouri. I have extensive experience working with people living with or affected by HIV and AIDS. I also have many years of experience helping teens and adults in all stages of family-building including infertility, pregnancy, decisions around abortion and adoption, and early parenting. I consider it a privilege to provide letters of support for gender-affirming medical care and third-party reproductive technologies. I strive to create an affirming environment for ALL people regardless of body size and ability, racial identity, gender identity, spiritual beliefs, relationship status, and sexual behavior.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: Pregnancy is a time of great excitement and possibility, but it is also physically and emotionally demanding and can be stressful or frightening, particularly for those with a history of trauma. I am passionate about helping individuals* experience all stages of pregnancy with as much choice and empowerment as possible. (*Not all who are pregnant identify as women; I celebrate and affirm all identities.)

specialities.name: Infertility
specialities.description: The experience of infertility may be the hardest thing an individual or couple has ever faced. I have a deep understanding of the toll it can take on a person's energy, mood, relationships, sense of worth, finances, and more. I can help you reclaim a sense of balance and strength so that you can continue working hard toward your dream of building your family.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I have 20+ years of experience living, working and volunteering within the queer community. I am familiar with many of the unique challenges faced by LGBTQ+ individuals and their families, and I also understand that your LGBTQ+ identity may have nothing at all to do with why you are seeking therapy. Either way, you and your relationships will be seen, valued and respected without exception.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I am deeply sensitive to the unrelenting challenges faced by those who have been assigned a gender that conflicts with their lived experience. I consider it a privilege to support clients in resolving this dissonance to whatever extent they choose, from explorations of identity and experiences through social and medical transitions.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Past trauma has a way of sneaking up on us, sometimes in ways we expect and sometimes seemingly out of nowhere. It can be disorienting and frightening both to us and our loved ones. You do not have to be held hostage by your past experiences. I can help you regain a sense of safety and empowerment that will have a positive impact on all areas of your life.

name: Khrystal Johnson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My practice emerges from a trauma-informed, culturally sensitive, and interpersonal lens of empowerment.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Life can be tough. That is why I developed an ENTIRE practice devoted to talking about it. I'll use humor and compassion so we can talk about what it means to be human. I identify as Black and Native and am an enrolled member of the Umatilla Indian Reservation here in Oregon. I have experience working with Native populations through traditional cultural practices living on the reservation as well as providing therapy at the Native American Rehabilitation Association (NARA). Before obtaining my master's in Counseling Psychology, I gained over 10 years of experience working within the realms of social justice, student leadership, and diversity development. After graduating, I gained additional training in DBT (couples and individual), interpersonal neurobiology, trauma-informed practices, relationship therapy, and therapy targeting BIPOC. I welcome alternative relationship structures, BIPOC, and QPOC.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Finding the right therapist can sometimes feel overwhelming. It’s no secret that how well you connect with your counselor is essential to flourishing in therapy, and you have a right to choose what works for you. Therefore, I offer the first session free, so that you can decide if my approach best suits your needs. In session, I will create a safe atmosphere where you can learn skills to deal with life's obstacles, explore your concerns so you can begin to resolve them, and gain a deeper understanding of yourself and where you are at in life. My therapeutic style involves walking alongside you on your brave and adventurous path toward rediscovery. I hope to facilitate your process through open, supportive, and genuine dialogue.

name: Avery Lewis
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Welcome to my page! I’m glad you’ve found your way here. I know that finding the right therapist can be an overwhelming process, so I thank
ideal_client: While I have worked with a wide range of individuals, I tend to work best with folks who experience relational and attachment challenges, C-PTSD, disconnection, grief and loss, eco-anxiety, and neurodiversity. Many of my clients identify as LGBTQIA+, have personal and/or generational histories of trauma, deeply feel the harmful impacts of capitalism, and live at the intersection of multiple marginalized identities.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy integrates relational-cultural, psychodynamic, and somato-emotional perspectives. These perspectives hold that we are shaped by our histories, both personal and collective, and that we carry patterns of thinking, feeling, and relating in our bodies throughout our lives, and across generations. By exploring our histories, we can often gain insight into our current ways of being, find greater understanding and compassion for ourselves and others, and pave the way for agency, choice, and deep connection in our lives.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a therapist, I aim to provide a collaborative, liberatory, and trauma-informed environment for you to explore your own depths, and attune to your own body and wisdom. I hold awareness of how dynamics of power and oppression may impact your health and wellbeing, and I strive to embody curiosity, respect, and cultural humility in my work. I believe that all people have the innate capacity to heal, and that healing happens when we center dignity, safety, and belonging.

name: Shanon Emerson
title: Somatic Practitioner
intro: You have a body. It has a language. You can learn that language.
ideal_client: The feeling of being stuck, like the gas and brake are going at the same time, is a symptom of your body being ready to let go of patterns and protections that are no longer needed. These protections were likely essential at another time in your life, and we can love them and thank them for their impeccable service. The first step is to begin to notice those patterns without judgement. Noticing them can create enough of a pause that we can begin to make different choices.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My philosophy, rooted in my training in both Somatic Experiencing and Depth Psychology, is that by noticing and allowing the feelings and sensations that arise within us, we can heal the patterns, behaviors, and defenses that limit our capacity for experience. This process fosters a deeper understanding of our authentic Self. As we come to know ourselves better, we begin to trust our inner guidance more than external influences like culture, family, and society, which often try to dictate our lives.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a queer artist and writer, mom of two adult kids, and curious explorer of what’s possible on this wild ride called life. I am trained in Somatic Experiencing (SE) and am a certified coach with the International Coach Federation (ICF).

name: Julian Morris
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I practice Gestalt therapy, rooted in existentialism and mindful embodiment. I specialize in working with LGBTQIA+ identified individuals.
ideal_client: I am a queer identified transman and have worked extensively with the LGBTQIA community. I am passionate about adapting body centered techniques in therapy to meet the needs of gender diverse clients. Clients who are interested in a less intellectualized approach to therapy tend to be a good fit. I also utilize mindfulness and meditation based approaches rooted in 10 years of Zen practice.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I specialize in working with clients who have big questions about life. Spiritual and existential quandaries welcome! I use a Gestalt and IFS framework that focuses on you becoming your own deepest resource. With couples I use this framework to peel back the layers of conflict to better understand each person's ground. The therapeutic goal is a stronger understanding of Self that brings a deeper connection to the experience of being alive. I use a dialogic approach in my work, which means I am listening to your language and the meaning that you make out of life. Together, we help bring unconscious beliefs, patterns, and habitual thoughts to the forefront to examine. This gives individuals and couples an increased awareness and an opportunity to make great change.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that every person is capable of growth and healing. The therapeutic process is much like fine tuning a radio. Our work is to lessen the static until core needs and emotions are clear enough to hear. As a therapist, I am a visitor in the overall journey of your healing. As such, I can provide a non-judgmental, compassionate, and caring environment for you to come into deeper relationship with yourself. Ultimately, I believe we are all equipped to be our own best healers. Therapy is a place to uncover this deep inner potential, as well as to grieve, to question, to explore, and ultimately to grow.

name: Leah Marinakis
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I’m passionate about and dedicated to helping people achieve meaningful, sustainable changes that align with their core values and aspiratio
ideal_client: I specialize in working with adolescents and young adults– a population I am particularly passionate about. I feel the challenges and growth that come with these stages in life are especially unique and meaningful.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe therapy is most successful when we find the path that truly supports the growth you’re seeking. In our work together, we will find an approach that fits your unique needs, drawing from my experience with a range of therapeutic orientations, including trauma-informed therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Mindfulness, and relational approaches.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: When I’m not working, I enjoy skiing, traveling, hiking, and exploring the outdoors. I also love curling up with a good book, watching a great movie or TV show, and most of all, I cherish spending time with friends and loved ones.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Identity exploration and integration, gender dysphoria, and lots of experience with other LGBTQIA+ issues.

name: Alycen Davis
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a mental health therapist specializing in EMDR, CBT, IFS, TF-CBT, DBT, and Psychodynamic interventions.
ideal_client: I welcome and support individuals from all backgrounds and walks of life. My practice specializes in working with those navigating OCD, mood disorders, trauma and PTSD, low self-esteem, anxiety, ADHD, Autism Spectrum, and depression. No matter your story or the challenges you face, my goal is to offer a safe, compassionate space where you can explore your strengths and begin to heal from the past.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My counseling style is trauma-informed, individualized, and paced to ensure comfort and readiness for each client. I am deeply passionate about helping individuals overcome the distress of their past and ease their anxieties about the future. I believe our childhood experiences play a significant role in shaping who we are, and I strive to create a safe, supportive space where clients can explore their past and process their trauma. With unconditional positive regard, I gently reframe perspectives shaped by past experiences, fostering healing and growth. My treatment approach is eclectic and tailored to each client’s unique needs. I am EMDR trained and use DBT, IFS, CBT, TF-CBT, strengths based approach, psychodynamic interventions (and more!) .

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a dedicated therapist committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive virtual environment. Here’s a brief overview of my approach: LGBTQIA+ Allyship: I support and advocate for LGBTQIA+ rights, ensuring a safe and respectful space for all. Cultural Competence: I value and respect cultural differences, continuously learning to communicate effectively with diverse backgrounds. Racial Justice: I work to dismantle systemic racism and promote equality in various sectors like education and healthcare. Disabilities and Chronic Illness: I am dedicated to providing compassionate and informed support for individuals with disabilities and chronic illness. Neurodivergence: I create inclusive environments for neurodivergent individuals; advocating for accessibility, challenging stigmas, and unmasking I am committed to creating a safe space for clients along with challenging and reframing thoughts/beliefs that are harmful to them.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Trained by Phillip Manfield

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Trained

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: IFS is a groundbreaking treatment modality that helps treat trauma, low self esteem, and anxiety (among many other issues)

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I use a wide range of theories and interventions. Everyone is unique so your treatment should be too!

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: EMDR, IFS

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: Experience treating clients with intrusive thoughts, obsessions, and compulsions

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Generalized anxiety, social anxiety, and health anxiety.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Competent in LGBTQIA issues

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Able to treated trauma from childhood abuse, neglect, and relationship violence.

name: Beau Henderson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Let's work together to tap into your innate potential to move towards growth, healing, wholeness.
ideal_client: I work with children, teens and adults who are struggling with issues like: anxiety, depression, divorce, grief, behavioral concerns, bullying, ADHD, trauma, self-harm, suicide, abuse, etc.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We'll work together to create a counseling process that meets your needs and provides safe, relationally engaging and reparative experiences. You are the expert on your life and we will utilize your strengths as well as the collaborative relationship between client and counselor to get you where you want to go. I work from a person-centered and experiential approach with special training in Child Centered Play Therapy and integrate techniques from attachment science, interpersonal neurobiology and sandtray therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As people are provided an environment and therapeutic relationship characterized by safety, acceptance, and therefore freedom to explore self, they are empowered to build a healthy self-concept, personal responsibility, self-direction, self-acceptance, decision-making skills, sense of control, self-reliance, coping awareness and skills, internal source of evaluation, trust of self and resiliency.

name: Kylie Dieringer
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hello! I am a self-proclaimed geek who is here to meet you where you are at and provide a space for you to process and get support.
ideal_client: My clients typically have anxiety or anxiety symptoms that make life just that much harder. I have experience with grief and trauma LGBTQIA+, ethical nonmonogamy, and polyamory. I currently work with clients who are anywhere from 20+.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My goal is to provide you with tools for your toolbox so that when life pulls a fast one, you have the tools to help regulate, process and get through it. I am direct, challenging, and interactive but also provide warmth and empathy to create the space that you need. I work from an eclectic style pulling from modalities such as Cognitive Behavioral, DBT and other mindfulness-based practices.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a counselor after trying to process and come to terms with the trauma and loss that I had previously experienced. It took me many years to be able to talk about what I went through and that's when I realized that sometimes, you just need someone to listen. Someone specifically who is a neutral party, someone who can look at what you're going through and empathize without judgement.

name: Bethany Ingram
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I provide holistic, relational, and trauma-informed therapy for clients needing support with grief, trauma, or life transitions.
ideal_client: My clients are typically experiencing various life transitions, including grief and loss, relationship issues, or healing from childhood or current traumas. They often feel hesitant to face their emotional pain and get to know the parts of themselves that are feeling stuck, helpless, hopeless, or disempowered. I believe that each of us has everything we need within ourselves to find healing and growth. It is my job to support my clients to connect to themselves and find that path within them.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize various techniques to help you cope with (and feel) difficult emotions, connect to your mind and body, and understand the impact of your past and present. I believe that a safe, supportive therapeutic relationship is vital to the healing process. I will provide empathy, curiosity, humor, and connection as we build trust and find a rhythm that works for us. I specialize in treating grief and loss, PTSD, including Complex PTSD and early childhood trauma, as well as anxiety and depression. My focus is in healing your relationships - with yourself, with others, and how you relate to the world around you, including the natural world. Depending on your needs, I might use short-term solutions focused interventions to find current relief and/or psychodynamic interventions that focus more on your childhood wounds and internalized belief systems. I rely heavily on the relational process and getting to know your strengths, needs, and relationships as an individual.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I approach my work with the belief that we are all connected - and our connections to ourselves, to others, and to the earth is where we find healing. I see my clients as the expert on their own lives and myself as a guide to support them to listen to themselves and trust themselves in their own healing and growth. I come to this work as someone who has experienced healing from trauma and grief within a therapeutic relationship, and it is my honor to provide the safety and connection to others as I have experienced in my personal life. This world is full of pain and trauma, systemic oppression, and humans hurting each other, yet I see an abundance of goodness and beauty in humanity, especially in my clients. I love shining this light of goodness and beauty within my clients when they find it difficult to see it in themselves. It is why I do what I do.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I approach therapy with the foundational perspective that we are all doing our best with the knowledge and experiences we have at the time. When we peel back the layers of pain, wounds, and trauma, we find our true selves. I enjoy guiding my clients back to themselves within the therapeutic relationship.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: I believe in the healing power of our connection to the earth. I encourage time spent in nature and enjoy connecting with my clients around their healing relationship with the world around them. I have limited sessions available for hiking or sitting in Forest Park, and these can be used for building increased safety and connection to nature.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: We must learn to truly feel our emotions rather than "thinking about feeling them". Our emotions live in the body, and I encourage connection to the body in order to get to know ourselves and move through the emotional pain we experience. Our body, especially our nervous system, can teach us about what we need to feel safe and find connection with ourselves and others. I teach my clients to "befriend their nervous system" to learn how to respond to triggers and increase safety.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: We will explore the relationship between our thoughts, feelings, and actions as well as how to build awareness of thoughts and emotions. I tend to connect traditional CBT to body-centered interventions, with the understanding that our nervous system states impact our thinking.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Our early development, especially our first caregivers, impact how we relate to ourselves and to others. I will help you understand how your childhood impacts your internal world and your external relationships, and I will help you build consciousness around subconscious patterns stemming from your childhood so that you can make necessary changes in the areas you have felt "stuck".

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is not something we need to "move past" or "get through". Grief is something we learn to integrate into our daily lives as the impact of our loss shifts and changes over time. We have to learn to keep living after a loss of person, pet, identity, relationship, etc has changed how we move through the world. It is my honor to support people to feel their emotional pain and have compassion for themselves in the midst of this pain.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma changes the way we relate to ourselves, to others, and to the world around us. I enjoy helping my clients understand how complex trauma or other traumas have impacted them and how to create safety within themselves and their relationships. This often entails learning to cope with triggers, building more connection between our minds and bodies, and processing and healing any internalized beliefs that stem from traumatic experiences.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I enjoy working with older children (10 and up), adolescents, and young adults. I have extensive experience in understanding adolescent needs and developmental tasks of this life stage.

specialities.name: Adoption Issues
specialities.description: The experience of adoption and/or foster care presents unique grief/loss and identity issues into adulthood. I enjoy working with children, teens, and adults who are adopted or have experienced foster care, and I have been certified in Foster and Adoptive Family therapy through Portland State University’s child welfare partnership.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Codependency typically looks like hyper-vigilance towards the emotional states of others, fear of disappointing others, difficulty setting boundaries, and tending towards "people pleasing" or "rescuing/fixing" others. I enjoy helping people learn to listen to and trust themselves, focus on their own emotions and perspectives, and set necessary boundaries for themselves and in their relationships.

name: Christine Titus
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I am a board certified Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) providing supportive therapy and/or medication management.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work with adults (ages 18+ only) on a broad selection of mental health concerns including depression, anxiety, grief & loss, adjusting to life changes, and stress management. I have a special focus on pregnancy and postpartum mood and anxiety support. My treatment approach is holistic, meaning I treat the whole person and view the mind-body connection as important to our overall well-being. As a PMHNP, I have been trained to understand how genetic, developmental, biological, environmental, and psychosocial influences can significantly impact our health. As a therapist, I utilize a combination of therapeutic theories and techniques to help meet your individual needs. I often incorporate elements of cognitive-behavioral, psychodynamic, supportive, and interpersonal therapy techniques into our sessions. In addition to therapy, medication can be beneficial and we can discuss whether this option may be the best choice for you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received my Master's degree in Nursing after completing the Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner program at Oregon Health & Sciences University. I am board certified by the American Nurses Credentialing Center and have been licensed and practicing since 2011. Prior to returning to graduate school, I worked as a Labor & Delivery RN caring for high-risk obstetric patients and their families. I have worked to unite my passion for reproductive health and mental health and have focused on the specialty of reproductive psychiatry since beginning my practice. I am passionate about supporting new parents and their families through the potential challenges experienced before, during, and after pregnancy and other reproductive life cycle changes.

name: Spencer Uemura
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Our intersecting identities and cultural experiences have led to the ways we are hurt, but also hold the keys to how we heal.
ideal_client: For my clients, these layers of oppression may result in anxiety, depression, trauma, and racial identity concerns. We'll work together to process your experience, draw out your strengths, and support your goals. I love working with Asian American adults, and other People of Color, to connect the impacts of history, oppression, and culture on mental health and wellbeing. If you are interested in exploring how facets of your identity and culture have affected your experience, I may be a good fit!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In session, I draw from narrative, compassion-focused, embodied, and anti-oppressive approaches as well as my own lived experience of marginalization. If your cultural experience has been left out of therapy in the past, I can be a good fit. I have received training in approaches such as psychoanalysis, CBT, DBT, Narrative Therapy, and somatic experiencing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: We are all essentially good, loving, creative, and courageous, but oppression hinders our ability to see that and act from that deep truth. With unconditional support, we can release the distress, nourish our resilience, and live out our values. I am a lifelong learner and engage in my own emotional healing work as a foundation of providing good therapy to others. Contact me through our group practice, Second Growth Counseling, and our team will support you through the set-up process. I look forward to working with you!

name: Miles Joyce
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: "It is no measure of health to be well-adjusted to a profoundly sick society."
ideal_client: Hello. My name is Miles and my heart is devoted to working with individuals, couples, and communities to feel more fully connected to a life of richness and authenticity. I maintain the relational and systemic perspective that problems exist between people, rather than within people. My clients tend to be folks from all walks of life who are interested in taking a holistic approach towards being in a healthier relationship with their wounds for the sake of greater response-ability and belonging.

approaches.My Background: I hold a master’s degree in Marriage, Couple and Family Therapy from Lewis & Clark College and a bachelor’s degree in psychology and behavioral neuroscience from the University of Portland. This path was set in motion in 2012 when I first began working in the unhoused population of East Los Angeles. This laid the groundwork for years spent working with similar populations in Portland via p:ear and New Avenues for Youth, overseeing culinary, music, and transitional housing programming. I additionally spent several years working in wilderness therapy as both a guide and manager at a program that specialized in leveraging the healing potential of the land to treat complex developmental trauma via an individualized approach. Together, these experiences have established an ethic of nuance in my practice, working to integrate the sometimes conflicting confluence of interpersonal, environmental, and political demands.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: My passion lies in what I’ve come to call “re-villaging efforts,” meaning that I see therapy as an effective catalyst for the culture-work necessary to heal the harm associated with being a human in increasingly troubled times. I have humbly apprenticed myself to the lineage of Bill Plotkin, Francis Weller, the School of Lost Borders, and others who have prioritized finding the therapeutic intersection of initiatory practices, contemporary rites of passage, and soul-centric practice. I have been trained in EMDR by the EMDR Institute founded by Dr. Francine Shapiro and utilize this approach to assist clients in reclaiming a sense of wholeness after the fracturing of traumatic experiences. I have special interests and additional training in men’s work, grief and loss, navigating transitions in identity, parenting, boundary issues or violations, sexuality, and religious trauma. Right now, I primarily work on telehealth and have limited availability for in-person walk and talk sessions.

name: Shawna Oliver, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Working collaboratively to assist individuals and couples in identifying their strengths & finding solutions to live with more contentment.
ideal_client: There are times when life feels overwhelming and stressful . This can lead to increased relationship conflict, feelings of isolation and loneliness. The answers are often held within ourselves and with support and guidance we can overcome these feelings. I work collaboratively using approaches that give people the tools to use throughout their lives.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe in creating an emotionally safe environment where individuals and couples can process feelings, develop new insights, overcome negative thinking, improve communications and set healthier boundaries. I believe counseling is a collaborative process and work with individuals and couple in developing goals that will best fit their needs. Not one mode of therapy works for all and I often use an eclectic approach designed to address the issues and achieve the desired goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and have been working in the human services field for the last 25 years. During my career I have had the opportunity to work with individuals and families who have experienced a variety of life crisis’ such as; depression, anxiety , divorce, abuse, relationship and marriage issues, parenting issues and grief and loss.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: It is important for couple to have a place where they can identify patterns that may be disruptive to the relationship. A place where positive communication can strengthen positive communication and both parties can be heard.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: Using an eclectic approach allows me to utilize aspects of other approaches or techniques that will better fit the needs of the individual or couple.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT focuses on awareness and reframing thoughts, emotions, and behaviors. It can help identify obstacles that prevent positive feelings about ourselves and those around us. Awareness is often the key to change. It is also a collaborative approach that give individual the power to create the change they seek.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Any form of abuse can have long-term implications on how individuals feel about themselves and those around leaving a feeling of isolation and depression. Sometimes all it takes is a safe place to begin to process and heal.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I have spent much of my career supporting women through many of life's challenges. Often times these challenges come in the form of abuse, trauma, divorce, grief and life transitions. This can interfere with how we perceive ourselves. It has been my experience that women often possess an inner strength that with help they can identify and grow.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: It is important for couple to have a place where they can identify patterns that may be disruptive to the relationship. A place where positive both parties can be heard and communication can be strengthened.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief and loss does not look or feel the same for everyone who experiences it. And grief and loss can be associated with not only losing a loved one but also a relationships ending, difficult life transitions, loss of employment, and many other challenges life presents. With support in developing the tools necessary, individuals can better cope with loss and still lead happier lives.

name: Kelly Washam
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I believe each person lives most fully when connected to their deepest self, unimpeded by the barriers and burden we accumulate during life.
ideal_client: I will help you discover what blocks your life's development. Counseling is an evolving process, which does not happen along the same path for each individual. However, most clients strive for the same thing, "to be happy." I work in a collaborative, strength's-based fashion to help you improve your life and your relationships. Life truly can be Content.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I promise to be supportive in every step of your journey. My goal is to help you grow from your struggles, heal from your pain, and move forward to where you want to be in your life. I achieve this by providing a neutral safe space, listening to your concerns, and customizing a treatment plan. I specialize in helping people struggling with relationships, life transitions, depression, anxiety, and addiction/substance use (your own addiction or helping you deal with a family members'). For the past 20+ years I have been providing confidential counseling enabling people to learn new ways of coping with life's problems. I believe change is possible.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that each person lives most fully when they are connected to their deepest self, unimpeded by the barriers and burdens we all accumulate during our lives. My work is to help people free themselves so they can live from a place of honesty, compassion and love. I believe we all have the capability to create the life we want to live. I will help you discover what blocks your life's development.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I provide couple counseling based on the works of Gottman and hope recovery. I utilize a variety of approaches to get to the core matter and help you reclaim the dynamic love of your relationship.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I provide confidential counseling that is based in strengths-based approaches, and motivational enhancement therapies. I also support and mentor in 12 step recovery, rational recovery, SOS, among others. I can help you get your life back.

name: Emily Kittelson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Let's work together to break and evolve the old patterns that no longer serve you.
ideal_client: I work with individual adults who are looking to reduce their symptoms of anxiety, improve personal relationships, and feel more in control of their lives. I find that many people who come to see me feel like they've been recreating the same old patterns in their relationships to others and to themselves. I want to help you explore these patterns and identify where they are rooted so that you can start making new choices about how to respond to familiar emotions and thoughts.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a counselor my goal is to help you process your experiences and gain a deeper understanding of yourself and the world we live in. I believe that the stories we tell ourselves are deeply influenced by our past and our cultural experiences, and these stories continue to shape our experience of the world around us. I use an eclectic trauma-informed approach of Mindfulness-based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Narrative Therapy. My aim is to help increase flexibility of thought so that we can re-write your narrative, lessen your distress, and shift your emotional reactions. I am curious and supportive in my approach of gently challenging you to consider new perspectives to your familiar patterns. My aim is to help you find a new way of relating to your past so that you can feel empowered to make the best choices for yourself. Let's work together to form and strengthen new neural pathways through exploring your old patterns and creating new narratives.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My career in mental health began working in residential foster care with children and adolescents. During my graduate internship I engaged youth and young adults in substance use and dual-diagnosis counseling. Since obtaining my degree I have worked in multiple mental health crisis settings with adults and children alike. I have a Masters degree in Mental Health Counseling from the University of Vermont and am currently a Licensed Professional Counselor in Oregon.

specialities.name: Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy
specialities.description: Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy is proven to be effective for at least 75% of people suffering from Obsessive Compulsive Disorder. I know how scary it can feel to repeatedly confront head-on the fears that are driving your distracting rituals, but science shows us that it's the best and quickest way to relief. I have completed intensive training on how to use Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy for OCD through the Cognitive Behavioral Institute.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I was first trained in how to use Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to treat substance use and mental health disorders while in my graduate school internship. I consider Acceptance and Commitment Therapy to be the newest wave of CBT that provides a more holistic approach to wellbeing. I use a client-centered approach that uses cognitive techniques to help build flexibility of thought.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: I am trained in providing Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) Therapy for Obsessive Compulsive Disorder. I have also worked with clients who have OCD using an Acceptance and Commitment Therapy approach. For some people a combination of these two techniques seems to be most helpful.

name: Kimberly Zeszutek, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Lets find new ways of being that feel aligned with who you really are. Address PTSD, ASD, emotion dysregulation, relationship skills.
ideal_client: Clients often come to me when they are feeling misunderstood by others, and they struggle to understand themselves. When there has been trauma experienced, often we want to have insight of how it impacts us and how to recover. People who are Autistic and Neurodivergent find me to recover from chronic invalidation from ablest environments. Through the natural environment we practice the self-care we know we need, and we are creative in what to do next for our goals.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Excited to relay! The Ecotherapy Geodesic Dome office is now open! FIRE Circle Neurodivergent teen group - now meeting in person at a local art collective! My style and practice align with adults, young adults, and adolescents; with a focus on Neurodivergent support. I provide a healthy balance of concrete skills with alternative informed approach. Sessions are co-created, meaning lead by your needs with therapist insight and challenges to help with growth. I am experienced in supporting complex emotions, transitions, relationships, suicidal ideation, self harm, depression, anxiety, and learning differences. Ecotherapy is introduced to liven the environment and integrate the healing powers of nature. My services are BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, and Psychedelic friendly.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My career in counseling began in 2007, when I graduated with a Bachelors in Psychology at the University of Minnesota, Minneapolis. Spending a few years in the Rocky Mountains, in 2014, I earned my Masters in Counseling at Regis University, Denver. I am heavily influenced by my internship which allowed exploration of ecopsychology. My background as a counselor includes ABA therapy for children diagnosed with Autism, residential counseling for adults with severe and persistent mental illness, domestic violence shelter advocacy, crisis response therapy, and DBT for teens and families. I have extensive training with a Full Fidelity DBT Model, however do not provide full Fidelity DBT in this practice. I have supported individuals and families in clinical center settings, home therapy, and outdoor adventure camps. My specialization has developed into supporting those who are struggling with suicidal thoughts, understanding neurodiversity, major life transitions, and/or behavior changes.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: I bring experience from ecopsychology research, trainings, and passion for integrating nature into daily life. Since the beginning of my career, have been supported by ecotherapy mentors who have encouraged me to explore the ways nature can be brought into the therapy room. This has evolved into creating ecotherapy collections and activities unique in my therapeutic practice. Stay tuned as I am creating an Urban Ecotherapy Garden location.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I value mindfulness as a part of daily life, and I have participated in many retreats and mindful practices. It was a perfect match when my clinical internship taught me the process of leading mindfulness for others, and integrating mindfulness as one of the primary DBT skills. Applying formal and informal mindfulness into daily life helps connect one with community, self, and feeling alive.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I have been trained and supervised by programs specializing in Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT). Within sessions, we discuss mindfulness and skill building to identify and understand emotions, tolerate stress and difficult social interactions. It is my belief that by actively applying DBT strategies, individuals become empowered, and thus more able to create an atmosphere promoting the achievement of personal goals.

specialities.name: Suicidal Ideation
specialities.description: Working with suicide since 2014, I am confident and skilled in approaching and supporting suicidal idealization for adolescents and adults. I support the zero suicided initiative for increasing discussion of SI to increase safety. I have extensive experience with high risk clients and supporting them into skill building, tolerating stress, and choosing thoughts of life rather than thoughts of death. I approach suicidal idealization and self-harm with a balance of empathy, concern, and hope.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: My structure of therapy follows Judith Herman’s theory of care for Complex Trauma integrated with concepts of behaviorism, such as consciously building skills to be able to successfully influence PTSD symptoms and have the skills to process trauma. I understand how traumatic events can surface into someone’s daily life as symptoms of nightmares, flashbacks, emotional dysregulation, suicidal thoughts, self-invalidation, self-harm, depression, and/or anxiety.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: Since 2007, I have developed a style of skill building and supportive therapy for those who identify with Neurodiversity and the Autism Spectrum. Many of these individuals have had to navigate against the grain of a neurotypical societies expectations. My goal is to assist individuals to become empowered by their neurodiversity, and to apply their value and strengths towards their personal goals and to over all positive growth of society.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is a common experience of many individuals in our culture due to trauma, expectations, and the value of individualism. Approaching depression with ecotherapy creates opportunities for reconnecting with the authentic self, the earth, and your community. I also recognize the struggle in depression by emphasizing safety planning for suicidal ideation and strengthening protective factors.

name: Arielle Ross
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Queer trauma therapy for curious minds
ideal_client: I provide compassionate, trauma-aware, attachment-focused therapy to help clients heal from trauma, manage their ADHD, and reduce anxiety. Right now, my practice is mostly full, but if you are an immigrant, refugee, asylum seeker or grew up globally mobile, like a third-culture kid, please reach out!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I incorporate mindfulness, creative interventions and personal writing into my practice, and draw heavily from emotion focused, attachment-based and internal family systems theories, which means I focus on learning to identify and name feelings, improve attachments to those close to us, create new meanings after we’ve experienced significant life changes, and offer our past and current selves empathy. I'm trained in EMDR and in Narrative Exposure Therapy, as well as DBT. I am committed to anti-racist and anti-colonial work, and draw from a feminist, queer-affirming & trauma-informed lens.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe we're all doing the best we can with the skills, knowledge and resources we have. I believe that we have an innate internal bent toward healing: that is, if we can heal, we will, and therapy can sometimes help us get out of our own way. I operate from a anti-oppressive, feminist, LGBTQ+ affirming and anti-racist lens, and am a really big history dork, so I like learning about your family history and how that might have impacted how you were raised, your core beliefs and how you were resourced or hurt by that history. In my free time I make food for mutual aid free fridges, am an active member of the Jewish community in Portland, and volunteer with climate advocacy organizations to get out the vote and advocate for divestment from fossil fuels. I also love dancing, hanging out with my partners, and playing board games.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am training in EMDR and working towards my certification. I have already seen incredible progress with folks with deep seated trauma using EMDR and have found it to be really effective in treating trauma.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I use DBT skills to teach coping and emotion regulation, mindfulness, & interpersonal effectiveness skills. I've run several DBT skills groups and I love helping people understand what mindfulness is, and how they can use it to slow down when they're in a lot of distress.

specialities.name: Immigration/Acculturation
specialities.description: I was raised as a Third Culture Kid, which for me means we followed my dad's job around the world, mostly in East Africa & Asia, from when I was 4 until I came to the US for college at 18. My first therapist job was working with refugees from Iraq, Eritrea & Burma. I want to support my fellow immigrants, the children of immigrants & other globally mobile folks heal from the trauma of moving, re-center their values, & figure out how to live authentically in this new culture.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I want to help folks who, like me, were late diagnosed with ADHD. We'll work on understanding symptoms, including new things we're learning about how ADHD shows up in AFAB and trans* folks. We can work on issues of shame and how not being "good enough" at things that were easy for others impacted your self-esteem. And we can work on creating concrete coping skills for sensory issues, organization & focus.

specialities.name: Sexual Abuse
specialities.description: I work with a lot of different kinds of trauma, but sexual and relational trauma are my main area of focus. I use IFS, EMDR and other tools to help you work through that trauma. I'm a strong believer in consent, and together we'll work on understanding your needs, identifying the boundaries you need in relationships to be safe and how you can explore your sexuality and sensuality safely.

name: Jennell Roden
title: Student Counselor
intro: I am a trauma focused Graduate Student Intern and I aim to provide nonjudgmental and compassionate support for self-discovery and healing.
ideal_client: I believe that everyone has the capacity within themselves to find healing and to create a life worth living. I recognize that life is hard, and that stress is held in the body in numerous ways, which can lead to adaptive behaviors that may no longer be effective and/or are harmful to ourselves or others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My aim in therapy is to increase my client's toolbox for coping strategies, while also providing a corrective relational experience to address attachment wounds and trauma. I know that reaching out for help can feel scary and overwhelming. Know that when you contact me, I will be respectful, nonjudgmental, and compassionate. I am currently a Graduate Student Intern, enrolled in the Masters of Arts in Counseling Program at the Multnomah Campus of William Jessup University. My coursework includes a trauma focus.

name: Amy Galaviz
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Women-centered support for individuals struggling with anxiety and other maternal mental health challenges in Oregon & Washington.
ideal_client: I work alongside women that often feel worn out, tired, overwhelmed and wondering what they are doing wrong and aim to get it "right". Many of them find themselves struggling and worry that things might not ever change. Together, we find their confidence, work through the challenges of being a mother, help find natural support systems, and identify what works to meet their needs, while supporting them along the way. www.mindbodymamapdx.com.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My focus of therapy stems from a Person-Centered approach which means I put the client needs in mind first. My goal is to create an atmosphere where you feel safe and comfortable while working to build a positive, open, trusting, therapeutic relationship. It is through this therapeutic relationship that I see you as the expert in your own life, while I strive to understand your personal perspective of the world around you. Throughout therapy, I aim to keep your needs in mind, without judgment while seeing you in a positive light as you move through challenges and grow. Together, with a focus on personal strengths and growth enhancement, we take a holistic look at your life, by examining each part of your world that has an influence on your well-being whether it be personal relationships with family and friends, work, or health. I believe that people have the power to create changes in their lives no matter how small and am there to support you along the way at any stage in life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that we all have the ability to make changes in our lives, given the right support, guidance and faith that things can get better. Whether you are a new or single mother looking for support & guidance, a mother of three looking for validation & understanding, or a women who is uncertain about parenting, I believe all women have the right to the same care and support regardless of your situation, values or personal beliefs. Therefore, I offer holistic care practices that take a look at each client as a whole person, an individual, and their own expert in what works for them. I hold space for you, taking the time to help you identify your goals for therapy and the things you want in life in order to create the life you love. (*Extensive training in Perinatal Mental Health & PMH-C certified). For more info visit: www.mindbodymamapdx.com

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: 'Whatever your story, you no longer need to be alone with it. This is what will allow your healing to begin.'~ Carl Rogers. Rogers believed that the therapeutic relationship was at the forefront of the healing process. As a Person-Centered therapist, I am here to support you, so that you can feel comfortable and safe while I walk alongside you on this journey to growth and healing. Visit www.mindbodymamapdx.com to find out more and get started on your journey to health & wellness today.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: Holistic care is two fold. As a provider I offer mental health services by utilizing natural modalities of talk therapy and various tools tailored to meet the needs of each individual client. Secondly, I examine your life holistically by taking a look at each area, identifying strengths and places that may need additional support, whether it be emotional, social or spiritual. Visit www.mindbodymamapdx.com to learn more.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness-based practices can help to slow the mind & create a sense of calm while tuning into the self. It can be a great form of self-care to give us a moment of peace in times of distress & a break from anxious thoughts that clutter the mind and keep us from where we want to be. Together, we will explore how anxiety shows up in your life and find mindfulness based practices that work for you. Visit www.mindbodymamapdx.com to learn more and get started today.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: Life after baby can be an unexpected experience filled with feelings and challenges you may not have anticipated. For some mothers, being surrounded by others who may not understand their struggle, can further lead them to feel isolated and increase feelings of despair. I am here to let you know that you are not alone, and I am here to help. Reach out today at www.mindbodymamapdx.com (*I am a Certified Perinatal Mental Health Provider.)

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Throughout life, we face many losses that can make it difficult to function. Whether someone has experienced a miscarriage or recent perinatal/postnatal loss, I help individuals work through grief that leaves them feeling helpless, lost or perhaps paralyzed with fear and sadness. I work alongside you, to help you get to a place where you feel like yourself again. Specializing in perinatal loss that includes terminations, miscarriages and/or abortions. Visit www.mindbodymamapdx.com to learn more.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can be a paralyzing feeling, riddled with symptoms of nausea, rapid heart beat, shallow breathing, racing thoughts, and/or excessive worry or fears. I work with individuals suffering from a variety of anxiety related issues including social anxiety, generalized anxiety, panic attacks and fears related to social places and encounters. Reach out to www.mindbodymamapdx.com to get started today.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: As a mother of three, I can identify how important is to to receive extra support during such a transitional time. As a practitioner, I focus my work to support women throughout each stage of motherhood from preconception, throughout pregnancy, during postpartum and beyond. Facing motherhood can be difficult, but with the right support you can find the joy it can bring. Reach out to a trained specialist today! www.mindbodymamapdx.com

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: My women-centered practice focuses on assisting women through all life stages including family planning, pregnancy, postpartum, parenting, infertility and self-identity. Visit www.mindbodymamapdx.com to learn more. *Certified Perinatal Mental Health Provider

name: Lacy Lowry
title: Licensed Art Therapist
intro: Life is challenging. I show up with compassion and curiosity to help my clients work toward personal empowerment, security, and joy.
ideal_client: Does life feel overwhelming life? Are you dealing with anxious thoughts or having a hard time motivating in the direction of your goals? I want to help you connect with your own inner strength and discover what might be getting in the way of living your best life. I like to work collaboratively with teens and adults ages 13 and up on issues such as anxiety, depression, life transitions, and divorce.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use creative methods to explore emotions and thought patterns that present in your life. Though verbal inquiry and art-making, together we use non-judgmental curiosity to better understanding your story and your needs. My work is trauma-informed and mindfulness-based. I believe that mental health is intimately tied to relationships, and that therapy can provide a safe setting to practice new ways of engaging with others and oneself. No art experience is necessary, but an openness to trying new things is always helpful.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that the relationship we develop with ourselves is the most important one but can not happen in a vacuum. Therapy is an important step toward living with intention and improving our connection with ourselves. I have personally experienced how art-making and mindfulness practices can facilitate this process. I believe every human is innately creative and curious, but sometimes negative messages, stress, and trauma block that natural flow. Our work together can help unblock it. Besides my training and experience as an art therapist, I have extensive training in Interpersonal Neurobiology. This framework guides my approach, utilizing attachment science, neuroscience, and poly-vagal theory to understand the body-mind-relationship connection. I have practiced yoga for over 20 years and maintain a personal art practice to stay connected to my own body and mind. I also love traveling and playing outdoors with my two teens and my dog Sunny.

name: Sarah Craycraft
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Are you feeling anxious or depressed? Are you struggling in your relationships? If so, I can help. Please give me a call.
ideal_client: I work with people who are struggling with anxiety, depression, relationship issues, and trauma. Helping women who are struggling through postpartum issues is something that I am passionate about. I’ve helped many couples, dealing with communication issues, affair recovery, and conflict resolution. I also have experience with families struggling with family relationships, parenting, and boundaries.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have a Master of Arts in Mental Health Counseling from Denver Seminary, and am a Licensed Professional Counselor. My approach to counseling includes elements from Person-Centered, Cognitive Behavioral, Existential, and Narrative therapies. Most importantly, I believe that your growth and healing happens best when you have a trusting relationship with your therapist, so I value building that relationship.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I desire to provide a warm and safe environment to help you work through difficult times. Whether you’re struggling with a relationship, going through a transition in life, or just need someone to lend a compassionate ear, I am here to help.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I believe that having a strong and trusting therapeutic relationship is key to experiencing growth.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT provides many tools that I believe are helpful in making actionable changes, so I use many techniques from this therapeutic approach.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: This helps us to answer some of life's more difficult questions, so I use some of these techniques as we get into the deeper issues in life.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: I have experience working with postpartum depression and anxiety. If you are struggling with the transition of being a new parent, it can feel incredibly overwhelming and isolating.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: If you find yourself feeling paralyzed by anxiety, it can be helpful to just have someone to talk to, and a place to gain some new tools for dealing with the stressors that come up.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: As women, we are often juggling so many different roles. You might be a partner, a mother, an professional, and so many others. Often, we need someone to talk to about how all of those roles fit together. If this is you, I can help.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Do you want to improve your life? Do you want to feel like you are thriving, rather than just surviving? If so, give me a call.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Communication, conflict resolution, affair recovery, and boundaries are just a few topics in marriage relationships that I can help with.

name: Beth Keeney
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
