intro: C. Beth Keeney is a dual certified Family Nurse Practitioner and Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner.
ideal_client: Beth who provides compassionate care that is driven by the needs of the individual. She is currently based in Central Texas and serves patients primarily through a telehealth platform.

approaches.My Background: Beth dedicated the first twelve years of her career to women’s health services as a labor and delivery nurse, then decided to pursue her family nurse practitioner degree at the University of Texas Medical Branch in Galveston. She then began working in the Student Health Center at Texas State University where she broadened her skills as a mental health practitioner and worked closely with the LGBTQIA+ community as a member of the Gender Affirming Hormone Therapy team. This experience sparked Beth’s interest to explore non-traditional treatments for mental health, such as ketamine therapy, which she provided for patients at a clinic in Austin, Texas. Her passion for mental healthcare then led her to pursue her psychiatric mental health NP certification from New Mexico State University.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Beth incorporates a holistic approach into her practice, helping others to explore and connect with their truest selves. She enjoys teaching patients about cultivating wellness in their lives and providing them with means toward self-empowerment. She is experienced in treating various mental health diagnoses through both traditional and non-traditional methods. Beth is excited to be a part of the team at Head Well and is proud to provide her services to the community.

name: melissa sanders
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hello and thank you for reaching out. I look forward to collaborating with you on your healing journey.
ideal_client: You are feeling stuck and unsure of how to move forward. You are dealing with unresolved trauma, depression, anxiety or other complications that are making life difficult. You may feel like you are "going through the motions" and cannot find a way to enjoy your life in the ways you want. You feel disconnected from yourself and others. You want to feel motivated to live to your fullest potential and make the changes needed in order to reach your goals. I strive to create a space for that process.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that the therapeutic relationship is an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of the Self and make choices that are more aligned with personal goals. I use a Person Centered approach using Somatic awareness, Internal Family Systems, Narrative Therapy, DBT, CBT and creative expressive tools. Creating a deeper connection to body responses, and discovering different perspectives to develop more self awareness, I hope to work as a facilitator for your growth. I believe that you are always the expert in your own life, and I welcome feedback and collaboration about tools that you find most useful for your progress. At our initial sessions, we will explore what brought you to therapy and some potential types of therapies that may be beneficial for your treatment. I often use creative expressive activities during our sessions, with additional focus on somatic body awareness to bring more awareness to physical responses to thoughts and emotions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As I child, I experienced traumatic events that I addressed through my own healing journey. I found that a combination of therapeutic interventions, including expressive therapies helped me identify the behaviors that were no longer serving me and strengthen my ability to access tools I was unaware of before. I believe that we all have the answers we seek already within us and the therapeutic relationship is a chance to have a supportive person to help guide you to understanding yourself on a deeper level of awareness. As humans, we develop behavior based on our experiences and what has provided us with our needs, even if this behavior is unhelpful or damaging to ourselves or our lives. I view therapy as a place where we can learn new ways to move closer to congruence with the people we want to be and the lives we want to lead.

name: Dylan Edwards
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: Therapy is self-compassion training. I pull from an eclectic array of mindfulness-based approaches to develop compassion and awareness.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with teens and adults experiencing anxiety, depression, adjustment disorder, substance use disorder or who have otherwise lost touch with their sense of self-worth and their potential for great change and transformation.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that even our most challenging emotions (confusion, anxiety, grief, shame, and obsession to name a few…) come to us as expressions of deep caring for ourselves and the world around us, and that these experiences can be truly amazing teachers when we know who and what we are dealing with. I believe that no matter where we are in life, we already possess the inherent healing wisdom to find ourselves through struggle. Therapy to me, is the process of revealing this tremendous power within to transform, heal, and guide us through difficult times and into ourselves again. I draw from eastern and western approaches to mental health and I work with a variety of mindfulness-based methods to build self-compassion and awareness to support finding a healthy trajectory in life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that at every moment there is potential to find relief and change the course of our lives. By building compassionate self-awareness we can tap into the amazing power we possess to connect with ourselves and others. I am a student of the spiritual and religious traditions of the world and support working with those from diverse spiritual backgrounds or anyone who might consider themselves at least “spirit curious.” I have a combined 10 years of experience working in the mental health field as a substance use disorder counselor, mentor/skills trainer for foster youth, and as part of a mobile crisis response team in Eastern Oregon. Prior to entering the field, I worked as a park ranger, nature interpreter, youth conservation corps leader and wilderness guide. I believe that nature can be a powerful ally on our road to wellness and I integrate nature-based paths to healing in my work. When not in the office, you’ll find me on the trail, in the garden, or watching the stars.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor II, CADCII

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor II, CADCII

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Mindfulness-based Transpersonal Counseling student (2nd year) at Naropa University

name: Giving Hope Psychiatry
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Compassionate psychiatric care focused on clarity, stability, and hope—supporting your mental health every step of the way.
ideal_client: Giving Hope Psychiatry provides medication support for adults experiencing anxiety, depression, ADHD, mood disorders, and sleep issues. We help clients who feel overwhelmed or stuck find stability and clarity through personalized psychiatric care. Our approach is compassionate, collaborative, and focused on real progress.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: At Giving Hope Psychiatry, our approach is rooted in compassion, collaboration, and clinical expertise. We believe that effective psychiatric care begins with listening—truly understanding each person's experiences, symptoms, and goals. From there, we work closely with clients to develop personalized medication strategies that support long-term stability and growth. We prioritize education and transparency, so clients feel informed and empowered in their treatment decisions. Our care is not one-size-fits-all; we recognize the complexity of mental health and tailor our support to the individual. Through consistent follow-up and thoughtful adjustments, we help clients achieve meaningful progress. Whether someone is new to psychiatric care or has had past experiences, we strive to create a safe, respectful environment where hope and healing meet.

approaches.Why We are a Good Fit for You: Giving Hope Psychiatry is a good fit for individuals seeking a supportive, non-judgmental space to explore their mental health needs with the help of experienced professionals. If you’re looking for personalized medication support—whether it’s your first time or you’re seeking a better fit—we take the time to understand your story and goals. We’re especially suited for adults navigating anxiety, depression, ADHD, mood disorders, and sleep challenges. Our team values collaboration and clear communication, ensuring you’re an active part of your treatment plan. Through telehealth, we offer convenient access to care across Oregon, making it easier to get the help you need from the comfort of your home. If you want compassionate, thoughtful psychiatric care that goes beyond symptom management and focuses on long-term wellness, we may be the right fit for you.

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: We provide personalized medication management focused on safety, effectiveness, and client collaboration. Our approach includes thorough evaluations, clear communication, and regular follow-ups to ensure medications are well-tolerated and adjusted as needed. We aim to empower clients through education and shared decision-making, creating a treatment plan that supports long-term well-being.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: We specialize in diagnosing and treating ADHD in adults, focusing on how it affects daily functioning, attention, and emotional regulation. Through careful evaluation and personalized medication management, we help clients gain clarity, improve focus, and feel more in control. Our approach is supportive, evidence-based, and tailored to the unique ways ADHD shows up in each individual’s life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: We provide evidence-based medication support for adults experiencing anxiety, whether it’s generalized, social, or panic-related. Our approach focuses on reducing symptoms like worry, restlessness, and overwhelm so clients can regain a sense of calm and control. We take time to understand each individual’s experience and tailor treatment to support long-term emotional well-being.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: We specialize in treating depression with thoughtful, individualized medication support. Whether you're facing persistent sadness, low energy, or loss of interest in daily life, we work to help you find relief and restore a sense of purpose. Our care is compassionate, evidence-based, and focused on helping you feel more like yourself again.

specialities.name: Insomnia
specialities.description: We help adults struggling with insomnia find restful sleep through personalized, evidence-based medication support. Whether you have trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking too early, we work to identify underlying causes and tailor treatment to improve sleep quality and restore daily functioning. Our goal is to help you wake up feeling refreshed and focused.

name: Sarah Kimes
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: Licensed Professional Counselor Associate, Qualified Mental Health Professional registrant
intro: I am here to offer a safe, accepting, and collaborative space for you to move forward into a place of genuine healing and recovery.
ideal_client: Maybe life has been getting harder lately, maybe you feel overwhelmed and hopeless, and sometimes it can be hard to believe in anything. Maybe you feel unseen, unheard, or uncared for? Maybe you struggle to trust people, maybe you feel alone or worthless. But you're not alone; I am here to support you in your journey to healing and wellness. I work with people who experience symptoms of PTSD, Complex/Developmental Trauma, Anxiety, DID, depression, ADHD, Suicidal thoughts, and self-harm.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My approach is person-centered, social justice-informed, holistic, narrative, and systems-oriented. Sessions with me might include; talk therapy, art activities, the use of cognitive therapies to support specific symptom management, verbally processing your thoughts/feelings/experiences, and collaboration to identify what you need to move forward after traumatic experiences and/or in the wake of on-going trauma and injustice. My background: For over a decade, I have been honored to support people living with PTSD, complex PTSD, developmental trauma, historical and religious trauma, suicidal thoughts, self-harm, domestic violence, the LGBTQ+ community, depression, anxiety, dissociative disorders, bi-polar disorder, refugees, and grief/loss. I have worked in a number of settings, including advocacy for suicide prevention, crisis mental health services, community mental health, abuse intervention and preventative services, homeless services, and private group practices.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I believe that everyone has the ability to recover. Healing is about working to achieve the lives we want to live, finding meaning in life and in our connections to others, the world around us, and most importantly, meaning within ourselves. I have chosen to specialize in trauma and complex trauma therapy because I believe that with the right support, compassion, and time people can process the things they have experienced and move forward; you have the power to change how you think, feel, and behave. It will take time, therapy takes time, but I strongly value the therapeutic process and relationship and will do my best to provide a space that feels comfortable and safe for you. We can't undo the past, we live with the pain of trauma and mental illness daily, but it doesn't have to define us. We can change and overcome symptoms of PTSD, Anxiety, Depression, Mood disorders, DID, self-harm, and suicidality. I became a therapist to ensure that no one has to face their pain alone.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Person-centered therapist.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: Extensive work using bioecological family systems theory in practice.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: Trained in EcoTherapy interventions.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: I see a person from a multidimensional lens.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have worked with client's experiencing symptoms of PTSD and complex PTSD for over 10 years, supporting people to address their symptoms, process their feelings, and move forward into their own unique version of wellness and recovery.

specialities.name: Domestic Abuse
specialities.description: I have worked in abuse intervention and preventation for years, working with victims and survivors of domestic and interpersonal violence, childhood trauma and abuse histories, and sexual assault survivors

specialities.name: Suicidal Ideation
specialities.description: I have worked with people experiencing suicidal thoughts for over 10 years, offering a safe space to process these feelings and work towards decreasing-and eventually eliminating- suicidal thoughts.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Over ten years of experience supporting clients with depressive symptoms

name: Terra Anderson
title: Somatic Practitioner
intro: Hi, I’m Terra. I am a queer, trans, kink-affirming, polyamorous, somatic sex and relationship therapist.
ideal_client: So...you want more ease, confidence and connection in your intimate relationships? You want to feel more awake to pleasure, present in your body, and clear about what you want and how to ask for it. Are you ready find more freedom in your sex life without feeling weighed down by shame, fear, or the past? I'm here to help you navigate the hard stuff on your path towards your most empowered sexual expression and pleasure-filled life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a somatic sex therapist, I help you tap into what your body needs to relax, unfurl, and connect to pleasure. We will work with both body and mind to build awareness, skills, and confidence in navigating sexual communication, consent, and connection. What does this mean, you ask? Whether talking about sex comes easy to you or not, sexual satisfaction isn't just about lip service ;) its a full-body experience. My approach to therapy explores how movement, sensations, and breath are gateways to understanding your needs, desires, clear communication, and most importantly, consent.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My passion lies at the intersection of identity, pleasure and embodiment. Everything I love in this world has to do with one of those three things. My approach to therapy is no different. I'm on a mission to create more accessibility to pleasure in the LGBTQIA+ community. That means deeper erotic exploration, healing internalized shame, developing epic communication skills, claiming reverence for our bodies, and trailblazing new ways to structure relationships that truly meet your needs and leave heteronormativity to shrivel and rot on the vine. I'm interested in changing the world for us. I want you and I to have all the ecstasy and self-love society never taught us we could have. That's what I'm passionate about.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: I'm an Erotic Blueprint™ Coach and I use this framework with my sex therapy clients as well. I love how this methodology gives clients the language to explore their body's unique wiring for arousal and learn to clearly communicate their desires.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I love working with couples and polycules to foster deeper empathy, stronger communication, and greater sexual satisfaction.

specialities.name: Dance / Movement Therapy
specialities.description: I use Authentic Movement as a therapeutic modality for clients interested in working somatically with their subconscious, and couples interested in learning embodied communication skills. I earned my Masters Degree in Dance/Movement Therapy, and while not all of my clients want to move as a part of their sessions, for those who are more physically and experientially inclined - I've got you!

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: My guess is that when it comes to sex and intimacy, you'd like to actually feel progress, not just talk about it. Right? My approach to therapy inherently includes your body as a gateway to knowing yourself and your needs on a deeper level. In our work together I will help you track your felt experience by way of your breath, sensation, and movement to create shifts on an embodied level.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Whether it be gender exploration, navigating transition, building confidence in who you are, creating more satisfying and expansive sexual experiences, or navigating polyamory, I've got you.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I've spent years supporting my clients to come more deeply into their true expression. I love working in this space, helping people discover their truth, explore gender expression, come to greater peace within themselves, and navigate transitions.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I love working with couples and polycules. I'm passionate about helping you create the relationship dynamics you desire.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: Eh, I don't love the phrasing "sexual problems" but I do specialize in helping you navigate obstacles and pathways to the sex life you crave. I am certified in the Erotic Blueprints™ and have been working in the sexuality field for over a decade. If its about sex, pleasure, or intimacy, I'm into it.

name: Matt Joslin
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I strive to understand and validate your lived experience, and sit with you in the discomfort, pain, and nuance that comes with it.
ideal_client: I work well with individuals who are seeking to create new ways of relating to themselves, others, and the world at large. I have found success in treating clients who struggle with negative self-talk, anxiety, conflict in interpersonal relationships, traumatic childhoods, and difficult life transitions, including grief and loss. Therapy can be a quite painful and challenging process and I seek to provide a safe, nonjudgmental space for you to show up as your authentic, unapologetic self.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from a client-centered approach that places significance on the therapeutic relationship. I work to get to know you as an individual, to know your stories, experiences, values, pain, strengths, and desires. I enjoy helping clients build upon their already existing strengths, utilizing them to build confidence and trust within yourself. I incorporate aspects of narrative therapy (the stories we tell ourselves), attachment theory (how we relate to ourselves and others), mindfulness (being present in our experiences), and somatic therapy (focusing on the impact of trauma on our bodies). I believe healing happens when we extend compassion, empathy, love, and care to ourselves and others, recognizing harmful patterns and working to change them. I believe that in order to heal our pain, we are required to feel and experience the depths of that pain. I value sitting with clients as they feel their pain, providing care, kindness, empathy, compassion, and humor in the midst of it.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I firmly believe in the human capacity and desire for growth, change, and connection. Humans are relational, social creatures that require healthy attachment to ourselves and one another in order to truly live. I also believe that the social systems in which we live create barriers for us to connect with ourselves and others, and that our individual pain reflects the societal pain of our environment. Working from a systems perspective, I am dedicated to providing inclusive, culturally-sensitive, affirming, anti-racist, anti-colonial care for all people, of all identities and expressions. As a white male, I recognize the need to educate myself on the experiences of others, especially marginalized people. In my spare time, I enjoy walking my dog, connecting with nature, reading, spending time with friends and family, and visiting wonderful coffee shops in Portland.

name: Madison Meron
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I am passionate about supporting adults, children, couples & families as they navigate the intersection of trauma and relationships.
ideal_client: Have you found yourself having the same argument over and over with your partner? Are you feeling overwhelmed by your child’s behavior after stressful experiences? Do you feel disoriented and alone after leaving a high control group or religious context? Have you ever been called "too sensitive" or do you struggle to separate yourself from the emotions of other people? If any of these situations resonate with you, we may be a good fit!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The foundation of my work as a therapist is forming a safe and trusting relationship with my clients. I view therapy as a collaborative process between therapist and client and take a strengths-based approach, believing you are not at a deficit and are not defined by a diagnosis or symptoms. I recognize that social justice issues are a major contributor to many mental health concerns and do not see my clients in isolation from the issues going on in our world. You can expect to move at a pace that is comfortable for you, learning to trust the wisdom of your body through engaging in play, artistic expression and embodiment practices. I believe that we already have resources within us, but that trauma (individual, family and on a systemic scale) has separated us from ourselves, each other and the earth. I have extensive training/experience using trauma-informed modalities, like IFS & EMDR, to help you feel more connected to yourself and your relationships.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: My areas of focus include: Family therapy & Parent support; Couples/Partner therapy; Empaths & Sensitive folks; Religious trauma recovery; and Foster care/Adoption support. I have had extensive experience in supporting trauma recovery for those with PTSD & other other post-traumatic diagnoses. I have worked in the community mental health setting supporting children, families and couples with relational & attachment traumas. I have led support groups for parents, LGBTQIA+ youth and in-school sexual assault recovery groups for high schoolers. Some specific traumas I have experience working with includes: Infant & early life trauma, sexual abuse/assault, foster care/adoption and religious trauma. I love helping people heal within the context of their important relationships and believe that lasting change comes when we address the entire system.

name: Shannon Dooley
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Shannon offers a client-centered collaborative approach to allow each person to identify and work on the goals that are important to them.
ideal_client: Shannon has experience working with PTSD, childhood trauma, attachment issues, anxiety, depression, and chronic pain. She identifies as queer and has experience working with LGBTQIA2S+ individuals. Shannon is comfortable working with individuals from a variety of different cultural backgrounds and experiences. She approaches her work through a trauma-informed lens and with a sense of humility. She works with teenagers and adults.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Shannon has a BA in Social Science and a Masters of Social Work degree from Portland State University. Shannon has experience working as a Massage Therapist which informs her interest and approach to working with trauma. She has experience working in community mental health with people experiencing severe and persistent mental illness and housing insecurity. Shannon is trained in EMDR, and is also trained in Cognitive Processing Therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In her free time, Shannon loves comedy, little dogs, going on adventures, and being out in nature.

name: Emily LaMarca
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: Master of Arts in Clinical Mental Health Counseling
intro: I cover most areas of mental health counseling and offer specialized treatment for trauma.
ideal_client: I work with clients on a variety of concerns including anxiety, depression, life transitions, grief/loss, and spirituality. I also have specialized training and experience working with trauma. With trauma treatment, my goal is to walk alongside you through healing. I am trained in EMDR and also use mindfulness, grounding, and cognitive techniques.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I believe the way we think often informs how we feel and behave. Together we can work on confronting harmful and distorted thought patterns in order to develop healthier and more hopeful views of life and the future. This can involve acknowledging past hurts and trauma, learning new ways to cope with anxiety or depression, practicing self-acceptance, developing and maintaining self-care habits, learning mindfulness exercises, and so much more. The counselor/client relationship is also an important piece of healing. I would like to partner with you in your journey and healing process. Wherever you are in that journey, I look forward to meeting you.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I have always been drawn to "helping" fields of work but a big part of why I have chosen to pursue a career in counseling has been my own experience as a client. I learned skills that have helped to change some of my perspectives and enhance my life. The personal growth and healing I experienced through the therapeutic relationship are things I will always carry with me. I hope that I can help others in a similar manner.

name: Leslie Magana
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Whether you’re struggling with relationship conflict, anger management, or personal growth, I provide a space for exploration and change.
ideal_client: I bring specialized training in anger management and behavior intervention, working with both heterosexual and queer couples where conflict and emotional regulation are key concerns. Many of my clients are navigating relationship stress, miscommunication, or struggling with accountability in their interactions. I also support queer individuals in exploring their gender identity, sexuality, relational structures, and the impact of oppression on their well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: By approaching every client with radical compassion and honoring their unique lived experiences, I can begin to gently confront harmful behavioral patterns. This process opens the door to tackle difficult emotions and the defense mechanisms that keep a person stuck. I believe that change is facilitated through deepened awareness of the beliefs, emotions, and cultural influences that shape us. This informed self-awareness combined with compassionate accountability, provides the foundation for growth. Relationships can be deeply fulfilling – and also incredibly challenging. My expertise lies in helping individuals and couples break harmful cycles, improve communication, and strengthen connections. Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), with an awareness of power dynamics and systems.

name: Mia Koenig
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: To learn, grow and heal from experiences. That's the focus.

approaches.What I Specialize In: My approach to therapy comes from a collection of viewpoints of connection and relationships with friends, family, and the self. I focus on repair between relationships and individuals wanting to cultivate a meaningful identity of self. Our collaborative work together will be fruitful with purpose and intention. I have a passion for working with adolescents and their families to navigate understanding and to promote growth as a system. My experience thus far includes a great emphasis on eating disorders and embodiment. I offer an integrative, client-centered approach using evidence based practices of narrative therapy, cognitive behavioral therapy, solution focused, positive psychology and mindfulness.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I have worked in a Partial Hospitalization Program for pediatric eating disorders since 2020 and have experience working with clients ages 6-50 struggling with Anorexia Nervosa, ARFID, OFSED and binging/purging disorders.

name: Malachi Harrison
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: A trans and neurodivergent provider with a passion for helping people thrive in the narrative of their own life.
ideal_client: As a child and family therapist who is neurodivergent and transgender myself, I have a passion for working with youth with ASD/ADHD, as well as youth who identify as trans and LGBT. I also work well with children and families with trauma backgrounds, and have experience in treating mood, anxiety, and behavioral disorders. It is crucial to support these young people with developing a healthy sense of self and belongingness, and to be able to develop a positive sense of identity in the world.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With an approach grounded in Narrative Therapy, I conceptualize change using the perspective that we are all living our own “narrative”, the story we tell ourselves about our lives and who we are as people. These narratives are accumulations of internal and external experiences, and we can be both empowered and trapped within these narratives. By supporting individuals in understanding these personal narratives, we can recenter the individual’s right to author that narrative in a way that emphasizes personal strengths and values to create meaningful change. Along with this, I incorporate a variety of techniques including play therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and Cognitive-Behavioral Therapy, and work from a trauma-informed lens using approaches of Collaborative Problem Solving and the Attachment, Regulation, and Competency Framework.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Human connection is a vital part of all of us; through this connection we find support, solace, and strength. It is my privilege to be in a position where I can extend that support through a therapeutic relationship, and use my knowledge and compassion to help others thrive. By working with children and their families, I aim to provide children and teens with a safe and encouraging environment to support development of their sense of identity and capability, as well as equipping their environment to continue to foster this growth.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I have had extensive training in working with youth on the autism spectrum and their families. By equipping families with the skills to support their children, and supporting youth with asserting their identity and autonomy in a world that is not built for them, I can support individuals using a blend of psychoeducation, skill building, play therapy, and talk therapy to help individuals build a positive sense of identity in the world.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: As a transgender provider myself, I have both the experience and training to provide services that take into context the experience of a client's gender identity and how that identity impacts their experience in the world. Using narrative therapy and ACT, I support individuals in exploring and asserting their sense of personal identity, and building personal strength in this identity.

name: Jason Wilkinson
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I join couples in their journey from miscommunication, loneliness, and pain, to one of trust, love, and peace.
ideal_client: Perhaps you have hit a rough patch in your marriage. You feel alone, agitated, and irritated at everything your partner does. You don't feel appreciated or seen. The relationship feels "off." You want to communicate better. You want to be on the same page. You want to feel like a team. If you are asking yourself, “Can this work?” the answer is "Yes!" You can improve your communication, successfully handle conflict, and find joy in your resources that you will gain in couples counseling.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Finding the right therapist can be challenging. It almost always comes down to relationship - whether this person “gets me.” I create a warm and welcoming atmosphere that allows for the you to be seen and known. You need to be able to share and explore what is causing pain or circumstances that brings you into counseling and given the space to discover the truth of your strength. It is my belief that the world benefits from people who are able to function with a great sense of contentment, wholeness, and self-efficacy - and that happy and healthy relationships with self and the significant persons in our lives help us reach that state of being. I help people feel empowered to tackle their concerns of relational and marital conflict, anxiety, depression, and low self-esteem by helping them develop the skills needed for emotional self-regulation.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: The increase of people struggling with anxiety and depression motivated me to become a counselor. Feeling trapped by the feelings of sadness or fear is not the type of life people want. I desire to walk with others to a place of freedom from those emotions. With over 18 years of experience working with teenagers, young adults, and parents, I have honed an ability to have positive interactions with individuals and couples in need of assistance. With an education in understanding how individuals, couples, and families are impacted by systems, I use an integrative approach that includes Restoration Therapy, Emotionally-Focused Therapy, and mindfulness. My process provides tools that empower clients to change painful systems or cycles that they are participating in. Having earned an MDiv degree has also prepared me to partici Having earned an MDiv degree has also prepared me to participate in conversations regarding spirituality if that is a part of your story you would like to explore.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I have extensive training as a couples counselor. My education in relational systems, or cycles, provides me with a unique perspective in seeing how each individual participates in the making of a whole. I use this to help couples discover ways that they may better relate to one another and strengthen their communication.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: My desire to see people living as their best selves has motivated me to gain the necessary skills to be a marriage and couples counselor. If you ever once thought or believed that you were your best self alongside of your partner or spouse, and you are curious if you can be that way again, then I have the training to help you grow in communication and compassion to help you find out.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a way that we cope with a specific emotion. We will work to uncover the emotion that initiates the coping behavior of anxiety, which then assists in lessening the reactive behavior.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Low self-esteem is caused by the negative messages we tell ourselves. We will explore these messages to discover what could be the causes, then work to create new neural pathways of what is true about who you are.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Having received an MDiv from Fuller Theological Seminary, I have the knowledge and experience to assist you in exploring your own spirituality and faith.

name: Heather Simpson
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Hi, I’m Heather, the Owner of Mindful Inquiry Therapy LLC, an intersectional, pleasure focused and trauma informed practice in Portland OR.
ideal_client: Whether you are struggling with stress, anxiety, depression, or relationship issues, you deserve a therapist who will be open and supportive yet willing to challenge you gently when needed. With an approach that combines connection and boundaries, we can work together to help you find the agency you need to move through life with pleasure.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work centers on providing intersectional, pleasure focused, trauma informed therapy for individuals, couples, and polyamorous /nonmonogamous folks to create a space for queer affirming, relationship counseling. My mission is to provide comprehensive and systemic relational therapy centered on providing spaces for self agency and trauma informed care. My philosophy and approach is centered on mindful, contextual, emotion focused and trans-generational practices.

approaches.Why We are a Good Fit for You: I am a speaker, advocate and mental health professional with a Masters degree in marriage couple and family therapy from Lewis and Clark College. I also holds bachelor degrees in psychology, philosophy, and women's and gender studies from the University of Michigan-Dearborn. As a queer Black woman, I am committed to providing trans-generational contextual and emotion-focused therapy to people of color, LGBTQIA+, non-monogamous, and kink communities.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: With previous degrees in Women's and Gender Studies and a background in sexuality I can affirm not only an understanding of LGBTQ issues from an academic perspective but also from a lived experience.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: Navigating cultural and systemic oppression has been a lifelong journey. it's important that I share the knowledge that I have cultivated with others. As a Black queer woman, living in marginalized spaces, I am able to understand systemic oppression from different lenses. With coursework stemming from women’s and gender studies, to philosophy to psychology I built a foundation of understanding to help clients acknowledge how systems of oppression operate In their lives snd create change.

name: Crystal Covelle
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I am a warm and compassionate listener, using a personable approach, offering tele-visit individual therapy.

approaches.My Background: My roles in the community have ranged from individual therapy, crisis line counselor, shelter worker, and support group facilitator, to yoga instructor and studio owner, as well as candlemaker and event organizer.  I'm a Clinical Social Worker Associate (CSWA). I received my Master of Social Work (MSW) from LSU. I am honored and grateful to support folks on their path. /// In my free time, I enjoy living room dance parties with my partner and our five year old kiddo.

name: Maria Bonacci
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I believe in approaches to living and healing that liberate us from systemic harm, and in care networks that center transformative change.
ideal_client: I provide therapy to people ages 18 and up. I specialize in working with queer and trans people, pot-stirrers, and outsiders.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My goal as your therapist is to help you feel more like yourself and to achieve the goals you have for your life. I bring training in multiple philosophies and styles, and consider my practice style eclectic/integrative. My approach is strengths-based and person-centered. I completed initial training in Emotion Focused Therapy in Fall 2021. I use Narrative Exposure Therapy for trauma to treat PTSD. I hold a Master's of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Portland State University. I have 20 yrs. of experience in public health and mental health via work in syringe exchange, sexuality education, HIV testing/care, early psychosis intervention, interpersonal violence advocacy, trans competency in mental health care, and most recently in psychiatric emergency care. My previous work and my political beliefs are a strong influence on my work as a therapist.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a White, queer, genderqueer person from the east coast. For those who are curious: Libra, Libra, Capricorn; ENFP; Enneagram 8. I am committed to anti-racist work. I am thoughtfully assertive. I believe in approaches to healing that don't reproduce systemic harm, and in care networks that center transformative change. I want to live in a world without police and prisons, and I am realistic about the work it takes to get there. I aim to support people to live a life that is aligned with their values and which helps them achieve their goals. I do this while keeping in mind that the wellness of one person impacts the wellness of their broader social circles and society at large.

specialities.name: Addiction Therapy
specialities.description: with a specialization in harm reduction. I have worked in various roles as a harm reductionist, including in syringe exchange and injection drug user health services, as a safer sex counselor, and in HIV/STD prevention and care work.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I utilize EFT in individual, couples and group work to connect presenting problems with deeper emotional context.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: "Attachment" is a way to explore how and in what contexts we feel safe. I have studied Interpersonal Neurobiology which is deeply rooted in attachment theory and the interpersonal emotional information we internalize and which as a result impacts our day to day interactions.

specialities.name: Panic
specialities.description: I have training in various therapeutic interventions to address panic and other anxiety disorders.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: My approach to addiction treatment is centered in harm reduction with a person centered approach. I want to help you examine your substance use and support changes as you are wanting to make them.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I am a queer, genderqueer person. I have worked in various roles alongside trans and non-binary people to provide therapy, advocacy, and documentation/letters for surgery.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: Tired of being asked about your "self-care" practices? Let's talk about ways we can create lives inside and outside the confines of capitalism that offer us room to process intense and complex emotional experiences.

name: Jenn Delaune
title: Student Counselor
intro: I work with individuals, adolescents, couples, and families. I'd be honored to support and walk with you on your life's journey.
ideal_client: I know I was born, and I know that I’ll die / The in-between is mine.” ~ Pearl Jam. How’s your in-between going? Are you living by your rules or someone else’s? Relationships not as great as they could be? Are family or work dynamics causing increased stress? Are you overwhelmed or overthinking about anything and everything? We are the experts of our own lives. But sometimes, we need help to work through the complexities to shape our ideal in-between.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I’m in my final year of completing my Marriage and Family Therapy graduate degree at Capella University, a COMFTE-approved program. I am supervised by three Licensed Marriage and Family Therapists: Shari Davison, Liz Gregory, and Dr. Terri Mathias. From an integrative therapy approach, I’ll help you navigate life’s entanglements, transitions, stress, anxiety, depression, relationship issues, family conflict, work/life imbalances, grief, and trauma. I’ve been in a committed partnership for 18 years, experiencing the ebbs and flows of relationships. I also have 20+ years of corporate experience, understanding its complexities and politics to help you discover ways to prioritize yourself in that environment. During our initial sessions, we will explore the issues you are comfortable with and work together to develop a strategy for dealing with them in a way that will help you regain your life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that fresh air can shift your mood and perspective, music is a magical healing tool, you’re never too old to play, and taking a nap is never a waste of time. I believe trust is earned, not given. I believe therapy is one of the best investments you can make for yourself. Through my own therapy and having a trusted therapist by my side, I’ve learned to successfully manage when my past seeps into my present, personal insecurities, anxiety, depression, grief, loss, and trauma. I wish the same for you and would be honored to walk beside you on your journey to healing. I offer a nonjudgmental and supportive space for your personal exploration. I’m allied with the LGBTQ+ community and incorporate cultural awareness and sensitivity into my practice. Healing and transformation take work, and it will be uncomfortable, but it is absolutely worth it.

name: Christopher Bartel
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I am a psychologist licensed in the state of Oregon, work analytically, and provide individual psychotherapy to adults.
ideal_client: I work well with clients who are seeking to establish a deeper understanding of themselves, are curious about their inner lives and how their history has impacted them and lives on in present day, gaining increased insight and awareness into aspects of their experience that may be inaccessible or unconscious, and using the therapeutic relationship to better understand their own thoughts, feelings, and ways of relating with others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I strive to establish a supportive, respectful, and affirming environment in which clients can identify and explore thoughts, feelings, beliefs, and recurring patterns of behavior that may be interfering with their capacity to experience a fuller and more satisfying life. I place a high emphasis on the importance of the therapeutic relationship, and I offer a collaborative, relational, and culturally sensitive approach in which both therapist and client are actively working together to deepen self-understanding and promote positive change.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a psychologist licensed by the Oregon Board of Psychologist Examiners. I earned a Master's and Doctor of Psychology Degrees in Clinical Psychology from The Chicago School of Professional Psychology (fully accredited by the American Psychological Association), and completed an APA-approved internship as well as a post-doctoral residency. I also completed additional postdoc training in psychodynamic psychotherapy at the Oregon Psychoanalytic Center and I am currently a candidate in psychoanalysis at the Oregon Psychoanalytic Institute. I am trained in psychoanalytic, humanistic/existential, and cognitive-behavioral techniques. I work with a wide array of issues surrounding anxiety, depression, interpersonal struggles, grief/loss, identity (including LGBTQ), and post-trauma concerns, including working with adult survivors of childhood abuse.

name: Timothy (Tim) Holt
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Hello, my name is Tim and I look forward to being your guide in re-establishing a sense of stillness in your daily existence.
ideal_client: The prospect of experiencing a change in our mental health is frightening, especially when there is a sense of losing control and our world is crashing in around us, as if, we have no place to find refuge. We all have the potential to be confronted by anxiety, depression, or other changes in our mental health that may require finding support, guidance, and direction from a provider that returns us to a sense of equilibrium.

approaches.My Background: I'm a psychiatric nurse practitioner, board certified, who has practiced in the mental health/psychiatric field for 27 years, which began after my education and additional training thru Oregon Health Sciences University in Portland, Oregon. I have treated the majority of psychiatric disorders that can be seen in such settings as outpatient mental health clinics in rural and urban settings, county jail and prison facilities, outpatient and inpatient substance abuse treatment facilities, adult foster homes for those with developmental disabilities/mental illness, psychiatric hospitals, and as a consultant to certain organizations at the state level that determine disability status. I use multiple tools in treating psychiatric disorders, but a frequently used tool is the use of medication and the use of cognitive behavioral therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe we should treat each individual with dignity, respect, and kindness and the hope that this would be reciprocated by the other individual. However, I realize this may not be the case with each individual and it's in this instance to set appropriate boundaries, especially to reinforce the importance of self-worth. I believe connection with others is important and for this to be an opportunity for self-growth, as well as lifting up those who are around us.

name: Shelby Hurd
title: Student Counselor
intro: Hi! My name is Shelby, and I am a Clinical Social Work graduate student at Portland State University.
ideal_client: My clients usually reach out to me due to feeling overwhelmed and struggling to navigate life complexities, such as relationship difficulties, anxiety, and life transitions. They often feel stuck and are seeking ways to make lasting change in their lives in order to make more room for joy and connection. I want to work together to help you feel confident in your abilities to overcome life's obstacles and break out of stuck patterns.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I see both individuals and couples in my practice. I offer goal directed treatment using Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT), and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT).

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: It is an honor for me to walk alongside my clients through their journeys of healing and self exploration. I bring a lively, open, and compassionate presence to my practice, and have room for humor in the work that we do together. I look forward to connecting and engaging in the work with you.

name: Samara Roman-Holba
title: Student Counselor
intro: I am a graduate student with Oregon City Counseling earning my Master’s of Arts in Counseling at Northwestern University.
ideal_client: In addition to my professional and educational background, my experience as competitive runner and queer woman who came out in adulthood have made me particularly interested in supporting clients through: -LGBTQ+ identity - Athlete identity and performance anxiety -Body image - Anxiety - Depression

approaches.My Background: I graduated from Vassar College in 2017 with a degree in biochemistry. I went on to pursue a Master’s of Science in Human Nutrition and a Master’s of Education in Community Nutrition Education at Columbia University and became a registered dietitian in 2021. I have worked as an eating disorder and sports dietitian in residential and outpatient treatment settings. While I loved working with people individually, I realized I wanted to be able to support clients with their mental health on a deeper level and began pursuing my degree in counseling.

name: Michael Viola
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Together we'll work to liberate your empowered creative Self. Allow me to support, guide, and coach you through this process
ideal_client: My clients are looking for support, guidance, and/or coaching through the process of getting to know, understand, liberate, and transform limiting patterns that prevent them from living their most fulfilled selves. My clients range in age from late teens to the elder stage of life. They are curious about approaching old problems in new ways and they are willing to take the plunge. I'm an educator as much as a therapist and I encourage any prospective client to reach out for a free consult.

approaches.My Background: I received my BA from Swarthmore College in Pennsylvania and my MA in Counseling from Southwestern College in Santa Fe, NM. I have also been educated and worked in the corporate and educational structures of NYC. I apprenticed with master herbalists in Ithaca, NY and Native healers in New Mexico and the Peruvian Amazon. I have been cultivating a life as a psychotherapist, shamanic practitioner, and artist. My journey has required me to explore and unify my inner Male and Female polarities along with the elemental energies of the directions (Earth, Air, Fire, Water). This union births the conscious and creative self within. We can then manifest in alignment with this Self, our Community, and The Earth, free from limiting energetic patterns. I work to assist others in this pursuit.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I view our patterns and habitual experiences as a function of vibration/frequency/resonance. We can hold the frequency patterns of earlier childhood traumas, cultural/religious narratives, ancestral wounds, and even past life tragedies. The beliefs that form from these experiences are stored within the body/mind frequency structure. When we liberate hidden patterns, purge them, and introduce new ones, we have effectively changed our resonant frequencies. The work is then to find the belief, in what it is rooted, and then to liberate the energy and introduce a new energetic imprint that is more appropriate. We can do this in many ways and I specialize in using shamanic techniques, including journey work, psychotherapy, and archetypal psychology to do this. My work has arisen from personal pursuits in the study of quantum physics/string theory, Jungian/Archetypal Psychology, Energy Psychology, Transpersonal Psychology, Somatic Body/Mind Psychology, Herbalism, and Vibrational Medicine.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I work to help you recalibrate your physical experience through processing your emotional and energetic pathways. Together we can pave new energetic pathways to affect present and future change in your behavioral habits and physical body. Through breathing, intention, focus, and visualization we can liberate somatically held beliefs. Intentional living, ceremony, and a regular spiritual practice can also be great tools in holding our truth, our words, and our behaviors in alignment.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: The framework of my therapy/coaching explores the relationship of self within the context of the greater whole. What does it mean to be in right relationship with all of the sentient consciousness around us? What is our relevance within all of creation? By honoring our deepest truths may we then connect with the deepest truths of others. I assist my clients in this process.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Intuition and a spiritual connection are what have informed my own healing. My deep connection permits others to find their own connection and to explore and strengthen it. This process will encourage the full flowering of our gifts as we share them. This truth is what we carry as potential in our hearts, what is meant to be shared in order to leave our unique mark in the world.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Trusting the process and embracing our power in any situation can help us grow. This is courage and it walks with us at all times. Sometimes its a little harder to see. I help you find that courage in order to surrender to the process of growth.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: There is a divine spark in all things. Each has its own purpose, plan, and destiny. In trusting this truth and respecting the interconnection of all things we recognize our own spiritual selves within the greater whole. From this concept we can begin to recognize our own spiritual power and utilize it to evolve, grow, and celebrate our lives.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Men need support. Men have feelings and need to feel and share them. Feeling vulnerable is part of that process. What are the imprints you've inherited as a man and how may they be preventing you from living and feeling vital and empowered? The fact that I have gone there myself allows me to hold the energy permitting my clients to go there as well.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: The concept of two-spirit is paramount in working with these issues. Embodying the spirit of electrical male and magnetic female is a gift and must be recognized as such. As a gay male myself much empowerment and strength has come from uniting these polarities and owning the power of uniqueness as our energy runs along the diversity of this spectrum. We are something far beyond what pop culture and religion designate us.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: We'll explore the elements that contribute to your anxiety and how to address each area. From deep conscious breathing, somatic processing, and shamanic journey we'll work to discover hidden elements for understanding and relieving anxious tension.

name: Wanda Burgi
title: Student Counselor
intro: When life feels upside down, I’m here - offering a space to breathe, support to lean on, and empathy that heals.
ideal_client: Is life not always making sense in this new season? Do you find yourself in a season of transition - a relationship shift, career change, loss, identity questions, or simply feeling stuck? I understand that life can have unexpected bumps that feel disorienting and difficult. Adjusting to change isn't easy, and it is completely normal to experience anxiety, grief, or confusion along the way.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach therapy through a trauma-informed lens, with the understanding that emotions are a vital part of our experience. They can offer insight into our needs, desires, and the challenges we face. I believe that our bodies also hold important clues to our emotional and mental states, and by tuning into them, we can deepen our understanding of ourselves and heal in a more integrated way. I am committed to walking alongside you on your journey toward healing, while providing a safe, supportive, and empathetic space where you can explore and honor this season in your life.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a therapist because I saw individuals and communities—across many different contexts—struggling, often without realizing they needed support. I noticed how people were acting and speaking from wounded places, sometimes causing harm to themselves and those around them. That moved me. I believe that spaces like places of worship, which are meant to offer refuge, often lack the mental health support needed for true healing and connection. My hope is to bridge that gap, helping individuals find the peace, self-awareness, and acceptance we all deserve. To me, therapy is about more than just coping—it’s about growing into a more compassionate and whole version of ourselves, for our own sake and for the sake of the communities we’re part of.

name: Kim Daglen
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: Master's of Arts, Clinical Mental Health Counseling
intro: Currently accepting new clients for telehealth only at this time. I look forward to working with you!
ideal_client: Feeling trapped by your circumstances or struggling to find meaning in your life? Maybe you feel powerless to change your personal or relational thought patterns and habits; fortunately, therapy can offer you a safe space to explore your inner world while providing valuable tools to diffuse negative thinking, develop greater self-love, and help you reach your full potential. We can all benefit from additional support to address specific problems in life or as a means to further personal growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I know that exploring emotions and discussing difficult or traumatic life experiences takes a great deal of courage and vulnerability. I welcome and honor you and your story. I draw a variety of experiential modalities such as mindfulness and body awareness techniques to help clients access greater calm, creativity, and joy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: With a foundation of trust, we can collaborate together on achieving your goals and unearthing a sense of peace and purpose. We can work together to increase self-awareness and presence of mind to create opportunities for growth and change in your life and relationships. I value providing a respectful, compassionate, and nonjudgmental space for all clients.

name: Kacee Markarian
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Your desire to heal, grow and thrive will be met by my compassion, curiosity and skills in effective psychotherapy.
ideal_client: As a radical therapist who is queer, fat and femme, I have a deep understanding of how hard it is to be a person at times. If you have struggled to find yourself, develop healthy connections, feel comfort and pleasure in your body and/or emotional resilience, I'm here for you.

approaches.My Background and Approach: With over 10 years of experience and a Master's degree from a world-renowned Institute in San Francisco that blends Western and Eastern perspectives (CIIS), I incorporate traditional and alternative views and methods to facilitate your personal exploration and discovery of new tools and strengths. My clinical orientation is psychodynamic, existential-humanistic and trauma-informed, while also incorporating good old-fashioned humor and creativity. We're all sparkling gems in our own ways. I will help you sand down your rough edges by patiently attending to your pain, add to your shine through loving celebration of your unique gifts, and grow in appreciation and acceptance of your dark "flaws." I also use art therapy, psychosynthesis and Gestalt perspectives and tools.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: You'll find my affirming, direct methods for treating eating disorders empowering as we identify underlying beliefs and feelings that result in cycles of control / out of control, combined with tools for creating healthier relationships with your body, mind, food and life. If you've been taking a GLP-1 or are considering it, my in-depth knowledge about the science and mental health aspects will help you hold complexity and deal with internal/societal biases, as well as hopes for a healthier you.

name: Robert Sena
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Grounded in a Person-Centered approach, Robert begins every therapeutic relationship by honoring the uniqueness and autonomy of the person.
ideal_client: Robert works with Depression, OCD, Anxiety, Eating Disorders, Bipolar Disorders, Borderline Personality Disorders, C-PTSD, Autism Spectrum, Identity Exploration. Robert sees clients ages 15 and older.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Grounded in a Person-Centered approach, I begin every therapeutic relationship by honoring the uniqueness of the client and what gifts they have to share with the world. I draw from the following approaches to help my clients in these ways; CBT: To help the mind become a place of safety and help, rather than chaos. DBT: To help my clients get their needs met; Physiologically and interpersonally. ACT: To help clients live a life worthwhile, to become emotionally flexible, and teach clients to relate to themselves through their values rather than their emotions. IFS: To explore the parts of us that protect deeply held pain, and to release and transform those exiled parts. Choice Theory: To practically assess the day-to-day decisions clients make and if they are aligning with their greater purpose. Gestalt: To help clients explore how they perceive, know, and understand themselves in context to their environment and world. TA: To help clients see interactions as equal and empowering.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe the inherent whole is deeply overlooked in culture today. I became a yoga instructor and practiced herbal medicine for years prior to becoming a clinician. I became a therapist because I wanted to learn the practical skills that help people to access the place of Self-assured confidence and their inner locus of control. I am interested in the person sitting in front of me and what I can do to help them access themselves in a way that is more safe, effective, comfortable, and actualizing to their fullest Selfhood.

name: Shari Cooper
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi, I’m Shari! I am a very empathetic and authentic person so I hope I can make you feel comfortable during our time together.
ideal_client: Do you feel like you don't fit in anywhere? Am I the only one who feels like this? Do I know who I am?

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Together we will create goals that fit your specific needs and wants. We will forever make necessary changes to create the therapeutic environment best for you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that all people were created equal, we were all just given funny quirks that we all get to muddle through life with. People need to feel joy in a time when everyone is uncertain of what’s next and I want to help guide those that need a little extra support. I will provide a warm and safe environment to ease any fears you might have about counseling. It’s not as scary as you might think!

name: Kristina Barnett
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I'm so glad you found me! If you're struggling with relationship issues, I am here to help.
ideal_client: I help couples & individuals heal their relationships to self and each other. I have worked with people in new relationships, long-term relationships, single people, people ending relationships, and people in poly relationships. Whether working with dyads or individuals, I am always considering childhood and adult attachment styles and bonds. Many of our human struggles emerge from troubled connections with significant people in our lives or with ourselves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I'm a systems thinker with a background in sociology and marriage and family therapy. I always consider your context including cultural, familial, and relational factors. I use a variety of models primarily centered around EFT and IFS, which are both models that focus on attachment, relational wounds, and creating secure bonds through a combination of mindfulness and reparative experiences in therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I bring an intersectional feminist, anti-racist, LGBTQIA2+-affirming, sex-positive perspective to the therapy process. I believe pleasure and ease are human birthrights. I believe the closer we can get to living out an authentic expression of our full, unique selves, the better we all are.

name: Adam Benjamin
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Old wounds and beliefs about ourselves can hijack our lives. Developing clarity and new practices lets us live more freely and fully.
ideal_client: I work with individual adult clients who may have persistent feelings of stuckness or sadness stemming from adverse life events, childhood trauma, attachment wounds, or dysfunctional/mentally ill parents. My practice is inclusive and I work with people of all races, genders, sexual orientations, relationship styles and faiths.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My clients develop lasting relief from compelling feelings and self-beliefs that may find their roots in childhood or adverse life events. Living fully means seeing current events clearly, but also developing flexibility in the reactions and expectations we developed long ago. These "old files" are stored in our felt, bodily experience as well as our stories about ourselves. The work of therapy is getting curious together not only about your thoughts and feelings, but also about your sensations and impulses -- the subtle machinery of experience that constitutes (and often limits) your range of choices. I am certified in Hakomi psychotherapy, a kind of mindful & experiential therapy, and have advanced training in resolving attachment wounding. I have a particular interest in working with individuals who grew up with a dysfunctional, immature, or mentally ill parent.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Therapy is my calling, but it is not my first career. I also have a PhD in Communication Studies and taught college courses before turning toward psychotherapy. In my spare time I enjoy repairing and riding old motorcycles. I grew up in the New York area and have lived in Portland since 2001.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: A thorough grasp of attachment theory is foundational to understand most forms of dysregulation or mental illness. I consider attachment patterns as I seek to tune in to each client's suffering. I also have training in attachment-based therapeutic techniques.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: Hakomi is an approach to therapy that brings mindful attention to bodily experiences, and an experiment-based approach to insight and change. I have extensive training in Hakomi and tend to use some of its techniques in most of my sessions. I borrow from Hakomi an attitude of compassionate respect for each client's organic process, and a basic stance of seeking to follow and unfold that process.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: 'Mindfulness' as used in my training background means 'sustained, non-judgmental attention and self-study.' This kind of mindfulness is not meditation; it is a therapeutic technique applied explicitly to promote insight and relieve distress. Mindful observation of one's feelings, sensations, and reactions, is a part of many therapy sessions, and may be done eyes-open or eyes-closed, as a client's comfort allows.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: Central to my approach is to understand the impact of historical or complex trauma, including the vagal and brain systems it often affects, and to help you develop ways to manage its effects on your nervous system.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: We encounter many forms of grief in our lives. I have conducted bereavement groups for those who have lost loved ones. I am also attuned to the grief that accompanies a lost childhood (for instance, when a parent has major mental illness), or lost innocence (the sense of safety, for instance, that disappears due to abusive or chaotic upbringing).

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: The corrosive effects of poor self-worth, and shame in particular, limit our capacity for flexible thinking and the range of choices we perceive in many situations.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression and anxiety are often situational, but just as often they are rooted in a core experience of ourselves that has persisted a long time, and resists any efforts to think our way clear of them. The mindful and experiential techniques I utilize allow access to the deep, core experiences and beliefs that need to be changed so that we can feel different and live with renewed energy.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I have a particular interest in working with men to overcome the legacy of toxic masculinity and the persistent burden of shame that it engenders.

name: Family Roots Therapy
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We are a team of counselors who believe that all families can overcome challenges and live happier, more harmonious lives together.
ideal_client: Are you a new parent struggling to adjust to parenthood? Are you worried about your child or teen's mental health? Struggling with recent change in your family such as grief, loss, divorce, or blending families? Tired of constant conflict, arguing, and fighting taking over your home? We can help. We have therapists with expertise and training in helping parents, children, and teens develop healthier relationships, reduce stress, and improve communication.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our therapists are highly skilled in different therapy approaches, including Child-Parent Psychotherapy, art therapy, play therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Gottman method, and postpartum/perinatal mental health. Because a mental health challenge in one family member affects all family members, we believe in supporting each person in the family holistically and meeting each person's needs. We believe that there is no one right way to be a family and that one family structure is not better than another. We want all families to feel welcome and included at Family Roots. That's why we have therapists who work with queer, non-binary, and trans individuals (children, teens, and parents), as well as polyamorous couples, blended families and divorced families.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Our counselors include Licensed Marriage and Family Therapists, Licensed Professional Counselors, and Licensed Art Therapists, as well as Professional Counselor Interns (who are working toward their hours for full independent licensure). Our counselors have a wide range of experiences, from working in community mental health to working in school, inpatient, or prison settings. Specialties include prenatal and perinatal mental health, parenting support using Collaborative Problem Solving and Positive Discipline, play therapy with young children, working with blended families and divorced families, and working with couples on the transition to parenthood.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Our child therapists have extensive experience in play therapy, including a specialized form of play-based therapy called Child-Parent Psychotherapy, which focuses on the parent-child relationship and increasing connection and attachment in young children. We are unique in having experience and training in working with children under 6 years old, which is a highly specialized area in counseling.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: Our therapists have a variety of backgrounds in engaging families in treatment. Specialized training in using Structural Family Therapy, Child-Parent Psychotherapy, and other relationship-based approaches allow our therapists to confidently treat the entire family and manage conflict within families.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: Our Licensed Art Therapist has experience in using art therapy to help teens explore their emotions, build self-esteem, and heal.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: We have therapists who practice from a family systems approach and have training in Marriage & Family Therapy, which includes specific training in working with couples. We use approaches such as the Gottman method and Emotion-Focused Therapy, which focuses on adult attachment styles and how your early relationships influence your close relationships in adulthood.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: Our postpartum/perinatal counselors have completed advanced training from Postpartum Support International to learn how to address the complex needs of postpartum individuals and families. This includes mothers, fathers, and couples. We have therapists who are competent in supporting trans and nonbinary individuals, who are often overlooked in postpartum treatment.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Our therapists who specialize in parenting have advanced training in using Collaborative Problem Solving and Positive Discipline. We coach parents in how to communicate effectively with their kids and how to listen to their kids' needs and address their children's challenging behavior with empathy.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Our family therapists have gone through specific training on working with families as a whole, not just individuals. Any changes or mental health issues in one person in a family affect the entire family. People don't exist in a vacuum! For that reason, family therapists focus on helping your entire family work through conflict around issues such as divorce, blending families, or reunification.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: We have counselors who have received specialized training in Child-Parent Psychotherapy, an approach that treats young children ages 0-6 who have experienced trauma, violence, or separation from a caregiver. Our child and teen therapists are also trained in play therapy and art therapy, and have experience working in schools and community-based settings.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
