specialities.description: Our couples counselors have completed training in using the Gottman method and specifically focus on helping couples transition to parenthood and navigate conflict around parenting. This can include co-parenting counseling with divorced or separated couples, as well as helping married couples improve parenting dynamics.

name: Ally Simone
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I have availability for new clients seeking extended EMDR and partnered therapy sessions as of October 2024
ideal_client: Many of my clients come to me for support on their trauma healing journeys, expressing a desire to break cycles, set boundaries, and develop a stronger sense of identity, self worth, and trust in themselves. I love guiding people toward more authentic and fulfilling relationships. I welcome clients of all identities (more on that below) and those attending therapy for the first time or the 50th time.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe every individual is the expert of their lived experience and is equipped with the resources they need to grow, change, and thrive, and I also believe we all need a little help to get there sometimes. I am here to walk alongside you in your journey, offering empathy, challenging harmful beliefs, and providing tools for personal growth. I view relationships through an attachment lens and explore emotions as a way to better understand ourselves and others. As a trauma survivor, I have a real understanding of how past experiences can shape our current realities, and the transformative power of processing old wounds. We will work together to create a safe and brave space where you can practice noticing and disrupting patterns that aren't serving you, identifying your needs, setting boundaries, and improving communication. While most of our work is done in session, I also like to offer reading and practices on topics like mindfulness, self-compassion, and nervous system regulation.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Systems theory is foundational to my work as a therapist, and I am always interested in exploring the factors outside of ourselves (e.g. family, culture, and politics) that contribute to who we are, what we believe, and how we feel. I welcome all parts of your identity into our work together and aim to co-create a space where we can explore these external influences as well as our own internal narratives. I am anti-racist, LGBTQIA+ and gender affirming, aligned with Health at Every Size principles, sex and kink positive, and deeply enjoy working with relationships in all types of configurations, including consensual non-monogamy, whether you identify as polyamorous, swingers, monogamish, or otherwise.

name: Marisol G. Westberg, Ph.D.
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I have been a sex and couple's therapist for nearly 10 years. I am a board-certified sexologist (ACS), certified sex educator (AASECT), and a licensed couple's counselor (LMFT).

approaches: I am sex-positive and am inclusive of alternative relationships and erotic minorities.I am an Assistant Professor in the Marriage, Couple and Family Therapy Program at Lewis and Clark College. I coordinate the Sex Therapy Track for the program where I teach sex therapy classes and supervise students in their clinical training. I am the author of the book: "Pleasure: The Secret Ingredient in Happiness."

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I am a sex therapist and couple’s counselor in Portland, OR. I am a board-certified sexologist (ACS), certified sex educator (AASECT), and a licensed couple’s counselor (LMFT).

name: Miranda York
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I specialize in working with people who've experienced childhood trauma. I'm glad you're here and hope this information is helpful for you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My practice is anti oppression and trauma informed. I am trained in psychodynamic and psychoanalytic therapy techniques, as well as various somatic techniques for trauma. I am warm and interactive. The therapy relationship can serve as a safer space to discover your old patterns of relating and try out new ones. I listen to you deeply, trying to hear what you are saying between the lines and work to empathically understand your inner conflicts and elaborate on unconscious dynamics that may be driving difficult patterns in your life. We will work together to explore the root causes of your struggles, to release these patterns and help you move towards more freedom, liberation, and ease in life. I work with couples to understand attachment conflicts, and I can also work with attachment in open relationships and polyamorous arrangements. Sometimes old traumas can cause reactivity and repetition in relationships, and we will explore this to enable more connection.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold the following credentials: Master's degree in Somatic Psychology, California Institute of Integral Studies Certificate in Drug and Alcohol Studies, Bellevue Community College Sensorimotor Psychotherapy Training for the Treatment of Trauma- Level 1 AEDP (Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy)- Level 3 EMDR- Basic Training Parts 1 and 2

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I offer EMDR for phobias and trauma. Some people who have more difficulty being open in traditional talk therapy may respond well to EMDR, in my experience.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I use mindfulness to guide you to understand your body's natural impulses that may have been suppressed due to shock traumas, relational traumas, or social conditioning. These natural impulses can help us understand the adaptive actions we need to take in life that flow naturally from our emotions.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: We will explore patterns of relating you learned in your family of origin and how these show up in your current relationships. This could take the following forms, for instance: how you expect others will receive you, what emotions and responses you automatically inhibit or express, what behaviors you typically engage in. This can illuminate unconscious programming and liberate more options.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I am familiar with various forms of relationships and enjoy working with people in couples, triads, or other non traditional arrangements. I also work with friends seeking therapy together and other relational dynamics.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: I enjoy working with historical and ancestral trauma and consider the impact of the cultural, social, and political context of your life and the lives of your parents and grandparents. This has an influence on all of us, and I believe it's important not to just look at the nuclear family as an isolated, apolitical unit with singular influence on our psychology, but to consider the broader context

specialities.name: Sexual Abuse
specialities.description: I work with adults who were sexually abused as children. I also work with adults who have experienced sexual abuse from intimate partners.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: PTSD can happen from a variety of adverse childhood and adult experiences. This can occur from physical, sexual, and emotional abuse as well as chronic poverty, oppression, addiction or growing up with a mentally ill or addicted parent. Complex PTSD occurs when we experienced more than one trauma (such as in the case of chronic childhood abuse).

specialities.name: Bipolar
specialities.description: Bipolar disorder can show up in a myriad of ways. Bipolar can manifest in: depressed agitation, a feeling of being on edge, difficulty with focusing and challenges with executive functioning, or you might think you have a personality disorder. I work with Bipolar 2 disorder and other low and mid spectrum bipolarity.

name: Jessica Janovicz
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am dedicated to helping individuals navigate life's challenges and find meaningful solutions.
ideal_client: I believe we are all a work in progress and when we feel most challenged, burdened or stagnant, this is the time that we are afforded the biggest opportunities for growth. By partnering to work together, we can identify and implement strategies that make daily life more manageable. I believe in creating a safe, non-judgmental space where clients can explore their thoughts and feelings. By focusing on your unique strengths, we can work together to develop practical strategies for positive change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: At Soulset Counseling, I specialize in Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and a Strengths-Based Approach, empowering clients to overcome obstacles and achieve personal growth. In our work together, I use evidence based strategies and interventions for emotional coping and wellbeing related to anxiety, depression, grief, life transitions, and other specialty areas.

name: Alisha Phillips
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I love my job. Witnessing my clients explore their potential for healing and growth through our work together is an inspiring privilege.
ideal_client: My typical clients are young professionals, though I enjoy working with people of all ages and life stages, and especially fellow parents. I specialize most in family and relationship issues- partnering, parenting, postpartum depression and anxiety, infertility and pregnancy loss, as well as communication, codependency, and divorce. My ongoing training has included Complex Trauma and PTSD, Holistic Nutrition for Mental Health, and Neurodiversity Affirming Therapy.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I will spend time getting to know you- your concerns, your strengths, your values, and your hopes for the future. Together we will work toward understanding your story and practice building on your strengths, identifying resources, and learning new skills. I work with each client in a unique and different way, which may include Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, and mindfulness and relaxation techniques. I have extra training in treating Complex PTSD. My background is in early intervention and parent coaching, building strong bonds and healthy attachment. Though I no longer work with children as clients, I still emphasize the importance of understanding the early experiences of my adult clients and their relationship with their younger selves and family of origin. I have a Master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Bushnell University, and a Bachelor’s degree in Family and Human Services from University of Oregon.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I moved from my home state of Alaska to Oregon as a college student and have lived here ever since, now settled down with my husband, three young children, and sprawling garden. I strive for values of simplicity, balance, acceptance, and kindness. I am especially passionate about caring for women and mothers and for helping people see their true selves through layers of systemic oppression, shame, and silencing. I am fascinated with the integration of Eastern philosophy and spiritual practices with Western psychology and academic pursuits. Clients of mine know I talk about the most recent discoveries in neuroscience in the same conversation as a Buddhist parable. I am a student and fellow traveler in many ways, rather than an expert. I chose to become a counselor because it is the most rewarding and enlightening path for me.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I was trained to use the DBT program to work with clients with a range of presenting issues, such as borderline personality disorder, bipolar disorder, depression, and anxiety. In my practice I will use DBT skills and worksheets with clients when useful and appropriate.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: My training and practice in therapy primarily uses a CBT model- identifying the ways that thoughts, feelings, and behaviors work together and can lead to feeling stuck, as well as be used to make changes and grow.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I have training as a Neurodiversity Specialist and combine therapeutic interventions for emotional regulation with education about the neurodiverse brain and executive functioning coaching. I also have lived experience as a person with ADHD, raised by someone with ADHD, and have a spouse and child with ADHD, and I want people to know that you can have an amazing, joyful, creative life by working with your brain's natural strengths and building supports for challenges.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Traumatic experiences build a system of thinking and reacting to the world, other people, and oneself in a way that prioritizes survival and safety over connection and acceptance. Many people underestimate how their present suffering is actually rooted in past trauma and toxic stress. I have completed level 1 of Janina Fischer's certification program for Complex PTSD and have over a decade of experience working in trauma intervention and recovery.

specialities.name: Infertility
specialities.description: A club where no one wants to be a member. Infertility is fraught with layers of self-identity, grief and loss, and challenges to communication and self-care. I have had extended training in this topic, as well as personal experience. Specifically, my clients have faced difficulty conceiving, pregnancy loss, IUI, IVF, secondary infertility, male factor infertility, body image issues, medical trauma, adoption disruption, and more. If you're on this road, you don't have to do it alone.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: My professional experience prior to becoming a counselor was as a parent coach. I have also worked in crisis intervention for parents who have a child that has experienced trauma as a licensed counselor. My approach to working with clients around parenting has to do with examining layers of personal history from childhood, parental identity development, attachment theory, and practical coaching based on child development.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: There are few more critically life-changing and difficult times in a person's life than the postpartum year+. Many women feel like their emotions at this time are "wrong" which leads to waiting to reach out for support. Often relationships with onself and others are tested. We are meant to have a caring, nurturing village and you are not alone! Please reach out, I will squeeze you in. I have training from WellMama, Baby Blues Connection, and Postpartum Support International.

name: Taylor Alderson
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: As a trauma-informed therapist, I specialize in helping individuals navigate the deep roots of emotional pain and psychological wounding.
ideal_client: My ideal client is an adult navigating the long-term impacts of emotional neglect, often rooted in growing up emotionally unavailable caregivers. I specialize in working with adult children of alcoholics, individuals struggling with SUD, adult survivors of childhood sex abuse, sex and love addiction, and complex PTSD. Drawing from my experience in trauma-informed care, EMDR, and depth psychological approaches, I support reconnecting with their embodied self, healing attachment wounds.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a trauma-informed therapist, I specialize in helping individuals navigate the deep roots of emotional pain and psychological wounding. My approach is integrative, drawing from psychodynamic therapy to explore unconscious patterns and relational dynamics, EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing) to resolve traumatic memories stored in the nervous system, and active imagination to engage the healing power of the psyche through symbol, image, and inner dialogue. I hold a deep respect for the complexity of trauma and the unique path of each individual’s healing journey. Whether working with developmental trauma, complex PTSD, or grief, my work is grounded in curiosity, compassion, and a trust in the psyche’s innate capacity to move toward wholeness. My goal is to support clients in accessing inner resources, restoring self-trust, and cultivating a more embodied, meaningful life.

My Philosophical approach to Psychotherapy includes a psychodynamic interpretation of mental and emotional processes rooted in psychoanalysis drawing from object relations, ego psychology and self psychology which aims to address the foundation and formulation of the psychological processes with the goal of reducing symptoms and improving people’s lives. My role as a therapist is to help people gain insight into their lives and current problems by evaluating and reviewing patterns that include emotions, thoughts, early life experience, and beliefs. Recognizing these patterns help people see how they avoid distress or develop defense mechanisms to cope. I believe these insights can allow for lasting change.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: Depth psychology proposes that the psychic process is partially conscious, unconscious, and semi-conscious. In practice, a depth therapist seeks to explore the thoughts, feelings, and motivations that lie at each level as a way to connect with the roots of the experience of malady that may include therapeutic traditions that explores the unconscious and involves the study and exploration of dreams, complexes, and archetypes. Depth Psychology is based on the theories of Carl Gustav Jung.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: "I bring a grounded, compassionate presence to working with individuals who have experienced abuse, offering a trauma-informed, client-centered approach that prioritizes safety, trust, and empowerment. My specialized training in EMDR and somatic-based therapies allows me to help clients gently process traumatic memories without becoming overwhelmed. Drawing from depth psychology, I also support clients in exploring unconscious patterns and reclaiming lost parts of the self.

name: Portland Counseling & Anxiety Specialists
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We specialize in treating anxiety, depression, trauma, relationship issues and grief. Your life can change for the better. We can help.

approaches.What We Specialize In: We are passionate about helping others. Each of us has experienced challenging times in our own lives, and we know how valuable good counseling can be. We are here to help you work through whatever you are struggling with and help you find satisfaction in your life. If you struggle with depression, PTSD, or anxiety, you are not alone. These disorders represent some of the most common mental health issues that impact Americans today. At one extreme, you may feel held back or triggered by life events in a way that makes you resigned to a less than fulfilling, yet still functional, life. On the other extreme, you may find that your anxiety, PTSD, or depression significantly impacts your quality of life and defines your sense of self. Whatever you’re struggling with does not define you, nor does it need to be a part of your future. Your life can change for the better. We can help.

approaches.More About the People We Treat: Our therapists are trained in one or more of the following: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Emotionally Focused Therapy, the Gottman Method, Internal Family Systems, Interpersonal Neurobiology, EMDR and Motivational Interviewing. Our counselors are qualified to treat anxiety, including generalized anxiety disorder, specific phobias, OCD, social anxiety, panic attacks, and trauma. Our counselors are also trained to help with abandonment issues, grief, couples counseling, shame, co-dependency, low self esteem, identity issues, relationship problems, depression and more.

name: Catherine Cooney
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Let my experience and skills assist you in creating a life you love.
ideal_client: The clients who benefit most from working with me are: - seeking a gentle, compassionate therapist who is direct and takes an active role in treatment - part of the LGBTQ+ community - longing to deeper their healing with body-based emotional experiencing - looking for trauma healing, especially around sex and betrayal issues - wanting to create lives of integrity and be accountable for past behavior

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My psychotherapy approach is a blend of my training and experience in Humanistic, Psychodynamic and Cognitive-Behavioral therapies. In addition, I have training in Trauma-informed, Attachment-based, Experiential, Psychodynamic, Cognitive Behavioral and Addictive Disease approaches. What this means in practice is that I meet you with a broad range of methods and 25+ years of experience enabling me to tailor our work to best meet your needs. It' s my honor to create a space where you feel fully seen and heard, and to enter into a journey with you toward your healing and wholeness. Some people prefer more talk therapy, some prefer more focus on feelings and physical experiences. I am interested in what works best for you and my commitment is to provide a safe, confidential, supportive environment for your healing and personal growth.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am Licensed Professional Counselor with a Master’s degree in Clinical Psychology. Since 1992, I have treated individuals, couples and families experiencing a broad range of mental health and addiction problems in both outpatient and residential settings. I have had specialized training in treating depression, anxiety, trauma, sexual behavior problems, and relationship issues including those experienced by sexual and gender minorities. I hold the Certified Sexual Addiction Therapist (CSAT) credential, and am a provider of Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing. In recent years, my concentration has been in treating individuals and couples experiencing sex and love addiction, intimacy disorders, betrayal, trauma, depression, and relationship problems. A member of the queer community, I also specialize in treating LGBTQ individuals. I work from a sex and kink-positive framework respecting every person's expression of authentic self.

specialities.name: Addiction Therapy
specialities.description: Certified Sex Addiction Therapist under the Board of the International Institute of Trauma and Addiction Professionals . Over 15 years of training and experience as a drug and alcohol counselor.

specialities.name: Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP)
specialities.description: A blend of interpersonal neurobiology, attachment theory, emotion theory, affective neuroscience and body-focused approaches, AEDP seeks to create transformational experiences through the in-depth processing of difficult emotional and relational experiences within the safe therapeutic relationship.

specialities.name: Sexual Addiction
specialities.description: Trained by Patrick Carnes, PhD, I am a certified sex addiction therapist and have been treating individuals and their partners or other family members for over a decade. I am a member of the Society for the Advancement of Sexual Health (SASH), and continually update my skills through training, consultation and research.

specialities.name: Internet Addiction
specialities.description: As a certified sex addiction therapist, a large part of my training and experience has been related to problem online behavior, including internet, pornography and/or cybersex addiction. Many people who struggle with internet addiction have some combination of online sexual and non-sexual behaviors, including gaming and social media addiction.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a member of the queer community, it's been part of my personal and professional journey to seek training, supervision and experience to become equipped to meet the counseling needs of LGBTQ individuals and couples. I continually seek professional development opportunities to stay informed on issues facing sexual and gender minorities.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Borrowing from my training in the Gottman method, Imago and Emotionally Focused Therapies, I have been honored to be part of the healing for many couples in both traditional and non-traditional relationship orientations.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am trained in several approaches to trauma, including EMDR. As a member of the International Institute for Trauma and Addiction Professionals (IITAP), I continually update my skills with state-of-the-art training and consultation.

name: Carli Barnum
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I'm a holistic, experiential therapist that specializes in attachment and trauma healing. I have individual and couple openings available.
ideal_client: My ideal clients are on a path to address trauma, boost self-esteem, and explore their future possibilities. They are usually dealing with PTSD, intrusive thoughts, residual childhood trauma, or low self-worth. I support couples through relationship difficulties and parenting. I am seeking clients that are open to self-reflection and dedicated to trying new approaches to habitual tendencies. If you’re ready for a supportive space to spark meaningful change, let’s get started!

approaches.My Background and Approach: I came to the counseling profession in an unconventional way. I worked as Peace Corps Volunteer in a rural town along the Dominican/Haitian border where I worked with school counselors to enhance their sex education curricula. In addition to my training as a clinical mental health counselor, I am also a trained school counselor. Because of this, my approach emphasizes skill sharing and understanding the why behind the how. As an experiential therapist, I facilitate transformative experiences that lead to those "AHA" moments and encourage clients to discover new ways of interacting with their environment. My goal is to create meaningful experiences that model and guide clients in forming fresh, fulfilling connections with themselves and the world around them.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that each individual is the expert of their own life. Because of this my approach is client lead and collaborative in nature. I look for progress over perfection, and I think having a strong connection to personal values serves as a compass for how to make life decisions. In my free time I plan art summer camps for low income students. I press flowers, do mosaics, and participate in a book club. I feel most alive when I am tending an altar or working in my garden.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I have completed the Externship in Emotionally Focused Couple Therapy through ICEEFT and am also Level 2 trained and certified in the Gottman Method. I integrate Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) and the Gottman Method (GM) to create a balanced therapeutic space that encourages guided emotional vulnerability and new ways of connecting, while also focusing on concrete goals and milestones to work toward both in and outside of sessions.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I utilize Parts and Memory Therapy (PMT), a modality similar to Internal Family Systems (IFS), to help clients release emotional burdens from the past and develop healthier internal dynamics. Through PMT, clients are guided to connect with and heal the 'parts' of themselves that hold onto difficult emotions or memories, leading to a greater sense of inner peace and wholeness. I am currently working toward becoming a certified PMT therapist.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I specialize in treating trauma using a person-centered approach, EMDR, Parts and Memory Therapy, Narrative Therapy, and Coherence Therapy. I create a safe, empathetic space for clients to explore and process their experiences at their own pace. Through these methods, I help clients reframe trauma narratives, release emotional burdens, and develop coping strategies that foster resilience and restore a sense of control and safety.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Using the Gottman Method to pinpoint where couples are missing each other, I guide them through Emotionally Focused Therapy to create moments where each partner feels seen, heard, and truly understood. In session we will address attachment wounds and facilitate a safe space to rekindle connection.

name: Kathy Cox
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Offering a warm welcome and compassionate, mindful attention as we attend to what you bring.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With warmth and open curiosity, I guide and support who you are and the concerns and intentions you bring. We make space to hear from the varied influences affecting your experience of life and take time to encourage and tap into the guidance of your inner knowing; mind, body, heart, & soul. In taking time to grow awareness of your inner and outer life, room is made for increased connections and understanding, paving the way for new choices and desired shifts. This bringing of focused, caring attention to what surfaces in session helps to improve the ability to notice and make sense of patterns, tend to feelings and sensations, address limiting beliefs, find clarity, discover resources, build trust, and deepen resilience. The work we do unfolds as we attune to and address what matters to you.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My training includes an M.S. in clinical mental health with a somatic emphasis and 2+years of study in the Hakomi method through M.E.T.A (Mindful Experiential Therapy Approaches). Ongoing studies I engage in include deepening my learning about the relationship between chronic pain/conditions, the mind-body connection, and the role of regulation as we encounter our inner and outer world. I value drawing from approaches that facilitate growth in awareness, self-compassion, self-acceptance, regulation, agency, and resilience. Informed by what arises in our work together, I may incorporate elements from mindfulness-based, body-centered, emotion-focused, relational, psychodynamic, or existential therapies. For the time being, I offer telehealth video sessions only.

name: Miya Tischler
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: As a mother and writer I believe healing happens through connection - to ourselves, to others, and to the natural world that holds us.
ideal_client: My goal in therapy is to collaborate with clients on their unique healing path. Therapy is a place where we can approach our challenges and wounds using the tools of narrative, movement, compassion, insight, and relationship. I work with clients to find the safest place to begin this journey- so you develop the readiness to know both the pain and the brilliance your body holds, in service of deeper self-recognition, integration, and aliveness. ​

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My relational-cultural (RCT) and attachment-focused lenses are multiculturally inclusive, trauma-informed, body positive, LGBTQIA+, poly-supportive, and honor neurodiverse ways of thinking and being. This is combined with a nervous-system informed somatic approach to working with trauma. I also have training in non-directive and directive play therapy, Lifespan Integration, polyvagal-informed yoga, breath-based stress reduction, and TF-CBT.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My path toward becoming a therapist has taken me around the world, delving with humility into multicultural wisdom while returning again and again to the question of how healing happens, and what is really broken. This path has made it impossible to ignore how deeply culture-bound our struggles are and how pervasively impactful our culture is on the self-talk that we do. I support my clients in questioning thought patterns that are not in the best interest of their growth and uncovering parts that need to be heard for them to grow into the experience of wholeness.

name: Scott Fletcher
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I help improve satisfaction in life and relationships by reducing the things that get you stuck and increasing confidence in self expression
ideal_client: Do you worry constantly, feel frequently on edge or have a persistent fear of failure or judgment? Feeling like you’re not good enough, not living the life you want to live, or that you’ve lost touch with the things that bring you happiness? Have little hope that you can live life in a fulfilling way? Have you had a traumatic experience that left you feeling disconnected and having a hard time trusting people, with the need to protect and numb yourself? If so, I may be able to help.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a believer that people possess incredible strengths and resources and that it is my job as a therapist to help folks creatively explore and access these natural talents. I assume that each person is the expert when it comes to their experience and my role is to help them gain insight into their own thoughts, feelings, desires, behaviors and goals. I take the role of experienced guide, pointing out things that might be helpful in achieving your goals, instead of the directive expert teacher who tells you what you ought to be doing. I have experience guiding people to make meaningful changes to increase their satisfaction with life. People I work with often report increased ability to recognize and respond more skillfully to life’s stresses. A sense of confidence, contentment, hope, fulfillment, safety and stronger connections with your important people is what I work to achieve with you.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: Some of the areas that I have experience in helping: - Anxiety, fears, phobias, and panic attacks - Depression, unhappiness and feeling stuck in life - Emotional awareness and expressive communication to improve quality of relationships - Various trauma including physical, sexual, emotional, relational and family of origin abuse - Young adults or teens looking to build independence and confidence in self-identity - Psychedelic integration or processing of recent profound psychedelic experiences - ADHD or challenges with feeling as productive and focused as you’d like to be - I am an LGBT+ ally and advocate for the marginalized -Men wanting to improve their relationships - Anger and frustration in relationships - Navigating Life transitions - Grief, loss and mourning

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I use Internal Family Systems (IFS) for the treatment of trauma.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: My therapy includes evidence-based mindfulness techniques to help treat a wide array of stressors

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I have years of experience using this evidence-based approach to help people reduce symptoms of depression and anxiety and to break negative thought patterns.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I completed level 1 training in Gottman Method for treating relationship issues. The Gottman method helps people communicate more effectively and strengthen overall relationship dynamics.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Over the years, I have helped many clients who are struggling with anxiety. I help people to understand their triggers so they can develop new perspectives that reduce the impacts of stressful situations. I use evidence-based mindfulness approaches to help people manage and reduce the physical symptoms that come with anxiety. Over time, confidence in ability to understand, reframe and reduce intensity of anxiety symptoms is gained.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can be overwhelming and leave people feeling hopeless that they will ever be able to live a fulfilling life. My experience working with people experiencing depression has given me tools to help people reconnect with the people and activities that bring interest back to life. I use Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Solution-Focused Therapy and relational therapy approaches to help people increase their ability to identify goals and make changes to achieve the things that bring satisfaction

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I use Narrative Exposure Therapy, Internal Family Systems (IFS) and Neurobiology to help people gain a sense of grounding and safety after traumatic experiences. Whether major life threatening incidents or painful emotional and relationship wounds, trauma can impact a person's ability to navigate life. I help people process and heal the emotional wounds in a safe space. You can also develop the tools to help cope with painful memories and begin to live a full life despite these experiences.

name: Greg Hertz
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: In-depth psychotherapy, grounded in relationship, supporting fundamental growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I practice psychoanalytic/psychodynamic psychotherapy, working in-depth over time with careful attention to fundamental growth processes. Recurrent emotional pain is calling for us to reconnect to our true self. It is very uncomfortable to be with all of our experience, yet avoiding feeling cuts us off from meaning and movement that we need to meet suffering with grace and growth. Our defenses against the fullness of our felt experience originate in adaptive strategies to preserve connection in early relationships. Certain feelings were unsafe for us to express and we learned to hide these parts from others and even from ourselves. The psychotherapy relationship helps us question these habitual limited ways of being and find more freedom, satisfaction, and peace.

The safety and stability of this space supports us to turn towards difficult experience with presence and curiosity. Together, we attend to the hidden by listening to intuitive ways of knowing such as feelings, associations, fantasies, dreams, and the body. In a relationship of deep acceptance and attunement, we shine light on what is happening in us at a fundamental level and have new experiences of what is possible. Greater awareness of ourselves brings a sense of wholeness and ease, a freedom to be ourselves and to realize our potential. This work is joyous and liberating. It is also difficult, demanding courage and capacity to be with the uncomfortable and unknown. The right therapy relationship can help us be with ourselves in a new way, reconnecting us with our life.

name: Sarah Hart
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Being human has struggles and challenges. I believe that we need positive support and reliable reflections from other humans.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is dynamic, collaborative, and Humanistic. I work from a culturally-informed & inclusive model & incorporate all aspects of an individual’s identity & experiences into treatment. My specialties include anxiety, depression, identity, Autism & relationships. I am uniquely suited to work with entrepreneurs and people in the Service Industry.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Training I hold a master’s degree in Counseling Psychology from Saybrook University. Coursework included counseling theories, individual, group and couple’s therapy, career and lifestyle planning, assessment, diagnosis, using research to inform the practice of counseling, human development and professional ethics. I also hold a Master’s degree in English from the University of Oregon. I currently train with Gestalt Associates Training Los Angeles (GATLA) in Seattle and have trained in the GATLA European Summer Residential Couples workshop.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: Therapy for Autistic people and those who love them. I work from a strengths-based perspective to help Autistic people develop a healthy identity and work with the challenges of being neurodiverse in a world that privileges the neurotypical.

specialities.name: Aging Concerns
specialities.description: I run a menopause support Group. Please inquire!

name: Madison Weiss
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Let’s collaborate as I hold space for you as part of your journey. Creative, psychodynamic, mindful therapy. LGBTQ+, individuals & couples.
ideal_client: If you are someone who seeks the equilibrium, safety, inner strength and peace of mind but may need some help getting there. Maybe you have moved away from where you want to be internally centered, or relationally. Whether to solve specific problems, or get answers, or you just want to delve more deeply into yourself and find out more. Therapy can help. I am here to shine a light in the darkness, and build a path we can walk down together, at your pace.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our work together will be creative, integrative and mindful. I have extensive training in psychotherapy and art therapy with a focus on social justice and diversity. Our sessions could include talk therapy, therapeutic art and sensory awareness. I believe change and healing develop within the bounds of a safe, trusted, ethical, and healthy therapeutic relationship. When you are ready, I can help you take back your power, build resiliency and remove roadblocks that are getting in the way.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I truly believe that both therapy and art saved my life. This is what motivated me to want to help others, as I can speak from experience. Going to therapy helped me manage feelings I just didn’t understand, and helped me to realize I didn’t have to carry around this pain all by myself. In therapy I was able to find relief, and compassionate support. I have always believed that everyone has the ability to grow and change, and as I continued in my own inner work, a healthier, happier person emerged. Having been there myself, I will be your ally. We will make a plan that's a road map that will keep us on course to uncovering, and working through what ever challenges life has thrown you. No problem is too big, or too small to address in therapy. I am here to listen, celebrate your triumphs and work on your issues with empathy and care. I value your privacy, and honesty, and building a collaboration that benefits you on your path of self-development.

name: Emily Bryan
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a LPC and Certified Sex Coach in training. My style of therapy/coaching emphasizes finding empowerment in your sexual self/identity.
ideal_client: I work very well with people who have struggled to find a good fit in therapy in the past or who are reaching out for help for the first time. I specialize in sexual health concerns, such as preorgasmia, performance anxiety, dating skills and/or sexual skills concerns, and sexual trauma. If you are interested in using EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing) to process your trauma, please let me know!

approaches.What I Specialize In: I specialize in the following areas: 1) Performance anxiety: difficulty maintaining or getting an erection, not having the physical response you would like during sex, difficulty orgasming or orgasming quicker than you would like, 2) Preorgasmia: maybe you’ve never had an orgasm or you have difficulty reaching orgasm, either solo or with a partner, 3) Dating skills and/or sexual skills concerns: maybe your’e new to partnered play or have recently received feedback that you are not meeting your partner’s needs, and 4) Communication style differences in relationships

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a therapist and sex coach because I want to change the world. I have been working in the mental health field since 2016, but have been passionate about sexual wellness since my undergraduate program where I facilitated Women’s and Gender Studies courses and wrote extensively on how to understand and navigate consent. Through these experiences, I realized that my true skills and strengths come from helping people through their sexual concerns. We live in a sex negative culture, which can make it difficult to feel safe being ourselves, and I want to change that! I also have an undergraduate degree in philosophy, which greatly influences how I show up in my practice.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I am an existential-humanistic counselor, which means I emphasize the relationship and the therapeutic container that we co-create. From this space as the foundation, I will ask curious and challenging questions to help you increase your understanding into yourself and to identify what matters most to you.

name: Jo Stone
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Jo uses a trauma-informed approach for therapy, incorporating art, play, music, and somatic techniques when appropriate.
ideal_client: Working with a diversity of people of many ages and backgrounds, Jo has gained her clinical experience facilitating therapeutic art groups for acute mental health treatment facilities (Aurora Mental Health), foster care & youth in transitional housing (Parrott Creek Child & Family Services), immigrants and refugees (Lutheran Community Services Northwest), and the Portland Air National Guard.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Jo, professional counselor associate, is passionate about helping children, teens, and adults discover their path to healing. She creates safe, inclusive spaces where individuals, families, and groups can explore their personal narrative to find healing in a language that speaks to them. Prior to her work at PATH, Jo provided art therapy for long-term hospitalized veterans as well as those receiving outpatient mental health services, and residential recovery programs (VA Medical Center). As a military wife and mom to 4, she understands the unique challenges military families face—frequent transitions, deployments, reintegration, and the invisible wounds of service—and is honored to walk alongside service members, veterans, and their families in their healing journeys. Her work is grounded in respect, empathy, and a commitment to creating a safe, nonjudgmental space where individuals can process their experiences, develop self- identity, and build resilience.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: With a MA in Art Therapy from Lewis and Clark Graduate School of Education and Counseling, Jo brings a compassionate, client-centered, strengths-based approach to her therapeutic work that honors the complex emotional and psychological experiences of those she works with. She is currently pursuing professional credentialing and continuing clinical development under supervision, with a vision of integrating art therapy into EMDR and Lifespan Integration. Balancing work and life, Jo spends her free time tending to her family, catering to her Frenchie's, Dolly Parton and Viktor Frankl, growing houseplants, hanging out with friends, and connecting with her local Portland community.

name: Jonathan E Scarboro
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I balance support and challenge in order to cultivate communication and connection, non-toxic masculinity, and creative expression.
ideal_client: I am especially interested in working with folks who are struggling to form deeper relationships with their community, their partner(s), or themselves. Communication and connection work can be especially healing for male-identified individuals who have been socialized to detach from their feelings and avoid intimate contact with others. For struggling artists and creatives, we can integrate unblocking into our regular therapy sessions, or take a shorter-term, solution-focused approach.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Sacrificing who we actually are in pursuit of who we think we should be can lead to alienation from ourselves, emotional distance from others, and a variety of behaviors in conflict with our actual goals and values. In some cases, parts of us may split off and become hidden beneath our awareness. Excavating and reintegrating these lost or buried aspects of ourselves can be a critical step towards overall well-being, and is crucial for our higher functions. I believe that forming deep connections with other people while remaining true to ourselves is essential to the changing and healing process. I will model this throughout our time together by bringing my authentic self into each session, talking with you frankly and openly, and looking for ways to draw out your fullness and complexity. My most important job as a counselor is to create a safe container for care and challenge to build upon each other at a pace that feels approachable to you.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Perhaps you’re having trouble connecting with other people or you’re doing self-destructive things but can’t understand why. Or maybe you’re numb to both pleasure and pain like you’re living life on autopilot. Or you have no idea what direction you’re headed in and no clue how to know what makes sense for you. All of these were true for me when I first started seeing a counselor during a stressful period involving the near-simultaneous dissolution of my marriage and business partnership. Though I initially resisted the idea of being in therapy, I eventually came to see it as a powerful gift. It now brings me great joy to offer this gift in turn. My clinical approach to creative recovery and unblocking is informed by my counselor training and my experience as a visual artist. For what it’s worth, I hold a Bachelor of Fine Arts, co-founded an interdisciplinary artist collective, worked at a major museum in Manhattan, and served as an arts programming director.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Men in this culture are socialized — often brutally — to disconnect from their feelings at an early age, and this is reinforced both covertly and overtly throughout adolescence and adulthood. We peel back the layers of shitty enculturation and trauma to unearth parts that have been shut away for years or decades. However painful, this process is a necessary part of healing and can deepen the quality of your relationships with your community, other men, your partner(s), and yourself.

name: Anna Claybaugh
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi, I'm Anna! I'm a queer, down-to-earth therapist who specializes in helping people liberate themselves.
ideal_client: You are ready to stop patterns that involve giving your power away. You are looking for more fulfillment in life and are ready to reclaim your authentic self. You are tired of feeling like everything else comes before your dreams, goals, empowerment and mental health. You who want to learn how to build more loving awareness and compassion towards yourself in order to support your best life. You are interested in learning more about what makes you who you are and create an authentic life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Utilizing a nonjudgmental approach that is person-centered, I will meet you where you are at to work on the concerns most important to you. I believe you are the expert in your experience and with a little guidance, you have the ability to heal yourself. Our work will be bespoke to your needs and may include eye movement therapy, internal family systems work, attachment healing, nature-based healing and collaborative problem solving. Most of us are stuck living in an avatar we’ve created to maintain safety, connection and feel belonging with our world. You are not alone in your experience. I will support you in identifying strengths, barriers and supports that interact with your ability to reach your goals. You are worthy of taking a step forward for you. Together, we can figure out what’s holding you back from securing happiness and abundance for yourself.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I deeply value working towards collective liberation and decolonial ways to being in relationship with the world and the beings in it. I am passionate about working with other LGBTQIA2S+ people and supporting them in living an authentic life. I am interested in the inner energetics of things and have been working with tea as a practice for this, in addition to other tools. Tea has been used for centuries as both a daily drinking tonic and as a medicinal beverage. I am trained in pouring Gongfu style tea as a tool to support you in understanding your energetics & healing from within. I believe that nature and being in right relation with earth can support our deep healing. If you want to learn more about how I can help, shoot me a message!

specialities.name: Accelerated Resolution Therapy
specialities.description: I have been practicing with this method since 2018, finding that it really supports people in shifting their traumatic symptoms. Often people will find this method most supportive when they feel like the cognitively understand what happened but still are struggling with physiological responses from that trauma.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Working with people navigating living their authentic, best queer life is something I am passionate about.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: Supporting other people who know what it's like to caregive and tend to those they love. Sometimes we get burnt out and need to shift things up for our own care.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: Utilizing evidence based interventions, we work with eye movements, memory reconsolidating and somatic coaching to heal and cope with past traumatic events.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety shows up in a variety of ways.

name: Majken Elek, MA
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We all deserve to feel aligned, safe and nurtured. Cultivating compassionate self awareness and acceptance are at the core of healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize a creative integrative approach, centered in mindfulness, somactics and attachment, to promote increased consciousness of thoughts, values, needs, and mind/body behavior patterns. Observing our emotional self awareness increases our ability to cope with stress, relationships, and life challenges. I will collaborate with you to move toward balance, wholeness, and a more integrated self. Free 30 min phone consultation and sliding scale fees. I am located within the Portland Insight Meditation Center. I do not accept insurance at this time, however, I can offer out of network billing and we can work together to find a session pricing that is realistic for you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a Masters in Counseling Psychology from Pacific University. I hold a BA from the University of Oregon. I have training in Vipassana Meditation, completing a 10 day silent meditation course in 2013. Additional training: CBT, DBT, MI, & CRM. I have clinical experience with addictions, and refugee populations and group experience in: mindfulness relapse prevention, grief, therapeutic journal writing, & mental health cultural adjustment. My credentials are also informed by my life experience. I have offered various support services while working in the education, corporate and non-profit fields for the past 15 years. This included serving a wide variety of ages, cultures. With these experiences I have gleaned valuable and applicable insight and wisdom which inform my practice giving me a holistic, open worldview. I’ve been told I have a warm, calm, stable presence. Hobbies: gardening & astrology. Places lived: Cannon Beach, Denmark, Boston, NY.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: ACT is an evidence-based intervention that uses acceptance and mindfulness mixed in different ways with commitment and behavior-change strategies, to increase psychological flexibility. The goal is not to get rid of of difficult feelings; but allow them to be present and what life throws at us in order to move toward valued behavior.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Our early childhood attachments with our caregivers creates a template for how we respond and relate with ourselves, and our relationships. They inform our beliefs about the world and from this, we internalize relational patterns. We can cultivate understanding of why we attached the way we did and how we can utilize neuro-plasticity to create new templates to get our emotional needs met.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Paying attention, on purpose, in the present moment non-judgmentally with curiosity and compassion. Mindfulness can help us relax and focus. It can help us reset, reduce stress, reset the body, and bring about personal growth and healing. When we have the experience of feeling and reflecting we can create more space to invite in trusting wisdom and choice.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Personal growth is a lifelong process unique to each individual. We will explore and delve into your values, attachments, desires and aversions to unearth thinking and behavior patters which inhibit your growth. Tapping intuitive self knowledge can generate insights and awareness to live with presence and increased balance as you determine your path.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: We live in a society where we have lost the value of believing in a force greater than our human selves. We will explore your history, beliefs, and spiritual goals, including roadblocks and barriers to help you embody your most alive spiritual self.

specialities.name: Aging Concerns
specialities.description: We will work together to embrace the natural cycle of being human, demystify the myths, and acknowledge the facts as we create a personal pathway of wisdom that feels safe, inspiring and unique to your journey.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Who are you beneath who everyone tells you, you are? Together, we will unfold the layers of negative conditioning and rebuild the authentic self through, thought awareness exercises, values exploration and empowerment visualizations in a safe, non-judgmental space.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: It is no wonder so many individuals suffer from anxiety. We live in a society that is constantly promoting fear. Together we will work to acknowledge and demystify the anxious mind, find stability and coping through grounding, behavioral and mindfulness exercises, and move towards valued action and balance.

name: Katie Solomon
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My approach is grounded in warmth, curiosity, humor, and compassion. I offer a free 15 minute consultation to see if we might be a good fit!
ideal_client: I provide therapy to adults and couples from a variety of backgrounds. I have experience working with trauma, anxiety, low self-esteem, chronic pain/illness, attachment/relational concerns, and other mental health concerns. I love working with clients who are curious about themselves, who want to grow their capacity to be present with their emotions, and who want to gain insight into their patterns. **Please note that at this time I am only working with OHP CareOregon and self-pay clients.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a trauma-informed, somatic, and relational therapist, I approach therapy with a lot of curiosity, gentleness, and eagerness to explore what is happening for clients in the present moment. I often encourage clients to check in with the sensations in their bodies and may highlight patterns I notice. I strive to create a non-judgmental space where clients can access and explore their emotions and experiences, enabling a deeper connection to themselves and others. I also like to bring (appropriate) humor into sessions. I believe that building a strong therapeutic relationship is a key part of the process! I draw from Gestalt therapy, attachment theory, AEDP, and Internal Family Systems. I have a non-pathologizing approach rooted in the belief that capitalism, white supremacy, patriarchy, homophobia, transphobia, and other systems of oppression all impact our mental health.

name: Maddy Engelfried
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: MA in Art Therapy and Counseling, School of the Art Institute of Chicago
intro: Hi! My name is Maddy, and I'm a queer professional counselor associate offering telehealth counseling and art therapy.
ideal_client: My ideal client is someone who is looking to adjust to a major life transition at any phase of life. I’m especially interested in working with chronically ill folks and cancer survivors, people who are neurodivergent, members of the LGBTQ community, clients who practice polyamory/ENM, and Jewish clients. I have a special place in my heart for nerds and artists.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have a background in art therapy as well as counseling, and I take a warm, compassionate approach to therapy. I’m deeply interested in people, and I like to lead with my curiosity, both in getting to know clients and in helping to understand what they’re going through. Research has shown that what makes therapy work is the therapeutic relationship, so I focus on cultivating that with every client I work with. I think every behavior has a reason behind it. We don’t make ourselves miserable because we want to! However, the coping mechanisms that fit one circumstance don’t always transfer well to the rest of our lives. By figuring out why we do the things we do and what we can do instead, we can start to shift our way of being in the world. A large part of my work is helping clients learn how to process difficult feelings about these changes. Therapy is hard work, but with creativity and humor, we can make real, lasting changes to our lives and relationships.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As an existential therapist, I think everyone has both the right and the responsibility to figure out what brings meaning to their life and do it on purpose. I strongly believe in the power of personal narrative. I've noticed that many people who come to therapy need help rewriting the stories they tell themselves about who they are and where their lives can go. Fortunately, we all have creative potential that we can harness to revise our personal stories and attack our problems instead of ourselves. As a nerd, I appreciate that it’s possible to think very hard about our feelings without actually feeling them. Unfortunately, the feeling part isn’t really optional - if you decide not to feel your feelings, your body will eventually feel them for you. Our society doesn't usually give us the time or tools to do this, but therapy can! When I'm not therapizing, I spend my time playing TTRPGs, drawing comics, and enjoying Portland's beautiful outdoors.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: I see therapy as a space to explore and rewrite the stories we tell ourselves. Narrative reframing offers a chance to view challenges from new perspectives and harness the creativity necessary for meaningful change. I strongly believe that taking control of our personal narratives can foster empowerment, develop resilience, and help us discover what makes our lives worth living.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I work with clients to discover what they find most meaningful, and figure out how they can bring more of that meaning into their everyday lives. I think therapy is a space where clients can do the difficult and rewarding work of figuring out what makes life worth living for them, regardless of the circumstances that brought them into therapy.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Feminist therapy isn't just about women's issues (though it certainly can be). It's about cultivating an egalitarian relationship between the therapist and client and recognizing that whatever our gender identity and expression, we all have things in our lives that oppress us and things that give us privilege. I see feminism as an essential lens to understanding the therapeutic relationship and the world at large.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: Motivational interviewing can help clients and therapists clarify therapeutic goals and make sure everyone is on the same page about why we're here. I've found that it's also a great way to have an open, honest conversation. I use motivational interviewing techniques in tandem with other therapeutic modalities to get a better sense of where my client is coming from and where they want to go.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: I've worked with people adjusting to overwhelming life transitions at many different stages of life, including teens getting ready to leave home, younger adults coping with homelessness, and older adults struggling with grief and loss.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: As a person who has practiced polyamory for many years, I have firsthand knowledge of the joys and complications of non-monogamous relationships. The transition from monogamy to ENM and the struggle to be understood by family can both be overwhelming. If you're looking to adjust your relationship structure or just need a therapist who knows terms like NRE and compersion, we might be a good fit!

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: It can be hard to make sense of devastating events that we hold in our collective memory and integrate the group narrative into our personal narrative. In my work with members of Chicago's Jewish community, I gained a new appreciation for the human need to cultivate joy, connection, and resilience in dark moments. I know this can look different for everyone, so I strive to stay culturally humble and curious in my work with people who are struggling with collective trauma.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I was a member of the queer community long before I was a therapist, and I believe that identity is a journey rather than a destination. I've also worked with queer youth and elders in individual and group therapy settings, and I've worked with the peers and parents of LGBTQ youth to help them better understand allyship.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I know firsthand how difficult it can be to integrate chronic illness into our identity while hanging onto our goals, dreams, and relationships. In my work with younger and older adults, I've noticed that adjusting to a new diagnosis can be a huge challenge at any stage of life. I use narrative and existential therapy to help clients explore their potential and integrate disability or illness into their life narratives while staying true to the other parts of their identities.

name: Health Allies Counseling
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Health Allies Counseling is a group practice that brings together a diverse group of therapists with a common goal of serving Oregonians.
ideal_client: Are you struggling to understand a relationship that may be abusive, trying to heal from trauma, or need support with gender, identity, or LGBTQ2SIA+ issues? Health Allies specializes in healing from narcissistic abuse, domestic violence, PTSD, and trauma. We also have many therapist who specialize and identify with the LGBTQ2SIA+ community. If you have struggled with any of the above, we can help you sort out your goals for healing and help you get to a better place.

approaches.How We Can Help You: We have a full team of staff available to help you address issues related to narcissistic abuse, domestic violence, PTSD and trauma. Each team member brings unique experience and skills to these issues - from using somatic solutions such as EMDR and art therapy, to individuals trained in parenting, family or child therapy, CBT, DBT, and more.

approaches.Our Values as Mental Health Practitioner: We operate from a social justice lens and stand with People of Color, immigrants and the LGBTQ2SIA+ community. We consider ourselves a trans-affirming, anti-racist, and progressive leaning practice. We are committed to providing an inclusive and safe space for healing.

name: Rainee Arevalo
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Welcome! My name is Rainee, and I am so happy you have taken this brave journey to seek therapeutic support.
ideal_client: My clients are often deeply feeling, highly sensitive people who have struggled to integrate all parts of themselves but are ready to experience the confidence that comes from owning painful chapters of their stories. I believe that clients have the power to reclaim their stories as the experts of their own lives. I work with individuals who deal with a variety of issues, such as trauma, attachment issues, anxiety and depression, relationship issues, and self-esteem/worth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy is a journey, a commitment to whole person healing for lasting change. I believe that clients have the power to reclaim their stories as the experts of their own lives. My therapy approach provides a personalized, collaborative, and empowering approach incorporating insights from a diverse strength-based theoretical framework, such as trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy, narrative therapy, internal family systems therapy, and attachment. I am EMDR certified.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In my free time, I love nature, gardening, music and watching movies.

name: Melissa Masini, LPC, LMFT
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I relish the privilege of getting to do this work with people. I'm interested in your story.
ideal_client: My favorite clients are sensitive souls in transition, people who see where they are stuck but don't know how to get unstuck, and people who are willing to use their imaginations.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I draw from Systemic, Emotionally-Focussed, Cognitive Behavioral and Narrative theories in my work. I begin therapy with creating a warm relationship as I get to know your current concern and past relationships. I investigate context and offer alternatives to unsatisfying patterns as we use current life examples and plan for long-term goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I graduated from the Marriage, Couples and Family Therapy Masters Program at Lewis and Clark College and have worked with individuals, couples and families in a variety of settings from residential treatment to research. My ongoing studies have included courses in sex therapy, Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), and mindfulness. In my personal life, I have been participating in an Anti-White Supremacy book and work group and have been learning as much as I can about Climate Change and my place within that work.

name: Sarah Blaszczak, M.A, LMFT
full_name: Sarah Blaszczak, M.A, LMFT (She, her, hers)
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I am fortunate to do this work I love, and honored to walk beside people, as they liberate themselves based on their deepest wisdom.
ideal_client: Welcome Welcome to my psychotherapy and coaching practice. Here you will find a warm, caring and confidential setting where we can look deeply at experience, changing your relationship to suffering. I am particularly enjoying working with people who are approaching or have had an initial non-dual or "no-self" realization, in order to integrate their new awareness and do deeper shadow work.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Between and within humans, multiple perspectives exist, and what is discovered depends on how observing happens. This understanding has led to my intense compassion for all kinds of human suffering, and delight in the unique paths forged. It is possible to ultimately drop attachments contributing to suffering, in order to experience the innately loving conscious beings we are. Here the focus is less on some idea of "right and wrong" and more on the wise discernment of what ACTUALLY contributes to suffering based on experience. My therapy practice is driven by a belief that if anyone had been through what you had been through, they would be exactly where you are. I also believe in equifinality; the idea that there are multiple paths to the same destination.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been working in the field for about 20 years. My license has afforded me the opportunity to work with a variety of clients in an array of settings. I have worked with couples, families and individuals in private practice settings, as a therapist at a drug treatment center for youth, as the lead clinician in an inpatient program for people who identified as female struggling with dual dianoses, as the Clinical Director of a transitional housing program for women leaving prostitution and escaping sex trafficking. My current Therapy and Coaching Practice is my love and joy. I support people in seeing through psychological conditioning and becoming more stable. We can then look into the true roots of suffering. I am particularly enjoying working with people who are approaching or have had an initial non-dual or "no-self" realization, in order to integrate their new awareness and do deeper shadow work.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Most of us have some ambivalence about most things because we have multiple motivations (to succeed, to be happy, to be liked for example). IFS is a way to reach consensus within ourselves, particularly if we experienced trauma.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Peace can come from meeting life’s suffering with clarity, grace and curiosity. Mindfulness allows us to know our patterns and motives more clearly so that we can see through our conditioning.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I adjust my approach based on your presenting strengths and challenges in collaboration with you. I do not expect you to adapt to my style. I am comfortable using a wide range of specializations, theories and approaches.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I am particularly enjoying working with people who are approaching or have had an initial non-dual or "no-self" realization, in order to integrate their new awareness and do deeper shadow work. If you are just at the beginning of asking bigger questions about existence, are in recovery and deepening your relationship to Higher Power, or have a history of religious trauma, I also have a great deal of experience and enjoy supporting people around these issues.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I have experience working with sexual problems including avoidance and compulsions. I also enjoy supporting individuals that have, or currently experience stigma and oppression around sexuality.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Mind identification can be incredibly painful and stress-inducing. I enjoy helping people inquire into the nature and substance of thought, in order to find peace without the content of thoughts having to change.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have a wealth of experience and use a wide variety of approaches to help people heal from their unique combination of trauma symptoms, including flashbacks, dissociation, panic, avoidance, depression, irritability and low self-esteem.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: So many marginalized populations and folks who grow up with abuse or addiction in their households adapt by living life from the outside in-adjusting to what they have been told implicitly and explicitly to be for other people in order to access love and resource. This also happens to be a symptom of codependency, a normal reaction to abnormal circumstances. I can help you reorient to yourself.

name: Amelia Mackle MSEd LPC RYT
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help teens and adults living with trauma, depression, anxiety, mood disorders, chronic pain, social anxiety, gender issues & life changes.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I embrace the interplay between psychology, energy, mind-body medicine and the science of the brain to approach counseling more holistically. In sessions with me, you may enjoy breath work, movement, meditation to shift neural connections toward healing and self care. Paired with traditional evidence based practices, this prepares all aspects of the self to move toward your personal goals and away from old patterns that no longer serve you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been licensed in the State of Oregon since I moved here over a decade ago from the Mid-west. I use a variety of traditional counseling theories to provide individualized care for my clients, drawing from Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, EMDR and Trauma Focused Care. I am also a Registered Yoga Teacher- 200hr through Yoga Alliance and this provides me with a clearer understanding of how our mind/body connection relates to all aspects of our functioning.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: I strongly believe in the mind/body connection and that both must be addressed to really thrive. I am trained in traditional, evidenced based psychotherapy, yoga, as well as nutrition and integrative medicine for mental health.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: My perspective is that the mind and the body cannot be seperated if we are to feel like we are wholly living. I use a variety of breathing techniques, yoga, body sensing and physical health approaches to bring the mind and body to healing together.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I have been integrating the coping skills from Dialectical Behavioral Therapy into practice with all my clients for many years. DBT skills are excellent life skills and can lead us to a more fulfilling life, no matter what life challenges we face.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Many of us have things we would like to see improve in our lives, like moving beyond survival or recovery to finding our personal best. Each of us have a different starting point and seeing growth in our lives is a very individual process. We may use a wide range of techniques to help you live and age well focusing on achieving a state of fulfillment.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I have experience working with teens and young adults in exploring gender identity. I also provide readiness evaluations for those seeking medical transitions.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma impacts many of our lives. Most of us can identify turning points where we felt something change in our lives. I have a variety of approaches that help get to a place of healing. I am trained in EMDR, yoga and am nationally certified in Trauma Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.

name: Lesley Smith
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
