intro: I want to help you feel ok with yourself and help to create a life you want to live, providing therapy in a way that meets your needs.
ideal_client: Do you notice moments where it feels like your emotions take over or else you numb yourself because you're afraid that if you feel your emotions they won't stop? I work with people to help them understand, cope with, and tolerate their emotions. I frequently see people who just experienced a major life change or feel like they're stuck and need something to change. I work with folks to help them figure out what their next steps are, so they can like themselves and their lives a little bit more.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) in the state of Oregon and I hold a Master’s of Arts in Social Work from the University of Chicago. The primary type of therapy I use is Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), with a trauma-informed, harm reduction, and anti-oppressive practice lens. I aim to be creative in my approach, meaning that I want to adapt to whatever approach best fits your needs. I am neurodiversity-affirming and love to find ways to make your life easier. I am currently being trained in Somatic Experiencing (SE) and am in the Advanced Year of training. SE is a body-centered trauma-healing modality. I also offer Safe and Sound Protocol (SSP) to assist in nervous system regulation. I specialize in working with people with anxiety, difficulty regulating emotions, recent life transitions, and communication issues. I am here to witness your emotions, help you find harmony, and discover where you want to go.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My main value is safety - I want you to feel safe during our time together. This is why I also say that I use anti-oppressive practice. To me, that means that I am constantly learning and growing along with you. It means that I am open to understanding the identities that you hold, beyond the labels, with the hope that you aren't needing to educate me. This also means that I will label racism, classism, ableism, homophobia, transphobia, and other oppressive systems when they show up in our time together. I do this because these systems of oppression impact our experience of the world and our relationships. I value curiosity and want to learn more about you and your relationships with the labels you hold. I take a non-judgmental stance and want to help you figure out what works best for you. also value creativity in the therapy space and want to make sure I am adjusting my approach to fit your needs. I look forward to exploring your needs and supporting you on your journey.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: This is the primary modality I use. I took a course on ACT during my Master's program and an intensive training on 2018. I attend a monthly ACT consult group and continue to access books and other resources on ACT.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I believe that our bodies hold so much information and need to be involved in the practice. I am being trained in Somatic Experiencing (currently Advanced Level 1 trained). To learn more about Somatic Experiencing check out - https://traumahealing.org/

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: Nature has so much to teach us. I am trained in using ecotherapy to assist in treating climate-related distress.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I incorporate aspects of Harm-Reduction into my practice. I am certified in Safe and Sound Protocol and incorporate this treatment, as appropriate.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I have ADHD and continue to learn more strategies and information to make life easier for folks with ADHD.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have a history of working with individuals experiencing anxiety.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I am a member of the LGBTQ community and have experience treating folks who are questioning and transitioning. I attend a weekly consult group with other providers who work with LGBTQ-identified folks.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I have experience working with female-identified people and am knowledgable on the unique experiences of these individuals and the ways that patriarchy influences our lived experience.

name: Savannah Auster
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I offer individual counseling to teens and young adults to help navigate life's challenges, build confidence, and foster personal growth.
ideal_client: Feeling overwhelmed by change? Struggling to navigate uncertainty, new responsibilities, or emotional challenges? Are you finding it difficult to balance your sense of self with the pressures of growing up, managing anxiety, or dealing with body image concerns and self-esteem? Whether you're facing a specific challenge or just feeling lost in the midst of life's transitions, I am here to support you.

approaches.My Background: I have experience working with teens and young adults navigating life transitions, developing adult responsibilities, managing anxiety, body image concerns, self-esteem, and coping with grief and loss. In our work together, I will utilize evidence-based practices such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to help you explore the thoughts, feelings, and emotions that are influencing your life. As a teen transitioning into young adulthood, you’re at a pivotal moment in life filled with change, uncertainty, and overwhelming emotions. My goal is to support you through this process by helping you uncover your best self, gain clarity, build confidence, set goals that align with your values, and learn to accept and embrace all aspects of who you are.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to counseling is comforting, non-judgmental, and goal-oriented. The type of therapy that I emphasize is a process of becoming whole – assessing all aspects of you as an individual. I believe that people have the means to make positive change in their lives when awareness is reached, goals are created, and consuming thoughts are reduced. I also believe that this type of change can occur most rapidly with the support of an empathetic, committed, and compassionate clinician. Additionally, I recognize that your experiences are shaped by a variety of factors, including societal influences, cultural and family backgrounds, gender roles, and the dynamics of your current relationships. My goal is to listen attentively and with an open heart, honoring your unique perspective and accepting you fully for who you are.

name: Phil Small
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I offer both short- and long-term, evidence-based therapy to address anxiety, mood disorders, and relationship concerns. Reach out!
ideal_client: You might be an excellent fit for my practice if you are currently navigating one of adulthood's many transitions, are experiencing chronic or acute anxiety or panic, or are affected by relationship issues, including family concerns. Throughout my training at top-tier programs, I have learned a range of evidence-based practices to help support individuals in their efforts to heal and grow.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Throughout more than a decade of dedicated clinical training, I learned to treat, guide, and support emerging adults and mid-life adults through understanding and coping with their specific circumstances and mental health concerns. I earned my PhD by valuing both clinical work as well as research -- a combination that led to me providing high quality, evidence-based care. I offer a warm, conversational therapy experience that is rooted in cognitive-behavioral and interpersonal practices. Treatment is structured into three phases: diagnosis and treatment, maintenance, and check-ups. This structure offers a road map to aid with expectations for your care, and will help support you moving beyond the concerns that have held you back.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I am a life-long learner, and am committed to challenging myself and my beliefs every day. As such, I believe black lives matter, trans rights are human rights, and that everyone should have access to quality care. I have led trainings for other clinicians about how to work with LGBTQIA+ populations and how to provide gender affirming care. Additionally, I have volunteered at a 24-hour suicide phone center, which helped fuel my enthusiasm and commitment to supporting the mental health needs of anyone who needs it.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: While my approach is rooted in the evidence-based practice of CBT, you will find that working with me feels conversational, comfortable, and constructive.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I am prepared to help you explore, understand, and move through your experience of anxiety using a range of cognitive, behavioral, and mindfulness techniques.

name: Margot David
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a clinical social worker (LCSW) with over 20 years of experience. I am licensed in both Oregon and Washington.
ideal_client: The focus of my training and ongoing study is on how the brain and body hold and sustain negative patterns from past experiences and relationships. We can identify how parts of you might be hanging onto old patterns to keep you safe from things that may no longer be threats, and to explore new choices.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I received my Master of Social Work (MSW) from Smith College School for Social Work in 2002. I have worked in a variety of settings including mental health clinics (all ages), cancer counseling with adults, hospital with adults in the medical system, college counseling, and private practice. The focus of my training and ongoing study is on how the brain and body hold and sustain negative patterns from past experiences and relationships. We can identify how parts of you might be hanging onto old patterns to keep you safe from things that may no longer be threats, and to explore new choices. I primarily draw from Internal Family Systems (IFS) and Sensorimotor Psychotherapy. I am Level 2 trained in IFS and Level 1 trained in Sensorimotor Psychotherapy. I incorporate other modalities such as CBT or EMDR (Level 2 trained), as they fit your needs.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: One perspective on how we operate is that every individual has a unique collection of parts made up of experiences, relationships, and biology that contribute to who we are. That collection of variables drives how we relate to our world in the best way we know how. Sometimes our best efforts seem not to work very well and we might feel especially anxious or depressed, or we have relationship struggles, for example. As a therapist, my hope is to help you develop a clear picture of the unique parts that drive you, so you don't feel so out of control. When you know your inner landscape you have a lot more agency over how you relate in the world, and that tends to calm the struggle. My goal is for you to walk away from therapy with a stronger sense of clarity about your strengths and about how to navigate the stuck places.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: I work with all clients through a trauma-informed lens, which means that I have had in-depth training on how trauma impacts the body, the brain, and how a person relates in the world. I draw from various approaches, primarily Internal Family Systems (IFS), in which I am level 2 trained, and Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, in which I am level 1 trained. I am also level 2 trained in EMDR.

specialities.name: Cancer
specialities.description: I worked for several years as a Cancer Counselor with oncology patients and their families. I am familiar with many aspects of the cancer process from diagnoses through treatment and post-treatment. I am also experienced in end-of-life decisions and issues of grief and loss.

name: Danielle Grover
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I offer comprehensive psychological assessment services, including ADHD and Autism testing, and typically have availability within a month.
ideal_client: Psychological evaluation aims to investigate the many different factors that could potentially contribute to long-standing areas of concern or difficulty. Examples of these can include early childhood history, traumas, neurodevelopmental (e.g., Autism and ADHD), or health-related impacts occurring individually or in combination. My goal is to help clients gain clarity regarding these contributing factors and related diagnoses, as well as receive tailored recommendations for the future.

approaches.What I Specialize In: My work has included positions in a variety of specialty and generalist capacities, such as ADHD and Autism clinics as well as primary care. I specialize in comprehensive testing for mood, anxiety, and neurodevelopmental conditions, as well as learning challenges. I am licensed to see individuals in OR.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My goal is to promote positive growth through diagnostic clarification and education.

specialities.name: Psychological Testing and Evaluation
specialities.description: I am a Licensed Psychologist who has been working or training in an assessment capacity for over 8 years. I am currently offering comprehensive psychological assessment services to help clarify diagnosis and recommendations for, but not limited to, ADHD, Autism, learning, mood, anxiety, personality, OCD, trauma-related conditions. I use a strengths-based approach to help individuals identify what they do well and how to use these abilities to be more authentic versions of themselves.

name: Slade Wolf
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Currently accepting clients with Providence, PacificSource, or OHP through Care Oregon and Trillium. Please go to my website for details.
ideal_client: My practice is one of thirds. About one-third of my clients are couples who are struggling to communicate and solve their problems respectfully. Another third is individuals struggling with some surface level difficulties of anxiety and/or depression. Under the surface is often a history of trauma and invalidation. Finally, a third of my practice is men working on being healthier and more respectful.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Firstmost, I use science to guide my practice so that all the work I do is backed by decades of strong research, indicating that it makes couples and individuals healthier. Specifically, when working with couples I use a behavioral skill-building approach. We will learn and practice effective communication skills so that you can resolve your conflicts respectfully and with increasing amounts of emotional intimacy. I use cognitive-behavioral therapy to help individuals conquer their depression and anxiety and learn the skills necessary to keep those symptoms at bay. I also specifically help men to improve their emotional wisdom and well-being, overcome anger and/or depression, and be happier and healthier humans, for themselves and their loved ones.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my master of social work degree at University of Washington in 2000. I have worked in a variety of settings as a clinical social worker: -Doing drug and alcohol counseling at methadone clinics -Providing psychotherapy at a community based mental health clinic -Program lead at Clackamas County Mental Health in a program for young adults who had developed schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, borderline personality disorder or other severe and persistent mental illnesses and who were also suffering with drug dependency -Coordinator for a program at Oregon City High School for students with social and emotional needs -Owner of Oregon City Counseling and co-owner of Men’s Resource Center, both of which focused on providing Domestic Violence Intervention groups for men -Currently the owner of Oregon City Counseling where I continue my work with men and have expanded to doing work with couples and helping individuals with anxiety and depression

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I use a behavioral approach to couples counseling. There is solid evidence that learning, and practicing communication skills builds healthier, more respectful, and more emotionally intimate relationships. I have been using this approach with couples, and with men focusing on their relationship skills, for nearly 20 years.

specialities.name: Anger Management Therapy
specialities.description: I use cognitive behavioral therapy to help individuals better understand where their anger comes from, rethink the beliefs that lead to that anger, and build solid skills for responding to difficulties in life differently.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: The science behind psychotherapy is clear: cognitive behavioral therapy is the treatment of choice for many conditions, including depression and anxiety. My training is in this treatment model and I have implemented it in my practice for over 20 years.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I have worked with men for over a decade to build the skills they need to live healthy lives and have happy, intimate relationships.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I help couples build the communication skills they need to respectfully resolve their conflicts while building emotional intimacy.

specialities.name: Anger Management
specialities.description: With over a decade of experience treating men who use aggression to solve their problems, I can readily help you discover healthier alternatives and build your emotional intelligence.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I am highly skilled in using cognitive-behavioral therapy to help you overcome your anxiety and build your ability to continue to manage those symptoms throughout your life.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I am highly skilled in using cognitive-behavioral therapy to help you overcome your depression and build your ability to continue to manage those symptoms throughout your life.

name: Elizabeth Olsen
title: Student Counselor
intro: Have you noticed behavior changes in your teen? Is your teenager struggling? Lets work together to help them live a better life.
ideal_client: Specialized therapy can help your teen navigate these difficult years. We will focus on understanding their struggles and creating strategies to help them thrive. Imagine your teen developing strong resilience and confidence. Our sessions will work towards improving their well-being and helping them find their place in the world.

approaches.How I Can Help You: Have you noticed behavior changes in your teen? Is your teenager struggling with identity issues, bullying, body image concerns, or feeling like they don’t fit in? You’re not alone, and help is here. If your teen is dealing with these challenges, they may feel isolated, anxious, or unsure of themselves. You might notice things such as withdrawal from family activities, declining grades, or mood swings. These issues can impact their self-esteem, mental health, and overall well-being, making it hard for them to navigate daily life and school. The pressure to fit in and find their place can feel overwhelming and exhausting.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: With specialized training in teen mental health, I am dedicated to helping teenagers overcome these challenges and build a brighter future. Picture your teen feeling more confident, connected, and capable of handling life's challenges. Take the first step towards supporting your teen by scheduling a free 15-minute consultation today.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I see anxiety as signal to stop and understand what is going on, and that it is something to understand and not fear. I love working with teens and young adults on examining underlying thoughts and behaviors and contribute to anxiety and aiding them in learning coping skills to overcome these issues.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Hardship and feeling depressed can happen to anyone. I believe in using various evidence-based approaches to aid my patients to view their worlds through a different lens. We may not be able to change the world, but we can change the way we see it.

name: Sarah Block
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I bring together neuroscience with a holistic approach to therapy for a balanced approach to healing and personal growth.
ideal_client: Are you an adult or adolescent feeling like life if really hard right now? Are you going through a big change? or feeling anxious, stressed, or depressed? I frequently work with people who struggle with anxiety, depression or are coping with grief and loss. Life can be really hard, but you don't have to get through it alone. Therapy can be helpful when we want to move through challenges, to find more peace, joy or balance.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy looks different for everyone. Everyone learns and grows in their own unique ways. My approach with each person takes into account what works best for them. What you can count on is that I’ll take a holistic approach to healing and emotional growth through body-centered modalities, trauma-informed practices, and culturally sensitive interventions that help empower you to set your own goals and work towards the life you want to live. I'll help you identify and explore your own positive beliefs and values that support you in finding more joy and meaning in your daily life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My pronouns are she/her. I live with my family in the Pacific Northwest, just outside of Portland, Oregon where I love getting outside as much as possible. Science, nature, and art have always been my favorite subjects and I’m always ready to dive in and explore life’s mysteries with curiosity. I can be serious but I can also be silly. I can be scientific but I can also be woo-woo. At the end of the day, I find it important to show up as my authentic self with my clients, and find the humor together where we can.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: IFS is another way of describing how we all have parts within us. If you've ever had a conversation with yourself (or an argument with yourself) you'll know what I mean. Parts work helps us deeply listen to ourselves, learn to appreciate and love all sides to ourselves and helps our internal word function a little smoother. I find it to be a very empowering and deep approach to healing that can make a big difference for folks.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: I hold a MS in Marital, Couple and Family therapy from Portland State University and have training and experience working with highly conflictual families. Family therapy can help systems increase healthy functioning and shift patterns that have been in place for years and sometimes generations. I utilize various family therapy approaches to help family meet the goals they set. Although I don't work with young children directly any longer, I love coaching parents and working with adult families.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am trained in Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing, which is a wonderfully powerful (and simple) tool for working through traumatic memories or difficult experiences. I typically integrate EMDR in with other modalities when the time is right for folks.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Working towards personal growth and wellness is an excellent reason to enter into therapy. Often times we get so busy in our daily lives, that we forget to put aside time to explore these important themes. I support people in identifying and exploring their own strengths, values and spiritual beliefs in order to live full and healthy lives. This process can begin at any time and at any age.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Many people attend therapy due to unresolved hurts and wounds from traumatic events in their lives. I support people in healing past hurts through a variety of talk therapies, and also body-centric modalities to deeply effect change and help people move on to find joy and balance in their lives.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can arrise in people's lives for various reasons; difficulty coping with life changes, relationship conflict, unresolved trauma, biological predisposition or living a lifestyle that is incompatible with your core beliefs or values. I treat Anxiety through a combination of finding ways to cope and reduce anxiety in the moment, and inviting clients to explore options for deeper healing.

name: Paige Cameron
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: MA, LPC C6978 EMDR Certified Therapist 339470
intro: Licensed Professional Counselor, EMDR Certified Therapist. Know that you aren't alone and I believe there is always hope, reach out today!
ideal_client: Inquire for openings! Are you feeling stuck, anxious, or perhaps wanting change, but not sure where to start? You're in the right place. We will work together using a variety of modalities to address your needs and goals. I specialize in working with clients experiencing Anxiety, Depression, Trauma, Grief and Loss, and Relationship Issues. I truly believe you, the client, have everything you need inside to heal, sometimes we just need support and guidance pointing us in the right direction.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Pleased to offer EMDR services as a Certified EMDR Therapist. I strive to create a warm, safe, and accepting environment where you can truly come as you are. I find that sometimes the best medicine is a bit of laughter and understanding that we are all humans in progress. I believe the client is the expert and already has everything they need to heal move forward inside themselves. Sometimes, we all need a little help to get unstuck, to see things from a new perspective, and to take a breath and realize how far we have come. In our work together, we will use Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Polyvagal Theory, and EMDR focusing on your strengths, bringing an awareness to how our body holds trauma, and utilize a variety of tools to create real change and bring healing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Therapy is deep, life changing work, and it is a privilege to be able to walk with someone on their journey towards healing. My passion is working with those experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, survivors of sexual assault, and loss and grief. My primary focus is individuals ages 14 and older. I am able to accept OHP insurance and can provide Superbills for the client to then submit to their insurance company. I also offer a "at the time of session" cash pay rate. Please reach out to see if we would be a good fit. I look forward to hearing from you!

name: Mary Bergeron
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi, I'm Mary! I love my job as a counselor. I specialize in supporting people who are in times of transition.
ideal_client: I specialize in supporting people who are facing transitions—whether it's navigating grief, adjusting to new roles, navigating relationship changes, or another challenge. Many of my clients come to me feeling overwhelmed and disconnected from themselves. Together, we work to explore meaning in their experiences, helping them reconnect with their core values, build necessary skills, and move forward with confidence. I understand how scary change can feel and I'm honored to help my clients!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My practice has been focused on much more than helping clients reach their therapeutic goals. Using Existential and Constructivist frameworks, I walk alongside clients offering them reflections, challenging unhelpful thought patterns, and gain insight on core beliefs and fears. I feel so passionate about helping my clients create a life that they enjoy! The feedback I have received from clients is that they appreciate my unconditional warmth, humor, and insight. Sessions might sometimes look like me listening, offering reflections and highlighting themes in a clients life. Other sessions might look like me naming unhelpful coping mechanisms or thought patterns, and gracefully challenging clients to notice what is happening in their body. Many of my sessions look different from one another because I care about what a client needs on any certain day. Our sessions are tailored to your needs!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am pretty passionate about helping people learn about themselves and create a life that they love. I think that understanding our own core fears and values is a gateway to living a life that is more aligned with our values, thus an authentic and fulfilling life. My clients are used to me harping on the importance of clear values! I believe change can happen at any moment, and it that it certainly begins with self awareness. This is the work I enjoy doing with clients! I knew from a young age that I wanted to help people enjoy life and that desire led to a career in counseling. As for my own life, I'm always looking to have fun, challenge myself and spend time in the sun. This oftentimes looks like hot yoga (for some alone time!), swimming, mountain biking, skiing, paddle boarding, enjoying a good meal or hosting friends at my home. Many of my clients know how much I love my Cocker Spaniel, Heidi, and she'll likely make an appearance in one of our sessions!

name: Celina Paul
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Celina is a Warm, Person-Centered & Strengths-based Art Therapy Associate who enjoys working with Children, Teens, Adults and Caregivers.
ideal_client: Celina works with Clients seeking support with ADHD, Anxiety, Depression, Attachment Wounds, and Trauma. She enjoys working with children, teens, adults, caregivers, as well as providing Art Therapy based Social Skills Groups, Emotional Regulation Groups, ADHD Skills groups, and offering Caregiver-Child connection/ repair sessions. Ideal Client's are willing to engage and explore as they build new structures for working through challenges.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Celina enjoys supporting people learning to navigate their emotional landscapes, as well as growing their capacity to connect with loved ones and create meaningful relationships. She works within a strengths-based, person-centered, trauma informed lens, and relies on art therapy, a systems framework, attachment theory, narrative therapy, as well as an awareness of intergenerational trauma, and holds a strong social-justice background. Celina works collaboratively with clients to assist their growth in sustainable and identity-affirming ways. She is EMDR trained and trauma informed.

name: Madeline Fox
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I support clients in understanding how their unique constellation of relationships affects their life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work with individuals to identify repetitive thoughts, ingrained expectations and outlooks that aren’t serving them and together we work to develop skills to address your unique challenges. We've structured modern life around the idea that one big relationship should be everything: the place where you get acceptance and intimacy, friendship and love, spontaneity and mischief. Everything all rolled into one. And for so many, and maybe you too, it’s just not working. Are you feeling deep sadness when you consider your life? Do you often struggle with feelings of hurt, disappointment, or anger? Do you feel like you just can’t ‘figure out’ how to make you life or relationships work? If you’re experiencing one (or many) of these, it’s time to shake things up. You don’t have to struggle through this alone, I’m committed to providing empowering guidance and insight to help you move forward toward the life you want to be living.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a Masters of Arts degree in Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy with an emphasis in sex therapy from Lewis and Clark College. I experienced working with diverse clients as a therapist in multiple community mental health settings. In the spring of 2023, I participated in an in-depth couples therapy training with Terry Real. In November of 2017, I immersed myself in training with Esther Perel around rethinking infidelity and better understanding how to work with couples and individuals who are struggling to maintain desire and vitality within their relationships. In 2016, I worked with Esther Perel and Terry Real in their Relate training program to more comprehensively understand the intersection of love, sex, and power, in modern relationships. When I’m not helping clients build satisfying emotional and erotic lives my favorite pastimes are setting up picnics under big shaded trees, reading fiction novels, making pot pie from scratch, and catching up with friends.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Love, passion, and a bit of mystery may have brought you and your partner together but for whatever reason, those elements are harder to identify at the moment. I will collaboratively work with you and your partner to access those experiences of tenderness in order to start healing and repairing the memories of hurt that can take place through the course of a relationship.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: Whether it is the family you were born into or the family you chose to create, we are impacted and impacting everyone that we hold dear to our hearts. I think great change can occur in your life when you include your family in treatment and explore the ways you are connecting and work towards shifting the moments of hurt and disconnection.

specialities.name: Premarital Counseling
specialities.description: We can look at marriage and unions as romantic decisions but I find that it is also helpful to view them as living and breathing contracts. What do you require from yourself and your partner in order to be satisfied by the relationship? I want to help you be clear about what you bring forward and what your partner does as well. What areas need to be expanded and what areas need to be shifted?

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: There is a great amount of cultural attention and significance paid to couples who are wanting to partner and marry one another. I want to support you in creating meaning and ritual to the ending of your marriage. I want to guide partners to reflect and say goodbye to one another in a respectful and loving manner.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: 'Sex is not a thing you do, it is a place you go.' Esther Perel stated this and I could not agree more. Unfortunately many of us have not been given clear directions on how to arrive to this place of sexuality, sensuality, and pleasure. I feel confident in supporting you and your partner(s) in exploring, expanding, and healing your sexual relationship with each other and yourself.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: We want freedom and intimacy. We want to feel like we’re at home and at the same time we want spontaneity. We want the security of deeply knowing someone but we’re afraid to let that person in. We seek everything from one person that a whole village used to provide. There are plenty of reasons why you might be feeling unsatisfied or hurt or betrayed or all of the of the above in your relationship.

name: Stacy Sheffler
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am here to join you with navigating complex feelings, attachment styles, trauma narratives, communication needs and strengths.
ideal_client: I am here to join you with navigating complex feelings, attachment styles, trauma narratives, communication needs and strengths. You may have relationship struggles, depression, anxiety, identity exploration or trauma experiences. I can join you in finding relief from those experiences. I am a part of the queer community and trans/non binary affirming.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am gender queer and focus on therapeutic work with the LGBTQ community and am transgender affirming and aware. I have focused my work with the LGBTQ community, but also very comfortable and competent with any other identifying person or couple. I have had a private practice in St John's since 2011. I ascribe to somatic, trauma focused treatment and practice EMDR. I also ascribe to cognitive based modalities as well and focus on understanding attachment styles and how they influence our relationships with others.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my bachelor's in psychology and criminal justice at Indiana University and my Masters in counseling at Eastern Michigan University. I spent several years working with adolescent girls struggling with substance use and 8 years working with adolescent boys at a residential treatment center focusing on sex abuse and trauma. In my private practice since 2011 I have worked with individuals, couples and families and focus on having a queer, trans, non binary affirming practice.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: How we attached to our significant caregivers in early childhood leads us to desire, gravitate and repel others. Understanding these styles can aid in seeking healthier relationships.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Utilizing a specific protocol with eye movement this modality can aid in reframing the intensity you feel around the trauma you experienced.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Understanding how we think impacts our behaviors and emotions. Reframing those thoughts can influence our experience with others and the world.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Living in a Cis world, LGBTQ people experience the world in a different lense and often have to navigate through those microdifferences that can cause pain, discomfort, anxiety or depression. Being able to assert and affirm your experience are necessary to feeling confident in your identity and how you experience this world and this world experiencing you.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: Navigating our gender identity can be layered with confusion, influenced thoughts or feelings from society, parents, or ourselves. Therapy can aid in navigating to understanding your gender identity to feel more at ease and comfortable while you become the self you want to be.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Often the experience you are having with your mental health can be rooted in past or current trauma. Looking at how to reframe those experiences either with cognitive based trauma work or EMDR can aid in releiving the intensity of the trauma.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is appearing to be an experience that all are having in this complex, ever changing world. Anxiety can be experienced with your thoughts and in your body. Therapy can aid in reducing the intensity of the anxiety and aid in coping in a way that feels better to you.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Thoughts of hopelessness, sadness, lack of interest in things you used to enjoy, sleep or appetite disturbances can overwhelm your system impacting your world. Therapy can aid in reducing the intensity of depression and aid in coping in a way that resumes you to the experience you would like to have.

name: Tory Harding
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Have you decided it's time to prioritize your mental health?
ideal_client: I can help you through difficult times and be your guide to strengthening yourself and feeling better. You're not alone and you're not without support. I bring my authentic self, my depth of experience, and a little bit of humor to every session. And above all, I enjoy working together to help you grow and become more resilient, mindful, and balanced. My approach is to use Science-backed methods balanced with empathy and intuition, instilling Holistic, whole-body awareness, being Less formal—co

approaches.What I Specialize In: I work with: Teens, adults, and seniors. All genders and cultural backgrounds. Anyone with general mental health concerns. The tools I use: ACT, CBT, DBT, Positive Psychology. I take a flexible approach depending on your needs and goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that there is a way to find a path to better mental health. Regardless of who you are, you deserve to have that support of a professional therapist that can help you make sense of life. We support the LGBTQIA+ community, veterans, and all of our lovely members of all backgrounds and ethnicities. We provide a safe space for those who want to voice their struggles with daily life.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I specialize in multiple areas of mental health including depression, anxiety, stress, PTSD, OCD, bipolar disorders, and more.

name: Patrick Bluett
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Specializing in relationship and sexual issues, I offer person-centered behavioral therapy to both individuals and couples.
ideal_client: Are you caught in an anxious spiral? Do painful thoughts cause knee-jerk reactions that hurt you or your relationships? Are you so stuck in patterns of thought that you cannot be present in the moment? In your body? Uncertainty and fear are facts of life and anxiety's function is to protect us from things that could hurt us. Anxiety means well, but usually it ends up doing more harm than good, robbing us of the experiences and relationships that could bring us joy - I'm here to help with that.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Specializing in relationship and sexual issues, I work with both couples and individuals to treat anxiety and other factors impacting their ability to connect securely and deeply with themselves and others. My approach to therapy is relational, inclusive and trauma-informed. I serve as an ally to my clients and provide them with a space to explore their deepest truths without fear of judgment. I work with my clients to cultivate deep insights, self-compassion and to accept and embrace their humanity. Our therapeutic journey will be one of courage, constructive discomfort, and ultimately, clarity. My role as a therapist is to accompany you on this journey, to guide, encourage and, most importantly, protect you as you grow in your awareness and understanding. As your therapist, I place great emphasis on our connection and rapport; I cherish laughter as well as tears; and I will ask of you only what is safe to explore.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have lived in Oregon almost my whole life and am deeply rooted in the Pacific Northwest. In my free time I am training for half marathons, planning my next backpacking trip and hosting board game nights. I hold a BA from the University of Oregon and an MS in Mental Health Counseling from Capella University and am a Licensed Professional Counselor under the Oregon Board of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists. I am also a member of the American Association of Sexuality Educators, Counselors and Therapists (AASECT) completing my requirements to become a Certified Sex Therapist. My practice is an inclusive and safe space for all - no exceptions. My practice is diverse, sex positive, LGBTQ-allied, kink-friendly and poly / ENM competent. I offer a free 20 minute phone consultation to ensure we are a good fit. If not, I will happily point you towards other therapists and resources to help you on your journey.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: What behaviors in your life are not serving you? What thoughts create those behaviors? What beliefs do you have about yourself that influence those thoughts? Cognitive Behavioral Therapy provides one of the most well-researched, evidence-based treatments for a host of issues ranging from anxiety and depression to sexual issues and provides a fantastic structure for uncovering core beliefs and challenging thoughts that create harmful patterns and tear down relationships.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: What did your earliest relationships teach you about love and intimacy? What patterns of behavior did you adopt in order to protect those relationships? How are those patterns serving you now? Adult attachment theory provides a valuable framework for understanding the ways that you form and maintain relationships in order to meet core emotional needs. Through therapy, we can identify patterns that might not align with your relationship values and learn better ways of finding and keeping love.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: You are not your thoughts. A thought is not a fact. When we learn to identify and sit with difficult thoughts rather than letting them take us for a ride, we begin to see that thoughts are like changing weather patterns. We become more aware, less attached and vastly more open to experiencing life by our own design. Mindfulness helps us identify the ways in which we are being reactive so that we can learn how to respond intentionally, making it a fantastic compliment to talk therapy.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Working from an attachment lens, I help my clients uncover the ways their behaviors impede their ability to connect deeply with others and practice secure ways to improve their loving relationships. I work with individuals and couples to improve communication, behaviors and loving practices to develop partnerships that serve each individual and bridge gaps in communication and physical intimacy.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: When men get caught in the idea of 'performance', they lose touch with the sensations that create pleasure and deepen intimate connection. When we are absent from pleasurable experience there can be devastating consequences for our relationship(s) and our personal wellbeing. I work with my clients to challenge the old paradigms and bring the focus back to connection and pleasure.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: As a practicing polyamorous person, I have a wealth of personal as well as professional experience working with relationships in all sorts of non-traditional configurations. Whether you're opening up your relationships, negotiating your agreements or processing difficult feelings that come along with navigating polyamory or consensual non-monogamy, my work can provide a space of healing, learning and growth so that you and your partners have more resource to love and enjoy one another.

name: Amanda Sawyer
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am warm and direct and excited to meet you and help you navigate important changes within your life.
ideal_client: Many people look at you and what you have in your life and assume you "have it all", but something is missing for you. You may be struggling with depression and anxiety and the wounds of your past. You may be extra hard on yourself, convinced this is the only way to reach your goals. Together, we will explore all of this, with compassion.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I balance empathy and compassion with a healthy dose of challenging you. I believe you have the power within you to change your unhealthy patterns in relationships and live a more fulfilling and embodied life. Therapy is not always a comfortable process. It requires us to turn toward ourselves in ways we likely have not done before. It is my intention to be right there with you in this process, so you know you are not alone. I am not the expert on your life and want to learn about you, from you. I am committed to providing you my honest feedback and building a rapport that helps you to share more and become open to the possibilities within you.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I use an eclectic approach to therapy, and operate from an ecotherapy lens. What is ecotherapy? It looks many different ways, depending on who the client is: some will opt for outdoor sessions and some will want to explore ways in between their sessions to increase the benefits of therapy by engaging in out-of-doors homework. I weave in knowledge about our connection to nature and how a disconnect from nature often adds to human suffering. Our modern, fast-paced lives were not designed with our well being in mind. Together, we will explore ways you might increase your connection with nature, of which we are all a part, and most of us are totally separate from.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have long enjoyed the work of John and Julie Gottman, Esther Perel, Brene Brown and Alexandra Solomon to name a few. I feel honored to help you achieve deeper connections and healthier relational self awareness to improve the quality of your relationships and in turn, your lives.

name: Rachel Starck, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide individual and couples counseling to address depression, anxiety, adjustments, parenting and stress management.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize a cognitive behavioral, solution focused, and mindfulness based approach to facilitating change with my clients meeting in person or online! I draw on my training in Dialectic Behavioral Therapy as well. Initially we will discuss your history, identify goals, and obstacles. Then we will clarify what you have the power to change (Yes, I am a big fan of the Serenity Prayer) and develop step by step plan for getting there. Depending on your goals, we will identify concrete skills, exercises, and behaviors for you to apply between our sessions. Frequency of our meetings can vary. We may meet weekly, every other week, monthly, online or in person as needed depending on your situation and goals. On the business side, I use MindEase Billing Service to submit insurance claims. If we opt to work together, they will call you to get insurance information, then clarify your benefits and let us both know what your financial responsibility will be.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a licensed professional counselor in the state of OR. I graduated from Lewis & Clark College in 1997 with a MS in Counseling Psychology after obtaining a BA in Biology. I volunteered in domestic violence shelters, worked for Oregon Youth Authority at Hillcrest Youth Correctional Facility, and then in adolescent residential treatment facilities under Morrison Center and Trillium Family services as a therapist and clinical manager. During this time, I studied DBT which fits well with my therapeutic orientation and also became qualified to provide supervision to therapist interns. I entered private practice in 2003 and initially specialized in working with adolescents and their families. I currently focus on helping parents with stress management, relationship, and parenting skills since becoming a parent in 2005. My office is N Portland where I have cultivated a professional community of healing practitioners, whom I share space with at The North Portland Growth Place!

name: Jane Sproul
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with adults who seek support for life-stressors and mental health conditions.
ideal_client: I respond fastest to emails at janesproullpc at hushmail dot com.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am easy-going, solution-focused and mindful of evidence-based practice. I'm an east-coaster who has lived in Portland for years. I work well with folks new to counseling, newly diagnosed or who have trouble paying attention or remembering what they talked about in a counseling session.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a master's degree in Counseling from Portland State University. I have completed professional development in bipolar disorder, intercultural communication and ADHD. I have worked in a healthcare setting for many years.

specialities.name: Early Recovery
specialities.description: I treat several conditions.

name: JR Fisher
title: Clinical Psychologist Resident
intro: My style is warm, direct, curious, and collaborative. Let's connect to explore your path to inner harmony.
ideal_client: It takes courage and vulnerability to seek therapy and I approach this work with great care and respect. I work with a diversity of individuals, many of whom have felt “stuck” or disappointed with some aspect of their lives. The root causes of persistent suffering are unique to each person and I'm curious to get to know you and how I can help.

name: Ryan Varian
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: My work is guided by the belief that mental health care should be compassionate, collaborative, and personalized.
ideal_client: If you’re looking for a psychologist in Portland, greater Oregon, or in Washington who offers culturally responsive care and evidenced-based therapy for anxiety, depression, identity development, and emotional wellness, I’d be honored to support you! Whether you’re addressing health concerns, navigating life as a neurodivergent individual, or transitioning in career or life, we’ll build a therapeutic relationship rooted in safety, empowerment, and connection.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With a background in community mental health and primary care behavioral health, I offer an integrative, culturally responsive, and values-based approach to therapy. I believe therapy is most effective when it goes beyond symptoms—when we explore your values, goals, and passions together. Through this lens, we co-create a foundation rooted in curiosity, connection, and emotional safety, opening space for healing and growth. I’ve had the privilege of expanding gender-affirming care at a community health system in Seattle and helped develop a behavioral health department embedded within a community center—where I facilitated programming focused on emotional wellness and connection. These experiences have shaped my commitment to making therapy accessible, affirming, and grounded in real-world community values.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Originally from the East Coast, I completed my bachelor’s in psychology at the University of Pittsburgh, then followed my love for nature and community to the Pacific Northwest, where I earned my Doctorate in Clinical Psychology from Pacific University in Oregon. I’ve put down deep roots in this part of the States, nurtured through meaningful connection and community. When I’m not working, you’ll likely find me: dancing to live music to connect with rhythm and community. practicing yoga to bring my awareness to the present moment. paddleboarding because nothing is more calming than being on the water. spending time outdoors with my dog, Jesse.

name: Christine Bethel
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: You are happy and successful, the one people come to for help, the couple others admire, the fixer. What no one knows is that on the inside, behind closed doors, you feel like a mess.

approaches: Perhaps feeling lost or like a mess doesn't begin to describe your current struggle. Maybe you worry you're permanently damaged or that your relationship has experienced too much pain and resentment to recover. The isolation of keeping it together for the world makes the exhaustion, worry, and unhappiness even heavier. You are not alone and you are not doomed to this place forever. You can be ok, you can feel happier, your relationship can be fulfilling again. Common symptoms of these hidden struggles include: anxiety, depression, numbing, & PTSD. Whether you're an individual finding your way back to happiness, a couple adding new depth to your relationship, or you are just desperately trying to make things work, please call me. I'd love to help. What you see is what you get! My style is relaxed but direct, I want to optimize your time and growth.

I've been practicing therapy for 10 years and continue to be amazed by the clients I meet and the growth they allow me to witness, teach, and support. My background and special interests include: Successful couples on the rocks & successful individuals struggling with self, potentially experiencing symptoms of depression, anxiety, addiction and trauma. Ask me about EMDR! *Please check out my website, cbetherapy.com, for more info and to schedule an appointment.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: As with systems theory, I find attachment theory to be an extremely helpful model in supporting clients. We are indelibly marked by our early bonds with caregivers and typically, what we learned in those relationships sets our beliefs about the world and determines the patterns we follow in future relationships. Not that we can't change, attachment theory just helps us understand why.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am EMDR Part I & II trained and find it to be one of the most valuable and efficacious tools I have gained in my 10 years in practice. Developed to address trauma and PTSD, it is now widely used for all sorts of challenges clients bring to therapy. Check out cbetherapy.com for an EMDR explanation and more specifics.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: No man is an island unto himself. Each person I work with is impacted by the various systems and relationships in their lives. This broad perspective allows me deeper understanding and insight into the challenges and solutions each client brings with them.

specialities.name: Sexual Abuse
specialities.description: My work has shown me that an astounding number of us have experienced sexual abuse. Perhaps your experience was recent or maybe it is from the distant past, maybe you have buried it deep or have addressed it before but now find it cropping up in your life and causing problems. You don't have to live with the pain you are experiencing, many tools, including EMDR, can bring you significant healing.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: For me, relationships make the world go 'round! I am passionate about couples, helping them grow, heal, and feel fulfilled in the context of their relationships. My work includes: partners who are dating, newlyweds experiencing challenges, empty nesters spicing things up, partners wrestling with separation, married, unmarried, traditional and non-traditional relationships.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is another extremely common problem faced by Americans. Again, you don't have to suffer alone and you can feel better. One of my favorite and most effective tricks to treating anxiety is EMDR. Friends, get ready to kiss anxiety goodbye!!!

specialities.name: Aspergers
specialities.description: I've met an increasing number of adults who have been struggling in their relationships or in other areas of their lives due to undiagnosed Asperger's. If you suspect this is you and would like some help to navigate areas of your life more successfully please give me a call. My Aspie clients have been some of the most delightful, intelligent, and quickest learners I have ever met.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression stats in the US are staggering, unfortunately, most of us suffer alone. You don't have to, you CAN experience relief. Symptoms can include lack of motivation, restlessness, sadness, irritability, insomnia/hypersomnia, weight loss/gain, clumsiness, forgetfulness, suicidal thoughts, among others. Depression is not a weakness of character or laziness. Let me help.

name: Natasha Laumei
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer therapy, clinical supervision, adult Level 1 Autism evaluations, and EMDR intensives, all within Oregon, Washington, and Alaska.
ideal_client: I am currently accepting clients for therapy and autism evaluations, as well as supervisees (LPC and MFT associates in both Oregon and Washington) for both individual and group supervision.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from a client-centered and collaborative foundation, supporting individuals looking to process and heal from trauma, develop further personal insight, improve relationships with self and others, and explore opportunities for growth, empowerment, and deepened quality of life. As a therapist I bring empathy, intuition, and humor into session and integrate trauma-informed, attachment-focused, anti-oppressive, neurodiverse-affirming, and feminist frameworks into my clinical approach. I utilize EMDR, parts-work, interpersonal neurobiology, somatic, narrative, creative expression, ecotherapy, and mindfulness-based approaches in my work with clients. All of my work is rooted in the belief that health and wellbeing are a right and not a privilege and I am so grateful to join each of my clients along their journeys of growth and healing.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My decision to become a therapist was informed by many things: studying human stories through the lens of creative writing and narrative structure, working with refugee families as an AmeriCorps volunteer, supporting teens at a therapeutic boarding school in the Sapphire Mountains of Montana, and my own lifelong journey of trauma recovery, growth, and healing. I am a white, cis, queer, neurodivergent woman, and in the rest of my life I love spending time in nature, being with my sweet dogs and sassy cat, traveling, and diving into my new love of Brazilian jiu-jitsu.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization & Reprocessing) can be used alone or integrated with other therapies to treat trauma, reduce distress, and provide significant psychological and somatic relief for clients. I am an EMDR Consultant and consider EMDR to be an incredibly effective and powerful tool for healing. For more information go to: http://www.emdria.org/

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: A relational approach in therapy highlights how our relationships with ourselves, others, and our world impact our overall wellbeing and happiness. I prioritize our therapeutic relationship in order to provide you with a safe space to explore changes within yourself and practice new ways of connecting with others and the world. I also draw from an interpersonal neurobiology framework, which understands the human experience through the integration of the brain, the mind, and relationships.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Narrative therapy examines the ways we are influenced by the stories we tell about our selves and our lives. When we explore these narratives and our ability to retell our stories in new ways we realize a powerful opportunity for healing. I have found narrative therapy to be an incredibly effective therapeutic tool -- fun, creative, and transformative.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: In addition to psychotherapy and clinical supervision, I provide neurodiversity-affirming comprehensive assessments for Level 1 Autism in adults as a member of the Empower Psychological provider team (https://www.empowerwhoyouare.com). I also support adults processing and integrating an adult diagnosis of autism through ongoing therapy.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I work with PTSD and complex trauma through an integration of multiple modalities including EMDR, parts-work, Interpersonal Neurobiology, and attachment-focused therapy. Together these approaches blend the science of neurobiology and the brain, personal narrative, and somatic experiences to allow for healing of your whole system, building safety and connection within your mind and body, and the world around you.

name: Sophia Kukladyer
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Hi! I'm Sophia and I'm the owner of PDX Therapy Center. I help individuals and their relationships to thrive! I can't wait to meet you.
ideal_client: I love relationships, connection, and the feeling you get when you are able to truly connect with others. This passion has driven me to form a practice where I specialize in working with individuals, couples, and families on relationship issues. If you are struggling in your marriage, wanting more connection with others, or finding yourself constantly arguing with loved ones, I can help.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist, specializing in couples and relationships. I am committed to serving a diverse clientele, including LGBTQ+ individuals, couples, and poly systems. I have completed Level One Gottman Method Couples Therapy and an Externship in Emotionally Focused Couples Therapy. I have 13 years of experience working in multiple settings including private practice, out-patient substance abuse clinics, schools, and various centers. I believe that every individual has the internal strength and resources to live a more fulfilling life and support them in cultivating these strengths to reach their goals.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I truly love relationships and the connection they can bring. I also understand the pain that occurs when our relationships are struggling. That's why I've dedicated the majority of my work to supporting individuals and their relationships, whether that involves the relationship with themselves or others. I received my Masters in Couples and Family Therapy and have completed the Level One Training in Gottman Method Couples Therapy and the Externship in Emotionally Focused Therapy.

name: Tyler Walsh
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: With curiosity, conscious connection, and openness we will explore your psychic depths to find a way toward wholeness and healing.

approaches.My Background: Greetings! I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) and Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor, practicing at Rose City Therapists and at Rainfall Medicine as a Ketamine-Assisted Therapist in Portland. I hold a Master of Social Work (MSW) from the University of New Hampshire and a B.A. in Environmental Studies from the University of Colorado. I am also a veteran of the Iraq and Afghanistan wars. My clinical experience includes inpatient behavioral health, intensive addiction treatment, individual counseling, and community mental health. In addition to traditional therapy, I am a 400-hour certified breathwork facilitator and a 200-hour certified Tantra Yoga teacher. My approach integrates Transpersonal Psychology, Jungian Psychology, Internal Family Systems (IFS), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), and Depth Psychology. I offer a grounded and compassionate presence, honoring each person’s innate wisdom and unique path toward healing.

name: Heidi Jacobson
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I am accepting new clients!
ideal_client: My work as a therapist is heavily influenced by Internal Family Systems (IFS) and Somatic interventions. I believe that it is through our connection between mind and body, and validation of emotions that healing takes place.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist, I believe that humans have an innate inclination towards growth and healing. I am committed to fostering a collaborative, accepting space where all individuals can reconnect with their inner- wisdom and navigate the ups and downs of life. My practice emphasizes the importance of self- compassion and nurturance of resilience to move through challenges.

name: Allison Browne
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Accepting group clients only for chronic pain support groups. Contact me for more information - I look forward to connecting with you!
ideal_client: Do you feel like no one gets how bad it really is? Maybe it seems like you're doing fine from the outside because it's hard to even name what's wrong? Or maybe it feels like your emotions would be too much for a friend to handle? The tagline on my website is "grounded therapy for people who color outside the lines." People don't fit into boxes. Set up a free consultation with me and let's see if I'm good match for you.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I use trauma-informed and evidence-based treatments with a heavy dose of humor and creativity. Clients often tell me that I am down-to-earth and appreciate the freedom to be irreverent. I will take your concerns seriously and meet you where you are. I am strongly influenced by research on attachment, cognitive psychology, emotion-focused therapy, mindfulness, and polyvagal theory. I emphasize attention to what’s happening in the here-and-now to help you create the change you want and access healing. I enjoy working with people from many different backgrounds. I began my anti-racist, anti-bias journey more than twenty years ago. I remain grateful for the patience and confrontation provided by my early teachers and mentors. I am willing to engage with openness around issues related to bias and oppression. I identify, in part, as a white, cis-gender, middle-age queer from the East Coast. I continue to do my own work around privilege and internalized biases.

name: Nate Wilson-Traisman
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I enjoy helping teens and families work through the challenges and changes of adolescence. I also enjoy working with adult individuals.
ideal_client: I work with adolescents, individual adults, and parents. I enjoy helping folks find new approaches for working with stress, anxiety, depression, adjustments to life transitions, and family-oriented relationship challenges. I often work with parents, helping them learn how to adjust their parenting approach to better meet the developmental needs of their adolescent/young adult. As a former athlete and coach, I love helping clients who are wanting to work on performance-related issues.

approaches.My Background: I am a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist with the Oregon Board of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists. I hold a Master's Degree in Couples and Family Therapy from the University of Oregon. During my Master's program, I worked as a therapist at PeaceHealth Counseling, providing therapy to children, adolescents, and families at an outpatient pediatric clinic. I also provided individual, couples, and family therapy at the University of Oregon's Center for Family Therapy. My previous professional experience includes coaching high school and college baseball, working in college admissions, and working as an academic support specialist for student-athletes at the University of Oregon. Prior attending graduate school, I had a brief career as a freelance journalist. As an undergraduate student, I majored in English literature, and was the captain of my college baseball team.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Deciding to see a therapist can be an intimidating process, and can be filled with all sorts of questions. My goal is to make therapy feel accessible and welcoming. My strengths-based approach draws on your strengths, resources, past successes, and hopes for the future. I believe the strength of the relationship between therapist and client is the single most important aspect of therapy. Consequently, my approach is founded on developing a strong working relationship with you. My therapeutic approach utilizes models of family systems therapy, cognitive-behavioral therapy, and mindfulness-based approaches.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: The adolescent years are filled with immense physical, emotional, and cognitive change. While this developmental period is undoubtedly exciting, it can also present adolescents and families with newfound challenges. My previous experiences—as a therapist, coach, and teacher—have given me exposure to the unique challenges of adolescence.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a normal human reaction to stress, but it can become problematic when it gets in the way of our goals, ambitions, and day-to-day needs. I use a combination of cognitive behavioral therapy, and mindfulness practice to identify negative thoughts/judgments of our anxiety experience, and to regain control of how our body reacts to anxiety.

name: Noelani Perkins
title: Student Counselor
intro: I strive to offer a space where marginalized voices have a say in their healing.
ideal_client: My heart lies with those who feel disconnected from the people around them; who don't typically see identities like theirs accepted in society; and who are navigating intercultural relationships. Whether you’re feeling lost and void of motivation, caught in relational distress, or wondering what makes you “you” I want to listen and support you every step of the way. I work with both individuals and couples experiencing life transitions, identity exploration, and who need a place to just "be."

approaches.My Background and Approach: I view individuals as resilient embodied beings with rich and complex histories where mind and body and soul are all interconnected. I believe that oftentimes, our bodies store and convey emotions and traumas before we even are mindfully aware of them. The body communicates beyond the verbal, and I hope to provide a comfortable space in order to listen and attune to your body and your experiences. I provide an integrative space using an emotion-focused, bodily-aware, and person-centered approach. My hope and goal in our work together is to provide an empathic space where we can explore unhelpful patterns, get down to the roots of your emotions, and figure out what's blocking you from living the life you desire. Sometimes this may look like talking, other times it may look like incorporating art and movement -- wherever you are and whatever you need, we'll figure it out together.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a first generation college graduate and woman of color, I have deep personal experience navigating confusing systems and figuring out myself how to get the help I needed. My heart and passion for helping people stemmed from scanning various counseling spaces and systems and not seeing anyone who looked like me. In a time when I deeply needed help, I could not find someone who looked like they could relate to my story or know of my lived experiences. This lack spurred me to pursue counseling and make my practice one of acceptance, empathy, and healing. I believe processing and healing is a relational and collaborative effort, where together we can work to build resilience and help you find your voice and strength to navigate whatever life may come your way. If you, too, have been feeling this lack of support or representation, I invite you to reach out and schedule a free meet and greet to see if we'd make a good fit. It would be an honor to walk this journey alongside you!

name: Luke Colbourn
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help people navigate their stresses and anxieties in new ways.
ideal_client: Does it feel like there's just too much on your plate? Has it felt that way for too long? When you experience chronic stress sometimes it feels like overwhelming, buzzing anxiety. Other times it can be a heavy weight where everything seems pointless. If either of those resonates for you, it's time for a change. Therapy can help, and I look forward to helping you find the insight and tools to live at ease.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer therapy that draws from the wisdom of the buddhist tradition and evidence based practices (such as ACT & CBT). It is both gentle and direct. Together we build a relationship of trust and respect as we explore your feelings and circumstances. The insights we uncover together guide us to the interventions that can help you. Throughout therapy you will be cultivating self-awareness and developing a tailored set of skills for handling life's stresses with greater ease.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe part of my role as a therapist is to help my clients uncover their inherent wisdom. Another part is to help alleviate suffering here and now. In both cases, I bring active and deep listening to build an honest and engaged relationship. Insight and awareness practices from the buddhist tradition are an important part of my worldview as a therapist: I am influenced by two decades of meditation practice, participation in retreats, and active study with lineage holders. These experiences have taught me that we are all co-creators of our shared reality, each of us being influenced and influencing others. I value being able to see from my clients' perspective to deeply understand their experience. I also value my years of teaching and outdoor leadership experience, which help me remain pragmatic and solution focused when needed.

specialities.name: Contemplative
specialities.description: Contemplative psychotherapy is based on integrating the wisdom of the buddhist tradition with modern psychology. We emphasize the present moment experience and each client's inherent mental and emotional well-being, and help clients recognize this quality in themselves. As a client your ability to move your awareness in a flexible and skillful way will grow, as will your ability to see your own wisdom.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT is a potent tool for working with depression, anxiety and trauma. Its focus on the relationship between thoughts, feelings and actions can offer personal insights. Clients build awareness of their 'automatic thoughts' and use this to uncover 'core beliefs'. In these ways it can pair well with mindfulness practices. CBT also offers effective tools for changing behavior

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: ACT is a subtype of CBT which focuses more on noticing our thoughts, feelings, behaviors, and asking ourselves if they are 'workable'. Do my actions move me toward my values, and if not what can I learn to do differently to help them line up more closely in the future? The 'acceptance' in ACT is not about passively tolerating problems in the world, it's about our own internal experience: noticing it, acknowledging it, and being with it.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is an expression of a nervous system that expects something bad to happen. For our ancestors, this might have come up briefly when confronted by a predator, and then resolve when they escaped (or didn't). Today, we live with lots of sources of abstract threat (what do my peers think of me? am I doing well enough at work/school?) and more immediate threat (is it safe to go outside my home?). These stressors add up. I work with clients to help create a sense of safety and ease.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Traumas we experience leave lasting imprints on us. They might be big, singular events that change our view of the world. They can also be a number of smaller disturbing experiences that add up. It is hard and not at all intuitive to try to digest these experiences.
