I help people break these experiences down so that they sit differently in the mind and body.

name: Amanda Feaver, MA, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with grief, relationships, and climate distress.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I love my work as a therapist. Before my graduate work in counseling and psychology I spent five years studying theology, developmental education and spiritual development. With a strong focus in mind, body, and spirit, I work with clients to find a deeper sense of congruence, wholeness, and presence. Counseling is a beautiful combination of compassionate presence and curiosity that leads to forward movement. Together, as we pay attention to your life, your loss, and your desires, you will become more aware of your own wisdom.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I’ve had the privilege of working with psychiatric patients, at community clinics, on crisis intervention teams, and in private practice. I’ve also spent time working internationally with people who have experienced extreme loss through the violence of war. Much of my work with clients here in Portland centers around grief from the loss of dreams, relationships, the death of loved ones, and our current ecological crisis. My clients come from a variety of communities and socio-economic backgrounds; through them I have learned so much about the strength of human beings. I thoroughly believe that positive and sustainable changes are possible for everyone and it is such an honor to witness the courage and resilience of the people and communities I work with as they seek growth, freedom and a new sense of well-being.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I utilize PACT (Psychobiological Approach to Couple Therapy) in my work with couples. This approach combines developmental neuroscience, attachment theory, and arousal regulation. PACT supports couples toward a new way of engaging. When secure functioning is the foundation of our partnerships we are able to expand in profound and satisfying ways, not only in our partnerships and families, but out into the world.

specialities.name: Accelerated Resolution Therapy
specialities.description: Accelerated Resolution Therapy (ART) is a bilateral eye movement therapy that utilizes memory reconsolidation and voluntary image replacement to help us get unstuck and expand.. Most people require 1-5 sessions to process specific events. This is not an ongoing treatment; these are integration and expansion sessions. Many folks come in to do a few ART sessions while working with another long-term therapist.

name: Zoë Muller
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Zoë's client-centered approach focuses on personal strengths and promotes developing individualized coping strategies.
ideal_client: Zoë's primary focus has been on delivering trauma-informed evidence-based therapy to children, adolescents and their families, and her professional experience includes comprehensive direct care across a wide spectrum of mental health concerns such as anxiety, OCD, attachment disorder, ADHD and neurodivergence.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Zoë incorporates concepts and individual modalities associated with life spandevelopment, behavioral change through CBT and ACT, play therapy, Adlerian child guidance, mindfulness and teaching self-regulation and social skills to neurodivergent population. She works collaboratively with families, caregivers, educators and other important players in the child’s environment to ensure a wrap-around support system that fosters growth and development. Zoe is fluent in Russian.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Zoë believes that parenting is one of the most important roles a person can undertake in their life, and that navigating the unique challenges of this role can be a gateway to a full and meaningful existence. She has extensive experience in providing behavioral support to parents of children with anxiety, OCD and neurodivergence, as well as evidence-based solution-oriented support to families dealing with mental health challenges.

name: Renata Austin
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome! I focus on serving multiracial, BIPOC, and immigrant communities through person-centered and relational therapy.
ideal_client: We might be a good fit if you are needing support with life transitions, family relationships and intergenerational patterns, friendships, racial identity development, discrimination/oppression, depression, anxiety, or grief and loss. I work with people of all genders, sexualities, races and abilities, with a focus on individuals who identify as multiracial, BIPOC, Filipina/o/x, children/grandchildren of immigrants, immigrant/refugee, bicultural, and/or neurodivergent.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In our counseling relationship I provide a safe place to be fully yourself, focus on challenges you are experiencing, and consider making changes that might be helpful to you. I help you look at things differently by making connections you may not be aware of and shining a light on things that are in the background of your experience. I practice counseling with a non-judgmental, validating, empathic and strengths-based approach focused on building trust so that you feel safe in sharing what you need to. I work collaboratively with you to discover unmet needs, underlying feelings, important values, and practical solutions in collaboration with you. I believe that individual issues don’t exist in a vacuum and have to be understood within the context of their relationships, family, and community. I seek to understand you through the intersection of your many identities (race, gender, sexuality, ability, class) and broach conversations about systems of oppression in my work.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I identify as a biracial 3rd gen filipina/white, able-bodied, neurodivergent cisgender woman. As a person who exists in the in-between, I have first hand experience navigating the challenges of not “making sense” to others and of feeling like I don’t belong, and bring this understanding into my work with clients. I’m also familiar with the mental health stigma present in AAPI communities, in particular the Filipino/a/x community. I grew up in Berkeley, CA and moved to Portland, OR in 2011. I completed my M.S in Marriage Couple and Family Counseling from Portland State University in 2020 and spent two years working as a counselor serving refugees, immigrants and other low income individuals at a local community agency. Before I became a counselor I engaged in supporting individuals and families around reproductive health, pregnancy options, early childhood, and parent engagement. Outside of my work I enjoy spending quality time with friends, gardening, camping, and playing music.

name: Ivy Campbell
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I believe that at the core of therapy is a safe and validating relationship that helps us build the tools to navigate our toughest moments.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with women and gender-expansive adolescents and adults navigating a wide range of concerns. I have specialized experience working with anxiety, depression, varying forms of self harm (including eating disorders), and with survivors of intimate partner violence or navigating difficult relationships.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a licensed Social Worker in the state of Oregon and New York who specializes in supporting adolescents, young adults and their families confronting a range of issues. I earned my bachelor's degree in Sociology and Masters Degree from NYU. I am currently enrolled at the William Alanson White Institute's Child and Adolescent Program. My approach is personable and affirming, informed by a holistic approach to care that aids in the promotion of wholeness and healing in the mind and body. Through this lens, I create an empowering environment, integrating the humor, honesty, and critical consciousness that is so integral to my personality inside and outside of the therapy room. My therapeutic orientation is trauma-informed and psychodynamic, honoring the complexities of your personal history while integrating relevant interventions in service of your unique needs. The goal is to find compassion for your hardships and find useful, long-term solutions.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I create a relaxed and open-minded space, integrating the humor, honesty, and critical consciousness that is so integral to my personality inside and outside of the therapy room. Calling on my background in Social Work, I support client’s in building greater self compassion through understanding how the systems in which we exist aid on our harm, and our healing. I am formally trained in the use of Dialectical Behaviors Therapy (DBT) to manage some of those tougher challenges through the use of emotional regulation practices, with the goal of increasing self awareness and balance.

name: Anya Hicks
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Do you hide parts of yourself (sexuality, passions, neurodiversity) but long for acceptance? I'll help you walk the path to your best life.
ideal_client: You came from a healthy family and are puzzled by anxiety and panic attacks, yet sifting through the past and looking who to blame is not your plan. Or your background may include adversity, even trauma, yet you do not want to rehash the pain. All you want is to enjoy lasting relationships and be free from nightmares and constant pressure to perform. Do you hunger for unconditional love but don't believe it could be yours? I'll help you find a greater wholeness.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that every person is born with intrinsic value while utterly dependent on caregivers who may do a good job or fail. But they do the best they could with what they had at the time. As you mature and adjust to others in order to fit in, your life becomes fragmented depending on the values, roles, and supports in your life. You may be vigilant and work hard to prevent disapproval, but this limits intimacy and trust. Do you control how close others are allowed into your world? You also may be a peacemaker and give to others more than they give back. Do you feel resentful or unappreciated? Do you bury anger and fear only to have them show up unexpectedly and hurt others? I do not judge people or behaviors. I believe in body-mind connection and the healing power of greater integration. There are several effective techniques, but my favorite is Brainspotting which allows you to calibrate your own processing, release stowed away trauma and rewrite your story.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: My career path to therapy was not linear, but every stage of life fits in now like a glass tile into a beautiful mosaic. Journalism taught me how to interview people with ease and it became handy for case management at Aging and Disability services. Stay-at-home parenting gave me appreciation for playfulness and humility to learn from younger generations. As a linguist, I worked inside court rooms and jail, assisted patients during acutely painful moments and at the end of life. But most of my involvement had to do with "side effects" of clients' circumstances. I desired to become and trained to be a healing presence in this world providing hope and tools for the clients to live better. I knew therapy was a good career because some gifted therapists helped me deal with similar struggles I help my clients. Some of the adversities in my life include loss of a parent at a young age and diagnosis of ADHD.

name: Shelley Gillespie
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Reach out! I'm currently open for new clients and have availability! I’m here for you and your experience.
ideal_client: I welcome your whole self, including parts that are marginalized by dominant society, the parts that hurt most, the ones navigating change. You may be experiencing grief and loss around the death of a loved one, or a memory loss diagnosis, loss of a role, grief over the climate, or a harm done to a family member. You may be experiencing a time of transition into parenting or into caregiving, or away from a familiar role. I'm here to support you toward the healing and growth you most want.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is collaborative and holistic. I draw on eight years of community-based therapeutic practice in which I’ve served people across the ages, from children to the oldest-old, and from different racial and class backgrounds, among other identities. I aim to co-create a therapy space that is welcoming, supportive and a source of liberatory health. Our sessions are based on your stated goals and our collaboration to reach the well-being you are seeking from therapy. As appropriate, I incorporate elements of Internal Family Systems, Cognitive Behavior Therapy, Narrative Therapy, expressive arts, mindfulness, and self-compassion. I recognize the role oppression plays on individual and collective well-being and tend to those dynamics, as appropriate. I’m committed to reflecting on my own biases as an integral part of being a social justice-oriented practitioner. I believe in the vast possibilities inside of us to tap into inner resilience and relational strength.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: “You are the sky. Everything else – it’s just weather.” -Pema Chodron. In our times of grief, and struggle for a healthy planet, for racial and social justice, and inner well-being and outer connection, how do we hold intense emotions and experiences and keep on? Life in these times often doesn’t feel like just weather. How do we know and feel that we are the sky-that inner sense of okayness as we are? How do we draw on the strengths of our inner selves and our supportive relationships to create a sense of wholeness? These are the kinds of questions I’m interested in answering in times of struggle, and in answering them, setting in motion practices that help nourish healing, fortitude, and even un-imagined growth. In seeking answers to questions that will be unique to you, I offer my compassionate witnessing, attuned curiosity, and collaboration to your healing and wellness. Please reach out to our practice and let us know what you would like therapy to support you with!

name: Jules Joannini
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I work with clients 16 and older struggling with anxiety, depression, and ADHD.
ideal_client: I work with clients 16 and older struggling with anxiety, depression, and ADHD, as well as those struggling with existential issues and issues related to boundary setting, self esteem, inner critic, and imposter syndrome. At this time I am offering family counseling, but not couples counseling.

approaches.How I Can Help You: As an L.M.F.T. I have been working with adults, adolescents and families over the past 13 years, in both private practice and community mental health settings. I utilize Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Internal Family Systems, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, as well as Mindfulness based practices in my work with clients.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe it is important for every person to have a relationship where they can challenge their beliefs and assumptions about themselves and the world. I value a relationship that encourages self exploration, insight and positive change. I work collaboratively with clients to provide a safe and supportive environment, one that allows reflection in order to develop new ways of handling life's challenges. My style is warm, nurturing and engaged, while at times honest and directive.

name: Donnella Wood
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: No matter who you are, it is possible to learn to open to yourself and others, heal from traumas, and experience new ways of being.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I understand that having a relationship in one’s life that is free of judgement and infused with compassion is essential in a healing process. When we feel truly seen, heard, and received, parts of us that have gotten injured or shut down have an opportunity to arise, be tended to with kindness and transform. These parts no longer need to be annexed and a more integrated way of being can emerge. The heart of my work involves helping you listen deeply to yourself and trust your own experience. I meet you where you are and work collaboratively to attend to your individual needs. Together, we’ll invite curiosity and the body as guides for our work. I believe that the body can be a central guide in healing. When you attend to the body and have the courage to establish a trusting relationship with your body, the potential for a more sustaining and integrative healing can happen.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My broad-based education has helped me engage innovative body-based and mindfulness practices that support well-being, body integration, and resiliency. I hold a Master’s degree in professional mental health counseling from Lewis and Clark College, am a Registered Somatic Movement Therapist, a long-time meditator, and have advanced training in Somatic Experiencing Trauma Healing. For over twenty years I have supported people to listen more deeply to themselves, cultivate body awareness, and develop the inner resources and tools needed to trust their experience and live with more ease and authenticity. I offer counseling, movement education & therapy, and coaching services. My practice is open and inclusive. I embrace the Health at Every Size model and have a weight-neutral orientation. I would welcome the opportunity to talk with you about how I might be of service. Please visit my website or don't hesitate to contact me for a free consult.

name: Vinnie Gwozdz
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome to Sense of Self PDX! I am here to help you to be understood and supported as you strive for the life and relationships you want.
ideal_client: I love to work with creative people and people who are struggling with anxiety/depression or feeling misunderstood in their world or relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I employ a person-centered humanistic modality which empowers you to be the author of your story, to be the captain of your ship, and to be the person you want to be. Our sessions will be directed by what is important to you and we will use fun and insightful tools such as sand-trays and genograms to help with this process. I believe everyone benefits from therapy as it carves out regular and structured time and space to process all that life throws at us!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my graduate degree in Clinical Rehabilitation Counseling in 2016 and have been a counselor/therapist since that time. I am a Sate of Oregon Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) and am a Certified Rehabilitation Counselor (CRC).

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Politics and Covid and wildfires and social/racial reckonings are just a few of the macro-level issues we're all dealing with on top of our own individual life-stresses and anxieties. The human condition has only gotten more complex in today's world (to say nothing of Social Media) and working together to process the ways anxiety can be helped and balanced can be one of the most helpful components of therapy .

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression sucks. Therapy helps. Here in Portland we experience stretches of bleak and grey that can seem endless. By working together we can help you get out of that feeling of being stuck in a rut, overwhelmed by life, or just plain sad.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships are hard. Relationships are also a fundamental part of being human. Together in our therapeutic relationship we can explore this tricky conundrum of building and maintaining your relationships with family and friends and co-workers and romantic partners. This can be some of the most rewarding and healing work in all of therapy!

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Self-esteem impacts almost every nook and cranny of our lives. Our self-confidence level determines so many things about how we live our lives and therapy can truly help us to build and maintain our sense of self in a world that sometimes seems bent on tearing us down. Everyone has great worth and therapy can be a good way to build that reminder into our cores!

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Loss and grief go hand in hand and are happening in our lives constantly in ways big and small. Having a space to process grief can be immensely helpful and that is one thing I would love to help you with!

name: Leslie Gellert
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Human beings are inherently resilient. I am excited about helping the people make changes in their lives that lead to balance and connection
ideal_client: At Willow Tree Therapy, my mission is to provide a nurturing and non-judgmental space for healing and personal growth. I am dedicated to supporting emotional well-being, resilience and self discovery, through compassionate and evidence-based care. My goal is to empower individuals and families on their journey to a healthier and more fulfilling life. My style is warm and collaborative, with a healthy dose of humor and fun. We will work together to identify and address your goals.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I specialize in working with clients during and after pregnancy, kids and teens. In grad school, I spent a year interning in a women's clinic and have worked with perinatal clients throughout my 16 years as a therapist. I also spent over 4 years in school based primary care clinics as a behavioral health provider working with kids 5-18 years old. I use evidence based therapies and a client centered approach to empower individuals and families.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Therapy is a collaborative journey where safety, trust and authenticity create the foundation for meaningful growth. My approach is grounded in empathy and deep respect for each person's unique story. I am interested in trauma informed care, mindfulness and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy. I believe that every person has the potential for growth, resilience and lasting transformation.

name: HEATHER MATHEWSON
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: Masters in Education in School Counseling
intro: Hello! Please set up a free 20 minute consultation to see if we are a good fit :)
ideal_client: I work primarily with adolescents, ages 11-14. Middle School is such a challenging time in so many ways: there are body changes, social changes, and a desire to know oneself and find direction. It can be hard to navigate, and my desire is to help this age group gain a better understanding of themselves, and help them grow into the people they wish to become.

approaches.My Background: I am a former middle school counselor in the Portland area, and due to my desire to help this age group more in depth, I have switched to counseling full time. As a school counselor, I led Anti Racism lessons, and cultivated an LGBTQIA+ inclusive space. I helped students navigate: Anxiety Depression ADHD Self-esteem/confidence building School/life balance Social challenges Life and school transitions Time management I am also well versed in helping families connect with school counselors for additional support in school as needed.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In my practice I use a person-focused approach. This means I trust my client to know themselves best, and my job is to help guide them in their own self discovery. I also use techniques from reality therapy: to help set achievable goals, and to provide a framework to reset when things go awry.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: My training and work as a former middle school counselor has set me up to have an in depth knowledge of adolescent development and the various challenges (personal, social, familial, and school) that adolescents face, and experience helping them face those challenges and thrive.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a common issue challenging today's youth. This can lead to social isolation, challenges with school attendance, of can even morph into panic attacks, eating disorders, and other larger challenges.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: During the ages of 11-14, adolescents are frequently looking to their peers to understand where they fit, or do not fit. When one is experiencing issues related with LGBTQIA+, this can be extra challenging. I have experience is with helping youth navigate their gender identity and sexual orientation, and helping normalize their experience, while acknowledging the inherent challenges they may be experiencing.

specialities.name: Panic
specialities.description: Experiencing panic, especially in a school setting, can be overwhelming. It can lead to school avoidance, and social fears. I have experience in helping adolescents with mindfulness exercises that can help them experience calm during a moment of panic.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Working with middle schoolers, self esteem is a common topic. Helping adolescents discover their inner strengths and how to feel secure within themselves is an important aspect of my practice.

name: Rushini Jayawardena
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi! Thanks for taking a look at my profile, I am honored to be considered to be a part of your journey.
ideal_client: Do you find yourself emotionally charged or activated but not know why you have such a "big" reaction to things? Or does it feel the opposite for you, where you feel numb and indifferent about the world? I enjoy working with clients to help peel back layers of narratives created by trauma, relational wounds, or just daily stressors. I honor and respect all the ways our minds and emotions try to protect us, but also acknowledge that these "protections" may be the very thing that is causing harm.

approaches.Our Background and Approach: I take a relational approach to therapy and strive to build unique and authentic relationships with my clients. My areas of focus with my adult-aged clients are: trauma, anxiety, life adjustments, inner child work, and navigating relational and cultural stressors. I identify as a POC and enjoy offering multicultural therapy services to other individuals in the community. I have the lived experience of being an immigrant and the stressors that come with navigating identity, values, and grief related to this process. I am also a certified trauma-conscious yoga instructor, certified complex trauma therapist and offer EMDR to clients who are interested.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Neither our happiness nor our pain happens in isolation. We are relational beings and I examine the ways in which these connections can be a great source or joy and hurt. I work to examine the narratives that are created from our relationships with our gender, sexuality, family of origin, intimate relationships and more.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I help clients finding grounding and safety while helping address unprocessed memories and experiences. I offer EMDR, Trauma Conscious Yoga and other methods of grounding and processing.

name: Kate O'Brien
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hello! Welcome to Inclusive Counseling with Kate O'Brien, LCSW! I am currently taking new clients for teletherapy appointments.
ideal_client: Are you struggling with a hard life transition you weren’t expecting? Are you wishing you had more coping strategies for your symptoms of anxiety or depression? Do you wish you had someone to talk to while feeling free of judgement or expectations? Do you want to process old hurt that is impacting your life? Are you wanting to play a more active role in your own life? Have you recently experienced a great loss and need support? Are you struggling LGBTQIA2S+ issues? I am here for it.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have over 12 years working with children, youth, families, and adults. Starting out on my journey I spent 6 years as a behavioral therapist working with neurodivergent children and youth providing various types of family support. After graduating from PSU with my Masters in Social Work, I spent years as a therapist and social worker in schools. I became certified as an Adoptive and Foster Family therapist as well as a Somatic certified therapist. I am also a board approved licensing supervisor. I use an attachment lens, systems theory, racial theory, queer theory, a fat positive lens, a strengths-based lens, a whole person approach, and anti-racist trauma informed framework. I believe that our relationship and shared experiences can be foundations to work through your challenges. With an integrative and relational process I believe that in this context, you will be able to heal old wounds and live a more full and satisfying life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that you are the writer of your own story and you know yourself better than anyone. I truly feel honored to be any part of someone’s journey. I believe anyone can heal and anyone can change. I am a person who has experienced trauma in childhood, struggled with attachment challenges, suffered great loss, and walked my own complex gender/queer journey. I believe all of these experiences inform my practice and how I can show up for you. As a white provider, I am committed to anti-oppressive and anti-racist practices. I attend regular trainings and engage in educational opportunities on anti-oppressive practice regularly. This will be ongoing work for me that I am deeply committed to. Over the past years I have honed in my practice to primarily serve the 2SLGBTQIA+ population and spent time supervising a team of therapists working at an 2SLGBTQIA+ healthcare clinic as well. I am deeply passionate about serving our community.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: My framework includes many lenses and theories but one of the biggest and most important is attachment. Taking a look at attachments you were able to form or unable to form when you were young, even an infant, play a large part in how you connect with people now! I believe uncovering aspects of your former attachments can really offer valuable insight with supporting your present situations and your future.

name: Jordan Knight
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi! It takes courage to seek support and I’m so glad you’re here.
ideal_client: I love working with people of all backgrounds. I recognize the role power, privilege, and oppression plays in individual and collective wellbeing, and I strive to approach my work with cultural humility. I really enjoy providing affirming care to the LGBTQ+ community. I work with adults of all ages and teenagers aged 14 or older.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic style is mindfulness-based, acceptance-based, and attachment-based. My approach to counseling explores the impact of family and other important relationships on your mental health and wellbeing. I tend to work well with individuals who want to get in touch with their emotions, explore patterns and histories, and who are open to trying new strategies.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: You might be struggling with anxiety, depression, trauma, body image, or relationship stress. Or maybe you’re feeling overwhelmed by managing ADHD or OCD in a neurotypical world. I hope to meet your pain with compassion and uplift your strengths. I hope we can work together to empower you to create a meaningful path forward. Please reach out if you think we could be a good fit!

name: Bonnie Lambert
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Bloom Wellness Psychiatry LLC *Accepting Patients
ideal_client: Mental health diagnoses can vary from depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, psychosis, and personality disorders, among others. I believe that all things exist on a spectrum, and the intensity will vary. Due to this, diagnosis is an ever-evolving process that won’t happen with one session, but several and with rapport and trust. Information gathered in the initial evaluation is thoroughly reviewed to establish a diagnosis.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have over 17 years of experience working in mental health, first as a licensed mental health therapist and then as a psychiatric provider. I grew up in Oregon, attending Portland State University for a Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice and Psychology (2002), then earning a Master of Arts in Counseling Psychology (2005). I achieved licensure as a therapist (LPC) in 2008 and then in 2013 began my nursing education, achieving my RN in 2014 and then board certification as an advanced practice Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner. I provide psychiatric evaluation, ongoing therapeutic medication management for adults and adolescents ages 15 and older. My work has led me through numerous levels of mental health care; outpatient (adult and children), inpatient medical as psychiatry liaison, inpatient psychiatry, emergency department, and correctional settings. Health and wellness are my focus that I'd like to translate into mental health. More info can be found on the website.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Holistic care involves the mind, body, and the environmental sphere in which we exist. Instead of only focusing on the medications, there will be a combination of psychotherapy and medication, either with an outside therapist or with capacity myself, where we can assess layers and apply appropriate interventions. Therapy is an essential component of mental health treatment. The combination of therapy and medication is often more effective than either alone. Therapy expands skills, often leading to a place where medications may not be necessary. As a therapist, then nurse practitioner, I often provide brief therapy with each session as part of the funneling down of medication effects matched with coping and self-care. More traditional therapy techniques can be learned in longer medication management sessions. I do not provide psychotherapy alone but can provide recommendations to those who do should you be interested.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: Targeted problem solving based intervention

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: Past informs, present and how we can have a more autonomous future.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: Collaborative goals, and dialogue

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: Historically credentialed as CACD-I which I let lapse due to LPC, and then RN and AP licensing. Work with two recovery rehab facilities currently.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: My first masters program was through Pacific University who's curriculum was primarily Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Major Depressive, and Anxiety disorders like OCB, PTSD, Panic Disorder, Social Phobia to name a few.

name: Allies In Change
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: Allies in Change is a nonprofit social activist organization and counseling services center, offering individual, couples, and group therapy
ideal_client: We offer individual counseling for men and women for a variety of issues including: managing emotions such as anger, depression, stress, and anxiety; building greater intimacy and connection in relationships with others including romantic partners, family members, and friends; coping with significant changes and transitions in life related to relationships, work, family, health, and other issues; and identifying and addressing behaviors that can undermine one's happiness, such as addictions.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Allies In Change offers extensive services treating domestic violence, abuse, and anger management. We offer group therapy for survivors as well as abusive partners, which includes men's groups, women's groups, parenting groups, and an LGBTQ+ Group. We also offer DV-informed couples therapy with DV-trained experienced therapists.

name: Krista Schimmelbusch
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Partnering with clients to help create thriving and satisfying relationships and greater well being.
ideal_client: I work with individuals, couples, families, and groups within the context of their current and prior relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I primarily employ Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) and Restoration Therapy (RT) techniques. EFT has proven the most effective success rate: 90% of couples who engage in EFT significantly improve their relationship and 70-75% of such couples no longer meet criteria for relationship distress after treatment. I am EMDR trained and regularly incorporate EMDR in my practice as desired by the client. Shame and trauma can keep us stuck in negative cycles of thought and behavior. I incorporate RT to address identity and safety wounds that feed into negative cycles and keep us disconnected from ourselves and others.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in the innate power of an individual to grow and heal given the right conditions. An accepting, caring, warm and safe atmosphere helps my clients feel supported as they work through challenges and build satisfying relationships.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: • Externship in Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), London, England. • Member, International Centre for Excellence in Emotionally Focused Therapy (ICEEFT). • Member, Portland Center for Emotionally Focused Therapy (PCEFT).

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: EFT Trained, EMDR trained and licensed and marriage family therapist

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: • Level 2 Certificate in Restoration Therapy (RT). • Trained in Play Therapy and Child Parent Relationship Therapy (CPRT). • Member, American Association for Marriage, and Family Therapy (AAMFT). • Member, International Centre for Excellence in Emotionally Focused Therapy (ICEEFT). • Member, Portland Center for Emotionally Focused Therapy (PCEFT).

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: EMDRIA approved EMDR trained

name: Lynne Coon
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Helping you break out of old habits and learn to feel more hopeful and positive about yourself and your life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I'm direct and down to earth. I use Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to help you make lasting changes. I’m a problem solver who loves mysteries so I enjoy the challenge of solving the mystery of how your brain works for, and against you. You may feel depressed, or struggle with self esteem and find it difficult to love yourself, perhaps because you’re a perfectionist, or hold yourself back because you're afraid you'll fail or believe that if you do or say "bad" things it means you're bad. I help you let go of being perfect and accept who you are, tolerate failure so you can take risks and get unstuck and love who you are by accepting all of who you are. For those who feel anxious I help you tolerate uncertainty, worry less about the “what if’s” in life and trust that no matter what comes your way you have the ability to handle it. I also specialize in Obsessive Compulsive Disorder and use Exposure and Response Prevention therapy to reduce or eliminate thoughts that cause you distress.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Since I was a child I've been curious about human emotions. I've always wondered what makes people tick. I was drawn to counseling for that reason and the desire to help those in emotional pain. I realized how much we create our own suffering through our beliefs about the world. We can't know what we don't know and so take our internal beliefs as the truth. We can be afraid to tell others how we think and feel for fear of being judged. Counseling is a safe place to share your inner most fears and get a new perspective. I feel privileged when clients seek me out and trust me enough to share the things that cause them emotional pain. I received my masters in counseling at Portland State and have worked with clients from many walks of life, sexual orientations and cultures since 2004.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: Just as a hammer doesn't work for every repair, one theoretical approach may not work for every situation. I utilize aspects of Cognitive Therapy, Transactional Analysis, and IFS when appropriate, to more effectively help you make lasting change.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I've been a CBT therapist for 15 years. I believe we unintentionally create our own misery in the way we interpret the world in childhood. We take those beliefs into adulthood and don't have the awareness to realize our original thinking may have been faulty. I work to identify the ways you view the world that cause pain instead of happiness and help you adapt healthier thinking patterns.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Often you can fall into letting anxiety be in charge of you and don't realize you can be in charge of it. I provide tools to help you address your anxiety in the short term then we'll work to identify the underlying causes. Once we know the triggers we can develop a plan to reduce or eliminate them.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: I sought additional training in Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) therapy for Obsessive Compulsive Disorder. While Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is the standard for treating OCD, traditional talk therapy doesn't work. Someone with OCD can understand their thoughts logically don't make sense but that doesn't stop the obsessions. ERP along CBT works!

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Not everyone likes working with depressed people. I am skilled at identifying each persons individual causes of depression. I help them to recognize the way their brain can distort thinking so they can learn to think in more realistic and accurate ways that reduces or eliminates depression.

name: Ellie Mental Health
title: Professional Counselor
intro: At Ellie Mental Health Oregon City, we are working to transform the culture of mental health and creating a space where you can be you!
ideal_client: We work with individuals and families ages 5 and up. We work with folks facing life transitions, dealing with grief and loss, healing from trauma, and folks with anxiety, depression, and emotional dysregulation. We have therapists that specialize in trauma, addiction issues, immigration concerns, and youth and family concerns. We offer treatment in English, German, Oromo, and Amharic

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We’ve created a comfy, judgment-free zone where you can be authentic, get real about where you’re at in your mental health, and receive the compassionate care you deserve. We strive to break down treatment barriers and provide you with customized counseling services that meet your therapy needs. We offer: EMDR Individual therapy, Family therapy, and Group therapy Therapeutic Life Story Work DBT CBT Motivational Interviewing Person centered, strengths based, compassionate work with all of the individuals who walk in to our space!

approaches.Our Values as Mental Health Practitioner: We value equity, inclusion, and safety for all people.

name: Hanna Maxwell
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Now Accepting New Clients! I work with individuals (ages 15+) dealing with anxiety, perfectionism, and complex trauma.
ideal_client: Maybe you have a box in your head that's labeled "Past Stuff." You put in all the things you don't like thinking about: hurts from your childhood, the memories of things you did that play on a loop in your head if you're not careful. Lately, things have been leaking out. You feel less in control of your life, and the memories that used to stay in the box are escaping. Or maybe you know the box is there and have a sense that you should sort through it, but you're not sure about doing it alone.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am trained in Story-Informed Trauma Therapy, a framework that helps us understand how your story - from birth to the present - informs your experience of life and the choices you make. I also come from a somatic perspective, and we’ll explore how you feel emotions in your body. In therapy, I’ll support you in developing your relationship with your body, your conscious awareness, and the wisdom that you have already inside you. By learning more about ourselves, our beliefs, and the strategies we've relied on to keep ourselves safe, we can begin to build a sense of trust in our selves and our bodies. This process isn't always easy or linear, and my role is to support you by providing presence and a safe relationship where change can occur. I believe you have immense value and a story that is waiting to unfold. It would be an honor and a privilege to sit with you in this next chapter of your life.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: Maybe you've thought about going to counseling but then paused because of thoughts like, "But my childhood wasn't that bad. Other people had it worse." Or you might feel that overall, life is going pretty well, even if you dealt with difficult things in the past. Somehow though, you still have symptoms that bother you - restlessness, difficulty in relationships, constant worry, periods of low mood and lack of motivation - and you might not know why. I love to help people not only resolve those symptoms, but help them understand where they come from. The comparison game of "who had it worse" doesn't have to prevent you from tending to the things in your life that were painful. I believe that it's important to understand yourself and your story so that you can experience health to the fullest.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: While anxiety is a normal part of life, being stuck in a pattern of constant worry, chronic tension, and stress can significantly impact you and the way you live your life. Many people have experienced more anxiety as the result of the pandemic and current world events, so you are not alone! We’ll look at how anxiety is working to protect you, your body, and the things you care about. We will work to learn new coping skills and different ways to tend to those anxious thoughts and sensations.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma occurs when our bodies, brains, and nervous systems don’t have enough resources to cope with what is happening to us. This could be a singular event – for example, being in a car accident - but it can also result from things like a challenging childhood, emotional neglect, or an abusive relationship. Your body may be carrying these past experiences, even if you hadn’t thought of them as traumatic. We'll approach these sensations together so you can begin to experience more freedom.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Perhaps you’re going through a faith change or deconstructing the belief systems you grew up in. Maybe you’ve recently left a religious community or are in the process of trying to decide whether or not to stay. Going through a major shift can reach far beyond where and how you choose to engage with spirituality; it can impact relationships with family and friends, your identity, even your vocation. We can create a place that’s safe for you to explore questions, doubts, and religious trauma.

name: Cherrie Mae Padua
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Having the courage to make changes in our lives can be a stressful time. I am here to support and encourage you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe finding the right therapist is a key part of having a successful and positive therapeutic experience. As a therapist, my approach is warm, honest, and encouraging. I utilize various evidence-based techniques but often draw from Narrative Therapy, CBT, and mindfulness techniques. I tailor my approach to meet your specific needs and work collaboratively to overcome roadblocks in order to move towards growth.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe everyone has the ability to reach their full potential. Through therapy we can gain a better understanding of our lived experiences, discover new parts of ourselves, and gain skills to promote conscious change to reach our goals. We all struggle, but we don’t have to do it alone.

name: Ashley Parkinson
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a strengths-based therapist who helps people manage stress, life transitions, substance use, anxiety, depression, and relationships.
ideal_client: Life can be deeply rewarding, but it can also feel like a never-ending pile of stress. You may be navigating relationships, career and caregiving responsibilities, finances, and health issues—all that in addition to a pandemic. You may notice that your tools for managing stress (alcohol, food, pushing yourself to the max) aren’t really cutting it anymore and may even be causing harm. The pressure can feel overwhelming. I"m here to support you in your search for more peace and joy in your life.

approaches.My Background and Approach: As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) and Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor (CADC-I), I practice therapy from a strengths-based perspective, meaning that I work with my clients to understand what strong, natural skills and talents they possess that can be used as launching points to tackle issues causing hardship in their lives. I personalize therapy to meet the needs of my clients, have deep respect for clients’ rights, and work to build a strong therapeutic alliance. I strive to be a genuine, warm, non-judgmental therapist, committed to creating a safe space for people to share their concerns.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I am a parent, daughter, sister, spouse, nature lover, and therapist. I use she/her/hers pronouns. I am a white, cisgender, heterosexual, middle-aged, body positive woman. I am a lifelong learner, read novels and therapy books for fun, love hiking, skiing and birdwatching, and believe in doing the same personal "work" that I support my clients in doing for themselves. I came to the field of social work 20 years ago and since that time have been privileged to work with people across the lifespan and from a wide variety of walks of life. While so many of our challenges are universal, I recognize that systems of oppression affect us each differently, creating privilege for some while making healthcare harder to access for others. I welcome people of all cultures, races, sizes, abilities, religions, sexual orientations, and gender identities in my counseling practice.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I rely heavily on a mindfulness-based approach in therapy to help clients train attention to the present moment (body sensations, emotions, thoughts) with compassion and non-judgment. Mindfulness-based practice can be very helpful in reducing stress, anxiety, depression and in treating eating and body image concerns as well as issues with substance use and addiction.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: I enjoy supporting people through life transitions, as these can be times of great growth and learning (as well as challenge and exhaustion). I have experience working with college students in "quarter-life crisis," as well as people facing "mid-life overwhelm" as they manage relationships, career, health, and caregiving of children and elders. Although stress is a normal part of big life changes, having support during difficult times can reduce symptoms and prevent further complications.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: I work with body image issues from a body positive, HAES (Health at Every Size) perspective, and from my own lived experience as someone who has learned to see beyond diet and fat-hating culture to a place of body acceptance and respect. I support my clients wherever they are in their relationships with their bodies through the principles of Intuitive Eating and Be Nourished's "Body Trust" model. I employ Motivational Interviewing to help people identify personal values and goals toward change.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Our relationships are the heart and soul of our lives--they often are what makes us get out of bed in the morning, and what gives us reason to grow, learn, and become better people. When our relationships aren't working, or when they are abusive, destructive, or harmful, we have difficulty functioning well in other areas of our lives. I support my clients in working toward healthy relationships through identifying the longstanding patterns that have become unseen obstacles to change.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Sometimes, even when we have it "all together on the outside," we secretly harbor feelings of dislike toward ourselves or feel like we are not valuable. Low self-worth often starts in childhood, or begins when someone experiences a harmful relationship or traumatic incidence. I support clients in boosting self-worth by exploring longstanding patterns of thought, feeling and behavior, and through mindfulness practice, boundary-setting, communication skills, and building on natural strengths.

specialities.name: Early Recovery
specialities.description: I am a Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor (CADC-I) and spent several years working in community addictions facilities focused on early recovery. I am knowledgeable about 12-Step, SMART Recovery, harm-reduction, and other recovery models. I support people in early recovery through a strong therapeutic alliance, shame reduction, encouragement, relapse planning, and referrals to higher levels of care as needed. I employ Motivational Interviewing to help people find internal motivation to change.

name: Kaden Winterkorn
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I offer support groups and individual counseling to the trans and non-binary community in Portland.
ideal_client: I love working with clients who are ready for change and want support in the process of transition– into new identities, relationships, careers, and ways of relating to themselves and others. Trans individuals face unique challenges, and we also have unique opportunities for joy, self-actualization, deep compassion and self-love as we unfold our identities and seek to live authentic lives.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Everyone’s path of healing and growth is unique; I work together with my clients to find an approach that feels right for them, honoring their wisdom, strengths, and preferences. My style is integrative– drawing from narrative therapy, IFS, mindfulness, and self-compassion practices. I meet my clients with deep respect for their process and approach our work together with creativity, curiosity, warmth, and an open heart. At the core of my practice is developing strong and trusting relationships with clients to guide the work we do together.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I believe we all have intrinsic wisdom about ourselves and our life paths; counseling can be a way to come home to that wisdom. In addition to individual counseling, I offer support groups for the trans & non-binary community. These groups are spaces for folks to build community, share wisdom and support, and find affirmation and sense of belonging with each other. If you would like to learn more, I’d love to hear from you.

name: Kelly Hubert
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer therapy for adults seeking support with depression, anxiety, relationships, stress, grief, perinatal mood, and parenting.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic style integrates psychodynamic understanding with relationship-based techniques, supported by evidence-based practices like Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT). I believe that exploring how past experiences shape current patterns can create meaningful insights that lead to lasting change. In our sessions, you'll find a nonjudgmental space where you can safely navigate difficult emotions while discovering pathways to healing and growth. I take pleasure in helping clients develop deeper self-compassion and practical strategies for creating a life aligned with their core values and goals.

name: Stephanie Bauer
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Helping women, therapists, and young adults as they handle the complexities of life.
ideal_client: I have a compassion for working with people who are ready to see change in their life. I have a passion for working with therapists and therapists in training. I enjoy working with women and finding boundaries, issues with hormonal imbalances, confidence, and anxiety to help find your best self. I think it is important to find a trusting connection in therapy that combines new challenges with growth and change. Penelope, my therapy dog, is excited to join our sessions!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use an eclectic approach to therapy including motivational interviewing, CBT, trauma based therapy, solution focused therapy, emotion focused therapy, and codependency individual and group therapy. I have a commitment to create a safe environment that fosters the growth of well-being of others in session. I enjoy working with clients to help cultivate the understanding that progress takes place in and out of session and is not always linear.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: Therapy for women: Specialities include codependency, depression, anxiety, grief, trauma, stress management, relationship and communication issues, spirituality issues, past trauma, sexuality, social justice, and family issues. I enjoy working with women on hormonal issues, endometriosis/PCOS support, fertility issues, postpartum, body image, aging, postpartum, boundaries,, sex and intimacy, finding outside providers/testing to help meet your needs. Therapy for therapists: It is very important that we take care of ourselves as mental health providers. Whether you are a student completing a graduate program or an established therapist, it is never too early or late to have additional support, grow, or meet goals. Therapy for young adults: I specialize in therapy for young adults (over 21). We can work together on transitioning into adulthood, life goals, college transitions, jobs, sex and relationships, impacts of social media, living with others.

name: Kelly Sullivan
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I appreciate the range of what people are looking for in therapy and work with individuals and couples using kindness, curiosity and humor.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My goal is to encourage people to reflect about themselves (their thoughts and their bodies), their experiences and their relationships using compassion, curiosity, and humor. My approach employs family systems, mindfulness, and interpersonal neurobiology. I am interested in building on people's strengths, and supporting them as they transform their reflections into different ways to navigate the world and their relationships.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker, with a Masters in Social Work from Portland State University. I have worked with people in private practice, agency, hospitals, and shelter environments. Over the years, I have gained the most experience in issues related to pregnancy, post-partum, adoption, infertility, bereavement and cancer diagnosis and survivorship. However, I have also worked with individuals and couples experiencing life transitions, overwhelming workplace stress, trauma, and relationship issues.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am certified in EMDR and have years of experience using EMDR with clients to treat PTSD and complex trauma.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: People that surrounded us during our childhood and youth influence our perceptions and relationships as do our early romantic relationships. I think of the current challenges a person faces within a framework of their past in order to help them consider different ways to be in the present.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: The post-partum period challenges people’s views of themselves, their careers, their relationships, and who they want to be as a parent. And all on very little sleep. I have received extensive training in pregnancy and postpartum mental health and worked in a hospital birthing center and NICU.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: In my private practice and in my work at a hospital birth center, I have witnessed a wide range of mental health, relationship, and health related issues that people can experience during pregnancy. This awareness informs my work around pregnancy as does the importance of helping people create space and energy for the upcoming labor and delivery and the ensuing adjustment.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I work with women and couples experiencing issues with infertility, pregnancy, pregnancy loss, post-partum adjustment and menopause. These experiences can change fundamental aspects of identity. They are times of culturally informed and biological transitions and can be full of overwhelming challenges. They can also provide a unique motivation for shifting old perspectives.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: While we will all experience losses in our life, each person's story is unique. I provide context and connection to other's experiences, while providing space to each person as they determine their own meaning and direction after loss. My work has spanned supporting people through pregnancy loss, the loss of a child and the death of a life partner.

name: Alexandra Leichter LCSW, LICSW, MSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: What would it be like if you finally felt heard? I'm a relationship & communication expert. I also specialize in neurodiverse couples.
ideal_client: Are you ready to create an intentional life path - moving in together or getting married? (Pre-marital Coaching) Are you and your partner miscommunicating, not having fun, wanting to make changes in your relationship? (Relationship Counseling) Are you deciding if you want to stay or if you want to go in your relationship? Do you feel stuck in indecision? (Discernment type services) Do you or your partner experience processing differences (AHDH, ASD)? Reach out to me!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am eclectic in my approach - I am Gottman Level One certified and PrePare Enrich certified (premarital services). I am a Certified ND Compass therapist - this is specific to those couples who are neurodiverse. I am also an ADHD Certified Clinical Services Provider. My main focus is helping people tell their truth, what it is they are scared to admit to themselves and others, in a safe, supportive way.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker in the states of Oregon and California and a Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker in the state of Washington. I have been in couples counseling myself and this is why I am passionate about what I do: I know it works. Call me, I offer free phone consultations.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: Prepare Enrich Pre-Marital Counseling Certified Facilitator: This is a leading relationship program, built on a solid research foundation. It is custom tailored to for each couple and provides exercises to build relationship skills. This is what I consider a preventative coaching process where I help couples focus on discussing important things prior to moving in together, marrying or choosing to partner with one another.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I have worked with couples throughout my career. I have additional training in Gottman and am certified in ND Compass (specific to mixed Neuro Type couples). I am also an ADHD Certified Clinical Services Provider.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: There are many theories and types of therapy that can be used when working with couples. I find that no two couples are a like, nor or the two individuals within that couple alike. I will assess your specific needs and will draw from my experience and schooling to not only help explain why you are in your current set of circumstances, but also how we can go about addressing your needs.

specialities.name: Premarital Counseling
specialities.description: Prepare Enrich Pre-Marital Counseling Certified Facilitator: This is a leading relationship program, built on a solid research foundation. It is custom tailored to for each couple and provides exercises to build relationship skills. I provide BOTH non-religious and religious based counseling. I am also happy to provide non Prepare Enrich premarital counseling.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I am an ADHD Certified Clinical Services Provider - I provide services both to individuals with a diagnosis or who think they might have a diagnosis of ADHD and/or those who are partnered with someone who has or possibly has this diagnosis. The majority of my focus in this area is the way ADHD impacts relationships, communication, misunderstandings and education so you can better understand yourself or your partner.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have worked with couples and families throughout my career. I have experience working with couples who are in the midst of marital issues, and general problem solving for on-going concerns and with those who want to better understand one another but are not in any type of crisis. I have additional training in Gottman therapy and also a certification in ND (NeuroDiverse) Compass - a type of relationship therapy that is focused on working with mixed Neuro Type couples.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Your life looks delightful but it’s still deeply unfulfilling. You’ve had enough of standing in your own way & giving too much power to what others think. You have bold dreams & desires but seek clarification & encouragement to achieve them. You want to increase your self-esteem to lead to better relationships & career choices as they currently don't feel in alignment with your needs, values, or overall satisfaction. Sometimes you feel outwardly self-confident but internally doubt yourself.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: More often than not people reach out to me because they are having communication issues within their relationship. Miscommunication is usually the result of misinterpreting what your partner has said, having different communication styles and the way our brains take in and process the information during that communication. I help clients identify the patterns in their relationships and better understand one another - I provide education, skills and a guidance on how to be open and honest.

name: Danielle Davis
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I use somatic, mindful, experiential, and attachment-focused approaches to support clients in healing trauma & re-finding home within.
ideal_client: I work best with adult + adolescent individuals who feel ready to work with their bodies / nervous systems towards healing trauma, who are excited by the idea of moving towards more easeful embodiment, and are perhaps specifically looking for a somatic, mindfulness-based approach to therapy. I do also adore working with my beloved LGBTQIA+ community!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach is organized by a belief that our bodies hold the secrets of our wounds as well as the intrinsic wisdom to heal them. At this site of embodiment, profound transformation naturally occurs: of wounding into self-knowing, of constriction into aliveness, of pain into resource. I practice trauma-informed, mindfulness-based and attachment-focused somatic therapy which invites you to slow way down & bring curious attention to the fabric of your inner world. Practicing non-judgmental attention to your moment-to-moment experience within the context of a safe and supportive relationship allows us to collaboratively study how your particular system organizes experience & to become aware of the patterns in operation & their origins. Throughout this map-making process, your system will organically show us what it needs in order to process and repair places of pain and stuckness. With kiddos, I use sand tray and expressive arts therapies, + family sessions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I work from a systems perspective that understands our individual self as being situated within & impacted by a nest of wider systems - generational, familial, societal, & global. These contexts - many of which have taken on oppressive qualities via the vehicles of settler colonialism, racism, cis-hetero patriarchy, & late-capitalism - impact us and the families we are embedded within profoundly; they inform how we experience ourselves in the world, imprinting our brains and our bodies, shaping us in often deeply unconscious ways. When we slow down and bring mindful, non-judgemental awareness to our here-and-now experience, subconscious patterns begin to reveal themselves, giving us the possibility to cultivate understanding, nourishment, resilience, and ultimately, transformation.

name: Jeremy Jones
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am accepting new clients to my telehealth private practice, at this time.
ideal_client: I work with those seeking freedom from compulsions, self-destruction, and limiting beliefs, helping them find self-acceptance and healthy coping skills. In therapy, we develop protective supports to replace challenging behaviors with functional, positive behavior. My practice offers reliable, effective care that's easy to engage with.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In the last 6 years, I've helped people cope with trauma, psychosis, depression, anxiety, health issues, and addiction. I take a holistic approach that considers all aspects of well-being, such as social, occupational, environmental, physical, intellectual, spiritual, and emotional. Through therapy, we will build protective supports and positive behaviors. I'm LGBTQIA+ affirming and committed to providing a safe, equitable space.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (OR License #C5359) registered with the O.B.L.P.C.T. I hold an MA in Applied Psychological Science from Pacific University. I worked as substance use disorder counselor with Cascadia Behavioral Healthcare. Up until recently I held employment as a dual diagnosis clinical supervisor with Columbia Community Mental Health. From my last two work placements I met the requirements to obtain my Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor II (Certification #19-09-24) registered with M.H.A.C.B.O. Finally, I have Board Certified-TeleMental Health Provider credential which identifies those professionals who are uniquely trained in best practices for delivering traditional behavioral healthcare through technological means. BC-TMH credential holders have met nationally established telemental health criteria.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: My educational focus on health psychology and the incorporation of my wellness approach has given me both the ability and resources to effectively work from a 'dimensional' approach in identifying the factors affecting the presenting issue.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: Because both the Holistic, Cognitive Behavioral, and integrated approach system I utilize-exploring how certain thoughts, behaviors, or emotions develop over a lifespan is a primary function in making lasting change.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I have educational and practical experience in providing CBT interventions for both individual and group settings for both residential and outpatient treatment.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Suicide for males is on the rise significantly in the United States. This has been related to the struggle of males being able to reach out for help and support due to barriers related to social stigma or previously held notions about the counseling process. I work to normalize and validate male struggles and toxic male messages through all aspects of treatment.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Mental health and addiction due to typically occur as distinct issues, and my practice works to ensure that we are examining and incorporating the relationship between mental health and substance use is it relates to the presenting issue.

specialities.name: Schizophrenia
specialities.description: I have significant experience in working with individuals with psychosis diagnoses in both a residential and outpatient setting.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Due to the interrelationship between mental health, substance use, and self-esteem-this is a primary objective of my practice to work on improving along with finding stability/control of internal processes.

specialities.name: Bipolar
specialities.description: I have extensive work in treating individuals who have recently been diagnosed with this disorder in understanding what the symptoms are, and how to best manage them in tandem with medications and therapy.

name: Angie Martin
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Experienced therapist who supports you in navigating what life gives you.
ideal_client: I help support adults who are experiencing depression, anxiety, relationship concerns, poor body image, ADHD and developmental and relational trauma. I help them recognize unhelpful patterns in their life and support them in building acceptance, confidence and peace. My clients seek to increase flexibility around rigid thinking patterns and are curious how to improve their quality of life, honor emotions and nurture healthy relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work to create a space that is welcoming, compassionate and affirming. I will approach you with a warm, non-judgmental stance and utilize the best therapeutic intervention that meets your needs. I am active in the process and provide modalities such as psychodynamic, narrative therapy and CBT. I have learned the value of practicing compassion while challenging clients to look internally and lead a life that nurtures well-being. Also, I feel a little humor goes a long way.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe mental health is a key component to healthcare. Though I have practiced therapy for over a decade, the client is the arbiter and authority of their well-being. I am happy to be a part of this journey with all clients. People don’t need to have a mental health disorder to seek therapy. Sometimes we just need someone to listen and offer extra support through life’s transitions and challenges.

name: Tara Rose
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My approach to therapy is rooted in liberation and I welcome those who are seeking an affirming, dedicated, and compassionate provider.
ideal_client: My primary area of focus is working with adults needing support with substance use, ADHD, anxiety, depression, and trauma who are trying to navigate a world that doesn't always feel safe. Many of my clients are members of the LGBTQ community, but I welcome anyone who resonates with what I have to offer.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I practice from a trauma informed, humanistic, anti-oppressive, and strengths-based framework. I also draw from parts/systems work, relational, and narratives therapies and EMDR. I am committed to providing gender and identity affirming care that allows for safe exploration to become closer to your true self. I also have a strong focus in trauma recovery and how the brain and nervous system have learned to adapt to keep you safe. We will connect about how your experiences have shaped thoughts about yourself, behaviors, and emotions, and how these create barriers for the goals you have in your life. We will also explore and consider the impacts of systemic oppression on your identity and sense of self. I take a non-pathologizing approach to working my clients, with a particular focus on those with marginalized identities. I wholeheartedly believe in your ability to be more connected with yourself and am excited to be with you on your journey.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I appreciate doing deeper work with clients and building a strong connection within the therapeutic relationship. Clients seeking a warm, compassionate, and patient therapist, will be a good fit for me. I also value incorporating humor and prioritize healthy boundaries. If you are looking to prioritize skill building and a therapist that is really direct we probably won’t be the best match. I wholeheartedly believe in your ability to be more connected with yourself and am excited to be with you on your journey.

name: Sophie Toolanen
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I specialize in deepening insight into the self, your relationships, healing from trauma, and effectively managing emotions and stress
ideal_client: Are you curious about how you came to think, feel, and act the way that you do? Do you struggle with having compassion for, or loving, yourself? Do you ever wonder why you just can't seem to relax, or trust yourself or others, the way others can? Do you often feel as though you are not enough, that you are unloveable, unworthy, shameful, or bad deep down? These are some of the questions that I can help you answer and some of the things we can change, should you want to.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is mostly insight oriented, but can also be solution focused, depending on your preference. In conjunction with classic "talk therapy", I like to utilize EMDR, DBT, and IFS strategies to resolve defenses, "stuckness", interpersonal difficulties, volatile emotions, and negative self-talk... much of which is often a result of unprocessed trauma from the past. I focus on identifying how your past influences your present and finding solutions for overcoming obstacles. I think of myself as the assistant detective on a case, where you are the lead, and your life is the case. * Please note that I am only working with adults at this time.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: - I will not judge you negatively by what you share with me, no matter how "ugly" (a judgment by the way) the truth sometimes is.
