approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) in Oregon and Texas, a Licensed Mental Health Counselor (LMHC) in Washington, a Licensed Professional Clinical Counselor (LPCC) in New Mexico, and a Licensed Clinical Professional Counselor (LCPC) in Montana. I have two Master’s degrees, one in Molecular Biology and one in Professional Mental Health Counseling. I am also a certified Ayurvedic Practitioner I integrate Ayurvedic Psychology into my therapeutic approach. I am committed to a life-long process of learning, and strive to work from a place of cultural humility to increase my awareness, knowledge and skills both personally and professionally. I have a special interest in working with other healthcare professionals, including doctors and other psychotherapists, as well as college students and clients healing from complex trauma.

specialities.name: Integral Therapy
specialities.description: My therapeutic style is a trauma and neurobiologically-informed, integrative approach to psychotherapy that emphasizes the importance of body, mind, and spirit in holistically treating underlying psychological and/or emotional imbalances and maintaining nervous system regulation.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I have been studying and applying psychodynamic principals in my clinical work since 2011. I also completed 2.5 years of clinical internship training with a supervisor trained in Control Mastery Theory, an integrated cross-theoretical cognitive-psychodynamic-relational theory.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: As an Ayurvedic Practitioner, I use a holistic style of assessment and treatment that acknowledges the importance of integrating body, mind, and spirit. This includes understanding how your unique physical and mental constitutions interact with the specific environmental and relational contexts in your life.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have a deep understanding of the impact of stress and trauma on nervous system dysregulation and mental/emotional well-being. I have studied various neurobiologically-informed trauma approaches such as Interpersonal Neurobiology, Control Mastery Theory and the work of Pete Walker. I have a special interest complex trauma, a form of prolonged/cumulative trauma that develops within interpersonal relationships, often associated with neglect and/or adverse childhood experiences.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: As an Ayurvedic practitioner, I have extensive knowledge of the mind-body connection. I can help you identify potential mental and emotional sources that may be contributing to your physical symptoms, including functional somatic symptoms. I also have a special interest in the psychosocial factors that are affected by living with gastrointestinal disorders, such as IBS and SIBO.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Using the principles of Ayurvedic psychology can assist in maintaining mental and emotional balance and well-being through understanding your unique psychological constitution in the context of your environment, as well as strengthening your ability to digest and integrate your life experiences.

name: Sara Rosenau
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: My intention is to support your growth by offering a non-judgemental environment for you to be exactly where you are right now.
ideal_client: My ideal client is anyone who is willing to show up for the journey. I'm here to be on the journey with you. I can help with accessing and naming feelings, working with limiting beliefs, setting boundaries and communicating needs, learning self-love and self-support, developing secure attachments in relationships, exploring more freeing sexual expression and practice, aligning more deeply with values, processing grief and loss, healing from religious trauma, finding new spiritual meaning.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist, I begin with the understanding that you are the expert of your own life and you have inner knowledge and capacity for healing. My intention is to support your growth by offering a non-judgemental and supportive environment for you to be exactly where you are right now. I will hold space for you to be with your pain, tell the truth about what’s wrong, explore limiting beliefs, find new insight, and make courageous shifts towards healing and deepening purpose. Through therapy, I hope you can begin to express your “full and free human-beingness.” My approach is relational and centered in your strengths and resilience. I tailor my approach to each individual. I specifically work with the mind-body connection and am trained to introduce mindfulness into sessions in a way that gently guides you to pay attention to the body’s signals to deepen your understanding of your struggles. Just having a willingness to be curious in self-exploration is a good place to begin.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I am a member of the LGBTIQ community. I am kink/poly aware and sex positive. I actively examine my privilege and seek to align my practice to support the thriving of all individuals, especially those who are marginalized by the dominant culture in areas of race, gender expression, and disability. I have deep values in social justice and volunteered my skills for Black Lives Matter and other social movements for liberation.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I am trained in Hakomi Mindful Somatic Psychotherapy (Level One). Hakomi understands that change comes not from our effort, but from our awareness. Hakomi uses mindfulness—a state of relaxed, nonjudgmental awareness–to study, activate, and directly experience the root causes underlying our habitual feelings, thoughts and behavior.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Particularly working with those diagnosed as adults. Support self-understanding, undoing shame, and behavioral shifts

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Working with mindfulness, increasing awareness of activation, and using the body as teacher and tool for self-regulation and soothing

name: Robin Friedman, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I enjoy empowering and supporting individuals on their path of personal growth, healing, life challenges and transitions, & wholeness.
ideal_client: Please check out my website at www.robinfriedmantherapy.com. My clients are individual adults who are willing and interested in making lasting positive change in their lives. I am licensed in both Oregon L5164 and Washington State LW61109761.

approaches.My Background: I draw from many disciplines and personal life experience. My formal education includes a BFA from Colorado State University and teacher education from University of California at San Diego. I earned my MSW from the University of Utah in 2004. I completed a certificate program in Person Centered Expressive Arts Therapy and level 1 and 2 training in EMDR Therapy through EMDRIA. Since 2000, I have attended many professional trainings and workshops including Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), trauma therapy, mindfulness and somatic based psychotherapy, and sexual assault crisis intervention training. I regularly attend conferences, professional trainings, seminars and ongoing peer consultation. Clinical Experience: Therapist since 2003, Private Practice since 2006, Supervisor for MSW interns and CSWA's since 2008, Senior Therapist at a Rape Recovery Center 4.5 years, Therapist at an outpatient adult substance abuse treatment center. As well as varied and wide life experience.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Therapy is a process and can help calm the storm, allowing room for self discovery, and positive change. Whether we are working long or short-term, we will allow each session to move in the direction needed at that time. My style is to be honest, accepting, respectful, spontaneous, intelligent, creative, and compassionate. You will have full permission to be and express all of who you are. I work from a client-centered perspective and a social justice lens. I believe each person has within them the ability to heal, and is ultimately the expert on their own lives. My role is to collaborate with you on the journey of healing, self expression, and identifying and honoring your unique strengths. As your witness, I will offer my presence, knowledge, and deep listening, as well as provide you with experiences and skills aimed at assisting you in healing, growth, and living in alignment with your self-identified values. In addition, I use the creative process whenever possible.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR Therapy stands for Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing. Level 1 and 2 trained with over 10 years experience. I very much enjoy this approach and use it often with clients in my practice.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I use Focusing and somatic based techniques to help individuals experience, except and heal emotions in the body. I also use mindfulness as a way become more centered and present, reducing anxiety and learning ways to get unhooked from unhelpful thoughts. I also offer ACT (acceptance and commitment therapy) skills for managing and unhelpful intrusive thoughts, learning to identify, be with and move through challenging. emotions, and shift in the direction of self identified values.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I come from a humsnistic and person centered perspective. Celebrating each persons capacity to heal and I honor each person with unconditional positive regard. Non-pathologizing feminist Multi-cultural, social justice approach.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have many years of experience effectively helping those who suffer from Post Traumatic Stress and complex trauma. I use a variety of aproaches including mindfulness, EMDR Therapy, art, and somatic approaches.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Using mindfulness , acceptance and commitment therapy, EMDR to treat anxiety

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I use expressive arts, mindfulness, person centered therapy, EMDR, and talk therapy to reduce symptoms of depression.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I've worked for many years with the LGBTQ+ population. I provide a safe, open and affirming environment for those who are coming to therapy because of stressors or challenges me related to gender or sexual identity, or who are working to understand their identity. I also provide a safe place for those who identify as LGBTQ+ or other identities who want to focus on other areas, but want be assured they have a safe place to be themselves and feel understood.

specialities.name: Sexual Abuse
specialities.description: I have worked directly with sexual able/assault survivors of all genders for many years including over 4 years as a therapist at a Rape Recovery Center. I work with adults who are survivors of any kind of sexual and physical abuse trauma from ongoing childhood abuse to single incident rape or other sexual violence.

name: Alana Harris
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor with 10 years of experience providing compassionate and supportive evidence based treatments.
ideal_client: My therapeutic approach integrates process based, behavioral, and mindfulness based techniques to promote a stronger sense of self while building skills to improve quality of life. I embrace acceptance and change strategies to build self-compassion while facilitating meaningful change. I work well with motivated young adults, adults, and LGBTQ individuals experiencing anxiety, depression, life stressors, interpersonal/relationship conflict, emotional dysregulation, and self-esteem issues.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe suffering is an aspect of human nature and everyone has the innate ability to tolerate and grow through difficult times, to find meaning and purpose in life. Sometimes we have to enter the paradox of pain to get relief from the pain itself. I have experience in community based mental health and have been intensively trained in mindfulness based stress reduction, CBT and DBT evidenced based treatment modalities. Prior to opening my own practice I was a DBT therapist for 3 years at Portland DBT Institute. Although I weave DBT skills into my practice, I value process based approaches as well as mindfulness and self-compassion work. My goal is to help plant seeds of self-awareness to propel perspective, introspection, agency and self-fulfillment. Every individual is unique and I tend to tailor client-centered relational and behavioral skill building techniques. With my approach I tend to work best with folks who are motivated and may want to do intentional work.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Human behavior is a fascinating thing. We hold a lot of truths about ourselves, sometimes opposing truths that coexist. We also have an innate ability to cultivate resiliency and develop new neural circuits in our brain chemistry. We can rewire faulty thinking patterns that for so long have influenced our sense of self and the ways we experience relationships and the world around us. If this feels like a journey you'd like to explore, feel free to reach out. A little about me, I live in SE Portland with my partner and our pup Doc. In my free time I you can find me in my garden, camping, biking, climbing, skiing and all the outdoor pursuits the PNW has to offer. Music has saved me many of times so you may find me bouncing around to shows and concerts. https://www.inwardcounselingllc.com/

name: Megan Maxwell
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Play-Therapy | Parenting Support | Individuals | Relationships Encouraging growth through acceptance, awareness, insight, and choice.
ideal_client: My clients include children, parents, families, relationships, and individuals across the lifespan. I support children and parents struggling with behavioral issues, explosive emotions, and navigating the hard work of childhood. I work with relationships addressing conflict due to communication and mismatched expectations. I help individuals managing anxiety, depression, self-image, trauma, and whose history holds them back from achieving the future they want.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapy work comes from a relational perspective that encourages growth through insight, self-acceptance, and choice. At its heart, all of my work is client-centered and built on a supportive therapeutic relationship. My approach is integrative and developmentally responsive to the needs of the client. I engage children in Child Centered Play Therapy. With relationships and adults, I go into deeper work using a Contemporary Gestalt approach. I believe that all people have the innate ability to self-regulate and meet our own needs in relationship with others. We adapt creatively to do the best we can with the tools we have and the circumstances we encounter. However, over the course of our lives we learn that some needs should not be expressed, or will not be met. My focus in helping is to bring awareness to unmet needs, insight into what gets in the way of us meeting them, and the ability to make a choice for the future.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Over fifteen years as a classroom teacher, I developed a strong understanding of the unique struggles and pressures faced by children and parents today. I found a passion for supporting children and parents with emotional and behavioral challenges with a strengths based approach. In becoming a counselor I have discovered that the challenges we face and lessons we learn in childhood follow us into our adult relationships and lives. These can be lessons we learn from our families of origin, from our community, or from society at large in relation to our identities and the ways that we move in the world. I believe in working with children and parents to build strong foundations for the future, as well as working with adult relationships and individuals to address the issues that arise from our past in order to move forward.

name: Kat Cordova Jimenez
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a licensed therapist working with children, adults, and families with 12 years experience. Clients tell me they feel I really care.
ideal_client: My clients want to make changes and gain insight about themselves. They may be dealing with depression, anxiety, or the impact of trauma and want new ways to cope. My clients might be feeling stuck or stressed out and need some support to make changes. My clients may have decided they want to change their relationship with substances. My clients may also be family members who want to work together to improve their communication, relationship, or maybe even repair harm that was done.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer compassionate and evidence-based therapy for you. My approach uses motivational interviewing, mindfulness techniques, and narrative work to help you gain the motivation and insight to make changes to improve your health and wellness. I have training in Collaborative Problem Solving, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy. I love to use art, play, and movement in my sessions. As we meet virtually or in person we will work together to develop strategies that empower you, enhance your resilience, and help you meet your goals. I believe that everyone has the answers they’re looking for and the capacity for change. My job is to help uncover those answers and build motivation for change so the new pieces of you can root and thrive.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe for us to see true mental health and wellness we need to change the systems around us to be focused on the needs of people over profit for the few. I chose to get into social work because of the focus on social justice in the field. I have participated in community efforts and organized events to advance racial justice and equity, increase police accountability, advocate for economic and ecological justice, protest wars abroad, and decriminalize immigrants in our community. My favorite quote is from Aboriginal activist Lilla Watson: "If you have come to help me you are wasting your time. If you have come because your liberation is bound up with mine, then let us work together."

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: I spent over a year in training and consultation honing motivational interviewing skills. This style of therapy is a way of helping you listen to yourself, clarify your own values and wants, and increase your own internal motivation to make changes to improve your mental wellness.

name: Andrew Rose
title: Professional Counselor
intro: I practice existential and talk-oriented therapy. My expertise is in working with people with chronic illnesses and their families.
ideal_client: Many of my patients experience extreme emotional states. This can be related to mental health issues, but also to parts of daily life that are outside of our control. I've found that encouraging self-compassion and mindfulness are helpful ways to allow greater flexibility and soothing. This is combined with traditional talk therapy techniques focused on long-term growth and understanding of oneself and what is all around us.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I practice depth psychology, meaning I believe that healing can only come about when we begin to understand the root causes of symptoms. We are all living in a world defined by the people around us, yet also by our absolute individuality and freedom of choice. Together with my patients, we work to understand how one’s view of reality colors other parts one’s life, including affect and mood. Rather than try to talk patients out of these feelings, I prefer to work on understanding how one’s place in existence can become such that one’s days become darker and the will to live in the world and the search for joy seem meaningless. To me, meaning is essential for any successful therapy. We have to find, through our choices and our view of reality, a way toward meaning. Meaning cannot be bestowed on you, and it must be reinvigorated regularly, but it is the most satisfying part of being alive.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: The first principle I rely on as a therapist is that of autonomy. Ultimately, it is the patient’s decision how much they want to share in therapy, or if they even wish to continue seeing a clinician. I also strongly value ethics. Most therapists take their ethical responsibilities seriously, but, regrettably not all. Confidentiality is more than the black-and-white text of HIPAA; it is a sacred trust. Patients must be able to trust that their clinician will withhold personal opinions and always offer unconditional positive regard. As therapists, we cannot make decisions for you, but helping you understand the impact of a decision and what is really at stake is a shared goal.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: My caseload is composed almost entirely of people suffering from chronic illness. I also lead a weekly group, sponsored and endorsed by the MS Society of Portland, designed to teach mindful self-compassion to partners and loved ones of people with multiple sclerosis.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: Part of the focus of my practice is with the families of those who are chronically ill. It is a huge burden—no matter how willing one is, and how much they want to care for their loved ones—to be responsible for someone’s day-to-day care. I try to teach partners and caregivers meditation techniques and self-compassion, both of which are evidence based and I have found them to be exceptionally helpful to many patients.

specialities.name: Family Caregiving
specialities.description: As part of my work with caregivers and partners of people with chronic illness, I have developed a great deal of experience navigating the logistical and interpersonal demands of being a caregiver.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I have worked with many transgender and gender questioning patients. I am trans-competent, highly sensitive to the importance of gender reaffirmation, and, as a member of the queer community myself, deeply invested in the rights and needs of the trans community.

name: Lauren Hisada
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Offering nature-based counseling to children & adults via OHP CareOregon & Self Pay. Accepting in-office, virtual & walk-and-talk clients.
ideal_client: Welcome! As an LPC and Registered Horticultural Therapist (HTR), I support children and adults (ages 10+) in navigating a range of challenges, including struggles with focus and overwhelm, self-worth and identity development, anxiety, trauma, and life transitions. Drawing on specialized training in DBT and Ecotherapy, I take a collaborative and experiential approach, helping clients to identify and shift unwanted patterns in emotional response, relationships, and behaviors.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Depending on your unique circumstances and needs, sessions may be offered through an online, in-office, walk-and-talk, or hybrid format. For clients who are interested in supplementing their treatment with horticultural therapy, we can work with plants in-office, virtually, or at local garden sites. Please inquire about seasonal children's horticultural therapy groups, which focus on strengthening emotional awareness, emotional regulation, self-trust, self-worth, and collaborative skills via therapeutic horticulture activities. Why Nature? Research shows that connecting with nature, both indoors and outdoors, can help reduce cognitive overload, improve mood, and foster a sense of balance and well-being. Engaging with our natural environment has been found to minimize stress, increase emotional resilience, and create a deeper sense of connection to oneself, others, and the broader living world.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I approach therapy with a commitment to social justice and a deep respect for your lived experiences. My practice is an affirming and inclusive space where we can explore how factors like sexuality, gender identity, race, culture, ability, and systemic inequities shape your story and impact your life. Together, we can work to unpack the ways that external systems and internalized messages influence your well-being, while empowering you to draw on your resilience and address the growth you desire.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: As a certified Ecotherapist and AHTA-accredited Horticultural Therapist (HTR), nature is my co-facilitator in the therapeutic process. Whether we're taking a walk, getting our hands in the soil and tending to plants, or drawing on nature’s lessons in conversation and mindfulness, building our relationship to the natural world can help us feel grounded within a broader ecosystem, thus fostering a deeper sense of connection, meaning, and acceptance in the context of life's natural rhythms.

name: Cassondra Arroyo Asla
title: Marriage and Family Therapist
intro: Welcome! Choosing someone to share your experiences with is a deeply personal and vulnerable decision. I’m honored to be considered.
ideal_client: I specialize in systemic, trauma-informed therapy for adults, couples, and families navigating complex trauma, PTSD, anxiety, and attachment issues—and I also work with individuals across various age groups. My approach helps clients recognize and transform patterns that impact their relationships, family dynamics, and emotional well-being.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I offer a safe, inclusive space where all identities, family structures, and relationship dynamics are welcomed. My approach is collaborative and compassionate—we’ll work together to bring healing, connection, and clarity back into your life. Whether you're an individual navigating a life transition, a couple working through relationship challenges, or a family seeking meaningful change and support, you'll find a grounded, down-to-earth, and genuinely supportive presence in our work together. As a woman of color, I understand how hard it can be to find a therapist who “gets it.” I hold space for those navigating generational trauma, cultural expectations, and the beauty and complexity of family traditions—while also learning to set boundaries and honor your individual needs.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Before joining The Path Center, I worked at a child- and family-focused clinic in Southeast Portland, where I provided support to marginalized youth and their families. I also co-led groups at The Portland DBT Institute, where I helped young adults, ages 18-25, develop crucial skills for understanding and managing emotions while navigating the challenges of chronic health conditions and mood disorders. Through my work with children, families, and adults, I’ve come to deeply appreciate the vital role early connections play in fostering emotional resilience. Being married for 17 years and raising five children has given me firsthand insight into the joys and struggles that come with balancing individual identity, nurturing a partnership, and navigating the complexities of parenting. I understand how these roles can sometimes feel overwhelming or conflicting, and I bring this lived experience into my work to create a compassionate and understanding space for my clients.

name: Audra Carmine
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
credentials: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate R8771
intro: I am honored to guide my clients toward their own self-healing impulse by creating a loving, space to be curious & receive support.
ideal_client: Do you feel anxious, hopeless, and have tried therapy before? Do you feel like you will never "get over" your trauma? Do you feel disconnected from yourself, and are seeking to live a more interesting, love filled life? I get it. That was me too. And I am honored to guide clients toward their own self-healing impulse by creating a loving, accepting space to be curious, receive support, and be witnessed with deep presence and attunement. You deserve a refuge. You deserve care

approaches.My Background and Approach: I earned my Masters degree in Clinical Psychology at Antioch University, and am certified in Somatic EMDR from the Embody Lab as well as Applied Polyvagal Theory in Yoga levels 1-3—both trainings led by Dr. Arielle Schwartz. I completed an 8 month training with Thomas Hubel on Ancestral Healing and Trauma, and a 16 week Breathwork course with Breathworker and author Jennifer Patterson. I also am a certified meditation teacher through Jack Kornfield and Tara Brach’s two year intensive training program.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My practice is rooted in an ethos of love, connection, kindness, & compassion. It is often our disconnection from care that leads us toward dis ease, anxiety, & that unbearable feeling of wanting to crawl out of our own skin. It is our reconnection with loving kindness that heals us. Our stories of anxiety and trauma are suddenly less alone. Therapy is, at its most essential, two individuals in a caring relationship. I have learned through years of therapy myself that I am deserving of love simply because I exist--and so are you. We get hurt by people, so we must heal with people. Therapy is a brilliant container in which to grow and remember who we really are. Without it, I would not be here. I would still be exhausting myself trying to get the love I so desperately wanted. Therapy is not the only way to grow and heal; however, it is a really clear, accessible, and effective path toward self-actualization, a more interesting life, strong boundaries, & love.

name: Bobbi Harrison
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: LQBTQIA+ and trauma informed. I love working with pregnancy, birth and postpartum, as well as couples & family systems. Let's find your way.
ideal_client: I support individuals on their reproductive journeys, including fertility, pregnancy, and perinatal mental health, with over a decade of experience as a teacher and doula. I aid clients through grief and pregnancy loss and have helped over 100 families in Central Oregon. I also offer couples and group therapy for relationship healing, work with kids and teens on self-discovery, and provide support for individuals and families affected by addiction.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I approach healing with a heart-centered and holistic mindset, deeply valuing the integration of mind, body, and spirit in self-discovery. My experience includes supporting clients through anxiety, relationship and behavioral challenges, life transitions, addiction, family trauma, and reproductive health journeys. I believe you possess the tools for healing within you, and my role is to guide you in accessing these resources to enhance your well-being. My practice is LGBTQIA+ and trauma-informed, utilizing various modalities tailored to individual client needs. I enjoy working with adults, youth, teens, couples, and children or adult children of alcoholics, always creating a safe space for healing. With a decade of experience as a teacher, life coach, and birth/postpartum doula, I empower women and birthing people on their reproductive journeys, including fertility, conception, pregnancy, and perinatal mental health. I would love to do this work together.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I became a therapist to support individuals through significant and transformative experiences. Prior to this, I worked in roles like teaching, wilderness guiding, and as a crisis responder, which reinforced my belief in the healing power of connection. My enthusiasm for individual, couples, and group therapy stems from seeing how vulnerability met with compassion can lead to healing. As a Birth Doula and childbirth educator, I supported over 100 families in Central Oregon, witnessing the myriad of emotions during pregnancy and postpartum. This experience fueled my advocacy for birthing people. I also enjoy working with youth and teens, drawing from my teaching background to help them navigate self-discovery. Growing up in a family with addiction, I understand its impact on dynamics and self-worth, which guides my work with individuals dealing with addiction. My practice emphasizes LGBTQIA+ and trauma-informed care. Ultimately, I aim to help people embrace who they are!

name: Tiffany Barr
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: My background in community-based treatment and street outreach has provided over a decade of experience in complex mental health concerns.
ideal_client: I work with adults on issues ranging from mood disorders, self image issues, self-destructive behaviors, severe persistent mental illness, and trauma recovery. I am currently only accepting private pay clients, however, I am sometimes able to provide sliding scale options to uninsured or OHP clients.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My practice, Cloud Garden Counseling, is rooted in resiliency of human spirit and the power of the therapeutic process to inspire and support change. With a broad foundation in evidence-based practices and trauma-informed care, I use Cognitive Behavioral, Dialectical Behavioral, and Narrative tools to support clients in gaining new coping tools and a deeper understanding of themselves. Together we work to reach individualized goals, strengthen support, and overcome old patterns and harmful influences. With this client-centered and strength based approach we can forge a path to understanding the influences that act upon you and the power you have to re-story you own life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a trauma survivor and person in recovery, my belief in our power to grow, heal, and change is deeply tied to personal experience. Since childhood I have relied heavily on storytelling and artwork to overcome difficulties and deepen my understanding of self and others. Writing and illustration remain steadfast tools and add great joy to my life inside and outside the therapy room. Though art and writing do not always come into therapy, I enjoy when the use of metaphor or visual expression joins naturally with other therapy tools.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have over ten years experience working from a trauma-informed perspective and utilizing DBT, CBT, and narrative tools to address the symptoms of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Complex Trauma.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I have over ten years experience in diagnostic assessment and treatment of ADHD symptoms. I work with clients to identify areas where ADHD symptoms are impacting their relationships and school/work performance. Together we can find the behavioral and cognitive interventions that best fit their needs and learning style.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I have over ten years experience working with people in recovery from drug and alcohol addiction. I am competent and comfortable working within the 12-step modality but also familiar and encouraging of other support programs that exist outside that traditional framework.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I have over ten years experience working from a trauma-informed perspective and utilizing DBT, CBT, and narrative tools to address the symptoms of unipolar and/or bipolar depression.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have over ten years experience working from a trauma-informed perspective and utilizing DBT, CBT, and narrative tools to address the symptoms of anxiety.

name: Alex Bistroi
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My goal is to help others get in touch with who they really are (including the armor and the masks) so they can live life with more joy.

approaches.How I Can Help You: Whether you’re struggling with depression or anxiety, are concerned about your life choices, or have difficulty finding joy, therapy can be a valuable tool towards self-discovery and positive change. My goal is to create a safe space in which you can be yourself without fear of judgment. I view the quality of the relationships I have with clients as crucial towards progress. I also aim to provide honest feedback to encourage exploration of painful emotions and memories which may have been obscured or hidden from awareness. I believe good therapy is a mixture of empathy, support, encouragement, and drive towards honest self-discovery. While I believe in the power of therapy, I try to not take myself too seriously and work to cultivate a sense of humility and fun about life in general.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a licensed professional counselor (LPC) in Oregon. I have completed post-licensure training in EMDR, Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT) for individuals and couples. I have a wide-range of experience working in crisis centers, addictions treatment, family therapy, and outpatient settings. I have a strong interest in working with clients who struggle with self-criticism and/or low self-worth.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR (Basic 1 and Basic 2).

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I completed training in Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT) for individuals. I also completed training in EFT for couples.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I completed EMDR basic training, and have further training in using EMDR for addictions, and in using EMDR to treat complex trauma and dissociation.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I often work with clients using EFT-based “empty chair” and/or “two-chair” techniques; these techniques are evidence-based and have demonstrated decrease in depression, anxiety, combating perfectionist tendencies, and improved ability to respond to self-criticism with self-compassion.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Self-criticism, self-contempt, and even self-hate are commonly associated with depression. I use EFT-based experiential exercises such as empty-chair dialogues with self-critical parts to bring these conflicts into the light in the therapy session, the goal being to help clients develop internal strengths to respond to internalized negative self-treatment.

name: Alissa Holmes
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a client-centered practitioner ready to walk beside you on your journey to growth, healing, and self-acceptance.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I consider myself an eclectic practitioner, meaning my approach is informed by a variety of evidence-based treatments. As a client-centered therapist, I tailor my approach to you and your needs. I believe that everyone has the capacity to heal, grow, and create positive change in their lives when given the right tools. My treatment approach is most strongly informed by Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, mindfulness-based techniques and motivational interviewing. My hope is that through our therapeutic relationship, my clients attain a sense of empowerment and resiliency, as well as the peace that comes with self-acceptance and embracing the here and now. While we can't always change our circumstances, we can always learn to respond to life's challenges in a way that correspond with our most deeply-held values.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I have undergone multiple trainings in ACT, which incorporates many principles of CBT as well as mindfulness-based techniques. In ACT, we use acceptance and mindfulness techniques in combination with behavioral changes to help you live a meaningful life based on your personal values. ACT skills are designed to increase your psychological flexibility - meaning you become better able to deal with change while living fully in the present moment.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness is the ability to pay attention to your experiences with openness and curiosity. Both formal and informal mindfulness practices help you hone this ability of shifting your attention and awareness to the here-and-now. Practicing mindfulness helps us access our wisest, inner selves, even when life is full of difficulties.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: Motivational Interviewing (MI) is a collaborative approach where we work together to explore your motivations for change. It is normal to feel ambivalent and uncertain about making a change in your life, even if you think it will ultimately benefit you. Together, we can develop an action plan for change that works for you and builds on your existing strengths.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I have worked extensively with people struggling with addiction in both outpatient and inpatient settings. I take a harm reduction approach and use motivational interviewing to help cultivate a change mindset, whether the goal is to reduce/modify one's use or to obtain total abstinence. Both goals are valid, and I offer a non-judgemental space to explore how substances may be impacting your life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety and anxiety disorders can easily overwhelm us and steal our joy from our day-to-day lives. While we can rarely make our anxiety disappear entirely, there are effective ways to quiet and calm our minds and our hearts so we can focus on the things that matter most.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can present itself in many ways, and often hand-in-hand with anxiety. Depression can make it difficult to connect with your values and your sense of who you are. In therapy we can learn to manage symptoms of depression, identify and deal with our triggers, and regain a sense of balance and purpose in life.

name: Anissa Bahrenburg
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I'm a sex and relationship therapist that understands the importance of a safe space. I'm trauma informed and non-judgemental.
ideal_client: My clients are typically adults, either individuals or in partnerships, who want to explore in some way issues around sexuality and/or intimacy. Some examples include: -Increasing sexual desire and curiosity -Exploring sexual or gender identity -Erotic mismatch / discrepancy in desire levels or desires of partners -Increasing sexual pleasure and satisfaction -Destigmatizing sex and reducing sexual shame -Exploring and determining sexual values and interests -Navigating non-monogamy

approaches.What I Specialize In: I specialize in Sex and Relationship therapy and Clinical Supervision. Sex therapy addresses physical or psychological areas related to sexual health. It is for an individual or individuals in relationship seeking increased connection, pleasure intimacy and an increased knowledge of your sexual self. Sex therapy is entirely talk therapy. Relationship therapy is for any type of relationship (couples/dyads, triads, polycules and more) seeking increased ability to connect with each other. General areas of focus: -Improving communication -Building skills in conflict management -Increasing connection, vulnerability, and understanding -Increasing intimacy and sexual connection -Defining relationship values and developing a shared vision for the future -Addressing challenges emerging from breaches of trust, trauma, loss, and more within the relationship -Identifying and addressing old trauma that is getting in the way of connection

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: -I believe that people have good intentions and are doing the best that they can in the moment -I am present focused and have a collaborative and direct approach -I support all types of relationships including polyamory, ethical non-monogamy, monogamy and more -I am kink/fetish/BDSM affirming -I am body positive -I believe in CONSENT https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pZwvrxVavnQ -I believe in remaining open-minded and curious

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: Also known as multi-modal or integrative therapy. I use brief eclectic therapy and incorporate aspects of multiple modalities including psychodynamic and cognitive behavioral treatment. I use the most effective methods available to address each individual client's needs.

name: Alexandra Winteraven
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: A space to feel, be real, and reconnect-with yourself, your body, and what matters most. Your full self is welcome here. CareOregon accepted
ideal_client: You’ve done the work, but old patterns still show up. You’re craving deeper connection-to yourself, others, and the world. Maybe you're grieving something hard to name: a relationship, a role, or a part of yourself. You might feel like the world is moving too fast while something inside you longs to slow down, feel more, and be met in your full complexity. I work with women, femmes, and gender expansive folks navigating grief, identity shifts, relational trauma, and tender transitions.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I’ve been practicing psychotherapy since 2013, with a focus on trauma, attachment, and somatic healing. My work is grounded in the wisdom of the body and guided by a bottom-up approach that centers presence, curiosity, and care. I specialize in somatic depth therapy—work that holds space for what’s complex, messy, and often left out of more conventional therapy spaces. Humor is welcome. So is shadow work. My approach is relational, intuitive, and feedback-based, supporting clients in tracking patterns, building capacity, and deepening connection with themselves and others over time. While you’ll gain tools, our work isn’t about quick fixes—it’s about meaningful insight and lasting change. I believe healing happens on a spiral, not a straight line, and I’m here to walk alongside you through the layers.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a queer, nonbinary therapist and active member of the LGBTQ+ community, I believe healing begins with reconnection—to our bodies, to each other, and to the earth. I’m committed to examining the impacts of whiteness, power, and privilege in my own life and the systems we’re embedded in. I hold a politicized and relational view of healing, one that centers embodiment, complexity, belonging, and deep care. My values as a therapist include transparency, curiosity, attunement, and integrity. I work best with those who are ready to challenge internalized norms and explore new ways of being. I’m especially drawn to the intersections of grief, justice, and the slow, sacred work of transformation. I’m also deeply nourished by earth-based spirituality, and drawn to Tarot, astrology, Human Design, and Gene Keys as ways of connecting with meaning, symbolism, and the unseen. Nature is medicine, and being in relationship with the natural world is central to how I live and heal.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Somatic therapy focuses on the profound connection between mind and body. Using physical sensations as gateways to healing, clients become aware of how trauma, emotions, and stress are stored in the body. With over a decade of experience studying diverse somatic healing practices, I’ve developed a unique approach that empowers individuals to access insights and healing beyond what traditional talk therapy can provide.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: Depth therapy explores the unconscious layers of the psyche to uncover hidden patterns, beliefs, and emotional wounds. I work with clients to engage with their inner world through dreams, symbols,archetypes, and deep self-inquiry. This approach seeks to reveal the deeper sources of distress and facilitate healing from the root causes, not just the symptoms. Depth therapy invites clients to explore their full potential and align with their true selves in a compassionate, exploratory space.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: Transpersonal therapy explores the spiritual, existential, and transcendent aspects of healing. I support clients in finding meaning, purpose, and connection beyond the self. Whether navigating spiritual crises, exploring altered states of consciousness, or seeking deeper alignment with your purpose, this approach integrates spiritual growth with psychological healing. Together, we create space for wholeness, connection, and a deeper sense of self.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Feminist therapy centers power from within, social justice, and equality in the healing process. I work with clients to explore how societal expectations, gender norms, and systemic oppression impact mental health and well-being. Through a feminist lens, we address identity, power, and privilege, fostering agency, autonomy, and voice. This approach supports growth and healing by challenging oppressive systems and creating space for authenticity, empowerment, and meaningful change.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: In navigating the effects of trauma, we often find ourselves trapped in old patterns. I work with individuals navigating PTSD, complex, and relational trauma by focusing on somatic and nervous system regulation. Rather than pathologizing, we explore how trauma is held in the body, using practices to release stored experiences and reconnect with safety. My approach blends trauma-informed techniques with body-centered practices to support healing and integration at a deep, relational level.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Living authentically as a queer person requires courage and self-compassion. I am attuned to the challenges faced by individuals in the LGBTQIA+ community, providing a space where your identity is celebrated and your experiences validated. My approach is inclusive, affirming, and trauma-informed, supporting clients in embracing their authentic selves and healing from societal marginalization.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: The journey of being a woman in today’s world can be filled with challenges. I work with women navigating societal expectations, personal identity, and self-worth. Through somatic and relational practices, we explore the impact of gendered experiences on the body and emotions. My approach fosters self-empowerment and healing, helping you reclaim your voice, agency, and a deeper connection to your authentic self in a world that often demands you play small and don't take up too much space.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships are complex, and navigating them can often bring up patterns that keep us from receiving the love and connection we need and deserve. I work with individuals exploring dynamics in romantic, familial, or platonic relationships, especially those facing challenges in open relationships, toxic patterns, or communication breakdowns. Together, we’ll examine these dynamics with curiosity and compassion, fostering healthier ways of relating and deeper emotional intimacy

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Spirituality is deeply personal, and it can be a powerful tool for healing and growth. I support individuals exploring their spiritual paths, integrating practices that nurture connection to themselves, others, and the world around them. Whether you're deepening your connection to the Earth, seeking alignment with your inner wisdom, or navigating the intersection of spirituality and identity, I provide a supportive, non-judgmental space to explore your unique journey.

name: Nathan Bauer
title: Clinical Psychologist Resident
intro: Are you tired of therapists starting their profile with a question? You might be now, but you may also understand my sense of humor.
ideal_client: Humor is something I like to incorporate into therapy; however, we can be serious about your concerns too. People of all ages struggle with the human universal of suffering and sometimes you need someone to sit with you in that, whether it be something you wish to change, or something that you cannot. The systems we live within often teach us to feel alone in our suffering. I'm here to show you that this does not have to be the case.

approaches.My Background: I provide both short-term and long-term therapy for a variety of issues, including depression, anxiety, and trauma. However, I believe that I have particular skills around supporting people navigating grief, traumatic loss, as well as substance use concerns. Much of my training/experience has been within college-counseling centers along with in-patient substance use treatment, where I ran multiple therapy groups for both grief and trauma. Our initial sessions will focus on finding what works best for you based upon your needs and goals. While I prefer to work from a Trauma-Informed Gestalt therapy perspective (viewing things as interconnected and contextual), I also draw upon ACT and CBT depending on each individual person with whom I'm working. At the beginning, we'll work to identify how directive or non-directive you wish therapy to be and whether you desire to learn skills or focus on deeper exploration.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I approach all of my work using a liberation psychology-based lens and strongly believe that much of the suffering people experience happens within the context of oppressive systems such as Capitalism, systemic racism, sexism, homophobia, and transphobia. I avoid using gendered pronouns (unless asked to do so by my clients) within my documentation so as to protect the confidentiality of those with which I work. I believe in affirming all held identities of my clients. I also recognize how financially stressful therapy can be and am happy to discuss sliding scale options with any potential client.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I have previously run a Living with Loss support group while also supporting individual clients in their grief. I have found that my general approach to therapy works well in helping people navigate grief and loss, and have received strong, positive feedback from clients about our work in this area.

name: Gillian Sleeman
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: If anxiety is a persistent issue for you and it is interfering with your functioning, I look forward to working with you to find relief!
ideal_client: We have all certainly experienced anxiety at some point in our lives, but if it is persistent and if it begins to interfere with your day to day life, you may have an anxiety disorder. This may include struggles with obsessions and compulsions, intrusive thoughts, worries, panic attacks or physical symptoms of anxiety. I work with adults, teens and children by providing specific tools and strategies to empower them to take control of anxiety.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and a the more specialized approach of Exposure and Response Prevention have been shown repeatedly to be the most effective treatment interventions for anxiety and related disorders, including OCD. While this is the primary therapeutic orientation used in my practice, I also believe that the relationship between therapist and client is very important in determining therapeutic outcomes. I consider my approach to be open and collaborative and we will work together to identify both long term and shorter term (week to week) goals to help you track your progress and feel that you are making important and lasting changes to your mental health.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I graduated from Lewis and Clark College with a degree in Marriage, Couple and Family Therapy. My experience prior to private practice included work in outpatient and residential mental health settings, working with children and adults on issues ranging from addiction to depression to childhood behavioral challenges. I have spent the last 6 years obtaining specialized training in the areas of anxiety and OCD and the use of CBT and ERP as treatment modalities, including completing certification at the Behavioral Therapy Training Institute. I am passionate about this specialty and the power of treatment and consider it a privilege to work along side my clients as they learn about these tools and use them to improve their quality of life.

specialities.name: Exposure and Response Prevention Therapy
specialities.description: ERP is the gold standard for treating OCD and other anxiety disorders. It is evidence based and highly effective. This is a behavioral intervention that we will work together to implement. I believe it is important to teach my clients as much as possible about these treatment approaches so that there is a thorough understanding of how they work and why they work!

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT views our behavior as fundamentally influenced by our thoughts and emotions. CBT allows us to better understand these maladaptive or 'dysfunctional' thoughts and replace them with those that have a more positive influence over our behaviors. While we certainly cannot control everything and everyone around us, our thoughts and feelings are aspects of our lives that we can gain control over.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Prior to beginning private practice, I worked as a Child and Family Therapist in an intensive outpatient setting for Trillium Family Services which is Oregon's largest provider of mental and behavioral healthcare for children and families.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: My private practice has focused on helping adults find the tools and the strength to manage the often overwhelming stress and anxiety that comes from the busy and demanding lives that we lead as well as anxiety that may be the result of loss, life transitions or stressful relationships.

name: Madilyn Long
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I provide an affirming and supportive setting wherein each client can build self-trust and realize their potential for healing and growth.
ideal_client: As a social worker, I love finding the individual within the noise of the systems we live in. Nothing brings me more happiness than seeing the "aha" moments during sessions that lead to more knowledge, joy and confidence in the lives of my clients. Whether you are experiencing a life transition, increased stress or anxiety, dissatisfaction with relationships or work, or would just like someone that will be on your side while you figure it out, I'm here for you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that all people hold within them an inherent ability to heal, connect, and thrive. With challenges that arise over the course of a life, that ability may become diminished or more difficult to access. I believe that a therapeutic relationship based on honest and mutual connection, trust and respect can be the catalyst for life-altering healing and change. I strive to offer an empathetic and affirming approach to all of my clients as they express themselves through their many identities, experiences, strengths, and challenges. I see my role as someone that will walk beside you, as a companion, as you find the solutions that work best for you. I value the right dose of empathy, compassion, and humor to help facilitate a safe and comforting environment in which you can engage and find your way to a more joyful and purposeful life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I chose to pursue a career in social work because I knew that through my education and experience working as a professional I would be exposed to people, thoughts, and experiences that were different from what I was familiar with. I have always been deeply passionate about helping others but often felt powerless when faced with the weight of all that needs "fixing" in our world. Through my work as a clinical social worker, I have found ways in which I can be most effective as an agent for social change. I continue to recognize, deconstruct, and acknowledge the ways in which I am privileged in an effort to leverage that privilege for good. I am a vocal and passionate advocate for education, harm-reduction and radical societal change in regards to the most vulnerable members of our society.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: I am a trained Brainspotting clinician and utilize this modality with many of my current clients to assist in processing traumas, both recent and past, and other emotionally significant events.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I believe that emotions are the unsung heroes of unlocking the mind and body connection. They provide a roadmap for how to effectively and efficiently address and process any number of issues that may arise in every day life. By helping my clients to first identify and then work with their emotions rather than resist them, I help them to access healing and growth that may have previously been unknown or unaccessible to them.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: As a social worker trained in systems-theory, I have come to believe that it is the quality of our interpersonal relationships that have the greatest impact on our overall mental health and wellbeing. By utilizing relational therapy, I assist my clients in identifying which relationships are most meaningful to them and how to ensure that those relationships are mutually-satisfying and beneficial to all parties involved. This often includes work around communication skills and boundaries.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I am a queer therapist with over 7 years of experience working clinically with the LGBTQIA+/Queer community including trans-competent and affirming care that includes free assessments and letters for gender-affirming procedures. I am a member of WPATH and GALAP as well as several LGBTQIA+ affirmative organizations in both Utah and Oregon. I am passionate about making my practice a comforting and affirming space in the midst of the massive amount of discrimination being leveraged at this time.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I grew up in Salt Lake City, Utah and was raised in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints (Mormonism). I recognize as an adult that this was a fairly unique culture to have experienced and can see the ways it influenced who I am today, for better or worse. I am interested in helping others find their way to happiness and comfort, within The Church or without, while remaining a vocal advocate for change within the organization in regards to racial, gender and LGBTQIA+ policies.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Through my own experience as a bone marrow transplant recipient, I learned first-hand the importance of having access to a mental health professional that could guide me and help me in processing all of the complex emotions that were unearthed before, during, and after my diagnosis and treatment. Because of that experience, I am passionate about providing the same support and assistance to others who are experiencing chronic pain or illness in navigating that road themselves.

name: Angie Morgan
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Angie. I've been a counselor for over thirteen years and I love the opportunity to help others find hope and healing.
ideal_client: Life can be difficult and we all have ups and downs. We all experience life transitions, such as changes in age, relationships, births, deaths, marriage, divorce, and changes in employment, to name a few. It is normal and common to have some difficulty navigating these changes, which may be accompanied by depression, anxiety, trouble sleeping, and other mental health concerns. I specialize in trauma therapy and in helping people heal and recover.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Let's work together to discover your best self and to help you live the life you've always wanted. I offer help for concerns such as depression, anxiety, self-esteem, life changes, and trauma. I use a strengths-based, trauma-informed, and person centered approach to counseling. I most often use IFS (Internal Family Systems), CBT, and Person Centered Therapy. I seek to provide a calm, trustworthy, non-judgmental, and supportive environment that allows for honest, real, and life-changing conversations. I believe that the best results happen when treating the whole person, which includes mental, physical, spiritual, relational, and intellectual parts of self. Let's work together to find your hope and healing!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that every person desires to obtain optimal health and well-being. I hope to provide space for people to truly be themselves and discover their full potential. I value a nonjudgmental stance, equality, inclusion, and believe that diversity is what makes this world beautiful. I am a member of the LGBTQ community and come from a religious background. I have experience in how these two worlds collide and would like to help be a bridge between the two. I support racial justice and want to be an advocate for change. In my free time, I enjoy the outdoors, hiking, camping, SUP, music, reading, and spending time with family and friends.

name: Kerrins Conroy III
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Kerrins (k-air-ence) or Kerry for short. Let's have a chat about how you are doing.
ideal_client: Anxiety, grief, depression and an over all sense of being stuck are all common themes that everyone experiences once in their life. All of which are manageable given the right support, which I feel like I can provide. I generally work with individuals, relationships, and families. Also, as a gay man I feel drawn to support members of the LGBTQIA+ community.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach counseling from an Existential-Humanistic approach, which allows you to discover new aspects of your life, and how to live a more intentionally fulfilling life. You will be met with empathy, and the understanding that your lived experience is more important than any preconceived notion as to how someone should be living their life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that when people are given support, validation, and empathy everyone has the capacity and potential to live a fulfilling life. Grief, anxiety, depression, and personal growth are all manageable with the right support. As a counselor, part of my job is to provide that support you may have not gotten before. Through exploration of different life themes, we will work together to create the life that you have always envisioned.

name: Katie Trageser
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello and welcome! I am an LPC in the state of Oregon, and I specialize in the treatment of eating disorders and anxiety related disorders.
ideal_client: My experience and specialization includes diagnoses and treatment of individuals struggling with eating disorders, disordered eating, chronic dieting, body image distress, and a variety of anxiety-related disorders. I take a Behavioral, Dialectical and Intuitive Eating approach to my treatment, where I teach clients a variety of skills and tools to manage distress, improve thinking patterns and self-talk, and heal/neutralize relationship with food/body.

approaches.My Background: The following is a snapshot of my education and certifications: -Bachelor of Science in Psychology: University of Oregon -Masters of Arts in Professional Mental Health Counseling-Addictions: Lewis & Clark Graduate School of Counseling Education -National Certified Counselor (NCC) -Certified Clinical Anxiety Treatment Professional (CCATP) 265977 -Licensed Professional Counselor in Oregon #C7773

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is an evidenced-based approach that focuses on how thoughts, emotions and behaviors influence one another. CBT targets unhelpful thinking patterns and emotions that often lead to unhelpful reactive behavior, and aids in rewiring neuro pathways through cognitive skill-work, exposure to stimuli causing fear, and managing distressing emotions using self-help strategies. Let's rewire the anxious brain!

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I specialize in the diagnosing and treatment of individuals with eating disorders and professional experience working in individual, group, residential, partial hospitalization, and intensive outpatient treatment programs. I utilize a Health at Every Size (HAES) and Intuitive Eating lens in my work, as I focus on going back to a grassroots approach of learning how to reintegrate instinct, emotion and rational thought into one's relationship with food and their body.

name: Cayley Mesterheide
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: Hello, I am Cayley Mesterheide, PA-C (certified psychiatric physician assistant). I provide medication management for mental health issues.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with adults and patients of different backgrounds. At Quimson Behavioral Health we are open and inclusive to all who seek help and mental health treatment. My focus is on medication management and incorporate therapy to help individuals navigate their understanding of their diagnosis and social/emotional lifestyle.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My passion for psychiatry began before I started PA school while working as a nursing assistant in the psychiatric unit of a hospital. While working at the hospital, I achieved my Bachelor of Science in BioHealth Sciences degree at Oregon State University. I then went on to pursue my Master’s in PA Studies at Lipscomb University in Nashville, Tennessee. My approach to treating mental health is holistic and includes a focus on medication management while incorporating supportive therapy and lifestyle modifications. I strive to connect with each and every patient and make it my goal to ensure that they feel heard and understood. Helping patients to find the right therapeutic regimen that allows them to function best in life brings me fulfillment in my career. I look forward to meeting and collaborating with you to help you achieve your mental health goals.

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: Our psychiatric practice works with individuals who have tried talk therapy and continue to struggle with management of symptoms impacting their daily functioning. We can work alongside your current therapist to help you overcome your obstacles.

name: Grace Carter
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a creative and intuitive counselor, with a warm and relational style.
ideal_client: Maybe you feel like nothing you do is good enough, sapping your energy and joy from life. Your critical inner voice as at a volume 10, and things just don’t feel worth attempting to do anymore. Generally, you feel worn out, and tired of repeating the same patterns. You feel alone. You wish for a feeling of peace with who you are, and a sense of confidence and clarity in your way forward. You want to feel joy and have a sense of contentment with your loved ones. You want to live your life!

approaches.How I Can Help You: I offer sessions that can target the specific areas that you are wanting to address. I offer trauma informed talk therapy and creative/somatic therapies for creative thinkers. Clients who work with me appreciate my warmth and compassion, and my illuminating insights. Check out my website and book a free consultation today!

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I’m no different from the clients I see. Like everyone else, I'm a human who has made many human mistakes. I've been through wonderful and difficult experiences. These experiences have shaped who I am, and how I help clients. Throughout my younger years as an adult, I struggled with emotional wounds that created real difficulty in my personal and professional life. During that time, I worked with a therapist whose warmth and guidance created a path for healing and peace. It was one of the most important and profound experiences of my adult life. I realized that I wanted to be a part of this journey with others, as a guide. I feel true awe and gratitude at being entrusted to do this work. I believe in this process and I have been through it myself. There’s no doubt, my life experiences are what led me to become the therapist I am today.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Internal Family Systems (IFS) uses Family Systems theory—the idea that individuals cannot be fully understood in isolation from the family unit—to develop techniques and strategies to effectively address issues within a person’s internal community or family. This evidence-based approach assumes each individual possesses a variety of sub-personalities, or “parts,” and attempts to get to know each of these parts better to achieve healing.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotionally focused therapy is an intervention based on scientific study of adult love and bonding processes and is designed to address distress in the intimate relationships of adults. Strategies from emotionally focused therapy can be used to help people connect with friends, family and romantic partners and improve emotional attachment.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: A modality grounded in the mind-body connection, somatic psychotherapy is the largest branch of somatic psychology. Contemporary practitioners of somatic therapy believe that viewing the mind and body as one entity is essential to the therapeutic process. This mind/body entity will move toward healing and growth of its own accord, given the right environment, and interpersonal interactions, when conducted in a safe and respectful manner, can positively impact and help regulate the mind/body.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: In psychodynamic therapy, therapists help people gain insight into their lives and present-day problems. They also evaluate patterns people develop over time. To do this, therapists review certain life factors with a person in therapy: emotions, thoughts, early life experiences and beliefs. Recognizing recurring patterns can help people see how they avoid distress or develop defense mechanisms to cope. This insight may allow them to begin changing those patterns.

name: Heather Hemmeger
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: As both a psychiatric nurse practitioner and a former pharmacist, I approach patient care from a unique, integrative perspective.
ideal_client: If you're seeking inclusive psychiatric care in Portland or anywhere in Oregon—especially for anxiety, depression, trauma, insomnia, or OCD—I offer a compassionate, integrative approach. My background allows me to strategically blend psychopharmacology and psychotherapy to support your goals, whether you’re adjusting to life transitions, navigating chronic illness, or managing emotional overwhelm. I will be here to help you every step of the way!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that balancing open communication with an in-depth understanding of medication management creates the opportunity for true mind-body balance and holistic healing. My experience in both inpatient and outpatient settings—as both a pharmacist and a board-certified psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner—allows me to blend strategic, evidence-based psychopharmacology with therapeutic interventions that support lasting change. In our work together, I will create a safe, inclusive, and empowering space that fosters self-compassion and long-term growth. My approach is evidence-based and intersectional, informed by the multiple identities and sociocultural contexts that shape each individual’s lived experience.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have expertise in mood disorders including anxiety and depression, often in the context of individuals experiencing major life changes, relationship difficulties, or problems at school or work. While I’ve worked with patients at all stages of life, I have extensive experience working with students in college mental health, and I am most passionate about helping older adolescents and young adults as they transition into adulthood and navigate the stressors of high school, undergraduate and graduate school. I am also enthusiastic about helping women who are navigating health concerns, including prenatal and postpartum. When I’m not working, you’ll likely find me: Curled up with a good book, nestled between my cats Remi, Rowan, and Rory. Practicing yoga & playing tennis to stay grounded. Exploring new restaurants & capturing the world through my camera alongside my partner.

name: Grace Silvia, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Deeply Respectful. Gentle & Empowering. Core Transformation.
ideal_client: I will support you in developing curiosity, compassion and mindfulness in the exploration of your inner and outer worlds. All of you is welcome--heart, body, mind, soul. My practice is client-centered, relational, and strengths-based.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I help you become allies with your unconscious. I will support you to listen to, have compassion for, and honor what your symptoms and problems are trying to tell you. There are gifts in your challenges, and together we will find them and bring the exiled parts of yourself home. This work is creative, sacred, and changes your life from the inside out. There is never forcing an agenda or pace, or pushing past "no." Our deepest selves want to grow and heal--we just need to re-learn how to follow that impulse.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I trained 2-1/2 years through the Hakomi Institute in body-centered, experiential, mindfulness-based psychotherapy. Eduardo Duran's work inspires me--he's a Native American psychologist who validates historical trauma and spiritual healing. My work is also informed by having experienced years of deep depression and a time of "cracking open," and through both was able to find profound meaning. I support people healing through grief; depression; hearing voices; anxiety; mania/spiritual emergency; childhood sexual abuse; acute and chronic experiences of oppression; historical trauma; activist burnout; compulsive eating; and people wanting to reduce or stop taking psychiatric medications. Special sensitivity to Jewish, women's and LGBTTSAAQQ+ (Lesbian/ Gay/ Bisexual/ Trans/ Two Spirit/ Androgynous/ Asexual/ Queer/ Questioning) identity and oppression.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: Hakomi is a body-centered, mindfulness-based approach. Hakomi uses body awareness to access the unconscious. Both trauma and brilliant, creative healing wisdom are stored in the body. By learning how to listen to and follow your body's cues, you will find a depth , ease and aliveness that working in ordinary consciousness can't access.

specialities.name: Feminist
