specialities.description: As a radical feminist, I believe my work must: > deeply honor each person's inner wisdom instead of pathologizing doctrine; > recognize the deep soul wounding that chronic and acute oppression, systems of injustice, and planetary pain cause; and > orient deep personal healing in service to becoming an empowered agent of change, rather than adjusting to being a cog in the machine.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: Whether talking about what happened yesterday or in your family growing up, we will work with what you experience as you explore it in the moment. That way the work is fresh, not a stale re-hashing of an old, stuck story. Using basic building blocks of gentle curiosity, compassion and honoring both what shows up as well as resistance to what shows up, deep transformation happens.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: How do we find a way to sit with anxiety, when it makes us want to crawl out of our skins? But it's likely desperately trying to protect us on a core level. Can we find a way to have compassion for its desperate work? It can become an ally if we can listen!

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Therapy should not be re-traumatizing! If you find yourself dissociating during or after therapy or dreading it, that is telling us something important to listen to. Working in a trauma-informed way means I will help you learn the signs of when you are beginning to re-experience the trauma, and how to bring yourself back into safety. The work must go at your pace, guided by your body's subtle cues and your inner 'no' and 'yes.'

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Deep sadness. Can we stop pushing it away, even for a moment, and listen to what it is desperately trying to tell us? This is no easy task in our culture of 'Produce!' and 'Be happy at all costs!' Yet there is so much to be sad about personally, societally and planetarily. Pushing it away makes it dig in deeper. But by honoring it, we can find its meaning, our passion and our unique call to action.

specialities.name: Schizophrenia
specialities.description: Many people hear voices, see things others don't, or have unusual beliefs. It's only a problem when it makes your life hard. What is labeled schizophrenia can be a brilliant response to trauma, a spiritual sensitivity needing a container, or....? It is for you to find your own meaning. I would be honored to support you on this path.

specialities.name: Bipolar
specialities.description: Deep lows and intense highs can wreck havoc on your life. But they can also be gifts of exquisite sensitivity, a response to trauma, or/and a spiritual awakening. I am learning from friends, clients and colleagues what can be helpful. I would be honored to share what I am learning and learn from you on this journey.

name: Aaron Armelie
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: I seek to establish, genuine, compassionate therapeutic relationships.
ideal_client: I offer evidence-based practices to help people navigate life challenges, build skills, and connect with and do more of what matters most to them in life. I previously worked in medical settings, and I have significant experience working with people who are experiencing various stages of cancer and survivorship, other health concerns, and their caregivers and loved ones. It is important to me to provide services that are informed by science, that are also collaborative and person-centered.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I strive to learn about and incorporate each person’s values, life experience, inherent wisdom and personal strengths into my work with them. My approach is very relational in nature, meaning, in addition to bringing my mind and professional experience to the care I provide, I also bring my heart. Over the years, I have had the honor of working with people who hold diverse identities and cultural backgrounds, and who come from many different walks of life. I believe that all of us, regardless of how different we are from one another, belong in this world and are deserving of respect, empathy and kindness. I strive to provide services that are culturally humble, equitable and inclusive. I believe that it is important to attend the broader context of people’s lives, strengthening those things that can promote health and wellbeing, such as meaningful relationships, and addressing factors that can contribute to social stress, such as marginalization and oppression.

name: Angela Keeney, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: *NOT ACCEPTING NEW CLIENTS AT THIS TIME. THANK YOU.* My approach to working individually with adults & teens is holistic, compassionate and rooted in the belief that we all have the capacity for positive change, deep healing and the ability to live an authentic and purposeful life.

approaches: My style of therapy is warm, collaborative and open to wherever the work may lead us, though I'll also help us to stay focused on your goals. I often use humor and creativity in my work. I'll check in along the way to make sure we're heading in a direction that is helpful and at a pace that feels right for you. The therapeutic relationship is one of the most important aspects of effective therapy, so it's important that this feels like a good fit. I truly love what I do and am endlessly inspired by the human capacity for growth and healing. My hope is to provide support, tools, and encouragement to help you find a greater sense of balance, authenticity, strength and overall well-being.

I'm a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), registered in the state of Oregon. I earned my Master's degree from Portland State University and completed my undergraduate work in psychology at Southern Oregon University. I have nearly 15 years of experience in the mental health field, including five years working in a residential treatment home for adolescent girls, and five years as a Child & Family Therapist in community mental health, prior to opening my private practice.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: While grief is most commonly associated with the death of someone close to us, we may also experience grief around a variety of other life challenges/transitions, such as the ending of a relationship, job loss, parenting milestones, loss of a deeply held belief, or a move to a new place. I can help you face grief and loss with courage, allowing for healing and a deeper sense of meaning to emerge.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can be a normal reaction to change, an anticipated event or other life stressors. When anxiety escalates, however, it can become disruptive & unsettling, affecting our sleep, physical health, relationships and overall well-being. I use mindfulness and cognitive-behavioral techniques to help clients reduce anxiety and increase balance, while also exploring/resolving the underlying causes

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Parenting is one of the most rewarding and challenging adventures we will embark on and one that can bring us face-to-face with our greatest sense of vulnerability. I am passionate about supporting parents of young/school-aged children through the many ups & downs - bringing more balance & awareness to your role as a parent and helping you learn effective strategies to raise healthy, happy and resilient children.

name: Cat Ward
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I support children and families through difficult times by creating a safe, nurturing and playful environment to foster growth and healing.
ideal_client: I work with children and families impacted by anxiety, attachment issues, family conflict, depression, traumatic experiences (during early childhood or more recently), social navigation needs and self esteem. I love working with autistic children and their families.

approaches.My Background: During my social work career I have worked providing social and clinical services to children and adolescents in residential facilities, community mental health agencies, intimate partner violence shelters, schools, in the home, and outpatient private practice. I have specialized training in working with neurodivergent children and children who have gone through traumatic experiences such as neglect, abandonment, attachment disruptions, bullying, changes in primary caregivers, physical and/or sexual abuse, and social rejection.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that every child and family has the potential for positive change. My practice is centered on the principle that positive change develops when children and teens believe they are accepted, understood and capable. My approach to helping individuals in therapy is accepting, empathetic, validating and encouraging. I use creative, expressive, playful and engaging techniques based on each client's interests, personal preferences and individual capacities. I welcome each client where they are developmentally and join in each child's world so that together we work towards growth and healing.

name: Gia Buckberg
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My goal is to encourage your strengths while being honest, direct and objective about the things that hold you back.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My hope is to work with individuals in transition who want to see results, be inspired to go further distances and reclaim their internal joy. Many of my clients come to me feeling professionally stuck or too anxious to address and tease out what it is that they truly want more of in their lives. My approach is intuitive and insightful. I listen intently and fully and appreciate humor and candor in our sessions. My approach is essentially eclectic. I honor that we as humans are unique individuals that may benefit greatly from a myriad of therapeutic supports. I often incorporate elements of CBT, solution-focused therapy and a life coaching approach into my practice. I have found the outdoor beauty of the Pacific Northwest to be incredibly healing. This inspiration has led me to offer the opportunity to conduct our sessions in the outdoors or in the office.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a MSW from the University of Minnesota and am licensed to practice clinical social work in Oregon. I have worked in a myriad of treatment facilities including residential, inpatient and outpatient centers. As a practitioner in private practice, many of my clients are challenged by life transitions, changes in their family dynamic or those who are generally feeling stuck where they are currently at in their lives. I believe that the therapeutic process is a collaborative one and I find this to be one of the most fulfilling elements of our authentic work together.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: Being the most flexible and multifaceted approach in my practice, this allows for the use of a myriad of approaches to address my clients most current pressing needs. In combination with other therapeutic modalities, it allows for the client to have more autonomy and to build upon what I call 'your very own toolbox of skills' to derive from when they are out in the world.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT is focused on helping clients deal with a very specific problem. In my experience, I have helped clients work through issues with their anxiety, anger, depression, emotional roadblocks relating to career transitions or relationship issues.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: Much of my therapeutic approach is derived from the life coaching perspective. We return to our common connections by loving, honoring and valuing ourselves and others. Wonder, curiosity and inquiry are the source of all learning. I believe awareness is the precursor to choice. Finally, contribution based on purpose generates true fulfillment and that connection is the wellspring of creativity

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: Much of my work has been supporting individuals who are currently in the throes of a change in their family dynamic. Helping a client balance the challenges of being a single parent and reestablishing a relationship with former spouse and navigating supporting their children after divorce are aspects that I feel where the life coaching perspective can be greatly beneficial.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Self-esteem issues may arise in all of us at some point in our lives. Many of us come into counseling with negative schemas that we struggle to let go of. These are thoughts we have been battling for years sometimes and my hope is to support my clients to delve deep into these and access their inner strength so that they can tap into their internal joy and be inspired to attain cadence.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: As we embark on our path, things come up and get in the way of our ability to tap into our internal joy. I help clients in managing their anxiety through elements of CBT, mindfulness, feasible goal setting and accountability.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Many of us experience periods in our lives where we feel stuck and I truly honor those individuals who are willing to come forward and say that they are tired of the daily struggles and that they need help. Through a collaborative approach, my hope is to guide clients into accessing the necessary tools that reside inside of them as a way to propel them forward.

name: Madeline Jacobs
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: We offer telehealth in OR, WA, AZ, MN, NM, and UT. In-office visits in Clackamas, OR / Layton and Lehi, UT available! Seattle visits soon.
ideal_client: I specialize in ADHD, anxiety, depression, medication-assisted opioid addiction treatment, and LGBTQIA2S+ mental health care, and see patients ages 18 to 64. I also speak Spanish. Visit https://skycloudhealth.com/ and click "Schedule Now" or call 503-694-3381 to be matched with the right provider for you. We are available for single-case agreements with Kaiser. Contact our practice for more info.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We primarily offer medication management services and are not currently accepting new patients for psychotherapy alone. Personally, I take a trauma-informed perspective on mental health care. For example, I am trained in EMDR (eye movement desensitization and reprocessing), an evidence-based trauma therapy. I also employ ADHD coaching, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), internal family systems (IFS), and mindfulness-based (MBCT) techniques. Intake available every week with our valued providers. Skycloud Mental Health is a clinical placement site for Yale School of Nursing students.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I'm a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner with a Master of Science in Nursing from Oregon Health & Science University, and have been working in the psychiatric field since 2015. I've worked at the Los Angeles LGBT Center, the largest LGBT Center in the US, and would love the opportunity to broaden the reach of LGBTQ+ affirming mental health care through telepsychiatry. I take a trauma-informed perspective on mental health care and am trained in EMDR (eye movement desensitization and reprocessing), an evidence-based trauma therapy. I specialize in ADHD, anxiety, depression, and transgender-related mental health care. I treat patients aged 18+ and am licensed in Minnesota, Washington, Oregon, Utah, and Arizona. I speak English and Spanish. I may not be accepting new patients with all insurances in all of these states. Visit https://skycloudhealth.com/ and click on Get Started to be matched with a provider who fits this same philosophy and suits your needs.

name: Deah Partak
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My goal is to help you develop the confidence to take-on the positives, negatives, and neutrals of your life story.
ideal_client: Are you seeking inner growth, balance in life, or help with anxiety, depression, compassion fatigue and trauma? I am here to help you experience and respond to life authentically and skillfully. Counseling with me is from a humanistic “you first” approach to help you incorporate your own unique values and strengths.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide therapy through existential (value, strength, and big picture-focus) and humanistic (you first, authentic, relationships based) styles. In session we can explore the here-and-now, examine thought patterns, develop self care plan, or even use humor to embrace life and yourself. In session we will focus on using your strengths and values to tackle depression, anxiety, loss, life transition, work-life balance, or self-esteem.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As long as I can remember, I have always respected the power of stories. Not just literature, but the real stories about our lives. We share our experiences, hear about our ancestors, and define who we are in this world through stories. Everyone’s story is important. Everyone has the right to author their own story and live their authentic life. Often our lives do not feel like our own because of difficult turns and twists. I find value in re-discovering resiliency and strength that is developed throughout life. I firmly believe we all have the power and strength to tackle life's stressors, joys, and tragedies. Gaining awareness of our values and strength helps us cope, thrive, and skillfully live life. I have had the privilege of being witness to the resiliency of many people with many struggles and many successes. This privilege formed and carries my belief that we all have the power and strength to tackle life's stressors, joys, and tragedies.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: I specialize in Compassion Fatigue and Vicarious Trauma. I am a Certified Compassion Fatigued Professional (CCFP). If you are a professional helper beginning to feel burnt out or traumatized by your work, this is a normal reaction that occurs to professional helpers. You can grow and cope with it! You owe it to yourself, family, friends, and clients to take action.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Life takes many twists and turns. Changes can be unexpected, planned, natural, feared, or welcomed. Sometimes the emotional stress can feel like too much. Change is inevitability; letting it control our emotions is not. There is always the opportunity to transform and promote growth and wellness. I look forward to the chance to help you transform and grow.

name: Jeff Guenther
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help people who feel anxious in relationships stop feeling anxious in relationships.
ideal_client: Have you been bouncing from relationship to relationship repeating the same tired patterns over and over again? Do you feel like it’s impossible to find someone who’s a good match for you? You must be exhausted and burnt out on the dating scene. I get it. It’s bananas out there. Therapy can provide you insight into how to get out of this rut. I look forward to working together and helping you find clarity so that you can grow.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Many clients believe it is the therapist’s job to make them feel better. While feeling better may be the outcome of counseling, it is not always the case in every situation. The therapist’s main role is to help the client feel the emotion more clearly and to perhaps provide insight as to why it is surfacing so intensely. Individual therapy is a safe place to experience emotions, no matter what they are or how they manifest. It may seem counterintuitive to think of therapy as not making you feel better, but if one can fully allow and accept an emotion without duress (which can prompt unhealthy or destructive reactions), then one can learn to handle stronger emotions in the future. If a client develops the capacity to endure intense negative emotions, then a process of normalizing and desensitizing occurs, thereby reducing the tendency to react and/or take action against uncomfortable feelings.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a very strong background in family and couples work. I received my master’s degree in marriage and family therapy from the University of Southern California, and my bachelor’s degree in child and family development from San Diego State University. Prior to going into private practice, I worked in the public school system providing individual, group, and family therapy to high-risk students. I also taught parenting classes on a regular basis. My therapeutic career started out at a crisis line here in Portland, where I mainly worked with people who were suffering from suicidal thoughts and severe anxiety. I have lived in Portland since 2005 and the bulk of my work focuses on seeing couples and individuals in my private practice.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Narrative therapy is my favorite therapeutic orientation. It’s the treatment that I study the most and find very compelling. I often observe the most improvement in clients when I use this type of counseling. Introducing new ways of thinking and believing can be a tricky thing but with the training and passion I have for it I often times see success.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I am a classically trained therapist and I specialize in psychodynamic theory. Psychodynamic theory was a focus of mine all through graduate school and I use this theory as a lens into understanding where behaviors, unhealthy and healthy, start from and how they have been reinforced through your lifetime. With a clear understanding of where you come from we can work together to unravel rooted behavior.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: My approach to counseling is modern and scientific and that is why I tend to use cognitive behavioral therapy in my sessions. I am able to provide you with many tools and techniques to deal with the problem in the here and now. Together we will influence your current way of thinking into something that feels more neutral or positive. There are many CBT interventions that I am able to employ.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Studying codependent relationships and personalities has always been the most interesting part of psychology to me. How people become attached in relationships and when it tips into an unhealthy or toxic attachment is what I specialize in. Much of my expertise come from studying relationships in graduate school where I obtained a masters in marriage and family therapy.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Self-esteem can be a tricky issue to address. There are many things that can be affecting it. I am very proficient at working with clients to explore all possible reasons your self-esteem, self-worth or confidence feels low. If it's situational we will figure out how to move through it and if it's rooted in past experience we will bring it to the surface and learn how to leave it in the past.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have a masters degree in marriage and family therapy. My training in couples counseling best fits couples that have been together a shorter time and would like to steer clear of repeating old unhealthy habits from past relationships. I see many couples that would like premarital counseling or couples that are newly married and experiencing some road bumps in their relationship.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Adjustment issues that I typically treat in my practice are adjusting to life after a break up or divorce, adjusting to your new environment after college and adjusting to moving to a new city and settling in after a big move. Many of my clients are new transplants here to Portland and are in need of some support while they settle into town.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is the issue that I treat the most in my practice. I provide my clients with tools and techniques that they can carry with them for the rest of their lives and pull from whenever they feel anxious. I am proficient at using cognitive behavior methods to provide coping strategies, using a narrative therapy approach to create mindfulness and non-attachment to your triggers while also addressi

name: Hello Me Therapy Group Practice
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We are a body-neutral, anti-diet, and HAES (Health at Every Size) aligned practice.
ideal_client: Trying to figure out how to take care of yourself and live a balance life can feel like an uphill battle. Hello Me commonly works with those who have been impacted by trauma, anxiety, depression, disordered eating, and have difficulties with maintaining health promoting behaviors. Many of our clinicians live in larger bodies and understand barriers that folks in larger bodies experience.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: At HelloMe Therapy, we believe therapy is a journey of self-discovery and healing. Our approach is personalized, combining empathy with effective tools to help you navigate life’s challenges. We specialize in Emotional Transformation Therapy (ETT), a powerful modality that helps release emotional blocks and transform how you process difficult emotions. ETT is designed to bring rapid, lasting change. We also offer Therapy Intensives—focused, immersive sessions that allow you to make significant progress on specific issues in a condensed time frame. Whether you’re dealing with anxiety, trauma, or relationship struggles, intensives can help you gain clarity and move forward faster. Please note, we are currently unable to accept insurance for therapy services. We offer flexible payment options to make therapy accessible to those ready to begin their healing journey. At HelloMe Therapy, we’re committed to supporting you in finding balance, healing, and transformation.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: We provide a brain based therapy similar to EMDR called Emotional Transformation Therapy (ETT). ETT also uses multidimensional eye movement like EMDR, but it also utilizes color to identify when the brain is dissociating and quickly treat this.

name: Patrick Nagel
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am an IFS therapist practicing in Oregon for the past 10 years. I am a musician and I strongly believe in creativity in and out of session
ideal_client: Many people can struggle with the gap between logical knowing, “I know I’m a good person” and emotional experience, “But I don’t feel like I am”. A primary focus of my approach is to close that gap and integrate outdated beliefs and patterns that no longer serve you. I work well with folks who have a foundational understanding of therapy or who have gotten stuck in the talk therapy circuit. I would ideally like to work clients who have an active interest in somatic based therapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide a safe and warm therapeutic space to explore your inner world, earn wisdom, and build stability. I specialize in trauma and PTSD using somatic/bottom-up approaches. I also specialize in working with LGBTQ+ folks, especially those exploring gender identity and gender transition. I practice Internal Family Systems (IFS), also known as “Parts work”. This process creates more self-leadership, more self-compassion, and deepens clarity. Another benefit to IFS is that it makes space of the ambivalence or hesitation of change. I have a very personable approach to the therapeutic process and believe it's important that you are treated and feel like a person in need of help, not seen as a diagnosis or label. My style incorporates Internal Family Systems (IFS), Attachment theory, and Brainspotting.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a therapist, I am in a unique position to see the impact and vulnerability of living life in our current world/society. You don't have to look very hard to find criticism, marginalization, and oppression in our daily lives. Through that understanding and earning my own wisdom I have adhered to certain beliefs and ideals. The frameworks I infuse into my work come from my identity in the LGBTQ+ community, being kink/queer positive, prioritizing social justice through a feminist lens, as well as practicing the HAES (Health At Every Size) model.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Also known as "Parts work", I have been practicing IFS for the past 4 years and have completely found my home in this theory. It uses such organic processes to identify different components or parts of your inner world. Some parts are protective in nature while other parts hold burdens and past traumas. IFS is a great process to help not only heal your underlying wounds but also incorporate the protectors along the way.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I have worked with trans and non-conforming folks for nearly a decade. I have worked with people in all stages of transition and exploration. I have years of experience in writing letters and helping clients pursue gender affirming care.

name: Deborah High
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I specialize in Trauma, Incest, Sexual Abuse, Violence in Relationships and Vicarious Trauma
ideal_client: I specialize in working with individuals, couples, families and groups dealing with trauma and violence in their lives. A majority of my clients are either struggling with childhood memories of emotional, physical and/or sexual abuse or they seek me out because they're currently in an abusive relationship and are feeling unhappy, scared or dissatisfied with their lives.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The act of doing therapy is a bit like tending to a garden; it takes diligence and care to achieve growth! It sounds challenging I know, but the outcomes and successes of working on yourself and your relationships far outweigh the negatives. We all have gardens that need occasional weeding and replanting, and when we are not taking care of ourselves, we can experience feelings of depression, anxiety, restlessness and frustration. In choosing to work with me, I will guide and encourage you by providing the necessary tools and resources that allow you to create a healthy and bountiful garden of your own.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In choosing to work with me, I will guide and encourage you by providing the necessary tools and resources that allow you to create a healthy and bountiful garden of your own. Counseling is a joint effort which cannot be successful without both of our commitments, hard work and courage. I also believe therapy provides a place to explore thoughts and feelings about relationships in your life as well as your relationship with yourself. This work allows you the opportunity to practice new ways of interacting with others in a safe and trusting atmosphere where you're not judged or criticized.

name: Kamiko McJimson
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi, I’m Kamiko, a Licensed Professional Counselor Associate (LPC-A) and the founder of Hope Heal Happiness Counseling.
ideal_client: I help teens, women, men, and couples heal from trauma, C-PTSD, anxiety, depression, and relationship struggles. Whether you're feeling stuck, overwhelmed, or disconnected, I offer a safe space to rediscover your confidence, joy, and purpose. At Hope Heal Happiness Counseling, we’ll work together to help you move from surviving to thriving. Let’s begin your journey toward healing and happiness—you're not alone.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I take an integrative approach to therapy, drawing on a variety of evidence-based techniques to help you heal, grow, and thrive. I use DBT and CBT to help you build emotional regulation, challenge negative thought patterns, and create healthier coping strategies. ACT empowers you to align with your values and find meaning, even in the face of adversity. EFT supports couples in improving emotional connection and communication. With psychodynamic and Jungian therapy, we explore unconscious patterns and unresolved past wounds to promote deep healing. I also use somatic techniques to address how trauma manifests in the body, helping you reconnect to your physical self. As a trauma-informed therapist, I prioritize safety and understanding, ensuring you feel empowered and supported every step of the way. Finally, IFS (Internal Family Systems) helps you navigate the different parts of yourself, fostering self-compassion and integration. No matter where you are on your journey I am here.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I deeply believe in the power of each individual to heal and grow, regardless of their background or struggles. As an LGBTQIA+ ally, I am committed to creating a safe and supportive space for all identities, where acceptance and understanding are foundational. I stand in solidarity with Black Lives Matter and advocate for racial justice, recognizing the profound impact that systemic inequality and trauma can have on mental health. I also proudly support minority communities, honoring the diversity of experiences that shape us. My approach to therapy is rooted in suicide prevention and self-harm intervention, recognizing the vital importance of safety and compassionate care. I prioritize creating a judgment-free space where people can open up about their pain and find pathways to hope and healing. Outside of therapy, I’m passionate about reading, music, and spending time with my family and pets. I believe in the resilience of the human spirit and am dedicated to helping others.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I take an eclectic approach to therapy, blending various treatment modalities to best suit your unique needs. Drawing from CBT, DBT, ACT, EFT, psychodynamic, Jungian, and somatic therapies, I tailor each session to address the root causes of your struggles and promote lasting healing. This flexible approach allows us to focus on your specific challenges, ensuring a personalized and effective path to growth, resilience, and overall well-being.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I approach therapy with a humanistic orientation, focusing on your innate potential for growth and self-actualization. By creating a safe, non-judgmental space, I help you explore your feelings, beliefs, and experiences. This approach emphasizes self-compassion, personal empowerment, and healing through empathy and understanding. Together, we’ll work to align your actions with your core values, fostering a deeper connection to yourself and a more meaningful, fulfilling life.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: In couples counseling, I integrate IFS, EFT, and the Gottman Method to help partners strengthen their emotional connection and communication. IFS allows couples to understand and heal inner conflicts, while EFT focuses on deepening emotional bonds. The Gottman Method offers practical tools to improve conflict resolution and intimacy. Together, we’ll work to rebuild trust, enhance communication, and create a more fulfilling, supportive partnership.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I specialize in trauma, PTSD, and C-PTSD, helping clients process and heal from the lasting effects of emotional, physical, or sexual trauma. My approach combines trauma-informed techniques like DBT, CPT, and somatic therapies to help you understand and regulate the body’s response to trauma. Together, we’ll explore the impact of past experiences, build safety, and work toward healing so you can reclaim your life, peace, and emotional resilience. Healing is possible.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I specialize in helping clients manage and reduce anxiety through evidence-based approaches like CBT, ACT, and DBT. I work with individuals to identify and challenge negative thought patterns, build coping skills, and develop mindfulness practices. Together, we’ll explore the root causes of your anxiety, increase emotional regulation, and create a path to lasting calm, clarity, and resilience in your daily life. You don't have to face anxiety alone.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I help individuals navigate and heal from depression using CBT, ACT, and psychodynamic therapy. By exploring underlying thought patterns and emotions, we work together to shift negative beliefs, improve mood, and rebuild a sense of purpose. I focus on empowering clients to re-engage with life, set achievable goals, and reconnect with their values. Healing from depression is a process, and I’m here to support you every step of the way.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I specialize in helping individuals navigate the complex emotions of loss and grief, whether from death, divorce, or major life changes. Using trauma-informed and psychodynamic approaches, I support clients in processing their feelings, honoring their grief, and finding ways to heal. Together, we’ll explore your unique experience and develop coping strategies to help you move through grief with compassion, while eventually finding peace and hope for the future.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in helping couples navigate relationship and marriage challenges, using EFT and CBT to improve communication, rebuild trust, and deepen emotional connection. Whether you're dealing with conflict, intimacy issues, or life transitions, I create a safe space to explore underlying concerns and foster mutual understanding. Together, we’ll work on strengthening your bond, enhancing emotional intimacy, and creating a healthier, more fulfilling partnership.

name: Alexandra Harrington
title: Student Counselor
intro: I believe one of the bravest things you can do is ask for help.
ideal_client: Taking the first step toward counseling can feel intimidating, and it’s perfectly normal to feel uncertain or overwhelmed by life’s challenges. Whether you're facing relationship struggles, navigating a major life transition, or feeling weighed down by stress or emotional pain, it’s important to know that you don’t have to face these challenges alone. I understand that reaching out for support takes courage, and I'm here to meet you with empathy and a nonjudgmental approach.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In therapy, my approach is rooted in Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) because it helps clients deeply connect with their emotions and understand the root of their struggles, whether they relate to relationships, personal transitions, or past wounds. EFT, combined with other therapeutic tools, provides a space where we can safely explore your emotional experience, helping you to heal, find clarity, and cultivate stronger connections with yourself and others. Whether you're healing from a relationship, managing stress, or trying to navigate significant life changes, we’ll work together to find strategies that are unique to your needs and values, empowering you to feel more present and connected in your life.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I may be a good fit for you if you’re looking for a therapist who brings warmth, curiosity, and a nonjudgmental presence to the work. I support individuals, couples, and families who are navigating relationship challenges, life transitions, or feeling overwhelmed by stress and emotion. My style is collaborative and compassionate—I’ll meet you where you are and walk alongside you as we explore what’s getting in the way of feeling more grounded, connected, and at ease. If you’re seeking a space where you can be yourself, feel understood, and move at your own pace, I’d be honored to support you on your journey.

name: Colleen Burke-Sivers, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am honored to be a therapist because I get to know people as their most genuine selves. I enjoy supporting people to a richer life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is straightforward and genuine. For those who like therapy terms, I am a Humanistic practitioner. I build a secure and trusting connection with each person and help them to foster these kinds of connections with the people in their lives. I have a unique ability to put people at ease in the therapy sessions and to work to uncover the stumbling blocks that are keeping them from living full and satisfying lives.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have 25 years of post-graduate experience, working in agencies, schools, hospitals and private practice. Some specialities include depression, anxiety, and other mood disorders. Some unique populations I like to work with include new parents, young adults, and people making major life transitions. However, I find I enjoy a variety of people and have worked with various populations and have experience with a wide range of issues.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: The psychodynamic approach takes into account the influences of your childhood on your current functioning and struggles. It looks at the person as partially a product of his or her original environment and helps each person understand how those influences are helping or hurting them to function today. The psychodynamic therapist will help you unlearn those influences that are no longer useful.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Humanistic therapy is based on Carl Rogers' theory of 'unconditional positive regard'. In other words, everyone is doing the best they can with what they have at the moment, and is accepted just as they are. Humanistic practitioners start from where the client is, and does not try to apply a 'one size fits all' approach, as each client will need a unique combination of approaches and techniques.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: Existential therapy explores meaning and purpose in life. It looks at deeper questions that people often wrestle: 'What is my purpose in life?', 'What is the true meaning of life?' 'What do I believe?' 'Why am I making the choices I am making?' 'What is the bigger picture.'

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Life is a series of losses, but most people are not prepared for the impact of significant losses on their psyche and sense of well-being. If you have recently experienced the loss of someone close, a relationship, or a dream, I will help you to come to terms with the loss and rediscover joy in life at a pace that will not rush you through your grief.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Your kindness and generosity are positive traits, but they often get out of control to the point that no one ever seems to be considerate of you. Codependency becomes a problem when your needs are never getting met in relationships, friendships, or even with acquaintances. I will help you look at the roots of your codependent behaviors and find new ways of relating in the world.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: The 21st century seems to be the age of anxiety. There is so much change happening all of the time. We are more aware than ever of the precarious state of the world and of our own human condition. Anxiety can be a useful tool or it can get out of control and be debilitating. I teach people to acknowledge and make sense of their anxiety while at the same time learn how to manage it effectively.

specialities.name: Bipolar
specialities.description: Bipolar disorder is such a difficult, confusing, and isolating illness. Those who suffer from it feel miserably depressed, alternating with boundless energy and ideas, irritability and impulsiveness. At times, you may feel ecstatic and other times, you have no idea why you ever felt that way. I help people make sense of their moods, swings, frantic thoughts, and unravel the mess of symptoms.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression robs a person of joy...and of perspective. When you are in a depressive state, everything seems difficult and meaningless. You believe that your view of reality is true and everyone else out there who seems happy are all looking through rose colored glasses. I have helped hundreds of people find their way out of this distorted and miserable state and back to their true selves.

name: Rhys Pasimio
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I represent a team that supports long term recovery support for every member, role, and relationship in the family unit.
ideal_client: New Pattern Counseling is an inter-disciplinary team supporting long term sobriety and trauma healing for individuals, couples, youth, and families. We specialize in the intersection between substance use, sex addiction, betrayal trauma, other trauma, and attachment distress. We promote healing and recovery through daily practices that transform a person's relationships to their body, to primary partners, children, peers, community, and seeks resilience through meaningful spirituality.

approaches.How We Can Help You: Our philosophy of healing is informed by modalities such as Internal Family Systems, The Task Model utilized among CSAT practitioners, Somatic Experiencing, Narrative Therapy, Existential Therapy, select tenets from 12 Step Philosophy, current day neuroscience, and other evidenced based practices. We are further informed by ideas derived from practitioners including Dan Siegel, Gabor Mate, Richard Schwartz, Patrick Carnes, Jenna Riemersma, Philip Mamalakis, and various spiritual practices. NPC places a high value on supporting counseling students, and registered associates working towards licensure. Supervision is provided, being informed by IFS, Narrative, Existential, and process oriented approaches. In individual and group settings, we help you train the muscle that is the focus of your attention. In this, we help you grow in awareness of all your inward parts, behavioral and emotional cycles, and learn to have healing conversations within yourself, and with others.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a Master of Arts in Counseling from Multnomah University. Major coursework included Integration of Psychology and Spirituality with emphases on Addictions Recovery and Social Concern. I completed additional coursework through Daystar Academy to earn my credential as Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor II. My graduate internship was at the Salvation Army Adult Rehabilitation Center, providing individual and group counseling. My post-graduate practice was at Cascadia Behavioral Healthcare providing dual diagnosis counseling. As a licensed professional, I practiced with Western Psychological & Counseling Services and taught in the Master of Arts Counseling Program at Multnomah University, prior to starting New Pattern Counseling.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Through curiosity, compassion, and a gentle courage, we can look inward and cultivate a network of healing relationships within our very own system.

specialities.name: Addiction Therapy
specialities.description: My addiction therapy is a combination of Internal Family Systems, Somatic, Narrative, ACT, and mindfulness approaches that emphasize daily practices to sustain the sober way of life. The goal of addictions therapy is for a person's whole life to be transformed, and all their relationships to be healed. This takes time, diligence, and community.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: Sometimes life presents us with problems that have no easy solution, impossible scenarios, profoundly disturbing questions, and unresolvable tensions. The problems seem to be endless and there is no escape in sight. In situations like these, sometimes the key to making it through is knowing we're not alone. ​​ I have hope that healing and abundant life can still be found on a difficult journey.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: My faith tradition of origin is Christianity. My spiritual formation has been highly influenced by eastern philosophies, postmodern thought and Orthodox Christianity. I will never preach, or pressure you to change, nor will I ever judge. However I believe that discussing spiritual, or ultimate things, is sometimes crucial to finding purpose and meaning in a chaotic world.

specialities.name: Sexual Addiction
specialities.description: Addiction to sex and pornography is a controversial issue, but one that I believe is very real, and one that is potentially highly destructive. Addressing a sexual addiction involves the most holistic counseling approach I have seen, as a sexual addiction is often related to other addictions, trauma, other mental health and relational challenges. I am committed to your holistic health.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a member of the community, I am committed to providing competent and culturally sensitive services to a frequently marginalized and underserved population. My approach is person-centered; I work to learn from you what you most need, then walk beside you as you grow into your ideal self.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: My training was in both alcohol and drug addiction. I've provided addictions counseling individually and in group settings in outpatient and inpatient facilities. I believe a dual-diagnosis approach is the most effective, because I recognize that most addicted people also have mental health challenges, and many many people with mental health challenges also use some chemical or behavior to cope.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma happens for many reasons and takes many forms. Whether or not you meet clinical criteria for PTSD, you likely have something painful in your story that can have unpredictable and distressing impact on your life in some way. This is especially true if you have addiction challenges. In order to provide holistic services, I believe a trauma informed and trauma focused approach is essential.

name: Katrina Thatcher
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: You're unique. Let's work together to untangle the social-emotional-behavioral knots that limit your ability to live fully.
ideal_client: I am a Certified Child-Centered Play Therapist and work with kids ages 3-8 yrs old and individual adults.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe you are the expert in your own life. I also believe that life is full of experiences that shape the way we perceive ourselves and relate to others, sometimes creating patterns difficult to untangle on our own. As a counselor, my primary focus is to support you in untangling these social-emotional-behavioral knots that limit your ability to fully embrace and accept your beautiful, unique self. I approach the counseling process as a means for you to better understand yourself and your relationships through the collaborative relationship that exists between client and counselor.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Play is kids’ most natural form of communication. Toys are to kids what words are to adults. Play Therapy, like counseling for adults, lets kids express their feelings and process their experiences in order to develop more effective strategies for managing their worlds.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: In our fast-paced, social-media-saturated, and achievement-driven society many adults and children struggle with anxiety. I am passionate about helping both children and adults build trust in their capacity to navigate life's challenges.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have special training in child development, parenting support and Child-Centered Play Therapy (CCPT), an evidence-based treatment approach for working with children ages 3-10. I have experience working with children, and their families, facing social, emotional, or behavioral challenges, or life transitions.

name: Kelli Warmouth
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm a LMHC, licensed in both WA and UT, with a M.E in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, emphasis in Sports Performance/Psychology.
ideal_client: I specialize in helping individuals with anxiety, depression, PTSD, ADHD, performance anxiety (common in artists and athletes), burnout, and grief. If you're feeling overwhelmed by trauma, life stage changes, a faith transition, college shifts, a new ADHD diagnosis, day-to-day stress, or challenges related to the female or LGBTQIA+ experience, I’d be privileged to be your therapist.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work is tailored to meeting you where you're at, and offering evidence-based compassionate services to help guide you toward your own powerful insight. It is your hour, and one that I strive to feel authentic, affirming, and non-judgmental. If you are trying to achieve better balance, peace, and clarity in life, I will provide the space and tools for you to be successful. In our sessions, we will use powerful tools, including Internal Family Systems, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Feminist Multicultural Therapy, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, to help you make positive changes and feel more joy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My work as a therapist is informed and oriented from a multicultural and social justice informed lens. I am a supporter and ally of the Black Lives Matter Movement and the LGBTQIA+ community, both in and out of my work as a mental health provider. From this lens, I believe we all operate within systems of the world around us. It is necessary then to consider the impact of these systems on our mental health and on our stories; whether these systems strengthen and instill power and wisdom within, or if they oppress and create barriers and pain. Together, we will zoom out and consider the ways your experiences are shaped by the world around you, and we will zoom in to understand the parts of yourself that are tired, hurting, and in need of compassion. By taking this 3-D view of yourself, you can expect to gain clarity, self-compassion, and direction toward greater happiness, healing, and peace.

name: beth rossi
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Welcome, thanks for stopping by!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I enjoy working with motivated adults with a focus on the importance of awareness, interdependence and communication. My work with adult individuals is sometimes motivated by challenging social constructions. I use a solution focused approach with behavioral, narrative and mindfulness interventions to support client treatment goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My husband and I (and my Pomeranian Nico) moved to Oregon from NYC in 2006. I immediately began working in social services. During my early career, I was fortunate enough to be able to work with local agencies serving marginalized populations. The goals were to support client safety and encourage general health and wellness. I continue to work from this model while collaborating on therapeutic goals with my outpatient clients. I served as an Addictions Counselor and Supervisor in residential treatment settings while attending Portland State University where I received my graduate degree in social work.

name: Joe Gianotti
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi! My name is Joe Gianotti (he/him) and I am a Professional Counseling Associate registered with the state or Oregon
ideal_client: As a counselor, I am here not to give advice or to tell you what you should be doing, but to provide new insights and frameworks to assist you during our work together. Through our collaboration, we will work through your concerns and problems and explore possible changes you can implement in your life, while acknowledging your sources of strength and resiliency.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: During my clinical experience, I have encountered working with issues around anxiety, depression, trauma, men’s issues, and social anxiety. I emphasize the importance of rapport and trust building, and believe that counseling can be effective and beneficial if a strong therapeutic relationship is formed.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Life can be full of stress, grief, and suffering, and as human beings, it can be challenging for us to navigate through all of the negative thoughts, emotions, and experiences that we encounter. Coming from a Humanistic and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy background, my approach to psychotherapy focuses on getting to know you and your unique experience so that we as a team can find better ways for you to live the life that you want to live. I believe that you are the expert of your own experience and I hope to create a space where you can authentically express yourself in a safe environment that is free of judgment.

name: Susan Evans, PsyD
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Welcome! I'm a clinical psychologist with over 18 years experience working in psychotherapy.
ideal_client: A variety of circumstances can lead us to seek psychotherapy. Sometimes it may be longstanding, difficult emotions, or perhaps painful memories brought you here. There may be a sudden loss, or a life-change that prompts you to seek the understanding and compassion that psychotherapy can bring. I work with people who seek relief, reflection, and insight. I believe that, when supported, we all have the ability to heal and grow, and we can know more emotional contentment, resilience and connection.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work in a collaborative style, incorporating techniques and theories from psychodynamic, humanistic, cognitive behavioral theories with the research on development, attachment and the neurobiological impact of trauma. Please use the link to go to my website where there is more info. And please free to contact me for more info.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received my doctoral degree over 15 yeas ago from the Wright Institute in Berkeley, CA and I am a licensed clinical psychologist in Oregon. In my training and working years, was lucky enough to be able to learn from gifted clinicians and teachers. I had the good fortune to train at UCSF at the AIDS Health Project, UCSF Child Trauma Research Project, and at the San Francisco Psychotherapy Research Group. I've since received advanced training in Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), EMDR, Buddhist Psychology, and PTSD treatments. When not working, I can be found walking my dogs, spending time with my family, digging in the dirt (both metaphorically and literally!) and dreaming of road trips.

name: Tara Sanderson
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: Dr. Sanderson and Associates is a multidisciplinary teaching practice that provides individual, group and psychological assessment.

name: Michael Pollet
title: Social Worker
intro: I welcome humor in therapy and offer a warm, judgment-free environment where you are safe to explore the uncomfortable.
ideal_client: I work with people navigating anxiety, depression, grief, and relationship challenges. You may feel stuck in patterns you’re ready to break free from but unsure how to start. Using the collaborative LifeMaps treatment plan, we will explore how your past has shaped your present and work to build self-awareness, uncover strengths, and foster change. My experience as a gay man raised in the South gives me a unique perspective that informs my understanding of cultural and family dynamics.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our work begins with building a strong therapeutic relationship. Together, we’ll uncover the unconscious conflicts and patterns maintaining your struggles and explore the underlying causes of your challenges. This process promotes the insight needed to interact more effectively with the world and develop strategies to manage the forces shaping your choices.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My goal is to create a space where you are safe to explore the uncomfortable. I welcome humor in therapy and offer a warm, judgment-free environment, where we can work together to navigate challenges, uncover your strengths, and make meaningful changes.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: The premise of psychodynamic therapy is making the unconscious (what is not readily in our awareness) conscious. The techniques of this modality help you gain insight into your inner processes and behaviors that you may not be consciously aware of. This process helps us become aware of patterns that occur in our behaviors, thoughts, emotions, and relationships. This theory also holds the belief that our past experiences greatly impact our current experiences and relationships.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: We will collaborate in a safe, supportive, and non-judgmental space where you can freely share your thoughts and emotions. Together, we will explore and uncover the underlying causes of your anxiety, fostering deeper self-awareness. This insight will empower you to make intentional changes in your behaviors and emotional responses, helping to alleviate anxiety symptoms and improve your overall well-being over time.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: We will collaborate to uncover the emotional patterns and past experiences that may be shaping your current feelings. This process is not just about understanding but also about healing. By bringing these underlying dynamics into awareness, you can begin to untangle the weight of unresolved emotions, rediscover your inner strengths, and gradually move toward a more fulfilling and balanced life.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a gay man, I bring lived experience to my work with people in the LGBTQIA+ community. We will examine the roots of shame, guilt, and other challenging emotions that may be tied to societal expectations, family dynamics, or past relationships. By uncovering these underlying patterns and the impact they have on your sense of self, we can work toward reducing the weight of these emotions.

name: Sharon Hale
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Hi! I'm a trauma-informed, relational therapist.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I am certified in Emotionally Focused Couples Therapy and Emotionally Focused Individual Therapy

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I am trained in NeuroAffective Relational Model, which is a somatic approach to therapy.

name: Shayla Pellerin
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I'm a compassionate counselor dedicated to empowering individuals on their journey to well-being.
ideal_client: My practice centers on affirming LGBTQ+ individuals. I specialize in identity exploration, coming out, relationship dynamics, and addressing mental health concerns like anxiety and depression, often exacerbated by societal stigma. I offer a safe, empathetic space for gender transition support and navigating minority stress, fostering resilience and authentic living.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to helping is grounded in empathy and collaboration. I believe in empowering individuals to discover their own strengths and solutions, rather than providing prescriptive answers. I prioritize creating a safe, non-judgmental space where clients feel heard and understood. Utilizing a variety of therapeutic techniques, tailored to individual needs, I aim to facilitate self-awareness, promote healing, and foster personal growth. I am committed to culturally competent care, respecting diverse backgrounds and experiences. My goal is to guide clients on their unique journeys towards a more fulfilling and authentic life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I deeply value authenticity, compassion, and social justice. I believe in the inherent worth and dignity of every individual, and I am committed to creating a safe and inclusive space for all. I strive to be an ally to marginalized communities, and I actively support the LGBTQ+ community, recognizing the unique challenges faced by individuals within this population. I believe in the power of empathy and understanding to bridge divides and promote healing. My dedication to cultural competency stems from a belief in the importance of acknowledging and respecting diverse backgrounds and experiences. I am committed to ongoing self-reflection and education to ensure that my practice is aligned with these values. My goal is to empower individuals to live authentically and thrive, free from judgment and discrimination. My drive to become a counselor was born from a desire to create a safe space for people to find their own strength, and to help them build a life where they feel understood.

name: Julianna Vermeys
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: It is my intention to create a nurturing, collaborative therapy experience through ethically integrated somatic and mindfulness practices
ideal_client: Are you aware of the struggles and traumas that leave you feeling uncertain and overburdened by the responsibility of supporting yourself? Do you know that there is a path towards freedom of oppression and limitations in your beliefs, and in your connection to yourself, but you need help, support and insight to help you feel worthy, cared for and full of life? I provide a mindfulness-based therapy experience as a way of being together, presently with your experiences, non-judgmentally.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide individuals, families, and teens the opportunity to safely and confidently explore your life experiences and help you feel whole and well. My therapy practice offers an opportunity to become accepting and empowered about your life experience, your behavior and choices. I offer thoughtful, collaborative, compassionate, embodied, client-centered therapy. Part of my practice includes calling attention to how the body is responding to narrative, discussion, emotion and using trauma-informed, somatic-based skills to support the body in the therapy process. By being in relationship with the body, one can learn to have a comprehensive understanding of one self so that change is holistic and intrinsic. I aim to create connection and belonging that supports the practice and process of awareness, acceptance and healing.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I am dedicated to offering an ethical and compassionate trauma-informed, somatic-integrated, honest, thoughtful and unconditional counseling experience. A mindful approach to any therapeutic technique or theory can offer healing and empowering results; improve your mood, health, ambition and relationships. In addition to my counseling credentials, I completed 500-hr Yoga training and have taught yoga and meditation since 2003. I offer private, couples and small group yoga when therapeutically appropriate. Yoga is one of several types of mindfulness-based tools I offer in my practice. I acknowledge as a white woman in the US my cultural appropriation of practices outside of my culture and heritage. I provide Clinical Supervision to counselor interns pursuing their LPC license in the state of Oregon. My intention as a supervisor is to offer a space for one to consider their role as healer, mental health counselor, and role in the greater community of health and wellness for all.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Each of us has the potential to be fully present by utilizing the vast communication potential of the body. I am highly skilled at utilizing the awareness of the sensation in one's body to guide a richer understanding of one's emotions, reactions and experience during therapy.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness helps develop self-awareness by slowing down to experience how the body, emotions and mind feel. In relationship with the body, one can learn to feel safe, calm down the mind and shift emotions. In the presence of a skilled therapist, mindfulness can be used to heal, improve and change your life. I have studied mindfulness for 20 years, incorporating it in all aspects of therapy.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I believe our attachments to our first caregivers offer us a window into how we feel and function in our current relationships and life endeavors. Using narrative and discussion to understand the complex web of attachment-based emotions and experience in the world, I can help you feel empowered and in charge of your life choices and behaviors.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have decades of experience treating and exploring with tools to alleviate debilitating feelings of anxiety and worry. I work with you to develop a strengths-based understanding of your worry. Coupled with evidence-based deliberate present-oriented practices, can provide lasting effectiveness with physiological reduction of stress in the body and mind.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I am dedicated to the conscious experience and expression of loss and grief both personally and professionally. Using thoughtful, compassionate, empathic therapy in conjunction with mindful somatic awareness, I can help you feel less traumatized by the pain of major or minor loss and grief. My hope is that my work with you will help you integrate your experience into a richer and more profound life right now.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am trained in trauma-informed counseling, a specialized skill set to help you safely examine and integrate the trauma of your life without re-traumatization (using a framework of understanding the nervous system and it's response to stress and trauma). With compassionate, gentle, attentive guidance, I will assist your reclaiming and harmonizing the present body and mind, daily skills to help you heal.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: In conjuction with my compassionate, collaborative, and client-centered approach to thearpy, I look for opportunities to illuminate moments of peace, joy and connection in life and our therapeutic relationship. Depression treatment can be a safe exploration of the richness of your emotions and respect for your depth of experience.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I use mindfulness tools, including somatic movement and awareness in therapy work with couples to offer a unique approach to sorting through and healing within relationship and marriage. I have expertise in family dynamics and systems to cultivate clarity and empowerment around family and partner relationships.

name: Sarah Martin
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am clinical social worker in private practice, and currently I provide tele-health services. I work with youth and adults.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I take a strengths-based and client centered approach with a strong social justice framework. I utilize language of narrative therapy to externalize issues and develop skills to overcome barriers. I use creativity to engage with people and establish a meaningful connection before moving forward with the therapeutic process.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a licensed clinical social worker with 7 years of experience in community mental health settings prior to private practice. I specialize in working with adolescents who are navigating the transition to adulthood as well as members of the LGBTQI community.

name: Griffin Oakley
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I’m Griffin Oakley, a trauma-informed therapist offering a safe, affirming space for healing, growth, and self-discovery. Let’s talk! 💙
ideal_client: I work with individuals navigating anxiety, depression, trauma, self-esteem, and identity exploration, including LGBTQIA+ clients and those healing from childhood trauma or abuse. Many of my clients feel stuck, overwhelmed, or disconnected and are seeking a safe, affirming space to process their experiences and build a more fulfilling life. Whether you're struggling with past wounds, navigating life transitions, or just need support, I'm here to help you heal and grow.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is compassionate, collaborative, and tailored to you. I believe that healing happens in a safe, nonjudgmental space where you feel truly seen and heard. Using an integrative approach, I draw from CBT, DBT, ACT, Gestalt, and Solution-Focused Therapy to create a plan that fits your unique needs. Whether you need help managing anxiety, processing trauma, exploring identity, or building self-esteem, I’ll meet you where you are with warmth and understanding. I focus on helping you uncover patterns, develop self-awareness, and build practical coping skills so you can navigate life’s challenges with more confidence and clarity. I work at your pace, offering both gentle guidance and empowering challenges to help you grow. My goal is to help you feel more connected to yourself, your emotions, and your values, so you can move forward with greater self-compassion and resilience. You don’t have to do this alone—I’m here to help.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As a therapist, my work is guided by values of compassion, affirmation, and empowerment. I create a safe, nonjudgmental space where you can explore your thoughts and feelings freely. I honor your unique lived experience, recognizing the impact of trauma, oppression, and identity on mental health. My approach is client-centered, using CBT, DBT, ACT, and Gestalt to help you find practical tools while building self-awareness. Therapy is not about fixing; it’s about empowering you to heal and grow at your own pace. I focus on helping you trust yourself, develop resilience, and move forward with hope and self-compassion. You deserve support, and I’m here to walk beside you, guiding you toward a fulfilling, authentic life.

name: Susan Lehman
title: Reverend
intro: Seeking a spiritual counselor? Know yourself as a powerful creative spiritual being!
ideal_client: My ideal clients want to grow spiritually as well as heal themselves. I have a great deal of experience working with the inner child, as well as children and parents. I prescribe to the theory that the client is capable of finding their own answers within, while I'm the guide on the side.

approaches.My Background and Approach: With over 40 years of experience working with families and children and a licensed minister, I have a wealth of practical knowledge and education to support you in unconditional love and without judgement. Willing to do Phone/Facetime/Zoom sessions at clients' request. Office in Northeast near Alberta Arts district.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have 40+ years of experience/training in Family Services, Certified Positive Discipline Training (C.P.D.T), Parent Education, Holistic and Rapid Transformation (H.A.R.T), Creative Therapy, Evolved Parenting and Co-Active Coaching models, Metaphysics, Infant/Child "whispering", crystal communication & spiritual counseling. I also incorporate shamanic practices and crystal healing as needed. I am a member of the LGBQ community. INCOME BASED REDUCED RATES.

specialities.name: Accelerated Resolution Therapy
specialities.description: I work with crystals and their energies to help create and amplify personal healing and intentions.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I have an eclectic approach, using various modalites, including traditional and spiritual/shamanic methods.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: I have received training at the Coaches Training Institute in San Rafael, CA in the co-active coaching model.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Working with parents/adults as well as children, sometimes there is an inner child who had to deal with abuse of all kinds. I can help you connect with them and bring healing.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: With over 40 years of experience working with families and children, I have a variety of techniques of ways to support parents. I am also a CPDT, Certified Positive Discipline Trainer.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: There are no fully 'functional' families, particularly families of origin. I can work with you to reduce power struggles and conflict with all family members.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I work with parents on really 'listening' to what the child truly needs. My first published book is "Eat, Play, Poop? Is that all there is?" available at sagesusan.com.

name: Bronwen Flores
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Bronwen Flores is a compassionate and highly skilled Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Bronwen Flores is a PMHNP-BC with over 12 years of extensive nursing experience, not including six years of dedicated service, and two deployments, as a combat medic in the United States Air Force. She specializes in integrative psychiatric care, seamlessly blending the strengths of both Western and Eastern medicine to promote holistic wellness for her clients. She is currently finalizing her Doctorate of Nursing Practice (DNP) at the University of South Alabama, where she obtained her Master of Science in Nursing (MSN) as a PMHNP. She also holds an ADHD Clinical Services Provider Certification and is in the process of completing her Integrative Medicine Certification at the IPI Integrative Psychiatry Institute. Bronwen also holds a certification: Mastering the Essentials: A Hands-On Introduction to Ketamine Administration, awarded by the American Society of Ketamine Physicians Psychotherapists & Practitioners (ASKP3).

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Her military tenure and bedside nursing career experience have profoundly shaped her approach to mental health, allowing her to understand the complexities of trauma and its long-lasting effects on individuals. Bronwen is deeply invested in fostering a patient-centered environment where collaboration and open communication are paramount. By partnering with clients, she aims to empower individuals on their journey to mental wellness, ensuring that each person feels valued, heard, and supported throughout their treatment.

name: Nicole Kammerlocher
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I help clients overcome relationship dissatisfaction and sexual difficulties of all kinds.
ideal_client: From exploring your sexuality or gender to working through relational roadblocks, I'd love to be there to help you through. Many of my clients are struggling with their relationship to sex, their relationship to sexuality, or their relationship to another person. If any of this sounds familiar, please reach out - we can schedule a free 30 minute consultation to talk about what you are going through, and if I would be a good fit for you.
