approaches.My Approach to Helping: Struggling with issues around sex, relationships, gender, and sexuality can be isolating because they seem private - you don't talk about them much, and it can seem like no one else is struggling the same way you are. You aren't alone in your struggle, and my top priority is to make sure you feel welcomed and accepted in our sessions. I use many different therapeutic techniques, but work primarily from Feminist, Cognitive Behavioral, and Emotionally Focused frameworks. I specialize in working with clients exploring their gender and sexual orientation, low sexual desire, and experiencing sexual disconnection. In our sessions, we will work together to explore your current relationship to sex and make a plan to build the relationship you want to have with sex through practical skills, tools, and deeper discussions about what sex means for you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I wanted to become a sex therapist because growing up as a queer kid in Oklahoma, it seemed like all of the messages about sexuality focused on why it's bad and how we should feel ashamed of sex. I saw how this hurts our relationships with ourselves and partners. I understand the challenges created when we feel like it’s not okay to talk about sex openly and honestly. I obtained my BA in Psychology and MS in Mental Health Counseling from Oklahoma State University and am currently training to become a Certified Sex Therapist through the California Institute of Integral Studies. For me, the most rewarding part of sex therapy is helping people build relationships with themselves and their partners that celebrate their authentic sexuality, and I would be honored to help you create deeper connections and explore your fullest sexual life.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I have received training in Emotionally Focused Couples therapy, which has some of the best outcomes for those struggling with relational issues. This therapy focuses on how we show up in relationships, and how we can show up differently and change the tune of a relationship from conflict to connection.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotionally Focused Therapy is based in attachment theory and focuses on recognizing how we experience our emotions, what we do with them, and how we can connect more effectively and fully with our partners.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Throughout my training I have focused on using CBT as a focal point for understanding how we struggle with mental health and wellness, and how we can work through these struggles. I also use many other modalities, and believe that it is my job as a therapist to be flexible and meet you where you are as far as what techniques work and which ones don't.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a queer person, it is important to me to create space in my practice to serve my community. Being queer myself does not mean that I share your experience - I almost certainly do not - but as I have trained to grow my abilities as a counselor, I have always focused my efforts around how I can use my knowledge to help my community with both general and LGBTQ specific struggles.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: As a queer person, it is important to me to create space in my practice to serve my community. Gender is a unique and complicated space, and no two people's process around their gender identity will look the same. Throughout my training, I have focused on working to apply what I have learned to help people navigate gender.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I am currently working towards certification by the American Association of Sexuality Educators, Counselors, and Therapists. This is one of the most thorough and rigorous certifications for professionals seeking to specialize in sex therapy, and through this process I have and continue to receive training on helping people with specific sexual concerns.

name: Colleen Van Zante
title: Student Counselor
intro: I am dedicated to empowering clients to uncover their inner resilience.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I lead with genuine empathy and a deeply inquisitive spirit, engaging directly and authentically. I strive to understand my clients’ concerns and worldviews within the context of societal, cultural, and contextual factors. Whether you have been in therapy for years or this is your first time, I welcome the opportunity to walk alongside you on this journey. I am committed to fostering an open and supportive atmosphere.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I am deeply committed to helping individuals navigate emotional challenges and strengthen their relationships. My interest in Emotionally Focused Therapy reflects my passion for understanding the role of emotions in healing and connection. I hope to foster emotional resilience, guiding clients toward healthier interactions and empowering them to create lasting, positive change in their lives.

name: Eric Nielson
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Welcome! I work with individuals (adults and teens), couples and families.
ideal_client: A basic guiding principle in my work is that, when we are able to really see and accept where we are, and who we are, we begin to heal and grow.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Overall, my style is what would be called humanistic and holistic, which means I see you as a whole person, with your own inner wisdom and innate health, who is in need of some guidance and assistance at this time in your life. It also means that I see the relationship between us as an important part of what will contribute to your growth. As such, I strive to create an open, safe and trusting relationship and setting for you to explore your life and experiences in a way that is authentic, healing and inspiring. A basic guiding principle in my work is that, when we are able to really see and accept where we are, and who we are, we begin to heal and grow. My way of working is informed by a number of therapeutic approaches, the primary ones being Gestalt Therapy and attachment-based therapies including Emotionally Focused Therapy, or "EFT" (for couples and families). I integrate trauma-based therapeutic approaches when this is helpful for my clients.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I graduated from Vassar College and then worked and studied at Esalen Institute in Big Sur, California, where I studied Gestalt Therapy and Gestalt Awareness Practice. I did my graduate training at the Institute of Transpersonal Psychology in Palo Alto, California before settling with my family in the Portland area. I have over 15 years experience doing individual, couple and family counseling. I started my career working with children and teens in a residential psychiatric setting. I have worked in a foster care agency providing counseling for foster children and foster families, and worked in community mental health providing intensive in-home therapy to support families going through crisis. As I transitioned to private practice work, I also focused more on working with couples and individuals, which have now become the main focuses of my practice.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: One of my primary influences is Gestalt Therapy and Gestalt Awareness Practice (a practice based in the Gestalt Therapy developed by Fritz Perls, and evolved by Richard and Christine Price). A primary tenet of Gestalt therapy is that, as we are able to come to greater awareness and acceptance of our experience in this moment, we allow the possibility of real and lasting growth and change.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I integrate Emotionally Focused Therapy (or, 'EFT') in my work with couples and with families. I have done training with Sue Johnson, one of the progenitors of EFT, and am engaged in on-going supervision and training in this therapeutic model.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: As the writer and teacher Stephen Levine put it, “To heal is to touch with love that which was previously touched by fear.” A basic guiding principle in my work is that, when we are able to really see and accept where we are, and who we are, we begin to heal and grow. There is a trust I have found in this, that if we attend to what comes up in this place, it will lead us through.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I have a background in transpersonal psychology and spiritual studies, and a genuine love and appreciation for the many spiritual traditions of the world. If you are interested in incorporating your spiritual path into our work, let me know, and we can talk about how to bring this into to the therapeutic work we are doing together.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: A large part of my practice is working with couples. I think this work is particularly meaningful, as it gets to the heart of our ability to love and be loved. In my work with couples, I work primarily from a model called Emotionally Focused Couple Therapy (often referred to simply as “EFT”). What I love about this model, simply put, is that it works. EFT has been well researched and has been demonstrated to be very effective with couples to facilitate lasting change.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Working with families is very close to my heart. For most of us, the family is our most fundamental unit of relationship and community. My work with families draws from Emotionally Focused Family Therapy and Dyadic Developmental Psychotherapy, both of which are based in an attachment perspective.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: One of the threads that has run through my work throughout my career is working with parents. I also have extensive experience working with adoptive and foster families, and working with families with children who struggle with things like Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD), difficulty with anxiety, anger or impulse control, and attachment issues.

name: Karel Chan
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Human first, therapist second. Mindful, holistic, and spiritually-influenced approaches to heal anxiety, depression, shame, and trauma.
ideal_client: Life feels hard for you right now. Maybe you're going through something painful — loss, breakup or divorce, family issues — or maybe it feels like no matter what's happening, you can't stop worrying and blaming yourself. You feel overwhelmed by emotions and often it seems like you're losing control. You tend to overthink everything and want to learn how to get out of your head and into the present. Together, let's explore the mind's landscape, change these patterns, and find your inner peace.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Mindfulness is the practice of observing everything that arises in the mind, including all of its deeply ingrained negative thoughts and feelings, without judgment or trying to either avoid or hold onto any of it. In doing this, you realize that you are more than the mind and that you're in control of how you respond to it. Together we work to help you overcome the negative thoughts, painful emotions, and unhealthy patterns that prevent you from living the life you were meant to live. Through mindfulness, cognitive behavioral therapy, insight and inner child work, and a compassionate humanistic approach, I guide you in understanding how and why the mind works the way it does, then learning how to train — yes, train! — the mind to respond to pain and life stressors in an empowered, confident, and healthy way.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I see my role of therapist as nothing short of a blessing. To walk on your path alongside you and witness your deepest heart is an unparalleled gift. I have the requisite degrees, trainings, and certifications to allow me to call myself a therapist, but I don’t consider those to be my true qualifications. Through my own emotional and spiritual work, I've healed from years of anxiety, depression, and complex childhood trauma. Today, I am grounded, focused, confident, and most importantly, at peace with what I have been both given and denied in this lifetime. It is my own process of falling apart, healing, and transformation that has enabled me to hold expansive presence for you, your story, your most exquisite pain. I understand suffering, how it plagues you, and how to meet you in it with unwavering compassion to guide you to do the same. Everything I bring to you in therapy, I have studied, practiced, and experienced for myself. I live my work, and I’m honored to join you in yours.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness is a two-pronged skill of awareness: noticing something arising, and nonjudgment: allowing it to simply be what it is. In learning, strengthening, and repeating this practice, we become expansive in our ability to be with any experience that life brings us, without feeling clinched, panicked, or pressured to "prepare for the worst." We also become deeply loving and compassionate of our humanness, no matter what we are thinking, feeling, or doing.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Our adult relationships reflect our earliest relationships in life with our families of origin. Whatever the quality of those relationships, they taught us powerful messages about love, how it's given, and sometimes what we need to do in order to receive it. If love was absent, inconsistent, or highly conditional, then we move through life feeling a persistent lack of belonging, no matter who we are with. Understanding that these messages are not true can open us to freely give and receive love.

specialities.name: Contemplative
specialities.description: We are often weighed down by self-defeating messages and interpretations of painful experiences, and think that there must be some answer "out there" to feeling better and being happy. I believe that the answer is deep within you, buried underneath all those messages and interpretations. We will work together to excavate the outer layers that have formed over the years and investigate the true heart, spirit, and wisdom that begins to shine through.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is the mind's way of trying to achieve peace and safety using thoughts and intellect to exert control, find solutions, and fix what's "wrong." The problem with this is that very few things require solutions, or are actually "wrong" or truly within our control. Peace and safety, though, are innate human needs, so the journey is learning to step away from thinking and into a space of courageously being with feelings of fear and unrest, building an inner strength and wisdom that we trust.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: How we learn to seek and then engage in relationships is formed in our earliest experiences with others: our families of origin, parents, caregivers. Whatever our environment tells us we need to do in order to be loved — even if it hurts or actually feels bad — we do. We will find and nourish those tender, scared, confused spots within you, so that you can embark on seeking relationships already feeling whole, ready to give and receive love courageously and open-heartedly.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Rather than see you through a framework of pathology or mental illness, in need of treatment or problem-solving, I see you as a human who has lost touch with their spiritual being and is feeling the anguish, isolation, and helplessness that comes from that disconnect. I will guide you to create room to listen and attune to the deeper truths of who you are, who you have always been.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: It is our human nature to change and seek growth; it is also our human nature to cling to sameness and fear the unknown. We often search outside of ourselves for solutions and direction to ensure that we are making the "right" choice as we age and develop, when truly the answers live within us. By attuning to and connecting with the wisdom of our souls, we will find that the path of our growth reveals itself.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Self-esteem, to me, embodies all of the ways we attend to and treat ourselves: self-love, self-compassion, self-governance. Much of our suffering stems from ways that we, as a survival response to neglect or abandonment when young, have neglected or abandoned our selves. Only by turning toward the forgotten, disconnected self can we come back online with a fully embodied presence and an intact esteem for the whole self.

name: Tony Lash
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide counseling for adults experiencing depression, anxiety, relationship/interpersonal problems, difficult transitions, and grief.
ideal_client: Do you feel stuck in your relationships, friendships, career, or personal goals? Our emotional barriers often have their roots in strategies we learned early in life to get us through difficult or painful experiences with others. I love helping you uncover these issues, exploring how they affect you in the present, and helping create a road map for change. As stuck as we may feel sometimes, change is always possible!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We all have inner strengths to draw on in our quest for growth. A trusting and supportive therapeutic relationship can be one of the most powerful tools to tap into these strengths and use them to work toward your personal goals. I integrate Object Relations, Internal Family Systems, and Emotionally-Focused Couple's Therapy in my work, with the goal of providing you with a safe, accepting, and nurturing space to work through unhelpful patterns and develop new ways of relating to yourself and others. I earned both a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology (2017), and Master of Arts in Clinical Mental Health Counseling (2020) from Portland State University. I am currently a Licensed Professional Counselor Intern, and am supervised by Sarah Williams, MA, LMFT, and Deanna Cor, PhD, LPC.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I have always had a passion for what connects us to one another. For over 30 years I expressed this through music, both as a music producer and performing musician. The most meaningful musical work I did always came from the more intimate spaces, helping to create moments where an artist's emotions could connect most directly with listeners. As I explored ideas for a new career, counseling felt like the most natural evolution of what I had always tried to achieve through music: helping people bring powerful emotions, whatever they may be, to the foreground. As a counselor, my greatest joy comes from providing the safety and trust needed for people to engage with and accept the parts of us we may find painful, neglected, or rejected so that we can carry them forward with us with compassion and validation.

name: Jessi Dey
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Offering affirming and supportive individual and relationship therapy with a warm, open and straightforward approach.
ideal_client: When you're in the middle of a hard decision..."Should I stay and commit to this relationship or should I get out now?”, "Look for a new job or go back to school?”, "Have a baby???" —those are among the moments that it can really help to reach out to an experienced therapist. And whether you’re dealing with a difficult dilemma or life transition or a more long-standing issue such as learning to better manage depression or anxiety, I'd be delighted to help you work through that hard spot.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I received my master’s degree in counseling from Portland State University in 2008, and I opened my private practice later that same year. The focus in my master’s program was on couples, marriage and family counseling. I completed both a practicum and an internship through Portland, State University, where I counseled individuals, couples and families. Additionally, I provided counseling services at the YWCA counseling center in Portland, as an intern, and a volunteer and have maintained my busy private practice for over 15 years . I have had the opportunity to work with people from diverse backgrounds and people in nontraditional relationships of many kinds. My style is warm, open honest, straightforward, humorous, and non-judgemental. I find that counseling is often a process of unraveling early messages we may have received about ourselves and the world, figuring out where they originated, discarding those that are unhelpful and getting back in touch with who you really are.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Therapy is about having a caring, objective, involved listener who is invested in helping you to create meaningful and lasting change and difference in your life. I work to create an atmosphere of acceptance, safety, and hope in the counseling office. My goal is to create an environment in which people can trust me. I believe my philosophies and approach are inclusive, and can be effective with both individuals and couples, as well as with clients with backgrounds different from my own. I feel honored to be given the opportunity to hear my client’s stories, and witness as they make connections between the past and the present, and learn to listen to their inner voice, and accept themselves as they truly are. As this happens, people can begin living a more full and satisfying life.

name: Heidi Scanlan
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I specialize in working with couples, teens, and adults with the desire to gain insight, heal, and change.
ideal_client: Are you dealing with relationship troubles, stress, burnout, depression, or the lingering effects of trauma, and wanting to feel more at ease? Our work will be collaborative: blending my expertise with your unique lived experiences. Together, we’ll utilize skills based techniques and EMDR to help you reprocess the past and build resilience. Through this partnership, you’ll gain clarity and develop practical strategies for living with greater purpose, harmony, and emotional well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Heidi specializes in the use of Eye movement Desensitization Reprocessing (EMDR), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), and solution focused treatment. Heidi also utilizes mindfulness practices and EFT tapping with her clients. Heidi has been noted to have a very warm energy that is a joy to be around. She brings her quick wit and questioning spirit to every session. I specialize in working with adults who are navigating past trauma and distressing events. I provide a direct, results-oriented approach to help you achieve your goals more rapidly. Additionally, I offer specialized support for individuals in the postpartum phase, guiding them through the unique challenges that arise during this critical time.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Graduating from University of Washington in 2012 with her Masters in Social Work Heidi Scanlan is a Licensed Clinical Social Worker, therapist, clinical supervisor, and coach. Heidi has worked as a specialist in medical social work, mental health, and crisis services. Heidi is fascinated with the mind and body connection and each person’s ability to transform and become better versions of themselves. Heidi is also training as a pilates instructor and working towards certification as she believes so strongly in the healing harmony of mind and body. Heidi loves being a therapist because she enjoys seeing clients light up with insights about themselves and their situations that forever change them. In her off time Heidi values traveling to sunny places, spending time with her large extended family, trying new cuisine, learning about different cultures, and being immersed in nature.

name: Kati Lear
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: We will work together to empower you to build self-compassion and meaningful connection through time-limited, evidence‐based psychotherapy.
ideal_client: I am passionate about helping people adopt a kinder relationship with themselves and build connections and authenticity with others. I specialize in working with adults struggling with shame, self-criticism, social anxiety, and reactions to stressful life experiences. I am also passionate about helping people explore what matters to them as they consider identity or purpose-related struggles or questions and clarify goals or values.

approaches.My Background and Approach: As a licensed psychologist and active researcher, I practice evidence-based therapies that science has shown are effective, such as Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and Emotion Focused Therapy. Therapy is a big investment of time, resources, and energy. The scientific data suggest that, for most people, the largest gains from therapy usually occur relatively early on treatment, often within the first few months. Therefore, to help my clients make the most out of their investment in therapy, I work in a time-limited model. That means that I see clients for up to 20 sessions focused on a particular theme, struggle, or issue, as a foundation to make real and lasting change. During our time together I will help you identify unworkable patterns and make concrete changes in your life. Fundamentally, my work is about helping people develop kinder relationships with themselves and others and, in doing so, build meaningful, nourishing connections in their lives.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I recognize myself as someone who has experienced much privilege in my life. I continually work to uncover the ways in which my lived experiences, biases, and privileges limit my perspective and understanding of others. In therapy, I pay keen attention to how these aspects may be impacting my understanding of you and our relationship. I am committed to understanding the richness of your experience and believe you are the expert on your life. For therapy to be effective, it is essential you feel seen, understood, and valued. Together we will work to create a supportive and brave space for you to explore the changes you long to make in your life.

name: Demir Crone
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I believe in supporting your clarity, growth, and understanding. We work together collaboratively towards your goals. Virtual therapy only.
ideal_client: I work with a variety of issues- trauma, attachment issues, sexual challenges, anxiety, depression, mood disorders, life transitions, LGBTQ+, and more. I work with couples and have done training in Emotional Focused Therapy for Couples. I am currently doing trainings in ISTDP for Couples, ATSIP (sex therapy), and in the Developmental Model. With individuals, I draw primarily on Intensive Short Term Dynamic Psychotherapy (ISTDP)- a powerful psychodynamic approach designed to create lasting change

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work at Bridges to Well-Being. I have done training in Emotional Focused Therapy for Couples. I am currently doing trainings in ISTDP for Couples, ATSIP (sex therapy), and in the Developmental Model. With individuals, I draw primarily on Intensive Short Term Dynamic Psychotherapy (ISTDP)- a powerful psychodynamic approach designed to create lasting change. Fun fact: ISTDP is supported by over 140 and counting high quality studies. My primary modality has been shown repeatedly to help everything from trauma to treatment resistant depression to mood disorders.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I focus on one psychodynamic therapy in particular called Intensive Short Term Dynamic Psychotherapy (ISTDP). It is a highly effective therapy designed to work deeply and profoundly. Many clients comment on the insight and transformation provided by it. ISTDP is also supported by over 140 studies proving its efficacy across a wide variety of psychological diagnoses and issues.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Emotionally Focused Couples Therapy, ISTDP for Couples, and the Developmental Model. All excellent modalities to support you!

name: Cat Bice
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I provide evidence based therapy with a warm touch. My focus as a therapist is on treating trauma and healing relationships.
ideal_client: Many of my adult clients are often people who describe themselves as being “do-ers” who have difficulty slowing down to understand their internal world. Quite a few are medical professionals, first responders, and veterans who have worked hard to train themselves out of their emotional reactions because of the need to focus and perform in their work setting. My teen clients are typically struggling with the impacts of difficult of traumatic experiences.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have been involved in mental health work since volunteering as a teen and my work has spanned a wide range of settings. My professional career started in the emergency department providing crisis intervention and spanned different roles in the hospital system before leaving to start my own practice. My history of in hospital work has given me insight into the particular stresses that medical professionals experience and sparked a commitment to working with physicians, nurses, and other health care providers.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I know finding a therapist can be a daunting task, so it might be helpful to know a little about me. I have a warm, open style with room for humor. I work to help clients feel safe and heard so we can attend to the emotions that underlie the distress that brought you into therapy. With that goal in mind, I tend towards a straightforward approach and have been called direct, but my directness comes with compassion and deep respect for how hard it can be to show up to the therapeutic process. My work is grounded in relationships and connection, so I show up as me to my sessions. I am a mom, an animal lover, a gardener, and a cook. I believe in life-long professional growth and along with continuing to grow my skills as a therapist, I bring a commitment to an anti-oppressive lens and actively work to understand the roles of privilege and bias on our individual and collective wellbeing.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I am certified as an EFT therapist for couples and inidividuals. EFT (emotionally focused therapy), an evidence based practice that works to help individuals and couples understand the patterns of internal reactions and reactions to one another that interfere with the closeness and contentment that they are seeking.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I am trained in trauma focused, evidence based CBT protocols that can be used in either individual or couples sessions. All of these approaches address the ways that traumatic experiences drive patterns of thinking and behavior that are no longer serving you in your life.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: My work with EMDR focuses on both recent and historical traumatic events and ways that individuals, even without a PTSD diagnosis, can integrate these experiences and reduce acute traumatic stress symptoms.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I work with individuals with both recent and historical trauma to integrate the experiences, reduce distressing symptoms, and get back to their lives. I have specific training and experience in providing treatment to those who have experienced trauma in their occupation, including first responders, veterans, and medical personnel. I am trained in short term, evidence based treatments including EMDR, Cognitive Processing Therapy, and Cognitive Behavioral Conjoint Therapy for PTSD.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I practice relationship counseling from an EFT model which works best when both partners are interested in participating in counseling. This approach focuses on exploring the emotions underlying our behavior and healing old hurts by creating opportunities for connection. The sessions help couples see and understand their hurtful patterns of interaction, then change this cycle as core emotions and needs are attended to.

name: Michael Crockett, PsyD
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Thank you for reaching out - Please take a moment to review my profile and website, and let me know if you have any questions.
ideal_client: Are you struggling to define yourself socially or professionally? Is anxiety or depression hindering your enjoyment of life? My clients have often come to a place in life where they feel stuck and are in search of a new direction.

approaches.My Approach to Helping:
I utilize an integrative approach drawing from mindfulness, CBT, and humanistic therapy systems. The focus is on what is happening in your life TODAY and how you want it to look differently. I strive to provide a safe, non-judgmental space so that you don’t need to continue struggling on your own.

I specialize in treating anxiety, depression, relationship, and identity concerns. Depending on your needs, we can take a directive approach targeting specific symptoms (e.g. social anxiety, excessive worry, panic attacks) or a less structured approach where you can reflect upon your life and identify what you want to pursue.

Together we can uncover the patterns in your thoughts, behaviors, and relationships that are holding you back, and establish a happier and healthier way of being in the world. I utilize a collaborative client-centered approach to provide the balance between supporting and challenging you that is necessary for promoting growth and change.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have studied psychology for a decade, completing a MA in General Psychology from NYU in 2007, and a PsyD in Clinical Psychology from Pacific University in 2014. My dissertation examined the influence of significant experiences (for example: a traumatic event or a spiritual emergency) on shaping one’s worldview and approach to living. For Internship I worked for Seattle University's Counseling and Psychological Services, providing individual and group therapy to students. Prior to operating a private practice I worked in a crisis line call center which I found to be challenging and rewarding work.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness involves attuning your attention to your immediate experience, without getting caught up in judgement. Practicing mindfulness allows you to live more fully in the present moment.

specialities.name: Interpersonal
specialities.description: Rogerian / humanistic / person centered

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT involves identifying and changing the maladaptive patterns in your thoughts and behaviors that are keeping problems stuck in place.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Stagnation can occur in any sphere of life: social, marital, spiritual, career, or otherwise. Counseling can help rejuvenate these areas and bring greater satisfaction and fulfillment.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can show up in a variety of ways: physically (eg. restlessness, fatigue), mentally (eg. racing thoughts, constant worry), and behaviorally (eg. avoiding places or activities, compulsions). Anxiety disorders manifest in characteristic ways that can often be addressed directly utilizing cognitive-behavioral methods of treatment without the need for medication.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Friends and family often have trouble understanding depression and wonder why you can't just snap out of it. I have suffered from this condition myself, and value this experience for the insights it has provided me in helping others. Although there is no magic fix, making small changes in a few different areas can help you cope and recover.

name: Cora Guren
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I am a Board Certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) looking forward to supporting you with your wellness goals.
ideal_client: I work with school-aged children, teens, and adults. Whether you are experiencing a current life stressor or a longer-term concern (such as ADHD, anxiety, depression and other mood-related disorders, PTSD, sleep disorders, or schizophrenia), we will work together to develop a treatment plan tailored to best support your individual needs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: You have taken the courageous and often difficult step of seeking help. It might help to know that I approach each new therapeutic relationship with warmth and curiosity. We are each unique in our life experiences, beliefs, joys, and struggles, and the most important thing I can do is to really listen. There are so many tools and approaches we can use, and there is no one “right” way to approach an issue. I believe in the importance of holistic approaches including exercise, mindfulness, psychotherapy, and medication. My practice style is diverse and is informed by cognitive therapeutic and humanistic approaches and an interest in Nonviolent Communication. I look forward to supporting you on this journey.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: The field of psychology is a long-term passion. As long as I can remember, I have spent my time trying to understand the human experience. I enjoyed studying in my PMHNP MSN program at Gonzaga University as well as my previous degrees, a bachelor of nursing degree at Linfield University and a BA in psychology from Carleton College. Prior to becoming a PMNP, I worked as a registered nurse for 17 years in a variety of settings across the lifespan including residential psychiatric treatment for children and adolescents as well as inpatient geriatric psychiatry. My education and experience leave me with a strong background to draw upon in my practice.

name: Grace Bezek
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Hi, I'm Grace! I offer trauma informed therapy for individuals, families, and relationships. Neurodivergence and Queer affirming.
ideal_client: My clients are individuals and relational systems grappling with challenges such as ADHD, relationship issues, self-doubt, and feelings of disconnection. They often find themselves burdened by trying to "get it together". They desire to be fully themselves and connect deeply with others, but trauma and societal harms can leave them feeling isolated. I support neurodivergent and queer identifying clients in recovering, connecting, and embracing their authentic selves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is grounded in two core beliefs: that we are all hardwired for connection and that we each already have the tools for personal and relational healing within ourselves. Yet, systemic obstacles, societal expectations, and trauma can leave us feeling frozen, unseen, and without a safe space to connect and be truly witnessed. I work with clients to recover from these experiences, develop new relationships with themselves and others, and commit to a process of uncovering their strengths and internal resources. I believe that therapy looks different for everybody. I operate from a place of curiosity and non-judgment, aiming to honor what is meaningful to you. My primary modalities are narrative, emotionally-focused, and solution-focused therapies. Together we will cultivate your unique path toward more authentic, fulfilling, and sustainable approaches to navigating life and relationships.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Dealing with ADHD, whether you have a diagnosis or suspect you might, can sometimes make it seem like everyone else has figured out how to do life while you're still trying to catch up. I understand the challenges that come with trying to navigate a world that doesn't always accommodate your needs. You're not flawed; it’s just about creating the right systems and tools to help you succeed. Together, we can develop strategies that work for you, turning your challenges into strengths.

name: Magdalene Kidd Vasconez
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I was inspired to work in the mental health field by my aunt, who was the first person in my family to become a LCSW.
ideal_client: If you're looking for a compassionate therapist who provides trauma-informed, evidence-based care, I’m here to support you. Whether you’re seeking EMDR treatment for trauma, or therapy for PTSD, anxiety, or relationship challenges, we’ll work together to create a plan that empowers you to move forward. I offer both in-person therapy in Portland and telehealth across Oregon and Georgia, making it easier for you to access care in a way that fits your needs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: When working with patients, I strive to create a collaborative, safe, and nonjudgmental space where your experiences and goals are valued and prioritized. I believe that meeting you where you are while gently encouraging forward movement, leads to successful growth and change. My approach is rooted in balance—helping you navigate where you are now and where you want to be. I look forward to supporting you every step of the way on your journey to healing and personal transformation.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: My approach to therapy combines evidence-based practices like Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT), and Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR). I also draw from Solution-Focused Therapy (SFT), Internal Family Systems (IFS), and Gestalt techniques to tailor the process to your unique needs.

name: Mike Revell
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Therapy is about creating opportunity for different choices. Let's talk about changes you want in your life and plan for how to get there.
ideal_client: I partner with people so they can find out what’s going on beneath the surface in their lives. When you’re feeling out of control, and nothing seems to be working, we can create a plan. We can examine why things are the way they are and what it will take to make a different choice. I can’t take away the problem, but I can help you learn a different way of dealing with it. I tend to work well with people that have some idea of the changes they want but struggle to get where they are trying to go.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: At times, my method can be very direct. I offer more than sympathy and acknowledgment of suffering. I will openly share with you what my experience indicates about your situation and how to approach the problem to get a different result. Other times, the right thing to do will be to take a moment and sit in discomfort. The path out of there is not always immediately obvious, and it will take practice to gain the awareness of what you need to give yourself in those moments.

I have worked in the mental health field for 13 years - first as a skills trainer and residential counselor in group homes for people with severe and persistent mental illness, then 8 years training and working as a therapist in community mental health clinics. This experience has shown me how useful a close relationship with open communication paired with evidenced-based methods can be in helping people to make different choices and get different results. While I primarily use an ACT (Acceptance and Commitment Therapy) framework, no single therapeutic modality is 'correct'. Therefore my approach is flexible and blends multiple styles including CBT, Existentialism, exposure therapy, and somatic awareness.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety shows up everywhere and stops us from doing the things we most want to do. It makes our brains run at full speed and our bodies feel the need to escape. I teach techniques helpful in managing both the mental and physical symptoms of anxiety.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is everywhere yet most people don't understand it. The brain's reward system isn't working properly, which leads to difficulty doing basic things in everyday life. It won't be easy, but we will work together to slowly build patterns of thought and behavior that help to break free of depressive cycles.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: As a therapist, I help people with ADHD figure out what actually works for their brain. We tackle the difficult stuff - things you have likely tried but not been able to maintain - like staying organized, managing emotions, and finding focus without judgment. ADHD brains work differently, and that's not a bad thing. Together we'll discover your strengths, build practical skills, and help you feel more in control of your daily life.

name: Stasha Christian
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Stasha is a PMHNP-BC with a background in emergency nursing and a long-standing commitment to whole-person care.

approaches.My Background and Approach: She earned her Bachelor of Science in Nursing with honors from Belmont University and graduated summa cum laude with a Master of Science in Nursing from Austin Peay State University. Stasha’s career began as a lifestyle coach, supporting individuals in overcoming internal obstacles and building meaningful change. That passion for guiding people through challenges led her to become an Emergency Medical Technician (EMT). While volunteering with the California Medical Assistance Team, she regularly trained with the Disaster Medical Assistance Team (DMAT) and participated in joint federal exercises with Urban Search and Rescue (USAR), gaining experience in crisis response and collaborative fieldwork. She went on to work as a registered nurse in the emergency department, where she developed strong clinical instincts in rapid assessment, emergency care, and interdisciplinary teamwork.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Caring for individuals and families in acute physical and psychological distress deepened her interest in mental health and ultimately guided her path to becoming a PMHNP. Today, that foundation informs her trauma-aware, integrative approach to psychiatric care. With a holistic and nonjudgmental perspective, Stasha is committed to thoughtful, evidence-based treatment that supports individuals in achieving stability and well-being—while honoring the mental, emotional, and spiritual dimensions of health. She values honest conversation, genuine connection, and collaborative care plans that meet people where they are. She brings this depth of experience into her psychiatric practice, offering thorough, person-centered assessment and care. Returning to the Pacific Northwest from Nashville, Stasha is excited to join the Head Well team and honored to support the mental health and well-being of the Eugene community and the greater Oregon region.

name: Kristen Brown
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Kristen is a dedicated Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner with a robust background in healthcare spanning nearly two decades.
ideal_client: Throughout her career, Kristen has worked in various settings, including long-term care, the Post Anesthesia Care Unit (PACU), Intensive Care Unit (ICU), neurology, orthopedics, and medical-surgical nursing. Her diverse experience equips her with a holistic understanding of patient care, enabling her to approach mental health treatment with compassion and expertise.

approaches.My Background: Kristen holds an Associate Degree in Nursing from Lane Community College in Eugene, Oregon, a Bachelor of Science in Nursing from Oregon Health & Science University (OHSU) in Portland, and a Master of Science in Nursing from Southern Adventist University. Starting her career as a Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) in 2006, Kristen spent seven years in that role before advancing to Registered Nurse (RN) in 2013. She furthered her expertise by obtaining her PMHNP in 2022 and is currently pursuing her certification in integrative psychiatry, enhancing her ability to provide holistic mental health care.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Kristen is particularly passionate about holistic health and Ayurveda, having studied the ancient practice rigorously. As a certified Ayurvedic Health Coach, she incorporates these principles into her patient care, promoting overall wellness alongside traditional psychiatric treatment. Her dedication to leadership and excellence was recognized with the Dean’s Leadership Award during her studies. Outside of her professional life, Kristen enjoys outdoor activities such as hiking, backpacking, snowshoeing, paddleboarding, and sailing. She is also passionate about yoga, meditation, and spiritual study, believing in the profound connection between mental well-being and a balanced lifestyle. Kristen is excited to join the Head Well clinic, where she looks forward to providing compassionate and comprehensive mental health care to her clients.

name: jane Newman
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My specialties include grief and loss/ life transitions, living with chronic illness and life skills including stress management. My areas of specialty often encompass issues related to anxiety, depression and diminished self esteem.

approaches: My goal is to provide a safe, supportive, confidential and non-judgmental environment- to serve you with presence and respect. While my work is predominantly humanistic and client-centered, I also draw from and rely on aspects of CBT (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy), Gestalt and Narrative Counseling techniques. My belief is that each individual has the ability to find his/her answers - my role is to help facilitate the process.

I have an MBA in Marketing and an MS in General Counseling. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), NBCC Certified. Currently in Private Practice, I have worked in Hospice and an Outpatient Cancer Center. I have facilitated Support Groups (Grief, loss, chronic illness), provided peer supervision, educational workshops and ceremonies of remembrance.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: The focus of my training is General Counseling with expertise in grief and loss; this work involves humanistic counseling theory - supportive, person-centered and non-judgmental. My role is to companion the bereaved, which involves a holistic and genuine presence. While other theories come into play during sessions (narrative, experiential,family systems, CBT,) my strongest focus is Humanistic.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Each family member may be unique, but is also part of a family 'system'. A life change or transition may interrupt the family system; the therapeutic environment can help to identify the common goal and provide the setting for enhanced communication and collaboration.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Working with clients dealing with chronic pain and illness is part of my experience in the area of grief and loss. Living with pain/illness is a loss of life as they knew it before - the process gives clients an opportunity to identify/discuss issues associated with their condition- to feel validated and supported; and to learn coping techniques.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Self esteem (or lack of) is inherent in so many of our lives. My role is to help people identify the fears, beliefs (negative thoughts) that effect one's sense of self; and to help challenge the negative thoughts/beliefs with more accurate 'stories'/ interpretations. The goal is to identify one's negative thoughts of self, and provide skills for the client reconstruct with healthier realities.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: My area of expertise is in grief and loss -having worked in Hospice and an Outpatient Cancer Center. Grief and loss encompasses life transitions, divorce, job loss, chronic illness and, of course, death. Grief is a natural, normal process and my role is to offer support, validate (normalize) and companion people through this process.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Having worked extensively in the area of grief and loss, anxiety is often a presenting symptom; working with clients to identify source of anxiety and either illuminate skills they have or help them find identify/learn skills to regulate the anxiety is part of the therapy process.

name: McKenzie Brock
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I embrace a compassionate and relational approach to healing through our bodies with mindfulness and creativity.
ideal_client: I am passionate about working with teens, adults, and the LGBTQIA+ community. I would love to help you to build skills to cope with trauma, anxiety, depression, grief and loss, and other mental health struggles while creating collective goals for moving forward and developing a deeper connection to yourself and your purpose.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In my work I embrace a strengths-based, relational approach, incorporating trauma-informed care, utilizing an attachment lens, while working with individuals and family systems. I am guided by mindfulness-based and somatic practices, feminist multicultural therapy, Accelerate Experiential-Dynamic Psychotherapy, Internal Family Systems, and also offer EMDR and EMDR Flash. I believe that we all hold immense wisdom from our stories. It is my joy to partner alongside people as they rediscover and reclaim their power.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a therapist because of the impact of my own healing journey. I believe that all therapists should be in therapy, doing their own work. The systems we live and work within are inherently traumatizing and we ALL deserve access to support and healing. As a member of the LGBTQIA+ community, it is my goal to bring more accessible service to our community.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am certified in EMDR and EMDR Flash. I use this modality from a trauma-informed lens and believe in being cautious and creating a safe container before utilizing EMDR processing.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I really enjoy using "parts" point of view in the therapeutic space. I find that getting to know your parts and how they show up can be a doorway to healing.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I use theories from CBT to inform my work with clients when appropriate, but also enjoying meeting you where you are and adapting therapy to meet your needs.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: I am passionate about supporting caregiver and other therapists, teachers, and people who give to others for their career. I have taken courses on vicarious trauma and caregiving.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I bring a trauma-informed lens to my work. I offer EMDR in a trauma-and-attachment-informed perspective.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: My goal is to provide a safe, healing, supportive space for community.

name: Haley Richter
title: Professional Counselor
intro: A pre-licensed MA level graduate in Professional Mental Health Counseling. Interested clients can add contact info to the waitlist.

name: Erol Berkeley-Hanson
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Accepting new telehealth clients, no wait list!
ideal_client: I primarily work with teens and adults and I specialize in seeing those working through transitionary periods in their life, school/work related-stress, family-relationship related stress, anxiety, ADHD, and parenting.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is based in cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and/or solutions focused therapy. Therapy doesn’t have to feel intimidating or formal—it’s about creating a space where you can be real, explore what’s on your mind, and make meaningful changes. Whether you're navigating a big life transition, dealing with daily stress, or just looking for a quiet space to sort your thoughts, I'm here to support you in a way that feels meaningful.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I bring a straightforward yet empathetic approach, infused with humor and a touch of sarcasm, to create a space that acknowledges both the weight of your experiences and the possibility for lightness. My goal is to build a therapeutic relationship where you feel comfortable bringing anything to the table.

name: Kelsey Weise
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I'm here to offer curious, open-minded collaboration in pursuit of your goals. Excited to meet you!
ideal_client: I enjoy and have experience working with people of all backgrounds: individuals, couples, children, and families. I'm especially passionate about working with queer and neurodivergent folx, and anyone struggling with grief or anxiety about our changing world and climate. Given that the strength of the therapeutic relationship is the #1 predictor of success in therapy, it's important that you see me as someone who can really "tune in" with you!

approaches.My Background and Approach: I believe that the healing process starts with deepening insight into how we connect with other beings and with ourselves, honoring all the emotions that move us—grief, sadness, anger, joy—as valuable signposts toward how we make meaning in the world. In therapy, we can work together to untangle complex thoughts and feelings with compassion and curiosity. I primarily draw from Narrative and Internal Family Systems (parts work) therapies, with sprinkles of Somatic work to attend to the mind-body connection. I also offer Ecotherapy, which involves more focused attention on (re)connecting with the natural world as a key facet of healing. These sessions take place primarily outdoors; either in our on-site garden, around the firepit, walking through the neighborhood, or even in nearby parks and forest trails. Interested? Let's consult and see if my Ecotherapy offerings are a good fit for you :)

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe our stories are shaped by the systems we are a part of: our families, social circles, political spheres, and ecosystems. Knowing that these systems interact with each of us differently, socio-cultural sensitivity is fundamental to my practice. I aim to hold an affirming and uplifting space for those with LGBTQIIA+, BIPOC, neurodivergent, and other socially marginalized identities. I especially gravitate toward work with my fellow neurodivergent and queer folx. I believe that internalized stories related to these identities can form unique complex traumas. I aim to unravel these norms and nurture a more liberated and affirmed sense of self. Connecting with the body and with nature are also key facets of my personal approach to healing & to my work as a therapist. But I know these connections don't come easily to everyone! We'll work with your current level of comfort at all levels. Above all, I believe you are the expert in your own healing.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: I completed a certificate program in Ecopsychology & Ecotherapies at Lewis & Clark Graduate School, including coursework in ethical and safety considerations unique to this approach. I have 2 years experience employing Ecotherapy interventions in my work as a therapist. What this looks like depends entirely on your comfort level, but might include exploring your relationship to your plants and pets; mindfulness-based activities outdoors; or simply taking walks outside while we talk!

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: With a background in research and training in this evidence-based approach, I'll help you get to know all the parts of yourself that work hard to help you, but might not get along so well! Just like when we say "a part of me wants X, but another part wants Y", conflict between the parts of ourselves often keeps us locked in frustrating (or at times even harmful) patterns. By building curiosity and compassion toward your parts and their roles, we can help them coexist more peacefully within.

name: Su Yim, MSW, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Chances are, other people in your life have already given you a lot of advice. "Do this, don't do that." It's not always that simple. As humans, we all struggle at some point. I love helping people develop a deep sense of confidence in who they are as they learn to handle what's holding them back.

approaches: When we meet, we will focus on your desires, worries, hopes, and fears. I will offer guidance, patience, and compassion as we focus on what makes sense for you. I am experienced in working with people going through grief and loss, relationship struggles, depression, anxiety, substance use, and trauma. Using evidence-based therapy tailored for you, you can learn to manage emotions, improve your loving relationships, make decisions that fit your values, and understand the roots of your actions. As a therapist experienced in brief and long-term therapy, I will help guide our work around what you need. Part of our time may be spent on acknowledging how the past influences you today, but I also believe the purpose of therapy is to move you forward. I balance compassion, comfort, and patience with a shared understanding that progress is important.

I am a licensed clinical social worker with a master's degree in social work from Portland State University and a bachelor's in journalism from Northwestern University. My experience includes work in community mental health clinics, local hospitals, crisis lines, and with university students. I have post-graduate training in EMDR, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, Motivational Interviewing, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Internal Family Systems, and trauma-informed care. I also have completed the required hours to become a certified alcohol and drug counselor. In working with you, my goal will be to listen not just to your story but to the themes and patterns of your life. I do not believe that you are broken, or that I have "the fix." I work from a strengths-based perspective, which means I believe that we all have inherent value and capabilities. I embrace our partnership as an opportunity for us to understand what's keeping you stuck, and how to move toward changing it.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I have completed multiple trainings in IFS, including Level 1 through the IFS Institute. To me, IFS is a non-pathologizing, openhearted approach to the complexity inside of each of us. Rather than assuming we are monoliths, IFS embraces all of our parts, whether they are ambivalent, in conflict, or rooted in the past, in a tender, empowering, compassionate way.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory is all about love and safety. How we experience that from an early age influences the coping skills we develop for all of our relationships, especially during times of conflict and struggle. I love that we can change how we feel about ourselves, our relationships and the world at large through the context of new, safe, reparative experiences.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: As humans, we are wired to connect. When our connections confuse or hurt us, we suffer. But it doesn't have to end there. By learning our individual and relationship patterns, we can turn our hurt into a chance for even deeper, more resilient relationships. Through emotion-focused therapy, we can learn to change the dynamics between us without assigning blame or stonewalling.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Surviving trauma is one thing; living the life you deserve after trauma is another. It takes a compassionate, centered, experienced clinician to guide you through that tough terrain. I help trauma survivors understand the past and develop coping skills to live life on today's terms.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is misery. Whether it's pervasive or situation-specific, anxiety sucks the spark from life. In my work with people with anxiety, I use cognitive-behavioral therapy, mindfulness, and acceptance and commitment therapy to build skills and awareness around their triggers and symptoms. Because life doesn't have to feel this way.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: People who have depression are some of the hardest-working people around; seemingly simple acts require huge effort. Using CBT, mindfulness, and interpersonal process, I have helped people lighten the burden of depression related to grief, addiction, chemical imbalances, life circumstances and more.

name: Lizza Chenven
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I believe each person has the internal resources needed for healing and change. Email to set up a free consultation!
ideal_client: Hello, I’m Lizza Chenven, LCSW. I work with couples and adult individuals to help identify and access your internal resources for making constructive change. The range of challenges we face in life is broad. I work with my clients to create lasting change in managing a wide range of problems, including depression, anxiety, eating disorders, trauma, relationship issues, grief, and many others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am particularly interested in couples work and continue to train in IFIO, which is the couples version of Internal Family Systems (IFS). I believe that each person has the capacity to experience emotional safety and connection in their life and relationships. As a therapist, I work with you to establish a trusting relationship and a welcoming space for your self-exploration.

name: Aaron Kelsay
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a trauma recovery therapist with extensive experience in the healing and recovery field.
ideal_client: Healing is a journey. For some, "healing" means reversing years of trauma, and for others it means 'getting out of my own head' or 'getting un-stuck.' For everyone, the path to healing is a difficult one, and it is lighter, easier, more meaningful when others join in with you. To you who have tried to go it alone, I invite you to reach out. Connecting with a counselor is a way to get un-stuck in your journey towards health, to bring healing to those deeper places of hurt.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My goal in working with a client is to help them develop the insight, skills, strengths, resources, and supports to work toward that state of being "healthy." I work with the best available, evidence-based modalities to support people on their journey towards health. This includes EMDR, trauma-based, and attachment-based modalities. What does all this mean? When you find yourself on your way towards healing, it will be because you have brought along with you many of the tools that we have developed and integrated in our sessions together. That may mean that the EMDR has re-wired your response to trauma memories. It may mean that you have developed new behavioral habits and routines, new boundaries, new ways of getting your needs met. As we help you on your journey, I will offer the best available skills, supports, resources for your healing, and my hope is that you will take away a few of the best fitting ones for you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: When I was younger, I was constantly anxious. I would read everything all at once for school, get all my HW done as fast as possible, worry about and plan for every possible scenario. Through my own counseling work, I've managed to slow down and better adapt to that way of thinking and being. It was also over the course of that healing experience that I noticed a shift in who I was and how I wanted to be in the world. I've shed and deconstructed much of my religious, spiritual, political values, just as I shed much of the pressure, self-criticism, and anxiety of my youth. What I kept from my upbringing was the "good stuff." I still value the ideals of love, hope, peace. The "love your neighbor" way has a more holistic meaning for me now in my chosen role as a counselor. Outside of the counseling office, my family and I choose to be open and affirming with the LGBT community, support BLM, and to work towards improving the material and spiritual conditions of all people.

specialities.name: Addiction Therapy
specialities.description: After years of working in intensive residential treatment, I have extensive experience working with groups, individuals using a number of modalities / interventions -- I am able to custom design a treatment plan for you, no matter where you are in your recovery journey, based on both my professional and personal, lived experience in mental health / substance use recovery.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I find that counseling very much lends itself to developing a regular practice of "being." Mindfulness-based interventions are just one of the ways that I support clients on their journey to healing, and I find that integrating DBT, meditation / mindfulness, and related practice are an excellent foundation for an ongoing healing and wellness program.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I have completed the required training in order to be certified as an EMDR therapist. I am able to implement the EMDR tools in session alongside the other theories and tools in order to address trauma and other related symptoms.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: The journey to healing is so much about relationship, and the "theory of attachment" is a wonderful way to put into words how we relate to everything in our world. I use the language of attachment alongside the other modalities in order for couples, individuals, groups to understand how and why they relate they way they do. This awareness allows us to adjust how we relate, and in doing so, move towards healing and health.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma is confusing, it's disconnecting, disorienting. Reversing trauma means re-developing and re-learning safety, trusting one's body cues, listening one's thoughts and feelings. It's a long journey, but it's well worth it. I have years of experience working with the most acute cases of PTSD, and I can say with confidence I have honed the skills to help clients move towards healing in this area.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: "Spirituality" hits at the core of the self, and can inspire everything from dread, shame, to joy and belonging. When this area is wounded, it is that much heavier and more difficult to ask for help. In this area, I have extensive training, background, and experience. My hope in that is to help you articulate the pain, the loss, the joys, the meaning, identity, and everything that is 'touched' by spirituality, in order that you may experience progress towards health and healing.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: "Anxiety" was something I experienced as "normal" until I started to put it into words. It was through my own healing journey that I realized there are other ways to be, think, and feel -- imagine if you could "let your guard down," enjoy every moment, and embrace what's coming. Through a combination of cognitive, somatic, and story-based interventions, you can move towards a more balanced, less anxious, more enjoyable way of being in the world.

name: Evoke Therapy LLC
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I offer a holistic, integrative, depth-oriented approach to help you cultivate awareness, open to change, and create meaning in your life.
ideal_client: If you’re feeling ready to make meaningful changes and willing to do the deeper work that lasting growth can take, you’ve come to the right place. My approach is warm and grounded, with a focus on self-awareness, insight, and real, supportive challenges when needed. Clients who connect with my work often find value in blending traditional therapy with practices like yoga, meditation, reiki, and dream exploration. I offer a space that’s LGBTQ+ affirming, kink aware, and culturally sensitive.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I take a non-traditional approach, and that’s intentional. I’m here to help you break patterns, face what’s been getting in your way, and build a life that feels more aligned with who you really are. Whether it’s relationship challenges, anxiety, or just feeling stuck or disconnected, I’m focused on helping you create real, lasting change—not just talk about it. I blend practical tools with deeper, intuitive work—like dream analysis, tarot, and symbolic exploration. I also draw from mind-body-spirit practices rooted in my background as a Yoga Teacher, Herbalist, and Reiki Master. For couples, I use the Gottman Method to strengthen communication, rebuild trust, and create deeper connection. You don’t have to fit a mold to show up here. Wherever you’re at, I’ll meet you there—with honesty, intention, and maybe a little magic.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I approach therapy with a deep awareness of the systems we’re all living under. As an anarchist, I believe in helping people understand and navigate the realities of class struggle and how systemic oppression impacts our mental, emotional, and physical well-being. Based in Philly, I run a community group that provides preventative care using accessible botanical medicine to those who can’t afford traditional healthcare. I’m actively involved in local mutual aid networks, committed to collective care, autonomy, and building alternatives to oppressive systems. Other parts of my identity include being neurodivergent, part of the LGBTQ community, and mixed-race--all lived experiences bring into my work. These identities shape how I navigate the world and the ways I connect with others, especially when it comes to recognizing and honoring the unique challenges we all face.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness can help you slow down and make conscious choices that are in line with your life path; living in a way that is less reactive to the world around you.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: Exploration of non-ordinary states of consciousness and use of mindfulness practices can be an effective way step outside of the ego and gain a wider perspective on one's problems. Holistic therapy takes into account the whole person—mind, body, and spirit—in the healing process. It integrates various therapeutic approaches and techniques to address not just the symptoms, but also the root causes of issues.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Narrative therapy is like crafting a story about your life where you're the author. Instead of focusing on problems as something fixed or part of who you are, we explore how these issues fit into the larger narrative of your life. By reshaping these stories, we can change how you see yourself and your possibilities.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: The Gottman Method is a practical and evidence-based approach to couples therapy that focuses on enhancing relationship satisfaction and stability. Through assessments and interventions tailored to each couple's unique dynamics, we work together to strengthen your bond and create a more positive and fulfilling relationship. The Gottman Method equips you with practical skills and insights to navigate challenges, deepen intimacy, and build a lasting connection based on trust and understanding.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships can come with struggles, whether that be in the area of communication, intimacy, and/or attachment issues. I utilize the Gottman Method to assist individuals and couples in navigating relationship challenges effectively. This evidence-based approach focuses on strengthening communication, fostering trust, and resolving conflicts constructively. I work with a diversity of relationship dynamics such as open relationships, kink, and non-traditional partnerships.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: In my practice, I specialize in helping individuals recover from abuse, with a focus on narcissistic abuse—often stemming from antagonistic relationships. My approach is grounded in understanding the unique challenges survivors face, offering a safe and supportive space to process trauma, rebuild self-worth, and foster healthier relationships. Together, we work to empower you to reclaim your life and create a path toward healing and resilience.

specialities.name: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD)
specialities.description: I specialize in supporting individuals with PMDD, helping manage emotional and physical symptoms. As an herbalist, I take an integrative approach, combining herbal remedies with practical coping strategies and emotional support. My goal is to help you find balance and relief, offering a holistic, non-judgmental space to explore and manage the challenges of PMDD.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Transpersonal therapy is a holistic approach that goes beyond traditional psychological perspectives to explore the spiritual and transcendent aspects of human experience. We focus not only on addressing immediate concerns but also on uncovering deeper layers of consciousness and personal growth. This therapy emphasizes the interconnection of mind, body, and spirit, encouraging clients to explore their inner wisdom.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have specialized training in counseling individuals and couples navigating non-traditional relationships. I understand the unique dynamics these relationships can bring, from communication challenges to managing multiple emotional needs. Whether you’re exploring polyamory, dealing with relationship shifts, or seeking support with boundary-setting and ethical communication, I offer a space where all relationship styles are respected and celebrated.

name: Kristen Genzano
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I focus on Women's Issues including Infertility, Postpartum, Childfree Women, Female Entrepreneurs, Mother/Daughter Relationships, & more.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: There is so much noise around us – particularly as women – it is often difficult to discern our own truth. I believe when we are given the space to slow down, reflect, and connect with our inner selves, we find the answers we are searching for. If you are feeling stuck, unsure of how to move forward, drained from listening to the expectations of those around you, therapy could be helpful. In our sessions together we will explore thoughts and feelings that may be interfering with your sense of peace, joy, and contentment. We will work collaboratively to create an environment where you can hear your own inner wisdom. In our work together, I will be honest and direct, gentle and challenging.
