I will do my best to understand your experience so that, together, we can discern a path forward that leads to your personal fulfillment.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Before I was a therapist, I worked in the corporate world. During this time, I witnessed many of the complicated challenges women face as professionals, as business owners, as mothers, as daughters, as partners, and as friends to one another. It was this experience that led me to become a Therapist. I attended Northwestern University in Evanston, Illinois. During graduate school I completed two years of advanced training in Mindfulness & Behavior Therapies and specialized in working with survivors of childhood sexual trauma. Since graduating I received additional training in Emotionally Focused Therapy for couples, Experiential Therapy, and Relational Psychotherapy. I created my practice to offer women a compassionate and nonjudgmental place to talk through the many unique challenges they face. To learn more about my practice please visit my website - www.kristengenzanotherapy.com

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: I specialize in working with women. In my practice, I am consistently looking at my client’s experience through the feminist lens. From this perspective I work collaboratively with my clients to allow for a more balanced, accepting, and self-compassionate experience of themselves.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Bringing mindfulness into one's life can lead to profound change. As a result, I aim to integrate mindfulness into my clinical work in a variety of ways. This intention is supported by two years of advanced professional training in Mindfulness & Behavior therapies. In addition to my professional experience, I maintain a personal meditation and yoga practice.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I am trained in Emotionally Focused Therapy and use this orientation to inform my work with individuals and couples. Emotions are central to the human experience. By being aware of and expressing our emotions we can more deeply understand ourselves. Deeper self-understanding gives way for more authentic self-expression.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: In 2015 I completed a year-long training and consultation group focused on perinatal/postpartum mood and anxiety disorders. I approach this work from a holistic perspective, collaborating with you to identify the multiple factors that contribute to your wellbeing during and after pregnancy.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: I focus on women’s issues including perinatal mental health. This may include emotional and psychological changes during pregnancy or as you try to conceive. In our work I will take into consideration the many factors—hormones, your environment, social support, family of origin issues— that contribute to your wellbeing.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Therapy isn’t solely for those in crisis or pain. If you feel a pull to expand, to transform, to grow, we can work together to explore the opportunities ahead of you. I have trained in a variety of treatment orientations related to personal growth. Be it behavioral, spiritual, or mental growth you are seeking, we will work together to identify blocks to growth and to expand possibilities.

specialities.name: Premarital Counseling
specialities.description: I have extensive training in Emotionally Focused Therapy, a structured approach to couples therapy anchored in the science of attachment and bonding. Through this lens we will work to create a secure foundation as you enter into a new phase of your relationship.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I have dedicated my practice to working with a variety of women’s issues including perfectionism, work-other-self balance, fertility issues, romantic relationships, mother/daughter relationships, and coping with experiences of sexual abuse.

name: Jillyan Medina
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I work with folks who identify outside of the box and don't fit into the "norm."
ideal_client: My practice specializes in serving the queer community, folks in larger bodies, and those who find themselves to be “other.” I am with my clients as a non-judgmental witness. I strive to maintain empathy, compassion, and openness with each of the clients I work with.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe problems occur in context and are influenced by our societal systems. I work together with my clients to replace old narratives, with a story that is more authentic and allows folks to engage with themselves more positively. I will always be transparent with my clients about the therapeutic process because I believe that collaboration and consent are vital to creating safety and trust. I bring genuine care into my relationship with my clients.

name: Don Marr
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Therapy that helps you heal old wounds and reconnect with your true self.
ideal_client: My ideal client is a sensitive, thoughtful adult who feels stuck in patterns of anxiety, depression, or self-doubt. You’ve done your best to cope but still feel overwhelmed, disconnected, or unsure of who you are. You might be longing for deeper peace, confidence, or meaning in your life. You're ready to make change, even if you're unsure how. I work best with clients who value creativity, depth, and want therapy that goes beyond just talking.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I help adults navigate anxiety, depression, trauma, grief, and self-doubt using Accelerated Resolution Therapy (ART)—a gentle, powerful method that doesn’t require reliving painful memories in detail. I also support highly sensitive people, deep feelers, and those stuck in perfectionism, people-pleasing, or rumination. Many of my clients are managing life transitions, strained family ties, or long-standing emotional wounds. I bring warmth, creativity, and structure to sessions, helping clients reconnect with themselves and move forward. I am in network with Moda Health, Aetna, Cigna, Regence BlueCross BlueShield of Oregon, Carelon Behavioral Health, and Anthem EAP (Bank of America).

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As a therapist, I value authenticity, creativity, and compassion. I believe healing happens when we feel truly seen and supported without judgment. My work is grounded in deep respect for each person’s inner wisdom and capacity for change. I aim to create a space that’s safe, collaborative, and gently challenging—where growth can happen at your pace. I also believe in the power of imagination and somatic awareness, especially when words fall short. Whether we’re using structured approaches like ART or simply exploring what’s coming up, I stay attuned to your rhythm and needs. I see therapy as a kind of improvisation—where we listen, adjust, and create together. Above all, I want you to walk away with greater self-trust, clarity, and freedom to be who you truly are.

specialities.name: Accelerated Resolution Therapy
specialities.description: As a Certified Master ART Practitioner, I’ve seen how Accelerated Resolution Therapy (ART) offers a powerful alternative to traditional talk therapy. Instead of revisiting painful memories in detail, ART helps clients gently shift how those memories are stored, leading to lasting relief from trauma, anxiety, and emotional pain. With advanced training and deep trust in the process, I help clients find clarity, calm, and healing—often more quickly than they ever expected.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: With training in Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), I help clients build on their existing strengths and envision the changes they want to see. While ART offers powerful resolution of painful memories, SFBT brings added focus to the client’s capacity for growth, hope, and forward movement. Together, these approaches help clients not only heal from the past but also take meaningful steps toward the life they want to live.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I specialize in treating PTSD through Accelerated Resolution Therapy (ART), a highly effective method that rapidly resolves trauma without needing extensive verbal processing. As a Certified Master ART Practitioner, I have successfully guided many clients to quickly find relief from trauma-related anxiety, intrusive thoughts, and emotional dysregulation.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: I help clients break free from codependent patterns, fostering healthier relationships and stronger self-worth. Using strengths-based, solution-focused techniques, I empower individuals to set clear boundaries, rediscover their voice, and build balanced, meaningful connections grounded in self-respect and emotional autonomy.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Using strengths-based and solution-focused therapy, I help clients transform low self-esteem and harsh self-criticism into genuine self-acceptance and confidence. My compassionate approach empowers individuals to recognize their worth, trust themselves, and foster lasting emotional resilience.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I specialize in anxiety treatment, using Accelerated Resolution Therapy (ART) to quickly reduce worry, panic, and overthinking. I help clients shift anxiety patterns, quiet internal noise, and cultivate lasting emotional calm and confidence.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: As a Certified Master ART Practitioner, I offer powerful, strengths-based and solution-focused therapy for depression, helping clients move beyond sadness, hopelessness, and low motivation. My compassionate approach helps individuals reconnect with hope, joy, and genuine emotional resilience.

name: Emma Keefe
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I hope to help you cultivate the kind of presence that holds your thoughts, feelings and experiences gently - without judgment or shame.
ideal_client: My clients enter into a therapeutic relationship with me often because they never learned how to listen to or love themselves. Many of my clients live with a harsh/distracting internal critic that pulls them out of the present moment and into chronic experiences of suffering. They might even live with or love others who echo or add new fodder to this already cruel inner-voice. My clients begin therapy because they want more out of relationships - with themselves, with others and with the world.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer the kind of therapeutic relationship that does not seek to pathologize your behavior, but instead, helps you slow down with your thoughts, feelings and experiences, compassionately. Through the help of relational-cultural therapy, we examine the quality of your relationships, both past and present, and determine how these relationships may impact the way you orient to yourself, others, and the world. Polyvagal theory encourages us to explore what feels safe, and unsafe, to your body, and how your body communicates messages of ease and dis-ease on a moment-to-moment basis. Lastly, Buddhist psychology inspires us to bring moments of suffering to the surface and practice building the tolerance needed to examine them gently. We consider how attachment, aversion, impermanence, and many other Buddhist concepts might play a role in your suffering, and how you might be able to meet them with more equanimity today.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a mixed-race, white and Mexican Indigenous demi-woman. I am polyamorous, pansexual, and am dedicated to providing gender-affirming care. As a white-passing woman raised in the United States, I understand the responsibility I have to provide anti-racist care and remove all characteristics of white supremacy from my formal education and counseling work. I am also dedicated to providing affordable mental health counseling in my effort to combat our economic system's ability to monetize relational safety, compassion and mental health care.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Relational-cultural therapy (RCT) highlights the importance of building mutually empathetic, authentic and empowering relationships with others. RCT prioritizes the concept of interconnectedness over the Western-European goal of hyper-individualism and self-sufficiency.

name: Ann DeWitt
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Currently Not Accepting New Clients My goal is for you to experience passion in your marriage and fun in your family.
ideal_client: I know the joy and tumult that families can be. I work with individuals, couples, and teens. I love working with individuals who are juggling their children, their marriage, and their extended family relationships while trying to honor their own needs and desire to make a meaningful contribution in the world. I have 25 years of parenting education experience. When working with teens, I especially enjoy working with high achieving, anxious teens, teen athletes, and teens who learn differently.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I bring wit and wisdom into our work. I share many practical tools and resources, and offer empathy and support to put them to use in your life. I have been teaching parenting classes for 25 years and have helped hundreds of couples increase affinity and communication, clarify their values, and get on the same parenting page. I find a sense of humor is essential in getting through this thing called life. We will laugh together and hopefully bring some lightness back into your days.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned by Master's Degree in Clinical Psychology in 1995. My emphasis has always been on helping people create fulfilling and healthy family relationships. I am licensed in California and Oregon.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: I am a Certified Parent Educator and have been teaching parenting for 25 years. I co-hosted a weekly parenting radio show/podcast called Passport to Parenting. I love helping parents to help their kids grow to be confident and competent young people.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I love helping teens by offering a supportive adult outside the family. I work with teens who are feeling anxious, sad and overwhelmed by the demands of school, friends and family.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I love working with couples, especially couples with children. We naturally shift between issues that come up in the marriage and issues that come up with the kids.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: There are lots of things for teens to worry about. I help teens who are anxious or overwhelmed by the expectations that are placed on them academically, athletically and socially to achieve.

name: Anne Pippert
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: As a Marriage and Family Therapist, I am here to support you and your loved ones on your journey toward healing, growth, and self-discovery.
ideal_client: I address a variety of issues with individuals including eating disorders, relationship and family conflict, anxiety, depression, emotional distress, and the struggle to find purpose and meaning in life. Using Gottman Method couples therapy, I help couples build a foundational friendship, manage conflict, heal from relationship trauma, and develop mutual goals and dreams for their future together.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe in highlighting the uniqueness of the individual, while understanding that we all function as part of a multitude of larger systems. The relationships we create with ourselves, with others, and with the world around us, can both transform and challenge us. In my work, I utilize treatment modalities including CBT, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, mindfulness-based practices, Emotion-Focused Family Therapy and The Gottman Method for couples. I have experience working with adults, adolescents, and families in residential, partial hospitalization and intensive outpatient eating disorder treatment facilities.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I have experience working with adults and adolescents with eating disorders in multiple treatment settings including residential, partial hospitalization, and intensive outpatient.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Trained in Gottman Method couples therapy (level 2 certification).

name: Emma Stern
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer empowered and embodied therapy for folks seeking to turn challenges and distress into a catalyst for deep healing and transformation
ideal_client: My clients are deeply empathetic and sensitive people. They can be prone to overextending themselves or creating impossible standards as they seek to show up in a meaningful way for themselves and those around them. They are real, raw, resilient, and often survivors of abusive, dysfunctional, or turbulent childhoods. They are ready to create meaningful change and let go of tendencies that are no longer serving them. They are the most inspiring people I know.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist, I am warm, real, relatable, and come with a sense of humor. I am committed to being honest and while I will hold you accountable in our work, I will always honor your discernment and expect you to be the expert on yourself. I specialize in work with complex trauma; anxiety; grief; codependency; premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD); recovering from perfectionism and people pleasing; and recovery from burnout during late-stage capitalism and global pandemic. I work from a psychodynamic and somatic lens that combines traditional talk therapy with mind-body inquiry and education about the brain, body, and nervous system. “Feelings” are literally physical manifestations of the brain and nervous system’s response to emotional stimuli. Through developing a cognitive understanding of the mind-body connection, we find manageable ways to face challenges and cultivate deeper compassion for ourselves and others in times of distress.

I work from a trauma-informed lens. As the body can be a source of pain and oppression, I hold somatic work with care. I also understand that the medical industrial complex can be harmful and am committed to normalizing and advocating for mental health care. Coming from a blended family that is White, Black, Latinx, and Jewish, I am committed to questioning identity dynamics, power, privilege, and positionality. I welcome the opportunity to work with clients from different backgrounds and seek to maintain humility and sensitivity in work with clients who hold different identities. I am dedicated to social justice and will support you in using your personal healing journey to work towards collective liberation and social change. I am EMDR trained. I am a yoga practitioner and instructor (E-RYT 500, YACEP) and upon interest will support you in bringing yoga philosophy and asana into your healing journey. Working alongside you is an honor and privilege I will treat with deep respect.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Somatic psychotherapy integrates body-based inquiry and mindfulness into traditional talk therapy. Much of our subconscious emotional experience manifests as physical tension and holding patterns. “Feelings” are literally physical manifestations of the brain and nervous system’s response to emotional stimuli. Through developing a cognitive understanding of the mind-body connection, we find manageable ways to face challenges and cultivate deeper compassion for ourselves and others.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: Psychodynamic therapy explores ways in which past patterns can manifest in one's present behaviors, actions, and responses to emotional material. It encourages clients to develop deep personal insight and understanding of the ways in which their personality and patterns have been shaped by life experience. This type of therapy works to bring unconscious material into conscious awareness so clients can understand ways in which their behaviors are beneficial and/or self-sabotaging.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: Holistic therapy honors each client's unique, complex, and multifaceted experience while also looking at the universal aspects of being human. This work combines mind-body integration and depth-oriented psychotherapy. Clients are encouraged to reflect on ways in which their presenting challenges show deep emotional, spiritual, and existential needs, longings, and desires. Clients are also encouraged to use their own inquiry to gain greater empathy and understanding of the human experience.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Feminist therapy takes into account dynamics of marginalization and systematic oppression. In therapy, I ask clients to consider ways in which race, gender, sexual orientation, culture, age, socioeconomic status, and ability status impact their lived experience. As a therapist, I am committed to questioning power, privilege, and positionality. I encourage clients to look at how white supremacy, toxic masculinity, and late-stage capitalism can severely challenge mental health.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR is a body-based technique that uses bilateral stimulation to mimic the brain's state in REM. This process encourages the brain's innate ability to heal from trauma and distress and has been proven to hold the potential to change the way in which we emotionally respond to triggering material. As a therapist, I practice EMDR through tapping and bilateral eye movement. EMDR can be useful in treating post-traumatic stress, anxiety, phobias, low self-esteem, and self-limiting beliefs.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a mental and physical response to stress that can become overwhelming and all consuming. Anxiety often shows up physically as rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, chest and throat tension, or challenges feeling grounded or steady in one’s body. Mentally it can show up as spiraling and worst case scenario thought patterns, intrusive worries, or dread. Chronic anxiety can lead to stress, fear, avoidance, and limit one's quality of life and enjoyment.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Codependency is very misunderstood in pop culture. Codependents are generally folks who grew up around challenging or dysfunctional relational dynamics and needed to prioritize others above themselves or walk on eggshells to avoid abuse or turbulence. This dynamic can lead to self-sacrifice, challenges around control and being controlled, people pleasing, and lack of boundaries. Codependency is common for folks who grew up around addiction or any form of abuse (especially narcissistic abuse).

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma is anything that causes an intrusion upon our minds and bodies that physically and mentally overwhelms our nervous system and overrides our conscious ability to cope and process. Post-traumatic stress is a normal response to an intrusion upon one’s sense of peace and ability to cope. When working with trauma, I recognize the ways in which trauma impacts folks not as disorder, but as a survival response and mark of human resilience. I prioritize client safety and agency.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Our experiences around loss are some of the most significant and universal yet many of us find we do not have ways to memorize, share, and honor the endings in our life. When we process endings and share experiences of grief and loss, we give voice to what once felt unspeakable. In doing this, we open up a courageous and compassionate aspect of our humanity that will help us ultimately find greater peace, deeper wisdom, and tremendous empathy.

specialities.name: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD)
specialities.description: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD) is a challenging condition that affects some individuals in the days leading up to their periods. It goes beyond typical PMS causing intense and sometimes immobilizing symptoms like anxiety, depression, irritability, mood swings, rumination, concentration challenges, negative self-talk, insomnia, and, in severe cases, suicidal thoughts. With greater awareness and the use of distress tolerance practices, PMDD can become more manageable and less overwhelming.

name: Sabrina LaGood-Robinson
title: Student Counselor
intro: The world is a beautiful and complex place, and sometimes we need help navigating through the nuance.
ideal_client: The world is a beautiful and complex place, and sometimes we need help navigating through the nuance. My goal as a counselor is to provide a safe and supportive space to my clients where they can explore their experiences while I offer warmth, I am open and excited to work with anyone who walks through my door, and hope to create a welcoming space for any and all demographics. I have an interest in working with teens and adults who struggle with anxiety, depression, and/or self-esteem issues.

approaches.How We Can Help You: The first step can be the hardest but you’re here! I’d love to help support you on your journey.

name: Raquel Harmon
title: Marriage and Family Therapist
intro: “When things are shaky and nothing is working, we might realize that we are on the verge of something.” - Pema Chödrön
ideal_client: I work with children, families, couples and individuals who are hoping to find new ways to move towards connection, cope through life transitions, or heal from past hurt. I'm passionate about supporting individuals, couples and families who are navigating relationship challenges, grief and loss, faith and spirituality, emerging adulthood, and clients who have ADHD, SPD, or Autism.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I believe that we all move towards wholeness when we have the safety and understanding we need to show up fully for ourselves and in relationship. My style is warm, non-judgmental, present, and hopeful. I want to offer you a space where you can feel seen and un-alone as you navigate life’s complexities, explore more intimately the systems (relational, societal, cultural, political, environmental, religious, etc.) that impact you, interrupt cyclical patterns you may feel stuck in, and find new movement towards a deeper sense of connection with and compassion for yourself and the humans and non-humans in your life and community.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My approach is present and human; I believe that reparative relational experiences are an intrinsic part of how we heal past wounds and repair relationships. I draw from Somatic Mindfulness, Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), and biophilic theories. My work is also influenced by interpersonal neurobiology and how trauma shows up in our body from day to day. I view care work as advocacy and strive to meet each person’s lived experience and wisdom with cultural humility and curiosity. I am continually prioritizing my own education and integration of anti-racist, environmental justice, and disability justice frameworks into my practice.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have worked for a number of years with children and youth and their caregivers facing a wide range of co-occuring mental health and neuro-developmental challenges; first in a public education setting, and for the past two and a half years as a Child and Family Therapist. I especially focus on family ecology, the nervous system, sensory and body awareness, the parent child relationship, co-regulation, positive parenting strategies, and draw from Emotionally Focused Family Therapy theories.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I grew up deep in the bible belt and spent decades grieving, evaluating, de-constructing, and eventually meeting with compassion a faith housed within a nuanced religious system. This lived experience continues to inform my own care for supporting others who have been impacted by Christianity, are seeking to more fully understand their own beliefs, or who simply want someone to walk beside them who understands and can honor and hold the complexities and culture of their faith experience.

name: Tess Krakoff
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi there, I'm Tess. I am a psychotherapist and work individually with adults and teens. Feel free to email me for a free consultation.
ideal_client: I offer individual therapy sessions to adolescents and adults. My therapy sessions are conducted in a comfortable, safe, and confidential manner. It is important to feel connected and my goal is to make sure that clients have a safe place to come for support. I specialize in working with several populations including adolescents, those identifying as LGBTQIA2S+ as well as Indigenous Peoples.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I provide culturally competent therapy and utilize an integrative, holistic, collaborative approach. By blending elements from different approaches, treatment is tailored according to each individual client’s needs. I am rooted in humanistic therapy, which is a client-centered approach that emphasizes unconditional acceptance. Sometimes it’s painful to face things about ourselves or our situations that we would rather ignore. It's worth it to face them because it gives us the opportunity to look at things from a different perspective, to ask different questions, to challenge ourselves, and ultimately to get more of what we want out of life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I listen with respect and curiosity. Psychotherapy can help you in becoming conscious of all parts of the self by improving self-awareness and self-expression, as well as sharing dreams, daydreams, metaphors, narrative stories, bodily sensations, intuitions etc. My pronouns are she/her/hers. I am an active member in the LGBTQ+ community. I am originally from New Jersey and moved to Oregon in 2015 to explore life on the West coast and to broaden my experiences. I believe that interpersonal relationships are important both in and outside of my work. When not at work, I enjoy spending time with family and friends, especially while travelling, camping, or on weekend trips to the woods or the coast. I also love to cook and try out new restaurants. Professional Interests: LGBTQIA2S+, social justice, human relationships, multicultural therapy, crisis intervention, trauma-informed care, IFS

name: Teamworks Non Profit
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Teamworks integrative health clinic is an LGBTQ+ specialized clinic committed to providing care to underserved Oregonians.
ideal_client: The behavioral health team will be a comprehensive, social justice oriented program that will include therapists and peer support specialists. Peers will provide services based on the intentional peer support model. This program will provide outpatient mental health services, such as individual and group therapy, case management and peer support, with a focus on providing specialized care to the LGBTQ+ community.

name: Jonah Stabinski
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: We can work together to make changes towards a life of richness and meaning. My work is about building and savoring a life you care about.
ideal_client: Even the most painful emotions have wisdom. Instead of seeing your mental distress as a disease, I view it as the brain telling us that things in your life need attention. This might relate to your body, relationships in life, old thought patterns, what you do with your days, to how society treats you. There are many roads that lead to suffering. I hope to work with you to identify the circumstances that make your situation unique, so we can better understand how to improve your well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: So often, we treat our pain like an enemy to be conquered. But pain is not the problem—it’s a signal, a call. It speaks in the language of longing: for connection, for safety, for meaning. In our work together, we won’t rush to silence it. We’ll listen. We’ll turn gently toward what hurts—not to fix it, but to understand what it’s asking of you. I’ll invite you to meet yourself with tenderness and patience, to grow your willingness to stay with what’s hard, and to take steps—however small—toward a life that feels rich and true. Change isn’t about erasing the hard parts. It’s about learning how to carry them with care, while making room for what brings you joy. As a Social Worker, I understand how mental health problems can be a product of an oppressive society. For this reason, I value anti-racism, queer and trans liberation, climate justice, compassionate immigration policy, and a strong social safety net.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Alongside my traditional therapy training, I have received certification in Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy from the Integrative Psychiatry Institute. My interest in this work comes from a desire to bridge the worlds of psychedelic healing and evidence-based mental health care. I believe that psychedelics, when held within legal, safe, and research-informed contexts, can offer powerful opportunities for growth. I also provide integration support for those reflecting on psychedelic experiences, with a focus on safety, support, and long-term change. Please note that I do not facilitate access to psychedelic substances or experiences outside of legalized settings in any way.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I specialize in treating: Depression, Psychedelics, Social Anxiety, and Generalized Anxiety

name: Alex Harrison
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi, I'm Alex. I'm a relational, trauma-informed therapist blending Jungian psychology, somatic psychotherapy, and creative expression.
ideal_client: Are you feeling lost and disoriented in a transitional time of your life? Frustrated with repeating the same patterns and losing touch with the magic of who you are? Maybe you have encountered adversity in your life that has left you feeling emotionally dysregulated and disconnected from yourself, others, and the world. Or maybe you are looking for support in finding meaning and purpose, reclaiming your inspiration and passion, and rewriting your story as one of empowerment and expansion.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is to help you explore the unconscious forces contributing to pattern repetition, emotional distress, and disconnection from self and others. I strongly believe we all possess an inner healing intelligence that speaks to us in a variety of ways, and my intention is to facilitate this process by listening deeply and providing space for you to express those parts of you that have been suppressed or discouraged out of fear or out of necessity. I am also trained in EMDR and somatic therapy and often incorporate techniques like meditation, art, and parts work to help access and integrate difficult life experiences, amplify your intuitive capacity, and remove the blocks keeping you from sharing the gift of your authentic self with the world.

name: Hanna Omori
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help women feel more connected, understood, and empowered by offering a warm, supportive space for growth and healing.
ideal_client: The Core Practice provides a safe and supportive space for your mental health journey. We believe in the power of connection and personal growth. Our dedicated therapists use evidence-based techniques to help you navigate life’s challenges, all while ensuring you feel heard and valued. Whether you're dealing with anxiety, relationship issues, or simply need someone to talk to, we're here for you. Join us at The Core Practice, where your mental wellness is our priority. Let's work together!

approaches.What I Specialize In: Do you often feel overwhelmed by the demands that come from being a woman, adulting with ADHD, or carrying racial trauma/cultural identity issues? Do you often second guess or suppress your needs or feelings and feel more disconnected from your sense of self as a result? Are you feeling stuck in a cycle of negative self-talk, guilt, or shame that has gotten internalized and it's been affecting how you feel about yourself, or your ability to be more present and how you show up in relationships? Are you presently grieving the loss of a loved one, a beloved pet, or parts of yourself and feel alone in your pain? I specialize in therapy for women experiencing mid-life transitions, intergenerational trauma, cultural issues, grief/loss, and/or ADHD. I provide a supportive and non-judgmental space for processing complex emotions in a way that feels safe to you and exploring the patterns that are getting in the way of you living a life that is more true to you.

name: Lindsay Day
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi! I'm Lindsay. I have experience working with trauma, domestic violence, body image issues, ADHD, and anxiety to name a few.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with clients with a variety of concerns. I love aiding in clients building awareness of who they are, have the ability to self-validate, utilize tools to ground and self-sooth, and have a better relationship with themselves which will benefit relating to others. I also focus on being trauma-informed and culturally competent with each unique client. I

approaches.My Background and Approach: I earned a Bachelor's degree in Psychology (2015) and I hold a Master's degree in Marriage, Couple, and Family counseling (2020), both from Portland State University. I have completed trainings that include risk assessment and mandated reporting, implicit bias, a 40-hour Domestic Violence training, and an Internal Family Systems (IFS) Circle Course training (2023). I have a passion for body positivity and body neutrality to combat the negative and detrimental affects of diet culture. I have knowledge , passion, and experience working with survivors of domestic violence and understand the complex nuances to that experience. As a neurodivergent clinician, I have knowledge and personal experience of ADHD and work as an ADHD teen coach as well.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I personally strive to be a lifelong learner and continue to grow my cultural competence as a counselor so that I may be better informed of the diverse clientele and their experiences that I hope to see and work with. As someone who holds several privileged identities, I will continue to be aware of and acknowledge the privileges that come with having those identities and how it will impact my work and future clients moving forward. I also believe strongly that mental health services and counseling should be accessible to all. I will use my privilege and position to advocate for accessibility for all in the need of mental health services and support. I also believe the relationship between client and counselor is the greatest change agent, so I focus and work to build trust and foster comfort for my client throughout the process. I strive to create a safe and comfortable place for my clients and my intentional use of humor adds to that.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: IFS posits that the mind is made up of multiple parts that can take on extreme roles or sub-personalities. Each part has its own perspective and memories and underlying the part is the person’s true Self, or core self. The goal of IFS is to heal wounded parts and achieve mental balance. In IFS, we are not aiming to remove any parts of ourselves that may be destructive; all parts are welcome and deserve to be healed. It is a great, non-pathological approach to mental health.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I not only have a diagnosis of ADHD myself, I also work with individuals on managing ADHD symptoms and also normalizing their experiences in a neuro-typical world. I also provide ADHD teen coaching through Portland ADHD coach.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: I recognize the prevalence of diet culture that permeates through consumed media. I aim to combat the messages that we all receive about our bodies and the "beauty standards" and facilitate a better relationship with one's body and with food.

name: Kelly Yan
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I support mental wellness through medication management and behavioral health counseling.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with diverse populations, including BIPOC, LGBTQ and non-gender traditional adults. I work in partnership with you, your therapist, and other members of your care team to manage concerns such as anxiety, depression, trauma-related disorders, mood disorders, psychosis, inattention, and neurodivergence.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My treatment philosophy is grounded in evidence-based practice and patient-centered care. I believe in using the gentlest interventions that will achieve your specific goals. I believe in holistic care and collaboration with primary care providers, therapists, and community partners. I do not perform ADHD assessments, but I can provide ongoing ADHD treatment. I do not prescribe benzodiazepines long-term.

name: Lauren Hoffman
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Hi! I’m Lauren (she/her). I specialize in working with ADHD, anxiety, trauma, relationship issues, and life transitions.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My values as a therapist are to provide non-judgmental, empathic, and culturally informed care, while emphasizing an environment founded on personal growth, openness, and honesty. I use a multi-faceted approach to therapy to best fit the unique needs of each client because I recognize one size does not fit all. I often work from a psychodynamic-relational stance, using the client-therapist relationship as a tool to increase my client’s awareness of interactions between self, others, and the world to improve decision-making and enhance life satisfaction. I also incorporate mindfulness-based, trauma informed techniques to promote insight with practical, here-and-now interventions. I have experience diagnosing and treating a variety of presenting issues, including anxiety, depression, mood disorders, trauma, adjustment, and ADHD.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: For ten years I have been providing individual therapy to a diverse population of adults and adolescents in a variety of settings, including inpatient clinics, a community mental health center, university counseling settings, and now private practice. I would be honored to assist you on your journey towards healing.

name: Robyn Cullen
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: As a queer, witchy therapist, I believe in a world where what makes us feel lonely & othered no longer separates us, it brings us together.
ideal_client: My clients are often professional helpers & healers looking for a space to, "just be the client." They are often going through relational transitions like divorce/separations/remarriage. I support men, women, non-binary, trans & genderfluid folks who are moving through confusing, challenging & painful life transitions. I meet them at the intersection of the mystical and the clinical. The "outsiders" find what feels like HOME here & I'm honored to be a guide & fellow traveler.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Becoming a therapist was a second career for me. After 10 years in the fast-paced world of corporate marketing, I was laid off during the 2008 recession. The much-needed career change directed my inner compass to a master's program in marriage and family therapy that same year. I had no idea how becoming a therapist would completely unravel EVERYTHING I thought to be true about life, family, love, relationships, spirituality, and ME. Such a gift. This is a space to talk about any of the nuances folks experience relating to (but not limited to) race, sexuality, gender, neurodivergence, ability, unearned privilege and/or advantage and anything else that may be or have been “taboo” in other areas of life. I bring this work to life through individual therapy for those in California & Oregon, group community-building gatherings, Usui reiki energy work and holding spiritual spaces for those who gave up on organized religion but deeply miss and yearn for a spiritual community.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe therapy is political - meaning that therapy as a practice & institution is influenced by and contributes to the politics of society. I acknowledge the privileges & advantages (both earned & unearned) that I hold as a working class white American citizen with settler ancestry and post-secondary education who presents as neurotypical, straight, and able-bodied. While my position as a non-straight, neurodivergent person with mostly-stable mental health has allowed me to generate more insights and compassion into these lived experiences, I am committed to listening, learning, unlearning, decolonizing, and growing within my personal & professional worlds. I live & work through a lens of anti-oppressive & anti-racism. I am constantly working to create supportive & supported spaces for those who are marginalized, oppressed & silenced to be seen, heard & witnessed by hiring and learning from mentors of the global majority.

name: Heather Asaadi
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Life is messy. In both/and counseling, we collaborate and hold complexity together to help sort through the mess and find more balance.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am passionate about building meaningful therapeutic relationships - it is within relationships that healing and growth occur. Within the safety of therapy, you can more fully explore your patterns, come to understand factors that contributed to your development, and find a balance between accepting yourself and changing patterns that are not serving you anymore. I work to be attuned to the systems that impact us, such as, the social and cultural effects on our lives, as well as, exploring how your identities intersect and interact with your environment. My approach is eclectic and trauma-informed. I gravitate towards relational/interpersonal therapies which emphasize exploring patterns of relational disconnection and enhancing connection. My practice is focused on collaborating using a dialectical framework, which is about looking through a both/and lens to appreciate complexity, find more balance, and increase compassion towards ourselves and others.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I am passionate about building a meaningful therapeutic relationship - it is within relationships that healing and growth occur. A meaningful therapeutic relationship is when we can feel zest and energy together, we feel that we matter to one another, and have the experience of mutually learning, growing, and empowering each other.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT) is a combination of mindfulness, CBT, and acknowledging that multiple truths exist at the same time (dialectics). DBT teaches skills focused on being mindful, understanding and regulating your emotions, tolerating distress more skillfully, and increasing effectiveness in interpersonal interactions/relationships. DBT informs my approach and I like to utilize concepts and skills from it with clients, but I am not practicing it to it's full fidelity in sessions.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Therapy is a great place to learn about the patterns you’ve developed (cognitive/behavioral/emotional/relational patterns), explore what has contributed to the development of these patterns, and work to change patterns that aren’t working for you anymore.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: I think it is important to explore how your identity and relational patterns are impacted by different systems: family, culture, society, & oppression. These systems can play a significant role in our mental health.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma impacts so much! It is useful to raise understanding of how trauma reacts in the body and brain and what trauma-related beliefs you might have developed. I'm trained in Narrative Exposure Therapy (NET), which helps process trauma, build more context around your trauma history, and empower you to change your narrative.

name: Jordana Krueger-Toscher
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Through a warm, down-to-earth, collaborative approach I'll help you to achieve your goals for change and find peace with the way life is.
ideal_client: My specialty areas include managing anxiety, ADHD, stress around work, family, dating, relationships, college and life transitions, improving self esteem and coping with infertility and childlessness. I am licensed in and accepting clients from Oregon, Washington and New York.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: By using Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) with a focus on mindfulness and your unique strengths, I can help you understand and change unhelpful thoughts, feelings and behaviors. Through our work you'll develop a better awareness of who you are, what you want and how to get it. I'll help you discover and feel confident in yourself, and figure out how to live the life you want. Together we'll identify problem areas or places where you feel stuck and find new ways of responding that will afford you more enjoyable, fulfilling outcomes. I'm dedicated to creating an environment of respect and appreciation for all clients' racial and ethnic membership, gender and sexual identity, social class, religious affiliation, nationality, body size, and disability status. Throughout our work I'll promote an atmosphere of openness, trust, and safety where all attitudes, beliefs, values, and behaviors can be freely explored and discussed.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: My experience and training make me especially qualified to help individuals manage a broad variety of concerns. I earned my bachelor's degree in psychology from the State University of NY at Stony Brook in 2003, and my master's degree in social work (MSW) from the University of Pennsylvania School of Social Policy and Practice in 2005. I then completed three years of intensive clinical practice and study, earning my LCSW (licensed clinical social work) credential in 2011. I have extensive training in evidence-based practices including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

name: Melanie Sellers
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Melanie offers nature based therapy focused on sexual embodiment and mindfulness to help you reconnect with the wisdom of your body.
ideal_client: My clients are individuals seeking deeper connection to their body, mind, and emotions. I work with adults of all genders and sexual orientations navigating challenges like intimacy, self-expression, trauma, and self-worth. My ideal clients are curious and open to exploring embodiment practices, mindfulness, and nature’s wisdom. Whether you’re working through relationship struggles, healing sexual shame, or seeking greater vitality, I offer a compassionate, holistic space to support your growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Change is a gradual and deeply personal process, and I believe your body holds the innate wisdom to guide you. My role is to support and empower you on your journey of self-discovery, creating a space where your autonomy leads the way. Together, we’ll move at a pace that honors your comfort and readiness, ensuring a personalized and self-directed exploration. Nature is central to my approach, offering a unique lens through which we can explore your experiences and deepen your healing. Reconnecting with the natural world can provide grounding, clarity, and insight into your relationship with yourself and others. Drawing on a variety of somatic and relational skills, I weave evidence-based practices from my CACREP-accredited master’s program at George Fox University with a holistic lens. This integration helps us connect the physical, emotional, and relational aspects of your life to foster growth, resilience, and a more embodied sense of well-being.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in the power of connection—to ourselves, to others, and Nature. My work is guided by values of inclusivity, authenticity, and holistic healing. As someone passionate about social justice, I aim to create a space where individuals of all identities feel seen, heard, and valued. I am deeply inspired by the interplay of nature and healing. I’ve always felt a strong bond with the earth’s rhythms, which I now integrate into my therapy practice. I also advocate for body sovereignty, sexual health education, and breaking the stigma around mental health and intimacy. Outside of my practice, I enjoy exploring nature, practicing mindfulness, and deepening my understanding of embodiment through ongoing training and research. My work is not just a profession—it’s a calling to help others uncover their innate capacity for healing and transformation.

name: Matthew Lucas MSW, CSWA
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: How are you? No really, How are you?
ideal_client: Change happens with compassion and support. Let's work together and take the time to discover barriers and examine patterns to author a story that aligns with a new vision for your future. You get to have the life you want and deserve. Let's work together to push against the boundaries that are no longer useful to you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Working collaboratively with compassion as the foundation. We will have an open, honest, empathic, and nonjudgmental exchange of ideas. The goal is to create a safe space where individuals feel heard. If you're experiencing shifts in relationships (family/ partner), feelings of anxiousness, or depression, let's work together to find ways to manage the complexities of life and relationships.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I've seen firsthand how ethnicity, culture, and gender influence who receives therapy and how it's delivered. As a Black gay clinician with intersectional identities, my goal is to reduce barriers and normalize therapy. For anyone who has experienced marginalization due to their identity. Let's start today.

name: Carrie R. Conklin
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Hello! I'm Carrie R. Conklin, a Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
ideal_client: I work with individuals, couples, and families on a wide variety of topics. Every client I work with comes with a rich history, unique view of the world, and specific culture that impacts their current functioning, values, and well-being. Some of the topics I work with clients on include: - Marital/Pre-marital Counseling - Relationship Distress - Communication - Values Identification - Identity - Anxiety & Depression - Church-related Struggles

approaches.How I Can Help You: Naming and identifying the feelings that cause us to react versus respond is hard work! Through hearing your story, we can begin to identify how you react from places of pain, and over time, identify ways that you can respond from places of peace. This will allow you to build a sense of self that aligns with your values, be more effective in your relationships, and address any "stuck points" that are impacting your life. The combination of the mind and body is a powerful healing tool. I am passionate about helping people access a calm and grounded state that creates a pathway to well-being, growth, love and safety. This is the beginning of hope and change. As a person who loves wholeheartedly, I welcome all people and am committed to supporting individuals, couples and families in their unique therapeutic journey.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In my free time I can be found reading a good book, listening to true-crime podcasts, traveling, eating delicious food with friends, and spending time with my family.

name: Kimberly Clifford
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: Kim is a certified physician assistant specializing in adult ADHD. She offers diagnostic assessments and medication management.
ideal_client: Kim owns PNW-ADHD clinic with her business partner Liz Hoke, LMFT. Kim and Liz provide holistic care to their patients by providing diagnostic assessments, medication management, lifestyle coaching, and behavior therapy tailored to adults with ADHD.

approaches.My Background: Kim is originally from Colorado, she earned her undergraduate degree from the University of Northern Colorado before attending PA school at Heritage University in Toppenish, Washington. Kim spent seven years in emergency medicine in Portland, Oregon, gaining valuable experience in acute care. She is passionate about volunteering, she works with nonprofits to provide direct medical care to those experiencing houselessness. She believes in always meeting her patients where they are at regardless of their current situation. Prior to attending PA school Kim worked as a massage therapist, working alongside other integrative medicine practitioners. She has the perspective of working in both the eastern and western medical world. While working in the hospital system she grew frustrated with the large healthcare machine and the lack of holistic interventions. She has now transitioned back to outpatient medicine where she can focus on integrative care for adult ADHD

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: We view ADHD not just as a diagnosis, but as a unique way of being where people experience the world in a non-ordinary way. People with this diagnosis have gifts that inspire new approaches to life's challenges. We understand the difficulties of navigating the modern world with ADHD both personally and professionally. We are dedicated to fostering a supportive environment where people in our community impacted by ADHD can thrive and achieve their full potential.

name: Regina Tricamo
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: If you would like to address a difficult moment or work on longer-standing issues, I look forward to talking.
ideal_client: Perhaps my most rewarding work is done with clients who wish to explore their family history and understand how it is impacting them now - the strengths, the challenging patterns. I enjoy working with therapists to help support them while addressing issues that come up in their work with clients. I enjoy working with individuals and couples - gay, lesbian, trans, queer, straight - as they consider or move forward with family-building or face fertility challenges.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and have been working in Portland since 2015. Sessions are collaborative, focusing first on your strengths and what is going well. Then, as we look at the difficulties you’re facing, we build on those abilities. I encourage listening to your own voice and building confidence as you experience transitions and challenges. You can expect sessions that are supportive, compassionate and sometimes challenging, with a good bit of humor. Using a Family Systems framework we identify how you are shaped by your family of origin and the impact that those patterns and roles play in your current relationships and sense of self. We work on the ability to make connections, create community, strengthen your voice and to expand your passions and interests. Additionally, we can draw upon Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, cognitive behavioral therapy and mindfulness to help support understanding and change.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have lived in Portland since 1997 and attended graduate school at PSU for my Masters in Social Work. I grew up in San Francisco and lived for years in Brooklyn, NY and carry a bit of the sensibility of each of those cities with me.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: We are all shaped in some ways by the context of our families of origin. As we identify patterns from our families, we have the opportunity to make different choices in our lives now. I find this to be some of the most exciting and fruitful work I engage in as a therapist and therefore I have worked for years with a mentor and consultation group to explore this approach in depth.

specialities.name: Infertility
specialities.description: I have experience working with individuals and couples, LGBTQ+ and straight, who are considering choices about parenthood - through pregnancy, reproductive interventions or adoption.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Whether depression is new to you or a frequent presence, I work with you using a holistic approach that looks at your current stressors, your history and ways in which you can better care for yourself to help you experience joy and engagement again. I have specialized training in depression and anxiety in pregnancy and postpartum.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: There can be so many types of losses - loss of community or job/career, death of a loved one, pregnancy loss (through termination, stillbirth, miscarriage). I allow time for full expression of grief, recognition of all of the losses that are attached to it and then, gradually, the building of meaning, purpose and healing.

specialities.name: Cancer
specialities.description: I have experience working with clients who have a diagnosis of cancer or other major medical issues. I look to support you in adjusting to this new reality, considering options regarding treatments and increasing your supportive connections with others.

name: Molz Wirtz-Wold
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: A clinician for 20 years, I specialize in supporting queer and trans adults, relationships/couples, and folks with Bipolar Disorder.
ideal_client: I work with couples and relationships where people are struggling to connect and understand each other, but would like to. I work with queer and/or trans looking for mental wellness, understanding their sexuality, and learning the language to express who they are and want they want. Many of my clients are neurodivergent. I am also trained in helping people with Bipolar disorder find their stability and peace.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My mission is to support my clients with a compassionate and creative approach, attachment-centered using research based methods. I want to help people discover ways to heal and move forward in their lives, and to feel more free to be their authentic selves. Transgender/non binary affirming and identifying: they/them Trauma-informed practices Trained in Emotionally Focused Couples Counseling (EFT) and Gottman for Couples In training for PACT Level One (Psychobiological Approach to Couples Counseling) Sex therapist, AASECT member Polyamorous friendly/knowledgeable Anti-racist, anti-oppression, committed to doing my own work Kink friendly/knowledgeable Queer Enjoy supporting other therapists, helping professionals Experienced/trained in supporting people with Bipolar Disorder Experienced, trained in supporting Autistic people, people with ADHD and other kinds of neurodivergence Health at Every Size supportive, fat liberation

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I enjoy helping people explore their gender (or lack of gender) in a safe environment. I come to this work from an existential perspective and love helping people explore concepts such as identity, personal meaning, freedom and change. In relationship work/couples counseling, I want to help people develop healthy connections and attachments to the people they love and to themselves. I believe couples are the experts on each other, and my job is to help them make more accurate guesses about each of their their feelings, wants and needs. I am fat, queer and trans. I benefit from white privilege and work to educate myself so I can minimize the harm done via white supremacy culture in the therapy room and beyond. In my free time, I love to garden, play analog and modular synthesizers, hike to hot springs, and eat all the delicious foods. I play a lot of video games (recent fave is Valheim), go see live shows, and updating our 1906 foursquare home with my wife.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I am trained in PACT: psychobiological approach to couples counseling. PACT is a fusion of attachment theory, developmental neuroscience, and arousal regulation. Understanding how the brain works provides a physiological basis for understanding how people act and react within relationships. In a nutshell, some areas of your brain are wired to reduce threat and danger and seek security, while others are geared to establish mutuality and loving connection.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Our relationships with the people who raised us gave us our foundation for understanding the world: are others safe or not? Can I trust people? As adults, we respond to those we care most about according to our experiences from birth to young childhood. Knowing our attachment styles can give us the ability to choose good partners, and have healthy relationships.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: Most of my clients are transgender and/or non-binary. I have taught masters level classes for other therapists on how to support clients around gender, and helping people explore their own gender identity is one of my favorite parts of being a therapist.

specialities.name: Bipolar
specialities.description: I enjoy helping clients learn how to manage bipolar symptoms and live as peaceful as life as they choose. I believe the societal stigma around bipolar is incredibly damaging and I work to help people thrive despite potential negative perspectives out there. I enjoy supporting people find rhythm and balance in their lives through attention to sleep, regular nutrition, awareness of drugs and alcohol on stability, adherence to medication if prescribed, and stress management.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: In relationship work/couples counseling, I want to help people develop healthy connections and attachments to the people they love and to themselves. I believe that my clients are the experts in their relationship, and it is my job and honor to help coach and guide them into more effective ways of relating. Many of us were not given models for what a healthy relationship looks like, nor how to disagree in ways that feel fair and just for everyone involved.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I have worked for 20 years with people of all ages who are on the autism spectrum, and other kinds of neurodivergence. I enjoy helping people learn what they need, how to advocate for themselves, and build self compassion. The world was not built for the needs of autistic people, and many times people blame themselves for not being able to fit in better, easier. Neurodivergent people deserve to have their needs met in ways that work for them, and I like helping them figure out how.

name: Danesh Oleshko LMFT
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Integral Psychotherapist who enjoys providing professional & open-hearted presence.
ideal_client: I enjoy practicing psychotherapy that is holistic and life-transforming. As an LMFT with depth specialization, I listen to your emotional heart and soul to heal the mind. The issues that you experience as an individual, couple or in relationship with family deserve attention with that kind of dedication. Trained in integral psychology with specialization in complex addiction issues, I'm also honored to have over a decade of apprenticeship with indigenous elders. This experience allows me to care

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My commitment is to provide effective therapy. You can expect genuine connection, active listening and engaged style with me. I'm curious and open-hearted. I studied Integral Counseling Psychology at the nation's leading school in this field: California Institute of Integral Science (CIIS) in San Francisco. I've been blessed with exceptional teachers and guides, leaders in the field of psychodynamic, person-centered and existential psychotherapy. Parallel to formal education, I've also been apprenticing with indigenous tradition keepers of ceremonial use of Sacred Plant medicine Ayahuasca: consciousness - expanding and purifying experience. I have specialized in mental health and addiction therapy by co-founding and developing holistic treatment programs for recovery, as well as working in an community mental health agency in Ashland that facilitated recovery alongside with family therapy, couples therapy and trauma-informed care. Welcome to my healing practice.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My core values are professional competence, empathy and genuine presence. I strive to learn and approach each session with an open heart. Becoming a therapist is an outcome of a long search my true calling in life. I feel blessed to have my purpose. As part of my learning, I've studied with leaders in the field of depth psychology; I've apprenticed under guidance of indigenous tradition keepers. I discovered deep passion for treatment of addiction and trauma: have pioneered and developed holistic treatment programs in South America. Currently, my private practice integrates psychotherapy with Ayurveda and traditional healing ceremonies with sacred plants of the Amazonian region. I live simple life on the Oregon coast with my wife and two curious dogs. I do yoga everyday, run in the woods and take my wooden boat on adventures in the Bay. In addition to providing depth therapy, I love to play music, Banya - finish sauna & hugging people I love.

name: Danielle LaBruzzo
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Therapy for trauma, relationships, and identity—rooted in safety, compassion, and the belief that healing is possible.
ideal_client: I work with individuals healing from trauma, managing addiction, and navigating relationships, identity, or family dynamics. This includes people affected by a loved one’s intense or challenging behaviors. My practice is inclusive of all identities and relationship structures. My clients seek to break patterns, align with their values, and build more authentic, connected lives.

approaches.My Background and Approach: With over 15 years of experience, I support individuals navigating trauma, addiction, attachment wounds, identity exploration, and relationship challenges. I provide inclusive, affirming care for people of all identities and relationship structures, including monogamous, non-monogamous, and everything in between. I also work with those impacted by a loved one’s addiction or emotional struggles. My approach draws from behavioral, attachment-based, and values-driven therapies, including ACT and CBT. I help clients build emotional regulation skills, interrupt harmful patterns, and create meaningful, lasting change. Therapy with me is compassionate, collaborative, and focused on aligning your life with what matters most. Together, we work to increase self-trust, expand your capacity for connection, and foster a deeper sense of wholeness in how you relate to yourself and others.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe therapy works best when it feels real, collaborative, and grounded in trust. I show up as a human first—warm, curious, and engaged. My goal is to offer a space where you can be honest, explore what’s been painful or stuck, and move toward something more aligned with who you are and what you care about. I welcome people of all identities and relationship structures, and I approach conversations around identity, culture, and power with openness and humility. I value creativity, connection, and a sense of humor in this work. I believe healing often starts with feeling safe enough to be seen—and grows through tending to your limits, honoring your needs, and rebuilding self-compassion. Outside of sessions, I spend my time being near water whenever I can and hanging out with my dog, Woody Harrelson—who occasionally appears in virtual sessions and takes his role as therapy assistant very seriously.

name: Donna Prinzmetal
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I believe healing is possible for everyone. Therapy can help you find tools and the inner strengths you didn't know you had.
ideal_client: In this time of uncertainty, many of us are dealing with increased anxiety, depression, isolation and relationship problems. It can be stressful for people working from home, either alone or with partners and sometimes kids they're trying to manage with on-line learning. In this time of pandemic, we are all in the same boat but we all have different reactions to these stressful times.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am warm, respectful and attentive, with a good sense of humor. I am a poet and believe in the healing power of creative expression. I use an eclectic approach and sometimes include writing and other creative outlets in my practice to further healing. My goal is for clients to feel heard and empowered.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my Masters in Psychology at Antioch University in Los Angeles in 1983. I became licensed in California in 1985 as a Marriage and Family Therapist. I moved to Oregon in 1994 and got licensed here. For over thirty years in private practice, I have worked with adults, adolescents, couples and families to provide a safe place to explore the possibilities for healing. I treat a wide range of issues and have a number of tools in my therapeutic toolbox. As a writer and a teacher, I understand that healing can come in many forms. Sometimes I incorporate creative visualization, writing and other imaginative processes to facilitate awareness and transformation. I have felt privileged to witness my clients make positive and dramatic changes in careers, relationships, sense of self and personal empowerment as they have emerged from some very dark places. Huge changes can begin with one small step. I believe that growth and healthy connections are possible for everyone.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: We all strive for healthy connections in friendship, work and intimate relationships. As a relational therapist, I focus on connection both in the therapeutic relationship and in the outside world. My goal is for my clients to nurture and develop strong, satisfying and empowering connections.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: As a psychodynamic psychotherapist, I am always striving to understand the situations and experiences, including early familial relationships, that have shaped my clients' lives. Therapy can illuminate the origins of conscious and unconscious choices, giving us the opportunity for healing and change.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: As a writer and a therapist, I am interested in stories. We live our lives based on our histories and the stories we have lived as well as the ones we tell ourselves. I sometimes use writing therapy to access and understand the narratives that have informed my clients' lives. If you know and understand your story, you have choices and it is easier to shape a new one.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: I help people with a variety of life transitions. If you have recently experienced a change in relationship, work, or family status, you might be feeling overwhelmed, depressed or anxious. Therapy can help you make sense of the changes in your life and can also help you make positive choices when embarking on a new path.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: As women, we are constantly defining and re-defining ourselves. As we journey through different phases of our lives, we sometimes face challenging decisions and difficult transitions. Therapy can help women develop a stronger identity, increased well-being and a sense of empowerment. Writing therapy can be enormously healing.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Struggles in relationships often have to do with individual stories and histories that are interfering in the present. Therapy can help couples find clarity when navigating an impasse, when trying to decide whether a relationship should continue, and can be effective when a relationship has lost its spark and there is a desire to enliven intimacy and connection.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Gaining an understanding of where the anxiety comes from can be helpful but isn't always enough. I work with clients to increase their emotional sense of safety and self assurance. We also work on strategies to better deal with anxiety-provoking situations.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: 'In a dark time, the eye begins to see' The poet, Theodore Roethke, recognized the opportunities available even in our most troubled moments. When you feel boxed in, therapy can help you find your way out of the tunnel into the light again. Healing is always possible.

name: Cassandra Walsh
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I am passionate about helping individuals process trauma and reclaim their power.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with folx who experience complex trauma and PTSD, with a focus on addressing childhood experiences, domestic and sexual violence, religious trauma, and experiences within the LGBTQIA+ community. My practice is a safe space for all individuals, including sex workers, immigrants, BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and People of Color), and people of all genders, sexual orientations, relationship structures, and people of all abilities.)

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Healing from trauma is a journey, and every step you take is a powerful act of self-care and resilience. No matter where you are in your process, I believe in your capacity for growth, change, and healing. Together, we can work toward a future where you feel empowered, whole, and connected to your authentic self. It’s never too late to reclaim your story and build the life you deserve.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I am deeply committed to practicing cultural humility, recognizing and respecting the unique identities and backgrounds of each client. My approach is sensitive to identity(s), including ethnicity, race, ability, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, immigration status, body size, socioeconomic position, and religion. Conversations about identity and culture are always welcome and encouraged in our work together. My commitment to social justice extends beyond the therapy room. I work to advocate for non-discriminatory practices, human rights, equity, and safety for all. It is my hope that these efforts contribute to a safe and therapeutic atmosphere where you can express your authentic self.

name: Richard Nalbandian
title: Clinical Psychologist
