intro: Richard Nalbandian, Psy.D., is a licensed clinical psychologist. His practice is based out of Portland, Oregon.
ideal_client: Dr. Nalbandian has extensive experience working with adults from various backgrounds on issues including anxiety, depression, grief, complex trauma, relationship struggles, family conflict, and personality troubles. He has worked in medical centers, universities, and community mental health clinics.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Dr. Nalbandian completed his internship and post-doctoral residency in Boston, Massachusetts as a fellow at the Danielsen Institute at Boston University. He has focused training in and provides psychotherapy for individuals, couples, and families. Additionally, he completed two years of post-graduate psychoanalytic training at the William Alanson White Institute in NYC for the treatment of Eating Disorders, Compulsions, and Addictions (EDCAS). Dr. Nalbandian's therapeutic style is relational and collaborative.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I approach therapy as a collaboration. I value the cultural context and story of each individual, and am particularly interested in areas of creativity, psychological trauma, immigration/acculturation, group dynamics, grief, and relationship issues. I have in-depth experience working with individuals in the helping profession (i.e., therapists, clergy, and medical professionals), artists, and survivors of trauma. I have experience and interest in exploring vocational pursuits/conflicts and intersectional identity development including neurodiveristy.

name: Luc Boudreau
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: PC-A, LMHC-A, OT Reg, MA, NCC
intro: I specialize in trauma-informed care & adopt an integrated approach that best fits each client.
ideal_client: Do you find yourself repeating unhealthy patterns despite knowing and wanting something different for yourself? That's where i can help. I specialize in helping people who struggle from the effects of trauma, relationships/dating, and issues around self confidence, self esteem, & perfectionism. Life can be hard but together, we can make it easier.

approaches.My Background and Approach: For the past 20 years, I've worked in various settings including inpatient, outpatient, community health, as a crisis counselor and as a college professor. As a therapist, i draw from several therapeutic frameworks in order to meet your unique needs. My approach integrates neuroscience with psychology to help maximize growth. I use an intuitive and integrated approach based on trauma-focused principles that restores the mind, the body, and spirit. I have specialized training in EMDR, IFS, CBT, ACT, Psychodynamic Theory, Attachment Theory, EFT & The Gottman Method. I offer services via telehealth for clients residing in Oregon & Washington, and in-person at my office in Hillsboro Oregon. I am also bilingual in English & French.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: My private practice was born from a deeply personal journey - one of struggle, resilience, & transformation. As a skinny, awkward kid, I knew what it was like to feel invisible, to battle social anxiety, & to carry the weight of rejection & bullying. The pain of those experiences was then compounded by years of trauma which left me feeling stuck, uncertain, & alone. Through my own healing, I discovered the power of self-worth, confidence, & resilience. Now as a therapist, I've made it my mission to guide others on their own path to self-empowerment. My calling is to help people break through self doubt, overcome past wounds, & step into the strong, confident lives they deserve. I help clients turn pain into power, fear into self confidence, & struggle into success. Now matter where you are in your journey, you don't have to do it alone. I'm here to help you show up for yourself, reclaim your confidence, and thrive - even in difficult moments.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am "EMDR trained" by EMDRIA and have also completed numerous specialized EMDR training protocols. In my practice, EMDR is often integrated with other approaches - such as IFS or attachment based therapy to support deeper healing, emotional regulation, and increased self compassion. I also engage in regular consultation with EMDR consultants.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I am "IFS trained" by the IFS Institute. I completed an extensive 6-month training program and continue to expand my knowledge through various continuing education opportunities. This training helps me guide clients in moving beyond symptom management and toward deep self understanding, emotional freedom, and inner harmony.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I've completed extensive training in CBT from the Adler Institute. This training has given me the tools to help clients better manage their emotional responses, break unhelpful cycles and improve their overall sense of well-being.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I have completed level one Gottman Method training through the Gottman Institute, a leading research-based approach to couples therapy developed by Drs. John and Julie Gottman. This training equips me with tools to help couples build stronger, more resilient relationships by improving communication, managing conflict, and deepening emotional intimacy.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I specialize in working with clients struggling with PTSD, and the lasting effects of trauma. My approach is grounded in a deep understanding of how overwhelming experiences can shape the nervous system, disrupt a person's sense of safety, and leave lasting emotional imprints. I use a combination of EMDR and IFS to support clients in healing from the inside out. Both are powerful, evidence-based methods for helping clients process traumatic memories without having to relive them in detail.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I help clients understand and overcome anxiety using a blend of evidence-based & trauma-informed approaches. Anxiety can take many forms - chronic worry, panic, social fears, or physical tension - and often reflect both current stress and deeper emotional patterns. I use a blend of approach that best meets the needs of the client including CBT, EMDR, IFS, ACT, & psychodynamic theory. These help to increase self-awareness, and support lasting emotional growth.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: I specialize in helping clients who struggle with low self-esteem, self-doubt, and inner criticism. My approach blends evidence-based and trauma-informed therapies to address the root causes, whether they stem from past experiences, attachment wounds, or internalized messages. My goal is to help clients reconnect to their strengths, develop a more empowering self-narrative, and build lasting confidence from the inside out.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I specialize in treating depression with a compassionate, integrative and evidence-based approach that addresses both the emotional systems and the underlying causes. Depression can feel like disconnection, numbness, hopelessness, or self criticism - and it often reflects deeper unresolved pain. My goal is to help you feel more connected, empowered, and capable of creating meaningful change in your life.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in helping couples & individuals navigate relationship & marriage challenges. Drawing from the Gottman Method, I support clients in improving communication, rebuilding trust, and strengthening connection through practical tools. I also use EFT to help couples move beyond surface conflict and access the deeper emotional needs and fears that drive disconnection. Rooted in attachment theory, my work focuses on helping clients feel safer, understood, and emotionally attuned.

name: Jillian Brown
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My desire in life is to support people in feeling secure in themselves, for one's body to be a place of comfort and home.
ideal_client: Why does this keep happening or why do I keep making the same choices over and over again? Why am I stuck in this pattern and how do I get out of it? Why am I having this experience, but other people don't have this challenge? If you are having these questions or experiences that's a good time to reach out to me. The subconscious is all about patterns and I'm excited about breaking patterns and creating new experiences!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a depth psychologist and infinitely fascinated by the subconscious mind and the vast wisdom and potential we possess, but don't often access. I tend to use modalities that bring forward subconscious material and support creating new neuropathways. Our brains and bodies are in full support of us being safe, happy and healthy in this world, we just need to find ways to work in collaboration with ourselves rather than living in conflict with different parts of ourselves.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a Masters in Psychology with a Counseling focus from Saybrook University. I have been working as a Hypnotherapist since 2011. I have a certificate in Process Oriented Psychology from the Process Work Institute. My favorite modality lately is Family Constellations. It is a powerful tool for creating big changes and also healing ancestral trauma. I have studied shamanic journeying, energy work, NVC, pre and perinatal psychology, and attachment theory is one of my main lenses.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I have worked as a hypnotherapist since 2011. Working on this deep level and doing energy work, past-life regression, life between life work, and shamanic journeys has taught me a lot about spirituality. I feel honored to be a safe space for people to bring their metaphysical experiences too and that they can know that they will be heard with an open heart and mind.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: I entered into this field with a passion for families to be able to feel safe and loved and cared for. I also long for families to be able to be their own unique beautiful selves in a system that supports individuality and self-expression. The parent child relationship is so important. I long for parents to have the security they need, so that they can offer that security to their children.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: I have worked with hundreds of people in support of finding love and appreciation for themselves. There are so many deeply ingrained messages around how we should or shouldn't look/act/be. I work with shifting those beliefs on a deep subconscious level so that it becomes easy to make healthy choices and you can have the confidence that you know how to take good care of yourself with ease.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: The work I do is focused on calming the nervous system. From what I have found to be true, anxiety comes from not feeling attuned to as a little one or from traumatic experiences where the body learned that it wasn’t safe. I work with people to connect to the anxiety to understand why it's there and how it can shift, but still provide the sense of safety and protection you need to feel okay.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I often find that depression comes from something being suppressed or stopped. It could be from now or from childhood. Giving the body/mind the space to express and be listened too generally allows for release and a freedom which gives rise to more creative lifeforce energy and flow.

name: Allison Riegel
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I use mindfulness, embodiment, creativity, dreamwork, and the therapeutic relationship to support deep exploration and meaningful change.
ideal_client: I love working with people who are interested in deep transformative self-inquiry, discovering old patterns, healing wounds, and tending to the soul. I support the full spectrum of human experience that clients bring to counseling. I work with people who want to build mindfulness and connection with their bodies, emotions, and truths—cultivating greater awareness and vitality, which ultimately allows for an expanded sense of fluidity within oneself and the world.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I create a safe therapeutic container which is nourishing, welcoming, and of the moment. I invite curiosity, play, and spaciousness, so that clients can engage in their own inner processes of self-understanding. People have described my therapeutic style as: nurturing, heart-centered, intuitive, curious, and graceful. I bring a grounded, sturdy, non-judgmental presence into therapy and strive to meet my clients just where they are at: in celebration of their unique ways of being. I come to this work not only with a sensitivity to the way clients describe their experiences—the words, culture, and body language they use in expressing their personal narratives—but also an acute awareness of the energy present in the therapeutic space. The more subtle fluctuation of connection and realization as it unfolds. We'll dig into old patterning, honor unmet needs, identify your strengths and desires, and support you in living a more connective, creative, and expansive personal truth!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in the mystery of the universe, and I witness and honor this divine energy as we engage in the work of transformation in psychotherapy. Dreams, Synchronicities, and our Relationship to Spirit are powerful allies as we build awareness and traverse the landscapes of our lives. Paying attention to our inner worlds opens doors into new realms of selfhood and individual flourishing. Engaging with the unconscious through dreamwork, the body, expressive arts, we uncover significant messages from the deep that have unparalleled potential power in guiding us in our growth and toward personal alignment. I'm also aware of the ongoing oppression that exists in our culture via colonialism, capitalism, patriarchy, and institutional racism which most deeply effects BIPOC and LGBTQ+ communities. As a cisgender, white woman, I recognize the horrendous effects of white supremacy and consciously work to unwind the ways in which it shows up in my life.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: I see each client as a unique, unfolding cosmos, full of potential, beauty, and the ability to heal and grow. Therapy is a place where all of this can be seen, affirmed, nurtured and allowed to become the foundation of a more fulfilled life experience. I support clients in identifying and healing personal wounds and transforming roadblocks, reconnecting to and strengthening their intuition, and developing a sense of deep self-trust, love, and internal support.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Embracing a path of self-knowledge is one of the most fulfilling and exciting aspects of psychotherapy. Through the process can be discovered treasure troves of inspiration, connection, and vitality. In this long-term work we are able to enter into the mindful healing of trauma, the tending of attachment wounding and begin the experiential journey into a deeper, more profound selfhood which can guide our lives.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I see the relationship to Spirit—the animating force of the universe—as a potent factor in therapeutic work. I embrace that each client comes with a different cosmology, personal religious history, and a plethora of spiritual experiences. Or someone might not have had any at all and wants to. I support clients in nurturing this vital connection and help in fostering relationship with the spiritual dimension. Exploring this area together often leads to moments of deep, personal healing.

name: Lavinia Magliocco
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am queer & a bicultural first-generation Italian-American with a chronic illness. My style of working together is warm, lively, & direct.
ideal_client: If you're dealing with CPTSD you may struggle with chronic illness, you may feel culturally outcast, or have anxiety, depression, chronic pain, substance or behavioral addictions, difficulty with boundaries, people-pleasing, creative blocks and low self-confidence. My experience includes working with people ages 15+, expertise as a movement therapist specialized in enhancing athletic performance, skills working with physical limitations, experience that informs my work now.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our body is a gateway to authenticity, resolving trauma, integrating emotions. I use Trauma-informed somatic & mindfulness based interventions. When appropriate, we may combine movement to build awareness, help you regulate intense feelings, work with trauma, chronic pain, anxiety, or depression. You can expect that I will listen deeply & challenge you to expand beyond your perceived limitations. I use a psychodynamic orientation which means we use the therapeutic relationship itself to explore your patterns. I may include IFS (Internal Family Systems), ACT (Acceptance & Commitment Therapy), DBT (Dialectical Behavior/Cognitive Therapy), Gestalt, Somatic, and existentially oriented interventions. As a long time student of Eastern wisdom traditions, my work is informed by Buddhist psychology, Taoism, and Qigong - a Chinese mindful movement healing practice which supports health and wellbeing. I am poly, sex, and kink positive with a harm-reduction lens toward addictions.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As a queer, bicultural first-generation Italian-American with a chronic illness I've experienced bullying, othering, & invalidation for physical symptoms. I've had two bowel excisions and resections, a double mastectomy, and other musculoskeletal surgeries. I know pain. My experience confirms that each of us has innate wisdom longing to guide our lives towards greater freedom, connection, and well-being. Though not in control of many things, we can free ourselves from behaviors, thoughts, and emotions that repeat unfulfilling patterns. Strategies that kept us safe in childhood may get in our way as adults. Being able to live in your body and express who you are is especially essential when we are burdened by systemic injustice and oppression. I am poly, sex, and kink positive with a harm-reduction lens toward addictions.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: We notice how you relate with me. This reveals a lot about how you relate to others & the world. We'll use this to examine your patterns of communicating & (dis)connecting. For example, you may not have been able to stand up for yourself in your family of origin. You may have had to please, appease, rage or flee, & you likely will do it with me. Together we'll reflect on our dynamics in the "here and now" to figure out: Is it still working for you, or would another way of responding work better?

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I incorporate QiGong, a Chinese medical-spiritual practice based on Traditional Chinese Medicine to help clients experience connection with their body in a non-performative, attuned way. Evidence based studies show that Qigong has been successful in alleviating symptoms of PTSD, chronic pain, anxiety, and depression. QiGong is a gateway to enhancing awareness, mindfulness, and self-regulation. QiGong is in alignment with Polyvagal practice.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I draw from an existential perspective, guided by the belief that each individual possesses wisdom capable of navigating life's complexities towards greater freedom, connection, and well-being. While we may not have control over many external factors, we hold the power to liberate ourselves from repetitive, unfulfilling patterns of behavior, thought, and emotion.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: J Pittman McGeehee, a Jungian spiritual teacher, wrote: "I alone must become myself, but I cannot become myself alone." Healing is relational, chronic trauma (CPTSD) wounds are relational wounds, so the therapeutic relationship provides co-regulation, allows your nervous system to learn new paths, and serves as a corrective emotional experience.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: People with chronic illness often come from difficult family of origin dynamics. I bring somatic, trauma-informed lens to working with chronic illness, pain, disability. As someone with Crohn's disease, I have personal experience with financial, sexual, career, and relational sequelae of chronic illness. I use an integral lens that includes mindfulness practices for symptom relief as well as practical skills to manage ADL's.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Being human inevitably arouses anxiety, often through trauma-related ruptures early in life. I work more with generalized anxiety disorder that shows up as social anxiety, body dysmorphia, compulsive thoughts and behaviors. through the lens that anxiety is often trying to keep us safe. I work relationally & use somatic interventions to help people learn self & co-regulation skills to connect authentically with Self and Other.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Physical illness & depression often accompany each other. Even without a diagnosable illness, depression lives in the body as a kind of heaviness, an inability to find satisfaction or joy, a sense of hopelessness that pervades all aspects of life. I use a somatic, relational, & trauma-informed lens with practices to help clients integrate skills that are not just cognitive. Although thoughts contribute to depression. I include mental, emotional, physical, and spiritual interventions.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: I'm first generation Italian-American, my Jewish grandmother was part of an extensive diaspora, & I'm also Sicilian. Our ancestors' lives inform us through patterns that live in our very cells. Whether through war, genocide, dispossession, abuse, violence, loss, and (im)migration, having a place to uncover stories, explore family dynamics, and make choices based on your preferences rather than constraints is crucial for personal recovery as well as healthy relationships.

name: Victoria Lamy
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I am a passionate CSWA who specializes in mood disorders, Anxiety, trauma, and women's issues.
ideal_client: Are you ready for support to start your journey on a path to newness, in a safe space, free of judgment? Are you Experiencing depression, or anxiety, just want a safe person to talk to,or want to heal from your past? Growth Mindset is here to support you with daily life stressors and letting go of the past, build a growth mindset, and bring out the authentic resilient you. Let’s work together to help build skills for the challenges you have been facing in your life.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I am a CSWA. I have worked with individuals in the criminal justice system, Individual counseling, EAP services, Primary Care, Urgent Mental Health Clinics, and provider telehealth and individual counseling. I specialize in mood disorders ,PTSD and trauma related disorders, Anxiety, and women’s issues. I am a CADC 1. I use a non judgmental, holistic, client centered approach. Growth Mindset offers a safe space for you to uncover your authentic self. A safe place where you can voice your shame, embarrassment , low self- esteem and change those feelings to a growth mindset of resilience. Let's work together to change your mindset and focus on being your authentic self and a resilient you. I provide Psychoeducational Worksheets, resources, and homework that will help support you through your healing process. I look forward to the opportunity to help you and your loved ones on your wellness Journey.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Everyone has the capacity to change and develop a growth mindset. Change is difficult and it takes time. We all have coping skills . Sometimes the coping skills that we are currently using no longer works for us and we have to find other ways to manage. Behavior services a purpose . It is an alert of an unmet need.

name: Ariel Anderson
title: Art Therapist
intro: The world we live in is becoming increasingly complex & disconnecting. I'm an art therapist who is committed to meeting you where you are at
ideal_client: Someone who is in outpatient addiction treatment and needs a mental health counselor familiar with dual diagnosis work. Someone who is in recovery for their addiction and needs mental health help from someone who will prioritize helping them stay in recovery. Someone who wants to quit one substance but not ready to quit them all and needs help from someone who understands and practices harm reduction without judgment. Someone with identity related struggles (gender, sexuality, neurodiversity)

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe in helping empower you to solve your own problems through cultivating confidence, positive regard, and gaining power over thought distortions. I believe that experiential learning through the art making process and the therapeutic relationship can help one increase their ability for creative problem solving, self soothing, thought exploration, emotional expression, somatic processing, healthy communication, and reflective distance. I believe in dealing with the complexity of this world through utilizing chaos theory– the more we fill up the metaphorical toolbox of coping skills, the more options we have to use whenever life brings us troubles or something unexpected, and the more we have an open mind to potential paths forward when we face troubles, the more likely we will choose a path that is in line with our values and helps us in achieving our desired goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I was born and raised in SE Portland, attended Linn Benton Community College, Oregon State University, and graduated from Marylhurst University. I identify as a pansexual female. In my free time I enjoy: making multimedia artwork, reading fantasy and sci-fi novels, listening to audiobook lectures about astrophysics and the universe, creative writing, cuddling with my Great Dane and binge watching TV shows, baking and cooking, hanging out with friends, and DIY projects. I am passionate about working with individuals struggling with addiction because I detest the stigma that exists for addicts and think addiction is intimately connected with one's other mental health struggles and treating them together is one of the best ways to create a holistic and effective relapse prevention plan. I am also passionate about helping folks stay in recovery because I know it is a life long journey, not a box that can be checked by going to treatment.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I worked in an inpatient addiction treatment center as a dual diagnosis counselor for 1.5 years.

name: Zachariah Meints
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I am grateful to help people to the other side of their problems. You deserve to find relief, clarity and satisfaction.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist, I’m inspired by being a part of the growth and healing process. Personally and professionally, I value bringing more kindness, vulnerability, self-compassion and creativity to the world. I enjoy working with a large range of clients and I specialize in helping clients heal from depression and anxiety, improve their interpersonal skills and overcome unwanted habits. I focus on creating a therapeutic atmosphere where people can truly feel safe, grounded, and open to exploration. Working with me means we will explore evidence based approaches and techniques, in a flexible way, with attention to your needs. I draw from fourteen years working in mental health, including a background in social work, which has offered me the opportunity to better understand intersectional oppressions and the process of liberation. We engage in change everyday, but working with a therapist can help us along when we get stuck.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: People can make positive changes in their life in many ways, including: Receiving attuned understanding, compassionate engagement with our internal dialogue, connecting with our emotions and bodies, and creating new behavioral patterns. I practice the evidence based treatment of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy. Certified in TEAM CBT. Trained in Motivational Interviewing. Informed in Emotion Focused Therapy, Internal Family Systems, and Somatic Experiencing. If my approach sounds like a good match for you, please reach out.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I have trained since 2020 with the Feeling Good Institute in weekly two-hour trainings in the application of an integrative CBT model using techniques from Gestalt, Interpersonal and Psychodynamic therapy.

name: Rachel Ward
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I offer thoughtful diagnosis and medication care paired with support that honors your whole wellness journey.
ideal_client: I believe in the equal importance between therapy, medication management, and lifestyle interventions in the management of mental health. I approach care from a wellness model, where the core belief is that you can heal from your current struggle and function in a very whole and rounded way without feeling weighed down by illness. My style is relational and collaborative, providing information, advocacy, and trouble shooting to help you make the best decisions about your care.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I earned my BSN from OHSU and MSN from Gonzaga, and bring over 12 years of experience to my work in mental health. I provide diagnostic assessments and medication management for a wide range of mental health concerns, and I often integrate therapeutic support into our sessions. My approach is warm, steady, and deeply relational—I take time to truly know my clients, offering encouragement, guidance, and practical help in the day-to-day. I value natural treatments and lifestyle changes alongside medication, and believe healing is possible with the right support. I work closely with our skilled therapists to ensure collaborative, well-rounded care tailored to your unique needs.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Mental health care became personal for me early in life. I grew up surrounded by loved ones who struggled for years without the support or answers they needed. I watched them slowly come back to life once they were truly seen—once the right diagnosis, medication, and support were finally in place. That transformation stayed with me and led me here. I approach this work with deep respect for each person’s story. I believe healing happens in relationships where people feel safe, listened to, and not rushed. My goal is to offer that kind of space—one that’s steady, caring, and judgment-free. I welcome people from all backgrounds and identities, and I’m here to walk alongside you at your pace. Outside of work, I love gardening, baking for my family, and spending time with my service dog, Molly—who you may get to meet if we see each other in person.

name: Melanie Muniz, LMFT #T1401
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Hello, I am accepting new clients. My hours are Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday 10-5.

name: Jackie Hamm
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a white, trans*agender, individual that enjoys connecting with others, and aim to help facilitate healing through connection.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with the LGBTQ2SIA+ community, communities who face additional barriers due to their identity, and neurodivergent folx. Trauma is extremely difficult to overcome, whether it stems from a one-time event, or an ongoing cycle. Therapy is important for healing, self-compassion, and confidence. It can be scary and intimidating to find a therapist, and I am here to make that search as smooth as possible.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that you are the expert of your own experience and that you are courageous for engaging in this part of your healing journey. The hardest part is often getting started and finding the support you need. With a collaborative approach to therapy, I hope to create a space where you feel understood, respected, validated, and strengthened to explore deeper layers of your experience while being open to self-compassion and growth. Through an eclectic therapeutic approach, we will explore and better understand your identities, your culture, and your overall lived experience to help empower you in the context of your life.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I value social justice, human rights, equity, personal autonomy and community. I try to live my life in a way that best reflects my values, while also advocating for others when possible.

name: Garrison Cox
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
credentials: Master of Arts in Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy
intro: I want my clients to feel deeply and honestly cared for inside and outside of therapy. Everybody has their own unique path toward healing.
ideal_client: I work with individuals and couples to explore and weed through the moral ambiguity of life. Together, we can explore your emotional experience, anxiety, depression, past traumatic experiences, relationships, and interpersonal patterns with depth, gentleness, and honesty. I have a special place in my heart and my practice for overfunctioners, overcarers, overthinkers, people who have a hard time getting their brain to quiet down.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: All beings have their own pathways toward transformation and integration. Sometimes, the result of transformation can feel like a broken bone calcified, or a lopped-off branch scarred over. Mentally and emotionally, these wounds and raw spots revisit us, make us feel vulnerable, anxious, angry, unable to connect or belong. I draw on somatic, systemic, experiential, and existential traditions of therapy and philosophy to support clients in exploring their personal obstacles and wounds in order to clear the way for self-agency and self-resonance. In session, this looks like slowing down and examining all the information available in the present - thoughts, memories, images, emotions, bodily sensations. I believe it is not enough to just gain mental insight in order to effect change; we also have to experience life and all its joys and tribulations differently in order to recruit our entire selves into the change process.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe every person is deserving of dignity. As an existential-humanistic therapist, I also believe that addressing the symptoms of our mental health struggles is not always enough to reconnect us with ourselves. Rather than isolate and eliminate, our work together (in therapy and in life as a whole) is to connect and embrace. Common wisdom and statistical study both show that life is about the quality of our relationships - and we're all in luck; the practice of therapy happens through relationship! Through the work of therapy, we can create opportunities to experience life differently. I identify as a gay man, and enjoy working with members of the queer community. I am passionate about helping people reconnect with their emotional experience in a world that prioritizes rationalization.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a primary driving force of our nervous systems. It's a necessary survival mechanism, but one that all too often feels like it's overflowing past its usefulness. I've experienced that kind of anxiety, and I had the benefit of somatic and Polyvagal Theory-focused therapy to help me adapt. Now I offer that same kind of therapy.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a gay man with a background in sex therapy, I personally understand many of the challenges that gay men face. I am an ally to the rest of the LGBTQ+ community and feel deep connection to the history of queer marginalization and its ties to racism, heterosexism, and transphobia.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: Compassion fatigue is a particular type of burnout that often affects those who spend a lot of their time caring for others. In this current world of near-instant global information and constant exposure to crisis - whether experienced personally or through the news - it can be hard to maintain a sense of compassion and empathy for others. For most caretaking people I know, this often results in self-judgment, shame, and irritation.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have experience working with adult survivors of both childhood and adult trauma. I use a slow-paced framework that emphasizes somatic exploration as well as deep attention to any moments of trauma exposure within or without the therapy. I believe working with trauma is the core of the field of therapy, and that many experiences of anxiety, depression, or other forms of emotional disruption are often due to our bodies' attempts to manage un-integrated traumatic experience.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships are often hard, and yet they're also so often the core facets of our lives. Relational therapy is a great place to untwist what often feels like an unsolvable puzzle. Through direct emotional experience in therapy, you can work toward making space in your relationship for love and connection and learning how to walk together through challenging experiences.

name: Janean VeDova
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Hi my name is Janean, I am a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in Oregon. Learn more about me here www.janeanvedovatherapy.com
ideal_client: Are you feeling disconnected or in conflict with yourself or in your relationships? Are you experiencing sex and intimacy issues? Are you in need of support from other women who can relate to you? Are you feeling anxious, depressed and isolated due to your current situation? I love helping people feel less overwhelmed and more connected to themselves and others. Through collaboration we will identify what is important to you for your happiness and work through any barriers.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I hold a Master’s Degree in Marriage, Couple and Family Therapy from Lewis and Clark Graduate School of Education and Counseling in Portland, OR. Major coursework included sex therapy, family and relationship life cycles with a strong emphasis on social justice in therapy and outside systems. I have extensive experience working with victims of sexual assault, families affected by HIV and other terminal illness, along with a background in family and civil mediation. I also hold a bachelor’s degree in Peace and Conflict and a minor degree in Philosophy. I work from a systemic framework, meaning I acknowledge the constraints and or strengths outside systems (i.e. school, work, court and religious communities) have on individuals, couples/partners and families. I also take into consideration biological, psychological, social and spiritual aspects of people’s lives. I am strength-based, I believe in focusing on the strengths, resiliency and successes of individuals and relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is integrative, collaborative, humanistic and eclectic. Trust is at the core of my practice. My goal is to establish trust from the start so clients can feel safe and comfortable opening up about the most vulnerable parts of their lives and selves. I know a client's trust is precious and I am always honored to receive it so that I can help and support each person the best to my ability. Without trust in the therapeutic relationship, the work can get stuck. It can feel endless and hopeless. Clients would say I maintain a trusting relationship where they can not only be open and honest but I can as well. It is my job to help each individual and relationship identify what is important and provide them tools to achieve health and happiness in their lives. I will kindly be direct, I will gently push and I will guide us to address difficult areas or behaviors of your life and relationships that may be creating barriers to growth and happiness.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: As a marriage, couple and family therapist I am trained to work with couples and I welcome all partnering arrangements (monogomous/open/polyamourous/ monogomous/heterosexual/same sex). I also specialize in sex therapy that is inclusive and non judgmental.

specialities.name: Nonviolent Communication
specialities.description: I have been trained in conflict resolution and mediation. I hold a BA in Peace and Conflict. Miscommunication is at the root of conflict. I can guide better communication and help resolve conflict you are experiencing in your life.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: As a marriage couple and family therapist I am trained in family systems. Families are unique, how they are configured, family rules and expectations, family roles and family of origin. Each family goes through family life cycles. I approach family therapy systemically and consider all the systems and relationships the family is involved in.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Women continue to be systemically oppressed in the systems we move in (ex. relationships, reproductive/human rights, family, work, healthcare, law). Women can gather together to share wisdom, strength, empathy, encouragements, compassion and support to help one another move through whatever is hard.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: I have extensive training in family systems and relationships.

name: Natalie Thomas
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: My name is Natalie Thomas. I am an avid horseback rider, and bargain hunter in my spare time, who loves live music!
ideal_client: Are you feeling crippled with anxious thoughts, and the fear of your next anxiety attack looming around the corner? Have you experienced life altering trauma which you struggle to move past? Have you found that confiding in friends isn’t enough anymore? In my practice, I strive to help my clients find ways to confront their anxiety and trauma triggers in a way that strips them of their power, and allows you to thrive in your life, free from the confines of fear.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that we all have innate strengths that we can build upon in our journey to better mental health. Rather than fixating on what is outside of our sphere of control, I guide my clients through a journey toward peace that comes from finding the ability to let go of external pressures, and use what is with in us to guide us through life. I use an ACT approach, as well as exposure therapy, equine facilitated therapy, CBT, strengths based, and EMDR to assist my clients in letting go of what they can’t control, and working to become their best selves, no longer trapped by anxiety and trauma triggers. I received my Graduate Degree in Counseling Psychology from Lewis and Clark College in 2019. I earned a Bachelor of Science in Communication from Portland State University in 2011. I have worked with those experiencing severe and persistent mental illness, trauma, anxiety, and depression since graduating with my Master’s.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that we are all capable of finding self love, and confidence. That we all have the ability to live a unique, and whole experience by addressing our fears, anxieties and triggers head on, and accepting what is outside of our control. The path to mental health does not have to be paved with re-occurring traumas, and tearful sessions, but empowering, educational, and even fun, outside the box therapeutic approaches. I offer equine therapy at a facility in Wilsonville, Oregon where clients learn about horsemanship, learn to ride, and learn to trust, build confidence, learn to regulate their emotions, and to form trusting bonds, while overcoming fears.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: I have worked with many clients who are struggling to adapt to major life changes. I primarily use an ACT approach to help clients settle in to the inherent unknown associated with change, while supporting them through complex emotions that come with new life phases.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I bring a lot of myself into my work with clients who experience anxiety, and take various treatment approaches, ranging from ACT to exposure therapy.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I’ve spent a large part of my career working with those experiencing PTSD. The fear that comes with trauma can be crippling at times, and learning to carry that fear with you into the unknown sometimes feels impossible. I work with my clients to navigate life with their trauma in tow, and to build strength from places of trial.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Marriage takes work. That’s one thing we know for certain. Learning to navigate another persons needs, emotions, the ways that they move through life and communicate can be really difficult. I believe that through solid communication, and staying firmly rooted in our sphere of control, healthy relationships will emerge. I work with couples, and individuals to navigate communication issues, and to shed light on individuals roles in the problems at hand.

name: Sonia Holdaway
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I specialize in relational work, helping you feel more connected to your loved ones and more confident in yourself and your relationships.
ideal_client: My clients come to me because they feel disconnected. Often from romantic partners, friends or family, and usually from themselves. If you have been struggling to feel connected to others, or have been feeling out of touch with your own wants, needs or values, I can help! Together we can address past hurts, communication struggles, and hard feelings about yourself or your relationship, and grow your confidence, self-compassion and connection with others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Trained as a couples therapist, my focus has always been on how we feel in relationship with ourselves and others. It can be so frustrating to feel like you are not coping or relating to others in the ways that you know you want to be, especially in this uniquely hard time. In our work, I will help you explore your pain, as well as your strengths. I will help you hold the things that make you feel worst about yourself or your relationship, and also find ways towards compassion and feeling capable and worthy of the love and acceptance you deserve. I want to empower you to connect with yourself and others on a deeply satisfying level. I will bring a calm presence and an open heart. I offer no judgment, and I believe no issue is too small or unimportant to bring to counseling. I welcome all forms of relationships and identities, and particularly enjoy working with fellow members of the LGBTQ community. Learn more about my specific therapeutic approach by visiting my website below.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am very interpersonal in my approach to therapy, and strongly believe that satisfying relationships are at the heart of growth and happiness. My clients would tell you that the therapeutic relationship is one of my favorite tools for change, and I want to genuinely know you and connect with the person that you know yourself to be. I have been working in mental health since 2013, including in eating disorder treatment and family therapy, and have a passion for supporting positive body image and sexuality. I have specific training in Emotion Focused Therapy both for individuals and couples. These experiences have come together to affirm my belief that we all deserve to have our needs met and to feel loved and accepted, most of all by ourselves. I would love to help you feel better in how you relate to yourself and your loved ones. Contact me or visit my website below for a free phone consultation, to see if this feels like a good fit for you.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Trained as a couples and family therapist, I specialize in relationship counseling. If you are feeling disconnected or like you seem to be just talking past each other, I can help. My approach is based in emotion-focused, family systems and Gottman principles, and our work provides a safe space for each of you to express yourself in new ways, using dynamic, in-the-room exercises to help interrupt hurtful patterns and create momentum towards a healthier partnership.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: My approach to counseling is grounded primarily in Emotion-Focused therapy, which encourages exploring and experiencing your emotions in real time in session, to help you connect with, and better articulate, your deeper needs. Many of us can understand our struggles very well on a cognitive level, but have trouble figuring out how to actually feel better. I love that emotion-focused therapy uses in-the-moment, emotional change experiences in session to actually create lasting change.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory is at the heart of my work with both couples and individuals. If you are wondering why you seem to have the same problems in relationships over and over, or you feel clingy or suffocated in relationships, I can help. My clients often say they find our work helpful for looking at the impact of attachment patterns on present and past relationships.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: If you are struggling to feel connected to others or feeling unsteady in yourself, relational therapy can help you strengthen your ability to relate to, and feel cared for by others. I am a highly relational therapist, and I love using the therapeutic relationship to facilitate healing from past traumas as well as to combat unhelpful patterns that are keeping you stuck.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in working with fellow LGBTQ+ adults and relationships. Whether you come to counseling specifically for issues around gender identity or sexuality, or are seeking a counselor who shares an LGBTQ+ perspective, I provide a safe, affirming, body-positive and sex-positive space where you are welcomed for who you are. Learn more about counseling for couples and individuals on my website: www.relationshipcounselingportland.com

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Trained as a couples and family therapist, I specialize in relationship counseling. If you are feeling disconnected or like you seem to be just talking past each other, I can help. My approach is based in emotion-focused, family systems and Gottman principles, and our work provides a safe space for each of you to express yourself in new ways, using dynamic, in-the-room exercises to help interrupt hurtful patterns and create momentum towards a healthier partnership.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: If you have a difficult relationship with your body, food, exercise, or all of the above, you are not alone. I love to help clients reconnect with an inner sense of health & balance in an affirming, body-positive space. I will support you in challenging external messages about how you should be, and help you connect instead with your needs, your values, and your intuitive healthy self. Visit my website for more info: https://www.relationshipcounselingportland.com/

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: In a society that prizes individual strength, it can be hard to open up with others. Your therapist should be someone with whom you feel comfortable sharing your toughest anxieties, and who genuinely cares about your experience. My goal is to help you feel accepted & supported when talking about your struggles, and to help guide you through to the other side - to feeling capable and in control of your own experience. Visit my website for more info: https://www.relationshipcounselingportland.com/

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: If you have been dealing with intense feelings of exhaustion, hopelessness, guilt or overwhelm, you are not alone. I want to help you find relief from your depression, whether it is a new experience for you, or something you have struggled with for a while. I use interpersonal and emotion-focused methods to help you feel connected and confident. Visit my website for more info: https://www.relationshipcounselingportland.com/

name: LaShaun Garrett-Fears
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Join me for a supportive therapy experience that blends empathy with directness, creating a safe space to prioritize your healing!
ideal_client: Navigating life's complexities is a journey filled with both challenges and joys. I empathize with the struggles of anxiety, worry, and sadness, as well as the moments of tranquility and happiness. In therapy, I provide a confidential, individually focused, culturally responsive approach. Specializing in evidence-based treatment for stress, life transitions, depression, anxiety, and trauma, my passion is empowering clients to discover satisfaction and resilience in their lives.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In the safety of our therapeutic space, I offer a warm, direct, and collaborative approach to help you navigate life's challenges. Specializing in aiding individuals through significant life changes, stress, anxiety, and depression. I address communication issues and guide you through the identification and expression of emotions in ways that foster positive growth and fulfillment. Together, we will actively define your goals, leveraging your strengths and insights to release self-limiting beliefs, resolve internal conflicts, and discard unhelpful behavioral patterns. This transformative journey empowers you to confidently embrace your truth. I'm a firm advocate for inclusivity, viewing it as a fundamental right. Join me in this holistic process of self-discovery and growth, where your well-being takes center stage, and your journey towards authenticity and fulfillment begins.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: The focus of my process centers on the strengths of your personal power, truth, identity, healing, hope and transformation. In my years of practice I have learned that it is impossible to heal what you cannot /will not name, it is my passion to support others in finding, learning to trust and honor their own voices so that transformative healing can happen.

name: Sarah Ellenwood
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I am an interactive therapist who encourages self compassion, alongside growth. I balance processing and skill building to foster relief.
ideal_client: Are you feeling alone with new or persistent issues? I serve unique individuals, couples and families with diverse therapy needs. I love working with parents needing support and skills to help their sensitive/higher needs children. Couples struggling to communicate and productively solve conflict can find an experiential approach to couples therapy. Folks struggling with patterned behavior and are curious about the why and desire strategies for change. You don't have to do it alone.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I wholeheartedly believe in this process and love the deep dive of therapy—the engagement with stories, emotions, patterns, and change. It’s a joy when clients really "bring it” to our work together. I also recognize that everyone’s path to healing is unique, which is why I believe in attachment-based therapy. This allows clients to verbalize unspoken pieces of their story—things they’ve sometimes never had the courage to admit to themselves. Bearing witness makes this work life-affirming, and can truly change your life. I use a relational and nonjudgmental style to build relationships with clients. I incorporate Emotionally Focused Therapy, a trauma informed lens, practical skill building, and humor to help clients grow. I also offer walking sessions when it's a good fit.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: IT BEGINS WITH THE CREATIVE PROCESS I’ve always viewed therapy as a creative, one-of-a-kind, collaborative process between therapist and client(s), and believe all individuals inherently know how to heal themselves, but need guidance and support when they have lost their way. I avoid pathologizing people and their thoughts, feelings, and actions. OPEN AND AFFIRMING I also know how oppressive our cis/het-centric culture can be, and am open and affirming to the many ways that people create and maintain relationships, including: LGBTQI+, BDSM, kink, non-monogamous or polyamorous relationships, and sex positive attitudes and choices. My goal is always to create a safe space and I’m celebratory in my approach to sexual and gender minorities. A note to LGBTQ Clients: I am not only a LGBTQ-affirming therapist; I am LGBTQ informed. If this is a component of treatment for you, or part of who you are, get yourself qualified help.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I provide an EFT and experiential approach to relationship issues. I have worked with relationships that are a few months old to many decades long. Couples that are ready to change their communication issues and address hurts that need repair. I can help with discernment of relationship status and separation as well. I have worked with couples that are non-monogamous or who are considering opening up.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I work with all genders and provide trans-competent care to clients who require this special training. I provide a non-judgmental space for exploration and to discuss thoughts and feeling about social and/or medical transitions. If you are needing a trans-affirming therapist for relational therapy or a different clinical focus, I may be able to help.

specialities.name: Cancer
specialities.description: I provide knowledgable care for clients coping with a new diagnosis, treatments, chronic illness, treatment decisions, family communication and death with dignity. This diagnosis can bring existential issues to the forefront and a comfortable space to talk, process, and feel understood can be invaluable.

name: Cameron Panfely
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am here to meet you where you are, and help you navigate your emotions, and life's challenges in a way that makes sense to you.
ideal_client: Sometimes life can be incredibly difficult, painful,and confusing, leaving us feeling distant from ourselves, and others. Whether you are experiencing overwhelming anxiety, depression, and anger, trauma responses, relationship conflicts, life/career transitions, or ADHD, I am here to meet you where you are, and help you navigate your emotions in a way that makes sense to you. I believe that every individual has the potential to heal, grow, and thrive when they have the necessary tools to do so.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that everyone is the expert of their own experience, and as your therapist, I am here to help you explore your experiences and achieve your goals in a way that makes sense to you. Our experiences shape us, and sometimes we lose sight of our worth and values, leading us to feel bad about, or distant from who we are. I want to take the time to really get to know you and understand your life experiences in a way that appreciates where you come from, and how you see the world. I view counseling as a collaborative process in which we will work together to address discomforts and focus on areas you want to grow in, or your goals and aspirations. I want to help you address the roots of your issues, while collaboratively developing solutions. It is my goal to provide you with both a safe, comfortable, and non-judgmental environment, and a genuine, positive, and empathetic relationship to work through these things.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Beyond anything else, this process is about feeling comfortable with your therapist, and that is where my focus lies. You can expect my full attention, intention, and engagement at every step of this process. My emphasis is on provide an empathetic, trauma-informed, and non-judgemental space that is conducive to exploration and healing. While I utilize parts of several theoretical frameworks (IFS, PCT, CBT, ACT, DBT, etc.), I work with my clients to develop a uniquely tailored and collaborative approach that emphasizes their individual needs, goals, and strengths. I take OHP insurance, excluding Care Oregon Advantage, Health Share of Oregon, Jackson Care Connect, and Coluumbia Pacific CCO. To ensure that my services are kept affordable I offer a sliding-scale pricing model. I'm here to support you and believe in your ability to grow. Seeking counseling is exceptionally brave, and I hope to be alongside you in your journey.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: In Rogerian Person-Centered Therapy, I'm your empathetic companion on your journey. I listen actively, ensuring you feel truly heard and understood. Without judgment or imposing solutions, I reflect your feelings, creating a safe haven for exploration. Together, we navigate the intricacies of your experiences, fostering self-discovery and growth. It's a collaborative process where your unique path is honored, and you're empowered to find your way to healing and well-being.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: When our self-concept is first developing, it is a reflection of how we think our primary attachment figures view us. That is a powerful idea that massively impacts our developing self-worth, and the way we interact with others, especially significant others. No matter if you have an anxious, avoidant, or disorganized attachment, attachment theory provides roadmaps to developing a secure attachment at any time in your life.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: As an individual with an ADHD diagnosis, I know first hand the ways issues surrounding focus, motivation, organization, planning, procrastination, and communication can be. What is less talked about is the way these issues can negatively impact one's self worth, and self-esteem. I have worked with many youth with ADHD to address behavioral issues in a compassionate way. I also have experience working with adults with ADHD, and teach and ADHD skills and counseling group that I designed.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Who we are, and the way we see the world comes our our past experiences, especially those with significant people in our lives. Past trauma often serves to disconnect us from who we really are. Working with trauma is something that I am passionate about, and I bring a compassionate, non-judgemental, and caring attitude to this work. Processing through unresolved trauma, developing effective coping skills, and offering self-compassion is my focus.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Feeling depressed can be beyond confusing. Often times we have no idea why we are feeling so down, and others its clear. Whichever the case may be, most of us tend to feel downright stuck when experiencing episodes of depression. I want to help you explore that "stuckness", and what is keeping you from enjoying, or appreciating your days.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Experiencing anxiety feels like a relentless storm within—a mix of fear, uncertainty, and racing thoughts. I approach this by offering a safe haven and acknowledging these struggles with empathy. Together, we unravel triggers, build coping tools, and cultivate resilience, fostering a path toward inner calm and understanding.

name: Ramiro Romo Jr
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I'm Ramiro, a bilingual Latino therapist. A child of immigrant parents, lover of tacos, and enthusiast of all things Pokémon.
ideal_client: Supporting those struggling with Anxiety, Depression, Family Dynamics (including parenting), and Sexual Dysfunction through a bilingual and culturally sensitive lens. I’m committed to helping clients learn how to build healthy versions of themselves, and moving away from shame. Many times, this includes exploring life's ongoing stressful challenges, processing traumatic experiences, and improving communication in our relationships.

name: Jessie Weisstein
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a Clinical Social Worker who prioritizes connection and building safety in the therapeutic relationship.
ideal_client: Even though you try and move forward in your life, painful experiences from the past always seem to get in the way. I am sure you have tried your best to forget, but it never works. I want you to know that you don't have to continue to feel like you have one foot in the present and one in the past. I provide a safe and affirming space for you to process the past so you can start to feel more present in your life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have been working with people who have experienced trauma for a over a decade. I use techniques that have brought relief to people suffering from PTSD and other trauma related issues. The most important piece of how I work is establishing safety in the relationship and never pushing clients to talk about issues unless they are ready. I use a variety of techniques including learning about the way your body holds trauma and increasing curiosity and compassion towards the ways you have learned to protect yourself from pain. I often use a technique called EMDR to help my clients reprocess traumatic events and reduce negative thoughts, feelings and sensations.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe strongly in the power of relationships to both shape who we are to heal. I believe that all people have the capacity to shift their lives in ways that align with their values. I was drawn to this work because of the profound impact that therapy can have on individuals and communities. I also believe strongly that all people have a right to healing and I use anti-oppressive practices in my work with clients. I am allied with the LGBTQ community and love supporting folks who are exploring their gender identity

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have been treating PTSD for over 10 years. I use a combination of polyvagal theory, EMDR and IFS to work with clients who have experienced trauma.

name: MaryBeth Hernandez
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am honored to support your professional growth through clinical supervision as you seek to become an LCSW in the state of Oregon.
ideal_client: I am an approved Oregon LCSW Supervisor. Through supervision, I will strive to help you reflect on your work, increase confidence in your clinical approach, gain understanding of yourself in relation to your work, and discuss clinical and ethical dimensions of mental health services. I am available to meet for individual supervision sessions weekly, twice per month, or monthly if you are also in a supervision group. My current fee is $100 per hour due at the time of service.

approaches.My Background and Approach: As a therapist, I work from a client-centered and trauma-informed lens, utilizing CBT, TF-CBT, CPT, MI, mindfulness, play therapy, and sand tray therapy. I have extensive experience treating trauma, depression, and anxiety with children, adolescents, and adults. I have experience working in a Child Advocacy Center, residential treatment, therapeutic foster care, and outpatient settings. I have supervised CSWAs and MSW student interns.

name: Cayla Panitz
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Individual and family counseling for adolescents and adults in Portland, OR. Telehealth and IN Person.
ideal_client: I work with people looking to heal their relationship to food and their body; those with eating disorders; people struggling with anxiety and depression, those coping with grief and loss, those who are navigating identity challenges and people healing from personal, systemic and interpersonal trauma.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I collaborate with people to help them live a more authentic, connected life. I approach counseling with a deep empathy and belief in the power of your strengths and encourage insight, empowerment and self-compassion. I rely on the creation of a strong therapeutic relationship and targeted interventions to do so. I also aim to point out the ways that our experiences are shaped by the systems we live within and are impacted by. My counseling style is sincere, collaborative, validating and often filled with nerdy metaphors, a good laugh and pet stories.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I’ve got PNW roots. I find happiness at Portland Thorns games, playing with the dog, getting outside and reading Samantha Irby books. I work within a relational, feminist, anti-oppression framework. I adhere to the Health At Every Size® paradigm and work to dismantle weight stigma and fat phobia. I am queer affirming and make every effort to create an anti-racist, inclusive environment for people of all walks of life including, but not limited to: body size/shape, gender, race, country of origin, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion and disability status. I am continually learning and growing in my own anti-oppression work. I received my Masters of Counseling Psychology from Lewis and Clark College. My experience involves individual, group and family work in a variety of settings and programs. In addition, I have specialized training in the treatment of eating disorders & the application of Intuitive Eating, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, and Emotion Focused Family Therapy.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I utilize Emotion Focused Family Therapy to support caregivers who are facilitating mental health recovery of their loved ones.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: As humans, we need and exist in relationships; to others, to the environment, to ourselves. I believe that one of the most important aspects of my work with clients is developing a strong relationship based around safety and expression and use these experiences in therapy to help people understand the ways in which they relate to other aspects of their lives.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I use ACT to inform my work with people across various areas of concern. I help people apply the principles of connecting with their current experiences, identifying the ways in which the relationships to our emotions and thoughts impact our lives and disconnect us from our values. I then help people change the relationships they have with their emotions and thoughts and move towards their values.

name: Amanda Frankel
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I bring a grounded, creative presence to therapy. My work is rooted in authenticity, acceptance, creativity, trust, and humor.
ideal_client: I work with adults, couples, and teens (14+) navigating life transitions, OCD, anxiety, grief & loss, chronic pain, relationship struggles, trauma (including complex and community-level trauma), and issues related to faith, identity, and self-worth. I’m LGBTQ+ affirming and committed to culturally responsive care. My approach is trauma-informed and mindfulness-based, integrating somatic therapy, parts work, Restoration Therapy, and nature-based practices.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I know that transformation can be messy, uncertain, and even frightening—but also deeply meaningful, energizing, and liberating. I will be your collaborator and guide as you as you explore your own path toward greater vitality, connection, and peace. I will support you as you navigate life’s challenges by fostering belonging, self-compassion, curiosity, and embodied resilience and help you cultivate your innate resilience and inner wisdom.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: I am a certified coach with experience working with clients ranging from students to executives. My coaching work is strengths-based and action-oriented, focused on behavior change that aligns with values, motivation, inner wisdom, and actualization.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: I fuse the foundations of therapy with the experience of being in a relationship with the natural world. Experiences in and with nature offer opportunities for perspective, confidence, resilience, and compassion.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I am a mindfulness-based counselor using modalities that help clients become more aware of thoughts and behaviors through mindful attunement, breath work, somatic practices, and meditation techniques.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: As a student of trans-personal counseling, my work is grounded in the understanding that the human psyche is not limited to one state of consciousness. In our therapeutic work, there is space for making meaning of our thoughts, behaviors, and experiences through that which transcends the individual, such as spirituality, dreams, mysticism, and more.

name: Sophie Bloch Miller
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I offer a safe space to explore your obstacles and offer strategies to help cultivate the life you desire. *couples sessions in EUGENE ONLY*
ideal_client: Are you struggling with the quality of relationships in your life? Do you find yourself repeating familiar patterns that lead to conflict and disconnection? Are you interested in exploring your patterns, learning new strategies, and feeling more hopeful and optimistic about creating satisfying connection in your life? I am passionate about the power of relationships to bolster our well being and am excited to support you (individually or with your partner) in building more effective relating.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: You are a unique embodiment of your life experiences, and as a therapist I bring genuine curiosity to know you and understand you, and help manifest your visions and dreams. My goal is to help you live a satisfying and fulfilling life, overcoming patterns that don't serve you. I offer both practical strategies and a supportive and safe environment for processing life and relational challenges. I am certified in Relational Life Therapy, developed by Terry Real, and completed certification in Healing Our Core Issues developmental trauma model. I draw from mindfulness, cognitive behavioral therapy, attachment theory, interpersonal neurobiology, nonviolent communication, and more. We will continually assess how things are going and make adjustments to ensure that your investment in treatment is providing you with meaningful outcomes. Clients tend to experience me as warm, accepting, creative, curious, insightful and encouraging. Expect to both laugh and cry during our time together.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am passionate about helping clients cultivate meaningful and satisfying relationships. I believe in the healing power of relationships, which has inspired my certification in Relational Life Therapy (work of Terry Real) as well as in-depth training in The Developmental Model of Couples therapy, and Gottman Couples therapy. I participate in ongoing training and consultation in RLT and find it to be an incredibly effective approach for healing old wounds and "growing up" in a way that allows us to have healthy and deeply satisfying relationships. We will examine and heal early wounds that interfere in the here and now, liberating your adult self to thrive in relationships! The RLT way is honest and direct, including "care-frontation" of ineffective patterns and honing more relational skills. I am continually humbled by the transformation that is possible when people are committed and motivated to make positive changes, especially in the context of intimate relationships.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I am certified in Relational Life Therapy, a model of couples therapy developed by Terry Real.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I utilize a range of mindfulness techniques, such as guided visualizations, various breathing techniques, reflective journaling, present moment sensory exploration and other body based techniques.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I draw from therapeutic models such as attachment theory, mindfulness, cognitive behavioral therapy, mentalization-based treatment, interpersonal neurobiology, nonviolent communication, narrative therapy, collaborative problem solving, emotional freedom technique and more. Additionally I am completing training and certification in the Healing Our Core Issues model (HOCI) which is focused on healing Developmental and Relational Trauma.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I am a Certified Relational Life Therapy clinician. I work from this model as my foundation and encourage clients to become familiar with the work of Terry Real. We will look at your relationship together, with curiosity and without judgment, to better understand the patterns that you find yourself in. We will then work from from the inside out and build new skills. I additionally have completed Training in Gottman Couples Therapy (levels 1, 2 & 3) and the Developmental Model of Couples Therapy.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: We all feel nervous and anxious sometimes, however many experience elevated states of anxiety in ways that interfere with getting through the day. It's exhausting, both mentally and physically. I have abundant training and knowledge about the somatic/nervous system manifestation of anxiety and will work with you from a body based as well as cognitive (aka thoughts) perspective to help you feel more confident about managing and resolving your anxiety.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I utilize a range of modalities to help address depression symptoms depending on the origin of your struggles and the techniques that resonate with you. We may explore cognitions using CBT, practice visualizations and mindfulness, examine family of origin roots of your feelings and focus on enhancing the quality of support within your relationships.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Self esteem is central to our well being and mental health. It is the life boat for survival during challenging times. I will help to identify and believe in your strengths and overcome old patterns of beating yourself up from the inside.
