I utilize the therapeutic relationship as well as attachment based treatment to increase insight into self and build strong sense of identity and self worth.

name: Ghassan Ammar
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a mindfulness-centered counselor practicing experiential somatic therapy and EMDR.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize mindfulness as a tool to assist you in exploring your present experience. Even when dealing with past events or future concerns, I find that paying attention to our current state yields a lot of insight. Paying attention to yourself includes all the different areas that make up who you are! This includes not just your thoughts and feelings but also your body. By becoming more embodied, we can begin to feel more into who and where we are in relationship to ourselves, others, and the world. I am also interested in the role of interpersonal neurobiology and the impact of stress and trauma on the attachment system. As such, I place a high value on cultivating a safe, warm, and loving therapeutic relationship.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I am a deeply committed activist and organizer for socialism, transformative justice, and non-hierarchical systems. I do volunteer work around conflict resolution processes to help cultivate healthier organizing cultures within social justice movements.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I utilize EMDR therapy to assist you in healing from trauma. EMDR stands for Eye Movement De-sensitization and Reprocessing, and is an evidence-based modality for the treatment of trauma. One of the many things I, and folks I work with, value about EMDR is that it doesn't require one to talk a lot about their trauma.

name: Art Chaklader
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Thank you for taking the first step, feel free to reach out for a free consultation. I am currently accepting new clients as of 5/14/25
ideal_client: I am currently taking new clients. My clients come from all walks of life. Whether you have lived in the area your whole life, or just moved to town. Whether you are struggling with up and down moods, are stuck in life, struggling with relationships or belonging in society, or just want to deepen an understanding of your life. I want to be able to listen, understand, and help you each step of the way. Consultations are always free.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Experiencing stress, anxious thoughts, unhealthy habits, and feeling depressed can be a part of the journey to a better you. I can help in providing a lens to that journey, to help you be mindful of where you have been, where you are, and where you are going. I also help provide the tools, to recognize barriers, and overcome old patterns. I have devoted my life to understanding psychology, working in the helping profession, and finding the right resources when things are out of my scope of practice. My style is person centered, informed, and really deeply rooted in creating an environment and relationship in which a person can feel like they can truly be who they are, and express fully what they want. My fees vary depending on the service, and I take many insurance plans. Please do not let cost be a barrier. I provide a free consultations to see if I would be the right fit for your counseling needs.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor with the board of Oregon, and have worked in a number of settings including Drug and Alcohol, Community Mental Health, School, Crisis Work, and private practice. I have M.A. in Mental Health Counseling from Marywood University, Licensed in Oregon, and I am a Nationally Certified Counselor.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Everyone has a story. Whether you think about your life story, or have not in awhile, it has had huge impact on who you are today. This is why when we feel lost in life, it can be so grounding to reconnect with your life story. This is exactly my aim. We start from the beginning, and tie your narrative to what is happening today. This gives you back your story, and helps you continue it on.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I have been lucky to study under a number of professors who adhere to the humanistic approach. For me, this is rooted in the idea that humans are ultimately good, and constantly attempting to move toward self-actualization. Under this template, the therapeutic relationship that we create in session is ultimately the tool that will provide the space for you to reach your goals.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT utilizes your thoughts to manage feelings and behaviors. We work together through in person sessions, thought/challenge records, and actively challenging homework to understand and change feelings and behavior. I'm committed to as much of this journey as you are to allow emotions and behaviors to change.

specialities.name: Immigration/Acculturation
specialities.description: As an immigrant to the U.S. myself, I have had a lifelong experience of acculturation. Changing one's culture, or attempting to fit it into another touches each aspect of one's life. In doing so, it can rock your identity as a whole. Please consider setting up a consultation appointment, to receive some professional support on this journey.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: The identity of man seems to have changed so much in modern times. It sometimes seems feels completely out of place today. Men's roles in work, relationships, even hobbies have been impacted. This is the place where we reconnect with your goals and dreams, and find actual workable ways of reaching them. No matter what place you are in life, there is always hope of moving forward.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Congratulations in taking a step towards overcoming the mountain of esteem! You know, that thing that always has something negative to say to you. That thing that limits your courage and holds you back from all the things you want in life. Join me for a consult, and let's take another step toward climbing this mountain.

specialities.name: Aspergers
specialities.description: Learning to live and thrive in a social world can be daunting. If you identify on the Aspergers spectrum, it can be completely overwhelming and unfair. This is the place where we use the scientific model to challenge your fears, understand yourself and limits, and ultimately find ways to reach your goals. Join me for a free consult to explore what we can accomplish working together.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: If you live in the PNW, chances are you have experienced or come across some depression. Whether you have been living with this for most of your life, or you are having a period in your life with more depression, this is the place we explore your relationship with depression, and ultimately find the best coping mechanisms to overcome.

name: Ellie Ritson
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I offer online therapy to kids, teens, and adults living in Oregon.
ideal_client: I work with kids, teens, and adults experiencing symptoms of trauma, anxiety, depression, or simply adjusting to difficulties in life. I'm calm and utilize a lot of feedback (FIT) to make sure the sessions are what you need. I'm down if you want to talk all session, if you would like to play an online game together, and everything in between! Therapy should be your time to get what you need when you need it- so I also have weekend availability for those who work or go to school.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches. I am trained in problem-solving therapy to find coping skills you actually like, cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to identify thought processes that can help you feel good, dialectical behavioral therapy (DBT) to explore , internal family systems (IFS) to connect with the pieces that make you you, feedback-informed treatment (FIT) to make sure you're getting what you need from our sessions together, and polyvagal theory to help you connect to your body. Most of the people I work with experience trust and emotional relief within the first month, followed by additional sessions to begin working on long-term healing and growth.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I value meeting you wherever you are in life, supporting you without judgement, finding tools together that really work for you, and practicing therapy within my own life and development so I really know what I'm talking about. I'm not going to tell you to exercise or give you breathing exercises that I've never done before of if you don't want to. Long gone are the days where a therapist is aloof, high, and mighty. Today I'm here to be your wellness partner and find what works best for you. Together we can tackle things at your speed and in a way that makes you feel empowered and at ease.

name: Amy Hughes
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I specialize in working with teens and Generation Z adults using a range of therapeutic interventions.
ideal_client: My preferred age range is 16 - 40. My work with clients has involved treating mood disorders and addressing identity concerns. My clients have been new to counseling or have returned to therapy, and are motivated to move forward. This is a time when you are figuring out who you want to be.

approaches.My Background: I earned my bachelor's and master's degrees from New York University. In my graduate program, I interned at a medical hospital and in the acute unit of a children's in-patient psychiatric center. In 1992, I began practicing as a therapist at an out-patient clinic in New York, where I lived for eleven years. Since that time, I have lived in San Francisco and Portland, Oregon. I have worked in other mental health settings and have taken hiatuses to work in other fields and raise a family.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I have completed hours of receiving supervision and continuing education courses in CBT.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I completed my graduate work in a program that emphasized psychodynamic training (NYU).

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I have professional experience working with adolescents and young adults presenting with sexuality and gender identity issues.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have clinical experience and professional expertise with clients struggling with mood disorders and low self-esteem, self-harming behaviors, and/or Social Anxiety.

name: Chidozie Urom
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I believe that humanity comes in all colors of the rainbow. I am a professional counselor intern in the stage of Oregon.
ideal_client: Are you always wondering why things just do not feel right? Because of obstacles such as anxiety, anger, grief or troubling emotions or past issues. Do you always fall into patterns and routines that are unproductive and cause distress? Perhaps I can help. It can be frustrating to be stuck in a maladaptive pattern. I believe you can be free with meaningful help. A holistic therapeutic approach coupled with evidence based practices can help you tremendously and I can't wait to be your guide.

approaches.How I Can Help You: Oftentimes, we lack awareness of how our thinking patterns affect our behavior, so I use cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to locate and change faulty assumptions that keep us from growth. CBT is an evidence-based treatment plan that is backed by science and research data. In addition, I believe that you are more than just an individual, but an integral part of society and the universe. I therefore makes use of Adlerian psychodynamic therapy. This treatment strategy is holistic and addresses all dimensions of the self. This includes social, occupational, physical, emotional and also spiritual. A strength-based approach which is mindful towards ethnic and cultural issues and concerns.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My mantra is that as a strong ally and observer of your life, it is my duty to guide you through your struggles towards resolution. While the journey may not be easy, we can learn to find joy in the climb. I immigrated from Nigeria at a young age. Young enough to know my culture and language and fresh enough to grasp the culture of the United States. I understand and relate to the struggles of minorities and immigrants. My experiences as an immigrant and minority has led to a calling in Psychology. I believe spirituality is valuable for those who seek it in all its form. I am a Christian and welcome all religious practices.

name: Milo Bissett
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Hello! I am a queer, psychodynamic therapist originally from Texas. Clients know me as collaborative, approachable, and a fierce advocate.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with teens, adults, and families. I am passionate about working with the queer community, neurodiversity, and trauma. As your therapist I will work to collaborate on treatment and we will learn and grow together.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I draw from Humanistic, Queer, and Systems theories. My background is in social justice and social work, I emphasize the impact of intersecting identities and cultural experiences on each client's journey. Through a combination of trauma-informed practices and techniques drawing from a variety of interventions, I provide a supportive space for clients to build autonomy, advocate for themselves, and navigate life’s challenges.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in building trust, authenticity, and genuine care with my clients. I center my client’s values, personal goals, and story to direct our focus, and work to adjust my approach to meet my clients however they show up. I am passionate about working with clients who feel burnout from systematic oppression, capitalism, and traditional expectations of what success and fulfillment means.

name: Lizzie Miller
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hello! My name is Lizzie. I’m deeply committed to helping clients process trauma and reconnect with their authentic selves.
ideal_client: If you’re carrying trauma from childhood, sexual assault, or domestic violence, you’re not alone—and healing is possible. I help clients process deep pain, reconnect with their authentic selves, and reclaim the power to create the life they truly want. Counseling is a rewarding and irreplaceable tool. I imagine my ideal client's reason for seeking help is self-love, a desire to live more authentically, and/or to reclaim their power.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With a foundation in trauma therapy, I also provide my clients with humanistic, person-centered, and feminist-based therapy tailored to their individual needs. Anti-oppression, feminist-focused clinical work focuses on recognizing the impact of systemic oppression, power dynamics, and social context on an individual's experience of trauma. My approach emphasizes empowerment, validation, and autonomy, centering on your lived experience. I draw from an integrative approach where I employ different modalities to tailor my services to fit your needs. Modalities I offer: Person-centered Therapy, Feminist Therapy, Narrative Exposure Therapy, mindfulness training, safety planning, risk assessment, somatic therapy, and trauma-informed care. My specialties include complex trauma, PTSD, interpersonal violence, and sexual assault. Together, we can create a genuine, open, honest, mutually respectful relationship built on trust where you can grow freely and focus on deep healing.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I chose mental health counseling after years of personal reflection and growth, shaped by my evolving values, beliefs, and goals. Therapy has been a transformative force in my own life—helping me navigate trauma, loss, and change—and I hope to offer that same sense of safety and healing to others. My passion for social justice has always been a central part of who I am, and now, through humanistic and feminist-informed counseling, I have the privilege of creating change on an individual level. Much of my clinical experience has centered on supporting survivors of domestic violence and sexual assault. I approach this work through a trauma-informed, anti-racist, and empowerment-based lens. I am deeply passionate about this population because violence disproportionately affects those who are already marginalized, and I believe survivors deserve space to process their trauma, reclaim their power, rewrite their narratives, and heal on their own terms.

name: Emily Radcliffe
title: Marriage and Family Therapist
intro: I help my clients develop more joyous and enriched lives, move through past and present traumas, confront challenges, and get un-stuck.
ideal_client: The clients I work with are motivated to work toward their goals and are willing to go to hard places to do so. I work with ages 14 and up - my practice includes individuals, couples and families. My clients often present struggling with anxiety, panic, or depression, and are influenced by or concerned with fitting the mold that society asks them to fit. Others are impacted by past trauma. I help my clients break free of the molds, find authenticity, and discover passion and purpose in life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am an Emotion-Focused therapist, which means I believe that emotions are a powerful piece of the puzzle of our internal landscape. To complete the puzzle, I also draw on Attachment Theory, Intergenerational Family Therapy, IFS, DBT, CBT, Mindfulness, Spirituality and earth/nature-based healing. I believe that our pasts, our surroundings, and our relationships heavily influence our current experience. Understanding these influences can be powerful, liberating, challenging, and even scary. I'm here to remind you, you're worth it. I bring my full and authentic self to therapy and I believe that a positive, trusting, open and safe therapeutic relationship (our relationship) is essential to successful outcomes in therapy. My first goal will always be to connect with you authentically and create safety in our relationship. Safety is not an objective state, and my job is to ensure the environment we create together feels safe to you. This allows us to explore and dive deep.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in the interconnection of life. As humans we form our world view based on our experiences, stories, and relationships. Let's be real... The world can feel like a really difficult and scary place to live right now, especially for those who have marginalized identities. I stand firm in my values of anti-racism, LGBTQ affirmation, body positivity and beauty at any size, anti-hate, anti-ableism, and valuing/affirming neurodiversity. I strive to confront and dismantle systems and societal narratives that make and keep humanity sick and keep my clients stuck. I've spent significant time working with individuals, couples, and families to help them break through barriers and step out of boxes and cycles that make them feel trapped and hopeless. I have done this both as a therapist and in community-based non-profits where I provided support and mentorship. I am committed to community engagement and consider community and connection to be essential to human wellness.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I believe that emotions make up a powerful part of our inner world and landscapes and I think it's important to value, honor and respect each person's emotional experience. By exploring, getting in touch with, and processing emotions I can help you learn more about yourself, find authenticity in relationships, set boundaries, and develop more self-compassion and resilience.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory has recently become more mainstream and a lot of folx are interested in how it applies to them or their partnership. I can help you explore your attachment style and how it manifests in your relationships both with others and yourself. I can also help you explore the roots of your attachment style in order to better understand how you got here. Learning about and naming attachment styles and wounds can be powerful and help foster secure attachment going forward.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I'm currently working on becoming fully certified as a DBT therapist, but in the meantime I tend to use a lot of DBT skills and tools in my practice. I've had success in implementing DBT to help folx with emotion regulation, developing self compassion, improving relationships and navigating conflict. DBT can be a valuable framework whether it's used in a structured curriculum format or intermixed with other modalities in a more fluid way.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I am also working on official certifications for Internal Family Systems therapy. Like DBT, IFS can be a very powerful framework and can help folx process deep trauma, get to know themselves better, develop more self compassion and work through challenges including (but not limited to) anxiety, depression, anger/rage, panic, PTSD, trauma and much more.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: I believe that part of the reason that we (humans) encounter challenges such as mood disorders and difficulties in relationships is because we have largely lost our connection to the most important life force - Mother Earth. I can help you foster a connection with the natural world that will aid in your healing journey as well as develop a fortified connection with your authentic self. Whether you're a "nature person" or not, EcoTherapy principles can be a helpful tool for wellness.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have significant experience helping folx manage anxiety and panic. My clients have had success in using several modalities to help manage anxiety in the moment and lessen the intensity and frequency of anxiety and panic. Additionally I've helped my clients explore and investigate the roots of anxiety and panic to address the cause and begin to heal those wounds.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I have extensive experience working with depression both in individuals and managing depression in family systems, couples, and parent/child relationships. I've helped folx develop self compassion, gently investigate the wounds that may have contributed to depression and implement strategies and interventions to manage intense feelings and move through difficult periods of time. Depression can feel debilitating and hopeless. I can help you increase hope and develop more resilience.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: For over a decade I've worked with youth, teens and young adults to help them manage everything normal growing-pains to intense family conflict, trauma, Panic Disorder, PTSD, anxiety, depression and more. I've also helped families more successfully communicate and understand each other - learn speak each other's language.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Feeling like you're just not connecting with your family? Are there past issues that have been overlooked or pushed aside? I can help bridge those gaps and process past conflict/trauma that contributes distance and misconnection. Family conflict can be challenging for all parties. I can help you examine and shift cycles, patterns and communication styles that don't serve your family, and create closer and more trusting relationships.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I have experience working with individuals, couples and families experiencing challenges around ADHD. I've worked teens and young people who were diagnosed at a young age as well as adults who are newly diagnosed. ADHD can present challenges in many aspects of life, not just in academic or work settings. I can help bridge gaps in understanding, develop strategies to support executive functioning, and help folx communicate and support each other through these challenges.

name: Melanie Treuhaft
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with individuals facing anxiety, depression, grief, trauma, identity crises, creative block, and relationship issues.
ideal_client: I work with clients who are creative, curious, and committed to developing their innate resilience. I welcome clients who are interested in introducing more creativity into their way of thinking. I often work with clients for whom arts are central to their personal and spiritual identity.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have a client centered approach to therapy and aim to meet each client where they are at by collaborating to create individualized treatment plans. I know that each client navigates a variety of oppressive systems and needs space to bring their specific perspectives and identities into the therapeutic relationship. I draw upon theoretical frameworks such as CBT, DBT, ACT, mindfulness, and parts work to create custom treatment plans.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: To ensure clients receive the level of care best suited to their needs, I work with individuals who are relatively stable and able to engage in weekly outpatient therapy. I am not the best fit for those currently navigating active suicidal thoughts, psychosis, or frequent crises, and I recommend connecting with providers who specialize in crisis stabilization or more intensive levels of care.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I completed a certificate in trauma at Antioch University which included courses on creative approaches to trauma and grief.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have worked with many clients that face anxiety. I acknowledge that the world we live in promotes anxiety inducing behaviors and that we are all working to achieve a greater connection to the present moment. I led a meditation therapy group and include mindfulness in my individual therapy.

name: Allison Hoyman-Browe
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My style is authentic, compassionate, and active.
ideal_client: Are you ready to live a more wholehearted, vibrant, and meaningful life? I support folks on a path towards developing more nourishing relationships, a better understanding their emotions, and living a life aligned with their values. My clients are people who struggle with burnout, anxiety, depression, or are facing big life transitions. I look forward to supporting you in developing skills and insight to lead a fulfilling life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My primary theoretical orientation comes from Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), a mindfulness based practice which seeks to foster psychological flexibility, give you the tools you need to navigate hard emotions and live a values driven life. I tailor my sessions to the client before me, addressing their unique needs and goals by integrating ACT with trauma informed and harm reduction approaches. I am trained in Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) a powerful tool for processing trauma. Our mental health is impacted by the world around us and I fundamentally believe that we all carry with us the impacts of our unique identities and positionalities, our families of origin as well as our found families, our experiences of joy as well as our experiences of trauma and oppression.

name: Stephanie Podasca
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer compassionate and trauma-informed Telehealth to residents of OR and WA. Here to help you navigate all the peaks and valleys of life!
ideal_client: My ideal client is a deep feeler—often a creative, healer, or first-generation American—navigating trauma, anxiety, identity, or burnout. They may feel stuck in old patterns, disconnected from themselves, or overwhelmed by life’s demands. They long for clarity, peace, and a deeper sense of inner freedom. Their goals include healing past wounds, building emotional resilience, and reconnecting to their truth. They want therapy that’s thoughtful, nonjudgmental, and honors their full complexity.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer trauma-informed therapy that integrates somatic work, mindfulness, parts work (IFS), and a spiritually inclusive lens. I specialize in supporting creatives, healers, and first-generation adults navigating trauma, anxiety, and identity. My approach is warm and collaborative, honoring the whole self as a path to deeper healing. In my practice, I take a holistic approach to therapy. That means we won’t just look at one part of you in isolation. We’ll explore how your mind, body, emotions, relationships, past experiences, and environment all weave together to shape your current experience.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As a therapist, I hold space that is grounded in curiosity, compassion, and care. I believe healing happens when we honor the whole self—mind, body, and spirit—and move at the pace of trust. My approach integrates somatic therapy, mindfulness, IFS, and a spiritually inclusive lens. I work from a trauma-informed foundation, supporting people in gently exploring what’s been hard to hold alone. As a Romanian-American and artist, I bring cultural humility, creativity, and lived experience into the room—especially when working with first-generation clients, creatives, and healers. Whether you're navigating trauma, anxiety, identity, or spiritual transformation, I’ll meet you with nonjudgment, warmth, and deep respect for your path. Therapy with me is collaborative and relational—we co-create a space where your insight, intuition, and voice can flourish.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: When we bring mindfulness into therapy, we build your ability to stay present with yourself, even in discomfort. We create space between stimulus and response. And we uncover what’s often hidden beneath automatic habits or overwhelming feelings. Whether we’re using breath, body awareness, grounding techniques, or mindful reflection, the goal isn’t to “empty your mind.” It’s to reconnect with yourself, your inner experience, and the choices you have in any moment.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: In somatic therapy, we slow down and tune in. You’ll learn to notice what’s happening in your body—tension, breath, sensations, impulses—and explore what those signals might be telling you. Together, we work gently with these experiences to release stored stress, increase regulation, and help you feel more grounded in your own skin. Whether you’ve experienced trauma, struggle with anxiety, or simply feel disconnected from your body, somatic therapy offers a path to healing that honors it all.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Parts work, including Internal Family Systems (IFS), is a powerful, compassionate approach to therapy that helps you understand the different “parts” or subpersonalities within you. These parts may hold different emotions, beliefs, or roles—like the inner critic, the people-pleaser, the angry protector, the scared child. Each part has its own story, and often, its own reason for being. IFS invites us to get to know them with curiosity and care.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Excessive thinking, worrying, future-tripping, panic, freezing, shutting down... Anxiety truly sucks! The majority of my clients would be diagnosed with Generalized Anxiety Disorder, which tends to mask underlying trauma, low-self esteem, and other behavioral issues. Luckily, there are so many helpful tools you can learn to overcome the helplessness that anxiety makes you feel. With mindfulness, somatic experiments, and education we will work together to get you through the worries and fears!

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: PTSD is a very challenging and unique experience for everyone - I have worked with many people who satisfied the criteria for PTSD, even though all of their experiences were wildly different! As a trauma-informed therapist, I initially assume that a traumatic experience is at the root of most human suffering and is the cause of the majority of symptoms such as anxiety, depression, addiction, etc. I engage in ongoing education to be an active helper at every phase of the recovery process.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Being a woman in this world is hard! It's important you work with someone that understands the array of challenges women are faced with from the time they are born and throughout life. I have the most experience working directly with women in both individual counseling and in women's-based recovery circles. I am passionate about helping women process their experiences of womanhood, motherhood, sexuality, challenges in the workforce, and overcoming trauma so they can live empowered lives.

specialities.name: Early Recovery
specialities.description: You have just made one of the most important decisions of your life in seeking recovery from addiction! It can be vital to set up your life with as many supports in place as possible as you start to uncover the challenging emotions, behaviors, and trauma that contributed to your addictions. I bring my personal background in recovery and harm reduction education, and I am attuned to both the challenges and gifts the recovery journey brings up.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Whether your spirituality is rooted in a religious tradition, a connection to nature, ancestral practices, or a personal sense of meaning, it can be a powerful source of guidance, strength, and healing. In therapy, we can include that part of you. Spirituality in counseling isn’t about imposing any belief system—it’s about creating space for yours. If spirituality plays a role in how you understand yourself, your suffering, or your growth, we can explore that together with care and respect.

name: Lynn Emmons LCSW, LICSW, RN, CADCI
full_name: Lynn Emmons LCSW, LICSW, RN, CADCI (she/her)
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I believe that we are all driven to heal and grow. Sometimes the barriers to our healing and growth are hard to define and address alone.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use a holistic, compassionate and client-centered approach utilizing your strengths and learning style to individualize your therapy course; my toolbox is made up of techniques/ interventions from an array of models/theories and my approach is also informed by what we now know about the brain. For those with alcohol/drug use/addiction, I will work from an abstinence-based or harm-reduction stance depending on individual goals and challenges.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have almost 40 years experience as a psychiatric and addictions nurse and clinical social worker (LCSW) and addiction counselor (CADCI), in hospital, residential, and outpatient mental health and addictions settings. My experience is with children, adolescents, young adults, adults and families. I have a passion for working with people who struggle with addiction and I will provide support for facing the difficulties of early recovery or when life's hurdles challenge recovery along the way. I also have worked with health care professionals with mental health/addiction problems and can help support the unique struggles of working in healthcare and managing self-care. I also have experience and enjoy working with college students.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: Going to therapy doesn't always need to be for a long time. Depending on the client's needs, solution focused brief therapy can quickly address current challenges from a strengths-based solution focused stance. I utilized this approach a great deal in an university student health clinic setting and found it very effective.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: According one of my favorite authors and experts in mental health, Daniel Siegel,'recent studies of mindfulness practices reveal that they can result in profound improvements in a range of physiological, mental, and interpersonal domains in our lives. ' I weave mindfulness into every therapeutic interaction as I believe it is the foundation for mental wellness.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: We are not our thoughts and feelings and yet we often function as if we believe we are. CBT helps create some objectivity about our thoughts and feelings, as well as increase our capacity to challenge and change them thereby improving our mood and beliefs about ourselves. I like using an integrative approach that often incorporates CBT skills.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Despite our society still stigmatizing this challenge, it affects us all either within ourselves, our families, our workplaces...everywhere. The human brain is vulnerable to chemicals and habits. I have many years of experience working in addiction and dual diagnosis treatment and I have a passion for working with individuals and families impacted by this common struggle. I believe in recovery.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: What a person thinks about themselves can hugely impact every aspect of their life. I enjoy helping folks explore where these stories about themselves come from and then write new stories.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Our connections to others are the greatest assets and challenges. Outside perspective and support can be really helpful to address relationship struggles. Communication glitches are a common problem. I utilize Non-violent communication skills, family systems, narrative and other models/theories very effectively with individuals, couples and families.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: To live is to experience loss. Grieving is a necessary and natural process; our culture and busy lives don't always support this process and people can get really stuck. Personally and professionally, I have a great deal of experience in helping people move through their grief process.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: In my experience working with clients, anxiety is a very common challenge for many. It hijacks the brain and can really inhibit living life fully. Fortunately, there are many ways I can help a person develop skills and ways to manage and decrease their anxiety

name: Rachel Kendall
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My mission is to help individuals and families formulate positive patterns of behavior that promote generational healing through Telehealth.
ideal_client: Understanding our own behavior, including it's origins is crucial to developing a healthy family dynamic and support system to increase resilience. Those with a desire to be well will find understanding of themselves and those around them with more compassion and acceptance than before. To facilitate this process, we can work on stress management techniques and practice the relationship skills to cultivate the support system that brings out the best in you and your loves ones.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am heavily trained in Family Systems Theory, where I like to utilize a genogram to help individuals and families visually understand the origins of their behavior. Also being trauma-informed with anti-racist alignment, my clinical orientation is rooted in the mission to serve vulnerable and marginalized populations because when everyone's needs are met, we become healthier and thrive as a society. ~Please Note: I am only offering Telehealth and No In-Person sessions at this time~ ***Oregon Health Plan Clients please schedule here: https://restorativefamilybalancellc.clientsecure.me/

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold an MS in Marriage, Couple and Family Counseling from Walden University. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor with the Oregon Board of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists. My clinical experience has involved serving vulnerable populations, including traditionally marginalized identities, neurodivergent individuals, those in recovery from addiction and/ or struggling to have their basic needs met. I chose to specialize in EMDR because it is so broad in helping clients heal from experiences and establish a greater sense of safety and promote generational healing. ~Please Note: I am only offering Telehealth and No In-Person sessions at this time~

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I received training from the EMDR Institute, founded by Francine Shapiro, who discovered it. In reading her text and as discussed in the training, we learned just how much memory influences our interaction with the world, and how our brain adapts to our experience. I love EMDR because it allows people to mindfully embrace the human experience in the present moment. Please note, I am only offering Telehealth at this time. EMDR is evidenced based to be effective both online & virtually.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness is a powerful tool because it enables you to observe your experience without interaction, thereby lessening the emotional intensity of an experience. With helping clients practice their resourcing for widening their 'window of tolerance' for stress, they can experience greater peace and become more thoughtful in their responses towards themselves and others.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: The premise of the family system is that it is the origin of where our world view forms and also how inherently 'safe' we feel. We also form attachments early on that can influence the type of relationships we have later on in life. Based on the values a family wants to have, I can help them re-establish connection, beginning with understanding their family/ system of origin.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: Although I am not a person of color, I have taken dedicated time to address and confront my implicit biases to fight against cultural and systemic oppression at it's core: to challenge the mindset of the oppressor, instead of simply sympathizing with the oppressed. One related training I did included 'How to be (Less) Harmful: Training White Helpers to Serve BIPOC clients.' https://www.ar-tic.org

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Finding the origins of behavior are helpful to changing it. In my work with families, I begin with helping them enhance their understanding of one another's frame of reference, which allows for greater empathy when working through conflict. By establishing the meaning behind certain behaviors, strategies can be implemented to better align with the values families want to abide by.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Childhood and adolescence are wonderful times in human development because there is so much discovery about oneself and the world. At times, the unknown can be uncomfortable. By offering a foundation of belonging and self-acceptance for children and adolescents, I can help them to establish a sense of safety as they expand their comfort zone and embrace their personal growth journey.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Suffering is a fact of life, however, that does not have to be the end of our story. By allowing yourself to be human and embrace your experience, you will begin to see yourself with greater compassion. That does not discount the fact that these experiences are often painful. By helping you feel safe within your body, you can process trauma to fully embrace all life has to offer.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: As someone who has struggled with anxiety, I have tried several methods to keep it at bay. Throughout the years in my healing journey, I discovered how much my nervous system was involved in my experience. I learned the brain responds to a threat the same way whether is either real or imagined. By practicing mindfulness with intentionality, we can stay present when anxious thoughts arise.

name: Brittany Eide
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I have always felt empathetic and sensitive and I experience a draw to knowing and connecting with all kinds of people.
ideal_client: I am very motivated to work with people who are willing to be introspective gaining insights into their daily patterns and blocks. These individuals typically have past experiences that are unconscious to them. We take our time thoughtfully identifying coping strategies built over time to get through these historic experiences of stress. After being present to the impact and providing validation and soothing we can work to rescript one's experience in the present.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is warm, attentive, curious, and sincere. I am invested in building a bridge quickly so as to foster connection and support the process. It is my intention to be real, vulnerable, and relatable. I am much more interested in connection than formality. I want people to feel comfortable and safe to explore anything and everything knowing that we are all human and doing the best we can.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I started in the field back in 1998 when I began my degree in psychology. From there, I got a Master's in Counseling Psychology and became a school counselor. I then became a Certified Relationship Coach and Certified Synergistic Play Therapist. I have served children, teens, and adults working through many different issues in my capacity as a therapist, school counselor, and coach.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I have received education and training from a multitude of different theoretical orientations and practices. I pull from various different modalities to help design the plan that best fits each individual.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: It is my aim to assist clients in reaching their goals in any relationship in which they feel they need guidance and support. My training was based off of the principles of interpersonal intelligence.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I have a passion for personal growth and pursue it consistently. I have taken many courses over the years to enhance my own process and also help clients in finding their individual path of growth.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have extensive training through The Relationship School. I spent time learning how to help individuals have healthy relationship with the people in their lives. I received top-notch education and hours of practice honing many skills from a model of interpersonal intelligence.

name: Heather Rensmith
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Relationship + Sex Therapy for folx on a mission to all-ass their romantic+sexual relationships. AASECT Certified Sex Therapist + Telehealth

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is one that values strengths and empowers people to pursue their ideal life situations. My goal is not to pathologize differences, but help people acknowledge their concerns, seek acceptance or accommodation and thier own versions of optimal functioning. I enjoy working with individual and couples who practice various relationship models and structures (monogamy, polyamory, non-monogamy, kink), who are part of the queer community, or who are still figuring out their community. I take an eclectic approach to therapy and draw upon common treatment approaches include cognitive behavioral therapy, Gottman Method Couple Therapy, Emotionally Focused Therapy, and narrative therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I most enjoy working with individuals and couples who are working on issues surrounding their sexuality and sexual health. Our work together could explore functioning (pain, erectile dysfunction, chronic or acute illness and its impact on sexual functioning), desire, arousal, and varying interests, communication, grief and loss, or trauma recovery. Sex therapy often involves education, validation, and normalization. I graduated from the University of Michigan School of Social Work in 2002 after obtaining by BA in Women's Studies from Michigan State University. I am licensed in the State of Oregon and Washington as a Clinical Social Worker. I have completed a Sexual Health Certificate from the University of Michigan School of Social Work in sex therapy and education. I am an AASECT certified sex therapist as well as certified by the Sexual Health Alliance in the treatment of Problem Sexual Behavior.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Using Differentiation, Emotionally Focused Therapy, Gottman Method, and others to help people achieve their relationship goals!

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: training in CBT and helping people examine how thoughts influence actions and behaviors.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Training specific to LGBTQ issues in Sexual Health Certificate Program

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: Treats common sexual problems including desire discrepenices, low desire, sexual functioning and pain for all genders. Post Masters sexual health certificate in Sex Therapy and Education. AASECT Certified Sex Therapist

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Sex and relationship therapy using various modalities to help achieve relationship satisfaction. Trained in Emotionally Focused Therapy and Gottman Method.

name: Gina Adorno
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: It's not for you to spend your one precious life spinning in circles. Want to recalibrate?
ideal_client: Most of my clients work with me on adjusting to some wild thing life just threw at them, and/or healing some combination of depression, addiction, trauma, or anxiety. As I am also a musician, I often find myself working with artists or other creative types, or people who are drawn to that style of thinking. Some people come to me seeking clarification on whether they may be autistic or have ADHD. Some already know and want emotional support dealing with a neurotypical-oriented world.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I work with a variety of issues using equally varied tools, depending on the client's needs, preferences, and proclivities. I also offer comprehensive neurodivergence-affirming autism and ADHD evaluations for adults. I draw from several research-backed approaches such as parts work, CBT and DBT, and motivational interviewing (a respectful, supportive, autonomy-forward approach for addictions). I specialize in working with people facing multiple diagnoses concurrently such as addiction and depression or trauma, or autistic folks who need to address mental health needs with a provider who understands how their neurotype may impact them.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Prior to becoming a therapist, I trained as a violinist and opera singer. My development as a musician informs my treatment approach as I see providing therapy as similar to developing facility on an instrument - a development of awareness, skill, self-concept, and self-confidence under whatever the given circumstances. It's a process of strengthening what supports you and weeding out tensions that may be holding you back from giving your fullest natural sound. I take an artistic stance to treatment and enjoy working with other artists frequently. My social locations: I am a white heterosexual cisgender female, LGBTQIA+ and BIPOC ally. Sex positive, adamantly gender affirming, and kink & poly friendly. I offer a free 15-minute consultation so we can connect and have a chance to ask a few questions. Currently accepting all listed insurances, however I can only take OHP CareOregon/HealthShare for evaluations or short-term treatment for now.

specialities.name: Addiction Therapy
specialities.description: I work with many people looking to change to their relationship to substances. I provide a nonjudgmental space for you to clarify your goals and support you in reaching them. I can help with abstinence or moderation goals if appropriate for the client, and we can take a look at that together. If you don’t know what you want yet or if you are even ready to make a change, we can talk it through, step by step, and get you where you want to go.

specialities.name: Psychological Testing and Evaluation
specialities.description: I provide neurodivergence-affirming adult autism and ADHD evaluations over telehealth. My assessment process is warm and therapeutic, using a combination of qualitative and quantitative measures to create a full picture of your neurotype, and includes a therapeutic feedback session where we discuss results and help you incorporate them into your understanding of yourself.

name: Jennifer Jim, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with individuals and couples in the areas of depression, anxiety, relational issues, attachment issues and work stress & burnout.
ideal_client: As you consider your needs, know that my background includes working with individuals diverse in age, race, county of origin, ability, sexual orientation and faith. If you are 18yrs of age and older, Individual please consider giving me a call for a free 15min phone session to begin your journey towards living your Renewed life. We can focus in on relationships, sleep and work performance as top areas highly affected by stress. I have a specialty working with professional resiliency.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Imagine a bulls eye and at the center of that bulls eye is your best life. The life filled with calm, gratitude and self-compassion. My approach will help you name and identify your goals for treatment. We will then work together to reduce the intensity and frequency of symptoms you are experiencing so you can begin focusing on how to use gratitude and self-compassion to move forward. My approach is both didactic and focused on cognitive work. I also however come from a somatic approach through Accelerated Resolution Therapy (ART). ART is an eye movement therapy that can address trauma, phobias, ADHD, and many forms of anxiety.

Due to the high demand for therapy services, I'm sure you've met with many clinicians who do not have availability for new clients. I'm included in that as I have a full roster. However, I wanted to offer something other than one-on-one therapy that can also help you. I have an M.S. in Education and am a former adjunct professor and clinical director. I used these skills and put together a self-help psychoeducational resource library that you can access for a monthly subscription. It isn't intended to replace therapy but be an added support while you wait or even in addition to treatment. The resource library currently has over 60 hours of content, and new material will be added each month. It includes the following: Stop Overthinking Podcast, Self-Talk Audit Workshop, Bold Goal Workbook, Burnout Prevention & Recovery Masterclass, and Stress-busting strategies training. If you're interested to know more, send me an email jennifer@renewtherapynw.com.

specialities.name: Accelerated Resolution Therapy
specialities.description: Accelerated resolution therapy, or ART, is a type of therapy using techniques such as rapid eye movement and image replacement, this approach works to recondition stressful memories, changing how they are stored in the brain to improve overall mental health. ART is helpful when you have stress-inducing memories or future fears.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: I use Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and Cognitive Behavior Therapy to bring you the tools you need for mental wellness.

name: Jacob Curtis
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help people address mood, anxiety, eating disorder, trauma, and addiction issues.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am now offering teletherapy. Every person comes to counseling with a unique background and need. In some situations ways of dealing with things that were effective in the past may no longer work. Others may be seeking enhanced wellness or balance in their lives. Counseling begins with a safe and supportive relationship. Often the counseling process involves identifying one’s values, as well as one’s beliefs about oneself and the world. I use research-informed approaches to help my clients identify problem areas, create goals, and try new ways of doing things that work for them in their unique situation. My theoretical approach to counseling is integrative, but draws from Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), CBT-I (for insomnia), Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (a type of CBT), and Existential Theory.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a Master’s Degree (MA) in Counseling Psychology from Lewis & Clark College, Graduate School of Education and Counseling and hold professional membership in the American Counseling Association. I am also a Certified Drug and Alcohol Counselor I (CADC I), a Nationally Certified Counselor (NCC), and a Professional Counselor (LPC) licensed by the Oregon Board of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists. My training includes: working with individuals and families; lifespan development; treating people experiencing anxiety and depression; cultural diversity; treating people who have experienced trauma and abuse; treating individuals with personality disorders; interpersonal effectiveness and communication strategies; diagnosis and assessment; Cognitive Processing Therapy for trauma; Cognitive Behavioral Therapy; Dialectical Behavior Therapy; Motivational Interviewing; treating people with addictions; and other treatments, modalities and interventions.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I have had training in Dialectical Behavior Therapy, and have engaged in this therapy practice for a number of years. This therapy approach helps people more effectively manage their emotions while enhancing their interpersonal skills. A core principle of this approach is building mindfulness skills.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: My work with clients includes looking at values, choices, and the meaning in their lives, from a non-judgmental perspective.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I often use the principles and practices of CBT (including CBT-I) to help people address depression, insomnia, and anxiety. It helps one look at their thoughts and beliefs, build insight about feelings, and identify patterns to make changes in one's life.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I have completed the EMDRIA part 1 and 2 trainings on EMDR. It can be a helpful method of addressing trauma, as well as other issues that cause distress.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: I have engaged in numerous trainings in Motivational Interviewing. I have successfully used this approached with many clients to help them identify and reach their goals.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have training in both Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) and Eye Movement and Desensitization Reprocessing (EMDR). Both of these therapies are evidenced based treatments.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I have experience and training working with people experiencing restrictive eating, body image distress, purging, rumination, and ARFID.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have had training in evidence-based approaches to treating symptoms of anxiety. I have used these approaches for a number of years.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I have had training in evidence-based approaches to treating symptoms of depression. I have used these approaches for a number of years.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I am hold a certification in alcohol and drug counseling from the Addiction Counselor Certification Board of Oregon.

name: Gretchen Klipp
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am passionate about therapy and the impact that it can have on one’s life.
ideal_client: My decision to pursue a career as a therapist was born from my own personal experience with therapy, which helped me overcome significant and sometimes paralyzing anxiety that was preventing me from living the life I desired. I am a strong advocate for eliminating the stigma that our society has placed, and continues to place, on mental health and I share my story with others in hopes of normalizing, validating and highlighting the benefits that therapy can add to each person’s life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach is client-centered and collaborative, based on the fact that you are the expert of your own life, with your own unique lived experiences, relationships, strengths and needs. Because we are all unique, I tailor my approach to each individual client, utilizing evidence-based techniques and methodology.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Together, we will identify and celebrate the strengths, insights and tools that you already possess and determine how we can apply those to other areas of your life that may need some love and attention. I feel honored and privileged to have the opportunity to support you on your journey.

name: Destry Stoner LPC, CADCIII
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I have availability for three new clients this summer. Let's connect to determine if I am a good fit for you and determine scheduling.
ideal_client: If you are suffering from unresolved trauma, anxiety, panic disorder, depression and/or addiction issues, I can help! These are very uncomfortable and debilitating problems. I will develop a treatment plan with you that is effective, often brief and will change and improve the quality of your life and relationships. I am trained in EMDR, which is a specialized treatment for trauma, PTSD, phobias and anxiety. This therapy is very rewarding and brings hope to situations that may seem hopeless.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a licensed professional counselor, I assist with trauma, PTSD, relationship issues, anxiety, depression and addictions. My orientation is Existential, I believe that when we have unresolved issues from our past and/or are not living in alignment with what is most important to us we feel incongruent. The ultimate goal for therapy is developing a life that is filled with congruence and happiness. I embrace research-based counseling techniques and tailor my approach to your individual needs and goals. I have extensive training in CBT, DBT, EMDR, Motivational Interviewing, and psychodynamic modalities and additionally specialize in the treatment of trauma (PTSD; abuse) and addictive behaviors (including substance misuse, video gaming, gambling, overeating, etc.). In my practice, I strive to create a safe, collaborative, non-judgmental atmosphere that will help you better understand the difficulties you're experiencing and learn about ways to overcome them.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe that therapy begins with a safe and respectful environment where individual and relational needs are compassionately addressed. It is my personal and professional commitment to assist each client in reaching a place of greater health, peace and wholeness through therapy. Please call or email me with any questions or for consultation. I am happy to speak with you more about the process of counseling, what to expect and discuss how I can be helpful given your particular situation and needs. Finding someone you can trust and confide in can lighten the burden and help you find answers and rediscover hope in your life.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (better known as “EMDR”) is a revolutionary mental health treatment developed by psychologist Dr. Francine Shapiro in the 1990s. By stimulating the natural action of memory processing through eye movement, EMDR helps people to access and “re-process” their traumatic memories and deep core beliefs. Backed by extensive scientific research, EMDR is recognized worldwide as effective treatment for emotional disorders.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I utilize this therapy method to help people identify their ideal self, the barriers that get in the way of being their ideal self and develop a shared understanding of what needs to happen/change to get there. This often includes value identification, belief evaluations and meaning from historical suffering. The goal for this approach in therapy is to be able to identify awareness for congruence and incongruence and aligning with life choices that promote safety, happiness and well-being.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: When it comes to mental health treatment, cognitive behavioral therapy is one of the most effective psychotherapy approaches. It teaches you how to navigate life’s daily obstacles. By making these improvements, your mental condition also shows positive change. CBT helps you identify specific challenges in your life and how to cope with them. It’s useful in many ways, including: Reframing thoughts, Managing emotions, Managing stress, Resolving relationship problems and Improving communications.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Dialectical behavior therapy (DBT) is a modified type of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). Its main goals are to teach people how to live in the moment, develop healthy ways to cope with stress, regulate their emotions, and improve their relationships with others. I utilize DBT in individual counseling to teach skills for managing emotion regulation, interpersonal communication, distress tolerance and mindfulness.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I or CBTI) is a short, structured, and evidence-based approach to combating the frustrating symptoms of insomnia. How Does CBT-I Work? CBT-I focuses on exploring the connection between the way we think, the things we do, and how we sleep. During treatment, a trained CBT-I provider helps to identify thoughts, feelings, and behaviors that are contributing to the symptoms of insomnia.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: I believe that people start using substances for many reasons. Unfortunately substance use causes unintended problems over time. I believe that not one type of recovery path fits all so I taylor my approach to what is meaningful and important to you.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Unresolved trauma is complicated and it causes many in-the-present life problems. This is confusing because we often have no idea why we are getting upset about something, feel certain ways or have unexplainable anger. I utilize EMDR to treat and resolve ptsd and unresolved trauma symptoms. I have found EMDR to be a great addition to my therapy practice.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: It is human nature to be in relationship with other people. Unfortunately sometimes people lean on us to heavily in areas that they are lacking and need support. In order to be there on this level for other people we sacrifice what is important to us. This causes a lot of problems that are often not easy to detect and understand.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Sometimes anxiety is situational and makes sense and other times it makes no sense at all. Anxiety is uncomfortable and scary. I approach anxiety by addressing unresolved issues from your past that is instigating your anxiety, while teaching you mindfulness, breathing and cognitive coping skills for continuous self-management.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression symptoms can be debilitating and frustrating. Situational depression makes sense while biological depression is frustrating and confusing. Depression is often linked to events from the past that need to be resolved. I utilize personal empowerment development, meaningful life development and increased happiness to destroy depression symptoms.

name: Lisa Kaiser
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: With optimism, joy, and an empowering spirit, I hope to provide a safe space for children, teens, young adults, and adults.
ideal_client: I work with children, teens, and young adults to identify and work through (process) trauma, grief & loss, and low self-esteem. With many lived experiences, I bring a compassionate understanding that adds calm and comfort to the conversation.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My focus is on trauma, grief & loss, and low self-esteem. My toolbox includes Restoration Therapy, Play Therapy, Art Therapy, ACT, CBT, DBT, SFT, EFIT, and family systems. I don’t believe there is a “one size fits all” approach and that all individuals are wonderfully unique with varying life journeys.

name: Carl Jensen
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I have been practicing as a therapist for over 25 years. My experience covers a large list of mental health problem areas.
ideal_client: While living our lives we all go through periods of struggle and difficulty. That's the nature of being human, and the problems come in many forms. Besides problem solving, you are someone who is invested in personal growth and gaining greater self understanding, and someone who understands that life involves adapting to change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is humanistic and client-centered. I value each person as an individual. I will work collaboratively with you to nurture and support the healing and changes you envision for yourself. Our overall work together often will also support movement toward psychological wholeness and spiritual integrity.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: " ... Psychotherapy and analysis are as varied as human individuals. Treat every patient as individual as possible ... the solution of the problem is always an individual one," wrote CG Jung. I believe that you believe that there is in you the possibility of being another sort of person, the one you were meant to be. I want to help you with that work. I'm a student of Jung, dream work, psychodrama, and spiritual disciplines. My background also includes Redecision therapy, group therapy, Transactional analysis, Gestalt therapy, and Structural family therapy.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: My approach is genuine, warm, and respectful. My earliest training was Rogerian, and I have many years of practice with this modality and active listening.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: I have significant background in Psychodrama therapy, as well as Gestalt therapy. When a client goes deep into a problem area, this approach may often be the most valuable. There are numerous therapeutic experiential interventions that have the potential to creatively begin healing or transform an individuals problem area.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: If it is the desire of the client, we can address treatment through the lens of the concerns being a spiritual problem. This kind of work may include a focus on using dreams, and/or identifying archetypal energies, and/or understanding astrological dynamics, that are related to present day concerns. Each of these approaches can provide unique guidance specific to the individual client. One goal of therapy being to reach a place of equanimity.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I am a student of Jung. See above description under transpersonal.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: I have several years experience working with families. Although I don't see families today, I can work with individuals experiencing problems with their family dynamics. I have training in Structural family therapy.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Life is about change, and about navigating whatever transitions are happening at a particular time. Personal growth also involves addressing both individual and interpersonal behavior patterns, negative emotional patterns, and family of origin issues.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: This can involve practicing greater compassion toward oneself. It can also involve addressing self criticism or that judgemental voice in your head, and/or addressing concerns involving shame and guilt.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: There is work to be done in processing the deep layers of sadness and other emotions, as well as the subsequent reactions that surface. Grieving comes in waves, and has it's own time frame.

name: Jdeanna Winn
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Accepting new clients. Are you struggling with feeling stuck in your daily life? Ready for the change you desire? I am here to help.
ideal_client: We all struggle at times in our lives and can use the help of someone who has unconditional positive regard for us. I invite you to start your journey today. Taking OHP (YCCO)

approaches.How I Can Help You: If you need help with deep inner work and recovery from abuse, or just life transitions and stress, I am committed to creating the opportunity for you to have non-judgmental, trauma informed, affirming safe space to process whatever life has brought you.

approaches.More About the People We Treat: Are you confused about a relationship that has ended? Are you struggling to understand what has happened? I specialize in abuse recovery work, and have specialized training in abuse intervention. I can offer a unique understanding and support for abuse recovery work. Are you artistic? or do you want to integrate creating art into your healing journey? I have a background in Art, and can mesh your use of art and expressing yourself with your healing journey. I am a member of the LGBTQ community. I offer understanding and support for all.

specialities.name: Domestic Abuse
specialities.description: I have extensive training in abuse intervention work that informs and helps with my work with abuse survivors. I also have personal experience that lends to my deep understanding of the issues faced for people who have been abused.

name: Sheri Bansemer
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I'm glad you're here. I invite you to spend a few minutes here looking around and know I'm here when you're ready for the next step.
ideal_client: Many people who find their work with me valuable might be struggling with healthy communication, working through what comes up for them with parents or around parenting, examining how best to raise neurodiverse children or how to exist in our society as a neurodiverse person, experiencing grief and loss, wrestling with spiritual trauma, or experiencing infertility, pregnancy loss, or adoption.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach counseling with the belief that you are a whole person with unique experiences, strengths, and challenges. I trust in your intrinsic wisdom and will support you as you gain a deeper understanding of yourself and the systems in which we live. We will work together to name patterns that are helpful and unhelpful and work toward creating healthy interactions so you feel confident navigating life with insight and autonomy. In my work with individuals, couples, families, children, and adolescents, I aim to create a safe space where everyone feels heard and where authentic communication is valued. Cultivating trust, compassion, and respect and ensuring you feel seen, heard, and validated is of high priority to me. I invite you to approach this path with curiosity and courage. My commitment is to accompany you with empathy, respect, and steadfast support as you navigate life's complexities and celebrate the fullness of your being.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: I have the following additional training: EFCT Therapist, Restoration Therapy Level 1 Certification, PDA North America Level 1 and Level 2 trained; additional training in Motivational Interviewing, Attachment theory, and Play therapy.

name: Rivka Sidelsky
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with queer and trans teens and emergent adults to find new paths forward, grounded in collaboration and liberatory values :)
ideal_client: My practice is focused around supporting queer and trans teens (13-18) and emergent adults (18-25). I enjoy working with young people who are seeking accompaniment in their self-exploration and desire to be active participants in the therapy process.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use an integrative relational approach to therapy, drawing on somatic, feminist, and parts-work orientations. I love partnering with clients to find creative and practical ways to meet the challenges you're facing while making more space for whatever it is that brings you alive. I believe we feel better when we feel seen and understood, when we have the resources we need, and when we connect with our power to create the changes we want. I offer a free 20–30 minute consultation to answer any questions you have and explore what working together might look like. Take a look at my website to see if what I offer could line up with your needs. If you're not sure, I'm always happy to talk it through together, and can provide other resources.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I work towards a liberatory approach to healing. This means that I believe the things which cause us distress often start not within ourselves, but with how the social and political world operates around us. The way forward is just as much about drawing on our shared resourcefulness and power, to cope with and transform our environments, as it is about finding new ways to exist within ourselves. As queers and trans', we come from vibrant lineages of resistance, mutual-aid, and collective power. I ground my work in these lineages and in the belief that it's our shared responsibility to carry forward these life-giving currents, making and remaking the world into one in which we desire to live.

name: Megan DeVoe
title: Student Counselor
intro: Whatever brings you here, I look forward to holding space with you.
ideal_client: You might be seeking steadiness, meaningful change, or simply a space to feel fully human. You may be navigating trauma, life transitions, or relationship shifts—alone, with partners, or as a family. You want to feel more grounded, authentic, and connected to yourself and others. Whatever brings you here, I offer a space where you can slow down, be seen, and move toward what matters most to you.
