approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe healing happens in community, and I understand the therapeutic space to be a community of its own—one where we imagine and develop new ways of moving through the world with greater authenticity, embodiment, and self-compassion. You are the expert on your experience. Together, I hope we can create a space for you to explore life’s challenges and cultivate tools to help you live more fully—whatever that looks like for you. My role is to remind you of your innate capacity for living a life that aligns with your hope and joy and to help you navigate life’s complexities with curiosity and care. My commitment is my authenticity, accountability, and embodied presence—meeting you where you are and heading with you toward where you want to be.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I offer therapy grounded in experiential, narrative, somatic, and systemic approaches. I affirm LGBTQIA+ identities, non-monogamy, and kink. I'm passionate about supporting blended families, survivors of trauma, and those navigating loss, abortion, or major transitions—with warmth, curiosity, and cultural humility.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: I’m a graduate trainee in Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy at Lewis & Clark College, where I’ve developed a collaborative approach grounded in experiential and narrative practices. With a background in Women’s Studies and experience supporting families and individuals in nonprofit settings, I bring curiosity, warmth, and a deep respect for each client's unique story and healing capacity.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: My work centers on supporting clients as they move toward deeper self-understanding, alignment, and growth. I help individuals, partners, and families identify patterns that no longer serve them, explore their values, and build the emotional tools needed to live with greater authenticity and intention. I see personal growth as a lifelong process—and therapy as a space where meaningful transformation can unfold through curiosity, connection, and care.

name: Dana McPherson-Deutsch
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I love what I do, and feel like I am exactly where I am meant to be. It is a privilege to work with my clients.
ideal_client: Whether you're feeling stuck, overwhelmed, or ready for something to shift, I’m here to help. I offer anxiety therapy, grief counseling, and support through life transitions in a way that’s grounded, compassionate, and tailored to your needs. My goal is to create a space where you feel seen, supported, and empowered to move toward the life you want—with clarity, confidence, and care. I offer in-person therapy in Portland and telehealth throughout Oregon and California, making it easier to acces

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In practice, I like to "meet you where you are", tailoring our sessions and treatment plan to meet your unique and specific needs. Taking the first step to seeking a more fulfilling and happier life- whether it's through improving relationships, getting "unstuck", or resolving issues from the past- takes courage and I have a lot of respect for that. I am here to support you in the process of finding a better way to be.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I am originally from the Midwest and have my undergrad degree from Wayne State University in Detroit. I got my BFA at Wayne State and worked as an artist and designer for years. In 2003, my first husband and I moved to Southern California where I ended up living for 20 years. In that time I moved away from design and into personal training, working exclusively with women to help them find their strength and be their best selves. After years of working in this field I realized that what I was really interested in was talking with my clients, helping them find solutions to the things in life that weren’t working for them. I decided to go back to school to pursue a Master’s degree in Social Work. I finished my degree in 2020, and went to work as a hospital and hospice social worker. After a few years of working in the medical field I decided I wanted to make the shift to Clinical Therapy, which is where I have been ever since.

name: Tamara Iliff
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Counselor and Registered Play Therapist serving children ages 3-10 and adults.
ideal_client: My practice focuses on supporting children who are struggling with anxiety, big emotions, self-esteem and relationship difficulties. I enjoy supporting children and their adults in fostering their feelings of attunement and connectedness with one another. I also enjoy supporting families as they navigate new developmental stages and stressors. In addition to my work with young children, I also provide individual counseling for parents who are caring for their emotional health and wellbeing.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I use play, expressive arts, and talk therapy in my practice with children and adults. My work is grounded in a person-centered approach, meaning that you can expect our work together to be relationally focused, collaborative and guided by your individual needs. I believe that understanding, self-compassion, and genuineness are foundational to healing and growth. My background includes extensive training in Child Centered Play Therapy, which is a developmentally responsive and relationally-based counseling intervention for young children who experiencing social, emotional, or behavioral challenges. I also enjoy supporting caregivers in their relationships with their children using Child Parent Relationship Therapy. I have a master's degree in Counseling and Development from Texas Woman's University and a doctorate degree in Counseling from the University of North Texas, where I specialized in play therapy and assessment of children.

name: Jessica Barnese
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I guide mindful, somatic exploration to help people shift beliefs, embrace change, and live in authentic alignment with their true selves.
ideal_client: I work with clients in a direct, down to earth way, focusing on emotional, relational, and mind-body connections. I respect each person’s individuality, shaped by their trauma and resilience, and provide both clear perspective and an embodied path toward a more integrated sense of self. My approach addresses attachment wounds, trauma, self-worth struggles, disconnection from instincts, grief, sexual embodiment, and challenges forming trust in relationship.

approaches.What I Specialize In: My work mainly draws on the Hakomi Method, in which clients are guided to slow down and tune into their present-moment experience so we can move beyond just the story and truly work with what arises as they relive it. We explore the deeply held belief structures that shape how current challenges are felt and understood and update outdated patterns to create newer, more aligned perspectives. I work with many clients who need support moving through life transitions, developmental trauma, and relational trauma. I deeply value working with female bodied people in the perimenopausal to postmenopausal stages of life, helping them uncover their innate wisdom during this powerful time. I also enjoy working with fellow therapists curious about somatic approaches, as they often find this work deeply enriching for their personal growth and professional practice.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In our work together, it is my goal to help you access the parts of yourself that are striving to come forward so that you can live a more satisfying and fulfilling life. I do not work to define what is right for you, but rather observe and collaborate with you to find the direction your own individual life force is moving you. My approach is based in the integration of mindfulness and somatic awareness to help heal past wounds, foster emotional and mental clarity, and cultivate deeper relationships. I use mindfulness to uncover old patterns and core beliefs, and use the therapeutic relationship to address relational and attachment issues in real time. The goal of our work together is to help you develop a secure sense of self and feel access to clear choice in your life, as well as the ability to form healthy relationships in ways that fit for you.

name: Carly Hernandez Kadell
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I have found my niche as an OCD and AuDHD specialist. I can help you explore neurodivergence, anxiety, and anything in between.
ideal_client: Hello. I am so glad you found me. If you find yourself at a crossroad in life, wondering where to go next, or how to move forward, I am here to help guide you.

approaches.How I Can Help You: A lot can happen in our work. Together we will review your current challenges, try to give them names, and talk about what the best option to move forward might be for you. My job here is to walk with you while we both figure this out. I often support my clients in deciding whether medications should be started, paused, or stopped entirely. I have a rich experience treating a wide variety of mental health issues with special expertise in the comingling between addiction and trauma, and geriatric psychiatry, to name a few. In 2021, I opened my private practice in order to expand my reach in offering deep, therapeutic engagement via telehealth. Since opening my practice, I have found joy in advancing my specialties further. In particular I am passionate about exploring neurodivergence including AuDHD, as well as identifying and treating OCD.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe one of the bravest things a person can do is open themselves to the possibility of change. I offer a compassionate, nonjudgmental space where there is no rush to find the end. I believe the journey is where we find growth. I am happy to explore that potential with you- with medications or in the therapy room.

name: Patience McGinnis
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: When life feels overwhelming or directionless, therapy can help you reconnect with clarity, confidence, and strength.
ideal_client: If you’re looking for a psychologist in Oregon or Washington who offers compassionate, culturally informed, and evidence-based therapy, I’m here to support you. Whether you're a college student navigating change, a young adult coping with anxiety, or someone seeking assessment for ADHD—I offer individual therapy and assessment services in-person in Portland, and via telehealth across Oregon and Washington. Let’s work together to create a plan that fosters clarity, connection, and resilience.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapy approach is tailored to each individual’s needs with an emphasis on honoring every person’s unique cultural identity. You deserve a space where your full self is welcomed and supported. Together, we’ll define your goals, strengthen your internal resources, and chart a path toward greater well-being and fulfillment.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: When I’m not helping my patients achieve a more balanced perspective, you will most likely find me: Reading Running local trails or exploring new hiking routes Backpacking locally and across the country in search of wide-open skies I love outdoor adventures, and nothing recharges me like a weekend backpacking trip in the beautiful Pacific Northwest!

name: Ryn Rising
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Queer, Trans, and neurodivergent folks deserve affirming care from counselors with lived experience.
ideal_client: I provide individual and relational counseling to adults from variety of backgrounds. So far, my clients tend to be trans, queer, autistic, neurodivergent, polyamorous or in non-traditional relationship, and families of queer and trans folks. I have experience working with trauma, grief, life transitions, gender/sexuality transitions, low self esteem, relational conflicts, chronic pain, and ongoing racism.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer a tailored approach to fit your unique needs and framework. Sessions typically involve Socratic questioning, mindfulness exercises, and creative interventions. I tend to encourage clients to bring attention to their bodies and explore how the body is responding to what we are talking about, as I believe the mind/body connection is imperative for regulation and growth. One of many ways I provide a affirming space is encouraging clients to bring their comfort items, stimming equipment, and to move their bodies in session. I attempt to minimize unbalanced power dynamics inherent in the therapeutic relationship by seeking feedback from clients on an ongoing basis. So far, clients have told me that my approach is warm, authentic, and direct.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a counselor because of my own lived experience as a client. Overall, I thought the field lacked authenticity, empathy, and understanding that the systems are not built for most people. What was most helpful for me and what encouraged me to join the field was a therapeutic relationship that was truly transformational. I became a counselor because I want to support people through their own transformations, no matter what that may look like. I became a counselor because I wanted to change the systems within the system.

name: Emily Warner
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Welcome! I am so glad you are here :) I am currently accepting Telehealth clients. I am happy to help you on your mental health journey.
ideal_client: Counseling is for everyone. Whether processing the past, finding contentment in the present, or looking at goals towards the future - I am so proud of you. I specialize in working with adolescents and young adults, exploring what it is to be in the quarter life stage and how to become your own person. From just entering high school to graduating from your grad degree program, or navigating independence - there is so much to process in our emerging adulthood. You are worth listening to.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My approach to counseling is integrative in nature. I believe that every individual is unique, and I love to match my style to the client rather than vice versa. I am rooted in person-centered theory, believing that the client is the expert on their own lives and healing can occur through empathy, congruence, and unconditional positive regard. I also integrate internal family systems, interpersonal theory, and expressive arts practices into my practice. Though my services are virtual there are still so many ways to integrate creativity into our healing and mental health journey. I have experience working with folks through life transitions, schooling, and differentiating their identities in emerging adulthood as well - and can bring a solution focused and/or identity exploration lens to the table. I am here to meet you where you are at, and help you achieve your goals and recognize the power you hold.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am from the PNW, having lived in Vancouver, Seattle, and Portland. I received my Master’s in counseling from Portland State University. My areas of focus while training to become a counselor were adolescence and suicide prevention. I previously worked for the Seattle Crisis Clinic as a teen suicide prevention specialist. I worked at Aloha High School as a school counselor for 2 years, providing counseling to students and families. In my free time I am also a licensed yoga teacher, and value the connection between body and mind. I have worked with theater nonprofits and public schools for a majority of my life - and have experience with the LGBTQ community. I believe in lifelong learning, and putting in active work to be an ally to by queer and BIPOC friends and community members. It is so much more than just a statement, it is a commitment to help create change. I also have a cat and love talking about pets!

name: Johanna Courtleigh
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Healing is the process of recovering the true self, so we can begin to live authentically and thrive. Moving into self-love, ease and peace.
ideal_client: Please see my web site, www.jcourtleigh.com, for more information about me and my work.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Together we explore the beliefs and patterns that hinder you from living fully, that keep you ‘safe’ and separate from self and others, and from fully experiencing, expressing and enjoying your unique self. As you become aware of and reclaim the parts of yourself that you have repressed, numbed or disowned, you are able to move toward a deeper sense of self-love, awareness, personal empowerment, ease and integrity--internally, and in your relationships with others. This allows for a deeper sense of emotional, mental, physical and spiritual security and integration; the experience of Coming Home to your Self.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (#C1612) and Hypnotherapist. I have been in private practice since 1991, and working in the helping professions for over thirty-five years. I have had a broad and varied background working with: • Depression • Low Self-esteem • Relationship Problems • Adult Children of Alcoholics • Eating Disorders • Co-dependence • Fertility • Stress management • Transitions • Grief and Loss • Separation and Divorce • Spiritual issues • General Life Confusion Beyond my formal therapeutic training, I have also trained in the Regression work of Dr. Brian Weiss, which is now the primary focus of my practice. This work is deep, powerful, fascinating and transformative.

specialities.name: Past Life Regression
specialities.description: I believe we are far more complex and mysterious than we can imagine. Most of the planet believes in reincarnation. Often problems and relationship dynamics seem to transcend present time. I've had the privilege of studying with Dr. Brian Weiss. Regression work can facilitate deep, powerful transformation, allowing patterns and conflicts to quickly resolve. Insurance is not accepted for these sessions.

specialities.name: Interpersonal
specialities.description: The relationship between client and therapist is an important part of the therapy. In that relationship, the therapist can model what a healthy relationship can sound, feel and look like--supporting the client to become more gentle, supportive and compassionate internally, toward themselves. This is a kind of re-parenting that assist the client in greater self-kindness, care, healing and growth.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Our thinking impacts everything! Our sense of self. How we relate to the world. What we allow, and what we believe we deserve. Much of what we've learned, and continue to repeat to ourselves, actually isn't true. We want to make our mind an ally, not an adversary. As we develop a healthier relationship with our own mind, our stress reduces, our self-esteem grows and life becomes easier.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: We are far more vast, complex and beautiful than our human minds can fathom. In my decades of working with people, I have found that a spiritual foundation based in curiosity and reverence allow for deeper healing and transformation. As we meet the mystery of our existence, and call in an awareness of something Higher, our lives expand in beauty, patience, understanding and greater peace.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: We come in as joy. Watch any toddler. But over time, we learn shame, inadequacy and comparison. We feel lesser-than, which undermines our sense of self-worth, worthiness and happiness. The mind turns on itself, and we plummet. What we were taught wasn't true! Therapy helps you recover your true self, and reclaim the enjoyment and sense of well-being that is your birthright!

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Life is full of losses. Most of us were trained to suppress our feelings and get over it. The people who taught us were folks who couldn't manage their own feelings. Grief in the face of loss is normal and deeply human. There's no right way or timeline to process our feelings. Therapy offers support so you can both feel, and learn to care for yourself in these deeply human, challenging times.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Everything is frequency. Ideally, our minds and bodies are a harmonious place for us to reside in. However, for many of us, stress has become an energetic habitual pattern. Healing is the process of learning how to bring compassion to our suffering, and cultivating techniques for self-soothing, so we can calm and nurture ourselves in times of stress--thus lessening anxiety, distress, fear.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Being human can be a daunting assignment. It's easy to fall into thinking of hopelessness and despair. We are raised with impossible expectations and a corresponding sense of inadequacy. How to manage? We must learn how to value, take care of and think kindly to ourselves, and make choices that support our highest well-being. To be our own ally instead of a cruel adversary.

name: Kestrel Fae Tippie
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I bring fierce compassion, determined courage, and a deep fascination for human tenderness and weirdness. Let's heal, grow, and thrive.
ideal_client: I am here to support the fixers, the doers, the helpers, the leaders, the creatives, the neurodivergent. If you’ve landed here, and you’re my people, you likely care and feel and think deeply, you are tending to and holding so very much. If you're struggling with trauma, burnout, dysregulation, stress, anxiety, depression, difficulty with relationships, or healthy boundaries, I can help. I know that can shift for you and transform into wellbeing.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I can help you: Heal stuck trauma that keeps you feeling distressed, shut down, anxious, isolated, and fragmented. Use therapy as a laboratory to re-pattern, experiment with, and integrate new ways of being. Experience your body as a safe refuge and wise communicator. Connect to Nature as a supportive refuge that cares for you. Increase creative access to joy, play, and passion. Find belonging with your people and build community. Nurture healthy relationships where you feel safe, cherished, held, and seen. Live your gifts and soul essence to bring what is needed into the world. Relish contentment, fulfillment, satisfaction, ease, and calm. Be available and present to enjoy the juice and goodness of life.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I have journeyed myself many times down this path, and supported many others. I will guide and accompany you with a compass to navigate by, a map of the territory we’re wading through, and a toolbox of skills and resources. We will create a transformative container in which you feel connected, supported, anchored, seen, and encouraged to practice and embody new ways of being. I know and trust completely that the life you long for is also longing for you and reaching back towards you. You can absolutely move through trauma and overwhelm to thriving. Let's get you rooted in deep belonging with life and connection with your people, relishing contentment and fulfillment, acting from your values of what matters most, and embodying your gifts for this world. That is so possible for you. If you can't access that right now, I'll hold it until you can see and trust it for yourself. Welcome. Your presence is a blessing and you are worthy of enjoying life and thriving. Let's journey together.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: If realizations alone would've solved your problems, you probably would've gotten there already- but that doesn't really work for trauma. That's why I work experientially, based in the body, and in alliance with nature. With drama therapy and role play we can embody, un-do, and re-wire past trauma and pain, and practice new ways of being. Through expressive modalities like sand tray and creative arts, you can access stuck material and liberate it in service of self-expression and healing.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: From a somatic foundation of working mindfully and dropping into the body, you can get to the heart of what is stuck to process and transform it. Somatics helps you to learn how to relate to your body as a safe refuge, a reliable communicator of your feelings and needs, and a wisdom keeper that can guide you.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: Ecotherapy can be incorporated via telehealth, or in sessions outdoors that invite in nature's input as a co-therapist to support your process. Relationship with nature is so absent in our everyday lives, so reconnecting can nourish deep wells within us that were in need and restore a sense of resilience and deep belonging. Time and time again, in outdoor sessions, I have seen nature attunes to us and respond to our process, emotions, and needs in astounding ways to offer support and healing.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR taps directly into the nervous system for re-wiring and reprocessing traumatic material, so you do not have to re-live overwhelming memories, go through flashbacks, get flooded, or even be able to access content verbally and talk through it in order to heal. EMDR can also help by "installing" new resourcing capacities or supports and re-wiring all kinds of patterns, beliefs, and behaviors.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Play is the natural language of children, and the best way to join your child in their world. I use play therapy to understand your child and what it is like to be them, help them process difficult or painful past experiences, try on new ways of interacting, and learn different healthier ways to get their needs met and relate to others. I involve caregivers extensively, to coach and support you with new skills, and bring you into occassional sessions to work alongside myself with your child.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: The worst things you have gone through in your life do not define you. You do not have to struggle with them forever. I work with clients somatically and with EMDR to transform the deepest roots of trauma in your body and nervous system- places that cognitive based talk therapy and realizations cannot reach. I'll teach you practical body based tools you can use every day to feel calm, centered, grounded, alive, safe, and free in your whole being.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Life as a neurodivergent person is its own special form of challenge and trauma. It's hard when you have never gotten the particular kind of support you need, with a lifetime of dealing with ableism without realizing that was a core part of your challenges, and feeling like 'why can't I just do the thing?!'. I specialize in ADHD'ers and Autistic folks like myself who need to work with someone with lived experience who understands these layers and works from a neurodivergent-affirming lens.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: I specialize in therapy for therapists, caregivers and helpers- we need our own place of support where we can drop our masks, our holding presence and emotional labor for others. You deserve a refuge where you can get really excellent skilled support, where you don't have to lead or function for anyone else, where someone else will hold your experience with wisdom and compassion. Where someone will help you see your patterns so you can make different choices that return you to life and vitality.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: I can help you learn how to stay anchored and connected to yourself and your own authentic needs and desires. From that place, we can figure out the healthy boundaries for your life and relationships that, as Prentice Hemphill says, "are the distance at which I can love you and me simultaneously". We will help you carve out a space to know yourself, so you can interact with others from freedom and peace, and control the only thing there is to control- your choices and your agency and your life.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: The dominant culture we are surrounded by and must survive within is destructive and exploitative and deeply unjust. It is corrosive to the soul and to the fabric of our belonging to each other and to Life. It is the cause of much of our suffering. You are not broken if you are struggling within it. I bring a liberatory, anti-oppressive, decolonial lens to therapy as a space where we unpack the influence of these forces and find life giving ways of navigating and dismantling them.

name: Brandy Tidwell
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Offering holistic, trauma informed, and culturally responsive psychological services for adults throughout Oregon and Washington
ideal_client: I specialize in complex trauma and PTSD, LGBTQIA+ and women’s health, somatic and mindfulness-based therapies, and psychedelic harm reduction and integration. I welcome clients of all backgrounds and identities, though I work best with women, queer, and gender expansive trauma survivors who are seeking to heal their relationship with their body.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe we each have a fundamental need to be seen, valued, and accepted for exactly who we are. My primary goal as a therapist is to provide a safe and affirming relationship where we can collaboratively explore who you are, how you came to be, and who you wish to become as we work together toward your goals. I practice therapy from a holistic and systemic perspective, taking into account the multitude of ways your physical, psychological, and relational health interact and inform one another. In session this might look like processing emotions through mindfulness and somatic exercises, practicing skills for regulating your nervous system, getting curious about your attachment style, learning to communicate your needs and boundaries, examining your belief systems, learning to relate with yourself more compassionately, and exploring ways to live in alignment with your values.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I’m a white, queer, cisgender woman. I grew up in a highly conservative and homogenous culture where I struggled to find a sense of belonging, which taught me the importance of diversity and inclusion, influencing my path toward becoming a psychologist and passion for working with marginalized communities. It is among my highest values to honor and celebrate diversity in all forms. I hold anti-capitalist, anti-imperialist, and anti-racist values. I work to educate myself about various cultural backgrounds while also meeting each client with openness and humility to learn about their unique experience and expression of their identities. I strive to be aware of my privilege and remain open to feedback about my impact in the world. I’m committed to the lifelong process of deconstructing systems of oppression within and around me and hope to contribute toward a more liberated, inclusive, and just world for all beings everywhere.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: I approach therapy from a theoretically integrative lens, building on a foundation of intersectional feminism, systems theory, interpersonal neurobiology, and trauma-informed care. I integrate a variety of evidence-based models tailored to each client’s concerns, background, and preferences. I have specialized training in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Dialectical Behavior Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Cognitive Processing Therapy, Prolonged Exposure, and Emotion Focused Therapy.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Our bodies and minds are inextricably interconnected. Yet, so many of us learn to disconnect from our bodies messages as a survival strategy. Somatic therapies harness the innate wisdom and healing intelligence of our bodies. They help us reconnect with our bodies’ messages, learn to honor our needs, reclaim our bodily autonomy, and tune into our deepest truths, values, and purpose. I’m a registered yoga instructor (RYT-200) certified in the Trauma Conscious Yoga Method (TCYM) of psychotherapy.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness is a practice of intentionally bringing awareness to our present moment experience with an attitude of non-judgment. It originated within traditions such as Buddhism, Hinduism, Yoga, Taoism, and Jainism and was later brought to the West by Asian immigrants. Mindfulness has increasingly been incorporated into healthcare as an evidenced-based approach to working with many health concerns. I value honoring the cultural roots of mindfulness and adapt mindfulness offerings to each client.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Traumatic experiences threaten our sense of safety and overwhelm our ability to cope, resulting in lasting adverse effects on physical, mental, emotional, social, and spiritual well-being. Many circumstances can be experienced as traumatic, and PTSD is only one of many possible outcomes. While I work with most trauma-related difficulties, I specialize in complex and interpersonal traumas, such as childhood abuse and neglect, sexual assault, intimate partner violence, and identity-based traumas.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I recognize the many challenges faced by queer people currently and historically and strive to provide inclusive and affirming mental health services that celebrate queer community and each person’s unique experience and expression of their identities. In addition to therapy, I offer brief assessment and referral letters consistent with WPATH guidelines for trans and gender expansive people seeking gender affirming medical services such as surgery or hormone therapy.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I understand how patriarchy and misogyny deeply impact women’s health and harm our communities as a whole, and I seek to support and empower women in the pursuit of equity and liberation. Throughout my career, I have sought specialized training in women’s health and advocacy, such as during my time at the Washington Corrections Center for Women and the Women and Gender Diverse Specialty Clinic at the Portland VA Medical Center.

name: Joey Tomlinson
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: "Rarely, if ever, are any of us healed in isolation. Healing is an act of communion." ~bell hooks
ideal_client: I work with individuals, couples and adult families who experience trauma, anxiety, depression, identity or life transitions, and relationship struggle. Many of the people I work with are queer, neurodivergent, non-monogamous, disabled or chronically ill. I take a liberatory, community oriented approach to therapy and will work with you to co-create a container that supports your innate capacity for healing, growth and connection.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I draw from narrative therapy and humanism in my work. Narrative therapy is all about your stories: the ones you’ve been told, and the ones that are yours to tell. I’ll work with you to understand and reimagine your stories, where they come from, what they mean, and what new stories might be possible. Humanism is about embracing you as a whole, messy person. We’ll explore different parts of you that might be in conflict with each other, might be hurt, or might be unseen. We’ll welcome all of these parts as valid and valuable components of your humanity. I’ll invite you to engage somatically, emotionally and relationally with feelings that come up and I’ll support you through the tender process of being with your authentic self.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that our emotional and relational wellbeing is deeply entwined with our communities and social systems, and I know that most suffering in this world is a product of systemic oppression. My goal as a therapist is to support you as an individual while also building our collective capacity to resist oppression and cultivate liberation for all people. I draw from lineages and theories of abolitionism, disability justice, queer feminism and other resistance movements in this work. I’m genderqueer, non-monogamous, live with chronic illness, and love being outdoors and growing food. In both life and work, I’m guided by values of liberation and collective care.

name: Sarabeth Casey, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello and welcome! I enjoy working with kids/teens, and offer them a safe place to talk, explore, and feel understood.
ideal_client: I've always loved listening to other people's stories and helping them to make sense of life events. I offer a patient and empathetic approach, practical interventions, and often incorporate play, art, and humor into sessions. While I have experience working with a range of ages, genders, and challenges, I especially enjoy working with kiddos who struggle with anxiety and making/maintaining social connections.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Change is hard. Talking about feelings can be hard. It is important to me that the therapy environment feels supportive and comfortable, and that clients feel heard and understood. My therapeutic approach is relational and collaborative. I tend to utilize cognitive behavioral therapy, mindfulness, and strengths-based approaches, along with psychoeducation for parents/natural supports. I may guide you/your kiddo to integrate other resources in the community to balance social-emotional-physical health.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I graduated from Lewis and Clark College in 2006 with my Master's degree and an emphasis in working with children, adolescents, and families. I became licensed in 2009. As a therapist, I've worked with youth in residential treatment centers, outpatient clinics, in the community providing crisis intervention, schools, and in a partial hospital day treatment program specializing in treatment of eating disorders. I have completed a certificate program through PSU for therapy with adoptive and foster families. I use a trauma-informed framework to gently gather information and help a client gain insight about how past experiences impact current feelings and behaviors. In my spare time, I volunteer with Guide Dogs for the Blind and adopted a "career change" pup, Cookie, now a certified therapy dog. She occasionally makes an appearance in sessions! I also enjoy running, reading, soccer, and art.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I have several years experience working at as an individual, group, and family therapist in an eating disorder specific clinic with adolescents and their supports. I make efforts to collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, including PCPs and dietitians.

specialities.name: Adoption Issues
specialities.description: I completed the Adoptive & Foster Family post-graduate certificate program, a collaboration between DHS and PSU, in 2018. More info can be found: https://www.orparc.org/

name: Grace Provost
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Welcome, I am grateful you are here.
ideal_client: Do you feel misunderstood or alone in your interactions, and find that arguments or conversations with others often leave you feeling confused or upset? Do you experience chronic pain, stress, or overwhelm, and often feel on edge or have racing thoughts? Do you struggle with concentration, overthinking, or analyzing your interactions with others afterward? Do you feel constantly on the edge of burnout, or like there's no escape from the daily monotony of being an adult?

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I create a safe and open space to explore the complexities of you, to help you tease apart your past and present to release what no longer serves you. I will help you step into presence and authenticity in your life, to find security and peace in your body. I combine knowledge in neurobiology, somatic work, IFS and EMDR. I draw from many modalities and enjoy collaborating with individuals to find a treatment plan that works best for their needs. If this resonates with you, please reach out for a free consultation to see if we are a good fit. I specialize in treating trauma, chronic pain/illness, codependency, anxiety, depression and neurodivergence. I work with adults of all ages, children ages 11+ on a case-by-case basis, and offer parent coaching.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I value social justice, radical love for all, self compassion, self attunement, somatic work, trauma work, evidence based modalities, intuition, expansiveness, connection with nature, slowing down, being strong and vulnerable and brave and scared all at the same time. I value all parts of everyone- all of our anxieties and fears and sadnesses, I value our inner children, our hopes and dreams, I value the little you that said "when I grow up I want to be a ___!"

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I combine EMDR and parts work/IFS as well as somatic work to help you find your center and draw from your strengths to engage in the untangling of memories that are confusing, sad, hurtful, and hard. Together we weave together your story that makes sense to you, empowers you and allows you to grow through everything you have been through.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I utilize parts work and IFS to explore anxiety and depression as parts of you that aim to protect you from feeling deeper feelings. This is a holistic and gentle approach that is evidence based and works well with a combination of thought based approaches and trauma work, if needed.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I utilize somatic approaches and trauma modalities to explore deeper sources of pain with you. I teach you to find safety in your body, even if sometimes it doesn't feel like home.

name: Joyce Yuan
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Licensed psychologist offering individual and couples therapy to those seeking meaningful change and self-understanding.
ideal_client: Adult clients of all age-ranges, genders, ethnicities, and cultural backgrounds are welcome. I ask only that you be curious about yourself and willing to explore new ways of understanding and approaching your problems. Common conditions I treat include depression, anxiety, trauma, and relationships problems. In recent years, I have worked extensively with young professionals, graduate and college students, and military veterans.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My goal in providing psychotherapy is to help people alleviate their suffering, improve their relationships, and understand themselves better. I believe all people have positive potential that can sometimes be stifled and find it rewarding to help others work through their obstacles. I have been trained in a wide range of theoretical approaches (including psychodynamic and cognitive-behavioral). I integrate insight-oriented and problem-solving techniques to best serve my clients' individual needs. I believe psychotherapy is a collaborative process by which thoughts and experiences are explored in a safe setting with a trained therapist. In order to help you resolve your problems and achieve your goals, it may be helpful to examine past life events that have brought you to this point, in addition to developing new coping skills and perspectives.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In addition to my private practice, I have worked at VA hospitals, where I provided psychotherapy to military veterans of all eras. I completed my undergraduate studies at Amherst College and my graduate training at the University of California, Berkeley. I have trained and worked at well-known medical institutions in Portland, New York City, and the San Francisco Bay Area. I also have a background in psychological research, studying emotional functioning in various clinical disorders.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: Psychodynamic therapy assumes thoughts, feelings, and motivations aren't always fully accessible to conscious awareness. However, behaviors and relationships can still be influenced by unconscious forces, sometimes in problematic ways. By exploring patterns of behavior and experiences that have shaped the way you think and feel, you can gain insight into what drives you and start making conscious changes.

specialities.name: Interpersonal
specialities.description: Interpersonal psychotherapy emphasizes the transformative power of relationships--both those you have with family, friends, and colleagues and that which you have with your therapist. This therapy focuses on developing corrective experiences, in which you can practice relating to people in new ways and start healing from damage done in previous relationships.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT is a popular evidence-based therapy that focuses on the relationship among thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. In this therapy, you will learn how to evaluate and challenge thoughts that give rise to negative feelings and behaviors. You will also learn how to change problematic behaviors by gradually exposing yourself to triggering situations while practicing new coping strategies.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is the experience of persistent sad mood and loss of interest in enjoyable activities. It can manifest in hopeless, self-critical thoughts, social isolation, and changes in sleep and appetite. Depression can occur in relation to a variety of life stressors (e.g., loss, illness, trauma). I have had success treating depression with cognitive-behavioral and insight-oriented techniques.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is the unpleasant experience of excessive worry, fear, and stress that can interfere with daily activities and your ability to rest/relax. Anxiety can manifest in repetitive thoughts and acute physical symptoms, such as heart-racing and difficulty breathing. I have had success treating anxiety with a combination of relaxation, problem-solving, and graded exposure exercises.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Through my work at veterans hospitals, I have gained experience at treating post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Symptoms of PTSD include unwanted memories of trauma, hypervigilance, and avoidance of perceived threats. Treatment can involve processing feelings about the past trauma, understanding how trauma affects your current thinking and behavior, and developing new ways to feel safe and empowered.

name: Daniela Blum
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I specialize in women's mental health with a strong focus on maternal emotional well-being.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I specialize in women's mental health with a strong focus on maternal emotional well-being. I have expertise in working with the perinatal population as well as high risk pregnancy, chronic illness, and neurodiversity. I am passionate about working with parents who are navigating complex children's needs. My work is relationship based, attachment theory informed, and I am trained in The Circle of Security. I am pursuing my PMHC through Postpartum Support International. I see patients in-person only at my office in SE Portland; my style is approachable, collaborative and non-judgmental.

name: Kimberly Noall
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer a safe place to explore difficult feelings, help open up new paths on your journey and move towards feeling better.
ideal_client: Does anxiety show up at the worst time? Feeling stuck in your negative relationship or communication cycles? I want to help you explore anxious thoughts that get in your way of the things you want and help you get your needs met. I offer a nonjudgmental, relaxed environment where you can discover and make connections between patterns of behavior and anxiety. Together we will get to know how "parts" of you show up and work towards empowering the Wise Adult in you to have a balanced life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The world is changing quickly and we are definitely feeling the impact. Feelings of being stuck, anxious, frustrated and depressed can be difficult to navigate. Finding time to process your feelings and repairing ruptures in your life and relationships may feel more stressful now. I want to help. I am curious about your world, how you experience it, how you are connected to it, and your desire to make positive change. We will work together to develop and refine goals that meet your needs and values. We will collaborate to identify and connect to your strengths and support systems, and give you tools to cope and change barriers in achieving peace of mind. My experience includes working with adults struggling with anxiety, negative communication patterns, relational and intimacy issues, domestic violence, divorce and parenting issues. I draw from a variety of evidence-based therapeutic models. My desire is to help you process the anxiety and depression that accompanies feeling stuck and

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my Master’s degree in Couples, Marriage, and Family Counseling from Portland State University. I employ my training in Emotion Focused Therapy for Couples, Family Systems, and the Gottman Method in my approach to the counseling process, as well as other person-centered and existential therapeutic interventions. In addition to couples work, I have a background in working with individuals and families adjusting to divorce, trauma, and co-­‐parenting issues. I also have ten years experience of crisis counseling with victims of domestic violence and four years of supervising counseling interns in a learning clinic.

name: Jason Jones
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: My style is pragmatic, conversational, genuine, and sometimes I interject my humor too!
ideal_client: If you’re navigating trauma, anxiety, identity exploration, or just feeling stuck, I’m here to walk alongside you. My approach is grounded, collaborative, and tailored to your individual needs—blending evidence-based therapies with compassion, curiosity, and authenticity. Whether you're seeking trauma-focused therapy, LGBTQIA+ affirming care, or support with anxiety and life transitions, we'll work together to create meaningful change at a pace that feels right for you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My decision to become a psychologist stems from personal and family experiences that revealed just how deeply depression, anxiety, and trauma can impact a life. Those early experiences fueled a passion in me to help others navigate their own pain, discover a sense of relief, and feel more empowered to live authentically. My ultimate goal is to create a compassionate and collaborative space where you feel comfortable and able to share your true self.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I was raised in the Midwest by a family of autoworkers before moving to the West Coast, where I’ve spent the past 25 years. I love living close to the mountains and rivers—it’s a perfect fit for my love of the outdoors. When I’m not working, you’ll likely find me: Singing karaoke or making jokes with friends Lifting weights or walking my dog Camping under the stars or exploring nature trails Soaking up everything the Pacific Northwest has to offer

name: Erica Ochsenreither
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer empathetic and trauma-informed telehealth sessions. Here to support you in navigating life's highs and lows with care and support!
ideal_client: I serve those struggling with depression, anxiety, navigating the effects of acute and/or complex trauma, those seeking to deepen their relationship with their body, and those desiring to change the way they show up in relationships.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I am a mental health counselor specializing in art therapy. I practice from an integrated model that combines expressive arts, somatic, trauma-informed, Internal Family Systems, Polyvagal, and attachment approaches. I draw upon these modalities and theories to craft an individualized and holistic approach. Additionally, I am trained in EMDR. What this can look/feel like in session is focusing on exploring and holding space for all parts of you, guiding you to become curious about what is happening in your body, offering resources to establish more safety, safely approaching what feels overwhelming, and reclaiming your wholeness.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am passionate about providing a warm, collaborative, empathetic space with opportunity for embodied healing. I will support you in weaving together thoughts, feelings, sensations, and beliefs in a safe and supportive relationship, deepening your awareness and, at times, challenging you toward your potential. Come as you are, to a soft place to land, where you can feel wholeheartedly human. I am always honored when folks resonate enough with my profile to want to speak with me. If you would like to learn more about what therapy might look like or how I can support you, please contact me via phone or email. I look forward to connecting with you and honor the opportunity to walk alongside you through this journey.

name: Dr. Sarah Kendrick
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Innovative therapy to gently, rapidly, & effectively restore safety, peace, confidence, & connection on the parenting journey.
ideal_client: I help liberate parents from the echoes of trauma, the squeeze of daily stressors, the mayhem of a dysregulated nervous system, the crushing weight of impossible expectations, and the embodied beliefs that keep them feeling powerless, hurting, or stuck. Whether wearily navigating pregnancy, postpartum, raising littles, midlife awakening, or facing unique challenges of parenting as therapists or veterans, please know there is a safe, healing, & less lonely way through. I’ll walk with you.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I’ve helped families cultivate post-traumatic growth, compassion, safety, connection, & resilience since 2002. I offer concierge-level support & carefully curated, accessible. short-term services with lasting transformation. I provide Therapy Intensives for rapid healing & resilience, Accelerated Resolution Therapy to transform sensations of suffering, Safe & Sound Listening Program for a calm, connected nervous system, Birth-Mapping for confident, safe, meaningful birth, and Postpartum & Parenting Support for compassionate grit to bear hard shit. My approach is rooted in a unique blend of clinical expertise and deep, personal understanding of the complexities of parenthood. I am a Certified Clinical Trauma Specialist (CCTS), Perinatal Mental Health provider (PMH-C), Master Accelerated Resolution Therapy provider, Meditation & Mindfulness teacher, Safe & Sound Protocol provider, and Childbirth Educator and bring highly specialized knowledge to guide clients from striving to thriving.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: “If we have no peace, it is because we have forgotten that we belong to each other” (Agnes Gonxha Bojaxhiu). At its heart, Toward Freedom is about reminding you that you’re not alone, crazy, broken, or disordered. That your symptoms make perfect sense and will change once you don’t need them anymore. That you are innately good, already whole, and worthy of belonging. That there’s no room for shame or time for hiding. That while our surroundings are increasingly unsafe or bewildering, we are inherently wired for safety & connection (and even flourishing!) Affective neuroscience offers us simple, gentle, innovative, & profoundly powerful ways to rewire & return to those states right in the middle of the chaos. Safe connection is the compass for all services. Other values include resisting duality, learning continually, affirming embodied wisdom, braving vulnerability, welcoming what is, and embracing ambiguity. Also- to transparency, a healthy dose of dark humor, & absolutely no bullshit

specialities.name: Accelerated Resolution Therapy
specialities.description: ART uses the brain’s natural ability to reprocess distressing images and sensations of suffering. With guided eye movements & visualization, ART rewires experience so we keep the facts but lose the pain. This gentle, effective approach requires no homework, no processing between sessions, & no need to verbalize trauma! Lasting relief occurs in an average of 1-5 sessions and the process is safe, grounding, empowering, and even fun. Clients are bewildered by immense change with so little effort.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I could have spent my whole life talking about trauma instead of moving it through. As a student who stumbled into the field, I was its biggest critic. I wanted evidence that the body mattered. In my most profound relationships now as client or healer, we don't talk a lot & the evidence is right there in the ability to process & release pain without analysis paralysis. I lead folx to learn from their own body how stress shapes the way they walk the world & they let it lead them toward freedom

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: The postpartum period brings pressure to be better than however & whoever we are in the moment. People plan for, mourn, & wearily raise babies fighting the inherent needs, aches, & discomfort of being human. I help folx find their wise & adaptive parts the world has deemed unruly, so they can feel the gorgeous-mess of it all & know that vitality is inherent too. The grasp of depression, anxiety, grief, or fear is not loosened by battle, but by the addition of safety, relationship, & being seen.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Years ago I saw a mom collapse on a stack of perfect-parenting books with shame-filled tears falling onto her baby's head. I hid the books & held them both (& still do that when I can). I'm now a Perinatal Mental Health & Trauma Therapist helping parents navigate depression, anxiety, scary thoughts, rage, shame, & the unbearable weight of impossible expectations. I help folx let go of getting it right so they become safe, seen, & supported on the embodied journey they are so perfectly made for.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: I'm a wounded-healer in the business of inter-generational healing. Folx talk about post-traumatic stress without recognizing the powerful potential of post-traumatic growth within families. Affective neuroscience offers an invaluable picture of how trauma was embedded in ourselves & our loved ones and ALSO of how to integrate & heal it rather than pass it on to our children. I help clients rewire how they show up in world to forge a safer path for raising healthy whole-hearted children.

name: Caitlin Truitt
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Offering trauma-focused therapy for adults.
ideal_client: I offer a safe, accepting space to work through concerns related to grief, PTSD, relationship issues, sexual assault, coercive control, spiritual trauma, and more. My style is warm and respectful, and we will honor your pace as we explore strategies for finding safety in your nervous system. I have experience working with LGBTQ folks and I welcome clients of all backgrounds.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Our bodies and minds are incredibly resourceful at adapting to our environment. When that environment is dangerous, our internal system creates powerful strategies to help us survive. Much of trauma work is about convincing our bodies that it's safe to let go of the survival strategies that are no longer helping us. When we feel safe enough to emerge from survival mode, we can uncover a stunning inner vibrancy and creativity that we never knew we had. My approach focuses on healing trauma using a somatic, relationship-based perspective. In session, I draw on attachment-based/psychodynamic therapies, somatic therapies, mindfulness, internal family systems, and nervous system regulation techniques. I am trained in somatic- and attachment-focused EMDR, which can be applied to childhood or adult trauma. In couples therapy, I also integrate concepts from the Gottman Method, as well as Relational Life Therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Because of the ways systems of oppression proliferate trauma, trauma therapy and anti-oppressive practice are one and the same. I am committed to keeping this idea at the heart of my work as a therapist. Working with LGBTQ folks in a variety of community-based and professional roles has been a meaningful part of my life for the last decade. My practice welcomes and affirms individuals of all sexual orientations, gender identities and representations, body sizes and types, cultural backgrounds, races, ethnicities, religions, spiritualities, and documentation statuses. I am affirming of ENM relationship structures and consensual nontraditional sexual practices.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Traumatic experiences are not processed like other memories. The brain does not assign a "time stamp" to trauma memories like it does to other past experiences, which causes our bodies to operate as if that trauma is still happening. This causes our nervous systems to go haywire and wreaks havoc on our bodies. Somatic approaches, like polyvagal theory, heal trauma by helping us find safety in our bodies, retraining our nervous systems to realize that we are no longer constantly in danger.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) is an evidence-based therapy designed to alleviate the effects of trauma. I am trained in Somatic- and Attachment-Focused EMDR, which can be used to treat both childhood and adult trauma. EMDR integrates neurobiology, somatic theories, attachment theory, and cognitive therapy to target traumatic memories and provide the conditions for the brain to properly reprocess them.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: For both couples and individuals, attachment theory can help uncover the root of relationship patterns. I love it because it can help us better understand our reactions and needs with compassion and gentleness, rather than shaming ourselves with harsh criticisms.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: When we grow up in tumultuous environments, our brains develop adaptations to help us survive. These adaptations become "parts" of ourselves that can stay on overdrive long into our adulthood, sometimes keeping us stuck in old relational patterns. Internal Family Systems is a powerful way to bring curiosity and compassion to these parts. When we offer acceptance and understanding to the parts of ourselves that we have been most critical of, they no longer have the same control over our lives.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: In a therapy setting, my work has focused on clients who've experienced trauma such as sexual assault, childhood abuse, grief/loss, systemic oppression, spiritual trauma, and violence. I believe that the antidote to trauma is safe and supportive connection. To be able to re-connect with others, we need to find safety in our own bodies. In session, I use a collaborative, body-centered approach that centers your self-determination. I am trained somatic- and attachment-focused EMDR therapy.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Past harm/trauma can cause us to operate off of relationship templates we learned from those who harmed us. We can get stuck in these patterns, often not understanding why. Other times, recent trauma can turn the relational equilibrium upside down. When one partner is struggling with the effects of PTSD, the other may have trouble adjusting or knowing how to respond. I work with trauma survivors and partners of trauma survivors to navigate these challenges and strengthen their relationships.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a member of the LGBTQ community, I have a particular passion for working with queer and trans folks. I have a background in LGBTQ community-based work and HIV services work, and anti-oppressive practice is at the heart of my approach. I offer referral letter sessions for trans folks seeking HRT or gender-affirming procedures. In order to mitigate gatekeeping practices, I adhere to the Informed Consent Model and offer a "pay-what-you-can" rate for letter-related sessions.

name: Jake H. Jacobsen
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I have 24+ years of working within the LGBTQ community. I have a specialty with trans/NB life and the process of grief/loss.
ideal_client: Psychotherapy is a collaborative process that begins by exploring the issues you bring into therapy in an environment of openness, and nonjudgemental curiosity. Together, we will work toward strengthening your inner emotional resources, and your ability to begin to make more satisfying life choices for a greater sense of wholeness, and harmony. I work with people of all nationalities, races, religion, sexual orientation and gender identities.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is eclectic including: Psychodynamic Psychotherapy, Attachment theory, Harm Reduction and Creative Arts Therapy. My practice experience includes counseling people with anxiety, PTSD/trauma (AIDS pandemic, 9/11, Covid) depression and other mood disorders, addiction, adult children of alcoholics, neurodivergent adults/youth, sexuality, gender identity (medical and/or social gender transitioning) for teens and adults who identify as transgender or non-binary and those who are questioning their gender identity, LGBTQ family/partners, people living with HIV/AIDS, and other life challenging conditions.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I've been in the LGBTIA+ community since I was a teenager, a main factor that led me into the field of psychology. In the late 1970's luckily I had a therapist that did not pathologize my coming out as queer and that meant the world to me. It meant that I could begin to envision a full life as a queer person in an era when everything I saw on TV, heard at school, or read in the newspaper told me that being queer was a pathology. Today we're in a time of profound socio-political change with a dramatic increase in anti-LGBT+ bills/laws attempting to stop trans youth rights to access healthcare in some states, racism and violence against POC, erasure of black history from education, anti-semitism, banning books, the effects of climate change and fears of rising autocracy. These issues are all interconnected and need to be seen and acknowledged in order to do the work towards the fight for social justice and our civil rights. Addressing these issues in therapy is fundamental for healing.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: In New York I lived through the AIDS pandemic and 9/11 working with people dealing with PTSD. Today we are living through another pandemic with Covid-19, as well as major socio-political upheaval. These events profoundly changed me as a person and as a therapist. Honing my skills in working with people dealing with trauma and loss became a focal point of my training as a therapist. Trauma and loss are often the roots of complicated mental health issues such as PTSD, anxiety and depression.

name: Reid Zweifel
title: Psychiatrist
intro: Dr. Zweifel is a Board certified psychiatrist based in Portland, Oregon. She provides both medication management and psychotherapy.
ideal_client: I treat a wide range of psychiatric conditions and have particular interest in anxiety disorders, depression, bipolar spectrum disorders, trauma, personality disorders, and psychotic disorders such as schizophrenia. I work with adults from diverse cultural, spiritual, and socioeconomic backgrounds.

approaches.My Background: Originally from the red rock country of Southern Utah, I completed my undergraduate and medical school training in Salt Lake City. Following medical school, I completed my psychiatry residency at Oregon Health & Science University (OHSU), where I also served as a chief resident. After training in Utah and Oregon, I’ve made Portland my home and now practice privately in the community.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I strive to offer thoughtful, individualized care through both medication management and psychodynamic psychotherapy. I work collaboratively with each person to understand the deeper meaning behind their symptoms, life experiences, and emotional patterns—while also providing evidence-based treatment to support symptom relief and long-term growth. I believe mental health and illness hold different meanings for each individual, and I strive to create a safe, respectful space where those meanings can be explored. My practice is grounded in curiosity, compassion, and a deep respect for each person’s unique story.

name: Julia Perretta
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I specialize in individual and couples therapy with an eclectic approach rooted in EFT, IFS, and somatic experiencing.
ideal_client: Have you been feeling disconnected from your partner? Working through transitional issues related to children, changes in careers, moving/adjustment, and/or retirement? Has there been an affair or other breach of trust? Have you tried having important conversations that end in arguments and never seem to find resolution? Does it seem like you keep having the same argument over and over? I'm here to help you reconnect with your love, passion, self, and goals.

approaches.My Background: I am a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist. I specialize in couples therapy with an eclectic approach rooted in EFT, attachment, neuroscience, somatic experiencing, and IFS. I also work with individuals, utilizing my background in DBT, IFS, solution focused, and somatic/mindfulness based modalities. I am a certified yoga and mindfulness instructor, which provides a lovely backbone for the other therapeutic approaches I utilize. I really enjoy working with couples experiencing conflict, distress, and infidelity, as well as individuals struggling with anxiety, stress, time management/organization, depression, life transitions, addiction, and eating disorders.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe that change is always possible. I tailor my therapeutic approaches to meet the needs of each individual client, couple, or family who I work with. I am trained in EFT, DBT, and solution focused methodologies. I operate from a trauma informed, body positive, feminist-identifying framework. When I first meet with a couple I gather information about attachment and past relationships which will guide us in tracking patterns of interaction and inform our work, in later sessions. Throughout the therapeutic process, we will explore emotions, patterns, parts of self that arise as you make your way through these patterns, and increase vulnerability and connection through emotion-focused interventions. In individual sessions I will gather information about your goals, and develop a personalized treatment plan to help you accomplish these goals. I support LGBTQI activism and the BLM movement by staying engaged and promoting social justice in and outside of the therapy room.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I have completed training in EFT and utilize this modality often with couples in my practice. Using information about attachment/interpersonal neurobiology, we will explore patterns in your relationship and track the "relational dance", identifying emotions that are occurring for each person, and exploring safety in vulnerability to increase connection.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I am currently training in IFIO (internal family systems couples therapy), and am finding great benefit in integrating "parts of self work" into my practice, with couples.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I am a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist trained in EFT and Gottman based approaches. I pull from theoretical paradigms such as IFS/IFIO (in training), attachment/interpersonal neurobiology, and somatic experiencing. Challenges with communication, trust, infidelity, connection, parenting/blended families, repair, and intimacy are often themes in my work with couples. I welcome couples in all phases of their relationship.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: As a therapist who is also a certified Yoga and Meditation teacher, I utilize self compassion and mindfulness based approaches to challenge systems of oppression that perpetuate compassion fatigue.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I utilize IFS- based approaches, mindfulness based interventions, DBT, and somatic methods to help individuals manage and overcome triggers for anxiety.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I am a HAES informed practitioner with a comprehensive, team-oriented approach to eating disorder treatment. I welcome individuals interested in (and actively pursuing) recovery. Together, we will identify barriers to achieving your treatment goals, explore ways of overcoming these barriers, and create a plan for care.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I love working with couples and individuals who are pursuing ethical non-monogamy. My therapeutic approach is inclusive to all types of relationships. I look forward to exploring your unique relational agreements, and identifying how we can tailor our work together to meet your needs and increase connection and experiences of security in relationship to self and other.

name: Ali Archer
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am an LPC providing counseling and ecotherapy for children, teens, and adults.
ideal_client: I have deep faith in our innate capacity for healing through growing in our relationship with others, ourselves and the natural world. I am passionately committed to supporting individuals with developing their self-compassion, resilience, and zest for life! Those who seek me out tend to be looking for support in healing trauma-related suffering for themselves or their child.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Ecotherapy is the practice of welcoming nature into the session, and the ways we can do so are endless. Ecotherapists are grounded in the fact that people are inherently inseparable from the natural world, and seek to facilitate and uplift the many ways nature nurtures our bodies and minds. This can look like: processing climate grief in my office, managing anxiety through developing your relationship with your garden, improving symptoms of stress/burnout through nature-based mindfulness, or taking a walk together outside. Together, we can decide what ecotherapy means in your healing. In addition to ecotherapy, I practice as a Level I Certified AEDP counselor with adults and teens, with a focus on improving relationships and healing relational and attachment wounding. My practice with children is highly informed by Child-Centered Play Therapy and interpersonal neurobiology. I often utilize somatic, mindfulness, and other experiential methods with all ages.

name: Jingyi Luan
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Jingyi is a bilingual therapist that offers therapy in English and Mandarin Chinese.
ideal_client: She has experience working with people from various backgrounds, especially young emerging adults, immigrants, international students, first-generation college students, and LGBTQIA+.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Jingyi is getting certified to become a Narcissistic Abuse Treatment Clinician who also works with people who are struggling with anxiety, depression, PTSD, intergenerational trauma, immigrant issues, academic stress, and relationship issues. She provides culturally trauma-informed Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectic Behavioral Therapy (DBT), and Polyvagal tailored to each client’s needs. Jingyi believes a good therapeutic relationship will enhance the effectiveness of the treatment modalities, so she focuses on relationship-building and supports each client with their self-discovery.

name: Colette Gordon
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi! I'm Colette. I'm a queer/trans/white counselor. I believe this world is hard, we get through it together, and therapy can help.
ideal_client: I work with so many queer and trans people. People who want and need a better world. People with big hearts who are often more compassionate towards others than they are towards themselves. People who value relationships, community and resistance, even if they feel isolated, heartbroken and discouraged. And while it’s not my life experience, I want to be here for trans women, transfemmes, people of color, and survivors of homelessness.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The heart of my work is providing politically informed relational talk therapy. I believe a lot of the best therapy comes from talking about the things that are hardest to say while being deeply heard and supported. I want to help you feel connected, cared about, and respected by me. I also want you to feel challenged, to know that I believe in you, and trust that I am working to keep your best interests at heart. I want to talk about what hurts. I want to talk about what’s going on in your relationships past, present, and future hopes + fears. I want to talk about our world and how politics, race, gender, class, ability, and so much more is impacting you and your relationships. * * * When trauma and other heavy life experiences are haunting you, I can walk through that with you using Narrative Exposure Therapy (NET). It’s a way of talking about and processing the past so it doesn’t loom as large now. It’s some of the most impactful work I do.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I might be a good fit if: You think it's time to talk about the hard stuff. You're open to being vulnerable and letting yourself be seen. You find it helpful to say things out loud and want a counselor who will think out loud with you. You want to look at the politics surrounding your life, relationships and struggles. * * * There are a lot of ways to do therapy but what generally matters most is the quality of the relationship you have with your counselor. It doesn't have to be perfect but it should be pretty solid. So don’t settle for me *just* because I’m queer and trans and can bill your insurance. That matters but it needs to be more than that. If you feel like we might click, check out my website for more, get in touch, and let's talk about it. I really value your considering putting your trust in me as a counselor and I will do my best to do right by you.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I believe we feel better when we feel connected. I believe connection comes from being seen, heard and understood in our relationships.
