I look at our relationship in this work as well as the other relationships and potential relationships in your life. I want to help you navigate the complexity of how to be yourself and have autonomy while also being in relationships with others. I approach boundaries more as a place of complexity to meet and negotiate rather than less as boundaries as demands

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Feminist in a way that's all about looking at the power dynamics in your life and talking about them. Feminist in a way that seeks to support both individual and collective empowerment. Feminist in a way that is wanting to be here for sex workers, trans women, and transition. Feminist in a way that is weight neutral, pro-fat liberation and gets feeling bad about your body. Feminist in a way that seeks to resist racism, capitalism, police/government/colonial violence, and other oppressive systems

name: Aaron Finbloom
title: Somatic Practitioner
intro: I offer parts work: a deeply imaginative, embodied therapeutic practice that fosters transformation by embracing your many selves.
ideal_client: Are you seeking a therapeutic approach that is embodied, imaginative, playful, and deeply transformative? My sessions offer a collaborative journey into the depths of your self, relationships, and world. Together we navigate the psychological, spiritual, and existential through curiosity, creativity, and deep inquiry—tapping into imagination, fantasy, fears, and desires as tools for transformation. I strive to keep this work accessible with affordable sliding scale rates.

approaches.My Background and Approach: To do parts work is to investigate our inner system of parts to more deeply understand them and thereby understand ourself. It is to find parts that are marginalized and help them feel accepted. It is to be a self-therapist for our inner family of parts and help them get along. It is to develop and strengthen parts that are missing or neglected. It is to gain greater awareness of our parts as they interface with the world. It is to be less controlled by our parts. It is to give "problematic" parts love, care, nourishment and acceptance so that they too can transform. My sessions integrate techniques of Psychodrama, Parts Mapping, Visioning, Process-oriented Psychology, Buddhist Meditation and Circling in an emergent relational process guided by the trauma-informed lens of Internal Family Systems (IFS). To read more about these practices, please go to my Parts Work website listed below. At this time I am only seeing clients virtually.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: For as long as I can remember I've been in love with questions. I adore the play of investigation – the curious back and forth that leads deeply and joyfully into the unknown. But this investigation gets even more fruitful when it looks into who and what we are, and when it leans into the emotions of this journey and the connection and intimacy between us curious humans. My foundational ethic is to foster curiosity, care and play towards our darknesses, and I believe this is what brings growth, transformation, healing and goodness in our world. Investigating my own inner parts, and learning how to hold them with tenderness and care, has had a tremendous impact on my own life, and I'm so very drawn to help others along this path. I hold a PhD in relational practice from Concordia University's Interdisciplinary Humanities & Fine Arts Program. I have received trainings in Circling, Psychodrama and Process Work. My sessions are deeply inspired by the trauma-informed practice of IFS.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: I work with Psychodrama and Visioning practices, which help bring a client into dramatic or imaginative representation of inner and external roles. These practices help significantly aid in expression, depth-work and distancing.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I work within an IFS model. This model helps to identify parts, un-blend them, and then find access to self-energy to provide relief to burdened managers and exiles.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I use Circling (an authentic relating practice) and Non-Violent Communication to work directly with clients in a relational setting, whereby we address issues, problems and facets of experience that are felt in the "here-and-now" relationship between client and therapist.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: With training in existential and philosophical counseling, I assist clients in delving into deeper questions that frame the contours of life, world and sense of self.

name: Emily Trum
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a clinical art therapist who loves to support increasing positive life experiences and perspectives for children, teens and families.
ideal_client: ages 3-10: play therapy to support skill building, trauma processing & increasing secure attachment 3-18: art therapy to support processing of life events, management of depression/anxiety, building interpersonal skill sets and relationship patterns/attachment styles with family members/loved ones, increasing attention/focus Also, working with family systems to support positive communication and reduce conflict

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I often use neuroscience based art therapy directives to support nervous system regulation and positive brain function. I am a person centered, attachment focused art therapist who often uses the Stages of Change and the Hero's Journey to support identification of self and goals in therapy to increase positive life experiences, make changes and increase personal identity.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that art is for everyone. Art making can support an integration of aspects of self for wholeness and healing. Art holds value in the process of creating, the resulting product or any range in between. Art has defined who I am and helped me process my own life experiences and integrate them into myself in a healthy manner. I personally make art to process my own stuff and continue to reflect on how I can interact with this world as a person that I like and am proud to be. It is my goal to help others engage in the world comfortable in their own skin with hope and direction.

name: Ashley Davis
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I provide a holistic approach that empowers clients to engage with their emotions, build resilience and heal through creative expression.
ideal_client: She is devoted to working with individuals navigating and processing issues related to identity, belonging, trauma, transitions and loss, while fostering a nurturing space for self-discovery and emotional growth. Her ultimate goal is to empower individuals to connect with their authentic selves, access their inner resources and create meaningful, lasting change in their lives. She aims to emphasize inclusivity and respect for the diverse experiences that shape each client’s journey.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am an art therapist in training, specializing in grief and trauma. By integrating the creative process and making art in the therapeutic practice, I hope to provide clients with unique and powerful tools for self-expression, exploration, and healing. Through a combination of methods, art therapy can be effective in helping clients achieve harmony between their emotional, intellectual, spiritual and physical aspects of life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As an adoptee and single parent, she brings a deep personal understanding of caregiving, personal growth, and the unique challenges of adoption. In her free time, Ashley enjoys anything to do with the outdoors like kayaking, fishing, birding, and whale watching. She also likes reading, running, playing guitar and creating art! She is consistently pursuing additional education and training to expand her existing knowledge and skills for the communities she serves and has plans to become a certified EMDR therapist.

name: Bennett Gibney
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a white, queer, non-binary therapist who partners with clients to help create meaningful change.
ideal_client: My heart has always gravitated to working with those in the LGBTQ+ community or those who hold a marginalized identity. I love working with a variety of personalities and issues. My work as a therapist is focused on providing a safe space for you to be yourself, free from judgement, to explore the roadblocks that are preventing you from living the life you want.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: It does not take much to see we live in a world built for white, hetero, cisgender people. Coming from a background in social work, my approach emphasizes the impact that marginalization and oppression can have on the mental health and well-being of individuals. Our culture, communities, and external worlds can be hinder our ability to manage stress and the emotional waves of life; and this is particularly true for those who feel “othered” or alone. As a queer nonbinary human, I’ve done my fair share of work to unpack my own internalized shame. I value the vulnerability that clients of all ages bring to the therapeutic space, whether that is exploring the pain of childhood wounds, examining relationships and significant events, or delving into the thoughts and feelings that are keeping folks stuck and from living the life they want.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a therapist, I am a firm believer that healing happens within relational settings. I will partner with you to better understand your unique experiences, needs, and emotions so you can create the meaningful change you seek.

name: Lee Lynch
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Queer/Trans Expressive Arts Therapist ready to show up for you with curiosity and care.
ideal_client: I tend to match well with folks who identify with one or more of the following identities: queer, trans, introverted, neurodivergent, highly sensitive. I especially enjoy supporting clients through big life transitions! (Examples: Coming into queer/ trans identities, relationship structural changes, grief & loss, moving, career changes, aging). *For Regence BCBS members- I am not in the "Legacy Network" but accept most other BCBS plans.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My practice is grounded in my training as an Expressive Arts Therapist. This means that depending on your preferences and style of processing, we have the option to incorporate visual art, music, movement, writing and play into sessions to explore other modes of expression beyond talk therapy. My hope is that therapy can be a place where you feel comfortable being yourself, so that we can work through things together that might feel otherwise uncomfortable or heavy to process alone. To learn more specifics about my professional experience, see my CV: https://www.expressiveartstherapypdx.com/pagecv

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Personally, I learned about grief & loss, and “feeling different” at a young age. These experiences have led me to be able to look at situations from many angles and listen deeply and respectfully. As a neurodivergent queer & trans person, I naturally frame my practice through a lens that challenges oppressive systems, including recognizing my own role in systems of power (for example, as a white therapist). In our work, I hope to create a space where you can feel safe(r) to bring your intersectional identities. I dream of a world where there is equitable access to housing, healthy food, healthcare and rest. What gets me through hard times: tuning into seasonal cycles, plant propagation, herbalism and home-cooked meals.

name: Asha Jetmalani
title: Psychiatrist
intro: I'm a physician, board certified in psychiatry since 2018. Visit my website to submit an inquiry for care www.stonecroppsych.com
ideal_client: As a person of color and member of the LGBTQIA+ community, I bring a unique perspective to my practice, specializing in psychiatric med management and supportive therapy for these communities. While I have extensive experience working with these populations, my practice is inclusive and welcomes individuals from all backgrounds

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer psychiatric medication management, psychotherapy and comprehensive psychiatric evaluations using a HIPAA secure virtual platform to patients in Oregon. My psychotherapeutic style is eclectic, drawing from a range of effective modalities including Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and motivational interviewing, alongside principles of Nonviolent Communication. I believe deeply in the power of holistic approaches to support mental well-being. Exercise, nourishing food, and connection with community are essential components of healing. If you are seeking ongoing psychiatric care, we will meet for 1-3 initial consultation visits to assess if we are a good fit for one another. If we mutually decide to move forward with ongoing care, we will collaborate to find an appointment schedule that meets your needs.

approaches.Social Justice Issues We Care About: I am dedicated to providing compassionate, inclusive, and trauma-informed care. My practice is rooted in principles of anti-racism and actively challenges systems of oppression, including anti-LGBTQIA+ discrimination and all other forms of marginalization. I believe that mental health care should empower individuals by validating their lived experiences and understanding how these intersect with larger systemic issues. I am committed to creating a safe, supportive environment where people from all backgrounds can feel seen and heard.

name: Allison Kennedy
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor enthusiastic about helping adult individuals in plenty of life areas, especially anxiety and trauma.
ideal_client: I look forward to setting up a treatment plan specific to your goals for yourself, and then moving forward from there. I believe that you are already the expert on your own life, and I am honored to be a part of the journey to provide support, guidance, understanding, and skills from evidence-based interventions that you may find useful to areas of your mental health that you may be struggling with.

approaches.My Background: I attended Florida State University to achieve my Masters of Science in Mental Health Counseling and attended Southern Illinois University-Carbondale to achieve my Bachelor of Arts in Psychology. I have always had a propensity for helping people mentally on a very deep level; it is my passion. I have experience in this field ranging from a residential eating disorder setting, to being a victim advocate and counselor for trauma survivors, to helping folks in a community mental health outpatient services setting serving just about every mental health diagnosis. I am now ecstatic about serving primarily adult individuals of all races, ethnicities, identities, sexual orientations, etc. within my telehealth private practice.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am committed to meeting you where you are by tailoring each therapeutic experience uniquely to your needs, strengths and abilities, goals, and within your boundaries. I am respectful, empathetic, kind, and curious. I aim to facilitate an open, warm, and trustworthy therapeutic relationship that will always keep your safety and best interest in mind. I hope you can find that we can be a good therapeutic fit and that you can place your trust in me on your journey to hope and healing. Let's set up an appointment to get you started on the path to reaching your goals. Call or email me to set up an appointment. I look forward to connecting with you!

name: Liz Cloud
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: You and I are equal partners in discovering how you can live a more fulfilled life.
ideal_client: Many of my patients report wanting to address concerns about anxiety, anger, and relationships. Some wish to engage in personal growth and feel a stronger sense of purpose and meaning in their lives. Coping with loss and addressing unfinished business in relationships are other common themes people wish to explore.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I'm glad you're participating in the important and sometimes challenging process of finding a therapist. Here's a bit about my therapy approach to help you learn if we might be a good fit: my goal is to support you to move through pain and struggle in a way you feel good about. My therapeutic style incorporates warmth, humor, and honest feedback. I prioritize creating a space for you to safely experiment with new ways of being and communicating. I strive to help you live in a way that inspires deeper fulfillment by harnessing your natural ability to cope with stress. Sometimes when the strategies that used to work for us no longer serve their purpose, we start to struggle and suffer. When we identify these patterns and have support in trying something new, there is relief from "stuckness."

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor and received my education from Pacific University's School of Professional Psychology. My patients are adolescents and adults, many of whom struggle with anxiety, difficult transitions, and loss. I feel privileged to have served the Portland community since 2009.

name: Julia Hilton
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am so glad that you are ready to connect and prioritize your mental health! I look forward to working with you!
ideal_client: Are you experiencing symptoms of anxiety or depression? Do you feel burnt out by the constant pressures of life? Are you struggling to connect with loved ones and find meaning in your life? My background has allowed me to help clients experiencing all of these challenges. I work alongside clients to help them identify their goals and create a customized roadmap to help them achieve the mental health and wellness that they are searching for.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have over a decade of experience working with adolescents and adult clients with diverse concerns, including anxiety, OCD, and depression. My approach to practice includes person-centered and trauma-informed treatment focused on assisting clients with clarifying goals and developing strategies to heal and move forward into their ideal lives.

name: Hailee Kendrick
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I integrate art therapy with talk-based approaches, offering a space where you can express yourself beyond words and at your own pace.
ideal_client: Will be open to exploring their lived experiences and emotions to better understand themselves through meaning-making.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I specialize in the treatment of trauma and employ Love Ethic as my practice framework. Love Ethic, developed by bell hooks, utilizes the dimensions of loving through respect, responsibility, knowledge, commitment, care, and trust. I integrate several modalities like, DBT, CBT, and mindfulness as tools to assist in the therapeutic process. We can examine the elements of your artwork and life together to uncover unconscious patterns that may impact you in meeting your goals. My goal is to nurture a safe environment for you to explore coping skills and yourself. My sessions are grounded in compassion, creativity, and collaboration.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I can provide mental health assessments for gender affirming surgery referral letters. Certified through the National LGBTQIA+ Health Education Center in 2025. I offer sliding scale for eligible clients.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: The benefits of art therapy include processing traumatic memories safely, at your own pace, through images, which can reduce their intensity. Making visible what’s inside can help validate emotions and makes them easier to understand. Regulating emotions through the creative process can help soothe your nervous system, helping with hyperarousal and emotional overwhelm. Grounding in the present, creating art forces focus on the here-and-now, which helps interrupt anxious spirals.

name: Amanda Lowrey
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I help individual adults, couples, and families, with anxiety, depression, life transitions, relational conflict, trauma & somatic healing
ideal_client: You are deserving to grow through what you've gone through! Whether you are facing significant life transitions, relational conflict, lost sense of self or wishing to expand your emotional awareness - My hope is to provide a therapeutic space that empowers you to reconnect with your own innate resiliency. I believe that through deeper understanding comes greater self-awareness and the ability to identify your truest needs, wants, wishes, desires and authentically express yourself!

approaches.What I Specialize In: I am passionate about working with emerging to middle-aged adults with a wide range of issues, including anxiety, depression, recovery from trauma, self-worth and people-pleasing behaviors, stress management, boundary work, career and identity exploration. In therapy, I often incorporate parts of self work, somatic and mindfulness techniques to help clients foster the connection between their mind and body. I also work with couples and adult families with a focus on multi-generational patterns and narratives, conflict resolution, enhancing intimacy and communication dynamics!

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Recognizing that you are the expert of your own life, I prioritize meeting my clients where they are at and tailoring therapy to meet their unique needs. As a trauma-informed, inclusive, and LGBTQIA2S+ affirming therapist, I value diversity and strive to create a safe and supporting environment where my clients feel hear and understood, I aim to provide a warm, curious, collaborative, person-centered and strengths-based approach with a sprinkle of humor!

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Our therapeutic relationship is the most important predictor of success in therapy! I focus on creating an environment where you feel heard, validated, and have a safe space to express your thoughts, emotions, and experiences. Together we can move towards having more connection, vulnerability and authenticity in your relationships.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: My work is mindfulness-based, experiential and humanistic, meaning I foster and respect my clients' self awareness and use the client's own present moment experience to inform us about what is needed. Mindfulness can help you feel more connected to your own inner strength, resilience and wisdom!

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Let's take a look at how your thoughts, emotions and behaviors interact and effect one another! We can then identify unhealthy ways of thinking and replace them with more beneficial thoughts that are in our own best interest. You’ll learn tools to practice outside of session in a practical, helpful way.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: We are all humans first. Your experiences and interpretations of these experience are central to understanding your place in the world. From a humanistic lens, we can explore these experiences and discover your unique self!

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Early childhood relationships, interactions, and experiences provide a blueprint for how we see ourselves, our relationships, and the world around us. Has the world felt safe? Have you found trust and reliability in others? Understanding your attachment style can be a powerful tool in unraveling old relationship patterns and fostering meaningful and secure changes!

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Learn to accept anxiety all the while working to change it! I often work with clients to explore how they feel, the roots of the obstacle, and understand their ineffective thoughts / behaviors through evidence-based modalities, while determining effective coping mechanisms. As well, I often incorporate mindfulness-based interventions to aid in resolving stress, overwhelm, and panic stored in the body.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: It's important to take time in recognizing and understanding how traumatic experience have impacted one's mental, behavioral, emotional, physical, and spiritual well-being! I often work with clients in exploring the connection between a trauma experience and associated emotional and behavioral responses. As well, I often incorporate mindfulness-based interventions to aid in healing trauma stored in the body.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Utilizing Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT) and the Gottman Method, I work with adult families and couples in resolving various issues! EFT concentrates on strengthening trust and bond between partners, while looking at how individuals process their experiences, emotions, patterns of interaction, and attachment. The integration with the Gottman Method's practical tools and interventions allows us to explore together the "dance" of interactions and emotional attunement.

name: Stephanie Thompson-McCollough
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome- I work with individuals, couples, and children/teens for in-person or virtual therapy visits. I currently have availability!
ideal_client: As a licensed professional counselor, I enjoy working with a variety of diverse clients. I believe that the client is the expert of their own lives and my goal as a provider to is empower clients to learn skills to get closer to their own goals. I believe that the strongest engine of change is the rapport between client and clinician and I work diligently to foster space for us to work collaboratively. I am specifically trained in DBT, CBT, MI, CPS, and EFT. I look forward to working together.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy Approaches 1 Person Centered Therapy is a collaboration. I am a guide to help facilitate reflection, growth, and opportunity for change. You are the leader of the therapeutic process. 2 Motivational Interviewing Change is uncomfortable. Together we can explore what is keeping you feeling stuck and preventing you from living your most authentic life. 3 Mindful Only when we are fully present are we able to truly experience our lives. Therapy can help each of us tap into being present and aware of each current moment. 4 Unconditional Positive Regard I believe each person is doing the absolute best they can within their circumstances. I provide therapy from this deeply empathetic place.

Life unfolds in complicated, beautiful, chaotic, and at times, immensely painful ways. As we make our way through, we often need support navigating the terrain of our inner world so that we can show up more fully to all that is happening in our outer world. If you’ve been feeling overwhelmed, disconnected, stuck or alone, then I’m glad you found your way here. I know from my own life experience that finding the right person to support you in your healing is both a vulnerable and important task. I feel honored to do this work and I am in awe of our ability as humans to accompany and support each other as we heal and grow. I have a background working in a variety of settings including PH/IOP, outpatient, emergency department, inpatient, and community based care. I also have experience working with a variety of different types of challenges including: depression, anxiety, grief & loss, family conflict, infertility, attachment, life transitions, parenting, self esteem, SI, eating disorder

name: Landon Michaels
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I am an irreverent, change-focused Psychologist that can treat a wide-range of issues in addition to specialty training in C-PTSD
ideal_client: If you've found yourself here, you are looking for change. My therapy approach will help you build new behaviors that align with the person you want to be and get control of behaviors that no longer fit your life. Because the path towards recovery and growth is difficult, I try to make the journey as enjoyable as possible. While providing empirically supported treatments, I mix in irreverence, bad puns, and a youthful energy.

approaches.What I Specialize In: have specialty training in working with survivors of childhood abuse using a novel treatment called Contextual Trauma Therapy. This treatment aims to help recover not only from the trauma itself, but also the dysfunctional environment in which it occurs. My skillset is uniquely built to address the wide array of issues that can result from PTSD/C-PTSD as I believe you have to specialize in more than just trauma to help work towards resolution.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have specialty training in Contextual Trauma Therapy which developed to address the unique difficulties that come from repeated exposure to traumatic events and the family environment that is involved. Contextual Therapy is a treatment that aims to treat both the impact of the dysfunctional family environment as well as the trauma itself.

name: Hunter Vaughn
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I provide culturally-responsive therapy for people from diverse backgrounds including sexual, gender, & relationship diversity.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach therapy as a collaborative process, recognizing that you and I both contribute valuable knowledge and expertise to our work. My experience is that when we combine our efforts, we are able to develop creative, personalized, and powerful ways for you to be more effective, engaged, and satisfied in life. I draw from a variety of psychological theories and techniques to tailor therapy to your particular strengths, goals, needs, and personality. For instance, we may work at increasing our understanding of your emotional experiences & why they occur; challenging & changing ways of being or thinking that no longer work for you; processing or reconceptualizing experiences & relationships; etc. Occasional “experiments” between sessions help to reinforce or inform our work; whether the experiment “succeeds” or “fails” we have new data. The overarching goal is to help you get unstuck, increase your understanding of yourself, & enhance your ability to adapt to and enjoy your life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my doctorate in clinical psychology from Pacific University in 2012 and have been working as a mental health therapist since 2007. I've worked in a variety of settings including community mental health and college counseling centers, gaining experience and training spanning all ages, many cultures, and the full range of socioeconomic statuses. I'm trained in a variety of theoretical and technical approaches to therapy, which allows me to tailor therapy to a client's particular needs, strengths, and situation. I continue to seek training, knowledge, and experience in working with all types of clients, but especially those identifying as sexual, gender, and ethnic/cultural minorities.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Since my undergraduate years, I've focused on developing my knowledge & skills for working with LGBTQ individuals, couples, & families. This passion extends to my graduate research with lesbian co-mother families, my clinical experience & training, and the focus of my practice. LGBTQ individuals have unique experiences, needs, strengths, & concerns. I strive to honor & incorporate these in therapy

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I continuously increase my knowledge and skills for helping clients address Gender Dysphoria. I'm well versed in the WPATH & the emerging 'Informed Consent' standards of care, as well as associated psycho-social challenges (e.g., social anxiety) experienced by transgender and gender-queer people. I help clients to embrace their identities through coming out, social and medical transition, & more.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: My training allows me to work with couples using a variety of approaches including Dan Wile's work, Emotionally Focused Therapy for Couples, and Gottman's theories and techniques (though I'm not yet certified in EFT-C or Gottman therapy). Couples are unique, multifaceted, and complex, and I strive to help them understand and resolve their conflicts, needs, strengths, and relationship dynamics.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have extensive training & experience helping people address & reduce generalized anxiety, social phobia, panic, trauma-related anxiety, existential anxiety, and more. I use various approaches and techniques depending on the person and the anxiety, including mindfulness, exposure techniques, challenging anxious thoughts, improving insight/awareness, processing experiences, & creating closure.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is one of the most common reasons people seek therapy, & I've worked with clients of all ages to resolve & recover from depression. Using theories & techniques from cognitive behavioral, mindfulness, insight- and relational-oriented therapies, and more, I help people understand why depression arose, when & why it recurs/remains, & how to reduce/eliminate, cope with, & manage it.

name: Dr. Steven Ruiz Bettencourt, Psy.D
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a compassionate licensed psychotherapist with over 39 years of experience and am a Martial Arts Grand Master.

name: Daniel Swenson
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a social worker who swears by evidence-based treatments but allows that there’s unknowable magic in the therapeutic relationship.
ideal_client: I work with adults who are seeking to decrease suffering, increase authenticity, build community, and pursue a life that aligns with their values. I strive to be anti-oppressive in my practice, and often that means helping other white men to unlearn racism and embrace feminism. As a musician and arts policy wonk, I have a special interest in working with artists and creative types whose fear and shame are interfering with their full expression.

approaches.My Background: My path to becoming a therapist was circuitous. I graduated college in 2000 and worked as a musician, arts policy researcher, and career counselor, before getting a Master of Social Work degree in 2014. I have always been a sensitive person and for most of my 20s relied on alcohol to avoid emotional discomfort. All of this lived experience informs my clinical work. As a person in recovery, I help people to skillfully approach, experience, and express their emotions, without falling into problematic coping strategies. As a career counselor, I coach people in working toward long term goals. As a policy researcher, I prioritize evidence-based treatments. And as a musician, I listen and respond mindfully and without judgment.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is behavioral and relational. I believe that changing ineffective behaviors, and recognizing thoughts as just thoughts (not facts), can free us to pursue the relationships, passions, and community that make life worth living. I also take a systemic perspective, and view capitalism as a driver of human suffering. Progress includes learning to reorient toward connection and mutual support over striving and consumption. I am intensively trained in Dialectical Behavior Therapy, and before opening my private practice, worked as a DBT therapist for seven years. I have also been trained in Exposure and Response Prevention, Behavioral Activation, and the DBT Prolonged Exposure Protocol. I am comfortable treating anxiety, depression, trauma, OCD, and substance use disorders, among other concerns. I have a keen interest in plant medicines, and enjoy helping people to integrate and consolidate the wisdom gained through psychedelic experiences into lasting behavioral change.

name: Jennie Hagen
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide warmth and humor, and will totally ask you about your family of origin. The best stuff is usually hiding just under the surface.
ideal_client: The world is ROUGH right now. For years it's been bringing up a lot of our old wounds that haven't fully healed, testing our coping skills, and asking us to be resilient in ways we didn't think we could (and honestly don't really want to most of the time). Through this all, there is so much light in all of us. Traumas big and small can help us get closer to our authentic selves. Processing and healing those old wounds helps us build resilience and find peace.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Change is a scary thing. Usually, people are ready to make changes when they’ve come to a couple different conclusions. You may have found that the ways you’ve tried to cope with an issue aren’t working and you’re feeling stuck. Or you may know that something in your current situation isn’t working but you’re not sure what to do about it. When people come to counseling, it’s often because they’ve recognized that the discomfort of things staying the same has become worse than the fear of the unknown. During our work together, I may ask you to try out some new ways of thinking or new behaviors. But first we will establish a foundation of trust. This helps create a safe space where you will be heard and understood; where you know you can open up without judgment. Moving at your own pace, we begin to edge gradually out of your comfort zone. By doing this mindfully we can make small changes that feel safe and attainable, while keeping a close eye on emotions that come up during the process.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: We as therapists don't have all the answers. You're the one driving the car down the path we navigate together, and I'm helping read the map (if only there was a GPS for mental health!) I'm constantly reading, learning, and absorbing to learn more about the world, my place in it, and how to better support the people I work with. I have the most training and experience in supporting the LGBTQ+ community and am building knowledge around racial justice topics. Black Lives Matter. I'm an intersectional feminist and can help even if you're not exactly sure what that means (I'd love to explain!). I also enjoy working with veterans and volunteer with the Returning Veterans Project. I'm a mom of two young children, and if you're a parent reading this - you're doing an amazing job. I see you, and know how hard it is. Everyone is doing the best they can with the information they have. Processing our traumas and building community help us to do better for ourselves & each other.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: Mental health doesn't exist in a vacuum. All parts of who you are as a person can affect (and be affected by) your mental state. I encourage people to examine what they notice in their mind, heart, body, and all different aspects of their life. This allows us to feel more whole as human beings, and can improve our relationships with all different pieces of our lives.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Identifying as female in our culture comes with so many landmines. Navigating relationships, work/life balance, parenting, misogyny, and so on. If you've clicked on this specialty, you know. I like to work from an feminist perspective to see how gender underlies other stressors. Feminism is intersectional, and if you identify as female (or on the feminine side of the spectrum) this space is for you.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Humanistic, or 'person-centered,' therapy focuses on helping you recognize your worth and value as a person. Using this type of therapy, I emphasize that you're the expert on your own experience, and that I'm here as a tool to help you identify what will work best for you. It encourages acceptance of yourself, just as you are, while also bringing about freedom to enact change.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Using mindfulness in therapy allows us to be still in the moment and examine a situation without attaching meaning to it. It encompasses topics like gratitude, meditation, relaxation, and being truly present to what's happening in the mind and body.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Identifying as female in our culture in 2023 comes with so many landmines. Navigating relationships, work/life balance, parenting, misogyny, rights to body autonomy, and so on. If you've clicked on this specialty, you know. I like to work from an feminist perspective to see how gender underlies other stressors. Feminism is intersectional, and if you identify as female (or on the feminine side of the spectrum) this space is for you.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Change is inevitable, but transitions can shake up our emotions, thoughts, and sense of self. It's very common for people to have intense reactions to new or different life circumstances. Together, we can find ways to help ease the discomfort of a new situation and begin to feel positive about going through changes.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma can comes in many different forms and affects everyone a little differently. I help people cope with and heal from trauma through validation, creating a sense of safety, and partnering together to figure out the best combination of tools to regain a sense of control over their experience. We always work at your pace and will only talk about difficult topics when you feel safe and ready.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is a complex diagnosis that can have varied causes. Often, people experience depression when circumstances in their life leave them worn down, defeated, overwhelmed, or feeling powerless. Medication can be a great tool in treating the symptoms of depression, but often doesn't address the source of the issue. Counseling can fill in those gaps and help you begin to heal.

name: Jonathan Penley
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Trauma and stress reduction therapist using EMDR, Ketamine Assisted Psychotherapy, Narrative Therapy, CBT, & VR through an attachment lens.
ideal_client: I help people who have ongoing symptoms and negative life impacts from recent and childhood/complex PTSD and desire to seek relief from distress and gain calmness, clarity, and confidence again. PTSD and stress affect people in a variety of ways, ranging from problems with addictions, anger, anxiety, compulsive behaviors, disorganization, distractibility, eating, emotional dysregulation, guilt, health, intrusive thoughts, panic, relationships, sadness, shame, sleep, work, and more.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have a strong background in psychotherapy research at both the undergraduate and graduate level, focusing on attachment, trauma, psychiatric interventions, brain imaging, and self-help interventions. I believe most mental health symptoms originate from early attachment and stressful events, and that revisiting these early life experiences helps people develop more adaptive emotional and cognitive responses to present-day stressors. I specialize in the evidence-based therapies of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing, Lifespan Integration, Group Therapy, and Neurofeedback for adults. Most of my clients enjoy the eclectic elements of these non-linear right brain therapies, ranging from brief exposure, insightfulness, mind-body awareness, and the unconscious. My approach is a combination of lightheartedness and kindness, alongside being directive and honest.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In my spare time, I enjoy spending time with my partner, pup, family, friends, listening to audiobooks, keeping up with the news, learning, whole-food plant-based cuisine, being physically active, attempting to forage for mushrooms, and being an imperfect "good enough" human.

name: Jessica Powers
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Virtual mental health and addictions counseling, ADHD evaluations, and clinical supervision in Oregon and Washington
ideal_client: Welcome! You’ve taken the first step toward personal growth, and that takes a lot of courage. The next steps don’t have to be quite so difficult! I can help you process and learn from the challenges you’ve faced in the past, support you during any changes you may be going through now, and suggest ways you can start to maximize your potential and maintain your overall well-being going forward. Whether you are looking for some or all of the above, I am looking forward to working with you!

approaches.My Background and Approach: My approach to helping is cognitive-behavioral, meaning that I am listening for negative thoughts (cognitive) that we can challenge and reframe more positively, as well as things that you can do (behavioral) to feel less anxious and more hopeful, and to take good care of yourself mentally, emotionally, and physically. I may also suggest many ideas drawn from dialectical-behavioral therapy (DBT), which is a kind of cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) that focuses on mindfulness, emotion regulation, distress tolerance, and interpersonal effectiveness. I began practicing in 2015 at an intensive outpatient center, and completed my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling in 2016. In the state of Oregon, I am a Licensed Professional Counselor, and Approved Supervisor Candidate, and a Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor. I am currently in-network with some Providence, PacificSource, Kaiser, and Regence/BCBS of Oregon health plans.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that regardless of what we have done or been through in the past, we can all live the life we want, both now and in the future. I can help you learn and grow from your experiences, and provide the safety and comfort in our sessions together that give you the confidence to follow through on the changes you want to make. Schedule your first session here: https://happyheart.clientsecure.me/

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: People with anxiety may feel nervous or “on edge,” worry a lot, and avoid doing things that make their anxiety worse. They may have physical symptoms, such as a racing heart, upset stomach, and sweating or shaking. Many of these also often cause difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or both. I help people learn coping skills and other lifestyle habits that help them feel less anxious.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: People with ADHD may have inattentive symptoms, hyperactive symptoms, or both, and can also benefit from learning the CBT and DBT skills I provide, which often looks like what many refer to as "ADHD coaching." Whether you are new or established client wondering if you have ADHD, we can schedule an ADHD evaluation and talk about how therapy, coaching, and other types of support or treatment may benefit you.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: People can become addicted to anything, not just drugs or alcohol. Someone may need help with their over-use or abuse of a substance or activity if it takes up so much of their time that they are neglecting, or are unable to fulfill, their other responsibilities. I help people achieve their goals to moderate or abstain from addictive substances or behaviors.

specialities.name: Early Recovery
specialities.description: Recovery is not just about getting sober or abstaining from addictive substances and activities, it is about establishing, and then maintaining, an overall healthy lifestyle, and learning how to handle triggers and setbacks. You can also be in recovery from an eating disorder, mental health issues, or a mental health crisis. I provide support to people in all of these types of recovery, as well as to people who are just beginning wanting to change, or who have had a recent relapse.

name: Jane Mayer
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I love working with those who are grieving and helping people who hunger for more meaning and health in their lives.
ideal_client: I help people grow who want to grow. I work with individual adults who are grieving, and those who are interested in growing and exploring new ways of relating to themselves, their work in the world, and others. Therapy, at its core, is a relationship between two people whose aim is to bring clarity and choice to the client. My goal is to work with clients with whom there is a meeting of our minds and hearts, and whose issues are ones which I can ethically and confidently address.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I tailor my approach to the needs of each individual client. My training is in psychodynamic psychotherapy, which helps me to grasp the impact of your life's experiences and their impact on your way of being in the world, your relationship to yourself and others. My additional training includes work with grief work, attachment theory and somatic-based therapies which help me frame for you how you interact with your feelings, beliefs, assumptions and choices. My interpersonal style is active, engaged, honest and humorous. Most of my clients report feeling deeply supported and challenged in their work with me.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: My specialties include grief and loss work for people facing loss of loved ones to death or life changes, illness in themselves or recovering from life in dysfunctional/alcoholic families. I specialize in working with adults who are grieving the death of their life partner/spouse. I became a psychotherapist because I love the life journey, despite how harrowing, joyous and confusing it feels at times. A lifelong seeker of health and resilience, I first pursued my own growth work (and continue to) and then entered social work to develop reliable skills to help others find health, choice and possibility. I have been licensed and in practice since 2000. My additional training has been in grief and loss work, sensorimotor/somatic psychotherapy and in parenting education.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: My original training is in psychodynamic psychotherapy. This theoretical orientation helps me to understand the family patterns and experiences of my clients and how they impact their sense of themselves, relationships and others. Often we are relating in ways that do not work, and our actions and beliefs are based on past scripts, rather than the choice and perspectives of our grown up selves.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Approaching my clients as whole, meaning-filled human beings allows me to help them discover themselves, beyond their current self-concept. By engaging in present-moment relationship and through encouraging my clients to discover their ability to function in new and creative ways, my clients can discover more choice, self-esteem, and integrity in how they interact with themselves and others.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: My primary professional interest has been to learn how to be present to people as they grieve their losses. Often, well-meaning loved ones want to rush the bereaved through their pain, as it can seem settling and unsettling. Grief is a part of life that few of us learn to do well, and I help people move through their grief, honor their losses and learn how to move forward at their own pace. I work with many adults who are grieving the loss of their life partner/spouse.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Specializing in life transitions, I work with clients who are facing the sometimes harrowing transitions that we encounter as humans: changing or ending relationships, learning to relate with our families healthily, partnering with significant others, parenting, occupational change, aging and grief and loss.

specialities.name: Family Caregiving
specialities.description: Facing the role of caregiver to a loved one, child or elder can be a daunting task. The balance between caring for oneself and caring for another requires skill, mindfulness and support. I help caregivers learn how to discern what self-care means for them, and how to maintain it amidst the stress, grief and hard feelings that emerge along the way.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: When one grows up in a family that is destabilized by the presence of alcoholism, traumatic loss, addiction, or insufficient parenting, we can adopt various strategies for relating to others that aren't healthy. These strategies leave us feeling as though we are sacrificing parts of ourselves to have love. I help people learn to relate healthily to themselves and others.

name: Miranda Nelson
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Identity disclosures: she/her/hers, cis-gendered, white, able-bodied, nuanced-practicing Mormon
ideal_client: Who I work with: thinkers, readers, existential crisis havers, people who keep getting told that they "need to stop intellectualizing their feelings," artists, ruminators, relationship navigators, critical thinkers, self-criticizers, closeted therapy skeptics, and those who are ready to start feeling a bit more alive.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I believe that most pathology stems from scarcity, and that our scarcity is not always obvious to us. We feel good when we have enough time, space, energy, money, mobility, information, and community. The first step is identifying what kind of scarcity you're experiencing. I believe that navigating scarcity makes us more creative (finding ways to make the most of the resources available) and compassionate (deep familiarity with one's own scarcity makes the scarcity of others more visible.) I believe that community is an especially important resource. Communities pool resources and give access to more time, space, energy, money, mobility, and information than we could ever secure on our own. Because of this, I believe in the healing power of relationships. Relational therapy involves investigating what might be interrupting your ability to experience a secure sense of community. It's working towards finding more belonging and feeling more at home.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy is not life, it's a dress rehearsal for life. My therapy style focuses on helping you connect deeply with others, manage conflict, maintain meaningful relationships, and put language to the parts of your experience you fear nobody can understand. The therapy space is a practice arena where you learn to cultivate belonging and feel a bit less alone. Therapy should be a space for you to explore your unique identity. I'm an LGBTQIA2+ advocate and ally, practice from a poly/ENM/kink-aware perspective, use a feminist/multicultural lens, and believe it is imperative to recognize systems of oppression in clinical work. I believe in the power of consistent, dependable, unfiltered relationships and prioritize rapport when working with clients. I believe in using evidence-based interventions to provide meaningful care.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Theories that inform my work: interpersonal theory, relational-cultural theory, Gestalt, Winnicott, Yalom & Leszcz group theory.

name: Joe Gianotti
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi! My name is Joe Gianotti (he/him) and I am a Professional Counseling Associate registered with the state or Oregon
ideal_client: As a counselor, I am here not to give advice or to tell you what you should be doing, but to provide new insights and frameworks to assist you during our work together. Through our collaboration, we will work through your concerns and problems and explore possible changes you can implement in your life, while acknowledging your sources of strength and resiliency.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: During my clinical experience, I have encountered working with issues around anxiety, depression, trauma, men’s issues, and social anxiety. I emphasize the importance of rapport and trust building, and believe that counseling can be effective and beneficial if a strong therapeutic relationship is formed.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Life can be full of stress, grief, and suffering, and as human beings, it can be challenging for us to navigate through all of the negative thoughts, emotions, and experiences that we encounter. Coming from a Humanistic and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy background, my approach to psychotherapy focuses on getting to know you and your unique experience so that we as a team can find better ways for you to live the life that you want to live. I believe that you are the expert of your own experience and I hope to create a space where you can authentically express yourself in a safe environment that is free of judgment.

name: Lily Robertson
title: Marriage and Family Therapist
intro: I guide women and couples through healing past trauma, empowering them to live authentic, embodied lives.
ideal_client: Trauma can leave us feeling disconnected—from ourselves and from those we love. Perhaps loneliness, self-doubt, or unworthiness have become all too familiar, making it hard to remember a time when things didn’t feel this way. But one thing is clear: you’re ready for change. You’re ready to understand the roots of your pain, to rebuild trust in yourself, and to embrace your true, authentic self. Most of all, you’re ready to feel whole again.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I help women and couples deepen self-awareness, build self-compassion, and create meaningful change. Our sessions are collaborative—I show up authentically, offering support and gentle challenge. Together, we’ll explore how past experiences live in the body and find a path toward healing, growth, and deeper connection. Here, you can show up as your raw, authentic self—without judgment. Over time, you'll gain the confidence to bring that true self into the world beyond therapy. You are the expert in your life; my role is to guide, support, and help you explore with curiosity. Together, we’ll create meaningful change and growth. Reach out today for a free consult.

name: Kayla Saeteurn
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I provide online therapy for teens and adults experiencing anxiety, depression, eating-disorders, and family related concerns.
ideal_client: I support teens and adults navigating anxiety, depression, eating disorders, and family challenges. Many of my clients feel stuck or overwhelmed. I offer a compassionate, client-centered space to unpack what you’re carrying and begin healing. My approach is trauma-informed, strengths-based, and collaborative, helping you reconnect with your inner voice and find a sense of clarity, balance, and self-trust.

approaches.What I Specialize In: Anxiety and depression can feel isolating and heavy, often impacting every part of life. I specialize in helping clients manage emotional overwhelm, perfectionism, racing thoughts, and low mood. My approach blends Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Internal Family Systems-informed work, and mindfulness. I hold certifications in CBT for anxiety and depression, Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), Trauma-Informed Care, and Nonviolent Communication. Therapy with me is gentle, empowering, and personalized. We will explore underlying patterns and help you build tools for greater calm, clarity, and self-awareness.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a therapist because I believe in the power of being seen, heard, and supported during life’s hardest moments. My own healing journey shaped my belief that change begins with connection and self-compassion. I work with clients experiencing anxiety, depression, disordered eating, and family issues. I hold a B.S. in Psychology from Oregon State University and have completed certifications in Eating Disorder Intuitive Therapy (EDIT™), Mindful Self-Compassion, Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), CBT, and Youth Mental Health First Aid. I also hold training in cultural competence, trauma-informed care, and working with families. Therapy is not about fixing who you are—it’s about honoring your full humanity and helping you reconnect with your resilience.

name: Kimberly Crow
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with adults who are seeking a better understanding of self and are looking for relief from trauma, anxiety, depression or addiction.
ideal_client: Change is hard! Ambivalence is an expected part of any change process. Many people believe that ambivalences means not caring. But, what if it means caring too much and not being sure what direction to take in life? I work to help you navigate your ambivalence.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from an integrative perspective, combining aspects of person-centered therapy, Motivational Interviewing, Mindful Self-Compassion, and psychodynamic perspectives. My goal is to collaborate with you to create a clear direction in the therapy process. I want both of us to know what issues we are navigating in order to use our time together well. You will have a strong voice in your treatment plan. I support harm reduction practices for many individuals. Group therapy is a passion for me. I lead groups for early recovery support, family members of opiate addicts, and creative blocks. I seek to provide a respectful and safe space to work in together.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My practice is built around an idea I learned as an actor: "Really talk, really listen." This means I work to be present and connected so our dialogue is honest and authentic. I focus on treating co-occurring mental health and substance use problems and previously spent 5 years working in residential substance use treatment. I graduated from Lewis & Clark College with an MA in Professional Mental Health Counseling - Addictions. I completed further training in Trauma Informed Care at Portland State University.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: Motivational Interviewing is a collaborative conversation with a focus on evoking change. It respects an individual's personal autonomy while clarifying barriers to success. It is a way of working through the discomfort of ambivalence, a frenemy of the change process.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: My work is informed by many theoretical perspectives including Mindful Self-Compassion, Motivational Interviewing (MI), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), psychodynamic philosophies such as Object Relations and Attachment Theory, Gestalt, Existential-Humanist philosophies and specific trauma interventions such as Interpersonal Neurobiology, Somatic Experiencing and EMDR.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR is a highly effective, evidenced-based protocol for trauma and other difficulties. It helps the brain reorganize memories, connect the mind with physical sensations and associate new meanings to events. EMDR is not a substitute for therapy, and I require that individuals seeking have concurrent psychotherapy with me or an existing provider.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: It is easy to underestimate how debilitating it is to live with PTSD. I believe it is important to focus on developing the ability to self-regulate through understanding the effects of trauma on the brain and body. My goal is for you to feel more connected to yourself and others, and to feel worthy of living a full and meaningful life.

specialities.name: Early Recovery
specialities.description: So... you've just changed your life. Now what? Navigating the deep and murky waters of early recovery can feel treacherous. Connecting through individual or group therapy can help keep you afloat in this transitional time.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: There are days when getting out of bed feels impossible. Everything seems to have lost its color and vibrancy. A diagnosis of major depressive disorder doesn't fully account for the many ways people respond to feeling depressed. I see depression as having different 'flavors.' Some folks get sad, some irritable, some feel permanently stuck. I focus on prevention and recovery from depression.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Drug use often begins as a coping strategy, yet it can derail use of all other ways of managing life stress, mental health issues or low self-worth. Therapy can create space to explore the role drugs have taken in your life, and help you decide what you want to do about it.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: Drinking often begins as a coping strategy, yet it can derail use of all other ways of managing life stress, mental health issues or low self-worth. Therapy can create space to explore the role alcohol has taken in your life, and help you decide what you want to do about it.

name: Kelley O'Gorman
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Kelley and I offer an non-judgmental, warm, kind and humorous space for exploration and life skill development.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I will always start with your strengths so you have a foundation to build from. I use a Narrative approach, then look at Family Dynamics and then Evidence Based Skills that we tailor to you. I am all about building your confidence and resiliency in coping with your life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I was a business gal once, I worked in advertising & at Nike building Niketowns. After the birth of my first child I became more interested in the ever changing brain. So I went back to graduate school. My focus was Marriage and Family Therapy as well as Addictions. Over the years it has become relationship therapy with specialties in: Depression, Anxiety, Relationships, Self Confidence, Skills & Goals.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: I am a believer in hearing yourself tell your story. Many times it has been in our mind for so long, that hearing it out loud it pretty powerful. Sometimes even funny to realize what you've been telling yourself. I am curious about your internal dialog. Is it happy & healthy? What we think becomes how we act & resond.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I offer a non-judgemental approach with a safe place to explore what you need to. I practice mindfulness myself and believe it's within all of us.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: When we look into your family system we are given the information that created your world view. You learned to be you - from your family of origin. This helps us find where the glitches may have been & then we can work on healing.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I am a Marriage & Family Therapist by education which looks at Family dynamics within context. This helps look at patterns, themes and solutions.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: I think we all have a tinge of codependency. The reason I work with is so often is many clients come from a background where codependency helped them survive. My goal is to break that habit & learn to love you.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is contagious - really. It's the emotion that we are most likely to absorb without realizing it. So most of us have some degree of anxiety. I can help develop skills that are scientific and relatable, so anxiety isn't prevelant in your world. I'm all about natural & skill based options to combat anxiety. I use my own skills and they work!

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: It's a pervasive and silent thing- depression. I've lived with it myself and have researched it for years.

name: Elizabeth Ellisan
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Individual and group therapy for LGBTQIA+ teens and young adults.
ideal_client: I'm passionate about helping adolescents and young adults in the queer community learn how to manage anxiety, navigate identity, and work with their brain. When we are growing into adulthood each day presents changes and new challenges. This constantly changing landscape can fill you with paralyzing dread and fear – therapy can help.

approaches.What I Specialize In: It is my goal to provide a safe, compassionate, and open space for you to navigate through life changes, identity changes, anxiety, panic, and past trauma. I can help with finding your voice and identity, coping with the impending sense of doom that comes with life changes, and identifying skills to move through anxiety and panic. It takes courage to begin therapy, even at the best of times. When you find the space, I hope you reach out and we can work together to find and maintain your personal sense of peace.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from a mindful, humanistic foundation. This means that you can expect my nonjudgmental attention to the present moment and a deep respect for your personal experience. I believe that you are the expert on your own life, and I believe you have the power to change the things that are no longer serving you, even when that change feels out of reach. I often use mindfulness techniques to help you remain in the present moment so that you can get the most out of your session. I incorporate creative interventions into therapy including pens, pencils, paintbrushes, games, and movement.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: At the point you are seeking professional services for your anxiety, it is impacting your life in big ways. Anxiety can be your best friend and your worst enemy. Anxiety can help you complete seemingly insurmountable work loads. Anxiety can prevent you from engaging in your life. I help clients find peace through identifying strengths and introducing new ways to cope with challenges.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have extensive training and experience working with teens and young adults. Adolescence is a period of stress; both for teens and the family members that love them. With stress comes growth and teens are growing a lot! They are managing day to day life and developing personally, cognitively, and emotionally. I enjoy supporting family and teens navigating this important life transition.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I love working with couples navigating the ways their relationship is changing over time. It is my goal to provide a safe, compassionate, and open space for you and your partner to identify what is working in your relationship and what isn’t. Seeking couples counseling is an incredibly vulnerable process and I strive to create a space where you feel safe to explore the tender parts of a relationship you’ve been nurturing for a while with your favorite human.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a member of the LGBTQIA+ community, I know how hard it is to find a therapist who is the right fit. I can offer a supportive, affirming environment regardless of sexuality, gender, and primary concern. I can help with identity exploration, coming out, microaggressions, and other aspects of a queer experience. I have training and experience working with trans and non-binary individuals, including teens and their families.

name: Morgan Fitz Gibbon
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I’ve been working with queer, kinky, nonmonogamous, and sex worker folx for a decade.
ideal_client: My clients do things differently. Their relationships, their identities, the things they’re passionate about are outside the norm. They find themselves feeling like outsiders, even with people they’re close to. Sometimes they’re rejected by people they love. Often they’re invalidated by society at large. Sometimes they have a sense that something about them is different from everyone else but they can’t put their finger on what it is.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist - OR T1128 Founder - Rebel Heart Therapy Crisis Intervention Team Member - Burning Man Emergency Services Former Clinical Supervisor - Lewis & Clark Counseling Ctr Approved Supervisor - American Association of Marriage and Family Therapy Master of Arts in Clinical Psychology, LGBT Affirmative Psychology Bachelor of Arts in Psychology and Deaf Studies I absolutely love what I do to help my clients because I’ve been there. I’m queer, kinky, and have 20 years of experience in ethically non-monogamous relationships. My life has been a zig-zaggy line with a whole lot of challenges in my path. From figuring out myself to my relationships with others I’ve gone through it. Because I couldn’t find therapists who understood what I was going through, I put in a lot of work and research to get educated on how to help myself. I became a therapist because I didn’t want anyone else to experience the bad therapy I had. I want to share with you what I’

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have been working with poly and open relationships for a decade and have two decades of lived experience in ethically non-monogamous relationships. Whether you've just started talking about opening up, struggling with jealousy, in a conflict with a metamour, or navigating complex relationship issues within your polycule I'm here to help.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: My graduate training focused on LGBT Affirmative Therapy. Affirmative psychotherapy works to heal the wounds of internalized homophobia, biphobia, or transphobia that can be an underlying cause for depression, anxiety, substance abuse, unsafe sex, relationship or intimacy problems and other difficult challenges faced by many LGBTQ individuals.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I have been working with clients with Gender Dysphoria for a decade. I have attended several specialized trainings for working with gender identity issues before and during that time. I have experience supporting individuals and families who are navigating the transition process and I'm able to write letters in support of your process as needed.

name: Kelsey Papadatos
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hello! My name is Kelsey and thank you for taking the time to read a bit about me during your search for a therapist!
ideal_client: I specialize in working with folks to heal the short and long term impacts of trauma of any kind. I center my approach around a culturally and identity-affirming lens, always in effort to consider how systems of oppression and harmful societal scripts could be impacting day-to-day lives and in turn, a person’s mental health. I enjoy working with adults, people navigating the systems and institutions that we live within, LGBTQIA+ folks, and those navigating difficult transitions in life.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker and have a Masters in Social Work, as well as a bachelors in both psychology and sociology. Since starting as a therapist, I have continued my learning and was trained in EDMR in 2023. I work from a trauma-informed, strengths-based, and culturally-affirming lens to consider how the systems clients live within affect how they interact with the world. I am passionate about working with folks living with the long and short term affects of complex trauma, LGBTQIA+ population, and young adults navigating difficult life transitions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: No matter where you are in your healing journey, finding a new therapist can be overwhelming, so my goal is help cultivate a safe environment to best meet your goals and needs. I like to show up in the therapy space with warmth, humor when appropriate, transparency, and authenticity in effort to create a genuine and safe therapeutic relationship.

name: Katherine Alexander
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Life can be adventurous. Offloading burdensome baggage is essential. I help my clients pack the right for their life's journey.
ideal_client: Families, couples and individuals seeking new ways of relating to themselves and others. Those wanting to improve their approach and response to life's adventures. My clients are creative, curious and courageous in their approaches to daily living. They seek healing and personal growth so that they can show up ready for whatever adventure is next. Note: All new client inquiries are currently being handled through the "Schedule Now" option. https://foragewellnesscollective.com/schedule-online

approaches.My Background and Approach: I like people. Teacher, coach, cross-cultural worker, and ministry leader are all career hats I have worn over the years. I grew up in a large family and understand the challenges that families face daily. For a decade I lived and worked outside the U.S. in different parts of Asia and Africa. I have learned to think globally and to appreciate ways of thinking, living, and worshiping beyond my own. Some of my clients include: -Those who want to change the trajectory and legacy of their families. -Couples who want to better understand themselves and their partners. -Those who are preparing for and adjusting to a new cultural context. -Helping professionals such as teachers, nurses, ministry leaders, etc. -Those who are curious about personal growth and healing.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: A little bit of support can go along way. I consider working with families, couples, and individuals to be sacred. Providing a safe and non judgemental space for others to explore their past, present and future is a privilege. When I am not with clients I enjoy cooking, hiking, gardening, family time, and adventures.

specialities.name: Immigration/Acculturation
specialities.description: Are you preparing to go work and live in a new culture? Are you returning from another? Needing to process the challenges unique to your experience? Let's talk.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I'm open, are you? This is an ideal place to ask questions. Verbalize doubts. Heal from past experiences and find a new way forward.

name: Israa Al-Hasani
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a trauma therapist with sixteen year of experience practicing multicultural and intercultural counseling.
ideal_client: I believe in therapy as a mutual journey of healing and discovery, where both client and therapist grow together. I specialize in working with refugees, immigrants, their first-generation children, and individuals with LGBTQIA2S+ identities. My clients have genuine desire to explore their authentic selves despite having navigated complex trauma, cultural displacement, or identity-based discrimination, they are ready to engage in deep, transformative work towards liberation.
