approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have both a Bachelor’s Degree a Master’s Degree (MSW) in social work, and I am licensed as a clinical social worker (LCSW). I have studied mediation and have had years of education at the Summer Institute of Intercultural Communication. More recently, I have acquired skills in the somatic, body-mind area of counseling: NeuroAffective Touch and Rubenfeld Synergy. These methods integrate conscious insights with unconscious discoveries that are communicated by the body when encouraged by awareness and gentle touch. I believe in this powerful type of treatment and see it as an adjunct to regular counseling work. For more information, please visit my web site at http://www.pravdacounseling.com

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I use Rubenfeld Synergy and Nueroaffective Touch, body-mind therapy methods that uses your body as the starting point, because your body is home to your thoughts, feelings, and your spirit. Touch heightens awareness both physically and emotionally and allows the exploration of levels of self-knowledge that are difficult to access through either talk or touch alone.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: My therapy approach is to use tools from several best practice therapy models, depending on my client’s issues and needs. Such models include Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Narrative Therapy, Rubenfeld Synergy, and Mindfulness Based Practices. For more information about my areas of focus, visit the Areas of Focus page at http://www.pravdacounseling.com

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: One of my central areas of focus over the past twenty years has been the empowerment of women and girls, and I have worked in many nonprofit organizations in the field. Recurring themes with which I have experience include gender dynamics in relationships, power relations between women, and family pressures, particularly on work/family/self development.

specialities.name: Domestic Abuse
specialities.description: I have worked in the domestic violence field and have extensive training in how relationship violence impacts a person. I also have taught Career Counseling at a community college. I love the excitement of helping people explore their dreams and link them to practical resources, drawing a map for how to get there.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: In addition to traditional talk therapy for issues such as self-esteem, I have studied Neuroaffective Touch and Rubenfeld Synergy, forms of treatment that enable clients to listen to the messages of the body and to bring awareness, understanding, relief, and transformation to their lives. This happens through gentle touch and reflective listening in a safe, supportive environment.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I specialize in the immigrant and refugee experience, and have worked for over twenty years as a cultural worker. As a first-generation Russian-American, I am able to understand and help individuals and families with tools to cope with depression, anxiety, post-traumatic stress disorder, acculturation shock, and other issues related to immigration.

name: Lori Eckel
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hello, I'm glad you're here. I specialize in supporting people impacted by serious illness, grief and loss or facing end of life.
ideal_client: I specialize in caring for people impacted by serious illness, grief and loss, caregiving, end of life and compassion fatigue. Together, we will connect you to your values, priorities, and sense of meaning in how you live, care, and/or work. The liminal (“in between”) space of serious illness and end of life can feel lonely or isolating. Counseling offers a space to contemplate wholeness, values, purpose, and relatedness to oneself and others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have trust in your ability to find healing and connection to your own sense of possibility, power, and choice whatever your circumstances might be. We can work together to discover meaning in living and dying, and to connected to what is most important to you. I bring a trauma-informed, anti-oppressive, anti-racist approach in my work and aim to be responsive and to affirm people of all races, genders, ages, abilities, and identities. There are many forces that contribute to health disparities and inequity. I bring mindful awareness to the way these experiences create vulnerability.

specialities.name: Cancer
specialities.description: I work with people facing new diagnosis, disease progression or recurrence, or navigating the experience of cancer survivorship. I have worked with people facing blood, tissue and solid organ cancers with specialty experience in gynecologic cancer and brain tumors.

specialities.name: Family Caregiving
specialities.description: I work with individuals and families to navigate the complex landscape of caregiving. Together we can explore the meaning for you in your caregiving experience as well as the strain in mind, body, or sprit, that may accompany this experience. I help you to process the shifting relational experience and expectations with your care receiver as well as create space to consider your own well being while you care for others.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I work with individuals experiencing their own loss of self, identity and function resulting from the illness experience as well as family members as they grieve the loss of their important other due to serious illness.

specialities.name: Alzheimers
specialities.description: I support individuals and families across the trajectory of Alzheimers and/or dementia. At early stage I help to process the newer diagnosis, participate in advance care planning activities and consider goals in care as well as help to anticipate changing care needs. As the disease progresses I help to facilitate dignity restoring or preserving interventions and support family members to manage the changing landscape of care needs.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: I provide support to health care workers impacted by the cumulative effects of caring and experiencing their own suffering. I also provide critical incident stress debriefing. I help health care providers to identify their own professional values, orientation, identity and connect to their own moral compass as they face compassion fatigue, burnout or moral distress.

name: Sakura Counseling
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Sakura Counseling is for people searching for a safe space to heal relationships and achieve new levels of awareness.
ideal_client: At Sakura Counseling, we aspire to create an environment that is all inclusive and provides a safe space for diversity in all forms to untangle the challenges that have been holding you back from being authentically you. We are collaborative in our approach, holding high regard for your experience in your environment, paying close attention to the many systems of our society that play a part in perpetuating oppression.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: We believe in creating collaborative healing relationships where your therapist will work with you to figure out the changes you want to make, then create an attainable, realistic plan of healing. We will then prepare you for the changes to come and develop tools needed to successfully integrate those changes into your current environment. We believe that you are the expert of your experiences and needs, so throughout our collaboration, we aim to allow you to feel free of guilt and shame and safe to be wholly, authentically you as you gain strength of understanding, while building new methods to cope and overcome.

approaches.Our Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a group practice, we have the ability to provide therapy for most issues with specialized areas of Trauma, Social Justice, Mutli-cultural concerns, Anxiety, Suicide, Grief and Loss, Domestic Violence, Couples Relationship Repair...just to name a few. We work with all ages and all walks of life without judgement and thoroughly enjoy working with individuals, couples and families. To find out more about our team go to sakuracounseling.org. We currently have one counselor, Nancy, who works with Moda. All other counselors are OHP, Cigna, Kaiser, Reegence and OOP only.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Having training in attachment theory serves as a solid foundation for understanding client’s development of maladaptive coping strategies and how this relates to the client’s emotional difficulties. Using this therapy, we can help clients increase self-compassion and kindness because clients who have attachment disorders/wounds often develop a negative self-view of themselves and others.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: We have seen the benefits of deep work to heal trauma and various other human concerns. It helps individuals accept, regulate, express, & bring awareness of the complexity of human emotions. Understanding emotions help guides us to our needs or wants.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Our clinic employs Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) to guide clients in embracing their emotions, clarifying values, and committing to positive actions. Through mindfulness and acceptance techniques, clients learn to manage distress, cultivate psychological flexibility, and align their actions with their values, ultimately leading to improved well-being and a more fulfilling life journey.

specialities.name: Coronavirus/COVID-19
specialities.description: Our clinic is a beacon of support, aiding clients in managing the anxiety stemming from the multifaceted challenges posed by the pandemic. Our services address the anxiety related to COVID-19, offering a safe & empathetic space for clients to voice their concerns & fears. We help you develop coping strategies that empower you to navigate the uncertainties related to health concerns. We help individuals facing disabilitly-related concerns due to the long term effects of covid & social isolation.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Victims often feel they are being degraded and often don’t feel their abusers see their innate worth as a human being. The abuse often centers around control and they will use many harmful techniques to maintain and/or gain control over their victims. Our clinicians have training and experience working with all forms of abuse and together we can create a safe space for you and break the cycle of violence.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Conflicts may arise at any stage in a relationship. Sometimes these conflicts grow in complexity despite our best efforts to resolve them on our own. Whether you’re a in new relationship, married, or facing separation, we can work with you to navigate and resolve the challenges you are facing. Our counseling clinic restores relationships through expert guidance, fostering understanding, effective communication, and renewed emotional connection.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Death & bereavement are universally inescapable events that we all have faced. Individuals may experience suicidal thoughts, numbness, or the disconnection, which often interferes with daily activities. What we do with the grief transition either gives us strength or hinders us from fulfilling our goals. Our counseling clinic offers compassionate support for loss and grief, providing a safe space to process emotions, cope with the pain, and find ways to heal and rebuild life after loss.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Healthy anxiety keeps us stay alert, tune into our surroundings, and does not interfere with our lives. Unhealthy anxiety is present even if there is not a perceived threat. It disrupts your life, & creates isolation. We firmly believe that you are unique, deserve a plan that is realistic, & will result in the highest level of recovery. Our clinic offers effective anxiety support through therapy, coping strategies, and personalized guidance, helping you regain control and find relief.

name: Natascha Yogachandra
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: MS, NCC, Certified Body Trust® Provider
intro: Providing liberatory and relational support to those wanting to reconnect to their bodies & Self.
ideal_client: My clients are often searching for ways to connect to their own Self and body, as well as others around them. This connection may have been ruptured by anxiety/depression, illness or disability, a loss, trauma, and/or oppression in its various forms. I often work with folks who are navigating changes and transitions, or with those who live on the borders of multiple marginalized identities.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe our work together is collaborative, and that you are the expert of your own experience. I view your coping mechanisms as wise strategies that your body has relied on over the course of your life. Together, we can examine these strategies, explore if there’s anything that might work differently/better, and introduce more choice into your internal landscape. I often rely on somatic practices, and look to your body as a powerful messenger. Even if your connection to your body feels severed or damaged, we will work to repair that line of connection at your own pace. I also draw guidance from Internal Family Systems, which views our inner system as a collection of parts that protect our core Self. I am firmly grounded in a decolonized approach to therapy, and will often address the external and oppressive systems that impact your well-being.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Brown, biracial, queer, woman living with chronic illness and disability. I grew up in both the US and in Asia. I experience the world in a marginalized body, while also holding many privileges (cis-gender, formally educated, US citizenship, midsized.) I do not believe in the “blank slate” therapist, and will always welcome conversations about how our identities (whether they overlap or differ) impact our work together. I have my own personal relationship with various forms of trauma, and have intimate awareness of the messy work it takes to experience our own path of recovery. I deeply believe in harm reduction and mutual aid. I am particularly interested in our relationships with our own bodies, and the way in which these relationships are affected by chronic illness, anti-fat bias, white supremacy, and capitalism. I recognize I am still learning and growing—and always will be—and I am committed to further grounding myself in anti-oppressive practices.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I've spent over a decade experiencing mysterious symptoms, experimenting with various treatments, and navigating our medical systems. I deeply know the frustration, fear, and complex grief of chronic pain and illness. While there is no way to fully understand each person's unique experience with illness and disability, my personal experience informs the way in which I hope to support others through their own acceptance and finding their own agency in the face of various health challenges.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: I am a certified Body Trust® Provider through the Center for Body Trust. My approach to body image concerns begins with examining and grieving all the messaging we have received about how our bodies should be and how they should look. With deep compassion, I work to create a space in which you can move at your own pace, reconnect with the deep wisdom of your body, and restore the feeling of being at home in your body.

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: As a mixed race woman, I am very familiar with feeling like an outsider. I moved around a lot growing up-I always desired to blend into my surroundings, but was never quite able to. Our relationship with our own racial identity is a complex one, deeply impacted by the micro- and macro-communities we live in. Our work together will be rooted in curiosity and compassion, allowing space to explore what your racial identity means to you, and leave behind narratives that don't serve you anymore.

name: Cassie Cole
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I work from a deeply integrative, person-centered, and holistic approach. We will collaborate together to curate the best plan of healing.
ideal_client: I have experience working with individuals of all ages and concerns, particularly children, couples and families. Growing up in a large family with 8 siblings and working as a nanny has allowed me a unique sensitivity to family dynamics and a strong understanding of the importance of supportive relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I hope to create a strong, collaborative, and egalitarian therapeutic relationship with my clients ensuring they feel heard, and respected throughout the process. I foster awareness and growth in the present moment, helping people explore how their life experiences have shaped their emotional worlds while striving towards forward movement with clarity and confidence. To create lasting transformation, I emphasize the interconnectedness of emotional, physical, and spiritual health. By showing up authentically with warmth and curiosity I work to honor a safe space for exploration, using humor and empathy to guide clients toward their goals.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am interested in helping people navigate their personal and relational challenges, always meeting them where they are at with constant humility and a willingness to remain teachable. I know by my own experience finding a therapist is confusing , frustrating and more difficult than it needs to be. I can’t possibly put all you need to know about me as a therapist (I sure wish I could) in these little boxes. I encourage you to try a few sessions out and decide how you feel after that. I will always support what’s best for you. And if you made it this far in the profile I look forward to working with you!

name: Vanessa Servellón
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I’m a Latina bilingual therapist and use she/her pronouns. I specialize in trauma, anxiety, body image issues and immigration evaluations.
ideal_client: Are you needing a space to process emotions and experiences? Are you feeling nervous, anxious or struggling to cope with your worries? Have you experienced trauma in your life and noticing it affecting your life today? Are you wanting to improve your relationship with food and/or your body? Maybe you are wanting to discover more about yourself and how you navigate the world. In sessions, you can learn techniques or coping skills and dedicate time to your emotional wellbeing.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My practice focuses on supporting individuals who are struggling with their relationship with food and/or their body’s and trauma. For this work, I use a Health At Every Size (HAES) and trauma informed lens. I believe it’s important to allow time to process experiences, learn coping skills and also how to find healing in a way that aligns with you and your values. We'll also explore how different parts of yourself can impact you in different life experiences. My practice is culturally sensitive, gender affirming and welcoming to all body sizes. I work through a holistic approach where I believe in including your whole self in therapy, which includes the mind-body connection, your background, values, beliefs, identity and any other important aspects that make up who you are. I believe that in order to experience the benefits of therapy, you have to connect and feel understood by your therapist. That’s why I value feedback through the therapy process. Every therapist has a different a

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Ever since I discovered the positive impact therapy can have, I became passionate about supporting others through their journey. Working on your mental health is a lifetime process. That’s because over time, you change and continuously go through different experiences. And some of these can even have long lasting effects on your emotional and mental health. Therapy can offer you a safe space to process these experiences, discover more about yourself and how you navigate the world, learn techniques & coping skills and dedicate time to your emotional wellbeing. It’s not easy to tell someone else about your experiences and emotions, it requires you to be vulnerable. I know what it can be like to step into the therapy world. It can be scary, but I

name: Angelica Nenchev
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a BIPOC therapist using somatic & talk therapy to help you work through barriers to connecting to your authentic self.
ideal_client: Are you needing insight on your barriers to growth and fulfillment? Or maybe you've cultivated insight and need support with what to do with it? I work with a variety of mental health and relational concerns using a collaborative, somatic-based approach. I am passionate about helping my clients let their insights settle into their bodies and relationships so that their changes are sustainable and holistic. My clients are curious about what life beyond survival-mode is like.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I specialize in substance abuse, eating disorders, relational issues, trauma, and oppression-based difficulties. I utilize an attachment-based, relational approach to explore your struggles in the context of your personal relationships and larger social structures. You can expect our sessions to be collaborative, compassionate, and culturally-affirming. I teach somatic-based skills to help integrate our work into the rest of your nervous system. I am trained in Somatic Experiencing (SE)-- a body-based approach for healing trauma. SE integrates the fields of physiology, psychology, ethology, biology, neuroscience, indigenous healing practices, and medical biophysics to release compressed traumatic energy in the body slowly over time. I supplement my somatic work with interventions from Acceptance & Commitment Therapy (ACT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), and Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT).

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I identify as an able, cis-gender biracial female. I am guided by cultural humility and enjoy working with people of all identities. I believe therapy should be a safe space for you to talk about and feel anything that arises at your own pace. My approach is guided by the principles of anti-oppression and social justice, so we will naturally address contextual circumstances that interfere with your sense of belonging and self-worth. I believe individuals grow through their relationships and are doing their best with the tools they have to adapt and respond to their environments. In my work, I help clients understand and appreciate the adaptations that have kept them alive, while also supporting the discovery of other options that promote choice, flexibility and empowerment.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Somatic Experiencing (SE) is a body-based approach for healing trauma. Trauma usually occurs when there’s too much happening, too fast, too soon. This can leave us feeling powerless, resentful, and stuck in unhelpful patterns that may be too rigid or too chaotic. SE techniques help the nervous system to discharge traumatic energy that gets stored in the body so you can move beyond survival mode.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: We live in a culture that constantly promotes dieting and fat-phobia. If you want a more peaceful and easy relationship with food or your body, counseling may help you explore the unhelpful beliefs and behaviors that get in the way. My eating disorder work is informed by the Health At Every Size (HAES) & Body Liberation frameworks.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Thinking about changing your relationship with substances? I’m happy to support you along the spectrum of change from questioning to long-term recovery. I believe you get to define your recovery goals whether that be harm reduction or sobriety.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma is more than a one-time event. It is the impact an experience (or multiple experiences) has on your wellness. Trauma causes disruptions to our cognitions, memory, body chemistry, relationships, expectations, and self-perception. I believe trauma can be transformed through therapeutic relationships thats support resilience and flexibility.

name: Cathy Wenberg
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Licensed Clinical Social Worker with a focus in supporting people struggling with chronic illness, grief, and life transitions.
ideal_client: My clients are people struggling with a variety of life's challenges. You may be overwhelmed by the emotional toll of chronic illness, disability, or caregiving, or struggling with the complexities of loss—whether from the death of a loved one or the end of a relationship. I help clients navigate these challenges, offering support as they find a way forward and regain a sense of control, purpose, and healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With over 20 years of experience supporting individuals navigating the complexities of life, I deeply understand the emotional and psychological impacts that accompany periods of change and transition. I utilize a strengths-based and person-centered approach to highlight each person's unique lived experience and capabilities. Through Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and psychodynamic interventions, I aim to help you build healthier thought patterns, cope with emotions, and address deeper-rooted issues that contribute to your overall distress. Life’s transitions, whether expected or unexpected, can be uncomfortable. However, with the right support, these moments can become opportunities for profound transformation. I look forward to supporting you as we explore the strengths and solutions that can help you lead a more fulfilling life, even in the face of life’s challenges.

name: Laura La Rosa
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Lets work collaboratively to strengthen the emotional intelligence you already have. We will craft an affirming narrative that supports YOU!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Life circumstances can feel overwhelming and bigger than us. As parents and adults we can feel stuck and unable to access our wiser selves to accomplish what we want for our children, ourselves and in relationship to others. As teens, we can get bogged down with expectations and feel like we are sinking. Navigating with-in our comfort zone can sometimes hinder our emotional and relational growth. Your growing awareness of these conditions that hold you back will inform our work together. I can assist you accessing your authentic self which may invite you to challenge old habitual patterns and ways of thinking. Our work together may also give you the insight and tools to skillfully navigate the circumstances in your life that you want to improve. Your relationship to yourself and others may deepen and you may start to create a positive life narrative. My goal is to co-create a space with you that is nurturing and informative so you can begin your exploration with curiosity and ease.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a licensed clinical social worker (LCSW) graduating with an MSW from Portland State University in 2012. I am seasoned therapist with over a decade of experience providing mental health services to children, adolescents, adults and families in urban and rural outpatient mental health clinics, community and residential settings. I am particularly drawn to working with adults and families impacted by depression, anxiety, grief, loss, trauma related conditions and everyday “circumstances” that get in our way. I am passionate about empowering clients to heal from historical and current conditions that hold them from the life they want. I utilize a variety of trauma informed attachment / narrative based interventions. I draw from a personal mindfulness practice with a wealth of lived and professional experience that deeply informs my relational approach to understanding and working with my client’s challenges. IF I DO NOT RETURN YOUR CALL WITH IN 3 DAYS, MY PRACTICE IS FULL.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: There is no better time than now to focus on a solution to your problem so that you can feel better sooner than later. I whole heartedly believe that you already have the innate capacity to solve your problems right now. Our work together will uncover what you already know so that you can move in the direction you want to go in your life. Lets get started it won’t take long.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: I have completed specialized training and practice in narrative based interventions. I empower my clients to explore their personal narrative, dis-empowering old story lines that no longer serve them ultimately encouraging them to craft a new narrative that embodies who they truly are. You are the navigator of your life and together will will identify a sustainable path to well being.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness based interventions invite us to examine what’s really happening in the moment that supports or hinders our well being. Mindfulness encourages working with unskillful habits and thoughts that keep us stuck and can reduce unnecessary suffering. I have embraced a mindfulness practice in my personal life for over 20 years and my practice informs my work with clients.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: It can be hard to live together under the same roof much less get along. I provide family therapy that can help members find their voice to advocate for their needs, understand one another, reduce conflict and maybe even help one another like each other again. Family therapy can help you discover the uniqueness of each family member so living together feels natural again.

specialities.name: Suicidal Ideation
specialities.description: I know that your thoughts of self harm are temporary. Your thoughts are not all of who you are, in fact they are one small part. Let’s work together to understand the pain that creates these thoughts and then lets create a new understanding about yourself that includes a positve narrative that supports who you really are. We are never our thoughts. Ever!

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: We are not our thoughts and we don't have to believe them. Body image struggles are likely attached to unskillful and habitual thinking. We can work together to dis-empower the habitual thoughts that hold you hostage. We can craft accurate thoughts that support your self esteem. Lets work collaboratively to improve your relationship to your body, mind and emotions.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma happens. It hurts. I can assist you in identifying historical or current circumstances that have caused you pain so that you might begin the process of dis-empowering the story lines that keep you stuck. From there, I can assist you in identifying a new narrative that is affirming and that supports your well being.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I provide individual therapy for teens and adults who are living with depression and other mood challenges. I understand that 'heavy' feeling that is all consuming and feels bigger than us. Let’s work collaboratively to identify the barriers and habitual patterns that keep you stuck and then develop a sustainable path forward incorporating your healing and improved well being.

name: Ashley Wilkins
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Feeling lost? Struggling to navigate these uncertain times? Unsure how to cope? I'm here to ​help.
ideal_client: Have you lost someone, experienced a significant change in your life, or find yourself feeling overwhelmed by what life has thrown at you? I’m here to support you in finding your new normal and help you feel less alone. As your therapist, I will work together with you to help you get from where you are to where you want to be. I specialize in issues of grief and loss, trauma, anxiety, sexual abuse, parenting, and overall life transitions.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am here to provide support and accompany you on your path toward healing. Healing is about more than just surviving, it’s about finding better ways to cope, acceptance and growth; and it can take time and extra support to get there. My therapeutic style relies on authenticity, empathy, and trust to provide a supportive environment for growth and change. I approach therapy as a collaboration and offer a space that is trauma-informed and free of judgement, recognizing the value and uniqueness of your life experience. I use clinical approaches like EMDR, psychodynamic theory, attachment-based therapy, mindfulness, and cognitive-behavioral interventions. I work primarily with adults but have extensive experience working with children, adolescents, and families; and have provided therapy in a variety of settings including schools, hospitals, and community mental health centers. I currently work exclusively through telehealth for clients based in Oregon or Illinois.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I'm passionate about what I do because of my own personal experiences with grief and coping with mental health challenges. Through my work I’ve been witness to the incredible resiliency of those who’ve experienced trauma; and a person’s capacity for growth and change when facing challenges. I rely on a systems lens that focuses on treating the whole person within their environment; because the truth is, problems don't exist in a vacuum. We are interconnected, shaped by our experiences: how we grew up, how we are treated, what access or barriers we’ve experienced, and whether we’re able to get our needs met. I consider all of this in determining how to treat the issues you bring to therapy. You are the expert on your life, and you get to set the pace and depth to which we work. Together we’ll identify and leverage your own inherent strengths to help you thrive.

name: Raina Moore
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Sometimes being a human being can be really hard. It can feel vulnerable asking for help. Just know, that people care and are here to help.
ideal_client: Feeling Overwhelmed? Anxious? Depressed? Like you've never quite fit in? Find yourself feeling stuck in a cycle? Perhaps a part of you knows that you are totally capable & yet have days where you just can't - that leaves you feeling defeated. I know how hard it can be to do your best and still struggle. As a neurodivergent queer therapist and a survivor, I get it and I want you to know, there still is hope. I work with folks to understand & help by providing assessments & resources within therap

approaches.What I Specialize In: I specialize in adhd, depression, anxiety, & trauma. Theories I use are Mindfulness, Trauma Informed CBT, EMDR, Somatic, Strength Based, Art & Inner Child Work. I work within a social justice lens, sex-positive lens, & health at every size lens. I work to create a safe space for the queer community, neurodivergent community, & fat community.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I grew up in foster care where I lived and moved into over twenty homes in the Midwest before I aged out of the system at the age of 21. I saw a lot of people suffer around me, including myself. I experienced different types of childhood abuse, trauma, and grief growing up. I also experienced systemic barriers from growing up in poverty, neurodivergent, existing as a plus-size (aka fat), and femme presenting person. I have learned a lot about suffering through my experience, my education, and my career. I know on a very deep level that it is possible to change your life, heal, and overcome. I would feel honored to help be apart of your process healing and growing.

name: Julie Kirchner
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Are you overwhelmed? I assist youth, adults, and families in navigating difficult times and improving overall well-being.
ideal_client: Are you in a family that is struggling to find its way? If so, I am glad you are here. Relationships can be a source of great happiness and also be a cause of unlimited hurt. Are your children struggling with family or life events? Are they having a hard time coping with changes? My goal is to help you or your child navigate your relationships and improve your overall well-being. I am here to help you reach your goals and enhance your objectives.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am here to listen and walk alongside you without judgment and help you work through life's many challenges. My goal is to create an atmosphere where you feel comfortable and safe. I use Strength-Based, Person-Centered, and Emotionally Focused therapies. I work with children, teenagers, adults, families, and couples with issues ranging from anxiety, depression, low self-esteem, grief, and difficult life transitions. I have strong foundational knowledge and have been trained in play therapy and parent-child relationships. I believe that everyone has the ability to heal, grow, and create a better life for themselves, and sometimes all they need is a little help.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a Marriage and Family Therapist, I bring experience in supporting children, families, and couples through a wide range of challenges. My personal journey as a wife and mother of four has deepened my understanding of the complexities of family life and the transitions that come with it. I have a strong interest in helping couples strengthen their relationships and navigate periods of change and transition. I am also deeply committed to working with children, providing guidance and support as they face emotional and developmental hurdles.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I enjoy helping families struggling with children and adolescent issues, from behavioral issues to feelings of depression and anxiety, to help them find ways to resolve their problems. I have training in play therapy for children as young as 3 years old. I also enjoy working with children who have physical or emotional disabilities. I'm here to help the child and family navigate through these difficult times that they may face.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Parenting can be hard on a couple's relationship. I can help you come together and parent on the same page while building stronger bonds with your children. I have additional training in parent-child therapy, and I am knowledgable in child and parent relationships and child developmental stages.

name: Stephanie Luz Hernandez
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Mental health provider and gender health specialist providing both in-person (PDX) and telehealth care.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with gender and sexual minorities, including transgender, non-binary, gender-expansive, and gender-non-conforming adolescents and adults. Many of my clients are navigating complex identities, internalized oppression, and experiences of marginalization. I also work well with folks exploring polyamory, kink, neurodivergence, family-of-origin dynamics, and creative expression. Whether you're feeling stuck, burned out, or yearning for deeper connection with yourself/others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My clinical work is rooted in gender-affirming care and extensive experience supporting LGBTQIA+ communities. I take a relational, trauma-informed, and liberation-centered approach to therapy. Together, we co-create a space of safety, empathy, and curiosity, allowing you to explore your story, heal wounds, and reconnect with your inner resilience. My focus is not on “fixing” you but on helping you access the internal tools you already hold. We work collaboratively to unpack anxiety, shame, gender dysphoria, early attachment wounds, or body disconnection, and to cultivate meaningful, lasting changes. I am a WPATH GEI SOC8 Certified Member.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Therapy, for me, is both personal and political. As a queer and trans therapist, I am committed to dismantling systems of oppression that harm our bodies, relationships, and sense of self. My practice is grounded in values of equity, bodily autonomy, and collective care. I support movements for trans liberation, racial justice, disability justice, and decolonial healing. Outside the therapy room, I’m a proud cat-lover and a synth music explorer, and creative practices that feed my spirit and remind me of the nonlinear beauty of healing. I believe everyone deserves access to affirming care, and it’s a privilege to walk alongside clients as they reclaim their voices and imagine new possibilities for themselves.

name: Ryan Harris
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi, I provide individual and family therapy to children, teens and adults. I provide both in person and virtual sessions. I have openings.
ideal_client: I enjoy providing individual and family therapy to a clientele of all ages and backgrounds. I work with clients who want therapy as a way to learn skills to manage symptomology or just need a safe space to discuss life stressors.

approaches.My Background: I have over 14 years of experience as a therapist working with children, families, adolescents and adults in multiple settings including inpatient, partial hospitalization and outpatient settings. From my experience I have came to understand that amazing change can occur when we are feeling the most stuck and hopeless. I also have special interest in working with people who identify as part of the LGBTQ community.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist I believe that my clients are the experts of their life. I enjoy collaborating with clients to identify and reach their goals such that they can feel successful in everyday life. I utilize a wide variety of therapeutic interventions including Motivational Interviewing, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Dialectical Behavioral therapy that are best tailored to my client’s individual needs. I believe strongly in the therapeutic relationship and that having an empathetic and validating person to discuss your concerns with can be healing within itself. However, while my style is empathetic, I also tend to be directive and will challenge my clients to explore different behaviors and thought processes that can lead to them reaching the goals that we have established.

name: Vedalia Zellers
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Providing individual & couples therapy to help you address old wounds, improve relationships, & experience life more fully.
ideal_client: If you're interested in addressing past trauma, exploring relationship patterns, and/or getting support for oppression and marginalization you face, we might be a good fit. I specialize in working with people who identify with oppressed groups, including clients who are disabled, chronically ill, neurodivergent, or adjusting to an injury or medical condition. I also work with couples looking to explore the roots of their interpersonal dynamic in order to open up possibilities for change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In individual therapy, my aim is to help you heal more deeply (from any loss, trauma, or pain that feels "stuck") by gradually traveling to places within yourself that you might be afraid to go. I hope that my accompaniment will make this task feel possible and that the rewards will be rich. In the process, you might discover a part of yourself – perhaps your capacity to play, rest, dream, grieve, be intimate, or receive care, for instance – that you buried long ago to survive. Recovering and reclaiming these parts, I believe, can help us feel more alive, expanding our sense of what is possible. In psychodynamic couples therapy, my aim is to help you understand how your history and your partner's history may contribute to the struggles you face today in your relationship. I'll encourage you to speak the truth to each other and examine any barriers that stand in the way. Deepening mutual understanding and compassion can help couples alter old cycles and find new ways forward.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I’m a white, queer, disabled woman with a lifelong visual processing disorder. Having a body and brain that differ from the so-called “norm” has led me to work, in concert with others, toward a more just and inclusive world. I bring an anti-oppressive lens to my work, meaning I recognize systems of oppression impact the mental health of individuals. Although we can’t “solve” wider issues of injustice within individual therapy, we can explore how those broader realities have affected you, and we can unpack “internalized” oppression (i.e., harmful beliefs you may have unintentionally absorbed). I'm influenced by disability justice: a framework of values developed by BIPOC, queer, disabled activists in the Bay Area which promotes the collective liberation of disabled people. Before becoming a therapist, I spent four years in rehabilitative healthcare working with survivors of Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) and eight years doing non-profit work including union and community organizing.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: We can curiously and non-judgmentally explore how relationship patterns from the past (for instance with parents/caregivers in childhood) may have impacted your relationship patterns in adulthood. This can pave the way for more self-compassion and more fulfilling connections with others. It may be especially relevant for people who have had a difficult relationship with a parent/caregiver or who've experienced trauma (including intergenerational trauma, complex trauma, or religious trauma).

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: People often want to "move forward" with their lives yet find themselves struggling with pain that carries an old, familiar signature (like feeling trapped, alone, judged, or overlooked to name a few examples). Day-to-day circumstances may feel extra bothersome if they remind us, on some level, of old wounds and buried emotions that are still vying for our attention. In therapy, we'll aim to co-create a space where it becomes possible to discover more about yourself and express the unexpressed.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: Whatever is on your mind can have a place in our therapeutic work. For some, this may sometimes include "big" questions. How do we find meaning and fulfillment? How do we make sense of human suffering? How do we grapple with death? Personal events (such as life transitions and losses) as well as global events (like climate change and genocide) sometimes lead people to ask big-picture questions, which you're welcome to bring to therapy.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: When relevant, I may draw on Dialectical Behavior Therapy skills to offer you concrete, practical strategies for coping with difficult situations. I interned with the Portland DBT Institute in 2021-22, where I co-led several therapy groups. Note: I'm not able to offer "full fidelity" DBT, but I might be a fit for clients who have recently graduated from a DBT program and would like some support in continuing to utilize DBT skills.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Learning to treat ourselves with gentleness and self-compassion can be one of the most powerful outcomes of therapy. I love working with people to improve self-worth and self-esteem, because I know it will serve them well for the rest of their lives, setting the stage for further growth and more vibrant relationships. This work can take many different forms, including unpacking old messages you may have received from your family or society and experimenting with new daily habits.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: Our unjust society affects people’s mental health on a daily basis. Depending on your identities, you may be coping with historical trauma, separation from family, unequal access to resources, negative judgments and assumptions from others, fewer opportunities, social exclusion, threats to your safety, hopelessness in the face of global injustice, and much more. In therapy, I'll invite you to bring in issues of any size. There's room to acknowledge and explore the complexity of your reality.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Losses happen not only when someone dies, but when we grow apart from someone, leave a community, reexamine our beliefs, give up on a dream, and more. Grief is natural, but the process can get interrupted when we believe we don't have the right to our feelings, maybe telling ourselves (or being told) that there's no point, or no time, or that other people have it worse. Acknowledging and working with our grief often helps it become "unstuck" and gives it permission to move through us.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Therapy is all about relationships, including your relationship to yourself, others, and any communities of which you are a part. Often, people's experiences of being hurt by others in past relationships interrupts their ability to form new connections that feel safe, joyful, and fulfilling. In therapy, we can work toward a deeper healing that paves the way for deeper connection.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I'm queer, and I enjoy working with queer, trans, and non-binary clients. Maybe you want to discuss barriers to coming out or transitioning, strain in family of origin relationships, religious trauma, or nervousness about dating. Maybe you want a place to celebrate your growth, self-definition, and efforts to build a life and relationships of your choosing. All of this and more has a place in therapy!

name: Michael Caylor
title: Student Counselor
intro: Hello! I look forward to getting to know you. Please check out my approach to helping to see if we would be a good fit for each other.
ideal_client: Using unconditional positive regard and empathy, I seek to collaboratively work with my clients to identify challenges and stressors related to anxiety, depression, and past traumatic experiences. My interests include working with adolescents, young adults, and adults to explore life’s many questions and problems.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that everyone is the expert of their own experience, and as your counseling intern and student, I am here to help you explore and achieve your goals in a way that makes sense to you. Our experiences shape us. They impact our view of self and our values, which can lead us to feel disconnected from self and others. I would love to sit down with you to get to know you and understand your life experiences in a way that values where you come from, and how you see the world. I view counseling as a collaborative process in which we will work together to address discomforts and focus on areas you want to grow in which can include your goals and aspirations. I want to help you address stressors and pain, while collaboratively developing solutions. It is my goal to provide you with a safe, comfortable, and non-judgmental environment as well as a genuine, positive, and empathetic relationship to work through these things. I am here for you and believe in your ability to grow.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Finding a counselor that works for you can be difficult! As a counseling intern and student, I will come to the meeting a blank slate with your best interest in mind. It is my goal to get to know you as best I can to help you identify and understand your emotions and experiences on a deeper level. This deepening of knowledge can help shift your perspective on your emotions, behaviors, and yourself. Then, together, we can determine if action is appropriate. If this sounds helpful or you would like to know more, please feel free to reach out for a free consultation. I look forward to seeing you!

name: Tracey Hoffman
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I am available for telehealth appointments and offer individual and couples therapy. I look forward to talking with you.
ideal_client: I am welcoming and affirming. I provide a safe space for your whole self to be accepted and to grow. I have worked with clients from a variety of backgrounds and cultures over the years and am a queer ally. Clients come in to address anxiety, mood, relationship challenges, and self-esteem. We might discuss unresolved earlier experiences and current patterns that have roots in the original family system, as well as impacts from challenging and/or traumatic events, attending to your strengths.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I specialize in individual and couples therapy for concerns such as anxiety, relationships family of origin issues, anxiety, self-esteem, depression, navigating change etc. I incorporate "Brainspotting" in my work, which is a technique similar to EMDR in terms of focusing your gaze while we're talking in order to help you process challenges and integrate healing at a deeper subcortical level (rather than solely from a more logical brain focus). We also work together in a typical therapy way to help you feel more resourced and process distress and stuck feelings/patterns etc.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a licensed Psychologist (previously licensed at the Master's level) and have been in the field over 25 years. I specialize in individual therapy with adults and couples therapy. I have taught graduate classes and supervise students, interns, and psychology residents. I continue to seek opportunities for learning and growth in this work that I love so much.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: Including Emotion-Focused, Gestalt/Hakomi, Relational and Attachment, and Contemporary Psychodynamic

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Studied neurobiology and emotions, DBT principles

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Advanced training in Emotion-Focused Couples Therapy

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Studied relationships and systems

name: Aleks Taylor
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Providing the queer, BIPOC, & neurodivergent community with mental health support, alongside psychedelic integration, via telehealth.
ideal_client: My clients are typically BIPOC, queer, and/or neurodivergent adults (ages 18-35) that are wanting to find support with depression, anxiety, trauma, neurodivergence, gender identity, struggles with self-esteem, bipolar disorder, adoption, religious trauma, systemic oppression, and/or psychedelic integration. Whatever you are going through at the moment, I will be here to walk with you and to support you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My practice is a combination of transpersonal and humanistic-relational therapy through an intersectional and harm-reduction lens. You can find out more about these models in the "specialties" section. My belief that you are the expert of your own life extends into the therapy room. I will work with you to foster an environment of safety and stability, where you feel comfortable working through whatever has brought you to therapy at this time. My hope is that you leave the therapy room with the feeling that you can navigate the world with confidence and authenticity, despite the challenges it throws at you. I also provide psychedelic integration. I approach integration from a holistic lens that works with all facets of your experience. All feelings about your journey are welcome here. I use theory and practice that is queer/trans affirming, neurodivergent-affirming, antiracist, sex and kink-positive, monogamous and non-monogamous relationship affirming, and person-centered.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As a therapist, I view my clients and their situations through an intersectional, social justice lens. This means considering all the societal factors that apply when addressing mental health concerns. Socioeconomic status, race, gender, age, sexual orientation, ethnicity, education, ability, and many more factors should all be considered in therapy, and when they are left out, those who are most vulnerable can slip through the cracks or get misdiagnosed. Together, we can work to address some of the root causes of suffering from external sources as we also work to build and maintain a healthier version of you, internally. When I'm not providing therapy, I spend time working with a racial equity group in the jam band scene as part of the BIPOC advisory committee and working as a volunteer trainer, supervisor, and integration coach for a psychedelic support line.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: Transpersonal therapy addresses mental, physical, social, emotional, spiritual, creative, and intellectual aspects. You are so much more than just your mind and body. Some therapies focus solely on how negative experiences have impacted you, but we will explore how joy and awe have also played a role in shaping who you are today. We can work on things beyond the physical world, as well. You are welcome to bring spiritual practices or rituals into our sessions, if you would like.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Humanistic therapy emphasizes the whole person. As a humanistic practitioner, I believe humans cannot be viewed as the sum of their parts or reduced to simple functions or individual parts of the self. As individuals, we are all unique beings and should be recognized and treated as such by therapists and the broader world.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Relational therapy is based on the idea that mutually satisfying relationships with others are critical and takes into account the ways in which social and familial factors relate to the relationships in your life. Together we will aim to build your sense of self and explore your agency, as well as building patience with and trust in others. I approach relationships of all structures with openness and care.

name: Joyce Korschgen
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We are an outpatient nature-based mental health clinic specializing in support for children, youth, adults and families.

approaches.What We Specialize In: Our mission is to provide services that improve personal well-being through facilitated contact and relationship development with nature. The Center at Heron Hill offers services for children, youth and adults. Our approach includes work with individuals, families, and groups. We are a group that varies greatly in training approaches. We operate off of a trauma-informed lens with a goal-focused practice. We utilize experiential therapy approaches such as hiking, archery, animal tracking, survival skills training, art and play, mindfulness, and animal-assisted therapies.

name: Mitchell Passadore
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi! I'm Mitchell! I'm a Professional Counselor Associate, here to support your mental health journey!
ideal_client: I enjoy working with all different populations but especially enjoy working with teens and young adults, people experiencing symptoms of anxiety, folks experiencing life transitions, and anyone experiencing men's specific issues.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I was trained in Portland at Lewis & Clark’s graduate school of education and counseling. I have specific training in treatment for anxiety disorders, PTSD, addiction, depression, and trauma utilizing principles of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Exposure Response Prevention (ERP), Motivational Interviewing (MI), Compassion Focused Therapy (CFT), and Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) in both individual and group settings.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that anyone can benefit from counseling and that no matter where a person starts, they deserve respect and care. I am here to help people live better lives and uncover patterns in thoughts and behaviors that might be causing distress. For this process to be most helpful, it is important to find someone who fits well with who you already are. My goal is to help facilitate positive, lasting change and I believe that there is a counselor out there who can help make that happen.

name: Abby Hall
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: A quirky, fun queer, east coast born dog parent, and therapist. Are you Ace, Poly, Queer.. This is the place for you!
ideal_client: I work with queer adult clients who come to therapy to process developmental or religious trauma and are working towards building a safer deeper connection with their identity, sexuality and self. I have a particular passion working with aro/ace clients as they navigate their identity, relationships, or understanding of a often under recognized sexuality.

approaches.My Background: I graduated with my Masters Degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from The George Washington University in Washington DC in 2019. Since then I have worked primarily in group practices working with wonderful clients all across the life spectrum. I worked with children and teenagers during my internships and early career, moving to adults from all walks of life later in my practice. While I have loved and learned so much from my clients throughout the years, I have become passionate about specializing my practice to working with queer adults, specifically those who are exploring their asexual and aromantic identities, as well as those who have histories with high demand religions or religious trauma.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide queer affirming sex therapy for adult individuals and couples who are wanting to explore their identity, sexuality or address sexual functioning concerns. I pull from attachment and trauma-based techniques in our sessions with the purpose of creating a better relationship with your self and body, and exploring your experiences with intimacy.

name: Kimberlee Harrison
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I specialize in anxiety, panic, trauma, identity exploration, grief, and Dissociative Identity Disorder (DID).

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I take an integrated approach to therapy that is tailored to each individual's needs. Collaboration is imperative for therapy to be effective, as I believe that every person is the expert of their life. Together we can work on empowering you to make the changes you want for your life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a Master of Science (MS) in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), a Certified Grief Informed Professiona (CGP), and a Level 2 Certified Clinical Trauma Professional (CCTP-II). I published a book in 2017 titled "Empowerment Through Mythology: A Clinician's Guide to Narrative Group Therapy for Survivors of Trauma and Abuse." I also have a YouTube Channel called "Mental Health Minute with Kim."

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I have extensive experience working with individuals who identify as LGBQTI+, addressing such issues as establishing their identity, coming out, transitioning, interpersonal relationships, discrimination, and oppression.

specialities.name: Dissociative Disorder (DD)
specialities.description: I have several years experience working with people who have dissociative disorders, particularly Dissociative Identity Disorder. I help clients work on cooperation and communication within their system, with a focus on safety.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I am a Certified Grief Informed Professional (CGP).

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have several years experience working with people who have PTSD and other trauma-related disorders.

name: Rachael Patoray
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide creative alternatives to help you explore, express, and heal...mind & body!
ideal_client: Trauma and previous life experiences are held within the body, not just in your brain! When you begin to notice that you no longer have control over the panic, anxiety, or other somatic symptoms. Your body is wise and deserves to be listened to. You deserve to be listened to...to be seen...and to be taken seriously! I work with female identified folks ages 18 and up and am LGBTQ+ affirming. I help folks regain their authentic voice, sometimes for the first time in their lives!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), and Registered Art Therapist (ATR),. I help clients identify and focus on their strengths using an IFS-informed Parts Perspective, Trauma-Informed Relational Therapy, Neurobiology Psychoeducation, and Person-Centered Approach. I employ the mind-body connection, apply Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, teach mindfulness techniques, review communication, address mood diagnosis, and use Art Therapy & Narrative Therapy. I provide a safe space to be heard without judgement and provide tools to make changes and to help folks get "unstuck". I have the pleasure of working with folks whose autoimmune systems have been affected or compromised, who are also struggling with physical illness, because of their trauma histories. I help clients understand the important connection between the body and the mind. I help my clients set down self-blame and help them focus on healing through self compassion and continued curiosity.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I'm a native Oregonian (though I've lived in many places, big & small, throughout the USA) but I'm happy to be back "home". I realized through my own journey, that art not only allowed me to express myself, but it allowed me to understand myself a little better too! I use art (as one modality) in my practice to help you do the same; to explore, understand, and heal. I do not expect artistic perfection, that is not what art therapy is about! It's about providing you another way to understand and express who you are, at any age! I'm also an animal lover and love witnessing my client's pets support them during processing work! I often encourage my clients to have their pets join them during sessions, for additional support! I received my Masters in Art Therapy/Counseling at Southwestern College in Santa Fe, NM. I'm a registered art therapist (ATR) and a licensed professional counselor (LPC).

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I employ an eclectic therapeutic approach that is tailored to your counseling needs. Some of the training and approaches I apply to our work includes but is not limited to: Art therapy, Brainspotting, grief/loss & trauma work, CBT, Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, IFS-Informed/Parts Work, Trauma-Informed Stabilization Treatment (TIST), and Trauma-Informed Relational Therapy.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: My professional training is in art therapy and I am a registered art therapist (ATR). Art therapy is about creating art in a therapeutic setting. The act of art making, as well as the art piece you create, will help you to explore and express yourself in a safe space. Creativity helps you tap-into and explore complex and overwhelming feelings and situations in a non-threatening way.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I apply Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, a trauma-informed somatic psychotherapy that combines traditional talk therapy techniques with body-centered interventions that directly address the somatic legacy of trauma; attending first to discover how the body remembered the trauma and then providing the somatic experiences needed for resolution.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Having a Chronic Illness can bring a whole other set of issues to ones life. I have the pleasure of working with folks whose autoimmune systems have been effected or compromised, who are also struggling with physical illness, (often) because of their trauma histories.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: The act of bullying (from others and oneself) seems to be existing at an all-time high. Self-esteem plays a huge role with the culture of bullying, both for 'the bullies' and their victims. Learning how to understand and accept ourselves instead of only comparing ourselves to others, is an important start to decreasing this culture of bullying and low self-esteem.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am certified in Trauma-informed stabilization treatment (TIST) which integrates techniques from internal family systems and sensorimotor psychotherapy, targeting clients with severe mental health challenges. I use Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, a trauma-informed somatic psychotherapy that combines traditional talk therapy techniques with body-centered interventions that directly address the somatic legacy of trauma.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can be debilitating, and my focus is to help explore what may be at the root of your anxiety symptoms and how to best help relieve these symptoms.

name: Liv Siulagi
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am a BIPoC therapist (she/her) trained in art therapy and CBT, with a strong background in intersectional feminism/ liberation psychology.
ideal_client: Struggling with anxiety, depression, or self-esteem? Life can be hard. On top of that, many of us have internalized messages, and learned relationship skills that make our lives even harder. If you would like change then we should talk. I work with adults providing telehealth mental health services and some in-person work for a variety of challenges such as: anxiety, depression, life transitions, living with oppression, and recovery from trauma.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I base my practice on Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, which means that during our sessions we will examine how your thoughts, emotions, and behaviors impact you. I ground this more "micro" with Liberation Psychology, basing my work on the belief that humans naturally strive for health and connection, but that we live in an oppressive society that limits our ability to heal from trauma, build lasting communities, and forge full, meaningful lives. Through compassion, open-mindedness, humility, accountability, authenticity, and my critical background in intersectional feminist theory I work hard to treat my therapeutic participants as equals: helping them develop insight, heal, and tune into their natural creativity.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As a mixed race (Samoan, filipina, and white), cis-woman raised in the primarily white city of Portland my lived experience of oppression and the privileged aspects of my identity have inspired me to examine my own role as an ally and advocate. In my final year at Lewis & Clark this interest led to a year-long research project focused on improving white allyship and avoiding performative activism in the field of art therapy. This work paired with my art advocacy, volunteer work with marginalized populations, and undergraduate research experience on sexuality has helped me dedicate myself to a reflective practice based in antiracism, liberation, and cultural humility.

name: Graham Sterling
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with individuals, couples and families. My specialty is strengthening relationships between partners and families

approaches.My Approach to Helping: It is my philosophy, that each of us are on a path that encompasses understanding who we are in relation to our surroundings. Answers are found through interpersonal connections and within ourselves. It is my job to offer a safe, supportive space and the skilled assistance that allows you to discover your strengths and the tools necessary to overcome life's hurdles.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have an MA in psychology and am a Licensed Professional Counselor.

name: Jodi Palensky
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Backed by science, fueled by heart. Meeting you where you are... from virtually anywhere.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with individuals and familes recovering from injury. I understand the complex challenges involved in recovery from moderate to severe brain injury, concussion, spinal cord injury, chronic illness, long-term COVID recovery, persistent pain, and other neurological or orthopedic injuries. Additionally, I work with people who are struggling with depression and anxiety, as well as individuals striving for personal growth.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Licensed in multiple states including Oregon, Nebraska, Alaska, Idaho, Illinois, Iowa, Maryland, Minnesota, New Mexico, North Dakota, Colorado, Michigan, Washington, Arizona, and Montana. I offer online psychology and counseling teletherapy services designed to connect your recovery plan to your home environment and help you heal, grow and re-engage with your life following life-changing events. I have worked with individuals and families recovering from tragedy for over 20 years. If you, your loved one, or your family is struggling to cope with and recover from significant life changes following an injury or illness, you are not alone. I am happy to support you during this challenging time to find ways to help you heal, grow, and re-engage with life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that we all have strengths, we all have the capacity for change and growth, and we all experience times of struggle. Acknowledging the struggle and reaching out for support and assistance requires courage. I honor that courage, and I feel lucky to be able to join people on their journey toward recovery from injury and illness, during times of personal struggle, and as they strive for their fullest potential.

name: Naomi Painter
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: When trauma creates unhelpful patterns and makes life decisions for us, it's time to seek help.
ideal_client: I am passionate about assisting those in helping professions, such as social services providers, healthcare professionals, social workers, educators, and, YES, therapists! Helpers are particularly susceptible to “burnout,” the effect of witnessing the trauma their clients and students are going through, while having only a limited scope of influence to affect the situation. I specialize in trauma, women's issues, life transitions, and anxiety. LGBTQ+ and poly-friendly.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Mindful, somatic experiential therapy: Hakomi is a form of sensorimotor psychotherapy (also called somatic therapy), consisting of guided self-study that uses mindfulness to access traumatic memories and harmful beliefs encoded in the body - those places in your body where you feel restless, uncomfortable, ill, or just plain “don’t go there.” Together, we will harness the power of mindfulness, creativity, curiosity, and presence to courageously dive in, unearth your pain, and reshape your experience of the world. Hakomi brings together the wisdom of Buddhist and Taoist teachings with modern scientific findings on how the brain changes itself through experience, not just talking about it.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Before becoming a counselor I was a family support worker and program manager for a home visiting program serving first-time parents, a special education paraeducator, a school counselor at the elementary, middle, and high school level, a case manager and program manager for a grant serving veterans experiencing homelessness, and an Aging and Disability case manager. My 15 years in social services and education gave me me a view of the rich tapestry of human experience, and a deep understanding of the toll working in the helping professions can take on people.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: Hakomi is a form of somatic therapy consisting of guided self-study that uses mindfulness to access traumatic memories and harmful beliefs encoded in the body - those places in your body where you feel restless, uncomfortable, ill, or just plain “don’t go there.” Hakomi brings together the wisdom of Buddhist and Taoist teachings with modern scientific findings on how the brain changes itself through experience, not just talking about it.

specialities.name: Sensorimotor
specialities.description: Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, an outgrowth of Hakomi method, dives deeper into the neurological and physical effects of trauma. Sensorimotor psychotherapy (SP) is a holistic approach to healing trauma or unhealthy attachment patterns formed in early childhood. It integrates the body and movement into traditional talk therapy to address and heal ongoing psychological and physical difficulties, and is considered a “body-centered talking therapy."

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I employ approaches from Relational Life Therapy, established by Terry Real (The New Rules of Marriage), as well as from Stan Tatkin (Wired For Love), Martha Kauppi of the Institute for Relational Intimacy, and Esther Perel.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: I have worked in case management for many years and am passionate about assisting those in helping professions, such as case managers, outreach workers, home visitors, and educators. Burnout, compassion fatigue, and secondary trauma come with the territory.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma doesn’t only come from the battlefield. A difficult childhood, a coercive or conflict-filled relationship, a toxic workplace, a natural disaster, an assault, a death, the loss of a friend or a support network…these things can shape our thinking, our behavior, and our well-being long after we’re supposed to be “over it.” If you’re not sure if you have experienced trauma, reach out and we can explore it together.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: It’s tempting to believe that we can leave our past behind, isn’t it? But our childhoods dictate so much about our adulthoods - who we choose as partners, the jobs we take, the places we go, and where we feel safe. The body holds on to it all. Perhaps it was the way you were parented, or living through multiple moves or displacement, being bullied or isolated, caretaking for a parent or sibling as a child, significant loss, or living in poverty.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships are hard. Even when things are outwardly going well, you may have a sense of dis-ease and doubt, or you may not be sure whether this is a healthy relationship. Talking with friends will only go so far. I can help you listen to yourself and elevate your partnership, even if your partner is not accompanying you.

specialities.name: Anxiety
