specialities.description: Anxiety is often a reaction to unresolved trauma, and it is our body and mind's way of trying to keep us safe. Somatic therapy helps uproot the traumas held in our bodies and thoughts and reduces the grip of anxiety on our behaviors and decisions.

name: Brian Hannah
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Licensed clinical social worker dedicated to empathetic, inclusive therapy, supporting queer identities and non-monogamous relationships.
ideal_client: I am honored to serve a diverse range of clients navigating complex relational, mental, and physical health issues. I support individuals through grief, trauma, queer identity exploration, life transitions, family dynamics, relational issues, ethical non-monogamy, anxiety, depression, and chronic health concerns. I'm passionate about assisting those who feel stuck or powerless and believe in everyone's potential for stability and well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use an integrative person-centered, systems-informed approach to therapy by blending somatic, humanistic, internal family systems, narrative, and acceptance-commitment therapy, all with the goal of providing an individually tailored approach for each client and situation. Trained in multiple psychedelic-assisted therapy models, I incorporate these methods to address complex issues such as existential anxiety, chronic health concerns, challenging psychedelic experiences, shame, grief, complex trauma, hopelessness, and spiritual distress. With a firm grasp on neuroscience, mindfulness, and transpersonal experiences, I help clients navigate both day-to-day concerns and larger macro (lifespan) themes. When it resonates with a client's values or interests, I also incorporate ritual practices and take-home work. My clients report finding me warm, intuitive, reflective, interactive, and skilled at providing a holistic and empathetic therapeutic experience.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe in the capacity for growth and change in all people. Just like the body heals a wound with the right support, our minds and spirits can heal with a warm, accepting presence. Being truly seen and witnessed is essential for healing, and I am honored to provide such a space for my clients. As a queer and non-monogamous person, I support those exploring their queer identity and ethical non-monogamy, recognizing the stigma and challenges faced by those outside normative culture. In my practice, all parts of my clients are welcome, especially the most challenging, dark, and stormy parts. These often ignored or disregarded parts (the "shadow") need examination, understanding, and integration; this is core to my practice. I am dedicated to creating a space where all aspects of my clients can be explored and understood, fostering healing and growth.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: My specialty treatment orientations include somatic therapy, where I incorporate Sensorimotor Psychotherapy into my practice. Trained in supporting people through both acute and developmental trauma, I address the connection between the body and mind to help clients process and heal from trauma, stress, and other emotional challenges. By integrating these techniques, I provide a comprehensive and holistic approach to therapy that supports the full spectrum of healing and personal growth.

name: Alicia Pasik
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello! My name is Alicia I am a licensed professional counselor.
ideal_client: Are you looking for a therapist who incorporates art therapy & sand tray therapy into sessions? Perhaps you have tried traditional talk therapy and haven't seen much success. Do you identify as autistic, have ADHD, or otherwise consider yourself neurodiverse? Are you going through a major life transition, and needing some help navigating the muddy waters? Are you looking for a compassionate therapist who will hold you accountable? If the answer to either question is yes, we may be a match.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have specialized training in helping adults with disabilities and mental illness. Additionally, my undergraduate degree focused on expressive arts therapy, which informs my practice today. I believe that incorporating imagery and art can facilitate a deeper understanding of oneself, as well as get to the core issue a lot faster than talking can do. Sometimes, there aren't words, and that is ok. As a licensed counselor in the state of Oregon, I am required to complete ongoing education annually. My previous role in an inpatient crisis center included extensive trauma counseling, for which I saw first hand how powerful of a tool the sand tray can be in helping process and integrate trauma. I understand that some folks are not interested in working with this modality, and I always go at the pace of the client. Some folks will go through years of therapy without ever touching the sand, and that is ok.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: The research shows that the biggest driving force for change is the therapeutic relationship. Thus, I prioritize our counseling relationship first and foremost. This includes having unconditional positive regard for you, as well as believing in your strengths and abilities. This also includes challenging you to see your own blind spots, or how you may be getting in your own way sometimes. I value authenticity, and have a warm, steady presence. Together, with our relationship as the safety net, we can dig deeper into what needs to be uncovered for your healing journey. I value uncovering all parts of ourselves, especially those parts that we may deem "bad" or "ugly" and having compassion for those parts.

specialities.name: Sand Tray
specialities.description: I am trained in the Sand Play method from the Sandplay Training Worldwide institute.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: My undergraduate degree coursework at Lesley College focused largely on art and expressive arts therapy.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I have extensive experience helping folks who are diagnosed or self-identify as neurodiverse. I see neurodiversity as a unique way of existing in the world, rather than as an issue to treat. Some challenges that may be experienced with this diagnosis include feeling different or misunderstood, sensory processing difficulties, and difficulty understanding social cues. I provide neurodivergent-affirming care and believe that you are the expert of your own experience.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: My previous work experience as a job coach for adults with disabilities informs my approach to treating ADHD. I am creative in my approach, and tailor it to your specific learning style. As a visual and kinesthetic learner, I have had great success incorporating visual aids to enhance our counseling sessions when indicated.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: At the inpatient crisis center, I had great success in treating adults with anxiety. I incorporate engaging the five senses as grounding techniques for anxiety, and include breath work. I can give you concrete tools to take with you outside of our therapy sessions to assist in treating anxiety.

specialities.name: Aspergers
specialities.description: Aspergers is no longer listed in the DSM, however, there are many folks who still self-identify with the diagnosis. I have extensive experience supporting this population in my work history at the crisis center, as well as a case manager and job coach for adults with disabilities.

name: Sibylle Dehart
title: Student Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Sibylle! I'm a queer, feminist counselor who believes that everyone is capable of connection, authenticity, and joy. Let's talk!

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: As part of my internship, I am currently being trained in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT).

name: Katie Emard
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer individual telehealth counseling services for adults located in the state of Oregon. Social justice is central to my practice.
ideal_client: I am deeply committed to and passionate about working with my LGBTQIA++ community, and identify as Queer and Lesbian. I have primarily worked with the Queer community for the past three years. I also have a special heart for the Indigenous community and exploring and supporting our unique challenges and spiritual and ecological connections. I have experience working with: BDSM/KINK, polyamory/relationship anarchy, BIPOC, parenting, trauma, disability, neurodiversity, poverty, death, and trauma.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe every human being has the inherent potential for positive change and self-actualization. At times we can feel overwhelmed by the search for life meaning and the daily struggles that are a part of life. We do not have to bear this burden alone. Support and guidance in a safe and comfortable, therapeutic setting can provide the space needed to explore pain, trauma, behaviors that no longer serve us, our strengths, our multiple identities, our own potential and the internal and external

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I see therapy as a collaborative process where we can access your own inner gold and uncover your truth and deep knowing. As a practitioner of feminist and Critical Race Theory modalities I understand that systems of oppression, such as: racism, trans-phobia, homophobia, sexism, and poverty contribute to mental health and impact the way we move through the world. We are all immersed in a culture that uplifts us, or steps down on us based on our identities. In therapy we can explore these aspects as well as your interpersonal and intrapersonal dynamics in order to find healing and growth. I am aware of the identities that I bring into the room as a counselor, and am deeply committed to addressing my own biases as a white passing person and around any and all other areas of privilege that I hold. I am committed to a process that is egalitarian and collaborative. You are the expert of your lived experience, it is my role to support and guide you through your personal exploration an

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I have worked with issues surrounding gender identity for the past three years. I have supported clients through gender affirmation surgery and have experience writing letters for transition surgery.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have worked with many individuals over the past three years that are involved with relationship anarchy/polyamory/open relationships.

name: Melinda Norman
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: A bridge between the psychological, physical, and spiritual
ideal_client: I work with those that have developed a distaste for illusion. My approach to therapy includes traditional cognitive behavioral therapies blended with somatic and shamanic healing. The mind is not the only part of you that needs to be addressed if you would like to live a life not conditioned by your past. I don't believe in "killing the ego" but rather learning to purify the archetypes we choose to pattern our experience through in order to embrace fear and evolve into self mastery.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: ****My practice is in person with the option of telehealth in specialized circumstances**** As a practitioner, I believe in walking with my clients as they become responsible for the creation of their experience. This is not a simple task and takes significant effort as this path requires the mastery of your impulses, emotions, and body. You must have bravery to look into your own shadow. It can be painful and ungrounding. This path is not for the faint of heart. We will walk into the experience that you are having together; not bypass it while simultaneously assisting you in developing the skills necessary to reflect who you are choosing to become. I will support you as you learn to alchemize your pain and reorder your relationship with your experiences.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I operate on optimism with the ever important understanding of realistic expectations. My treatment focuses include *Generational trauma *Soul Retrieval/Power Retrieval *Regression therapy *Narcissistic abuse recovery *Abandonment and attachment *Somatic Trauma Therapy *Non religious spiritual development

specialities.name: Past Life Regression
specialities.description: The methodology that I use is called Depth Hypnosis. This method can be used to move into a past life, but the experience that you are having that parallels past life events needs to be explored as well.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: This approach focuses on the movement away from identifying with the ego self which has been created as a protective response to the experience of emotional pain.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I blend a mixture of energy work with my training in PSIP (psychedelic somatic interactional psychotherapy---which can be done non medicated) to assist clients in releasing stored trauma from their body.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: I have training in core Shamanism which includes soul and power retrieval, energy medicine, ritual, and other forms of traditional healing.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: I specialize in helping others recognize the impact of generational experiences that lead to us experiencing traumatic situations.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: My training is in core Shamanism and Buddhist philosophy. These are principles and practices that can be used to alter perspectives on events leading to personal empowerment rather than feeling trapped in victimization. I also specialize in supporting spiritual awakenings.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Recovery from child, spousal, and often times abusing ourselves. I work with generational trauma where we work on understanding the effects that parents and grandparents with mental health issues have had on your life.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Codependency has many roots which often stem from childhood abandonment or lack of development. We can work together on healing these traumas and creating new behavioral patterns which allow you to live independently of others.

name: Annie Vail
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), Certified Hakomi Therapist (CHT)
intro: I am deeply committed to supporting my clients on their journey towards healing, growth, and living more fully into their best life
ideal_client: My clients often seek deeper awareness and connection with themselves, their relationships, and their purpose in the world. My practice predominately employs mindfulness-based modalities, making it an excellent fit for clients who are open to incorporating mindfulness into their therapeutic journey. Clients often seek support with developmental trauma or attachment issues, anxiety, relationship challenges, a sense of belonging, a harsh inner critic, grief, life transitions, or feeling stuck.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am both a Certified Hakomi Therapist and a Licensed Professional Counselor. My approach is ultimately holistic and somatic. I draw from variety of mindfulness, somatic, and attachment-based therapeutic modalities, including: -Hakomi Therapy -Internal Family Systems (IFS) and Gestalt -PACT Couple Therapy -Recreation-of-the-Self (RCS) -Somatic trauma release -Compassionate communication/ Non-violent communication (NVC). This combination of approaches fosters healing, empowerment, self-awareness, inter-relational awareness, transformation, authenticity, and creativity. My therapeutic style is a blend of compassion, warmth, and support, as well as being relational, grounded and direct. I aim to create a safe and empathetic environment for clients to explore and address patterns that hinder them from achieving their desires and goals. My true passion lies in supporting my clients to know themselves better, heal from the past, and step further into their own authenticity.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that beyond the struggle and pain of life is an innate wisdom that guides each person to their wholeness. As my client, I will see you in this wholeness, not your wounding. Your unique strengths, wisdom, and resources become allies in the therapeutic process. I will celebrate and embrace you exactly as you are now, while supporting your movement towards greater well-being. I will help you to compassionately see and understand the impact of core patterns and beliefs that give rise to your current circumstances. I am deeply committed to holding a systemic lens for all clients, but especially those with marginalized identities. Throughout my adult life, I have prioritized ongoing education and awareness about privilege, power dynamics, and oppression. I believe it is essential to consider how systems of power and privilege relate to each person's experience and I welcome these considerations and inquiries in my office.

name: Diane Ornelas
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide therapy for ADHD, anxiety, depression, self-esteem/social/relationship issues, & ALT lifestyles. I am Neurodiversity affirming.
ideal_client: Do you consider yourself an over-thinker? Introvert? Atypical or Alien? Do you have ADHD or wonder if you do? Are you overwhelmed with anxiety due to difficulty being your authentic self around others? Do you live an alternative lifestyle or are you in a nontraditional relationship/s? Are you a digital nomad? Are you having trouble adjusting to life changes or new roles? Then I would love to work with you!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am an ADHD specialist also treating co-ocurring disorders such as anxiety, depression, self-esteem, and relationship issues. I serve clients across the gender spectrum, with a sex-positive approach & am an Altsex/Kink/Poly-Friendly clinician. I am also LGBTQ+ affirming & vegan affirming, provide support to social activists, sex workers, veterans, minorities, & am Spanish speaking. I work with clients on adjusting to new responsibilities & roles, personal growth, & determining the root cause of your distress. I will also teach you to silence your loud inner critic. I am both directive and non-directive; easy to talk to, but will call you out if you're being inauthentic, self-deprecating or self-sabotaging. I use various therapeutic & coaching techniques, & provide education on your symptoms. My techniques are accompanied by humor & rapport building to ensure our relationship is a trusting one, so you can be honest without feeling judged. Video sessions offered!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Bilingual (English/Spanish) Licensed Professional Counselor in the State of Oregon, as well as Licensed Mental Health Counselor in the State of Washington. I hold a Doctoral degree in Clinical Psychology completed at Albizu University in my native state of Florida, and am currently pursuing licensure as a Clinical Psychologist in the state of Oregon.

name: Tessa Rose
title: Professional Counselor
intro: I believe that everyone is capable of making positive changes in their lives. I support my clients to find home within themselves.
ideal_client: Amongst the turmoil of life, there is something that many of us are missing. I support my clients to reclaim their purpose, love, and build self empowerment. I work with folks of all races, genders, sexualities, life and psychological experiences, bodies, and abilities. I am passionate about working with folks who may experience depression, anxiety, transitions and transformations, gender and sexuality journeys and identities.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Using methods of Process Oriented Facilitation, I integrate Process Work into my practice in a variety of ways: through dreamwork, exploring body symptoms, and slowing the process down. My approach to therapy is unfolding what happens in the present moment. By connecting to what's happening inside ourselves we can access our power, combat our inner critic, get in touch with sources of anger, rebuild trust, and find a sense of safety within ourselves. I aim to work with my clients on self love and reconnecting to the feeling of what it means to be at home and at peace. I don’t push my clients to dive too deep before they are ready, as true transformation is a process that takes time. As long as you’re open and willing to explore, we can work together at your own pace towards positive growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that everyone is capable of making positive changes in their lives. My mission is to help clients reach their fullest potential by providing a safe and supportive space. Through my counseling services, I help my clients to learn to empower themselves, conquer their inner critic, and learn to live in love. I specialize in a holistic approach to counseling, which means that I take into consideration the mental, emotional, physical, and spiritual aspects of wellbeing. My goal is to help my clients gain personal insight, discover their unique strengths, and ultimately create a life filled with joy and fulfillment.

name: Naomi Wright
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: I empower young people and families to break free from stuck patterns with compassionate, science-based therapy.
ideal_client: I work with families and young people (ages 0-22) who feel caught in repetitive cycles—whether it’s a child facing tantrums, sleep, eating, or toileting challenges, or a teen/young adult struggling with anxiety, sadness, or relational conflicts. If you’re a caregiver or youth navigating trauma, neurodiversity, or simply feeling overwhelmed by life’s hurdles, my practice offers a supportive space to spark lasting change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use evidence-based strategies to truly understand your unique challenges and strengths. Together, we set clear, actionable goals and develop a practical toolkit tailored to your needs. For young children, I work directly with parents to reshape daily interactions and foster positive behavior, while with older youth, I balance individual sessions with family time. We start with small, manageable steps—practicing new skills between sessions—to build momentum toward meaningful change. Many see progress in as few as 10-15 sessions, though ongoing support is always available. My focus is on creating a collaborative, empowering process that helps you break free from old patterns and embrace a healthier, more connected life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe therapy is a collaborative journey, where you are the expert in your life and I bring expertise in evidence-based treatments. My background includes working with diverse families in county hospitals, shelters, and community clinics—experiences that echo my own humble beginnings in rural Oregon. These experiences taught me that many challenges are beyond our control, yet change is possible. Grounded in scientific research on trauma and interpersonal dynamics, my work is also enriched by a creative, theater-inspired approach. I tailor interventions to fit your family’s unique context, blending serious, structured work with moments of levity to foster resilience, growth, and connection.

name: Morgan Lyons
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I want to help you find values-aligned ways to respond to painful circumstances and connect to what matters to you, even on the hard days.
ideal_client: We all deserve lives full of joy, opportunity and love. Too often though, we all find ourselves in places or periods where these things are scarce, or blocked altogether, sometimes in ways that are out of our control. While I deeply enjoy working with a wide range of clients, I specialize in supporting individuals who find themselves in moments of scarcity hopelessness, or powerlessness, to build out lives with more meaning, space, and joy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Working from a stance of curiosity, compassion, and non-judgment, my hope is to partner with you in building the skills and tools to navigate whatever life throws at you. Through our work together, I will aim to support you in fostering the vulnerability to love yourself and others, the strength to approach pain, and the flexibility to touch meaning and passion even on your hardest days. My practice is grounded in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, and other mindfulness-based approaches. With over a decade of experience providing counseling services, much of my work has focused on supporting the LGBTQIA+ community, survivors of violence and abuse, unhoused youth, and individuals struggling with self-harm and suicidality.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My most cherished values include community, compassion, self-determination, and joy and I strive to embody these as a provider. I am committed to engaging in anti-oppressive practices and actively work to uphold anti-racist, trauma-informed, sex-positive, and body-positive lens in my practice. The principles of Harm Reduction are important to me and central to the way I approach my work. If it sounds like I might be a good fit for you, give me a call or a text! We can schedule a consultation and talk through what you’re looking for. Alternatively, if you would like to know more about me, my background, or training before reaching out, feel free to check out my website linked on this page.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I have extensive advanced training in ACT and consider it my “therapeutic homebase.” I have received active regular mentorship and consultation in this modality for 8+ years.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I have received intensive training and supervision in Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) and have previously worked in a full-fidelity DBT clinic. While I currently incorporate several elements of DBT into my practice, it is important to note that DBT, when practiced in its full form, is a multi-faceted approach that includes components such as group skills training and phone coaching, which are not part of the services I offer at this time.

name: Sasha Rosenfels, MA, LMFT
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: We'll work together to deepen your understanding of yourself and your relationships in order to feel calmer, confident and more connected.
ideal_client: Respect, compassion and empathy are the cornerstones of my counseling practice. I provide a safe environment where you can explore your experiences and how they have shaped you. You'll learn to understand yourself, your thoughts, feelings and your needs and examine your relationships with others so that you can nurture and deepen those relationships. Most importantly, you'll learn to view yourself through a more compassionate lens, building a calmer inner experience and more caring self-view.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My specialty is relationship-related issues, which most often include your relationships with your partner, your children, as well as your own parents. We'll explore the ways these relationships impact you, expand your awareness of unhealthy patterns of interaction, increase connection, and learn to thrive instead of just survive.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Our life experiences hold the all the extremes; immense joy and profound love as well as overwhelming frustration and emotional struggle. I am incredibly grateful to be able to offer support to individuals as they navigate the huge ups and downs of this complex journey.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: In my work, I may employ components of ​Compassionate-Based Mindfulness, Attachment-Based Therapy, Inner Child Work, and Somatic Therapy. I utilize these approaches in order to help individuals explore the experiences that shaped them, including bringing awareness to the way emotional struggle shows up in the body. Work in these modalities helps individuals foster a new, more compassionate relationship with themselves and others.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: We will utilize Family Systems approach in order to identify patterns of interactions and work to implement new, more helpful ways of communicating and interacting.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Though I don’t provide couples therapy, I do provide individuals therapy with a focus on improving relationships, particularly familial relationships. In sessions, you will be provided the opportunity to explore theses relationships, working to build tools and mindsets to help you and your loved ones thrive.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Supporting parents and caretakers in developing and implementing tried and tested strategies and mindsets that support their child's mental and emotional well-being. This work may also involve deepening your understanding of yourself and your past experiences in order to strengthen your ability to support your child when they are in need.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Women face unique challenges which may include but are not limited to restrictive gender norms as well as inequality on multiple levels both within and outside of their family systems. If interested, women are allowed the space in individual sessions to explore their own unique experiences as women and to discover and build upon their inherent power and value.

specialities.name: Anger Management
specialities.description: Helping individuals identify and work to manage feelings of anger through mindfulness tools as well as through working to increase each individual's sense of safety and connection with one another.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Along our journey through life, we often experience a stressor or series of stressors that may be understandably overwhelming. In sessions, individuals unpack these experiences, identify and process the affects they've had and build tools to help them manage both the emotional and logistical consequences of these stressors.

name: Shannon Haan
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I believe it is my honor to hold space for the stories of others and would love to support you in navigating and understanding yours
ideal_client: I have experience working with a diverse range of folks and aim to have my practice embrace diversity in gender, race, sexuality, abilities, body size, and perspectives. While I have worked with folks from different backgrounds and across numerous areas, I find I work best in the following areas: anxiety, depression, historic and relational trauma, life transitions, relationship issues, queer identity, chronic health conditions, grief, psychosis, and substance use.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have received training in multiple approaches which I use in my practice including Motivational Interviewing, CBT, Internal Family Systems, and Mindfulness-based practices. I am currently part of a group studying Internal Family Systems and parts work to apply this lens and technique to my approach, as well as a supervised group to expand understanding my work through a racial justice framework. I also understand healing through a somatic lens, centering the experience of our bodies and the wisdom they hold. Through my experiences working in the mental health field for almost 10 years, I deeply value low barrier and client centered care and aim to orient my practice around these principles. My work is relational and I believe you are the expert of your story, it is my job to co-create a safe environment for you to become deeper in touch with your own internal wisdom. **We have an income-based sliding scale payment arrangement to offer for folks without insurance benefits.**

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a white person and a cis woman, I seek to educate myself regularly on anti-oppressive perspectives and approaches to inform how I work, and live. I am a member of the LGBTQ+ community and this as well as a feminist lens is a guide to my life, my connections, and my work. I am also someone who lives with a chronic health condition and I believe in and practice deeply in my life the understanding of the mind body connection, and how to honor and care for our bodies even within a less than supportive culture. My goal is to build a collaborative space with you to work together, and create a sense of safety and non-judgement for your healing. During my free time, I love to be cozy at home with a book and a cup of tea, spend time with friends, play board games, go dancing, swimming, traveling, and spend as much time in nature as possible.

name: Elissa Barbee
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I enjoy working with individuals seeking to gain a deeper awareness of self through an exploration of the mind, body and spirit.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize an integrative model drawing from components in Mindful Self-Compassion, Person-Centered therapy and Motivational Interviewing. I tend to work through an attachment lens and often utilize somatic interventions and 'parts' work. I support Harm Reduction practices where it is the appropriate fit for the client. As a dual-diagnosis counselor I am skilled in providing an effective healing space for those affected by mental health concerns, addiction, and trauma and am proficient in working with health care professionals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My background and training as a dancer has guided my intrigue in the connection of the mind and body, particularly how we experience, store and express memories & emotions in the body. Through our work together we will explore this phenomenon and increase your awareness of bodily communications and how to utilize them to support your holistic well-being. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) with the Oregon Board of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists. I also hold a Certification in Alcohol and Drug Counseling (CADC I) through the Addiction Counselor Certification Board of Oregon. I graduated from Lewis & Clark’s Professional Mental Health and Addiction’s Masters program and have been working in a variety of different settings ranging from residential to private practice since.

name: Therese Long
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: You've taken the first step. Now let's see if we're a good fit so we can start the work to meet your goals!

approaches.My Background and Approach: My style is direct yet gentle and I speak from an honest heart. I pull from various models but most often utilize Narrative Therapy, CBT, and mindfulness based techniques. Through a combination of these modalities, I work to help clients re-write unhealthy narratives and adjust patterns or ways of thinking that reinforce these inaccurate self-views.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a masters in Marriage and Family Therapy through Lewis and Clark and am a licensed therapist in the state of Oregon. My work is done through a systemic lens with the understanding that we are always influencing, and being influenced, by the systems around us. I have experience with children ages 5 and up, couples, families, and individuals. I believe strongly in incorporating holistic perspectives into therapy and working to bring mind body aspects into the room to fully address concerns. I also provide supervision to LMFT Interns and LPC Interns working towards licensure in Oregon. Please inquire about cost through email.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Throughout the years I have done work around empowering women to find their strength within, resist or challenge social expectations, and open conversations around 'taboo topics'.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have worked as a Child and Family Therapist in community mental health for the last 5 years. My experience includes supporting families through transition, assisting parents in restructuring expectations and setting limits, and increasing communication within family system. My work also includes running girls groups for adolescents that target self esteem, social expectations, and self worth.

name: Wendy Jensen
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Asking for help is a sign of strength. The good news is it gets easier with practice. Good for you for taking this first step.
ideal_client: I am most passionate about working with individuals who feel like they are "not good enough: or who feel broken or flawed on some way. So many times we take on unconscious beliefs about our life from early on that stem from trauma, neglect, abuse or loss and those hidden but powerful beliefs end up dictating most of the rest of our life. These negative core beliefs that we took on as children have amazing power over us all of our lives, until we heal them. Let me help you do that.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a licensed therapist here to guide you in a process towards goals that you decide in therapy. I use curiosity, self-disclosure (where helpful/relevant), and challenging questions to help you uncover the hidden baggage that is keeping you from being your best self.. The way in which we cope in the world is greatly influenced by how we see the world. Dealing with anxiety, depression or grief can be difficult but I believe by using "baby steps" in a safe space, growth and healing happen quickly. My goal is to facilitate an awakening within you and deep healing of long-held problematic patterns and destructive core beliefs that are keeping you from living life to its fullest and finding joy and peace of mind in your daily life.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: As an experienced therapist, I work with people who have experienced trauma in their life, no matter how big or small, whether it be in their family of origin, their relationships, their work place or their communities. My clients often feel overwhelmed and confused by their past experiences, and how those have impacted them emotionally, physically, socially and psychically. Navigating through life's transitions is hard enough, but it can be downright daunting when we have "baggage" hanging on from our past. Lets work together to explore those wounds, and old belief systems to heal from past traumas, develop self-acceptance and understanding, gain more self-compassion and confidence and move toward a healthy, happier life. I use a variety of approaches including Energy Psychology/Body Centered Techniques for releasing trauma quickly and permanently, Shamanic healing methods including soul retrieval, EMDR, Emotionally Focused Therapy, Past Life Regression and Hypnotherapy.

name: Suzanne Sanchez
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Suzanne, a gentle guide for the hurting soul—I help you heal, grow, and reconnect with the truest parts of yourself.
ideal_client: Is anxiety responsible for hardship in your life? Maybe you are a parent distrustful of your judgment. Maybe you are a teen worried about school, peers, sports, or just doing a good job. Maybe you struggle with body image and engage in unhealthy behaviors. Maybe you worry about safety because you don't fit into the majority culture. Maybe life just changed up big time for you and you need some support navigating this life transition. If any of these are you, I will be a great fit for you!

approaches.My Background and Approach: I believe we all have the power to change habits and feelings through increasing our self-awareness. We often know what it is we need, but we need help establishing commitment to change. I believe all people are good, we just need help to see the good inside. Most importantly, I believe as a therapist, I am responsible for seeing a person’s entire environment as perpetuating a problem rather than a person wholly being at fault. I help my clients examine how their mental health and behavioral issues are affected on the different systemic levels of their life. I have much diverse experience as a therapist and have worked in residential settings, outpatient settings, schools, hospitals, and day treatment programs. I have a M.A. in counseling psychology from Lewis and Clark College, Portland (2007), and I have a B.A. in both psychology and in sociology from the University of Minnesota, Twin Cities (2000).

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I use a Health at Every Size (HAES) approach in counseling and am firmly anti-diet culture. I’ve served on boards focused on supporting individuals and families affected by eating disorders, and I teach an annual course on eating disorders in the certification program at Lewis & Clark College Graduate School, where I’m adjunct faculty. Cultural identity is also deeply important to me. I’m half-Asian and half-white (mostly Finnish), and I understand the experience of moving through the world as a multiracial person and a person of color in the Portland-metro area. I love working with cultural identity in all its forms, and I believe everyone—yes, even white folks—has culture that shapes their emotional health. I’m also a spiritual person in the sense that I believe we’re all connected. Practices like gratitude and meditation are key to mental and emotional balance, and I enjoy helping people find what that looks like for them.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: Motivation is always changing in that some days we might feel very motivated to change and others we feel little motivation. Through use of motivational interviewing, I am able to work with you where you are at and help you find what it is that motivates you to want to make change in your life.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: I use experiential techniques to help clients access parts of their sub-conscious mind. Examples may include art therapy techniques, role-playing, writing, and play therapy. Through experience, insight is often increased, and as self-awareness grows so can self-esteem, self-confidence and motivation.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Thoughts, emotions, and behaviors are all inter-connected. In making alterations to your perspective, you will also be able to change how you feel and change habitual behavior. Through identification of core beliefs, challenging thinking errors, and use of chain analysis, I help clients make changes in their life.

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: I work with people who want to explore how racial identity shapes their experiences. Cultural identity influences how we see and move through the world—whether we’re part of a dominant group (like white individuals) or a marginalized one (like people of color). Understanding racial identity can be a powerful and healing part of therapy.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I’ve worked with teens for many years, and they’re truly my passion. I know how to connect with adolescents in a way that feels safe and real. I help them understand their needs, recognize their strengths, and learn to advocate for themselves. Most of all, I offer them hope and encouragement to be fully and unapologetically themselves.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Low self-esteem often comes from a mix of life experiences. I help clients untangle the stories and messages that have led them to feel “not good enough” and guide them toward new perspectives. Together, we work on welcoming imperfection and building self-acceptance rooted in compassion and truth.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I have extensive experience treating eating disorders and understand the complex struggles individuals face. I also work closely with parents, partners, and friends to help them support their loved ones. Within eating disorder treatment, I work specifically with negative body image, body dysmorphia, orthorexia, emetophobia, ARFID, people in larger bodies, teens, people of color, athletes, and those with co-occurring disorders.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is something almost everyone faces these days. I help clients recognize how anxious thoughts show up in their lives and teach tools to manage them with awareness and compassion. Instead of trying to eliminate anxiety, we work on living with it in a healthier, more balanced way.

name: Carly Henderson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Working with individuals and families.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My practice is guided by the belief that every adult and child strives to do the best they can. The individual or family system may need assistance in developing necessary skills and guidance in solving problems. Working collaboratively with clients I help them to narrate new ways of interacting with their environment.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I was born and raised in Oregon, and have spent several years overseas in the UK, Europe, and Africa. I have Master's degrees from Lewis & Clark College in Counseling Psychology and from University of Cambridge in Social and Developmental Psychology. I completed my undergraduate work in Psychology, also at Lewis & Clark in Portland. I have worked as a counselor since 2002, first as a Professional School Counselor in the US and overseas, and then in the private sector since 2011. Additionally, I spent two years working as a Behavior Consultant for children in a large public school district in Oregon. I have additional training in Interpersonal Neurobiology, EMDR, Somatic therapy, developmental/attachment trauma, Collaborative Problem Solving, and Positive Behavior Interventions and Supports.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing), which is an evidence based treatment for PTSD as well as several other concerns (e.g., developmental/attachment trauma, phobias, addiction, anxiety).

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I have and continue to participate in graduate education and professional development that focuses on attachment and attachment related trauma. I continue to participate in graduate classes through Portland State University's Trauma Informed Services and Interpersonal Neurobiology (IPNB) programs and participate in an advanced study group focusing on trauma, attachment, and IPNB.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I am a Gottman Seven Principles trained educator, a Gottman Bringing Baby Home trained educator, and have completed the Gottman Level 1 couples training.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: I hold a masters degree in Social and Developmental Psychology - my thesis research focused on parent-child communication and conflict. I have additional training in Collaborative Problem Solving, Positive Interventions and Supports (PBIS), and Interpersonal Neurobiology (the brain/mind/relationship connection).

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: We know a lot more than we did only decades ago about how trauma is stored in the brain and body, about how it is activated by present experiences, and how to effectively process and integrate traumatic memories. I utilize EMDR, somatic techniques and Interpersonal Neurobiology to assist clients with trauma.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I am trained in Collaborative Problem Solving and have had several years of experience working with children and adolescents - ages 3-20 both in and out of the school setting. I have worked within the Special Education system and can assist families with what is an often confusing process. I use art and play techniques, interactive activities and include parents and other family members in therapy

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I am a Gottman Seven Principles and Bringing Baby Home trained educator and have completed the Gottman Level 1 couples training. Additionally, I have and continue to participate in graduate education and professional development in Interpersonal Neurobiology (IPNB). I incorporate the Gottman Method, IPNB, and Emotion Focused Therapy (EFT) in my work with couples.

name: Jen Masotja-Wright
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Jen believes that through support and collaboration, her clients can achieve positive outcomes on their journey towards healing and growth.
ideal_client: As a proud member of the Queer community, Jen has a strong interest in supporting clients in the areas of LGBTQAI+, children, adolescents and teens, first responders, natural disaster and trauma survivors, individuals experiencing anxiety, depression, and family transitions due to divorce, parenting struggles, abandonment, and complex familial relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Jen takes an evidence-based, person-centered, and strengths-based approach when working with clients with theoretical frameworks such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Narrative Therapy, Attachment Theory, Family Systems Theory and EMDR. When preferred by clients, Jen utilizes grounding techniques and breathing exercises to prepare clients for sessions ensuring there is a healing, open and safe space for sharing and growth. Jen is a parent to two incredible children who are biracial/bicultural (African and North American) and although she can never know what it means to walk through the world as a person of color, she does have experience advocating for, providing support to and being ally for communities of color.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: With a strong focus and commitment to a work/life balance, Jen loves spending time enjoying all the beauty and joys of the Pacific NW with her wife, kiddos and 2 dogs. She embraces time in the kitchen exploring the tastes of many cuisines and listening to music from her favorite artists.

name: Psychology & Wellness Group PDX LLC (Group Practice)
full_name: Psychology & Wellness Group PDX LLC (Group Practice) (She/Her, He/Him, They/Them)
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We are a group practice. In person and virtual. Self pay, private insurance & OHP. We look forward to meeting you! SE & SW locations.
ideal_client: We see teens 15 and above and adults. We see individuals, groups, families and couples. Because we have different clinicians in our practice, we work with different issues. From anxiety and depression to emotional manipulation and personality disorders, we want to have a genuine therapeutic relationship with you. We take OHP, insurance and private pay. We offer free initial consults. We love working with people who are ready to get to the heart of the matter and are ready for insight and change.

approaches.Our Background and Approach: I (Stephanie) am the owner of our group practice, supervisor, & a psychotherapist. I have years of experience treating different mental health issues but specialize in personality disorders and trauma / emotional manipulation. I am psychodynamically oriented. We have awesome therapists: Ames (Art, ADHD, Autism), Marissa (Music, Trauma), Sam (Teens), Aubry (Mental Illness), Sean (Relationships), Donna (Eating Disorders) Alex (SPMI), Jeremy (SPMI), Jessica (Teens). They have different interests and styles. Relational, kind, intelligent, curious, strength based, focused, mindful, invested, supportive, art based and allies of multiple communities. What we have in common is our passion for a genuine therapeutic relationship based on trust and collaboration. We want to get to the heart of the matter with you and help you alleviate your emotional suffering. We want to help you deal with the current problem and help change your long term patterns. We love what we do and we hope it shows!

approaches.Our Personal Beliefs and Interests: We believe in hope & inclusivity & equality. We all have dogs or cats that own us. We believe in the greater good. We take OHP & insurance; we want people to have access. The therapeutic alliance matters to us. Yes, we need to make a living; what is more important to us is to help others & enjoy our lives doing the thing that matters. Call for fee info. Stephanie - coffee drinking Buddhist, owns the practice. Savannah - practice manager, front line for our practice & dog lover. Becky - smart, funny, our insurance & billing wizard & admin. Kori - front desk and our friendly client engagement specialist. Therapists: 9 of them! All different humans who are interested in different areas of counseling and all work in person and via telehealth. We would rather see you in person in either our Tigard or Sellwood offices. Please contact us with questions. Our therapists have multiple interests and diverse personalities. We hope you become part of our community!

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: All of our therapists work with relationships. This is the foundation of good psychotherapy. We are a good team and work well together and have the ability to develop good relationships with our clients. We are interested in treating the unique person that steps through our door. Since we have multiple providers with different specialties, we will stick with relational for now. Some are newer to our practice so we are currently updating the information here and on our website.

name: Kent Yoder
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I specialize in anxiety, depression, grief, and trauma, using an integrative approach. I’m committed to inclusivity and social justice.
ideal_client: My clients come from diverse backgrounds, facing challenges like anxiety, depression, grief, and trauma. I create a supportive, inclusive environment for everyone, working with clients to explore their unique experiences, develop practical tools for healing, and cultivate personal empowerment. Together, we focus on creating lasting change, navigating difficulties, and promoting mental well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that each of us has a natural impulse toward growth, healing, and connection—with ourselves, others, and the world around us. However, life experiences, cultural backgrounds, and relationships shape the narratives we tell ourselves and the patterns we follow. While these can serve as strengths, they can also create barriers that make it difficult to navigate change or healing on our own. Therapy provides a space to slow down, reflect, and gain clarity. I strive to create a supportive and collaborative environment where clients feel safe to explore the emotions, experiences, and challenges that are shaping their lives. I take an integrative approach to therapy, drawing from modalities that honor the mind-body connection, personal narratives, and the ways we are shaped by relationships and environments. I am in the process of training in EMDR, an evidence-based approach that aids in the resolution of traumatic memories and deeply ingrained emotional patterns.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a member of the LGBTQIA+ community and a committed BIPOC ally. My work is deeply rooted in social justice, advocacy, and an understanding of the ways systemic oppression impacts mental health. I also have significant multicultural and international experience, which informs my perspective and ability to hold space for diverse experiences.

name: Laura Wood
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm licensed in Washington and Oregon and work with adults and teens. I approach this work with curiosity and want to understand your truth.
ideal_client: You are doing the best you can with the cards you were dealt. I would be honored to work alongside you as you take on this healing journey. My goal is to create a space where you can show up unapologetically - all raw emotions welcomed. I work primarily with people who identify as sensitive and are experiencing anxiety, depression, life transitions, low self-esteem, and/or have a history of trauma.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize a relational and integrated approach in therapy, primarily drawing from the following therapies: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy; Motivational Interviewing; and Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing (EMDR). I strongly believe that we are doing the best we can with the resources we have. We all have lived experiences that shape the way we engage with the world and people around us. Unfortunately, sometimes that means skewed perceptions, relational patterns, and coping mechanisms. By bringing attention to the experiences that have framed your worldview, together, we can explore healthier patterns of relating and coping. I strive to provide a supportive, collaborative environment to foster this growth. I am also committed to creating an inclusive and safe space for people from all cultural backgrounds and communities.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I have had the privilege of working with diverse populations in outpatient community mental health, providing group and individual counseling to adults and adolescents with a range of mental health and substance use concerns. Through this work, I've learned that I work best from a lens of curiosity and collaboration. I help clients understand their internal experience with non-judgment.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I have formal ACT training. I utilize this modality in order to help clients identify their values and help them better align their actions with these values, instead of getting swept away by avoidance behaviors or other emotion-driven actions.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: I have worked with clients who are mandated to treatment and those who find it difficult to make lasting changes. I find that this approach is most helpful in meeting people where they're at in their journey.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am EMDR-trained and use this modality to help reprocess events that have had a lasting impact on someone's life.

specialities.name: Panic
specialities.description: Panic is extremely distressing. At times, it may feel like you can't possibly survive in your own skin. Although it may feel hopeless, we can help you develop skills to alleviate symptoms in the moment when panic is surfacing. I have experience educating clients on the brain activity involved with panic and teaching concrete self-regulation skills to manage acute stress symptoms.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Research shows that our brains are not fully developed until age 25. This presents adolescents with challenges that many adults have trouble relating to and understanding. I have experience educating youth and families on the developing brain and working collaboratively with adolescents to help them make choices that will promote healthy brain development.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: I approach codependency concerns by focusing on identifying unhealthy relationship patterns and helping set appropriate boundaries.

specialities.name: Early Recovery
specialities.description: The first few weeks of sobriety can feel hopeless and overwhelming; this is a time when the intense emotions you previously numbed with substances flood in. Be kind to yourself and know that what you are feeling is normal. For the last several years, I have had helped clients slow down and hone self-regulation skills to avoid relapse.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Being wrapped up in addiction can feel incredibly discouraging at times. However, there are tools you can use and lifestyle changes you can make to alleviate cravings and manage triggers. I am dual-credentialed as a Licensed Professional Counselor and Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor II and have worked with clients with co-occurring mental health and substance use concerns helping them obtain sobriety.

name: Jessica Lynn
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I'm Jess, a board-certified psychiatric nurse practitioner (PMHNP) licensed in Oregon to provide medication management and psychotherapy.
ideal_client: Are you someone currently experiencing difficulty with your mood or having trouble managing anxious feelings? Or do you struggle with obsessive thoughts or anxious rumination that interfere with your daily functioning or quality of life? If so, there are evidence-based, effective treatments available.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is thorough, holistic, and person-centered. I believe in taking the time to truly understand you, which may mean that we don't reach a diagnostic conclusion on the initial visit-these decisions should not be rushed. I consider myself a LGBTQIA+ ally with a trauma-informed approach. I utilize a combination of evidence-based medication, therapy, and natural options tailored to your unique needs. While my focus may often include prescribing medication, it's important to me that we prioritize finding the right approach for you, ensuring an individualized and effective treatment plan. I currently utilize cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and supportive therapy in my work together with clients.

name: Jamie Krahulec
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I use expressive therapy approaches with adults and children, and also walk-and-talk (outdoor) therapy.
ideal_client: Knowing what or how to say something can often feel overwhelming. I work with people living with depression, grief, struggling with self-identity, neurodivergence, and who are part of the LGBTQIA+ community. I specialize in working with adults and children ages 2-10. I incorporate sensory experiences into sessions to help people process what’s happening in their world using their own language. I offer walk-and-talk which is therapy outdoors- nature has a significant influence on mental health.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach represents my personal philosophy that we are all connected to and shaped by one another and that we each have our own perceptions of reality based on our unique experiences and observations. I consider myself a person-centered therapist and use psychoeducation to offer you understanding how brain development nuances show up in your life. This means that I consider it my role to offer you authentic and genuine reflections, help increase your self-confidence, and help strengthen your mental capacity to handle internal and external stressors (that you have likely already been facing daily). I have a master’s degree from George Fox University and my training includes expressive art therapy, interpersonal neurobiology and psychopharmacology, trauma-informed cognitive behavior therapy, psychopathology, child/parent relationship therapy, sand tray therapy, gender-affirming play therapy, and using narrative therapy to help a person live with grief and trauma.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Being alive can feel really hard sometimes and it is easy to feel stuck in sadness. I believe that every part of you has validity and worth and that even the most unhealthy moments do not mean you are a failure or lost forever. There are no time-limits or rules when it comes to emotions, especially grief. Our brains are incredibly complex and are experts at hiding and misdirection. Sometimes our “bad” thoughts and behavior occur because our minds are trying to protect us and survive. I believe that no one is defined by their mistakes. I think people are always in the process of rediscovering themselves. Some stories are intertwined with tragedy and challenges, and I think that our time together is for you to tell yours. I consider my role as a therapist to be a person who helps you explore the different parts of yourself and helps you look towards the future with purpose. I want to sit beside you, listen, and hopefully offer clarity/relief. I want you to know that YOU ARE ENOUGH.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: The benefits of nature on mental and physical health are well documented and are the reason I offer outdoor therapy. My approach is through a “walk-and-talk" which can mean a stroll through a park, walking a trail, or hiking-- whatever level of comfort a person may have and want to pursue. Incorporating sensory experiences into therapy is a great way to access and integrate languages that are not available with words.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: I use child-centered play therapy integrated with expressive art therapy because I believe that to help children requires using their own language and taking care to communicate within individual developmental parameters. I’ve had training for children and parents including gender-affirming play therapy, parenting amidst the pandemic, trust based relational intervention, child-parent relationship therapy, trauma-focused CBT and am working towards certification as a Registered Play Therapist.

specialities.name: Expressive Art Therapy
specialities.description: I incorporate sensory experiences into sessions to help people process what’s happening in their world using their own language.

specialities.name: Sand Tray
specialities.description: Incorporating sensory experiences into therapy is a great way to access and integrate languages that are not available with words.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I use child-centered play therapy integrated with expressive art therapy because I believe that to help children requires using their own language and taking care to communicate within individual developmental parameters. I’ve had training for children and parents including trauma-focused CBT, gender-affirming play therapy, parenting amidst the pandemic, trust based relational intervention, child-parent relationship therapy and am working towards certification as a Registered Play Therapist.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is deeper than sadness and death is not the only loss that must be experienced in order to grieve. The swirling emotions within "grief" are messy, confusing, frustrating and contradictory. My training has taught me techniques to help people process, acknowledge, and learn ways to adjust to living. One of the most important parts to understand/accept is that every grief experience is unique and no matter the way it shows up in your reactions or behaviors, it is trying to serve a purpose.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have noticed that the biggest reason for relationship distress seems to come from communication and this is not unique to a type of relationship. I can help you learn how to find meaning in the empty spaces. I believe we all have capacity in our hearts to love more than one person and as long as the partnership is consensual then there is no reason why multiple relationships should be an issue for anyone not interested.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: My training in topics related to human growth and development has provided me with physiological knowledge that has helped people learn the language to help them bridge relationship barriers within themselves and with others. Especially for youth the interwoven narratives of identity can be confusing and can cause distress and my role is to help untangle. My lived experience has given me the confidence and awareness of resources to advocate for and support people in whatever capacity is needed.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Being alive can feel really hard sometimes and it is easy to feel stuck in sadness. I believe that every part of you has validity and worth and that even the most unhealthy moments do not mean you are a failure or lost forever. There are no time-limits or rules when it comes to emotions, especially grief. Our brains are incredibly complex and are experts at hiding and misdirection. Sometimes our “bad” thoughts and behavior occur because our minds are trying to protect us and that is okay.

name: Liz Powers Wells
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Skilled, attuned in-person & online therapy for neurodivergent individuals & families specializing in play and trauma therapy.
ideal_client: I work with neurodivergent kids, teens, and adults navigating anxiety, overwhelm, or burnout—often related to ADHD or autism. Neurodivergent individuals often need a creative therapist who can tailor approaches designed for neurotypical people. Many of my clients are seeking understanding, connection, and strategies that respect their unique experiences. I also help parents and families strengthen bonds and meet the needs of children whose nervous systems process the world differently.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work is rooted in a deep, unwavering belief in every person's potential for growth. I am guided by curiosity, empathy, and a commitment to being fully present with you. I draw from my EMDR training and attachment-based, trauma-informed approaches to help clients recognize patterns, soothe their nervous systems, and reconnect with their inner strength and self-trust. For younger clients, I provide a safe, non-judgmental space through child-centered play therapy to facilitate authentic expression and self-discovery. I also help parents understand and strategize around behaviors that may seem challenging but are often the child’s way of expressing a deep need for connection and support.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I like to imagine a world where we could create a society in which everyone's needs are met and we all have a place. I think the right kind of therapy can challenge capitalist systems that often leave neurodivergent and otherwise disabled people behind. I’m fascinated by how the neurodivergent brain offers fresh perspectives on disrupting broken systems. I believe that strengthening interpersonal connections in therapy can ripple outward, shaping not just individual lives but communities and future generations.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: I’m pursuing certification in play therapy under the supervision of a Registered Play Therapist, with extensive training and hands-on experience, including running groups. My approach is rooted in Child-Centered Play Therapy (CCPT), which trusts in a child’s innate capacity for growth when offered safety, presence, and respect. CCPT fits with how I see kids: capable, creative, and deserving of space where their voice leads the way.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I work with autistic clients across the lifespan, tailoring therapy to their sensory needs, processing styles, and ways of relating. With deep personal and clinical insight into how the autistic nervous system differs, I offer an approach rooted in safety, self-trust, and relief from overwhelm. I see trauma as a near-universal part of the autistic experience—not because of autism, but because the world too often demands conformity over authenticity.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I specialize in anxiety, especially in young people who feel crushed by the pace and pressure of modern life. Many of my clients carry quiet dread about the future—climate, politics, survival—and feel it in their bodies before they have words for it. I help them slow down, make space for their feelings, and find small, steady ways to guard their peace. Therapy becomes a place where their sensitivity is not a liability, but something worth honoring and protecting.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have experience in child development and specialized training in Child-Centered Play Therapy (CCPT). I create a space where children can express themselves freely through play. I trust that every child has an innate drive toward growth, and my role is to provide the safety, warmth, and attunement that allow this to unfold. Drawing from my work in schools, homes, and the community, I support children in processing emotions, building self-esteem, and navigating challenges at their own pace.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: With decades of training and experience providing consultation and training to teachers, parents, and multidisciplinary teams, I help parents uncover the emotional truth behind their child’s behavior, recognizing that all behavior is communication. I offer sensory support and attachment-focused strategies, collaborating with parents to develop practical solutions that foster connection, emotional regulation, and well-being for the whole family.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I approach PTSD with an understanding of how trauma fractures the self, drawing from my EMDR basic training, attachment, and parts work to explore the hurt, protective, and surviving parts of you. I guide you through uncovering the emotions and beliefs that shape your responses, honoring the parts that help you hold on and those that need healing. Through this work, we create a space for integration, where your nervous system can begin to find safety, regulation without pushing through pain.

name: Melissa Owens LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I can help you heal relationships, traumatic experiences and addictive/compulsive behaviors.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I can help you get unstuck; strengthen your communication, connections, relationships and boundaries; free yourself from addiction, addictive relationships, and compulsive behaviors; heal emotional reactivity and stop hurting yourself and those you love. I am skilled in DBT, Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR); Somatic Experiencing; Internal Family Systems (IFS) and other Ego-State therapies involving mind/body awareness using breath, movement and imagery, as well as Jungian Active Imagination and Kundalini Yoga therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been providing therapy for over 20 years. Prior to establishing a private practice, I served as Clinical Supervisor and Addictions and Mental Health Counselor at DePaul Treatment Center, an adult dual diagnosis residential program. I worked on both the men's and the women's floors and became familiar with the interaction between trauma, relationship difficulties, and addictive/compulsive behavior.. I have been an ESL Teacher and Bilingual Education Coordinator and worked at a Women’s Resource Center as Skills Trainer. I earned an MA in Counseling Psychology with Addictions Specialty at Lewis & Clark College. Prior to that I held a Teacher Certification from the University of Alaska. I earned a BA in literature from the University of California, San Diego.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDRIA approved Level II training and over 15 years experience using this treatment.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I have extensive experience working with couples in conflict, repairing wounds and distance, infidelity issues, traumatic backgrounds, anger, sexual problems, or problems of substance and/or sexual addiction. I use strategies from John Gottman, Terry Real, Dan Wile, Imago Therapy, and David Schnarch's Crucible approach. I can help you repair your relationship.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I am trained and experienced in traditional DBT therapy, which I have taught to large groups of residents in treatment and also used extensively in individual therapy to work on addictions, emotional reactivity, relationship problems and compulsive behaviors.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I am trained and experienced in a variety of approaches to relationship and marital issues, including anger, cruelty, withholding, infidelity, sexual problems, addictions, trauma and emotional reactivity.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have formal training and extensive experience using Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR). Internal Family Systems (IFS) and body oriented psychotherapies to heal the wounds of traumatic experiences. Trauma is unhealed unintegrated experience and healing is possible.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I teach emotion-body/mental-pattern awareness, and what to do with that awareness. I use Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, body centered psychotherapies and Yogic techniques to show you how to manage anxiety. I have practiced Kundalini Yoga for over 30 years and can teach you to make use of breathing techniques to calm the nervous system at will.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I use a mindfulness based approach to healing depression and depressive anger through small changes in habits and large changes in perspective.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: I have extensive training in the treatment of substance abuse as well as addictive and compulsive behaviors (shopping, sexual addiction and porn use). I use a harm-reduction approach including the Sinclair Method for alcohol abuse.

name: Mara McLoughlin
title: Speech Therapist
intro: Speech therapist whose neurodiverse, multicultural, and multidisciplinary team specializes in social skills coaching.
ideal_client: If you or your teen/young adult is struggling socially due to adhd, autism, or social anxiety — we can help. Our team teaches a modified version of UCLA's PEERS program. We add in neuroscience-informed nervous system education, mindfulness, and interoception skills to lay the foundation for better social communication and social interaction. We know that it's painful for parents to watch their child struggle socially and not know what to do. Our team is multi-disciplinary & multi-cultural.

approaches.What We Specialize In: My team specializes in a community-based, proactive approach to mental health. We work with autistic and other socially struggling teens, young adults, and their parents. Our lens is neurodiversity-affirming and informed by the social model of disability and the latest autism research by actually autistic researchers. We teach in a group setting, entirely via Zoom. Class materials, handouts, videos, class roster is all provided to families for the 16-week masterclass. We provide a safe, sheltered small group context in which participants are seen and heard, validated and acknowledged. These are not soft skills — these are hard skills. We've got your back.

approaches.Our Personal Beliefs and Interests: Being effective is doing what works. We teach interpersonal — and intrapersonal — skills to anyone who is motivated to learn more about themselves and others, and how to use discernment to navigate the social world. It's complicated! And even those who have great social skills don't necessarily know how to teach them.
