Ours is an experiential approach that also trains the environment — in this case, the family context — to look at behavior through an empathy lens. We teach about self-regulation and co-regulation, which is the strongest safety cue. We believe that humans heal in community. We are a multilingual, multicultural team of speech therapists, occupational therapists, direct support workers, and licensed professional counselors — a crackerjack group to which your family will have full access throughout the 16-week course.

name: Michelle Anderson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a radical queer therapist offering relationship counseling and trauma processing for people who want more closeness, joy, and justice.
ideal_client: I work with queer couples and relationships of all configurations, as well as individuals with childhood and/or relational trauma. I tend to be a good fit with people who have been told they are "too sensitive" or "too emotional," who want to undo harmful messaging received in childhood and/or from larger systems in order to live in greater alignment with their values.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe a safe therapeutic relationship can be a foundation for harnessing community, connectivity, interdependence, and joy. I aim to build trust with authenticity, non-judgment, and humor. I believe in working through emotions and sensations, not around them--that rather than offering band-aid approaches, "the poison can be the medicine." This means leaning into stuck feelings in order to release them, often with a blend of mind-body approaches, including inner child and parts work. I'm here to help you find your true, core self, not fit you into a box.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I have Advanced Level attachment-focused training through the EMDRIA-certified Center for Excellence in EMDR Therapy.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I love working with queer couples and relationships. I work within an emotionally focused framework, meaning connecting via our feelings is the key to gaining closeness and healing attachment wounds. We may also delve into how each person's "protective parts" and unconscious messaging received in childhood are contributing to an unwanted relationship cycle.

name: Kate Keating
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello! If you're struggling with anxiety, depression, or other painful patterns, let's meet and discover new paths forward.
ideal_client: Are you hoping to understand painful patterns that have been plaguing you for years? My practice focuses on understanding the roadblocks that are in your way, making peace with these obstacles, and moving beyond them. Couples: are you stuck, recycling the same conflicts and arguments? Are you hoping for deeper satisfaction? We will make sense of these concerns as we learn new relational moves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize a Person-Centered approach that often draws up Narrative Therapy, Internal Family Systems, Emotionally Focused Therapy and mindfulness interventions. Additionally, I'm trained in EMDR and can guide you through that experience. Most of the time, my therapeutic style looks like a natural conversation, but things will be moving and shifting and at times we will engage in specific interventions. Our work together will be collaborative and creative. I strive to provide a sanctuary for my clients away from the chaos of life, a space just for you. You will be challenged in this process, but I want our sessions to be something you look forward to each week.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My work as a counselor started in schools, where I've worked with hundreds of middle and high school students, supporting them (and their parents!) through the incredibly tricky time of pre-adolescence and adolescence. Since then, I've expanded my scope to include therapy with adults and families. I hold a Master's degree in counseling and have advanced training from the Portland Dialectical Behavioral Institute and Portland State University.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR from an EMDRIA training program.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I have taken an post-graduate course on ACT and am drawn to the gentle, compassionate nature of the approach. I think you'll find it to be transformative.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Because I am interested in self-harm, suicidal ideation, and anxiety as presented in pre-teens and teens, DBT is especially relevant for my practice. I have read various DBT manuals and have attended advanced training at the Portland DBT institute.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: While I am not certified as an IFS therapist, I have educated myself extensively on this transformative therapeutic approach.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety impacts so many of us. I'm endlessly curious about how this symptom manifests and why humans continue to be plagued by it. Through therapeutic interventions, we can make peace with anxiety and, in doing so, loosen its grip.

specialities.name: Self-Harming
specialities.description: Self-harm was a common reason students came to see me in my work as a school counselor. I have researched this issue extensively and have advanced training from the Portland DBT institute.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: This is a special interest of mine. My expertise in this area comes from endlessly researching this topic, being a parent myself, and working with parents in my practice.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Having worked with hundreds of middle and high school students, I have a strong sense of the prevalence of depression amongst young people. In my time as a school counselor, I've engaged students in therapeutic interventions to address their depressed states.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I co-facilitated a grief group for middle school students with a clinician from the Dougy Center. The group was specific to students who had lost an immediate family member. I've also done a lot of personal reading about grief and loss.

name: Louise Davis
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a therapist that incorporates somatic therapy, mindfulness practices as well as nature-based interventions in our sessions together.
ideal_client: In sessions, we explore both talk therapy as well as body-based approaches in your healing journey. I am excited to incorporate yoga principles and practices into her sessions. I often include nature-based techniques as a form of teaching and healing. I have recently completed the Integrative Trauma Coach Training, with a focus on body-based trauma-informed practice using somatic therapy, mindfulness/meditation and breathwork.

approaches.My Background: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker, and received my MSW from George Mason University and have extensive experience working with adults, families and youth in the Washington D.C. area, Arizona and Oregon. In recent years, I have focused on adults experiencing life changes such as empty nesting, divorce, career changes, retirement, caring for a family member, loss/grief, and supporting professionals in the social work profession. I provide supervision to those seeking licensure and I am a RYT 200-hour yoga teacher.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My approach is to provide a safe space for individuals to process their feelings, own what is theirs, and release limiting beliefs about themselves. It is my belief that everyone has the answers within themselves and the role of therapy is to support individuals on their own unique journey. It is equally as important for a therapist to have a strong commitment to their own growth in order to show up and be present for others.

name: Mary Hacopian
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Hello my name is Mary Hacopian and I am clinical psychologist that has a private practice in Beaverton.
ideal_client: Over the past ten years, I have worked with a diverse range of clients in my private practice. My practice consists of families, adolescents, and adults of all ages. I have a lot of experience working with depression, anxiety, and PTSD. It is rewarding to witness the growth and progress of my clients as they work towards healing and self-discovery.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe in providing a safe and interactive environment for my clients to delve into their thoughts and emotions. Through collaboration, I assist them in overcoming obstacles and uncovering their inner strength. I offer support and guidance to help clients reach their goals and start living the life they desire.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Throughout my career, I have been committed to promoting mental health and wellness for all individuals, regardless of their background or circumstances. I believe in the power of therapy to facilitate healing, growth, and empowerment, and I am dedicated to helping my clients achieve their full potential.

name: Jackie Turner
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Hello! It's not always easy to reach out for help, but I’m so glad you’re considering taking that brave step. Let's talk.
ideal_client: Are you wanting more connection with the world around you, but feel trapped by past wounds or narratives that make you want to hide away? Are you a person who has been told they are too sensitive, and are struggling to make sense of your unique way of relating to the world? Are you working through family-of-origin wounds, walking through grief, or are you and your partner navigating conflict in your relationship? For these issues and others, I would love to walk alongside you on your journey.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I'm an integrative therapist who incorporates aspects of attachment theory, Parts work/IFS, emotionally-focused therapy, and ecopsychology. While I offer insights, observations, and gentle challenges, my priority is to guide you toward building the skills you need to uncover and connect to your internal sources of strength, insight, intuition, and integrity. In couples and relationship therapy, I will compassionately challenge you to identify and grow from your well-worn patterns and do the brave work of stepping into more authentic connection with your partner. Healing comes when it is meant to, and sometimes we have to move through the muck and the messiness before we reach moments of breakthrough. I provide a safe and positive container for you to move through these difficult periods on the journey toward greater connection to one another.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I support every person's right to be honored for who they truly are, and I believe in educating myself as a therapist to support my clients in their identities. I work to attend to issues of oppression and marginalization as they arise, while also holding onto the fact that you are your own, complex, nuanced self. I am open to all spiritual and religious belief systems and respectful of how much or how little you want to include these beliefs/traditions in your therapy work. I believe strongly in every person's right and ability to define their unique values, and I emphasize building inner trust, integrity, and discernment in the process of living your values in the world. No matter who you are, I believe that you are worthy of dignity, respect, and care. I am firmly opposed to dehumanization and injustice in all its forms, and I believe in approaching everyone with curiosity, humility, and in good faith.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: We put a lot of pressure on our romantic relationships - we are expected to be everything to each other. We idealize our partners and then struggle with disillusionment. This is a lot to navigate and it's easy to lose sight of each other and lose sight of that initial spark. In couples therapy, I support and encourage you in opening up to a different kind of experience with your partner, as well as developing the skills needed to build an authentic, interdependent connection.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory is my main theoretical orientation and informs most of the work I do. I believe that we are all wired for connection and need it for survival - as a result, our relationships are essential, yet we often have relational wounds that can make it hard for us to connect, all the way down to the nervous system level. As such, it is central to our well-being to be able to explore and understand our patterns and learn to attend to those deep needs.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I utilize parts work and aspects of IFS extensively in my work. We all contain multitudes, as the saying goes. Our inner protectors can use a variety of tactics to keep us safe, but these can often cause us trouble in other ways. In therapy we work to bring insight and voice to those multitudes we contain within us, and we also, importantly, work to build a stronger connection to your core self to allow you more agency to take back the reins and develop self-trust.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Are you healing from family-of-origin or relational wounds that have led you to suppress your true self to please others? Do you put others ahead of you, to the detriment of your own needs? Are you struggling to figure out who you are, what you want, and how to live an authentic life that is still full of love and connection? In therapy, we'll work to untangle the old stories keeping us stuck, and work toward transcending them.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: ​In couples and relationship therapy, I will compassionately challenge you to identify and grow from your well-worn patterns and do the brave work of stepping into more authentic connection with your partner. Healing comes when it is meant to, and often when we least expect it. Sometimes we have to move through the muck and the messiness for awhile before we reach moments of breakthrough. I provide a safe and positive container for you to move through difficulty and into deeper relationship.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: To grieve is to love. We might grieve the end of an era of our lives, the end of an important relationship, or the death of a loved one. We might grieve events occurring in our world that feel out of our control, or we could be experiencing griefs we are struggling to name but that we still feel acutely. I have supported clients of many ages in navigating grief and loss, and I lean on existential and transpersonal psychology in my work in this area in particular, in addition to attachment.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Sometimes, we find ourselves lost in the universe. Maybe we have lost touch with our spirituality after spiritual abuse, but are still longing for a connection to something greater. Maybe we are unpacking old, limiting, or oppressive beliefs from our religious, spiritual, political, or community groups, and are unsure of where to find our authentic intuition, spirituality, and integrity. I work to support clients in building an authentic connection to what is true for them, without shame.

name: Lev Schneidman
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: My goal is to support clients to become the most alive and connected version of themselves through somatic mindfulness and self exploration.
ideal_client: Are you struggling to connect with pleasure in your life? Do you feel numb, anxious or disconnected from your body? Do you long for more connection with yourself and others but do not know how to take that next step towards what you want? This practice integrates the principles of somatic therapy, mindfulness, and the exploration of pleasure, sexuality and queerness to promote overall well-being and personal transformation.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I believe in creating supportive and empowering spaces where individuals can explore, notice, and redefine intimacy and pleasure as it relates to oneself, others, and the world. My approach is first and foremost to help build, grow, and reinforce one’s relationship to oneself. I received my master's in social work at San Francisco State University in 2017. I have worked both in direct client care and in macro social work in the Oregon State Public Health Department because I believe that change must be made both on individual, community and institutional levels. My background is working with LGBTQIA2S+ communities.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In my therapeutic approach, I practice mindfulness and somatic approaches, always moving at a pace set by those I work with. This means the client leads the sessions, and I'm here to guide and support them. I believe in a person-centered and relationship-centered approach, which is also deeply rooted in trauma-informed care. Sex and pleasure positivity is an integral part of my practice. I am also polyamory and kink affirming. Together, we can explore and understand the messages your body sends – the "yes," "no," and "maybe” messages that allows one to move towards the life they want. I deeply value the courage and vulnerability it takes to begin therapy and, as a practitioner, I'm committed to fostering trust within the therapeutic relationship. I firmly believe in supporting my clients to access their internal strength and wisdom to navigate life's challenges with some support.

name: Kiersten Lindahl
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Welcome! My name is Kiersten, and I am a marriage and family therapist associate I work with teens, individuals, & relationships.
ideal_client: I believe that people are relational beings that innately crave connection with others and reach for it in the best way they know how. When there is a feeling of disconnect between yourself and the world or with those in your life, it can be lonely, saddening and confusing. I aim to help my clients explore what is causing them distress whether individually or relationally.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach each client with the understanding that their story and experience is unique to them. I seek to join with clients in a respectful way that acknowledges their own wisdom through practical, supportive, and empathetic connection. I recognize the array of challenges a person will come into my office facing and I seek to integrate emotions, thoughts, experiences and actions to hopefully move towards a happier more fulfilled life.My work is approached from a collaborative blend of different theories including Attachment, Family Systems, Emotion-Focused, and Internal Family Systems. Some of my goals with using these theories are to increase awareness and insight around your patterns in relationships and where you are getting stuck. We may do this by using your emotions in times of distress as information rather as something to avoid or be afraid of. We may look at some parts of us that are confusing and frustrating and try to approach them with curiosity as opposed to criticism.

name: Amy Manion
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I am passionate about providing a welcoming, collaborative, comfortable space that supports my clients through the growth process.
ideal_client: I have a special interest in perinatal mental health, including pregnancy and postpartum, and supporting individuals and couples as they navigate the parenting process. I also have an interest in supporting children, families and adults who are looking for strategies to effectively manage ADHD symptoms. Working with individuals, couples, and families who are seeking solutions for connection, intimacy, and overall satisfaction in their lives is my passion.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize compassion, humor, and respect in my work with the goal of assisting my clients as they move towards positive changes and living a more authentic and meaningful life. Together, we can make connections, gain insight and question some of the underlying, unconscious, and outdated patterns that may be keeping you stuck or holding you back.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I have additional or certificate level trainings in sex therapy, perinatal mental health, ADHD, CBT, Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), Emotionally Focused Individual Therapy (EFIT), Internal Family Systems Therapy (IFS) and also completed Level 2 training in Gottman Method Couples Therapy.

name: Richard Marshall
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I'm here to help you navigate life’s trials and transitions in a supportive, respectful, and safe space.
ideal_client: I work with individuals, couples, and families. I help individuals with many issues, including anxiety, depression, relationship problems, family conflict, and addiction issues. I assist couples in building warm, loving connection by guiding them to communicate in new, helpful ways in which they truly feel seen and heard, and also by teaching them to use new tools to move from disharmony back to harmony. I provide families a space to be heard and seek to restore balance and connection.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Life can sometimes hand us more than we can easily handle. At these times, I help clients navigate life’s trials and transitions. I believe that everyone has abundant natural strengths and capacities to draw from to achieve goals and move closer to their desired life. I collaborate with you to harness and amplify your own strengths in the service of achieving your therapeutic goals, and achieve personal and relational well-being. I provide a warm, inviting, and respectful space for you to explore and express your thoughts and feelings. I view people holistically, considering various life contexts, including biological, psychological, family, social, cultural, spiritual, and also including race, socio-economic class, gender, sexual orientation, and ability. I endeavor to help clients build a sense of interpersonal connection in their lives, by finding their voice, and also by building accountability.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I bring a systemic, culturally-sensitive, relational, and trauma-informed perspective to my work with you. Additionally, I am a lifelong musician and am always open to exploring ways that music or other creative expression can be a positive and supportive part of your life.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotion Focused Therapy (EFT) is an evidence-based treatment, and together with Relational Life Therapy (RLT), is the therapeutic model I most commonly use with couples. Its power comes from its ability to tap into people's primal need for a close attachment bond to others. It helps people express their softer, more vulnerable emotions with the aim of increasing connection and closeness to others.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I use Terry Real's Relational Life Therapy (RLT) model when working with couples and individuals dealing with relationship problems. It incorporates family of origin work, inner child work, and powerful relational tools to foster meaningful, connected, and fulfilling relationships.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I use IFS (also referred to as "parts" work) with clients in order to heal wounded parts of ourselves and come to rely more on our immutable core selves. The goal with IFS is to help clients become more compassionate, curious, clear, creative, calm, confident, courageous, and connected.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: Since I began practicing, I have used my graduate level training in family systems theory in order to help individuals and families identify and interrupt unhelpful recurring patterns of behavior and bring about lasting, positive systemic change. Additionally, family systems-informed therapy can help clients heal from damaging inter-generational trauma.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: I enjoy using Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT) because it uses the client's own goals as a motivation for change. Therapy is therefore custom tailored to the individual client, harnessing the transformative power of the client's own strengths and interests, and builds upon ways the client may already be solving their own problem.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: My Masters level training focused on family systems theory as used in the treatment of a wide variety of family problems, including couple and marital conflict. I have used this training since 2013 to help couples resolve conflict and foster deeper connection and relational well-being. I commonly use Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT) and Relational Life Therapy (RLT) when working with couples.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety might be the most common problem I have helped people overcome. I also have some familiarity, as I have suffered from an anxiety disorder myself. There can be many causes and forms of anxiety, and I work collaboratively and holistically in supporting clients to find solutions that work best for them.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression and other mood disorders are very common among people seeking therapy. I have helped many people make lasting positive changes to their mood by working collaboratively and holistically in supporting clients to find solutions that work best for them.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: My Masters level training focused on family systems theory as used in the treatment of a wide variety of family problems. I have used this training since 2013 to help families resolve conflict and foster relational well-being.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: I have specialized Masters-level training in treating addictions which I have continually utilized in my practice. This training incorporates family systems theory, which examines and aims to restructure ways in which the entire family can organize its behavior around those family members suffering from addiction.

name: Caroline Kinsley
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: As a dance/movement therapist & counselor I will invite the mind and body to join in the therapeutic space.
ideal_client: Are you ready to begin or continue your therapeutic journey? If you are curious or open to incorporating dance/movement and mindfulness based practices into your therapeutic space, welcome! I offer Telehealth dance/movement therapy & psychotherapy services. Clients I work best are experiencing worry, sadness, emotional discomfort and are open to explore additional ways to express, soothe, calm, and understand what is coming up for them.

approaches.What I Specialize In: My work experience includes working with individuals over the past 5 years managing depression, anxiety, relational trauma, perfectionism, people pleasing, and difficult transitions. I approach these experiences with a variety of evidence-based lenses, adjusting to what best meets the needs of my clients, including dance/movement therapy, psychodynamic/psychoanalytic theory, internal family systems therapy, trauma informed practices, mindful self compassion, and mindfulness based cognitive behavioral therapy. I’ve worked with adolescents and adults in a variety of settings, including private practice, school-based, community mental health, and partial hospitalization. Just as I encourage my clients to do, I continue to seek opportunities to learn, and discover new approaches and ways of moving through my therapeutic practice.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My personal values are relationship building, promoting integration, and exploring through movement. I love understanding, supporting, and relating with people. I find the more we join, the more we know and discover common interests and humility. As something I value, I hope to share this very same with others as well. My value of integrating the body and mind throughout the whole therapeutic process is reflective in my life as well. A large part of what I love to do involves movement. I’m a dancer, yogi, skier, backpacker, and whitewater kayaker. These activities fill my cup-they allow me to move through wild places with others in many different ways. Being a member of these communities allows me to spend time with others in embodied and authentic ways.

specialities.name: Dance / Movement Therapy
specialities.description: As a Board Certified Dance/movement Therapist, I've obtained the highest national certification achievable by the American Dance Therapy Association professional organization. As such, I approach the work from the lens' of psychotherapy and exploring how the mind and body can work together in the space. I have extensive training working with individuals managing depression, anxiety, relational trauma, and self-esteem concerns through the use of dance/movement therapy.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I incorporate the use of mindfulness based strategies such as meditation, guided visualizations, and mindful movement experiences into my sessions. I've attended numerous continuing education courses and consultation groups focusing on the use of mindfulness based approaches to therapy.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Understanding why you are constantly worrying and preparing for worst case scenario is not a simple process. This process requires the mind, body, and emotions to work together. I have extensive experience working with individuals to shift their understanding and relationship with anxiety. I offer a space where exploring and resourcing happens in multiple ways offering a holistic approach of addressing anxiety symptoms.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Being able to understand and trust oneself is key to feeling confident. Through dance/movement therapy and mindfulness-based approaches, there will be space to strengthen this inner relationship. You will explore how to build the relationship with non-judgment, kindness, and love. We will explore how to make this a strong foundation as life will bring novel and unexpected situations. Therefore, if you do temporarily lose trust in yourself you have skills to kindly return back again and again.

name: Carmen Ryan
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I create a safe space for families struggling with behavioral or emotional issues at home and/or school, specializing in education success.
ideal_client: I create a safe, non-judgmental space for children 4-14 and their families through deep listening and observation, forming an authentic, trusting, compassionate relationship where understanding and healing can begin by processing difficult experiences, thoughts, or behaviors. I take a whole-brain, whole-body approach to customize a treatment plan for each client, building upon their strengths and gifts to create a calm, grounded client that finds joy and can set goals to pursue their dreams.

approaches.My Background: I've served families, students and staff as a school counselor for the past 11 years in primary and middle school settings developing inclusive practices where all students attend their home school and learn in general education classrooms, collaborating with internal and external specialists to ensure every student fully accesses their education in order to unleash their genius. I'm pursuing my professional counselor license to deepen my work with families, helping them find more peace and balance at home, as well as navigating the school setting to ensure they have the resources and support they need for their student(s) to thrive. I've earned many certificates and highlights include Play, Nature and Art Therapy; Trauma-Informed Practices; Crisis Prevention and Care; YogaCalm; and Collaborative Problem Solving. My dream is to create a healing focused rescue farm for families that have experienced trauma.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Humans are designed with a space within us that yearns to connect with our creator, and this need is filled in different ways - something I honor with my clients. Faith and community are my greatest strengths, and I’ve explored and grown them in many ways through the years. I love nature and how we are interconnected, as we can't be whole without this understanding and interaction. I have a heart and passion for rescue animals, as helping them heal is such a special process that has shown me the power of love, understanding and patience.

name: Dmitri Dosamantes
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I specialize in individual, family, couples and gender therapy.
ideal_client: I provide support to individuals and families to find conflict resolution, experiencing grief, couples needing help reconnecting, or communicating, and folx across the LGBTQ spectrum. I also specialize in gender therapy. I am WPATH trained and provide assessments and letters for gender affirming care.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is solution focused, relational and affirming. I strive to be culturally competent, and inclusive of all ways of being. I work from a compassionate and collaborative, strength-based approach, and capitalize on what works for you. I view the therapeutic process as an opportunity for us to work together to identify and address barriers in your life. Together we will find what best fits you.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: Gender therapy is one of my specialties. I am WPATH trained and gender affirming. If you identify as Transgender, NB, Agender, questioning, or anything else know that you are included and welcome. I meet you where you are at.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I've worked with the LGBTQ community for many years. If you are struggling with coming out, or questioning your sexuality, know that wherever you are in your journey, I am here for you.

name: Rachel Boll
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help young adults and those in life transitions navigate anxiety, depression, and trauma, fostering clarity, resilience, and self-growth.
ideal_client: My clients are young adults and individuals facing major life transitions who feel overwhelmed, stuck, or uncertain about their next steps. They may struggle with anxiety, depression, or unresolved trauma, seeking clarity and deeper self-understanding. I provide a compassionate, supportive space where they can process emotions, build confidence, and move forward with greater resilience and purpose.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe in a holistic, body-mind approach to healing. My work integrates EMDR, Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), mindfulness, and somatic therapy to help clients process trauma, shift negative thought patterns, and reconnect with themselves. Many of the people I work with carry unresolved pain in both their minds and bodies, and I guide them in releasing stored trauma in a way that fosters long-term healing. Using somatic awareness and mindfulness techniques, I help clients develop a deeper connection to their emotions and nervous system. EMDR and CPT provide structured ways to reprocess painful experiences and reframe limiting beliefs. My approach is gentle but transformative, helping clients feel safe while exploring the deeper layers of their struggles. My goal is to empower each person to move through life transitions with resilience, clarity, and a renewed sense of self.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I am deeply committed to mental health accessibility, trauma-informed care, and social equity. I work to create a welcoming, affirming space for all individuals, including LGBTQ2A+ communities, BIPOC individuals, and those impacted by systemic oppression. My approach to therapy acknowledges the ways that social and cultural factors shape mental health, and I strive to provide culturally responsive, identity-affirming care. I believe in the mind-body connection as a tool for empowerment and in helping clients reclaim ownership over their healing process. Whether working through intergenerational trauma, societal stressors, or personal identity struggles, I encourage clients to find strength in their story. Through my work, I advocate for self-determination, healing, and emotional resilience.

name: Neil Panchmatia
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My work has a strong social justice orientation, providing an accessible, equitable and inclusive counseling experience in OR and WA.
ideal_client: My work is trauma informed, culturally responsive, and uses a social justice framework to provide an empowering and supportive safe/brave space to my clients. My practice and presence are continually shaping to affirm and center the experiences of marginalization/ exclusion that my clients experience. I also hold space for existential and spiritual contemplations of self exploration and growth. I hold an intersectional perspective on identity formation and negotiation, and celebrate difference.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Like acorns destined to become mighty oaks, I believe that we naturally gravitate towards more fulfilled and authentic versions of ourselves: thriving by achieving our highest potentials. I look forward to joining you on this journey by providing unconditional/unwavering support and empowerment. I am a Queer, person of color, kink/poly, and fat/body affirming, neurodiversity and disability centering intersectional feminist therapist who uses a non-hierarchal, collaborative and individually-tailored approach to therapy. I work from a place of cultural humility and an ever-improving understanding of my own intersections of privilege/marginalization. I believe that healing, growth and thriving result from a holistic integration of the mind, body and spirit. As my client, you will be in the driving seat of your therapeutic experience: You will have a say in determining the goals we work on, the pace we take, the approaches we adopt, and the outcomes we aspire towards.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I work with individuals and couples/unions from all sociocultural backgrounds. I specialize in therapy for: anxiety/panic, depression, post-trauma recovery (C-PTSD), body image issues/eating disorders (HAES), living with marginalization/oppression, learning allyship for marginalized groups, and living with disabilities/ chronic pain or illness. I graduated from Portland State University with a Masters in Counseling, and have accrued intensive experience working in different clinical settings over the last few years. I am multilingual (fluent in English, Gujarati, Hindi, Swahili, and Punjabi), and as a therapist, I draw heavily from my own experience as a transnational citizen: believing fully in the interconnected nature of our human experience. My theoretical orientation as a clinician is an integration of existential therapy, Internal Family Systems (IFS), and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT).

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I use tenets of ACT in my work as it holistically encapsulates the essence of true healing: learning skills while being holistically congruent with oneself.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: I have extensive training in Gestalt therapy as a therapeutic modality that has an existential-humanistic leaning.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I use tenets of Existential Humanistic therapy in my work, as I believe that we all gravitate naturally towards self-determination and holistic congruence. Self-examination and self-awareness are key steps for this - supported in therapy. I use core tenets of Compassion Focused Therapy (CFT): such as self-acceptance, emotional regulation systems, and compassionate/content living.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: I extensively use tenets of Internal Family Systems and parts work in my therapy.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: As a therapist and individual, I am keenly aware of the challenges of today’s sociocultural environment in our country and strive to do therapy that meets the unique needs and challenges of my clients – from a place of cultural humility and understanding of my own intersections of privilege/marginalization. Therapy is your place to heal, thrive and rebuild your resources to continue living.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a queer immigrant of color, I am personally familiar with the challenges we experience and navigate as individuals and a community. I am keenly aware of the healing and collaboration we need to work towards within our community, and the activism for rights and freedoms still left to do outside of it. I identify as nonbinary (genderfluid) and use he/they pronouns.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: Too often we are told we are not good enough and we need to change how we look, sound, move etc. Entire businesses run on making us feel less than. In such a cultural environment, being ourselves fully and unapologetically is the best revolution we can engage in. I work with clients using tenets of HAES and Intuitive Eating to create tailored programs of radical self love and body diversity.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I specialize in working with individuals experiencing anxiety, phobias or panic attacks. I also focus on working with individuals navigating post-trauma recovery and living with PTSD. I use tenets of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) and other current trauma informed modalities to create an individually-tailored therapeutic approach for my clients.

name: Lauren D'Agostino
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I believe the work of therapy is to come home to ourselves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that the work of therapy is to come home to ourselves. Who we are is a blend of the ways we were raised, supported, marginalized and tended to. Our selfhood is our own and co-created by the people around us, and therapy is a gentle process of forming nourishing ties to others and learning to trust our own inner knowing. I work from a somatic and intergenerational framework, assisting clients in weaving together our bodies, minds, relationships and ways of knowing. In therapy, I will ask you challenging questions, validate your sorrow and rage and shine a light on your innate strengths. I will walk with you while we explore your histories, identities and dreams. I work in-person, virtually and ecotherapeutically (outdoors).

name: Joanna Sullivan
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I am a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner, proud mom, dedicated member of the LGBTQI+ community, and a feminist.
ideal_client: My areas of specialty include preconception, pregnancy and postpartum psychiatric care, as well as care for people in the perimenopausal transition. Additionally, I offer affirming care for LGBTQI+ and neurodivergent individuals. I also enjoy caring for healthcare providers, parents and people going through life transitions, such as divorce.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I hold advanced training as a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) from Frontier Nursing University. My clinical training includes private practice telehealth for adults, working with children in an outpatient psychiatric clinic, as well as caring for people with a wide range of complex mental health needs in a hospital setting. Before I expanded my practice into psychiatry, I spent many years as a Certified Nurse Midwife. It has been a privilege to support individuals in various areas of reproductive health, such as family planning, prenatal and postpartum care, gynecology, and menopause management. Additionally, I’ve presented on topics such as providing care for same-sex couples and transgender parents. From 2019 to 2022, I was recognized as one of Portland Monthly's Top Nurse Midwives. If you are looking for a partner in your mental health journey, I would be honored to walk that path with you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Kinfolk Psychiatry is centered around the belief that everyone deserves care that’s compassionate, inclusive, and tailored to their unique experience. I offer psychiatric services, including medication management, to help you find the care and solutions that are right for your unique needs. As a small, primarily telehealth psychiatric practice in Oregon, my goal is to support you in navigating life’s transitions and mental health challenges. Whether you’re struggling with anxiety, depression, OCD, bipolar disorder, or other mental health concerns, I’m here to provide the support you need in a way that is tailored to your individual experience.

name: Jill Lees
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I see myself as a facilitator and supporter, guiding clients through their life challenges.
ideal_client: I specialize in supporting female clients who are grappling with anxiety, depression, life transitions, and or grief/loss. I firmly believe that you are the expert of your own life, and my role is to facilitate your journey towards self-discovery and empowerment. In my therapeutic practice, I primarily employ solutions-focused, somatic, IFS, EMDR, and psychodynamic approaches.

approaches.Our Background: Over the past 5 years, I have gained experience in diverse settings, including pediatric oncology and transitional housing for single parents. In my current practice, I specialize in working with women. I decided to become a mental health provider because I genuinely enjoy learning about others. I believe that people have the answers to their own life challenges within themselves, and I find fulfillment in facilitating their journey to uncover those solutions. I have also been a Reiki healer for over a year, and I find joy in providing support to those who may not find it in their everyday lives. I take pride in being a trustworthy, empathetic, and non-judgmental person. As a woman, I can relate to many of the struggles that women face in the mental health realm. My goal is to help women empower their voices and find the strength to be their authentic selves.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I am a lifelong learner always engaged in different trainings. I've completed trainings for for Internal Family Systems (IFS) and Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR). I believe in a holistic approach and recognize that there is no "one-size-fits-all" solution for every client. For me, it's crucial to have a diverse array of tools in my therapeutic toolkit to support each client's unique journey to healing. To maintain my clinical license, I am required to complete 40 hours of professional education every two years. I continuously seek out educational opportunities that will further develop and strengthen my skills, particularly in working with women dealing with anxiety, life transitions, and grief and loss.

name: Christine Finucane
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I'm Chris. My greatest passion is helping those who who have feelings of inadequacy, unresolved trauma and addiction using somatic approach.
ideal_client: Do you struggle with not feeling happy, fulfilled with your life? Do you struggle with depression, anxiety, low self-worth? Do you struggle with fatigue and low energy? Do you have a self-critical part that says you aren't good enough? Do you struggle to feel fully present in your work and relationships? My passion in being a therapist is helping people who don’t feel good about themselves and/or their lives. They may struggle with depression, anxiety, low self-confidence, addiction(s), PTSD.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We will use both mindfulness and Somatic Experiencing, an approach developed by Peter Levine, Ph.D., to help you come into easeful alignment with your physiology. When we are alignment with our physiology we learn to trust ourselves and our own innate inner wisdom. We are no longer living in a state of fear, anxiety and worry. I am also trained in brainspotting through phase 2 which can be a very powerful modality to heal repressed trauma. I have also recently completed a training program in Somatic EMDR.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I am very proactive in addressing all kinds of discrimination such as racial, ethnic, culture, gender, sexual orientation, ableism, etc. I am committed to addressing any systemic barriers that our patriarchal society is responsible for. I have been involved politically to address many of these issues. I work somatically with the nervous system to heal all forms of trauma.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Bringing mindful presence to areas of challenge and pain is an important part of my approach to therapy regardless of what the problem area is. We are taught that escape is the best way to cope with problems in this country/culture. Self-medicating via substances, food, sex, internet, shopping, etc. is broadcast to us on many different media platforms. Mindfulness is just the opposite. It is learning how to bring compassionate presence to our pain vs suffering.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Similar to mindfulness, Somatic therapy, also known as Somatic Experiencing, is a body focused approach to healing. Research has shown that unresolved trauma is energy that is stored in our body. Learning to befriend our bodies and to notice when we are caught in a traumatic reaction in our nervous system such as fight, flight, freeze is the first step to healing. Please see my website for more information.

specialities.name: Addiction Therapy
specialities.description: I believe there are many approaches to healing addiction. The disease model is one of the most prevalent models for understanding addiction. There are helpful components of this model such as issues of control centered around the object of addiction and the thinking that accompanies this. Addiction can also be a response to unprocessed trauma. Developing a mindful approach to treating addiction allows for a different relationship with it. Change is possible when we learn to live in the present.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: I have completed phase 1 of brainspotting and will be taking phase 2 soon. I use brainspotting in conjunction with other forms of therapy to help with repressed traumatic memories. Working with the eyes, places where we may unconsciously gaze to help process emotional material can help to bring repressed memories into awareness and allow them to release. Please see David Grand's work for more information.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: I believe in meeting people where they are in the process of change. Sometimes we can feel "stuck" in the change process and are not sure how to move forward. Motivation Interviewing offers support to the change process itself identifying areas we may feel stuck, barriers to change and examining all areas of the change process including resistance to change and fear about change. This focus can then allow people to move forward if that is what they truly want to do.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Working with people who have experienced traumatic events and helping with their healing process is one of my greatest passions. I work with all kids of trauma, early childhood trauma or complex trauma as it is known and adult onset trauma. Trauma is the result of the nervous system being overwhelmed and incapable of processing the trauma at the time of the event. Working with the body and nervous system to recognize and allow for completion and release of the stored trauma is the healing.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: I have been working in the field of substance use related disorders or addictions for over 30 years. All addictions have some characteristics in common. Addiction is a neuropathway in the brain that impacts thinking and behavior. Control is another component of addiction. We all want to be in control and not being in control is very challenging. Addiction can also be a coping strategy for dealing with unresolved trauma. Developing trust and self-compassion is an important part of healing.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Loss is a natural part of our life cycle yet we are not taught healthy methods of coping. Elizabeth Kubler Ross's stages of grief have helped us learn about grief as a process not just an event. Grief becomes complicated when there are previous unresolved, often in childhood, death and other losses. My work is to help people heal from all their losses, to develop recognition of the emotional pain and a compassionate presence towards oneself and towards one's pain.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Codependency has become a catchall term and has somewhat lost its meaning. It often involves caretaking of others, often family members, and this pattern often originates in childhood. Control is another issue often present for those in codependent relationships. I work with people to identify their own needs and desires, to establish healthy boundaries in their relationships which can then allow freedom to attend to their unmet needs and desires and ultimately to healing and freedom.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Physical pain is almost always accompanied by emotional pain. Attending to them both is essential for healing. The ACE study (Adverse Childhood Experiences) shows a strong correlation between childhood trauma and the later development of chronic health conditions. My approach is to bring mindful presence to areas in the body where trauma and stress is stored. This mindful presence can also allow for the release of physical pain.

name: Liz Mungovan
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Glad you're here! Navigating anxious attachment/people-pleasing? Find warm, authentic support to breathe easier and feel seen. Let's connect
ideal_client: Are you hungry for connection, yet plagued by a fear of rejection? Does your heart race while you wait for them to read your text, convinced that they won’t respond? When you’re honest with yourself, do you dream of being deeply witnessed and celebrated by another, despite being your own worst critic? If at times you feel caught on a see-saw of longing for love and connection while downplaying your own needs, desires, and strengths, know that there’s nothing innately wrong with you at all.

approaches.How I Can Help You: You are worthy of the fulfilling and life-affirming relationships that you seek. But it’s possible that your ability to co-create these types of stable connections is impeded by unprocessed past relationship wounds, painful early childhood memories, or struggles relating to your attachment style. Let’s get into it, and journey into the heart of who you were, who you are, and who you’ve yet to become. Together, we’ll gently meet those fragments — I call them “parts” — of yourself that are shut down from past trauma, or still sweaty-palmed from unhealed anxieties or outdated embarrassments. Informed by evidence-based modalities such as Emotionally Focused Individual Therapy and Internal Family Systems, we’ll cultivate a gutsy self-compassion that fuels your resilience, opens you up to fresh possibilities, and empowers you to find — and hold onto — the relationships that you’ve been wishing for.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: If you're a young adult (20-35) navigating the aftermath of toxic relationships—romantic, familial, or platonic—let's collaborate to reclaim your power and create a future where you thrive. I enjoy and have experience working with BIPOC and LGBTQ+ communities and see the knowledge and resistance of oppressive systems as an essential part of my work as a licensed therapist. Additionally, if you're navigating complex trauma, regardless of your background, and resonate with my approach, please reach out. I would love to hear from you.

name: Adam Ellis
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: We offer telehealth in OR, WA, AZ, MN, NM, and UT. In-office visits in Clackamas, OR / Layton and Lehi, UT available! Seattle visits soon.
ideal_client: I specialize in anxiety, ADHD, PTSD, bipolar disorder, trauma, and military health, and have treated most diagnoses in the DSM.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have been offering medication management since 2015 for diverse patients who have a broad range of mental health needs. While serving 20 years as a naval officer, I have developed a strong active listening skills and a high level of consideration and respect for others. I aim to use my experiences to help you optimize wellness, and provide psychiatric care with a trauma-informed and LGBTQIA-informed perspective in mind. I currently treat ages 13+.

approaches.More About the People We Treat: Skycloud Mental Health is a clinical placement site for Yale School of Nursing students. We are accepting new patients for medication management via telehealth in OR, WA, UT, AZ, MN, and NM as soon as this week. In-office appointments are available near Portland, OR, with offices in Seattle, WA and Salt Lake City, UT coming soon! Go to our website, skycloudhealth.com, and click "Schedule Now" to register and schedule online. Alternatively, you can call our office at (503) 694-3381, extension 2, to register and schedule over the phone. There is a therapy waitlist available on our website. We are available for single-case agreements with Kaiser. Contact our practice for more info.

name: Ashlee Adams
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hey there, my name is Ash. I am a non-binary, queer, licensed clinical social worker. Now taking new in person and virtual clients.
ideal_client: Are you feeling anxious, disconnected, or overwhelmed? Do questions around identity, trauma, or relationships leave you feeling stuck or unseen? I’m here to help. My approach is warm, queer-informed, and collaborative, creating a space where you feel safe to explore and heal. I believe you are the expert in your own life, and together, we’ll work to untangle the challenges you face while building on your strengths. Whether you’re navigating questions of gender, sexual orientation, or systemic pr

approaches.How I Can Help You: With training in various therapy modalities I typically rely on Internal Family Systems therapy. I tailor my approach to each client’s unique needs, focusing on what works best for their system, and working together to fit the right approach. Additionally, I offer pre-surgical assessments for individuals seeking gender-affirming surgery.

name: Sara Carmona
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a compassionate and collaborative therapist specializing in reproductive mental health.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a compassionate, collaborative and dynamic therapist specializing in the treatment of pregnancy and postpartum mood and anxiety disorders, fertility concerns, miscarriage, abortion, difficult birth experiences, and perinatal loss. My role is to create a safe and nurturing environment so you may explore difficult issues, strengthen your inner resources and build a repertoire of skills to use moving forward. I use conversation, practical strategies, and mind/body interventions to help you understand your emotions, make decisions that fit your values and help you live a more satisfying life.

approaches.Why We are a Good Fit for You: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker in the state of Oregon and hold a Masters Degree in Social Work from Portland State University. As a Certified Perinatal Mental Health Therapist, I pursue advanced training in the diagnosis and treatment of reproductive mental health concerns. My professional affiliations include the National Association of Social Workers, Postpartum Support International and an allied member of the Perinatal Mental Health Alliance for People of Color.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: Nearly 1 in 6 women and 1 in 10 men experience a perinatal mood or anxiety disorder. The symptoms arrive at a time when the demands and the stakes are high; the last place a postpartum parent wants to be is in a therapist's office. As a parent of 3, I understand. We will balance the exploration of feelings with concrete steps to help you feel better and come to enjoy parenthood.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: I specialize in perinatal mental health which includes making decisions about starting a family and the journey to birth. For some, the path is straightforward. For others, it winds, bends and leads to unwanted places - infertility, loss, sadness, anxiety, or grief. I help families address these concerns so they move toward parenthood feeling exceptionally supported, encouraged and well.

name: Angi Moe-Kyllonen
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: In a safe, non-judgmental space, we will gently explore the unfolding present moment, where profound insights often emerge.
ideal_client: It is through acceptance of what is that change can begin. Working towards unconditional self-acceptance and the gentle revision of your story nurtures growth and healthy, authentic expression. I work with individuals and couples through a variety of issues- transitions, anxiety, depression, relationships, conflict, loss, and parenting.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am trained through Naropa University as a counselor with a transpersonal orientation and specialization in mindfulness. Professionally, I have years of interpersonal relationships working with people of varying identities, in a role that required active listening, empathic communication, trust, and understanding. Educationally, I have training in gestalt therapy, Internal Family Systems, Humanistic Psychology, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, DBT, Mindfulness based therapy, Emotionally Focused Therapy, Somatic Therapy, and Transpersonal Psychology.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My lifelong curiosity about the human experience, sparked by my first psychology course, continues to fuel my passion for understanding both myself and others. Forever a curious soul and an avid reader, I am deeply drawn to the journey of personal growth and the richness of contemplative conversations. I believe that while our natural inclination is towards expansion, life experiences can make it feel unsafe to do so. By cultivating self-awareness and mindfulness, we can reconnect with our inner wisdom. Recognizing our fundamental need for connection, I believe that when we operate from a place of self-understanding, our relationships can thrive. My own life journey, including the profound and humbling experience of being a wife and mother to three wonderful children through various stages of parenting, has deepened my understanding of human resilience and the complexities of these relationships have been my greatest teachers.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Understanding Attachment Theory is a vital component of healthy relationships in our lives. Awareness of your own attachment styles can lead to profound growth in your interactions.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: Gestalt therapy highlights the adaptations we have made throughout our lives to cope with our emotional environments. These adaptations are often outside of our consciousness. Bringing awareness to ways of being that no longer serve us can facilitate deep healing and insights.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness rests in our capacity to ground ourselves in present awareness. Anxiety emphasizes angst about the future and depression lies in concern with the past. It is only in the present moment that we have any agency. Cultivating mindfulness can nurture tremendous acceptance of what is and peace in our lives.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Somatic therapy is incredibly beneficial to healing trauma. Trauma is unprocessed emotion stored in the body. It is the thinking mind that creates our often inaccurate narrative of our lives and experiences, but it is the body that rests in truth. Through somatic or body awareness, we can make our way beyond the thinking mind and into our felt sense, accessing deep healing and fostering self-trust.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: The word "transpersonal" literally means "beyond the personal." Transpersonal psychology takes a step back to look at the whole or our sense of connection to something larger than ourselves – maybe nature, humanity, a sense of the sacred, or even just a feeling of awe and wonder, experiences that give life a deeper sense of meaning and purpose. They could be spiritual in nature, moments of profound insight, or times when we feel a strong sense of unity or interconnectedness.

name: Whitney Summerer
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I help individuals navigate attachment & relationships—warm, trauma-informed, neurodivergent-positive. LGBTQ+, ENM/poly, grief, trauma.
ideal_client: My ideal clients are curious, insightful people interested in deepening their self-understanding and improving their relationships. Whether navigating ethical non-monogamy/polyamory, relationship challenges, grief, life transitions, or questions of identity, my clients value vulnerable exploration both inside and outside of session. I welcome creatives, LGBTQ+, neurodivergent folks, and non-conformists. Available to clients in OR.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach is warm, relational, and deeply collaborative. I create a thoughtful, affirming space where you can explore your emotions, relationships, attachment experiences, and core beliefs with curiosity and compassion. Drawing from attachment theory, narrative therapy, psychodynamic depth psychology, and parts work (IFS-inspired), I help you gently examine patterns that no longer serve you, develop new insights, and integrate meaningful changes into your life. Our sessions will not just be about talking, but also about building self-awareness, resilience, and practical skills for growth. I’m neurodivergent-positive and affirming of all relationship structures, identities, and experiences. Whether you're navigating ethical non-monogamy, relationship complexities, grief, or life transitions, my aim is to help you cultivate deeper connection, clarity, and a sense of genuine belonging within yourself and your relationships.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe therapy is most impactful when rooted in authenticity, curiosity, and meaningful connection. My practice is deeply informed by anti-oppression principles, feminism, and intersectional awareness. I’m committed to providing affirming, culturally responsive care to clients of diverse identities, relationship structures, and experiences. As a queer, polyamorous person myself, I understand firsthand the value of compassionate, stigma-free support. I'm particularly passionate about supporting creative and non-conforming individuals, and advocating for increased visibility and acceptance of bisexuality and ethical non-monogamy. My work is also shaped by my ongoing commitment to learning—regularly pursuing specialized trainings in attachment-focused therapies, polyamory and ENM-affirming practices, and somatic and trauma-informed approaches.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I utilize attachment-focused therapy to help clients understand their relational patterns, heal attachment wounds, and build secure, connected relationships.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: My approach explores unconscious dynamics and past experiences to help clients gain insight, resolve inner conflicts, and make meaningful, lasting change.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: I specialize in helping clients examine and rewrite personal narratives, empowering them to challenge limiting beliefs and live more authentic, fulfilling lives.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: I help clients understand their relational patterns within family contexts, exploring intergenerational dynamics and promoting healthier interactions.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in navigating complex relationship dynamics, helping clients improve communication, build deeper intimacy, and resolve patterns of conflict.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: As a poly-affirming therapist, I offer guidance in exploring boundaries, managing jealousy, fostering trust, and creating authentic, sustainable connections.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: My trauma-informed approach integrates attachment-focused, somatic, and narrative techniques to help clients heal past wounds and rebuild resilience.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I work with clients seeking deeper self-understanding, helping them explore identity, challenge limiting beliefs, and cultivate a more authentic life.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I provide compassionate support to those experiencing grief, aiding them in processing loss and finding meaning during life transitions.

name: Kimberly Reilly
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I'm Kim, and I'm honored to embark on a healing journey with those of you who are furthering your path of growth and healing.
ideal_client: I love my work as a Therapist, and find that I work well with many different issues that you may be struggling with, including issues of depression, anxiety, trauma, mood swings, self-worth, codependency, marital, interpersonal/relational dynamics, women's issues, adoption issues, cultural, transracial, and racial identity issues, family conflict, domestic violence, and spiritual issues, including death and dying.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I value a collaborative approach to therapy, that allows for clients' strengths and wisdom to unfold, and be heard. We'll start with what's current in your life, and find ways you can improve your sense of control around your thoughts, emotions, and body. I draw upon many different evidenced-based therapies such as Internal Family Systems (IFS), CBT, DBT, Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), and Mindful-based philosophies that address the root cause of your pain or struggles, vs. just treating the symptoms. I am solution and compassion focused, and approach treatment from a non-judgmental awareness of how we got to where are. I engage in, and appreciate ongoing professional development training regularly, in order to constantly improve my skills set, and support system.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Becoming a Therapist is something I was meant to do from an early age. Because my own multi-generational family system was often challenging and painful, it gave me the opportunity to learn first hand, what many of my clients experience also. Without these early challenges, I could not be as complete, compassionate, self-aware, self-forgiving, self-loving, self-expansive, or as self-evolving as a therapist, or person, as my healing journey has allowed. I love what I do, and I value the opportunities that the difficult experiences in life, provide us. The human condition is not easy, no matter what the grass may look like on the other side. Growth, wisdom, and inner healing can only arise out of the ashes, and from these ashes come the seeds of rebirth, and life itself. The field of psychology and therapy have come such a long way, and it is a very exciting time to be a therapist. Never before has treatment been so cutting edge, effective, and had so much research to back it up.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Level 1 and 2 Basic EMDR training.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I have completed the IFS Institute Online Circle 6 month Program, as well as IFS Level 1 Training. This is one of my favorite evidenced based therapies, and continue to do trainings and certification programs with the IFS Institute.

name: Kristin Tebow
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: If you’re struggling to cope with life, I can help you navigate these feelings, and offer a path forward!
ideal_client: Whether you experience anxiety, depression, have experienced trauma, relationship difficulties, feel alone, confused or lost, we are here to help you through those tough times. Skills-based practices help with change and coping, in addition to supportive understanding.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapeutic approaches are determined based on needs, and may include: cognitive-behavioral therapy, attachment therapy, EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing), relationship therapy, and supportive therapy.

approaches.Our Values as Mental Health Practitioner: My mission is to serve individuals experiencing mood disorders, attachment difficulties, addiction, difficult life experiences, anxiety, grief and loss, women's issues, gender issues, confusion, relationship difficulties, feeling stuck in life, and those looking for growth and development. Whatever you are experiencing, you are not alone, and you can change.

name: Kelly Hirstein
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: You are so much more than your thoughts and impulses! I use an integrative, compassionate and mindful approach to supporting my clients.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My intention is to connect with you as a unique being, and to offer support and curiosity to the life experiences and challenges that bring you into therapy. Our work together may include the use of traditional talk therapy, interpersonal connection, present-moment experience, mindfulness, experiential and body-oriented approaches, studying thoughts and impulses, exploring dreams, spirituality and existential experience. My hope is to lead clients towards a greater sense of self-awareness, that can lead to more choices in the way you respond to or engage with life experiences. In addition to counseling, my background in Nutrition and Massage Therapy provide me with knowledge and awareness of physical health challenges, body symptoms, and lifestyle concerns.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I graduated from Lewis and Clark college in Professional Mental Health and Addictions with a focus in Eating Disorders and Somatic Psychology, and I have a certification in the Treatment of Eating Disorders. I am Certified Hakomi therapist, with additional training Attachment, and Re-creation of the Self through the M.E.T.A. Counseling Center (Mindful Experiential Therapy Approaches). This work is rooted in mindfulness and body-oriented approaches, and I completed a year long internship with this as an educational focus and approach to counseling. I have also studied with the Process Work Institute, which is based in Jungian dreaming process, body symptoms, shamanistic and spiritual exploration, and experiential approaches.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: The experience of loss and grief can arise in so many ways throughout our lives. Taking time to honor what has come and gone, whether it be a family member, a beloved pet, relationship, a job, all of these things deserve to be honored and given the space to be properly grieved. Grief can feel complex, because it also entails other emotions, like sadness, anger, resentment, confusion, and can be unique to each person. Grief also connects us to love, and can lead to new heart openings and growth.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: Our relationship to food, nourishment, and our body is the longest one we will have. Struggling with body image and weight is so common, and there tends to be so many emotions in connection to this. I offer a holistic approach to working with Eating Disorders, including the mind-body connection, encouraging growth and change in kind and compassionate ways. I explore behaviors and impulses with curiosity, they may be messengers for needs and emotions trying to come through and express themselves.

name: Hart NW
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We help you reconnect with your strengths so you can move forward with clarity and confidence. Here, therapy isn’t one-size-fits-all.
ideal_client: If you’re navigating challenges like trauma, addiction, anxiety, depression, grief, or life transitions, you’re not alone.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: At Hart NW Counseling, we believe everyone has the power inside them to heal and live their best lives. Instead of telling you what to do, we help you find your own answers. Our therapists are caring partners in your journey, ready to reflect your true self and provide guidance when needed. We use honesty, humor, and kindness to empower you to create your own path.

approaches.Our Values as Mental Health Practitioner: At Hart NW Counseling, your autonomy and personal wisdom are deeply honored. We strive to work with both clients and clinicians who are open to challenging their own biases and embracing a mindset of openness and growth. By cultivating mutual respect and understanding, we empower our clients to explore their true selves and achieve meaningful change.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: At Hart NW, we recognize that trauma impacts not only the mind and body, but also the spirit. Post-traumatic stress can disrupt your sense of trust, safety, identity, and connection to something greater. Whether your trauma stems from a single event or long-standing patterns, we hold space for the complexity of your experience. Our therapists integrate approaches such as Brainspotting, Parts Work, somatic awareness, and intuitive guidance to support healing at every level—mental, emotional, phys

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: At Hart NW, we approach healing through a harm reduction lens—recognizing that all behavior has meaning and that change is not a linear path. Rather than focusing on abstinence or perfection, we support clients in making informed, self-directed choices that reduce risk and promote well-being. Our therapists honor each person's autonomy and readiness for change, creating nonjudgmental space for exploration, safety, and growth. Whether you're navigating substance use, coping strategies, or other l

name: Ivy Katz
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
