ideal_client: As of Winter 2023, I am not accepting new individual or couples but do have openings in my Men's Groups

approaches.My Approach to Helping: (I am currently only accepting new clients for Men's Group Therapy) In my experience, life is better and easier if you have someone that understands you, sees it from your point of view, and helps you navigate through it. A good therapist is like a fellow traveler who journeys with us into awareness, facilitating the insight necessary to heal and grow. I am a passionate facilitator of this process, helping my clients make sense of their lives and relationships, heal what's kept them stuck, explore new ways of being and live richly. The therapy we do is deep and has long-lasting effects, and the changes become your second nature, even after therapy ends.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Before becoming a therapist, I worked for six years as a welder, four years as a homesteader, and ten years as a political organizer and activist. At age 40, I spent four years finishing my undergraduate degree and earning my Masters degree in Social Work. I've worked for the past 26 years in Portland, first at community mental health clinics and then for the past 22 years in private practice. I completed two years in post-graduate studies in Contemporary Relational Psychoanalysis, and advanced training in marriage and couples therapy. I have a 30+ years meditation practice and have taught mindfulness meditation to personality disordered clients in outpatient settings.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: While primarity psychodynamic (exploring underlying habitual thoughts, beliefs and behaviors), I also am trained in attachment theory, Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), Cognitive-Behavioral therapy, marriage and family therapy, Jungian-based depth therapy, and contemporary Relational Psychoanalysis.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I help couples identify negative emotional interactional styles rather than assigning blame. One safety has strengthened, the underlying emotions or hurt, anger, fear, and sadness emerge that allow couples to more deeply communicate while re-establishing trust. With trust strengthened, we can negotiate differences, heal past wounds, and let go of disconnecting beliefs and attitudes.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Since 2002 I have offered ongoing weekly Men’s Groups designed for men to embrace and explore our struggles with anger, shame, fear, grief, loneliness and sense of personal power -- in service of a life with passion and connection. By supporting each other's experience we explore deeply our own unique expression of masculinity, learning how to feel increased aliveness while holding our struggles with compassion and heart.

name: Jon Fox
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I use mindfulness-centered, somatic therapy approaches to help you discover your unique strengths and inner resources.
ideal_client: Do you find it difficult to get your own needs met in relationship, taking care of everybody else but yourself? I can help you become empowered to create more balanced, rewarding, and successful relationships in your life. Do you feel lonely, distant, and disconnected from your partner or other important people in your life? Through our work together you can achieve greater trust and intimacy with others.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I draw from gentle and highly effective mindfulness-based, mind-body approaches to counseling. These approaches help clients make profound changes and rapid progress towards their goals. I received a Masters degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Portland State University in June 2012. I completed my internship at the M.E.T.A.(Mindful Experiential Therapy Approaches) Counseling Clinic in Portland, Oregon, where I counseled individuals, couples, and groups. In June 2013, I graduated M.E.T.A.’s Two-Year Comprehensive Training in Hakomi, RC-S, attachment interventions, and trauma release methods.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Like you, I’ve struggled with old emotional wounds and hard to break habits that have inspired me to embark on the path of increasing my self-awareness, self-acceptance, and sense of connection with others. I believe in your innate wholeness and value your unique situation, perspective, and path. I know the importance of creating a safe, secure, and open relationship with you that can guide and support your growth and healing and allow you to explore your creativity, passions, and connection to your inner guide.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I use Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) with couples to help clients understand their deeper emotions and needs and communicate them in an effective way to their partners. EFT focuses on our attachment styles, wishes and longings, along with needs important to our personal identity. EFT is one of the most evidence-based, effective modalities to help couples find increased connection, reduce conflict and improve communication.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: Hakomi is a body-centered psychotherapy based in mindfulness that believes that change happens through accessing the interface between our mind and body. Using this method we can uncover core beliefs and psychological patterns and revive the body’s knowledge as a resource. Increasing our awareness and enabling emotional release at this deep level of ourselves, change becomes attainable.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: My main approaches to therapy blend Eastern wisdom with Western science and include the use of mindfulness. I draw from Hakomi and RC-S (Re-Creation of the Self) approaches that allow us to uncover unconscious motivations for our behavior, hidden strengths we never knew we had, and cultivate a compassionate and non-judgmental attitude towards ourselves and others.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: In our individual or couples counseling sessions you can learn: How to communicate your needs to your partner in a more effective way; What are your spouse’s triggers and how do you use this knowledge to prevent fights and also learn to repair the damage when things go awry; How to treat your partner with compassion and empathy to foster greater understanding, respect, and acceptance.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: If you tend to regularly sacrifice your own needs in a relationship to meet your partners and feel resentful about this, you may be using a codependent strategy in your life. Over time, this can lead to depression, anger, anxiety, lack of self-esteem and sense of who you are. Your needs are important too. I like helping individuals and couples create more balanced and rewarding relationships.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I practice trauma therapy using mind-body counseling approaches which enable you to feel the connection between the traumatic memories stored in your body and the thoughts, beliefs, and habits that cause problems for you throughout your life. With my body-centered approach, healing these wounds becomes attainable. Together, we can propel you to feel comfort, ease, and vitality in your life again.

name: Nicole Dove
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I graduated with my master's in science in Mental Health Counseling in April 2024 and work as a nurse in addition to counseling.
ideal_client: I work with various challenges including infertility, pregnancy and postpartum, anxiety, depression, eating disorders, stress management, grief and loss, and marriage/relationship.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Counseling is a process by which we work together to identify and work on what you bring to our sessions. My approach to counseling involves helping you to identify strengths within yourself and develop self-awareness. My therapeutic approach is eclectic combining numerous theoretical approaches and techniques including mindfulness, CBT, person centered, and solution focused.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: As a working mom of of two children I can relate to the stressors of life. I also have been a labor and delivery nurse for over 15 years. I would love the opportunity to work with you and help navigate life.

name: Mara Topazio
title: Somatic Practitioner
intro: I offer adults practical tools for self transformation and support for embodied positive change. Inclusive. Trauma-informed. Soul centered.

name: Ursula Hurley
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome! My goal is to help you take meaningful steps forward on your journey and continue to make progress independently.
ideal_client: I help individuals with Eating Disorders

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe people can change and I choose to see the good in everyone. I want to help you with your struggles past or present, to learn to stay present and to keep moving forward. I have trained in Cognitive Processing Therapy to treat trauma. I have worked at a partial hospital level of care in the treatment of eating disorders and have experience using Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Motivational Interviewing. I can provide education to family, friends, partners and parents for ways they can support their loved ones.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have an M.S. in Marriage and Family Therapy from Lewis & Clark College, as well as B.A.'s in Human Development and Family Sciences, and Education from Oregon State University. I have experience working with preschoolers through adults, and in partial hospital and intensive outpatient treatment. My work now is to focus on the struggles with anorexia/restrictive eating, bulimia, binge eating, exercise addiction, body image, comparisons and self-esteem. My goal is to incorporate Health At Every Size, Body Trust and Intuitive Eating to take some of the pressure off and get your supports on board in ways that you will find helpful.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: Anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder, over-exercise, restriction, purging, dieting, body image, self-esteem, health at every size, Certified Body Trust Provider, intuitive eating

name: Andrea Weber
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Openings as soon as the second week of July for new patients. In person availability on Wednesday afternoons. Virtual availability T-Th.
ideal_client: My patient-centered approach prioritizes individual needs and goals, respecting each person's values and experiences. I collaborate with clients to offer evidence-based treatment options, including medication management and integrative therapeutic interventions, to facilitate their mental health journeys. I specialize in adult depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, and PTSD, and I have received additional training in mental health care for women and veterans.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With over a decade of healthcare experience, my nursing career evolved from providing medical and mental health care in hospitals to focusing specifically on mental health, which I find deeply rewarding. This passion led me to earn an advanced nursing degree as a PMHNP from Gonzaga University and complete a PMHNP Residency at the Mann-Grandstaff Veterans Affairs Medical Center. Committed to cultural humility, sensitivity, and responsiveness, I have served diverse patient populations across urban and rural communities in Oregon and Washington. I am an LGBTQ-affirming provider.

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: My main focus in our work together will be working with you to come up with a medication regime that best supports your whole self and health.

name: Maia Bellavia
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Offering relationship and intimacy therapy for ALL Individuals, couples/families (of all flavors, configurations, and sizes). LGBTQIA
ideal_client: I help people navigate life changes and challenges. Whether struggling with communication, intimacy, or simply feeling disconnected. Specializing in relationship and intimacy therapy for ALL, specifically for the LGBTQIA, BIPOC, and ALL sexually marginalized communities. * I am happy to bill insurance for sessions with couples, if verification can be made that individuals individuals insurance will accept the billing codes 90847 or 90846. Otherwise, sessions will be billed as cash pay.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer personalized therapy sessions to help develop deep self-worth and confidence to overcome any challenges and live a more wholehearted and fulfilling life. Striving to provide supportive psychotherapy during each appointment. My practice involves using an eclectic approach based on your needs, including Solution-Focused Treatment, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, Mindfulness, Somatic Therapy, and Positive Psychology therapeutic approach. Valuing a holistic, integrative treatment approach, which includes behavioral strategies, to equip each client with skills and strategies to improve their quality of life.

name: April Oliver
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I provide individual mental health counseling sessions -via telehealth-for adult residents of Oregon or Washington. Thank you for surviving.
ideal_client: My specialty is focused on people who have or are still experiencing traumatic events. Therefore, I work with those that also may be managing; depression, anxiety, and (complex) PTSD. I also support those who have been oppressed and marginalize due to; LGBTQIA+, gender, sexuality, and neurodiversity. In therapeutic session we may also address concerns regarding; relationships and attachment, relational violence and abuse, sexuality and identity, and intergenerational trauma.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I believe the therapeutic relationship between the client and a counselor is a collaborative one. I believe you are the expert of your life, and I am a facilitator of change and processing. I am an engaged therapist. I will ask questions to invoke self-inquiry and discovery. I offer resources, handouts, apps, and YouTube videos to support techniques we learn within our sessions. I utilize Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), which is a client-centered approach with a focus to empower you to take action to meet your goals and expectations, which are set and controlled by you, little steps at a time. Aspects of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT), Internal Family Systems (IFS), and Somatic Therapy as relied on as needed.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am an interactive mental health counselor. I ask questions, and inquire about past tools that have worked, as well as discover together tools that will support you specifically. I offer homework and techniques to practice via YouTube, apps, or with handouts. I am very supportive and encouraging. I believe in you. I am affirming to your beliefs and identity. My practice is focused on trauma, which means looking at where your trauma is currently affecting your life. Within sessions, time and energy is spent processing your current thoughts, behaviors, and emotions that are influenced by past trauma. Utilizing techniques that can help you understand, make peace with, and make other choices outside of repeating unwanted thoughts and experiences. If you're ready to put in the work to find progress, I'm a good fit for you.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma can cause a variety of symptoms and experiences that can be a distraction in your quality of life. In a therapy session, we focus on symptoms and remedies. I will not ask you to recall every detail, instead the focus is on understanding the experiences of symptoms in your daily life. For example, what it looks like, feels like, and how it causes you to respond. Together we will discover the techniques and tools that can help you specifically and reduce the intensity of your daily life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Trauma can cause a variety of symptoms and experiences that can be a distraction in your quality of life. In a therapy session, we focus on symptoms and remedies. I will not ask you to recall every detail, instead the focus is on understanding the experiences of symptoms in your daily life. For example, what it looks like, feels like, and how it causes you to respond. Together we will discover the techniques and tools that can help you specifically and reduce the intensity of your daily life.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Trauma can cause a variety of symptoms and experiences that can be a distraction in your quality of life. In a therapy session, we focus on symptoms and remedies. I will not ask you to recall every detail, instead the focus is on understanding the experiences of symptoms in your daily life. For example, what it looks like, feels like, and how it causes you to respond. Together we will discover the techniques and tools that can help you specifically and reduce the intensity of your daily life.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Trauma can cause a variety of symptoms and experiences that can be a distraction in your quality of life. In a therapy session, we focus on symptoms and remedies. I will not ask you to recall every detail, instead the focus is on understanding the experiences of symptoms in your daily life. For example, what it looks like, feels like, and how it causes you to respond. Together we will discover the techniques and tools that can help you specifically and reduce the intensity of your daily life.

name: Justin Rock
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Helping individuals and families reach through the difficult to grasp the beautiful.
ideal_client: I believe that the human experience is often challenging and tumultuous, yet these experiences provide the possibility of creating deep meaning for our lives and personal growth. Therapy is one path for individuals and families to move from pain and confusion to joy and wonder. My goal is to create a space and relationship with my clients to engage in their lives so they can engage boldly with the awe of being human in this world.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize existential-humanistic therapy to reach through the difficult and towards the beauty of life. I work collaboratively with my clients to create a safe and supportive relationship for them to explore being with themselves and being with others in the world. Too often we want to look “out there” into the world to find an answer to our struggles. Instead, I believe we are capable of creating our own answers. For this reason I work with diverse clients, among them clients challenged by death anxiety, identity death/grief, depression, anxiety, lack of fulfillment, life transitions, relationship issues, personal growth, LGBTQ issues, and polyamory & consensual non-monogamy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I became a therapist over a decade ago because of the pathologizing marginalization that occurred to many in the Poly and ENM community in Portland. This requires honoring the clients experience and knowledge whoever they are and for whoever they are becoming. This is true for, in my opinion, for every human. Therapeutic work is possible when the humanity is seen in each other, not the pathology. I am a founding member of Existential-Humanistic Northwest, a professional non-profit which is here to impact the world through our commitment to and passion for existential-humanistic values of authenticity, integrity, responsibility, inter-connectedness, inclusion, and awe. I am also an Adjunct Professor at Lewis & Clark College in the Marriage and Family Therapy program and the Art Therapy program, teaching classes such as: Introduction to Therapy Theories, Addictions in Family Therapy, Polyamory and Ethical Non-Monogamy, and Family Development.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: I am a founding member of EHNW (Existential-Humanistic Northwest). I studied philosophy as an undergraduate at Lewis & Clark College. During this time, I studied predominantly phenomenology, existentialism and philosophy of mind. I have focused my therapy training in Existential-Humanistic therapy and provide E-H Supervision.

name: Carly Rubin
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Relationships shape our lives.
ideal_client: I believe that healing happens both in and out of the therapy room — through reparative emotional and relationship experiences. Therapy is one tool to guide you along your path. My training is focused on working with people navigating relationship dynamics of all kinds. I work with trauma-informed methods like Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), somatic practices, Internal Family Systems (IFS), and attachment theory to support your journey at your own pace, in your own way.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Hi! I'm Carly (she/her). I’m a Licensed Marriage & Family Therapist, adjunct professor, and supervisor to therapists-in-training. Working with intimate partners and helping people navigate relationship dynamics is at the heart of my life’s work. I believe in individual and collective healing and liberation for all people through trauma-informed relational work that honors everyone’s unique experience. I use methods like Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT), Internal Family System (IFS), attachment theory, and somatic practices that encourage self-compassion and open us to transformational connection.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I am honored to work with people of all gender expressions, sexual orientations, neurotypes, relationship models, races, religions, ages, sizes, and disabilities. I am a sex-positive therapist and work from a trauma-informed perspective. Let me support you in discovering the tools you need to help you thrive!

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Emotional patterns and inner dynamics are always influencing our connections. By illuminating the undercurrents of your relationship, therapy can help nurture alignment, intimacy, and fulfillment — no matter what shape your relationship takes.

name: Brian Pollock
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: As a board-certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP), I am committed to providing inclusive, affirming care to all.
ideal_client: If you're looking for inclusive psychiatric care in Portland or other areas in Oregon, and you need support managing anxiety, depression, ADHD, or trauma, I offer a collaborative approach that integrates medication management and evidence-based therapies, Whether you’re navigating health challenges, identity exploration, or emotional overwhelm, we’ll create a plan rooted in your strengths and values. I am here to help you!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to mental health care is compassionate and collaborative. I take the time to understand your unique story, challenges, and goals—balancing medication management with holistic support to help you regain stability and achieve lasting well-being. While my specialties include depression, bipolar disorder, and anxiety disorders, I also have extensive experience supporting clients navigating ADHD, PTSD, OCD, chronic illness, and trauma. I am passionate about providing LGBTQIA+ affirming care, ensuring all individuals feel seen, supported, and validated in their mental health journey. I especially enjoy working with young adults navigating major life transitions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My diverse experiences—working with underserved communities, university students, and individuals from diverse racial, ethnic, and LGBTQIA+ backgrounds—have shaped my commitment to culturally competent care. Having lived in South Florida, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, and Spain before settling in Portland Oregon, I bring a broad perspective to understanding different cultural backgrounds and life experiences. In my free time, you’ll find me: Spending time with my favorite people, my wife and child, and also our pets Khepri, Ellie, Kirin, & Pinky. Enjoying my simple rituals, like making the perfect cup of coffee. Working out at the gym, to anchor me in the moment.

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: I am an experienced psychiatric nurse practitioner with 15 years of clinical experience. I have worked in multiple settings and have experience working with a wide range of diagnoses. My expertise is in the areas of mood disorders and anxiety disorders.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I received specialized training through Behavioral Tech. I have led DBT groups for many years, and previously I helped develop and launch a DBT program for college students. I have worked as a part of a larger DBT program and have experience with DBT skills training and Consultation Teams.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I specialize in depression. I originally started my career working in a research clinic focusing on treatment resistant depression. Over the last 15 years I have continued to develop my knowledge base and experience with the aim to help people find the right medications to keep them feeling well.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I specialize in all anxiety disorders including but not limited to Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD), Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD), and PTSD.

name: Erin Winn Oliva
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Welcome! I am here to offer compassion, connection, reflection, and validation while you navigate life's greatest challenges.
ideal_client: I specialize in therapy with individuals & their loved ones experiencing mental health challenges during the perinatal period - this includes while trying to conceive, pregnancy, & postpartum. We experience the most drastic biological & emotional changes of our lives during this time, & these changes can be shocking, scary, confusing, & overwhelming. You deserve a space for processing & healing as you navigate life's most significant transition into parenthood.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My therapy style is collaborative & flexible, tailored to the preferences of you as the client. I approach all individuals through a trauma and attachment lens, & find it deeply beneficial to explore how our pasts shape the way we navigate the present. I offer reflection & alternative perspectives to help you approach challenges in new ways. I invite you to include your loved ones in our sessions, as I believe healing happens as a family/community. I have been working in the mental health field since 2016, and running my own business since 2021. My clinical history includes integrated behavioral health care in a midwife/OBGYN clinic, trauma-focused therapy, individual and group therapy with immigrants and survivors of domestic violence, therapy and case management with houseless individuals, and extensive experiencing performing psychological evaluations for immigration cases.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My practice is rooted in my social justice philosophies– all human beings deserve access to quality mental health care; all human beings deserve a safe space to be vulnerable and honest; all human beings deserve time dedicated to healing from the inherent challenges/trauma of everyday life. I believe that societal healing depends first on the healing of the individual. My practice welcomes individuals of all races, genders, sexual orientations, and abilities.

name: Stefanie Cruz
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: The therapeutic process can be one of self-discovery and healing. I am here to help support your journey!
ideal_client: Do you need support in coping with anxiety and/or depression, or needing to make meaning in a new life transition, or dealing with feeling “stuck” with yourself or in a relationship? I am here to provide guidance toward your own inner insight and understanding, layered with cultural understanding that is unique to you and your experience.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I consider therapy a collaborative process between a therapist and client(s). I work toward helping others develop more effective strategies that will result in more success as it relates to meeting their goals within the realm of the individual self and interpersonal relationships. I work with individuals and families from a systemic lens that allows exploration of issues around racism, sexism, and classism (to name a few). Overall, I utilize approaches rooted in a variety of areas depending on client needs. Much of my background stems from cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), brief-solution focused therapy (BSF), acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), and motivational interviewing (MI).

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I became a therapist to offer BIPOC representation to our local community. As I began my journey in mental health, I did not see very many providers that looked like me or represented cultural awareness I thought was key in understanding the complexities of an intersectional experience.

name: Christa Brennan
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I use humor, creativity and compassion to help you reach your goals, make meaning of suffering and rekindle inner joy.
ideal_client: Trying to find the right therapist can be a daunting task, so I’m really happy you are here. I help people with a variety of needs such as unpacking past traumas, dealing with a specific situation or need a new perspective for their future. Clients I see are typically going through a transition, grieving a loss, or looking for meaning.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Using elements of art therapy, drama therapy, IFS, EMDR, and the latest research on how to regulate the nervous system I approach your situation with compassion to help you confront unhelpful patterns of thoughts and behaviors, break free from guilt/shame, rekindle inner-joy and cultivate resiliency for an integrated sense of self.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in your innate ability to heal, to make meaning from suffering and bounce back from adversity. I am an LGBTQ+ ally, cisgender woman with over a decade of experience working in the field. Specific areas of focus include grief, loss, addiction, domestic violence, sexual abuse, anxiety, depression, ADHD, and relationship issues. In 2012, I developed an art therapy workshop called Broken Bowl based on the Japanese philosophy of Wabi Sabi and Kintsugi. Wabi Sabi embraces the flawed or imperfect aspects of life and Kintsugi is the practice of repairing broken pottery with gold. I guide individuals through a process of confronting change, accepting impermanence, and deciding how to move forward with what is left. If you are interested in participating in this workshop please reach out for upcoming dates.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: As a licensed substance use counselor, I have spent the last 10 years working directly with folks experiencing houselessness, having issues with the criminal justice system, trauma and addiction. So much of addiction is based in unresolved trauma which is why I take a judgment free, harm reduction approach.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Many of my clients are members of the LGBTQ community. We work on issues around gender identity, transitioning, coming out to family members, healing from religious trauma and internalized homophobia.

name: William Steiner
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: William Steiner is a Licensed Clinical Social Worker who provides empirically supported individual therapy for adults ages 18 and older.
ideal_client: Many of us struggle to manage issues such as stress, social isolation, depression, anxiety, fear, loss, and difficulty in relationships. At the same time, many people are just feeling generally overwhelmed with life and the current circumstances. You don't have to be alone with these struggles. I believe you are the expert on your own experience, and that therapy can help you better understand yourself and the factors causing you distress and preventing positive change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use a person centered approach with CBT and mindfulness based interventions to support client treatment goals. I take an eclectic approach to therapy, which allows for more flexibility in applying a variety of interventions that meet the specific needs of my clients . I believe the therapeutic alliance is the prerequisite to any success and I try to collaborate with my clients to build an authentic supportive relationship that leads to greater personal insight and growth.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Working with a therapist can bring relief, but can also feel overwhelming and stressful. For that reason it is important to find a therapist that is a good fit and that is someone you feel like you can work with comfortably. I understand this is a difficult process and so offer a free initial check-in/ consult to see if we might work well together. Please feel free to reach out if you are interested in scheduling.

name: James Whalen
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide a safe space for you to explore the impacts of ADHD, men's issues, depression, and anxiety, and help you learn to manage them.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with clients who are struggling to identify a stable self-image, whether that be due to large-scale social pressures, family dynamics, trauma, neurodivergence, or other causes. Many of my clients have been invalidated by others or themselves for so long that they've lost contact with their own needs and emotions, or struggle to advocate for them without self-criticism. I have training and experience working with men and people who are neurodivergent, and am both myself!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our time in therapy will focus on teaching you effective skills to change the way that you relate to yourself, your emotions, and your thoughts, while also exploring and validating the reasons that you developed your current patterns in the first place. I pride myself in my deep sense of empathy, and have been told often that I have a calming, nonjudgmental presence that helps my clients feel safe and heard. I have nine years of experience in the mental health field, often treating clients at their most difficult moments, and I try to learn from and use that experience to help my clients move through challenging times safely.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe strongly in the power of counseling to change lives: I'm in this field because I've experienced it firsthand. I also know that reaching out for help can be challenging, especially when you're struggling. You're already making progress towards change by starting this search and being on here! I would love to help you continue that journey.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy teaches us to learn how to sit with our distress and accept it, in order to help us relate to our thoughts and feelings in ways that don't increase the suffering that's natural to your situation. It helps us learn to live our lives according to our values, with the understanding that we have control of our behavior and not our thoughts. ACT is most helpful for clients with anxiety and depression.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy is one of the oldest and best research-supported modalities that we have, and has been adapted to a wide range of presenting issues, though it originated with depression. It's also the gold standard for therapy treating ADHD at present. CBT focuses on identifying the links between our thoughts, our emotions, and our behavior, as well as patterns in how those three interact that are causing harm in your life.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I do not provide the full course of DBT. It's a therapy with a high degree of commitment required from both parties, and therefore would not be appropriate for once-weekly telehealth services. However, there are many skills and concepts in DBT that are broadly applicable, and I bring in these elements when it feels like they would be helpful on an individual basis. These include mindfulness skills, distress tolerance skills, and dialectical concepts.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in working with people who identify as male, and am interested in exploring the intersection between your own concepts of masculinity, society's expectations, and mental health. I enjoy helping men find ways to relate to and regulate emotion that utilize the strength and resilience that masculinity can provide, while also recognizing the ways that expectations of men and the ways we relate to emotion can harm us. I am also comfortable addressing concerns about male sexual health.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: As someone who has been diagnosed with ADHD myself, I have the lived experience of managing associated symptoms, as well as the training to ensure that my interventions with you are evidence-based. I recognize that ADHD comes with both biological differences and cognitive impacts that can be unpacked and re-oriented to serve your particular style most effectively. I'm also very familiar with how ADHD's intersection with identity can make symptoms look different in every individual.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I have several years of experience working with people who have experienced intense and often treatment resistant depression, and I understand how hopeless and frustrating it is being stuck in the negative thought and mood cycles that are a part of its cause. I take a two-sided approach of working to challenge these negative thought patterns while also helping you to recognize the things you're grateful for in your life, and your own strengths.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety has many forms, and almost all of them are uncomfortable, painful experiences. I tend to use my calming presence to help anxious clients feel safe in the therapy environment. Once we've established a sense of safety, we can move on to learning about the roots of your anxiety and how to change your relationship with those roots so that you can learn to respond to your symptoms more effectively.

name: Dove Garvan
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I'm a relationship technician who helps lovers of all stripes untangle tricky communication knots so they can thrive anew.
ideal_client: You and your love(s) have found something truly remarkable in each other, and along with that, you've run into some conflicts that have proven surprisingly challenging to negotiate. You want to add a keen detective's eye to the situation to help you find out where things went off the rails. I'll empower you with lasting strategies to efficiently restore flourishing functionality to your love connection. You seek an active choreographer with a directive, firm and humorous approach.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Whether I'm treating individuals or couples, I work with all clients through a relational lens because healthy relationships are foundational to human thriving. I am a technically-focused clinician with masters' degrees in Conflict & Dispute Resolution and Couples & Family Therapy. I will help you view your interactional patterns in '3-G' (the good, the great and the gnarly!). From there, we'll guide them to full functionality using your individual and partnership strengths as fuel for the journey. Alongside exploring your attachment histories and patterns, I will help you build expertise in giving your partner(s) feedback about what you need in ways that keep negotiation moving along effectively. My job is to help restore your communication to its finest purpose: a technology for connection, security and satisfaction. To do this work in an informed and respectful way, I counsel from an inclusive and socially just lens.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: Love comes in many shapes and forms. I support clients of all racial, sexual and religious backgrounds with curiosity, humility, and the common sense to provide referrals if it's evident that I'm out of my depth. Hablo español, y me encanta apoyar a la comunidad hispanohablante en Portland. I am a poly & kink-affirming, sex-positive provider. If you've often wished for an ally to help with resolving 'messy human stuff,' I can't wait to join your team as a cheerleader and educator of effective communication and conflict resolution.

name: Alana Duschane
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: CURRENTLY ACCEPTING PATIENTS, INCLUDING TELEHEALTH.
ideal_client: Licensed in California (35221) Oregon (2855) and Washington state (PY61106051). I am a trauma informed, somatically oriented psychologist who is trained in ERP, TF-CBT and EMDR. I offer psychotherapy and psychological/educational testing to children, teens, and adults. I work from a client-centered approach utilizing evidence-based treatment approaches (CBT, DBT, ERP, EMDR). I specialize in anxiety, OCD, trauma, mood disorders, addiction, bipoc, sexual identity/gender, neurodivergence.

specialities.name: Psychological Testing and Evaluation
specialities.description: I have extensive training and experience in providing psychological testing for children, adolescents, and adults for a variety of psychological problems.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: As an addictions counselor, I was trained and continually utilized motivational interviewing to promote behavioral change in addiction and co-occurring disorders.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I have been trained in providing CBT for various disorders for children, teens, and adults for over 10 years.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have experience and specialized training in the assessment and treatment of children and adolescents. I have provided comprehensive psychological evaluation for learning disabilities, ADHD, social, behavioral, and emotional functioning, and various child and adolescent issues. I have been trained in Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavior Therapy for Children (TF-CBT).

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: My doctoral dissertation was part of a larger study with UCLA examining a medication-assisted treatment for alcohol dependence. I have had years of education and years with working with addiction treatment and I also received my certification as an addictions treatment counselor (CATC-V).

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I completed specialized training through the International OCD Foundation in cognitive behavior therapy (CBT) in the treatment of obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) and anxiety related disorders. I have provided treatment as a senior clinician at a treatment clinic specializing in anxiety disorders.

name: Robin Bodhi
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Trauma-informed counselor helping empaths heal anxiety, codependency & PTSD through somatic, mindfulness & holistic approaches.
ideal_client: With complex PTSD/chronic anxiety from early childhood trauma it can be difficult to feel connected to self and others. These challenges impact every area of your life impeding the ability to access a sense of happiness and overall well-being. I help clients address how their challenging past interferes with the ability to feel embodied, and connected impacting the ability to have fulfilling authentic relationships. Establishing a strong sense of self is key.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Brain spotting is a technique I use to specifically address trauma. It has a strong somatic component in which the client guides their own process. I bring in an emphasis in somatic awareness and mindfulness to my counseling sessions. Because of my history as a body-worker I'm skilled in helping others connect with themselves through embodied approaches: such as mindfulness techniques, guided meditations, and somatic practices. My work is relational as I believe many issues start with a lack of proper and healthy early attachment. My focus is for my clients to feel safe and cultivate a more solid foundation of sense of self. Addressing unconscious patterns is a key component in creating change. I offer psychedelic integration for individuals who are needing support prior to and after a psychedelic (or medicine) journey. Sometimes journeys can be hard and having support to integrate the insights and/or lessons received is essential and just as important as the actual journey.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Becoming a therapist was a natural next step in my career.. After working for many years as a body/energy worker my focus began to shift toward helping people with trauma so I furthered my education and received a MA in clinical mental health. During this time I became aware of how important it was to address my own personal trauma so dove deep into studying somatic trauma focused work as well as nervous system regulation. I now integrate these into my counseling work along with brain-spotting and other modalities. A large part of what calls me to do counseling is my desire to help others feel empowered and help them create the lives they want. I believe that people can have rich and meaningful lives and it is necessary to examine what gets in the way and actively address and change deeply en-grained patterns. Through learning new skills and with sufficient support I can help you create the life you desire.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: As a trauma-informed therapist trained in Brainspotting, I specialize in helping clients access and heal deep emotional wounds stored in the nervous system. With years of experience using this powerful modality, I guide clients through focused eye positions to unlock unprocessed trauma, release stuck energy, and restore emotional balance—supporting lasting healing beyond talk therapy alone.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I specialize in somatic-based therapy, helping clients heal trauma through body awareness and nervous system regulation. By tuning into physical sensations, emotions, and survival responses, I guide clients to release stored stress, build resilience, and reconnect with their bodies. My approach supports lasting change by integrating mind, body, and spirit for deep, embodied healing.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I use mindfulness-based therapy to help clients develop present-moment awareness, emotional regulation, and self-compassion. Through gentle, trauma-informed practices, I guide individuals in observing thoughts and sensations without judgment, creating space for healing, clarity, and inner peace. Mindfulness supports nervous system balance and empowers clients to respond rather than react to life’s challenges.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: I offer holistic counseling that addresses the whole person—mind, body, and spirit. Integrating trauma-informed therapy, somatic practices, mindfulness, and spirituality, I help clients heal deeply and sustainably. My approach honors each individual’s unique journey, fostering balance, self-awareness, and empowerment to create meaningful change and greater well-being in all areas of life.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: I help empaths and trauma survivors heal from codependency by reconnecting with their sense of self. Codependency often stems from childhood trauma and shows up as people-pleasing, self-abandonment, and fear of disconnection. Through a trauma-informed, somatic approach, I guide clients to set healthy boundaries, regulate their nervous systems, and build relationships rooted in self-trust, emotional safety, and inner empowerment.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I specialize in working with individuals healing from PTSD and complex trauma. Using a somatic, trauma-informed approach, I help clients regulate their nervous systems, process stuck survival responses, and reconnect with their sense of safety and self. My work supports those who feel anxious, disconnected, or overwhelmed by triggers, guiding them toward empowerment, emotional resilience, and inner peace.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I help clients understand and heal the root causes of anxiety through a somatic and trauma-informed lens. Anxiety is often a signal from a dysregulated nervous system. Using mindfulness, body-based tools, and nervous system regulation, I support clients in calming their inner world, building resilience, and reconnecting with a felt sense of safety, clarity, and confidence in daily life.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I support individuals and couples in navigating relationship and marriage challenges rooted in trauma, codependency, and attachment wounds. My approach blends somatic therapy and nervous system regulation to build trust, improve communication, and foster deeper emotional connection. I help clients create healthier patterns, set boundaries, and cultivate relationships rooted in safety, respect, and authenticity.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I integrate spirituality into healing by guiding clients to reconnect with their inner wisdom, intuition, and sense of purpose. My approach honors each person’s unique spiritual path, blending mindfulness, somatic practices, and trauma-informed care. I help clients move beyond survival into soul-aligned living, cultivating inner peace, self-trust, and a deeper connection to something greater than themselves.

name: Amanda Ball
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm a queer and polyamorous woman with ADHD who feels deeply. As a therapist I love providing affirming care to my communities.
ideal_client: You might be my client if you are… queer, polyam, kinky,gender-defiant, neurodivergent, sensitive, artistic, or revolutionary. You might be feeling… stuck, overwhelmed, unmet in relationships, unsatisfied with life, or like you're at a crossroads. You’re probably less interested in charting out your thoughts and more about tuning into your own voice and becoming empowered.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe in deep and lasting change that goes beyond surface level “interventions.” I delve into attachment, core beliefs, defining life experiences, and parts work to help you experience deeper insights and make changes in your life. We’ll do plenty of talking, but I deeply value using mindfulness, somatic awareness, experiential processing and our rapport/relationship to move beyond “talk therapy.” I can be intuitive and probing but also gentle and compassionate. I’ll be your biggest fan but cheer you on loudest when you challenge yourself.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: BLM, intersectional feminist, affirming of neurodivergence (ADHDer here!), sex/kink positive. There is no such thing as being “judgement free” but I hold space for multiple truths. I believe capitalism is significantly harming our mental health (among other things). I worked in public health for a long time so reproductive health freedom and access to trans healthcare are very important to me (and I know a bit about it!) I’m a queer, polyamorous, able-bodied but neurodivergent white cis-woman from a middle class background. I endeavor to hold my privilege responsibly, confront my internalized isms, and hold space for imperfection in the process.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory helps us untangle the complex web of early learning that can make engaging in fulfilling adult relationships difficult and painful. I hold special training in a method called Primary Attachment Therapy, which elicits the attachment system between client and therapist in real time, allowing for mindful observation and re-processing of attachment templates.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: I hold an intersectional feminist worldview, which means that I look not just at individual circumstances that impede personal growth, but also effects of systemic oppression fostered by a culture of white supremacy, patriarchy, homophobia and ableism. I hold all worldviews with gentleness and respect, but this perspective is foundational in my own understanding of the larger context of our work.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: Hakomi uses mindfulness to go towards your “core material,” or deeply ingrained beliefs about yourself and the world. By uncovering and examining these beliefs, we aim to discard inaccurate beliefs that no longer serve you, and gain new, life affirming experiences that help you understand the truth of yourself and the world, thereby living in alignment with each.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: My clients come from all walks of life, but I especially enjoy serving my clients from the queer community. For me, queerness is just another part of who you are, not part of 'the problem.' I aim to understand your unique story, but I won't need you to teach me the basics. Or, if you are still exploring, I can provide an open, non-pressuring environment to do so.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Exploring your relationship values can help you ground into what you really want and need, and create the relationship orientation that is right for you. I have knowledge of many different types and styles of polyamory, non-monogamy, and open relationships. I hold the belief that any type of relationship can be healthy with the consent and honestly of all partners.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Feelings of not being enough are often at the roots of depression and anxiety. Low self-worth can hold you back from leading the life you want, or pursuing the jobs and relationships you deserve. I use a combination of self-compassion techniques, and mindful exploration of your own intuitive knowing, to elicit and ground in your internal sense of self-worth.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: Missed or mis-diagnosis of ADHD can leave adults with this condition feeling defeated or incompetent. As a person with lived experience of being diagnosed late in life I can help you evaluate if your symptoms are consistent with ADHD, de-stigmatize what it means to live with ADHD and collaborate with you on what supports will work best for you.

name: Kelly Allen, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello! Thank you for considering me as your therapist! I provide individual and couples counseling online and in person.
ideal_client: I am so excited you are on this journey for yourself. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor at Senua Counseling Clinic, with many years of experience providing counseling for individuals and couples. I provide both in person and virtual therapy options. It is an absolute privilege to work collaboratively with my clients to help them achieve the quality of life they desire and I am passionate about creating a safe and supportive environment for my clients.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We live in a very difficult world and we could all use some extra support sometimes. I specialize in working with individuals and couples and helping them achieves their therapeutic goals. I have worked extensively with anxiety, depression, mood disorders, stress related issues, and couples concerns such as difficulty with communication or desire. I primarily work with adults aged 18 and up. I have been in practice for over ten years and have worked in many outpatient environments. I am trauma informed and LGBTQ+ allied.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that we can all change and grow when we feel ready and have the right support. Having an inclusive practice is very important to me and I welcome clients of all ethnicities, genders, and sexual orientations. I became a counselor to help others through their most difficult times in life and I am passionate about helping you become the best version of yourself.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I work with all anxiety disorders and have experience treating panic, excessive worry, and rumination.

name: Bethany Haug
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I practice relational, insight-oriented therapy, and I specialize in treating trauma, self-esteem, and anxiety.
ideal_client: I work well with individuals who want to explore who they are and feel more connected to themselves and others. The clients I see often identify with having a history of trauma and may struggle with self-esteem, depression, or anxiety. My goal is to provide the safety needed for exploring the emotions and inner conflicts that underlie the issues bringing you to therapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is relational and exploratory. We'll explore your relationship with others, the therapy relationship, and past experiences. I'll encourage you to freely express what's important to you, and what's on your mind. When we express freely, significant themes emerge that can lead us toward areas of inner experience to explore further. This often involves bringing curiosity to protective patterns as they emerge in our work. We'll integrate your experience of old and new ways of being, so that new meaning, choice, and flexibility can emerge.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I am a queer therapist and my work is guided by the belief that our intersecting identities play a significant role in our lives and the therapy process. I believe that you deserve to have a therapeutic relationship where you can bring your whole self, and I look forward to welcoming and learning about all parts of your life experience. I embrace nonviolence as a guiding value and strive to provide care that aligns with greater freedom and harmony, within yourself and within the world.

name: sandeep kumar
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: As a licensed psychotherapist that works with individual adults and children, I have witnessed therapy’s ability to transform a person’s life. I use mindfulness to cultivate presence of mind that facilitates this process. I specialize in serving children, adolescents, men, and people of color.

approaches: I use Compassion Focused Therapy, which is similar to Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT). Both focus on the inner thoughts that drive behaviors. The process uncovers thoughts, examines what motivations and questions their relevance to the current situation. While CBT seeks to change thoughts, I ask my clients to accept thoughts that had been useful in the past. Negative self-talk develops at a young age and can be detrimental for healthy thinking and perspective. My style of therapy brings greater awareness to self-talk. It’s difficult to sustain this process without an equal amount of compassion. I emphasize self-kindness and awareness when working with self-talk. I believe in the benefits of positive self-talk and positive thinking, but it works best when authentic. I ask my clients, “What do you want to create for yourself in the world? What do you want for and from your life?” A person who believes that one can get what one seeks, stands a better chance of attaining it.

I've practiced meditation and martial arts for over 20 years, and after teaching children’s classes in the Japanese martial art, Aikido, I became interested in the intersection of mental health and the learning process. I saw that the mind and body were at an optimal learning receptivity when one was calm. As I worked with more students, I realized that many students lacked the confidence to accomplish what they wanted. I entered private practice, as a way to provide dedicated, ongoing healing for adults and children who seek a better way to experience their lives through improving self-esteem, and examining belief systems. We are often unconscious of core, ingrained beliefs, the narratives we hold about our own lives and how events fall into a constructed narration. Therapy allows a person to step back and see the narrative as something one has created, and can be recreated to follow a new journey where one is at greater choice.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I've practiced mindfulness meditation for over 20 yrs, and I understand the frustrations that are part of the process of learning to focus the mind. Mindfulness is not just a side part of my therapy practice, but a primary component that I use to connect the insight and awareness into one's motivation, and the development of empathy and compassion for oneself and others.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I draw on a number of modalities including: Narrative (looking at the story you tell yourself and how to reconstruct new ones), Jungian (art and dream work when appropriate), Eastern Psychology (yoga, Aikido, meditation and general Eastern philosophy), Body-centered (derived mostly from my work with Aikido), Holistic (as I try to look to weave various areas of life into a healthy whole).

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT focuses on inner thoughts that drive behaviors. The process involves uncovering thoughts, examining what motivations might inspire them, and questioning whether they are still relevant to the current situation. CBT seeks to then change these thoughts. I diverge from CBT in that I don’t ask my clients to directly change thoughts. I encourage clients accept how thoughts might have been helpful.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: As a person of color, I understand the reality of coping with systemic oppression when one is of a cultural, sexual, gender or other minority. I make efforts to be sensitive to how this appears in my clients’ life, including challenging therapeutic modalities that are often conceived by and for those of majority status. I offer a safe space within today’s political climate.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: Western culture tends to focus on the material world, not just commercialism, but also on things that we can see and believe to understand. When we step into the unknown and gain greater ease embracing the unknown, our life can open up in unexpected ways. I have an Eastern perspective and often bring in concepts of meditation, yoga, and martial arts into the here and now of one's life.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Feminism has rightly challenged women's oppression. However, patriarchy impacts men as well as women. Gender roles are shifting in our society, and I offer a space to unpack and examine what that might mean in your life and how you can live a more authentic life, free of social expectations.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: For 10 years, I've worked with children, teens and young adults at the K-5, middle, high school and college level. I help children age 8 & up with mental health and its impact on their scholastic and general self-esteem. I'm interested in working with children and adolescents coping with anxiety, bullying issues and children who perceive themselves to think and feel differently than others.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: If you suffer from general anxiety, social anxiety, or other anxiety, I can help through the use of mindfulness practices and assisting you in uncovering the root causes of the stress. As society becomes more fast paced, social media takes our attention, or our children become time-pressured, training the mind to respond in a way that effectively calms during stressful moments becomes essential.

name: Peggy Russell
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Together, we will remove old patterns and responses, allowing for the emergence of sustainable, healthy coping mechanisms.
ideal_client: I provide therapy for a diverse population including LGBTQIA+ clients, those experiencing life transitions, intimate partner violence, grief, loss, childhood trauma, PTSD, panic disorder, attachment wounding, depression and anxiety.I believe every human is unique; therefore, I approach therapy as collaborative, tailored to each individual. I honor this step you are taking to care for and invest in yourself. I believe in a therapeutic relationship built on value, compassion, trust and warmth.

approaches.My Background and Approach: As a therapist and a human, I believe that being seen and heard in the caring non-judgmental presence of another creates an environment where deep healing can occur. I practice from a mind-body holism approach, meaning I honor the inseparable union of mind and body. Many of my clients benefit from somatic healing where years of previous talk therapy has only touched the surface. Together we will navigate a path towards understanding the natural somatic and emotional responses associated with difficult life events. I believe we all deserve to feel comfortable in our own skin and at home in our own life as we tend to our basic needs for love, acceptance, connection and safety. I hold a Master’s Degree in Counseling from Oregon State University, and have various continuing education coursework in trauma informed care, adverse childhood experiences, inner child work, grief and loss, somatic work. Currently I am working towards becoming a Certified Hakomi Therapist.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My own lived experience of grief, loss, intimate partner violence, and challenging life transitions found me at a breaking point. From this place I discovered the healing properties of therapy and somatic work. Through yoga, meditation, somatic experiencing, and being deeply heard by another, I began to grow and heal, turning pain into purpose I followed this passion into the field of counseling. I am grateful to pursue what I truly believe is my life’s purpose, and I am so glad you took this step to explore the gift of therapy. I am humbled and honored to share in your journey.

name: Clifford Henry
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I offer an inclusive space for all individuals, couples, and partners to heal, deepen communication, & grow.
ideal_client: Are you feeling the weight of anxiety, depression, or unresolved trauma? Wrestling with your identity or facing challenges in your relationships? Many people I work with are on a journey to find clarity, balance, & peace. If you’re committed to becoming more intentional in your life and breaking free from the generational patterns that no longer serve you, we could be a great fit. Together, we’ll navigate what’s holding you back and guide you toward the growth and authenticity you seek.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach therapy with a gentle touch but don’t shy away from being straightforward when needed. I offer empathy but will also gently challenge you to grow. Humor is always welcome in our sessions—it’s great for breaking the ice, connecting us, & sometimes giving us a new way to look at things. My therapeutic approach is rooted in honoring your lived experience and innate wisdom that comes from your lived experiences. I believe you are the expert of your lived experience & meeting you where you are. I bring tools from Liberation Psychology, Emotion Focused Therapy, Gestalt, Internal Family Systems, Somatic Embodiment and BrainSpotting. At the core of my approach is rooted in the therapeutic relationship and collaboration. From our very first session, my goal is to foster hope and nurture trust. We will set clear goals to guide us, ensuring we work together towards genuine transformation, personal growth, and self-acceptance. I work with individuals, adults and couples.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I’m passionate about creating inclusive, affirming spaces where all clients feel safe and valued. As a BIPOC and Latinx counselor, a proud ally of the LGBTQ+ community, and an advocate for social justice, I believe everyone deserves access to compassionate mental health care. My journey toward becoming a counselor was fueled by a desire to help others uncover resilience, heal from past wounds, and experience meaningful transformation. I draw on trauma-informed, holistic approaches, with specialized training in relational therapy, mindfulness, and somatic techniques. When I’m not in the therapy room, I volunteer with the Liberation Institute a community-based mental health clinic as the Portland Director of Equitable & Inclusive Therapy Practices. My work and my values are intertwined: I believe in showing up for my clients with warmth, integrity, and a deep commitment to fostering growth and healing.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I recognize that every client is unique and has varying needs throughout their therapy journey. To honor this, I use a flexible, integrative approach, blending different therapeutic models to best support each person's individual experience.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I approach therapy through a relational lens, which emphasizes the unique dynamics between individuals and the interplay of past and present experiences that shape their relationships. My work integrates evidence-based techniques from the Gottman Method to enhance communication and conflict resolution, as well as Emotion-Focused Therapy (EFT) to foster deeper emotional connection and understanding. In addition, I am currently on track for certification in Relational Life Therapy (RLT).

specialities.name: Racial Identity
specialities.description: I utilize Relational Cultural Therapy to sensitively and effectively explore how the various personal and cultural relationships in your life have shaped you and impacted your well-being. Additionally, as a BIPOC, second-generation LatinX individual, my lived experiences have instilled in me a deep appreciation and empathy for those navigating the complexities of self-discovery.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Exploring your relationship values can help you clarify what you truly want and need, allowing you to create a relationship structure that feels right for you. I bring knowledge of various forms of polyamory, non-monogamy, and open relationships, and I believe that any relationship can thrive with the consent and honesty of all partners involved. Together, we can find the path that best supports your authentic connection and well-being.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I offer couples counseling to partners of all orientations & genders, understanding that relationships can be challenging & may require support to thrive. Using the Gottman Method and Emotionally Focused Therapy, I help couples build strong foundations for communication and trust. I also incorporate attachment theory to explore how early experiences shape our relationship patterns. Together, we’ll establish firm ground rules, ensuring a safe space where everyone can feel heard and be vulnerable

name: Sae Gally
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I am a queer, non-binary, somatic therapist and Zen Buddhist practitioner.
ideal_client: You sense that your life has meaning, but maybe you haven't been able to feel your aliveness, curiosity, and vitality lately. Perhaps you feel caught up in the slog of everyday life, the hustle of work and relationships, and you have lost some essential part of yourself. Maybe you feel successful in life like you've achieved what you've set out to accomplish, but now you don't know what's next. Therapy can help. I can support you in living a life that is unquestionably meaningful to you.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My approach is client-centered, trauma-informed, and relational. I work with you to establish a sense of safety so that you can explore your edges and grow into the parts of yourself that you are ready to embody. We will help cultivate the wisest parts of yourself, uncovering a foundation that will support you in your daily life and work outside of our sessions. We will work towards body-centered sessions, allowing the non-verbal awareness of your body to guide your growth and integration. All of my work is rooted in an awareness of systemic oppression. I recognize that many of our struggles and coping mechanisms are healthy adaptations to an unjust world. I believe that our individual healing is a part of the work of our collective liberation. While we work together with a focus on your well-being, we support the whole community's well-being, in turn.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: The somatic & mindful approach to integration practiced in Hakomi is a resource that I bring to each of my sessions. I trained at the Hakomi M.E.T.A. Institute of Portland.

name: Galina Arintcina
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: EMDR Therapy to help clients process childhood trauma traumatic experiences, build self-esteem, reduce anxiety, and rediscover joy.
ideal_client: You feel pulled in all directions—work, home, endless responsibilities—leaving little time to catch your breath. The pressures of daily life, the pressure to perform, and the pain of past experiences, build up, draining your energy and well-being. Anxiety, depression, low self-esteem, and self-doubt are tough burdens to carry, often leaving you feeling stuck, drained, and disconnected from yourself and others.

approaches.What I Specialize In: You don’t have to carry this weight alone; together, we can move you forward. As a Registered Associate Counselor, I provide practical, evidence-based therapy for clients in Oregon via telehealth. My approach is direct yet supportive, grounded in EMDR and Internal Family Systems (IFS), both highly effective, research-backed methods. With these tools, we can work through the pain and help you build resilience, self-worth, and expand your toolkit for navigating life with greater ease and confidence. Imagine facing challenges from a place of strength and self-compassion, knowing you are loved and worthy just as you are. Even in the hard moments, you’ll feel equipped to handle what comes your way, trusting your capacity to move forward with peace and purpose. I’m here to support you every step of the way.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Therapy is not one-size-fits-all; there are many approaches to understanding and supporting change. Some focus on behavior alone, offering new patterns to follow. While this can be helpful, I’ve seen how challenging it is for people to simply “change” without addressing the deeper reasons behind their actions. My approach recognizes that every behavior has a purpose, even when it’s not serving you in the way you’d hope. Instead of just focusing on what to change, we’ll explore why those behaviors exist, uncovering the underlying needs, emotions, or beliefs driving them. Together, we’ll identify alternative choices that feel aligned with your values and goals, keeping your integrity and individuality at the center of our work. This way, change becomes not just achievable but sustainable, empowering you to move forward in a way that feels authentic and meaningful.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I specialize in EMDR, a highly effective, evidence-based approach for processing trauma and other distressing life experiences. My training in EMDR, including advanced EMDR 2.0 techniques, equips me to help you reprocess painful memories, reduce emotional distress, and foster resilience. I’ve worked with diverse populations, including those facing PTSD, developmental trauma, and attachment issues, guiding them through transformative healing.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I believe that IFS is a great way to understand how things work. IFS helps explore and harmonize internal “parts” or subpersonalities. My expertise in IFS will help you understand the protective and wounded parts and foster self-compassion and internal balance. I use this approach in combination with EMDR to address complex emotional challenges and help achieve deep, lasting change.

name: Brad Poser, MS, CRC
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Everybody struggles with feelings of self worth or discouragement. Whether from personal loss, social difficulties or bumps in our relationships, it's easy to forget these emotions are a natural part of the human experience. It's even harder to remember it's okay to ask for help when overwhelmed.

approaches: We all get bogged down with what we ‘should do’ or worry about how we are ‘supposed to’ feel. Through no fault of our own, these thoughts can become overwhelming. We lose track of what makes us who we are, what gives us our sense of self worth. When these thoughts won’t go away, sometimes everyone needs a helping hand. Other times, we just need a break from the world and a safe place. Emotions aren't something we can easily just think our way out of. They are real. Just like any pain, they can require real attention. There is no therapeutic formula that 'fixes people.' I believe in meeting people where they are, in listening to their stories and finding their strengths.

I hold a Masters of Science in counseling and was an RSA Scholar. I am a member of the American Counseling Association, a certified rehabilitation counselor (CRC) and an LPC intern with the Oregon board of licensed therapists. I have years of experience working with the Poly and LGBTQ community. I was also a ADA and social services support professional for ten years, both in Portland and elsewhere. I have advanced training or certification is Depression/anxiety, Mindfulness, Motivational Interviewing, Trauma recovery, PTSD, Autism, TBI, Disability rights and case management.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have a focus on Non-Monogamous or open relationships. These partnerships can be difficult to navigate. Despite intentions, jealousy, fear and difficulties with self worth can easily be present. Often, understanding support can be difficult to find.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma is another human condition that some folks think can be just 'wished away'. Even things that happened years ago can echo into the present. Unwanted thoughts and emotions can jump into our minds and make daily life hard to focus on. I have experience helping people come to terms with trauma. With the right skills, it is possible to make room for the past and re-enter your life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I specialize in social anxiety and phobia. I use a narrative and mindfulness approach to normalize and limit fears of social engagement.

specialities.name: Autism
