specialities.description: I have ten years of experience working with individuals with autism. My specialty is helping parents understand and relate to a child with autism. I also have experience assisting individuals with autism who are struggling with anxiety or frustration

name: Kaci Schmitt
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: LPC, LMHC, LPCC, NCC | Oregon License #: C5770 | Washington License #: LH61062126 | California License #: 15755
intro: In our work together, we will discover the peace, strengths, wholeness, and sense of connection that already exist within you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a strengths-based, relational and compassion-focused therapist in Portland, Oregon. I love working with adolescents and adults with anxiety, depression, and difficulty adjusting to change and indecision, as well as helping clients process and integrate grief and loss into their lives. My approach to therapy is guided by my belief that through our work together, we can create a safe space where you can find peace, develop your own intuition and wisdom to make your own choices about what's right for your life, and create new meaning to live in a more balanced, free, and gentle way. Therapy is a safe place where we can process your life together. I believe that you are your greatest source of wisdom and that in our work together, we can uncover what is keeping you stuck and find the resources you need to move forward. I believe that compassion and warmth are essential to therapy, and I prioritize creating a strong therapeutic relationship with my clients.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I help my clients explore their unique challenges and life situations so that they can uncover joy, contentment, and ease, as well as find solutions to unresolved issues and process and manage trauma and pain. I encourage my clients to look within themselves to find their own strengths, resources, and inner wisdom. And because being a human is not always easy, I encourage my clients to develop deep self-compassion and curiosity about themselves and their lives. This process is complex, and each person is unique, so I approach each client individually and with care and compassion. Many of the clients who find me (or whose parents find me) tend to be highly sensitive individuals who are empathic, attuned to their environments and other people (and often had to be beginning in childhood due to trauma), and want to live happy, meaningful lives but who are overwhelmed by their current challenges or find themselves “stuck” in certain emotional, relational, or life patterns.

name: Jooyoung Oh
title: Professional Counselor
intro: Jooyoung brings Creativity and Process Work in order to deepen our understanding of self as a sentient being.
ideal_client: As a Korean immigrant, I find working with Asian American and Indigenous Pacific Islander clients to be most effective and rewarding. Our community has a unique individual and group process, and it is important to understand and honor the unique struggles we carry. Common topic includes shame, internalized oppression, model minority myth, micro-aggression, invisibility, fear and anxiety coming from anti-Asian racism. Supporting BLM movement starts with understanding our racial identity and our a

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Explore long and short-term body symptoms, nighttime dreams as well as half dreams (flash of images or stories) to deepen an understanding of oneself Explore patterns in whom we fall in love with or we have a conflict with to understand what is being marginalized within oneself Explore childhood dreams and memories to understand our life myth I follow the code of ethics in therapy for practitioners in USA. It means… > Confidentiality. What you share stays with me. An exception of when there is a possibility of self-harming or harming others), equal power > Co-creation: I am not here to give you any advice as someone superior in any way. We are in this together.

name: Lena-Liis Kiesel
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I believe strongly in the therapeutic relationship and that people possess the strength, ability and resilience to make positive change.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from a Humanistic background and incorporate Attachment, Acceptance Commitment Therapy and Family Systems as well as other modalities including mindfulness as needed, individualized by client.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a specialty in substance abuse and am a CADCI. I have also worked extensively with couples and use the Gottman Method. With children I have experience with play therapy and sand tray. Brainspotting is a more recent addition to the modalities which I feel comfortable using.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: I am a certified CADCI

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I use mindfulness techniques tailored to each client.

name: PAULINE ROBERT
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Pauline Robert SHE/HER Licensed Clinical Social Worker
ideal_client: I have over 10 years of experience working with people from all backgrounds in a wide array of settings. I specialize in trauma treatment, particularly complex, developmental, and Adoptee attachment trauma. Other areas of focus, experience and dedication, include: domestic violence, sexual abuse, and race-based trauma. I am dedicated to women's issues of gender inequality, and the empowerment of finding our voices and identity throughout our evolving life span.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a Mental Health Therapist and licensed Clinical Social Worker in Oregon, I engage with compassion, respect, humor, and directness. Whether we are working to increase emotional stability, heal trauma, or find our personal meaning, my aim is to guide you in your goals toward empowered well-being. Building upon insight, personal strengths, and self-compassion, we can all develop a greater connection to ourselves and those around us. I engage with clients using a trauma-informed, culturally affirming approach. I use a variety of evidence based interventions, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing (EMDR), Life Span Integration and Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction. I look forward to meeting and working with you.

name: Shannon Garcia
title: Art Therapist
intro: I am a person-centered somatic art therapist passionate about using creativity and body attunement to support growth and wellness.
ideal_client: Feeling messy, overwhelmed, lost, questioning or stuck? Need somewhere safe enough to be seen as a raw and imperfect human? Come as you are! I’m here for it! I’m passionate about supporting clients (age 14 - elder) in navigating life transitions, neurodiversity, grief, trauma, anxiety, depression, identity and chronic illness in the context of their individual experience and backgrounds.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have over a decade of supporting people across the life span in their creative journey, and ready to support you in your mental health and wellness journey as well. I work somatically and with art processes to offer a holistic approach to therapy. Therapeutically, I have worked with adolescents through adults, and am excited to support you in your goals. I have a MA in Art Therapy from Lewis & Clark, and undergraduate degrees from the Institute of American Indian Arts and Pacific Northwest College of Art. I also have a Soul Based Somatic Trauma Training Certificate from the Somatic Nature Therapy Institute, and I carry a Wilderness First Responder certificate. I come to this work from a background as an art educator and an artist. Art opens doors, and I found that my students would open doors that I could hold space for as a human, but not therapeutically. That, along with taking several semesters of psychology pre-reqs, led me to completing a Master's degree in art therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Therapy is relational work, and I believe that my biggest job is to create spaces for healing that address your goals, and support humans in integrating experiences that live within our bodies that are holding us back, slowing us down, or otherwise keeping us from living full and healthful lives. I do that by using art processes, mindfulness, and body attunement to process deep work, create space in our minds for stress and anxiety reduction, and to honor experiences and perspectives with intention, compassion and warmth.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: I hold an MA in Art Therapy from Lewis & Clark and have worked for 2 years in a cancer healing center as well as 1 year in an academic setting for students a few steps out of general education who need mental health supports in an academic setting. I have worked with clients with chronic illness, trauma, anxiety and depression, neurodiversity, aging, legacy, and grief.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I have a Soul-Based Somatic Trauma Training Certificate from the Somatic Nature Therapy Institute. This is a 9-month training that centers the body and the felt sense of experiences to explore and work with resourcing, trauma, attachment, and soul-based interventions. I have integrated this work into my art therapy practice with cancer patients and with adolescents at a social emotional focus alternative school.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: As an intern at a social emotional alternative school, I worked with students with autism and comorbid diagnoses, including anxiety, depression, suicidality, bipolar and chronic illness. Our goals centered student needs and social emotional development in context of their lived lives, by centering them as wonderful and rich experts of themselves, integrating their special interests and co-creating our work to best support their development.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Everyone experiences anxiety on some level from time to time. When anxiety affects day to day functioning, or when you want to change how you relate to it, it's time for some support. I have worked with folks across most of the life span to create space to lessen the severity of anxiety through art therapy and somatically.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is one of the most human experiences, and it is meant to be experienced in community, rather than in isolation. The thing about grief is that when it's bump up against, other grief comes up to be tended as well. Beyond the loss of someone or something loved, grief can be ambiguous, anticipatory, complicated, disenfranchised, traumatic and more. I have tended grief in community through grief groups, and as community in individual work.

specialities.name: Cancer
specialities.description: I have supported people in their cancer experiences for 2 years at a local cancer healing center. From a transpersonal oriented program, I companioned people in their experience, created curriculum to support stress and anxiety relief, and to expand opportunities to LGBTQ+ folks who at that time did not have any group offerings at local cancer centers. I worked with many experiences that tend to coincide with major life and health transitions: trauma, divorce, parenting, caregiving, and grief.

name: Victoria Solon
title: Student Counselor
intro: With collaborative, affirming, and culturally attuned care, I’m here to support you.
ideal_client: I’m here for those seeking support in navigating identity, relationships, life transitions, and cultural or systemic challenges. I honor your unique background and center inclusivity, curiosity, and collaboration in our work. Together, we’ll explore your stories, highlighting resilience, reclaiming your voice, and fostering meaningful transformation.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Originally trained as a psychotherapist in Brazil, I bring a multicultural lens to my work. I’m currently pursuing my MA in Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy with a specialization in sexuality. My therapeutic approach is grounded in collaborative-dialogical and narrative practices, influenced by postmodern and social constructionist ideas. Clients are the experts in their lives and my role as the therapist is being the expert in the process of doing therapy. I maintain a position of “not-knowing” - being genuinely curious and non-judgmental - by exploring possible routes in therapy in partnership with my clients. This allows me to cultivate a therapeutic relationship built on clients’ autonomy, with openness, collaboration and respect, creating a space where clients feel safe and supported to re-author their lives and embrace transformation.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As a queer, neurodivergent, and Latina therapist-in-training, I bring lived experience and deep care to my work. I approach therapy through a socially just lens, honoring the ways identity, culture, and systemic forces shape our lives. I strive to create an affirming space where clients — especially those from marginalized or underrepresented communities — feel seen, heard, and supported. My work is grounded in curiosity, collaboration, and a commitment to deconstructing dominant narratives. I believe healing happens in relationship, and I am dedicated to walking alongside clients as we open new possibilities for meaning, reclaim their voice, and move toward the life they aspire.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: I am a graduate trainee in Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy with a specialization in sexuality. I am in the ongoing process of learning and becoming a therapist who works with individuals, couples, and families through a culturally attuned, socially just, and affirming lens. My approach focus on conversation, curiosity, and shared understanding, and when necessary, I integrate from other evidence-based approaches as conversational resources.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: I see therapy as a social construction, grounding my work in Collaborative and Narrative Therapy, which focus on conversation, curiosity, and shared understanding. This way of being positions me in a respectful, partnership stance, we'll explore your stories, deconstruct dominant narratives, and co-create new meanings, fostering mutual transformation. I also hold certifications in Narrative Therapy and in Collaborative-Dialogical Practices, allowing me to better support clients.

specialities.name: Cultural Congruence
specialities.description: I’ve had the opportunity to work with diverse populations in Brazil through private practice, volunteer work, and externships. I am committed to continuously expanding my knowledge and becoming increasingly culturally aware and responsive. I strive to support and honor each client’s lived experiences, identities, and cultural backgrounds as essential parts of the therapeutic process.

name: Helen Zwiebel
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hello! I'm located in East Portland working as a sex and relationship therapist. My specialty is consensual/ethical non-monogamy.
ideal_client: I focus on helping people curious about and/or practicing consensual/ethical non-monogamy, solo poly, relationship anarchy, and any alternative relationship style. I am BDSM/kink-aware and LGBTQIA+ friendly.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy is about the relationship and therapeutic alliance. We will create a safe space where you feel seen and heard. This space will be free from judgment and built on authenticity. We will work in collaboration with a strong focus on building confidence and trust in yourself. You will be provided guidance and support to process what life has presented you. Any goals set will be based on your values. Evidence-based practices used include Motivational Interviewing, Feedback Informed Treatment, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am invested in helping this community. It is a privilege to help people define and feel empowered about their sexuality. I hope to be a part of the normalization of our bodies, desires, and behaviors. Specialties Consensual/Ethical Non-Monogamy (CNM/ENM) Relationship Issues Sexual Expression Stress and Life Transitions Also experienced in: Age group 18+, BDSM/kink, Body positivity, Coping with life changes, Enthusiastic consent, LGBTQIA+, Mindfulness, Pain management, Personal growth, Self-esteem, Severe and Persistent Mental Illness (SPMI), Sexual problems, Sleeping difficulties

name: Heidi Savell
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I bring a warm and collaborative approach to help you get unstuck, ease anxiety, navigate relationships, and improve connections to others.
ideal_client: I work best with those who are ready to engage in the process of making changes. Most of the people I work with are looking to develop deeper self awareness, ease anxiety, shift long held beliefs, or let go of habits that have become harmful. I have almost a decade working with individuals and couples who are exploring non-monogamy or polyamory

approaches.My Background and Approach: I will work with you at your pace to help you identify the goals most important to you, while also supporting you in letting go of whatever may be getting in your way. I find it can be most effective to focus on your areas of strength as well as areas where you are experiencing problems, as I believe your already existing strengths and skills can be used to help you bring your life more in line with how you would like it to be. My training and skills include a blend of attachment theory, compassion-focused therapy, non-violent communication, and cognitive behavioral therapy. I also incorporate parts work/Internal Family Systems.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I provide counseling to those who: *Want to find better ways to cope with stress and anxiety *Are in a relationship that needs support around communication, connecting, and managing conflict *Identify as polyamorous or non-monogamous and are wanting experienced, competent care and support *Are dealing with low self-worth, perfectionism, or self-criticism *Are experiencing challenges with personal or professional relationships *Have experienced a life change and want to clarify how to handle it *Want to improve relationships with family members or other loved ones

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I use attachment theory to inform the work I do with individuals, couples, and family members. I believe it is crucial to overall mental wellness to understand your patterns and needs around connecting with others and finding relational safety.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Finding competent care when in a polyamorous or non-monogamous relationship can be a challenge. I have nearly 10 years of experience supporting polyamorous and non-monogamous individuals and couples, and I provide therapy that honors the complexity, nuance, joys and challenges of navigating life and relationships within a non-monogamous context.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can be overwhelming and impacts all areas of a person's life. I will work with you at your pace to help you identify and reconnect with the things most important to you, while also supporting you in letting go of whatever may be getting in the way of experiencing more ease.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have training in the Gottman Method as well as Emotionally Focused Therapy, and I bring a blend of these two models to the work I do. I can help you improve communication, ease conflict, and deepen your understanding and compassion for yourself as well as your partner(s).

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: I have experience working with many different types of families, including blended families, LGBTQ families, siblings, and parents with adult children. Divorce, substance use, mental health challenges or major life changes can impact the whole family, and I have found that coming together to address feelings and work on communication can improve relationship satisfaction, as well as give family members a sense of empowerment

name: Shannon LaDouce
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: APPOINTMENTS AVAILBLE this week! I'm an experienced Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner that provides Medication management.
ideal_client: As a mom and Army Veteran, I am passionate about supporting those who have dedicated their lives to service (of all types!) I am adept at working with the "givers" - the folks who are often over-extending to those around them. Whether you're a veteran navigating the challenges of post-service life, a healthcare provider managing the pressures, a mom juggling the demands of parenthood, or the friend everyone turns to, I am committed to creating a safe space for you to receive support.

approaches.My Background: My decade of nursing experience spans across every chapter of life, from labor and delivery to end of life and cancer care. -Outpatient mental-health facilities -Active-duty army registered nurse, variety of inpatient hospital settings all over the country -Nursing leadership -Nursing faculty and clinical instructing

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am also an International Sports Sciences Association Certified Fitness and Nutrition Trainer, and along with medication management, love to talk about ways to support your overall wellbeing.

name: Chad Ernest, MS, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My name is Chad Ernest and I am a Licensed Professional Counselor, who believes in the best in you.
ideal_client: Whether you are an individual struggling with stress, anxiety, depression, emotional duress or other mental health issues; a parent challenged with the behaviors of your child; a partner in a relationship having communication issues or problems with connection and intimacy; a family having a hard time getting along and managing emotions in the same living space; I am here to help you through your journey in discovering the best ways to work through your struggles.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe in a client/family centered approach with collaboration in treatment between the counselor and client/family. The goal of counseling overall is wellness and/or reconciliation with one’s self, family and the community. I am an integrationist in my counseling theory, which means that I believe in incorporating various theories into my practice to suit the needs of whom I am serving. My practice is based on the following theories and interventions within them: Various evidence based practices; the Family Checkup Model; Person-centered; Existential; Gestalt; Psychodynamic; Narrative; Strength Based; Cognitive Behavioral; Rational Emotive Behavioral; Reality; Feminist; Family Systems Therapy; and Collaborative Parenting. The approach utilized is based on your needs and facilitated with you or your family and your partner.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a BA in Psychology and Philosophy from the University of Wisconsin-Madison received in 2000. I have an MS in Mental Health Counseling from Capella University received in March 2011 and a Graduate Certificate in Marriage and Family Therapy from Capella University received in December 2010. I am a member of Counselors for Social Justice (CSJ) and American Counselors Association (ACA).

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I utilize Collaborative approaches to working with couples. I conduct in depth interviews to highlight what both partners feel is happening in their relationship and then find the best approach to assisting in working through these struggles. I do not promise that all relationships work out, however. It is up to each individual in the relationship to want to make that happen.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
specialities.description: Motivational interviewing is a great technique for helping with individuals and families who are struggling to make a change in their lives for the better. Finding where you are in the Stages of Change can help you identify where you want to be and how to get to a place where you can make long lasting and impactful beneficial changes in your life.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: I utilize a Family Systems approach in working with families. I take this a step further and help families to look at the environments around them as well as the supports in these environments. Working to help families see how their survival in a system impacts how they raise their children and how the choices they make can change the way they live for the better.

specialities.name: Coronavirus/COVID-19
specialities.description: We are offering in person, phone and video sessions.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Parenting children can be like being dropped in the middle of a forest with only the clothes on your back and having to find your way out and survive. We don't have all the answers to working with children and sometimes our own experiences with our parents was not the best example either. I am like the woods guide who helps you learn techniques to become better at what you already know.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Whether you're child is struggling in school, has behavioral issues, been diagnosed with ADHD, a learning disorder, or is on the Autism Spectrum, I can help with learning more about how to manage behaviors and work with the children on understanding, coming to terms with, and overcoming their symptoms.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Self-esteem is the cornerstone to many mental health issues. Depression and anxiety find both their roots in low self-esteem. Being able to feel confident and good about one's self can be challenging, but with my help we can rebuild a positive self-image.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have a lifetime of experience, both personal and professional, with helping couples work through relationship issues. Struggling with communication, thinking about divorce/breaking up, or just fighting a lot? I can help.

name: Katie Playfair
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm an OCD specialist but because of the overlap in symptoms, my practice is overwhelmingly neurodivergent. OCPD, ADHD, Autism, SPD, etc.
ideal_client: Clients who like my practice and find it different than previous therapy experiences tell me that I'm directive, involve them as an equal partner in their treatment, educate them about mental health concepts in general, and push them to be compassionate and loving with themselves while they push hard to change their lives. I help people feel "normal," learn to live better with their anxiety, and manage it long-term.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide therapy in-person and online across Oregon and Washington and education services worldwide. Technically, my approach draws from cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), and more recently, Radically Open DBT (learning & training in process). More generally, I want to be your partner in discovering a better relationship with your mental health and/or work life. I want to empower you by providing education and transparency about how I see your experiences and what the evidence says about how we can help you live better. My hope is that you walk away from our meetings together knowing what works for you and what doesn't, in terms of mental health care, so it's knowledge you can use way beyond our therapy relationship. Also, therapy can be really fun and I hope to make it that way for you!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Beyond my clinical work, I really enjoy helping other clinicians integrate evidence-based therapies into their own personal style. Evidence-based practice doesn't have to be dry and mechanical. In fact, I think that the difficult work of therapy is much more tolerable for clients when we bring our unique selves, our senses of humor, and our humanity into the consulting room. I work with other clinicians via formal trainings, consultation with licensed clinicians, and supervision of associate clinicians. In my personal life, I am a mom of three kids and two dogs, living with ADHD, and navigating the challenges of middle-age and perimenopause. Firmly in the sandwich generation, I live with my spouse, kids, and my dad. Multigenerational living is rich in meaningfulness and challenges. Coming from a family of physicians and nurses, I apply that knowledge to help ensure that my clients are seeking high quality consultation from appropriate medical professionals while in counseling.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: ACT is a "third-wave" behavior therapy that my clients and I agree, is much more tolerable approach to treating many diagnoses. I love ACT for a few reasons: 1. We emphasize CLIENT values in choosing which symptoms we're treating and how we're approaching the treatment. 2. It's transdiagnostic. The same skill can benefit multiple people with different diagnoses. ACT skills can benefit someone with depression, anxiety, OCD, or other symptoms. 3. It's neurodiversity-affirming.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT is a very evidence-based approach to changing your behavior, thereby changing your thoughts, and finally, changing your feelings. I rarely use CBT in isolation (I like to combine it with ACT) but CBT techniques are still my go-to approach for many common anxiety challenges. I’m specifically trained in Supportive Parenting for Anxious Child Emotions (SPACE) and I work with the parents of teens and young adults.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: Some of my clients need support in exploring their values, career directions, or simply making progress in a part of their life they feel stuck on. I use an Acceptance and Commitment Therapy approach to coaching, whether it's career coaching, ADHD coaching, or partner coaching for the loved ones of people with OCD, ADHD, Autism Spectrum Disorders, etc.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: OCD includes Illness Anxiety Disorder/Health Anxiety/hypochondriasis, obsessions, compulsions, skin and hair picking, and some other types of more severe anxiety you might not know are in the OCD cluster. This is one area where I've done a lot of specialized training. I use neurodiversity-affirming Acceptance and Commitment Therapy + Exposure and Response Prevention for most clients with OCD and related disorders. e

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: My first career was in management consulting for technology teams. This experience has given me a lot of insight into career counseling subjects beyond the material we're required to know as counselors. I know about the workplace cultures of many major employers in Oregon and Washington and clients tell me that this experiences has been helpful in discussing their work-related stressors with me. I also have a career counseling guide and framework for helping clients with career change.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I've been through multiple pregnancies, difficult deliveries, pregnancy loss, and perimenopause and have helped clients navigate these life experiences as well. I help clients with anxiety histories plan for possible pregnancy-related anxiety, depression, or OCD and provide support for those who were completely surprised by the arrival of these symptoms.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: While I understand the benevolent aims of the "ADHD is a superpower" crowd, it's also a disability for many people. Living with a brain with a bit too much power and a little too little control is exhausting and demoralizing. I help clients with ADHD better understand their brains, identify their strengths and experiences of success, and then develop customized approaches to living better with this neurodevelopmental disorder.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: Like most clinicians of my generation, we weren't given much education about autism in school. As our understanding of it has expanded, it's become clear to me why some clients with "OCD" are less successful with traditional ERP. If "OCD" is better explained by Autism, we need a neurodiversity-affirming approach to treatment, not a one-size-fits-all protocol developed on neurotypical people in a lab. I work with Autistic clients' team to develop the right approach for them.

name: Emily Shiraishi
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I specialize in providing individual therapy to people who want to break free from their patterns of self-doubt and worry.
ideal_client: Your worries are draining you of time and energy. The life you want seems out of reach. You forget to take care of yourself because you’re so busy taking care of others. You feel misunderstood or isolated because of cultural issues. You want to work with a therapist who will listen deeply and holistically, who respects your identities and perspectives, and also collaborates with you to take your next steps in healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I help people change their relationship with anxiety and self-doubt by guiding them to address the roots of the problem. By focusing on the past and the present as well as working to uncover more of your emotions and needs, we can better understand how things got stuck and empower you to chart a new path forward.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I long found that people felt safe confiding in me. I became a therapist because it felt natural to me. I also get inspired by the strength and wisdom of my patients as well as my peers and mentors. I feel fortunate to do this work; to help improve the quality of people's lives.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Your worries are taking up too much time and energy, and blocking you from the life you want to lead. They are getting in the way of your relationships and stopping you from reaching your goals.

name: Ashlee Garau-Brittingham
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I really believe the relationship between client & therapist is everything! My space is inviting, warm, & nurturing.
ideal_client: Do you find it hard to slow down uninvited thoughts & feelings of worry/dread or criticism? Do you neglect your wants & needs to prioritize others? Having repetitious thoughts of guilt, worthlessness, or fearing you are never good enough? Or even struggle to understand/break patterns of behavior that do not support you? I know it can be so scary & feel uncertain to find new paths to explore. I’m here to help decrease these experiences with the somatic & narrative therapy practices I use!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: It is so common to have internal voices encouraging avoidance, judgment & shame toward ourselves. Unfortunately, these voices don’t invite curiosity, awareness, empathy, or collaboration, which is where so much of therapy & healing live! I can help you understand why unwanted emotions arise, how to build new intentional skills to avoid repeating unhelpful patterns or reactions & give you a sense of being in control. I will provide tools that you can take everywhere to help slow down racing thoughts, clarify your intentions, & support your body to become regulated & centered. Therapeutic approaches I draw from surround narrative therapy, mindfulness, attachment, CBT, motivational interviewing, family systems therapy, & sensory-motor arousal regulation treatment (SMART). Safe space is so important! I create this environment by being curious, compassionate, & relational focused. It's also not uncommon for there to be laughter & humor in the moments we are both being relational humans.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I really believe every person holds innate strength & capabilities to pursue self-acceptance, growth, change, healing, & empowerment! I also take a position that firmly trusts all feelings are neither good or bad, right or wrong. Feelings are truth tellers & help provide context to what we are experiencing. Many clients describe trying to manage an unwanted feeling through avoidance & resistance because they lack the skills or have a belief that the strong or unwanted feeling is “bad/wrong”. I have witnessed when people are taught the skills to feel the honesty & vulnerability of an unwanted feeling, they find new perspectives, self-trust & opportunities to navigate toward a different outcome of that is more aligned of their values and needs.

name: Hudson McCarthy
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hello, I'm Hudson. I'm a queer Professional Counselor Associate, CADC-R and an Eco-Therapist. I'd love to hear how I can be of support.
ideal_client: I identify as a queer, neurodivergent, non-binary counselor. Being part of and working with these and other marginalized communities has given me the opportunity to work with a wide variety of folx from diverse backgrounds. I've worked with individuals experiencing struggles from depression, anxiety, psychosis, bipolar, life transitions, grief, ethical non-monogamy, kink, trauma and grief. I'm here to help create a warm environment that fosters trust.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I take an existential-humanistic approach with an anti-racist, social justice and holistic lens which means I see the client being the expert on their own life and I am there alongside them in support of their healing journey. I incorporate an eclectic variety of modalities that is unique to each individual as we work collaboratively in session. Some of these modalities include but not limited to: DBT skills, somatic therapy, harm reduction, creativity and trauma informed. I graduated from Lewis and Clark College in 2024 with a Masters of Art in Professional Mental Health Counseling focusing on Addictions and certifying in Eco-Therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a counselor I strive for a calm, compassionate, empathetic and authentic energy. Life is hard, messy and sometimes even chaotic. I strongly believe that everyone has the capacity within themselves to see hope again when it was once lost. As someone who holds various marginalized identities, I know first hand how challenging it can be to have self compassion, patience with yourself in times of healing and growth, and I also know that it's very possible with persistence, resilience and just continuing to work on personal growth. My interests of focus reside in harm reduction approaches to substance use, incorporating nature into therapy and creative strategies to navigating hard feelings and working with folx who are just transitioning into adulthood to later adulthood. I enjoy leaning into just having raw, authentic dialogue in sessions and feel that with time a strong therapeutic relationship will be made that feels safe.

name: Al Newman
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: My goal is to offer collaborative therapy to neurodivergent and LGBTQ+ individuals, couples, and families, fostering growth and well-being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that, although the human experience can be challenging, it holds the potential for deep meaning. My goal is to work with you to help you re-write your stories in order to create the meaning and connection you wish to see in your life. I take a collaborative approach and while I may pull techniques from various evidence-based practices, I believe that safety in therapeutic relationships takes time to foster. Thus, I primarily use narrative, existential-humanistic, and attachment-based approaches to help you untangle the many possibilities for relating to yourself and the world around you.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As a queer therapist, I use systemic approaches to explore how oppressive systems affect LGBTQIA+ individuals and other marginalized groups. Issues like capitalism, white supremacy, and heteronormative standards impact all of us. In therapy, we can work together to unpack and challenge the internalized messages and negativity these systems create.

name: Reyah Travis
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I primarily support couples and families wanting to regain contentment and satisfaction in their relationships.
ideal_client: My ideal client is someone in a relationship with a romantic partner, family member or loved one who is wanting to rewire their normal communication patterns in an efficient and evidence based way with the goal of having happier relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I practice emotionally focused therapy. We focus on cultivating emotional intimacy, not on deciding who is right or wrong or “fixing” someone or a challenge. Basically we run communication drills in session to rewire how we connect with the people that we love that leads to eveyrone feeling more connected and satisfied in their relationships.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I’m a mom, democratic socialist, animal lover, and believer in political engagement to improve our world. I offer emotionally focused couples and family therapy. I have training and specialization in themes related to indigenous culture, houselessness, suicide prevention, DID and the plural community, racial equity, and abuse prevention.

name: James Reling
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello, I have openings for new clients and adults seeking Autism/ADHD assessments, see my website to schedule.
ideal_client: My ideal client is an adult who suspects they might be neurodivergent, such as late-diagnosed Autistic or ADHD individuals. They are typically curious, open to self-discovery, and seeking professional guidance for clarity and validation in understanding their neurodivergent traits. They value a supportive and affirming therapeutic approach that honors their unique experiences. If you're on a journey of self-discovery and yearn for clarity, I'm here to provide comprehensive support.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I specialize in working with "late-diagnosed" Autistic and ADHD adults, offering support in your exploration of neurodivergence. Being neurodivergent myself, I can empathize with the challenges you might face, and that is why I started offering Autism/ADHD assessments in the first place. My program includes: Thorough Assessment: We delve into your experiences and traits, guided by your perspective. Neurodiversity-Affirming Testing: An in-depth evaluation to confirm your neurodiversity. Personalized Guidance: Tailoring support to address how your neurotype impacts various aspects of your life. Future Roadmap: Providing recommendations and resources to guide your next steps. I'm committed to creating a stigma-free and safe space for your neurodivergent self-discovery. You don't have to go through this alone. Feel free to reach out to initiate your assessment process by going to my website and scheduling a consultation.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I'm an autistic individual myself, which gives me a unique perspective. I've faced denial and struggled with my own misconceptions and stereotypes about autism. I also understand the societal stigma around neurodivergence, making it challenging to discuss with family and friends. I've experienced a lifetime of wanting to connect with others but often feeling misunderstood, leading to strained relationships. Most of my clients come to me when they are looking for answers to better understand themselves so they can lead more fulfilling lives. As a therapist, I prioritize your goals and won't push specific interventions like social skills training unless you express a desire for them. I'm here to listen, help you process, and choose what you want in your life. I'm open to exploring your special interests, understanding their importance, and using them to aid in emotional expression.

specialities.name: Hakomi
specialities.description: I have completed training and a year-long internship in Hakomi Mindfulness-based Body-Centered and Experiential Psychotherapy and largely draw from this approach. This involves using mindfulness and nonjudgmental curiosity during therapy sessions to connect to your somatic (bodily) experience and how they connect to your emotions to heal wounding.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Trauma (from big events to the accumulation of smaller invalidating experiences) is stored in the body, as is resilience and the potential for healing. By learning how to listen to and follow your body's cues, you can heal in ways that may be less accessible to traditional talk therapy. I am currently in a three-year training to become a Somatic Experiencing Practioner.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: With your consent, I use mindfulness during therapy sessions to guide you toward your present experience and learn how to use mindfulness during everyday life to be more present and fulfilled.

specialities.name: Aspergers
specialities.description: Well, we don't use the term "Aspergers" anymore, but there is no option for autism or neurodiversity. I work with neurodivergent clients from an affirming lens. Being autistic is not the problem; the problem is we live in an ableist culture that centers neurotypical experience. So I focus on understanding my neurodivergent clients' experiences, working with their strengths, and helping them with changes they wish to address, rather than what society deems as "appropriate" or "normal."

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: My training in working with people who have disabilities includes chronic pain/illness, which can be particularly tricky to navigate when these disabilities are not 'visible' to others. Many people with chronic pain/illness can feel alone and misunderstood by their medical providers, family, friends, and employers.

name: Holly Wigmore
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: An IFS practice focused on trauma processing in a supportive, nonjudgemental, and relational environment.
ideal_client: Looking for a therapist can be overwhelming. Maybe you are experiencing anxiety, hopelessness, or can't quite put a finger on what you are feeling. Maybe you have experiences with PTSD, trauma, or dissociation. Maybe you've been on a path of healing for a long time, or maybe you just started today. I want to support your connection to your own innate inner wisdom that holds the keys to healing the wounds that keep you from where you want to be or where you want to go next.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I hold a Master of Science in Counseling from Portland State University. I have completed IFS Level One training through the IFS institute and continue to engage in consultation with IFS certified practitioners. IFS is an evidenced based therapeutic model that seeks to support understanding the complexities of each individual through their parts. Through this work, we work to expand our curiosity, compassion, and care towards our unique parts that make us whole. While the focus of my practice is Internal Family Systems, I also draw from Emotion-Focused, Family Systems, Gestalt, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, and somatic interventions. I deeply value collaboration, creativity, and authenticity in the therapeutic relationship I cultivate with my clients.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I come to the field of mental health with an eclectic background as a theater artist and educator. I deeply value collaboration and approaching the counseling relationship with authenticity and a nonjudgmental attitude. As a therapist, I’m interested interpersonal and emotionally focused theories that seek to explore why and how we show up in relationships with others. My work is dedicated to including anti-racist, anti-oppressive, anti-heterosexist, anti-fat biases, and trauma-informed practices. As an able-bodied white cishet counselor, I see my privileges as a responsibility to continually consider how my identities and experiences interact with folx that I work with. I work with AR-TIC (Anti-Racist Trauma Informed Care) as a facilitator which works to decentralize whiteness in healing practices.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: IFS is an evidenced based therapeutic model that seeks to support understanding the complexities of each individual through their parts. Through this work, we seek to extend curiosity, compassion, and care towards our unique parts that make us whole. In my work as a trauma therapist and as a client, I have found the IFS model a deeply validating, normalizing, and gentle way to work through processing trauma.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Embodied practices that move beyond talk therapy are vital to how I help clients move towards healing trauma. Our bodies hold trauma and also hold the keys to our healing. Through somatic interventions, we will get creative in how we can use your own innate resilience to connect with your core self and move toward the best version of you available.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Working with relationships is a unique opportunity to enter the venn diagram where the experiences of two individuals meet. I have experience in work with couples where trauma or mental health concerns are impacting relational function. I utilized EFT, attachment, and interpersonal interventions to help improve communication, connection, and understanding between partners.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: The focus of my practice is trauma processing and supporting clients toward resolving what feels unresolvable. I work with clients with acute, chronic, complex, and systemic/ancestral trauma presentations as well as dissociative/depersonalized presentations and traumagenic personality disorders. Central to my practice is providing a stable, dependable, and compassionate relationship in order to begin the healing process. As Yalom says “it’s the relationship that heals".

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Working with relationships is a unique opportunity to enter the venn diagram where the experiences of two individuals meet. I have experience in work with couples where trauma or mental health concerns are impacting relational function. I see relationship therapy as a unique opportunity to help improve how you function together and work to heal old attachment wounds. I utilize EFT and family systems frameworks to increase your understanding of one another and your emotional experiences.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Do you find yourself in a perpetual cycle of hyper-vigilance, panic, or worry? Feeling keyed up or on edge? Do you worry about how others are perceiving you or have fears that you might be "the problem"? From both a therapist and deeply personal perspective, I understand how difficult day to day can be when you are experiencing anxiety - whether it be a new occurrence or a lifelong struggle. Let's work together to help better unstick those stuck anxious parts trying to help!

name: Jennifer Yamin
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: How you experienced your world early on shapes how you have come to understand the world today.
ideal_client: Whether you are struggling with your life partner, have wounds from your family of origin, or you are trying to find a new sense of who you are, I believe that therapy creates an opportunity for healing in the areas where we need to be seen the most.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I focus on contextual and intergenerational factors that have shaped your relationship with yourself and others. This includes uncovering attachment injuries that may have occurred both in your history and in current relationships. These events from our past often cause us to reenact unhealthy scenarios, in hopes of a different outcome. Using a variety of techniques, including Narrative, Solution- Focused and EMDR, I will help you reframe your story, allowing you to make choices that better serve you. I believe you are asking me to take you somewhere you haven’t yet been. As your guide and companion, we will walk this journey together, but you will get there by your own resiliency and courage.

name: Christina Dunning
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer an authentic therapeutic relationship in which to honestly explore and grow how you relate with yourself and with others

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Using our counseling relationship as a foundation from which to grow and heal, together we can explore patterns of interaction and ways of being, deepen understanding and acceptance of underlying emotions and needs, and help you gain freedom in choosing how to be in the world and with those you love. I work from an attachment and family systems perspective, exploring internal parts (Internal Family Systems) and patterns (both internal and relational). I see counseling as a place to collaboratively explore patterns and roles that were once helpful or necessary, but no longer serve us, and as a place to practice new ways of being and connecting in the present moment. I also see counseling as a place to grow understanding and acceptance of our authentic selves.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Using our counseling relationship as a foundation from which to grow and heal, together we can explore patterns and roles that were once helpful or necessary, but no longer serve you, deepen understanding and acceptance of underlying emotions, values and needs, and help you gain freedom in choosing how to be in the world and with those you love.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Often times, coping skills that were helpful earlier in life become patterned ways of relating. While these can continue to serve us in certain situations, they can also get in the way of connecting meaningfully or can lead to conflict with those we love. In counseling, we can explore those patterns together and develop and practice new ways of relating and connecting.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: So often, the patterns of relating we develop in childhood persist in our adult relationships. This can be particularly apparent in our relationships with family. Counseling offers a place to explore those patterns and a space to develop and practice new ways of relating in a meaningful way as families grow and change.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: In childhood, we often learn that there are parts of us that are acceptable and parts we must keep hidden. We do this because it is necessary for our survival to maintain our relationships with our caregivers. When our caregivers are not able to meet our needs, we can learn to exile them, and to instead tend to the needs of others. In our work together, we can begin to grow awareness of these patterns, to meet them with curiosity and compassion, and to learn new ways of relating to ourselves.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: In our society, women are so often taught to put their needs second and to be warm and consistently pleasant to those around them. While these qualities can sometimes be helpful, they can also trap us in patterns in which we lose track of our needs and disconnect from our authentic selves. Counseling offers a place to reconnect with oneself and explore and practice boundary setting and self care.

name: Heather Mitchell
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: As a compassionate guide that listens to you deeply, I will help you explore those strengths and limitations that make you your unique self.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can lend oneself to feel lonely, isolated and hopeless. With gentleness & acceptance I come alongside this part of your journey to offer comfort and soft tools/ideas for growth and change.

specialities.name: Infertility
specialities.description: For many years I have been working with clients who are experiencing the trials, fears, and potential grief and loss due to infertility and/or miscarriage. This can be a difficult, very isolating experience(s). It can help to have someone safe to talk to and gain support from.

name: Danielle Ropp
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Honored to work with individuals and couples to process life transitions, navigate relationships, and improve health and mental well being.
ideal_client: During your individual therapy session, we will work one-on-one to explore thoughts, feelings, habits and experiences to gain a better understanding of yourself and to develop coping skills to achieve goals and improve your well-being. For Couples, we will work to identify effective ways to repair and improve your relationship, resolve conflicts, learn how to communicate, break negative cycles, heal from betrayal, and increase intimacy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I place a strong emphasis on developing insight and empathy within a non-judgmental and compassionate environment. From a strengths-based perspective, I work to empower clients to gain the skills necessary to address and resolve problems, change behaviors, improve relationships and navigate and cope with stressors.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I earned my master’s degree in social work from Boise State University. I have over 14 years of experience practicing as a nurse and working within social services providing counseling and care coordination to adolescents, adults, and families. My therapeutic background is rooted in medical and health psychology, assisting individuals and families coping with normal or unwanted transitions, chronic illness, end of life issues, and those experiencing symptoms of anxiety and depression. I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker through the Oregon Board of Licensed Social Workers and I am an active member of the National Association of Social Workers (NASW).

name: Brittany Miller
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I believe therapy is a collaborative process, and I am committed to partnering with you to overcome barriers and make meaningful changes.
ideal_client: While most of the people I see struggle with anxiety, depression, stress, life transitions, low self-esteem, I also have specific experience supporting sex workers, veterans and people struggling with symptoms of ADHD. I have lived experience as a queer person, a neurodiverse person and as an adoptee.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The beginning of our work together will be centered around understanding your unique experiences and building a safe, trusting relationship. Whether you’re dealing with stress, anxiety, depression, or simply seeking personal growth, my goal is to provide a compassionate and nonjudgmental space where you can explore your feelings and learn to embrace vulnerability. As we move forward in the therapeutic relationship, we will work to help you break free from any rigid thought patterns or overwhelming emotions that keep you stuck. This will allow you to pursue a more enriching and satisfying life. I specialize in assisting individuals to navigate this process by using evidence-based practices, particularly Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

approaches.More About the People I Treat: Inherent to all these treatments is scientifically validated skill-building. These skills can include mindfulness, self-compassion exercises, and values and goals clarification. Research shows that these practical tools can make a significant difference in your everyday life. I’ll ask you to incorporate these skills outside the therapy room and we’ll work together to find the ones that work for you. I believe that therapy is a collaborative process, and I am committed to partnering with you to overcome barriers and make meaningful changes.

name: Nancy Masters
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: We offer telehealth in OR, WA, AZ, MN, NM, and UT. In-office visits in Clackamas, OR / Layton and Lehi, UT available! Seattle visits soon.
ideal_client: She has more than 10 years of experience and specializes in treating patients with depression, anxiety, ADHD, bipolar and sleep disorders, opioid addiction, as well as patients in the LGBTQIA+ community with care needs related to gender dysphoria/transgender-related mental health care. She treats patients ages 18+ in Oregon and Washington.

approaches.How We Can Help You: Skycloud Mental Health is a clinical placement site for Yale School of Nursing students. We have intake appointments available within a week! We are currently accepting new patients for medication management via telehealth in OR, WA, AZ, UT, MN, and NM, and have a therapy waitlist available on our website. In-person visits available near Portland, OR, with offices in Seattle, WA and Salt Lake City, UT coming soon! Go to skycloudhealth.com and click "Schedule Now" to register for an appointment. Alternatively, you can call (503) 694-3381, extension 2, to register and schedule over the phone. We are available for single-case agreements with Kaiser. Contact our practice for more info.

name: Francis Aurora Otto
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm a Somatic Psychotherapist for people who want more nourishing relationships. I help unwind trauma and reweave the patterns that limit.
ideal_client: I offer an embodied and relational healing process for people seeking more nourishing relationships. Most of our relationship patterns develop as adaptations to early attachment dynamics and trauma. As a body-oriented and attachment-based therapist, I help people change and transform from the inside out. It's change you can feel.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer a gentle and collaborative approach to help heal the deep hurts that hold us back. Each one of us has adapted to our life circumstances as best we can. The patterns we learn are rooted in our early relationships and in our body. These patterns are deep and precede words. Together, I help you attune to, unwind, and rewire these patterns. In each session, I offer simple and effective homework practices to support your healing process. My goal is to help you cultivate more resilience, ease, and wholeness in your relationships and in your life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a 4th generation Portlander who's experienced the city go through a lot of change. I have a Master's Degree from Naropa University in Somatic (Body) Psychology and Movement Therapy. For the past 20 years, I have worked as a counselor and therapist with experience in community-based addictions and mental health treatment. I have also been a performer and child play specialist. Over the past 18 years, I have played with over 20,000 children. This unique perspective and experience has taught me how to heal adults. Along with this, I bring extensive training in Interpersonal Neurobiology (the brain science of relational healing), Body-Mind Centering® (the embodiment of developmental change), Biodynamic Cranial Therapy (a gentle approach to unwinding trauma), and Biomechanics (the science of healthy alignment and movement). My goal is to help you have more nourishing relationships in your life.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Our earliest relationships form the templates for how we interact and what we expect from others. These patterns live in our body and in the ways that we engage with (or avoid) others. Over the past 10 years, I have learned how to recognize and work with individual attachment styles and relationship patterns through my in-depth studies with Bonnie Badenoch, PhD, LMFT.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Somatic refers to the lived experience of the body. Not just having a body, but living in a body. As all our patterns are grounded in our body, we won't just talk about what's going on. Instead, we'll attend to how your body has uniquely adapted to your life. We'll focus on sensations, feelings, and movements in helping you find your greater wholeness.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Just as the patterns that hold you back were wired within your earliest relationships, they only transform when met with gentleness and care. Understanding the neuroscience of relationship can help you understand and transform your challenges.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Our current struggles are often rooted in our earliest attachment relationships. These early patterns live in our body, in how we perceive and interact. By attuning to these patterns in a collaborative and compassionate way, we can learn how to rewire them and discover renewed resilience and ease.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Traumatic experiences are overwhelming and leave lasting impact. The most impactful aspect is feeling alone with what you've gone through. Together, I work to gently meet and attend to what it's been like for you and help to regulate these feelings so they don't take over and derail your life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: The body let's us know how it's doing through feelings of anxiety, fear, and panic. By learning how to attend to and care for these feelings, we can re-pattern how we respond to the circumstances of our life, which are often unpredictable. Empathy and body attunement are the tools we use here.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Having gone through Lyme Disease, I understand the invisible suffering of chronic pain and illness. There is the condition you suffer and the fact that many people do not perceive or believe your experience. I work to support with all aspects of your what you are going through.

name: ALISSA BURNHAM
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi, My name is Alissa, Licensed Clinical Social Worker and Perinatal Mental Health Specialist.
ideal_client: My two specialty areas include perinatal mental health and young adults 18-26 years old. I am a certified perinatal mental health specialist offering support across the perinatal phase including pregnancy, postpartum anxiety and depression. I also offer services to clients struggling with parenting and issues in their primary/family relationship. I have 10+ years of experience working with young adults around anxiety, depression, life transitions, identity, and relationships/family challenges.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach is collaborative, curious, relational and compassionate. I create a non judgmental space for you to explore challenging issues, strengthen inner resources, and learn new skills for moving forward. Through our discussions and evidence-based therapy methods, we will work together to understand your emotions/thoughts, make decisions aligned with your values, and live a more satisfying life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: A central part of my work is holding an anti-oppression framework and examining oppressive social structures including racism, classism, sexism, ableism, heterosexism. This could look like naming micro aggressions in the workplace, internalized capitalism and how it may cause you to label yourself in particular ways. Intersectionality is a core value personal and professional value, understanding how the world perceives and interacts with you and the impact this has.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is one of the most common symptoms I see in my practice. I have found a blend of cognitive behavioral therapy and mindfulness reduce client's anxiety.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: I am a perinatal mental health specialist offering services to across the perinatal phase including pregnancy, postpartum, anxiety, depression, relationship changes, and parenting challenges.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: Parents often come to me with concerns and challenges including depression, anxiety, adjusting to a whole new life, shifts in primary/family relationships, feeling isolated and surprised by how they are feeling and what they are experiencing.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: I have worked with clients looking for support in parenting decisions, concerns around "Am I doing this right?" and considerations around parenting styles based on culture, background, personality, etc. We create a path forward that feels consistent with personal, family values and needs.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Most of my clients at some point in therapy discuss challenges in their primary relationship and/or marriage. We explore needs/values in relationships, attachment styles, and role models as a child to give us a sense of how you may want to move forward and/or what changes you'd like to see.

name: Day Hancock Murphy
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I am a black, trans nonbinary therapist who is here for collaborative, mindful trauma work outside the lens of systemic, colonial mindsets.
ideal_client: Is your relationship going in circles? Do you struggle with what was done to or against you and notice that it sits around your shoulders like a weight? Are you acting in a way that doesn't feel authentic or true to your personhood? I offer deeply relational, systemically-informed counseling for BIPOC and LGBTQ+ community, or anyone who simply feels like an outsider. I primarily see Individuals (16+, elders welcome), Couples,poly folks, and adult-child and parents

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a proud trauma and CSA survivor. Living with the effects of trauma on a daily basis is hard, and it can feel like you're the only person in the world who knows what you're going through. Know that you're not alone, and that I'm here to walk alongside you and help you to build a life that's worth cultivating. My approach to therapy is rooted in empathy, authenticity, and a deep commitment to creating a safe, non-judgmental space. I strongly believe in the power of the therapeutic relationship and work diligently to build trust and rapport with each of my clients. I want you to feel seen, heard, and accepted exactly as you are. You're allowed to curse, cry, yell, and do what you need in the space we create to truly embody and express yourself.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a systems therapist, you can expect that I will ask questions about what you are doing outside of yourself to create a full life as we explore what is currently holding you back. What does your support network look like, how do you create joy, do you have hobbies, if spirituality of any kind is a factor in your life, are you doing enough to fill your cup? How can we make more opportunities to connect and build community? How does your privilege, lack of privilege, existence in a white-dominated society impact you? What in the larger world could be impacting your ability to thrive and build? My current modalities that I use first and foremost are IFS and EMDR as well as Narrative and somatic therapies. As many of my clients experience trauma I find that these are models that are particular useful for healing and that connecting with the body through exercises, yoga, taking walks, guided visualizations, can be particularly helpful and have been a large part of my personal journey.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am EMDR trained with goals of advanced EMDR training in the near future.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I am a Level 1 IFS practicioner who loves to use the work with all forms of trauma, especially intergenerational and historical trauma. Parts work can be a powerful tool in the toolkit for helping to unstick difficult feelings

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: My grad education involved extensive work with couples which I have carried into my personal practice. Much of my caseload features couples, ENM, and polyamorous individuals as well as monogamous couples. Building trust and intimacy, navigating communication struggles, and entering the world of nonmonogamy in particular are areas that I find myself navigating with couples often.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Much of my work with clients is around treating the effects of trauma. Many of my clients are impacted by complex trauma and worsening symptoms due to systemic oppression and racial trauma.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: I find that many of my clients come to the work with a history of trauma that may even go back generationally to impact them.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I love working with members of my own community! Some examples of what we can speak of are, coming out late in life, coming out in stages, simply existing, socializing, and becoming a LGBTQ adult, navigating being a queer teen, the possibilities are endless.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have worked with a variety of polyamorous individuals relationally and individually on issues around overperforming and underperforming at home, stress , lack of intimacy, and rebuilding trust and strenghtening bonds after ruptures.

name: Lee Scher
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I specialize in supporting people with relational trauma, and neurodivergent people (especially adhd, autistic, and bipolar folks).
ideal_client: For many years I've specialized in supporting highly sensitive, creative and spiritually oriented people. In recent years I've realized the overlap between these very positive traits, and neurodivergence, so more recently I've expanded my practice to also focus on people with adhd, autistic and bipolar neurotypes. Throughout my career I've been supporting people with C-PTSD (chronic trauma symptoms) from family trauma.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My approach is deeply informed by Buddhism and Jungian psychology. As I listen to clients I am listening for the core feelings they are expressing and the images that are arising, whether in their dreams or waking life. By reflecting back the feelings and images I hear, I can support them in understanding the journey they're on, what's at stake for them, and how they can act on their own behalf and advocate for themselves in relationships.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: My central inspiration as a therapist is to help people listen more deeply to and trust their own experiences. We are not all the same, and generic advice cannot help you for your own way forward. Your own body/feelings is your most trustworthy source of guidance. My job as a therapist is to support you in listening to and trusting your own experience, as well as in sorting through what you find there.

specialities.name: Contemplative
specialities.description: Contemplative therapy focuses on authentic presence, deep listening and empathy. I show up, make space for you to explore your experience, and share my own genuine responses. Basically, I cultivate an authentic relationship with you, where you have space to listen to your own experience.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I have specialized for several years in working with clients with Autistic neurotypes.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Since beginning practice 16 years ago I've specialized in working with clients with childhood trauma (C-PTSD), caused by childhood neglect and/or abuse.

name: AJA BENNETT
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I'm a compassionate mental health therapist who practices from a trauma informed, culturally responsive perspective.
ideal_client: I specialize in the areas of trauma recovery, including relationship, intergenerational, childhood, medical, and occupational related trauma. I also treat anxiety, PTSD, mood disorders, substance abuse as well as life transitions, grief, divorce, family conflict, stress management, occupational stress, and provide tools to strengthen relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach is compassionate, trauma-informed, and tailored to each individual. I integrate evidence-based techniques such as Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), Solution-Focused Therapy, Narrative Therapy, and Motivational Interviewing to help clients reframe harmful thought patterns, build resilience, and achieve meaningful growth. My approach is nonjudgmental, open-minded, and affirming, ensuring that your experiences and concerns are respected and understood. I strive to create a culturally responsive, inclusive, and safe space for all my clients. My communication style is warm, empathetic, and collaborative. I strive to create a safe, nonjudgmental, and affirming environment where clients feel truly heard and understood. Working with me feels supportive and empowering, as I meet each client where they are and guide them with compassion, respect, and encouragement.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: My journey to becoming a therapist is deeply rooted in my lived experiences as a Black woman navigating life stressors and systemic barriers. Growing up in the Deep South, I witnessed the resilience and strength of my community in the face of adversity, which inspired my passion for mental health and social justice. These experiences shaped my understanding of the importance of culturally responsive, compassionate care. Becoming a therapist has allowed me to turn my challenges into a source of empathy and insight, empowering others to heal, grow, and embrace their authentic selves.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT is a practical, evidence-based approach that helps you understand the connection between your thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. By identifying unhelpful patterns and learning new ways of thinking and responding. Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT) is an evidence-based treatment for PTSD, grounded in (CBT). It helps you identify how trauma has shaped your beliefs about yourself, others, and the world—and supports you in developing healthier ways of thinking and and moving forward.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Narrative Therapy is a collaborative, empowering approach that helps you explore the stories you tell about yourself and your experiences. Often shaped by past events, culture, or relationships, these stories can influence how you see yourself and what you believe is possible. In therapy, we work together to separate you from problems, identify strengths, and create new narratives that align with your values and preferred identity.

specialities.name: Motivational Interviewing
