specialities.description: Motivational Interviewing is a supportive, non-judgmental approach that helps you explore and strengthen your own motivation for change. Instead of telling you what to do, we work together to understand what matters to you, uncover any ambivalence, and build confidence in your ability to take meaningful steps forward. It’s especially helpful when you're feeling stuck, uncertain, or navigating life transitions.

specialities.name: Solution Focused Brief Therapy
specialities.description: Solution-Focused Therapy is a practical, goal-oriented approach that helps you identify what’s working in your life and build on those strengths to create meaningful change. Rather than focusing on problems or the past, this therapy emphasizes your resources, resilience, and vision for the future. Together, we’ll explore small, manageable steps that move you closer to the life you want—starting from where you are right now.

name: Paul Weaver
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Currently accepting new clients for telehealth only at this time. I look forward to working with you!

name: Brittany Schreurs
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi! I am a mother (of two daughters), wife (to an amazing husband), friend, and believer that one person can make a difference.
ideal_client: Life can be hard. School/work/life are not what you thought it would be like. Add on to that relationships, family, friends, and other obligations that just seem to pile up. Tiny little things can become so big...sometimes they become so massive that it feels as though you'll never find your way through! If this sounds like something you've experienced - it doesn't have to be this way. Sometimes speaking with someone, learning new skills, reflecting, and confronting our own thoughts can help!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work with clients who may be struggling with self confidence, self esteem and self worth that can cause anxiety and depression. These often have an impact on our relationships and daily life. Together we can look at how to best use your areas of strength to overcome these obstacles. I will be honest, transparent, understanding, empathetic, but I may also question, confront, and summarize. We are only human, so I may make mistakes. This isn't a one way street, it is a partnership. I will expect you to give feedback, question, and confront, but ultimately feel safe in doing hard work. I am a part of your journey. Only you know what will ultimately work for you in your life. (Who knows you better than you! Am I right?!) We will work together to determine how and why things aren't going as planned and how to get it all back on track so that you can start feeling and living your authentic life.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am a retired educator and born and raised Texan who has traveled and lived all over the world, I have connected with people of different backgrounds, religions, cultures, languages, and values. I have experience working with neurodiverse and marginalized populations and am a passionate ally! And, I would be thrilled to work with you so that you can take steps to live the life of your dreams.

name: Jess Brunelle
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I enjoy working with folks in the LGBTQ+ community of which I am a part of, and anyone of diverse backgrounds and perspectives.
ideal_client: I often work with people who have survived adversity throughout their lives whether it's childhood trauma, mental health, socioeconomic barriers, or societal stressors. I am a relational therapist who looks to create a relationship with my clients of safety and dignity. My clients tell me that they feel seen and heard by me and our collaborative work is meant to provide empowerment and choice. I am skilled at providing support around Autism, ADHD, OCD, sensory sensitivity, depression and C-PTSD.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Are you not feeling seen or heard? Have you been coping the best that you can with depression, anxiety or trauma symptoms, but life is still a struggle? Let me help you on your journey to recovery. There are so many ways to help unique, individual people with their challenges. Each person has different needs and I treat each client with respect, dignity and autonomy. Collaboratively, we can create therapy goals and demystify the process together. I am a client-centered, licensed mental health therapist. I specialize in trauma therapy and working with youth. I have 15 +years experience using various modalities including trauma-informed CBT, DBT, Somatic Experiencing, psychoeducation, and trauma-informed Play and Expressive Arts Therapy. Also, I work with anxiety disorders, OCD and depression. Please take a chance and reach out. I am here to help.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I am involved in the work of helping others. I am dedicated to continuing my own learning and healing journey and I feel that as a community, we are here to support each other in solidarity. I have worked for the LGBTQ+ community, of which I am a part of, for 30 years in various volunteer capacities. I am a non-binary, queer human with parents who are first-generation American. I am passionate about social justice for BIPOC, and the intersectionality between socioeconomic issues, multi-generational trauma, equal rights for all women, and lack of resources for groups of under represented individuals. I have researched and participated in programs aimed at expanding my knowledge about trauma and how it affects us cognitively, emotionally and somatically. Most importantly, learning how to support others as they seek to heal from and thrive with a trauma history. I specialize in neurodivergent challenges, as well as gaining insight around masking and honoring our unique view of the world.

name: Tate Sprite
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: Naropa University, MA Mindfulness-Based Transpersonal Counseling
intro: Are relationships hard? Are people stressful? I specialize in helping you heal your relationship to yourself, others, and the world.
ideal_client: I usually work with self-conscious outsiders, who may even be helpers or leaders, who are stressed out by people or who struggle with boundaries. They want to be free of the intense self-criticism and instead feel belonging and connection. In working with me, they develop a healthy sense of self-compassion, grow empowered to connect with people authentically, and find their voice in the world. -- I may be able to take your insurance. Reach out for details.

approaches.How I Can Help You: My main therapeutic modality is Emotionally Focused Therapy. This attachment-based approach is non-pathologizing: we trust that a person’s inner experience as well as their actions make sense in some way that is trying to help. What has healing power is when you have enough safety in a relationship (e.g. with a therapist) that you can recognize your patterns and befriend your own emotions with compassion. Once you have new, more connected emotional experiences in real time, you start to find a new sense of self. Your capacity to navigate human experience grows. Then you can safely begin to deepen into difficult experiences from the past, to now directly feel and see and integrate them in a new, better, fuller way. Gradually, these changes shape a new story of yourself and your life, and naturally lead to new actions. This approach is known to be helpful across a variety of diagnoses but especially with those facing depression, anxiety, and the effects of trauma.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I may be a great fit if: ~~ you want to do attachment work ~~ you practice mindfulness, or want to start ~~ you want to be more aware of your body or do somatic work ~~ you've exhausted your options with talk therapy ~~ you are right-brained, artistic, holistic, or intuitive ~~ you don't just want new tools and behavioral skills, you want to re-organize your basic operating system for doing life ~~ you're already committed to personal growth or have done a lot of work on yourself ****** My special affiliations: ~~ born and raised outside the US ~~ dysfunctional family ~~ spiritual seeker from when I was a kid ~~ lived through the violent fall of communism ~~ spent many years in a cult ~~ highly intelligent and highly sensitive ~~ am queer in a number of ways

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Overall, I describe my approach as attachment-based, trauma-informed, mindful, somatic, compassion-focused, experiential and existential. While I draw on my study of the modalities listed below (and some that weren't on the list), my main model is Emotionally Focused Therapy. It centers relationship and emotional experience. I'm pursuing certification in Emotionally Focused Therapy for individuals (EFIT) and receive regular supervision and training by certified EFT supervisors.

specialities.name: Social Phobia
specialities.description: I work especially with people who experience this sometimes paralyzing fear of being seen by others. I mainly support them to develop self-compassion, put their inner critic in its proper place, learn mindfulness and somatic awareness, participate in new and positive experiences of relationship, hold their right boundaries, know who they are, connect to their voice, take safe risks, and be authentic. In working with me, they develop a new relationship to themselves, others, and the world.

name: Kelly Aldinger
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Appointments available within 1-2 weeks. I'm passionate about helping people access their own strengths through medication and therapy.
ideal_client: I am honored to meet you, wherever you are. I treat most mental health issues, and have special clinical interest in working with young adults with mood disorders, relationship/attachment issues, & OCD. I genuinely enjoy working with folx who are LGBTQ, who are struggling with low self-esteem, and who are motivated to make big shifts to what's not working for them. I welcome all 18-40.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: **TO START SERVICES, COMPLETE THE NEW PATIENT REQUEST FORM at www.upwellpsych.com/contact** Aloha! I'm a doctor of nursing practice who is passionate about helping people access their own strengths. I am committed to walking beside you as you gain insight, learn new skills, and grow the self-belief to create the life you want to live. I firmly believe that one path does not fit all, and my life is evidence of that. I worked as a therapist prior to becoming a PMHNP, and bring a diverse set of professional, educational and life experience to each session. Using empathy and authenticity, my goal is to help you find and live your own truth.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I've grew up in Hawai'i, and that spirit of aloha pervades my ethos in life. After growing up on a small island, I spread my wings and have lived on 5 continents and speak a bit of Spanish, French, and Woolof. You can often find me listening to the latest psychiatry/psychology podcast, reading books in the hammock, or suiting up to surf Oregon's cold coastal waters.

name: Cameron Donley
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Specializing in early adulthood / quarterlife, helping individuals find and navigate their paths in life.
ideal_client: I tend to be a good fit for those who: • Are feeling overwhelmed or dehumanized by modern life • Were raised in growth-limiting environments (judgmental family/religious systems, abusive/controlling parenting styles) • Were parentified as children • Are struggling with shame or anxiety • Have unresolved trauma • Are feeling confusion about what they want from their lives • Have more than one cultural identity • Are looking to feel more whole and live a more authentic existence

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My goal as a therapist is to support your individual freedom - to help you become more fully yourself. I see you as an individual with your own unique experience and story, and your own path towards growth and healing. As a result, I do not have a "cookie cutter" approach to therapy. Instead, I blend several different approaches in my work to meet you where you are at and support you in your process. I am a trauma-informed therapist, and I implement a blend of EMDR, somatic work, mindfulness, and internal family systems/parts work to help clients process their trauma and unwind distressing patterns.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a Jungian lens, and my therapeutic perspective is deeply informed by feminism, social justice, and liberation psychology. My understanding of quarterlife is heavily influenced by the work of Satya Doyle Byock (who views quarterlife as a developmental stage of adulthood). My therapeutic approach is whole-hearted, fully engaged, and collaborative. My intention is to honor your path, and create a safe space in which you can be more fully yourself.

name: Skyler Johnston
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome! I assist youth, adults and families to navigate difficult times, process past traumas and improve overall well being.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have undergone numerous trainings in trauma focused cognitive behavioral therapy (TF-CBT) and collaborative problem solving (CPS) and meet with a consultant weekly to ensure model fidelity. I’ve found these to be extremely helpful tools but of course everyone is different. For that reason, I work to adapt a unique approach depending on the client’s wants and needs. In general, I try to build a strong genuine relationship where people can feel safe and understood.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a Master of Arts in Counseling Psychology from Lewis and Clark College. My undergraduate work was in psychology and creative writing and I have been passionate about personal development and mentorship for over twelve years. I have five years’ experience working with individuals across a wide spectrum of presenting concerns. My practice is further backed by extensive academic study of counseling theories, trauma informed care, psychopharmacology, couples counseling and substance abuse.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: Coaching allows one to bring about positive changes in their life more quickly and efficiently than they might on their own. Coaching makes use of collaborative goal formation, problem solving and accountability.

name: Sally Van Meter
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm a Licensed Professional Counselor with nearly 4 decades of experience. I have openings for new individual clients age 18 and up.
ideal_client: If you're feeling stuck, challenged, frustrated, repeating patterns that no longer serve you and do not know how to live your best life, let's work through these things together. If you're not sure of your goals or what is preventing you from moving forward that is a fine place to start or continue on your path to change and healing. Life can present us with many surprises including anxiety, trauma, depression, aging, illness, grief and loss. These are all so human. Healing is possible.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I understand that our world has chaos and many challenges. With more than 35 years of practice, I know personally and professionally that change and healing are possible and I also understand that can be hard to trust. I invite you to gently step in and find comfort at a pace that works for you. I serve as a support and guide in helping you in healing your challenges with anxiety, depression, trauma and other mood and relational disorders. My approach is supportive, client centered, culturally aware, and strength based with a mind/body/spiritual approach. I work with you on what is most important to you and how you want to live your life. I employ treatment modalities matching your needs; accepted for a Level I IFS training, am IFS Informed, CBT, Trauma informed, 6 week Psychedelic Therapy and Integration Certificate, enrolled in Advanced Training, and approach healing with helping you experience the parts of you that are clouding your unique and whole Self.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I was an unhappy teen, as my father's Post WWII PTSD erupted untreated, and although creative and playful, I knew something was terrible unsettled in me. My family was a hotbed of conflict, drama, secrets, substance abuse and violence. Through mentors, education and personal therapy the SELF in me that I believe we are all born with and that it is whole and intact underneath our traumas and symptoms, began to shine and I found a career that was all about focusing on what is authentic and true for each individual and frequently gets squashed early in life. I have deep intuition and sense when others are not ok with what is going on for them and maintained that intuition and desire to find out what could be done about this, for myself and my clients and after some 4 decades, this is still true. I have personal and professional experience that I bring to my clients that yes, you too can change and heal and ultimately, that is inside of you.

name: Jordan Karr
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: I offer evidence-based and compassionate care for individual adults and youth.
ideal_client: I work with clients experiencing a variety of concerns, including day-to-day stressors, anxiety, depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and more.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I strive to create a comfortable and safe atmosphere for each of my clients. I have a warm and compassionate personality, as well as a strong sense of humor that will help us connect along the way. My clinical approach draws on Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT). Together, we'll explore what behaviors and thoughts support or hinder your efforts to move closer to your values. Along the way, you will learn to navigate difficult emotions and painful thoughts with greater mindfulness, acceptance, and self-compassion.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe change and healing is best inspired by connecting with what matters most to you, whether that be friendship, family, safety, nature, or whatever else! It's our values that drive our best actions and help us face life with resilience. I care deeply about human rights, diversity, nature, and compassion so these values show up in my work with clients. Together, we may examine how societal factors drive many of the mental health issues of today, how to connect with nature in a way that enhances mindfulness and activates awe, and how to maximize compassion in our relationships and self-talk.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Are you feeling overwhelmed by stress, worry, panic, or self-criticism? I specialize in using ACT and CBT to support folks struggling with generalized anxiety, perfectionism, phobias, social anxiety, panic, health anxiety, and harsh self-criticism.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: Do you struggle with unwanted thoughts or fears, overthinking, rumination, or time-consuming compulsions? I specialize in using ACT, CBT, and Exposure and Response Prevention to support folks struggling with OCD.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Are you feeling overwhelmed with sadness, hopelessness or feelings of worthlessness? Are you struggling to feel interested, motivated, or inspired? I can help! I use evidence-based approaches like ACT and CBT to support clients with depression.

name: Tim Perez
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Hi, My name is Tim Perez and I would like to help you realize the absolute value that resides within your core!
ideal_client: I see school-aged children, teens and adults who struggle with ADHD, depression, bipolar disorder and other mood-related disorders; OCD, PTSD, general anxiety and other anxiety-related disorders; sleep disorders; schizophrenia and other psychosis-related disorders.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Mental Illness has a way of making us feel devalued. My focus is to help you rediscover, restore, and retain your sense of individual value or worth. I primarily offer medication management therapies coupled with talk therapy and an ongoing emphasis on education into my patients' conditions. I find that many who come see me may have a history of being treated for a mental health condition without achieving satisfactory relief. I will take my time with you, listen, and seek your buy-in before WE determine the direction of YOUR treatment. I may use medical, psychological, logical, religious and spiritual approaches to help with your concerns, which ever you feel helps you the most.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I feel strongly that all people have value and worth that is intrinsic and not defined by the whims, rants, and ideas of the multiple opinions around us. Our worth is like the sun, it is always shining bright and is extremely powerful. So are we. I believe that much of our mental illness issues come from our lack of realizing who we really are. Mental health and stability comes when we are enlightened to our own personal worth and value and that we must all accept ourselves first, before we truly have the capacity to help, love and serve others. Yes, offenses and anxieties will come; they are all around us. But realizing who we really are and treating ourselves with love and respect first, will give us the power to help those around us. Let's meet and see if we can explore together your absolute value! After all, your worth is as bright as the sun :)

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: As a Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner, medication management and expertise is a core part of my training and practice. Since not all therapists are able to utilize medication therapy, I felt that it is important for me to at least consider (but not always implement), medications as AN option for mental health. Medications may help some of my patients do their own internal work that is essential for healthy change. But medications alone are not sufficient, only a help for real change.

name: Alison Jones
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My approach is holistic and affirming, and guided by an anti-oppression, pro-liberation lens.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I believe we are all born with the innate capacity to be connected to our feelings and needs, without judgement or shame. Experiences in life, and sociocultural messages, all inform and influence our understanding of ourselves, our feelings of worthiness, and our connection with these deeper parts of ourselves. Sometimes, in experiences of trauma or prolonged stress, we develop ways of existing and coping that are necessary for our survival, but over time may no longer be needed, and can decrease feelings of connection, with self & others. You are not broken, you were born with innate wisdom, and therapy can support the process of reconnecting with the insight that is your birthright. Therapy can be supportive of quieting the noise, sinking into this deeper inner knowing, and support living a life rooted in authenticity, self-trust and self-compassion.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have over a decade of experience working with individuals impacted by a broad spectrum of lived experiences, including trauma, depression and anxiety, who also experienced impact by systems and oppression. My theoretical orientation is most often more holistic and fluid to meet your goals and areas of interest or focus, and highly informed by utilizing an anti-oppression, pro-liberation lens, rooted in liberation psychology, intersectional feminist theory, systems theory and humanistic psychology. My clinical lens is trauma and racial justice informed, strengths based, and responsive to supporting you at all stages of life. I also have interest in all mindfulness-based approaches, as well as Eastern philosophy, and my theoretical orientation and perspective is also influenced by the brilliant work of Pema Chodron, bell hooks and Angela Davis.

name: Ren Fonbuena
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Ren's work is rooted in the belief of the inherent worth and respect for all persons.
ideal_client: Ren is currently a CSWA while pursuing her LCSW. She is working toward her Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor hours. Ren works with people seeking help for a variety of struggles including those seeking treatment for: Addictions Anxiety Bipolar Chronic Illness Depression

approaches.My Background and Approach: Ren is passionate about working with people to live their best life possible. She identifies as queer and a part of the LGBTQ+ community and works to be an inclusive therapist including being a poly and kink positive clinician. Rens work is rooted in the belief of the inherent worth and respect for all persons. Ren started at community college and went on to earn a Bachelors of Liberal Studies for California State University Stanislaus. After teaching elementary and English as a forgein language, Ren went back to school for her Masters of Social Work from Walden University. She has worked in a variety of settings in social work and counseling.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Ren is a newcomer to Oregon (2020) and has embraced the Pacific Northwest lifestyle. When not playing with her three dogs, she is usually reading Jane Austen fanfic or playing Dungeons and Dragons with her spouse.

name: Emily Stasko
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: We will work to create a brave space for you to explore what is and isn’t working in your life and how you want things to be different.
ideal_client: I specialize in evidence-based treatments for trauma, anxiety and distress related to health and fertility issues. My specialty areas include interpersonal & combat-related trauma, perinatal mood & anxiety disorders, and coping with chronic & new health diagnoses. I have interest and experience working with Veterans and LGBTQ+ individuals. I also work with depression and anxiety related to life changes, challenges with sex & sexuality (especially as impacted by trauma), and stress management.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My overarching goal as a therapist is to help you do more of the things you want to in your life, despite the pain and distress that you may experience. Regardless of the type of work we are doing, the context of your life and your values are key to helping you meet your goals. For individuals processing past trauma, this means focusing on what you would like to be doing if the trauma took up less space in your life. For those who are struggling with chronic or new health diagnoses, this means looking at how you understand your health conditions and how to live a meaningful life despite them. The annoying truth is that we often can’t change the source of your distress- we cannot change the past, erase past traumas, or undo reality. We can however help you change your perspective, build skills to cope with your realities, and invest in your version of a meaningful life. You are the expert on your life. For therapy to be effective, it is essential you feel seen and understood.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: We are all shaped by the worlds we live in- by our communities, our experiences, and our identities. As someone who has moved frequently (first as a military brat and later by choice), I learned early on that my experiences were not always the same as those around me. This has given me both awareness and a particular interest in understanding how people navigate the changes involved in starting over- whether that is in a new place, a new job, or new relationships. As someone who has also managed chronic health conditions since I was young, I have first-hand knowledge of what it can be like to navigate life with visible and at times restrictive health issues. My experiences have shaped me as a therapist and helped me deepen my connection with clients. I strive to be authentic and self-aware and pay keen attention to how my life experiences may be impacting my understanding of you and our relationship. I approach each client with compassion and without judgement.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I provide these orientations: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, CBT (e.g., Cognitive Processing Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Conjoint Therapy for PTSD, CBT for Insomnia), Integrative Behavioral Couples Therapy, Exposure Therapy, Liberation Psychology, LGBTQ Psychology and Queer Theory

name: Nadine Luensman
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Trauma and eating disorder therapist for Washington and Oregon
ideal_client: If you are seeking help with trauma, struggles with food, your body, or anything in between, there are options other than what we have been taught. Our culture and our world often create an environment for people that encourages self denial. A wide variety of traumas often leave people with chronic feelings of fear, trouble with sleep, relationship distress, and dependence on something that might harm them.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am passionate about growing self-compassion and acceptance in my clients. I have years of experienced working with people using Health and Every Size and trauma informed care. My goal is to guide my clients into paradigm shifts that lead to healing and a more fulfilled life.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My number one values as a therapist are empowerment and autonomy. These values of guide me to work with my client in a way that emboldens their personal intuition to find healing that feels best to them. This usually includes work on self-discovery, self compassion, emotional regulation, and support through small and large life changes. I am especially passionate about walking alongside people from the LGBTQI+ community, promoting body size equality, and helping people who suffer from suicidal thoughts.

name: Peter King
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I believe that each individual's life is unique, and I approach counseling with respect for your personal experiences, values, and beliefs.
ideal_client: I work with individuals facing depression, anxiety, trauma, life transitions, and men’s issues, offering a compassionate, tailored approach. My work integrates Existential Therapy, Attachment Theory, and Ecotherapy, helping clients explore the connections between emotional well-being and the world around them. Whether you’re navigating PTSD, complex-PTSD, or simply seeking growth, I provide support through your journey with a focus on self-awareness and healing through relationships and nature.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I’m a Professional Counselor Associate with a Master’s degree in Professional Mental Health Counseling and a Certificate in Ecotherapy from Lewis & Clark Graduate School of Education and Counseling. I also hold a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology from Portland State University. My clinical work focuses on depression, anxiety, trauma (including PTSD and complex-PTSD), life transitions, career success, and men’s issues. I work with children (ages 10+), adolescents, and adults, tailoring my approach to each individual’s unique needs. I integrate Existential Therapy, Attachment Theory, and Ecotherapy in my practice, helping clients explore the connections between their emotional well-being and the world around them. This holistic, client-centered approach emphasizes healing through relationships and our connection to nature. I believe that understanding the interplay between personal struggles and external relationships is key to emotional growth and healing.

name: Cheryl GreatHouse
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Avid traveler, sailor, cat mom AND counselor. Experiencer of cultures & respecter of differences. Army veteran (1991-1994).
ideal_client: The poet Rumi said, "What you are seeking is seeking you". You are here, on this page, because you are seeking some sort of healing. It's here, waiting for you. Are you tired of feeling triggered? Are you fed up with trying to fit in? Are you ready and willing to cultivate healthier relationships, tap into your true nature, follow your own path, and embrace a more joyful existence? It is time to level up your world, and this is where the journey begins!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer you a strengths-based, compassionate environment for you to face what you've endured while dismantling the painful core beliefs that developed with those traumas. Using methods such as CBT, Narrative, and Acceptance and Commitment therapies, along with EMDR, you will find your way back to your center, and gain a sense of peace with your past.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: There is a new culture emerging. A culture that openly and collectively challenges the way of antiquated convention. With it comes optimism and a sense of community for an older generation that was coerced into repressing their unique views, beliefs, and actions so they might fit in. Now there is an opportunity to empower those courageous enough to be on the front lines of a revolution that calls for being unapologetically authentic. As I have found my way through this complex, often scary, experience of living a life less ordinary I have also discovered other sojourners who’ve offered up tools, guidance, & support. With this community at my side, I have been empowered to follow the direction of my personal truth. The result of this has found me in the midst of a more exciting, fulfilling, and inspired life. This is my wish for you!

name: Ryan Dawson
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a licensed clinical social worker (LCSW) based in Portland Oregon. I have been practicing since 2007 and work with adults and couples.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) based in Portland Oregon and have thirteen years experience working with people who struggle with symptoms of mental illness, alcohol and drug use, family and relationship troubles, chronic illness, complications of grief & loss, and other life challenging situations. I have a Masters of Social Work with a Minor in Mental Health & Chemical Dependency from Eastern Michigan University with expertise using Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT), Mindfulness practice and Motivational Interviewing (MI) to help clients work through difficult issues and to produce change. When working with clients, I believe it’s essential to develop a solid connection using a person-centered approach, meeting someone where they’re at, and providing a compassionate, honest and safe place to discuss what’s going on in their life.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I was introduced to a counselor when I was in high school that impacted my life and helped me get through a very difficult time. Learning the attributes of healthy relationships, developing coping skills, and learning how to evaluate my decisions dynamically affected the course of my life and eventually led me to pursue a career helping others.

name: Sitting by the Well Psychotherapy, LLC Ardiana Halilaj
full_name: Sitting by the Well Psychotherapy, LLC Ardiana Halilaj
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome! My approach to therapy is relational and depth focused!
ideal_client: We all need a trusted and caring companion when facing our most difficult moments in life. The therapeutic process has the potential to become a sacred place where we meet, re-connect with and befriend our own inner parts and companions, be they challenging or empowering on our ever-unfolding soul journey. It is always a privilege and honour for me to BE in that space with my clients, walking alongside them as they are being held and challenged in the deep care of our therapeutic relationship.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a bicultural person who has lived most of her life in a country that is different from where I was born and raised. This gives me a unique perspective and approach to therapy. I relate to and deeply value the 'in between' spaces that we all live in throughout most of our life. This is the space where we meet the exiled parts of us that yearn to reunite with the whole. Holding the tension of these opposite realities in our bodies and minds, can be unbearably difficult, feeling stuck, torn and suffering deeply. As a result, we develop harmful ways of coping that perpetuate a behavioral pattern that can be wounding to our self and others. Often these patterns are encouraged by the culture and/or family we grew up in, and sometimes they were even helpful to us. And yet, if we can find other ways to be with our bodies and our inner suffering tremendous healing may occur. We may learn effective ways to harness wisdom in a way that propels us towards living more fully.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is person and relationship centered, collaborative and to deeply attune to bring your strength and inner wisdom to utilize in our therapeutic process and your growth. It's my belief that depression, anxiety, addiction and other symptoms show up to initiate us on this journey of healing. My depth oriented psychological approach with a focus on embodied feeling will enable us to take a deeper dive into the issues that bring you to therapy, by looking beneath the surface of symptoms, and toward the root of suffering. Together we will explore and try practical approaches to closely pay attention to your body's sensations, feelings, beliefs, images, dreams, actions and other aspects of your inner world. The more you learn about yourself in a non-judgmental way, you may develop more agency over some life choices and relate to yourself with increased compassion. This deeper connection with yourself can lead to relating to others in also, a deeper and more effective way.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: Theoretically I draw from depth and Jungian psychology, psychodynamic, attachment and system's approaches. This simply means that in our work together, I pay attention to and integrate information that rises from the unconscious through your dreams and images, your body's sensations, creative instinct, as well as more conscious realities such as your thoughts, beliefs, feelings, actions, relationships and other important practicalities of life. This approach tends to be more enriching to you.

name: Family Ties Counseling Center
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We help couples and families thrive. Our therapists work with children, teens, and their families. We welcome individual adults as well.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our skilled therapists have been trained and practiced in family-systems. A family-systems approach seeks to avoid blaming or diagnosing any one person because problems are seen as the result of the relationship dynamics within the system. We also have chosen our experienced therapists with great care. The therapists at Family Ties Counseling Center know a lot about how to be in relationship. Just as important as their education and training is their capacity to be authentic, compassionate and insightful. Collectively, we have over several decades of experience working extensively with adults and children, families and relationships.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: We have clearly observed some common values held by those who were helped the most. If you connect with our values listed below, then you will most likely benefit from our approach at Family Ties Counseling Center: Inclusion Truth Prioritizing Closeness & Connection Open to Change Good Enough Parenting Willing to Get Help Strive for Love & Respect

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Couples Counseling becomes a safe place where both you and your partner can find and rest in the deeper connection of the love you both share. Healthy committed relationships and marriages are about balancing connection & intimacy with independence & autonomy. Ideally, each influences and helps the other. Couples therapy helps to achieve this balance in your relationship.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Using mindfulness with counseling, habitual feelings and thoughts become the focus of awareness. Mindfulness, when applied skillfully, can help slow down the process of therapy to a pace that feels safe, lowering noise and increasing inner sensitivity and insight potential.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: Family systems sees your presented marital, family or even child's problems as the outgrowth of the underlying relationship dynamics. This is illuminating because family systems avoids blaming or diagnosing any one person as THE problem. As you are probably well aware of, there is already too much blaming already going in the first place.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: When relationships within a family are strained, parents are powerful leaders to bring their family to a place of harmony. Parents will be the leader in this process because adult brains is more developed, more adept and stronger. You have greater skills (even if sometimes you don’t feel like it).

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: When addressing family conflict, it can be helpful to get most or all family members for a session to work toward a common goal. Because each family member is impacted by family events, each member can contribute unique ideas about how to address the challenges. In your first session, your counselor will assess your particular family situation and then formulate a plan to meet the goals.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Your kids are held up and nurtured by many different relationships. From siblings, to parents, to grandparents, to friend, and teachers, your child thrives when they are connected to many safe and caring people. When your child experiences a difficulty, they need a therapeutic approach that takes into account their most essential relationships.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationship Counseling becomes a safe place where both you and your partner(s) can find and rest in the deeper connection of the love you all share. Healthy committed relationships are about balancing connection & intimacy with independence & autonomy. Ideally, each influences and helps the other. Relationship therapy helps to achieve this balance in your relationship.

name: Darin Bergen
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I'm a licensed psychologist specializing in helping individuals overcome depression, past traumas, and helping people recover from divorce.
ideal_client: Do you just want to feel better? Feeling overwhelmed by painful emotions, or feeling numb, empty and robotic as you go about your life? Maybe you have both - you feel like you're going through the motions with little to look forward to, and then you have painful feelings that overwhelm you out of nowhere. Most people I work with also struggle with feeling alone - regardless of whether they are surrounded by people or not.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We will work directly with your emotions. I will help you learn to navigate your feelings effectively, learning how to get beyond feeling "nothing" and increasing your capacity so painful feelings no longer overwhelm. We will heal the old emotional wounds that cause you so much pain. You will not be alone in this work, I will be there every step of the way. As much as I believe in the transformation that happens in therapy, I know that you don't have to go through it alone. I show up fully and help build a connected relationship so that I can help carry the burden, and you don't have to do it on your own. Last, therapy with me will be active and focused. Our work happens together and transformation happens in the therapy session. I won't be just telling you things and expecting you to go home and practice techniques. I won't sit quietly in the background. This isn't an intellectual exercise. We do the work together.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in you. I believe in people. I believe much of our suffering comes from feeling alone with very painful emotions that we didn't know what to do with. I believe that as a result, we tried to find ways to make ourselves feel better and unfortunately those patterns can lead to more pain later on. I believe that while we all have a worst version of ourself, activated by suffering, we also have a best version of ourself - and therapy should help you live that version of yourself. I believe in you. Beyond the small world of therapy, I recognize that there are systems of power that function to repress people. I know that those people, living in oppression, have been blamed for their own suffering. I will not perpetuate this. I recognize my privilege because I have nearly every privilege. I stand as an ally to those who are oppressed. I am committed to doing the work of undoing my own internalized biases and prejudices, and playing my part in dismantling systems of power.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: My primary approach is Accelerated Experiential Dynamic Psychotherapy (AEDP). This is a newer approach to therapy that focuses on the transformation of painful emotions, and this healing is done in relationship. We believe that painful aloneness is core to the experience of human suffering and undoing that aloneness is a main focus of the therapy. I believe in this approach because of the science, but also because it is the kind of therapy I have found most helpful for me, as a client.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: My Emotion-Focused Therapy (for individuals) training has roots in the beginning of graduate school and it helps with the processing of emotional problems and healing old wounds. EFT has a strong basis in the science of emotion and therapeutic change. I have completed the Level 1 and Level 2 Emotion-Focused Therapy training with Les Greenberg.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: My background in ACT shows up when I help people connect with what they value most and how to live those values in their daily life. I have participated in extensive training in ACT over the years. I am a past President of the Oregon chapter of the Association for Contextual and Behavioral Sciences (OACBS), the international organization for ACT practitioners.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Surviving trauma has long lasting effects and most people don't realize how treatable it is. We have a number of effective treatments and I am passionate about helping people recover! I start with a stabilization phase where you learn techniques to regulate emotions, improve relationships and re-engage in life. I then offer reprocessing therapies that can help you leave the past in the past.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is so painful because it affects so many areas of life - often covering everything with a sense of emptiness and making normal tasks so tough. I work on helping you access the emotions underneath the numbing, so you can begin to re-engage in vital living. We also spend time healing longstanding woundings that caused the pain in the first place.

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: Divorce is one of the most stressful events a person can experience. I know because I've been through it. Because of that, I'm passionate about helping people through the divorce and finding healing. On the other side is a happy life - I know because I've seen it so many times. I typically start by processing the pain and loss of divorce before focusing on building a new life that you love.

name: Charlene McCleoud
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Welcome! I am a Licensed Clinical Social worker in Oregon. I specialize in providing cultural sensitive services within the BIPOC community.
ideal_client: Are you experiencing challenges with depression, stress, anxiety, racial discrimination/racial trauma, relationship issues, parenting concerns, or family conflict? Do you find it difficult to engage fully with others because of these concerns? Are they impacting your daily life and overall well-being? Are you seeking support and empowerment to create a change? Are you looking for cultural specific services? Do you need help identifying/ prioritizing what you’re experiencing?

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have gained collective knowledge and skills to provide the best service possible to individuals with mental illnesses. The tools that I'll provide I have been perfecting throughout my career. I will utilize and share these tools and techniques to assist individuals like yourself face the challenges you may be experiencing within this present moment. I am a cognitive behavioral and solution-focused therapist. I recognized the benefit of these tools and how they will positively impact your life. We will work collaboratively to address the difficulties that are bothering you. We will work towards gaining control over your body and thoughts that may be self-limiting now. I have assisted individuals within the BIPOC community. My experience is focused on trauma, recognizing culture as essential to successful engagement and treatment, and mental health issues with adults.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe therapy is about gaining insight into your true self. Many of us navigate this thing we call life expecting no challenges, fear, or worry. These aspects are constantly a part of our life, and we carry the inner power to face the difficulties we may experience. It's up to you to identify and unlock your inner strength and acceptance through therapy. Recognizing most of the work is completed between our sessions and outside of treatment. As your therapist, I serve as a facilitator throughout your healing process. It's up to you to take that first step, towards the direction you have envisioned for your life. Healing is a process and can happen in many ways. I enter this field with a non-judgmental and open mind. The client is the expert in their situation and holds the solution to their healing. I work in a collaborative environment and believe individuals should be involved throughout their treatment process. My work is built on empathy, respect, compassion, and empowerment.

name: Genevieve Cleverley
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I hope to work together to co-create a therapeutic space where you feel safe and heard while sharing your story!
ideal_client: I have experience working with a adults and teens with a variety of concerns, including anxiety, depression, adjustment/life transitions, childhood trauma, relationship issues, ADHD and more. I have enjoyed working with many clients from diverse cultural and economic backgrounds and acknowledge the impact of power and oppression on mental well-being and treatment. I am queer, trans, and poly/kink affirming and committed to social and racial justice.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: By working together we can address your concerns and explore creative ways to make change while acknowledging your inherent strengths and resilience. My approach is eclectic and trauma-informed. I incorporate interventions from modalities including narrative therapy, Internal Family Systems, and ACT in treatment. As a person-centered therapist, I believe it is necessary to be collaborative and transparent in planning treatment. I enjoy helping clients find unconventional ways to incorporate art, music, and other forms of creative expression into their healing journey.

name: Anastasia Zankowsky
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: **Immediate Availability** Helping couples & individuals find clarity, healing, & security.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that self awareness and connection can heal. My practice is a place where we can build safety and vulnerability, and work together to help you better understand yourself and your distress. I can help you find clarity, maintain healthy relationships, & live more intentionally, whether you are ready to dive into the deep end, or you are just treading water in your day-to-day. My practice has at its foundation an awareness of systemic oppression; I understand that we do not exist in a vacuum, and healing ourselves and coping with the challenges in our lives requires acknowledging and working against the systems of oppression that contribute to them. I work through a framework that is relational and strengths-based, and is LGBQA, trans, poly, and kink affirmative. Therapy is not always easy, but here you can regain a sense of control and create momentum. Let's connect to discuss what you need and how I can help you.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am a white, queer, jewish, currently non-disabled therapist who is committed to anti-oppression work in and outside of the therapy room. I am a palliative care trained clinician (meaning I work with people who have serious illness, and/or their families, from diagnosis onward to cope with the trauma and existential crises related to illness), have worked in hospital systems and cancer centers, and have trained in couples and family therapy at the Ackerman Institute in New York City. I work through a framework that is relational and strengths-based, and is LGBQA, trans, poly, and kink affirmative. I help those are who are managing: Grief & loss Anxiety & Depression Trauma & PTSD LGBTQIA sexuality or gender identity (incl. trans, non-binary, & GNC identities) Poly, kink, or sex work dynamics Relationship, couple, & family conflict Healthcare burnout

name: Douglas Counseling
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Douglas Counseling is all about relationships. We specializes in couples counseling working with couples and individuals.
ideal_client: If you've been stuck feeling too much conflict and not enough connection we can help. Dealing with relationships is challenging and most couples struggle to make lasting changes on their own. If you have been thinking about starting couples counseling to work on your relationship we

approaches.Our Background and Approach: Our therapists have extensive training working with couples and relationships. We use a variety of therapy models to help our clients including Relational Life Therapy (RLT), Emotionally Focused Couples Therapy (EFT), Gottman Method, and many others. Our therapists on staff have years of experience helping couples and individuals navigate challenges in their relationships and lives. Our practice also has sub-specialties in the areas of affair recovery, men's issues, and women's issues. We have licensed therapists including Licensed Professional Counselors, Licensed Marriage and Family Therapists, and Licensed Clinical Social Workers.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: At Douglas Counseling we believe that all clients are capable of making lasting changes to positively impact their lives. We believe that each person has the capacity to gain insights, change thoughts, manage feelings, gain skills, and create a happy and healthy life. Our values include approaching each client with acceptance and understanding. We strive to create a safe and non-judgmental environment for our clients to share their experiences and challenges.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Our couple's therapists have years of experience and countless hours of training in helping couples build happier and healthier bonds. Our therapists have advanced training in popular relationship models including RLT, EFT, Gottman Method, solution-focused therapy, discernment counseling, and many others.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: Douglas Counseling has been working with and specializing in men's issues for over a decade. We have developed tried and trusted methods for helping men gain valuable insights, change harmful thinking, and develop practical skills that lead to lasting change. Areas we address in men's issues include relationship struggles, dealing with stress, working with anger, parenting challenges, finding balance in life, navigating family issues, and improving self-esteem.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: Douglas Counseling has a specialty in working with women's issues. We work with women to help them uncover the core issues behind the challenges they face. Common areas of focus with women include improving boundaries, empowerment, achieving healthy self-esteem, managing caretaking roles, finding equity in relationships, and learning to speak out from an assertive place.

name: Misty Bottorff
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I believe that everyone has the ability to lead their best life and my approach to therapy is a collaborative and strengths-based one.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with diverse populations and providing a safe place for all. I am trauma-informed and come from a strengths-based approach, using a variety of modalities including Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), dialectical behavioral therapy (DBT), and solution-focused therapy. I am honored to work with individuals who trust me with their stories and enjoy walking alongside my clients as they go through the therapeutic process.

approaches.My Background: I graduated with my master’s degree in social work in 2014 from the University of Kansas then went on to earn my clinical licensure. I also hold a graduate certificate from Portland State University in Infant/Toddler Mental Health. I am passionate about helping others and have several years of experience working with children, adolescents, families, and the perinatal population. My experiences include working in community mental health, short-term crisis stabilization, group practice, and the healthcare setting. I was born and raised in the Pacific Northwest and after a brief stint in Kansas, moved back to Oregon in 2017. When I am not working, I enjoy spending time in nature with my partner, live music, video games, camping, and spending time with family and friends. I also have an amazing daughter and daughter-in-law. I am a huge animal lover and have a rescue French Bulldog named Poppy and grumpy rescue cat named Max!

name: Jenna Atwood-Tarczon
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I approach therapy through an Intersectional Feminist lens. I view healing as collective empowerment and a collaborative process.
ideal_client: The work I do is often focused on supporting folks with chronic illness and disabilities and those facing life transitions. Many of my clients are seeking support in career transition and workplace stress and oppression. My clients generally come to me seeking to build confidence, improve self-esteem, and regain their inner power.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I specialize in empowering individuals to embrace their inner strengths and build confidence amidst life’s many changes and challenges. As a dedicated mental health and career counselor, I am passionate about helping clients redefine their paths with positivity and purpose. As your counselor, we'll engage in a collaborative process wherein you are the expert of your own lived experience and I am a guide and comrade in your healing journey. I have 13 years of experience in the field of rehabilitation including mental health, physical disability, and vocational rehabilitation. I have specialized training in career counseling and assessment as well as disability justice, adjustment, and acceptance. I'll help you to understand both the internal and external factors involved in mental health conditions and will help you to regain your inner strength and power.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As my theoretical orientation is Intersectional Feminism, I do see the political as personal. As such, political dialogue is welcome in counseling sessions. I view healing and developing inner strength as an integral part of the process of building collective well-being.

name: Emily Wagner
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi! My name is Emily, and I would love to help you find unapologetic freedom from difficult life experiences and anything holding you back.
ideal_client: I love being that little voice reminding you to be your truest, bravest, best, most authentic self! I am highly trained to work with trauma of all kinds. I have specialized training in relationships as well, and love working with the LGBTQ community. I also help people navigate grief, loss of meaning, anxiety, depression, and life transitions. I love having clients from all cultural backgrounds and walks of life. ​You are safe with me if you are wild at heart!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I'm known to give unconditional empathy and warmth, while providing direct and honest feedback. I view you as a whole person, and I care for all the parts that make you who you are. Building a close and trusted relationship is very important to me. I help you understand and regulate your emotions while using a trauma-informed therapy structure safe for your brain. I help you find solutions based on what you're naturally good at. Sometimes, we do go into the past to understand the now. We may question your thoughts and beliefs about yourself, and other times we will look to the body as a source of wisdom. These techniques are also called: Emotionally-focused (EFT); Trauma Informed; Strength-based; Psychodynamic; Cognitive-behavioral (CBT); Somatic; Internal Family Systems (IFS); Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy (KAP)

specialities.name: Sexual Abuse
specialities.description: I worked in sexual assault and domestic violence advocacy for several years, then became a therapist to work with my clients on a deeper level. I have had many trainings in sexual trauma, including a specialized internship. Today I use a feminist and trauma-informed approach to help my clients restore a sense of safety and power.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a member of the LGBTQ community and fierce advocate for our rights, I love helping my clients find an inner sense of freedom and peace, while navigating issues that can come with these identities, such as religious trauma, family tension or rejection, self-advocacy, people pleasing, boundaries, self-concept, or learning to remove internalized systems from your relationships.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have over 2000 hours of training in trauma, from childhood experiences to gun violence or natural disasters. I have a certificate in Trauma-Focused CBT, though I tend to use a more relational approach in treating PTSD.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: I love helping people feel grounded to themselves while in the midst of what can feel like chaotic life changes. I focus on strengths and help you redefine what you want you want from this new chapter in life. Then, we can look at tackling any barriers that are getting in the way, such as anxiety or freezing up. When we do these transitions with support, they can feel like catalysts for knowing ourselves on a deeper level, giving us the confidence to make brave and beautiful life choices.

name: Brittany Neighbours
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I look at therapy as an opportunity to be creative and curious, to assist you in connecting with your whole self and honor authenticity.
ideal_client: Life can be overwhelming at times and you may feel anxious, depressed, stuck, angry, lost. Maybe you feel like you can't move freely without fear. Maybe you feel misunderstood in relationships. Therapy can feel scary - it's hard to be open with another person and to experience emotions and sensations that feel painful. I hope to create a safe space for you to explore different aspects of yourself - thoughts, emotions, physical sensations - to increase self-compassion and insight.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: There are many ways to create growth, vibrancy, and peace in your life. I integrate several orientations including Reichian somatic therapy, cognitive-behavioral therapy, Gestalt therapy, trauma-informed care, and humanistic methods. I emphasize attention to the present moment so that you can really connect with yourself and make adjustments as needed. My style is thoughtful, humorous, and down-to-earth, and we'll explore your experiences gently. You have an innate drive towards wholeness and well-being, and a therapeutic relationship that is accepting, creative, and curious can support this process. I take a collaborative approach towards counseling, blending techniques to best serve each person and welcoming feedback to increase trust and safety.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that every person has the capacity for growth and to make real contact with life and others. Sometimes the things we do to protect ourselves get in the way of true contact. I have spent many years learning to be truly present and accepting of myself and my experiences, and I hope to support you in a similar process. I also believe that each person is the expert in their own life, and I want to help others understand and honor their own needs and wants. Each person strives for some sort of authentic expression, it looks different for everyone, and space is needed for that expression. In my free time, I enjoy urban hikes, hanging with my two cats, volunteering at a farm sanctuary, live music, and karaoke. I really strive to reduce the amount of harm caused to other beings and the planet as much as possible. Prior to starting my journey in mental health care, I worked in a lot of retail settings, as a sociopolitical campaign advocate, and at a movie theater.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I have specialized training in Contemporary Reichian Somatic (Orgone) Therapy, and have been part of a program that includes group and individual supervision for this approach since 2017.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I have devoted much of my professional career to developing skills from a humanistic perspective, pulling from person-centered (Rogerian) and Gestalt approaches. I have engaged in individual and group supervision, personal research, and graduate training to learn these skills.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I approach anxiety holistically and address the connection between thoughts, behaviors, emotions, and physical sensations. I use several techniques, including but not limited to cognitive restructuring, exposure, mindfulness, emotional awareness and acceptance/tolerance, and addressing avoidance.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I work gently with individuals who have experienced trauma, starting with increasing their sense of physical and emotional safety. I use several techniques, including but not limited to stabilization/grounding, somatic approaches, and breath work. I also support clients in adjusting beliefs about themselves to increase self-compassion.

name: Jami Howell
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I am a licensed Clinical Psychologist with a doctorate from the School of Professional Psychology at Pacific University. I completed my internship & residency in the counseling center at Portland State University, & I have been in private practice in downtown SW Portland since 2012.

approaches.My Background and Approach: If you are feeling stuck, overwhelmed, or dissatisfied, I can help you understand what is getting in your way and develop tools to help you move forward. My aim is to create an environment where you feel safe to explore your problems without being judged. Once we have established a working relationship built on mutual trust, honesty, and respect, my goals are to help you better understand your problems, identify obstacles that have inhibited your capacity for growth and support you in the process of making positive and often times difficult life changes. I've been training in Gestalt theory since 2008. I believe in the importance of understanding you as you are & attuning to your thoughts, feelings & actions to heighten your awareness. My approach is collaborative, client-centered & compassionate. Engaging in therapy is a courageous step. I would be glad to talk with you about how to start living the life you want. Set up a free phone consultation, and see my website.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In my practice, I work adults and adolescents which includes separate sessions with their parents. I treat people with wide range of mental health issues from various diverse backgrounds. My areas of expertise include grief counseling, body image issues, eating disorders, & relationship struggles. My approach is grounded in psychological theory and research.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory relates to the long-term interpersonal relationship style we have and how it affects our present day relationships with others. It's based on the general premise that attachment styles we developed in our early years influence our patterns of interacting in close relationships in later years.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Humanistic theory is a holistic approach that pays special attention to positive human potential. It encourages self exploration and viewing ourselves as a 'whole person' greater than the sum of our parts. It incorporates self-awareness that helps the client change their state of mind and behavior from one of reactions to a healthier one with more productive self-awareness and thoughtful actions.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: Gestalt therapy helps people get in touch with and talk honestly about their unfulfilled needs. It raises awareness of the patterns people have established in their lives that can be problematic and lead to being stuck. Gestalt is a strengths-based perspective that does not reduce people only to a diagnosis or set of issues.It’s an approach that helps us expand ourselves and increases confidence

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I help individuals who struggle in relationships with their romantic partners, friends, family, co-workers and anyone else that is relevant in their life.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I work with people who have lost loved ones to suicide, accidents and age related medical illness and premature death to cancer and other sicknesses. In addition, I've helped people who have lost jobs, marriages, connections with family and friends and more.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: My practice includes working with the full spectrum of eating issues including body image concerns, weight management, binge eating, anorexia, bulimia, and obesity.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety issues are very common and can include panic attacks, obsessive thinking, compulsive behaviors, constant worrying, and irrational fears. Anxiety often goes hand in hand with depression. I work with people with all of these struggles and any other anxiety issues.

name: Katie Kotsovos
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with adults on issues such as anxiety, depression, trauma, disordered eating and body image.
ideal_client: If you're struggling with negative beliefs or intense feelings about yourself--or your body--you know it's not easy to simply flip a switch and think or feel differently. In fact, those thoughts and feelings are your inner system's attempts to try to cope. The thing is, they don't really work that well, do they? I enjoy helping folks explore the root causes of those responses and access the internal resources they need for healing, so they can live more freely.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is warm, collaborative and transparent. I’m happy to share why we do what we’re doing in therapy and explore what I can offer from my skillset that resonates with you. I draw from a variety of therapeutic approaches to help folks embrace the present moment, connect to what’s going on in their bodies and work with their emotions. I also help clients explore the impact of trauma (big or small) on their current functioning and work towards feeling more regulated and self-compassionate. I’m trained in Eye-Movement Desensitization Reprocessing (EMDR), which can help alter one’s relationship to negative beliefs and distressful memories. I’m also a Health at Every Size (HAES)-aligned therapist. HAES is a weight-neutral approach to care that recognizes the harm of the thin-centric model.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My utmost goal is to create a safe space for your healing. If you've been harmed by the dominant culture we live in or by your family of origin (even inadvertently), I believe your growth requires a reparative experience of feeling that your emotions are valid and who you are matters. I strive to do that always by meeting you with empathy and respect. While I am not a member of the LQBTQIA2S+ or BIPOC communities, I am dedicated to cultural competency education and understanding the dynamics of privilege and oppression in all their forms and the impact that has on one’s mental health.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I'm trained in Internal Family Systems (IFS) and Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing (EMDR). These approaches can help us appreciate how your system is trying to keep you safe and create reparative experiences so you can feel safe when you actually are. This can also be applied to attachment trauma (abuse, neglect or invalidation) experienced early in life.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I have many years experience working with disordered eating at the outpatient level and previously in day treatment. My approach includes practical strategies for regulating eating and accessing support, as well as (perhaps more importantly) exploring what drives your eating disorder, working with the related emotions and building motivation for recovery.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: I'm deeply committed to a Health At Every Size framework at my practice. Our body image work may include challenging toxic patriarchal norms, exploring the impact of living under them and unburdening they legacy of shame you've been handed. Your body is deserving of love, dignity and respect.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I can help you build strategies to manage anxiety by increasing mindfulness practices and tending to your physical experience of symptoms. I can also help you explore the function of your anxiety and find more affective, healthier ways to meet those needs.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: If we think of depression as a messenger from you system that something isn't working, I can help you explore what exactly that is. From there, we can build a plan to move towards what will work. If this points to past experiences that still influence your thoughts and feelings, we can work on healing those. You deserve to feel better.

name: Jennie Hayes, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I think counseling is always useful, even when there's nothing "wrong." We get a lot of chances to go, go, go but not a lot to slow down and reflect. Usually it takes some crisis of feeling or relationship to tell us it's time. I see those crises as opportunities, doorways to deeper understanding.

approaches: I work from an existential humanistic perspective, using emotion focused, narrative, internal family systems and reality therapy approaches. Before becoming a therapist I worked in advertising as a writer, helping brands find and make meaning. I bring that creative perspective to my work.

I'm a Nationally Certified Counselor and Licensed Professional Counselor Intern with a Clinical Mental Health counseling degree from Portland State University. I work with couples, individuals and teens ages 13 and up who are facing challenges like: job stress, creative blocks, relationship struggles, self esteem, depression, anger, anxiety, gender identity, spirituality, sexuality, major life transitions, and grief and loss.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I specialize in relationships that fall outside of the conventional models, and love helping individuals in those relationships explore and communicate their needs, learn to navigate challenges in a healthy way and build stronger bonds of trust and connection.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: We are a cultural turning point for women, a reckoning coming at a time where women still face enormous amounts of misogyny, internalized misogyny, role expectation, discrimination, harassment and social expectations about everything from looks to childbearing to relationships. I love working with women as they process trauma and transitions, explore their identity and come into their own power.

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: Even relationships that are ready to end have so much to teach us about ourselves—if we're able to open ourselves to learning. I specialize in helping people ready to end relationships process the hurt and say goodbye in order to discover new relationships and ways of being together.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: From the second we're born, relationships challenge us at our deepest level. Safety, vulnerability, shame, betrayal, commitment: they hit on our greatest fears and meet our fundamental needs. It's a place where we can grow the most and the fastest. I love working with couples because it's all right there in the room, in the moment, to be explored and unpacked and learned from.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Loss alway takes more from us than the person or relationship we've lost, and grief doesn't happen in any one way or on any one's timeline. But with care and connection, there can be deep meaning and healing in even the most profound pain.

name: Amy Altenberger
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Grief and trauma. When experienced, these can define us. But it doesn’t have to be that way.
ideal_client: I am a Licensed Counselor in both Oregon and Washington. I am happy to see you in person at my office or via telehealth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a Licensed Professional Counselor trained in Art Therapy and a yoga instructor, I am able to offer experiential therapy, mindfulness, as well as breath and movement work to promote healing and connection. It is my hope that through our work together you will feel felt, heard and nurtured. Over the past 25 years, I have worked with children and adults who have experienced anxiety, depression, grief and trauma. I am deeply committed to working with clients who have experienced loss and help them with their journey.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe in a collaborative and nurturing approach to counseling.
