I feel that people are shaped by the culture in which they were raised, the experiences they have had, and the stories they create about themselves. Through our work together, I will help you tell your story; to find your voice, and create a new narrative. Through the use of mindfulness, breath and body work you will develop techniques to decrease anxiety, feel empowered and connected.

specialities.name: Expressive Art Therapy
specialities.description: I hold a Masters Degree in Expressive Art Therapy and I was an Adjunct Professor in the Graduate Art Therapy Program at Marylhurst University. I incorporate art, movement, breath and mindfulness in our sessions. Talking about trauma can be difficult, art therapy allows you to express yourself and tell your story without using words in a safe non-judgmental space. You don't have to be an artist to use art therapy and we can discuss if this is the right modality for you.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: With all trauma comes loss and grief. I have dedicated my career to working with individuals dealing with grief and loss related to trauma. My focus has been on working with trauma, both current and historical. I also have experience in working with acute and prolonged grief.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: I have over 25 years working with children and families., as a Child and Family Therapist working in schools and as Mental Health Consultant for an Early Childhood Program. I am a Certified Positive Discipline Parent Educator and have led multiple parent education groups and provided trainings on parenting to educators.

name: Jenn Garlock
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I specialize in helping folks who have experienced trauma at the hands of another person to heal their wounds and take back their lives.
ideal_client: Are you struggling with anxiety, depression, or a nagging feeling that something just isn’t okay? Have the difficult experiences of your past started to come back to the surface? Maybe this is all having an impact on your relationships and your ability to go about your daily life. You are not alone. I help survivors of childhood and interpersonal trauma look at how their experiences have shaped them and explore how to take back their lives from the memories that have burdened them for so long.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I specialize in working with folks who have experienced trauma by the hands of another person, including sexual assault or abuse, physical abuse or neglect, emotional abuse or neglect, and verbal abuse. Many of my clients have experienced multiple incidents of trauma, of various types, by various people. It can be so difficult to trust others after being hurt by people in your life. I know that putting your trust in a therapist is no different, and I don't take that responsibility lightly. Trauma therapy is tough work, and it happens best in the context of a safe and supportive relationship between therapist and client. I am here to hold the unspeakable things with you so that you don't have to do this by yourself anymore. Together, we will work to build a trusting and authentic relationship where you can feel safe enough to explore what happened in your life, the ways you have survived, and how to get unstuck and move toward a life that is ruled by you, not the trauma.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a survivor of trauma myself, I am intimately familiar with the powerful impact therapy can have on a person’s life. I know what it is like to put your trust in a professional during your most raw and painful moments, and I treat this responsibility with a great deal of care. It is this personal experience that led me to focus my therapeutic work on helping others who have experienced trauma. You deserve to be heard, respected, and embraced for who you are, and your story deserves to be told. I truly love my work as a therapist, and I feel so fortunate to get to do this for a living. It is a privilege to walk alongside my clients as they take back their power from the memories that made them feel powerless. When I'm not with my clients, you can find me exploring the outdoors with my dog, Wally, curled up on the couch reading a good book on a rainy day, or spending time with friends exploring the Portland food and music scenes.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I use Internal Family Systems therapy, attachment therapy, EMDR, and psychodynamic therapy to help my clients identify what happened to them, explore how this has impacted their lives, their relationships, and their self esteem, and make steps to create the lives and relationships that they want for themselves.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: I use Internal Family Systems therapy, attachment therapy, EMDR, and psychodynamic therapy to help my clients identify what happened to them, explore how this has impacted their lives, their relationships, and their self esteem, and make steps to create the lives and relationships that they want for themselves.

specialities.name: Sexual Abuse
specialities.description: I use Internal Family Systems therapy, Attachment therapy, EMDR, and Psychodynamic therapy to help my clients identify what happened to them, explore how this has impacted their lives, their relationships, and their self esteem, and make steps to create the lives and relationships that they want for themselves.

name: Katharine Frissora
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I am a doctorally prepared Psychiatric and Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP) with 15 years of healthcare experienc.
ideal_client: My ideal patient is ready to take an active role in their mental health journey. If you’re seeking a holistic approach beyond symptom management, I’m here to help. Whether facing a life transition or exploring root causes, we’ll create a treatment plan that addresses the whole picture. By blending traditional psychiatry with a holistic lens, we’ll uncover and treat underlying imbalances, supporting lasting healing and wellness.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Having personally navigated my own mental health journey, I understand how overwhelming it can feel. Those experiences have shaped my compassionate, personalized approach to care. Mental health isn’t one-size-fits-all, and I honor each person’s unique needs. Whether through mindfulness, lifestyle shifts, or creative outlets like art therapy, I help clients build treatment plans that feel truly aligned with who they are. I strive to create a safe, judgment-free space where individuals can explore emotions, build resilience, and develop practical tools to manage daily stress. While medication can be a helpful part of treatment, I also emphasize holistic approaches—nutrition, movement, and mind-body practices—to support whole-person healing. My goal is to not only address symptoms but also uncover root causes, helping clients find balance, strength, and lasting well-being. Healing is a journey, and I’m here to walk alongside my clients every step of the way.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that each of us, as individuals, is doing the best we can in any given moment, shaped by our unique experiences and personal circumstances. We are the best experts of our own bodies and lives, and it’s important to honor that truth. Compassion—both for ourselves and for one another—is a powerful healing force, something the world could always benefit from a little more of.

name: Ann Staple, MA, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with adults navigating a wide range of both normal and unwanted transitions and life events.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from a nonjudgmental, strengths based perspective. I love helping people tap their unique abilities and resources - often forgotten during difficult times. Our work will be rooted in your goals - what you want to achieve. I will provide tools to help you manage difficult emotions and collaborate with you to generate new possibilities and implement change. I offer a complimentary 15 minute consultation.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received my master's degree in Counseling Psychology in 2004 from Lewis and Clark College. I have been practicing as a therapist for 19 years. I spent 11 years of those years working as an Employee Assistance Counselor helping adults experiencing major life events. I have also worked in community agencies and for a state health department.

name: Celeste Endlich
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Laid back, relational, and affirming support along your path.
ideal_client: I'm passionate about working with adults of all ages and the LGBTQIA+ community. I often work with artists/creatives/entrepreneurs, neurodivergent individuals, untraditional life path takers, individuals in helping professions, and Veterans. I enjoy supporting people in increasing self-compassion, navigating life transitions, and exploring identity. I have experience supporting individuals experiencing anxiety, depression, mood disorders, PTSD and trauma, grief and loss, ADHD, and OCD.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I view therapy as a creative and collaborative process and intend to bring curiosity, authenticity, humor and warmth to the space. Together we can explore the experiences, contexts, and aspects of your identity that make up who you are and influence how you move through the world. We can learn approaches to assist you to self soothe, communicate more effectively in your relationships, and identify emotions and process experiences. I believe in identity-affirming care, cultural humility, social justice, ongoing learning, and I strive to create a nourishing therapeutic environment that fosters healing, connection, and transformation. I work from a strengths-based relational framework. I am guided by and draw upon a variety of approaches that I am trained in which include EMDR, Internal Family Systems Parts Work, Mindfulness and Stress Reduction Techniques, DBT Skills, Expressive Arts Techniques, and Somatic Approaches.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: My life experiences and ongoing healing journey brought me to this work as a therapist. I believe in humans' capacity for growth, learning, and change and I think we all need assistance along the way. As a therapist, it's my aim to help you clear the path and connect with your own inherent strengths and capacities. My goal is to help you explore your own inner landscape, tune into your own knowing, and to be a support alongside you as you walk your unique path. I provide Telehealth therapy to clients in the state of Oregon and in person walk and talk nature based therapy in the Portland Metro Area. I am currently able to accept private pay and sliding scale, however I am in the process of being paneled with several major insurance companies in Oregon.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR and find it a valuable approach to support work focused on the processing of trauma. I find EMDR most effective after we have taken time to learn skills that will support you through difficult emotions and have built a safe container within the therapeutic relationship.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I work from an IFS parts work perspective and find it a valuable way to get to know and understand you and the different parts of you that may show up in our work together and in your life experiences.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I have background and experience in utilizing mindfulness based approaches. I enjoy guiding meditations, introducing mindfulness based skills and concepts, and supporting you in connection to the present moment.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I strive to create a safe, connected, and affirming space.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I work from a trauma informed perspective in my work and utilize EMDR and grounding techniques to support trauma processing.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: I am passionate about supporting individuals in their efforts to increase self-compassion, work towards more positive self-talk, and in identifying anchoring practices that support wellbeing.

name: Zoe Wade
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Zoë, your go to for relationship issues. I help unpack and repair the grief that comes with the loss of past relationships.
ideal_client: We will work well together if you want a therapist that is more than just a listening ear. I enjoy debunking irrational thoughts that often lead to self sabotage and giving tangible tools each session. I look forward to helping you experience the kind of relationships that have aways felt out of reach.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: 1. Exploring childhood traumas, feelings of abandonment and wounds from previous relationships that may be impacting you in your relationships today 2. Creating new narratives that make vulnerability and obtaining closeness in relationships feel more safe 3. Healing unresolved feelings from any past relationships that did not work out

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: In our work together, we will go beyond a surface approach of therapy, and dig deep to discover ways to get the security you need out of relationships. We will heal the wounds of breakups and unpack the baggage you don't want to bring into your future.

name: Jenna Washburn
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
credentials: MA: Mental Health Counseling - Specialization in Addictions
intro: I will always approach our work together with the fundamental understanding that humans have limitless abilities to heal and grow.
ideal_client: I work with clients all across Oregon to help them find freedom from their inner tyrant. Whether that tyrant is Anxiety, Depression, Addiction, Trauma, or that harsh voice inside you that tells you're not enough. I also offer Focused Therapy for the following issues: - Relationship Struggles - Caretaker Burnout - Chronic Perfectionism - Building Healthy Boundaries - Surviving Narcissistic Abuse - Counseling for Empaths. Check out my website to learn more: https://www.empathiccounseling.org

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My counseling style is one based on empathy. Empathy is healing. It’s empowering. And it provides a space free from judgement where we can go beneath the surface of a problem and explore its depths. Weeding out the root of a problem is how to create real transformation and revolutionary change I have a double Masters degree in Counseling and also in the the field of Sociology. My education has given me a unique perspective to explore with both a micro and a macro lens. I seek to know my clients as novel individuals with their own unique experiences. And to also understand them within the context of their cultural and societal backgrounds. My theoretical orientation includes narrative therapy, depth psychology, attachment studies, and family systems. I tailor my approach based on each client’s needs and wants, incorporating different behavioral, cognitive, or emotional interventions as suits each individual person.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: As a fellow Empath and Highly-Sensitive Person, I understand the hardships us Empaths face. I understand the struggle to create healthy boundaries. The overactive caretaking of others to the point of fatigue. The chronic perfectionism and believing we are never doing enough. The endless chain of relationships with people exhibiting narcissistic behavior. That’s why I’ve created Focused Therapy to address the above issues and to empower you to heal, grow, and ultimately thrive.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: Depth therapy provides the basis of my orientation because it's the beneath the surface and in the depths that real change is made.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I have researched attachment theory and utilize its theories in most of my therapy interventions, particularly on issues of family systems, relationships, trauma, and boundaries.

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Narrative therapy enriches my counseling techniques by: bringing in elements of larger societal narratives impacting clients; allowing the clients space to tell and oftentimes rewrite their own story; and providing a creative space for metaphor, imagery, and exploration.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: While I also use CBT often, I always pair it with Emotionally Focused Therapy because it allows a more well-rounded approach and links together the cognitive with the emotional spheres of a client's experience.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: Family Systems is all about recognizing how a person impacts and is impacted by the systems within which they interact - starting with their family of origin and extending into larger societal systems.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have worked with clients of all ages on issues of anxiety. Especially after the past year, it's safe to assume that everyone is experiencing some level of it. And yet, anxiety can show up in a myriad of ways: panic, fear, insomnia, low self esteem, chronic perfectionism, or that constant sinking feeling that everything is on the verge of falling apart. I offer a unique counseling method that seeks to address the symptoms of anxiety as well as discovering the root causes.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can look and feel a number of ways. It can be the lack of motivation to get anything done. Or the overall numbness to all or any emotions. It could also be nearing the edge of feeling like you can't take it anymore. I offer empathic counseling for people struggling with depression. However, if we don't make a good fit, I'm also happy to offer referrals to other counselors. My main goal is that you get the care you need.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: I specialize in treating clients who have experienced narcissistic abuse over their lifetime. The term narcissistic abuse is used to categorize the way a person experiences emotional abuse and manipulation when in a relationship with someone exhibiting narcissistic behavior. This “relationship” does not necessarily have to pertain to a romantic partner. It could also be with a family member, a friend, a coworker, or any other important relationship that is impacting your life.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: As a recovered codependent, I understand the struggles of codependency. And I also truly believe in our power to heal from it. Codependency can sometimes be hard to spot and a person can quickly fall into a codependent relationship without realizing. I offer a counseling program called Focused Therapy that helps to address issues of codependency along with skill-building techniques to cultivate awareness and eventually bring about healthy connection with others.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: Caretaking is an act of love. But the yang to this beautiful yin is that sometimes you care and tend so much to others, that there’s nothing left over for yourself. This can make you feel burnt out, fatigued, drained, and possibly even resentful. That’s when caretaking can become overactive. I offer a Focused Therapy program to bring some focus back to you. You deserve to heal, to spend some energy on yourself, and to fill your own cup so you can get back into the world refreshed & renewed.

name: Kaijah Bjorklund
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Find the path to help you reach your untapped potential, work through obstacles with EMDR and somatic based therapy.
ideal_client: My clients come from a wide variety of backgrounds. I have experience working with different communities and subcultures that can be marginalized. I provide a non-judgmental empathetic space to support discussing challenging and often taboo subjects, allowing individuals to address the difficult, challenging or traumatic parts of their experiences in the world.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I draw from the relevant neuroscientific research that is emerging within the field of psychology that provides a deeper understanding of behaviors and experiences. As a Somatic (body oriented) counselor I consider the importance of your felt experiences and how they impact you. I engage the power of mindfulness, or the practice of self-awareness, which builds bridges in different parts of the brain, and allows for new possibilities in emotional patterns and access to new choices. I don’t have a one-size fits all approach to what I do. I offer support and acceptance for what each person brings to counseling and what their needs are. I consider humans not to be pieces and parts but an interconnected whole. I have a variety of tools and strategies to assist in understanding what is happening and then taking action.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that every person faces challenges and has areas in their life where they may suffer. Everyone can feel alone and isolated at times and counseling support can help reduce the feelings of isolation and provide tools for managing symptoms. I believe that individuals in marginalized communities may not only hold individual trauma but collective and historical trauma that is necessary to address.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can feel overwhelming and all-consuming. What if there were a better way to manage your anxiety instead of it managing you? There is. Though humans have a natural stress response, sometimes it can become so overwhelming that it becomes paralyzing. Therapy for anxiety helps you get in tune with your natural stress responses and get anxiety under control. I specialize in the treatment of anxiety and related disorders using a variety of evidence based techniques including EMDR.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma and PTSD can impact the way you function, feel, think behave and what you believe about yourself. Symptoms of all kinds are treatable. I use a Trauma-Informed Therapy to address the psychological, emotional, relational and physical problems that past trauma can create. My approach draws from numerous sources including Neuroscience, Sensorimotor, EMDR and IFS. I offer many highly effective and evidence-based strategies and interventions for healing the effects of trauma.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Unhealthy and repeated patterns are a continual source of suffering if you don't understand how you entered into the cycle. I support clients in understanding the roots of unhealthy relationships with my training in Emotionally Focused Therapy and identify how to meet their true needs in relationships. You are capable of creating new patterns of loving and relating with others. If you were never taught how to have a healthy relationship how would you know how? You can learn.

name: Lorraine Storm
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I’m a licensed professional counselor trained in marriage and family therapy and health coaching. I take integrative approach to helping clients balance their lives and relationships to create health and fulfillment with a style that is strengthening and empowering.

approaches: In times of distress, it is natural to seek a guide, teacher, or healer, and a therapist can be all of these things. More than just someone to listen to what you’re going through, a counselor provides a sounding board and opportunity for reflection, feedback and increased self awareness. I look at the individual as both a unique entity, and as part in a number of a number of larger systems. I integrate various therapy techniques and incorporate a global perspective- integrating health and lifestyle changes that can improve your mental health. Regardless of the modality, the most important factor predicting success in counseling or coaching is our personal connection – it doesn’t matter how good someone’s advice is, it’s not going to help you unless the person who’s giving it is someone you respect and trust.

I hold a Master's degree in Marriage and Family Therapy from Portland State University. My undergraduate degrees are in Psychology and Studio Art from the University of Redlands. I am also a Certified Integrative Health Coach. I have worked with children, adolescents, and families providing in-home and community-based therapy and crisis response. I have also worked in school-based settings providing individual and family therapy to students from a variety of backgrounds. I have extensive training in child development and trauma-informed therapy, as well as Strategic Family Therapy and Family Systems counseling. I am passionate about helping couples strengthen communication and deepen connection.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR is a method of processing trauma and helping you think about it differently so that it doesn't bother you anymore. Often we are stuck in negative beliefs about ourselves regarding our trauma when in fact we did what we could or did not have control over the outcome. EMDR helps you use your adult mind to process past trauma objectively.

specialities.name: Nonviolent Communication
specialities.description: Nonviolent Communication is an excellent tool to learn what your own feelings and needs are, as well as how to express them to others in a way that opens the conversation and increases understanding, rather than creating or perpetuating a conflict where each party is trying to 'win.' This will help you develop more compassion for yourself and others, and deepen meaningful connections with others

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: Western medicine tends to be very specialized, and often focuses on treating symptoms rather than the underlying cause of illness. But a person’s mental health is affected by the food they eat, the quality of their relationships, and how they spend their time. As a trained health coach, I look at the individual as both a unique entity, and as part in a number of a number of larger systems.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Relationships are not one-size-fits-all and the ones you design yourself can be potentially the most fulfilling. Although non-traditional relationships face many of the same issues as traditional ones, they also have the potential to amplify or emphasize problems, especially around insecurity or jealousy. I affirming and knowledgeable of poly and open relationships.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Raising kids is tough! So much has changed in the last couple of decades with technology and culture that adolescents today experience numerous problems we never had to deal with growing up (and some we did!). I have worked with kids and families on a variety of topics in home, community, and school-based settings, so I have a variety of tools to address common problems.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Every relationship experiences ebbs and flows, and while some degree of conflict is normal, at times it can get to a point where it seems impossible to solve it on your own. This is where a couples therapist can help. As a trained marriage and family therapist, I will help you better understand one another and reconnect to the love and excitement that made you fall in love in the first place.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is very common - we all experience it to some degree, but when it keeps you from doing the things that you love and are important to you, a change is needed. It can be a result of over-analyzing or over-thinking situations to the point that it no longer serves you. I will help you “get out of your head” and embrace your inner strength to enjoy the things that are important to you.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is something many people face in modern times. Causes can be internal (self-esteem issues, chemical imbalance), external (resulting from unhealthy relationships or abuse), societal (feeling isolated, experiencing pressures around your job or money) or even global (climate change, discrimination, poverty, etc). You don’t need to face these challenges alone, and I'm here to help.

name: Anne Morgyn
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I offer compassionate care that supports your transformation out of feeling stuck in relationship to your body and your authentic self.
ideal_client: I work with a variety of concerns for elders, adults and teens (14+), here's some of my specialties that may resonate with you: *burnout, overwhelm, chronic fatigue *food and body image struggles *chronic illness/pain, autoimmune disorders, cancer *neurodivergence and highly sensitive people *parenting and caregiving *divorce and co-parenting *identity exploration *spiritual exploration, religious or cult trauma *breaking intergenerational patterns *mid-life transitions *ageing *complex trauma

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I'm committed to the sacred process of finding and living your most authentic Self in whatever stage of life you may be in. I believe in you, I believe you have a story that deserves to be heard and I believe you have a deep intelligence within you that can help guide you towards well-being. It is my passion to help you understand, accept (maybe even love!) and learn to trust yourself. Our work together centers on safety, collaboration and inclusion and I believe in meeting you where you're at without judgement or bias and keeping it compassionately reaI. I bring over a decade of experience as a LMT specializing in nervous system regulation. Like our bodies, therapy isn't "one size fits all" and I have many tools to draw on to help. I have experience in treating eating disorders and trauma. I am a certified Somatic EMDR provider, am becoming a certified Body Trust provider and have additional training in Internal Family Systems and Somatic Psychotherapy.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I'm a HAES aligned, identity-affirming therapist who welcomes all clients including LGBTQIA+, neurodivergent, disabled, BIPOC, and poly folks. You deserve care that can hold space for your whole self, where all parts of you are welcome. I also acknowledge the many current oppressive systems in power. Sometimes an important part of our work will be to investigate these systems and how they have infiltrated your sense of self, worth and safety. I also strive to keep any inherent power imbalances between us in check by practicing humility towards this process and keeping you centered as the expert of your experience. I'm a life long learner and committed to my own personal growth. I believe in walking the talk, I've seen the power that the right fit of therapy and therapist can do and I consider it a privilege to be able to pay that forward with others.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: I've trained in and worked with teens and adults struggling with eating disorders along with competency training working with those who are LGBTQ+ or neurodivergent. I currently work with those that have a history of an eating disorder and are in the maintenance phase of their recovery or those with intrusive disordered eating. I also offer support for parents, family and partners of those with an eating disorder.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am a certified Somatic EMDR provider and have completed an extensive training program in healing trauma that included Polyvagal Theory, Embodiment, Compassionate Mind Training, Internal Family Systems, Somatic Abolitionism, and Interpersonal Neurobiology. I understand the difference between PTSD and CPTSD (complex trauma) and how to approach both as well as have lived experience healing from past trauma.

specialities.name: Aging Concerns
specialities.description: Having worked with teens (14+) up to elders, I understand that transitioning through different life stages greatly impact our mental health. I particularly understand the effects aging has on women's bodies as well as how mid-life presents us all with an opportunity to confront our mortality that can feel both disruptive and also potentially transformational.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I have lived experience with a variety of spiritual and religious environments as well as professional experience and training. I understand the very personal process of spiritual exploration and identity. I hold a wide space for accepting how this shows up for you (or doesn't) and how you may want to bring that into our work together. I am also cognizant in understanding the harm that can come from spiritual organizations and how to regain your sense of self outside of these experiences.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: I work with caregiver burnout, sensory overwhelm, changing generational parenting patterns, addressing intrusive trauma that affects parenting, parenting children with an eating disorder or who is neurodivergent, and loss of sense of self as a new parent. In addition I also work with women navigating divorce and co parenting. Alongside the challenges, I help parents accept the messiness and reality of parenting while finding realistic self care and celebrating the many joys and rewards.

name: Rebecca Kinman
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: A proud Queer and neuro-divergent clinician. Now offering Walk-And-Talk/Outdoor therapy in the Portland, Oregon area.
ideal_client: You’ve already tried therapy. You’ve talked and talked about it until you were blue in the face, but still, nothing has changed. That’s exactly what we will address. We won’t just talk about your problems; we will take tangible steps in every session toward getting your life together.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I earned my Bachelor’s degree in Women, Gender, and Sexuality Studies from Portland State University. I went on to complete a Master’s in Clinical Social Work at the same institution. During my studies, I explored topics like racial equity, housing for LGBTQIAA+ seniors, trauma-informed care, feminist therapy, solution-focused therapy, migration, anti-oppressive models of care. Beyond my academic work, I have post-graduate, on-the-job training in the assessment and treatment of ADHD (Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder), Bipolar I and II, and Obsessive Compulsive Disorder (OCD) among others. I take an eclectic and creative approach to therapy. My work draws from several therapeutic modalities, including Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT), psychodynamic therapy, and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT). I have supported clients dealing with conditions such as depression, anxiety, trauma, ADHD, Autism, gender dysphoria, and others.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I understand that wellness is a privilege. Therefore, we I am committed to challenging and confronting the effects of capitalism racism, ableism, colonialism, misogyny, homophobia, transphobia, and xenophopbia (among others). I especially acknowledge the negative impact of late-stage capitalism on mental health and I do my best to empower clients as the ultimate experts in their own health and well-being. I also believe that the real healing takes place outside of the therapy room. That's why I am passionate about offering an alternative to what is traditionally known as "talk therapy." With consent as the foundation for every session, I work collaboratively with clients to identify personal goals and develop practical strategies that help them carry their new skills into everyday life.

name: Adam Von Passow
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My role is to walk the path with you and begin to develop the skills needed to move through the unexpected challenges of life.
ideal_client: When life is challenging, we all need support, understanding, respect, and compassion. As humans, we benefit greatly by connecting with a support system so we understand we are not alone on this journey. Psychotherapy is our chance to connect to that support in a safe environment where we can explore, learn and grow.

approaches.My Background: I have 24 years of experience working with diverse populations young and old. I have worked with people to help them move through substance abuse, mental health issues, and coping with loss/grief. For the last 15 years, I have been working in hospice care, helping families transition through this life stage and related grief experience. While getting my master’s degree in social work, I was fortunate to have a great mentor who taught me about EMDR and hypnotherapy. EMDR is a specialized form of psychotherapy that uses eye movements to reprocess and reintegrate traumatic experiences. When we reprocess our trauma we can change how it affects our mind, body, emotions, and behavior. This is an elegant and powerful form of healing that I incorporate into my practice.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: When I am not working I feel it’s important to connect with nature so I explore all the Pacific Northwest has to offer. I also love writing songs, playing music, and recording music. I also get into exercise, so I run, play basketball, and skateboard with my kids. I also practice moving energy with Qigong, Tai Chi, and Yoga, which I have done for the last 20 years.

name: Shane Ladd
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I work with individuals that experience trauma. I specialize in PTSD, Loss and Grief. I'm here to help you through your healing process.
ideal_client: I work with clients impacted by trauma. A traumatic experience is like an injury and can have a long lasting effect on you and impact the way you perceive and interact in the world. If you are an individual experiencing trauma you may have difficulty regulating emotions such as anger, anxiety, sadness and easily feel overwhelmed or numb and shut down. Due to the trauma, our brain operates in a survival mode and finds ways to cope and not always healthy ways.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a counselor, I will provide a safe environment, a comfortable place to land while we explore and examine how your trauma impacts you daily. In the therapeutic space, I will provide support, psychoeducation, tools and skills that are appropriate to your treatment goals. Through this collaborative process you will expand awareness, grow, heal and as a result cultivate a more adaptive life narrative that will empower and strengthen you. Our fit as client and therapist is essential to your healing process. I hope collectively we can bring curiosity and compassion in the therapeutic space. I am a trauma-informed therapist, my clinical work is integrative in nature. I’m grounded in a Person-Centered Approach that is enhanced by a number of supplemental theoretical orientations such as: Narrative Therapy, Compassion-Focused Therapy, Somatic Therapy, CBT, and Parts work (IFS) to name a few.

In addition to being a Trauma informed therapist, I also work with bereaved parents. I am TFMR Mom that had a stillbirth. Through this experience, I have become incredibly passionate about serving mothers and parents who have experienced TFMR (Termination for Medical Reasons), Stillbirths and Child Loss at any point. The grief that accompanies this loss is tremendous and isolating. It would be an honor to walk beside you and support you through this heartbreaking loss and assist you in navigating through your grief. My counseling style is genuine, personable, and creative. My personality is warm, inviting and direct. It is my focus that you feel heard, seen and respected. I look forward to accompanying you on your journey of inner-healing.

name: Jocelyn Wagman
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I’m Jocelyn, a highly-sensitive therapist committed to social justice.
ideal_client: I focus on helping adults navigate life’s challenges and (re)discover their true selves. Whether it’s parenting, grief, burnout, or another of life’s challenges that’s brought you here, through our work together, you’ll better understand your needs and discover your unique pathways back to your true self. For people with high-sensitivity, these issues often feel especially intense, and it can help to work with someone who understands this trait.

approaches.My Background and Approach: As a therapist, I draw from practices based in mindfulness, self-compassion, polyvagal theory, internal family systems, and trauma-informed care. I lean into my high-sensitivity to offer warm, connected, compassionate therapy, and can help other highly-sensitive people learn about and work with this trait. I completed my graduate training in social work in 2015 and also hold a Masters degree in public health. I’ve worked extensively with people navigating serious illness and loss and their families in hospital settings. I regularly participate in trainings and consultation groups to continue to grow as a therapist. I am a parent and a step-parent and am continually learning and stretching from these experiences too.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I chose social work because of its emphasis on social justice. I believe that most of the struggles we experience are rooted in various forms of oppression, and actively participating in dismantling these oppressive structures is important to me. I strive for anti-racism and all forms of anti-oppressive practice. I especially enjoy working with parents because of how rich my own experience step-parenting and parenting is. There are constant invitations to confront my own old wounding and grow as a parent. Over the years of my training, I've learned so much from the field of interpersonal neurobiology and from child development perspectives like RIE that have helped me as a parent - helping other parents learn how to understand their own and their children's behavior is immensely rewarding.

name: Madeline Ball
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: My passion is working with individuals and couples working towards more fulfilling sexual expression and relational bonds.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with couples facing a variety of difficulties from LGBTQIA+ factors, sexual concerns, attachment wounds, or family trauma. We will through these with openness and curiosity to help you achieve your relationship goals. I enjoy working with individuals developing their gender and sexual expression, or couples whether it is how to open your relationship, heal from religious upbringing, or find more pleasure in sex.

approaches.My Background: I was raised in a Roman Catholic family where my sexual and gender identity was not only not dismissed but downright restricted. By the time I entered into a queer friendly and sex positive community the freedom I felt was empowering. I discovered the desire to encourage my community to heal from the collective wounds we face. I recognize how hard it is to confront these attachment wounds and choose differently, however I believe there is always a chance to grow more meaningful and impactful relationships. I am excited to use my knowledge and experience to connect and work with you towards a more fulfilling relationship with yourself and others. I hope to promote healthy relationships and help others increased sexual pleasure and dive further into alignment.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I value depth, longevity, and presence. These three values are woven through sessions as we dive deep into what you believe and who you aspire to become, encourage insight into the present moment, and use that insight to create lasting change in your life. I might be a good fit for you if any of the following apply: -You are ready to dive into a deeper understanding of yourself -You are stuck and struggling to figure out the next step in your relationship/life -You want more fulfilling sexual pleasure [from a variety of sexual disorders, KINK/bdsm, or otherwise] -You and your partner are considering marriage or want to revamp a relationship you have been in for years -You are LGBTQIA+ -You are interested in opening your relationship or are struggling in an current ENM relationship -You are eager for more in life!

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: Working with the trans community is an intimate and complex dynamic as we shift through how you navigate the world with this identity.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I adore working with couples in any stage of poly relationships. Whether you are considering what it might be like to open, are experiencing the range of emotions that comes with having an open relationship, or have been open for years.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I am working on my AASECT certification and have treated many different sexual problems from pain during intercourse (vaginismus) and ED to how to incorportate kink/bdsm into the relationship. I have worked with individuals and couples on these topics.

name: Katy Hartnett Boruff
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a seasoned clinician who has been providing quality mental health treatment to young adults (ages 18- 40) for the past 16 years.
ideal_client: Do you struggle with anxiety that can be quite debilitating and that persists despite your daily efforts to manage it? Depression that drags you down and prevents you from enjoying your life fully? The impact of unresolved trauma making it difficult for you to respond to events in your life successfully? I create a gentle and safe space through a nurturing therapeutic relationship to support the growth of emerging adults so that they may lead expansive, fulfilling lives.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My mission is to provide quality mental health services to emerging adults ages 18-40 through treating anxiety, depression, trauma, sexual identity concerns, and relational difficulties. We will work together to alleviate symptoms, help you learn to let go of outdated coping strategies (substance use, numbing or disordered eating) to help you meet your goals. I practice Gestalt therapy in a warm and supportive environment, where I will help you gain insight into past patterns of behavior that are no longer useful, help you uncover barriers that are holding you back, develop new ways of coping, and build on existing strengths.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: What sets me apart from other practitioners is that I specialize in the unique challenges of emerging adults and I am introducing Gestalt therapy to a younger population. Most people seek me out for my experience in working with young adults and because they seek a counselor who they feel can understand them and their individual concerns. I provide a new, different approach that you may have never tried before. I have experience working with all gender identities and racial backgrounds. I strive to honor your unique experience and I work to hold space to help you understand how your specific set of life experiences has informed your way of being in the world.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: I have studied Gestalt Therapy with a mentor for the past four years, building on my already expansive knowledge of psychodynamic psychotherapy. I’ve been amazed at what a powerful method of therapy Gestalt therapy is and the transformational effects it has in my clients’ lives. It draws on some principles of Buddhist psychology and mindfulness which I find valuable for increasing one’s ability to be present in their life.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: While I work with a variety of presenting concerns, I have extensive experience working with survivors of childhood abuse and neglect and those whose anxiety has not responded well to previous forms of treatment.

name: Heather Phillips
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I offer counseling for folks who are going through life transitions, and who are feeling "stuck" due to past trauma or difficult situations.
ideal_client: Are you experiencing a change in life that feels overwhelming or disorienting? Are past experiences causing you to feel "stuck" or showing up in ways that are no longer serving you? If so I would love be part of your support team. I primarily work with adults and adolescents, and welcome folks of any identity. I have specific training in treating trauma, including reproductive trauma, infertility, grief/loss, and perinatal mental health.

approaches.My Background: My work as a therapist has been focused on the goal of helping children and families thrive. For the last 5 years I have worked in a medical clinic with Nurse Midwives, OBGYNs, and other providers as a therapist. In this role I provided mental health therapy to treat mood disorders, and provided support with various issues related to parenting including adjustment, navigating high risk pregnancies and parenting children with medical issues, grief and loss related to pregnancy loss and/or infertility, and healing from birth related trauma. I am licensed as a Perinatal Mental Health Clinician (PMH-C) through Postpartum Support Int'l and I started my career working for over ten years as Mental Health Therapist in school-based health clinics. That experience was foundational to my work supporting folks in all stages of their journeys to either become parents, parent children in their care, or move through traumatic grief and loss.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I value and respect the diversity of individuals, and my practice is rooted anti-oppressive and anti-racist frameworks. I am committed to lifelong learning and cultural humility, and make this a priority in my professional and personal education and growth. I welcome individuals from all cultures, races, abilities, religions, sexual orientations, and gender identities to work with me.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: I have extensive experience treating perinatal mood disorders and supporting folks with other challenges and struggles related to their reproductive health, or parenting journeys. I am licensed as a Perinatal Mental Health Clinician (PMH-C) through Postpartum Support International. I am also trained in Interpersonal Therapy for the Perinatal Population, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Trauma Focused-CBT, and The Incredible Years Parent and Child Interventions.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR, and have found it to be transformative in treating people with all types of trauma experiences including complex developmental trauma.

name: Susie Barrios
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a therapist with over 30 years experience. Life has taught me that understanding, acceptance, compassion are essential to healing.
ideal_client: There are so many life conditions that bring suffering. Our power lies in how we react to what life brings. Often we try our best to cope, but find ourselves stuck in old patterns and behaviors that don't help. I work with people who want to learn about what they need, and grow their ability to cope and thrive in their lives. This includes people navigating life transitions, relationship challenges, anxiety, depression, grief, aging, and trauma-related issues.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My belief is that each person has the ability to find their answers and to grow their capacity to navigate life’s challenges with courage and lead a fulfilling, connected life. My work is grounded in trauma-informed approaches, mindfulness, and creating a safe, compassionate relationship supporting personal growth and transformation. My approach honors that each of us is unique, and that no one therapy approach is right for everyone. I work with clients to discover what they need and how to best support them in healing and thriving in their lives.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe in the human capacity to change, grow and cope with the painful challenges that life brings. We all have needs and strengths. Mental health issues arise when our attempts to meet our needs bring more suffering. I believe that we can deepen our understanding of how to best meet our needs, further our strengths, and grow our ability to live meaningful lives.

name: Jen Yerty
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Somatic Mindful Experiential Integrative
ideal_client: I'm a trauma specialist, with an emphasis on social justice. I work with clients with PTSD/complex PTSD, DID, depression, anxiety, mood/emotional dysregulation. I specialize in BIPOC and LGBTQ populations, somatic interventions, and trauma processing. Licensed in OR/WA/ID/FL. I run Zoom yoga groups: Monday Restorative 1-2pm Wednesdays Gentle 11-12 Yoga Nidra 2-3pm OHP covered/PacificSource/Moda/OOP accepted **Reduced rate spots available.** Message me for more details!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: You can change your own life. I view my role as guiding that process, to help you identify and process things that might be getting in the way of you becoming the best version of yourself. My work is based on hope, and a strong belief in every person's ability to change, grow, and heal themselves. I tailor the therapeutic experience to the client, but generally find success with somatic interventions, mindfulness, narrative, experiential, behavioral, emotion-focused process work, and yoga, influenced by Zen philosophy of acceptance, non-attachment, self-kindness, and non-judgment, and I feel strongly that therapeutic collaboration with clients is crucial to treatment. I'm originally from the Midwest but have lived on the East and West Coasts, so I talk fast, am direct but empathic, and swear a lot with clients who are comfortable with that. I've been in Portland for over a decade now, and I share a space with 3 (loud) cats and a dachshund.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I hold a CADC-I, and am trained in Somatic Experiencing and Brainspotting to facilitate trauma processing, and have a 200-RYT certification in yoga. Social justice is an important part of my therapeutic orientation and philosophy, and I prioritize working with marginalized populations, including LGBTQ and people of color. I have experience working with clients with complex trauma, dissociation, attachment challenges, mood disorders, psychosis, personality disorders, and marginalized populations, including BIPOC, LGBTQ+, and houseless populations. I received my Masters in Counseling Psychology at Santa Clara University (Santa Clara, CA) a Masters in Adult Education and Training, and my Bachelors in English Language & Literature at the University of Michigan (Ann Arbor).

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I have training in somatic and mindfulness techniques pioneered by Bessel van der Kolk, Stephen Porges, Pat Ogden, Ron Kurtz, Babette Rothschild, and Peter Levine. I have specific training in Somatic Experiencing. This practice involves a lot of silence as we slow down and listen to your system and how it reacts to the world around you. We begin to notice your system gently pendulating from positive to negative and back, and enhance ability to stay in a calm nervous system state.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: I use brainspotting as one way to process trauma. This modality is similar to EMDR but with some differences in procedure. What I like about it is that clients don't need to talk to process their trauma, and I've seen real results from clients who have undergone this treatment. It's very challenging work and not something I will do right away with clients, as I want folks to have a good understanding of their system and how to regulate before they go into a brainspotting intensive session.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I use a trauma-informed mindfulness practice that incorporates zen and cognitive behavioral techniques. This can include sitting and walking meditations, focused object practices, and mantras. I also integrate yoga into sessions, and offer hatha, restorative, beginner, and restorative yoga groups that are covered by insurance.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I find Internal Family Systems really helpful to better understand and have compassion for all of our parts, as we are all multiple. I work with IFS to connect with protective parts, exiled trauma parts, and managerial parts to create better communication with all parts of you.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am a certified trauma specialist through PESI, and have training in working with clients with PTSD, complex PTSD, and DID. I've also been asked to speak to graduate classes as a specialist in this field. I use a variety of techniques, but begin by working through Judith Herman's 3-stage process that prioritizes establishing safety before processing trauma and terminating treatment. I am trained in Somatic Experiencing, Brainspotting, and Accelerated Resolution Therapy for trauma processing.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I specialize in LGBTQ populations, including trans, non gender-conforming, and poly populations. I consider it an honor to be trusted by so many in this community. I have specialized training in working with LGBTQ populations, especially trans folks, and continue to update my training.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have experience working with a range of anxiety disorders. I generally work on coping skills using mindfulness, gradual exposure, processing (ART, brainspotting), and a zen focus, along with practical behavioral interventions.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I've worked extensively with depression, from mild to severe, and found that many people don't even know when that's what they're suffering from. I generally use CBT, experiential, and mindfulness practices to alleviate depression, and work with clients to find a purpose and meaning in their life, and find sources of support and happiness.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: 'To the privileged, equality feels like oppression.' Oppression takes on many forms in the lives of the oppressed, from financial challenges to negative self-talk, substance use to mental health challenges. Working on eliminating systemic oppression is a focus of my life and therapeutic work with clients.

name: Stacey Berry
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I primarily treat children and adolescents in OR and WA. I have recently transitioned to private practice and have immediate openings.
ideal_client: I welcome clients with anxiety, depression, functional symptoms, sleep difficulties, behavior problems, gender fluidity, and medical illnesses to see if, together, we can promote your wellness.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I prioritize connection and bringing myself into the room in order to facilitate comfort and rapport with my clients. I adapt how I work with clients based upon their age/developmental level and personality. I primarily utilize cognitive behavior therapy (CBT), behavior therapy (BT), and motivational interviewing (MI) techniques in session. It is a joy to help youth understand the way that the mind and the body are connected and to learn skills that will assist in their overall wellness.

name: Rochelle Schwartz
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I want to help you find your best self, and find meaning and joy in your life. To create a safe space for this transformation, I offer acceptance, deep and genuine empathy, humor when helpful, whole-hearted listening with a nonjudgmental disposition, and weekly skills to practice outside of session.

approaches: I believe we all have the inner resources to heal ourselves, and that sometimes we need help accessing those resources; I guide you in the discovery and application of those resources. Approaching therapy from a deeply compassionate, genuine, and sometimes humorous angle, I offer a client-centered approach. We talk about your goals, identify the obstacles getting in the way of your success, and develop tailored-to-you skills to help you through these barriers. When feels right to both of us, we assess progress made and discuss maintenance of changes so that you may sustain your progress without therapy. I approach each individual utilizing techniques from evidence based cognitive behavioral therapy and mindfulness-based stress reduction. Along the way, clients often find more peace, self-acceptance, understanding and life direction. Together, we work toward increasing your satisfaction with yourself and life. I find deep meaning in helping others, and am honored to do this work.

I have a background in multiple therapies such as cognitive-behavioral, mindfulness, existentialism, humanistic, dialectical behavioral therapy, ecotherapy, and collaborative problem solving. I have a Masters in Counseling, over six years in private practice, and 11 years of experience in a variety of mental health settings. Though I don't accept insurance, I'm able to provide you with all necessary information for you to do so yourself if paying out of pocket is not an option. I offer telemental health and phone sessions to help reduce travel time, traffic frustrations, cost of gas, as well as to serve those in rural areas and those who find it difficult to leave the house - please inquire if desired!

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Much of my approach stems from mindfulness - slowing down, connecting with the present, and noticing your thoughts and feelings without judgement. The first step in the process of change is awareness, and mindfulness is an incredibly useful tool in this. I've taken an 8-week training course on Mindfulness-based Stress Reduction, and have seen much change in clients when using this approach.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I am a very open, genuine, and honest person, professionally and personally. I believe that you are the expert on yourself, and that we all need a little clarity at times. I will help you put together the pieces of the puzzle that is you, to lead to a strong sense of self, of confidence, and of trust within yourself.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: My graduate education was largely based in CBT. I find it a useful tool in getting started, before digging deeper. Many clients have discovered irrational beliefs that have, til now, shaped their world view. Examining these can be a huge step towards change.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Many of us experience anxiety to a disruptive level at some point in our lives. And, you can control it. I provide skills and tools on how to cope and reduce anxiety. Through my education, experience, and passion, many clients have found relief and gained a greater sense of self control.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Self-esteem and confidence affects so many aspects of our lives, from our self image, to work, to relationships, to child rearing, etc. Many of us speak much worse to ourselves than we would tolerate from others, or do unto others. If you would like to be free from this self-torment, and feel more confidence and connected with your true self, I would love to help guide you in this.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: Some issues that we struggle with as adults begin in childhood, and many of us wish we would have learned strategies much earlier in life. Because of this, those aged 14+ is an area of passion for me. I have experience working with adolescents in my practice, as well as at an at-risk high school, and teen pregnancy shelter.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can be debilitating and draining, and it can also be alleviated. I have experience treating depression, with results. Because of my education and training, I can offer support and guide change towards peace within yourself.

specialities.name: Political Climate
specialities.description: Politics and climate degradation are two areas that are interlinked and anxiety-inducing. I am well studied on climate chaos and anxiety, and can help you process these hopeless and overwhelming thoughts and feelings.

name: Emily Ott, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: You can expect therapy with me to be warm, compassionate, honest, and direct with room for humor. I look forward to meeting you!
ideal_client: I specialize in working with clients who have symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), anxiety, depression, and OCD. I am interested in working with clients who are open and willing to explore how their experiences have informed their thoughts, feelings and behaviors. My hope is that we will be able to identify and possibly shift patterns that are no longer serving you, so that you can more often live in alignment with your unique values and goals moving forward.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide evidence-based treatments for adults who are interested in addressing symptoms of PTSD, OCD, anxiety and depression. I am trained in Cognitive Processing Therapy (CPT), Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), and well as Exposure Response and Prevention (ERP). The type of treatment modalities provided will be unique and tailored to each individual depending on symptoms and most appropriate approach. I also offer trauma-informed Yin style yoga classes to support healing and nervous system regulation in the body. I am a certified yoga instructor (200 RYT) and enjoy implementing gentle movement and breathing techniques to invoke the “rest and digest” parasympathetic nervous system that puts the body at ease. This can radically counter trauma-related symptoms and chronic stress, which so many of us experience throughout life.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Prior to moving to the PNW and becoming a mental health therapist, I was working in the New York City performing arts industry. While I still love the performing arts, the 2020 pandemic allowed me to reflect on my own values and goals, while also providing the time to go back to school for my Masters in Social Work from the University of Southern California. Similar to the performing arts, clinical social work includes the themes of valuing stories, cultivating empathy, and seeking to understand the human experience. This is a wonderful professional fit for me and I'm honored to have the opportunity to be a mental health provider.

name: Melissa DeForest (Peterson)
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Helping teens & adults overcome eating disorders, trauma, and relationship struggles by building self-compassion, resilience, and connection
ideal_client: I specialize in working with teens & adults struggling with eating disorder and body image issues, trauma, anxiety, depression, relationship and women's issues. I work with individuals seeking to gain insight into how past experiences may be causing present distress, in building emotional resilience, and in challenging shame. Whether an individual, intimate relationship, or family session, I help my clients achieve healthier relationships with themselves and those around them.

approaches.My Background: My experience in the mental health field started in 2012, where I began my work in higher levels of eating disorder treatment (residential, partial hospitalization, and intensive outpatient). Most recently, I served as Regional Director of Clinical Services for Monte Nido, where I oversaw all five treatment facilities in the state of Oregon. In this time, I gained extensive experience working with teens, adults, and families going through the eating disorder recovery journey, and am a Certified Eating Disorder Specialist-Consultant. My graduate training is in working with intimate partners and families, and I believe wholeheartedly that communication and connection is essential to the healing process. I am trained in Cognitive Processing Therapy, an evidence based approach to trauma. I am a registered supervisor for LPC and LMFT Associates in the state of Oregon. In addition to Oregon, I am licensed to see clients virtually in California and Washington.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe healing happens through relationships. My approach integrates attachment theory and emotion-focused therapy, focusing on authentic communication, emotional expression, and systemic change. I view each person as unique, shaped by their context, and believe behavior makes sense when considering one's life experiences. I help clients explore how unique systems, past experiences, and identities influence their lives, and collaboratively set goals for growth. As a HAES-informed, anti-diet, fat-positive provider, I am committed to respecting all bodies and challenging harmful societal expectations. I prioritize building strong, trustworthy, and collaborative relationships with my clients in order to support a safe space for emotional exploration, conflict resolution, and trauma processing. I believe in the possibility of change and growth for each of my clients. I see therapy as an opportunity for connection and I bring empathy, transparency, and humor to the space.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: As a Certified Eating Disorder Specialist-Consultant, I have 13 years of experience treating clients with anorexia, bulimia, binge ED, ARFID, and OSFED, and have worked in higher levels of care (intensive outpatient, partial hospitalization, and residential). I believe in full recovery and understand that eating disorders, while innately harmful, often provide emotional safety and a coping mechanism through difficult life experiences.

name: Laurel Barnes
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I work with adults of all ages, providing both in-person and virtual therapy.
ideal_client: What gets me excited is the opportunity to work with clients who are motivated to grow, change, and learn. It's important to me that clients I work with feel safe to be vulnerable and honest.

approaches.My Background: I've been a social worker since 2008, but before that I gained experience working in public health, and LGBT family advocacy. Since getting my MSW, I've worked in Child Welfare, and as a Medical Social Worker specializing in pediatric oncology. As a clinician, I work with clients around issues related to grief and loss, life transitions, adoption, neurodivergence, identity, family of origin, relationships, and chronic or life-limiting illness.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a person who carries a lot of privilege. I recognize that I am responsible for my own learning about the role I play in perpetuating oppression. I became a social worker specifically because I was interested in being an advocate for LGBT parents within the child welfare system. At that time, marriage equality was a big focus and I raised my voice for that purpose. As I've grown, and our culture has become more polarized, talking about the issues that matter to me and also affect all of our mental health, like misogyny, racism, ableism, weight-bias, classism, have come to play a bigger part of my practice.

name: Allison Amo MA, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Using a holistic approach, I work collaboratively with individuals, couples, families; supporting their path towards healing and wholeness.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide a collaborative and holistic mind-body approach to psychotherapy. I believe that every individual has an innate capacity to heal and deepen their connection to self/others. I offer practical tools to help you achieve a greater sense of growth and well-being and find relief from the unhealthy patterns that keep you stuck. It is my goal to create a safe and compassionate environment in which your unique strengths and resources can be accessed, and the negative experiences from the past that continue to affect the present can be uncovered and resolved. I specialize in working with adolescents and adults who experience relationship issues, depression, anxiety, trauma, substance abuse, and eating disorders. Within these modalities, I integrate EMDR, attachment theory, IFS, sensorimotor psychotherapy, and somatic based approaches to provide the most comprehensive and holistic care.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a master's degree in counseling psychology from Lewis & Clark College with an emphasis in Eating Disorders and Addiction. My training includes clinical experience in both partial hospitalization and outpatient levels of care with children, adolescents, and adults. I offer four years of experience in a partial hospitalization and intensive outpatient level of care as the Primary Therapist at the Eating Disorder Center of Portland and Program Director at Center for Discovery Portland Outpatient, which allowed me to work with an array of eating disorder symptoms and co-occurring conditions. I specialize in working with adolescents and adults who experience relationship issues, depression, anxiety, trauma, substance abuse, and eating disorders. NOT ACCEPTING NEW CLIENTS AT THIS TIME

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I strongly believe that our attachment experiences, from birth through adulthood, shape the way that we relate to ourselves and others. I will help you understand this lens through which you see the world, and open up possibilities for growth and healing, which ultimately leads to a more authentic and meaningful connections.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR is an integrative approach that helps facilitate a natural healing process in all individuals. EMDR has been extensively researched and proven to be effective in relieving all types of difficulties. The goal of EMDR is to leave you with the emotions, understanding, and perspectives that will lead to healthy/useful behaviors and interactions. EMDR can offer healing and empowerment.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: At the core, I believe that the past influences the present, and it is important to examine some of the deep roots that may be causing you issues as you move towards healing and growth. Counseling can provide you an opportunity to recognize and resolve these blocks and develop effective tools for working through them.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: If you are struggling with addiction, whether it be alcohol, prescription medication, sex, food, gambling, street drugs, or any other mood-altering experience, recovery is possible. Through therapy, I will support you in gaining insight into the function the addiction has served in your life, learn effective coping skills, and develop an increased sense of options and potential.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have extensive experience and training in issues around child and adolescent mental health issues, including eating disorders, body image issues, and substance abuse. Through therapy, I support children and young adults in expressing and exploring their lived experience and understanding of things, resolving emotional blocks, and ultimately, heal and grow.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: Eating disorders are complex as they directly impact our physical and emotional well-being. I believe that full recovery is possible and I am passionate about helping individuals regain balance and hope in all areas of their life. Through therapy, we can work towards understanding the function that the eating disorder has in your life and explore the emotions and patterns that contribute to it.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: If you are struggling with feelings of anxiety, panic attacks, or stress that feels unmanageable, counseling can provide an opportunity to not only learn new ways of coping and managing the anxiety and stress, but also offers you a space to gain insight into patterns that are keeping you stuck, and ultimately, bring healing and wholeness to yourself.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can be an isolating and hopeless experience, but there is hope. Through therapy, I can support you in gaining insight into the root causes of your depression, develop coping skills, and find healing and wholeness on the other side.

name: Esther Berg
title: Marriage and Family Therapist
intro: Ready to find peace and clarity in life's journey? Let's navigate challenges together and create a path to your well-being.
ideal_client: I work with introspective individuals and couples navigating anxiety, relationship struggles, life transitions, and questions of identity. Many of my clients feel stuck, overwhelmed, or disconnected. I offer a warm, grounded space to explore emotions, shift patterns, and reconnect with their authentic selves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe healing happens when we feel secure enough to turn inward and gently explore the layers of our experience, both the conscious and unconscious. My approach is warm, collaborative, and grounded in depth-oriented, somatic, narrative, and IFS-informed therapy. I meet you where you are, honoring your inner wisdom while offering gentle guidance to help you uncover patterns, heal emotional wounds, and reconnect with your authentic self. Together, we create space for new emotional experiences that promote self-trust, resilience, and deeper connection with others. I view therapy as a journey of remembering, reclaiming, and integrating the parts of yourself that have been left unseen or unheard.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Trained in emotionally focused therapy, I guide individuals on a journey of self-discovery, healing deep emotional wounds, & boosting self-esteem by looking at how past attachments have shaped your emotional world. We'll explore how your emotions can be harnessed as potent tools for personal growth. With couples & relationships, I assist partners in unraveling how their attachment styles impact their interaction, promoting emotional closeness & healing the scars of attachment-related experiences

name: Christa Loveland
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi My Name is Christa Loveland LCSW, I am excited to help you to identify and reach your goals!
ideal_client: I work well with all people that are ready to heal and transform ! I believe each person is capable of healing no matter what their history is. Many of my clients are survivors of trauma and have symtoms of anxiety , depression and emotinal dys regulation , I use a varieity of interventions to help them identify the best tools to help them heal, Incuding DBT,CBT, psyco- analaysis , dream work, expresive therapies
