approaches.My Background and Approach: I am an LCSW and received my education from the University of Oregon and Portland State University I graduated from the Graduate School of Social Work at PSU and am licensed as an LCSW with the state of Oregon . I have worked in many settings including community mental health and non profits serving children and families . family therapy. I have more recently over the last five years worked with families in need of re unification and I have also worked with addictions and strenght based approchs to supporting folks in recovery and have a CADC licence . I have worked and advocated for my clients within multiple systems including DHS child welfare, family court, and victims servicies , I have worked with children and families that have experienced multiple layers abuse.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a personal belief in the human spirit and the power of the individual to heal. I strongly support survivors of all traumas and feel honored to be trusted as part of that healing process. Under the right circumstances I believe that trauma and be transformed in to creativity and healing. I have training in DBT, CBT, Psychoanalysis, Dream work and expressive therapies. I look forward to using my combination of experience education and passion for healing to help you transform your trauma and begin to live the life that you want to live.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have worked for over 15 years with families that have experienced trauma ,abuse and family loss. I have worked with

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Over the last 5 years I have provided support, therapy and resources for families in need of reunification and family therapy

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have many years of experience in working through anxiety with populations of folks experiencing anxiety , I often use DBT , guided meditations ,breathing and grounding exercises and dream work to address this issues I have taken many trainings and have years of experience

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I have many years of experience treating depression successfully! different tools work for people and I like to offer things to try and then get feedback on what is working so we can focus on that.

name: Margot Standeven
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: Masters in Marriage, Couple, & Family Counseling
intro: I hope to motivate you to take constructive risks to promote self-understanding and encourage a new way of connecting with others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Being resilient allows you to recover and adapt to difficult experiences. Instead of being overwhelmed, the resilient person is able to manage their strong feelings and impulses and communicate their concerns and needs. Resilience is not a trait that you either have or do not have. It involves behaviors, thoughts, and emotions that can be learned and developed in all of us. Couples who are resilient are open, attuned, and responsive to each other. They are able to recognize their deepest needs and longings, and risk reaching out to their partner to communicate and connect. Most often, couples who develop an enhanced emotional connection also experience greater intimacy and sexual satisfaction.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received a B.Ed from McGill University in Montreal, Canada and earned my Master’s degree in Marriage, Couple, and Family Counseling at George Fox University in Portland, Oregon. After graduation, I spent five years volunteering at William Temple House before launching my private practice. I have obtained advanced training in Emotionally Focused Therapy ad have worked primarily with couples over the past decade.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: We each have a particular attachment style that determines how comfortable we are in proximity to others. Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT) helps couples understand the attachment style of each partner and the dynamic that exists between them.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Our work together would help each partner understand their part in the couple’s negative cycle and create vulnerable communication, so as to create a stronger couple bond.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: EFT helps couples recognize and understand the negative cycle that interferes with their communication. With this awareness, less time and energy is spent on regulating negative emotions and protecting individual vulnerabilities. Instead, the partners can turn to each other for comfort and support so as to be resilient and meet life’s challenges

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in couple counseling and the interactions between partners, with extensive training and supervision in Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT).

name: Leslie Yeargers
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: LPC, LMFT, Certified Sex Informed Couples Counselor
intro: I am an LPC and LMFT who has a passion for working with couples and families.
ideal_client: Do you experience stress in your relationships? Do you wish you could communicate better, understand your partner on a deeper level, and feel more connected? Maybe your partner or child is exploring their sexuality, gender identity or actively transitioning. These are unique experiences that call for a unique set of skills. I work with couples and families from all walks of life to heal their relationships and form deeper connections.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have a Master's in Applied Behavioral Science with an emphasis in Family Systems Counseling from the Leadership Institute of Seattle (LIOS) program. I also have a background as a job search coach and career counselor. I know the impact issues related to work and job-seeking can have on your self-confidence and your relationships. I apply trauma-informed, narrative family systems theory, internal family systems, emotion-focused techniques, and Gottman tools to help your intimate or family relationships feel more connected, grounded, and supportive. I have a client-centered, humanistic, collaborative, and when necessary, directive approach to support you and your loved ones on your journey to find more meaning in your lives together. I am also a certified sex informed couples therapist and am EMDRIA trained-- EMDR can be a powerful modality for resolving trauma and cognitive/emotional/behavioral patterns that impact your relationships.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe we are relational, spiritual beings in search of connection, expression, purpose and growth. As such, the quality of our relationships to our selves, partners, friends, extended family, pets, nature and work environments affect our personal identities and overall well-being. I see my role as helping people build deep connection with themselves and their loved ones to more deeply express their uniqueness and purpose in the world. As a cisgender, heterosexual provider with LGBTQIA friends and family, I want you and your family to know you are not alone in your experience of living with identities outside of societal norms. As a family systems counselor, I want to do what I can to help you and your family repair, and then build, your connection so that you can live authentically with mutual love and support.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Whether you are wanting to strengthen your relationship or end it well, I strive to listen to what your relationship goals are and work with you collaboratively to help you meet those goals. I work to help your resolve misunderstanding and sort out the emotions you bring to your interactions with each other.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: Families take on a life and dynamic of their own. Sometimes a family can be deeply impacted by outside stressors or when a member is struggling. Through deep listening, I help you sort out what's going on in your family and assist in helping you develop resilience and deeper connection.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: Every person, couple, and family are unique and therefore require individual approaches. My training includes a variety of theories and techniques ranging from solution-focused, to narrative, to multi-generational family exploration. With couples, I draw for tools and concepts of the Gottman method and Emotion-Focused Therapy. Regardless of technique, I endeavor to deeply listen and use my skills and training to help you achieve your therapeutic goals.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am EMDRIA trained in both EMDR and Flash Technique, both powerful and effective methods for processing trauma. I also use EMDR in a couple setting when appropriate, to help couples move through unresolved traumas that are impacting the relationship. Provided the foundation of the relationship is strong, it can feel supportive and affirming to have your partner witness your trauma healing process.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I have taken several self-study trainings in IFS and incorporate it into my practice to heal parts of ourselves that have been neglected due to trauma.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I support the transgender, non-binary, and LGBTQ community with living in the world as their authentic selves. I also work with their families and loved ones to foster deeper connection and understanding of one another.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: Being transgender or non-binary presents a unique set of personal and social challenges. Simply stated, our society has not caught up with what it means to identify as a gender other than the one you were assigned at birth. When a family member transitions, it can put a strain on family dynamics. To that end, I support all family members in the transitioning process to build understanding and deepen familty connection.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Sometimes the pressures of the world can affect our family relationships. Busy parents may lose touch with their children and children may be stressed by school, peer pressure, and academic and social expectations. This can lead to conflict in the family. I strive to deeply listen to each member to understand your dynamic and shift to healthier relational patterns that foster love and connection.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Over time, we can lose the connection with our partner that brought us together in the first place. We become emotionally distant and out of touch with each other. By using emotion focused, non-violent communication, and integrative couples and sex therapy, I strive to help you strengthen your connection to each other and deepen your relationship.

name: Lily Suhanovsky
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I offer holistic, compassionate therapy sessions blending psychology, somatics, brainspotting, spirituality & neuroscience to support you
ideal_client: I support individuals who feel overwhelmed, disconnected, or caught in cycles that no longer align with their true selves. Many of my clients navigate anxiety, life transitions, relationship challenges, trauma, or self-worth struggles. I work well with highly sensitive people and those seeking deeper self-awareness. With deep presence and compassion, I hold space for healing, emotional regulation, and self-acceptance, helping you cultivate greater harmony and authenticity in your life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I take an integrative, holistic approach to therapy, drawing from psychodynamic, somatic, and relational-cultural perspectives. We explore not just your current struggles but also the deeper patterns and life experiences that have shaped you. My work is rooted in presence, compassion, and honoring your innate wisdom—believing healing comes from reconnecting with parts of yourself that may have been disowned or unacknowledged. In sessions, we focus on shifting distressing patterns, processing emotions, cultivating self-compassion, and engaging in grounding or movement-based practices to regulate your nervous system. I integrate neuroscience and somatic awareness to deepen your mind-body connection, build emotional resilience, and create lasting change. The therapeutic relationship is a powerful container for healing. Through warmth and collaboration, I support you in reconnecting with your intuition, empowering you to live authentically and create greater harmony in your life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a Master of Arts in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis & Clark Graduate School of Education and Counseling, alongside a Bachelor of Science in Neuroscience from Union College. My studies included interpersonal neurobiology and Polyvagal Theory, which inform my work with the mind-body connection. I am also trained in Brainspotting through the Pacific Trauma Institute, which allows me to support clients in processing trauma. Additional certifications in Yin Yoga and Yoga for Trauma further enrich my holistic approach to healing.

name: Lucia Kilday
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I am an ANCC board-certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner with a Master’s degree from The George Washington University.
ideal_client: I have a trauma-informed approach and treat people of every educational, socioeconomic, and ethnic background, as well as every sexual orientation. I treat patients ages 16 and up in the states of OR, WA, and UT. I specialize in treating Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD) and eating disorders, areas where I have developed expertise and a deep understanding of the challenges individuals face. I am certified in Exposure and Response Prevention therapy, an evidence-based approach for OCD.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I believe in the power of collaboration and empowerment in mental health treatment. I work closely with my patients to develop personalized treatment plans that integrate medication management, therapy, lifestyle modifications, and complementary therapies. My goal is to not only alleviate symptoms but also to promote long-term mental health and well-being. I am dedicated to staying current with the latest research and best practices in psychiatric care to provide my patients with the highest quality of care. I look forward to partnering with you on your journey to mental wellness.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am dedicated to staying current with the latest research and best practices in psychiatric care to provide my patients with the highest quality of care. I look forward to partnering with you on your journey to mental wellness.

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: I am certified in Exposure and Response Prevention (EXRP) therapy, an evidence-based approach for managing OCD symptoms.

name: Bronwyn Santaella
title: Student Counselor
intro: Working towards food freedom and body trust is a radical act.
ideal_client: Having recovered from an eating disorder myself - I know all too well the impact this disorder can have on all aspects of life. My ideal client is an adolescent or young adult struggling with an eating disorder, body image issues, or disordered eating patterns. I provide a supportive, nonjudgmental space to explore the emotions, stress, and life transitions that often underlie these struggles. I’m here to help you reconnect with yourself, build trust in your body, and move toward healing.

approaches.My Background: I hold a BA in Feminist Theory from UC Santa Cruz, where I developed a deep understanding of the complex intersections between identity, culture, and the body—foundational to the work I do today. Over the past five years, I’ve worked extensively in all levels of eating disorder care, including residential treatment, partial hospitalization programs, and intensive outpatient programs. This experience has given me a comprehensive, trauma-informed perspective on the recovery process and the many ways disordered eating can manifest and evolve. I’ve supported clients through the full spectrum of eating disorders, including anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder, and ARFID. My approach is relational, intersectional, and rooted in social justice. I strive to create a space where clients feel seen and supported as whole people—not just diagnoses. I’m especially passionate about working with adolescents and young adults who are ready to begin or deepen their healing journey.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I come to this work with a deep commitment to fostering empowerment, radical self-love, and liberation for my clients. My approach is grounded in the belief that healing from an eating disorder isn’t just about food, it’s about reclaiming your body, your voice, and your right to exist unapologetically. My politics and background in feminist theory shape the way I see and support my clients. I recognize the systems of patriarchy, capitalism, and white supremacy that fuel disordered relationships with food and body image. I believe recovery is a political act, and I work to create a space where clients feel safe to explore not only their personal narratives, but also the societal messages they’ve internalized. I'm passionate about working with adolescents and young adults because I believe in their power to disrupt harmful norms and build something more authentic. Together, we’ll work to unlearn shame and rebuild a foundation of compassion, strength, and self-defined worth.

name: Sarah Mustafa
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: My passion is to support & empower individuals, couples, and families as their co-pilot on their journey to healing & offer a path forward.
ideal_client: I am delighted that you found the courage to consider what could be your first brave step to seeing a different perspective for change in your life. I love working with a wide range of people, including depression & anxiety, sex & relationship challenges, trauma, and stress management. I like for potential clients to know that therapy will be challenging but hopefully rewarding. So, I hope to co-create an inviting space for you to freely express yourself & explore the depths of your emotions.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer individual, couple, and family therapy. My style is interactive, cultural, empathic, warm, direct, and intuitive. I share the premise that human behavior occurs within family, social, and cultural contexts. Additionally, I have a multicultural approach that bridges cultures of all kinds allowing for understanding and sensitivity to help clients feel more comfortable being understood and validated in their experience. Finally, I know the importance of understanding how race, gender, social class, sexual orientation, abilities, language, country of origin, and other social identities/locations intersect to maintain systems of power and privilege within couples, families, and communities. With that, I value a therapy that is non-pathologizing, non-blaming, and sees clients as experts in their own lives. So, as your therapist, my motto is to be your co-pilot to help support clients in increasing their self-compassion and self-confidence to achieve the life goals they desire.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have always been interested in relationships & what it takes to make them work. I come from a big family with many siblings and parents from different cultures. So I have grown up with an ongoing urge to learn how to navigate multiple relationships and be a part of two different cultures. Relationships of all kinds can be tricky & source exceptional joy & significant discomfort. Working with families and couples to connect well and find comfort with differences has been rewarding work. I support individuals to learn to have the courage to speak their truth with honesty and compassion. Feelings are complex. Creating understanding for people to create authentic conversations and emotionally healthy relationships can make room for connecting better to find a solution. As a multiracial person of color (Saudi Arabian & Black American), I cherish culture's uniqueness in people's lives. My cultural background has allowed me to be sensitive to cultural diversity & appreciate all cultures.

name: Breena Beck
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Trauma-informed therapist supporting individuals & couples, providing inclusive, affirming, and non-judgmental support.
ideal_client: I support people who are experiencing life transitions and times of change. I believe that you can't have change without some loss and it is important to have a space where you can process the complicated feelings that come up along the way. I feel passionate about supporting those who are becoming new parents and who are in the pregnancy/postpartum period. I have a great deal of experience working with anxiety, depression, and trauma and I really enjoy working with couples.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I’m a trauma-informed therapist & I utilize various therapeutic interventions including EMDR, Emotionally Focused Therapy, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, & Mindfulness. I encourage clients to focus inward & practice compassionate accountability. I support clients as they learn to allow emotions to inform rather than control. I received my master’s degree in Social Work from New York University. I’ve worked in various settings including schools, outpatient mental health clinics, & private practice. I have provided therapy to individuals, groups, & families of many different backgrounds, with a variety of mental health challenges. I am committed to creating a space that is inclusive & affirming to all who seek support.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I value honesty, transparency, compassion and humor as a therapist. I prioritize taking time to build a strong, trusting relationship with my clients. I want to understand as much as possible about who you are and how your experiences have shaped you in order to best support you.

name: Nina Landey
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work to help you free yourself from ways of being that aren't working for you and help you step into how you prefer to live your life.
ideal_client: We should have a “good fit” which is why I offer free consultation. I love working with people at any stage of relationship, especially supporting communication. I am warm, direct (native New Yorker), collaborative, and work well with creative people; I often will use metaphor and imagery. I am at ease talking about sex and gender, and love helping people release shame. I'm not a good fit for those needing higher levels of support as I may take weeks off at a time in the summer.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I integrate mindful, experiential techniques into my work from attachment therapy, EMDR, and Hakomi. I believe all people come into the world with potential to be their best, authentic selves. We then have experiences from which we develop beliefs about the world and strategies for how to navigate through it. These become a template for living our lives and we often apply them to situations and relationships where they don't work. Together, we will work to reveal deeply held beliefs that may be blocking you. In my view, these beliefs solidified in response to emotional wounding in childhood, or to trauma. In a safe environment, I will provide support, empathy, and understanding. Our relationship can be a foundation for safe exploration and evolution. Together, we may be able to fill in missing experiences or reprocess traumas that have formed limiting beliefs. With experience and support, you can reset your patterns and experience more fulfilling ways of interacting with the world.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC). I earned an M.S from Portland State University, where I focused on marital, couples and family therapy. I have had professional training in the Hakomi Method, RC-S, and Primary Attachment Therapy from M.E.T.A., where I also completed a year-long internship. I have completed full basic training in EMDR, along with Flash Technique and Attachment Focused EMDR. I also have training in grief counseling from The Dougy Center for Grieving Children and Families, where I was a volunteer facilitator. Before this, I earned a B.A. in English-Theatre from Barnard College and an M.F.A from the Yale School of Drama. I only see people via telehealth, so if you are looking for in-person sessions, I wouldn't be a good fit. I'm happy to work with couples/relationship clients who are in different locations in Oregon.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I believe everyone can benefit from therapy. Self-study can illuminate patterns of behavior and thinking that have been holding you back from a more satisfying life. I believe that you can transform the beliefs that have limited your internal experience and your relationships and you can learn more fulfilling ways of interacting with the world.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I have helped younger and older queer couples and individuals. I welcome people with any gender or sexual identity and expression. I am completely affirming of LGBTQIA+ individuals and couples. You are safe with me.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I focused on relationship issues in my Master's degree in Marriage, Couple, and Family Counseling. I love working with people at all stages of relationships; pre-commitment, during parenting, and in high conflict times. I am happy to work with you on navigating communication, sexual issues, infidelity, parenting conflicts, or exploring the future of your relationship. I work with all kinds of relationships, including poly, co-parenting, adult child/parent, and bands/artists.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Your feeling of safety is paramount. We will move at a pace that is right for you to first find safety, and then reprocess traumatic memories that are affecting your life. I am fully basic trained in EMDR and Attachment Focused EMDR. I may also be a good fit for processing a single incident trauma (ex. accident, medical trauma, single incident humiliation, specific phobia). Make an appointment for a consultation to see if we are a good fit and to learn more about how we can find relief for you.

name: Preston Turner
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Howdy! I've 7+ years experience with teens/young adults working through OCD, Anxiety, Depression, and more. Find, love & live your values :)
ideal_client: I work with anyone and everyone open to learning about themselves and how to promote & sustain change in their lives. My practice is guided by Collaboration, Creativity, Accountability, Acceptance, & Patience. Whether this is your first time, don't know where to begin, or need help reaching your goals, we will work together to make the change process serve you best. While I work with people across the lifespan, I have a specialty working with adolescents and their family, particularly with OCD.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our time together starts by exploring your values and learning how we can make the therapy process align best with you, ironing out the wrinkles standing in your way. While our initial sessions together are more structured, later sessions will reflect a structure that best suits you. During our initial consultation, we discuss what you'd like from treatment and see if we're a good fit. Afterwards, during our 50-minute intake session we learn more about each other and establish a treatment plan allowing us to stay mindful of your goals, how we reach them, and how they change. I often encourage my clients to practice certain exercises outside of session to nurture relevant skills and experiences to best serve their treatment goals. Additionally, I reserve multiple reduced-fee slots in my caseload for those needing assistance.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Openness and acceptance of uncertainty is key to how I grow and learn. It allows me to act and learn from experience rather than worry, and find new insights. Whether this leads me to gain unexpected skills and perspective from an eclectic source of hobbies like bouldering, tufting rugs, roasting coffee, or building instruments, to incorporating an eclectic approach to treatment, branching insights and concepts from across disciplines. Among the various things I am interested to learn more about, one example is the intersection of behavioral strategies with music therapy.

name: Lewis & Clark Community Counseling Center
title: Student Counselor
intro: Providing low-cost, culturally sensitive and affirming counseling and therapy services. Proudly serving Portland and the greater metro area.
ideal_client: We work with clients across the lifespan: youth (K-12), adults and families. Our therapist-trainees and counselors-in-training are ready to meet you wherever life finds you.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: The Lewis & Clark Community Counseling Center provides low-cost counseling and therapy services that are culturally sensitive and designed to help with challenges including, but not limited to: depression, sexual intimacy, stress, marriage and family problems, domestic violence, experiences of oppression or injustice, substance abuse, problem gambling, eating disorders, school or career concerns, and trauma. All therapeutic services are strictly confidential and are available in English; limited services are available in Spanish. We provide individual, couple, family, and group therapy options.

approaches.More About the People We Treat: We share the space with the Lewis & Clark Problem Gambling Services (PGS), who aim to relieve the suffering associated with problem gambling by providing high quality treatment to individuals, couples, and families. All PGS services are free and confidential. We are dedicated to supporting social equity by providing easily accessible and culturally sensitive treatment. As a graduate training and research center, our interdisciplinary team is charged with developing innovative and effective approaches to treatment, sharing what we learn with others, and training the next generation of problem gambling treatment providers. We also offer Sex Therapy services, which addresses wide-ranging issues concerning sexuality and relationships. Sex Therapy at the Lewis and Clark Clinic aims to increase awareness and action in regards to sexual oppression.

name: Hanh Nguyen
title: Professional Counselor
intro: I'm counseling intern passionate about supporting adults navigating anxiety, grief, life transitions, and identity exploration.
ideal_client: Do you ever feel like you're holding everything together on the outside while quietly unraveling inside? Maybe you're the strong one in your family or community, but you’re exhausted. You might be navigating anxiety, grief, or life transitions that have left you feeling unmoored. I work with adults—especially women and BIPOC clients—who are ready to reconnect with themselves and explore their stories in a space that honors their identity, resilience, and complexities.

approaches.My Background: As a counseling intern earning my Master of Arts in Counseling at Northwestern University, I’ve had the privilege of furthering my education and honing my skills working with adults navigating anxiety, depression, grief, and life transitions. My clinical experience includes supporting individuals in crisis settings, facilitating therapeutic groups, and offering one-on-one support to help clients feel grounded and empowered.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe healing happens in community and that therapy can be a space to come home to yourself. As a first-generation Vietnamese American woman, I understand how identity, culture, and intergenerational experiences shape the way we move through the world. I’m committed to practicing from an anti-oppressive, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive lens. I care deeply about advocating for marginalized communities, particularly BIPOC, LGBTQIA+ folks, and children of immigrants. Outside of the therapy room, I love movies, arts and crafts, and spending time with my dog Tofu and my cat Margot. I believe in the power of softness, laughter, and storytelling as part of the healing process.

name: Molly Young
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: Welcome! I'm Dr. Young (they/them). I am a Licensed Psychologist & Sex Therapist serving erotically marginalized clients in OR & WA.
ideal_client: I provide affirming sex and relationship therapy for partners who are 21+ and identify as queer, gender-expansive, kinky, and/or non-monogamous. Common areas of focus include identity development related to gender, sexuality, and relationship structures; exploration of kink and BDSM; navigating non-monogamy; addressing communication difficulties arising from chronic misattunement; and tending to the impact of relational and sexual trauma.

approaches.My Background: I received my Master of Arts degree in Clinical Psychology and my Doctorate of Psychology in Clinical Psychology from Pacific University in Oregon. My graduate research focused on exploring psychologists’ cultural competence in working with clients engaged in kink/BDSM. I have completed 200+ hours of additional training in the Holistic Sex Therapy training program through the Institute for Sexuality Education & Enlightenment.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I take a sex-positive, trauma-informed, and liberation-centered approach to mental and sexual health. I affirm all consensual sexual expression while honoring asexual and aromatic identities. My goal is to create a space that challenges shame, resists pathologization, and empowers clients to embrace their authentic selves, desires, and sexual agency.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I integrate attachment theory into sex and relationship therapy to support clients in making sense of how past experiences—especially in early relationships—can influence how we connect, communicate, and experience intimacy today.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Grounded in feminist theory, I’m especially passionate about supporting those who are erotically marginalized—including queer, trans, kinky, polyamorous, disabled folx, and sex workers whose desires or identities fall outside of mainstream norms. In our work together, we can explore the ways culture, power, and oppression shape our access to pleasure, safety, and sexual self-expression.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Drawing from relational-cultural therapy, I focus on healing through connection. Trauma and shame often thrive in isolation, especially around sex and intimacy. Together, we can work to rebuild trust—in yourself and in your relationships—by fostering mutuality, emotional safety, and meaningful connection.

name: Veronica Carmenate
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: The journey to creating awareness and change is guided through a supportive and collaborative therapeutic relationship.
ideal_client: Do you struggle with navigating the relationships in your life; both the ones you have with others and the one you have with yourself? This struggle affects our ability to connect with others, our self-perception, and the way we talk to ourselves about our world. Do you wonder if navigating these relationships can be easier? That you can feel more grounded? More in control? Now more than ever people are struggling to approach their relationships in ways that feel authentic and meaningful.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe it is possible to be in relation with others and ourselves in a way that is grounded and intentional. I provide support for navigating relationships in three avenues: Parenting support specializing in parenting with childhood trauma, being a cycle breaking parent, parenting with anxiety, emotional regulation in the parenting role, strategies for instilling emotional intelligence in children, and strategies for instilling self-empowerment in children. Couples therapy specializing in ethical non-monogamy, boundary setting, and communication strategies. Individual therapy specializing in anxiety and life transitions, identity, and relational challenges.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: Together we will raise awareness to faulty relational patterns, identify ineffective thought processes, and improve clarity in self understanding to create grounded and genuine relationships with ourselves and others. I offer a sliding scale fee and can provide a superbill for insurance reimbursement. Please contact me to discuss these options.

name: Emily Yang
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi there, I’m Emily (she/her). Healing and hope are possible, and we can find it together.
ideal_client: I often work with clients seeking to deepen an understanding of themselves and build strong skills around navigating the "big things" in life. I specialize in working with new parents, students, women, folx navigating religious deconstruction, and BIPOC individuals. You might be someone who is exhausted from looking for a therapist who looks even a little like you. Maybe you are feeling anxiety, grief, heaviness, sadness, and even anger about..everything. You may be someone at a crossroads with

approaches.My Background and Approach: My priority is to create a space that feels safe and comfortable for you to bring your full self to the counseling room. This means holding space for your wins, losses, joy, and pain. I take a collaborative approach and enjoy utilizing a relational and emotionally focused approach. I may also utilize behavioral approaches when helpful. Healing and hope are possible, and we can find it together.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: My desire to become a therapist began when I walked through my own spiritual and cultural deconstruction, which led to first hand experience of my own depression and anxiety. Part of my healing has been creating space to advocate for my intersectional identities as a second generation Taiwanese American woman and mother, and process the grief that comes from institutional religious and emotional trauma. Now, I believe uncertainty can feel clear, our stories are nuanced, and healing is collective.

name: Kathleen Thompson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Let's explore what could be and how to be you.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have a very process, relational style. I am trained in many different methods to help people understand why we do what we do & to learn betters ways of coping & relating. How we learned to connect to others in our early years impacts us everyday. Let's work on new ways of connecting & being in the world.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have training in Career Counseling, Addiction recovery & relapse prevention; couples therapy & attachment styles; Healing from trauma including EMDR & Lifespan Integration. I also work with adults who are neuro-diverse (Autism) including testing/assessment. Let's work together to build strong relationships or find meaningful work.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment Theory is about discovering that how a person was cared for & related to in their early years still effects us. When we were young we learned if the world was safe or not. To make us feel safe we isolated or became people pleasers. These patterns continue on into adulthood & can be very disruptive to relationships. There are ways to feel emotionally safe so you can thrive.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR is becoming widely used to treat trauma. This method helps the body reveal what has been hidden from our consciousness related to past trauma or painful events.Chronic overwhelming feelings often indicate the body is working hard to manage outward stress/experiences while managing inward fears from the past. It is possible to feel more at ease in your body as well as move forward in life.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: For over 100 years the field of Psychology has made the patient/client feel like they were the problem. What would it mean if you realized that the role you took on as a child is still impacting you today. Many people do not realize that when it comes to family dynamics we actually had few choices in how to act or be. By examining your family system we can discover the authentic you.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Humans do not want to feel pain & love to repeat things that feel good. Every person I know who misuses substances/gaming/sex/gambling has been to avoiding bad feelings generally related to their past. Add the chemical component in our bodies & you get people who keep doing what they should not do despite how much loved ones beg for it to stop. It is time for you to start feeling & living better.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Very often people feel stuck in their work OR feel like their career has not even started. Being in a job that is a poor fit can be frustrating & even lead to depression. This impacts our personal life & relationships. Further, the rapid advancement in technology is creating new opportunities, but can seem overwhelming to know where to start. Lets put our heads together to see what is possible.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I generally work with individuals, but what we talk about is their relationships. Like it or not how people related to us in our early life generally continues to impact our adult relating until we can recognize patterns & learn to manage the flood of emotions that can erupt when we are with the people you love most. Let's work together to repair old & more recent relationships.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: There is so much new information coming at us about PTSD. Basically, it is when we feel hi-jacked by our senses/body because of past events that were (or seemed) life threatening. These experiences can be from combat, Domestic abuse, accidents, but more often from chronic difficult childhood experiences. It is time for you to heal.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: Many adults wonder if they have Aspergers or Autism because work isn't going well, relationships are a struggle & stress is difficult to manage. Understanding how your brain & body works is the most important way to move forward. We can work together to determine if you are neurodiverse & to find your niche vocationally as well as building confidence in relationships.

name: Sabrina Sheehy
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My therapeutic style is empathic, relational, and humanistic. I work from an attachment-based framework to examine self and relationships.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I primarily view treatment through an attachment lens, however I also have training in various modalities, including Cognitive-Behavioral, Solution-Focused, Humanistic, Relational, and Trauma-Informed therapy. Having a background in clinical social work means I see each client in a holistic way, with the understanding that ones' community and family systems impact their overall well-being. I have worked with adults, children, and families in both schools and in community mental health settings. I have a gained specialty training and practice in working in perinatal mental health and have enjoyed supporting birthing individuals and their partners during pregnancy and the post-partum period. Experienced in serving the LGBTQIA+ community, I enjoy helping individuals navigating life transitions, whether it be more fully expressing one's gender or coming to terms with one's sexual orientation later in life. I also work with providers in the medical and mental health community.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a proud and passionate member of and advocate for the LGTBQIA+ community and welcome clients of all sexual orientations and/or gender identities. I also strive to live and practice with an anti-racist framework, and actively look for opportunities to become a more knowledgeable and competent advocate for racial justice and disability justice.

name: Emily Haygeman
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Neurodiverse-affirming. Currently accepting clients for Psychological Evaluation and Independent Educational Evaluations, ages 3 to adult.
ideal_client: I offer comprehensive psychological evaluations (for adults and children) for autism, nonverbal learning disorders, learning disabilities, ADHD, and anxiety, depression, and mental health, and giftedness, including Independent Educational Evaluations. I approach all evaluations, including those for autism, from a strengths-based, neurodiverse-affirming, trauma-informed, and LGBTQ+ affirming perspective.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: With over 15 years of experience working directly with families and children, I offer a compassionate and integrated approach through a variety of evidence-based modalities. My quality psychological evaluations result in a comprehensive psychological report, and I aim to "tell the story" of an individual rather than simply assign a "label." All evaluations yield individualized recommendations for home, school, and therapeutic environments. Following evaluation, I provide a client-centered, in-depth feedback session aimed at empowerment. I closely follow the work of autistic self-advocates and leaders in the area of neurodivergence such as Dr. Devon Price and Dr. Nick Walker. I am constantly improving my work through self-reflection, learning, reading, and advocacy. For adult autism evaluations, I utilize measures that are appropriate for adults rather than relying on measures best suited for children. I recognize populations that have been left out of our diagnostic samples.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that psychological evaluation should be a therapeutic process. I am an advocate for my clients, and see the evaluation process as an opportunity to empower an individual to know their strengths and challenges. I don't believe in simply assigning a diagnosis. All of my evaluations offer more than simply diagnostic clarity. I am a member of the LGBTQIA2S+ community and take an affirming approach in regard to my clients' identities. My services are trauma-informed. I also understand that as a white psychologist, I have been afforded much privilege in my life. The field of psychology has a varied past in that direct harm has been done, particularly to BIPOC and indigenous populations. I am committed to understanding these issues in an ongoing capacity in order to mitigate the impact of my biases and privilege on my clients' experience.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I offer up-to-date psychological evaluations for a range of neurodivergent presentations including autism, ADHD, Nonverbal Learning Disabilities and other learning disabilities, as well as mental health presentations including anxiety, depression, and PTSD. I am also available for Independent Educational Evaluations (IEE) and giftedness evaluations.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have years of experience assessing for and treating anxiety disorders in children and adolescents.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I offer in-depth psychological evaluations and Independent Educational Evaluations (IEE) to assess for the presence of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder and related executive functioning differences in children and adults.

specialities.name: Aspergers
specialities.description: I have over 10 years of experience working with children, teens, and young adults with Autism, including Autism Level 1 (previously referrred to as Aspergers). I lead social empowerment groups for children and adolescents. I currently offer autism evaluations for children, teens, and adults.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I have over 15 years of experience working directly with autistic children, teens, and adults. I am neurodivergent myself and offer an empowering approach. I follow the work of autistic self-advocates and work from the lens of the neurodiversity model.

name: Kat T. Kosmos
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: Hey there, my name is Kat Kosmos. I identify as a gender non-binary (they/them) psychologist. I'm glad you're here.
ideal_client: I work with individuals navigating gender identity, anxiety, depression, trauma, and relationship challenges. My clients include LGBTQIA+ individuals, those exploring their gender or sexual identity, and anyone seeking more authenticity and fulfillment. I offer a safe, non-judgmental space to explore your unique experiences and emotions. Together, we’ll work on strategies for growth, healing, and empowerment, meeting you where you are to support your journey toward self-discovery and well-being

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am committed to co-creating a compassionate, affirming, and non-judgmental space for individuals from all walks of life. I believe in building a collaborative space where your unique experiences, struggles, and celebrations are honored. I understand that life can feel overwhelming at times. I aim to help build a supportive space where you can express yourself freely, identify and express your feelings, as you work towards growth, healing and radical self-love. My therapeutic style is grounded in evidence-based practices, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and mindfulness techniques. Together, we will create a personalized plan that honors your individuality and helps you build resilience, clarity, and self-awareness.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Being human means we're always learning about ourselves in the contexts that we find ourselves in. Sometimes, that can be really overwhelming when we attach parts of ourselves to the learning process. We can find ourselves saying, "It's too late for me to learn this," or, "I should have known this [XXX] years ago." I hold the firm belief that this ability to learn, and unlearn, is something to be celebrated. It is through learning that we nurture our growth edges to becoming our authentic selves. We all have growth edges that need self-compassion and nurturing! Together, it is my goal that we unlearn some of the ways we have interacted with these areas of growth and help you move towards authenticity and healing.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I have experience navigating Gender Identity both professionally and personally. I have offered therapeutic services, including letter writing for gender affirming care, for trans and gender non-binary folk for approximately eight years. Each person is different, though I often find that exploring the person as a whole facilities towards authentic gender identity exploration rather than focusing exclusively on gender identity.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I have worked with folks on the autism spectrum in different capacities for over 18 years. Working as a direct support professional for individuals with cognitive and intellectual disabilities is what fostered my drive to continue my education and enter the field of psychology. I specialized in intellectual and psychological assessment in my internship and postdoctoral years while simultaneously building a therapeutic caseload with these presentations.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I have identified within the LGBTQ community since I was in high school and have explored my own identity throughout my life in this framework. Professionally, I worked with college aged folks exploring their own identities within the community and continued building competency in this community throughout my education and profession. I believe that "competency" does not have a specific end date and instead is an ongoing active process of learning more.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: ADHD is hard! I was diagnosed with ADHD as an adult and have found multiple tactics that work (and plenty that don't) in my day to day. I often work with folks who have ADHD and work with them to find behavioral techniques that work for them. Creativity and curiosity are two of the most important factors I have found when exploring how to navigate living with neurodiversity both personally and with those I work with.

name: Elaine Kovacs
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I'm Elaine Kovacs, LCSW, and I specialize in grief, caregiver support, and life transitions.
ideal_client: I provide individual therapy to adults (18+), and I am particularly attuned to the needs of family caregivers/parents, older adults, and those struggling with major life transitions. With personal experience as a family caregiver and a parent, I understand the complexities of emotions that can arise, as well as the difficult family dynamics that can merge. I offer a safe and supportive environment as you navigate the family environment, healthcare systems, and your own self-care needs.

approaches.My Background and Approach: With over 12 years of professional experience in a variety of outpatient, crisis care, and hospital settings, I am experienced in navigating the challenges of the various healthcare systems. My hope is to provide a safe and welcoming space amid a difficult period in life, while providing concrete tools and positive, supportive feedback. While I utilize a variety of modalities depending on your needs, I am particularly experienced in the following: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Narrative Therapy, Existential Therapy, Mindful Self-Compassion, and Solution Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT). I also am deepening my skills in trauma-informed approaches such as Internal Family Systems (IFS) and Written Exposure Therapy. I graduated from the Master's in Social Work program at the University of Texas at Austin in 2013, and before that I obtained a BA from the University of California, Berkeley in 2005.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: While I did not initially study to become a therapist, I found my way to this profession in my 30s after personal loss and grief. It has been my mission since entering the social work field, to provide support and empathy to caregivers, grievers, and those feeling lost. I have a special interest in the needs of adults and older adults as they are navigating grief, aging, and a shift in identity. But I am also open to exploring how other major life transitions--from a death, a break-up, a career change, an illness, or traumatic event--can also shake the very foundations of one's sense of values and purpose. My goal is to provide a space where I walk alongside you, honor your inherent worth and value, and share in the despair, anger, and anxieties of life's struggle. If I have provided a space where you can feel 'seen,' I feel joy in making this my profession.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I have expertise in phases of grief as well as the complexities of each person's unique experience. I have a history of working with adults and older adults processing loss amid the death of a partner or family member when working in hospice and home health settings. I also have had my own personal grief journey that continues to provide a sense of meaning and purpose after loss.

name: Sean Robertson
title: Clinical Psychologist Resident
intro: Welcome. Welcome. Welcome.
ideal_client: You may be reading this for many reasons, and I imagine your reason comes with many layers that are known and unknown at this time. You may be feeling overwhelmed by stress, or insecure about your life; frustrated, hurt, or fearful about your safety or belonging in this life. You may be feeling proud about your choice to seek to improve your life with the help of a professional. You may be feeling and thinking all or none of things. Whatever your reasons, I welcome them.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: From my experience, the first thing that will happen is we’ll try to see if we could work well together, or not. That typically is hinted at strongly and quickly, and it’s something we’ll navigate throughout our working relationship. I will frequently check-in to make sure the goals and style of your services with me match your hopes to the best of my ability. So that you know, the styles I was trained in and that I am most comfortable working within are existential-humanistic ways of relating, psychodynamic ways of exploring, and cognitive-behavioral ways of thinking or doing. I also have acquired additional specializations in treating psychological trauma. Some call this form of therapy an “integrative perspective.” Basically, it means I welcome your desire for healing that is special to you, and I will attempt to meet you with the various fields of expertise that I have gained in my short life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe your life is a gift. But, I am betting that gift of your life has been hard to swallow, often. I am willing to bet further that others have not always seen your life as a gift. I know, for me, life doesn't always or even mostly feel like a gift because life circumstances seem to just be "thrown at me" without asking me permission or checking to see if I’m prepared to receive what life is "throwing". The trick, I think, is to look at that “thrownness” of life as an opportunity to exercise the freedom to choose—whether that is to openly weep about the loss of a loved one, “laugh in the face of danger,” or to set very clear boundaries (and protect those boundaries) to whomever might be trying to take the right to choose away. My hope is that all of us humans come to a place of accepting our life with honest gratitude and honoring our choices to respond to the gift of life with respect and openness. So, I welcome the gift of your life and how you have responded to your life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: There is an infinite amount of rational life experiences to be wary and careful of. To many people, that reality I just mentioned is overwhelming. It can cause a person to become increasingly preoccupied with preparing for a future that may be threatening in some way or form. And the justifiable, understandable response to that is anxiety. The trick, I believe, is understanding your need to protect yourself and those you care about while balancing ways to relieve your need to protect.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: There are many ways to consider depression. Most point to neurobiology: serotonin or dopamine deficiencies. Many say it is a set of behavior habits that are difficult to change. Some say the behaviors of depression is an "anger for the world toward inward," and is perpetuated by self-limiting beliefs and attitudes. Others claim depression is the loss of a personal purpose and meaning in life. All of these approaches get at the big picture, in part, of your suffering. I can help you explore why.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Our past experiences can haunt us. We can get trapped trying to understand the horror that we witnessed or avoid reliving the terror we once lived. We can get endlessly lost in trying to undo those experiences or prevent any type of those experiences from happening ever again. Ultimately, the challenge of PTSD is grieving what happened in a way that helps us make meaning for our current life and future goals.

name: Lauren Saville
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work collaboratively with clients to empower them, facilitate growth and healing, and help create meaningful lives and relationships.
ideal_client: Most of my clients come from diverse populations and are committed to pursuing a life based on their values, rather than what society defines for them. My clients like to take an active role in their healing process, are open to self-reflection, somatic exploration, and creative interventions.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As each client is unique, I use a variety of skills and techniques to meet my clients' needs in the way that feels comfortable and empowering for them. My tendency is towards experiential methods, which can include incorporating somatic work, exploring different parts of self, and expressive arts therapies in addition to traditional talk therapy. My theoretical orientation draws largely from Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Internal Family Systems, somatic experiencing, and anti-oppressive counseling. I have specialized training in trauma, sex therapy, and expressive arts therapies, I also offer ketamine assisted psychotherapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am an active member in queer communities, kink communities, and polyamorous communities. I am involved in work supporting transgender rights. I am also a part of the theatre community, focusing on uplifting/telling stories through the lens of trans, queer, female, fat, disabled, older, and BIPOC actors, and exploring issues of oppression with young people. As a university professor and community educator, I work to train and equip counselors in better serving diverse communities.

name: Brandon Johnson
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Life gets stuck sometimes, and finding freedom can be hard to do on your own. I’m here to join with you to face whatever life has for you.
ideal_client: I work with couples, families, individuals, parents, and teens with their relationships and life challenges. I am honored to partner with people experiencing depression, anxiety, relational conflict, parenting challenges, trauma, uncertainty about life decisions, or any reason to reach out for a partner in navigating a way forward. I enjoy working with people from all backgrounds and perspectives and incorporate each person’s own values, beliefs, and expertise in their own life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach starts with respecting each person’s story and perspective and builds toward goals from there. I value engaging people holistically in the process of healing, pursuing goals, and seeking resolution. I work with couples, families, adults, and teens in a variety of approaches, based on the needs of each person or family. Every person and family are different and are worth responding to in a way that fits them uniquely. At the same time, certain underlying aspects of being human are shared by us all, and I try to connect through those pieces of shared humanity to bridge across differences and build understanding and real, shared experience in our time together. Some of the ideas I draw on to do that work is from Emotionally Focused Therapy, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Interpersonal Neurobiology, and other sources.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe all of us are worth something, even when we struggle to see it in ourselves or each other. Learning how to make sense of ourselves, each other, our history, and our present helps to put things in order and allows us to feel at peace within ourselves, even when life around us may still be unpredictable or out of control. I hold onto hope for more joy and peace, even and especially when my clients can't do that for themselves, with the goal of sharing it together. My role is to join you regardless of anything in your past or present so that we can calm the storm, find the break in the clouds, and rise into the sunshine together.

name: Jennifer Stratton
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: In an atmosphere of safety, earned trust, and attuned connection, I help foster gentle yet pro-active care with warmth and encouragement.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is highly relational and aimed to provide deeper awareness of relationship--with self, with others and with your place in the world at large. Patterns and ways of being are habituated and strengthened over time and repetition of experiences--even emotional experiences. The tendency to avoid pain is a core, fundamental human drive. As humans, we come up with some pretty effective and brilliant ways to avoid pain. However, much of the pain that we strive to avoid is historical pain, with origins in our relational history--re-enacted in both conscious and unconscious ways, presently. My aim is to support your sense of agency and self-compassion--to attend to you and your pain in collaboration in the present. Together, we uncover inner resources and new opportunities to resolve pain rather than avoiding! We find resolve amidst changing circumstances, habituated patterns and outdated ways of being and beliefs of self. In safety and in relationship.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In addition to my training to become a licensed professional counselor in the state of Oregon, I have several years of experience working with folks on the substance use disorder spectrum and their loved ones. I have worked across various levels of care from in-patient and partial hospitalization to out-patient. My ongoing studies include training in Attachment-Focused EMDR, Mindful Self- Compassion Teacher-Training, Hakomi and Recreation of Self Models, and attachment-based, relational therapy. Interpersonal neurobiology, attachment & development, trauma and early experiences of stress inform the way I conceptualize human struggles and the way I approach care. I currently offer counseling via telehealth video services only.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness is a way of paying attention to our experience as it is happening in the moment. As we learn to pay attention to our experiences as they are happening, we are better able to notice our common reactions and responses and the subtleties that often otherwise go unnoticed. Therapy allows the special opportunity of slowing down and get connected to ourselves in mindful awareness.

specialities.name: Adjustment Disorder
specialities.description: Each stage and phase of life has unique challenges and opportunities for an evolved self to emerge. We are certainly feeling change simmering on every level in our current world. On some levels, we adjust quickly to change--we are designed to adapt. But we evolve slowly--almost minutely--over time. I love offering a safe and supportive place for clients to pay attention to themselves and the ways they are being stretched in the change process--and walking with them through that process.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: Humans have evolved to avoid pain, approach reward-- implicitly and below the level of consciousness. I have several years of experience in treating individuals and families afflicted with addiction and helping them understand this complicated arena, reduce shame and stigma and regain access to empowered choice. The power of human connection, belonging and purpose are vital in treating patterns of substance abuse and often overlooked. Recovery is about more than abstinence alone!

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am passionate about working with folks who have experienced stress and trauma in their childhood with lasting impacts into adulthood. Adverse childhood experiences alter the structure of brain which can have implications over a lifetime. Often referred to as "little t trauma" it includes chronic experiences of pain and the related impacts on development and coping with stress. Nervous-system regulation and attending to early, painful experiences are areas of focus in treatment.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Codependency at a basic level is a deeply personal misunderstanding of needs and boundaries with misguided attempts to connect, to receive love and to feel valued. Learning to understand oneself and one's needs can be a rich experience. Learning to develop a compassionate, loving core of self is a priority in this work. My training in Mindful Self Compassion has been a solid foundation of training for this type of work.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is a general term for the several manifestations of experience that tend to produce nervousness, fear, apprehension, and worrying. These experiences can affect how we feel and behave, and they can manifest somatically as symptoms and patterns in the body. Responding to ourselves amidst these types of difficulties can be challenging. MIndful, compassionate awareness and support can help!

name: PK Foss
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I specialize in Brainspotting for queer, trans, Neurodivergent/spicy brains, chronic pain, and wrap around couples therapy.
ideal_client: My clients are looking for deep and lasting change. Often they’ve done talk therapy and only gotten so far. At the core, you’re probably here because you know you want to do or feel something different and when it comes down to the moment, you don’t feel like you can. You feel stuck in the same feelings or behaviors that you’ve known. I love working with neurodivergent brains, therapists, queer and trans folks, chronic pain, and anyone dealing with trauma and/or shame.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use Brainspotting as a foundational part of my work with clients. We use it to reprocess and move feelings, triggers, and reflex actions that keep people stuck. Most people when they’re not overwhelmed or triggered can figure out what it is they need to do and how to live by their values. Most couples when they’re in a good place can communicate well together. Brainspotting is one tool I use to help get people to the place of being able to access their best self and respond rather than react. Then if needed, we do some work around whatever skills are needed to move forward. This can include communication skills, boundary setting, stress harnessing, neurodivergent brain harnessing/management, etc. I also utilize some Gottman methods when working with couples and parents.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a queer, anti-racist, feminist, mama who lives in Portland. If I could step outside of capitalism entirely and live my dream life, I would contribute by growing food, cooking things, fermenting things, feeding people, and doing Brainspotting for people who want or need it. I’d also spend a lot of time adventuring with people I love. Especially, surfing, white water rafting, and open water swimming. As a therapist, I love my job. I figure if we’re not laughing a bit, we’re doing therapy wrong. I love seeing people make changes and feel proud of themselves. I got into this job because I needed to learn a lot and do my own work. I’m here because I know how good it feels to do it and see change. I want to help other people do theirs with empathy and a belief that we're all doing the best we can in the moment and sometimes we need help to do better.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: I’ve found Brainspotting to be such a helpful tool for moving things that are stuck for people, that I am not taking new clients who are not interested in it as part of our work together. It has been a focus of my professional development and personal growth in such an impactful way, that doing therapy without it feels like leaving my best tool out of the room.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I work with couples to manage their conflict, strengthen their friendship and appreciation, and to create intimacy through long term relationship shifts. With couples I utilize Gottman Method therapy, which is research based and tested. Couples therapy, believe it or not, can be an enjoyable and deeply healing process. I also utilize Brainspotting with individuals to support the couple work when we get stuck.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I utilize Gottman Method with couples in order to manage conflict, deepen their friendship and intimacy. One of the most important keys to long-standing contentment in a relationship (even when there’s significant conflict!) is learning how to repair the emotional harm partners have caused for one another. Couples therapy, believe it or not, can be an enjoyable and deeply healing process.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: I love working with parents on a variety of issues including but not limited to; co-parenting more efficiently, behavior change with your kids, and becoming the type of parent you want to be. I base a lot of my work with parents in Gottman Method Emotion Coaching, which is research based and tested.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: I am both personally and professionally involved with LGBTQ community and am very aware of the dynamics of being part of those communities. I find that, like so many oppressed groups, it is important to find support with someone who you don't have to teach the basics of your experience to along the way.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I work from the Gottman Method of couples therapy, which is research based and tested and considered by many in the field, the most effective roadmap for helping relationships to become stable and happy. I also use Brainspotting as part of a wrap around couples therapy, to help each person move through issues that keep the relationship stuck.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Post Traumatic Stress is the brain's natural way of dealing with trauma when it has gotten stuck and hasn't been processed. I work from a variety of research based methods to assist clients in processing their trauma so that they can move through it and get to the other side. My primary tool at this point is Brainspotting.

name: Coleen Moreno
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am an LCSW - Licensed in Oregon & WA. Are you curious about what a 'well-lived life' might mean for you with acceptance & compassion?
ideal_client: I enjoy working with people who are on a purposeful journey, looking a little bit back, gazing a little bit ahead - finding the courage to figure out how to live right now. Having the freedom from judgement can bring vitality and energy into one's life. Your growth is what happens between sessions: You are the driver. Most people I have worked with have a thirst for insight, even if it takes time to find the right words, or the direction, to pursue their goals and desires.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Coleen Moreno has years of 16+ experience helping adults grow into the people they want to be. She would like to offer to walk with you to encourage greater psychological flexibility and emotional safety. Maybe you are worn thin by old patterns but don’t know how to get to the next good place? Perhaps you have been listening to the voice of an Inner Critic and have judged yourself too harshly, or even unfairly? Coleen appreciates where you are and invites you to explore what you want for yourself right now. She offers sessions for individuals age 21+ and is open to address important relationship concerns, but does not offer couples work. Coleen is licensed in Oregon (L5249) and Washington (LW 60681599)

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Counseling can be an act of healing and redefining purpose. Clients notice they have more freedom to unearth questions about themselves and often find a revised sense of meaning. I enjoy the process of watching people find their way to feeling better. Some of the skills I offer in session can help. EMDR and other trauma-informed methods can greatly reduce anxiety symptoms. Looking at the source of a client’s depression and how it has functioned can be freeing. In session, the use of action methods, such as inner dialogue and role reversal, can bring understanding and healing to relationships. Tools such as NVC (Marshall Rosenberg's work) often helps clients communicate with less emotional strain and guilt. Few of us are taught how to understand and manage emotions and unhelpful thoughts. To be able to walk with another and explore how it feels to be living this human life is such a valuable moment and is worth the time and effort.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have worked with adults to help reduce symptoms of anxiety related to health, social environments, self-esteem and relationships of all kinds.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I have worked with adults to help reduce symptoms of depression related to health, social environments, self-esteem and relationships of all kinds.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: I have worked with adults to help reduce symptoms of trauma related to health, social environments, self-esteem and relationships of all kinds.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: I have worked with woman-identified adults to help increase personal growth and satisfaction related to health, grief and loss, social environments, self-esteem and relationships of all kinds.

name: Elena Logvinenko
title: Psychiatrist
intro: Psychiatrist determined to really understand you, and to work together toward an individualized, effective treatment plan

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Please see my website for more info about me, my practice, and my general vibe :)

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: While I don't offer standard DBT in my private practice (since it requires a treatment team and group therapy), DBT heavily influences my therapeutic approach, and I love working with folks who have completed a formal DBT program once they have built up their skills are ready to safely "step down" to a less intensive format (something along the lines of a weekly individual exploratory therapy).

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: As a board certified and Harvard trained psychiatrist, I have the education and expertise to diagnose and treat a broad range of psychiatric issues. I integrate my knowledge of psychopharmacology with my psychotherapeutic skill and intuition to individually tailor treatment to each patient's needs, preferences, sensitivities, and lifestyle.

name: Marissa Kendall
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I believe in the power of feeling seen and supported, and that everyone has the potential for growth.
ideal_client: I have witnessed the profound healing that happens when individuals feel truly seen, heard, and emotionally held. I believe that every person carries the innate capacity for growth and resilience; often, what fosters that growth is a nurturing space where your emotions are acknowledged and your story is honored. I'm passionate about supporting individuals through identity shifts, struggles in their relationships, intimacy issues, depression, anxiety, and internalized shame.
