approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach is rooted in Emotionally Focused Therapy, Internal Family Systems, and Person-Centered principles. I focus on helping clients recognize and reshape emotional patterns, strengthening their connection to themselves and others. By fostering self-compassion and understanding, I support clients in creating more secure, fulfilling relationships—both internally and externally. I'm passionate about supporting individuals through identity shifts, struggles in their relationships, intimacy issues, depression, anxiety, and internalized shame.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that every part of us is shaped by the need for connection and protection. When we learn to approach our emotions with curiosity rather than judgment, we create space for healing and growth. My role is to guide you in deepening your relationship with yourself, helping you move from disconnection to a place of emotional security and wholeness. I use she/her pronouns. Outside of work, I enjoy any type of craft, photography, and spending time outdoors with my dog.

name: Caty Buckley
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Welcome! I am a friendly and relatable therapist who specializes in supporting teens and young adults.
ideal_client: Are you (or your child) struggling with anxiety or worries? Are there relationships that you find extremely challenging? Do you sometimes wonder if you are really "Ok" and coping with life's stressors well enough? Adolescence and young adulthood can be a challenging time. Your identity is forming, you are seeking independence and also making big decisions about yourself and your future. Connecting with you and understanding your story/needs is where we start and then the fun begins!

approaches.My Background and Approach: So, for part of my life, I work at an area high school. Another part is working in private practice with young people and finally, I have my own teenagers who are navigating issues just like you. I am knee-deep in teenagers/young adults and I wouldn't have it any other way! I think my clients like working with me because I am easy going and playful in sessions. I'm relatable and truly bring no judgment to sessions. Additionally, there is no topic that is off limits to talk about. I bring my quirky, off-beat sense of humor into sessions and feel like it's important to balance hard work with fun. You drive the bus and my job is to be a tour guide to provide you with ideas and questions about where we might need to go to reach the goals you set for yourself. It's a collaborative approach and I depend on you to communicate with me about what works for you and what might not. I truly believe that the magic happens when the client and therapist really "vibe" with one another.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I actually don't believe that every therapist is a good fit for every client. Sometimes a therapist's style is really not the best match for a client's particular personality traits or preferences. According to some of the clients I work with, they appreciate me because I don't just tell them what they want to hear. I like to think of therapy as just having a conversation with a caring, unbiased person about things that can sometimes be hard to talk about. My role in that conversation is to be like a mirror to reflect back to you both what you are describing and also what I am observing. I believe that we don't get results if we stay in our comfort zone and my job is to (gently) support you as we, together, push that comfort bubble to expand a bit r over time. It is a true joy in my life to see young people do things they never thought they could do, to address pain and challenges that have long been buried, or to just feel liberated by telling their story.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: I have completed Level 1 Brainspotting.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I have completed Level 1 of EMDR and will be finding a time to take a level 2 in the next few years.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I am part of a professional development group where we have focused on IFS for several years. I have taken various IFS trainings as well, though am not officially certified.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I have worked with teens and young adults for over 25 years! I work at a high school with students, have teenagers and I only see young people in my private practice. I have worked with youth from extremely diverse socio-economic, racial, geographic, and religious backgrounds. I am familiar with kids struggling with being a first generation citizen in to the US, kids who are applying prestigious colleges and youth who are working on launching themselves into adulthood.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: As someone who has starggled with anxiety in my life, this has always been a strength of mine, since I can easily get into the brains of anxious clients. Additionally, I have attended countless trainings and have many tools to provide clients to work with their anxiety. I strive to approach anxiety as a part of the client and not a villain but more something to be understood and managed.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Family dynamics in the best of circumstances can be challenging but when there are external stressors, like a divorce, or someone has substance use issues, conflict can be exacerbated. I support clients using a variety of tools, including Parts Therapy (IFS), CBT, DBT, polyvagal theory to enable them to examine their role in their family, work within the family system (if safe) and to honor their own unique experience of the home and relationships within that home.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have been trained both in brainspotting and EMDR. I utilize those tools along with CBT, DBT, and IFS (among others) to first establish a sense of safety and then, at the client's own pace and comfort level, begin processing the challenges they are facing/have faced due to their trauma.

name: Claire Tuft
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I offer a warm, non-judgmental, creative space to support folks navigating anxiety, depression, life transitions, relationships, and trauma.
ideal_client: I specialize in trauma-informed practices and work with a diverse range of individuals & couples—folks struggling with anxiety or depression; those wanting to tend to intimate & social relationships; individuals wrestling with identity, alignment of values, or career-oriented concerns; and people who are working through grief and life transitions. With my own background in the arts, I also work closely with people who identify as artists seeking support in that aspect of their lives.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work is shaped by my belief in the power of personal narratives and the capacity to reclaim and reshape one's story, fostering new skills, resilience, and a greater quality of life. I view counseling as a collaborative process and am dedicated to supporting and empowering clients on their path towards healing and growth. When working with clients, I take a person-centered and strengths-based approach, drawing from evidence-based practices such as Trauma-Focused Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (T-CBT), Narrative Therapy, Internal Family Systems (IFS), and Attachment Theory. I like to incorporate mindfulness strategies and creative-based approaches, and while I am not yet certified, I am pursuing training and certification in EMDR.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Prior to pursuing my career as a counselor, I spent the last fifteen years working professionally in Theater and Film as producer, actor, and casting director. It was my own meaningful experiences over many years as as a client myself, commitment to repair and self actualization, and deep curiosity and compassion for the human experience that inspired my pivot to counseling. Creative expression and the arts are still a central part of my life, and I aim to continue integrating these passions into my therapeutic work in the future. Outside of my work as a counselor and my creative pursuits, I enjoy traveling, writing, running (slowly!), and spending time (especially in nature) with my partner and pup.

name: Peggy Fulda
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hey, I'm Peggy. I support people working through Big T and little t traumas: sadness, loss, disconnection, despair, and identity questions.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am no good to you, your family, or your community if I cannot provide some level of ease and safety in our work together. I value relationship above all. My extensive experience working with immigrants, refugees, wilderness programs and international students have shown me that talk is not the only route to resolve distress. In a world that often feels foreign I use my background in Sensorimotor therapy approaches to help you understand and navigate the terrain within and around you. You don't need to be fixed; you are not broken. You are living in a space which attempts to distance each of us from ourselves, our heritage, each other. Mental Health is a western term to describe universal issues, regardless of socioeconomic status or geography. I offer a rest stop that lets you understand the beauty in how far you have come and the tools you need for your next journey. There is important work to be done even in the dark places and there is no need to do it alone.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My practice is body-centered, culturally engaged, and justice driven. My lived experiences as a partner, sister, daughter, aunt, granddaughter of Holocaust migrants, and product of a multiracial family all enrich and deepen my work supporting others. My studies of sociology, anthropology, and public health form the foundation of of clinical care. My professional work with refugees, immigrants, indigenous youth, exchange students, and other folk from elsewhere ground me in social justice frameworks and a critical engagement with power and privilege in the therapy room.

specialities.name: Sensorimotor
specialities.description: Sensorimotor says that your body's sensations, your emotions, and your thoughts all hold value and important information necessary for your recovery and wellbeing. Getting out of your head, out of your thoughts and into your body may allow you to access new routes to healing.

name: Nateesh Noakes
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Therapy for those trying to be okay in a world that makes that nearly impossible. You don’t have to do it alone.
ideal_client: My ideal client is curious about therapy and open to discovering new ways of relating to themselves and the world. If you’ve ever felt out of place—or like you’ve had to hide parts of yourself to fit in—this can be a space to show up fully. You don’t need to be fixed. You need a place where your complexity, truth, and growth are honored. I’m here to walk with you as you uncover what’s already within.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: At the heart of my work is the belief that every client brings unique strengths and qualities to the therapeutic process. I focus on these strengths to help individuals navigate challenges such as anxious feelings, depressive thoughts, and traumatic experiences. I take a strength-based, client-centered approach and see clients as active participants in their personal development. I honor experiences and work collaboratively with clients to identify the therapeutic methods that best meet their needs.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: As a therapist, I believe in creating a compassionate, inclusive space where you feel heard, empowered, and capable of meaningful change. My approach is collaborative and tailored to your unique needs, drawing on evidence-based practices like ACT, MI, CBT and Solution-Focused Therapy. I also incorporate elements of Internal Family Systems to help you explore and understand different parts of yourself with curiosity and compassion. My focus on empowerment, advocacy, and humor helps to create a supportive environment for personal growth. If you're ready to show up, invest in yourself, and engage in the process, I’m here to support you every step of the way.

name: Timothy Anderson
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Psychologist. 15+years experience. I work with a diversity of populations and issues.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I work collaboratively with folks by exploring thoughts, feelings, and actions. We will do this as a means to gain insight and achieve wellness. We will also discuss tools and coping strategies to manage stressors and concerns. I am a licensed Clinical Psychologist. I hold a Doctorate degree in Clinical Psychology and Master’s degree in Counseling Psychology. I have practiced in the San Francisco, Central Pennsylvania, and Nebraska. I have been in Portland for the last 5 years.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am committed to working to give the highest level of care to my patients. I value education and learning. I work continuously expand my education and skill set to meet the ever-changing needs of our community. I work to promote equality, diversity, and inclusion. I value the relational dynamics of therapy and work to provide a relationship most conducive to counseling. In my spare time I enjoy family, friends, community, reading graphic novels, hanging out with my golden retriever, skateboarding, and playing heavy metal music

name: The Hope Connection Counseling Services
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: We are a group of private practitioners and student interns. We provide quality affordable mental health services to numerous populations.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our therapists and interns are trained in numerous theories and can work with all of life's challenges. We have a mind-body holistic approach to our treatment facility. You can read each person's bio on our website or you can reach out by email or phone and our intake coordinator will assist you with finding the right therapist for you. We have offices in SW Portland and in Newberg.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Specialties include: PTSD, Eating Disorders, Men's and Woman's Issues, Anxiety, Depression, Loss and Grief, Play Therapy, Child-Parent Relationship Therapy , Prepare/Enrich Assessment, Sex Trafficking, Illness and End of life stages

name: Maddie Andrews
title: Student Counselor
intro: I believe in the inherent strengths of each person & I am dedicated to helping clients recognize, understand and build upon these strengths.
ideal_client: Every individual possesses the potential for a fulfilling and meaningful life; Often, we simply need the right support to unlock what already lies within. I believe in the inherent strengths of each person and I am dedicated to helping clients recognize, understand and build upon these strengths. In collaboration, we can navigate challenges, cultivate resilience, and forge a path toward purpose and fulfillment.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach emphasizes emotional well-being, strengthening relationships, enhancing communication, and fostering resilience. I create a collaborative and empathetic space that acknowledges your unique needs and concerns within the broader context of societal, cultural, and systemic influences. I have extensive experience working across diverse communities, ensuring that our sessions are inclusive and respectful of your individual background and identity. Whether you face challenges in relationships, career transitions, or personal growth, my commitment is to support you to tap into your inner strength and resources to create meaningful impact for your life.

name: Jessica Besner
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi there, I'm Jessica. I’m an empathic, intuitive and flexible therapist with a passion for learning, adventures, and live music.
ideal_client: My work is centered around empowering womxn and gender diverse folx, especially those who have experienced interpersonal trauma, with a focus on complex trauma and dissociation. I enjoy working with adolescents/young adults, neurodivergent folx, and have special interest in working with those who have experienced religious trauma, survivors of narcissistic abuse, and those interested in psychedelic integration work and ketamine-assisted psychotherapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) with over seven years of experience and a background in clinical psychology. I offer psychotherapy for healing from developmental trauma and attachment wounding from a holistic, feminist, and resilience-based lens, using Internal Family Systems (IFS, aka parts work), Dialectical-Behavior Therapy (DBT), and both mindfulness-based and somatic approaches. I have years of experience diagnosing and treating ADHD, and am currently offering ADHD evaluations in a limited capacity. I am CURRENTLY OPEN TO CLIENTS SEEKING Ketamine-Assisted Therapy (KAP) and PSYCHEDELIC INTEGRATION therapy. I am also currently enrolled in a Somatic Attachment Therapy Certificate program, and recently completed a certificate in Integrative Somatic Trauma Therapy. Past completed trainings include Internal Family Systems and Psychedelic Integration. I completed my doctoral internship at PSU, and hold a master’s degree in Clinical Psychology from Antioch University.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Growing up as a deeply sensitive, neuro-divergent child in an invalidating environment, I know what it’s like to experience abandonment and feel like there is something wrong with you. I understand how difficult it can be to be open and vulnerable when your experiences and emotions have not been responded to adequately, resulting in attachment wounding. It is my belief that we all have the capacity for secure attachment, and that all healing occurs through safe connection with self, one another, and with nature. Being human can be both deeply painful and joyful, and I am here to hold space for it all. My own personal healing journey was propelled by spirituality, yoga, and psychedelics. I believe in the power of psychedelics and plant medicine as a pathway to healing for some, and am here to walk with you and guide you on this path, should you choose. My values and approach: - Heart-centered - Strengths-based/feminist - Cultural humility, anti-racist -LGBTQ+ affirming -HAES

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Currently completing a Somatic Attachment Therapy certificate, completed coursework in Attachment & Complex Trauma. Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy (KAP) & Psychedelic Integration/Harm Reduction I am a certified KAP provider through Fluence and Journey Clinical and am currently offering KAP both in-person and through tele-health if necessary. I have completed training on psychedelic integration through Fluence and am currently in training to become a Somatic Psychedelic Facilitator.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: Was a focus throughout my early training, co-facilitated several DBT skills groups for adolescents, adults and college students. Continue to integrate DBT skills into sessions. Completed training while living in Vermont.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: specifically Relational-Cultural framework. This became a foundation for my work after moving to Portland and working with more diverse folx. It is also trauma-informed which laid the groundwork for my specialization in trauma work . Takes cultural trauma and social context into consideration and normalizes traumatic responses. Collaborative approach which reduces power differential in therapy and allows for attention to the ways that privilege and power shows up in relationship.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Completed PESI's intensive training on IFS in 2020, have been practicing since then. Continuing to learn about somatic IFS and the value of bottom-up processing. Also interested in using this modality for KAP and psychedelic work.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Studied somatic methods during my training, including Trauma-Sensitive Yoga for Complex PTSD. Attended body-centered conferences in early training. Currently completing Somatic Attachment Therapy Certificate and hold a certificate in Integrative Somatic Trauma Treatment, both from the Embody Lab.

name: Kim Spencer
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My intention is to create and hold a space where children, teens, young adults, and parents can explore life experiences and themselves.
ideal_client: People who have found my work helpful include: -Children/youth experiencing life stressors or anxiety -Neurodivergent children/youth -Active and engaged parents wanting a deeper understanding of their child’s development and emotional health -Young adults seeking a space to slow down, discover self beliefs and connect with all parts of themselves

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use relationship building as the foundation of my therapy practice. I believe feeling seen, held, and safe are vital components of being able to grow. My hope is to create an atmosphere where the people I meet with feel met and known which will allow us to walk together through vulnerability. With all my clients I take a Neurobiological approach, which is a fancy way to say I think a lot about nervous systems and how to regulate them. Our nervous systems need co-regulation before they can learn to self-regulate. Together we will explore what feels soothing to your/your child’s particular system and build strategies from there. I use Child Led Play Therapy strategies in my work. I also pull from Attachment Theory and child development to support young children and their parents. For older clients I use more talk therapy, informed by Internal Family Systems (IFS) or parts work and Narrative Therapy techniques. My style is client centered, collaborative, affirming, and trauma informed.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a White, cisgender female. I have a deep connection with nature and feel the most restored in the forest or by the river. I grew up in the Midwest and completed my Bachelors degree in Social Work at Central Michigan University. I relocated to Portland 10 years ago and completed my Masters of Social Work at Portland State University. I interned and then worked at Morrison Child and Family Services for a total of 5 years. During my time at Morrison I became certified in Parent Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT) and completed my licensure. In my professional life I have been a daycare provider, camp counselor and director, paraprofessional, preschool teacher, and worked in a therapeutic school before becoming a therapist. I have over 18 years of experience working with children of all ages. In my personal time you can find me at the river with my dog, Nova, hiking in the forest (and hugging a tree or two), having coffee with friends, reading, or reflecting over tea.

name: Ravnoor Sahni
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I work with individuals and couples experiencing stress, anxiety, depression, grief, difficult life transitions and relationship problems.
ideal_client: I work best with clients who are motivated to engage in a therapeutic process that fosters self attunement as well as relational responsibility and who value open communication, collaborative problem-solving and vulnerability to address their challenges.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My personal lived experiences, my background in Medicine and my professional training in family systems approach all inform my therapeutic style. My approach is conversational, client-centered, strength-based, trauma-informed, and culturally sensitive. I draw from SERT, EFT, PACT, IFS, Gottman, Narrative and Solution Focused Therapy. I also utilize mindfulness and somatic approaches. I tailor each session based on what works for you and your family, chosen or biological, as I believe that each individual, couple, and family is unique. I utilize a decolonizing, intersectional, body positive and an anti-oppressive lens in therapy and operate from a framework of relational equity and social justice. I am inclusive of all races/ethnicities, gender, sexual and relational orientations. I am passionate about centering and working with individuals, couples and families from BIPOC, LGBTQIA+ and other historically marginalized communities.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: We all hold multiple intersecting identities. Some of these identities afford us privileges and power in society while others can be marginalized and oppressed. As a person owning multiple minoritized identities, I understand why some of us build walls around ourselves to feel safe from relational injuries and systemic traumas. It might feel unsafe to take down this wall but that is exactly what I will invite you to do, brick by brick during sessions, at a pace that feels safe yet challenging. I would understand if that protective wall comes back up after the session. Sometimes that wall is necessary for coping with past and present injuries, and we get to those vulnerable places, that have either never been explored, or have been sealed shut due to shame, sadness, fear or anger, I will be by your side as a collaborative guide and shine light on your inner strength and resilience. Feeling seen, heard and understood in a safe space is one of the best ways to heal, grow and connect.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: Trained in level 1, level 2 and Brainspotting with couples.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Advanced training in Emotionally Focused Therapy for Couples (completed Externship and Core Skills through The International Centre For Excellence In Emotionally Focused Therapy. Currently pursuing certification in EFT for Couples) Advanced training in Psychobiological Approach to Couple Therapy (PACT). Advanced training in Gottman Method Couples Therapy.

name: Alli Santa
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I practice from empathy and genuine understanding as I've known what it's like to experience tragedy. My passion is helping others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use different approaches to help each client with their individual difficulty. Therapy is a very personal experience and can sometimes be a little scary and/or overwhelming. I facilitate a judgement free and safe environment where I encourage clients to express their frustrations as well as help them gain knowledge and insight to inspire healthy beliefs and attitudes towards the difficult situations life throws their way. I've also been known to incorporate a little humor throughout the healing process. "Sometimes the smallest step in the right direction ends up being the biggest step of your life."- unknown

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My clinical education and training begain in 2003. I have a B.S in Speech Language Pathology and an M.A in Counseling with an emphasis in clinical mental health. I'm a registered associate through the state of Oregon and I'm a certified Clinical Trauma professional. I'm also a member of the American Counseling Association.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: Having experienced several traumatic events throughout my life and having watched family and friends experience trauma, I have learned what trauma can do to our minds and bodies. I have worked with many adolescents and adults who have experienced trauma and I have completed clinical trauma certification programs.

specialities.name: Domestic Abuse
specialities.description: Having left an abusive marriage, I understand the pain that domestic abuse can cause. Domestic abuse can be physically & psychologically damaging as well as traumatizing.

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: Being a divorced individual, I understand the pain and the loss a divorce causes. It's a difficult experience to process as you're grieving the loss of a marriage while trying to re gain a sense of self and find a new direction in life.

specialities.name: Suicidal Ideation
specialities.description: I have had family and friends who have experienced suicidal ideation and self harm. This has inspired me to help others. I have worked with several adults and teenagers who have experienced suicidal ideation and have found CBT and DBT to be effective types of treatment.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have experienced anxiety myself over the years and I have worked with numerous teenagers and adults who have struggled with different kinds of anxiety. I help clients identify the cause(s) of the anxiety and use different approaches when working with them to form a treatment plan. I now offer an anxiety and depression group for extra support weekly.

name: Melanie Ramsey
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I specialize in evaluations and medication management for children, adolescents and adults with ADHD/ADD, anxiety, trauma & mood disorders.
ideal_client: I provide support and treatment for children, adolescents and adults who are feeling distressed or stuck because of depression, anxiety or attention deficit / hyperactivity disorder (ADHD or ADD). While I specialize in medication evaluations and treatment, my approach to wellness is holistic and treatment plans are individualized for each unique person. I strive to partner with patients and families to empower them to make positive live changes and feel better.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I provide psychiatric evaluations and medication management for children, adolescents and adults. I specialize in anxiety, mood disorders, and ADHD/ADD. I have experience in a multitude of settings and disorders including crisis management, depression/bipolar disorder, anxiety, ADHD, trauma, substance use disorder) across the lifespan. I enjoy collaborating with therapists and other providers in the community to ensure the most comprehensive care. I provide convenient videoconference appointments and I am in-network with most PPO insurance plans.

approaches.Why We are a Good Fit for You: Are you experiencing distress due to internal conflicts, trauma, relationships, fears, or feeling stuck? Do you feel anxious, depressed, and unmotivated? Some things are just too difficult to go through alone. Working with someone in a safe and compassionate environment without judgment can be the key to your understanding and growth. Your success and happiness are rooted in a partnership that we share. You do the hard part of being vulnerable; to the best of my ability, I will work to listen to and understand you, before developing a shared treatment plan. I am honored to support you on your journey to mental wellness.

name: Nicole Bongard
title: Student Counselor
intro: Nicole is a graduate student earning her Master’s of Arts in Counseling with Northwestern University.
ideal_client: I offer therapy for those struggling with anxiety, depression, women’s issues, and grief and loss. I use a psychodynamic lens with CBT and mindfulness-based interventions to help my clients better understand themselves. I believe each individual is unique, and should be treated as such. I work to value the client's strengths and weaknesses, while acknowledging the importance of each individual's identity throughout the therapy process.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I hope to help clients: -Build a strong therapeutic alliance to foster growth in relationships -Work through past traumas to heal the mind-body connection -Use mindfulness and grounding techniques to connect with the body -Identify inner strengths to empower and improve one's self-esteem

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Human beings drive connection and connection drives us to better understand ourselves. What I love about counseling is how it offers everyone a safe space to explore themselves, their relationships, and the world around them. This is so important to developing, growing, and becoming the best version of yourself possible.

name: Carol Roberts MA LPC LMFT
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Today you are one step closer to a new you where you feel empowered and on a positive path to growth and well-being.
ideal_client: NO SPACE FOR NEW COUPLES OR FAMILIES, AT THIS TIME.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: For over 30 years, I've had the honor of assisting couples, families, and individuals of all ages, as they identify, clarify and find constructive coping strategies to deal with issues relating to anxiety, depression, grief, anger and relationships. As a Marriage & Family Therapist, I especially enjoy working on issues such as affair recovery, attachment disorders and phase-of-life challenges. I prefer to work with those who have clear goal goals, and who are solution-focused.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a dually-licensed (LPC and LMFT), multi-modality therapist with over 30 years of collective experiences of empowering individuals and families, my goal is to help you uncover your true potential and lead a life that is worth celebrating. While we can't change difficult situations of the past, we can work together to better understand and resolve challenges in your life. By applying complementary therapy approaches and techniques, we will unearth long-standing behavior patterns or negative perceptions that may be holding you back from experiencing a more fulfilling and meaningful life. If you're looking for extra support and guidance through a challenging situation or you're just ready to move in a new direction in your life, I look forward to working with you to achieve your goals.

name: Veronica Valenzuela
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Connection. Relationship. Meaning. These are the things we need to feel secure in the world and to lead full lives. Without them we simply wither and our world shrinks, leaving us feeling scared, anxious and without hope. During these times we need connection with another trusted human.

approaches: Counseling provides the opportunity to create this connection and also allows you to explore concerns, fears, hopes and aspirations in a safe place. Together we can navigate significant life changes or events, your search for identity or meaning, as well as struggles with depression, anxiety or self-esteem. We will work collaboratively as I believe you are the expert in what you need and want. I incorporate mindfulness and attachment therapies into our work according to each client's unique preferences.

Master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Portland State University. National Certified Counselor (NCC), member of the American Counseling Association (ACA) and the National Board for Certified Counselors (NBCC). Received additional in Hakomi Mindfulness and Attachment therapies through Mindful Experiential Therapy Approaches (M.E.T.A) in Portland, Oregon.

name: Sharad Yadav
title: Student Counselor
intro: I believe that what is broken in relationship can only be healed in relationship. I offer that healing rooted in evidence based practices.
ideal_client: Emotional and relational pain can’t be easily categorized with words like anxiety and depression. Each of us have our own stories and our pain is as unique as we are. Whether it is learning to carry the existing burden of a mental health diagnosis or exploring the sources of pain and worry, what helps more than labels is the ability to tell our stories in a way that is as hopeful as it is truthful. I provide a space where you can be seen and understood so that we can address what hurts together.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I view the counseling relationship as a kind of partnership where the client brings what they can of their authentic presence while the therapist brings the empathy, skilled observation and non-judgmental understanding needed to draw out the inner strength and wisdom of the client. Seeking help is an emotional risk. My desire is to honor your courage and create a safe environment for you, in all your uniqueness, to be seen and understood so that together we can face your problems and discover how life might become more manageable.

approaches.Social Justice Issues We Care About: As the child of immigrants, raised in a rural setting, I also maintain a passion for racial justice and identify with minority experiences. Having suffered with both depression and anxiety, weathering spiritually abusive environments and attending to the severe mental suffering of friends and family, I know both the pain and hope involved in healing from psychological and spiritual wounds. If you’re struggling, please reach out and book a free consultation or make an appointment. You’re not alone.

name: Desiree Guzman
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: People possess an unlimited capacity for growth and change. My role as a therapist is to assist you in working towards your goals by offering support, validation, as well as practical tools that will assist you in working towards achieving those goals.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am solution focused. One of my previous places of employment involved training new staff. This was invaluable experience for me because it taught me the need to adapt my training style to the needs of the people that I worked with. Each person that I work with is unique and requires a slightly different approach. Some individuals prefer assigned homework and other individuals may prefer to work in session on suggested techniques. For this reason, I routinely check in with people that I work with to see what is and is not working in our sessions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Most of my training and experience has been in working with individuals who have experienced trauma. I previously worked at a homeless shelter where I worked with individuals who struggled with a broad range of challenges that included substance use, mental health issues, job loss, or were fleeing a domestic violence situation. I have hospice and home health experience as well, and have worked at agencies where I primarily worked with couples and provided life coaching as well.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: My graduate program concentrated on incorporating cultural competence in my work with individuals. We examined the effects of ongoing systemic oppression as well as how the dominant narratives effect our sense of person hood. There are multiple realities within a sociopolitical and cultural context that are defined by race, gender, as well economic status.

name: Eshe Boyette
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Welcome! If you’ve felt like traditional talk-therapy just doesn’t work, somatic therapy may be right for you.
ideal_client: You have the power to overcome the harmful effects of trauma. Whether you’re seeking coping skills for daily challenges, need to process past experiences, or want a space to vent about stressors in your life or job, you’re in the right place. I support clients to create lasting change by helping them strengthen multiple areas of their lives. We’ll work well together if you’re ready to apply what you learn in our sessions and if you’re looking for a therapist who can validate and challenge you at

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I emphasize a relational approach in therapy, as I believe our therapeutic relationship is key to our work together. I will encourage you to be your most authentic self and live in line with your values using a blend of therapies. My primary approaches include Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, Parts Work, and Acceptance & Commitment Therapy. I’m here to support you at any stage of your recovery journey. Starting therapy with someone new can feel daunting, but my goal is to create a relaxed and comfortable environment. Don’t hesitate to reach out with questions. I look forward to meeting you!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a therapist who understands trauma recovery on a personal level, I am passionate about walking alongside others on their path to healing. It's an honor to support people in their recovery process, particularly because I personally know the strength that it takes. It is incredibly rewarding to watch people begin to believe in themselves again. In my free time, I like to practice yoga, go to the gym, read, cook, and spend time outside hiking or just hanging out.

specialities.name: Sensorimotor
specialities.description: Sensorimotor Psychotherapy is a body-oriented therapeutic approach designed to treat trauma, attachment issues, and other mental health difficulties. It combines traditional talk therapy with body-centered techniques to help individuals process trauma and emotional difficulties through awareness of physical sensations and body responses. I find it truly invaluable to individuals who struggle to understand their complex experience.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is a therapeutic approach that blends mindfulness with cognitive-behavioral principles. Instead of struggling with your thoughts or categorizing them as "good" or "bad," ACT focuses on helping you detach meaning from your thoughts, making you less reactive to them. You'll learn to live in line with your values and enhance psychological flexibility—the ability to face challenging situations and emotions without resisting or avoiding them.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: As a therapist who understands the challenges of living with chronic health issues, I’m passionate about supporting others who struggle to find peace in their bodies due to illness. Whether you're seeking help to reconnect with your body, process grief, or work through traumas that affect your nervous system’s reactivity, I’m here to guide you. Together, we’ll create a space where you feel validated in the difficulty of your experience and empowered to make meaningful changes within your control

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Trauma can have devastating effects on our lives, but it is possible to peel back its layers to find freedom. By working together, we can address your most challenging symptoms—whether it’s regulating your nervous system, managing flashbacks, being true to yourself without feeling triggered, or navigating difficult relationships—bringing you closer to relief and freedom.

specialities.name: Eating Disorder
specialities.description: Eating disorder recovery doesn't have to feel grueling or impossible.I am committed to supporting individuals on their journey toward healing and self-acceptance. Through a compassionate, non-judgmental approach, I work with clients to explore the underlying emotional, psychological, and behavioral factors that contribute to disordered eating. Together, we will develop healthy coping strategies, challenge negative thought patterns, and rebuild a positive relationship with food and body image. My

name: Allie Corcoran
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: You're not alone in this—I’m here to offer a space that’s warm, honest, and grounded in real connection.
ideal_client: I enjoying working with adults, teens, and couples to gain a greater sense of wellbeing through healing pain, building insight, and creating more joy. I like to help people who are motivated to make positive changes in their lives, whether that means taking steps now or by building awareness of patterns which no longer work.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is authentic, non-judgmental, trauma-informed and inclusive. I use a combination of behavioral, emotional, and mindfulness-based approaches to meet you where you are. The therapy approaches I use are CBT, DBT, ACT and EFT. It's a lot of letters, I know. I'm happy to chat with you about what might fit best for you! Therapy should be made-to-order. From me you can expect acceptance, validation, affirmation, kind and honest feedback, and insights/tools. I value inclusivity and welcome diversity in gender, sexuality, race, body size, and ability in my work. On the logistical side of counseling, I am in-network with the insurance companies below for individual counseling only and will bill for you; couples counseling is paid out of pocket at $165/55-minute session and not billed to insurance.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Though pain is inevitable it doesn’t have to prevent us from living a fulfilling and meaningful life. I'm big on self-compassion and acceptance and use a fair amount of those ideas in my work with clients. I believe in embracing who we are and bring my true self to sessions, so with me you can expect some good-natured sass and playfulness and a lot of honesty. If it sounds like I may be a fit for you, let’s talk.

name: Ajna Rae
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I honor the opportunity to witness you becoming fluent in the language of your inner wisdom.
ideal_client: I am most passionate about working with individuals who suffer from the lasting effects of trauma. My clients also benefit from our work together addressing depression, anxiety, addiction, attachment disorders, relationship issues, and more. I am a relational therapist, so as a client of mine you will learn that I value the healing that can happen within the therapeutic relationship itself. My clients appreciate my collaborative approach as we work together make positive changes.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe we all have the ability to heal and grow from our sources of wounding. We can attend to issues of depression, anxiety, addiction, anger, codependency, and more that can arise from unresolved past experiences and current struggles. My collaborative therapeutic approach is rooted in mindful awareness and acceptance, informed by relational and attachment models, and guided by an appreciation of each person’s unique existential search for meaning. I aim to foster a space where you can engage in your present experience, show up as you are, and find awareness, choice, and support in the life that awaits you. You are a complex system of your experiences. We will work together for you to become more aware of yourself and discover possibilities for choosing a more fulfilling and satisfying relationship with yourself and others. Change can happen!

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: At the core of my values is a true understanding that you know yourself better than anyone else. It is sad to me that even in a society that values independence as much as ours, there is such a lack of promoting self-efficacy. As a therapist I believe that my job is not to fix problems or make quick judgments, but rather that the purpose for my presence in the therapeutic relationship is to offer unconditional respect of your uniquely complex human Self. It is extremely important to me that each person I sit with comes to understand their inherent strengths as they work towards their individual values. I know that we all have the capacity to exist in authenticity.

name: Yulia Tsarenko Carey
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Empathetic mental health professional offering therapy in English & Russian. Specializing in anxiety, depression, trauma and performance.
ideal_client: My clients are diverse individuals on unique mental health journeys. I offer a safe space where they can openly explore thoughts, feelings, and behaviors without fear of judgment. Employing an integrative approach, I adapt therapy to suit each client's needs, fostering collaboration and empowerment. My ideal client is an athlete struggling with performance anxiety, injury recovery, or disordered eating; or a non-athlete facing anxiety, depression, or trauma affecting daily life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In my approach to helping, I create a safe, culturally sensitive space where clients lead their mental health journey. Clients actively participate, and we build a roadmap to navigate challenges together. My stance encourages open exploration of thoughts and feelings. I'm dedicated to empowering clients to address unique mental health challenges. I specialize in helping clients transform challenges into strengths. For athletes, I address the psychological aspects of injury recovery and performance anxiety using evidence-based approaches. For non-athletes, I offer trauma-informed care and practical strategies for anxiety, depression, and emotional regulation. My approach is direct and collaborative. Collaboration is at the core of my therapeutic philosophy. I see my clients as active participants in their healing process.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My personal beliefs in therapy are grounded in the core values of empathy, collaboration, and respect for each individual's unique journey. I firmly believe that every person holds the key to their own well-being and is the expert of their own life. My role as a mental health professional is to provide a safe and supportive environment where clients can explore their thoughts, emotions, and behaviors without fear of judgment. Cultural sensitivity is a cornerstone of my practice. As an immigrant myself, I recognize the profound influence of cultural backgrounds on mental health. This awareness informs my integrative approach, where therapy is tailored to meet each client's specific needs and preferences. I see diversity as an asset and celebrate its richness in the therapeutic process.

name: Corri Rekart
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: I specialize in medication management and lifestyle coaching and care about supporting clients as they navigate their mental health journeys
ideal_client: Weekend and Evening Appointments Available! I serve patients ages 18-99 of all identities and abilities.I have a passion for helping individuals navigate their mental health journeys. I specialize in working with clients who are seeking medication management to make significant changes in their lives, particularly those who have faced ongoing struggles with mental health issues and haven’t found the right solutions. We will work together to develop the best treatment plan for your mental health

approaches.My Background and Approach: I graduated from Rush Medical University School of Nursing and have worked in child, adolescent, and adult psychiatry. I am a Doctor of Nursing Practice who is board-certified in Psychiatry. My focus is collaboratively working to utilize individualized, evidence-based, integrated treatment strategies with clients. Many people face similar challenges, and together we can explore alternative solutions that resonate with you and your unique experiences. My goal is to create a safe and empathetic space where you can express your feelings and work towards meaningful change. I support alternative methods of treatment such as esketamine, TMS, lifestyle changes, and chronotherapy and provide education and referrals for those services.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I can assist with medication management, mood disorders, and alternative treatments. A typical treatment plan includes personalized strategies, regular support, and consistent monitoring through a collaborative approach. You can expect to experience improved mental well-being, enhanced coping skills, and a more balanced life.

name: Camillia de la Garza Thompson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: You were made for times like these. Now is the time to face the beliefs that hold you back, and step into the person you deeply want to be.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I know that it is through relationship that we achieve deep and lasting change. The therapeutic relationship is unique in the way it supports personal growth so that we can set social constraints aside in order to explore how we truly feel. Therapy is serious business, but it can also be enjoyable. I bring joyful humor as well as compassion to the work. With a background in religious, spiritual, and cultural studies I go where you need to go, holding space for your truth to emerge. I believe our problems are sacred answers in disguise, which supports a non-pathologizing and collaborative approach to treatment. We are already whole, no matter what circumstances have led us to seek counseling, and the work of psychotherapy is a process of remembering this wholeness. Please note, at times the PTC messaging system does not deliver messages. If this happens, please reach me at therapywithcamillia@gmail.com

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received my Masters Degree in Counseling Psychology with an emphasis in Depth Psychology from Pacifica Graduate Institute. I am a Certified Movement Analyst through the Laban Institute of Movement Studies in New York City and have studied with many maestros. I bring a rich life history and a background of cultural psychology into my clinical work. My approach is rooted in extensive time abroad studying, living, and traveling through diverse regions of the globe. From these experiences I have come to know that we are cultural, spiritual and biological beings and bring this sensitivity and awareness to my approach. This allows me to appreciate and support the unique orientations my clients bring. Please note I do not bill insurance directly but can provide documents for out of network coverage.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment theory is solid research. It is also a set of modalities. Because it's not just a theory, I use a relational approach. It's about heart. Everything we can experience happens in it's wild/stiff/boring/complicated motion. We will explore it in a safe, stable, conversational way.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: My ability to explore the body-mind interface is supported by years studying dance movement therapies, a degree in movement analysis from the Laban Institute of Movement Studies in New York City, training in Hakomi and other modalities. I am also a self-proclaimed interpersonal neurobiology geek and love bringing this psychoeducation into my work :)

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I have studied mindfulness-based meditative traditions with various cultures experientially all over the world. I draw from these experiences, as well as the CV above. I know how to create a state of mind that allows us to explore your selfhood without judgment and with greater curiosity.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: Psychological theories and practices have historically perpetuated the cultural and systemic oppression of marginalized identities. I offer a safe space to challenge these inherited stories to support your being as you authentically desire them to be.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: In alignment with my cultural studies, I see gender issues as an intimate piece of our identity, often without conscious choice or recognition. Sometimes, therapists spend your time trying to solve society's problems by making them your problems. There is a difference. I want to facilitate your empowerment, however that feels for you.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships are the foundation of life. Quite literally. They are also where our greatest struggles arise, even in chosen relationships. This complexity can sometimes overwhelm and confuse us, while enticing us to lean into old patterns. You have stories. And they are welcome here... without taking over. Through an exploration of present and past experiences, I make use of experiential modalities to create new experiences that allow for an expanded sense of what is possible in relationship.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Who doesn't have some anxiety these days? But really, I have extensive experience helping people with these feelings, and helping them to the other side. We're all dealing with these wild times, as they impact us as individuals, in our own unique ways. No pathologizing here.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Life is complex. Studies show that those who have "depression" are those who see things as they are. However... there are many perspectives, which may come without complicity or self blame. Sometimes what's happening is a disconnection from Self because Life can be demanding. I want to hold space for you to grieve what needs grieving, to find humor in what may be dark to others, and to find your own, special sweet Truth.

name: Meghan Rich
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Engaging therapy can be a challenging, yet deeply healing and rewarding.
ideal_client: You will be supported you as you process your past, heal emotional wounds, deepen self-awareness, grow in relationships, craft your future, claim your power, speak your truth, seek inner peace, and embrace your humanness. As a client, you are committed to the process and willing to persevere through the uncomfortable phases of the therapy, with curiosity and courage.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My counseling style is grounded in a person-centered approach through a humanistic lens. It is trauma informed, integrative, holistic, intuitive, sprinkled with humor, and infused with authenticity. I specialize in addressing self-esteem, managing symptoms of bipolar disorder, healing acute and complex trauma, and recovering from narcissistic abuse. I am trained in EMDR therapy, which is an incredibly effective approach to relieve acute and complex trauma and so much more. It's always an honor to bear witness to the profound healing that transpires through this remarkable, and relatively rapid, method of treatment. Additional issues: anxiety, attachment issues, bipolar disorder, boundaries, career changes, codependency, communication, depression, divorce/separation, domestic/relationship abuse, existential concerns, gender expression and identity, gender transition, infidelity, life changes, relationships, self-discovery, self-esteem, sexuality, spirituality, and more.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: After 20 years in the marketing design and fine art fields; I realized I had been drawn toward the mental health field throughout my life. In my mid 40's, I pursued a Masters Degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Regis University in Denver, Colorado. After graduating in 2020, I opened a private practice and contracted with several counseling groups in the Denver metro area for four years. In 2024, I became dual licensed (LPC) to serve clients in Colorado and Oregon. I've relocated to the Portland Metro area—where I was born and raised—to live close to my family again. It's wonderful to be back home!

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I became "EMDR trained" in 2019 and have provided countless of clients with this highly effective method that can produce remarkable results. (EMDR is the abbreviation for Eye Movement and Desensitization Reprocessing.) Learn more about it here: https://www.emdria.org/about-emdr-therapy/

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: In 2019, I became EMDR trained through the Trauma Recovery, EMDR Humanitarian Assistance Programs. This method of relieving the distressing memories, thoughts, emotions, and symptoms resulting from acute and complex trauma is remarkably effective; often with rapid results.

specialities.name: Bipolar
specialities.description: Navigating daily life with a diagnosis of bipolar disorder can be very difficult. Maintaining awareness of one’s thoughts, moods, and behaviors is essential to one's overall wellness and a quality of life. I believe that how a person manages their symptoms is a personal choice. Together, we will explore a variety of approaches and discover what works best for you.

name: Beth Bogdon
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I’ll walk beside you to deepen your self-connection through embodied imagination, helping you discover your inner wisdom.
ideal_client: My practice welcomes individuals who sense something deeper calling them - a longing for meaning, understanding life patterns, or exploring their inner landscape. Rather than fixing what's wrong, we unfold the natural wisdom within you. Through dreams, inner images, and the body's wisdom, we will connect with aspects of you that have been disconnected or made unconscious. Together, we'll explore your inner world with curiosity, allowing transformation to emerge naturally.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I deeply believe in our innate capacity for wholeness and the wisdom that emerges when we create space to listen deeply to ourselves. My approach is shaped by Jung's understanding that the psyche speaks through symbols and images, and that our ongoing development continues throughout life. At the heart of my practice is a reverence for the mystery of becoming. While our culture often pushes for quick fixes and logical explanations, I've found that real transformation emerges through patience and curiosity. Like the natural world, human development has its own timing and wisdom. I'm particularly drawn to working with the imagination as a bridge to the unconscious. Through my training in Embodied Imagination, I've witnessed how this gentle approach allows hidden aspects of ourselves to emerge and be integrated, leading to a deeper sense of wholeness. I see myself as a companion on the journey, helping to create conditions where healing and growth can occur.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I deeply believe in our innate capacity for wholeness and the wisdom that emerges when we create space to listen deeply to ourselves. My approach is shaped by Jung's understanding that the psyche speaks through symbols and images, and that our ongoing development continues throughout life. At the heart of my practice is a reverence for the mystery of becoming. While our culture often pushes for quick fixes and logical explanations, I've found that real transformation emerges through patience and curiosity. Like the natural world, human development has its own timing and wisdom. I'm particularly drawn to working with the imagination as a bridge to the unconscious. Through my training in Embodied Imagination, I've witnessed how this gentle approach allows hidden aspects of ourselves to emerge and be integrated, leading to a deeper sense of wholeness. I see myself as a companion on the journey, helping to create conditions where natural healing and growth can occur.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Sometimes coming to therapy is about exploring, where you have been and what your next life steps will be, or to explore deeper patterns that keep appearing in your life. I would love to be alongside you in this process!

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Many people experiences life events that impact them physically and emotionally. A person may find themselves fearful, unexpectedly remembering a past event, difficulty going places, and many more experiences. I work with people to regain a sense of safety and, if appropriate, use my training in trauma processing to decrease how symptoms impact your daily life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Sometimes worries about life events, social situations, or general worry impact how a person lives their day to day life and I will work with you to move towards personal values with self-compassion.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can feel like the weight of a heavy blanket, where life becomes difficult to navigate. One might feel disconnected from important relationships. I will work with you to feel more connected to yourself and others.

name: Rhen Miles
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hello, seeking support can be a confusing journey. Everyone deserves to be heard and supported. I am here to answer questions.
ideal_client: You might be wanting to better understand yourself to feel a little less stuck. You may struggle in relationships, with self-esteem, and feel overwhelmed by emotion. We will work together to understand these experiences and develop new patterns of relating with yourself. You might be wanting support to feel more confident, self-soothe, and explore your beliefs and somatic responses. I integrate somatic, cognitive, and emotion-based approaches so you can bring these aspects together.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My core approaches currently include increasing awareness of parts of self (Internal Family Systems), understanding how our current experiences of ourselves and others have been influenced by relationships throughout life (attachment theory), increasing emotional regulation and grounding skills through an understanding of nervous system states and somatic-emotional-cognitive connections (polyvagal theory). I infuse a trauma-informed and anti-oppressive lens throughout these frameworks. My approach is influenced by the following theories and frameworks: Attachment theory Critical Race and Intersectional Theories Internal Family Systems Liberation Health Model Non-violent communication Polyvagal Sensorimotor Psychotherapy Safe and Sound Protocol Trauma-sensitive and responsive

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: There is deep value in the healing capacity of relationships. This requires the growth of a sense of safety through being seen, heard, and valued for all parts of self that one brings into therapeutic settings. There is not one avenue of healing and I aim to facilitate a collaborative space where your internal expertise can be nourished. To foster a collaborative dialogue, transparency around identity, privilege, power, and oppression can be integrated into discussions. I believe it's important to situation our individual experiences withing broader systems of power.

name: Jackie McGivern
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Happily and creatively here to support your self-discovery, and guide you toward healing your relationships with food, body, others & self.
ideal_client: While I specialize in providing support to individuals, families & carers encountering eating disorders & related issues, I'm here to support your mental health reclamation, however that may look. Whether you're ready to make change or perhaps just ready to start thinking about it, I provide a space for you to process, feel & navigate through it. My goal is to support you in getting where you want to go, be that toward recovery, harm reduction, rest, relief. Let's figure it out together.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is client-centered and collaborative. Creativity is key; I provide therapy that is shaped to fit YOU - your preferences, your needs, your goals. I believe in doing things differently. Healing and self-discovery is far too complex & personal for there to be a standard practice. I offer 3 modes of therapy: (1) In-Person (office) (2) Virtual (3) Outdoor/Exposure Therapy. Outdoor/exposure therapy consists of an in-person meeting that takes place at a nature or community-based location as determined in collaboration with you. - Better able to access emotions in nature? See you at Mt. Tabor. - Ready to challenge a fear food? I'll join you. - Interested in exploring mindful movement? Let's go. - Want to explore a new resource? I'm happy to help! *I find a mix of these 3 modes can elevate the therapy process by providing a dynamic path for you to explore healing across a wide range of environments & real-life experiences.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: Rates vary depending on mode & length of services. Sliding scale available. [ I do not currently accept insurance but I am able to provide a superbill to support you in seeking reimbursement for services from your insurance provider. In some cases, I am able to request a single case agreement for services to be covered under in-network benefits. ] EMAIL @ jackiecool.pdx@gmail.com

name: Kellie Collins, MS, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I love to help others see in themselves the core gifts that make them unique. You are stronger than you think!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a mental health therapist, and clinic director, I work from a client centered, integrative approach. I utilize cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), Dialectic behavioral therapy (DBT), and solution focused therapy. I also believe that we need to work together, as a team, to help you achieve your goals. The body and mind are greatly connected and intertwined, which is why I believe in a holistic approach to mental health care. I am happy and honored to provide you with a non-judgmental, safe space for you to tell your story, set your goals, and become the person you were meant to be. I have a very warm approach and want, above anything else, to meet you where you are at so we can work together towards your goals!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have been in the mental health field for the past 12 years and have done much of my work in non-profit, community mental health and medical field, which I believe has been incredibly important in being able to work with all kinds of clients. I am an advocate and ally for the LBGTQ+ community and providing inclusive therapy is very important to me. I also identify as a feminist. I have dealt with anxiety and panic myself, since the age of 14, and this actually led me to this field, wanting to help others who went through the same kind of struggles that I did. I have found with the right balance of counseling, self-care, and improvement of self-esteem, you really can have the kind of life you have always wanted. I would love to help you reach your goals!

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I utilize mindfulness for many of my clients who experience anxiety in different forms. This may look like deep breathing, meditation, progressive muscle relaxation, and learning to be in the present (often a combination of all of these!)

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: CBT provides excellent tools to deal with anxiety, depression, OCD, and other road blocks. In a short period of time I can teach you relaxation techniques, mindfulness exercises, and how to refute negative thoughts that clutter your mind so that you can focus on what you truly are passionate about!

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I work with couples using primarily the Emotion Focused model of couples work. I love watching couples learn to communicate and grow towards each other! If you are wanting to strengthen your relationship, improve your communication, and learn to express your feelings in a healthy way, couples counseling might be right for you. I am an inclusive therapist and work with all couple dynamics, including the LBGTQ+ community and folks in the poly and kink communities.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have extensive experience with anxiety disorders, chronic worry, and panic attacks. As someone who had her first panic attack at age 14, I can not only empathize with people who struggle with anxiety, but have learned many amazing tips and tricks along the way in my own journey towards health!

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have worked with many couples of all orientations to learn now to communicate and build a better life together. Here are some topics I work with most often: Navigating the path to intimacy Effectively sharing and communicating emotions Creating romance between best friends Juggling career, children, and intimacy Being vulnerable Building and repairing the safety of trust

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Family conflict is incredibly stressful and hard to understand when you are wrapped up in it. Counseling can help tremendously with clarity and learning to set healthy boundaries with family members so that you can be the best version of yourself in a family unit. I work with many different types of families, but specialize in self-care for family members that deal with estrangement or boundaries.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Navigating chronic illness along with mental health symptoms can be difficult, but you don't have to go it alone. I can help you utilize tools to successfully manage these conditions and have the best quality of life for you and for your family.

specialities.name: Coronavirus/COVID-19
specialities.description: The world is nuts right now. We could all use some extra support.

name: Jasmine Quistorf
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: MA in Professional Mental Health Counseling
intro: Hi! I'm Jasmine, and I love working with folks navigating neurodivergence and/or trauma.
ideal_client: If you're feeling alone, scared to be yourself or even unsure of who you really are, or stuck in rigid patterns that aren't serving you anymore, I can offer you a soft landing to explore these challenges with someone who can relate.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As someone who is personally neurodivergent and trauma recovering, I have a deep connection to this work. I love supporting others in their journeys of peace finding, and I have a lot of gratitude for being able to learn from the folks I support. Therapy can be really scary for a lot of people, especially those of us who have been judged, unwelcome, or harmed by others. This is why the therapy space I aim to create with you prioritizes acceptance, openness, and comfortability. Whether we're sitting attentively in chairs working on deep processing or hanging out on the floor with some snacks and coloring books, the therapy we do together adapts to what your system needs in order to feel secure. My style is direct, honest, engaged, warm, and empathetic.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Three goals I aim for as a therapist are to: 1. Honor your unique experience. Your lived experience matters. I work with you to identify your unique needs, preferences, and goals. Whether you're dealing with anxiety, social challenges, reactivity to triggers, or just navigating the world as a neurodiverse individual, my goal is to create a tailored approach that works for you. 2. Focus on your strengths. Neurodivergence is often framed as something that needs to be "fixed" or "cured." I take a strengths-based approach, highlighting the ways your brain works in its own beautiful, creative, and insightful ways. We will explore how you can use your strengths to navigate the world around you. 3. Provide a safe, non-judgmental space. As a neurodivergent therapist, I understand the importance of a space where you feel truly seen and heard. You won’t have to explain yourself here or worry about me making assumptions about how you should think, feel, or behave.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I'm EMDR trained, specializing in using this approach to help clients process trauma and distressing memories. EMDR helps rewire the brain’s response to traumatic experiences, promoting healing and emotional regulation. I incorporate it alongside somatic, creative, and mindfulness techniques to support clients in their journey toward relief and recovery, always tailoring the approach to individual needs.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I specialize in eclectic therapy, drawing from a variety of therapeutic approaches to meet the unique needs of each client. By combining techniques like somatic therapy, mindfulness, and creative interventions, I tailor treatment to address the whole person—mind, body, and spirit. My focus is on flexibility and adaptability, ensuring that the methods used are always the best fit for each individual’s healing journey.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I work from a humanistic approach, focusing on the whole person and their innate capacity for growth. I create a warm, empathetic space where clients feel heard and understood, helping them explore their emotions, relationships, and self-concept. By emphasizing authenticity, self-acceptance, and personal empowerment, I support clients in navigating life’s challenges and cultivating a deeper connection to their true selves.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: I approach therapy holistically, considering the interconnectedness of mind, body, and spirit. I integrate somatic techniques, mindfulness, and creative interventions to support healing on all levels. By focusing on the whole person, I help clients address emotional, physical, and mental health challenges, fostering balance and well-being. My goal is to empower clients to connect deeply with themselves and navigate life’s challenges from a place of wholeness.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I offer a warm, compassionate space for healing from PTSD. With a focus on EMDR, somatic techniques, creative interventions, and mindfulness/meditation, I help clients process and release trauma in a gentle, supportive way. Drawing on guidance from trauma-specialized mentors, I tailor each session to your unique needs, empowering you to regain balance, resilience, and peace. Together, we’ll work through your experiences at your pace, supporting your journey toward healing.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I work with clients to treat anxiety using practical, research-supported techniques to regulate the mind and body. Somatic interventions, such as body awareness and breathwork, tap into the body’s wisdom to release tension and activate the parasympathetic nervous system, calming the stress response. Creative techniques engage the brain’s neuroplasticity, allowing new neural pathways for emotional processing. Mindfulness practices lower cortisol levels and improve emotional regulation.

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I focus on creating a safe space for individuals with autism to express themselves authentically. Using creative techniques and somatic practices, I help clients manage overstimulation, navigate social challenges, and regulate their emotions. With over eight years of experience, I’m committed to understanding each person’s unique experience and offering support tailored to their needs, always honoring their individuality and fostering confidence.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I approach ADHD with a deep understanding that it’s not just about focus, but about navigating overwhelm. Using somatic techniques, mindfulness, and creative interventions, I help clients regulate their nervous system and find clarity. It’s about honoring how their minds work, offering strategies to manage distractions, and creating space for them to feel grounded and confident as they navigate the world.

name: Stephanie Morfitt
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: My goal is to help you find balance in your life, feeling at peace with who you are, and expressing your needs in relationships.
