ideal_client: If communicating with others is difficult, if you constantly feel nervous, are grieving, or having family and relationship problems, I am here for you. I have a passion for working with people overwhelmed by anxiety, self-doubt, or persistent sadness. You may struggle finding balance in your life, feeling at peace with who you are, or expressing your needs in relationships. I help those stuck in patterns of overthinking, people-pleasing, or avoiding difficult emotions.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I help adults move beyond just “getting by” to create real, lasting change. If you’re tired of quick fixes and ready for meaningful transformation, you’re in the right place. I specialize in TEAM-CBT, a structured, science-backed therapy model that focuses on Testing, Empathy, Agenda Setting, and Methods—four elements that support deep healing and measurable growth. We’ll track your progress with mood surveys and feedback so we stay aligned with your goals every step of the way. This isn’t therapy that just feels supportive—it’s therapy that works. I use evidence-based tools and genuine connection to help shift the beliefs, habits, and patterns that keep you stuck, replacing them with strategies that foster confidence, clarity, and connection. Whether you’re new to therapy or returning after a break, I offer a grounded, growth-oriented space where healing feels not just possible, but likely.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I specialize and certified in TEAM-CBT, a structured, science-backed therapy model that supports deep healing and measurable growth. We’ll track your progress with mood surveys and feedback so we stay aligned with your goals every step of the way.

name: Ariel Oakes
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I believe people can heal and live a meaningful life. I use EMDR, and more to empower my clients to build the life they are proud of.
ideal_client: No matter what you’ve been through or how stuck you feel, you are not defined by your pain, your past, or how others have treated you. You are not too broken or too much. I am here to walk alongside you as you face your suffering, strengthen your relationships, and grow your self-esteem. I work with teens and adults who are facing the hard stuff: trauma, complex trauma, anxiety, depression, identity struggles, family hurt, relationship issues, suicidal ideation, and domestic violence.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My presence in the therapy room is direct, compassionate, and deeply respectful. I’m here to listen kindly and hold space for your most painful and vulnerable moments. I describe myself as “stubbornly nonjudgmental,” and my hope for you is that you can find relief from your suffering. Unfortunately, this can be a difficult process, and healing doesn’t come when we stay comfortable. I care deeply for my clients, which sometimes means giving them tough love. If you are looking for a counselor who will just nod along, and tell you what you want to hear, I’m probably not a good fit for you. I’ll challenge you to look at patterns, ask hard questions, and do the work that leads to real, lasting change. As Churchill said, “If you’re going through hell, keep going.” But don’t worry, we will do it together.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: My clinical experience spans a wide range of settings, including work with foster youth, survivors of domestic violence, and individuals navigating serious mental health concerns. I specialize in complex trauma, and understand the impacts that trauma has on survivors emotionally, physically, relationally, and spiritually. Throughout my career, I’ve worked with clients from many different cultural, ethnic, religious, political, and personal backgrounds. I honor each person’s unique perspective, and work with you to find your version of healing, purpose, and self-respect. In my personal life, I am married and have a sassy free-roam bunny. I enjoy writing, backpacking, and knitting. I can be spotted in the wild in a comfy cardigan, and with a black americano in hand.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I remember how hard it was to be a teenager, and it has only gotten worse for teens today. Tweens and teens get a bad reputation, but I love working with them! My studies focused on at-risk youth, laying the foundation for my long-standing commitment to working with teenagers. I don’t treat teenagers like they are children, because I’ve seen how transformational therapy can be for young people when they’re met with respect, consistency, and care. Today, I work with individuals ages 10 and up.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Whether it was in childhood, from a partner, a boss, or anyone else, abuse is never okay and is never your fault. I work with clients to work through the complex trauma that comes from abuse. I use EMDR and other trauma therapies to come alongside my clients and walk with them towards a life free from abuse, and the distress that has held them back. I help clients process distressing experiences and shift how those memories live in their bodies and minds.

specialities.name: Domestic Abuse
specialities.description: It is so painful to be betrayed by someone you love. Home is supposed to be where you can rest, so when there is manipulation and violence, it can destroy your life. I have a passion for working with domestic violence survivors. I completed the 40-hour domestic violence advocacy training, and worked with survivors for to support them as they make sense of the abuse they suffered and work to reclaim their strength and identity.

name: Gayle Waitches
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Navigating this human journey is challenging. It is our nature to crave a safe, attuned, and responsive place to share ourselves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My study of medicine and counseling continue to awaken my awe and sensitivity to the challenges and wonders of being human. I offer a holistic, inclusive, openhearted approach to therapy which welcomes all of who you are and rests on the belief that you hold unquenchable and trustworthy impulses for health, wholeness and Self-love. Our work together will be a safe and collaborative journey through which you lead the way through your life’s digestion process. A crucible for transformation, deep intimacy with oneself or another requires courage and authenticity. Tuning in and honoring your inherent wisdom allow you to carve a more congruent life which feels “true”, empowering and deeply satisfying. Potential vehicles to guide your therapeutic journey include Mindfulness, Internal Family Systems, AEDP, Hakomi, Attachment, Emotion Focused Therapy, Interpersonal Neurobiology, Polyvagal, Relational Life Therapy, Intimacy from the Inside Out and Multicultural Humility.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: A lifelong learner and practitioner, I am both a physician and a marriage, couple and family therapist intern. I obtained a MA from Portland State University while also immersing in a year-long internship at the M.E.T.A. Institute (Mindfulness Experiential Therapeutic Approaches) where I studied Hakomi and other mindfulness-based approaches. I also hold a Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree. While I continue to practice radiologic medicine, a yearning for deeper human connection and soulful exploration created a shift in my practice toward the study of mental and emotional well-being. Radiology and counseling share similarities as both require exploration and insight beyond the surface. Therapy offers a loving, safe, consistent and collaborative relational space through which to reacquaint more deeply with oneself. My training in the holistic world of Osteopathy braided with my conviction in the resilient human spirit are foundational for my counseling approach.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Internal Family Systems suggests that our inner world is comprised of many varied parts, each with different opinions, beliefs and energies. It also suggests we hold within a calm, wise and loving Core Self. The work of IFS is to heal the wounded parts and restore balance within our system by attending to our often child-like parts which need loving care.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: We hold within a wise and reliable compass which is uniquely our own. Mindfulness and somatic practices are some of the tools to becoming more trusting of and familiar with our inner truth.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotion Focused Therapy suggests that our emotional inner life can be our most valuable guide rather than felt as mere states of being. As we allow ourselves to more deeply experience our emotional climate, we can become more intentional, aware and discerning with our life choices.

specialities.name: Coronavirus/COVID-19
specialities.description: As vital as air and water, feeling connected and safe are essential states of well-being. How do we tend the collective and individual impacts of Corona? Feelings of fear, anxiety, loneliness, anger and grief are expected yet can be challenging to navigate. Let's gather via tele-sessions to compassionately explore, allow, shift and perhaps realize greater connection and calm in the uncertainty.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: We all have within an inner toolbox-reliable and trustworthy resources of self-love and self-regulation. But maybe during life's travails, we've lost connection and access to, or belief in this wellspring of knowing. And yet, we never lose our veritable tool box- we can just get reacquainted.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: The quality of our relationships, particularly our intimate ones, is vital to our sense of life satisfaction. We need to feel connected, seen, loved and chosen. But relationships can also be challenging. Sometimes we rely on strategies that sabotage comforting connection. Creating a safe space to be vulnerable and unpack our protective and sensitive parts can allow for deeper intimacy.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Our culture often places an expiration date on grief's timeline. But for those of us who have known grief-who have lived the full body experience of loss as a visceral, shattered, flattened, leaded amputation of life as we once knew it- understand that grief will not be censored. Honoring and tending and holding and loving our grieving parts-- this is the spacious journey through.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Life is challenging. We are bombarded daily with its impact. It makes sense that we would have an anxious part that feels fear or unease. In fact, this part even has wisdom to share. Often when we get to know this worried part more deeply, our system can relax and trust a bit more.

name: Brooke Lavarias
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Compassionate therapist supporting kids, teens & adults through anxiety, depression, ADHD, and life’s tough transitions.
ideal_client: I work best with children, teens, and adults navigating anxiety, depression, ADHD, and life transitions. My ideal clients may feel overwhelmed, stuck, or unsure of how to cope, but are open to support and ready to explore new ways of understanding themselves. I especially enjoy working with people who are sensitive, thoughtful, and striving to make meaningful changes in their lives. You're not alone—I’m here to help you move forward with compassion and clarity.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I offer a supportive, nonjudgmental space to help you navigate challenges like anxiety, depression, ADHD, and life transitions. Together, we’ll identify what’s keeping you stuck and develop tools to help you feel more confident, connected, and in control. Whether you’re overwhelmed by big emotions, struggling to stay focused, or adjusting to a new stage of life, I’ll meet you where you are and walk alongside you as you move toward growth and healing. My approach is collaborative and compassionate—I believe therapy works best when you feel heard, understood, and empowered to make meaningful changes. I welcome children, teens, and adults into my practice and tailor sessions to meet your unique needs. You don’t have to face it all alone. I’m here to help.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe everyone deserves to feel seen, heard, and valued. As a therapist, I’m passionate about creating inclusive, affirming spaces for all identities. I'm especially committed to supporting neurodivergent individuals and those navigating anxiety, depression, or major life changes. I'm trained in Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT) and have a strong foundation in evidence-based practices. I became a therapist because I know how powerful it can be to have someone truly listen and walk alongside you in hard times. My goal is to help you feel more grounded, empowered, and connected to yourself and others.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: I am certified in Parent Child Interaction Therapy and Parent Child Interaction Therapy for Toddlers. This is a version of therapy that incorporates the guardian in developing skills of a play therapist and other parenting skills to help support their child through trauma, anxiety, depression, adjustments, and other mental health concerns.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: As a certified PCIT clinician for the last several years, I have worked a lot with young children.

name: ANDREW HAUCK
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I incorporate practical skills and mindfulness meditation with existential therapy to treat ADHD, anger/abuse, and depression/anxiety.
ideal_client: The human experience is not easy, so we wear masks, we put on armor. Our true self gets hidden away… and we may even forget who that is. Casting away those masks, those layers of armor, can take us to dark places. I’m here to support you unconditionally until, together, we find that inner light again.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I treat ADHD, anger/abuse, and anxiety/depression by incorporating CBT, ACT, and IFS into mindfulness-based existential therapy. Practical skills and coping mechanisms only go so far... By exploring your past, discussing the human condition, and examining your hopes and fears, you can find meaning & purpose, resilience, and enduring peace of mind. In vulnerability there is a deep well of strength. With self-awareness and greater focus, we can take back control of our own minds, forgive ourselves, and heal relationships. By reuniting with the lost and damaged parts of ourselves, we find authenticity, what matters most to us... our true self is revealed!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe we need to show some compassion to ourselves, because life is often difficult and there is no guidebook! But we can endure, thrive, and find real, lasting happiness with the right tools and support. Whatever is going on, whatever happened, you don't have to bear the weight alone. We can reexamine our values and create new meaning for ourselves. Everyone deserves a chance to become their authentic self, to feel belonging and acceptance, to feel known and understood. Additionally, I understand that growing up as a white male in the USA has left me with plenty of blind spots. I embrace diversity, equity and inclusion as necessary parts of a strong community. I am open to feedback and willing to admit when I've misunderstood. From our differences, we can learn from each other, and by acknowledging the past, we can go together toward a better future. No matter our background, we all deserve love, respect and an equal seat at a round table.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Your self-esteem can improve by identifying your strengths, exploring meaning and purpose, and gaining insight through greater self-awareness. The more you know who you are, and why you are, the easier it is to find compassion for yourself and to love yourself fully. I believe it's possible for everyone to experience real self-love and, with encouragement, embrace their whole self.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Fear is a powerful tool of survival, but we don't need it as often as our mind seems to think! By understanding the source of our fears, we can learn to conquer them. Together, we'll search for the origins of your anxiety, explore your defense mechanisms and where they come from, and work to leave those unhelpful thinking patterns behind. You can move forward with curiosity and confidence.

specialities.name: Anger Management
specialities.description: People who struggle with anger can learn to overcome it when shown compassion and given a judgment-free space to examine their thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. We'll address the deep-seated, unconscious beliefs, thought patterns, and historical traumas that cause anger to well up and explode. By getting in touch with your mind and body, you can learn to catch yourself before losing control, and find real, consistent peace of mind.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I know there are a lot of things that are difficult to talk about as men, especially with other men. What we're taught about strength and weakness makes it difficult to open up and talk about our true, underlying feelings. It makes it hard to even know what those feelings are. There is a lot that society expects of men, much of it contradictory and outdated. No topic is out-of-bounds.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: It's hard to find support when you're grieving. Many people just don't know how best to support you, and maybe it feels like they're avoiding you. We all need to deal with grief in our own way, and, together, we'll figure out what that looks like. If you're weighed down by the loss of someone or something, or even if some victory has come at a cost, we can learn to keep on living.

name: Jill Walsh
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Using a holistic approach, I work with adults & youth with symptoms of trauma, anxiety, depression and ADHD to achieve growth and healing.
ideal_client: My clients are individuals who are looking to explore their emotional experiences and personal histories in order to build inner strength. Whether they're struggling with anxiety, low self-esteem, communication challenges or complex relationship issues, I'm here to support their innate ability to change. I’m body positive, sex positive, and I affirm neurodiverse, disabled, BIPOC, trans, and LGBTQIA+ folks.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is one of collaboration. I believe that clients are in the most successful position for positive and lasting change when they are effectively reinforced by an ally throughout their process. To achieve this transformation, I focus mainly on individual work by utilizing Strengths-Based Narratives, Cognitive-Behavioral modalities, Internal Family Systems techniques and Art Therapy. At all times, I strive to provide client-driven services with an emphasis on encouraging feedback regarding all aspects of my treatment approach. During sessions, I aim to create connection through open communication, warmth, laughter and authenticity.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a clinician, I derive my philosophy of care from a deep value of service, honoring diversity, empowerment, social justice, ethical practice and the importance of interpersonal relationships. Through years of work in community mental health, I've learned to understand people, families and the systems that impact the human experience.

name: Leslie Jones
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help facilitate meaningful change in your life. My hope is that you deepen your understanding of yourself, and achieve personal resolution
ideal_client: Are you wanting to talk about fears that you have? Take a look worries that keep surfacing? Reduce tension that seems to always be below the surface? I love working with clients that experience a range of moods and feelings, yet often feel alone or self-conscious about sharing. Clients will find a space to explore family issues, troublesome patterns, difficulty in moving forward, and the discomfort of shame and embarrassment.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I draw on several important modalities in the work we do together. My foundational training of process oriented work helps enhance a deeper understanding of what may be causing repeated distress and challenging patterns of behavior. I utilize Emotionally-Focused Therapy to help deepen the process of talking about hard topics, while looking for and finding the root causes of distress. I compliment this, when wanted, with cognitive techniques that help reach resolution.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a licensed professional counselor (LPC), as well as a registered art therapist. I have a master's degree in counseling and art therapy from Marylhurst University. I have many years of professional experience working in community mental health agencies. My clientele included children, adolescents, adults and families. I have completed two levels of training in Emotionally-Focused Therapy, an approach that helps identify root causes and primary emotion. I offer talk therapy for adults focusing on depression, anxiety, shame, faulty communication patterns, wounds from family history, grief, emotional buttons that feel tender and overwhelming, and living in a complicated world.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I love working with couples to help them reduce the angry 'hot spots' that impede connection. Together, we identify triggers and repetitive patterns, and help find ways to rekindle closeness and intimacy.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: I have formal training in Emotionally-Focused Therapy. This modality has enhanced my ability to help clients see the foundational causes of the emotion that comes to the surface; the root cause is able to be addressed and remedied. I have been able to apply this theory to all of the clinical work I do.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: This approach looks at some of the obstacles or barriers that may be preventing you from living a life true to yourself. We all have many challenges inherent to life on earth. Knowing yourself more deeply can help shift life goals from "getting by" to honestly reflecting,experiencing authenticity, and feeling regard for yourself and where you want to go.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I have many years of experience working with the distress of anxiety and worry. It can feel tiresome and paralyzing to be gripped with worry, even when your logical brain wants to tell you "let it go." There is a ton of advice out there on how to reduce anxiety. Much of it is good! But sometimes you need to find a supportive space to express the worry, and look at ways to alleviate its hold. There are many techniques that can be helpful, and we can being exploring those together.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Many people struggle with some level of self-doubt or a lack of confidence. While not uncommon, it can be very painful to feel you are not good enough, worthy, or too scared to ask for what you need. Through listening, exploring past experiences, and validating what you are going through, you will strengthen the core belief that you are enough.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I have helped clients express grief over the loss of partners, friends, family members, the ability to have a baby, and pets. I have come to learn that grief comes in myriad forms. I maintain safety and expertise in providing a venue for clients to be heard and express the pain of profound loss.

name: Caitlin Reidy
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: As a sex therapist, I provide a safe, compassionate, & non-judgmental space for individuals and couples to explore these sensitive topics.
ideal_client: My mission is to help you explore life as your authentic self. I want to make space for you to understand I believe that therapy is a collaborative process that can promote connection and strength. I feel that clients are the experts in their own lives and experiences, my goal as a therapist is to act as your guide in navigating the path to growth and healing. Our thoughts, feelings, and experiences are informed by the systems that surround us, shaping who we are and how we engage in the world.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I decided that I wanted to become a therapist in response to my own navigation of relationships and sexuality. Sexuality has always fascinated me but I grew up in an environment where repression was the norm. I always held the belief that sex is a normal part of life, and began looking more critically at the messages that I had grown up with. As a result, one of my primary goals as a sex therapist is to deconstruct narratives of shame or guilt that may have been internalized, and develop a safe, fulfilling relationship with clients.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I adopt an integrationist approach and practice therapy from a systemic, trauma-informed lens, applying frameworks such as EFT, IFS, and narrative therapy. I incorporate social justice and equity into my approach to therapy and believe that it is critical to creating a safe relationship free of judgment. I am excited to walk alongside you on your path.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I am an LMFT who specializes in sex therapy! This means that I have received special training to work with individuals & couples who are navigating a variety of sexual difficulties. In our work together, we use therapy as a space to explore, process, & resolve the emotional, psychological, & relational impacts of sexual issues. Some of the most common issues that I work with include sexual shame, anxiety, trauma, gender identity, sexual orientation, & sexual dysfunction in relationships.

name: Muriel McLachlan
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello! I am a psychotherapist who specializes in working with children and their parents to improve patterns of relating.
ideal_client: I work with young children, specializing in ages 3 - 8 years old, providing psychodynamic child-centered play therapy services, including work with sand tray therapy when appropriate. I help families with issues related to ADHD, Adjustment, Anxiety, Emotional Dysregulation, and many other challenges of childhood. I provide parent therapy, coaching, and general support as needed in conjunction with individual child therapy.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a psychotherapist who holds a Master's Degree in Risk & Prevention (Mental Health Counseling) from Harvard University. I have worked with young children and families in hospital, clinic, school, and community mental health settings. My theoretical orientation is primarily psychodynamic and attachment-based, though I also integrate mindfulness strategies into my work. I have specialized training in nondirective play therapy, collaborative problem solving, internal family systems therapy, and psychodynamic psychotherapy with preadolescent children and adults. I specialize in working with families of young children on a range of issues including anxiety, depression, adjustment difficulties, emotional dysregulation, and parenting challenges.

name: Kris Cavanaugh LPC, CADCI
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I believe you are the expert on you and working together we can find opportunities to explore barriers and build skills to foster growth.
ideal_client: Are racing thoughts, anxiety, or a sense of being stuck making daily life harder to manage? Have you experienced a recent loss or life transition that feels overwhelming or hard to make sense of? I work with people who are navigating tough transitions, dealing with mood challenges, or just trying to make sense of things when life feels a bit too heavy. I offer a compassionate space to explore your experiences. My approach blends empathy with evidence-based tools to help you process emotions.

approaches.How I Can Help You: People seek therapy for different reasons but most often because they have been unable to 'fix' something that feels off in their life. I believe every individual and family operates within its own unique culture and system. My goal in working with clients is to maximize existing strengths, facilitate insight into patterns of behavior and foster the development of new skills, while honoring the uniqueness of each individual or system.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Many years of working with people has taught me that there is no one way to 'do therapy'. Individuals interact with their world in very unique ways based on how they have experienced life. I feel it is my job to understand how individuals perceive themselves and their worlds before I can offer to help them through a difficult situation. Together, we identify and clarify strengths and skills that exist in each individual to be used as building blocks. Through a process of looking at how thoughts, emotions and behaviors interact and influence each other, we can challenge and adapt those thoughts or behaviors that are damaging and replace them with more effective ones. These tools can then be used on a daily basis to help maneuver through the everyday situations that can sometimes be so overwhelming and often destructive.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive Behavioral therapy is one of the best ways to address depression and anxiety symptoms. It helps look at and shift some of the thoughts that can negatively impact how you feel and act. Sometimes our perceptions and thoughts about events or people or even life become so automatic that we aren't even sure what we are responding to anymore.

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I've been working with kids and teens for over 10 years in schools, treatment centers and in private practice. When family dynamics change or a kiddo starts to struggle with anxiety or depression an objective listener can often be the catalyst to change and encourage the communication and life skills that every parent wants their kids to learn.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can be a feeling we experience a little here and there or something that is paralyzing to day to day life. I help people manage those feelings by learning to stop fighting themselves and accept their fears in an empowered way.

specialities.name: Divorce
specialities.description: Deciding to end a relationship can be a confusing and fearful process. People often feel stuck and unsure of their future. Confronting those what ifs through a therapeutic relationship can help individuals clarify emotional wants and needs as well as learn to communicate those needs in the now and for future relationships.

name: Ember Von Letkemann
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi. I use EMDR, ART (Accelerated Resolution Therapy)and other somatic approaches to help folks to feel more at home in their bodies.
ideal_client: I help folks who are adjusting to newness in their lives and would like support in doing so. I also like to work with folks who are working through past challenges that affect them today. I work with adults and teens treating anxiety, depression, and adjustment challenges.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Through EMDR and other body based methods, I hope to support you in feeling at home in your body. At times life comes with challenges that can prevent us from feeling authentic and whole. I aim to help folks to regain and strengthen their sense of contentedness, while acknowledging the challenges in their environment. I have experience working with healthcare professionals, including those who offer crisis services. Through EMDR and other body based approaches, I like to help people to find relief from anxiety, depression and post traumatic stress. I like to work with clients who are looking to regain or strengthen their sense of self, and sense of meaning. Finding a good fit for therapy is important. Please feel free to contact me for a consult or with any questions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in each person's innate ability to heal. This can happen in a variety of ways, one being through the counseling relationship. I have a special interest in nature, it's cycles and the lessons that it can teach us about life and healing. I have worked directly in mental health crisis services for many years and find that personal and/or professional crisis can be an opportunity for profound, positive change. Through EMDR, expressive arts and other body based approaches, I hope to help folks to feel more at home in their bodies. Helping folks to find or regain their authenticity and sense of meaning is my hope.

name: Jamie Hoover
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Aloha, I'm Jamie! I'm a Professional Counselor Associate in Sherwood but offer virtual sessions as well!
ideal_client: I work with clients from all sorts of backgrounds, and tend to work best with those who are open to making changes in their life based on their goals. I also have had positive experiences working with individuals who have trauma, anxiety, depression and/or relational/attachment concerns. Ideal clients are ones who are willing to be challenged in a supportive way, and are open to learning, setting boundaries, communicating, and emotional regulation exercises.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My therapeutic approach is rooted in a trauma-focused, person-centered framework that prioritizes the unique needs and experiences of each client. I create a safe, empathetic environment where clients feel heard and validated, fostering a strong therapeutic alliance. Specializing in trauma, anxiety, depression, and relationship/attachment issues, I integrate evidence-based practices to support healing and growth. I empower clients by respecting their autonomy and encouraging self-reflection, helping them uncover inner strengths and resilience. By tailoring interventions to individual needs, I guide clients on their journey of self-discovery and recovery, promoting lasting change and emotional well-being.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Becoming a therapist was a deeply personal choice for me, shaped by my own experiences with trauma and the absence of support during my upbringing. I intimately understand the profound impact that compassionate guidance can have, and I chose this path to be the change I wished I had in my own life. My personal history fuels my passion for helping others navigate their struggles, offering the empathy and understanding that I once needed. By providing a safe space for healing, I aim to empower clients to overcome their challenges and find resilience within themselves. My journey from adversity to advocacy drives my commitment to making a positive difference in the lives of others.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I'm a Certified Clinical Trauma Specialist for Individuals and strongly believe in people's ability to overcome their circumstances. I have extensive trauma training for a variety of situations ranging from childhood trauma to adulthood.

name: Simone Gotter-Nagle
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi, I'm Simone and I'm here to be your sounding board, your encourager, and your collaborator as you take this incredible next step forward.
ideal_client: Trauma, abuse, depression, anxiety, loneliness, oppression, or broken relationships are experiences that leave a lasting impact on how you think about yourself, other people, and your place in the world. These aren't events we can forget about or just simply move on from. They are events to understand, reconcile, and grow from. That process requires an intentional and thoughtful investment in yourself and the experience of therapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I value a collaborative and supportive approach to working with individuals, adolescents, and families who are struggling with mental health issues, substance abuse/dependence, and abuse and trauma. I take a bio-psycho-social approach to addressing what you see as your top priorities, which means we look at the problems you are facing as complex, multi-faceted issues in need of creative and holistic approaches in resolving. When we work together, we create a plan that would include weekly or bi-weekly therapy meetings focusing on how to reach emotional well-being and include goals in areas like physical health and exercise, advocacy for support or resources at school or work, and goals around building friendships or increasing social activity. I work with you as your partner and hope to empower you through this process of growth and development to reach a place where you feel stable and supported in your life now, as well as hopeful and peaceful about your future.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I completed my MSW at USC in 2008 and was excited to move back home to Portland, where I began my career working with adults, children, and families who have faced mental health substance abuse struggles, stemming from life experiences of trauma, abuse, and lack of support. I have worked in many roles as a social worker, including in the corrections system and in mental health day treatment and interpersonal violence programs. I have been trained in EMDR, trauma-informed care, collaborative problem solving, restorative justice, neurobiology of trauma, cognitive behavioral therapy, and relapse prevention. It’s important to me to acknowledge how power dynamics and systemic oppression has impacted others and openly discuss how our relationship can be a restorative experience as you work towards your goals. I offer also mental health consulting and teach as an adjunct instructor in the PSU School of Social Work.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I have been trained in relational therapy and value the idea that satisfying relationships are essential for our emotional well-being. I take social factors of race, class, gender, and culture as well as the power dynamics that develop as a result of these factors, and examine how they have influenced your relationships and how our therapeutic relationship is a parallel process for growth.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I value the humanistic psychology approach because I believe it is essential to look at the individual as a whole and focus on self-efficacy and actualization. The problems people experience are a natural response to how difficult it is to live in our world and we can work together towards personal growth. Humanism encourages me to look for new ways to grow, connect, become healthier and happier.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Throughout my education and in follow-up trainings, the foundation of CBT has been an important part of how I approach specific strategies for changing and restructuring thought and behavioral patterns that contribute to distress and unhappiness. Together, we utilize this approach to evaluate the interconnected relationship of your thoughts, feelings, and behaviors to make positive changes.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I began my career working with adults dealing with co-occurring mental health and substance abuse issues and this experience showed me that our emotional health and well-being are complexly linked with abuse or dependence on alcohol, drugs, or behavioral compulsions like internet use, gambling, gaming, or sex. In overcoming addition, we work to understand where it came from and where you go next.

specialities.name: Domestic Abuse
specialities.description: Over the past three years, I have been trained in and have worked with individuals who have or are experiencing interpersonal violence, coercive control, and emotional abuse by an intimate partner. I have worked with individuals at all stages in of the relationship, including living in or ending the relationship, and will meet you wherever you are at as you consider how to move forward.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have been trained in trauma-informed care and in many ways of viewing trauma, including the neurobiology of trauma, relational and intergenerational impact of trauma, and of the mental health and behavioral struggles caused by traumatic experiences. I have worked with children and adults in multiple settings and have unique view on how trauma shapes our development at different stages of life.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Throughout my career, I have worked with people of all ages experiencing anxiety, typically stemming from abuse, trauma, and lack of meaning and social supports in life. I have been trained in working with people struggling with social isolation, intense worry and fears, generalized anxiety, and struggles of motivation and achievement using cognitive-behavioral and solution-focused therapies.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: For over 10 years, I have worked with people of all ages facing many issues on the continuum of depression and have been trained in solution focused, relational, and cognitive-behavioral styles of treatment. My approach to depression is to understand the biological, psychological, and social sources that have caused you to experience depression, then develop a holistic plan to address each source.

name: Miranda Bayard-Clark, LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I support new/expectant parents, couples facing infertility, those deepening relationships, and navigating the known donor process.
ideal_client: My ideal clients are couples or individuals who are new or expectant parents, those experiencing infertility, and couples looking to deepen their relationship. I also assist couples navigating the known donor process, providing guidance and support to help them make informed decisions and smoothly navigate their journey.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have completed Level 2 training in Gottman Method Couples therapy, and see mostly couples in my practice. We will have a first session together to gather information, followed by two individual sessions, and finish with a feedback session, where I summarize my assessment and create a specific treatment plan for the couple.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Even the happiest of relationships can be strained with challenges over the years. From finances, inlaws, new baby, to lack of intimacy, couples are tested to the fullest, especially during major life changes. Many of my clients are couples who are working to maintain their relationship as a couple. Using client strengths, Emotion-Focused couples counseling, and Gottman techniques, I will support you in finding balance in your personal life, and your relationships. I hold a Masters degree in Counseling Psychology from Lewis & Clark, and am a current member of the International Center for Excellence in Emotion Focused Therapy.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Humans learn attachment from their primary caregivers. This relationship we have with our parents directly reflects our relationships with our friends, other family members, co-workers, and intimate partners. I work with clients to identify their attachment, and how it can help or hinder their personal success in creating and maintaining relationships.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: I have completed Level 2 training in Gottman Method Couples Therapy, and primarily see couples in my practice. Using Gottman therapy is unique in the fact that couples get a full assessment of their relationship to help guide the treatment of couples therapy. The assessment is done in three sessions. Couples will learn tools for managing conflict and also improve friendship and intimacy.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Attachment is one of the key drives all humans need. We learn attachment from our primary caregivers, which is translated to our intimate partners. When we feel emotionally secure and attached, we feel good and safe. When our emotional connections are not validated, we feel threatened. I work with couples understand each other on a primary level, and create strong, secure attachments.

specialities.name: Premarital Counseling
specialities.description: Premarital counseling is a great investment to your relationship, and I support couples through this life stage. You will learn how to better communicate your needs resulting in more productive disagreements, and increase overall marital satisfaction. When engaged in premarital counseling, your union can begin and grow with healthy patterns established.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: The dreaded 'shame voice'. We all have it, and lets admit, it gets in the way at times. I work with clients to learn to identify when shame has taken over and now in control, as well as learning to quiet that piece of ourselves and allow us to move forward in life feeling more confident and secure.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships can be hard, and just like owning a car, relationships need some regular maintenance to make sure it's running smoothly. Whether couples are healing from infidelity, adjusting to new roles as parents, or just coming in to improve communication, I support couples in their journey towards a deeper and more intimate understanding and connection. See my website for assessments offered.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a therapist, I offer specialized support for couples navigating the known donorship process. This includes helping you understand the emotional, potential legal, and relational implications of using a known donor. I facilitate clear communication between the couple, and provide professional guidance to ensure everyone feels comfortable and well-informed throughout the journey.

name: Kayleigh Rogalski
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: Hi, I'm Kayleigh. I'm glad you're here! Let's see if I'm a good match for you.
ideal_client: Trauma, insomnia, and chronic illness can impact so many areas of a person's life, including relationships, important activities, and mental health. I love helping people feel like themselves again, especially older adults, women, queer folks, fat people, and the neurodivergent. Yes, this world is chaotic and scary, but let's flex your agency and help you re-connect with yourself.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I'm trained as a health psychologist, and I am well-versed in treating chronic conditions like POTS, hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS), long-COVID, and overactive bladder. I have contributed to a published article on patients' experience of living with POTS. I also offer CBT-I, the gold-standard treatment for insomnia. If you have a chronic condition or belong to a marginalized community, healthcare interactions can be traumatic, and I am particularly versed in treating medical trauma. I offer both standard EMDR and intensive EMDR for people short on time or looking for big changes in a short period. I'm also passionate about weight stigma, having published, presented, and written a dissertation on the topic. I would love to support you healing your relationship with food (e.g., binge eating) and your body.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: This world is frightening for so many of us right now. We're regularly facing existential threats that impact our safety, housing, environment, healthcare, and overall wellbeing. And yet, we still have the agency to calm our nervous systems, to connect with ourselves and others, to get better sleep, to overcome our traumas, and feel better in our bodies. I would love to help get you back to you.

specialities.name: Insomnia
specialities.description: I am trained in providing cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I). It is the gold standard treatment for insomnia, working more effectively and with fewer side effects than any prescription or OTC sleep aid on the market. It is data-driven and you can see improvements in your sleep in just a couple weeks.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Talk to someone who "gets it." I'm knowledgeable about POTS, hEDS, IC, overactive bladder, long COVID, chronic fatigue. I can support you connecting with appropriate healthcare providers, establish self-management routines, and discern when to rest and when to push. I can help quiet your "anxious" bladder so you can sleep through the night, get back to important activities, and finally take that trip.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I work with PTSD, sub-clinical trauma, and medical trauma. I am trained in eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy and I offer EMDR intensives (i.e., basically marathon therapy sessions to get through a lot in one chunk of time).

name: Olivia Pennelle
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Hi, I'm Olivia, CSW-A. I'm here to support your mental well-being with compassion and care. Let's thrive together!
ideal_client: love working with neurodivergent, LGBTQIA+ folks, and anyone feeling like they need to carve out space for their identity. I particularly enjoy working with teens navigating their identity and/or neurodivergence, in affirming, strengths-based, and practical ways. That might be developing ND-friendly communication strategies, supporting parents to implement these ideas, and finding sensory relief in a very bright and loud world.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: While my title is a therapist, I see my role as a co-collaborator, and it’s an honor. In my work I strive to provide support and problem solve in a trauma-informed and strengths-based way. Central to my approach is a focus on self-empowerment, autonomy, and self-direction. What that means is, I believe that we are all experts in our own lives and the therapeutic process should collaboratively strengthen and bring to the surface the skills and inner strength to harness our innate wisdom and strength. As a therapist associate, and fellow human, I am not an expert on what is best for you, but I can help you figure it out.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As a person who lives in a larger body and navigates multiple disabilities and identities, I actively support HAES, disability justice, and making the world a more inclusive place for people like us to take up the space we deserve.

name: Ronald L Johnson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer mindfulness-based and holistic services to those affected by stress, anxiety, depression, and various unwanted addictive behaviors. Stressors can be from work, relationships, or concerns about the World, among others. Addictive cycles can include drugs, alcohol, food, or romantic patterns.

approaches: Clients engage in several traditional counseling approaches to reconnect with a deeper sense of self, including talk therapy, mindfulness meditation on the breath and inner emotions, and scanning and awakening of the energy field of the inner body. These create healing and meaning in one's life and promote a positive outlook. Gradually, less constrictive thought processes replace these conditioned reactions and released energies are poured into new areas of growth. Clients may receive support for physical regimens at local gyms or yoga studios, as well as reassessment of educational goals, occupational, and relational potentials to provide for holistic, long term health.

I received a bachelor's degree in psychology and religious studies from University of California, Santa Cruz, where I really enjoyed studying. I started learning yoga and martial arts there, and was introduced to Zen master Kobun Chino Sensei. I studied meditation with him at Zendo Santa Cruz and practiced there independently. Back home in Oregon, I trained in alcohol counseling at OHSU and earned a master's in psychology and creative writing at UO Eugene. More recently I obtained additional educational requirements for my LPC studying mindfulness through Walden University online. I have published papers on poetics of mindful awareness and the various counseling modalities related to consciousness development and personal growth. Besides counseling I teach yoga classes around Portland that include harmonium and chant practice.

specialities.name: Holistic
specialities.description: My practice is holistic because I am very focused on mind-body issues. These include encouraging clients to develop a good diet and exercise plan, besides recognizing negative and habitual thought patterns. I also train people to connect with the inner wisdom of the body, and become more aware of their emotional intelligence.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Besides long experience as a meditator and yoga teacher, I have studied considerable research on the use of mindfulness-based methods to heal and improve typical counseling complaints, and understand how to use mindfulness to restore a sense of the richness of life to one's experience.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: At University of California, Santa Cruz, I took the Humanistic Psychology track, and so was exposed to the beautiful learnings and teachings of Carl Jung, Carl Rogers, and Abraham Maslow, along with the genius of the wisdom traditions of Native Americans, Mexican shamanism, Buddhism, Sufism, and the physical practice and inspiring philosophy of Yoga.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Author Deepak Chopra says drug addiction is a 'misguided spiritual quest' and this makes a lot of sense to me. Break the habitual pattern of drug use and we break lots of old destructive patterns in our lives that have unconsciously been using or even draining our energy. When we free ourselves from these we find a sense of liberation, meaning, and direction along our path.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I train both partners in meditation and mindfulness techniques so they learn to communicate without stress and use the relationship itself to enhance personal growth, awareness, and provide a lifelong spiritual path.

specialities.name: Anger Management
specialities.description: Anger issues are usually related to stress and trauma from the past! We can work through these and learn mindfulness techniques to keep us in the present moment and help us to monitor triggers before they become explosive.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Mindfulness meditation practices help us to become more aware of emotional intelligence in the present moment and allow us to be less involved in dwelling on past trauma or future worries, even as we become able to make plans for our lives more clearly.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Learn to watch and change negative thought patterns that lead to depression - through mindfulness meditation techniques and cognitive therapy. Let go of past trauma, focus on the present, and move your life forward!

name: Allison Medford
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Individual counseling fostering peaceful minds through genuine connections, a good dose of humor, and flexible approaches to therapy.
ideal_client: Do you find yourself prioritizing others' needs while struggling to make space for your own? Are stress and overwhelm taking a toll on you? If you're ready to explore, heal, and grow, know that seeking support is a courageous step toward change. I specialize in working long-term with clients who value a strong therapeutic relationship—one that offers support through both challenges and successes. Together, in a safe and compassionate space, we’ll navigate obstacles as a collaborative team.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I currently offer individual counseling and am not accepting new couples or family clients at this time. My approach is rooted in Social Justice, Feminist, and Humanistic perspectives, allowing me to tailor our work to your unique needs. I provide trauma-informed care to help you build resilience and harness your strengths. Whether you're navigating trauma, anxiety, or simply need a supportive space, we’ll work together to find your path forward. I am especially passionate about supporting queer and BIPOC communities and remain dedicated to ongoing learning to provide the most inclusive and affirming care possible. My practice is anti-oppressive and culturally humble, ensuring you feel seen, heard, and respected.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As your therapist, I honor the uniqueness of your journey. My approach is authentic and engaged, creating a welcoming, non-judgmental space where you feel truly seen and heard. Therapy is a collaborative process, and your insights shape our work together. Whether you're facing anxiety, depression, trauma, or relationship challenges, I’m here to support you. Let’s explore what works best for you and prioritize your well-being.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I believe in the power of authentic and collaborative relationships as the foundation to provide trauma-informed care that recognizes the impact of past experiences on your present well-being. I champion social-justice orientations with feminist, anti-oppressive, and humanistic values. Our therapeutic work will focus on building resilience, empowering you to heal, and tapping into your inherent strengths using a variety of interventions that suit your evolving needs.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: Though many therapists will say they use "art therapy" in their treatment, it takes specialized training to call oneself an Art Therapist and register with the ATCB. This distinction identifies me as uniquely qualified to use art making and creative interventions with advanced knowledge of the creative process, evidence based interventions, and honor for your expressive voice in your journey to self discovery and growth. Master's Degree in Art Therapy, GWU 2010 ATR #22-230

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR (Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing) techniques, which allows me to provide basic EMDR services for phobias, self discovery, and trauma work via telehealth services.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: Blending many treatment orientations (ie Social Justice, Feminist, and Humanistic frameworks), I am an eclectic therapist who uses a variety of interventions to build a personalized plan that suits your needs. I provide trauma-informed care to help you build resilience and leverage your strengths.

name: Kelly Richardson
title: Social Worker
intro: Your path of healing and growth is very personal. I'm here to listen. My clinical approach is warm, genuine and compassionate.
ideal_client: Are you struggling with trauma, relationship issues, parenting, substance abuse, anxiety or depression? Are you LGBTQIA+? Polyamorous? I honor your inherent wisdom and ability to heal. I use mindfulness, Somatic EMDR, Brainspotting, and Somatic therapies, among others. We consider the different influences in your life, from trauma, anxiety and depression, to family systems and social and institutional oppression. Together, we work toward your liberation and healing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My work is an anti-oppressive, trauma-informed and strengths-based practice. I draw from the Liberation Health model and I integrate Somatic EMDR, Brainspotting, Polyvagal theory, Internal Family Systems (IFS), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Narrative therapy, Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT), attachment theory and more.

name: Shay Larken
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with those seeking to heal from trauma, increase emotional wellbeing, build resilience, and feel more connected to self and others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work with complex trauma and grief and the ways it manifests in our mind and body, coping strategies, and relationships. While relationships can cause harm, relationships can also heal. My work draws from multiple mind-body therapies and theory, including: polyvagal therapy, somatic therapies, Internal Family Systems (IFS) parts work, AEDP, Interpersonal Neurobiology, and mindfulness. I incorporate a bottom-up (somatic) and a top-down (cognitive) approach, where you learn to move into the felt experience of deep emotions and sensations, but also engage your ability to challenge trauma shaped beliefs about yourself and others. I offer a warm and authentic presence, combined with a commitment to staying current on leading research and practices in complex trauma therapy, providing you with a supportive path toward healing, growth, integration, and connection.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received my Masters in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis & Clark College. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), and a National Certified Counselor (NCC). During my prior corporate career, I felt a calling into a healing profession, but this required a radical life shift, one where I moved into a place of stillness, turned inward, called upon profound courage, and relied on my intuition to choose a new path. I know what it looks like to appear high functioning, but feel tormented and confused by the dark remnants of trauma within the body, beliefs, and relational patterns. My move into this work is rooted in the awareness that we cannot heal alone, and recovering from trauma and how it shows up in our life must tend to all of you - your mind, body, emotions, and soul. I believe we heal when we are seen, heard, and known. Seeking help is brave and your inquiry will be met with compassionate attention.

name: Mahalia Lind-Diamond
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I help individuals heal from trauma that may be impacting their self image and important relationships.
ideal_client: I work with clients who are suffering from anxiety and depression, who are experiencing PTSD or are looking to process and heal from trauma. I also work with individuals who are struggling with their self esteem. Supporting young adults through life transitions is something that I have experience with and deeply enjoy! I also enjoy working with people exploring anti-oppressive relationship structures that are queer, polyamorous, or kink friendly.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is collaborative, warm, gently challenging and validating. I believe that we all have the innate ability to heal, grow, and break patterns, but sometimes we need support in gathering more tools to be able to do so. We often carry both our darkest moments, and experiences of excitement and joy alone. It is my belief that we heal through relationship. This is where we are able to reveal our truest selves and heal the wounds that we have both inherited and developed throughout our lives. I utilize tools from psychodynamic, emotion focused, somatic and attachment based lenses. My approach to counseling is relational, meaning I will ask you to both notice how you relate to me in our sessions, and how you relate to your self and body. We will practice noticing physical sensations that arise in your body and make connections between our therapeutic relationship and how it might mirror other dynamics in your life.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: While therapy will not solve systemic oppression, it is a place that we can examine our role in those systems and how they impact our lives. I am committed to continually exploring my place in oppressive systems and how my identities interact with those of my clients. I try my best to make therapy accessible to everyone through offering sliding scale options for those paying out of pocket. If you would like to share your concerns about OHA taking away pre-licensed counselors ability to accept OHP HealthShare insurance starting July 2025, please use this link to do so: https://fastdemocracy.com/campaigns/tICYT3fdX/Protect-Access-to-Your-Mental-Health-Provider/

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I provide a space where we can gently explore past trauma and investigate the effects of it in your daily life.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Together we can shift unhelpful thought patterns and make space for more compassion.

name: Kat Schoolland
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Child Anxiety, Phobias & OCD. I help kids and families stop the spiral and courageously take back their lives one step at a time.
ideal_client: Anxiety, Phobias, Obsessive Compulsive Disorder in kids can show up in big ways and leave families spiraling. I get that you can’t always prevent kids from struggling, but we can give them the skills to thrive in the face of life's challenges. With skill building through Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Exposure Response Prevention (ERP), I help kids and parents develop a toolbox of evidenced based strategies to face their fears and courageously take back their lives from anxiety & OCD.

approaches.What I Specialize In: With skill-building through Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) and Exposure Response Prevention (ERP), we help kids and parents develop a toolbox of evidenced based strategies to face their fears and courageously take back their lives from Anxiety and OCD. The therapy we provide focuses on teaching children to be aware of their own emotions, to notice and critically evaluate their thoughts and to employ adaptive behavioral strategies, mindfulness, and other self-soothing skills to help themselves remain grounded in difficult situations rather than getting swept away by worry or big emotions. For over a decade we have successfully helped children build skills to manage stress, improve mood, increase self-regulation, and optimize potential. My playful, energetic, and collaborative style connects with kids and I prioritize finding fun, developmentally-appropriate ways to individualize treatment. If you're feeling stuck give me a call, I can help.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I understand that you want the best for your child. You're proactive about their emotional well-being and ready to support them through the challenges of growing up in today’s world. You recognize the importance of resilience and emotional intelligence, and you're looking for expert guidance to foster these qualities in your child. I believe in a collaborative approach, where therapy isn't just a service, but a true partnership. I believe strongly in the power of mindfulness & self-compassion. I integrate these principles into my own life and in my practice, creating a rich toolkit of techniques and exercises for those I works with. These skills are designed to guide my young clients on a path of self-care and acceptance, helping them build a lifelong habit research shows can profoundly impact their well-being. Through this approach, I offer a meaningful way for kids to connect with themselves and the world around them in a positive, impactful manner.

name: Linda Berlingen
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am a caring person, skilled at listening, who will act as a mirror, reflecting back your deepest knowing and personal truth.
ideal_client: I love working with adolescents and adults struggling with the challenges life presents to everyone. I have a special interest in helping people with trauma backgrounds to feel whole.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I specialize in existensial therapy and Rogerian Therapy, assisting clients in finding meaning in life experiences while be unconditionally positively regarded.

approaches.Why We are a Good Fit for You: Sometimes we need a caring person, skilled at listening, who will act as a mirror, reflecting back our deepest knowing and personal truth. The act of entrusting another in this manner helps us to realign with our wisest self. We begin feeling more at ease and clearer about our intentions. Choices begin to reflect who we really want to be in the world. Suddenly, we are noticing and appreciating what is right and joyful in life more of the time.

name: Brian Thompson
title: Licensed Psychologist
intro: An active approach to meaningful living.
ideal_client: I work with adults with most anxiety-related problems, OCD (including Pure “O” and relationship OCD), trichotillomania, skin picking, panic, and health anxiety.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a licensed psychologist and Director of the Portland Psychotherapy Anxiety Clinic, specializing in evidence‐based treatments for anxiety, stress, and worry. My clinical work focuses on conditions such as OCD (including Pure “O” and relationship OCD), repetitive hair pulling, skin picking, trauma/PTSD, panic, and health anxiety. I primarily draw from Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) for its flexibility and scientific rigor, frequently incorporating exposure therapy to help clients approach challenges. I tailor each session to your unique goals, teaching practical skills that foster meaningful change. Typically, treatment lasts between 10 and 30 sessions—enough time to see tangible results while ensuring you feel that every session is a valuable investment in your well-being.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that therapy works best when it’s a collaborative, structured process that respects your time and your unique journey. I’m committed to helping you build a life that aligns with your values by focusing on skill-building and actionable change. I value a transparent, goal-oriented approach where you are an active participant in your healing. Outside the therapy room, I engage in ongoing research, clinical training, and professional collaboration to continually refine my methods. My passion lies in empowering clients to transform barriers into stepping stones for a more meaningful, connected, and vibrant life.

name: Andrew Conner
title: Marriage and Family Therapist
intro: I help Millennials and Gen-Z individuals have more satisfying relationships and build self-esteem.
ideal_client: My clients struggle like you do. Despite being intelligent, kind, and creative, life is hard. When we first begin therapy, my clients feel like their relationships are lacking. They’re having issues with family, friends, and partners. They wonder why they keep having the same experiences in relationships, and what they can do about it. They wish they knew why things keep playing out in the same way. They feel like they’re not good enough, and that it’s their fault.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: During therapy, I encourage my clients to reflect on how their past experiences with important people in their lives might be influencing how they go about their lives today. In addition to discussing things that have happened in the past, I ask my clients how they are feeling about me and relating to me in the moment. This can provide valuable insight into how they might relate to others outside of the therapy room. I welcome the discussion of dreams during therapy as a way to facilitate deep listening. I invite my clients to connect to their bodies and notice how emotions might be showing up there. I help my child client's express their feelings through the symbolic language of play.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I value inclusivity in my work. I welcome clients of all gender identities and sexual orientations, and those who are in a process of exploration. I welcome clients of all racial, ethnic, national, religious, and caste backgrounds.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: I believe that the unconscious mind has a real influence on our day-to-day lives. I believe that important past relationships come to bear on our present relationships and way of being in the world.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: I believe that communication with the unconscious mind through dreamwork and active imagination can help us to access the wisdom of our inner depths.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness can help us to experience life in a different way. This shift in perspective can help us to reexamine our relationship to our own suffering.

specialities.name: Play Therapy
specialities.description: Play therapy allows children and pre-teens to communicate and process their feelings symbolically through play.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I am a certified teacher of The Realization Process, an embodied path to spiritual awakening, personal growth, and healing created by Judith Blackstone.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Sometimes the burdens of life can feel too heavy to bear. I endeavor to help relieve the weight of depression by providing my clients with compassionate witness.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I completed my initial training as the first male-identified person to offer therapy at the YWCA Silicon Valley Domestic Violence Support Network. I have since worked extensively with youth who have immigrated to the United States from Latin America seeking safety. My work with survivors of trauma has informed my perspective on how to help clients relate to the personal and collective wounds that we all carry.

specialities.name: Compassion Fatigue
specialities.description: My years of experience working at mental health agencies gave me insight into the realities of secondary traumatic stress. I understand the challenges that activists and people in the helping professions face as they attempt to maintain self-care and work towards making the world a better place at the same time. I endeavor to provide a refuge for those seeking balance and struggling with burnout.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I believe that it is important for men to reexamine the standards of masculinity that have been put forth by our cultures. I offer a non-judgmental space for male-identified persons to process their feelings regarding their place in a changing world. I take inspiration from Robert Bly, Joseph Campbell, Robert A. Johnson, and the mythopoetic men's movement.

name: Catherine Palmer
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My goal is to help you enhance your relationships, improve your emotional well-being, discover your strengths, and re-empower your life.
ideal_client: Is your relationship or your life not quite where you would like it to be? Are you feeling stuck or misunderstood? Are you struggling with anxiety, codependency, depression, or grief? Do you feel as if your past trauma is negatively impacting your current life? If so, I am glad you are here. As a therapist, my goal is to help you enhance your relationships, improve your emotional well-being, rewire the way you think, discover your strengths, and re-empower your life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am skilled at helping individuals who are experiencing relationship problems, anxiety, grief, depression, low self esteem, lack of motivation, past trauma, life transitions, and family of origin issues. Whatever your concerns, we'll work together to improve your life. I am warm and nonjudgmental, yet interactive and engaged. Your time with me will provide a safe space to explore your personal goals, gain insight on what is most meaningful to you, and work around any difficulties that may be holding you back or disempowering you. In couples therapy, I can help you break dysfunctional cycles and replace old, worn-out ways of interacting with more intentional and compassionate ones. In addition to teaching new communication and life skills, I can help you expand and reorganize your emotional responses in a way that helps increase empathy and understanding, engenders self-growth, and brings greater intimacy and joy. www.marriagecounselinginportland.com

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my MS degree in counseling from PSU, with a specialty in Marital, Couple and Family Therapy. I've been certified by the NBCC and I have additional, long-term training in Emotion Focused Therapy for Couples, Emotion Focused Therapy for Individuals, EMDR and Internal Family Systems. I've been able to help many individuals, families, and couples create healthier, more satisfying relationships with themselves and others. It's a profound experience to witness the ways in which people are able to overcome their struggles and empower themselves. It brings me great satisfaction to be able to help others make permanent positive changes in their lives and relationships. I also have a Ph.D. in Science and have discovered that my knowledge of both psychology and biology provides me with powerful tools as a counselor. I believe in the interpersonal neurobiology concept of 'inspire to rewire' the brain via a nurturing therapeutic relationship.

name: Shannon Glade, LMFT
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
credentials: MA from Lewis & Clark Graduate School of Counseling
intro: I am a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in NE Portland using somatic & mindfulness, as well as relational approaches to therapy.
ideal_client: My work is focused on helping individuals, couples, and parents heal and gain the necessary skills to improve personal and relational wellbeing. I work with helping people to improve emotional management, symptoms of anxiety and depression, relationship conflict, life transitions and more. My ideal client is motivated for change and is willing to put in effort to get the results they are looking for.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy involves a focus on mindfulness as well as somatic experiencing, while incorporating a variety of other, evidence-based techniques to best suit individual needs. In sessions this often means learning acceptance and other mindfulness skills, learning to connect the mind and body, processing emotions & past events, improving coping & communication skills, and increasing self-compassion. I provide a safe space for LGBTIQA identifying individuals and couples.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a Master of Arts degree in Marriage, Couple, and Family Therapy from Lewis & Clark College. I graduated summa cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Psychology from Portland State University. I worked in community mental health with individuals and families before starting a private practice. I have experience facilitating groups with both adults and children concerning a variety of mental health topics. I continue to educate myself on issues relevant to mental health and therapy through continuing education courses, readings, supervision and consultation.

name: Emily Walker
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: My ultimate goal is to meet my clients where they are and help empower them to draw upon internal and external resources of strength.
