ideal_client: You know yourself best. Maybe you're struggling with feeling overwhelmed by your emotions or feeling "stuck" like something is missing. Maybe you're struggling with your relationship with body and/or gender. Or perhaps you've noticed that old coping skills are no longer working. The world can be overwhelming and navigating transitions doesn't have to happen alone. My job is to ensure that you feel seen and heard while we work together to discover what support you're needing.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I utilize a relational approach with a creative flair; each session is catered to fit the needs of the individual. I am passionate about treating disordered eating and eating disorders, supporting people through life transitions and navigating the difficult choices that happen at critical periods of development. My use of art therapy in combination with traditional talk therapy allows clients to connect with themselves, their bodies, thoughts, emotions, and relationships at a deeper level without the limitations of words. Art therapy is accessible to anyone, not just an “artist”, as the purpose behind the art making is the process not the final product.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I offer deep and personal awareness of LGBTQ+ concerns and hold an anti-oppressive lens. I also work from a Health At Every Size approach and aim towards dismantling diet-culture narratives that are harmful and deeply internalized. We all deserve a safe space to process, explore, and challenge the impact of systemic beliefs while working towards self-acceptance and compassion.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: Body Image Issues can come in a variety of forms, whether it be rooted in disordered eating, gender dysphoria, trauma, chronic illness, or self-esteem. I am comfortable and passionate about helping my clients repair their relationship with their body. I worked in a residential facility for eating disorders and have experience supporting recovery from anorexia, bulimia, binge eating, and ARFID.

name: Heidi Colligan
title: Student Counselor
intro: I care deeply about human development and believe everyone has the power to grow and change.
ideal_client: Are you feeling stuck or caught in a place you don’t want to be? You don’t have to navigate life's challenges alone. Whether you are a teenager, single adult, couple or family, my goal is to support you with gentleness and respect.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Using a Narrative Therapy approach, I help clients explore the stories they tell about themselves, identify patterns that no longer serve them, and begin to shape new, empowering narratives.I also focus on the mind-body connection, recognizing how emotions are experienced physically and how stress, anxiety, and trauma can impact both body and mind. Together, we’ll work to understand these connections, develop emotional awareness, and integrate mindfulness and grounding techniques to foster healing and balance. Therapy can be a powerful space for gaining clarity, strengthening resilience, and moving forward with a deeper sense of purpose. Let’s work together to help you reconnect with your authentic self and create meaningful change.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: “Owning our story can be hard, but not nearly as difficult as spending our lives running from it.” Brene Brown

name: Heather Knapp
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi there! Welcome to Momentum therapy. To start, I am so glad you are finally taking this opportunity to take care of you. You are worth it.
ideal_client: I believe in creating a space that will provide you with the courage and strength to empower your life and support you where ever you may be in your journey. Today is a new day. A new start. Let's work together to create a life that is more fulfilled, meaningful and heading the right direction. It will not always be easy but it will be worth it. Let's do this. I encourage you to come as you are. Being able to be real and ready for these life challenges and developing healthier ways to manage.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: A bit about my approach to therapy: In therapy, I utilize various theories, modalities and approaches depending on your specific concerns and needs. I have worked in many different areas over the last 26 years including grief work with children and adults, PTSD, depression and anxiety. Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is aimed at changing unhelpful thinking and also learned behavior patterns. I have found the use of art as a great way to express what cannot be said in words. I cannot say enough about importance of self care planning. What you can expect from our first session: Change in our lives does not happen overnight and remembering that change is a process. It is important to be kind and gentle to yourself along the way. This is something I strongly encourage. Small goals that are achievable are very important that can lead to those larger goals. Therapy should not feel stressful but something you look forward to that gives you more than what you started with.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe everyone is unique, important and valuable. Being able to be heard, understood, cared for and respected is something that I want you to feel when you are in therapy with me. I am currently the clinical director for a non-profit that helps families and children in grief. Loss changes life and having the right support to navigate through this is important. I feel I can provide you with the right tools and support. I have experience in working with those who have experienced a loss by suicide. I have walked this road myself and know the immense challenges and pain associated with this type of loss. I am here. I consider myself an athlete and know the struggles that can come along in the area of sports and competition. Feelings of low self worth, anxiety and fear of failure or not being able to be successful are constant worries as an athlete. Being able to find yourself and to enjoy what you do so well at is something that I can work with you on.

name: Bryce Cohan
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Hi, I'm Bryce! I work with individuals and relationships at Family Ties Counseling Center.
ideal_client: I know how hard having vulnerable relationship conversations can be. Maybe you feel a surge of anxiety when you think about having a big talk, maybe you learned early in life there’s no point, maybe you struggle to find the time in the grind of daily life. It’s hard. It’s also worth it. I believe that our connections to others, especially our loved ones, are the largest influence on whether we lead fulfilling and happy lives.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am drawn to relational therapy because I believe healthy partnerships are fundamental to people's quality of life, yet this area often receives insufficient direct support. I am particularly passionate about providing support to clients who struggle to find help due to their sexual and gender identity or their relationship structure. As a queer and non-monogamous therapist, I offer clients a level of familiarity with these areas that remains rare, even in Portland. I will do my absolute best to help everyone in the room feel seen and understood and work from that base to figure out what comes next. My therapy style is warm and present and straight forward; we’ll talk about goals, and timelines, and how to stabilize quickly so that getting from one week to the next feels less challenging. I offer free 15 minute phone consultations to get a better idea of whether I’d be a good fit for you. I look forward to talking.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I grew up right here in Portland, and while I’ve spent time living in other states and countries, Portland has always felt like home. I love the city and I love the beautiful environment around us, but Portland has always been home because of my relationships with friends, family, partners, and community. When I am not at work, I’m dragging my friends and partners to secret swimming holes, fiddling around with endless projects--often involving woodworking or computers--and sharing good food and quality time with loved ones.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have been non-monogamous for more than a decade and I integrate my personal experience and training in relational counseling with people who practice all different sorts of relationships.

name: Andrea Mize
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Identity-affirming individual & relationship therapy for adults. Queer, kinky, non-monogamous, and intimate industry professionals welcome.
ideal_client: I believe you're here because something in your life isn't working as you would like it to. I would like to help you tap into your internal, intrinsic ability to identify where the problem is, make changes where you can, develop self-compassion if that is lacking in your life, and heal what hurts. Whether you are just figuring out who you are and have known for some time, I provide an affirming and knowledgeable collaborative environment for you to make the change you need to.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer both brief problem-oriented, solution-focused therapy (6-20 sessions) and longer-term, open-ended psychotherapy depending upon your needs. I provide support and compassion while challenging you to move towards your stated goals. Our sessions will be more of a conversation and collaboration with feedback flowing both directions to help you make the movement you seek. Productive therapy and life change happens when a solid, trusting relationship forms between client and therapist. One of my strengths as a therapist is forming that bond quickly with my clients so that we can identify and address problems together. While therapy takes time, I endeavor to help the change process along, providing encouragement and insight to aid carefully yet efficient growth. I encourage an open dialogue about how our fit is in sessions to ensure you are receiving the best support and aid that I can provide.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I share many identities with the people I serve and have a long personal history with invisibility. I bring a personal and professional understanding of the toll invisibility takes. While many people have identities reflected in community membership, we can often feel separated from these spaces and people. I believe most of us don't fit neatly into boxes, including ones designed for those of us left out of traditional spaces. Sometimes we don't feel seen in our relationships even if we do not experience invisibility or marginality in kthe world. I recognize that we can all feel missed and misunderstood no matter who and how we are. A sense of belonging and inclusion are some of the key factors in mental wellness. I strive to help my clients find safety, security and belonging in themselves to carry with them when encountering places, spaces and situations where they do not feel supported or understood.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: I focus on the development of healthy relationships as part of mental health. This includes understanding boundaries as well as understanding the importance of attachment in our relationships. I am a whole person that develops a relationship with you in the treatment. While the therapy is focused on you, I understand that concerns that arise in your life outside of therapy will likely show up in our relationship. We can address them openly so you can use that knowledge outside of therapy.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I tend to draw from many different theories and perspectives as I have not found one particular method that suits all or most clients. I appreciate the many theories and interventions I have had exposure to and have found most to be useful in some way for some clients. I work instinctively relying on the relationship built and the requests that clients make such as needing a particular understanding or type of skill in order to determine which approaches to draw from.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: My graduate training program was based in psychodynamic teachings or "meaning-making" of your life and experiences. I continue to seek out continuing educational opportunities to support this foundational understanding of human behavior as I beleive it helps create context for how we are and show up in our lives. I combine elements of each of the treatment approaches I listed to create a foundation that addresses your particular needs.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: I am a kink-aware AASECT-certified sex therapist with a focus on holistic and integrative approaches. I have extensive experience with, am a proponent of, and have have received prior training in, the benefits of kink-oriented practices in personal growth and healing. A particular area of specialty is in transitions from one type of sexual identity to another as well as fluidity in sexual identity.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have a 20+ year personal history with this identity, with a focus on LGBTQIA community in consensual nonmongamy. In addition I have attended numerous trainings over the last decade and continue to immerse myself in new developments taking place in the various communities attached to non-monogamy in its many forms and manifestations.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I am an identity-affirming clinician for all gender identities. I have had a lot of experience with supporting nonbinary, genderqueer and gendervoid folks. I offer therapy to support those who are gender-questioning as well as those who have a trans history or gender nonconforming identity that is not a focus of therapy, and want someone who understands how this part of identity affects how they interact with the world and how the world responds to them.

name: Liz Ward
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Relationship & individual therapist specializing in non-monogamy, kink/BDSM, ADHD, Autism, LGBTQIA+ issues, and gender identity.
ideal_client: While I work with people of all backgrounds, most of my experience has been working with clients who are navigating LGBTQIA+ issues, gender identity, queer identity, non-monogamy/polyamory, kink/BDSM, sex and sexuality, asexuality, geekiness/nerdiness, religious/spiritual trauma, ADHD, Autism, relational and family trauma, anxiety, and depression. I work with couples/polycules and individuals who are 18 years and older.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy is a place where a person is provided the space to create change and growth in their emotional and mental wellbeing, which with time, can extend to other areas of their life. I believe that this is possible through fostering a therapeutic relationship where one feels safe to explore all the pieces of themself. As a therapist, I believe in the connection between our bodies and minds, and in allowing new experiences to propel growth. My work is grounded in queer theory, awareness of systemic injustice, and trauma-informed care. In the practice of therapy, I lean into somatic practices, parts work, mindfulness, emotions, and experiential components. I am DBT Trained. While I use some elements of DBT when appropriate, I also draw from other modes of therapy such as Emotionally Focused Therapy, Somatic Psychotherapy, Narrative Therapy, and Acceptance and Commitment therapy.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: As a non-binary, queer, non-monogamous, white, AuDHD, and invisibly disabled person, I aim to understand all the parts of your identity and how they may show up in your life. I seek to understand you as best as possible knowing that you are a unique person with a depth of life experience that has led you to where you are today. My best work is done collaboratively, supporting you in achieving the outcomes you want to see by bringing my knowledge to the room. My goal is to empower you to build and maintain the life that you want to be living. If you are interested in working with me, feel free to reach out at the contact form below. I offer free 20-minute consultations so we can determine if we'd be a good fit to begin therapy.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: I am DBT Trained and integrate aspects of DBT into therapy as appropriate. I find DBT helpful in navigating challenges with emotional distress, emotional dysregulation, interpersonal challenges, and foundational skills that can help create a baseline to engage in life from.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: One of the reasons I decided to be a therapist was to work with couples, especially folks who are non-monogamous, knowing that there is not enough support for ENM and polyamorous people. I spent much of my graduate studies along with education afterwards focusing on how to help people develop relationships that work for them.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: Relationships don't always fit the story our society has taught us to expect. I come from the perspective that relationships work best when they can be defined and agreed upon by the people within them, and I aim to help you explore what that would look like for you.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: Gender is a complex and nuanced spectrum of experience. It is different for everyone, and worth examining to understand what your unique gender experience looks like. Exploration of gender identity is for everyone - you don't have to be transgender to explore your gender identity!

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships are hard! It is completely normal to have ebbs and flows in our relationships, especially if they are long-term. Just because it's normal to hit rough patches doesn't mean it's easy to navigate. I am here to help you navigate next steps in your relationship, whether that is making conscious and intentional efforts towards staying in your relationship, changing the agreements or structure of your relationship, or even if it means ending the relationship altogether.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: Sexuality can be challenging to navigate, especially considering the things we have learned (or that we didn't) about what sexuality means for us as individuals. Our sexuality is linked to so many aspects of our experience. I can help you gently sort through all these layers and understand how the things you learned have impacted you today so that you can engage in your sexuality in a way that feels best for you.

name: Bri Dittlinger
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hi, I'm Bri! A clinical social worker who specializes in healing the survivor inside each of us!
ideal_client: I am a clinical social worker specializing in work with adolescents, young adults, and families; my comfortable age range is ages 14-40. My ideal client is looking to find healing and peace through a holistic, systems based, trauma informed approach.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My theoretical training and interests include Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Family Systems Theory, Narrative Therapy, Mindfulness Based Interventions, Polyvagal Theory, and Trauma Informed Interventions. I believe in a holistic, systems based approach to healing, and offer telehealth only services on Tuesdays and Fridays.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a social worker, advocate, therapist, and trauma survivor. I have been in the field for a decade, and my favorite part of this work is witnessing the strength and resilience of the people that I get to work with! I believe in an open and honest approach to therapy, using storytelling, psychoeducation, analogies, somatic healing, and plenty of real talk. This process can be heavy and difficult, yet also rewarding and powerful. It takes a strong person to confront their trauma narratives and embrace their inner alpha, congratulations on starting your journey to conquer that challenge!

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Trained in MBSR and MBCT

specialities.name: Narrative
specialities.description: Utilize narrative therapy and storytelling in session

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: Trained in IFS skills integration in sessions

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Grad certificate in CBT

name: Catherine Caruso
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: We are all doing the best we can. I strive to help build resilience, efficacy, calm, and joy to make our best even better.
ideal_client: I am a firm believer in finding the strengths within us to create the change we would like to see. Finding love for yourself in this moment is key to identifying the work that is needed for you to become the best version of you. I offer an encouraging/supportive space to work towards these changes.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our work will help you identify and focus on your strengths. It will help you bring attention to and interrupt the behaviors you wish to change. Part of my role in your journey towards wellness includes offering emotional regulation skills for the here and now to help with the longer journey. We will work together to reduce distress, allowing you to work on deeper/bigger issues should that be your intention. I offer DBT, CBT, and Interpersonal Neurobiology along with a myriad of modalities to best suit individual needs.

approaches.Social Justice Issues I Care About: I work firmly in harm reduction. This applies to all areas of my work, but in substance use care and mental health. We can reduce harm by adding safety, supports, and knowledge.

name: Adrian Larsen Sanchez
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I am a clinical psychologist & psychoanalyst and have experience working with diverse people towards emotional growth and insight.
ideal_client: I work with people from various and intersecting backgrounds to address their particular human struggles and dilemmas, including depression, anxiety, trauma, unstable moods, grief, personality difficulties, relationship issues, and challenging behaviors and patterns.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach therapy as a collaboration, rooted in understanding each person as an individual in the context of their family, history, culture and daily life. I particularly value the vital role of deepening insight into emotional issues, developing satisfying relationships and realistic self-esteem for healing, growth and sustainable symptom relief. I primarily practice psychoanalytic psychotherapy, an evidence based treatment, though I am also able to integrate techniques from other therapy models (e.g. cognitive and dialectical behavioral therapy). [Read more about psychoanalytic psychotherapy here: http://www.apsa.org/content/psychoanalytic-psychotherapy.] As a part of my practice, I also offer collaborative/therapeutic psychological assessment (testing). In collaborative/therapeutic assessment, patients are engaged to develop questions about themselves to be addressed through the assessment. Validated psychological tests are used to help illuminate underlying difficulties.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my doctorate in clinical psychology at Pacific University and completed my clinical internship at Jacobi Medical Center/Albert Einstein College of Medicine in NYC. I completed my postdoctoral fellowship at Kaiser Permanente, NW Division and a fellowship in psychoanalysis at the Institute for Psychoanalytic Education/NYU School of Medicine. I am a graduate of the 4 year psychoanalytic training program at the Institute of Contemporary Psychoanalysis in Los Angeles.

name: David Singer
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Hello, my name is David. I'm a Licensed Clinical Social Worker with over 19 years of experience. I am licensed in Oregon and Washington.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with those experiencing grief/loss, major life stressors, depression, stress, anxiety, LGBTQ issues, men's issues, new medical diagnoses as well as many others. I provide assessments for emotional support animals.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: CERTIFIED MINDFULLNESS-BASED STRESS REDUCTION COUNSELOR TRAINED IN ANIMAL ASSISTED INTERVENTIONS - EMOTIONAL SUPPORT ANIMAL ASSESSMENTS APPROVED TO PROVIDE CLINICAL SUPERVISION TOWARDS LCSW IN OREGON

name: Glynis 'Glee' Lumb
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I use art or talk therapy with a positive strength-based approach to help clients resolve internal conflicts so they can begin to thrive.
ideal_client: Are you tired of struggling to thrive in relationships? Do you feel anxious and overwhelmed, shutdown, or frustrated in life? Interacting with others can be overwhelming when you have experienced trauma, grief, depression or anxiety. Folks who are seeking calm, mindful, creative, and intentional healing will find my approach helpful. I also collaborate with neurodivergent folks of all ages who want to feel accepted and understood for their unique way of solving problems and also improve.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide a wholistic, eclectic approach uniquely tailored to the individual or group pulling from 20 years of experience in human services, parenting, and clinical practice. I collaborate with clients to build positive experiences in a caring therapeutic relationship through talking (Person Centered, CBT), somatic approaches (Lifespan Integration, Trauma Informed, Art Therapy, Parts Work), mindfulness, playing (children), sand and art therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Trained and experienced in Art Therapy, Attachment theory, Trauma Informed Care, Solution Focused, Dialectical Behavior Therapy, Sand Tray, Lifespan Integration & Somatic Approaches, Flash Technique for Trauma Processing, Mindfulness and Spiritual Practice. I work through a lens of neurodiversity and intersectionality.

name: Taffy Spencer
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Trauma-informed, inclusive care using ACT, CBT, & somatic therapy to help clients heal & thrive. Immediate daytime and evening availability.
ideal_client: Being human is complicated. You might feel stuck repeating painful patterns, weighed down by old wounds, or overwhelmed by anxiety about the future. You want to break free, heal from past experiences, and experience genuine peace of mind. You’re looking for a therapist who offers compassion, trust, respect, and real tools for change. You want to feel safe being your authentic self. Together, we will explore your unique story, uncover strengths, nurture resilience, and build the life you deserve.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy can help you reconnect with hope, purpose, and your true self. Finding a therapist who can create a safe, non-judgmental, and constructive environment built on mutual trust and respect is critical to the success of the therapeutic process. We will work in collaboration to set attainable and meaningful goals for therapy, and I’ll tailor my practice to work with your style and needs. I am trained in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), somatic therapy, and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), and I integrate these tools with elements of narrative and solution-focused therapy modalities. I also incorporate the science of neurobiology into my work with clients because many people find it helpful to better understand how the brain works.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: My point of view as a therapist is strengths-based, trauma-informed, and social justice-oriented. I warmly welcome clients from all walks of life and particularly enjoy working with people with diverse life experiences, including the LGBTQ+ community, people living with ADHD or autism, and people of color. My role is to be your helper, ally, and guide in your travels as you work through the past and move toward a healthier, brighter future.

name: Ryoka Kim
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I became a psychologist to help those who are undergoing various life transitions.
ideal_client: I work with adult clients through individual therapy to address stress management associated with relationships, careers, and serious illness. Being at a crossroads often invites us to go deeper within ourselves to discover our values and inner voice. With an approach based in the mindfulness and biopsychosocial perspectives, we’ll cultivate self-awareness and intentionality to achieve your goals through tangible and manageable steps.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Additionally, I specialize in addressing end-of-life concerns, including caregiver stress, family communication, and grief. Facing death brings various challenges, but it can also lead to a powerful experience of appreciation and meaning. Whether it’s about one’s own mortality or a loved one’s, I assist my clients to feel educated and prepared to deal with the transition.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Oregon always had a special place in my heart, ever since I spent a magical year at the University of Oregon as a Japanese exchange student. After 12 years of moving around the U.S., I finally found my way back and have been living in Portland since 2017. I enjoy traveling, a good cup of coffee on a foggy morning, and am passionate about cooking with plenty of garlic!

name: Emma Larson
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I specialize in working with the LGBTQIA+ community, the neurodivergent community, those navigating religious trauma, and grief/loss.
ideal_client: My approach as a counselor is collaborative, trauma-informed, and grounded in curiosity, compassion, and social justice. I hope to create a space where you don’t have to filter or shrink yourself—where we can explore what matters to you, dismantle what doesn’t, and help you feel more at home in your life and body.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My style is eclectic and anchored in self-exploration, cultural awareness, and self-compassion. I draw from frameworks like IFS, Feminist, and Existential Therapy that explore how our different parts intersect and how the world around us shapes our reality, values, and relationships. Therapy with me highlights authenticity, depth, and laughter. I earned my Master’s in Counseling from Lewis & Clark College. Outside of therapy, you’ll likely find me knitting on the couch with a cat (or two) in my lap, catching a local drag show, or chasing a sunbeam to sit in.

name: Brooke Hammond
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I provide an open and non-judgmental space for you to safely explore the issues and patterns that bring you into therapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I specialize in treating the symptoms of trauma (anxiety, fears, phobias, nightmares, flashbacks) using Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR). EMDR is a remarkably effective tool for resolving traumatic or painful events from the past that continue to affect you today. EMDR can bring relatively quick relief from troubling feelings and memories. It does not erase the painful memories, but rather, takes away their physical and emotional impact. EMDR might be useful for you if: you have been feeling “stuck” and unable to “get over” certain events or feelings; you find yourself repeating patterns throughout your life that are damaging to you or the people you care about; you have experienced a significant traumatic event or a series of hurtful incidents that continue to influence your feelings and behaviors.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have over 20 years of experience working with children, adolescents, and families in a variety of settings, including community-based mental health agencies, prisons and immigration detention centers, families’ homes, schools, international social service agencies, and psychiatric hospitals. I work with survivors of domestic violence, abuse, trauma, and torture; immigrants and refugees; LGBTQ; people experiencing depression and anxiety; and people struggling with transitions, grief, and loss.

name: Tina Lilly, MS LPC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Supporting you in finding courage and strength to live and love well
ideal_client: I work with individuals and couples who are committed to change, want to be challenged, and are time conscious (life is short). This includes following through with in between session therapeutic assignments and honest communication.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to counseling is based on the belief that we are here to wake up to the fullest expression of ourselves. What we may feel instead is a poignant dissatisfaction with our career, partner, body, or self. I draw from insight-oriented spiritual traditions and contemporary body-mind practices to support you in your quest for meaning, purpose, authenticity, and connection.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My training includes a Master's degree in counseling (PSU), EMDR, post-graduate training in EFT, sex therapy, hypnosis, and other modalities. I am also a writer, book author, and meditation teacher.

specialities.name: Hypnotherapy
specialities.description: I use hypnotherapy for many of my clients' problems and have seen amazing results in a short amount of time. For more information visit www.tributariesofjoy.com.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I'm a seasoned, directive and effective couples therapist. I help couples wanting to prepare for marriage, improve communication, heal from betrayal, rekindle romance and deepen sexual connection in long-term relationships, and with many other needs.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR (Level 1 & 2) and use EMDR frequently and effectively with clients.

specialities.name: Sexual Problems
specialities.description: Sexual expression is a fundamental human need. Intimately connected to our sense of self, sex is an opportunity to ask for what we want for our growth as individuals and partners, to play, to feel alive and creative, and to transcend, if only momentarily, the experience of our mortality.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: I have over two decades worth experience working with women starting a family. Before becoming a therapist, I've attended births as a doula, taught prenatal yoga and childbirth education. I'm also the author of a book about yoga and childbirth and continue to support women therapeutically during the childbearing years.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationship issues repeatedly surface in the clinical areas I specialize in (pregnancy, parenting, infertility, post-partum adjustment, dating, divorce). I also specialize in issues related to sexuality.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression sucks. It sucks desire, motivation, agency, energy, joy and vitality, i.e. all the things that make life worth living. It can make life seem pointless, but there is a point to depression, a way to be with it, and a way to be without. I can help you figure out how.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief and Loss are frequent 'clients' of mine. Whether they arrive in the wake of losing a loved one, a pregnancy or a child, a relationship or a marriage, an ability or a dream, they are allies in integrating difficult life experiences, and deserve nurturing and attention.

name: Bella Box, DC
title: Somatic Practitioner
credentials: Retired chiropractor, 200 yoga teacher training certification, T'ai Chi Chih accredited teacher
intro: I offer a 10-week private lesson in tai chi chih p-both on-line and in person. I also offer private yoga lessons both in-person and on-line
ideal_client: My yoga and t'ai chi practice attracts both students who are brand new and those with some or a lot of experience. I am a retired chiropractor. I founded the Holistic Health Clinic in Beaverton where I treated patients, facilitated clinic administrative issues and served as clinical director for 32 years.

approaches.How We Can Help You: I became a licensed LMT in 1982. My undergraduate degree was in clinical psychology, which I completed in 1978. I earned my chiropractic license in 1985. I became an accredited t'ai chi chih teacher in 2000. Finally, I became a yoga teacher in 2023. My psychology, chiropractic and massage therapy has informed my t'ai chi and yoga teaching style. I teach with a holistic lens, listening to my students to identify the learning sweet spot. I specialize in trauma informed sensitive brain approach with my teaching style. I flourish with students who struggle with depression, anxiety, Complex PTSD, Bipolar I and II.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My philosophy is to help my students heal through moving their bodies, developing their mindfulness, learning to chant, and by providing a healing presence. Volunteer Service: Tommy, our 7-year old schipperke and I are a therapy team for Hospice. This work has been a calling for me. Assisting a client move from active living to active dying is a profound privilege. The Divine is easily recognized during the dying process. Additional Volunteer Service: I teach a group yoga class at Bybee Lakes Hope Center. This is an amazing program that teaches life skills to folks who have previously been houseless and having substance abuse. I love being an ancillary member to facilitate deep healing through yoga.

name: Allison Spector
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I believe in the power of healing through connection.
ideal_client: Are there are things from your past that are continuing to impact your daily life? Do you feel like there are things about yourself or your behaviors that you don't fully understand? Do you feel overwhelmed or overstimulated by life’s responsibilities? If so, I may be able to help. By collaborating together, we can build awareness of the automatic patterns and habits that create distress in your life and actively work towards dismantling unhealthy narratives and beliefs.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy is deeply vulnerable work, but by building trust in the therapeutic relationship we can explore and identify automatic patterns and habits that may be keeping you from feeling your best and work together to practice new ways of living. In my work, I pull from a variety of theoretical approaches including Brainspotting, EMDR, CBT, Family Systems Theory, Internal Family Systems, Attachment Theory, Narrative Therapy, Polyvagal Theory, and Mindfulness Based practices.

name: Nicole Falk
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: Psychotherapy with a holistic approach.
ideal_client: If you feel overwhelmed with all of the changes in your life and in the world around you, or conversely feel numb and detached, let's talk. I practice with a variety of clients, however I specialize in adults experiencing the effects of life changes and transitions, codependency, relationship issues, and managing work/life balance.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: For many of us, the hardest challenge to overcome is to ask for help. If you're reading this, you've already found the courage to start becoming the best version of yourself. While as an individual you are unique, none of us are perfect and we all experience conflict, hardships, and a variety of emotions. I believe our life experiences as well as cultural background influence the way in which we interact with the world. I am a strong proponent of collaboration and I view the therapeutic relationship as a team.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I have a gentle approach to building relationships combined with down to earth 'real talk' about what can help you feel better. I often incorporate mindfulness techniques into our work together, and am someone who's open to feedback and learning about your unique perspective on the world. Please keep in mind I offer TELEHEALTH appointments only at this time, with daytime availability Monday through Thursday.

name: Mikaylee Dato
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm Mikaylee, and I am excited you are here taking this step towards bettering yourself! If you are ready to get started today, reach out.
ideal_client: Are you tired of carrying the weight of unresolved trauma or difficult life experiences? Well you are in the right place! I work with individuals who are ready to break free from the cycles that are keeping them stuck and provide the tools necessary for lasting change so you can live a more fulfilling life. I bring insight and dedication to helping clients feel seen and empowered to grow from life’s challenges and develop resilience and greater well-being.

approaches.How I Can Help You: Life can be a wild ride, but you don’t have to do it alone! I utilize a client centered, strengths-based, trauma informed approach to therapy. I offer a safe and collaborative process to guide you to evaluate, understand, and process thoughts and experiences that will allow for significant healing. I will meet you where you are at and draw upon your strengths to empower you as you process all life has thrown at you, as well as challenge thoughts, beliefs, and behaviors that might be keeping you stuck. With my holistic approach, I will integrate all facets of your life into our work. I tailor my theory and interventions to meet each client's individual needs and abilities and therefore, have understanding and practice in various evidence-based modalities. I am also trained in EMDR.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: In my time as a therapist, I have worked in both inpatient and outpatient settings providing individual, group, and family counseling. I have also enjoyed providing therapy services to multiple private and public elementary and high schools to make access to care easier for students and families. As an Oregon native, I’ve always loved the outdoors—whether it’s hiking, camping, wake surfing, snowboarding, or snowshoeing. I enjoy exploring new places, immersing myself in different cultures, and connecting through food. When I’m not out adventuring, you’ll find me with a great cup of coffee or tea, binging a good show, and soaking up quality time with my favorite people.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I successfully treat symptoms of PTSD through EMDR and other interventions. Most of my clients see symptom reduction within weeks of starting EMDR and trauma therapy.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I am an ADHD specialist with extensive training and experience in assessing, diagnosing, and treating ADHD.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I extensive training and experience in assessing, diagnosing, and treating depression

specialities.name: OCD
specialities.description: I have experience helping clients navigate all kinds of OCD obsessions and compulsions. With the right tools, you can manage and eliminate your OCD for good!

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I extensive training and experience in assessing, diagnosing, and treating anxiety.

name: Zoe Presley
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am passionate about supporting the mental health of my community through counseling and nature-based approaches.
ideal_client: Are you feeling alone, afraid, or overwhelmed? Are you having difficulty navigating profound adjustments to your life or your relationships? Are others in your life depending on you to guide them through difficult times? I will help you achieve a sense of calm and a perspective of hopefulness.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: During the COVID-19 outbreak, I am offering Telehealth (video or phone counseling). For the past decade, I have specialized in treating depression, anxiety, relationship challenges, and stress. My approach to your wellbeing includes practical tools, mindfulness, and gentle compassion.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: For well over a decade, I have guided individuals and groups in cultivating wellbeing. I am trained in Transcendental Meditation, and as a Depth Psychotherapist and Forest Therapy Guide. My approach is supportive, interactive and experiential, including mindfulness, somatic (body-based), and depth psychotherapy, as well as practical approaches to support you in feeling grounded in yourself and at peace with your life.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness is a necessary practice in our modern world, where we can easily feel overwhelmed, confused and frustrated. Maintaining awareness of our body, our thoughts, and the impact of our thoughts on our behavior and relationships supports us to stay grounded. With years of experience practicing and teaching meditation, I share powerful tools to help my clients build their own practice.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: Since childhood, nature has been my sanctuary for creative exploration and healing. As a psychotherapist, the majority of my practice occurs either out-of-doors or within an elegant yurt sanctuary at my retreat space in Portland's NW Hills. I have seen dramatic positive changes unfold as we allow ourselves to learn from and interact with the natural world.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is often experienced as feeling separate from the world as if you are all alone, or the heavy weight of apathy and fatigue. I address depression with curiosity, sensitivity, and care utilizing a variety of therapeutic approaches focusing on empowerment and understanding. The clients I have treated for depression have expressed how counseling has brought them hopefulness and deep peace.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: My unique professional experience with nature-based therapy and Cross-Cutural Music and Sound Healing offers helpful alternatives to conventional approaches. Treating anxiety is about cultivating safety in your body and mind. I will show you how to develop a loving, supportive relationship with your self.

specialities.name: Coronavirus/COVID-19
specialities.description: You are not alone if you're experiencing a heightened sense of fear, isolation, anxiety or depression at this time. Somatic and mindfulness approaches to therapy are very helpful in times of overwhelm and crisis, and I am here to support you in these ways.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Having experienced my own health challenges in the past, I can empathize with the frustration and isolation of physical pain and illness. However, as you deepen your relationship with your body, you will connect with a deeper, healing essence that resides within us all. This has been true for me, and can also be true for you.

name: Anne Thompson
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: When life brings challenges to your mental health or relationships, there is an opportunity for resourcefulness, resilience, and hope.
ideal_client: I have worked with clients with a wide range of concerns including depression, anxiety, relationship and communication problems, parenting problems and grief and loss. I also helped many people who have experienced physical trauma or emotional abuse.

approaches.How I Can Help You: My therapy style is warm and interactive. I am compassionate, curious, trauma-informed, and social-justice oriented. I believe that counseling support helps people feel less isolated and alone when facing lifes difficulties. My approach combines emotionally focused approaches, cognitive-behavioral methods and a depth and attachment perspective to help you achieve self-awareness and healing. Together we will define goals and objectives to meet your unique and specific needs. I am committed to helping my clients experience change outside the therapy room. I look forward to working with you!

name: Sarah Lange
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am accepting Individuals, couples and families using OHP insurance.
ideal_client: Do you want to make a change? Coping skills often developed early on in life and were important to help get you to where you are today. They can arise from a childhood that seems "normal" or one filled with trauma and struggle. Coming to therapy is a step in healing the wounds from the past and working with the struggles of today. I can help you process your lived experience at your pace to help you move forward and make positive changes in your life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My goal as a therapist is to help my clients experience transformative change in their lives. I am interested in going deep to find out what our subconscious is creating in our lives and how self-understanding can help shift our unwanted patterns.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I use a holistic approach to therapy drawing on Family Systems theory, Existential, Attachment theory and Psychodynamic therapy lenses. I also use tools like mindfulness, and somatic practices. I believe in “inner healing intelligence,” the intrinsic knowledge that each of us possesses about how to heal ourselves.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Exploring what attachment was like in early childhood can help us understand what is going on in adult relationships.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: As parents we have a beautiful opportunity to do better than was done for us. I would love to support you in this tender time.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I help my ADHD clients adjust to the challenges and gifts that come with an ADHD diagnoses.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I use Emotional Focused relationship therapy techniques. I also help clients stop avoiding conflict and start getting their needs met with their partners.

name: Sprout Therapy PDX
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: If you’re reading this, we already know you’re struggling.
ideal_client: Maybe you’re having trouble “adulting”. You’re feeling like every one else seems to have it all together, why can’t you? You might feel like you’re out of control of your life. You’re tired of doing the same things over and over again with no results. Maybe you’re seeing your child, partner, or loved one facing their own mental health challenges and you feel helpless to create change. This is not the best your life can be. It will get better- and we're here to help you get there.

approaches.Our Background and Approach: We know how hard it is to finding someone who gets it. Who’s relatable and real. Who’s going to be there to weather your storms and get down and dirty with the weird stuff that makes us all human. Who you can laugh with as well as cry. We just want you to know- we are here to help.

approaches.More About the People We Treat: We work with young adults, kids, teens, families, and couples of any kind. Our team works with trauma, anxiety, depression, and many other treatment issues. We are an LGBTQIA+ allied practice and identify as progressive and anti-racist. We are now accepting Oregon Health Plans (OHP) clients with authorization. Contact us for more information on your specific coordinated care organization.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: We specialize in supporting clients with depression, whether it's situational, persistent, or associated with other mental health conditions. Drawing from a variety of therapeutic modalities such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), psychodynamic therapy, and mindfulness techniques, we collaborate with you to navigate through the complexities of depression to effectively manage and alleviate the symptoms of depression, fostering a path towards greater emotional well-being & resilience.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: We believe the relationship between clinician and client is the groundwork that leads to effective therapy. Creating a solid connection and mutual respect allows deep work to occur in the therapy room.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy works strategically to help you identify your thoughts, feelings, and behaviors, and how they all interact to create your internal world. We may use CBT in tandem with exposure and response prevention (ERP) for folks dealing with symptoms related to OCD, panic, PTSD, or anxiety.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: We are trained to consider presenting issues from a contextual family systems lens and are always considering complex intergenerational trauma and other family dynamics in our work with all clients- whether you come to therapy with your family or as an individual.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: Many clinicians at our practice identify on the LGBTQIA+ spectrum, and all of us at Sprout have experience working with queer folks. We all consider ourselves lifelong allies to our LGBTQIA+ community.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Our team loves working with couples and relationships of all kinds! We have expertise working with open, poly, or ethically non-monogamous individuals, couples, and polycules.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is one of our greatest afflictions as a society. We frequently work with clients with anxiety disorders of all kinds, including panic, OCD, and PTSD. We use many approaches to treat anxiety, but pull from cognitive behavioral therapy approaches, mindfulness, and exposure and response prevention (ERP) to help you learn skills to manage these intensely uncomfortable experiences.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: The low lows of depression are not fun. We aim to stand beside you as you cope with depression and help you get back on your feet again, using interventions from CBT and DBT.

name: Jacqueline Lydston, MSW, LSWAIC
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Welcome! I offer individual therapy to clients interested in addressing many life issues, from a warm, client centered, relational approach.
ideal_client: Are you feeling depressed, anxious, stressed? Have you experienced pain, trauma, abandonment, fear, rejection? These are all experiences with which I am familiar and which I can help you to work through. Are you a medical professional who's been overwhelmed by COVID? Or a first responder who is struggling with feeling overworked and under appreciated? I can help you as well. I work with a wide array of clients who are trying to make sense of their lives, their feelings, and their thoughts.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In your therapy, I will work carefully to provide a calm, warm, safe space in which to explore your unique self, and what happiness, satisfaction, and fulfillment looks like for you. I will accompany you as you discover meaning and purpose in the face of difficult feelings, experiences, and thoughts. As therapy progresses, we will talk about everything that is important to you; therapy is about you and your life, not just the therapeutic “tricks and tips.” Your body and mind constitute an original and resilient Self, and we will base your therapy on its resources. The point of your therapy is to help you make your life better as you define it, and I will do my utmost to tailor my approach to your needs. As we work together, it is my deep hope that you come to feel that I understand, respect, and honor who you are and what you value. I work from a relational, client centered approach, informed by IFS, CBT, DBT, and psychodynamic perspectives.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that we are all unique individuals, worthy of and deserving of respect, care, ease, and comfort. I believe that healing is not only possible, it is imperative. If you have had traumatic experiences, you deserve to heal. If you are overwhelmed, you deserve to have a place in which to rest and learn new coping skills. If you are confused, you deserve to have a place in which to find clarity. And if you simply want to know yourself better and learn to value and love the unique person that you are, you deserve a place in which you can discover your uniqueness and celebrate it. I am here to help you with any or all of the above; it is my privilege to work with you toward whatever goals you wish. Therapy is about you and your goals as you define them. I pledge to work with you on that journey.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have worked since 1989 with women and men who have survived abuse in their lives, whether from childhood or adulthood.

specialities.name: Personality Disorders
specialities.description: I have worked since 1989 with people struggling with borderline personality disorder.

name: Caitlin Schrage
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi, I'm Caitlin- I'm a compassionate, strength-based therapist here to support you on your healing journey.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with adults who are navigating big transitions, perinatal mental health, carrying the weight of trauma, or feeling stuck in the cycles of anxiety, burnout, or disconnection. My clients often identify as LGBTQIA+, Women, parents, BIPOC, neurodivergent individuals, or folks who have felt unseen in other spaces.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I am a licensed clinical social worker with over a decade of experience supporting adults through complex life challenges. My background includes work in community mental health where I've supported individuals navigating severe mental illness, trauma, substance use, and housing instability. I bring a warm, grounded presence to the work, and I'm committed to providing inclusive care. Therapy is not one-size-fits-all, and I believe in tailoring treatment to each individual’s unique experience, strength, and needs. My approach is compassionate, strength-based. II specialize in trauma informed therapy and draw from approaches like Attachment Theory, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing (EMDR), and Emotionally Focused Therapy (EFT).

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that everyone is unique and cannot be fit into a box. Everyone is worthy, and has capacity for growth, healing, and change. I became a counselor because I hold a core belief that everyone deserves to feel valued, find their voice, and live a life that reflects their truth. I've seen this potential in my work and in my personal life. This belief is what continues to guide me. Before becoming a therapist, I was an artist and still use creativity as a tool to help people connect with themselves in new ways. My Approach is warm, relational, and grounded in both social justice and mental health training. I specialize in trauma treatment and have completed 50 hour EMDR training and am training in perinatal mental health. I love working with folks who identify as LGBTQIA+, BIPOC, women, creatives, parents, and those navigating transitions.

name: Hussein Idow
title: Social Worker
intro: I’m a compassionate therapist specializing in anxiety, depression, trauma, and relationship challenges, committed to helping you thrive.
ideal_client: My clients often face overwhelming anxiety, lingering depression, past trauma, or struggles with relationships. They seek a safe, supportive space to explore their emotions, develop healthier coping strategies, and build resilience. Whether you're navigating life transitions, managing stress, or working through unresolved pain, I’m here to help. My approach is tailored to your unique needs, creating a path toward healing and personal growth. Together, we’ll work to restore balance and fulfillmen

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use evidence-based approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), to support clients in overcoming challenges. With over a decade of experience, I’ve worked extensively with individuals facing anxiety, depression, trauma, and relationship struggles. My goal is to provide a safe, nonjudgmental environment where you feel empowered to share your story and explore the root causes of your struggles. Together, we’ll develop practical coping skills and strategies for lasting change. My approach is collaborative, compassionate, and tailored to your needs, ensuring every step of your journey is aligned with your goals for growth and healing.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I believe that everyone deserves a life filled with purpose, connection, and joy. Therapy is not just about addressing challenges—it’s about discovering your strengths, embracing your unique qualities, and unlocking your potential. My interests include exploring mindfulness practices, promoting emotional resilience, and creating tools for personal empowerment. I’m passionate about providing culturally sensitive care and ensuring every client feels seen, heard, and valued. What sets me apart is my genuine commitment to understanding your experiences and guiding you toward meaningful progress. Whether you’re seeking relief from emotional pain, navigating difficult relationships, or striving for personal growth, I’m here to help you succeed. Together, we’ll work to create a life that feels truly fulfilling and aligned with your values.

name: Kombai Nonnarath
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi there, I’m a trauma therapist, I focus on supporting individuals navigating the intersections of culture, trauma, and neurodivergence.
ideal_client: I offer culturally responsive care for BIPOC clients and neurodivergent-affirming therapy for those navigating trauma, codependency, and struggles with self-esteem. My work centers adults with intersecting identities who are ready to break old patterns, reconnect with their values, and move through life with clarity and intention. I bring a warm, collaborative, and authentic approach to therapy, creating a space for meaningful change.

approaches.Our Background and Approach: I’m deeply committed to working with multicultural communities and honoring the complexity that comes with layered identities. As a relational therapist, I draw from a range of modalities guided by intuition and what feels most supportive for you. I integrate holistic practices with evidence-based approaches like Internal Family Systems (IFS) and Brainspotting. In our work together, I will invite you to explore deeply, ask tough questions, and gently bring awareness to the patterns that may be holding you back. My goal is to walk alongside you as you reconnect with your inner wisdom and strength. I invite you to approach this journey with openness and curiosity, as we reflect on the experiences that have brought you here. Together, we’ll co-create a space where you are empowered to heal, grow, and thrive.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Growing up in Oakland as a 1st generation immigrant has deeply informed my perspective on identity, resilience, and healing. With roots in Animism and Buddhism deeply woven into the cultural and spiritual practices of my upbringing, I am inspired to carry forward the healing legacies of my family lineage.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I use IFS (Internal Family Systems) to help you get to know the different “parts” of yourself, like an inner critic, a people pleaser, or a worried part, that show up in thoughts, feelings, or behaviors. Rather than pushing these parts away, we gently explore them to understand what they’re trying to protect or express. Together, we’ll connect with your core Self, your calm, curious inner leader, to bring more clarity, healing, and balance.

specialities.name: Brainspotting
specialities.description: Brainspotting is a gentle way to heal without needing to talk through all the details of your trauma. It helps your brain process what’s stored deep inside, where talking alone can’t always reach. During a session, I’ll guide your gaze to a specific spot and we’ll pay attention to what thoughts, feelings, or body sensations come up. Once we find a “brainspot,” your mind will do the work it needs. When things settle, we’ll take time to ground and begin integrating your experience through a brief

specialities.name: Immigration/Acculturation
specialities.description: Navigating mental health across cultures can be complex - especially for those who identify as Black, Indigenous, People of Color (BIPOC) and neurodivergent. Cultural expectations, stigma, and the absence of shared language or understanding often make these conversations difficult. When neurodivergence is also part of your experience, it can add another layer that’s often overlooked. I offer a space to explore how culture, trauma, and neurodivergence shape your sense of self and relationships. T

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: If you’ve experienced emotionally immature parenting or narcissistic relationships, you may carry deep wounds that affect your self-worth and how you relate to others. As a strength-based therapist, I support you in untangling these patterns and reconnecting with your sense of self. What you’ve been through is not your fault and healing is not something you have to do alone. Together, we’ll explore how past attachment wounds may be shaping your present, creating space for clarity, healthy bounda

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is a deeply personal and often non linear experience. It can arise from many kinds of loss, death, changes in identity, relationships, health, or major life transitions. In grief work, we create space for your emotions to unfold naturally, without rushing toward “closure” or minimizing the complexity of what you carry. Together, we will explore the layers of your loss, honor what has been meaningful, and support the integration of grief into your life in a way that feels authentic. Our wor

name: Martha Carlson
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Welcome to my profile. I'm glad you are taking this step to work on the things that are holding you back.
ideal_client: Would you like to feel less anxious or worried? Is better sleep a goal for you? Are you wishing for an improved relationship? There's no better time than right now to begin working on the things that are holding you back and keeping you from engaging in the life you want. My mission is to provide compassionate and personalized teletherapy that empowers you to navigate life’s challenges, foster emotional well-being, and achieve lasting growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: We will work together to determine which style and type of therapy will work best for you. There are so many to choose from and your buy-in will increase the chance that therapy will reap the benefits you are seeking. I deeply believe in harnessing your strengths in our work together.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe growth and exploration is a useful tool at any age or stage in a person's life. I value compassion, candor and humor.

name: Kelsey Marple
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I will help you identify core needs, heal trauma, and form a healthy personal identity so you can move towards genuine connectedness.
ideal_client: Working with clients to find grounding and direction as they adjust to transitions, heal trauma, form a healthy personal identity, and overcome shame so that they can step into life with genuine presence is one of my greatest joys.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach towards therapy is relational and trauma-informed. Often, I find that people are aware of the hurdles keeping them from living life to the fullest, but can benefit from professional support in actively working through them instead of staying stuck in a cycle. I view counseling as a collaborative effort and help my clients to recognize their strengths, identify needs, understand conflicts, discover new options, and make informed choices in a warm and non-judgmental counseling space through empathy and curiosity.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: We create habits and patterns of how we exist in the world, sometimes without our consent. I believe you can create a new way of moving through life, and being in the world. I hope to empower you to ditch what isn't serving you any longer, and to make decisions and habits based out of your true values and needs.

name: Terry Moody
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: Supporting you through challenges and helping you connect with your innate capacity to heal and create a meaningful, clear, connected life.
ideal_client: I work with adults and couples facing grief, loss, and challenging transitions; depression, anxiety, addiction, and questions of identity and worth; PTSD, dissociation, and relational trauma; relationship and communication issues; career and role transitions; ADHD, those who identify as highly sensitive, and creative people. For couples, I create space to explore intimacy, communication patterns, and the dynamics of your connection, while helping you write a new chapter in your shared journey.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Healing happens through authentic presence and the warmth of connection – with ourselves, each other, and the world that supports us. I see myself as an ally and guide, committed to holding a clear and compassionate space to support you in coming home to who you really are. When we allow ourselves to be seen by another in the space of unconditional positive regard, the knots of suffering are softened and can begin to untangle. Inspired by the power of therapeutic connection, my passion is supporting people in accessing their innate capacity for healing and creating lives filled with meaning, clarity, beauty, and wholeness. I view healing as a collaborative journey where we work together to find the most honoring ways to support your goals. This journey is a dance between effort and ease, depth and levity, fueled by courage, commitment, and plenty of humor.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I draw from diverse psychotherapeutic, spiritual, and somatic traditions, including Internal Family Systems, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, Buddhist psychology, polyvagal theory, neuroscience, and mindfulness traditions to meet each client and each moment exactly where you are. Therapy works on both cognitive and deeper levels, tapping into the innate wisdom of the body and mind to heal life’s inevitable wounds, both sudden and accumulated over time. I’m formally trained in EMDR and Lifespan Integration, powerful modalities for processing trauma and integrating fragmented experiences. These processes transform our perspectives on ourselves and our lives, offering a lens of safety, self-compassion, and aliveness, and gifting us with a greater sense of connection. While change can feel challenging at times, I believe the healing journey is equally filled with joy, ease, and expansiveness, and should be “good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end."

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Our earliest relationships become blueprints for how we navigate love, trust, and connection throughout our lives. I help you recognize patterns that developed in childhood as adaptive responses to your environment and explore how these strategies may be serving or limiting you now. In the secure base of our therapeutic relationship, you experience what it feels like to be truly seen, understood, and valued, allowing for neural rewiring and healthier relating patterns.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR recognizes that our bodies hold memories and wisdom that our minds alone cannot access. Trauma lives not just in thoughts, but in the nervous system, breath, and posture, and affects our felt sense of safety in the world. Through bilateral stimulation, we help your brain reprocess traumatic memories, allowing them to be integrated rather than remaining stuck in hypervigilance or numbing. We work somatically, honoring your body as an ally in healing.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: With over two decades of contemplative practice across meditation, breathwork, and yogic inquiry, I bring embodied understanding of how mindfulness transforms our relationship with ourselves and experience. Mindfulness isn’t solely stress-reduction – it’s a way of being where we meet each moment with presence, curiosity, and compassion. We learn to observe thoughts and emotions without being overwhelmed, creating space for wise response rather than reactive patterns.

specialities.name: Transpersonal
specialities.description: Therapy is inherently sacred work where deepest questions of meaning, purpose, and connection are explored. I honor clients across all spiritual and religious beliefs, understanding our connection to the sacred – however we define it – is often our deepest source of strength and resilience. For some this is traditional religion, for others nature, creativity, or service. I create space where your unique relationship to the sacred can be honored and integrated into healing.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: ADHD is a unique neurological difference with both challenges and extraordinary gifts. I view it not as a deficit to fix but a brilliant mind operating at different frequencies. Together we explore how your ADHD brain works – its patterns of attention and awareness, creativity and energy – developing strategies that honor your gifts while building practical skills that work with your natural ways of being. We also heal from feeling “different” or “not enough” in a neurotypical world.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is your nervous system’s attempt to keep you safe in a world that can feel overwhelming or unpredictable. Rather than eliminating it, we learn what the anxiety is trying to tell you and develop a different relationship with it. Anxiety lives in the body as much as the mind, so we use somatic approaches, including breathwork and mindfulness for grounding. You learn to notice anxiety without being swept away or afraid of it, discovering that beneath lies deep care, sensitivity, and wisdom.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief is a natural part of human existence that, when embraced, deepens our capacity for meaning, connection, and joy. Whether you're navigating the death of a loved one, relationship endings, health changes, career losses, identity shifts, a major life transition, the loss of a dream, or what Francis Weller calls the “sorrows of the world,” all grief deserves witnessing and care. Using creative, somatic, and evidence-based approaches, we transform pain into something generative.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression feels like dense fog where joy feels distant and muted. It’s not personal failing but complex response to life experiences deserving compassion. Sometimes depression protects when overwhelmed or signals disconnection from authentic self. We develop gentle relationship with depression while building strategies, using somatic, creative, and mindfulness approaches to restore aliveness.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: PTSD symptoms are evidence of survival instincts working overtime, not signs of being broken. Trauma lives in the body, and healing happens when your nervous system understands you’re safe now. Using EMDR and trauma-informed approaches, we gently process memories for integration. We work at your pace, helping you reclaim agency, wholeness, and connection after trauma.

name: Matthew McCullough
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Areas of focus: loss of faith/religious trauma, substance use/harm reduction, integration therapy, relationship issues, depression, anxiety
ideal_client: I can assist with many of life's difficulties, and you are a great fit if any of the following apply to you: You are struggling to find meaning or how to determine next steps after leaving a religious group. You are contemplating making changes to your substance use but not quite ready to commit to treatment. You are experiencing relationship issues, especially nontraditional forms. You are experiencing impacts to your quality of life due to anxiety, depression, or other mental health concerns.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to counseling centers around identifying the things that matter the most to you and the strengths and abilities you’ve used to survive in this life so far, creating a safe space to look more closely at the difficult areas of life that don’t appear to have easy answers. I see therapy as a healing and creative process, where my training and knowledge act as a mirror to help you unlock your own expertise on yourself. I have over five years of outpatient counseling experience, including individual counseling and group therapy facilitation. My experience includes mental health counseling, substance abuse treatment and process addiction treatment (gambling, technology, etc.), and crisis management and intervention. I ascribe to a humanistic-existentialist philosophy and utilize Acceptance and Commitment Therapy, Solution-Focused Therapy, and Internal Family Systems. I also incorporate mindfulness and somatic-based skills from a neuroscience-informed basis.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My practice is affirming to all people, with particular awareness of the unique ways religion and spirituality have impacted LGBTQ people. I am familiar with the particular concerns transgender individuals face, and the transitioning process. I am open to clients who practice diverse relationships styles (polyamory, kink/BDSM). I strive to maintain cultural humility, both by remaining active in my education around diverse populations, and by being open to and welcoming critical feedback.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I have had a lifelong interest in spirituality since I was a child raised as a Presbyterian. After my own crisis of faith in my middle school years, I have pursued knowledge of world religions, and deepened my knowledge of theology and philosophy. I have extensive knowledge of both Christianity and Buddhism, though personally identify as having a secular spirituality. I see ways in which spirituality can be a tremendous help to one's mental health, as well as a cause of stress and trauma.

specialities.name: Polyamorous and Open Relationships
specialities.description: I have a wide knowledge of different ways people relate to each other and strive to create a non-judgmental environment where the unique situations one may face are treated with respect. I am also familiar with the range of gender identities, and have been with several friends through their transitioning experience.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I offer instruction in using mindfulness and somatic techniques to help create room around anxiety to allow for greater flexibility in one's life.
