I have extensive knowledge of Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), which is a modern approach to getting back to a life worth living so that anxiety no longer runs the show.

specialities.name: Political Climate
specialities.description: In this current era, many people are experiencing the stress that comes along with existential uncertainty, locally, nationally, and ecologically. My existential-humanist background recognizes approaches these concerns without pathologizing or oversimplifying. Instead, I help you determine what approach is right for you, as well as providing tools to manage and work with uncomfortable emotions we inevitably face when considering our human predicament.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: I've worked in an outpatient addiction recovery program for the past 3 years, and previously worked in a gambling addiction treatment program for 3 years. I am knowledgeable on both chemical and process addictions (gambling, internet, etc.). My personal philosophy is centered around harm reduction principles where the focus is on your goals, including moderation if you choose.

name: Mariah Beltran
title: Clinical Psychologist Resident
intro: Hi there! I'm honored you've stopped by. I'm accepting new individual clients!
ideal_client: I have experience working with individuals seeking support for disordered eating behaviors, body-image concerns, trauma-related concerns, identity development, & the spectrum of relationship concerns. I am passionate about supporting women of color, in particular – Latina/e women & women who are of mixed race/ethnicities. My philosophy is that clients are the experts on their lives & I am honored to walk alongside them as they find their optimal health.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a Chicana feminist psychologist, my specialty is working with clients on their relationships with their body, themselves, & others as they navigate life changes. My multicultural feminist training includes anti-racism/anti-oppressive work & LGBTQ+ empowerment. I have worked with all ages, though I specialize in young adulthood/adulthood. I aim to guide clients as they work toward their own definition of health & finding their empowerment. I am dedicated to working collaboratively & aim to infuse every session with empathy, curiosity, compassion, collaboration, and a little bit of humor. If you're in a space ready to grow & heal, please schedule a free consultation.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: As I've said, client's are the experts on their own lives and get to determine what their ideal health looks and feels like. As I've also mentioned, as a Chicana feminist, I recognize we contain multitudes and exist on this Earth with all it's influences (both great and no so great, or down right bad). With this in mind, I believe we are all humans doing our best with what we've got. My personal beliefs beyond that is that every human has a right to bodily autonomy, to love and be loved by whomever, and that the only way we get better is through a safe community and mutual aid.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: Feminist therapy for me functions as the lens in which I understand client's presenting concerns and then use various interventions from other orientations for treatment. Basically this means that one of the goals in every session with me is to empower the client in front of me and help them find their internal power.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: In my training and research, I examined the impacts of body image concerns on BIPOC folx, women-identified individuals, and trans and gender-expansive folx across the lifespan.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: In my training and research, I focused on the experiences of women, specifically Latina/x women.

name: Brettyn Gibson
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I offer virtual parenting support using techniques from play therapy.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am trained as child play therapist, but am currently focused on helping parents learn these same skills to offer therapeutic interactions to their children in their own homes. I’m currently offering virtual parenting support services in Oregon and Washington.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a child & family therapist who specializes in family & child play therapy. I especially value working with families and on helping children and families grown and heal following traumatic experiences. I am a Licensed Marriage & Family Therapist (LMFT), registered with the Oregon Board of Licensed Professional Counselors and Therapists (OBLPCT) and the Washington State Department of Health (DOH). I am supervised by Dr. Kimberly Jayne, PhD, LPC, RPT-S, CCPT-S. I am happy to answer questions about the supervision process.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: Research has shown that motivated parents can be trained to be as effective as play therapists using play therapy skills with their own children, with as little as 20 hours of Child-Parent Relationship Therapy training and and support.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Children don't grow in isolation. Parents are the most important people in the lives of children. I'm happy to help support parents through the challenging and rewarding process of raising children.

name: Rhyver Rudick
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: Hi! I am Dr. Rhyver (pronounced "river") Rudick, a non-binary trans queer hispanic psychologist with over 17 years of clinical experience.
ideal_client: I specialize in therapy with teens and adults (individual and relationships), and have experience across outpatient and inpatient settings. I greatly value working with LGBTQIA(2S)+ individuals, and those of non-conforming identities. I love the work I do, and genuinely care about those I work with. I encourage you to reach out, and either way, wish you the best on your wellness quest.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist, I greatly honor and celebrate the uniqueness of our own life stories and personalities. The interventions I offer are carefully tailored to your concerns, needs, and personal style. I integrate empirically validated approaches with a mix of traditional therapy and metaphysical healing components. I provide a therapeutic presence that is grounding, nurturing, and sincere. Together, we will combine your own self-knowledge and life expertise with my clinical expertise. I will co-journey with you to explore the depths and peaks of your experiences, and to provide support and reminders of your greatness along the way.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I embrace evaluating the “light” and “dark” within you, as well as the many roles and identities you simultaneously juggle as an individual. I want to take the time to learn about your path thus far, and to collaborate with you about potential obstacles that prevent you from living a life more aligned with your own values and sense of inner and outer peace.

name: Catherine Gobel
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I love being a therapist. The work I do is very relational, each and every session is focused on where you are at and what you need most.
ideal_client: If you identify as a Highly Sensitive Person, I am here to help you learn new tools to take the best care of yourself and navigate the overstimulating world we live in. It can be a gift to be so emotionally tuned in to other people but often times it can lead to issues with people pleasing and difficulty advocating for or even understanding your own needs. I'm here to help you have compassion for yourself and set boundaries that will improve and strengthen the relationships in your life.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I want therapy to be a safe space for you to feel vulnerable touching into and understanding your emotions and what they're trying to teach you in a way you haven't before. I like to use mindfulness and somatic tools to help you regulate your nervous system in order to make positive change. Once we build a safe, trusting relationship, hopefully we can make space for parts of you that you haven't had access to before to tell us what their needs are. A lot people have a very critical voice in their heads. My goal is to help us understand why that voice feels the need to criticize you and rewire your brain to be able to hold you accountable to achieve the goals you want to achieve while holding compassion for all the parts of you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am often told that I have a very non-judgmental grounding presence. I've been through some hard things in my own life and I'm proud of the ways I've learned to understand myself and navigate my own difficulties. I feel the experiences I've had provide me with a unique opportunity to understand deeply what you're going through and learn how we can address whatever you're wanting to work on.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: We an use EMDR to process past traumatic events and alleviate how they may impact you today.

specialities.name: Body Image Issues
specialities.description: I work from a Health at Every Size Lens to help you accept your body where it is at.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: I am trained in boundary setting and will help you work to understand what your needs are in a relationship and how to honor them while maintaining connection.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: I have a lot of experience working with people around issues of grief and loss. I'd love to hear more about a loved one you've lost and help you understand how you can keep that relationship alive. I'm also here to work with non-death losses- maybe you've been through a big transition and are grieving the life you used to have.

name: Osakpolo Uwoghiren
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: Osakpolo Uwoghiren is a board-certified Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner trained to provide wide range of mental health service
ideal_client: Prioritize Your Mental Well-being. At Progressive Psychiatric Consultant PLLC, we believe mental health matters. Our dedicated team of professionals is here to support you on your journey towards better mental well-being. Discover a range of resources from therapy options to medication management, tailored to your unique needs. Together, we can create a happier, and healthier you. Take the first step today! Mental health matters. Wellness Journey.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Osakpolo Uwoghiren is a board-certified Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner trained to provide a wide range of mental health services to patients and families. She has worked with a diverse population of clients throughout her years of clinical experience in inpatient psychiatric settings, outpatient psychiatric settings, correctional settings, and psychiatric emergency rooms. She enjoyed her role and take the initial interest in client. Her optimal goal is to provide the highest level of functioning. She strongly believes in an integrated comprehensive approach to psychiatric care and my core belief is focused on patient centered philosophy. We worked together to meet your specific goals and needs. We are here for your needs and value you as individual. Contact me today.

name: Jonathan Green
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I offer to counsel for a diverse array of needs in order to help individuals thrive in their goals and personal lives.
ideal_client: Sometimes, life gets hard. We all experience difficulties that span from life events to day-to-day happenings. I seek to work with people to develop effective ways to cope with the hard times and thrive in the good times. In the therapy room, developing an egalitarian relationship is important to me, and being authentic and cooperative is the key to getting real work done in a way that helps you with your specific needs.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Through the modalities of CBT and ACT, a multitude of areas can be addressed and I can help individuals understand their past in a context that will breathe growth in the present and future. Through my experience in victims advocacy and crisis intervention, I have a strong base for continuous growth in supporting individuals with anxiety, depression and grief. The work I do is always in consideration of cultural contexts. Although I seek to be competent in my approach to each individuals life experience, humility is at the forefront to learn clients feelings and experiences through their eyes. In the therapeutic relationship, I seek to join the client in their experience and add dimensional understanding to how we can be effective in the work we do together.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I value the idea that the client is the expert on themselves. Although as a therapist I have (and continue to) study methods in which to be an effective advocate and resource for growth, it is the client who can only understand what is truly best for them. I am an active member of the LGBTQIAA+ community and seek to promote a world in which we can thrive and be treated with decency and respect. With this desire, I have worked with The Trevor Project as a crisis counselor for at-risk LGBTQIAA+ youth and continue the mission of advocacy through educating and learning in my free time. Core to who I am as a person is the belief that everyone deserves to be heard, and it is my job to listen, learn, and ensure is congruent to their intersectional experience.

name: Anna Schaum
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Currently working exclusively as an organizational strategist and executive team consultant.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Maybe you've tried coaching or therapy before, but were frustrated by a lack of action, assertiveness, empathy, or engagement by the practitioner. Your family history isn't necessarily short on trauma, nevertheless you survived and even thrived. You sense that if you could understand it all better life would improve, personally and professionally. I get it. I was a world class professional symphonic musician before becoming a personal leadership coach and therapist, and understand how to help you successfully leverage the complementary powers of attuned listening and deliberate practice. My ideal clients are high achievers searching for meaning, direction, community, support through loss, and/or renewed purpose.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I use a unique blend of self awareness tools to help you tune in to your own creative flow. We'll reduce your stress, clarify your intentions, define what success means now, and lay the groundwork for your next right steps. Equally comfortable with teams and individuals, I've been called a "team whisper" more than once. Feel free to contact me to discuss how I can help you and/or your team thrive.

specialities.name: Experiential
specialities.description: I am a Board Certified Practitioner of Psychodrama, Sociometry and Group Psychotherapy (www.psychodramacertification.org), am qualified to train therapists in this modality, and teach at Lewis & Clark College in Portland, OR and Antioch University in Seattle.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: As a Personal Growth Specialist, I view the human condition as a giant opportunity to keep expanding awareness and exercising creativity to meet challenges. Journaling, collaging, dreamwork, I Ching, as well as targeted tools like CBT exercises can be utilized to open minds and break up outworn thought patterns. A personal growth approach can make even the most difficult times more meaningful.

name: Amanda Roberson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I have mindfully created a place that is warm, inviting, and comfortable where we can explore, reflect, and heal from the past.
ideal_client: I feel passionate about helping older teens and adults heal from experiences that continue to surface and affect their mental, emotional, and physical wellbeing as well as relationships with others. If you feel as though you're struggling to hold it all together, but desperately need someone to talk to then I'm the therapist for you! With me you don't have to be picture perfect. We can laugh, cry, explore fears, and heal past wounds so you can find the inner peace you've been longing for.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach integrates several different modalities based on your preference and individualized needs. My primary therapy modality is EMDR due to it's efficacy in reducing physical, emotional, and cognitive distress as a result of past hurts. I also use CBT, DBT, ACT, and Mindfulness regularly in my practice.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My background includes in depth work with survivors of domestic violence as well as longterm treatment of anxiety, depression, and trauma/stressor disorders. I have been in practice for 5 years and enjoy working with folks from all walks of life who are currently experiencing barriers to living their most fulfilling life. I am an expert cheerleader, accountability partner, and heart holder. Therapy with me is more than "just listening" and isn't about giving you unwanted advice. I seek to establish an authentic and deep connection built on trust, safety, and compassion. I look forward to meeting you!

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: ACT is an acceptance based model created by Steven Hayes that teaches about the importance of living in accordance with values and accepting what we cannot change. As a client participating in ACT therapy, you would be expected to identify values, discuss barriers that prevent living in accordance with values, practice acceptance of things outside of your control, and make lifestyle changes.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: EMDR is a leading treatment for those who have experienced adversity and trauma. Through use of eye-movements or bilateral tapping, one can reprocess past memories of trauma to reduce emotional distress, uncomfortable physical sensations, and negative self-talk.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: DBT nicely expands perspective by providing alternate scenarios through use of dialectics and accompanying skills. Created by Marsha Linehan, this modality offers several coping skills to use in extremely emotional moments. The coping skills fall into the following categories: interpersonal effectiveness, emotion regulation, distress tolerance, and mindfulness.

specialities.name: Abuse
specialities.description: Abuse is defined as the cruel and violent treatment of a person. Abuse can be psychological, emotional, verbal, sexual, or physical and may have long lasting effects depending on the type and duration of the abuse.

specialities.name: Domestic Abuse
specialities.description: Domestic abuse is the cruel or violent treatment carried out by one's romantic partner. The abuse can be characterized as psychological, emotional, verbal, sexual, or physical. Abuse by one's partner typically starts with efforts to maintain power and control through manipulation, blame, minimization of one's feelings, and lying. It may amplify to more overt acts of violence over time.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: PTSD is a cluster of symptoms that may arise after a person has experienced a traumatic event. This is the body and mind's way of trying to protect itself after experiencing an atypical event. Symptoms experienced include recurrent memories/flashbacks of the event as if it's happening in real time, avoidance of people/places/things that serve as reminders, depression, and anxiety symptoms.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: If you experience anxiety then you are familiar with the uncomfortable sensations (pounding heart, sweating, tingling, muscle tension), racing thoughts, constant worries, concentration difficulties, irritability towards others, and restlessness. There are different subtypes of anxiety, some of which include generalized, social, panic disorder, and various phobias.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is characterized by daily low mood, loss of interest in usual activities, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, sleeping too much or too little, changes in appetite, hopelessness, worthlessness, and, in severe cases, suicidal thoughts or actions. A depressive episode is when these symptoms are experienced continually for 2+ weeks.

name: Bri Puetz
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Foster a kinder relationship with yourself, cultivate connection and fulfillment, heal from the past, and gain tools to navigate life.
ideal_client: I support clients wanting to change persistent beliefs of not being good enough, heal from their past, and build more connection, joy, and fulfillment in life. Many of my clients want to understand patterns they feel stuck in, confidently manage negative thoughts and feelings, develop a kinder relationship with themselves, and feel more at ease in life.

approaches.My Background: I have nearly 10 years of experience working as a therapist in both community mental health and private practice settings. I hold a Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Western Washington University. I'm licensed at the state level, hold designation of National Certified Counselor from the National Board for Certified Counselors, and am also a Level II EMDR trained clinician. Specialized post-degree formal training has included Eye-Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) training and supervision through the EMDRIA approved Institute for Creative Mindfulness, and Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR). In addition to my clinical work, I have served as an adjunct instructor for the Psychology Department at Columbus State Community College.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: A compassionate therapeutic relationship is the foundation of my practice. This space is client-centered, collaborative, and fosters curiosity and non-judgmental challenging. I aim to address barriers and underlying factors contributing to clients’ current concerns, and equip them with the tools and insight to confidently navigate life moving forward. My approach blends evidence-based therapies, including cognitive-behavioral based therapies, mindfulness-based therapies, and EMDR. These therapies focus on increasing awareness of thoughts, emotions, and behaviors while developing practical strategies to respond to them effectively, building insight around unhelpful patterns and practicing alternatives, fostering self-compassion while unlearning self-limiting beliefs, identifying and communicating underlying needs, processing past experiences impacting the present, and aligning actions with values to live more intentionally and to create meaningful change.

name: Brittney Dane
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I work with adults (18+) and couples dealing with anxiety, depression, relationship difficulties, low self-esteem and OCD.
ideal_client: I love hearing the unique story each client and couple brings to our work together. While I am focused on treating anxiety, depression, relationship difficulties and OCD, I am also happy to work with individuals interested in nature-based therapy. Whether you are feeling lost, alone, or wanting growth, I'm here to help!

approaches.Our Background and Approach: I am a Masters Student Intern and QMHP under the supervision of Justin Little, LMFT and Judith Faustima, LMFT. I am currently completing my master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Oregon State University – Cascades. I am a Certified Level I Restoration Therapist. I also have training in a variety of other counseling theories and techniques, including crisis management. I have experience working with youth and adults living with severe anxiety symptoms and obsessive compulsive disorder. With almost a decade of wilderness guiding experience and a lifetime of finding joy and comfort in nature, I love to blend my personal passion with the empirical support behind nature-based counseling techniques. I believe that nature-based counseling should be accessible to everyone and am able to provide a virtual nature-based experience through video and phone mediums while you enjoy a private natural setting in your favorite park or even in your own backyard.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I was drawn to the counseling field because I cherish the journey of self-discovery and the transformative potential within each of us. To me, being a counselor is to walk the path alongside another person, being a support in navigating life’s challenges. We live in a society that values individual strength and self-reliance, yet the profound impact of collaboration and community support in fostering resilience and growth is not often recognized. It is an honor to be brought into your community, your system, and to share in this work with you.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I help my clients gain insight into their problems and patterns using an integrative approach that draws from narrative therapy, attachment theory, and person-centered therapy.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I also use evidence-based treatments like cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), alongside mindfulness practices and nature-based therapy to help inspire meaningful and lasting change.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: I am a Certified Level I Restoration Therapist, a model that draws from attachment theory, mindfulness, behavior change and family dynamics to assist clients in identifying fight/flight patterns showing up in their moments of distress. We then collaborate on a plan to increase mindfulness and identify more loving and trustworthy actions to practice on a weekly basis.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I work with adults to understand and reduce anxiety and increase mindfulness and constructive behaviors and practices. I will take the first few sessions to get to know you and customize a plan to help you meet your goals and improve your wellbeing.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I work with couples to gain both insight and skills regarding patterns of conflict, and help them practice more life-giving patterns in their lives and relationships.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I work with adults to identify ways in which depressive patterns and symptoms show up, and then collaborate with clients to increase mindfulness and constructive behaviors and practices to improve mood, motivation and energy. I will take the first few sessions to get to know you and customize a plan to help you meet your goals and improve your wellbeing.

name: Anna Brown
title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: MA in Clinical Counseling, Specializing in Addictions
intro: Hi! I'm Anna (she/her). I specialize in addiction counseling, recovery maintenance, and see both individuals and couples.
ideal_client: I work well with clients struggle with identify their own emotions and needs, are coping with issues related to neurodivergence, are curious about their relationship with substance, or are seeking support with recovery maintenance outside of a 12-step model. I am a harm reduction oriented counselor and use a collaborative and holistic approach to treatment. I support couples by exploring ways to strengthen communication and conflict resolution skills to deepen your connection.

approaches.How I Can Help You: Deepening our capacity for self-compassion decreases the internalized shame we come into contact within our selves and others. My approach is to lead with curiosity to distill habitual judgment; by expanding your own self-understanding, you are creating internal space to process old hurts and heal.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Autonomy, collaboration, and humor are my guiding lights as a therapist. This is your therapy and it can look however you need it to. I love collaborating with clients to determine what they want more or less of in their life and tailoring therapeutic goals to reflect unique needs. Humor reminds us that we are two people in a room *or a zoom* learning together and that therapy is not just a sad and scary space to process pain - it is also a tool that can help you find more joy, love, and connection in your life and relationships.

name: Gillian Chachere
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I welcome all adults in need of support and compassionate space.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I believe that change takes place within the framework of strong, healthy relationships. I strive to be a partner in healing, building a bond of trust and connection in which clients feel safe unpacking difficult emotions. I also use cognitive-behavioral tools to help clients problem behaviors and life patterns. I have a strong grounding in feminism and social justice advocacy, and provide a safe space for all human experience and identity.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I provide depth-oriented trauma therapy to children, adolescents and adults, using both relational interventions and a knowledge of the effects of trauma on the brain. I also have a focus on the difficult and painful issues that come with infertility and pregnancy loss. In addition to these specialties, I work with issues around relationships, family dynamics, children's and adolescents' behavioral issues, parenting tools, self esteem, body image, anxiety, depression, and many other areas of mental health.

specialities.name: Infertility
specialities.description: I have had personal experience with infertility and pregnancy loss that informs my work. There are unique struggles around infertility and pregnancy loss, and it's often difficult to feel understood by someone who hasn't been through it.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: My educational background is in feminist psychoanalysis, and I approach women's issues - body image, reproductive issues, sex and relationships, parenting, trauma, etc - from a strong feminist perspective.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I offer couples counseling to partners of all orientations and genders. Relationships are hard, and sometimes we need someone to help us hear and be heard. I establish firm ground rules and maintain them, making sure that everyone feels safe being vulnerable.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have many years of experience helping children, adolescents and adults deal with the aftermath of trauma using mindfulness, narrative therapies and strong interpersonal support.

name: Amanda Melbostad
title: Student Counselor
credentials: 200 RYT, MA Art Therapy Student Intern
intro: I am a student intern at Live True Counseling getting my MA in Art Therapy from Lewis & Clark. I identify as queer and am a 200 RYT.
ideal_client: Are you currently overwhelmed and burned out by daily life and navigating our oppressive systems? Feeling a loss of connection to your soul and purpose? Have you been on a healing journey for some time and needing a more wholistic approach to healing and mental health? I offer a trauma-informed, art and somatic therapy from a neuroqueer, anti-racist framework. I work with you to explore what it means to incorporate your creativity into the therapeutic relationship.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a relational therapist, I work from a nueroqueer anti-racist framework and lean on existential, queer, narrative and mindful theories while also utilizing strategic and evidence based practices. I believe its important to balance evidence based tools with some of the magic and mystery of ancient techniques we haven't quite figured out how to measure yet. As a certified yoga instructor I use movement, mindfulness and art to gently guide people into connection with their true self which is where healing can begin. My focuses include Somatics, Trauma, toxic work environments, Queer 2SLGBTQIA+ experiences, and grief.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that healing is a basic human right, and we all hold the potential to heal. The struggles of daily life and oppressive systems can cause us to lose connection to our soul and purpose, leading to our suffering. Our bodies not only hold the stories of our lives but that of our ancestors. There is no one magic tool or way to heal, everyone's journey is unique and I believe a good therapist guides you to find the answers and tools that are right for you.I have been a long time change agent and active participant in enacting change within the oppressive systems I've been a part of; from leading a corporate employee resource group fighting for gender equity, volunteering with the Black Resilience Fund and p;ear for over a year. I've been a part of large fundraising efforts for Leukemia and Lymphoma society and Undestructable (DV & IPV organization).

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: I have been a creative and artist the majority of my life with 2 previous art degrees, I am now acquiring my MA in Art Therapy at Lewis & Clark.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I am a 200hr certified yoga instructor with six years of teaching experience with vinyasa, hatha, slow flow and my recent love, restorative. I enjoy incorporating meditation and breath work into my mindfulness practice and classes.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I am a certified yoga instructor where I was awakened to the power the body mind connection in the healing process. I have taken several Somatic Therapy classes and will be enrolling in the Tamalpa Institutes Expressive Arts Somatic Training to become a Registered Somatic Movement Educator (RSME).

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: Although I don't love the term expertise, I do have a keen eye to detect systems of oppression and the conditioned stories we internalize. This came through my experience in the corporate apparel world, the help of amazing mentors and a DEI certification, as well as listening to the diverse people around me.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: My experience with loss and grief comes from my own personal experience of loosing my father and beloved pup, as well as working at Legacy Cancer Center and the mentorship of two incredible supervisors.

name: Beverley Duke-Young
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I've been a practicing psychotherapist for over 20 years. It is a privilege to have you come in and be open to change for the better.
ideal_client: If you have been feeling anxious and/or depressed, isolated, overwhelmed, lonely and afraid, you are not alone. We are living in some very challenging times. This can especially be of concern when there is uncertainty in the workplace, a relationship that is either not happening at all or you are struggling with improving your communication. Often old traumas from earlier in life can be getting triggered as well, often leaving you feeling exhausted and uncertain how to feel better.

approaches.How I Can Help You: If you have never been to talk with a counselor, I assure you that I will do my best to help you feel safe and relaxed. As a seasoned therapist there is not much new that I haven't heard or helped people find ways to deal with and resolve in a more satisfactory manner. I value your trust in feeling you can share your burden and leave feeling better than when you came in. I don't think most people need endless sessions of therapy unless there has been serious traumas. Often just talking about things with someone who is not involved with you is very helpful. I work with you to support you in making the decisions in what you are seeking to manifest.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I have dual degree: B.S. in Psychology and Sociology and a Master of Science in Counseling, Education & Psychology. I am licensed as a Marriage Counselor with many years of continuing educations in specialties in the field. I am also trained in the field of addictions treatment and work with codependency issues.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I have trained for years under Terry Real's Relational Therapy which helps teach couples how to build and work on developing respectful relationships; this builds on many areas including an understanding of control issues, boundaries, entitlement, shame. What each person experienced in their family of origin impacts and creates some of the roadblocks. How is the best conflict resolution managed between a couple. How to build resiliency and trust and develop empathy.

specialities.name: Addiction Therapy
specialities.description: Many people are caught up in some destructive patterns that can be very difficult to change. Understanding other options to intervene on our habits that have us rather than us having them is necessary to being able to act in our own best interest. Learn with me what it takes! Attachment issues play a huge role in why we become so addicted and attempt to control what we have no real control over.

specialities.name: Eclectic
specialities.description: I find that the relationship that is able to occur between the therapist and the client is going to have more to do than any techniques used which is secondary. My 'eclectic' approach has allowed me to draw upon many years of experimenting with what works, therapy-wise. It doesn't have limits to a particular style so I'm free to bring the best to my approach. I am continually evaluating with the individual what is needed to bring a greater sense of peace in body and mind.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: As a student of Terry Real's Relational Living, I embrace the principals of building and practicing respectful relationships, which often is learning to improve communication skills. Learning what you grew up in from your own family of origin suggests where some of the unhealthier attitudes grew out of. What kind of relationship do you want to create? What would you like to change in how you show up in your relationship? How will you feel when these changes are made?

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: One of my favorite areas to help you is to build good boundaries, improve your own self-esteem and how to be compassionate with others while not losing your sense of who you are in the process. This area encompasses many areas of our life as you will find out when exploring it with me. Resolving conflict with others, whether friends, family, coworkers and supervisors, we can reach deep inside you to find out what some of the blockages are about when there are unaddressed parts of us.

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: As an experienced Certified Alcohol & Drug Counselor III, I can work in a number of ways with you if you are beginning to become concerned about your drinking/drug use (or a family member). I also work with those who have been through treatment and are facing issues with relapse. I do complete assessments and help refer you to an appropriate kind of treatment approach.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Probably one of the most common complaints expressed by people today which can range from a long-term condition to a situation in your life where there just doesn't seem to be enough time to manage all your responsibilities in a balanced way, feeling a sense of well-being rather than a constant state of stress. I rely on a number of therapeutic approaches to help you find a healthier way to live.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: This is such a debilitating feeling or set of feelings to have; it zaps your zest for life and often people are afraid it will never go away. I have worked with this for as long as I've been a therapist and I assure you that you do not have to accept it as a way of life. I will help you bring about a a state of well-being that allows you to have hope and relief from depression.

name: Jennifer Violette
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I provide a compassionate space where you can explore what matters most and navigate life's challenges. Health at Every Size advocate.
ideal_client: My primary focus is supporting individuals navigating anxiety, depression, boundary issues, perfectionism, trauma, life transitions, grief/loss, body image issues, women's issues, and shifting sense of identity. I also support people who may need specialized focus in Health at Every Size principles; Intuitive Eating; psychedelic integration; pregnancy and birth issues; parenting; and adapting to changes in social class.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy is more than overcoming struggles or navigating life’s challenges—it’s about connecting with yourself and what truly matters to you. In our work together, I offer a compassionate and collaborative space where you feel heard and empowered. At the same time, we will take a direct approach, aimed at challenging patterns, reframing perspectives, and exploring new ways of being. I use a trauma-informed, person-centered, and holistic approach to this work, acknowledging the deep connection between the mind, body, and spirit. I often use emotional experiencing, thought defusion, acceptance, and mindfulness exercises to support your growth and healing. Inclusion and cultural humility are core values of my practice, where people of all identities and backgrounds are welcomed, can feel safe, and are valued.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I value an environment grounded in authentic connection, empathy, acceptance, and learning. My practice is rooted in balance, recognizing the importance of addressing both the challenges and strengths that clients bring to the therapeutic process. In therapy, clients are supported to explore their values, navigate life's complexities, and create meaningful change in their lives. I believe in challenging societal norms and promoting body positivity and acceptance for all body types. I am passionate about supporting fat liberation and actively working to deconstruct bias toward fat individuals. My goal is to empower clients to embrace their bodies and cultivate a sense of self-worth that transcends societal expectations.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I specialize in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), which helps bridge the gap between navigating thoughts and feelings and taking meaningful action. By learning how to engage with challenging thoughts and feelings, mind-body awareness, identifying what matters most to you, and aligning with your values, we can move toward the life you want to live.

name: Alex Farmer
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I offer a grounded, compassionate space to explore your emotions, relationships, and values—and support meaningful, lasting change.
ideal_client: You might be struggling to understand your emotional experiences, feel stuck in relationships, or be experiencing an overwhelming desire for change, and have no idea how to start. You might feel alone in these experiences, and have a strong sense that nothing can be different. Therapy can be an environment in which you no longer feel alone and a safe place to explore the deepest experiences of suffering and shame.

approaches.My Background: I am guided by the belief that people are the experts of their experience and are highly capable of making changes that align with their values. Together, we can explore ways to increase your ability to navigate your psychological wellbeing, relationships, and find ways to develop resilience in the face of adversity. My ultimate goal is to create a trusting space and support you in feeling understood, cared for, and listened to. Feeling more grounded and connected to yourself, others, and the world around you can offer an opportunity for real change. During my time as a therapist, I have worked with a wide range of individuals struggling with depression, anxiety, complex trauma, grief and loss, identity and relationship issues, and difficulties with emotional regulation. I utilize an anti-oppressive and culturally sensitive foundation, and have found that a strong therapeutic relationship utilizing research-based practices can result in authentic and lasting support.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have received training in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), Dialectical Behavioral Therapy (DBT), Internal Family Systems (IFS), and Narrative therapy approaches. I utilize mindfulness-based practices and strive to create a trusting relationship grounded in nonjudgment and unconditional positive regard for you as the client. I look forward to being alongside you in your journey towards growth and healing.

name: WILLIAM TEMPLE HOUSE
title: Student Counselor
intro: Our mental health services emphasize high-quality treatment, respect, and affordability.
ideal_client: We work with individuals across the lifespan, people in relationships, and families of all backgrounds to support them in achieving their therapeutic goals. Our sliding scale fees range from $1 to $80, making us one of the most affordable options in the city. Sessions are available by appointment, both in-person and via telehealth, and are conducted by student interns, alumni, and volunteers.

approaches.Our Approach to Helping: With more than 20 providers, we offer a diverse range of identities and lived experiences. We utilize a variety of therapeutic modalities and interventions that are tailored to each individual's needs, promoting a personalized approach. Our work is grounded in a person-centered, trauma-informed framework, which emphasizes transparency, collaboration, respect, and empowerment. Whether working with individuals, couples, or families, we strive to create a supportive and safe space where clients can work toward their therapeutic goals. Our sliding scale fees, ranging from $1 to $80, make our services accessible to a broad range of clients, and sessions are available both in-person and via telehealth.

approaches.Why We Started this Group Practice: In 1965, a group of Episcopalians opened a counseling center on NW Marshall St with a phone, card table, and an orange crate for a chair. They named the place after William Temple, the late Archbishop of Canterbury known for his commitment to social justice. Before long William Temple House (WTH) grew into a trusted community resource offering counseling, food, clothing, and more to thousands of individuals and families in the community. Founding director C.T. Abbott, a visionary priest and mental health counselor, led WTH until his death in 1990. More than 50 years later, WTH continues as a place of healing and hope through services supporting the whole person—mind, body, and spirit. Our staff, volunteers, and supporters come from diverse backgrounds, and what brings us together is our shared vision of a stronger community. We're proud to serve our neighbors as an equal opportunity provider and strive to create a comforting place that is open and inviting to people of all backgrounds.

name: Polly Gravely MS, LPC, MFT
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello, I'm Polly. I enjoy being a therapist, helping people evolve out of stuck situations and ways of being, into more fulfilling lives.
ideal_client: Being human is hard because life is uncertain. We all, at times, need an assist. Maybe you're low and you can't shake it. Maybe anxious thoughts keep you awake at night, over and over. Maybe you and your partner have arguments that never fully resolve and that connection you once had remains out of reach. I'm trained in attuning to the unconscious emotional patterns that constrict us. I've helped hundreds of people understand how and where they get stuck, and develop their agency to shift out.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I’m trained in relational dynamics with a specialty in Emotion Focused Therapy and differentiation. These skills help me track how people get stuck in rigid ways of relating, either with themselves -- such as stuck in loops of anxiety or depression -- or in how they relate with someone else – perhaps reactive patterns of criticism and defensiveness. We are all constantly in relationship, either with people around us, or with ourselves. We learn our patterns from our first family and typically repeat variations of the same pattern. I help by increasing your awareness about these relational patterns – internal and the external, to notice where there’s constriction and limitation, and why. When we have awareness, we can have positive change. Common issues I treat: Individuals: a self-critical voice that creates defeat; a fearful inner voice that undermines confidence. Couples: codependency, disconnection, reactivity, unhealthy conflict or avoidance of it, discrepancy of sexual desire.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Twenty something years ago I worked as a reporter in the US Senate in Washington D.C. Every day I had to find and report a story and it was typically related to conflict and clearly dysfunctional. I moved to Portland and retrained as a therapist. These days I have such a meaningful career helping people out of stuck places, and often sorting through conflict to resolution! There is a way through and it begins with understanding. I listen to what's underneath people's words, below the reactive emotions, and support growth into a more integrated, empowered life.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: My degree (M.S. in Marriage and Family Counseling) is specifically focused on relational dynamics and I have extensive training in couples' work. I can help you understand how your relationship ran into trouble and how to find the way back again.

specialities.name: Coaching
specialities.description: I use the PRINT Survey assessment to enhance understanding of the way people react and how they relate by explaining the “why” behind their behavior – - why people act as they do - why they make certain choices - why they are attracted to certain things - why they function better in certain situations than others Everyone has core motivations that drive their actions and behaviors. PRINT® reveals what these motivators are and in doing so, clarifies people need.

specialities.name: Emotionally Focused
specialities.description: Emotion-Focused Therapy is my primary modality. It's an approach that guides people underneath words, actions, and reactive secondary emotions, to underlying primary emotions, which are frequently out of awareness. I know how to listen to these underlying feelings and help people tune in so they understand what's really the problem and what they really need.

specialities.name: Self-Esteem
specialities.description: Most of us have an inner critical voice that keeps us in line, but for some of us that voice is punishing. Maybe your inner voice tells you that you're not good enough, that you look bad, and flings other criticisms at you. It's hard to live with a voice like that. I work to listen, to understand, and gradually shift this voice so that it trusts you, takes its right place, and works in support of you.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: My foundation as a therapist is all relational. When we are stuck in ourselves, we are stuck in our relationships, and vice versa. I have a lot of specific trainings in couples work to help open up emotional dynamics so that places that feel tight, restricted and even hopeless can begin to open and change.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Life is always happening to us and it can feel overwhelming. We may want to get some control of things, but we can't so the anxiety escalates. I can help you reduce the symptoms, and develop an awareness about the anxiety so that gradually it softens and you have more agency in life.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Life is full of ups and downs, we live that all the time, but sometimes life can feel too much and hopeless. I can assist you using a combination of symptom relief and self-exploration so that gradually the sadness can lift and you are better able to cope.

name: Dore Everett, LCSW
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Together we will address obstacles that limit your freedom. We will create a safe/healing/creative environment to meet your desired goals.
ideal_client: Lets cut though the noise of our busy life and competitive culture. Many of our beliefs- about ourselves and the world are projections of the past showing up non-consciously in the present. That's the way our brain works. Let's use our practice to be present and making a choice to step into the present moment, something new and our own potential.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My method of service is eclectic, strengths based and is a mindfulness-centered, somatic approach that is relational and empathic. I meet people where they are without judgment or expectation to explore: limiting personal beliefs/habits and ways to step into your strength and potential to become your best self. I trust in the wholeness of every human being to aid in the discovery of our natural state of thriving and balance.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: My MSW training and degree was received at the Hunter School of Social Work, NYC. I have post graduate training in the use of Gestalt, CIMBS (Complex Integration of Multiple Brain Systems) as well as extended training with the M.E.T.A. Institute: includes- Attachment work, Mindfulness, Trauma, Hakomi and RC- S. I have extensive experience as a grief/ bereavement counselor and hospice social worker as well as working in drug and alcohol treatment. Prior to my career as a social worker I worked as a freelance artist in New York and San Francisco.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness used in therapy is a state of attention to become aware of current experience: somatic, cognitive, energetic and emotional. The present experience is then explored, without judgment, to make connections to patterns of belief and behavior.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: An interdisciplinary, holistic approach to study the experience of the body to reveal and understand the interaction of our body structures with our thoughts, beliefs and actions.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Attachment work in therapy explores how dysfunctional attachment templates get represented in adult relationships by clients developing a personal, healthy, therapeutic relationship with their counselor. This relationship lays the groundwork to understand clients’ attachments to others through consistent and supportive communication.

name: Pearl Waldorf
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Relationship is everything. I bring new frameworks, humor and queer wisdom to all I do. Let's free you up to live a vital, meaningful life.
ideal_client: Ya'll I work with folx who have never quite "fit." I work with Queer and Trans folx, mixed race, cross-culture, creative folx who are creating their place in the world. I work with folx whose childhoods were confusing, neglectful, shaming & who have, maybe ever since, been mixed up thinking something's wrong with them. My clients are neurodivergent in gorgeous and struggle-y ways. My clients are nerdy AF. They care about the world & desire skills to stay self connected & emotionally well.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Our human physiology is a brilliant system which can guide you to life you wish to live. I work experientially and collaboratively to build connections to your inner wisdom. Through a combination of psychoeducation, somatic and relational approaches, I offer an empowered excursion into the world of your self. My work is deeply grounded in an attachment orientation, which supports a deep sorting process: As a client you'll begin to feel, choose and act from a sense of who you truly are vs. from historical models that no longer serve you. Offered in both individual and group formats, our work creates a space that activates knowing what is *right* for you, as well as clarity about where your lines are. This is not about cutting people off. I'll help you grow the solidity that comes from moving through your life connected to what you think, feel and want. I'm looking forward to meeting you to learn more about how I might be of help.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My key values Number 1: Dignity... every human is distinct. You bring a unique gift to the collective. "Wellness," is NOT an interior job. It's thoroughly relational. Culture, the systems we are swimming in, your family's location within those systems, your access to community influence your experience of worthiness. THIS is healing work. Number 2: Nourishment... To live well is to be nourished here & now. We live in a culture that disrupts our access to simple life goodness. Most of us have work to do to recognize flow, sweetness, vitality & yet the searching itself can create the road blocks. It's complex discernment I'm here to help with. Number 3: Process... Life is an opportunity in every unfolding moment. We skip these moments in a thousand ways if we are not paying attention. There is the content of life. That jerk at work, the dream of a home etc. Looking at the process... the how, boundaries, interior patterns in play enlivens new perspectives. Let's take a look together.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: In the therapy relationship, we can begin to understand what gets in the way of connection for us. Together, we are detectives in search of answers to the conundrum of what makes connecting hard, life satisfaction illusive and vitality available in such small or intermittent reserves.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: It is during our early development that our ways of understanding relationship are being mapped into our brains. Attachment therapy can awaken these networks for reconfiguration. Deep change is possible in how we experience ourselves, in our ways of connecting with others and in our capacity to act effectively in the world.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: The body holds the story of our lives in the present moment. We can work here and now to heal the wounds which thwart satisfaction in our lives. Through deep listening we learn to attend to the wisdom deep in implicit memory system and to sort what's past from what's actually happening right now.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Sometimes working with an individual or group therapist to sort through our relationship issues can save our most tenuous connections. Rather than placing the pressure directly on relational struggles that are founded on insecure attachment strategies, why not make room for ourselves to discover our deeper solidity and bring this back into our connections.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: Setting clear boundaries as adults has everything to do with how we were reflected and tended to as little ones. It's easy to mix ourselves up with others, if we were not valued for simply being our unique selves. We can't learn our own yeses and nos in a vacuum. What's exciting, is we can learn differentiation as an adult, with the guidance of a skilled attachment therapist.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: An activated Nervous System can make satisfying engagement with others nearly impossible. My anxiety clients may feel confused about why you struggle as you do. When asked about your history, it's likely you'll say you had good parents. Parents who provided you with everything you needed. I dig deeper with my clients to understand, what may have been missing and to begin filling in the gaps.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is a way we protect ourselves from overwhelming experiences. If we have no functional way to regulate ourselves through life's emotional stresses and relationships' natural shifts in and out of connection, often our nervous systems will jump in, take over and shut us down. Engaging with a skilled Attachment therapist, can support reigniting the aliveness that is your human birthright.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: I am an assimilated white, Jewish identified cis gendered queer able-bodied woman. The anti-racism work I have been engaged in over the past few years is transforming my spirit, my world view and my lens on the work of relational therapy. Together we can help you ground into your own privileged and subjugated identities with an aim towards more more community and work effectiveness, more relationship satisfaction and deeper enjoyment in your life.

name: Kristina Stuart, LPC, NCC
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I work with a variety of clients to help facilitate change, acceptance, and compassion. I welcome the opportunity to work with you.

approaches.My Background and Approach: I have been working with individuals in the mental health field since 2005, beginning my journey working with children and adolescents in a variety of settings. I completed my internship at Washington County Corrections working with addictions and recovery, facilitating individual and group therapy in Seeking Safety and Mindfulness Based Relapse Prevention models, and later provided adult outpatient therapy for a non-profit agency. I received a Bachelor of Science in Psychology, and hold a Master of Art in Counseling Psychology. I am a Certified EMDR provider, meaning I have completed all EMDR trainings and have completed certification tasks proving my efficacy. I also utilize Cognitive Behavioral Therapy , DBT, and Mindfulness to help make fundamental changes in perspective and to help shift the way you view your personal experience.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe that everyone has the capacity towards achieving personal fulfillment. Together we can identify barriers in your life that are making this difficult to achieve. As your therapist I will provide guidance and support on your journey. I will work with you to create self-directed goals and allow a safe place to explore feelings, experiment with new perspectives about yourself, and accept challenges, all as part of the process of change.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I am a Certified EMDR provider, meaning I have completed all EMDR trainings and have completed certification tasks proving my efficacy. This therapeutic technique is a transformative way to heal both single incident and complex trauma, as well as depression and anxiety related issues, through adaptive resolution. Through EMDR, painful events and traumatic memories are reprocessed resulting in a decrease in distress and a reconstruction of negative beliefs.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is a structured therapeutic approach with emphasis on teaching skills to change thinking and behaviors that are getting in the way of mental health by working with cognitive restructuring and behavioral changes. CBT is an evidence-based and highly effective approach to counseling and was the basis of my graduate education.

name: Mitchell Passadore
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi! I'm Mitchell! I'm a Professional Counselor Associate, here to support your mental health journey!
ideal_client: I enjoy working with all different populations but especially enjoy working with teens and young adults, people experiencing symptoms of anxiety, folks experiencing life transitions, and anyone experiencing men's specific issues.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I was trained in Portland at Lewis & Clark’s graduate school of education and counseling. I have specific training in treatment for anxiety disorders, PTSD, addiction, depression, and trauma utilizing principles of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Exposure Response Prevention (ERP), Motivational Interviewing (MI), Compassion Focused Therapy (CFT), and Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT) in both individual and group settings.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that anyone can benefit from counseling and that no matter where a person starts, they deserve respect and care. I am here to help people live better lives and uncover patterns in thoughts and behaviors that might be causing distress. For this process to be most helpful, it is important to find someone who fits well with who you already are. My goal is to help facilitate positive, lasting change and I believe that there is a counselor out there who can help make that happen.

name: Raquel Mayer
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm honored to support you in your journey towards growth, healing and self-exploration.
ideal_client: You are the expert of you -- You can help decide what your process in therapy will look like - whether that is getting support around a life transition, seeking coping strategies for pandemic fatigue, managing anxiety, processing body image concerns, navigating boundary issues in relationships, coming to terms with identity, or struggling with feelings of shame, I am here to listen without judgment and sit beside you with care and affirmation.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As a therapist, I use a client-centered, trauma-informed, interpersonal, collaborative and transparent approach. I have experience in supporting clients with histories of complex and oppression-based trauma, domestic and sexual violence, and substance use. I am passionate about working with folks around body acceptance and/or LGBTQ+ identities and experiences. I approach clients with compassion, empathy, and unconditional positive regard, providing them with support and validation while helping them to meet their therapeutic goals.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My journey as a therapist began with my experience as a client. Starting therapy, I didn’t know what to expect, but I left sessions feeling affirmed and supported. Through the powerful therapeutic relationship, I learned to have more compassion for myself and in turn, built my capacity to have more compassion for others. Working with a therapist changed me in profound ways and inspired my pursuit to provide counseling for others. I hold a master's degree in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis & Clark College and a bachelor's degree in Psychology and Women's & Gender Studies from Sonoma State University, providing the foundation of my interest and knowledge in social justice and counseling. I am a white, queer, fat therapist with an awareness of how social identities impact life experiences and the therapeutic relationship. My hope is to hold space and offer tools along the way that help to build upon your unique identities and strengths.

name: Danielle Solari
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I’m Danielle, a therapist and perinatal mental health specialist who provides trauma-informed and person-centered therapy.
ideal_client: My primary focus is working with those on the journey to parenthood or are navigating the challenges that come with being a parent. I work with individuals coping with pregnancy, postpartum mood disorders, infertility, and loss. In addition, I work with adolescents, and adults who wish to address experiences with trauma, life transitions, anxiety, or stress. Life can be hard – I see therapy as a place to share your story, in its entirety, without concerns that you need to censor yourself.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Everyone has the potential to grow and thrive, and my approach to therapy centers on empowering clients to develop the skills and insights necessary to access the changes they want to see. Through our work together you can expect to gain a deeper understanding of yourself and your needs, practical tools for managing difficult memories and current stressors, identify your strengths, and be provided with a supportive space to explore all the parts of you. My sincere hope for you is that therapy can help you reach your goals, increase your use of tools and resources, and ultimately stop coming to therapy!

name: Brianna (Bri) Bray
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Accepting new clients! I practice a collaborative, systemic approach with individuals & couples to gain awareness & promote personal growth.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with couples through an emotionally-focused approach. I provide a welcoming and safe environment where couples have the opportunity to connect and heal. I am trained to work under a relational lens, meaning that I believe we are influenced by our relationships and it is in these relationships where the healing process begins. I also work with individuals who are coping with body dysmorphia, disordered eating, anxiety and depression.

name: Samantha Rott
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: I believe that our past informs our present, in how we connect to and experience our lives. I am here to support you finding your voice.
ideal_client: Do you experience anxiety, depression, PTSD, parenting struggles, relationship dynamic issues or changes, major life transitions, or personal identity concerns? I am here to support you finding your voice within yourself and your close relationships. I work with children (3+), preteens, teens, adults—individuals and couples—and families residing in Oregon and/or Washington.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy primarily follows Integrated Therapy utilizing Psychodynamic, Attachment, and Family Systems theories. My pronouns are she, her, hers and I look forward to learning yours. I find behavior to be an important opening to explore the underlying feelings an individual is experiencing in response to others. I view therapy as a collaborative process in which you are the expert of your own life and I am an empathetic and supportive guide helping create a brave, accepting space. With you willing to explore the past experiences that are relevant to seeking therapy today, I provide reflections to offer alternative perspectives for possible change. This is a process of discovery within your systems of influence, such as your family—however you may define this.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I enjoy spending time with my partner and children, other family, traveling, and anything outdoors. I have additional training in Child-Parent Relationship/Filial Therapy, Child-Centered Play Therapy, Sandtray Therapy, Family Therapy, Couples Therapy, as well as training in Trauma Response Services, specifically Risk Assessment and Suicidality Crisis Intervention Techniques, Traumatology and Trauma-Informed Care, Interpersonal Neurobiology of Trauma, Race and Trauma, and Grief and Loss Across Lifespan.

name: Jasmine Ziter
title: Qualified Mental Health Professional
intro: I am honored to work with clients who are seeking to reintegrate joy into their lives with holistic mental health treatments.
ideal_client: Are you grappling with anxiety, depression, or symptoms from PTSD? If you're seeking a path to healing through diligence and soulful work, I'm here to walk alongside you. Together, we'll uncover ways to ease these burdens and invite joy back into your life. Through a compassionate and grounded therapeutic connection, we'll journey together, empowering you to nurture your well-being and embrace a fulfilling existence.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: As a therapist, I am passionate about guiding individuals on their journey to reclaim mental wellness and navigate life's challenges through genuine, wholesome, and playful connections. I embrace a holistic approach, weaving in the natural rhythms of everyday life and the healing power of the environment. My practice is enriched by the wisdom of Buddhism, Taoism, and other nature-based spiritual traditions, highlighting the profound connection between body, mind, and spirit. I believe in the transformative power of physical movement to harmonize our energies and nurture our well-being. Dedicated to addressing burnout from the pressures of capitalism and the weight of ongoing oppression, I aim to create a space of empowerment and balance.

name: Fran Witt
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Fran’s approach to counseling is client-centered and humanistic.
ideal_client: I primarily work with trauma survivors (including survivors of domestic violence), anxiety, OCD and related disorders (e.g, phobias), and depression. In addition, I have recently started helping folks navigate ADHD.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Fran strongly believes that each client is the expert in their life and may utilize various interventions to meet each client’s individual needs. She primarily uses Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) and Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) from trauma and diversity-informed lenses. Learning and implementing Exposure and Response Prevention (ERP) and exposure-related trauma interventions are some of Fran’s passions. Leadership is another one of her passions, and she enjoys leading any chance she gets. Fran has worked with a variety of populations, including inpatient and nonprofit. She has experience treating domestic violence, depression, and anxiety. Her special interests include trauma, anxiety-related disorders (e.g., OCD, phobias), systems, marginalized populations, and gender/sexuality concerns. She is committed to providing unconditional positive regard, warmth, acceptance, safety, authenticity, and collaboration to clients.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe everyone has the right to show up in this challenging and messy world as their authentic self--especially marginalized populations, such as the BIPOC the LGBTQ+ communities. I enjoy providing support and working with marginalized populations to better embrace their genuine selves and navigate life. One way I assist clients from marginalized populations is by utilizing my own values such as anti-oppression, anti-racism, inclusion, diversity, equity, human rights, and social justice. In addition, some of my other values are empathy, open-mindedness, and kindness. Outside of the therapy room, you will likely find me spending time with my cat, making arts and crafts, hiking, advocating, thrifting, gardening, and engaging with my friends and loved ones.

name: Wild Wish Counseling
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: NOT ALL WOUNDS ARE VISIBLE - YOUR EMOTIONS PLAY A VITAL ROLE IN FINDING WELLNESS.
ideal_client: Our philosophy is based on the belief that you possess the power to change, and it is our role to help you become aware of how to understand and utilize your own inner strength.

approaches.Our Background and Approach: Wild Wish Counseling is a clinical group practice that offers support to individuals across all ages and identity. Through various services and treatment options, we offer an eclectic style of therapies. This requires our clinicians to be highly skilled and knowledgeable in the most recent research and evidence-based treatment for mental health concerns. As a community we face many challenges of depression, anxiety, trauma, PTSD, grief/loss, gambling, addiction, sexual identity, attachment or behavior issues and relationships which means that specialized care and a commitment to education and training is imperative to providing ethical and knowledgeable care to all individuals.

approaches.Our Personal Beliefs and Interests: Wild Wish Counseling clinicians advance their expertise by focusing on advanced training and holistic theories which requires passion and commitment to the field of emotional health. All graduate interns participate in ongoing supervision and consultation. Graduate interns attend accredited online or local programs because we believe in providing the best care with a pledge of quality in providing services to the community. We believe that interest in your life, identity, and narrative are most important to the therapeutic process of healing.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: Trained through EMDRIA Consultant and follow standard protocol for evidenced based outcomes.

specialities.name: Gottman Method
specialities.description: Level 1 & Level 2

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Feelings of sadness are natural feelings that everyone experiences throughout their lifetime, however when those feelings develop into intense and overwhelming thoughts, it can be a tough process to pull yourself out of. Wild Wish offers the help you need to bring you back to a happier healthier you. Depression isn’t always brought on by a sad or traumatic event and can last as little as a day to a lifelong battle. Sometimes we don't have a reason, but you do not have to face it alone.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Individuals who have experienced a traumatic or terrifying event (often life threatening) can develop flashbacks, nightmares, severe anxiety and uncontrollable thoughts about the event. Wild Wish Counseling works with our patients to help manage the intense feelings surrounding a traumatic or terrifying event. Although the instigating event may overpower coping resources available at the time, it is nevertheless possible to develop healthy ways of coping and diminishing its effects.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety is an unprecedented response to any type of threat in reality or imagined. The fear of what could happen, is happening or is yet to come can bring an overwhelming sense of fear or apprehension with the capability of causing physical symptoms. Wild Wish Counseling works with our patients to help manage these intense feelings of fear and nervousness. Whether a big event or a small stressor in life is causing anxiety attacks, our team will help bring you to a healthier state of mind.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Suffering the death of a loved one can have a tremendous impact on your emotional wellbeing and last for years to come. We, as people, form strong bonds with our friends, family and loved ones. When those bonds are broken, the aftereffects can be extreme, overwhelming and unpredictable. Wild Wish Counseling can help challenge and approach these feelings in a safe and healthy environment.

name: Julie Jorgensen
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am a creative individual who values family, friends, animals, nature, and spirituality. I bring experience and empathy to my work.
ideal_client: With 25 years of experience working primarily in school settings, I have supported children and their families through a range of challenges, including trauma, ADHD, other neurodivergent themes, anxiety, loss, and learning difficulties.
