approaches.What I Specialize In: My background includes play therapy, sand tray, expressive arts, and collaborative problem-solving.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I firmly believe that the strength of the therapeutic relationship is crucial to effective therapy. Finding a therapist with whom you feel a strong connection can make a significant difference in the therapeutic process. With 25 years of experience working with children and families, primarily in school settings, I bring a wealth of knowledge and a deep commitment to emotional awareness and self-regulation.

name: Lucius Wheeler
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I help people to navigate challenging life experiences, grow, and make choices that bring them a sense of meaning and wholeness.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Integral therapy begins with a basic attitude that all people have a tremendous capacity for change, and that we all contain within us a natural impulse towards healing. Therapy is a collaborative relationship, I will invite you to “lead the way” as we explore what is present for you. It is important to me that you feel seen, heard, and empowered in the therapy process. Together, we will work towards the creation of an atmosphere of safety and trust that supports your healing process. My work is experiential, using dialogue and awareness to help those I work with to understand themselves and regain a sense of agency in their lives.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Professional Counselor in the state of Oregon. I received my master's degree in Integral Counseling Psychology from the California Institute of Integral Studies in San Francisco, CA. My graduate and post-graduate experience includes specializing in psychedelic integration services, working as an outpatient drug and alcohol counselor, a school-based mental health therapist, and an intensive outpatient mental health therapist. Previously, I worked in the field of personal growth and natural healing for over a decade. My work is informed by my own process of growth and learning, which has helped me to understand the challenges and opportunities in every life change. I receive ongoing training and supervision in Gestalt therapy from Gestalt Therapy Training Associates Northwest, Gestalt Associates Training Seattle, and other professional trainers.

specialities.name: Integral Therapy
specialities.description: Integral Therapy is fundamentally oriented toward wholeness. The integral approach is also profoundly optimistic, as it affirms every person's capacity for transformation, healing, and growth. I received an M.A. in Integral Counseling Psychology from the California Institute of Integral Studies in San Francisco, CA, and integral philosophy forms the foundation of my therapeutic work with clients.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: Gestalt is not only a type of therapy, but also a way of understanding human experience and the process of change. As a Gestalt therapist, my goal is to help you become aware of your needs, interests, and habitual patterns, and to support you to make choices that are meaningful and satisfying for you. I receive ongoing Gestalt training and supervision from multiple organizations and trainers.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: With a male gender identification comes certain social norms and expected roles. What does it mean to you to be authentically yourself in a male body? For over a decade, I have been a participant in and facilitator of men's circles and rites of passage ceremonies. In groups and individual sessions, I take an experiential, relational approach to men's work, helping you to connect with your inner wisdom so you can craft a life of integrity, meaning, and purpose.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can be a very reasonable response to stressful life circumstances. It can also be the result of holding ourselves back from taking new risks to pursue our desires and interests. Every response to the world makes sense in context. I can support you in the process of understanding your experience of depression, and finding new, more satisfying possibilities.

name: Nick Hebert
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I’m a queer, compassionate therapist dedicated to empowering you to tap into your strengths and overcome life’s challenges.
ideal_client: I work with individuals navigating anxiety, shame, low self-worth, relationship and intimacy challenges, sexual concerns, identity questions, and trauma. My practice is especially affirming for LGBTQIA+ and queer folks, as well as those exploring poly and kink-positive relationships. If you’re seeking a collaborative, supportive space to uncover your strengths and work through life’s complexities, you’ll find a warm welcome here.

approaches.How I Can Help You: Over time, we all develop stories—once protective, now sometimes limiting—about ourselves, others, and the world. These narratives, often shaped by experiences of marginalization, can leave us feeling unworthy or overwhelmed. In our work together, I honor your unique journey by exploring these stories and uncovering the strengths you already possess. I specialize in supporting those grappling with anxiety, shame, low self-worth, relationship challenges, intimacy and sexual concerns, identity questions, and trauma responses. As a queer therapist with extensive experience serving LGBTQIA+ communities and individuals in poly and kink-positive relationships, I bring both professional expertise and personal understanding to our work. I believe that genuine healing happens in a collaborative, evolving relationship—one where we embrace both laughter and tears as we navigate the path to growth.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I’m dedicated to supporting individuals who grapple with challenging inner narratives—those feelings of anxiety, shame, and low self-worth that may have originated from past hurts or marginalization. I work with clients facing relationship and intimacy struggles, sexual concerns, and identity questions, helping them uncover the strengths they already possess. My practice is especially affirming for LGBTQIA+ and queer communities, including those exploring polyamorous or kink-positive relationships. Every client brings a unique story and inherent resilience, and together, we work to transform those narratives into pathways for growth and authentic living.

name: Tracy Bryce Farmer
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Making the decision to engage in therapy is an act of strength.
ideal_client: Do you go over and over moments that happen in your life in your head? Do you blame yourself for things that might not be under your control? Are you afraid there is something wrong with you that is different from other people? Self-attack is my primary practice interest.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use an interactive approach where you will no longer feel alone in looking at your life. I combine work on feelings with concrete skills that will help you begin to make changes from the first visit. I enjoy working with individuals, couples, families and groups on personal, relational and professional growth.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Talking with me is different. It's lively and emotional and practical. I have a Master's in Fine Arts degree and I bring creativity to the change process. My Master's in Social Work degree will empower you to deal with oppressive systems. I became a Certified Alcohol and Drug counselor because addiction affects so many of us. I started my training in New York City more than 20 years ago and I update my education continually. I can support you to cope with your past in a safer way, in order to make the present work better for you in the here and now.

specialities.name: Relational
specialities.description: Improving relational understanding and functioning improves our well-being. Sometimes that means moving closer to people. Sometimes it means distancing ourselves. Our relationship supports you to study and improve the relationships in your life.

specialities.name: Psychodynamic
specialities.description: Psychodynamic theory started the whole field of mental health treatment. Repressing our thoughts and feelings leads to painful symptoms. Our emotional challenges stem from our history. We are also hugely impacted by oppressive systems. Psychodynamic therapy says let's talk about all of it, at your own pace.

specialities.name: Family Systems
specialities.description: We all start in our first goup: our original family systems. These early family relationships play out again and again in our current lives. If we don't like aspects of our first group, we can study them and the patterns they have created. We can make changes as we see fit.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: Relationships can be so tricky because the complex system of one person meets another complex system. Relationships offer the hope of feeling seen and understood. I can support your goals for increased connection along with the freedom to be yourself.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Many people have undergone trauma and don't realize its impact on their lives. PTSD symptoms can include fear, worry, conflict, self-loathing and shame. Let me help you get to the bottom of what you have experienced so you can feel more free.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Life can be traumatic. Our brains are structured in relationship. My ongoing training means I work hard to understand the way your brain is uniquely wired. I empower you to approach your anxiety with curiosity so you can pursue the life you dream about.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: We make a false distinction in this country between mental and physical health. Our brains are major organs that are vulnerable to stress in same way as other systems in our bodies. I welcome the chance to help you figure out what is causing your brain difficulty so you can take care of it.

name: Sarah King
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I provide holistic perinatal and postpartum therapy services. I encourage clients to honor their intuitive nature and maternal wisdom.
ideal_client: Motherhood can be both beautiful and deplete you emotionally, physically, and spiritually. Yet, here you are putting forth effort every day to honor the most influential role that could be asked of you, being the primal source of nature and nourishment to your baby. You are the superhero in all of this, yet mothers are often the most forgotten. Let me help you, while you take on the world and this new transformation. At Yaga Healing Place, we are here for the mamas.

approaches.My Background and Approach: My clinical framework is deeply rooted in attachment theory, emphasizing the intricate and vital mother-child relationship. It's striking how easily society trivializes the journey of conceiving, birthing, and nurturing a child, assuming that a healthy baby equates to a perfectly aligned mother, regardless of her physical and emotional challenges. The reality is that motherhood is a complex journey, often portrayed simplistically by society, leaving women feeling forgotten or disconnected in the postpartum period, almost like an afterthought. As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker, I merge my professional expertise with my personal journey through motherhood and the postpartum period, offering empathetic support as you navigate this profound transformation. My aim is to help you find acceptance and validation for your experiences, fostering a sense of safety as you navigate the diverse facets of motherhood.

approaches.Why We are a Good Fit for You: At Yaga Healing Place, we are a group of clinicians united in our vision to provide inclusive and specialized therapeutic services dedicated to improving the lives of women, parents and families. Our providers work together under the same empowerment goal; holding a safe and nourishing space for the healing and rewilding of your feminine power. Currently, Yaga Healing Place offers trauma-informed, mental health services to all women, AFAB folks, and their families. Through individual, group, and intensive therapies, you will be provided specialized and holistic mental health care as you navigate through your healing. Our goal is to expand to other whole-body-focused disciplines to best nourish your mind, body, and spiritual needs during your journey through all shades of motherhood.

specialities.name: Infertility
specialities.description: Helping women process and find acceptance for their unique fertility and motherhood journey. Helping hold space for things we cannot control.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: Provide specialized postpartum mental health care for women throughout their postpartum journey.

specialities.name: Pregnancy (Prenatal Mental Health)
specialities.description: Specialized in providing perinatal mental health services for women in all shades of their motherhood journey.

specialities.name: Women's Issues
specialities.description: To live a well-rounded healthy life, we recognize and honor a woman's holistic, mind-body-spirit connection.

name: Sunya Grantham
title: Marriage and Family Therapist Associate
intro: Ditch blame and resentment...Connect, mend, and strengthen your relationship.
ideal_client: Have you and your partner been sweeping things under the rug? Or maybe you're having the same ol' dance to a different song. Increased stress, broken trust, and life transitions tend to shine a spotlight on the elements of our relationships we've hoped would go away. It can cause us to act in ways we never thought possible and be counterproductive to our desired intent for connection.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: When our relationship has become (or has been) the cause of distress we often create a negative story of our partner that is difficult to re-write. Once our mind views our partner as a source of hurt and pain, it becomes difficult to see them as anything but potential danger. This further entrenches the negative story of our partner and our relationship; it seems unfixable. I help clients identify the thoughts and feelings causing them to behave in ways that prevent them from getting what they want out of their relationship. I provide my clients with education and practical tools to disrupt unhelpful communication patterns to help them share what they need from their partner in more productive ways. You can begin to interact in ways that leave you open to a renewed sense of connection and more positive story. What is consistent in my approach is: collaboration, an empathetic attitude, and laughter. Much like you would expect in your significant relationships.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am committed to providing affordable therapy to persons within marginalized groups. I reserve sliding scale slots for BIPOC and LGBTQ identifying clients. I completed a M.A. in Marriage & Family Therapy at Pacific Lutheran University. I have experience working with couples and families experiencing high conflict, infidelity, and people living with a person impacted by mental illness. I offer a poly affirming space which acknowledges the challenges members of this community face. In addition, I have specialized training in Medical Family Therapy, allowing me to respond to the impact of chronic illness and disability on relationships.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: Much like the work I do with couple and marriage issues, I focus on the patterns of interactions that find families in explosive arguments and struggling to resolve conflict. By creating a safe space, families can learn to express uncomfortable feelings to increase their understanding of each other. I seek to provide communication tools that facilitate conflict resolution and reduce blame.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: My work with clients involves incorporating biological, psychological, social, and spiritual components. I offer support by allowing for the expression of feelings and challenges in navigating chronic illness. In some cases, I collaborate with medical providers to improve communication and support client's sense of agency.

specialities.name: Personality Disorders
specialities.description: I work with couples and families who are living with a loved one who is diagnosed with a personality disorder. I address the feeling of 'walking on eggshells' typically described by loved ones. I also recognize the very real fear of rejection and heightened emotional sensitivity characteristic of BPD. Therapy includes elements of DBT, developing a wise mind approach, and effective communication tools.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I approach this work by identifying patterns of interaction couples find themselves stuck in. Work includes focusing on understanding the needs of the other and learning to appreciate differences. Work around infidelity consists of determining relationship commitment, examining the dynamics of the relationship before the affair, and rebuilding the trust of the hurt partner.

name: Molly Sterling
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Welcome! My name is Molly Sterling and I am an able bodied, White, cis woman. I provide individual, trauma-focused therapy to adults 18+.
ideal_client: I work with adults in individual therapy focused on healing past trauma, developing effective coping strategies to manage anxiety or panic symptoms, or navigating a difficult life transition, such as new parenthood. I particularly enjoy working with perfectionists, people employed in the helping professions, and individuals who find it hard to "get out their heads".

approaches.My Background and Approach: I graduated from The Evergreen State College in 2005, with a BA in Fine Arts. I then completed a Masters in Art Therapy Counseling from Marylhurst University in 2011. I have experience in a variety of clinical settings, including residential/subacute care, inpatient psychiatric hospitals, community mental health, and outpatient therapy. I have been a Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) in the state of Oregon since 2015. Along the way, I have discovered a passion for working with trauma, including complex/developmental trauma and how early attachment patterns continue to show up in our relationships as adults. I would describe my therapeutic style as relational and eclectic, meaning I don’t adhere to one modality exclusively. I am trained in Somatic and Attachment Focused (SAFE) EMDR and also utilize modalities such as IFS/Parts Work, Mindfulness, Compassion-Focused Therapy, and expressive arts in my work with clients.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in the power of connection and curiosity, and I strive to meet clients with compassion, wherever they are on their healing journeys. I am committed to providing therapy that is collaborative, responsive, and affirming. Though I do not identify as part of the LGBTQIA+ community, I am an ally and am committed to understanding dynamics of privilege and oppression. I am neurodivergent affirming and Health at Every Size informed. Outside of work, I enjoy spending time with friends and family, including my partner, son, and our two cats, Ollie and Vesper. I am also involved in my community, helping organize neighborhood events and volunteering at my son’s school. I am Oregon born and raised, and am continuously grateful to call this beautiful place my home!

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I utilize Somatic and Attachment Focused (SAFE) EMDR, which is a highly effective trauma reprocessing modality focused on reducing distress associated with past memories while also redefining our beliefs about self. SAFE EMDR brings more awareness to the somatic (ie, body-based) aspects of trauma reprocessing, as well as how early attachment patterns impact our view of self, our relationships, and our behaviors. I completed my SAFE EMDR Level I training in 2019.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I specialize in treating PTSD and other trauma-related diagnoses, including complex and attachment trauma. I utilize Somatic and Attachment Focused (SAFE) EMDR, other somatic modalities, mindfulness, and compassion-focused therapy.

name: Katie Kilbourn
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Support for daily stressors, trauma, loss, and change. I'm here to listen, collaborate, and empower the change you want to create!
ideal_client: Are you struggling with your day-to-day? Feeling the impacts of systemic oppression? Are you navigating loss? Are you doing any or all of this as a queer, trans, or neurodivergent person? If you answered yes to any of those questions, I have a hunch we'll be a good fit for one another. In our work together, we'll focus on creating a safe, trusting, open relationship with one another. I use a highly relational approach in my work, because this is where the healing happens!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: In our work together, we'll focus on creating a safe, trusting, open relationship with one another. I use a highly relational approach in my work, because this is where the healing happens! I work from a compassionate, anti-oppressive, and evidence-based approach, recognizing that you are the expert in your own experience. We'll utilize techniques from a range of therapeutic methods like AEDP, Polyvagal Theory, CBT, Motivational Interviewing, Harm Reduction, and DBT. Therapy with me is a place where all emotions are welcome. We’ll explore tough feelings and memories, but we’ll also likely share some laughs along the way! Life is complex, and I’m here to support you as we navigate it together.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I’ve worked with adults across all stages of life, and I truly believe there’s always room to grow and learn more about yourself! In my own history, I've navigated anxiety, depression, grief, sexuality, gender, and PTSD. One of the most supportive forces in my own healing and learning has been working with compassionate, warm, understanding therapists. (Shout out to all the amazing therapists I've had!) I entered this career field in the hopes that I could help others the way that I've received help, but I've stayed because this work of human connection and healing is so deeply beautiful and meaningful. This is a hard time to be a person, in a world that's already hard! If you need a therapist who understands that, and will support you without telling you to "logic your way out of it", then I might be your gal/they :)

name: Aaron Good
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I provide psychotherapy and career counseling to people seeking for personal, professional, or relational growth.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I provide mental health and career counseling to individuals and couples dealing with life's challenges. Do you want to understand more about yourself, about your identity, about the way the patterns you've learned in the past might no longer be serving you? Do you deal with the challenges of depression, anxiety, guilt, past trauma, and grief or loss? Come on in and we can explore all of it in a supportive environment. Looking for help finding a new career? Trying to apply to new jobs but feeling like your skills are out-of-date? Do you want to stay at your current job but want to focus on your strengths? A professional career counselor might help - let's collaborate on figuring out what might work for you. Are you looking to deepen intimacy in your relationship, overcome conflict, or simply communicate better? We can work as a team to find what's working in your relationship and build on that while overcoming the barriers to satisfaction.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I hold a Master’s Degree in Counseling from Portland State University. Major coursework included: human growth and development, counseling theory, career counseling, ethics, disability, and understanding human relationships. I have taken workshops on topics such as group facilitation and overcoming oppression. I am also a Certified Rehabilitation Counselor, a specialization that focuses on vocational rehabilitation and adjustment. I have additional coursework in ecopsychology and ecotherapy - work that recognizes the role that nature plays in our lives and weaves it into therapy itself.

specialities.name: Career Counseling
specialities.description: Perhaps you’re unhappy with your job, unsure about your career choices, or just looking for a change. We can collaborate to find what isn’t working about your current situation and explore steps towards a more rewarding career. This can range from practical work like job searching, resume building, or specific tests, to navigating the internal and interpersonal patterns that hold you back.

specialities.name: Nonviolent Communication
specialities.description: Nonviolent communication is a skill I teach both individually and in a group. I utilize and teach its core skills of nonjudgmental observation and taking ownership of feelings without blame in my work with clients.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: I couple humanistic counseling with Reality Therapy, using our desire for connection and meaning in our lives to drive client-centered behavior change.

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: I use ecotherapy in various forms - in its simplest form it involves weaving in awareness of the natural world into our counseling sessions. We can also take therapy outside, into one of our city's many beautiful parks. If you'd like we can address specific issues such as climate change, environmentalism, grief over habitat destruction, and more, using a variety of ecotherapy methods.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: Who am I? Where is my life headed? What does it all mean? These are questions we're sometimes able to keep out, but there are times they bubble to the surface. When that happens, let's work on figuring out what your values are, what you want from the future, and how to get there.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I use an emotion-focused, systems, and nonviolent communication approach to helping individuals and couples improve their relationships. We'll work on building compassion for ourselves and our partners, and practice reflecting what our partners might be feeling.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I use an approach that builds insight into the causes of anxiety, provides coping mechanisms for managing that anxiety, and support for the challenges involved.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression can take many forms - quite often we may appear happy to others but be filled with self-doubt and worthlessness. We'll work together to build connection with the world around you, find your joy, and understand how to avoid the thought-traps that led us into depression to begin with.

name: Mattie Boucher
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I enjoy supporting clients to better understand themselves, live aligned with their values, and feel more empowered in their relationships.
ideal_client: As a queer and trans person myself, I am most passionate about working with my community. I also have a special interest in working with neurodivergence, complex trauma and dissociation. I believe as we grow, we find creative and resilient ways to best exist in our families of origin and environments. Sometimes, the ways we learned to be when we were younger are no longer serving us or authentic to who we are now.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is deeply relational and collaborative with a focus on attachment. I feel a safe and strong therapeutic relationship is the most important element of therapy to create an environment that makes growth possible. I currently use various interventions and techniques from different theories depending on what the client’s goals are in order to be client-centered, including DBT, CBT, EMDR, Ego State Therapy, Attachment theory and Polyvagal theory.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Many of the things we work on in the therapy room are directly related to the impacts of the external systems we are a part of, such as white supremacy and capitalism. For this reason I strongly believe an abolitionist, anti-racist and health at every size perspective is important to move toward healing and liberation in this work and aligns with my values outside of the therapy room as well. When I am not in session with clients I can be found puzzling, tinkering with my plants, reading, playing basketball or spending time with my senior dog on a very slow walk.

name: Ofelio Resendiz
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: As a gestalt therapist, I will help you become more of who you are and find ways to lean into your resilience to overcome your distress.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have experience working with Adolescents, Adults, Families, and Couples experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, and identity issues. I approach therapy with the understanding that we are all shaped by experiences throughout our lives in context with our family of origin and cultural background. These experiences inform how we make meaning in our lives. I believe the therapeutic relationship is the most important element of therapy within which we collaborate to discover a meaningful change. I primarily practice Contemporary Gestalt Therapy, an evidence-based practice that seeks to build awareness in the present moment and understand how you make meaning of your environment. From this perspective symptoms of mental illness are our attempt to cope with inner and environmental distress. Our work in therapy will be supporting these symptoms and becoming curious about their intended function which paradoxically leads to their resolution.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I earned my Masters in Applied Psychological Science, with an emphasis in Latino/a Psychology from Pacific University. I have experience working with culturally diverse populations which include Asian, Native American, and Latino/a/x, Adolescents, and adults. I utilize EFT for relationship work. I also conduct sessions in Spanish for patients needing a Spanish-speaking clinician.

specialities.name: Gestalt
specialities.description: I have been in Gestalt supervision, consultation, and training in Portland since 2018. I am also in post-graduate advanced clinical training at the Pacific Gestalt Institute in Los Angeles, California.

name: Daniel Hilley
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I believe in the power and importance of finding humor and giving ourselves grace as we work to heal our relationships and ourselves.
ideal_client: If you are struggling with partner relationships, parenting or parent-teen relationships, I have nearly 20 years of experiencing helping people just like you. I've long been the therapist who loves to work with snarky and defiant teens, as well as adults who are reluctant about coming to therapy. Maybe you fear being blamed or being seen as "the problem" - and I can assure you that you won't be. I specialize in healing those relationship rifts and improving connection and communication skills.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Over the years I have continued to refine my skills, interventions, and perspectives to incorporate new research as well as simply learning over time what works and what doesn't. In most cases, there are many roads to healing. I will help you to figure out which strategies make sense FOR YOU. And if something doesn't make sense, I want my clients to tell me or challenge me. My suggestions and strategies are grounded in solid theory and research, and I will always be able to explain why I'm thinking the way I am. AND that doesn't mean it has to make sense to you, so let's talk about it. I am a big believer that the most important work for change comes outside of the session, so I'll provide exercises, reading, and other resources for you to practice with between sessions. Together we'll find what makes sense to you and what works for you - and my biggest goal is to work myself out of a job, because therapy shouldn't last forever.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: The path of my career has taken me to the umbrella of "relationships" of all kinds - I worked with families and teens for the first part of my career. Between 2010 and 2015 the most formative training of my career occurred: Bullies to Buddies (Izzy Kalman) and Pragmatic Experiential Therapy for Couples (PET-C, Brent Atkinson) overlapped and shaped how I view strained and problematic relationships, and since that time I have adapted much of Atkinson's approach for family relationships, with particular emphasis on parent-teen relationships and find it both fascinating and deeply rewarding. I have extensively studied Interpersonal Neurobiology (aka how relationships shape the mind) and obtained certification as a Sex Therapy Informed Professional (CSTIP with Tammy Nelson). I come with a wealth of background, steeped in research-supported methods and perspectives. I love what I do and after almost 20 years, I still get excited by the growth and change I see in front of me every day.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: Extensive training in Pragmatic Experiential Therapy for Couples (PET-C) as well as Interpersonal Neurobiology for Couples.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: Extensive Training in Impersonal Neurobiology, which is the study of relationships influence on the mind. In healing relationships, we are often tending to the relational attachment and developmental attachment wounds in one or more partners.

name: Lisa Wittorff
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I delight in working with folks who fall outside the norm. Do you feel the world is just not a good fit for you or your child? I can help.
ideal_client: I enjoy working with folks who don't quite fit in. Maybe you just found out that you are autistic or have ADHD. Maybe your kid is the one who keeps getting sent home from school for biting other kids. Perhaps you are realizing the reason your body has never felt right is because it doesn't match your actual gender. It could be that you have anxiety about going out in public. All of you, and other folks who don't fit into the "normie" stereotype are my favorite type of people to work with.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I use an evidence-based yet intuitive approach to working with people. I have many years of experience, and that helps me to be able to quickly assess how to work with you in a way that works best and helps you to make progress. We laugh together, cry together and grow together. I am direct, which means I say it like it is, I don't sit back and just reflect what you've said. I help you think and feel through what's happening in your life and what you'd like to be different. I help you figure out how you can think and feel differently about your life, so you can change it.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a Licensed Clinical Social Worker in Portland, Oregon. I have many years experience working with families and children with special needs. I especially love working with children who are not neurotypical, including diagnoses such as RAD, FASD, ASD. ADHD and other challenging behaviors that don't include a diagnosis . I am also the adoptive parent of 3 children from foster care who are now young adults. My children have been through almost every struggle and diagnosis possible, so I have a lot of “hands on” parenting knowledge. I have tried many kinds of parenting throughout my journey, and discovering Mindful Parenting and Collaborative Problem Solving finally made everything going on with my children and the families I work with make sense. I was able to use these tools to transform my relationship with my children, and help other parents change their relationships as well. To learn more, check out my website at wiseowlcoaching.org , or email me at wiseowlparenting@gmail.com.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I have been certified as a court expert in attachment.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness often makes people think of yoga and meditation, and while those can be part of mindfulness, it is so much more. Mindfulness, simply stated, is being present, and being kind. Those 2 simple concepts are very complex ones to apply to parenting (or life in general!).

specialities.name: Adoption Issues
specialities.description: I worked as an adoption social worker for 12 years, and also have 3 children through foster care, so I understand both personally and professionally the challenges of adoptive parenting. I also have been certified as an expert in attachment theory and have worked with many children with attachment issues and Reactive Attachment DisorI der.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: The basis of my parenting philosophy is a combination of mindful parenting, brain based science, and Collaborative Problem Solving. I blend all three of these philosophies in my practice. Taking into account the age, developmental level and needs of the child, along with the needs of the parent(s), I help you design a style of parenting that best suits your family.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I have navigated the journey of gender with each of my children, and helped many parents navigate this journey with their children. I can help you too!

specialities.name: Autism
specialities.description: I have worked with many people who have been diagnosed with autism later in their lives. This carries with it a special kind of trauma that is in addition to the struggle of being neurodivergent. I know how to work with that and help you navigate and heal from your historical trauma. I also work with parents of autistic children, helping them understand their children's needs and how to parent them.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I have worked with many children and adults with ADHD, helping them to learn to work with their unique brains.

name: Wes Harris
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am dedicated to helping people find inner-peace, stability, and contentment in the face of what ever hardships they are facing.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I incorporate a variety of approaches into my way of working with people and believe that it is important to collaborate to find an approach that fits the client's needs. That being said, I often utilize Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and other mindfulness based approaches. Many people benefit greatly from having the opportunity to talk through the challenges they are facing in life. Additional benefit can be had from focusing on a particular difficulty and developing a focused plan to bring about change. Counseling is not a one-size-fits-all endeavor.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: I hold a masters degree in professional mental health counseling from Lewis & Clark College. I am a Licensed Professional Counselor in the state of Oregon. My professional experience has brought me into contact with a wide variety of people. I specialize in supporting people struggling with difficult mood states, and who are seeking to remove obstacles to their wellbeing. I am also a Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: I have expertise in ACT and have spent a lot of time in ACT consultation groups and taking advanced trainings. I am passionate about this approach and working with clients who are open to learning more or putting their experiences with ACT into practice.

name: Ranann Bell
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Let's go for a walk and allow nature to support us!
ideal_client: I work with folks going through all types of life transitions, exploring difficult family dynamics, experiencing grief, and working through trauma. Together, we can put one foot in front of the other and learn from mother nature's deep wisdom.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Outdoor therapy is centered around the belief, experience, and scientific backing that nature can offer grounding, calm, and clarity. Nature supports us in feeling more relaxed and open, allowing you to explore your emotions more freely. The rhythmic movement of walking releases built-up energy and tension, helping you process difficult feelings. In each session, we’ll take a walk in one of the beautiful parks Portland has to offer, using the natural world around us as a supportive backdrop for your healing process.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe in a holistic approach to therapy, where nature becomes our guide. I created Bellflower Therapy to offer clients a unique experience—one where we step outside the walls of a traditional therapy room and into nature. My approach focuses on walking side by side, allowing the natural environment to be a healing partner as you explore your emotions and work through life’s challenges.

name: Katheryne Lewis
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hi there! My name is Katheryne (She/her) I'm here to join your team as you navigate all the complexities of being alive in this world.
ideal_client: I work with individuals, families, and partnerships of all ages and backgrounds. My passion lies with working with LGBTQIA youth as they find their voice and become active participants and decision-makers in their lives. However, I am honored to work with everyone as we explore and deconstruct the harmful narratives that are often adopted from families, partners, communities and oppressive social constructs. We can move with a curiosity that makes space for your fully unique self.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a Licensed Mental Health Counselor in Washington (MHC.LH.61475994) and a Professional Counselor Associate in Oregon (R7357). My practice is oriented to Narrative Theory and Ecopsychology. Celebrating each individual’s uniqueness, I aim to help clients understand their stories within a larger sociocultural context while encouraging them to make room for meaningful narratives. Narrative theory emphasizes that our stories are not only our own, but are comprised of the narratives that society may have of us. It is important to embolden the voice of the client as they work to rewrite the storylines of their identity. I work to help clients create meaning while also acknowledging and holding the larger systems of oppression accountable for the barriers they continuously uphold. Additionally, I pull components from a variety of modalities and currently am in the process to become a certified ADHD clinical services provider.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: With a background in environmental conservation and currently in the process of re-indigenizing my understanding of conservation, I hold true that in order for our ecosystems to thrive, it embraces all that is queer, diverse, strange, unique, beautiful, and mystifying. The fact is, there is nothing queerer than nature. Imagine the thriving community we could cultivate if we choose to use nature as a mirror and model for success. As a queer Black woman and a clinician, my goal is to help my clients understand their unique existence in this greater ecosystem, ready to be embraced for all that they are. These identifies inform how I show up in the world and have always been affirmed in how I relate to our natural spaces. While that may not be everyone's cup of tea, it grounds me in my values and allows me to relate to others in the human and beyond human world.

name: Christopher Marquardt
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Hello. Me: Therapist. You: Client. Work together? Call to find out...
ideal_client: I see a range of clients. My clients are likely looking for medium to long-term therapy and seeking to make meaning out of their lives. They are likely to be ready to try something new or different in their lives and seeking support to get there. Typically my clients are from 20-40 years old and struggling with purpose, substance or relationship issues.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer a unique counseling experience: I blend compassion with a dash of directiveness topped off with a heaping dose of encouraged autonomy or suggested self-advocacy.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I worked in Education for a long time and wound up being a teacher for students with severe behavioral disorders. Much of my work, in that position, was around helping those kids make better decisions. It was during that time (and my own time seeing a therapist), that I decided to pursue this field as a career. I realize that not all therapists are the same and I really hope to bring significant, life-changing change to/with my clients. I am a Returned Peace Corps Volunteer and value people from all different backgrounds, races, religions, ethnicities, genders, sexual preferences, ability levels, etc. I consider myself working towards the tenets of anti-racism and have taken the anti-racist small business pledge. I have experience with meditation and try and incorporate morality into all of my actions. I love the Timbers.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: Who are you? Where are you going? How to make the most of what you've been dealt? How to cope with the unfortunate situations that are present? How to celebrate the positives?

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: This lens investigates the words, thoughts and behaviors you, as a client, uses. If we can understand and gently shift/change these, there's a chance you'll make better changes.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I tend to build emotional connections to my clients- I hope to mitigate the pain caused by other suboptimal relationships you've had in the past. For clients this looks like establishing a connection to someone who knows them very well and represents a reflection of their better self which, for one reason or the other, you may be unable to see.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I recognize the unique social constructs and constraints present for a man in our modern society. I encourage my male clients to accept their maleness and work towards a more holistic version of themselves.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: We are all in relationship. I work with clients to improve, or increase, relationships. For those I see who in the couple's therapy portion of my practice, we work to understand emotions, increase communication and build skills to work together better.

specialities.name: Drug Dependence / Abuse / Addiction
specialities.description: Many of my clients come seeking counsel, advice or assistance in managing drugs or alcohol. I work with this delicately, as this particular issue is tough to treat. My hope is that we determine some shared goals and start monitoring and working toward meeting them.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: I think this is the most common thematic topic for all clients seeking therapy. I try and establish a system where we can work together to envision a desired future and then construct pathways towards realizing that which the client wants.

name: Natalie (Nat) Day
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Nat Day, LCSW has a waitlist at https://skycloudhealth.com/ Accepting Cigna, Aetna, PacificSource, BCBS, single-case agreements with Kaiser.
ideal_client: Nat is dedicated to serving adults who feel othered or isolated in their lives and supporting self acceptance, connection, and community. She specializes in working with trauma, mood disorders, body image issues, addiction, chronic illness, sex therapy, and OCD. She is allied with the LGBTQIA+ community, Body Positivity movement, sex workers, and polyamorous/open relationships.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Nat Day, LCSW and graduated from Boise State University with a Masters in Social Work in 2018. Over the last decade she has worked in a variety of settings: residential treatment, on-campus college counseling, substance abuse treatment, inpatient psychiatric care, and community mental health. Nat has earned a certification in treating trauma (Certified Clinical Trauma Professional Level II), 20+ hours of training from the Be Body Positive Institute, sex and couples counseling, and training in polyvagal theory and somatic approaches. She is currently enrolled in a certification program through the Center for Positive Sexuality. Specializing in the treatment of trauma, addictions, and sexuality (with special focus on kink/BDSM/sex work), her approach to therapy is eclectic, drawing on a variety of evidenced based practices, including DBT, CBT, attachment therapy, relationship trauma, existential therapy, harm reduction, and body image issues.

name: Linnea Stenhouse
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Attuned presence and care as you explore the safety and ground within, stepping further into your agency, strength, and unique identity.
ideal_client: We might be a good fit if you are a helper by profession or lifestyle; have a loved one experiencing mental health distress; in a major life transition; seeking gender affirming care; processing grief and loss, communication challenges, relationship difficulties; feeling safe in the world; being a sensitive person. I value authenticity, transparency, and curiosity. My approach is mindful, relational, radical, and existential.

approaches.My Background and Approach: You know change is constant, and yet, it can knock the wind out of you. It is often disorienting, unsettling, and can call into question basic assumptions you have about yourself, your identity, your relationships. Even when you’re moving in your desired direction, adjusting to change brings up a lot of shit. To complicate matters, you may have unknowingly created complex internal systems to bypass or avoid painful aspects of your life throughout your development. Over time you grow, adapt, change, but old worn out ways stubbornly stick. Therapy can be a space to shed through old skins that no longer fit, discover new ways of being, and explore and process yourself, your relationships, community and context. My approach is relational, collaborative, liberatory, and trauma-informed. I practice with transparency and believe in a non-hierarchal approach to healing. To learn more about my approach, please check out my website!

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I pay attention to and am curious about, how power and oppression show up in and outside of the therapy room. I believe we are wounded not just by individual life experiences, but by collective and historical forces, lineages of power, oppression and privilege, and present day context. My commitment to this radical practice includes ongoing evaluation of how my whiteness, femmeness, queerness, and the myriad of other identities and experiences I’ve had, show up in my role as therapist and beyond. My lens of considering layers of context includes existential perspectives and the mystery of our broadest context of living (and dying) as human beings. I love to zoom into the minutia of our nervous system and its response to daily life and also zoom way way out to the absurdity of our existence as strange beings on a floating ball. Considering our many layers of living can help cultivate mindfulness of the present moment and place us in the room in a more meaningful and alive way.

name: Kate Robinson
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Greetings! I love being a Licensed Professional counselor and I look forward to helping you on your journey to be your best self.
ideal_client: Many struggle with finding their optimal balance of emotional and physical well being at different periods in their life. When finding balance is complicate by mental illness, chronic pain, or loss, life can feel unbearable. I believe that regardless of what barriers arise, every person is capable of taking steps towards feeling more fulfilled in life. My experience of trauma and loss as a teen and learning how to work through hard times helps me connect with clients on a deep level.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I utilize Cognitive Behavioral, Strengths-Based, and Mindfulness - Based treatment approaches. During the past 17 years, I have worked in Inpatient and outpatient treatment settings. In private practice my focus is on individual counseling for adults. My areas of specialization include working with individuals with Acquired Brain Injury (TBI, Concussion, Stroke, Tumor, encephalitis.) as well as helping people who are struggling with symptoms associated with Chronic Pain, Depression, Anxiety, and difficulty adjusting to life changes. My treatment begins with gathering some history and learning about what brings you to counseling. In the time frame that works best for you, I will help you identify what is not going well and what is keeping you from the life you want to lead. I will be an empathic listener and encourage you to practice new ways of thinking about what is troubling you and teach ways you can make subtle changes to start feeling your best.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Life changed drastically for me when as a teenager I suffered a traumatic brain injury and spent several months in the hospital recovering and relearning everything. My recovery was aided by receiving individual counseling which helped me learn how to adapt to all of the emotional and physical changes as well as losses I experienced. Professional help put me on the right path and is one of the reasons I decided to become a counselor myself. Over the years, I gained confidence and focused my energy on helping others. I have been, and continue to be active in the brain injury community as a volunteer and public speaker. I was recently invited to be a guest speaker at a Symposium about Traumatic Brain Injury and PTSD in Warsaw, Poland. My interests include spending time with my family, gardening, meditation and traveling. I am fluent in French and my undergrad degree was in French studies. I love to learn and take advantage of any opportunities to expand my knowledge as a counselor.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: I have participated in numerous CBT trainings and continue to learn about and practice this treatment approach. I have found that it is very effective for most clients and have seen positive results.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: Chronic Pain can be so frustrating and exhausting. It often leads to symptoms of depression and /or increased use of medication that can make the condition worse and lead to overuse. From my own experience with chronic pain as well as from working at a chronic pain management center, I have learned the pain management skills that appear to best provide relief and maximize functioning. I focus on the cognitive aspects and thought processes that can help decrease pain.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Symptoms of PTSD often cause distress, impaired functioning and can negatively impact personal relationships, the ability to work and the ability to participate in social activities that used to be enjoyable. Unhealthy coping skills such as increased drug or alcohol use are not uncommon. By learning healthier coping skills, relaxation techniques, and new ways of thinking, relief is possible.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety disorders are fairly common but can at times be very uncomfortable and sometimes debilitating. I most often treat individuals with Generalized Anxiety Disorder, Panic Disorder and Social Anxiety Disorder. I find that by teaching clients about Cognitive Distortions, behavioral coping strategies, mindfulness techniques, and stress reduction techniques, anxiety symptoms can be managed.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: Depression is an often overwhelming condition that affects a person emotionally and physically. For those who have not suffered from this illness, it is hard to explain how it feels. I believe that Depression is manageable with or without medication, depending on the individual. I primarily utilize Cognitive Behavioral Therapy to help clients cope with and ultimately alleviate depression symptoms.

name: Zara Roth
title: Professional Counselor
intro: Lonely? Nihilistic? Sad? Scared? Angry? Restless? Insecure? Bitter? Confused? Let me help you cope through it.
ideal_client: With the state of the world, mental health is at an all-time low and we are all experiencing collective trauma. I take climate, pandemic, economic, political, societal, and cultural problems into account, on top of personal issues. My goal has always been to help those with trauma, personality disorders, and depression/anxiety by diving into the unconscious, cultivating self-awareness, and creating practical solutions. My clients are diverse and range from 16-65+ yrs old.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I hold a graduate degree in mental health counseling from Northwestern University, as well as a certificate in child and adolescent psychology from The Chicago School of Professional Psychology. My therapeutic approach is eclectic and well-rounded, and I have a background in psychodynamic psychotherapy which allows me to dive into the unconscious, create self-awareness, and formulate practical solutions for clients dealing with trauma, personality disorders, depression, and anxiety. I previously worked at a DBT clinic specializing in borderline personality disorder and high-acuity patients; as well as at a rehab clinic where I led the mental health IOP group therapy program for those with PTSD and severe anxiety/depression. I aim to create an environment of validation, authenticity, unconditional positive regard, acceptance, and inclusion in my practice.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I take an individualized approach to each client and tailor treatment plans based on their unique and specific needs. I use established therapeutic modalities and somatic, sports, music, art, and laugh therapy. I believe that many existential questions can be answered using the wisdom of philosophers throughout history. I have a particular interest in working with marginalized communities and advocating for multicultural and feminist issues. I believe a main factor in mental health issues is the natural human reaction to a society which makes us sick. My focus includes the psychology of capitalism, complex trauma, ADHD, BPD, eco-anxiety, non-dogmatic spirituality, and psychedelic therapy.

specialities.name: ADHD
specialities.description: I have ADHD myself and have learned how to cope with it over the years.

name: Laura Riley
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I value offering a safe container for connection, authenticity, mindful compassionate awareness to support healing, embodiment and growth.
ideal_client: The individuals and groups I work with are women, non-binary, LGBTQ, and BIPOC. The areas of growth I love to support are folks wanting to connect more deeply with themselves through mindfulness, somatic awareness, attachment healing and spirituality. Folks who desire to deepen self awareness, explore healing around developmental attachment patterns, navigating grief/loss, learn empowered new ways in relationships, strengthen intimacy and authentic expression with themselves and others.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I work from a somatic-based, relational and holistic approach supporting individuals and groups. At the center of the therapeutic relationship is our present moment connection. Everything revolves and evolves from the place of mindful connection. The orientations that I work from are Sensorimotor Psychotherapy, EMDR, expressive arts, Ketamine-Assisted Psychotherapy, experiential and process groups, NeuroAffective Touch.

specialities.name: Sensorimotor
specialities.description: You will cultivate the practice of slowing down to explore and witness with mindful awareness your embodied experience. Through embodied awareness, in connection with another, you will begin to be aware of the unconscious and unresolved patterns living in the body-mind that impact healthy relationships and being fully aligned with the open heart. With compassionate awareness you can begin to heal, resolve and feel more empowered in how you choose to relate to yourself, others and the earth.

name: Avery Bill
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I currently have openings for new OHP clients. Please contact me to schedule a free consultation and see if it feels like a good fit.
ideal_client: My practice is informed by contemplative and somatic practices with an emphasis on mindfulness and nervous system regulation. Healing occurs through genuine and supportive relationships. Being a part of your life path is a privilege. I look forward to connecting and learning more about you.

approaches.What I Specialize In: I specialize in talk therapy both online and in-person. Our relationship and compatibility is the foundation for productive therapy. The therapy process can yield positive growth and help you to gain insight, reduce your suffering, and enjoy life and relationships more by moving through discomfort rather than avoiding it. I am here for you and we can figure this out together. I am a trauma-informed provider and I believe that we can learn how to better regulate our emotions and our stressed out nervous systems, be less reactive, and experience lasting change. I am a flexible, caring, and non-judgmental practitioner who is present and attuned with you. I am educated in a variety of strategies to help you to access and integrate past trauma and make sense of things now. I am passionate about integrating tools that really work for you, including process/talk therapy, yoga, meditation, and sound therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a clinical social worker who strives to support and advocate for my clients. As a parent myself I have a strong awareness of the difficulties of parenting, especially with all of the stressors in our lives recently. I believe that many of us are stuck in a chronic state of flight or flight/nervous system activation due to the level of stimulation and demands of our modern lives. Together we can assess your stressors and come up with a plan and tools to help bring you into a more peaceful and balanced state of mindfulness and understanding. In my personal life I am a practitioner of Buddhism, yoga, and a Reiki master. I enjoy cats, camping, and my VW bus.

name: Rhea Morais
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I am passionate about helping young adults recover from trauma and find healing, growth, and meaning in their lives.
ideal_client: My clients often find me at a time when they don't quite know who they are yet. They may be struggling to figure out their place in the world or feel sensitive and easily overwhelmed. They often feel lost, alone, and at war with themselves. I enjoy working with young adults who struggle with issues related to complex trauma, low self worth, depression, anxiety, existential/spiritual crises, life transitions, relationship issues, LGBTQ+ issues, identity exploration, and psychedelic integration.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I genuinely care about each of my clients and believe that the therapeutic relationship can be a powerful tool to help facilitate growth and change. I work with clients collaboratively and approach our work through an integrative lens, meaning I don't believe in a one-size-fits-all approach to therapy and instead draw from a number of different therapeutic frameworks based on individual clients' needs. I primarily come from a depth-oriented approach and my work is influenced by existential-humanism, gestalt therapy, somatic therapy, and psychodynamic frameworks. What this looks like in practice is that I may bring attention to your emotions in the present moment, your felt sense of emotions in your body, exploration of your past and its influence on the present, exploration of what gives your life meaning, and your experience of what it's like to be you as a complex individual. I work with clients of all backgrounds and take into account the cultural contexts clients are coming from.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I aim to deeply listen to and understand my clients, and strive to create a safe and supportive environment where you are free to explore and heal from your pain with someone on your side. I believe humans are capable of growth, change, resilience, and tremendous strength and courage in the face of life's sufferings. I love empowering clients to find this within themselves as well as a sense of hope, joy, creativity, choice, meaning, connection to themselves and others, self-compassion, and authenticity.

specialities.name: Depth Therapy
specialities.description: I work with clients on addressing the root causes of their distress rather than finding surface-level solutions. I help clients explore and get to know their inner worlds and strive to create a safe, nonjudgmental environment that encourages self-reflection.

name: Arianne Cozi
title: Student Counselor
intro: Together we will unwind challenges, release deep emotional blocks & rewire your nervous system to find a path that's fulfilling and joyful.
ideal_client: Weekend/evening hours available. I'm a trauma-trained counselor, welcoming adults (14+), couples and families from all walks of life who are facing concerns like: Depression, mood disorders, grief & phobias; Relationship challenges; Life transitions (career, divorce, empty nest, retirement); Coping habits like drugs, over- and under-eating, excessive exercise & serial relationships; Anxiety & ADHD; and Psychedelic integration (making meaning and integrating insights into daily life).

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Together we will pair somatic healing alongside talk therapy. I practice a flexible cross-therapy framework so that together we can lean into the approaches that best fit your needs, such as narrative, psychodynamic, sensorimotor, Internal Family Systems (parts work), Gottman Method (couples), or others, and I may suggests books or passages to deepen emotional understanding. I bring particular expertise to: workplace and leadership, divorce, family addiction, court, menopause and diverse body sizes and shapes. I hold a bachelor's degree from Harvard University and have completed my coursework for my master's degree in clinical mental health counseling.

approaches.Why We are a Good Fit for You: I am transitioning from a related career (in my case, 20 years in psychology journalism). I bring a deep knowledge base, cutting-edge clinical skills, and a wealth of life experience, like raising children, workplace leadership, menopause, mid-life relationship transitions, family addiction, and the full spectrum of life experience. I look forward to collaborating.

name: Erin Davis
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I’m a non-binary, queer therapist based in Portland, offering virtual care so you can access support no matter where you are in Oregon.
ideal_client: You’re seeking a deeper understanding of yourself—craving clarity, connection, and a sense of ease that feels just out of reach. You sense there’s something more beneath the surface, within you or the world around you, but it feels elusive. My clients often share this feeling, and together, we explore the deeper layers of your experience, uncovering insight, healing, and a path toward the fulfillment and peace you deserve.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I’ve spent nearly a decade in mental health and social work, starting in child and family services before shifting to adult outpatient therapy. My approach is rooted in Internal Family Systems and I am able to offer EMDR for trauma and DBT skills and existentialism in our time together, but my greatest strength is seeing you—fully and without judgment. I meet you where you are and help you find a way forward that feels both achievable and meaningful. Therapy with me is a balance of directness, empathy, and collaboration, creating a space where real change can happen while you feel deeply supported. My lived and professional experience shape my work, allowing me to offer insight, practical tools, and a therapeutic relationship built on trust. Together, we’ll navigate what’s holding you back and build a path toward healing that actually works for you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am a queer identified, non-binary therapist. Many of the clients I serve hold identities in the LGBTQ+ rainbow. I use a trauma-informed lens to approach the work I do and have extensive clinical experience working with individuals at any point in their journey. My background as a social worker and therapist also includes working with individuals who experience suicidal thoughts, self-harm and who have complex trauma histories. I believe that healing and change are possible for all people. I am sex-positive therapist as well and believe that finding pleasure (not just sexual) in all areas of life is possible and deeply important for lasting change and healing to take place. The lenses I use most frequently in therapy include: integration, trauma-informed care, existentialism, cognitive behavioral therapy, attachment theory, and positive psychology.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I just received certification in EMDR and am excited to be able to offer this technique to my therapy tool set. The EMDR technique I learned is called FLASH, and it's a much gentler way of treating trauma triggers than traditional EMDR, while still being evidenced based and in line with EMDR.

specialities.name: Internal Family Systems (IFS)
specialities.description: I frequently use Internal Family Systems (IFS) in my work with clients. By helping clients better understand the different parts of themselves and how these parts are sometimes negatively impacting their day to day lives. Often our parts are developed in child hood to 'protect' us, however, as we grow up, the types of protection these parts offer, become hindrances and hurtful to ourselves. Identifying these parts, showing love and compassion to them and then giving them a better 'job' is key.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Since starting in social work in 2013 I have worked with countless people with mild to severe anxiety. Anxiety often stems from deeply held, negative, subconscious beliefs we have about ourselves and from traumatic or challenging experiences in our past. From excessive worry, restlessness, trouble with leaving the house and being social, to difficulty stopping fearful and negative thinking; I have had the privilege to witness and support people on their journey towards peace and healing.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: As a queer identified therapist I have the privilege of understanding the perspectives of my clients as it relates to gender identity, sexual orientation and gender expression. Religious trauma, family trauma and rejection are common challenges queer individuals face at all walks of life. I have helped people understand their gender identity more, grow beyond childhood wounds of rejection and abandonment and explore new sexual identities.

name: Julia Chapman
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I work collaboratively with clients to help develop goals and tools to increase confidence in themselves in their relationships.
ideal_client: I provide affirmative psychotherapy to adult individuals and couples of different cultures, genders and sexual identities. My areas of focus are family conflict, co-dependency and 12-step recovery, trauma, and couples work. I also enjoy working with clients entering into new parenthood.

approaches.How I Can Help You: I believe therapy has the power to transform people's lives and improve their relationships. My approach is collaborative and relational. I strive to help clients develop goals and strategies to increase self-knowledge and awareness of strengths. I assist clients in processing how past experiences may contribute to insecurities, unhelpful patterns in relationships, and professional dissatisfaction. Throughout the therapy process I help empower clients to change their life narratives by expressing and pursuing what they want in their lives.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: I believe strongly in the power of therapy to transform your life. My background is in public health and sex education, but I found that working directly with people is what I was most drawn to. I began my work in Los Angeles where I lived for many years and now am pleased to call Portland home.

specialities.name: Codependency
specialities.description: I have completed trainings by the Meadows developed by Pia Mellody. I work with clients to build self-esteem and confidence by learning to set boundaries in relationships, ask for what they want, gain acceptance and understanding of themselves, and build satisfying relationships.

specialities.name: Family Conflict
specialities.description: My therapy framework is largely psychodynamic, so I work with clients to understanding dynamics, patterns and roles they play in their family currently, as well as coping strategies they developed growing up. My experience ranges from helping clients share secrets, individuate financially, process life changes like deaths and marriages, and repair damaged relationships.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I have experience working with couples on issues ranging from sexual and emotional intimacy to infidelity and life transitions. My work with couples centers on changing patterns of communication and developing more positive ways of interacting. I help couples explore how past relationships, childhood wounds and feelings about themselves creep into their relationships in unwanted ways.

specialities.name: Historical Trauma
specialities.description: I work with trauma survivors to help change the way they feel about themselves by processing shame, rediscovering a sense of power and safety and rewriting their life narratives. I have done training in the Trauma Resiliency Model (TRM) which helps address the impact of stress on the body.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: Navigating emotional, physical and social changes after having a baby can be incredibly isolating and challenging. I work with new parents to help them adjust, modify expectations, and find support after this big change in life. As a parent myself I also have empathy and knowledge about new parenthood.

name: Sally Rudolph
title: Licensed Art Therapist
intro: I weave together creative approaches, somatic awareness and talk therapy to address deep-seated wounds in body, mind and soul.
ideal_client: Grief, loss of health, change in a relationship, or job, or home- all of these things can feel overwhelming. They may leave you feeling stuck, weighed down or disconnected. You may be searching for a non-judgmental sanctuary to explore your struggles. In sessions we tap into your innate abilities, the wisdom of your body, and your creativity, to help process and work through obstacles, in order to align with your true self and experience transformation.

approaches.My Background and Approach: As an art therapist, I offer creative opportunities for growth that are informed by IFS (Internal Family Systems) somatic approaches, journaling, and regular talk therapy. I offer a supportive, hands-on way to process and transform life challenges. Art therapy is based on the belief that we all have creativity within us that can help us heal, grow and integrate our experiences. I have worked in community mental health, day treatment, hospice and the hospital settings. In private practice I have experience working with trauma, anxiety, depression, health crisis, and grief. I have a particular passion for life transitions that may cause grief, such as loss of health, the death of an important person, relationship changes, or existential grief. I provide workshops, groups and individual counseling. I am a licensed-certified art therapist in Oregon (LCAT) and board-certified art therapist (ATR-BC). I have a BS in Human Services, a BFA in Art Education and MA in Art Therapy Counseling.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: These are the things I believe in for myself and for any other human being: Art is able to express crucial things we don't have words for. We all have untapped wisdom within us. Everyone deserves to be seen and heard, just as they are. We all need more meaningful connection. Our bodies send us messages that are important to listen to. Everyone has creativity within them. Nature is medicinal. Making things feels really good! We should all strive to find and be our authentic selves. We are whole just as we are (even with imperfections.)

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: In my view, anxiety is a sign from the nervous system that it could use help feeling more regulated. Somatic approaches and IFS (Internal Family Systems) can tap into how our body communicates with us, and how to tend to the physical and mental sensations of anxiety. I have been trained in Somatic Embodiment and Regulation Strategies, IFS as well as Trauma-Informed CBT that have informed my understanding of anxiety and how best to regulate it.

specialities.name: Cancer
specialities.description: I have had experience working with life-threatening illnesses, including cancer, for over a decade. From both personal and professional experiences, I have come to believe that tending to the emotional state of patients and caregivers is a crucial part of managing the illness. I have work experience in hospice, palliative care, and other chronic illnesses. I also have as a personal history with serious illness and medical trauma.

specialities.name: Chronic Pain or Illness
specialities.description: I have over a decade of experience working with health crisis, medical trauma, chronic pain and life-threatening illnesses. From both personal and professional experiences, I have come to believe that tending to the emotional state of the human being, and befriending the body are crucial to managing the illness. I have specialized training in somatic therapy, as well as creative approaches to tending to illness and pain.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: For over 4 years I have offered 6-week Art Therapy for Grief groups. The groups provide a chance to use creativity to process the death of a significant person. I also offer individual grief counseling. I believe humans are designed to grieve in community, with witnesses and support. In addition, creative approaches to grief can be profoundly helpful when words don't suffice. Workshops for Loss are offered a few times a year also.

name: Gabi Villaseñor
