title: Professional Counselor Associate
credentials: M.A. in Professional Mental Health Counseling
intro: Growth and change can often present difficult challenges and I encourage clients to discover and embolden their own inner resources!
ideal_client: I specialize in working with adults, new parents and women in their postpartum journey. Many of my clients are looking for greater embodiment, more vitality and wholeness in their lives. I also work with adult clients who are experiencing ecological depression caused by climate change and climate anxiety.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is formed from developmental and attachment based models, mindfulness and somatic practices while utilizing a feminist lens. I am grounded in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) as I believe that psychological flexibility and living by one's values are pertinent to our mental health. I practice from a non-judgemental, trauma informed, strengths based and curiosity driven approach to help clients get to where they would like to be in their lives. I do this by creating a collaborative environment where clients feel supported and encouraged to be courageous, because that is what therapy is, a courageous endeavor!

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe all people deserve the chance to live a life driven by meaning, value and connection. The form of counseling that I take part in focuses on internal and relational growth, and empowerment. I practice from a social justice lens meaning that I am committed to understanding the impact of systemic oppression on my clients' mental health and well-being. Therapy should be a place where you can feel heard and seen!

specialities.name: EcoTherapy
specialities.description: I offer experiential outdoor therapy in the form of "walk and talks" at local parks throughout the Portland metro area. We meet outdoors for the 50 minute session and invite the natural world into our frame of reference. Having our bodies in movement outdoors is inherently healing and can be a practice of regulating and grounding that can be taken into the clients everyday life.

specialities.name: Postpartum
specialities.description: I'm currently registered for an Advanced Perinatal Mental Health Psychotherapy Training taking place in Feb. 2025.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Ecological grief and climate anxiety are two very real stressors that contribute to many peoples experiences of the natural world today. It can be debilitating and stressful to work on these existential issues alone. I'm very passionate about this work. I've received eco-therapy training as part of my graduate studies at Lewis and Clark college and am currently part of Dr. Thomas Doherty's cohort workshop on "Eco and Climate Therapy Consult Group Training course."

name: Zoë Schwartz
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: I want to help you seek greater balance in your life, gain self-acceptance, and develop the confidence to pursue growth.
ideal_client: My goal as a therapist is to provide a supportive space where you can develop the skills and perspective necessary to enhance the quality of your life, heal from trauma and shame, and begin to live in greater alignment with your values. I hope to work with folks who seek to better understand, regulate, and monitor their emotions, as well as have a desire to unpack the power dynamics and systemic factors that influence how we experience the world.

approaches.My Background and Approach: Using a trauma informed lens to helps my clients explore the familial, relational, and systemic factors that have shaped their experiences. By teaching mindfulness techniques and pulling from different modalities such as, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy and Dialectical Behavioral Therapy, I aim to help you develop awareness of the interactions between your thoughts, feelings, and behaviors and a greater sense of agency in your personal and emotional life. It is an honor to have the opportunity to collaborate with you on your path to healing and pursuing what living a truly fulfilling life means for you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe that change is possible and that growth is an inevitable and often painful part of life. Together we will develop the insight and tools that can improve the quality of your relationships and allow you live in a more authentic and intentional way. People are the experts of their own experiences and I see it as a fundamental part of my role to remain non-judgmental in our work together. Using a strength-based therapeutic style centered around your knowledge and experience allows us to find strategies that will best support you in managing challenges such as negative self-image, anxiety, and depression. I value the fundamental importance that trust, humor, and transparency play in this process. My past experience includes working with children, adolescents, and families, survivors of intimate partner violence, those experiencing homelessness, and students with disabilities. I am passionate about social justice and motivated by the vision of liberation for all oppressed peoples.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Helping you understand the connection between your thoughts, feelings, physical sensations, and behaviors will support you in developing the coping mechanisms necessary to feel more in control of your life, and guide you towards making desired changes that will lead to decreased depression, anxiety, and increased self-esteem.

name: THRIVE Clinic
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: At THRIVE, we believe in the power of science and the art of compassion. Our clinicians are experts in masterfully matching clients with evidence-based interventions that are effective and time-limited.

approaches: All THRIVE clinicians practice cognitive, behavioral, and mindfulness-based interventions that have significant research to support their effectiveness. In general, the relationship between a THRIVE clinician and client is not unlike that between a coach and player. THRIVE clinicians help you identify your goals, define a skills-based approach for attaining your goals, and practice, practice, practice until you no longer need a coach! We focus on the right balance of active engagement (i.e. skills building and practice) and compassionate encouragement (i.e. validation and cheerleading).

Our clinicians are graduates of well-established medical institutions, rigorous clinical psychology departments, and respected social work and counseling programs. Our clinical staff is comprised of LPCs, MAs, MSWs, PhDs, and PsyDs. We also have a psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner (for med management) and a registered dietitian. All of our staff is concurrently practicing at the Portland DBT Institute and is comprehensively trained in DBT.

specialities.name: Family Therapy
specialities.description: Family therapy can be a powerful intervention - especially for those with a loved one suffering from mental illness. Several studies, for instance, have indicated that family environment can significantly impact the course and outcome of mood and psychotic disorders. At THRIVE, we practice Family-Focused Therapy, an evidence-based therapy for teens and adults struggling with mood disorders.

specialities.name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT)
specialities.description: While we do not offer full-fidelity DBT through the THRIVE clinic, all of our providers are comprehensively trained and concurrently practicing in DBT with our sister clinic, the nationally-renowned Portland DBT institute. This means that intervention offered at THRIVE are augmented by a deep toolbox of DBT skills and are guided by dialectical thinking.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: As a class of interventions, CBT has received more empirical support than any other type of intervention - and this is precisely why our practice has a strong emphasis on CBT. We like to think of ourselves as cBt (i.e. little c, big B) in our implementation of CBT, meaning that we tend to emphasize cognitive change through experience, exposure, and skills building.

specialities.name: Medication Management
specialities.description: For many people, medication can provide the steady foundation for life-changing therapy. Our medication manager is a Board Certified Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner who is intensively trained in DBT and attends weekly case consultation meetings with THRIVE therapists and dietitian. Our PMHNP is a seasoned diagnostician and practitioner who has experience in treating teens and adults.

specialities.name: Insomnia
specialities.description: At THRIVE, we believe in the power of sleep and have formed a knowledgeable team of sleep treatment providers who practice gold-standard interventions that improve sleep. In fact, recent guidelines by the American Medical Association designate CBT for Insomnia as the first-line treatment for insomnia. We also treat CPAP difficulties and recurrent nightmares using evidence-based protocols.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Although anxiety is a debilitating condition, research has uncovered powerful and relatively quick interventions for reducing symptoms of GAD, social anxiety, panic disorder, phobias, and PTSD. Namely, we practice cognitive behavioral therapies for anxiety including exposure-based therapies (e.g. graded exposure, prolonged exposure, interoceptive exposure).

specialities.name: Bipolar
specialities.description: Research indicates that bipolar disorder is best treated with a combination of medication and psychotherapy. At THRIVE, we offer both medication management and evidence-based therapies for teens and adults with bipolar disorder. Our clinic manager, Dr. Christopher Hawkey, was intensively trained in Family-Focused Therapy by the treatment developer, Dr. David Miklowitz.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: When it comes to depression, we rely on cognitive, behavioral, and mindfulness-based interventions to improve mood and decrease risk of relapse. Specific interventions that we use include behavioral activation, cognitive-behavioral therapy, mindfulness-based cognitive therapy, and acceptance and commitment therapy.

name: Tara Roland
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I'm glad you're here! I can help to illuminate and heal what feels hidden under the surface causing challenges for individuals.
ideal_client: Do you find yourself constantly worried that something bad might happen? Do you feel held back from deep connections and intimacy out of fear of rejection or abandonment; meanwhile craving attachments to others? Have you struggled with feeling not good enough or too much, beliefs that block from aligning with your authentic self? I see you! Most of my clients have experiences with feeling highly sensitive and struggle with anxiety, depression, grief and loss, trauma, and life transitions.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer a safe, non-judgemental, and compassionate environment to explore, reflect and process. I'm trained on interventions such as EMDR (eye-movement desentization reprocessing), parts work, psychodynamic, grief-informed and trauma-informed, psychological astrology, and energy work & somatic therapies. Everyone is unique and my approach to therapy honors this by using an eclectic style. I pull from a lot of modalities to support my client's. My goal is to learn from you and help to facilitate desired healing and growth. You are the expert of your life and I am here as a guide. This physical reality can bring experiences of suffering. Know that you are not alone; and there is transformational power being witnessed in your truth. Come as you are. I welcome all parts of you.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I believe we all hold gifts in this world and often times they are the ones that have been passed down throughout our lineage; at first disguising as trauma-responses. As we begin to heal, we get the opportunity to peel back the layers and reclaim ourselves as whole, worthy, and complete through the alchemical process of being open to transformation. My learning in the field of therapy has not only been in the classroom and gaining hours to complete my licensures. I too have been through the process of knowing what it is like on the other side of the seat in session work. To me, this is vitally important when working with clients as I know the vulnerability it takes to entrust someone with the deepest core of ourselves. Remember it is a privilege to hear your story! I'm fascinated with honoring creative aspects within the field that can be just as powerful as traditional modalities. I'm often learning new philosophical, theological, and mystical teachings and tools to incorporate.

name: Casandra Perks
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Hi! I'm Cas. I offer a compassionate space where you can feel supported and truly seen on your journey of healing and growth.
ideal_client: I work with those experiencing anxiety, depression, grief and loss, major life changes, stress, disability/chronic illness, or work issues, as well as those wanting to build self-confidence, trust in themselves, quiet their inner critic, or gain a deeper understanding of themselves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: When we work together, you can expect a warm, down-to-earth presence that offers a compassionate, non-judgmental space for you to deeply reflect and explore your thoughts, feelings, and stories. I value humor, both in life and in work, so you can expect a little of that as well. I use a trauma-informed, person-centered approach, believing that with the right support, everyone can grow into their best self. I don't have the answers to how you should live your life, you ultimately know what will be best for you. Life can be busy and distracting, making it feel rare to have dedicated time to focus on our needs, which can leave us feeling overwhelmed, unclear, or stuck. Sometimes it just takes slowing down and doing a bit of digging and reflection to clarify or make sense of things. Whatever it is that may have brought you here today, I would be honored to have the opportunity to understand your experience so you feel seen and supported along the way.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: Much of our work will focus on your strengths, highlighting the skills and resiliency you’ve naturally developed over the years, all while supporting you in developing new ways of coping if old patterns are no longer working. Together we will build tools to help you move toward the healing and growth you want to see, even if that simply means growing more comfortable sitting with the uncertainty life holds. Other methods I incorporate into my practice include psychodynamic theory, somatic noticing, and mindfulness. I believe what we have experienced in the past affects how we live in the present. If it feels safe and comfortable for you, we can use somatic noticing to tune in to your body, exploring your experiences on a deeper level. Becoming a therapist has been deeply driven by my own life experiences of loss and yearning for self growth. I really love this work.

name: Dr. Heidi Christensen
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: I provide deep meaningful therapy, helping you connect to your innermost, grounded self. Our work together will be collaborative, relational

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Therapy is the place of healing and possibilities – where we can work together to resolve the pain that is present in your life. Our work will start with healing the current symptoms such as stress, depression, anxiety, or relationship issues. Imagine the freedom that comes from being able to understand yourself more deeply. Imagine giving yourself hope, freedom, and love. That is exactly what will happen when you embark on this therapeutic journey. The process of transformation and healing will bring up feelings and experiences that you haven’t felt in a while. It will not be easy. We will develop tools and support to process and heal these feelings and experiences in a place of care and safety. Some people find that this is enough and might be a good place to stop. For others, it might have incited curiosity about what is also present that might not be in their awareness, and this process can be longer.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My counseling philosophy honors the strengths you have, the wisdom of your experience, and connecting to your inner truth. I focus on bridging the outer part of yourself (that which we normally associate ourselves with) with the inner part of yourself (the more intuitive and spiritual part of our being). This focus is provided in an emotionally safe environment where you can explore whatever issue is present. As a depth-oriented therapist, my approach is a collaborative, related style. I use this style with individuals, couples, and groups. I also utilize current cutting edge research such as Gottman method and Brene Brown's Daring Way, and I take a Jungian approach to dreams, unconscious content, and creativity.

name: Leticia Meza
title: Clinical Social Work Associate
intro: Hi, I’m Leticia! I provide compassionate, client-centered care to support your growth, healing, and well-being. Let’s navigate this together
ideal_client: While I have worked with a wide range of age groups, most of my experience comes from working with older adults. I am particularly passionate about working with young adults as they navigate transitional phases of life. Additionally, I enjoy working with individuals who are trying to navigate the complexities of the systems and institutions we live within.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am a bilingual therapist offering therapy in English and Spanish (and Spanglish works too!). As a Latina woman, I have a deep connection to and understanding of the Latino/x/e community. I am passionate about providing culturally specific care that honors and integrates each client's unique background and experiences into our therapeutic work.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I want to acknowledge the courage it takes to prioritize your mental health, whether you are continuing your healing journey or starting therapy for the first time. I understand that seeking support can be challenging and requires a lot of strength, so I am glad you’re here! I view the therapeutic relationship as a collaborative partnership where we work together to support your growth and healing. In that I also honor that we are all the experts in our own life and that my role as a therapist is simply to walk alongside you and create a safe and supportive space that can help you meet your goals and needs.

name: Nicole Mayeda
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I'm a clinical psychologist who likes to help individuals uncover healthy dependence, boundaries, and emotional freedom. A BFRB specialist!
ideal_client: My clients tend to hold high standards, and struggle to get out from under them. They often suffer from anxiety, OCD and/or BFRB behaviors. They may even be ambivalent about adjusting their standards because they are seen as essential to their success, and are confused about life without them. My clients are used to prizing accuracy, productivity, rationality, excellence, and consistency, but often at the expense of spontaneity, intuition, fulfillment, self-expression, and flexibility.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I have worked throughout my career with anxiety, depression, and chemical / behavioral addictions. I researched binge eating and body-focused, repetitive behaviors (BFRBs) such as compulsive hair pulling and skin picking for my doctoral dissertation, and continued jobs in the field of impulse control and OCD behaviors thereafter. In my community work, I commonly treated individuals with substance use disorders; eating and body image disorders; gambling, porn, and shoplifting addictions; codependence and people-pleasing; perfectionism, formal OCD and OCD-related conditions, and general anxiety and depression. My private practice has a special focus on anxiety, OCD, and BFRBs (@bfrbtherapist on Instagram) currently, supporting teens, adults, couples, and families affected by these behaviors. Lastly, I run groups, consult, and teach, drawing from psychodynamic, ACT, ERP, CBT, DBT, IFS, and somatic approaches.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I make my role about liberating people, and incorporate liberatory values (e.g. abolition, body positivity, restorative justice, anticolonialism, racial equity) into my psychotherapy work. I believe in whole-person healing. I don't want to teach people to simply block behaviors while all of their underlying pain, anxiety, or frustration persists unaddressed. I want people's stuck patterns to lift organically - because they are happier, lighter, and don't need them anymore. I am passionate about unpacking the complexities in situations, such as the social and cultural underpinnings that make your mental health about more than your individual commitments. Together, we can create a healing journey through values, early origins, healthy dependence, intrinsic worth, self-determination, intuitive listening, and radical repair.

name: Morgan Vanderpool
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: If you’re seeking somatically liberated care with a queer, non-binary & neurodivergent spin, you’ve arrived.
ideal_client: If you’re craving what it feels like to live in balance, authenticity, strength, integrity and alignment with your essential well-being… and interested in working in a liberatory, neurologically, and ecologically grounded way, with a highly experienced, trauma-sensitive, queer, non-binary, and neurodiverse therapist, then you’ve come to the right spot!

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I facilitate restorative, body-based experiences in which clients practice: creating balance within their nervous systems, while designing a relationship with self, others and their environment that fosters opportunities to opt out of trauma-based patterns embedded in systems of oppression, and into a liberated relationship with their body, mind, & relationships.

approaches.Why I am a Good Fit for You: If you’ve been seeking a brave and compassionate space to explore your relationship with gender, neurodivergence, trauma survivorship, sex-positivity, kink, interracial relationships, polyamory, community/collective living, trauma sensitive (re)parenting, and more, I would love to connect with you and collaborate in supporting you in your restorative and regenerative journey.

name: Meaghan Lewis
title: Clinical Psychologist
intro: I am a licensed clinical psychologist in Oregon. I specialize in providing the most up to date interventions supported by research.
ideal_client: While I am trained as a generalist, I have particular expertise in the areas of trauma/PTSD, women's mental health, substance use, anxiety, depression, and OCD. I provide evidence-based, behavioral/cognitive therapies including acceptance and mindfulness-based interventions and trauma-focused treatments. I have specialized training in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and the gold-standard treatments for PTSD, anxiety disorders, substance use, depression, and general mental health difficulties.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to psychotherapy is evidence-based, compassionate, and tailored to your needs. I consider therapy a collaborative process and would love to work with you to create meaningful and lasting changes. I earned my Ph.D. in clinical psychology at Western Michigan University. I also completed my pre-doctoral internship at the VA Pacific Islands Health Care System in Honolulu, HI and subsequently relocated to the Pacific Northwest to complete a three year VA advanced fellowship in mental illness research and treatment at the VA Portland Health Care System. As an intervention-oriented psychologist, my goal is to help you see results quickly and make improvements that last. I work together with my clients to provide the treatments that research says work and to help you function better now. If you are struggling, I may be able to help.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I am committed to anti-racist practice, women's empowerment, and welcome clients from all backgrounds. I believe that Black Lives Matter and strive to be allied with the BIPOC community as well as the LGBTQIA+ communities. I also consider myself a body positive psychologist. During therapy, I welcome conversations related to diversity, equity, and inclusion including microaggressions that occur within and outside of the therapeutic context. I am particularly passionate about helping women and persons with marginalized identities to overcome systems of oppression that present in their daily lives and to live in a way that is fulfilling and in alignment with personal values.

name: Mikaela Rodriguez
title: Psychiatrist
intro: Hi, I am a psychiatrist who offers psychotherapy for ADHD, ADHD evaluations, and medication management. LGBTQAI+ & neurodiversity-affirming
ideal_client: To get started click **SCHEDULE NOW** above and complete a PATIENT INQUIRY FORM WAITLISTING new clients for ADHD evals, therapy for ADHD as the primary issue (common secondary issues we can also work on include anxiety, depression, cannabis/alcohol use, and insomnia), and medication management (I am not prescribing stimulants or benzodiazepines, I can make recs for starting/optimizing these) Visit **** https://www.ohsu.edu/providers/mikaela-rodriguez-md **** to view past client ratings.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I offer collaborative, empathetic, and evidence-based medication management and psychotherapy for anxiety, depression, ADHD, cannabis & alcohol-related issues, insomnia and sleep problems, phobias, hair-pulling/skin-picking behaviors, and more. I also offer comprehensive diagnostic ADHD evaluations (2 hours+). ADHD Therapy: I specialize in helping individuals develop skills to overcome ADHD-related challenges (e.g., time management, organization, planning, motivation, procrastination, and more) while also addressing the shame and feelings of inadequacy that often accompany ADHD.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I offer appointments online via secure video Monday's-Thursday's 9 am - 4 pm. Established clients can schedule and cancel their appointments online through their secure patient portal. Due to my psychiatry practice being virtual-only I do not currently prescribe controlled substances (stimulants, benzodiazepines). I can collaborate with your PCP, sharing detailed recs for how/why to start a stimulant, if needed. I am in-network with Pacific Source, Moda, and Blue Cross/Blue Shield commercial plans only (not OHP, Medicare). To increase my availability to individuals with limited financial means, I am not accepting new cash-pay or OOP clients. am not currently offering formal CBT-Insomnia only sessions. To get started click **SCHEDULE NOW** above and complete a PATIENT INQUIRY FORM (a response is not guaranteed).

specialities.name: Alcohol Abuse and Alcohol Dependence
specialities.description: I offer recovery-oriented psychotherapy and medication management for alcohol-related concerns. I typically prescribe naltrexone and non-habit forming medications to help with insomnia, anxiety, and depression (such as propranolol, hydroxyzine, and antidepressants). I am not a good fit for clients who need benzodiazepines, have required medical detox for seizures or other withdrawal-related concerns in the past year, or who have been discharged from a residential program in the past 3 months.

name: Kristen Cole
title: Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioner
intro: My medication management practice focuses on depression, anxiety, obsessive-compulsive disorder, bipolar disorder, and trauma.
ideal_client: I use a trauma-informed approach to mental health that includes both medication management and psychotherapy. I employ a Health at Every Size philosophy that prioritizes whole person wellness above a weight-centric perspective. In my practice, the client is at the helm of choosing what issues to work on. A holistic approach is favored over one-size-fits-all formulas.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: As most people today are touched by mental health struggles, whether it be their own or their loved ones, we can use those experiences to learn to ground spiritually and mentally. I strive to understand the person in their present state and identify the root cause of distress in their life.

approaches.Our Values as Mental Health Practitioner: I believe that everyone in the healing profession should undergo their own journey of self-exploration, to better understand the people they’re treating. I am here to facilitate that process of healing.

name: Kerry Headley
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: Let's reimagine your story so that growth feels less like struggle and more like a goal you can accomplish.
ideal_client: If you are recovering from spiritual abuse and/or a high control group (cult), you may be wondering how to just be a "normal" person. Maybe you can feel that underneath what happened to you, is a more genuine you. You have big picture dreams (meaning, purpose, identity) but feel blocked by day-to-day issues like self-esteem, perfectionism, and worthiness. Together, we can figure out what values make you sing and which ones hold you back. I am also LGBTQ-affirming as a straight, cisgender woman.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: Consider what you believe about yourself—negative, limiting things you still tell yourself even though part of you knows it's not true. Ideas you’ve learned within the group, church, etc. How accurate are these narratives? Do you feel like you can’t do something or be something because within you is the voice of a leader, pastor, group member, or even the former you who was in the group? What would it be like to choose a different story—one based on your beliefs and what you care about? You may have forgotten about your strengths and abilities. Therapy offers space for you to tell your stories as well as rewrite them. Part of healing from religious trauma and/or coercive control is taking the role of the main character in your life story--a story that makes you feel whole. I can help you set realistic, inspiring goals and provide support as you work toward meeting them.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: Collaboration: I am a person-centered therapist, which means you are the boss of you. I won't give you homework if you hate that (but I'm happy to provide therapeutic tasks that can help you continue the work between sessions if you like). I don’t make people meditate (but we can discuss mindfulness-based stress reduction techniques if you are curious). Creativity: You are a unique person. We get to know each other. We figure out together what’s most likely to help you meet your goals. Humor: Laughter makes the difficulties more bearable. Compassion: Change is often hard, and growth can feel like struggle. Being seen and understood helps while we are learning to remember who we are.

name: lisa anne ross
title: Somatic Practitioner
intro: Learn skills that connect you to your inner knowing, shift painful patterns, and risk authentic self-expression for a more fulfilling life.
ideal_client: I work best with folks who are ready to engage deeply with their inner world—those who are eager to learn and implement the inner skills that lead to change. My clients often describe themselves as introspective and committed to personal growth, and are navigating topics such as struggling with self worth, relational challenges, or spiritual disconnection. I work with people of all identities, bodies, backgrounds, and relationship structures— your lived experience is honored in our relationship.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: The work I do, Core Energetics, is grounded in the belief that lasting change doesn’t come just from insight, but from felt experience. I help clients notice what’s happening beneath the surface: in posture, in sensation, in emotion. We slow down and listen to the body’s signals, tracing them to the patterns they reveal—often shaped by early relationships, past overwhelm, or what had to be hidden to stay safe. Rather than pathologizing or striving to fix, we follow those threads with curiosity and use both grounding techniques and expressive movements to explore their wisdom. This process of embodiment helps folks learn to make friends with a wider range of emotions. Over time people feel more connected to their agency and more at home in their own skin.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I believe healing doesn’t happen in a vacuum. We’re shaped not only by our families and interpersonal relationships but also by the systems we live within. I hold a lens that recognizes the impact of racism, capitalism, anti-fat bias, ableism, transphobia, and other intersecting forms of oppression as part of the landscape we’re navigating together. Truth telling is at the heart of my work, and that means acknowledging that I live and work on the traditional lands of the Kathlamet, Clackamas, Clowwewalla, Wasco-Wishram, Multnomah, and Skillot bands of Chinook; the Tualatin Kalapuya; the Molalla; and many other tribes who lived along the Columbia and Willamette rivers before European settler colonialism forcibly displaced them. In both my personal and professional life I’m committed to the ongoing, imperfect work of interrupting white supremacy and other inherited systemic-isms.

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: Core Energetics explores the intersection of body, mind, and spirit using embodiment practices to bring consciousness to the flow and constrictions of energy in our body, mind, and emotions. I’ll guide you in applying awareness and movement to unwind the physical and energetic armor that formed as we developed from childhood into adulthood, leading to an authentic self unbound by insecurities.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: Mindfulness, from a therapeutic perspective, is a conscious awareness of our present moment. In Core Energetics, cultivating mindfulness is the basis from which we are able to track and transform our lives. You’ll learn how to bring consciousness to your body, beliefs, emotions, and behavior by cultivating an 'objective observer self'.

name: Emily Berry
title: Licensed Professional Counselor
intro: I'm a radical, relational therapist and clinical supervisor. Visit www.emilyberrycounseling.com to learn more.
ideal_client: I primarily work with the LGBTQ+ community, femmes, and highly sensitive people who are seeking a space for self-exploration and growth. I bring my genuine presence, empathy, humor, and a social justice lens to my sessions with clients.

approaches.My Background: During my difficult younger years, I discovered a longing to understand what humans need in order to live healthy, meaningful lives. I was often told I was "too sensitive," and while a part of me worried that that was true, in my gut I knew it wasn't a problem. It was a gift. I wanted to be a part of shifting our society’s narratives about mental health and emotional wellbeing by being someone who welcomes and connects with the humanity and vulnerability of others. Being a therapist is not just a job for me - this work is in my bones. Nothing is more meaningful to me than helping others discover the strength and wisdom within themselves to live their most authentic, invigorated life - a journey I have been on myself as well. I’m so grateful to be doing what I love in this amazing city.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: First and foremost, I am a relational therapist. Earning my client’s trust is my number one priority. I challenge the conventional, medical model of psychotherapy which is rooted in seeing therapists as experts and their clients as patients with a disorder that needs to be "treated." I don’t see humans this way. People are way too complex and interesting for that. I understand the human condition in a holistic, strengths-based way - each of us is adaptive, resilient, and got to where we are for a reason. I value staying engaged in my personal and professional growth through advanced training and social justice oriented education. I am committed to anti-racism and anti-oppression and bring these values to my work. I genuinely invest in my clients and deeply honor the trust and bond that occurs in therapy.

specialities.name: Attachment Theory
specialities.description: I believe deeply in the power of human connection and how it shapes us. Our earliest significant relationships heavily influence how we learn to see ourselves and relate to others and the world. These dynamics evolve over our adult lives. It can be tremendously helpful to look at these histories and patterns to learn about ourselves and make change from a deeper place of self-understanding.

specialities.name: Feminist
specialities.description: When we reflect on our feelings and experiences, it is important to acknowledge the various systemic and societal influences at play. Over our lifetime, we naturally internalize messages from our culture that ultimately inform our beliefs about ourselves in the world. Feminist therapy focuses on understanding this in order to help us move beyond limiting beliefs and live a truly authentic life.

specialities.name: Existential
specialities.description: Many of us are on an ongoing journey to understand our life's meaning and purpose. We are all longing to feel a sense of self-worth/uniqueness, as well as a sense of belonging/connectedness in the world as we grow and change. With the right support and self-awareness, I believe we all have the capacity to live an expansive, meaningful life.

specialities.name: LGBTQ Issues
specialities.description: With a strong background in social justice and a personal connection to the LGBTQ community, I am dedicated to working with issues around LGBTQ identity development and navigating relationships and the world within this context. I am trans and non-binary affirming and dedicated to staying informed on the needs and struggles of the entire queer community.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: We are dynamic beings who are shaped by our experiences. I don't see mental health struggles as a sign that something is "broken" or "wrong," but rather an understandable reaction to one's experiences that we get to examine together. I use a framework of Interpersonal Neurobiology to understand the impacts of trauma. Once we understand how experiences have impacted us, we can make more conscious decisions about what needs attention and healing, and what we want to focus on and change.

specialities.name: Loss or Grief
specialities.description: Grief/loss is a particularly special and delicate piece of the human experience and our understanding of mental health, as the process of grief/loss is universal, yet distinctly unique to each individual's felt experience. I believe grief plays a much larger role in our mental health struggles than most of us realize. I use this framework to support clients in building self-compassion and self-understanding, as well as growing their capacity to hold and move through life's painful experiences.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: We all experience anxiety to some degree. Anxiety is a natural reaction to feeling unsafe or uncertain, and it often escalates when we aren't trusting ourselves in those fears. Sometimes we get trapped in a cycle of anxiety, and it feels impossible to break free. In therapy we work to make sense of the roots of your anxiety, as you learn to tolerate, manage, and alleviate some of that discomfort through finding a real sense of self-trust, wholeness, and clarity.

specialities.name: Gender Identity
specialities.description: I enjoy supporting trans and non-binary clients in their path of gender liberation–whatever that looks like. I am trained through Brave Space to write letters on behalf of trans clients for any medical interventions they might need. I have been (and continue to be) on my own personal gender journey.

name: Rebeca Rocha
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I am an LCSW with a Ph.D. in Psychology and Culture, providing social justice-oriented, trauma-focused, and culturally sensitive services.
ideal_client: The majority of my clients are young and middle-aged adults from historically marginalized cultures and racial backgrounds. In order to serve our community efficiently, I prioritize individuals from historically marginalized groups or those with specific cultural needs..

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I approach my work with compassion, full presence, and a nonjudgmental stance, focusing on individuals' strengths. Witnessing the transformative journey of self-acceptance is a profound passion of mine. It would be an honor to earn your trust and accompany you on this special path. Taking into account each person's unique wishes and needs, I have effectively utilized therapeutic interventions such as Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), Somatic Experiencing (SE), Motivational Interviewing (MI), and Mindfulness. My experience includes working with diverse populations, including domestic violence survivors, unaccompanied immigrant and refugee youth, and individuals addressing trauma, grief, depression, substance use problems, psychosis, and anxiety. While recognizing the impact of oppression, ableism, racism, misogyny, heterosexism, and trauma on well-being, I commit time to understanding the resources, qualities, values, and resilience of those under my care.

approaches.My Values as a Therapist: I hold the belief that humans are inherently social beings, continually influencing and being influenced by their environment. Furthermore, I acknowledge the profound connection between the body and mind. Following traumatic experiences, our bodies may retain the impact of those events as we strive to endure and move forward with our lives. Lacking sufficient support, these traumas can become overwhelming, manifesting in diverse forms like anxiety, depression, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), substance abuse, and a range of other physical and mental health challenges.

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I have received my Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) training in 2012 /2013 through EMDR Humanitarian Assistance Program (EMDRHAP).

specialities.name: Somatic Therapy (Body Centered)
specialities.description: I am a Somatic Experiencing (SE) practitioner. I have received the 3-year professional training from SE International. SE is a body-oriented therapeutic approach for trauma healing.

specialities.name: Mindfulness-based
specialities.description: I have employed Mindfulness practices in my work since 2012. I have attended a DBT mindfulness training through the Behavioral Tech in 2012 and a mindfulness training in 2016 through PESI.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: I have 6 years of experience working with immigrants and people of color. I have a PhD in Clinical Psychology and Culture, and I am knowledgeable about issues of systemic oppression. Having come to the U.S. as an immigrant from Brazil myself, I have a deep understanding of the challenges of adjusting to a new country or being part of a historically marginalized group.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: I have a PhD in Clinical Psychology and Culture. Spirituality is a important cultural component. My dissertation explores spirituality, religion, and substance use problems.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR and have experience working with individuals with significant trauma history. I am enrolled in the Somatic Experiencing 3-year professional program. I am in the last year of the program.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I am trained in EMDR and Mindfulness practices to manage symptoms of depression specifically. I have also provided services to individuals with a history of depression and worked as a crisis therapist from 2018 to 2020. I also am specialized in risk assessments and working with individuals who are considering suicide.

name: Greg Campanile
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: I am passionate about helping people connect with themselves and live a life that feels meaningful and integrated.
ideal_client: I work with individuals with a variety of issues including, but not limited to, anxiety, depression, relationship problems, trauma, grief and loss, and sustaining recovery. I aspire for my practice to feel welcoming to clients of any cultural background, race, gender, worldview, or faith.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach to therapy is psychodynamic. I have found the Internal Family Systems model to be helpful, and also use motivational interviewing, expressive arts interventions, and mindfulness training when appropriate. I have a background in arts and music, and creativity has an influence on the way I practice psychotherapy. Every client is unique, and I try to tailor my approach to meet your specific needs and to help you achieve your goals. I may be able to negotiate a sliding scale fee for clients paying out of pocket and experiencing financial hardship.

name: Lesley Burke
title: Licensed Art Therapist
intro: I offer transpersonal, somatic art therapy and specialize in working with trauma survivors and neurodivergent adult clients and supervisees
ideal_client: I enjoy working with highly sensitive, neurodivergent, creative and deep-thinking humans who are navigating life transitions, grief, healing trauma, feeling blocked, or experiencing a spiritual emergency and needing support in grounding and integrating. I support the LGBTQIA community, including those on the Ace spectrum, and people in non-monogamous or poly relationships. I also work with those leaving religious groups, child free people, and peri/menopausal women.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My approach is very client-centered and I tend to be more non-directive although I do provide feedback and reflections, and will introduce skills and practices when appropriate. I believe everyone deserves a chance to heal and that therapy can help facilitate a connection to a client's inner healing intelligence. Some of the ways I approach therapy include art therapy, somatic therapy, parts work, and transpersonal therapy. I specialize in psychedelic integration and transpersonal art therapy.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: Art making is a personal path for me that is about much more than the finished work. From processing emotions and experiences, to moving energy or simply enjoying the flow state and process of creation, the creative process is the best healer. My counseling and psychology training was very structured, clinical and scientific. Always fascinated by nature and science, I can be a quiet observer, logical thinker and problem solver but I am first and foremost an artist and mystic at heart. In my free time when I am not making art I like to go hiking, work out, spend time with my pets, and take care of my many houseplants and herb garden. My personal spiritual beliefs and practices include nature-based spirituality, yoga philosophy, hermeticism, and I identify as a witch and recovering Catholic.

specialities.name: Art Therapy
specialities.description: I am a board certified registered art therapist (ATR-BC) and enjoy helping clients engage with their own creative energy to facilitate healing. This may look very different depending on the individual, but can include painting, drawing, collage-making, art journaling, photography, sewing, or sculpture/ mixed media. I generally use the “art as therapy” approach which means that the art-making process itself is heal

specialities.name: EMDR
specialities.description: I have completed the basic EMDR training (40 hours plus supervision) through the EMDR International Association, and have been practicing with this modality since 2016. EMDR is believed to activate the nervous system to move traumatic experiences from being stored in the body to the form of narrative memories, and can help relieve hyper vigilance, anxiety, depression, feeling shut down, emotionally overwhelmed and other trauma exposure symptoms.

name: AJ Bruce
title: Professional Counselor Associate
intro: Therapy for men focused on building emotional intelligence and improving communication of their emotions with loved ones.
ideal_client: As men, we're often socialized to disconnect from our emotions, which can make it difficult to identify or express what we’re truly feeling. This not only affects our relationships but also causes personal distress, leaving us feeling stuck and isolated.

approaches.How I Can Help You: The great news is that growth and healing are within reach. I’ve supported many people in navigating their emotions, building stronger relationships, and gaining confidence in who they are. Work with me involves practical tools to understand your internal world, manage overwhelming feelings, and uncover patterns that may be holding you back. As you grow in emotional intelligence, you’ll deepen your connections and develop a stronger, more authentic sense of self.

approaches.More About the People I Treat: I work with people who are seeking to better understand and express their emotions. Whether you’re dealing with anger, depression, anxiety, relationship struggles, or personal growth challenges, I help people build emotional intelligence and improve communication. Many people come to me feeling stuck in unhealthy patterns, disconnected from their emotions, or struggling to navigate difficult conversations. Together, we’ll work to overcome these barriers, leading to healthier relationships and a deeper, more authentic sense of self.

specialities.name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT)
specialities.description: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) is an evidence based approach to therapy that helps us process and change our relationship with uncomfortable thoughts and feelings, rather than push them away. The beautiful thing is that when we make room for life’s less comfortable experiences we also make room for the joyous ones. Rather than trying to ‘conquer’ your struggles, ACT empowers you to transform them into stepping stones toward personal growth.

specialities.name: Men's Issues
specialities.description: I specialize in helping men build emotional intelligence, express their emotions, manage anger and stress, improve communication, and navigate relationships and personal growth challenges.

specialities.name: Depression
specialities.description: I specialize in treating depression by helping you transform your relationship with difficult thoughts and feelings through Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT), mindfulness practices, and building a genuine, supportive therapeutic bond to guide you toward healing, meaning, and joy. Together, we'll work to identify your core values and take meaningful steps toward a life that aligns with what truly matters to you.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: I specialize in treating anxiety by helping you break free from the endless cycle of trying to 'not think about it' or 'just not worry.' I use Acceptance and Commitment Therapy and mindfulness practices to help people transform their relationship with anxiety, rather than avoid it.

specialities.name: Anger Management
specialities.description: I specialize in helping people understand and manage their anger by exploring its underlying causes and developing healthier coping strategies. Rather than repressing emotions, I help clients change their relationship with anger, and navigating difficult emotions in more effective ways.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: Whether it's a single traumatic event or the lasting effects of long-term trauma, I help people explore its impact on their lives. I assist clients in changing their relationship with painful memories and emotions, supporting them as they process their experiences and take meaningful steps toward building a life that reflects their values.

name: Danette Gillespie-Otto
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: Greetings BIPOC womxn! Communion is being together and speaking the language of the heart. Let's undertake your healing journey together.
ideal_client: I specialize in working with Womxn and Femmes of color dealing with anxiety, depression, trauma, relationship concerns, workplace stressors, racism, sexism, heterosexism and cultural dislocation.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: I am an intuitive, attachment-based therapist who specializes in working with Womxn and Femmes of Color. Together we unravel the knots that bind you from the inside out. I offer compassion, connection, fresh perspective and practical tools to aid in your healing. I use cultural sensitivity, interpersonal neurobiology, sand tray therapy and cognitive behavioral therapy in sessions.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: I received my Master's of Social Work from the George Warren Brown School of Social Work at Washington University in St. Louis, Missouri in 2000. I have been a licensed clinical social worker since 2007. I have worked in community mental health, quality improvement, administration, local government, mentoring, research and private practice. I specialize in working with African-American, biracial and multi-racial clients of African descent, though I work with clients of all racial and ethnic backgrounds. I provide a holistic assessment and support that is individualized to your unique needs. I practice in a way that forms bridge between biology, psychology and spirituality--balancing these aspects of the whole. Give yourself the gift of deep alignment and healing. You deserve it!

specialities.name: Interpersonal
specialities.description: Interpersonal Neurobiology demonstrates how we as humans help each other weather the storms of life through relationship and attuned, compassionate care. I am currently in training with Bonnie Badenoch, PhD, one of the leaders in the field of interpersonal neurobiology, and this has become my main mode of practice.

specialities.name: Cognitive Behavioral (CBT)
specialities.description: Cognitive behavioral therapy, or the relationship between thoughts, feelings and behaviors, is my secondary practice modality. I have extensive training in this model.

specialities.name: Cultural and Systemic Oppression
specialities.description: Prior to becoming a psychotherapist, I received training as a facilitator on issues of diversity and systemic oppression. Thus, my clinical lens is honed to not only recognize our individual and family experiences, but our group identity traumas as well. In therapy, we work with both your unique personal experience and your group identity experience.

specialities.name: Spirituality
specialities.description: For people for whom spirituality is a main focus of their lives, I enjoy incorporating a spiritual perspective into my therapeutic work. I work best with clients who have a non-dualistic spiritual perspective or mystical leanings.

specialities.name: PTSD
specialities.description: I have specialized training in the treatment of trauma, using both cognitive behavioral approaches and interpersonal neurobiology. I have worked with traumatized people for over 10 years.

specialities.name: Anxiety
specialities.description: Anxiety can plague our lives, making it difficult to function. I specialize in connecting with the parts of ourselves that are living in conscious or unconscious fear, bringing care and compassion to these parts.

name: Kimberlee Dennery
title: Licensed Clinical Social Worker
intro: I provide online therapy to individuals in Oregon. You can schedule an intake appointment with me by clicking "Schedule Now."
ideal_client: When you’re going through something difficult—whether it’s a recent life transition or something you’ve been carrying for a long time—it can help to talk with someone who listens with care and without judgment. I provide a safe, inclusive space for clients to be heard, seen, and supported while exploring what matters most to them.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My goal is to help you reconnect with your internal resources and feel more grounded in yourself, especially during times of stress or uncertainty. Therapy isn’t about fixing you—it’s about supporting you as you find ways to make sense of what’s happening and move forward with greater clarity. Clients have shared that they feel comfortable in sessions with me, often appreciating my warmth, authenticity, and sense of humor. I believe in taking an individualized approach, drawing from therapeutic frameworks like mindfulness, Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), narrative therapy, and family systems theory. Together, we’ll find what works best for you.

approaches.Why I Became a Therapist: Even as a high school student, I was drawn to psychology and sociology—I knew early on that I wanted to be in a helping profession. Over the years, I’ve worked in a variety of settings, including hospitals and outpatient clinics, supporting adolescents, adults, and older adults. These experiences have deepened my belief that mental health care should be compassionate, accessible, and affirming for everyone. In addition to individual therapy, I’ve provided support for families and couples, helping them navigate changes, improve communication, and better understand each other. My clinical training includes advanced coursework through Therapy Training Boston in family and couples counseling, which continues to inform my work with clients today.

name: Noah Carolan LMFT
title: Licensed Marriage Family Therapist
intro: If you are seeking help due to issues surrounding personal trauma, I may be able to help.
ideal_client: Chronic depression and anxiety, relationship issues, unwanted behavior (including addictions), racing thoughts, or chronic low self-worth, are problems within my specialty.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: The basis of my training as a family therapist focused on systemic principles and practices. In essence this is a contrast to the individual-focused heath model, and instead emphasizes understanding and utilizing the context (i.e. relationships, societal and cultural factors, etc..) of our lives to make treatment more effect. My primary clinical emphasis is around treating emotional trauma, which I offer the treatment method of EMDR therapy for. I also have significant training and education in attachment theory, and attachment-related interventions. Additionally I enjoy working with and welcome members of all cultures, ethnicities, and backgrounds into my practice. Included in my interests and training is work with members of the LGBTQ community.

name: Richard Halpern
title: Professional Counselor
intro: Parenting is amazing + challenging! Let's create a "parenting toolkit" co-parents can use now to positively impact your child's behavior.
ideal_client: Any parent with a parenting challenge! Sole, coupled, separated, or divorced - open to exploring positive ways to co-parent, build your parenting confidence, and working with your children to team up to create a happier home. Any couple seeking to resolve communication break downs, unpack different attachment styles, defining relationship roles. The goal: to feel seen, heard, and understood. Teenagers who are struggling with teen life. Wanting to feel good/better about themselves.

approaches.My Approach to Helping: My counseling approach is practical and down to earth. My focus is on positive parenting and couple strengthening strategies, which are easy to apply right away. I also work with couples to resolve conflicts and establish ground rules so that you feel seen, heard, and understood. To help ease your parenting anxiety, we develop a structured plan forward, while emphasizing your strengths and parenting style. You deserve a life feeling balanced, energized, and fun! For separated or divorced parents, we focus on co-parenting as a team, even after a difficult breakup. For sole parents or dealing with a relationship ending, we focus on self care and community resources. My practice is affirming to ALL parents and couples from diverse relationship orientations, LGBTQ+ friendly, and empathetic to the trauma of tough break ups. It starts with a deep breath and a free consultation. Sliding fee scale. In keeping with social distance during this pandemic, all sessions are via video.

approaches.My Personal Beliefs and Interests: My career has traversed working with parents in a huge variety of settings. I coordinated a public School Counseling program K-12 for 16 years and am a licensed School Counselor in Oregon. I worked with parents on the many issues that impact kids at school. I also coordinated an alternative program for children age 11-17 arrested for minor crimes. We worked with parents to teach empathy to their child. I currently teach the class: Helping Children Cope With Family Change for Multnomah Family Court. This is exclusively for separating & divorcing parents. My Masters Degree is in Counseling from the University of Montana; my B. A. in Psychology is from the University of Tennessee. I'm certified as a Trauma Informed Coach, a Certified Positive Discipline Parent Educator, and a Master Trainer with the Oregon Registry (workshops for child care professionals). As a divorced father, I positively co-parented raising 2 wonderful kids with their mom.

specialities.name: Couples Counseling
specialities.description: I integrate a couples counseling approach to positively learn how to co-parent as a team or resolve conflicts. Areas of focus: Developing positive habits around communication, understanding our unique communication styles, defining our relationship roles, and discovering our shared (or different) values. Empathy is key. Our goal? To feel seen, heard and understood, all to foster better connection, intimacy, and trust from a non-judgmental place.

specialities.name: Intervention
specialities.description: My focus is offering practical interventions as a strategy to reduce the likelihood of conflict. Example: If a child is prone to (what feels like) too many temper tantrums, what can we do to help both the child and parent see a pattern in the behavior, and practice self regulation techniques? Solution = stop the tantrum before it ever begins.

specialities.name: Humanistic
specialities.description: A Client Centered approach developed by Carl Rogers was the philosophical core of my Masters and I still bring it into my practice today. It emphasizes a nondirective, nonjudgemental, empathetic approach that empowers and motivates the client in the therapeutic process. This counseling is based on Rogers’ belief that everyone strives for and has the capacity to fulfill his or her own potential.

specialities.name: Relationship / Marriage Issues
specialities.description: I've been teaching the class: 'Helping Children Cope With Family Change' for 4 years as a Parent Educator for Multnomah County Family Court Services. I have met with hundreds of parents in a discussion group format, all of whom are moving through conflict which resulted in a separation or divorce. My approach is to offer practical solutions and experiential exercises to encourage communication.

specialities.name: Personal Growth
specialities.description: The experience of raising children is an opportunity self-reflect and to explore your current beliefs about parent-child relationships. The intense personal growth which we can discover though being a parent (and learning from our children) can be affirming, challenging, and incredibly exciting! Personal growth is a constant compass bearing in my Counseling practice. I'm also certified as a Trauma Informed Coach and have lots of familiarity dealing with breakup grief.

specialities.name: Parenting
specialities.description: Kudos to you for being open to exploring ways to be better at parenting! This is a hugely rewarding endeavor, but did not come with an instruction manual. I can help! I'm Certified as a Parent Educator in nationally recognized Positive Discipline + Nurturing Parenting Programs. 25+ years experience working with parents, Currently am a Parent Educator for Multnomah Family Court. And, a dad myself!

specialities.name: Child or Adolescent Issues
specialities.description: I coordinated a public school counseling program and was a K-12 School Counselor for 16 years. I met with students with personal, academic, career, and family issues (caseload 400+ students). I dealt with just about any problem you can imagine, and did so in an easy going yet structured way students related to.
